Three-time Formula 1 world champion Nelson Piquet received the Gregor Grant Award at this year’s Autosport Awards.
The accolade for Lifetime Achievement in Motorsport, has previously been awarded to drivers including Nigel Mansell, Niki Lauda, and Alain Prost.
“The time I had in motor racing was fantastic,” Piquet said as he received the award.
“To learn and work with a team was the most important.
“There is something that I want to say to everyone who is participating in motorsport: Racing taught me so many things in life, to be more responsible, to be on time and all of the things have made me successful outside of motor racing also.”
Piquet’s F1 career spanned over 14 years, in which he took more than 20 race wins. He took his first victory with Brabham in 1980, a year before securing the championship with the team.
After a more disappointing 1982, Piquet took the championship again in ’83.
The Brazilian switched to Williams in 1986, finishing third in the title race in his first season with the team, before taking his third title the following year.
He also raced in the Indy 500 and 24 Hours of Le Mans.
Derek Warwick, who was President of the British Racing Drivers’ Club until earlier this year, also received the Gregor Grant Award.
rewrite:
At the recent Autosport Awards ceremony, three-time Formula 1 world champion Nelson Piquet was presented with the Gregor Grant Award. This honor recognizes Lifetime Achievement in Motorsport, an accolade previously bestowed upon notable drivers such as Nigel Mansell, Niki Lauda, and Alain Prost. Upon acceptance, Piquet reflected that his period in motor racing was a fantastic experience, emphasizing that the collaborative process of learning and working within a team was paramount. He further offered counsel to current participants, stating that racing instilled in him vital life principles, including heightened responsibility and punctuality, which subsequently contributed to his success beyond the sport.

Piquet's Formula 1 career, spanning fourteen years, yielded over twenty Grand Prix victories. His inaugural win occurred with the Brabham team in 1980, preceding his first World Championship with the same constructor the following year. After a less successful 1982 season, he reclaimed the championship in 1983. A transition to Williams in 1986 resulted in a third-place finish in the drivers' standings that year, followed by the capture of his third title in 1987. His competitive endeavors also included participation in the Indianapolis 500 and the 24 Hours of Le Mans. The Gregor Grant Award was also conferred upon Derek Warwick, the former President of the British Racing Drivers’ Club.

Former France Coach Michel Dies At 70
Former France captain and coach Henri Michel is dead, according to reports in France.
Michel passed on at the age of 70 after a protracted illness on Tuesday.
Born in Aix where he started his football career, Michel played 58 times for France.
He became a coach and led the French team to Olympic gold in 1984 in Los Angeles and third in the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.
The Frenchman also coached Morocco, Cameroun, Tunisia, Côte d’Ivoire, Equatorial Guinea and Kenya.
Michel was officially named a Nantes legend last Friday.

NEW YORK (CBSNewYork) — It’s that time of year again, when New York baseball fans come together for the annual Subway Series between the Mets and Yankees.
The series kicks off Monday night in the Bronx.
As CBS2’s Otis Livingston reported, the Mets are coming off a dominating series against the Phillies, winning three of four down in Philadelphia.
The Yankees, meanwhile, lost two of three to the first place Red Sox.
Sunday’s loss was in excruciating fashion, but for the next four days Big Apple bragging rights are on the line.
Two games will be played at the Stadium, followed by two at Citi Field.
The Yankees are reeling after Sunday’s loss to the Sox, when Aroldis Chapman gave up a game tying homer to 20-year-old phenom Rafael Devers in the 9th. They went on to lose in the 10th, and are now five and a half games out in the division race.
Meanwhile, the Mets — despite winning three of four in Philly — have been out of the playoff race for much of the season, but they have Michael Conforto to look forward to seeing.
Conforto crushed his team-leading 26th home run of the season Sunday.
No matter what the situation, it’s always an important Subway Series showdown.
The Bombers lead the overall regular season series 63-45, and fans could be in store for an offensive explosion in game 1.
Starting pitchers Luis Montero and Luis Cessa have both struggled mightily this season.
rewrite:
The annual Subway Series, a regular-season interleague competition between New York City's Major League Baseball franchises, the Mets and the Yankees, commences this week. The four-game contest begins Monday evening at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, with subsequent games scheduled at Citi Field. This series arrives following divergent outcomes for the two teams in their preceding matchups. The Mets enter the series with considerable momentum, having secured three victories in a four-game series against the Philadelphia Phillies. Conversely, the Yankees concluded their series against the American League East-leading Boston Red Sox with two losses in three games, including a particularly disheartening defeat on Sunday.

The Yankees' loss was secured in extra innings after relief pitcher Aroldis Chapman surrendered a game-tying, ninth-inning home run to Boston's 20-year-old standout, Rafael Devers. This result places the Yankees five and a half games behind in the divisional standings. The Mets, despite their recent success, have remained largely non-competitive in the postseason race for the majority of the season. A notable positive for the franchise is the performance of outfielder Michael Conforto, who hit his team-leading 26th home run on Sunday.

Historically, the Yankees lead the all-time regular-season series 63-45. The opening game may feature significant offensive production, as both projected starting pitchers, Luis Montero and Luis Cessa, have posted notably high earned run averages this season. Regardless of the teams' respective standings, the Subway Series consistently represents a significant event for the city's baseball enthusiasts.

Revellers from a Dundee pub proved that they had a very dark sense of humour when they turned up at a local bowling green carrying a coffin.
Dougie Taylor, 50, a member of the Maryfield Bowling Club and Stobswell Bar regular, said plans were already afoot for next year’s event after a cowboy riding a costume bull led a procession into Maryfield Bowling Club accompanied by pallbearers carrying a life-size casket containing the Grim Reaper.
The hilarious video, which was posted online on Sunday afternoon, was the build-up to an annual bowling match which sees Stobswell Bar regulars vying to take bragging rights as the bottom of the bar compete against the top of the bar in lawn bowls.
The annual bowling event has “escalated” over recent years after it was set up in memory of former Stobie Bar barmen, John Ward.
The 90-second clip shows a number of revellers from the Stobswell Bar young team coming along Madeira Street being led by a cowboy while a purple flare is set alight.
The procession comes to a halt as coffin bearers make their way into the bowling club to unveil a man wearing a Grim Reaper costume inside.
Dougie said the “light-hearted” antics had made for a “great day”, although some people may have been perplexed as the group made their way up the Forfar Road on Sunday afternoon.
He said: “Every year the lads try and outdo themselves – there is talk of trying to get a plane involved in it somehow next year but there was over 100 people there yesterday – we’ve been doing it for the past four years now.
“It is titled the top of the bar vs the bottom of the bar – basically the young boys against the old boys. Fortunately I still find myself in the young team and we took the victory on the day.
“We put the Grim Reaper in the casket on Madeira Street and we walked him in – we had one of the old team’s names on the casket.
“It was hilarious. After the match the celebrations continued in the Stobswell Bar – there’ll be a few sore heads today.”
rewrite:
Participants from a Dundee public house demonstrated a notably macabre sense of humour by arriving at a local bowling green in possession of a coffin. Dougie Taylor, aged 50, a member of the Maryfield Bowling Club and a regular patron of the Stobswell Bar, indicated that preparations are already underway for next year's iteration of the event. This follows a procession into the Maryfield Bowling Club that featured a cowboy riding a costume bull, accompanied by pallbearers carrying a life-sized casket containing an individual dressed as the Grim Reaper. A video recording of this incident, shared online on Sunday afternoon, served as a prelude to an annual bowling match. This contest sees regulars of the Stobswell Bar competing for ceremonial honours, pitting those who frequent the lower end of the establishment against those who congregate at the upper end in a game of lawn bowls.

The annual event, established in memory of former Stobswell Bar staff member John Ward, has reportedly "escalated" in scale and spectacle in recent years. The ninety-second clip depicts a group of younger patrons from the bar proceeding along Madeira Street, led by a cowboy figure, with a purple flare ignited for dramatic effect. The procession halts as the coffin bearers enter the bowling club to reveal the Grim Reaper costume within. Mr. Taylor characterised the "light-hearted" proceedings as contributing to a "great day," while acknowledging that the spectacle may have bewildered some observers as the group traversed Forfar Road that afternoon.

He elaborated: "Each year the participants endeavour to surpass previous efforts—there is speculation about potentially incorporating an aeroplane in some capacity next year. The event yesterday attracted over one hundred attendees, and we have now conducted it for the past four years. The competition is formally titled 'the top of the bar versus the bottom of the bar,' essentially constituting a match between younger and older patrons. I remain fortunate to be classified with the younger team, which secured victory on this occasion. We placed the Grim Reaper effigy into the casket on Madeira Street and proceeded with it into the club—the casket bore the name of a member from the opposing, older team. The atmosphere was highly amusing. Post-match celebrations continued within the Stobswell Bar, undoubtedly resulting in a number of individuals experiencing headaches today."

Harvey Weinstein borrowed $1 million from his company last year in the months before public revelations of his alleged sexual misconduct plunged the movie studio that bore his name into bankruptcy.
In all, Weinstein took home nearly $3 million during his last half year at the award-winning studio, new court papers say. Additionally, Weinstein Co. paid nearly $2 million to service a debt Weinstein personally guaranteed, which was owed to a company controlled by billionaire Len Blavatnik. Records filed on Tuesday in the bankruptcy case of Weinstein Co. detail what Weinstein, his brother and studio co-chief Bob Weinstein and other leaders received from the company before and after misconduct allegations against Harvey Weinstein were published in October.
Millions of dollars in pay, expense reimbursements, advances and loans went to the Weinstein brothers and to David Glasser, a top executive the studio fired in February, after New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman, in a lawsuit, lambasted the company for failing to investigate and address the misconduct claims against Harvey Weinstein. Glasser’s lawyers have disputed his firing and said he “acted appropriately and responsibly whenever allegations of misconduct were brought to his attention.”
Bob Weinstein took nearly $6 million in compensation and other payments, while Glasser, the company’s former chief operating officer, took more than $4 million in the year before the March 19 bankruptcy filing, according to papers filed Tuesday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del. Some of the money that went to Bob Weinstein is listed as payments on a loan he made to the studio. Additionally, Bob Weinstein received more than $600,000 in expense reimbursements in the last four months of the year.
An expanded version of this report appears on WSJ.com.
Also popular on WSJ.com:
Amazon to start offering in-car deliveries.
How to dress like a billionaire.
rewrite:
In the months preceding public disclosures of alleged sexual misconduct by Harvey Weinstein, which precipitated the bankruptcy of the eponymous film studio, Mr. Weinstein obtained a $1 million loan from the company. Recent court filings indicate that, in total, Mr. Weinstein received approximately $3 million in compensation during his final six months of employment at the award-winning studio. Furthermore, The Weinstein Company disbursed nearly $2 million to service a debt personally guaranteed by Mr. Weinstein and owed to an entity controlled by billionaire Len Blavatnik. Documents submitted on Tuesday to the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware in Wilmington detail the financial distributions to Harvey Weinstein, his brother and co-chairman Bob Weinstein, and other senior executives both prior to and following the October publication of misconduct allegations.

Substantial sums in the form of compensation, expense reimbursements, advances, and loans were allocated to the Weinstein brothers and to David Glasser, a senior executive terminated in February. This termination occurred after New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman, in a civil suit, criticized the company for neglecting to properly investigate and redress the allegations against Harvey Weinstein. Legal representatives for Mr. Glasser have contested his dismissal, asserting that he “acted appropriately and responsibly whenever allegations of misconduct were brought to his attention.”

According to the bankruptcy filings, Bob Weinstein received nearly $6 million in combined compensation and other payments in the period leading to the March 19 bankruptcy petition. This figure includes repayments related to a loan he extended to the studio, alongside over $600,000 in expense reimbursements during the final four months of the preceding year. David Glasser, the former chief operating officer, received more than $4 million in the year before the bankruptcy filing.

Now this is flying the friendly skies.
An overwhelmed mom flying on Finnair with four kids had her hands full — but an off-duty pilot took control by feeding one of her babies.
Finnair Capt. Tom Nystrom offered to hold one of the woman’s infants, who appeared to be on cloud nine as the amiable airman dutifully held up a bottle.
“I have children of my own… so it came natural to me to help this customer with her babies,” Nystrom, who was on the flight as a passenger, told the Independent.
Nystrom even swapped kids with the mom when others in her brood became fussy.
The airborne act of kindness stood in stark contrast with United’s ejection of a passenger to make room for an airlines crew member, a violent act that sparked a public-relations debacle.
Flight attendant Ami Niemela lavished praise on Nystrom and her other airborne colleagues.
“Naturally one cannot travel with two babies on one’s lap, so we had to solve the dilemma of missing lap, otherwise it would have been a no go for mom and the kids,” she wrote on Instagram.
“Luckily we had our positioning crew on board and wonderful Tom took the task of being the extra-lap. Don’t you find them quite adorable!”
When they landed at the Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, Niemela posted an adorable photo of the uniformed captain smiling at the camera as the chubby-cheeked baby gazed at him.
“Acts of kindness, priceless,” an Instagram user posted.
Another took a swipe at embattled United Airlines, which has faced a fierce backlash across the globe for yanking Dr. David Dao, 69, from his seat and leaving him battered and bruised.
“United airlines beats their customers while finnair takes care of even babies,” wrote isabelbjon.
Finland’s flag carrier capitalized on the heart-warming act by posting a message on its official Twitter account.
“Kudos to our purser @finami & pilot Tom! Story about a pilot looking after a baby is simply adorable,” tweeted Finnair, which last month was awarded Best European Airline at the TTG China Travel Awards for the second year in a row.
rewrite:
A notable incident of in-flight assistance underscores the divergent approaches to customer service within the aviation industry. A passenger aboard a Finnair flight, a mother traveling with four children, faced considerable difficulty managing her infants. The situation was alleviated when an off-duty Finnair captain, Tom Nystrom, who was traveling as a passenger, intervened by offering to hold and feed one of the babies. Nystrom later explained to the Independent that, as a parent himself, the act of assistance felt natural. He further accommodated the mother by periodically holding different children as needed during the flight.

This episode of spontaneous aid was publicly commended by flight attendant Ami Niemela via Instagram. Niemela clarified the operational necessity of the intervention, noting that aviation safety regulations prohibit a single adult from holding two infants on their lap. The presence of the positioning crew, including Nystrom, provided a crucial solution, allowing the family to travel. Niemela subsequently posted a photograph at Helsinki-Vantaa Airport featuring Captain Nystrom, in uniform, holding the infant, which she described as an adorable outcome of the collective effort.

The incident attracted significant positive attention on social media, with many commentators explicitly contrasting this compassionate act with a contemporaneous and widely publicized event involving United Airlines. In that case, a passenger was forcibly removed to accommodate airline staff, an action that resulted in injury and provoked global criticism and a public relations crisis. Social media users directly juxtaposed the two events, highlighting Finnair's supportive service against the other carrier's coercive approach.

Finnair's corporate communications strategically amplified the positive narrative. The airline's official Twitter account praised the crew members involved, sharing the story under the caption "simply adorable." This publicity aligns with the carrier's recent brand achievements, including being named Best European Airline at the TTG China Travel Awards for a consecutive year. Thus, a routine act of crew assistance was transformed into a significant public relations asset, emphasizing a corporate ethos of customer care and favorably distinguishing the airline's service model within the competitive industry landscape.

CALGARY — About 100 people are out of their homes after an overnight four-alarm fire that extensively damaged their Calgary condominium.
A total of 64 suites were evacuated when the fire broke out early Wednesday morning at the four-storey complex in the southeast neighbourhood of Inglewood.
There were no injuries and residents say a group of neighbours went around pounding on doors telling everyone to get out.
Eight engines and four ladder trucks were called to the scene and a neighbouring condo was also evacuated as crews fought to keep the flames from spreading.
Fire officials say there’s heavy damage to the top floor of the complex, while floors below have water damage.
The cause of the fire is under investigation but residents say the blaze appeared to start on a fourth-floor balcony.
“It was frightening for us because we’re older people and we wanted to be sure everybody is out,” said resident Pat Tetley. “We’ve had alarms before go off, and people take them for granted. Once you saw the fire, you know this is time to leave.”
Tetley’s wife, Jane, said some of their neighbours were handing out coffee, blankets and even pairs of shoes once everyone was outside.
“People just ran out with nothing on their feet, so we’re very grateful this isn’t the middle of winter,” she said.
The exterior of an adjacent building was also damaged.
Calgary fire Chief Steve Dongworth said it’s too early to determine the cause of the fire. (CFFR, CTV Calgary)
rewrite:
An overnight four-alarm fire at a condominium complex in Calgary’s Inglewood neighbourhood has resulted in the displacement of approximately one hundred residents. The incident, which occurred in the early hours of Wednesday morning, necessitated the evacuation of all 64 suites within the four-storey structure. Firefighting efforts involved a substantial deployment of resources, including eight engine companies and four ladder trucks. As a precautionary measure, an adjacent residential building was also evacuated to prevent the spread of flames. Preliminary assessments by fire officials indicate extensive damage to the complex’s top floor, with significant water damage sustained on the lower levels. The exterior of a neighbouring building was also affected.

While the official cause remains under investigation by authorities, residents reported that the blaze appeared to originate on a fourth-floor balcony. There were no reported injuries. Residents described a communal response to the emergency, with neighbours alerting occupants by knocking on doors to ensure a complete evacuation. Pat Tetley, a resident, noted the gravity of the situation compared to previous false alarms, stating, “Once you saw the fire, you know this is time to leave.” Following the evacuation, neighbours provided immediate assistance, distributing items such as coffee, blankets, and footwear to those displaced. Jane Tetley observed that many residents exited without proper attire, expressing relief that the event did not occur during winter conditions. Calgary Fire Chief Steve Dongworth has stated that determining the precise cause of the fire is premature at this stage.

The NAACP will teach East Chicago, Indiana residents how to use lead testing kits this week. The training comes as residents continue to cope with lead contaminated soil and water.
The Calumet neighborhood in East Chicago is part of a federal toxic waste cleanup site contaminated with lead and arsenic. The neighborhood is also having a problem with lead leaching out of drinking water service lines.
The NAACP is partnering with Indiana State University and the Union of Concerned Scientists to teach residents how to use kits to test for lead in soil, air, and water. The NAACP’s Denise Abdul-Rahman says it will also help school-aged children cope with a legacy of lead contamination.
“[It will] peak their consciousness and awareness,” Abdul-Rahman says, and “give them tools, and to teach them some forms of empowerment.”
Abdul-Rahman says the training is necessary because of a systemic failure of government at all levels to protect some of Indiana’s most vulnerable residents.
The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency continues to remove lead contaminated soil from the neighborhood. And the Department of Housing and Urban Development recently approved the demolition of a lead contaminated housing complex which was forcibly evacuated over the last year.
rewrite: This week, the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) will conduct training for residents of East Chicago, Indiana, on the utilization of lead testing kits. This initiative responds to the ongoing challenges posed by lead contamination in local soil and water supplies. The Calumet neighborhood, situated within a federal toxic waste cleanup site due to lead and arsenic pollution, additionally faces issues of lead leaching from drinking water service lines. In partnership with Indiana State University and the Union of Concerned Scientists, the NAACP will instruct residents in testing for lead in soil, air, and water. According to the NAACP’s Denise Abdul-Rahman, the program also aims to assist school-aged children in confronting the legacy of contamination by raising their consciousness and providing empowering tools. Abdul-Rahman attributes the necessity of this training to a systemic governmental failure at all levels to safeguard some of Indiana's most vulnerable populations. Concurrently, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency continues soil remediation in the area, and the Department of Housing and Urban Development has sanctioned the demolition of a lead-contaminated housing complex, whose residents were forcibly relocated over the past year.

Talk about a revenge game.
According to Howard Eskin of 94WIP in Philadelphia, the defending Super Bowl champion Eagles will host the Vikings on Thursday, Sept. 6 to open the NFL season.
When #NFL schedule comes out sources tell me #Eagles will play #Vikings to open season Thursday night September 6th in Philadelphia. It’s rematch of NFC Championship game. @SportsRadioWIP — Howard Eskin (@howardeskin) March 19, 2018
This, of course, is a rematch of last season’s NFC Championship Game, in which the Eagles absolutely throttled the Vikings, 38-7.
A lot has change since then, and there’s more to come.
Instead of Case Keenum, the Vikings’ quarterback will be Kirk Cousins. Carson Wentz, who is recovering from torn knee ligaments, might be under center instead of Nick Foles, who led Philadelphia past Minnesota in January.
The Vikings will also have running back Dalvin Cook back, and who knows what else could happen over the next few months before training camp opens.
Minnesota is 13-10 all-time in the regular season against Philadelphia but 0-4 in the playoffs.
rewrite: The forthcoming NFL season opener presents a compelling narrative of postseason redemption. Per reporting by Howard Eskin of Philadelphia’s 94WIP, the defending Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles are scheduled to host the Minnesota Vikings on Thursday, September 6. This contest constitutes a direct rematch of the previous season’s NFC Championship Game, wherein the Eagles decisively defeated the Vikings by a score of 38-7. Significant roster alterations have transpired since that encounter. The Vikings will feature quarterback Kirk Cousins, replacing Case Keenum, while Eagles quarterback Carson Wentz—recovering from a knee ligament injury—may return to supplant Nick Foles, who orchestrated the January victory. Minnesota also anticipates the return of running back Dalvin Cook. Historically, the Vikings maintain a 13-10 regular-season advantage over Philadelphia but are 0-4 in playoff meetings, underscoring the heightened stakes of this early-season confrontation.

Lady Gaga shared the first image on Monday from her film remake of A Star is Born, also starring and directed by Bradley Cooper.
The classic Hollywood tale of two stars colliding, one whose career is on the upswing and the other’s waning, has been made three times previously, most recently in 1976 starring Barbra Streisand and Kris Kristofferson.
Lady Gaga, who will be billed under her real name, Stefani Germanotta, wrote beside the image of herself and Bradley on Instagram: “I am so excited to star in my first movie alongside someone I’m so lucky to call my friend. I always wanted to be an actress on the big screen.”
She added, “The story of ‘A Star is Born’ is so special and I’m so grateful to Bradley for making my dream come true.” She signed off by saying: “Can’t wait for you to meet Ally. She has her first scene in 5...”
The film marks Cooper’s directorial debut and, in addition, he is co-producing the project and co-writing it. He will also play country music legend Jackson Maine who is struggling to keep his career on track. Lady Gaga is hopeful singer Ally who Jackson not only takes under his wing but also becomes romantically involved with.
Fans in Indio, California for last weekend’s Coachella music festival kickoff - at which Lady Gaga was one of the headliners - received an added bonus when they were offered $10 tickets to feature as extras in scenes being filmed at the site for the new film. All proceeds from the sales will go to Lady Gaga’s Born This Way Foundation.
A Star is Born is due for release next September.
rewrite:
On Monday, the inaugural promotional image was released for the forthcoming cinematic remake of *A Star Is Born*, featuring the musical artist Lady Gaga and directed by and co-starring Bradley Cooper. This narrative, a classic Hollywood archetype depicting the intersection of two careers—one ascending and the other in decline—has been produced on three prior occasions, with the most recent iteration released in 1976 starring Barbra Streisand and Kris Kristofferson. In the accompanying caption on Instagram, Lady Gaga, credited under her legal name Stefani Germanotta, expressed her enthusiasm: “I am so excited to star in my first movie alongside someone I’m so lucky to call my friend. I always wanted to be an actress on the big screen.” She further noted the significance of the story and her gratitude to Cooper, concluding with a preview of her character: “Can’t wait for you to meet Ally. She has her first scene in 5...”

This project represents Cooper’s directorial debut; he also serves as co-producer and co-writer. His role is that of Jackson Maine, a country music legend grappling with a faltering career, while Lady Gaga portrays the aspiring vocalist Ally, whom Jackson mentors and with whom he becomes romantically involved. During the recent Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in Indio, California, where Lady Gaga was a headlining performer, attendees were offered an opportunity to participate as extras in scenes filmed on location for a fee of ten dollars. All proceeds from these ticket sales are designated for Lady Gaga’s Born This Way Foundation. The film is scheduled for release in September of the coming year.

An escaped inmate is back in jail after leading Dallas authorities on a hunt for him -- and his accomplice is there now, too.
Scroll for more content...
The Dallas County Sheriff's Office says 28-year-old Daniel Brown was captured Sunday evening at a Motel 6 in Grand Prairie. He was with 28-year-old Dieasha Owens, a woman police believe helped him get free from the Dallas County Jail's Suzanne Kays Detention Facility, where he was imprisoned on multiple theft charges.
Brown was discovered missing Sunday morning during an inmate count. He was assigned to work in a kitchen area at the jail; detectives are reviewing security video and believe he may have escaped through a dock area.
Brown is now being charged with escape. He was being held in the jail after a March 2018 arrest on five charges of property theft.
Owens was also arrested at the motel and was booked into the Dallas County Jail Sunday evening with a $5,000 bond, facing a charge of facilitating escape of a correctional facility.
rewrite: Following an extensive search, an escaped detainee has been apprehended and returned to custody alongside a suspected accomplice. The Dallas County Sheriff's Office reports that Daniel Brown, aged 28, was captured on Sunday evening at a Motel 6 in Grand Prairie. He was accompanied by Dieasha Owens, also 28, whom authorities allege assisted in his escape from the Suzanne Kays Detention Facility. Brown, originally detained on multiple property theft charges from a March 2018 arrest, was discovered absent during a routine inmate count on Sunday morning. Preliminary investigation, including review of security footage, indicates he may have exploited his assignment in a kitchen area to exit via a dock. Brown now faces additional charges for escape. Owens was simultaneously arrested and booked into the Dallas County Jail with a $5,000 bond, charged with facilitating escape from a correctional facility.

Baycrest Health Sciences chooses Caradigm Single Sign-On and Context Management
Baycrest Health Sciences (Baycrest), a firm into geriatric residential living, healthcare, research, and innovation, has selected GE Healthcare company Caradigm's Single Sign-On (SSO) and Context Management for identity and access management.
Baycrest is an academic health sciences center fully affiliated with the University of Toronto and offers a care experience for aging clients combined with an extensive clinical training program for students.
It will use Caradigm SSO and Context Management to streamline user access and clinical workflows, as well as to improve mobility and efficiency.
Caradigm SSO and Context Management has been built for healthcare to simplify clinician workflows.
It reduces clicks, simplifies authentication and guides clinicians to the appropriate patient record in seconds across multiple applications.
By removing the need to repeatedly type usernames and passwords, Caradigm SSO and Context Managementenables users to securely access clinical and business applications, which streamlines clinical workflows.
Baycrest Health Sciences executive director for information and technology Maria Muia said: “After in-depth evaluations of identity and access management solutions, it was clear that Caradigm offered the best single sign-on solution to meet the needs of our Centre. The power of Caradigm’s SSO and Context Management solution together provides clinical efficiency and will help to improve care provider and patient experience.”

A 14-year-old girl who died after colliding with a decorated banner pole on Siem Reap City’s Pub Street during Sunday night’s Khmer New Year festivities was electrocuted, and a spa owner was arrested, city police chief Tith Narong said on Monday.
Mony Rothny ran into the iron pole in front of Baray Spa in Svay Dangkum commune, Mr. Narong said.
The pole, decorated with lights and connected to an extension cord running into the building, carried a current after it came into contact with the extension cord’s socket, the police chief said.
He said the pole likely shocked the girl, who was soaking wet after taking part in water fights as part of the celebrations.
The teenager, from Kompong Speu, was pronounced dead at the provincial referral hospital, but her family took her to Royal Hospital in Siem Reap City for a second opinion and received the same determination, Mr. Narong said.
Duong Sokha, chief of the provincial police’s serious crimes bureau, said Meas Sopheak, the spa owner, was arrested on Monday afternoon and would be sent to the provincial court this morning for questioning.

Barattini, who is serving imprisonment without bail ahead of her trial, told La Voz that she suffered great psychological harm because of the leaked tape.
“I cut his penis but not completely: I injured him. It wasn’t complete: I injured him,” she said, according to a translation of her jailhouse interview.

Hospital employees were unable to reattach his penis, Fox News previously reported.
The incident rings similar to the case of Lorena Bobbitt, a woman who, in 1993, cut off her husband’s penis while he was sleeping.
Bobbitt said she did it because she “snapped” after her husband allegedly raped her the previous night.

Sunday came and went without the NHL issuing any further discipline to Bruins forward Brad Marchand for his high hit on John Tavares on Saturday night.
Marchand was assessed a five-minute major penalty for the hit, after taking a direct route to Tavares and leveling him to the ice with his shoulder, but will not face any other repercussions from the NHL’s department of player safety.
Tavares said Monday he wasn’t worried about the lack of punishment, leaving it simply as, “the video speaks for itself.”
Head coach Doug Weight’s reaction was more pointed.
“Things are targeted, things happen spontaneously,” Weight said Monday. “But to me, the ones that are premeditated, it’s unfortunate when we only look at results. So if Johnny lies there and he is hurt, there’d probably be something done. I don’t know the logic in that.”
That wasn’t the only chippy play of the game. David Backes was later ejected in the third period for head-butting Andrew Ladd, but the department of player safety has not announced any fallout from that hit, either, as the Bruins appeared to get away relatively scot-free on both accounts.

Artificial heart maker Carmat has obtained approval from France's national drugs agency (ANSM) to resume a heart implant trial, sending the company's shares more than one fifth higher on Wednesday.
"Carmat has provided the elements allowing for the resumption of the trial, meeting satisfactory conditions of safety and risk control," ANSM said in a statement late on Tuesday.
ANSM had ordered Carmat to suspend further implants last December following the death of a patient in October.
The patient who died had the artificial heart implanted at the end of August last year and is the fifth patient to die with one fitted.
He was the first of 20 patients in a second so-called 'pivotal' phase of tests, which is a prerequisite to market the product in the European Union.
Carmat's products could represent a major medical breakthrough if proven reliable. They are designed for people with end-stage heart failure, a deadly condition where the heart is unable to pump blood adequately around the body.
In a statement, Carmat also said it continued to take steps to expand this trial into other countries, and was preparing to open a new production site to strengthen the industrial means necessary to carry out the study.
"The site should be operational by the end of the year and would also eventually enable the manufacturing requirements for the prosthesis' first commercial launch phases to be met," it said.
Carmat's shares, which fell to multi-year lows following the earlier halting of the heart implants tests, rose 21 percent to by 0720 GMT.
(Reporting by Wout Vergauwen and Pawel Lapinski. Editing by Jane Merriman)

The French National Agency for the Safety of Medicines and Health Products (ANSM) has granted authorization for Carmat to resume its clinical trial of an artificial heart implant. This decision, announced on Tuesday, precipitated a significant increase in the company's share price, which rose by more than one-fifth during trading on Wednesday. The ANSM stated that Carmat had submitted the requisite documentation to permit the trial's continuation, confirming that satisfactory conditions for safety and risk control had been established.

The trial had been suspended by the ANSM in December following the death of a patient in October. This patient, who had received the implant in late August, represented the fifth fatality among recipients and was the first participant in a second, pivotal phase of testing. This subsequent phase, involving a planned twenty patients, is a necessary prerequisite for securing regulatory approval to market the device within the European Union.

Carmat's artificial heart is intended for patients with end-stage heart failure, a condition characterized by the heart's inability to maintain adequate blood circulation. The device thus represents a potential major therapeutic advancement, contingent upon the demonstration of its long-term reliability. In a separate statement, Carmat indicated ongoing efforts to expand the trial into additional countries and disclosed preparations to operationalize a new production facility by year's end. This site is intended to bolster the industrial capacity required for the clinical study and to subsequently fulfill manufacturing needs for initial commercial distribution phases.

The resumption of testing follows a period of decline in Carmat's share value, which had reached multi-year lows after the initial suspension. Following the ANSM's announcement, shares recovered sharply, trading 21 percent higher by 0720 GMT.

SEVEN-TIMES champion Serena Williams moved up a gear at Wimbledon to beat Bulgarian qualifier Viktoriya Tomova 6-1 6-4 on Wednesday and reach the third round.
The 36-year-old American barely broke sweat in a one-sided first set but was tested by the world no. 135 in the second without ever looking troubled. While the Centre Court crowd clearly appreciated the sight of Williams in full flow they took a shine to the plucky Tomova who battled hard to make a match of it.
Camera Icon Serena Williams is gunning for her eighth Wimbledon title. Picture: AFP
Even ultimate warrior Williams, who was unable to defend her 2016 Wimbledon title last year because she was pregnant, applauded a couple of her opponent’s winners late in the second set before completing victory in 66 minutes. “It was better than my first round and I’m happy that I’m going in the right direction,” said 25th-seeded Williams.
Serena’s victory followed elder sister Venus’ hard-fought battle to see off Romania’s Alexandra Dulgheru 4-6 6-0 6-1.
Camera Icon The champ showed her displeasure after losing this point. Picture: AP
Five-time champion Venus, 38, turned up the heat after getting off to a rocky start and defeated her world No. 141 opponent in just under two hours, advancing to the third round for the 18th time in her career.
Elsewhere, Karolina Pliskova proved too strong for Victoria Azarenka in the battle of former world No. 1s, prevailing 6-3 6-3 in 72 minutes to enter the third round at Wimbledon for the first time in her career.
Camera Icon Bulgaria's Viktoriya Tomova was plucky but no match for Serena Williams. Picture: AP
The Czech world no. 8 had lost in the second round at the All England Club for five straight years since 2013.
She next plays in-form Romanian Mihaela Buzarnescu, who hardly broke sweat as she dismissed Briton Katie Swan 6-0 6-3 in one hour 14 minutes.

Her next opponent will be in-form Romanian Mihaela Buzarnescu, who advanced with a straightforward 6-0, 6-3 win over Britain’s Katie Swan in one hour and fourteen minutes.

Iranian President Hassan Rouhani blasted U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday, saying the American sanctions against Iran are a “crime and aggression”.
“Iran will survive this round of U.S. sanctions as it has survived before. This U.S. government will not stay in office forever ... But the history will judge other nations based on what they do today,” Rouhani said during a visit to Vienna, according to Reuters.
The Iranian President, who is visiting Europe in an attempt to save the 2015 nuclear deal after Trump pulled out of it in May, also warned his country could reduce its co-operation with the UN nuclear watchdog in the wake of the fresh U.S. sanctions against Iranian oil sales.
“Iran’s nuclear activities have always been for peaceful purposes, but it is Iran that would decide on its level of cooperation with the IAEA,” Iranian state news agency IRNA quoted Rouhani as saying after meeting Yukiya Amano, head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna.
“The responsibility for the change of Iran’s cooperation level with the IAEA falls on those who have created this new situation,” he added.
Trump pulled out of the deal under which sanctions on Iran were lifted in return for curbs to its nuclear program. Washington has since told countries they must stop buying Iranian oil from November 4 or face financial measures.
European signatories to the deal are trying to save the accord, which they see as crucial to forestalling an Iranian nuclear weapon.
Tehran has demanded that Europe come up with an economic package to offset the effects of the U.S. withdrawal but so far has found Europe’s proposals to be unsatisfactory.
On Tuesday, Rouhani visited Switzerland, where he said Iran will respect the nuclear deal with world powers as long as the country's interests are preserved.
"After the JCPOA [nuclear deal] we showed very clearly that whatever promise we make, we stand by," said the Iranian president.

But history will judge other nations based on what they do today." His comments were disseminated by the Reuters news agency.

He reiterated Iran’s adherence to its commitments, stating, "After the JCPOA we showed very clearly that whatever promise we make, we stand by."

When your alarm clock goes off and your eyes snap open, what’s the first thing on your mind? Do you calculate how long you can hit snooze? Are you already going over the day’s to-do list? Mindlessly checking your phone?
If any or all of these morning habits sound familiar, you’re definitely not alone. As a matter of fact, 60 percent of people check their phones immediately when they wake up, according to a 2015 survey. Not only should you stop using your smartphone in bed—seriously—but these mind-numbing routines are among what you’ll regret most in life. So why not take a different approach?
In a commencement speech at Stanford University in 2005, Steve Jobs advised his audience to start each morning with one specific sentence. Doing so, he said, will change the way we approach our day-to-day lives. Jobs got the idea after reading a quote about death when he was 17. From then on, he started each morning by looking in the mirror and asking, “If today were the last day of my life, would I want to do what I’m about to do today?”
Now, try it for yourself. Asking yourself this powerful question every day requires you to deeply consider what you do on a daily basis—and if you find fulfillment in it. It can also help you narrow down your tasks to the essential ones. Instead of wasting time with mindless activities like browsing the Internet, you’ll start filling your days with more satisfying things, such as spending time with family and friends. (By the way, these two ages will be the happiest years of your life.) Plus, you’ll stop worrying about what other people think of you; your energy and focus should be elsewhere, like improving yourself, reaching your goals, and making an impact on the world.
Now that you have made a habit of asking this one simple question every morning, congratulations! You’re one step closer finding the secret to living a fulfilling life.
Source: Inc.com

Consequently, adopting an alternative morning practice is advisable.

In his 2005 Stanford University commencement address, Steve Jobs proposed a specific morning ritual, asserting it could fundamentally alter one’s daily perspective. This recommendation originated from a quotation concerning mortality encountered during his adolescence. From the age of seventeen, Jobs initiated each day by confronting his reflection and posing the following inquiry: "If today were the last day of my life, would I want to do what I am about to do today?"

Implementing this daily practice necessitates profound introspection regarding one’s routine activities and their alignment with personal fulfillment. It functions as a filter, prioritizing essential tasks while diminishing time allocated to trivial or passive pursuits, such as aimless internet browsing. Instead, individuals may redirect efforts toward more substantively rewarding engagements, including nurturing familial and social relationships—periods which research suggests correlate strongly with life satisfaction. Furthermore, this reflective exercise can diminish preoccupation with external judgment, reorienting focus toward self-improvement, goal attainment, and contributing meaningfully to the broader community.

Cultivating the consistent practice of this morning interrogation represents a significant step toward structuring a more intentional and potentially fulfilling existence.

Jaguar has introduced a new app integration that allows some drivers to use their car’s touchscreen to pay for fuel.
The Shell app, described as a new cashless payment app, will work with several Jaguar Land Rover models. With it installed, you can drive up to any pump at a Shell service station in the UK, and instead of using a card at the pump, you'd use the vehicle’s touchscreen to select how much fuel you require and then pay via PayPal or Apple Pay.
Android Pay will be added in 2017. Also, Jaguar said its cars will eventually work with the Shell app at Shell stations around the globe. If you want to make sure you were charged the correct amount, an electronic receipt will be displayed on the touchscreen. A receipt will also be sent directly from the pump to the driver’s email address.
Jaguar stressed that expenses and tax returns will be made much simpler with this Shell integration, as there will be no receipts to lose since they're sent electronically. The Shell app with in-car cashless payments will be available to download in the UK from 15 February. You can expect it in other markets globally sometime this year.
The 2018 Jaguar F-PACE performance SUV, F-TYPE and XF and XE sports saloon model ranges, as well as the latest Land Rover models, will be the first cars to work with the Shell app.
Jaguar said this is the first in-car, fuel-payment system to be offered.
rewrite:
Jaguar Land Rover has launched an integrated application enabling drivers of select vehicles to conduct fuel transactions directly via the in-car touchscreen. This system, developed in partnership with Shell, functions as a cashless payment platform compatible with several Jaguar and Land Rover models. Upon downloading the Shell application, drivers at participating Shell service stations in the United Kingdom can initiate payment from the vehicle’s console. The interface allows the user to specify the desired fuel quantity and complete the transaction using linked digital wallets, currently supporting PayPal and Apple Pay, with Android Pay integration planned for 2017.

To ensure transactional accuracy, an electronic receipt is generated and displayed on the touchscreen immediately following purchase. A duplicate receipt is transmitted automatically from the fuel pump to the driver’s registered email address. Jaguar emphasizes that this digital process simplifies expense tracking and tax documentation by eliminating physical receipts. The company further notes that the service will subsequently expand to Shell stations worldwide.

The application will be available for download in the UK beginning 15 February, with a global rollout anticipated within the year. Initial vehicle compatibility includes the 2018 Jaguar F-PACE performance SUV, alongside the F-TYPE, XF, and XE sports saloon ranges, as well as the latest Land Rover models. According to Jaguar, this represents the automotive industry’s first fully integrated in-car system for fuel payment.

rewrite:
University of Oklahoma President David Boren has formally distanced the institution from remarks made by Board of Regents member and former Oklahoma City Mayor Kirk Humphreys, who drew widespread condemnation for comparing gay individuals to pedophiles. In a statement issued Monday, President Boren clarified that Humphreys was not representing the university’s position and emphasized that he does not share the regent’s views, reaffirming the university’s commitment to being a diverse and inclusive community.

The controversial comments were delivered during an appearance on KFOR-TV’s public affairs program over the weekend, during which Humphreys also drew a parallel between gay people and politicians who have recently resigned following allegations of sexual misconduct. In response, the LGBTQ advocacy organization Freedom Oklahoma has demanded Humphreys’ removal from the Board of Regents should he fail to issue an apology. Executive Director Troy Stevenson characterized the remarks as disheartening and dangerous, particularly for LGBTQ youth who already experience harassment and bullying. Stevenson further indicated that his organization plans to protest a real estate project in Oklahoma City owned by Humphreys’ family business absent an apology.

Additional criticism came from the president of the university’s LGBTQ Alumni Society, Joe Sangirardi, who on Monday called for Humphreys’ resignation. Sangirardi asserted that a regent’s role is to support students, not to attack them. Similarly, a spokesperson identified as Baker described the comments as “outright disrespectful, out of line, and ignorant.”

Humphreys has not publicly addressed the growing controversy. A staff member at his office indicated he was out of town and unavailable for comment on Monday, and he did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press. The situation remains unresolved as calls for accountability and an apology continue from university-affiliated groups and advocacy organizations.

Robbie Williams will be joining his former Take That band members for a one off special on the finale of Gary Barlow's Let It Shine.
Robbie Williams will once again take to the stage with Take That for the final of 'Let It Shine' next weekend.
The 'Candy' hitmaker has agreed to take to the stage with his former bandmates Mark Owen, Gary Barlow and Howard Donald on the popular BBC talent show on February 25 to give the nation a special performance of one of their biggest hits.
Picture | BBC
The 43-year-old singer will also take on the role of guest judge alongside Gary, Dannii Minogue and Martin Kemp as they decide, along with the public, which band will be crowned the winners of the series following weeks of performing on stage.
Robbie said: "I’m looking forward to being back with Gary, Mark and Howard on 'Let It Shine' and am excited to be a guest judge for the very special final."
Robbie's decision to rejoin his band, which he left in 2014, comes soon after Gary revealed that he would like the Could It Be Magic hitmakers to celebrate 25 years together in 2017.
And Robbie's return won't be permanent as he's got solo ventures to push through with including trying to crack America.
Picture | BBC
He said recently: "Nobody knows who I am. I can look at them and they can look at me. I get to stare at them and they get to stare at me, but they don't stare because they don't know who I am. I don't like this. I want this to change.
"Back in the 1990s when I went out there to promote my album I was not really dealing with fame very well at all - if I am honest I was not really dealing with much very well. It was when I realised that the more fame I got, the more insane I became. So I just stopped as I needed a place where I was not famous, because that would be the most sane thing to do. So I just lived over there and nobody knows me. Now I have changed my mind and I really regret it."
rewrite:
Robbie Williams is scheduled to reunite with his former Take That bandmates for a singular performance during the finale of the BBC talent programme *Let It Shine*, hosted by Gary Barlow. The event, set for February 25, will feature Williams alongside Gary Barlow, Mark Owen, and Howard Donald in a rendition of one of the group’s most notable songs. In addition to performing, the 43-year-old artist will serve as a guest judge on the panel, which includes Barlow, Dannii Minogue, and Martin Kemp. This panel, in conjunction with public voting, will determine the winning act of the competition series following several weeks of televised performances.

Williams commented on his participation, stating, “I’m looking forward to being back with Gary, Mark and Howard on *Let It Shine* and am excited to be a guest judge for the very special final.” This reappearance with the group, from which he formally departed in 2014, occurs shortly after Barlow expressed a desire for the band to commemorate their twenty-fifth anniversary this year. It is noted, however, that Williams’s involvement is not intended as a permanent return to Take That, as he remains focused on pursuing independent projects, including efforts to expand his commercial presence in the United States.

Regarding his American endeavours, Williams has recently reflected on his relative anonymity there, a situation he now views with regret. He observed, “Nobody knows who I am... I don’t like this. I want this to change.” He contextualised this by referencing his difficulties with fame during the 1990s, a period when he was promoting a solo album. Williams acknowledged that he managed fame poorly at the time, noting a correlation between increasing notoriety and personal turmoil. This led him to deliberately reside in a location where he was unrecognised, which he deemed “the most sane thing to do.” He has since reassessed this strategy, expressing a desire to alter his current profile in the American market.

A British diver said he swam for miles to safety after a shark stalked him when he lost sight of his boat off the coast of Australia on Friday.
John Craig, 34, told Australia’s ABC News on Sunday he was diving off Shark Bay in Western Australia when his boat encountered engine troubles and was swept away while he was underwater. He came up for air and the boat with his diving partner was nowhere to be seen.
“I had been splashing and screaming for some time and my heart rate was sky high,” Craig recalled to the news site. “After five minutes it was clear I was on my own.”
But Craig wasn’t the only one in the water. He soon spotted a tiger shark that was “within arm’s reach” away. Another sandbar shark was also circling behind him.
“It was easily the biggest tiger shark I’ve been in the water with and that’s saying something having worked as a dive instructor for over 10 years,” Craig said, describing it to be three times the size of him.
Craig added he was soon surrounded by the deadly animal that darted at him occasionally. In an attempt to save himself, he decided to swim to shore. The diver swam for four miles and eventually lost the tiger shark that was “following” him.
“I thought this was it, this is how I’m going to die,” Craig said.
An exhausted Craig made it to the shore three hours later and could “barely stand.” Meanwhile, search crews were out in the sea looking for the diver. He eventually caught the pilot’s attention in a plane.
Craig said the near-death experience has left him “eternally grateful.”
rewrite:
On Friday, a British diver reported swimming several miles to safety after being stalked by a shark following the disappearance of his boat off the Australian coast. In a Sunday interview with Australia’s ABC News, John Craig, 34, recounted that he had been diving in Shark Bay, Western Australia, when the vessel experienced engine failure and drifted away while he was submerged. Upon surfacing, he found no trace of the boat or his diving companion.

Craig described to the news outlet that he had been shouting and splashing for some time, resulting in an elevated heart rate. “After five minutes it was clear I was on my own,” he stated. However, he was not alone in the water. He soon observed a tiger shark in close proximity, “within arm’s reach,” with a sandbar shark also circling nearby.

Craig, who has worked as a dive instructor for over a decade, noted that the tiger shark was exceptionally large, estimating it to be triple his size. He explained that the animal soon surrounded him, making occasional darting movements. In response, Craig initiated a four-mile swim toward the shoreline, a decision he believed was necessary for self-preservation. During this arduous journey, he eventually eluded the pursuing shark.

Reflecting on the ordeal, Craig admitted, “I thought this was it, this is how I’m going to die.” After approximately three hours of exhaustive swimming, he reached the shore in a severely fatigued state, barely able to stand. Concurrently, search and rescue operations were underway. Craig ultimately attracted the attention of a pilot in an aircraft.

He expressed that the near-fatal incident has left him profoundly and “eternally grateful” for his survival.

input: The Congress veteran leader and also the spokesperson of the party Manish Tewari launched his latest book-Tidings of Troubled Times-in a highly politically charged event in which not only BJP’s Yashwant Sinha was present but also Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal of Aam Aadmi Party shared the dais.Hinting about the book Tewari, on Thursday, said that the book tells about the political developments in the last 12 months."Book is a statement on the politics in India and at the world level," Congress leader said.Tewari who was recently in news for aggressively criticising PM Narendra Modi informed that the book is available on Amazon, Flipkart and Palimpsest.Talking about his Congress party in the same event, Tewari acknowledged that Congress had some problems, but given another chance, it won’t be repeated.“There was a certain degree of arrogance, complacency in the UPA government. But one thing I can promise, given another chance, it won’t be repeated,” said the former minister Minister of Information and Broadcasting.Also, while responding to a question on dynasty politics in his party and the elevation of Rahul Gandhi, Tewari said, “There have been elections in the party and there is a process at play which will soon culminate.”Tewari also said that opposition parties have not collapsed in the country in the fight against the presently ruling BJP.

Congress veteran and party spokesperson Manish Tewari launched his latest book, *Tidings of Troubled Times*, at a politically significant event. MERRIAM, Kan. -- It was a New Year's Eve celebration like never before for this family.
Breanna Borlase and husband Matthew welcomed two baby boys into the world early Sunday morning.
New Year's Eve babies Colton and Corbin have five siblings waiting at home.
"He said that we should have New Year's babies and I told him that you can't really plan things like that.
But they can be a surprise.
The identical twin boys arrived just after 1:20 a.m. Sunday morning at Shawnee-Mission Medical Center.
Corbin was born at five pounds, three ounces, and Colton -- born just a minute later -- was 4 pounds, 10 ounces.
Mom says they rang in the new year.
"Everybody had said 'oh, don't expect crying. They will be real quiet,' and that was not the case with them. They were very vocal."
Hospital staff even had to switch up the New Year's Eve baby gift basket because it only had enough goodies for one baby.

Breanna and Matthew Borlase welcomed identical twins, Corbin and Colton, shortly after 1:20 a.m. at Shawnee Mission Medical Center. Corbin, born first, weighed five pounds and three ounces, while Colton, delivered one minute later, weighed four pounds and ten ounces. The infants join five older siblings awaiting their arrival at home.

BERLIN (AP) — About 150 skiers who were stuck on a broken chairlift in central Austria for several hours were rescued safely Monday, by helicopters and mountain rescue teams, Austrian police said Monday.
Styria provincial police said on Twitter that all the skiers taken off the Rosenkranz chairlift at Kreischberg mountain north of Klagenfurt were uninjured.
The lift stopped working early in the afternoon working because of technical problems. Three helicopters and several mountain aid groups were involved in the operation, the Austrian news agency APA reported.
Local media reported that it would have taken too long to repair the broken chair lift, so authorities decided to start evacuating the skiers.
Authorities informed the stuck riders with loud speakers in several languages that they would rescue them. Members of rescue team then climbed up to the chairs from below and brought some of the people down with ropes. Others were lifted up onto helicopters.
The stopped chairs were 7-10 meters (23-33 feet) above the ground. The weather was comparatively mild, so no one suffered any ill-effects from cold.
rewrite: On Monday, Austrian authorities successfully conducted a rescue operation for approximately 150 skiers stranded on a malfunctioning chairlift in central Austria. According to Styria provincial police, the incident occurred on the Rosenkranz chairlift at Kreischberg mountain, north of Klagenfurt. The lift ceased operation in the early afternoon due to technical issues. Given that repairs were estimated to require excessive time, authorities initiated an evacuation. The operation, involving three helicopters and multiple mountain rescue teams, was coordinated by Austrian police and reported by the APA news agency. Rescuers communicated with passengers via multilingual loudspeakers before ascending to the chairs, which were suspended seven to ten meters above ground. Some individuals were lowered using ropes, while others were airlifted by helicopter. All skiers were extracted without injury, a outcome facilitated by comparatively mild weather conditions that prevented cold-related distress.

Tommy Taurima is widely known as one of the last composers of the golden era in Māoridom to come from the Hawkes Bay region. He’s known for his famous tunes Kotiro Māori, Te Rina and many others.
His contribution to Māori music and songwriting spans over six decades. He was only 18 years old when he wrote his first waiata for his local Mormon-choir group and kapa haka, during his time in Hamilton, Waikato.
Now at 80 years old, he continues to write music for many different occasions such as Te Matatini. His niece Te Rina Pomare says, “I only know 40 of his waiata that he’s composed.”
“He also composed a song to celebrate Te Matatini and to also acknowledge the late Tama Huata, the former chairman of Te Matatini. He completed that piece of music last year in August.”
Mr Taurima was also part of a cultural movement in Hawai’i and assisted in building the Polynesian Cultural Centre’s profile.
rewrite:
Tommy Taurima is recognized as one of the final composers from the Hawke’s Bay region to emerge during the golden era of Māori music. He is renowned for his celebrated waiata, including Kotiro Māori and Te Rina. His contributions to Māori music and composition extend across more than six decades. At the age of eighteen, while residing in Hamilton, Waikato, he composed his first waiata for his local Mormon choir and kapa haka group.

Now eighty years old, he continues to produce music for various events, such as Te Matatini. His niece, Te Rina Pomare, notes, “I am familiar with only forty of his composed waiata.” Among these works is a piece composed last August to commemorate Te Matatini and honor the late Tama Huata, its former chairman. Additionally, Mr. Taurima participated in a cultural movement in Hawai’i and contributed to enhancing the profile of the Polynesian Cultural Centre.

A San Lucas man accused of firing shots at a San Miguel home was transported to San Luis Obispo County Jail Monday to face charges of attempted murder and assault.
Members of the Sheriff’s Gang Task Force transported David-Zosimo Pacheco Carrasco, 24, from Monterey County Jail, where he had been in custody on suspicion of a parole violation, according to a press release from the Sheriff’s Office.
Carrasco was identified as the suspected gunman in the shooting of a house in the 1700 block of Mission Street on the night of June 5. No one was hurt, but two adults and three children were inside the home at the time, the Sheriff’s Office said.
The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office identified Carrasco as a potential suspect in June and arrested him on June 14 with the help of other local and state agencies on a warrant for an alleged parole violation.
Charges include attempted murder, assault with a firearm and shooting at an inhabited dwelling, with felony enhancements because the attempted murder was committed with a firearm and Carrasco has prior felony convictions. Both priors listed, which occurred in Monterey County in 2008 and 2013, were gang-related, according to the criminal complaint.

Ave Maria Meditations
Being in this joyous Easter season and as we approach the Centennial of Our Lady’s apparitions at Fatima, this is a beautiful and timely prayer of consecration!
Act of Consecration to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and Immaculate Heart of Mary
Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and Immaculate Heart of Mary, I consecrate myself and my whole family to You. I consecrate to You: my very being and my whole life…All that I am…All that I have…and all that I love. To You I give my body, my heart, and my soul. To You I dedicate my home and my country.
Mindful of this consecration, I now promise You to live a Christian way of life by the practice of virtues.
O Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and Immaculate Heart of Mary, accept this act of consecration, which I make out of pure love for You.
Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy on me! Immaculate Heart of Mary, be my salvation! Jesus, meek and humble of heart, make my heart like unto Your merciful heart! Amen.
rewrite:
Amidst the joyous observance of the Easter season and in anticipation of the centennial commemoration of the Marian apparitions at Fátima, the following prayer of consecration is presented as a particularly fitting devotion.

Act of Consecration to the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary

O Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and Immaculate Heart of Mary, to You I consecrate myself and my entire family. I consecrate to You my entire being and life, all that I am, all that I possess, and all whom I love. I surrender my body, heart, and soul. I dedicate my home and my nation.

Conscious of this dedication, I pledge to strive for a Christian manner of living through the cultivation of virtue.

O Most Sacred Heart of Jesus and Immaculate Heart of Mary, deign to accept this act of consecration, offered from sincere devotion.

Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, have mercy upon me. Immaculate Heart of Mary, be the cause of my salvation. Jesus, meek and humble of heart, form my heart to be like Your own merciful heart. Amen.

Xabi Alonso's decision to leave Real Madrid for Bayern Munich in 2014 was not an escape and was purely down to his desire to test himself in another country again.
After joining from Liverpool five years prior, Alonso somewhat surprisingly opted to leave the Santiago Bernabeu after winning the Champions League, prompting speculation he was pushed out.
But the experienced midfielder has nothing but fond memories of his time in the Spanish capital as he prepares to return to his former hunting ground on Tuesday, when Bayern will look to overturn a 2-1 defeat from the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final tie.
"It was not an escape. I did not flee from anything," Alonso, who will retire at the end of the season, told El Pais.
"It was not like I was uncomfortable at Madrid. I had been at the club for five years, won the Champions League and had to make a decision whether I wanted to try another country or retire at Madrid, where I was very happy.
"The final decision went very quick. Pep [Guardiola] really wanted me at Bayern and I took a very difficult decision by leaving Madrid on a voluntary basis.
"A lot has been said and written about my departure, but the truth is quite simple. I wanted to test myself in another country before retiring.
"You have to know when to say goodbye. I always try to leave at the right time."
rewrite:
Xabi Alonso's 2014 departure from Real Madrid to Bayern Munich was not an act of avoidance but rather a deliberate choice motivated by his aspiration to experience a new competitive environment prior to retirement. Having joined Madrid from Liverpool five years earlier, Alonso's decision to leave the Santiago Bernabéu following a Champions League victory was met with speculation regarding a potential forced exit. However, the midfielder refutes this characterization and retains positive reflections on his tenure in Spain as he prepares for a return with Bayern Munich in a crucial Champions League quarter-final second leg.

Alonso, who will conclude his playing career at season's end, explicitly stated, "It was not an escape. I did not flee from anything." He elaborated, "I was not uncomfortable at Madrid. After five years, having won the Champions League, I faced a decision: either remain at a club where I was very content or seek a new challenge in another nation. The process was swift; Pep Guardiola's strong interest in bringing me to Bayern was a significant factor. My departure was entirely voluntary, though the choice was profoundly difficult."

He further clarified the simplicity of his rationale amidst considerable external conjecture: "The fundamental truth is that I wished to test myself in another country before retiring. Understanding the appropriate moment for departure is essential; I consistently aim to leave at the correct time."

Welsh Conservatives have pledged to give free bus travel to all 16-24 year olds in Wales, and have urged Labour ministers to do the same.
The Green Card - which the Tories said could cost up to £25m a year - would also give a third off rail tickets.
Education spokesman Darren Millar said young people suffered high car insurance and the lowest wages.
The Welsh Government dismissed the plan as "fantasy economics", saying it would consult on a new discount travel pass.
The current MyTravelPass scheme gives 16-18 year olds a third off bus fares.
Mr Millar said the Welsh Conservatives' "exciting offer for young people" would also protect the environment and help save local bus routes from the axe.
His colleague Russell George, the Tories' economy spokesman, added that travel costs could be a "huge barrier" to education, training and job opportunities.
'Fag packet' economics
"We are committed to building a stronger economy and a fairer society, and we believe that young people should benefit from the same travel concessions offered to Wales' over-60s," he said.
The Conservatives said the scheme would be funded by scrapping the education maintenance allowance (EMA), which they have previously proposed.
A Welsh Government spokesman said: "These Tory proposals have been made up on the back of a fag packet.
"To think you can provide 350,000 people with free bus travel and a third off rail fares for £25m is fantasy economics."
The spokesman added that the Welsh Government would be launching a consultation next week on plans to launch a replacement for MyTravelPass in April.
"It will be a discounted travel scheme grounded in reality, that can encourage more young people onto Welsh buses," he said.

Darren Millar, the party’s education spokesperson, justified the proposal by citing the financial pressures faced by younger demographics, including elevated car insurance premiums and relatively low wage levels. He further contended that the policy would yield environmental benefits and aid in preserving vulnerable local bus services. Russell George, the Conservative economy spokesperson, emphasised that travel expenses can constitute a significant impediment to accessing education, training, and employment opportunities, stating the party’s belief that younger people should receive travel concessions comparable to those available to residents over sixty.

The Welsh Government, however, has dismissed the proposal as "fantasy economics." A government spokesman characterised the Conservative costings as speculative, akin to being "made up on the back of a fag packet," and questioned the financial viability of providing free bus travel and discounted rail fares to an estimated 350,000 individuals for the stated sum. The Conservatives indicated the scheme would be financed by terminating the Education Maintenance Allowance (EMA), a measure they have advocated previously. In contrast, the Welsh Government confirmed it will commence a public consultation regarding a successor to the existing MyTravelPass programme, which currently offers a one-third discount on bus fares to 16–18-year-olds. FG’s savings bond allotment drops to N607.3m in June
The Federal Government allotted N607.3 million in its June 2019 and 2020 savings bond sales, a figure that is lower than the N790.85 million it allotted in May, the Debt Management Office (DMO) said.
The allotment results were obtained from its website on Wednesday in Abuja. It said that N271.56 million was allotted at 13.18 per cent with 425 successful subscriptions to mature in June 2019.
DMO also said that N335.7 million was allotted at 14.18 per cent with 496 successful subscriptions maturing in June 2020. This figure indicates a drop in allotments and subscriptions over the past months.
The savings bond introduced in March is targeted at the lower income earners to encourage savings and also earn more income (interest) compared to their savings accounts with banks.
In its maiden sale conducted in March, the Federal Government allotted N2.1 billion to 2,575 subscribers while it allotted N1.2 billion to 1,798 subscribers in April. In May, the subscription dropped to N790.85 million for 1,233 subscribers.
The savings bond designed to help finance the nation’s budget deficit is also backed by its ‘full faith and credit’.
Interests are to be paid at regular periods with principal repaid at maturity. They have a tenure of between two and three years and a minimum size of investment of N5,000 and maximum of N50 million. It is aimed at deepening national savings culture, diversifying funding sources for the government and providing opportunity to all citizens, irrespective of income level to contribute to national development.
It will also enable all citizens to participate in and benefit from the favourable returns available in the capital market.
The next offer will open on July 3 and close on July 7, the DMO said.

In June, the Federal Government of Nigeria allotted a total of N607.3 million through its savings bond program, a decrease from the N790.85 million allotted in the preceding month of May. This information was disclosed by the Debt Management Office (DMO), with the detailed results published on its official website on a Wednesday in Abuja. The June allotment was divided across two bond series. For the bond maturing in June 2019, N271.56 million was allotted at an interest rate of 13.18 percent, resulting from 425 successful subscriptions. For the bond maturing in June 2020, N335.7 million was allotted at 14.18 percent, with 496 successful subscriptions. These figures signify a continuing decline in both the total value of allotments and the number of subscriptions over recent months.

The Federal Government Savings Bond, inaugurated in March of this year, is principally aimed at lower-income earners. Its objectives are to encourage a savings culture, provide a source of investment income yielding higher returns than standard bank savings accounts, and democratize access to government securities. The bond is also a instrument for budget deficit financing, carrying the full faith and credit guarantee of the Federal Government. The instrument features a tenure of two to three years, with periodic interest payments and principal repayment upon maturity. The minimum investment is set at N5,000, while the maximum is N50 million.

Historical data illustrates a downward trend in subscription volumes. The inaugural sale in March saw an allotment of N2.1 billion to 2,575 subscribers. This declined to N1.2 billion for 1,798 subscribers in April, and further to N790.85 million for 1,233 subscribers in May, prior to the June allotment of N607.3 million. Beyond deficit financing, the bond program is designed to deepen the national savings culture, diversify government funding sources, and offer all citizens, regardless of income level, an opportunity to contribute to national development while participating in the capital market.

The DMO has announced that the subsequent offer cycle will commence on July 3 and conclude on July 7.
