SEATTLE (AP) — The Latest on courts blocking the president's efforts to keep transgender people from enlisting in the military (all times local):
5:20 p.m.
A third federal judge has blocked President Donald Trump's ban on transgender people joining the military.
U.S. District Judge Marsha Pechman issued her ruling Monday in a case brought by several plaintiffs, including a soldier based in Washington state and two young men who hope to enlist.
Washington Attorney General Bob Ferguson also intervened in the case to challenge Trump's policy.
Pechman found that the ban likely violates the plaintiffs' rights to due process and to equal protection under the law without advancing any government interest. She also said it would harm the state's efforts to protect its residents from discrimination.
Pechman blocked the government from imposing the ban pending further proceedings.
Judges in Maryland and Washington, D.C., also have ruled against the ban. It had been due to take effect Jan. 1.
___
8:10 a.m.
The Pentagon official tells The Associated Press that transgender people can enlist in the military beginning Jan. 1, despite President Donald Trump's opposition.
The new policy reflects growing legal pressure on the issue and the difficult hurdles the federal government would have to cross to enforce Trump's demand to ban transgender individuals from the military. Two federal courts already have ruled against the ban.
Potential transgender recruits will have to overcome a lengthy and strict set of physical, medical and mental conditions that make it possible, though difficult, for them to join the armed services.
Maj. David Eastburn says the enlistment of transgender recruits will start Jan. 1 and go on amid the legal battles. The Department of Defense also is studying the issue.
rewrite:
On Monday, United States District Judge Marsha Pechman issued a preliminary injunction against the enforcement of a presidential directive barring transgender individuals from military service. The ruling, delivered in the Western District of Washington, represents the third such federal judicial order blocking the policy. The litigation was initiated by several plaintiffs, including an active-duty service member stationed in Washington state and two aspiring enlistees, and was joined by Washington State Attorney General Bob Ferguson. In her opinion, Judge Pechman determined the ban likely constitutes a violation of the plaintiffs' Fifth Amendment rights to equal protection and substantive due process, while failing to serve a compelling or legitimate governmental interest. The court further noted the policy would impede state efforts to combat discrimination against its residents. Consequently, the injunction prohibits implementation of the ban pending further judicial proceedings. Earlier rulings from federal courts in Maryland and the District of Columbia had similarly enjoined the policy, which was originally scheduled to take effect on January 1.

Concurrently, a Pentagon official confirmed to The Associated Press that the military will begin accepting transgender recruits on January 1, notwithstanding presidential opposition. This decision reflects the mounting legal challenges to the ban and the significant procedural obstacles the administration would face in enforcing it. Prospective transgender recruits must, however, satisfy the same stringent medical, physical, and mental health standards applicable to all applicants, a process acknowledged to be rigorous. Pentagon spokesperson Major David Eastburn stated that enlistment will proceed as planned on the first of the year, even as related litigation continues. The Department of Defense has also indicated an ongoing internal review of the matter.

New photos emerged Saturday of a new prototype of Iran’s stealth fighter jet, previous models of which were mocked by aviation experts who predicted it “would never fly.”
The updated version of Qahar F-313 stealth fighter jet was unveiled during an exhibition for Iranian President Hassan Rouhani, The Aviationist editor David Cenciotti reported. The exhibition showcased the achievements made by Defense Minister Brig. Gen. Hossein Dehghan within the last two years.
The prototype had the same shape as its 2013 predecessor but featured multiple changes, including a bigger cockpit, non-plexiglass canopy, dual exhaust nozzles, dorsal antenna and FLIR (Forward Looking Infra-Red) turret installed to the nose of the fighter jet.
The F-313 was first unveiled in February 2013, though it was criticized for being too small. The cockpit couldn’t accommodate a “normal-sized” pilot and the wings weren’t big enough to get it up in the air, according to The Aviationist.
The original version also had a slew of technical errors. The engine was not properly built, putting the back of the aircraft at risk of melting from heat. The craft’s air intakes seemed too small, the blog said.
Ahmad Vahidi, Iran’s defense minister at the time, said Iranian aerospace experts designed the jet to fly at a low altitude, carry weapons and land on short runways, according to DailyMail.com.
Iranian news site Khouz News did publish photos of F-313 appearing to fly over mountains in 2013, but was accused of photoshopping the image, DailyMail.com reported.
It’s still unclear if the new prototype would be able to fly. The jet conducted taxi tests on Saturday during the exhibition.
Recent statements released said that the F-313 fighter jet will be “a light close air support aircraft,” The Aviationist reported.
rewrite:
On Saturday, new imagery surfaced depicting an updated prototype of Iran’s Qaher F-313 stealth fighter, a design whose earlier iterations were dismissed by aviation analysts as unlikely ever to achieve flight. The revised model was presented during an exhibition for President Hassan Rouhani highlighting accomplishments under Defense Minister Brigadier General Hossein Dehghan over the preceding two years, as documented by The Aviationist editor David Cenciotti.

While retaining the general configuration of the 2013 variant, the prototype exhibits several modifications. These include an enlarged cockpit, a canopy constructed from materials other than plexiglass, dual exhaust nozzles, a dorsal antenna, and a Forward Looking Infra-Red (FLIR) turret mounted on the aircraft's nose. The original F-313, unveiled in February 2013, faced significant technical criticism. Analysts noted its diminutive scale, contending the cockpit was insufficient for a pilot of standard stature and the wingspan inadequate for generating necessary lift. Further critiques identified design flaws such as an improperly configured engine, posing a risk of aft-section heat damage, and undersized air intakes.

Former Defense Minister Ahmad Vahidi previously asserted that domestic aerospace engineers designed the jet for low-altitude flight, weapon carriage, and operation from short runways. Although Iranian media circulated photographs in 2013 purportedly showing the aircraft in flight, these were subsequently alleged to be digitally altered. The operational capability of the new prototype remains undetermined; it performed taxi tests during the exhibition. Recent reports indicate the aircraft is intended to function as a light close air support platform, though its developmental status and aerodynamic viability continue to be subjects of international skepticism.

ISTANBUL, April 30 The head of an Iranian satellite television network channel who last year was sentenced in absentia to six years in prison by a Tehran court was shot dead in Istanbul together with a business partner, Turkey's Dogan news agency said on Sunday.
GEM TV founder Saeed Karimian and another Iranian were driving in Istanbul's Maslak neighbourhood after 8 p.m. (1700 GMT) on Saturday when their car was stopped by a jeep and shots were fired, Dogan said.
Karimian was found dead by emergency services arriving at the scene, Dogan said. His associate was taken to hospital but could not be revived.
It was not clear if there were multiple shooters. The jeep was later found abandoned and burned. Istanbul police declined to comment on the shooting when contacted by Reuters.
Dogan quoted the mayor of Istanbul's Sariyer district as saying initial police findings suggested the shooting may have prompted by a financial disagreement involving Karimian.
GEM TV is known for entertainment satellite channels that dub foreign films and Western television programmes into Farsi for Iranians. It also produces movies and TV series.
But in Iran, where the government tries to instil Islamic values by strictly regulating popular culture, the satellite broadcaster's programming has angered authorities, who view it as part of a cultural "soft war" waged by the West.
Last year a Revolutionary Court in Tehran tried Karimian in absentia and sentenced him to six years in jail on charges of "acting against national security" and "propaganda against the state". (Reporting by Ece Toksabay; Additional reporting by Bozorgmehr Sharafedin; Writing by David Dolan; Editing by Ros Russell)

The incident occurred in Istanbul’s Maslak district after 8 p.m. local time on Saturday, when the vehicle transporting the two individuals was intercepted by a jeep, after which assailants opened fire. Emergency services pronounced Karimian deceased at the scene, while his associate was transported to a hospital but succumbed to injuries. The perpetrators' vehicle was later discovered abandoned and burned. Istanbul police have declined to provide commentary on the ongoing investigation when contacted by Reuters. GEM TV operates entertainment channels that broadcast foreign films and Western television programs dubbed into Farsi, in addition to producing original cinematic and serial content. Within Iran, where state authorities enforce strict regulations on popular culture to promote Islamic values, the network’s programming has been a source of official condemnation. Iranian officials characterize such broadcasts as instruments of a Western-led cultural "soft war" aimed at undermining national values. The judicial proceedings against Karimian last year reflect the Iranian government’s broader efforts to criminalize media activities perceived as oppositional to its ideological and security frameworks.

Saints have beaten several other interested clubs to sign exciting back rower James Bentley from Bradford Bulls on a three-year deal.
Dubbed the best player in the Championship “by an absolute mile” by former Saints’ star Leon Pryce, 19-year-old Bentley made his debut for the Bulls against Oldham last season.
He’s gone on to score 15 tries in 23 appearances and has been one of the Bulls’ standout performers.
“James is a quality young player and we are pleased to bring him to the club,” said Saints’ head coach Justin Holbrook.
“He’s powerful, strong and is consistent in his performances week in week out.
“He knows he has a lot of improvement in him, too, and he’s looking forward to developing in our system.”
Bentley played for Oulton Raiders before progressing through Bradford Bulls’ Academy ranks.
He said: “I can’t wait to get over there and get started. It was a big decision to leave, an emotional one as well but I am looking forward to be playing at the top level. It is a decision I’ve made to further my career.
“I’m expecting the step up to be hard, it’s going to be a lot faster and a lot tougher but I am looking forward to and going head first into the challenge.
“I can’t wait to get over there; some of the players that they have like Ben Barba and Jon Wilkin, are just great players. I can learn from them and become a better player.
“I’m committed to the Bulls for the rest of the season I want to finish with my time here on a high.”

He is powerful, strong, and demonstrates consistent performance on a weekly basis. The decision to depart was significant and emotional, but it was made to advance my career at the highest level. I anticipate the transition will be challenging, involving a faster and more demanding standard of play, yet I look forward to embracing this challenge fully.”

He further noted: “I am keen to join a squad containing players of the calibre of Ben Barba and Jon Wilkin, from whom I can learn to improve my own game.” Bentley affirmed his commitment to the Bulls for the remainder of the current season, expressing a desire to conclude his tenure with the club successfully.

BEIJING, April 28 A court in China on Friday jailed a former chairman of Baoshan Iron and Steel, who went on to become vice mayor of Shanghai, to 17 years for bribery and graft, a state broadcaster reported.
President Xi Jinping has waged war on graft for more than four years, vowing that all corrupt officials, from powerful "tigers" to lowly "flies", will be weeded out, and warning that a failure to do so could threaten the ruling Communist Party.
Ai Baojun had used his positions to amass more than 40 million yuan ($5.8 million) in assets from 2000 to 2014, a court in the southern city of Zhangzhou ruled, according to China Central Television (CCTV)
Ai is the most senior official from China's financial hub to be sentenced in the corruption campaign. He could not be reached for comment.
The court also ruled that 5.8 million yuan of Ai's personal assets be confiscated and returned to Baosteel and to Shanghai city, CCTV said.
Ai was given a lenient sentence due to actively providing details of his crimes, which he accepted and apologised for, the court said, adding that many of the bribes were accepted by relatives without his knowledge.
China's top anti-graft watchdog stripped Ai of his party and state positions in January 2016 after an investigation found him guilty of breaking party discipline rules, as well as the crimes he was sentenced for.
According to his official biography, Ai ran Shanghai-based Baoshan Iron and Steel from 1998 to 2007 before taking up a Shanghai vice mayor post until 2013.
He then became head administrator for Shanghai's free-trade zone, the first such zone on the Chinese mainland.
Dai Haibo, a deputy secretary of the Shanghai government and former deputy head of the free trade zone, was stripped of his post in May 2015, following an investigation by the anti-corruption watchdog.
Cui Jian, vice president of the Baosteel Group, the parent of Baoshan Iron and Steel, was placed under investigation in March 2015 on suspicion of "serious disciplinary violations," a euphemism for graft.
Baoshan Iron and Steel declined to comment. (Reporting by Christian Shepherd; Editing by Robert Birsel)
rewrite:
On April 28, a Chinese judicial body sentenced a former chairman of Baoshan Iron and Steel, who subsequently served as a vice mayor of Shanghai, to seventeen years’ imprisonment on charges of bribery and corruption, as reported by state media. This sentencing occurs within the context of a sustained anti-corruption initiative, ongoing for over four years, which has been characterized by national leadership as a critical campaign targeting malfeasance at all levels of authority. The initiative emphasizes the systemic risk that corruption poses to governance.

The court in Zhangzhou adjudicated that the defendant, Ai Baojun, illicitly accumulated assets exceeding 40 million yuan (approximately 5.8 million USD) between 2000 and 2014 by exploiting his official positions. The court further ordered the confiscation of 5.8 million yuan from his personal assets for restitution to Baosteel and the Shanghai municipal government. In its ruling, the court noted mitigating circumstances, citing Ai’s active cooperation in disclosing the details of his offenses, his admission of guilt, and his expression of remorse. It was also noted that a portion of the bribes were accepted by relatives without his direct knowledge.

Ai Baojun represents the most senior official from China’s primary financial center to receive a sentence under the ongoing anti-corruption drive. Prior to his sentencing, the national disciplinary inspection authority had expelled him from his political and governmental roles in January 2016 following an investigation that confirmed violations of party discipline alongside the criminal acts.

Ai’s professional trajectory included leadership of Baoshan Iron and Steel from 1998 to 2007, followed by service as a vice mayor of Shanghai until 2013. He subsequently assumed the role of chief administrator for Shanghai’s pilot free-trade zone. This case is situated within a broader pattern of disciplinary actions within Shanghai’s political and corporate spheres. For instance, Dai Haibo, a former deputy secretary of the Shanghai municipal government and former deputy head of the free-trade zone, was removed from his post in May 2015 following a disciplinary investigation. Similarly, in March 2015, Cui Jian, a vice president of Baosteel Group, was placed under investigation for alleged serious disciplinary violations, a term often denoting corruption-related offenses. The involved corporate entity, Baoshan Iron and Steel, has declined to provide commentary on the judicial proceedings.

TULSA, Okla. (AP) - A Tulsa police sergeant will be the face of a new cable TV show aimed at looking at law enforcement work from officers' perspective.
A&E says Sgt. Sean Larkin is host of "PD Cam." The 30-minute show will offer unfiltered video from police body-worn, dashboard and helicopter cameras.
Larkin has worked for Tulsa police more than 20 years and says law enforcement has gotten negative media coverage in recent years. He says the show will help police work become more transparent.
"PD Cam" debuts July 19.
Tulsa Police Chief Chuck Jordan in 2017 canceled his department's contract with another A&E show. Critics say the real-time "Live PD" shows incidents of racial profiling and caters to viewers' worst fears and biases. Jordan said it made his city look bad.

Larkin, a twenty-year veteran, contends that recent media portrayals of policing have been predominantly negative and believes the series will foster greater transparency. The program is scheduled to premiere on July 19. This initiative follows Police Chief Chuck Jordan’s 2017 termination of the department’s involvement with A&E’s "Live PD," a program criticized for allegedly displaying racial profiling and exploiting public anxieties. Jordan concluded that the earlier show depicted the city unfavorably.

Coffee lovers, we have some bad news: No two cups of Joe are completely the same. And while you’re out here spending big bucks on your daily morning brew—it’s just one of the problems all coffee lovers understand—don’t you want to maximize its rise-and-shine powers?
Thankfully, HuffPost, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, and EnergyFiend.com teamed up to give us the scoop on just how much bang we’re getting for our buck at our favorite coffee chains. As it turns out, the milligrams of caffeine per ounce of coffee vary from chain to chain. You can view the complete round-up here.
McDonald’s coffee might be a cheap on-the-go beverage, but odds are, its caffeination powers won’t last long; one cup only contains nine milligrams of caffeine. On the other hand, Dunkin’ Donuts and Peet’s Brewed Coffees fall in the middle of the spectrum, with 12.7 and 16.7 mg of caffeine respectively. Starbucks packs a punch at 20.6 mg of caffeine, so if you need a serious wake-up call, it might be worth it to splurge on that $5 beverage. (On another note, you’ll never believe what Starbucks was almost called.)
But to get really hyped up, go for a coffee from Deathwish. This self-proclaimed brewer of the world’s strongest coffee is no lie; just one cup contains a whopping 54.2 mg per ounce of caffeine. But don’t worry, the website assures us, one cup won’t actually kill you. In fact, it turns out that you can drink way more coffee than originally thought—and actually live longer, too.
rewrite:
A notable challenge for coffee consumers is the significant variability in caffeine content across different commercial preparations, despite often substantial personal expenditure on daily consumption. To optimize the stimulatory effects of coffee, it.e is therefore pertinent to consider the specific caffeine concentrations offered by major vendors. Data compiled from sources including HuffPost, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, and EnergyFiend.com reveal considerable disparities in milligrams of caffeine per fluid ounce among popular chains.

For instance, McDonald's coffee, while economical, provides a relatively low concentration of approximately nine milligrams per ounce. Mid-range offerings include Dunkin’ Donuts and Peet’s Brewed Coffee, with 12.7 and 16.7 milligrams per ounce, respectively. Starbucks espresso beverages deliver a higher concentration of 20.6 milligrams per ounce, representing a potent option for those seeking a pronounced stimulatory effect. The most extreme caffeine concentration is found in Deathwish Coffee, which markets itself as the world's strongest brew, containing 54.2 milligrams per ounce. The company asserts this level is safe for consumption. This aligns with broader epidemiological research suggesting moderate to high coffee intake is not associated with increased mortality and may correlate with greater longevity. Consequently, informed selection based on caffeine content can allow consumers to better align their purchases with desired physiological outcomes.

It's a service that eliminates ads from videos, lets you grant free monthly subscriptions to support streamers, and now includes several free games each month.
Even if you'll never use the streaming service, all Amazon Prime subscribers should snag the free Twitch Prime subscription and download these free PC games from the Twitch desktop app; they're yours to keep forever. And if you do love and use Twitch, then Prime and its myriad goodies is just the cherry on top.
The selection will change monthly, so we'll keep this space updated as new games arrive. For July, Twitch is giving away a staggering 21 free games in honour of Amazon's upcoming Prime Day, with new titles rolling out daily 'til then. But some are only available for a couple days or maybe a week, so be sure to mind the dates listed below.

He said: "I did see that there was quite a bit of backlash for the song. I respect people shedding light and standing up for the LGBT community - that's a great thing.

The 'Say You Won't Let Go' hitmaker has admitted he doesn't "feel the urge" to explore relationships with his own sex, but insists he can "appreciate a handsome man".
He added to The Sun's bizarre column: "What percentage do I have to be to appreciate a good-looking man? I definitely think a lot of guys are handsome. I don't feel the urge to act upon it but I can appreciate a handsome man for sure."

Recently, Charli XCX leapt to the singer's defence, insisting the song was written using a "valid" experience Rita had had with a female.
She said: "I know from when Rita invited me to be a part of the song, this song was about a specific experience that she had with a woman.

BARCELONA, April 30 Rafael Nadal won a record-extending 10th Barcelona Open title on Sunday by thrashing Dominic Thiem of Austria 6-4 6-1, collecting his second claycourt title in a row.
Nadal, who won the Monte Carlo Masters for a 10th time last week, romped to the title without dropping a set on the newly renamed Rafa Nadal court at the Real Tennis Club in Barcelona, and needed just 90 minutes to finish off Thiem.
Thiem had beaten the 14-times Grand Slam champion on clay in the Argentina Open last year and earned a place in the final by beating world number one Andy Murray for the first time in his career on Saturday, but he proved no match for Nadal.
The Mallorcan took a while to impose himself on Thiem on an overcast day in Barcelona with the cold weather slowing down the court.
Thiem earned the first breakpoint of the match but Nadal recovered and eventually took the first set by breaking his opponent in the 10th game.
There was no let-up in the second set from Nadal, who broke the 23-year-old Austrian twice in a row before serving for the championship. (Editing by Clare Fallon)

On Sunday, April 30th, in Barcelona, Rafael Nadal secured a historic tenth Barcelona Open championship, defeating Austria’s Dominic Thiem in straight sets, 6-4, 6-1. This victory marks his second consecutive title on clay, following his record tenth Monte Carlo Masters triumph the previous week. Competing on the recently renamed Rafa Nadal court at the Real Club de Tenis Barcelona, Nadal captured the trophy without conceding a single set throughout the tournament, concluding the final match in precisely ninety minutes.

Thiem, who had previously defeated the fourteen-time Grand Slam champion on clay at the 2016 Argentina Open and secured his final berth by overcoming world number one Andy Murray for the first time on Saturday, was ultimately outmatched. Under overcast conditions in Barcelona, where cooler temperatures reduced court pace, Nadal required several games to establish dominance. Although Thiem earned the first break point opportunity, Nadal reclaimed momentum, securing the opening set with a decisive break in the tenth game. The second set witnessed no respite, as Nadal achieved two consecutive breaks against the twenty-three-year-old Austrian before serving conclusively for the championship.

These symbols will type Bengali characters first but if "~" will be followed, it will remove previously typed Bengali character and then type the symbol.
Symbols & ~ * : ^ | ' have special meaning. You can type this way & = &~ ~ = ~~ * = *~ : = :~ ^ = ^~ | = |~ ' = '~

A consonant followed by ZWJ character will produce half-formed consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‍ন = prash^n
A consonant followed by ZWNJ character will produce dead consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‌ন = prash^^n

rewrite:
The following delineates a systematic transliteration scheme for generating Bengali script from Roman character input. The foundational mapping of Bengali numerals to their Arabic equivalents is as follows: ০=0, ১=1, ২=2, ৩=3, ৪=4, ৫=5, ৬=6, ৭=7, ৮=8, ৯=9.

Specific diacritics and punctuation marks are invoked using designated key sequences: the Hasant/Viram (্) is contextual; the Nukta (়) is represented by *; the Urdhacomma (ʼ) by '; the Avagrah (ঽ) by &; the Isshar (৺) by ~; the Bengali ana sign (৹) by a~; the Bengali Rupee sign (৲) by Rs~; the Taka sign (৳) by T~; the Devanagari danda (।) by |; the double danda (॥) by ||; the Indian Rupee sign (₹) by Rs; and the Swastika sign (卐) by +~. The Zero Width Joiner (ZWJ) and Zero Width Non Joiner (ZWNJ) are represented by ^ and ^^, respectively.

A critical procedural rule governs the input of these special symbols. Typing a sequence (e.g., &) initially produces its corresponding Bengali character. However, if the tilde (~) is subsequently entered, it deletes the preceding Bengali output and instead renders the literal symbol. To produce the literal forms of the reserved symbols &, ~, *, :, ^, |, and ', one must type &~, ~~, *~, :~, ^~, |~, and '~, respectively. Standard English punctuation and symbols—namely [ ] { } ( ) < > - + / = ; . , " ? ! % \ _ $ @ #—translate directly into their identical counterparts.

Ligature formation is automated per the system's rules. The ZWJ and ZWNJ characters are instrumental in generating alternate glyph renderings. A consonant followed by a ZWJ (^) yields a half-formed consonant character (e.g., প্রশ্ন = *prashn* vs. প্রশ্‍ন = *prash^n*). Conversely, a consonant followed by a ZWNJ (^^) produces a dead consonant character (e.g., প্রশ্ন = *prashn* vs. প্রশ্‌ন = *prash^^n*). Furthermore, when two Roman characters represent a single Bengali vowel diphthong (e.g., *ai*, *au*), the ZWJ character serves as a logical separator to parse them into distinct vowel entities, without being inserted into the final output.

BRASILIA Major Latin American currencies appear more likely to hold their ground in coming months than they did in March, but they remain vulnerable to increased volatility coming from abroad, a Reuters poll showed on Thursday.
Estimates from top banks and research firms still suggest the currencies will probably give back part of their recent gains.
However, one-year forecasts for the Mexican peso and the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar firmed from last month's poll, indicating reduced expectations of a complete reversal in the region's largest currency markets.
The 12-month forecasts strengthened for the Mexican peso to 19.875 per dollar from 20.87 in March and the Brazilian real to 3.295 from 3.35. Also gaining were the Colombian peso to 3020.0 from 3054.17 and the Chilean peso at 669.13 from 670.
Outlooks weakened for the Argentine peso, to 18.0 per dollar from 17.60 in March, and the Peruvian sol, to 3.38 from 3.36.
The Mexican peso has led gains among Latin American currencies this year, rebounding from all-time lows on hopes that U.S. President Donald Trump will not impose heavy tariffs on Mexican exports to the United States as he had threatened.
A series of interest rate increases by the Mexican central bank and its direct intervention in local currency markets with hedging contracts also explain the peso's newfound strength. As long as volatility remains low, higher interest rates should keep supporting the peso.
"Carry attractiveness has increased notably," wrote Rabobank senior strategist Christian Lawrence. "This is particularly true compared to other Latin American currencies," including Brazil, Chile and Colombia, which have cut rates over the past year.
Volatility has also declined in Brazil to around record lows, central bank chief Ilan Goldfajn said this week, despite what he called an "especially uncertain global outlook."
A source of potential instability is the U.S. Federal Reserve, which has so far raised interest rates at a very gradual pace, with no surprises. An acceleration of rate hikes could drain capital from higher-yielding emerging markets such as Latin America.
(Additional reporting by Noe Torres in Mexico City, Nelson Bocanegra in Bogota, Hernan Nessi in Buenos Aires, Ursula Scollo in Santiago; Editing by Ross Finley and Lisa Von Ahn)
rewrite:
A Reuters survey conducted on Thursday indicates that major Latin American currencies are positioned to demonstrate greater resilience in the near term compared to March, though they remain susceptible to heightened volatility stemming from external factors. Despite this improved near-term outlook, projections from leading financial institutions and research analysts continue to anticipate a partial retracement of recent appreciations.

Nevertheless, one-year forward forecasts for the Mexican peso and the Brazilian real against the U.S. dollar have firmed relative to the previous month's survey, suggesting diminished expectations of a full reversal in the region's most significant currency markets. Specifically, the 12-month consensus strengthened for the Mexican peso to 19.875 per dollar from 20.87 in March, and for the Brazilian real to 3.295 from 3.35. The Colombian peso also saw a firmer outlook, moving to 3020.0 from 3054.17, while the Chilean peso edged to 669.13 from 670. In contrast, projections weakened for the Argentine peso, to 18.0 per dollar from 17.60, and for the Peruvian sol, to 3.38 from 3.36.

The Mexican peso, having rebounded from historic lows, has led regional currency gains this year. This appreciation is largely attributed to receding concerns over the imposition of substantial U.S. tariffs on Mexican exports, a policy previously threatened by President Donald Trump. Furthermore, a cycle of interest rate increases by the Bank of Mexico, coupled with its direct intervention in domestic currency markets through hedging contracts, has contributed to the peso's relative strength. Analysts suggest that, provided market volatility remains subdued, elevated interest rates should continue to provide support. Christian Lawrence, a senior strategist at Rabobank, noted, "Carry attractiveness has increased notably," particularly in comparison to other Latin American currencies, such as those of Brazil, Chile, and Colombia, which have engaged in monetary easing over the past year.

In Brazil, central bank president Ilan Goldfajn observed this week that volatility has declined to near-record lows, despite what he characterized as an "especially uncertain global outlook." A persistent source of potential instability remains the monetary policy trajectory of the U.S. Federal Reserve. While the Fed has thus far proceeded with a gradual and predictable pace of interest rate increases, any acceleration in this tightening cycle could precipitate capital outflows from higher-yielding emerging markets, including those in Latin America.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) -- Frankie Ferrari had 19 points and Jordan Ratinho scored 17 to help San Francisco beat Santa Clara 70-59 on Saturday night.
Ferrari and Ratinho combined to shoot 14 of 23 from the field, including 4 of 7 from 3-point range. Matt McCarthy added 12 points on 6-of-9 shooting for USF (13-12, 5-7 West Coast Conference).
The Dons used runs of 14-4 and 9-0 to open a 14-point first-half lead before going into the break with a 35-23 advantage. KJ Feagin scored 11 points, and Henrik Jadersten scored the final six, in a 19-5 spurt that made it 42-all with 14 minutes to play, but Ratinho answered with a 3 and then made a layup to push the lead back to five points. Feagin's layup trimmed Santa Clara's deficit to 58-57 with five minutes left, but Ferrari countered with a 3-point play and the Broncos made just 1 of 10 from the field from there.
Feagin had 15 points, and Henry Caruso scored 12, for Santa Clara (8-16, 5-7).
USF shot 55 percent from the field and outrebounded the Broncos 34-21.
rewrite:
On Saturday evening, the University of San Francisco Dons secured a 70-59 victory over Santa Clara in a West Coast Conference men's basketball contest. Frankie Ferrari led all scorers with 19 points, while teammate Jordan Ratinho contributed 17. The duo combined to make 14 of 23 field goal attempts, including 4 of 7 from three-point range. Matt McCarthy added 12 points for USF, which improved to 13-12 overall and 5-7 in conference play.

The Dons established an early advantage, utilizing scoring runs of 14-4 and 9-0 to build a 35-23 halftime lead. Santa Clara responded in the second half with a 19-5 surge, capped by six consecutive points from Henrik Jadersten, to tie the game at 42 with 14 minutes remaining. Ratinho immediately answered with a three-pointer and a layup to restore a five-point lead for USF. Although a KJ Feagin layup brought Santa Clara within 58-57 late, Ferrari converted a critical three-point play, and the Broncos managed only one field goal in their final ten attempts. Feagin finished with 15 points for Santa Clara (8-16, 5-7). USF shot 55 percent from the field and held a decisive 34-21 rebounding advantage.

Middle Belt youths dissociate region from Igbo quit notice
By Nkiruka Nnorom
Middle belt youths have condemned the recent quit notice issued Igbo living in the North by Arewa Youth Consultative Forum, saying Igbo, just like other Nigerians, have the right to live in any part of the country.
The youths, acting on the platform of All Middle Belt Youth Forum, AMBYF, said in a statement by the National Leader, Mr. Aluh Moses, and the National Secretary, Mr. Andzayi Jonathan, that the entire Middle Belt region was not part of the act.
According to the statement, “we condemn, in very strong terms, the so-called Kaduna Declaration by northern youths’ coalition in its entirety, as it is a deliberate act of driving wedge between northerners and easterners.
“That the Middle Belt region is not part of the northern region. Hence, the All Middle Belt Youth Forum distances itself and the entire Middle Belt region from such obnoxious declaration.”
They urged the northern youths to retract the declaration in the interest of peace and security.

In an official statement released by the organization's National Leader, Mr. Aluh Moses, and National Secretary, Mr. Andzayi Jonathan, the Forum explicitly distanced the Middle Belt region from the declaration. The statement characterized the act as a deliberate strategy to create division between northern and eastern populations and reaffirmed the constitutional right of all Nigerian citizens, including the Igbo, to reside freely in any part of the nation.

The AMBYF emphasized a critical geopolitical distinction, asserting that the Middle Belt is not a constituent part of the northern region. Consequently, the organization declared that neither it nor the territory it represents is associated with what it termed an "obnoxious declaration." The statement urged the coalition of northern youth groups to retract the notice unequivocally, citing the paramount importance of national peace and security. This position underscores ongoing political and ethnic delineations within Nigeria and highlights a regional commitment to national unity against divisive rhetoric.

Lafia – Africa’s richest man and Chairman of Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, has said that he would like to be known as the biggest philanthropist on the continent.
Dangote stated this on Wednesday in Lafia while disbursing N130 million micro grant to 13,000 vulnerable and less privileged women in Nasarawa State.
“I do not only want to be known as Africa’s richest man but the biggest philanthropist in Africa. I will continue to use my resources and my voice to help shape a better Nigeria and Africa as a whole,” he said.
Dangote said he started the foundation in 1993 to improve the lives of the less fortunate and make a positive difference in the growth of Nigeria.
He said the four major goals of the foundation were health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment and disaster relief.
He explained that the grant scheme was one of the components of the economic empowerment programme of the foundation.
Dangote said it was aimed at providing disadvantaged and vulnerable women in the country with a one-off unconditional N10, 000 cash transfer to boost their household income generation.
” This we believe will help their vulnerability and meet their livelihood needs,” he added .
He explained that the programme, which was launched a few years ago, was targeted at a minimum of 1,000 women in each of the 774 local government areas across the country.
“It is estimated that we would spend about N10 billion with some states with a large population getting a little bit more.
“We at Aliko Dangote foundation are happy to continue providing support to the most vulnerable and deserving members of the society across the country,” he said. (NAN)
rewrite:
During a ceremony in Lafia on Wednesday, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, Chairman of the Dangote Group and widely recognized as the wealthiest individual in Africa, articulated his aspiration to be foremost identified as the continent’s preeminent philanthropist. The occasion marked the disbursement of micro-grants totaling one hundred and thirty million Naira (N130,000,000) to thirteen thousand vulnerable and economically disadvantaged women in Nasarawa State. Dangote emphasized that his objective extends beyond financial stature, stating, “I do not only want to be known as Africa’s richest man but the biggest philanthropist in Africa. I will continue to use my resources and my voice to help shape a better Nigeria and Africa as a whole.”

He recounted establishing the Aliko Dangote Foundation in 1993 with the mission of enhancing the welfare of underprivileged populations and contributing positively to national development. The Foundation’s interventions are structured around four principal pillars: health and nutrition, education, economic empowerment, and disaster relief. The grant disbursement event exemplified the economic empowerment component, specifically designed to provide a one-off, unconditional cash transfer of ten thousand Naira (N10,000) to each beneficiary. This initiative aims to augment household income generation among disadvantaged women, thereby mitigating their vulnerability and addressing fundamental livelihood needs.

Dangote further elaborated that the nationwide programme, inaugurated several years ago, targets a minimum of one thousand women in each of Nigeria’s 774 local government areas. The aggregate projected expenditure for this initiative is approximately ten billion Naira (N10,000,000,000), with allocations adjusted to account for demographic variations across states. In concluding his remarks, Dangote reaffirmed the Foundation’s commitment: “We at Aliko Dangote Foundation are happy to continue providing support to the most vulnerable and deserving members of the society across the country.”

A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23. (Gai Phanalasy / FOX5)
A two-year-old girl died Tuesday being struck by a car in a southwest Las Vegas hospital parking lot on April 23.
Metro Police said at about 3:13 p.m. that day, the girl was walking with her family between cars at the St. Rose Pediatrics parking lot, near Buffalo Drive and the 215 freeway. A Mercedes Benz was passing through the lot and hit her.
The driver, a 35-year-old Las Vegas man, was cooperative and stayed on the scene. No impairment was involved, police said.
The girl appeared to have a severe head injury, police said, and was taken into UMC Trauma for treatment. Police said she died on May 8 at UMC.
Metro police said the girl's mother was directly supervising her daughter when the crash happened.
Doctors called the injury "horrific," police said.
A 31-year-old woman, a two year-old girl and a six-month-old girl were also in the car, but no one inside was hurt, Metro said.

According to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the incident occurred at approximately 3:13 p.m. in the parking lot of St. Rose Pediatrics, located near Buffalo Drive and the 215 freeway. The child was walking with her family among parked vehicles when she was hit by a Mercedes Benz traveling through the area.

The driver, a 35-year-old male resident of Las Vegas, remained at the scene and cooperated with authorities. Police confirmed that impairment was not a factor. The child sustained a severe head injury, described by attending physicians as "horrific," and was transported to UMC Trauma for treatment. She subsequently succumbed to her injuries on May 8.

Police noted the girl's mother was providing direct supervision at the time of the collision. Three other occupants—a 31-year-old woman, a two-year-old girl, and a six-month-old girl—were inside the vehicle but were uninjured.

In a series of public statements, Representative Adam Schiff, the ranking Democrat on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, has articulated a consistent position regarding investigations into Russian interference in the 2016 U.S. election. ANKARA (Reuters) - The deputy chairman of Turkey's main opposition Republican People's Party (CHP) said illegal acts were being carried out in favor of the government in Sunday's referendum on expanding the powers of the presidency.
"Many illegal acts are being carried out in favor of the government right now, but 'No' will win in the end," Erdal Aksunger told reporters at his party headquarters, referring to an election board decision to accept unstamped ballots.
A statement on the High Electoral Board's (YSK) website hours before polls closed said it would count ballots that had not been stamped by its officials as valid unless they could be proved fraudulent, citing a high number of complaints that YSK officials at polling stations had failed to stamp them.
With 80 percent of ballots opened, support for the constitutional changes that could hand President Tayyip Erdogan sweeping new powers stood at 53.9 percent, according to the state-run Anadolu news agency.
(Reporting by Gulsen Solaker; Writing by Ece Toksabay)
rewrite: In Ankara, the deputy chairman of Turkey’s primary opposition party, the Republican People’s Party (CHP), asserted that unlawful activities benefiting the governing authorities were occurring during the referendum concerning the expansion of presidential powers. Erdal Aksunger stated to reporters at the party headquarters, “Many illegal acts are being carried out in favor of the government right now, but ‘No’ will win in the end.” This remark referenced a decision by the High Electoral Board (YSK) to accept unstamped ballots as valid unless proven fraudulent. The YSK issued a statement on its website prior to the close of polls, justifying the measure due to numerous complaints that its officials had failed to properly stamp ballots at polling stations. According to the state-operated Anadolu news agency, with 80 percent of ballots counted, support for the constitutional amendments granting President Tayyip Erdogan extensive new authorities stood at 53.9 percent.

The first of 10 people killed in the Toronto van attack has been identified as an employee of a US-based investment management firm, according to a report.
Anne-Marie D’Amico worked at the Canadian headquarters of Invesco located near the mile-long stretch where Alek Minassian allegedly plowed a Ryder rental van into a lunch-hour crowd, killing 10 people and injuring 15, according to the CBC.
Peter Intraligi, president of Invesco Canada, confirmed her death to the outlet.
“Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with all those impacted by this tragic event,” Intraligi said. “I can now confirm that unfortunately one of our employees has succumbed to her injuries. Out of respect for her and her family, we will not be providing any further comments.”
Minassian, 25, was due to appear in a Toronto courtroom at 10 a.m. Tuesday. Police said that charges against the suspect would be provided at that time.
The incident began about 1:30 p.m. Monday around Yonge Street and Finch Avenue and ended when Minassian was collared about a half-hour later after trying to goad police into shooting him.
“We’re all putting our pieces together to see exactly what we have,” said Toronto police Chief Mark Saunders, adding that the attack “definitely appeared deliberate.”
Garry Clement, a former Royal Canadian Mounted Police chief and, told the CBC that he thinks the cops involved “deserve to be commended because they demonstrated a lot of restraint.”
Footage shot by a bystander showed police arresting the man as he shouted: “Kill me” and pointed an object at a cop, who replied, “No, get down!”
When the suspect said, “I have a gun in my pocket,” the officer responded: “I don’t care! Get down!”
The attack shook the usually tranquil streets of Toronto, a major tourist destination. The city, which has a population of 2.8 million, recorded 61 murders last year, Reuters reported.
“This kind of tragic incident is not representative of how we live and who we are,” Mayor John Tory told reporters.
Prime Minister Justin Trudeau called the incident a “tragic and senseless attack.”
The city’s iconic CN Tower, which is normally lit up in the evening, went dark Monday evening.

The initial fatality in the Toronto van attack, which resulted in ten deaths, has been publicly identified as an employee of an American investment management firm. According to a report by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), Anne-Marie D’Amico was employed at the Canadian headquarters of Invesco Ltd., situated proximate to the approximately mile-long section of Yonge Street where the incident occurred. The alleged perpetrator, Alek Minassian, is accused of deliberately driving a rented Ryder van into pedestrians during the lunch hour, killing ten individuals and injuring fifteen others. Peter Intraligi, President of Invesco Canada, confirmed Ms. D’Amico’s death to the outlet, stating, “Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with all those impacted by this tragic event. I can now confirm that unfortunately one of our employees has succumbed to her injuries. Out of respect for her and her family, we will not be providing any further comments.”

Minassian, aged 25, was scheduled for a court appearance in Toronto. Authorities indicated that formal charges would be presented at that time. The event commenced at approximately 1:30 p.m. on Monday near the intersection of Yonge Street and Finch Avenue, concluding roughly thirty minutes later with the suspect’s arrest after he attempted to provoke officers into using lethal force. Toronto Police Chief Mark Saunders remarked that the investigation is ongoing, noting the attack “definitely appeared deliberate.” Garry Clement, a former Royal Canadian Mounted Police superintendent, opined to the CBC that the responding officers “deserve to be commended because they demonstrated a lot of restraint.” Bystander footage corroborates this, depicting the arrest while the suspect shouted “Kill me” and gestured with an object, to which an officer responded with commands to desist.

The violence profoundly disturbed the typically tranquil environs of Toronto, a major metropolitan and tourist center. As reported by Reuters, the city, with a population of 2.8 million, documented 61 homicides in the preceding year. Mayor John Tory asserted to reporters that “This kind of tragic incident is not representative of how we live and who we are,” a sentiment echoed by Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, who characterized the event as a “tragic and senseless attack.” In a symbolic gesture, the city’s iconic CN Tower, ordinarily illuminated in the evening, remained dark on Monday night.

input: How much money do American teachers make? If your answer to that question is "not enough," you are definitely not wrong! But as recent teacher strikes have highlighted, some states are doing a much worse job of keeping teachers housed and fed than others. The folks at personal finance site HowMuch put together some maps of the average teacher salary in all 50 states using data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and there is way too much variation here for our liking. The maps showing middle and high school teachers' average earnings, which you can see over at HowMuch, show a similar pattern. HowMuch averaged out the median elementary, middle and high school teacher salary to calculate the top 10 states for teacher pay overall: 1. New York: $81,613 2. Alaska: $80,627 3. Connecticut: $78,567 4. California: $76,523 5. Massachusetts: $75,720 6. New Jersey: $72,460 7. Oregon: $69,643 8. Virginia: $68,707 9. Maryland: $67,173 10. Rhode Island: $67,050 [HowMuch] Not on the top ten list? West Virginia, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Colorado and Arizona, where teachers have walked out to protest low wages and insufficient benefits in recent months. If the wave of strikes continues, maybe teachers can turn all the light blue states on the above map regular blue. Or even — dare we hope? — dark blue.
rewrite:
The compensation of public school teachers in the United States exhibits significant interstate disparities, a point underscored by recent labor actions. While a consensus exists that educator salaries are generally insufficient, data reveals that certain states perform markedly worse in providing adequate remuneration. An analysis by the personal finance platform HowMuch, utilizing Bureau of Labor Statistics figures, maps the average annual salaries for teachers across all fifty states, highlighting a concerning degree of geographical variation.

The pattern of disparity is consistent across instructional levels, as illustrated in separate maps for middle and high school educators available on the HowMuch site. By averaging the median salaries for elementary, middle, and high school teachers, HowMuch calculated the ten states with the highest overall teacher compensation: New York ($81,613), Alaska ($80,627), Connecticut ($78,567), California ($76,523), Massachusetts ($75,720), New Jersey ($72,460), Oregon ($69,643), Virginia ($68,707), Maryland ($67,173), and Rhode Island ($67,050).

Conversely, states including West Virginia, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Colorado, and Arizona—where educators have recently engaged in strikes to protest low wages and inadequate benefits—are absent from this top tier. The continuation of such labor movements may potentially catalyze wage increases, shifting states from lower compensation levels (represented in lighter shades on the source maps) to higher ones (darker shades).

There is no shortage of options.
"We have a very good understanding of the needs of our football team," Newsome said. "What we try to do is to match that with the players."
Some things to know about the Ravens' draft:
TIGHT END NEEDED
The leading receiver on the team last season was tight end Benjamin Watson, who joined the Saints as a free agent.
A replacement is sorely needed, and after failing to secure one through free agency, the Ravens will look to snag one in the draft.
"There are some pretty good ones out there. And they're of the athletic variety, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence," said Joe Horitz, director of college scouting.
One of Newsome's best picks was tight end Todd Heap, selected in the first round in 2001 even though the Ravens already had future Hall of Fame star Shannon Sharpe.
TRADE OR NOT?
Newsome cryptically mentioned the possibility of trading the No. 16 pick, but DeCosta likes the idea of drafting in the middle of the round.
"We're in a good spot for a lot of different reasons," DeCosta said. "I think 16 is a good spot to be in this draft. It plays well to our needs and different strategies."
VOLCANO BREWING
Coach John Harbaugh has been in the Ravens draft room since 2008, and when it comes time for Baltimore to make a pick, he just gets out of the way.
"I'll tell you, it's like a volcano, kind of. It's festering, like, 'Is this thing going to blow?' It never quite blows, but there's so much tension," Harbaugh said.
In the end, though, it's Newsome's call.
"Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh said, "and we all feel good about it."
HITS, MISSES AND BARGAINS
Perriman missed the entire 2015 season with a knee injury, caught 33 passes in 2016 and last season had a mere 10 catches for the league's 29th-ranked passing attack.
Newsome also struck out with safety Matt Elam at No. 32 overall in 2013. But he recently found two fourth-round gems: Defensive end Brent Urban in 2014 and offensive lineman Alex Lewis in 2016.
___
For more NFL coverage: http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP_NFL
By David Ginsburg, The Associated Press
rewrite:
The Baltimore Ravens enter the NFL draft with a comprehensive array of strategic possibilities at their disposal. General Manager Ozzie Newsome emphasized a methodical approach, stating, "We possess a thorough understanding of our football team's requirements. Our objective is to align those needs with the available player talent." Several key considerations define the organization's pre-draft posture.

A pressing need exists at the tight end position. The departure of Benjamin Watson, the team's leading receiver in the previous season, to the New Orleans Saints via free agency has created a significant void. Having not addressed this need in free agency, the Ravens are anticipated to target a tight end in the draft. Joe Horitz, the director of college scouting, noted the availability of promising prospects, describing them as "athletic, pass-catching tight ends that certainly could help impact our offence." Historical precedent supports such a selection; one of Newsome's most successful draft decisions was choosing tight end Todd Heap in the first round of 2001, despite the presence of future Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe on the roster.

Strategic positioning regarding the sixteenth overall selection presents another focal point. Newsome alluded to the potential of trading the pick, while Assistant General Manager Eric DeCosta expressed a preference for retaining it. DeCosta characterized the spot as advantageous, stating, "We are in a good spot for a lot of different reasons... It plays well to our needs and different strategies."

The atmosphere within the draft room during selection decisions has been vividly described by Head Coach John Harbaugh, a fixture there since 2008. He likens the tension to "a volcano... festering," though he clarifies that the process, while intense, remains controlled. Ultimately, the final decision rests with Newsome. "Ozzie pulls the trigger and makes a decision," Harbaugh affirmed, "and we all feel good about it."

The draft history of the Ravens under Newsome reflects a mixture of outcomes, underscoring the inherent unpredictability of the process. Wide receiver Breshad Perriman, a first-round choice in 2015, has been hampered by injuries and limited production. Safety Matt Elam, selected in the first round in 2013, did not meet expectations. Conversely, Newsome has demonstrated an ability to identify value in later rounds, as evidenced by the selections of defensive end Brent Urban (2014) and offensive lineman Alex Lewis (2016), both of whom were chosen in the fourth round and have contributed effectively. This record of hits, misses, and bargains informs the complex calculus facing the franchise as the draft commences.

Over time, however, Edmonton’s location — and, in particular, the lack of direct flights from New York — came to feel like a plus, rather than a minus.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
“There was something attractive about doing it in a place where there wouldn’t be a whole set of eyes seeing the work and judging it before it’s fully baked,” Ms. Chavkin, who had never been to Edmonton and had never heard of Citadel, said.
Then there was the money.
The American dollar stretches further in Canada. And Citadel was not asking for much — the theater agreed to spend what it usually spends to stage a musical (about $600,000 Canadian) and also agreed not to seek a royalty from future productions (nonprofits that help develop commercial shows often get a percentage of Broadway profits).
The commercial producers would pay the rest of the costs, and bring their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and significant set elements to upgrade what they would find at Citadel.
Photo
“There was no question it was financially in our interest to go to Canada,” said Ms. Isaacs, who is producing the show along with Mr. Kirdahy, Dale Franzen, and Hunter Arnold.
During just three weeks of rehearsal and four previews, Ms. Chavkin restaged the show several times over, with new cast members, including Reeve Carney (“Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark”), in three of the five main roles. At first, a rail line bisected the stage; the creative team scrapped that design after a single performance. There were several experiments with how best to deploy characters added for the Edmonton production in an effort to bring to life, as it were, those toiling away in hell.
“We’re trying to walk this line between maintaining the metaphorical and poetic world, and also trying to deliver a satisfying story,” Ms. Mitchell said. “The only way we know where it comfortably wants to sit is by going too far in one direction or another.”
The Citadel says that if it worked on a Broadway-aimed show again, it would dedicate a staffer to managing relations with the commercial producers, because immigration and budget issues proved more time-consuming than anticipated.
rewrite:
Edmonton’s geographical situation—specifically, its absence of direct flights from New York—gradually came to be perceived as an asset rather than a liability. As director Rachel Chavkin, who was previously unfamiliar with both the city and the Citadel Theatre, noted, there was an appeal in developing a production in a location removed from the immediate scrutiny of the prominent theatrical centers. This distance allowed the creative process to unfold without the pressure of extensive external observation and judgment during its formative stages.

Financial considerations also played a decisive role. The favorable exchange rate increased the purchasing power of the American dollar in Canada. Furthermore, the Citadel Theatre’s requirements were comparatively modest: the institution committed only its standard expenditure for mounting a musical, approximately $600,000 Canadian, and waived any claim to future royalties—a departure from the common practice wherein nonprofit developmental theaters typically secure a share of subsequent commercial profits. The commercial producers assumed responsibility for all remaining costs, supplementing the theatre’s existing resources with their own sound and lighting equipment, a revolving stage, and substantial set pieces to enhance the production value. Producer Tom Kirdahy confirmed that the economic rationale for selecting Canada was unequivocal.

The developmental period in Edmonton, comprising three weeks of rehearsal and four preview performances, was characterized by significant creative evolution. Director Chavkin repeatedly reconfigured the staging, integrating new cast members—including Reeve Carney in one of the five principal roles—and substantially revising the production’s visual and narrative elements. An initial design concept featuring a rail line dividing the stage was abandoned after a single performance. The creative team conducted multiple experiments regarding the staging of characters unique to the Edmonton iteration, aiming to effectively dramatize the narrative’s infernal setting and its inhabitants. Writer Dave Malloy described the process as navigating a tension between preserving a metaphorical, poetic framework and delivering a coherent narrative, a balance discovered only through exploratory extremes.

Reflecting on the experience, the Citadel Theatre administration observed that any future collaboration on a production with Broadway aspirations would benefit from assigning a dedicated staff member to oversee relations with commercial producers. This recommendation stems from the unanticipated administrative complexities, particularly concerning immigration and budgetary matters, which required considerably more time and resources than initially projected.

An employee stands outside a Lowe's home improvement chain in Austin, Texas, U.S., February 27, 2017. REUTERS/Mohammad Khursheed
NEW YORK Shares of home improvement retailer Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) could rise by 20 percent or more, helped by better projected earnings growth this year and greater room for margin improvement, Barron's said on Sunday.
Companies such as Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N) are uniquely positioned due to their strong outlook, as a healthy economy and improving real estate markets in most of the United States encourages homeowners to undertake renovation, Barron's said.
These companies are also "Amazon proof", the report said, noting that home improvement was low on the list of categories the retailer is expected to penetrate.
U.S. retail heavyweights including Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N) and Kroger Co (KR.N) have been locked in a fierce battle against Amazon Inc (AMZN.O).
While both Home Depot and Lowe's are poised for growth, Lowe's could be more attractive now, due in part to its lower price-to-earnings ratio, the report said.
Lowe's shares trade at $82, or about 18 times projected earnings of $4.63 per share for year ending January 2018, while Home Depot trades at $147, or 20.4 times estimated earnings of $7.19 per share in its current year, Barron's said.
Lowe's same-store sales performance has lagged Home Depot's the past several quarters, mainly due to its focus on do-it-yourself customers who spend less on big-ticket items than professionals.
However, the retailer is taking steps to boost per-store revenue, which would help narrow the valuation gap, Barron's said.
Lowe's offers investors exposure to one of retail's strongest sectors, the potential for 15 percent annual earnings growth and a "shareholder friendly" management, according to the report.
(Reporting by Devika Krishna Kumar in New York; Editing by Meredith Mazzilli)
rewrite:
On February 27, 2017, an employee was photographed outside a Lowe's home improvement retail location in Austin, Texas. According to a report in Barron's on Sunday, shares of Lowe's Companies Inc (LOW.N) possess the potential to appreciate by twenty percent or more. This outlook is supported by stronger projected earnings growth for the current year and significant opportunity for margin expansion. The publication noted that home improvement retailers like Lowe's and Home Depot Inc (HD.N) occupy a favorable position, benefiting from a robust economic climate and strengthening real estate markets across much of the United States, which incentivizes homeowners to invest in renovation projects.

The report further characterized these firms as relatively insulated from competitive pressures posed by Amazon.com Inc (AMZN.O), a dynamic contrasting with other major U.S. retailers such as Target Corp (TGT.N), Wal-Mart Stores Inc (WMT.N), and Kroger Co (KR.N), which are engaged in intense competition with the online giant. The home improvement category is considered less susceptible to e-commerce penetration. While both leading companies in the sector are positioned for growth, Barron's suggested Lowe's may currently present a more attractive investment proposition, partly due to its lower price-to-earnings multiple. Specifically, Lowe's shares trade at approximately $82, or eighteen times the projected earnings of $4.63 per share for the fiscal year ending January 2018. In comparison, Home Depot trades at around $147, or 20.4 times its estimated current-year earnings of $7.19 per share.

Although Lowe's comparable-store sales have trailed those of Home Depot in recent quarters—a trend attributed to Lowe's greater reliance on do-it-yourself customers, who typically spend less on high-value items than professional contractors—the company is implementing initiatives to increase revenue per store. These measures are expected to help narrow the valuation gap between the two retailers. The report concluded that Lowe's provides investors with exposure to a resilient retail segment, the potential for annual earnings growth of up to fifteen percent, and a management team committed to shareholder returns.

A proposed Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup competition due to take place in Düsseldorf next season has been postponed for a year due to a scheduling conflict.
The event had been scheduled to be held on a temporary ramp in the Espirit Arena in January, the same venue which hosted the World Table Tennis Championships last year.
Organisers have determined, however, that there will be "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" in the 54,000 capacity venue due to other events also taking place there.
"Because of this, the decision was made to postpone the event from the 2018/19 season until the 2019/20 World Cup season, where the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised," said the International Ski Federation (FIS).
"At this time the proposed schedule for the Düsseldorf Snowboard and Freeski big air World Cup will see the competition held from January 2 to 4, 2020."
The Big Air event in Düsseldorf had been due to take place in the Espirit Arena ©SOP Architekten
The Big Air World Cup season is due to begin in Cardrona in New Zealand in September and continue with events in Milan, Beijing, Canyons in United States, Quebec and Oslo.
"While the cancellation of this season’s Dusseldorf event is disappointing for all parties involved, excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe," FIS added.
"With Düsseldorf 54,000 seat Espirit Arena - home to the Fortuna [football team who recently earned promotion to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season] - lined up to host the competition, the Düsseldorf snowboard and freeski big air competitions are set to be season highlights in January 2020."
rewrite:
The inaugural Snowboard and Freeski Big Air World Cup competition, scheduled for Düsseldorf in the forthcoming season, has been deferred by one year owing to a scheduling conflict. The event was to be staged in January upon a temporary ramp constructed within the Espirit Arena, a venue which previously hosted the World Table Tennis Championships. Organisers have concluded that, due to concurrent events at the 54,000-capacity stadium, there is "insufficient time to realise the construction of the competition ramp" within the required timeframe.

Consequently, the International Ski Federation (FIS) announced that "the decision was made to postpone the event from the 2018/19 season until the 2019/20 World Cup season, where the safety of the athletes can remain paramount and the true vision for the competition can be fully realised." The rescheduled Düsseldorf World Cup is now provisionally set for January 2 to 4, 2020.

The broader Big Air World Cup season will commence as planned in Cardrona, New Zealand, in September, with subsequent events in Milan, Beijing, Canyons (United States), Quebec, and Oslo. While acknowledging the disappointment caused by this season's cancellation, FIS expressed considerable anticipation for the 2020 event. The federation stated, "excitement for the 2020 event is high as the FIS snowboard and freeski tours look forward to bringing World Cup big air action to one of the great cities of Europe."

The competition is poised to be a highlight of the January 2020 calendar, leveraging the significant capacity and profile of the Espirit Arena. This venue also serves as the home stadium for Fortuna Düsseldorf, a football team recently promoted to the Bundesliga for the 2018/19 season. The integration of a major winter sports event within such a prominent urban and sporting infrastructure is expected to enhance the spectacle and stature of the World Cup tour.

MIAMI (WFLA) – CarePlus Health Plans is notifying customers after a privacy breach that occurred on Jan. 17.
The breach occurred due to a series of programming and printing errors, resulting in Explanation of Benefits letters being mailed to the incorrect CarePlus member.
The EOBs impacted with the errors were mailed out on Jan. 9 and Jan. 16. Roughly 11,200 members’ information as sent to another member.
Personal financial information and Social Security numbers were not contained in the letters.
The information disclosed included:
Member name
CarePlus identification number and plan name
Date(s) of service(s)
Provider of service
Services provided
CarePlus has no information that any data has been inappropriately used.
Anyone who notices any changes in their EOB statement, SmartSummary or medical records that are unfamiliar to them, or customers who have any questions, should contact CarePlus at 1-800-794-5907, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
WHAT OTHERS ARE CLICKING ON RIGHT NOW:
rewrite: CarePlus Health Plans has issued a notification to its members regarding a privacy incident that transpired on January 17. The breach originated from a combination of programming and printing errors, which led to the misdirection of Explanation of Benefits (EOB) documents to incorrect member addresses. These erroneous mailings were dispatched on January 9 and January 16, affecting approximately 11,200 individuals by exposing their information to another plan member. The compromised data encompassed member names, CarePlus identification numbers and plan names, dates of service, provider names, and descriptions of services rendered. Notably, the letters did not contain personal financial details or Social Security numbers. CarePlus currently has no evidence suggesting any misuse of the disclosed information. Affected members or those with inquiries are advised to review their EOB statements, SmartSummaries, and medical records for unfamiliar entries and to contact CarePlus customer service at 1-800-794-5907 between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. with any concerns.

Recently it was reported that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club and Scuba Club lost their official University recognition. A "risk assessment" deemed the clubs too risky. What a shame! The Caving Club has sponsored regular trips for 70 years; the Outing Club is nearly 100 years old.
What has changed over the past 100 years that would cause Penn State University to take such a drastic step? Lawsuits, lawyers, and a whole lot of money.
According to student leaders of these organizations, losing campus recognition means a club will no longer be covered under the university's $1 million liability insurance policy. I will put it more bluntly: It is too risky for Penn State to continue insuring these clubs because of the constant threat of lawsuits. That pot of a million bucks is just too attractive to plaintiffs' attorneys. The propensity to sue in our overly litigious society puts Penn State and any large organization with deep pockets right in the cross hairs of lawyers.
While some might blame Penn State for being too cautious, the university is not really to blame here. It must make these decisions mindful that attorneys are always looking for the chance to strike. And it's not just "dear old State." Thanks to abusive lawsuits, entire industries have disappeared in Pennsylvania and the cost of goods and services continue to rise as the explosive costs of litigation are factored in. Penn State and its students are just the most recent victims.
It begs the question: Where will the plaintiffs' attorneys strike next? Perhaps the table tennis club?
Curt Schroder
Executive director, Pennsylvania Coalition for Civil Justice Reform
Hatrisburg
rewrite:
Recent reports indicate that the Penn State Outing Club, Nittany Grotto Caving Club, and Scuba Club have had their official university recognition revoked following a risk assessment that categorized their activities as excessively hazardous. This development is particularly regrettable given the longstanding histories of these organizations; the Caving Club has facilitated regular excursions for seven decades, while the Outing Club has operated for nearly a century.

The pivotal question is what has shifted over the past hundred years to prompt such a decisive action by Penn State University. The primary drivers appear to be litigation, legal counsel, and financial exposure. As explained by student leaders of these groups, the loss of institutional recognition means the clubs will no longer be covered under the university's liability insurance policy, which provides up to $1 million in coverage. More directly, the university likely perceives the continuation of this insurance as untenable due to the persistent threat of lawsuits. The substantial insurance fund represents a tempting target for plaintiffs' attorneys. In an increasingly litigious society, entities like Penn State, with considerable financial resources, become natural focal points for legal action.

While some may criticize the university for excessive caution, the institution is not principally at fault. It must operate under the reality that attorneys are perpetually seeking opportunities to initiate claims. This phenomenon extends beyond Penn State; in Pennsylvania, entire industries have reportedly diminished due to aggressive litigation, while the costs of goods and services have risen as businesses incorporate escalating legal expenses. Penn State and its students are merely the latest affected parties.

This situation raises a broader concern: which activities or organizations will be targeted next by such legal strategies? Even seemingly low-risk groups could potentially face scrutiny. The underlying issue underscores the need for a balanced approach to risk and liability within the academic environment.

After shocking the football community in 2017 and nearly defeating the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship, it appears the bookies over in Vegas are still somewhat skeptical about the Jacksonville Jaguars. In the latest early odds by Las Vegas Super Book, that was exactly the case as they gave the Jags 20-to-1 odds with six other teams.
Odds to win next year's Super Bowl, via @LVSuperBook: Patriots (4-1)
Steelers (8-1)

Cowboys/Rams/Seahawks/49ers/Jaguars/Texans (20-1) — Will Brinson (@WillBrinson) January 29, 2018
What’s interesting about Super Book’s odds is that the Pittsburgh Steelers, who the Jags beat twice at Heinz Field, are ranked way ahead of the Jaguars with 8-to-1 odds. Something else that will grab the attention of Jags fans is that the Seahawks, who missed the playoffs and were defeated by the Jags, also have 20-to-1 odds.
One reason for the Jags’ questionable odds could be due to the strength of schedule in 2018, which will be much more difficult than 2017’s. rewrite:

This is evidenced by the early Super Bowl LIII odds released by the Las Vegas Super Book, which positioned the Jaguars at 20-to-1, a ranking shared with six other franchises.

Several factors may contribute to this cautious assessment. The Jaguars are projected to face a substantially more challenging strength of schedule in the 2018 season compared to 2017. Furthermore, persistent doubts regarding the consistency of quarterback Blake Bortles, notwithstanding his documented improvement, appear to influence this positioning. The odds generally favor teams perceived to possess elite-level quarterback play.

These preliminary valuations remain highly fluid and are subject to significant revision following impending free agency movements and the NFL draft in March and April. Monitoring shifts in these odds throughout the offseason will provide a useful indicator of the franchise's evolving standing within the analytical perspective of the betting market.
