MELBOURNE Australia pace spearhead Mitchell Starc and batsman Chris Lynn have been named as part of a formidable squad for next month's Champions Trophy in England and Wales despite nursing injuries.
Starc was forced to pull out midway through the India tour last month with a fractured foot while Lynn has been sidelined with a shoulder injury during the Indian Premier League.
Both are expected to be fit for Australia's opener on June 2 against New Zealand.
"Our medical staff will continue to monitor Mitchell and Chris’s recovery from their respective injuries but we are hopeful they will be fit in time for the team’s departure on May 18,” selector Trevor Hohns said in a media release.
James Faulkner, man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final against New Zealand, has been omitted from the 15-man squad named on Thursday, with selectors opting for all-rounders Moises Henriques, Glenn Maxwell and Marcus Stoinis.
Young fast bowler Pat Cummins and James Pattinson, on the comeback trail after suffering stress fractures in his back, were included in an imposing pace battery along with Josh Hazlewood and John Hastings.
"Both James and John have made very good returns from injury and are bowling well for their respective teams in the English county competition as well as both contributing well with the bat," Hohns said.
"When you also add Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins to the fast bowling artillery it becomes a very exciting proposition for Australian cricket."
Legspinner Adam Zampa is the sole specialist spinner in the squad, while batsmen Usman Khawaja, George Bailey and Peter Handscomb have missed out.
World champions Australia, who lost their top ranking to South Africa earlier this year, will bid for their third win in the quadrennial one-day international tournament after back-to-back triumphs in 2006 and 2009.
Squad:
Steve Smith (captain), David Warner, Pat Cummins, Aaron Finch, John Hastings, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Moises Henriques, Chris Lynn, Glenn Maxwell, James Pattinson, Mitchell Starc, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Adam Zampa
(Reporting by Ian Ransom; Editing by Amlan Chakraborty/Peter Rutherford)

Team officials anticipate both players will be available for Australia’s inaugural match against New Zealand on June 2.

"We are optimistic they will attain fitness prior to the squad's departure on May 18," Hohns remarked. The fifteen-player roster, announced on Thursday, notably excludes all-rounder James Faulkner, who was awarded man-of-the-match in the 2015 World Cup final. The Australian team, which recently ceded its top one-day international ranking to South Africa, will pursue a third Champions Trophy title, having previously secured the tournament in 2006 and 2009.

MORRIS, Minn. — A 94-year-old Minnesota man whose wife died after battling cancer built a swimming pool in his backyard for children in his neighborhood.
Keith Davison’s wife of 66 years died last year, KARE 11 reports.
“You just can’t imagine what it’s like,” he said. “You cry a lot. That’s just the way it is because she’s not here.”
Davison then decided to do something different to fill his time.
In the spring, the retired judge had an in-ground pool built. In July, the pool, which is 32 feet long and 9 feet deep, opened — and kids from all over the neighborhood came to swim.
“I knew they’d come,” Davison said.
Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren, is usually seen sitting in a chair next to the pool, watching the kids swimming, laughing and having fun.
“I’m not sitting by myself looking at the walls,” Davison said. “What else would you think of doing where you could have a whole bunch of kids over every afternoon?”
rewrite: In Morris, Minnesota, a ninety-four-year-old widower constructed a residential swimming pool to serve neighborhood children following the loss of his spouse. Keith Davison, whose wife of sixty-six years passed away after a struggle with cancer, described the profound loneliness of bereavement. Seeking purposeful activity, the retired judge commissioned the installation of an in-ground pool measuring thirty-two feet in length and nine feet in depth, which opened for use in July. The facility has since attracted numerous local youths. Mr. Davison, who has three adult children but no grandchildren, frequently observes the children’s recreational activities from a chair beside the pool. He notes that this project alleviates the isolation of widowhood, providing daily social engagement and a constructive alternative to solitude.

By Liana B. Baker and Olivia Oran
April 12 Morgan Stanley's chief compliance officer Billy Fenrich is leaving the firm just over a year after being named to the position.
Fenrich will be replaced by Raul Yanes, according to an internal Morgan Stanley memo reviewed by Reuters, which was confirmed by a firm spokesman.
Fenrich is joining quantitative hedge fund AQR Capital Management as its chief legal officer, according to an AQR spokeswoman.
Yanes was most recently a litigation partner at the law firm Davis Polk & Wardwell and had also served in a number of senior positions under president George W. Bush, including staff secretary and assistant to the president and senior counselor to the attorney general.
Fenrich joined Morgan Stanley's legal department in 2014 from hedge fund PointState Capital. He was named chief compliance officer in 2016, replacing longtime compliance chief Stuart Breslow. He had also worked at Davis Polk.
Compliance officers have become critical figures on Wall Street since the financial crisis, helping to ensure that bankers and traders stay out of trouble and avoid massive fines. (Reporting by Liana Baker and Olivia Oran in New York; Editing by Tom Brown)

HOLLYWOOD stars including Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler were forced to evacuate their homes as the deadly fire in California continues to burn.
President Donald Trump has declared a state of emergency and ordered federal agencies to help with rescue efforts.
White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters said Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed Trump and Vice President Mike Pence on a wildfire prevention roundtable today.
Walters said the White House “continues to closely monitor the situation” and is urging “anyone ordered to evacuate during a wildfire, do so immediately and listen to your local and state officials”.
Camera Icon Firefighters monitor a blaze beside Highway 33 near Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP Camera Icon Firefighters comb through smouldering ash in the remains of dozens of homes destroyed by the Lilac Fire in San Diego. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
She also said the White House “extends its thoughts and prayers” to everyone affected by the fires that have been tearing through Southern California.
Authorities today issued new alerts about unhealthy air from smoke and ash sent up by the growing wildfire.
Celebrities including former Glee star Lea Michele, talk show host DeGeneres, along with Hilton and Kylie Jenner were forced to flee their homes and, in Jenner’s case, her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters.
Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery restaurant in the foothill enclave of Montecito, said customers were wearing masks.
Camera Icon Flames erupt on mountainsides in the Los Padres national forest north of Ojai. Picture: AFP Picture: AFP
He said smoke was so thick that visibility was down to a few metres and a layer of ash was coating the streets.
Regulators were warning resident in parts of Santa Barbara, Ventura and Los Angeles counties to stay indoors, avoid vigorous outdoor activities and not do anything to stir up ash.
Even residents of Montecito and neighbouring Carpinteria who weren’t under evacuation orders opted to leave because of the thick blanket of smoke.
rewrite:
As the ongoing wildfires in California continue to pose a significant threat, numerous high-profile residents, including celebrities Ellen DeGeneres, Paris Hilton, and Chelsea Handler, have been compelled to evacuate their residences. In response to the crisis, President Donald Trump has issued a formal state of emergency, directing federal agencies to assist in rescue and containment operations. White House spokeswoman Lindsay Walters reported that Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue briefed both the President and Vice President Mike Pence during a wildfire prevention roundtable discussion. Walters further stated that the administration is "closely monitoring the situation" and strongly advises all individuals under evacuation orders to comply immediately, adhering to directives from local and state authorities.

The White House also extended its "thoughts and prayers" to those impacted by the fires ravaging Southern California. Concurrently, authorities have issued new public health alerts regarding dangerously unhealthy air quality resulting from pervasive smoke and ash. This has prompted further evacuations among notable figures, including former *Glee* star Lea Michele and businessperson Kylie Jenner, who was required to vacate both her home and her Kylie Cosmetics headquarters.

On the ground, conditions remain severe. Richard Sanchez, a manager at Jeannine’s American Bakery in Montecito, observed customers wearing protective masks, noting that dense smoke reduced visibility to mere meters and deposited a layer of ash throughout the streets. Official regulators have warned residents in affected portions of Santa Barbara, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties to remain indoors, abstain from strenuous outdoor activity, and avoid actions that might disturb accumulated ash. Even in areas such as Montecito and adjacent Carpinteria, where mandatory evacuations were not in effect, many residents chose to depart voluntarily due to the overwhelming smoke, illustrating the extensive disruptive impact of the blazes.

A World War One grave in France marked as that of an unknown soldier has been identified as the resting place of an army officer from Scotland.
The headstone at Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, near Reims, was dedicated only to "a major" of the Royal Engineers.
Detective work by David Tattersfield, of the Western Front Association, identified the major to be an Alexander Soutar, a minister's son.
Maj Soutar was born in Cullen and grew up in Glasgow and Thurso.
He fought at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendale in 1917, before being shot and killed by a sniper on 28 May 1918 while helping to defend the village of Hermonville, near Jonchery-Sur-Vesle, from an attack by German soldiers.
One hundred years after his death, Maj Soutar's descendants have gathered at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery where he lies to honour him.
A new headstone with his name has been erected.
rewrite: A previously unidentified World War One burial site in France has now been recognized as the grave of a Scottish military officer. The headstone at the Commonwealth War Graves Commission Cemetery in Jonchery-sur-Vesle, near Reims, had been inscribed solely to "a major" of the Royal Engineers. Research conducted by David Tattersfield of the Western Front Association established that this officer was Major Alexander Soutar, son of a minister. Born in Cullen and raised in Glasgow and Thurso, Maj Soutar served at the Somme in 1916 and Passchendaele in 1917. He was killed by a sniper on 28 May 1918 while aiding in the defence of Hermonville against a German assault. On the centenary of his death, his descendants assembled at the cemetery for a commemorative ceremony, following the installation of a new headstone bearing his name.

ROCHESTER, Mich. — Tai Odiase had 19 points, on 8-for-8 shooting, and three blocks, Godwin Boahen hit four 3-pointers and finished with 16 points and Illinois-Chicago beat Oakland 79-73 on Friday night for its fifth win in a row.
Marcus Ottey added 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson had 13 points, nine rebounds and seven assists for UIC (13-11, 8-3 Horizon League). The Flames have eight conference wins for the first time since finishing the 2007-08 season 9-9 in Horizon League play.
Odiase had a dunk and two layups during a 6-2 spurt that made it 17-14 and UIC led the rest of the way. Ferguson converted a 3-point play to spark a 10-2 run that pushed the lead to 11 points before Boahen's 3-pointer made it 40-30 at the break. Nick Daniels hit a 3 that pulled Oakland (14-10, 6-5) within two points with two minutes to play, but Ottey made two free throws and Odiase hit a jumper to make it 76-69 and UIC made 4 of 6 free throws in the final 32 seconds to seal it.
Martez Walker had 21 points and Jalen Hayes scored 15 for Oakland. Kendrick Nunn added 20, but shot 3 of 22 from the field, including 1 of 10 from 3-point range.
rewrite:

Godwin Boahen contributed 16 points, including four successful three-point field goals. Supporting contributions came from Marcus Ottey with 15 points and Tarkus Ferguson, who posted a stat line of 13 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists.

This victory improves UIC’s record to 13-11 overall and 8-3 within Horizon League conference play, marking the first time the program has achieved eight conference wins since the 2007-08 season, which concluded with a 9-9 league record. The Flames established control in the first half, concluding the period with a 40-30 advantage following a 10-2 scoring run. For Oakland, Martez Walker led all scorers with 21 points, supported by Jalen Hayes with 15. Despite a 20-point effort from Kendrick Nunn, his efficiency was hampered by a 3-for-22 shooting performance from the field.

The Center for Law and Social Justice at Medgar Evers College is a winner of the Brooklyn Community Foundation’s Annual Spark Prize, which recognizes exceptional nonprofits rooted in Brooklyn that advances racial and social justice. The center will receive $100,000 in general operating support from the foundation.
CLSJ is one of five organizations receiving the prestigious Spark Prize, along with the Cave Canem Foundation, Exalt Youth, GRIOT Circle and the Red Hook Initiative. The organizations, each receiving $100,000, were selected from a pool of over 130 applicants by a 30-member committee of Brooklyn leaders in business, civics and philanthropy. All will be honored February 8 at a celebration breakfast hosted by actress and comedian Ana Gasteyer that includes a tribute to Hildy J. Simmons, a philanthropic leader and longtime Brooklyn Community Foundation board member.
“We are absolutely thrilled to be selected as a winner of the Spark Prize Award,” said Esmeralda Simmons, Esq., founder and executive director of CLSJ. “It is our mission to advocate for and assist African descendant and disenfranchised communities on racial justice issues such as voter rights, educational inequity, police violence, as well as tackling issues that impact women of color, and this award will help us further that mission.”
The Brooklyn Community Foundation is dedicated to Brooklyn’s charitable community and partners with donors and community leaders to bolster nonprofits, strengthen neighborhoods and increase opportunities for youth. Simmons expressed gratitude to Foundation President and CEO Cecilia Clarke for aiding social justice initiatives in Brooklyn. She also thanked the Brooklyn community for their continued support.
Medgar Evers College’s renowned Center for Law and Social Justice provides advocacy, training and expert services in a personal manner. CLSJ conducts research and initiates advocacy projects and litigation on behalf of community organizations and groups that promote human, national and international understanding.
The Spark Prize, sponsored by TD Bank with support from National Grid, is presented by the Brooklyn Community Foundation in partnership with the Office of the Brooklyn Borough President and the Brooklyn Chamber of Commerce.

FORD COUNTY – One person was injured in a 3-vehicle accident just after 4p.m. on Tuesday in Ford County.

As the pickup approached the intersection at Lariat Way, a 2001 Cadillac DeVille driven by Jose G. Soto-Gonzalez, 30, Dodge City, attempted to cross U.S. 56 from Lariat Way.

We live in a society where people are quite judgmental about how a woman dresses or behaves. Sadly, in our country, a smoking and tattooed women are still considered promiscuous.
Kriti Sanon is all set to question this stigma with her role of Bitti in her upcoming film Bareilly Ki Barfi. Talking about it, the actress was quoted as saying, "Smoking is not good for health and should be avoided. I am a non-smoker, but the point we want to make is that girls who smoke, who are fond of body art or break into a jig are not characterless."
She further added, "Our society has a very small bracket for 'good girls'. That bracket needs to broaden up or change. When a guy is moophat or smokes, he is not considered characterless, but you judge girls too fast. This is seen more in smaller towns. In an arranged marriage too, only a girl is asked all kinds of questions. I really want this to change."
On the other hand, Kriti's alleged relationship with Sushant Singh Rajput has been grabbing headlines time and again. Recently while talking to a leading daily, here's what she had to say-
"Gone are the days when enjoying a movie or dinner with a co-star would be called a date. There is nothing wrong in being friends with your co-actors and if that involves dinners or movies, why not? It's sad if I stop socialising with a friend, just because people are cooking up stories. I am not answerable to any one. I would still hang out with my male friends and people can assume anything they like. As for Sushant, I don't have control over what people talk about us. I have already spoken enough about it."
Directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwary, Bareilly Ki Barfi also stars Ayushmann Khurrana and Rajkummar Rao and is slated to release this week.

Regrettably, within a national context, women who smoke or possess tattoos are often erroneously conflated with promiscuity. Addressing this issue, Sanon has stated, "While smoking is detrimental to health and should be avoided—I am a non-smoker myself—the essential point is that women who smoke, appreciate body art, or dance spontaneously are not devoid of character."

She elaborated further, noting, "Our society maintains an exceedingly narrow definition of the 'good girl.' This paradigm requires expansion and revision. When a man is outspoken or smokes, his character is seldom impugned, yet women are judged with undue haste. This phenomenon is more acutely observed in smaller towns. Even within the context of arranged marriage, women are subjected to disproportionate scrutiny through intrusive questioning. I am deeply committed to seeing this change."

Separately, speculation regarding Sanon's personal relationship with fellow actor Sushant Singh Rajput has recurrently attracted media attention. Commenting on this scrutiny to a prominent publication, she remarked, "The era when sharing a meal or film with a colleague constituted a 'date' has passed. There is no impropriety in fostering friendships with co-actors, and if such friendships involve social activities, that is entirely acceptable. It is regrettable to consider curtailing a friendship merely due to fabricated narratives. I am not accountable to public conjecture and will continue to associate with my male friends irrespective of assumptions. Concerning Sushant, I cannot govern public discourse about us, and I have already provided sufficient commentary on the matter."

Directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwary and featuring Ayushmann Khurrana and Rajkummar Rao, *Bareilly Ki Barfi* is scheduled for release imminently.

Yemenis check the damage in the aftermath of a reported air strike by the Saudi-led coalition in the Yemeni capital Sana'a on March 8, 2018. AFP
The US Senate has teed up a vote on ending the US military involvement in the Saudi war on Yemen.
Spearheaded by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee and Chris Murphy, the resolution would not include the US alleged targeting of al-Qaeda elements in the impoverished country, Press TV reported.
Once the Senate reconvenes on Tuesday, the lawmakers could have up to four hours of debate; therefore, a vote is expected at approximately 4:15 pm.
If passed, the measure would require all US forces to leave the war-ravaged country within 30 days.
"You know it's a new precedent. ... I think a lot of members on our side are trying to figure out what a yes vote means and what a no vote means," Texas Republican Senator John Cornyn told The Hill.
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle have already voiced opposition for the US support for Riyadh, implicated in war crimes in the neighboring country, but it is still unclear whether the effort could garner enough votes.
rewrite: On March 8, 2018, residents of Sana'a, Yemen, surveyed damage following a reported aerial bombardment by the Saudi-led coalition. This context underscores ongoing legislative action in the United States Senate, which has scheduled a vote to terminate U.S. military involvement in the Saudi-led campaign in Yemen. As reported by Press TV, a resolution introduced by Senators Bernie Sanders, Mike Lee, and Chris Murphy seeks to end support for the coalition but would exempt U.S. operations against alleged al-Qaeda elements within the country. Upon reconvening, the Senate will allocate up to four hours for debate, with a vote anticipated around 4:15 PM. Passage would mandate the withdrawal of all U.S. forces from the conflict zone within thirty days. Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) noted the measure sets a "new precedent," creating uncertainty among members regarding the implications of their vote. While bipartisan criticism exists over U.S. support for Saudi Arabia, given allegations of war crimes in Yemen, the resolution's prospects for securing sufficient support remain uncertain.

Former Dortmund coach and eye witness Thomas Tuchel arrives at the trial against Sergej W., no family name given due to German privacy laws, who is charged with detonating three bombs targeting the Borussia Dortmund soccer team bus last April, at the German state court in Dortmund, Germany, Monday March 19, 2018.the trial (Bernd Thissen/dpa via AP)
BERLIN (AP) - Borussia Dortmund's ex-coach Thomas Tuchel has testified at the trial of a man accused of bombing the German soccer club's bus that the attack was partly responsible for his departure.
Defender Marc Bartra and a police officer were hurt in the April 11 attack as the bus left a Dortmund hotel for a Champions League match against Monaco. Dortmund played, and lost, the game a day later.
The dpa news agency reported Tuchel suggested Monday at suspect Sergei W.'s trial that the attack led to a disagreement with chief executive Hans-Joachim Watzke over rescheduling the game, probably because "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn't."
Tuchel says it was a mistake to schedule the match a day later.
Tuchel was fired in May after an inconsistent season.
rewrite:
On Monday, March 19, 2018, former Borussia Dortmund coach Thomas Tuchel arrived to provide testimony as an eyewitness at the German state court in Dortmund. The proceedings are against an individual identified only as Sergej W., in accordance with German privacy statutes, who stands accused of detonating three explosive devices targeting the Borussia Dortmund team bus in April of the previous year. In his subsequent testimony, Tuchel stated that the attack contributed to his eventual departure from the club. The bombing occurred on April 11, 2017, as the bus departed a hotel en route to a UEFA Champions League match against AS Monaco, resulting in injuries to defender Marc Bartra and a police officer. The match was rescheduled and played, with Dortmund losing, one day later.

As reported by the dpa news agency, Tuchel suggested during the trial that the attack precipitated a disagreement with club chief executive Hans-Joachim Watzke concerning the decision to proceed with the match on the following day. Tuchel implied the divergence in perspective stemmed from their distinct experiences, noting, "I was sitting in the bus and he wasn't." He further characterized the rescheduling as an error. Tuchel was dismissed from his position in May 2018 following a season of inconsistent sporting results. His testimony underscores the profound and lasting institutional repercussions of the violent incident, extending beyond the immediate physical harm.

A COMMUNITY day has been arranged to spread awareness of a disability benefit campaign.
The free event, which will be held at Set The Bar next to Wrexham Bus Station, will take place from 1pm to 11pm tomorrow in aid of the Save The Welsh Independent Living Campaign (SWILG).
There will be a number of performances throughout the day including Wrexham One World Community Choir, Luke Gallagher, Jamie Hamilton and more.
Disability campaigner Nathan Lee Davies is encouraging residents to turn out and support the event, which is expected to draw visitors from all over North Wales.
He said: “SWILG is an absolutely vital movement and a campaign that must be won.
“I implore people to come along to our completely free community day and I would encourage everyone to get involved with us on this SWILG campaign.
“We currently have a fantastic exhibition on in Theatre Clwyd, Mold, which we are proud to have put together.
“People such as the film-maker Ken Loach, to performers like Attila The Stockbroker, to some English and Welsh MPs and AMs, to Welsh Labour Grassroots/
Momentum to the local Labour parties in Clwyd South and Wrexham have given their full, official support.
“I cannot tell you how much that means to me and thousands like me.
“As I say, this is a campaign we simply cannot afford to lose.”
The Welsh Government became responsible for supporting those who had been receiving Independent Living Fund payments after the UK government closed the scheme in June 2015.
According to the charity Disability Rights UK, Welsh Independent Living Grant funding will continue during 2017-2018, but local councils will meet with the people receiving them to discuss the replacement support they need – by March 31, 2019, all recipients will receive their support from local councils.
To find out more about the campaign, search for @SaveWILG on Facebook.
For more information about the community day, search for the event 'Save the Welsh Independent Living Grant (SWILG) Community Day' on Facebook.

Aussie Rules: The Gympie Cats' clash against Bundaberg's Across the Waves last weekend resulted in the Cats disputing the final score.
After singing the club song, thinking they had secured a hard fought victory, the Cats were told they had lost the game by two points.
Cats officials recorded Gympie 12.12 (84) and Across the Waves 12.8 (80).
The goal umpires recorded Across the Waves 12.8 (80) and Cats 11.12 (78).
Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay said the Cats were in the process of disputing the final score.
"We believe we kicked three goals in the final quarter but the goal umpires only recorded two,” he said.
"The papers have been lodged to AFL Queensland with proof backing up our belief. Hopefully we hear back this week.”
Gympie welcomed back Madry Tonkin who was sidelined due to a suspension from last year.
"Despite playing his first game of the season, Tonkin played well,” Findlay said.
"He was rotated through a few different positions and he handled it well.”
Cats' Jack Cross had another stand out performance, backing up from last week's game.
"He played up forward and was quiet creative,” Findlay said. "Jack won contested possessions in the midfield and when the game was to be won, he kicked a crucial goal.” Cross and Tonkin were not the only stand out Cats players; Jesse Lawrence had a great game in the midfield.
Cats head back to Bundaberg this Saturday to play Brothers Bulldogs at 3pm at Brothers AFL complex.
rewrite:
In a recent Australian Rules football fixture, the Gympie Cats contested the official outcome of their match against Bundaberg’s Across the Waves. Following the conclusion of the game, the Cats celebrated with their traditional club anthem under the belief they had achieved a narrow victory, only to subsequently be informed that the official scoreboard reflected a two-point defeat. A discrepancy exists between the scorekeeping records of the competing teams. Gympie officials documented a final score of 12.12 (84) for the Cats against 12.8 (80) for Across the Waves, whereas the appointed goal umpires recorded the result as 11.12 (78) to 12.8 (80) in favour of Across the Waves.

Cats coach and co-captain Courtney Findlay confirmed the club has initiated a formal dispute regarding the tally. “We maintain that three goals were scored during the final quarter, though only two were officially registered,” stated Findlay. “Documentation substantiating our position has been submitted to AFL Queensland, with a response anticipated this week.” The match also marked the return of player Madry Tonkin from a suspension carried over from the previous season. Findlay noted that despite Tonkin’s absence prior to this season opener, his performance was commendable as he adapted effectively to several positional rotations throughout the game.

Furthermore, player Jack Cross delivered another prominent performance, building upon his form from the preceding week. Operating in a forward capacity, Cross demonstrated considerable creativity, secured contested possessions in midfield, and converted a decisive goal at a critical juncture of the match. He was joined in strong form by teammate Jesse Lawrence, who excelled in midfield duties. The Gympie Cats are scheduled to return to Bundaberg this Saturday for a 3pm fixture against the Brothers Bulldogs at the Brothers AFL complex.

A racist manspreader assaulted a woman on the subway because she asked him to give her a bit more room to sit down, police said Saturday.
The 34-year-old victim was seated inside a northbound E train on Tuesday at around 5: 10 pm when the man sat down, partially on top of her, police said.
When she asked him to move for a moment so she could readjust herself, he shouted: “Just because you’re African American, you think you can go on your Kanye West rant, you black b***h,” according to cops, who have released an image of the suspect.
Later, as the woman was preparing to exit the train, she bumped his bag, prompting him to spit on the back of her head, said police.
The matter escalated even further when both passengers left at the 7th Avenue stop in Manhattan. When she grabbed the man’s backpack to confront him, he punched her in the shoulder and spit in her face again, and then fled back onto the train, police said.
Police describe the man as white-Hispanic, in his 30s, and approximately 5-foot-9 and 150 pounds.

All 26 Labour MPs in the North East have signed a joint letter calling on the Government to increase transport funding in the region.
Their plea follows similar requests for extra funding to improve the A19 in our area as part of this paper's Safe A19 campaign.
Our campaign logo.
Among the signatories are Sunderland MPs Julie Elliott, Sharon Hodgson and Bridget Phillipson, South Tyneside MPs Stephen Hepburn and Emma Lewell-Buck, Easington MP Grahame Morris and Hartlepool MP Mike Hill.
Along with their party colleagues, they are highlighting what they see as the inequality between what is spent on transport in the North and London "with London receiving more than double the amount the North receives per head of the population".
The letter, addressed to the Secretary of State for Transport, Chris Grayling, demands to know what his department intends to do to address "the lack of investment in the North East’s transport systems".
It also asks for urgent steps to be taken to increase funding levels to address "ongoing chronic and historic underfunding in transport infrastructure across the North East of England."
Ian Mearns, MP for Gateshead, said: “the recent Institute for Public Policy Research report, Future Transport Investment in the North, with figures taken from official government statistics, graphically highlights the huge disparity in spending plans on transport infrastructure between the North East of England and London.
“It is widely recognised that there is no doubt that our transport infrastructure in the North East is, at best, poor and in many cases dreadful.
"Therefore, this is an urgent and unified appeal for government action to rectify a long-term problem.”
More than 2,000 people have already signed our campaign for an inquiry into the number of accidents on the A19 with more than 70 people suffering injuries last year in a stretch of dual carriageway from Wolviston, near Hartlepool, to Boldon.
The joint Sunderland Echo, Hartlepool Mail and Shields Gazette petition can be signed at Change.org by searching for Safe A19: A call for an inquiry into safety on the dual carriageway through the North East.

Therefore, this is an urgent and unified appeal for government action to rectify a long-term problem."

Concurrently, public support for the *Safe A19* campaign continues to grow. Over two thousand individuals have endorsed a petition advocating for an official inquiry into the frequency of accidents on the A19. This follows data indicating that more than seventy persons sustained injuries last year along the dual carriageway segment between Wolviston, near Hartlepool, and Boldon. The joint petition, organized by the *Sunderland Echo*, *Hartlepool Mail*, and *Shields Gazette*, remains accessible for signature on Change.org under the search term "Safe A19: A call for an inquiry into safety on the dual carriageway through the North East."

SEATTLE (AP) – Landlords will not be allowed to screen tenants based on their criminal records under a measure passed by the Seattle City Council.
The ordinance unanimously approved Monday says landlords can’t screen a tenant based on arrests or convictions. Landlords also won’t be able to ask about or consider arrests that didn’t lead to a conviction. The law won’t apply to adult sex offenders.
Supporters say the rise in online criminal background checks have made it harder for formerly incarcerated people to find housing and get back on their feet.
Councilwoman Lisa Herbold, a bill co-sponsor, says landlords can still screen tenants based on other factors, such as employment, credit scores and income ratios.
The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposed the measure, calling it poor policy with unintended consequences. The group says a mandate offering no supportive services won’t encourage landlords to take chances on under-qualified applicants.
rewrite: The Seattle City Council has unanimously enacted an ordinance prohibiting residential landlords from utilizing criminal history as a screening criterion for prospective tenants. Effective Monday, the legislation bars consideration of both arrests and convictions, including instances where an arrest did not result in a conviction. The mandate exempts registered adult sex offenders. Proponents argue that the prevalence of digital background checks has created significant barriers to housing access for individuals with prior incarcerations, hindering their reintegration. Councilwoman Lisa Herbold, a co-sponsor, clarified that landlords retain the right to evaluate applicants using alternative metrics, including employment verification, credit history, and income-to-rent ratios. The Rental Housing Association of Washington opposed the measure, characterizing it as flawed policy that may yield adverse unintended consequences. The association contends that a regulatory mandate unaccompanied by supportive services fails to incentivize landlords to assume the perceived risks of leasing to applicants with potentially disqualifying backgrounds.

WOODMERE, N.Y. (CBSNewYork) — A Far Rockaway man is facing criminal charges, accused of posing as a police officer at a Long Island synagogue.
Congregants heading for prayer services inside the Young Israel of Woodmere Temple are still disgusted by one visitor’s attempt Saturday to portray himself as law enforcement.
“He tried being a cop, impersonating a police officer,” Macis Rand of Nassau County said.
Rand says some congregants inside the Temple knew the man who tried to portray himself as a police officer. Rand is particularly angry it happened on the Sabbath.
“When I heard the news, that’s pretty crazy doing it to a schul, I don’t know what he was hoping to gain from it,” Rand said.
Temple security staff says 28-year-old Mikhail Mikhaylov first parked in an unauthorized spot then walked in wearing an NYPD baseball cap with handcuffs, mace, and a gold badge.
The head of security told police “I heard him say he was a cop but did not see his ID.”
When asked for ID, Mikhaylov allegedly said “you mean my shield?”
Mikhaylov then reportedly told security his ID was in his car before going to the parking lot and racing away.
Security wrote down his license plate number and arrested him at his home the next day.
One neighbor says it’s part of a disturbing trend.
“It particularly happens in the law enforcement area because a lot of people ride around pretending to be cops because they want to be somebody they’re not,” neighbor Pete Wagner said.
Congregants say Mikhaylov said he had a gun and two knives in the car, but he’s facing no charges for that. His legal aid attorney says he simply went to the temple to pray.
Temple leaders did not comment on whether Mikhaylov is a congregation member.
He’s now facing criminal impersonation charges in the second degree and is being held on a $2,500 bond.
rewrite:
A resident of Far Rockaway is confronting criminal charges following an alleged incident of police impersonation at the Young Israel of Woodmere synagogue in Woodmere, New York. According to reports, congregants arriving for Sabbath services remain disturbed by the individual’s actions this past Saturday. The suspect, identified as 28-year-old Mikhail Mikhaylov, initially parked his vehicle in an unauthorized area before entering the temple premises. He was reportedly attired in an NYPD-branded baseball cap and was in possession of handcuffs, a chemical irritant, and a gold badge.

Temple security personnel state that Mikhaylov represented himself as a police officer. When subsequently asked for official identification, he allegedly responded, “you mean my shield?” before claiming the credentials were located within his automobile. He then proceeded to the parking lot and departed rapidly. Security officials recorded his license plate number, facilitating his arrest at his residence the following day. The director of security informed authorities that while he heard Mikhaylov declare he was an officer, he did not observe any form of identification.

Some members of the congregation indicated they recognized the individual. One congregant, Macis Rand, expressed particular dismay that the event transpired on the Sabbath, questioning the perpetrator’s motives for targeting a synagogue. The incident has elicited concern among local residents, with one neighbor describing such impersonations as part of a troubling pattern wherein individuals falsely assume law enforcement identities.

Although congregants reported claims that Mikhaylov possessed a firearm and two knives within his vehicle, no related charges have been filed. His legal representation has stated his purpose for visiting the temple was solely for prayer. Temple leadership has declined to comment on whether Mikhaylov is a member of the congregation. He currently faces a charge of criminal impersonation in the second degree and is being detained on a $2,500 bond.

THE CANADIAN PRESS
HALIFAX -- Professors and support staff at the Nova Scotia Community College have agreed to new six-year collective agreements.
The Nova Scotia Teachers Union, which represents the two bargaining units, says a vote on management's final offer was held Tuesday.
Faculty members voted 55 per cent in favour of the offer, while 64 per cent of voters with the professional support bargaining unit were in favour.
The union says the agreements, which run from Sept. 1, 2014 to Aug. 31, 2020, were ratified following the vote and include a seven-per-cent wage increase over the six-year terms.
Under legislation, the employer is required to freeze the years of service used to calculate an employee's retirement service award as of March 31, 2015.
However, the union says under both agreements employees can either choose to collect their service award based on their salary at retirement, or collect it immediately based on their salary as of March 31, 2018.
rewrite: The Nova Scotia Community College has ratified new six-year collective agreements for its faculty and professional support staff. Represented by the Nova Scotia Teachers Union, both bargaining units conducted a vote on the employer’s final offer this Tuesday. The agreement received approval from 55 percent of faculty voters and 64 percent of the professional support unit. These contracts, effective from September 1, 2014, to August 31, 2020, incorporate a seven percent wage increase across the term. Legislative requirements mandate a freeze on the years of service used to calculate retirement service awards as of March 31, 2015. However, the ratified agreements provide employees an option: to receive the service award based on salary at retirement or to collect it immediately, calculated from their salary as of March 31, 2018.

The Children’s Museum of the Brazos Valley, in conjunction with the City of Bryan Animal Center and the Veterinary Technology program at Blinn College, opened a new exhibit this weekend.

Residential developers get floor-area bonuses for including “affordable” apartments and for providing certain public amenities such as plazas — so why not also for arts and cultural facilities?
That’s a proposal by Charles S. Cohen, who just reopened the modernized Quad Cinema on West 13th Street to widespread cheers. As a major landlord who’s also an active film producer and distributor, he’s interested in bringing art-house movie venues, live theater and dance and related activities to neighborhoods lacking them.
Noting that arts institutions are “hard-pressed to find space” due to the same cost pressures that have driven out many small stores and restaurants, Cohen proposes zoning changes to allow residential developers to build more apartments — in exchange for making arts space available for free in the same building.
He said the situation is so dire that, “Lots of art cinemas around the country are resorting to a nonprofit form of operating, having to rely on personal donations from those who want to support them.”
So, he suggests, “Why not have the Department of City Planning incentivize creation of cultural amenities in areas where there’s demand for them?” He said that while the Planning Department would set the basic zoning framework, the Department of Cultural Affairs could be involved in vetting specific arts uses at a given location.
rewrite:
Charles S. Cohen proposes that residential developers receive floor-area ratio bonuses for incorporating dedicated arts and cultural facilities, analogous to existing incentives for providing affordable housing units or public amenities like plazas. Cohen, a significant property owner and an active film producer and distributor, recently reopened the renovated Quad Cinema on West 13th Street. He advocates for integrating art-house cinemas, live theater, dance spaces, and related cultural programming into neighborhoods currently lacking such venues.

He observes that arts institutions face severe spatial constraints, displaced by the same escalating real estate costs that have forced out numerous small retail and restaurant businesses. In response, Cohen recommends zoning modifications permitting residential developers increased density in exchange for allocating perpetually rent-free space for cultural purposes within the same development.

Cohen characterizes the predicament as dire, noting that many art cinemas nationwide are compelled to adopt nonprofit operational models dependent on private donations for survival. Consequently, he poses the question: “Why not have the Department of City Planning incentivize creation of cultural amenities in areas where there’s demand for them?” Under his proposal, while the Planning Department would establish the overarching zoning framework, the Department of Cultural Affairs could participate in evaluating the suitability of specific cultural uses for designated locations.

SYDNEY (AP) — A period of personal reflection in a South African jungle has convinced Australian tennis player Bernard Tomic that he's ready to return to the court.
Tomic quit the reality television show "I'm A Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here!" after only three days, saying that was long enough to reflect and realize "how I played last year and where I should be."
He said his short time in the jungle was his first break from his "fast-paced" lifestyle and gave was "a wake-up call."
"After being there for a couple days, it made me depressed and it made me a bit sad and I didn't want to continue doing that to myself," Tomic told News Corp Australia. "I need to get back on the court.
"I just started recently to get back and feeling good. I won a couple of matches at the Australian Open in the (qualifiers). I just regret leaving that last month-and-a-half behind. It wasn't the right thing for me to do."
But Tomic's comeback may depend on his ability to repair his relationship with Tennis Australia and national Davis Cup captain Lleyton Hewitt.
Hewitt has indicated Tomic's Davis Cup career may be at an end after he rebuffed several attempts to draw him back into the fold and said in an interview that Australia couldn't win the Davis Cup without him. Asked if Tomic would play for Austalia again, Hewitt said "it's highly doubtful."
"He's made some mistakes. It will be a long way back," Hewitt said. "He's digging a big hole for himself that he may never get out of."
rewrite:
Australian tennis professional Bernard Tomic has concluded that a period of introspection undertaken in a South African wilderness environment has prepared him for a return to competitive tennis. Tomic departed the reality television program *I’m A Celebrity…Get Me Out of Here!* after a mere three-day participation, asserting that this duration was sufficient for contemplation regarding his recent professional performance and future trajectory. He characterized the brief jungle experience as his initial respite from a “fast-paced” lifestyle, describing it as a significant “wake-up call.”

In statements to News Corp Australia, Tomic elaborated, “After being there for a couple of days, it induced feelings of depression and sadness, and I chose not to persist under those conditions. I need to return to the court.” He reported a recent resumption of training with positive effect, citing several victories during the Australian Open qualifying matches. Tomic expressed regret over his actions in the preceding month and a half, acknowledging, “It wasn’t the right thing for me to do.”

However, the viability of Tomic’s comeback appears contingent upon reconciling his strained relations with Tennis Australia and national Davis Cup captain Lleyton Hewitt. Hewitt has suggested Tomic’s Davis Cup career is likely concluded, following the player’s rejection of multiple overtures for reintegration and Tomic’s public assertion that Australia could not win the Davis Cup without him. When queried about the potential for Tomic’s future selection, Hewitt responded that it was “highly doubtful,” noting, “He’s made some mistakes. It will be a long way back. He’s digging a big hole for himself that he may never get out of.”

PHILADELPHIA (AP) - The fourth nor'easter in three weeks is set to smack the East Coast on the first day of spring.
The bulk of the dangerous, wind-driven snow and sleet is expected to wallop New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware and parts of eastern Pennsylvania before heading off to Nantucket early Thursday, the National Weather Service said.
Sleet and freezing rain are expected Tuesday afternoon, the first day of spring. On Wednesday, about 6 to 9 inches of snow is expected, with some areas getting nearly a foot.
The jet stream, the upper level river of air that guides weather, is stuck in a plunging pattern that brings plenty of moisture from the south up the East Coast, said Brian Hurley, senior forecaster at the National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center.
Four nor'easters in three weeks is highly unusual, but it happens when a pattern locks in. And that's happened, Hurley said.
Officials are cautioning against unnecessary travel Wednesday afternoon and evening, when snow could be falling as much as 3 inches an hour.
Widespread power outages are possible, especially Wednesday, with gusts of up to 35 mph at times.
"Upper level patterns like this tend to repeat and you tend to get these serial storms, one after the other," weather.us meteorologist Ryan Maue said, adding that Europe will get the same drumbeat of storms a few days later.
But "the calendar is catching up to spring," Maue said. "Thankfully, you're going to see some spring pretty soon."
___
AP Science Writer Seth Borenstein contributed to this report from Washington.

rewrite:
A fourth nor’easter within a three-week period is forecast to impact the Eastern United States coinciding with the vernal equinox, the first day of spring. According to the National Weather Service, the most severe conditions, characterized by wind-driven snow and sleet, are anticipated to affect New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and portions of eastern Pennsylvania before tracking toward Nantucket by early Thursday. Meteorological projections indicate an initial phase of sleet and freezing rain on Tuesday afternoon, followed by snowfall accumulations of approximately six to nine inches on Wednesday, with localized areas potentially receiving up to twelve inches.

Brian Hurley, a senior forecaster at the National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center, attributes this persistent storm activity to a blocked upper-level pattern in the jet stream. This configuration facilitates the advection of significant moisture northward along the Atlantic seaboard. The occurrence of four such cyclonic systems in rapid succession is climatologically anomalous, yet consistent with such an entrenched atmospheric regime. Officials have issued advisories against non-essential travel for Wednesday afternoon and evening, when snowfall rates may approach three inches per hour. The combination of heavy, wet snow and wind gusts potentially reaching 35 miles per hour raises concerns for widespread power outages, particularly throughout Wednesday.

Meteorologist Ryan Maue of weather.us noted that such persistent upper-level patterns often generate serial storm events, a sequence also expected to affect Europe several days later. However, Maue observed that seasonal progression remains inevitable, stating that spring conditions are anticipated to prevail in the near term. This report includes contributions from AP Science Writer Seth Borenstein in Washington.

Sri Lanka's captain Dinesh Chandimal, left, and Angelo Mathews run between the wickets during the third day's play of their third cricket test match against India in Pallekele, Sri Lanka, Monday, Aug. 14, 2017. (AP Photo/Eranga Jayawardena)
PALLEKELE, Sri Lanka (AP) — Sri Lanka was heading for a heavy defeat in the third test against India as it slumped to 82 for four in its second innings at lunch on Monday.
India skipper Virat Kohli enforced the follow-on as he chased a series sweep after his lineup made 487 in its first innings and bowled out Sri Lanka for 135 inside 38 overs.
Sri Lanka needed to make a further 270 runs to avoid innings defeat.
Resuming day three at the overnight total of 19 for one, Sri Lanka lost opener Dimuth Karunaratne (16) when he was undone by Ravichandran Ashwin's extra bounce and ended up gloving a catch to Ajinkaya Rahane at slip.
Mohammed Shami then took two wickets from two overs to reduce Sri Lanka to 39-4. Night watchman Malinda Pushpakumara (1) was caught behind by wicketkeeper Wriddhiman Saha and Kusal Mendis shuffled across the stumps and was adjudged leg before wicket for 12.
Skipper Dinesh Chandimal and former captain Angelo Mathews added an unbeaten 43 runs for the fifth wicket to ensure there were no further breakthroughs before lunch.
India is 2-0 up in the series after winning the first test in Galle by 304 runs and the second test in Colombo by an innings and 53 runs.
rewrite:

By the lunch interval on Monday, August 14, 2017, their second innings had deteriorated to 82 for four, requiring a further 270 runs merely to avoid an innings defeat. India, having declared its first innings at 487, had bowled Sri Lanka out for 135 in under 38 overs, prompting captain Virat Kohli to enforce the follow-on in pursuit of a series sweep.

Commencing the day at an overnight score of 19 for one, Sri Lanka’s innings quickly faltered. Opener Dimuth Karunaratne (16) was dismissed by Ravichandran Ashwin, gloving a catch to slip off extra bounce. Subsequently, Mohammed Shami claimed two wickets in two overs: nightwatchman Malinda Pushpakumara (1) was caught behind, and Kusal Mendis (12) was adjudged leg before wicket after shuffling across his stumps, reducing the hosts to 39 for four. A partnership of 43 runs for the fifth wicket between captain Dinesh Chandimal and former captain Angelo Mathews provided some stability, preventing further loss before lunch.

India entered this match with a commanding 2-0 series lead, having secured victory in Galle by 304 runs and in Colombo by an innings and 53 runs. The collaborative effort between Chandimal and Mathews, while offering temporary resistance, did little to alter the match’s overwhelming trajectory in India’s favor.

The notorious “Son of Sam” killer, David Berkowitz, will undergo an emergency heart surgery at an Albany hospital, sources said Monday.
Berkowitz, 64, terrorized New York City in a shooting spree that murdered six people from 1976 to 1977 and claimed a possessed dog gave him orders to kill.
He wounded seven with his .44 caliber Bulldog revolver.
Many of his victims, including a couple and friends, were sitting in cars.
“Inmate Berkowitz has been transferred to an outside hospital and remains in the custody of the Shawangunk Correctional Facility,” the New York State Department of Corrections said in a statement.
Sources didn’t immediately comment on his recovery Monday.
One of America’s most notorious urban killers, Berkowitz was arrested on August 10, 1977, 11 days after his last murder.
For months he eluded police in one of the biggest manhunts in the city’s history, mocking cops in letters given to the media.
“I’ll be Back. I’ll be Back,” Berkowitz wrote after one shooting and signed off with the message, “Yours in Murder Mr. Monster.”
While in prison, Berkowitz became an evangelical Christian.
He now refers to himself as the “Son of Hope” instead of the infamous Son of Sam.
Berkowitz is incarcerated at the Shawagunk Correctional Facility in Wakllkill in Ulster County, near Albany Medical Center.
His prison journals are featured on his website run by supporters because he is barred access to the internet. He has apologized to his victims and their families.
In prison, Berkowitz writes journal essays on faith and repentance and contributes to school-based projects for students in psychology, criminology and sociology who want to learn more about the criminal mind and the criminal justice system.
His neighbor, retiree Sam Carr, had a black Labrador retriever named Harvey, which Berkowitz claimed had pleaded with him to kill. He also believed Sam Carr was a powerful demon and was referring to him when he later called himself Son of Sam.

Tourism leaders have hailed this year's Blackpool Air Show as one of the busiest ever.
Early figures show more than 100,000 people reportedly turned out to watch the two-day aviation extravaganza in the skies over the Promenade.
Crowds pack onto the Promenade for Blackpool Air Show 2017
But spectators have claimed the packed Promenade was filled with even more people that ever before.
Exact figures will not be gathered by tourism body Visit Blackpool until later in the year.
Visitors and local residents enjoyed an action-packed programme of displays, featuring the RAF Typhoon, Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, the Breitling Wingwalkers and the world-famous Red Arrows headlining both days' events.
This year was the first time air show favourites the Red Arrows performed on both days of the event, with viewers giving the show a rapturous reception.
Blackpool Council deputy leader Coun Gillian Campbell said: "Moving the Air Show from its usual Sunday and Monday to Saturday and Sunday meant that even more people got the opportunity to see this fantastic free entertainment.
"It was by far and away the busiest weekend we have witnessed in Blackpool this summer.
"We have to give enormous credit to all the pilots who showed off their incredible skills and talent, giving the tens of thousands of people attending the event an opportunity to witness some thrilling aerobatics.
"I’m very proud of everyone who took part to make the 108th annual air show a very special occasion."
In addition to the spectacular in the skies, there were stalls and displays on the ground, including the Red Arrows ground team, Help for Heroes and the Royal British Legion among many more.
Blackpool Air Show took flight in 1909 - and was the first official air show ever staged in the UK.
The 2018 show has been scheduled for Saturday and Sunday, August 11 and 12.
rewrite:
The 2017 Blackpool Air Show has been characterized by tourism officials as one of the most heavily attended iterations of the event on record. Preliminary estimates indicate that in excess of 100,000 spectators gathered over the two-day period to observe the aviation displays conducted above the Promenade. Anecdotal reports from attendees suggest the Promenade was exceptionally congested, with many asserting the crowds surpassed those of previous years. Official attendance statistics will be compiled and released by the destination marketing organization Visit Blackpool later this year.

The event featured an extensive programme of aerial demonstrations. The Royal Air Force Typhoon, the Battle of Britain Memorial Flight, and the Breitling Wingwalkers all performed, while the world-renowned Red Arrows aerobatics team headlined on both days. This year marked the first occasion the Red Arrows have performed across the full duration of the two-day show, a scheduling decision that was met with enthusiastic approval from the audience.

Commenting on the event, Blackpool Council Deputy Leader, Councillor Gillian Campbell, stated: "Rescheduling the Air Show from its traditional Sunday and Monday to a Saturday and Sunday format enabled a broader audience to access this complimentary public spectacle. It constituted the most populous weekend witnessed in Blackpool this summer. Considerable recognition is due to all participating pilots, whose demonstration of exceptional skill provided tens of thousands of attendees with a thrilling aerobatic experience. I extend my pride to all involved in orchestrating the 108th annual show, ensuring it was a particularly memorable occasion."

Complementing the aerial activities, a range of ground-based exhibits and stalls were present, including representations from the Red Arrows ground team, Help for Heroes, and the Royal British Legion. Historically significant as the United Kingdom's first officially staged air show, originating in 1909, the Blackpool Air Show is scheduled to next occur on Saturday 11th and Sunday 12th August 2018.

Activists burned U.S. and Israeli flags in front of the American embassy in Jakarta on Monday in a fourth day of protests in Indonesia against President Donald Trump's recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
Several hundred protesters from an Islamic youth group rallied outside the embassy, burning flags and images of Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu.
Wearing white robes, the protesters unfurled banners reading "U.S. Embassy, Get Out from Al-Quds" and "We are with the Palestinians." Al-Quds is the Arabic name for Jerusalem, the historic Middle East city that is a holy site for Jews, Christians and Muslims.
A weekend protest at the embassy attracted several thousand people and similar protests have been held in other cities around Indonesia, the world's most populous Muslim nation.
Indonesian President Joko "Jokowi" Widodo has strongly condemned Trump's move, which he described as a violation of U.N. resolutions.
Indonesia does not have diplomatic ties with Israel and has long been a strong supporter of Palestinian aspirations for statehood.
Trump's announcement Wednesday overturned decades of U.S. policy, and a longstanding international consensus, that the fate of Jerusalem be decided as a part of a peace deal between Israel and Palestine.
Israeli and Palestinian claims to the city's eastern sector form the core of their conflict, and Trump's announcement was seen as siding with the Israelis.
rewrite:
On Monday, a demonstration occurred outside the United States embassy in Jakarta, marking a fourth consecutive day of protests across Indonesia in response to President Donald Trump's formal recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital. Several hundred members of an Islamic youth organization gathered at the embassy site, where they set fire to American and Israeli flags alongside effigies of President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The protesters, attired in white robes, displayed banners bearing the messages "U.S. Embassy, Get Out from Al-Quds" and "We are with the Palestinians." Al-Quds is the Arabic term for Jerusalem, a city of profound historical and religious significance to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

This event followed a larger weekend protest at the embassy involving thousands of participants, with analogous rallies occurring in other Indonesian cities. As the world's most populous Muslim-majority nation, Indonesia has witnessed significant public opposition to the U.S. policy shift. President Joko "Jokowi" Widodo has issued a strong condemnation of Trump's decision, characterizing it as a contravention of United Nations resolutions. Indonesia maintains no formal diplomatic relations with Israel and has consistently supported Palestinian aspirations for sovereign statehood.

President Trump's announcement last Wednesday represents a substantive reversal of longstanding U.S. foreign policy and an established international consensus, which had historically deferred the status of Jerusalem to final-status negotiations between Israel and Palestine. The conflicting Israeli and Palestinian claims to East Jerusalem constitute a central issue in the dispute, and Trump's declaration has been widely interpreted as aligning the United States with the Israeli position.

MOSCOW (The Borowitz Report)—Russian President Vladimir Putin is “starting to get concerned” that the puppets he installed in the executive branch of the U.S. government “might not be up to the task at hand,” sources confirmed on Tuesday.
According to the sources, the flame-out of the national-security adviser Michael Flynn was only the most recent event that has caused Putin to wonder if the figureheads he propelled into office are “just too dim-witted” to serve the goals of the Russian Federation.
“When you choose a puppet, you’re looking for a sweet spot,” one source close to Putin said. “You want to choose someone who’s dumb enough to be manipulated, but not so dumb that he can’t find the light switches.”
“Increasingly, it looks like we missed that sweet spot,” the source said.
Putin is reportedly willing to have a “wait and see” attitude with his current puppets, but, if things do not improve markedly, he will not hesitate to “make some changes,” the source said.
“President Putin knew that this bunch didn’t have a lot of experience in government and that there were bound to be some growing pains,” the source said. “But geez.”
rewrite:
MOSCOW (The Borowitz Report)—Sources indicated on Tuesday that Russian President Vladimir Putin is growing apprehensive that the individuals he facilitated into prominent positions within the U.S. executive branch may prove inadequate for their intended objectives. These sources suggest that the resignation of National Security Adviser Michael Flynn represents merely the latest incident prompting Putin to question whether the figures he helped elevate are sufficiently competent to advance the strategic interests of the Russian Federation.

A source close to Putin explained the inherent difficulty of such selections, noting the necessity of identifying individuals who are pliable enough to be directed, yet not so inept as to be incapable of executing basic functions. This source conceded that, increasingly, this balance appears not to have been achieved. While Putin is reportedly adopting a "wait and see" approach regarding the current appointees, the source stated he will not hesitate to instigate personnel changes should performance fail to improve significantly. The source acknowledged that Putin anticipated a period of adjustment given the cohort's limited governmental experience, but expressed pronounced disappointment with the extent of the difficulties encountered thus far.

A woman counts Chinese Yuan banknotes as she sells tickets for a job fair in Beijing, China, February 11, 2017. REUTERS/Jason Lee
SHANGHAI China should look to strengthen the role of the yuan as an international reserve currency to help maintain financial stability and deter capital outflows, a senior central bank official said in a commentary on Thursday.
The country should "strengthen the renminbi's reserve currency status" and its "free usability" amid pressures of currency depreciation, Zhu Jun, director of the international division of the People's Bank of China (PBOC), said in a Shanghai Securities News commentary.
This would strengthen international trust in the currency, raise tolerance for fluctuations in its exchange rate and "lower the possibility of capital outflows caused by confidence issues," the official said.
The official's comments come after U.S. President Donald Trump said his administration would not label China a currency manipulator, backing away from a campaign promise, even though he said the U.S. dollar was "getting too strong".
The yuan CNY=CFXS fell 6.6 percent against the dollar in 2016, its biggest annual drop since 1994, as it was pressured by worries about slowing Chinese growth and a strong dollar, which has spurred capital outflows from many emerging markets.
"International reserve currency status can greatly increase confidence domestically and internationally in the currency, reducing chances of economic and financial crises," Zhu said.
He added it also reduced the need to accumulate large foreign exchange reserves.
The yuan joined the International Monetary Fund's basket of reserve currencies in October last year, a milestone for China to be recognized as a global economic power.
(Reporting by Adam Jourdan; Editing by Amrutha Gayathri)
rewrite:
A vendor counts renminbi banknotes while distributing tickets for a recruitment fair in Beijing, China, on February 11, 2017. REUTERS/Jason Lee
SHANGHAI — A senior official from China’s central bank advocated on Thursday for reinforcing the international role of the renminbi as a reserve currency, arguing that such a move would support financial stability and mitigate pressures from capital flight. In a commentary published by the Shanghai Securities News, Zhu Jun, director of the International Department of the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), stated that China should “strengthen the renminbi’s reserve currency status” and enhance its “free usability,” particularly amid depreciation pressures. According to Zhu, elevating the currency’s reserve role would bolster international confidence, increase tolerance for exchange-rate volatility, and “lower the possibility of capital outflows caused by confidence issues.”

These remarks follow recent statements by U.S. President Donald Trump, who indicated that his administration would not designate China a currency manipulator—a departure from earlier campaign pledges—despite noting that the U.S. dollar had become “too strong.” In 2016, the renminbi depreciated by 6.6 percent against the dollar, its largest annual decline since 1994, driven by concerns over China’s economic slowdown and a strengthening U.S. dollar, which has prompted capital outflows from numerous emerging economies.

Zhu further contended that reserve currency status significantly enhances both domestic and international confidence in a currency, thereby reducing vulnerability to economic and financial crises. He added that this status diminishes the necessity for accumulating substantial foreign exchange reserves. The renminbi’s inclusion in the International Monetary Fund’s Special Drawing Rights basket in October 2016 marked a milestone in China’s recognition as a global economic power.

(Reporting by Adam Jourdan; Editing by Amrutha Gayathri)

Posing for a selfie, at first glance of this image you would think it is pop princess Taylor Swift.
But in fact, the girl in the picture is a lookalike that is an absolute dead ringer for the singer – even her most hardened fans have been fooled.
April Gloria, from Kansas is a cosplayer and often posts sultry selfies for her 70,000 Instagram followers.
But with her blonde bob hair style with swept over fringe, blue eyes and a love of wearing red lipstick, she looks exactly like “Shake It Off” hitmaker.
And even her poses are exactly the same as the singer’s and she often posts selfies with her pet cats – similar to Taylor.
On one of her pictures, one of her followers wrote: “Omg she looks just like Taylor swift!”
While another said: “Could she look anymore like Taylor swift?”
And one added: ‘Ummm this girl looks more like Taylor than Taylor.”
Taylor is thought to be taking a break from the limelight at the moment after telling fans at a concert in Texas last week they were attending her one and only gig of 2017.
It is unclear what the Blank Space star will think of her doppelganger April.

At first glance, the subject of this photograph, captured in a selfie pose, bears a striking resemblance to pop music icon Taylor Swift. KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- A busy intersection in the Northland was shut down for hours on Thursday following a serious crash.
“What happened today is that there was this gentleman coming east on 152 (Highway), and I don’t know the circumstances but he hit one of the vehicles on the back and that gentleman has been transported to an area hospital,” Louis Ortiz with KCMO Police said.
Officers said a black pickup suffered the most damage. Firefighters on scene had to use the jaws of life to pry the door open in order to get to the male driver and get him to a local hospital.
The other vehicle involved in the crash was a Brinks truck. The company provides secure logistics and cash management services across the United States, so at any given time these trucks could be carrying hundreds of thousands of dollars.
“Those are pretty solid vehicles so there’s not much damage; however, there is enough damage that it opened up some of those compartments,” Ortiz said.
That sent a lot of money flying in all directions, covering the road.
“There’s $26,000 -- or over $26,000 worth of change,” Lee Mulinex said, who works with Impact Tow and came to the site to help clean up the change and get the highway back open.
“Everything -- pennies, nickels, dimes quarters and the gold dollars was scattered all over the highway, just stacks of it,” Mulinex said.
But when the cleanup effort ended, Mulinex and the other volunteers got a nice surprise.
“We picked up probably about 85, maybe 90 percent, of the money that was scattered on the highway, and they took the money with them,” Mulinex said.
But they'll never find all those coins.
“But they said that they had all that they wanted to recover, so whatever you find stick in your pocket they said,” he explained.
The eastbound lanes of Highway 152 opened back up around 3 p.m. after being closed since before noon Thursday.
Police say the driver of the Brinks truck sustained minimal injuries in the crash. The driver of the pickup truck is in critical condition at an area hospital.
rewrite:
A serious vehicular collision necessitated the prolonged closure of a heavily trafficked intersection in Kansas City, Missouri’s Northland region on Thursday. According to Officer Louis Ortiz of the Kansas City Missouri Police Department, the incident involved a male motorist traveling eastbound on Highway 152. “The circumstances remain under investigation, but the individual struck the rear of another vehicle and has been transported to a local hospital,” Ortiz stated. Authorities reported that a black pickup truck sustained the most severe damage, requiring emergency personnel to employ hydraulic rescue tools, commonly known as the “jaws of life,” to extricate the male driver. He was subsequently transported to a hospital and is listed in critical condition.

The second vehicle involved was a Brinks armored truck. Brinks provides secure logistics and cash management services nationally, meaning its vehicles frequently transport substantial sums of currency. Officer Ortiz noted the structural resilience of such vehicles, stating, “Those are pretty solid vehicles so there’s not much damage; however, there is enough damage that it opened up some of those compartments.” The breach resulted in a significant dispersal of currency across the roadway.

Lee Mulinex of Impact Tow, who assisted in the cleanup, reported that the scattered funds consisted entirely of coinage. “There’s $26,000—or over $26,000 worth of change… Everything—pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters and the gold dollars—was scattered all over the highway, just stacks of it,” Mulinex described. The cleanup crew, comprising Mulinex and other volunteers, successfully recovered a majority of the dispersed coins. “We picked up probably about 85, maybe 90 percent, of the money that was scattered on the highway, and they took the money with them,” he said. Notably, the Brinks representatives informed the volunteers that they had recovered all the currency they intended to, implying that any remaining coins could be retained by finders. “They said that they had all that they wanted to recover, so whatever you find stick in your pocket they said,” Mulinex explained.

The eastbound lanes of Highway 152, which had been closed since prior to noon, were reopened approximately at 3:00 p.m. The driver of the Brinks truck sustained only minor injuries in the collision. The incident remains under investigation by local authorities.

Joseph N. DiStefano writes about Philadelphia-area enterprise, and the people and money that make it go.
The Reinvestment Fund, the Philadelphia-based nonprofit lender and redevelopment-policy shop, says it has raised $12.5 million in tax-benefit investments from life insurer and annuity sales giant MetLife Inc. to set up a Clean Energy Fund, to lend money at low rates of interest for “affordable, longer-term capital to small and mid-sized energy retrofit projects nationwide,” said Reinvestment Fund executive director Don Hinkle-Brown in a statement.
Clean Energy Fund’s first project is partial financing for the $6 million Affordable Community Energy Services Co., a California affiliate of Colorado-based Mercy Housing, which calls itself “the nation’s largest nonprofit owner of low-income housing.” The project will provide “energy retrofits” by Affordable Community’s energy contractor, Bright Power, in hopes of saving electricity, water, and gas use by 6,000 Mercy tenants in 9,000 Mercy apartment buildings on the West Coast. Mercy is active in Southern and Western states.
The project will help “decarbonize” apartments, said Peter Goldmark, the former Rockefeller Foundation President and Environmental Defense Fund executive who now promotes green energy projects as head of the New Energy Model Organization (NEMO).
The Reinvestment Fund says the Clean Energy Fund will make it easier for small and middle-market landlords to qualify for clean-energy contracting arrangements that have mostly been targeted to government agencies, hospitals, colleges, utilities, and corporate users.
Reinvestment Fund says it has lent $115 million for solar installations, energy-efficiency retrofits, and other energy projects since 1993. Reinvestment Fund is best known for financing affordable-housing, charter-school, day-care, and small-business projects through federal tax-benefit programs and bank and insurer community-financing programs, and for research on urban redevelopment.

rewrite:
Joseph N. DiStefano reports on commercial enterprise within the Philadelphia region, focusing on the individuals and capital that drive its economy. The Reinvestment Fund, a Philadelphia-based nonprofit organization specializing in lending and redevelopment policy, has announced the establishment of a Clean Energy Fund. According to a statement from the Fund’s executive director, Don Hinkle-Brown, this initiative was capitalized with $12.5 million in tax-advantaged investments from MetLife Inc., a leading life insurance and annuity provider. The fund’s purpose is to offer low-interest financing, thereby supplying affordable, long-term capital for small and mid-sized energy efficiency retrofit projects across the United States.

The inaugural project for the Clean Energy Fund involves partial financing for the $6 million Affordable Community Energy Services Co., a California affiliate of Colorado-based Mercy Housing. Mercy Housing identifies as the nation’s largest nonprofit owner of low-income housing. Through its energy contractor, Bright Power, the project will conduct energy retrofits across 9,000 Mercy apartment buildings on the West Coast. The anticipated outcome is a reduction in electricity, water, and gas consumption for approximately 6,000 tenant households. According to Peter Goldmark, former President of the Rockefeller Foundation and an executive at the Environmental Defense Fund, now leading the New Energy Model Organization (NEMO), such projects contribute to the decarbonization of residential buildings.

The Reinvestment Fund indicates that the Clean Energy Fund will improve access for small and mid-market property owners to clean-energy contracting arrangements, which have historically been directed toward larger entities such as government agencies, hospitals, universities, utilities, and corporate clients. Since 1993, the Reinvestment Fund has deployed $115 million in financing for solar installations, energy-efficiency retrofits, and related energy projects. The organization is primarily recognized for financing affordable housing, charter schools, daycare facilities, and small businesses through federal tax-credit programs and community investment initiatives with banks and insurers, as well as for its research on urban redevelopment.
