Image copyright Police handout Image caption Jerry Drake Varnell drove a cargo van - which he believed to be packed with explosives - to a bank in downtown Oklahoma City
A 23-year-old has been arrested and charged with attempting to blow up a bank in Oklahoma City, the FBI says.
Jerry Drake Varnell allegedly told undercover investigators that he hoped his actions would "cripple the government" and cause a "revolution".
The criminal complaint alleges that shortly after midnight on Saturday he attempted to set off a fake bomb.
Speaking to undercover agents, he cited the film Fight Club and the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing as inspiration.
The FBI says that on 12 August Mr Varnell drove a cargo van - which he believed to be stolen and loaded with 1,000lbs (453kg) of explosives - to BancFirst in downtown Oklahoma City.
Days earlier, he recorded a message to be posted online after the attack, telling an undercover informant that it was important to have a statement ready to post to social media in order to prevent other groups such as the so-called Islamic State from claiming credit for the attack.
On Saturday, he parked the van in an alley beside the bank, and then attempted to dial a number with a mobile phone, thinking that would trigger the explosion, the FBI said.
FBI officials say the device was inert, and there was never any danger to the public.
"I can assure the public, without hesitation, that we had Varnell's actions monitored every step of the way," said Kathryn Peterson, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI in Oklahoma.
Mr Varnell is charged with attempting to use explosives to destroy a building in interstate commerce and faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted.
Anti-government extremist Timothy Mc­Veigh's 1995 bombing on a federal building in Oklahoma City left 168 people dead.
The attack is considered the deadliest homegrown domestic terror attack in US history.
rewrite:
According to a Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) statement, a twenty-three-year-old individual has been apprehended and charged with attempting to detonate an explosive device at a bank in Oklahoma City. The suspect, identified as Jerry Drake Varnell, is alleged to have driven a cargo van—which he believed to be both stolen and laden with approximately one thousand pounds (four hundred fifty-three kilograms) of explosives—to the BancFirst building in downtown Oklahoma City in the early hours of August 12. The criminal complaint indicates that Varnell subsequently parked the vehicle in an alley adjacent to the bank and attempted to initiate a detonation remotely via a mobile telephone.

Federal authorities report that the explosive device was inert, posing no actual threat to public safety. Special Agent in Charge Kathryn Peterson of the FBI’s Oklahoma office stated, “I can assure the public, without hesitation, that we had Varnell's actions monitored every step of the way.” Investigative documents reveal that Varnell allegedly informed undercover operatives that his intended act was motivated by a desire to “cripple the government” and instigate a “revolution.” He reportedly cited as inspiration the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing and themes from the film *Fight Club*.

Prior to the attempted attack, Varnell is alleged to have recorded a manifesto intended for online dissemination, advising an undercover informant that a pre-prepared statement was necessary to prevent other entities, such as the so-called Islamic State, from claiming responsibility. The 1995 bombing referenced by Varnell, perpetrated by anti-government extremist Timothy McVeigh, resulted in one hundred sixty-eight fatalities and remains the deadliest incident of domestic terrorism in United States history. Jerry Drake Varnell now faces federal charges of attempting to use explosives to destroy a building engaged in interstate commerce, an offense carrying a potential penalty of up to twenty years imprisonment upon conviction.

ARLINGTON, Va. — Washington Capitals forward Nathan Walker will become the first Australian player to dress in an NHL game when he makes his debut Saturday night against the Montreal Canadiens.
Walker grew up in Sydney after he and his family emigrated from the United Kingdom when he was 2. After his brother Ryan was exposed to the sport, it became clear Nathan had pro potential and he moved to the Czech Republic at age 13 to play minor and then junior hockey.
"It definitely made me a little bit more independent earlier on," Walker said. "I think it just made me mature quicker."
On the ice, Walker said practicing twice a day with HC Vitkovice's under-18 and under-20 teams helped his game mature.
"It's definitely a big jump," Walker said. "You've got a lot more time to work on your skills while you're younger."
Walker has played just seven games in the Australian Ice Hockey League back home. Internationally, he had six points in four games as Australia won the International Ice Hockey Federation World Championship Division II in 2011 and then two assists the next year in the IIHF World Championship Division I.
Walker said he hasn't thought much about being the first Australian to play in the NHL.
"At the end of the day, I'm just another guy on the team, another guy in the league, another guy playing the sport we all love," Walker said.
Walker is no stranger to NHL history. After playing for the United States Hockey League's Youngstown Phantoms and American Hockey League's Hershey Bears, Walker became the first Australian selected in the NHL draft when the Capitals took him in the third round in 2014.
Washington general manager Brian MacLellan has noticed significant strides in Walker's game since then.
rewrite:
On Saturday evening, Nathan Walker, a forward for the Washington Capitals, is poised to become the inaugural Australian athlete to participate in a National Hockey League contest upon his debut against the Montreal Canadiens. Walker’s early life involved emigration from the United Kingdom to Sydney at age two. Following his brother Ryan’s introduction to ice hockey, Nathan’s professional potential became evident, prompting a relocation to the Czech Republic at thirteen to pursue competitive minor and junior hockey. Reflecting on this transition, Walker noted that the experience fostered earlier independence and accelerated his personal maturation.

Regarding his athletic development, Walker attributes significant progress to his tenure with HC Vitkovice, where intensive twice-daily practices with both the under-18 and under-20 squads facilitated substantial improvement in his gameplay. He characterized the shift to a concentrated training environment as a considerable advancement, providing enhanced opportunity for skill refinement during formative years. Domestically, Walker’s experience in the Australian Ice Hockey League is limited to seven appearances. On the international stage, he contributed six points across four games during Australia’s 2011 IIHF World Championship Division II victory, followed by two assists the subsequent year in Division I competition.

When considering his pioneering status as the first Australian in the NHL, Walker maintains a perspective focused on team integration, stating, “I am merely another member of the team and the league, engaging in the sport we collectively cherish.” His path to this milestone included stints with the Youngstown Phantoms of the USHL and the Hershey Bears of the AHL, culminating in his 2014 third-round selection by the Capitals, which marked the first NHL draft choice of an Australian player. Washington General Manager Brian MacLellan has since observed marked and substantial advancements in Walker’s overall performance.

SAN FRANCISCO — A woman who was found dead Wednesday in a stairwell of a power plant at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital had dementia and vanished from a nearby mental health facility 10 days ago, her daughter said.
A staff member found the body at about 1 p.m. The county medical examiner’s office identified the woman as Ruby Andersen, 75.
An autopsy was pending.
“I don’t know how she died,” her daughter, Charlene Roberts, told KRON-TV . “Did she have a stroke or fell? I don’t know what happened.”
Roberts, who gave her mother’s age as 76, said the woman had dementia and two hearing aids and went missing on May 20 from a mental health facility.
“We almost hired a private investigator” to look for her, Roberts said.
Hospital spokeswoman Rachael Kagan said the woman was not a patient at San Francisco General but noted that there were other facilities on the same campus operated by the San Francisco Department of Public Health. They include the 47-bed Mental Health Rehabilitation Center.
Andersen was found in a stairwell that usually is locked and only accessible to maintenance workers, Kagan said.
“We are very concerned how this could have happened,” she said.
Police, public health and sheriff’s investigators were working on the case.
Five years ago, the body of a missing patient was found in a stairwell at the same hospital, more than two weeks after a patient disappeared from her room.
An autopsy determined that 57-year-old Lynne Spalding had been dead for several days before her body was found in a stairwell that was supposed to be routinely checked by security.
The Sheriff’s Department, which is responsible for the hospital’s security, paid Spalding’s family $3 million to settle a legal claim.

Roberts, who stated her mother was 76, noted that Andersen also utilized two hearing aids. A staff member found the body at approximately 1 p.m.; an autopsy is pending. The Sheriff’s Department, responsible for hospital security, subsequently settled a legal claim with Spalding’s family for $3 million.

× Thai Prime Minister: cave will become “an important tourist spot”
The Thai cave at the center of an international mission to rescue a soccer team and its coach is likely to become a tourist destination, government officials say.
As rescuers worked around the clock to free the 12 boys and the man who coaches them, Thailand’s Prime Minster Prayut Chan-o-cha said on Tuesday that the cave in the northern province of Chiang Rai was “likely to become famous nationally and worldwide.”
“It will eventually become an important tourist spot,” he said in a Facebook live video stream from his office. “Therefore we have to come up with [safety] measures to accommodate the tourism activities.”
The prime minister added that in the past authorities lacked a good map of the cave, but that following the mammoth rescue operation “we should have a better diagram to create safety.”
The Tham Luang Nang Non cave network made headlines around the world after the boys, aged between 11 and 16, and their 25-year-old coach disappeared on June 23.
The group became stranded in the flooded tunnels after a relentless downpour of rain, until two British divers discovered them perched on a small ledge of dry land nine days later.
Rescue teams are now racing to free the boys before more rain is forecast next week, and are working on solutions ranging from teaching them to dive to drilling an escape route.
Once the mission is complete, authorities plan to repair the damage inflicted on the cave, and upgrade the area to a national park.
The cave network is already well-known by locals. For the first kilometer (0.6 miles) or so inside the cavernous entrance, limestone rock formations hug high ceilings, creating an almost amphitheater-like atmosphere.
Jongklai Worapongsathorn, the deputy director-general of the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, told Thailand’s Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) that the department had set its sights on developing the cave into a tourist destination.
The plan would include signs making it clear to tourists which parts of the cave they should stay clear of, he said.
rewrite:
The Tham Luang Nang Non cave system in Chiang Rai Province, Thailand, which has been the focus of an extensive international rescue operation for a youth football team and their coach, is anticipated to be developed into a significant tourist destination according to statements from government officials. During the ongoing efforts to extricate the twelve adolescents and their twenty-five-year-old coach, Prime Minister Prayut Chan-o-cha remarked that the site is poised to gain considerable national and international recognition. In a live broadcast from his office, he explicitly stated that the location “will eventually become an important tourist spot,” necessitating the implementation of comprehensive safety measures to manage future visitor activity. The Prime Minister further noted that prior cartographic data of the caverns was insufficient, but the extensive rescue mission is expected to yield detailed diagrams essential for ensuring visitor safety.

This cave network garnered global attention following the group’s disappearance on June 23rd, after they became trapped by sudden flooding caused by seasonal rainfall. They were located nine days later by British divers on a narrow subterranean ledge. As rescue teams expedite operations ahead of forecasted precipitation, employing strategies from dive training to potential drilling, authorities are concurrently planning for the site’s future. Post-rescue intentions include rehabilitating any operational damage and designating the area as a national park. While the caverns are already familiar to local communities, featuring expansive limestone formations near the entrance that create a theatrical ambiance, official development plans are now being formalized. Jongklai Worapongsathorn, Deputy Director-General of the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, confirmed to the Thai Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) that the department aims to formally establish the cave as a tourist attraction. Proposed measures include the installation of clear signage to delineate restricted zones within the cave system for public safety.

Plans have the old library in Gulfport coming back to life. (Photo source: WLOX)
Ground work on one of the most anticipated projects on the coast is moving right along. The future site of the Mississippi Aquarium in Gulfport is undergoing dirt and drainage work.
There's another project in the works that ties right in to the needs of the big attraction. While technically not a part of the incoming aquarium's property, plans have the old library in Gulfport coming back to life to play a big role in the operations of the attraction.
"We're restoring the library, maintaining the architectural integrity of the building, and re-purposing it to a highly functional, brand new, intermodal center," said Coast Transit Authority Executive Director Kevin Coggin.
Coggin just signed a 40-year lease with the city for the $1.6 million property. Once renovated, Coggin said the bottom floor will be dedicated to CTA business, including a hub for transportation and possibly a food court.
The top 14,000 square feet will be rented out to the aquarium for administrative offices and classrooms. According to Coggin, the only thing standing in the way of construction is an approval by archives and history, which he says is almost there.
"The community will see actual renovation take place on this library this summer," Coggin said.
He hopes to be up and running in the location when the aquarium opens. Then, future plans include a public tram way across Hwy. 90.
"We're going to operate a public tram across to bring people back and forth with a route. You'll be able to bike across and walk across, and there's a lot of good elements to that, too. One of them is safety," said Coggin.
So far, Coggin said work to bring the $8.9 million library renovation to light has been making big strides, and he's looking forward to being a part of the economic boom expected in the city once the attraction opens.
The Gulfport City Council is considering an agreement Tuesday to fund part of $633,000 in improvements near the future CTA center.
Copyright 2017 WLOX. All rights reserved.
rewrite:

Concurrently, a complementary project is advancing to support the major attraction's operational needs. Although not situated on the aquarium's direct property, the historic Gulfport library building is slated for rehabilitation and will be integral to the facility's functions.

Kevin Coggin, Executive Director of the Coast Transit Authority (CTA), has confirmed plans to restore the library. "We are restoring the library, maintaining the architectural integrity of the building, and repurposing it into a highly functional, brand-new intermodal center," Coggin stated. This follows the recent execution of a 40-year lease agreement with the city for the $1.6 million property. Upon renovation, the ground floor will be dedicated to CTA operations, serving as a transportation hub and potentially incorporating a food court. The upper level, encompassing 14,000 square feet, will be leased to the aquarium for administrative offices and educational classrooms.

Coggin indicated that final approval from archival and historical authorities is pending but imminent, representing the last procedural hurdle before construction can begin. He anticipates visible renovation work to commence during the summer, with the goal of having the center operational in tandem with the aquarium's opening. Subsequent phases of the project envision implementing a public tramway across Highway 90. "We plan to operate a public tram to transport visitors across the highway, and the route will also accommodate pedestrian and bicycle traffic, incorporating significant safety enhancements," Coggin explained.

The $8.9 million library renovation project has reportedly achieved substantial advancements. Coggin expressed optimism about contributing to the anticipated economic revitalization in Gulfport following the aquarium's launch. In a related development, the Gulfport City Council is reviewing a proposed agreement to allocate funding for a portion of $633,000 in infrastructure improvements adjacent to the future CTA intermodal center.

BEIJING May 3 China will further regulate local government debt issuance and financing, six government agencies said in a joint statement on Wednesday, reinforcing recent steps to bolster financial risk controls.
China has taken aim at potential cracks in its financial system, ramping up regulatory checks with various high-flying officials calling for action against an alarming level of leverage.
In the statement, the government agencies, including the National Development and Reform Commission, the finance ministry, the central bank and securities and banking regulators, said China would push for a clearer boundary between local governments and their financing vehicles.
Local governments are strictly prohibited from injecting public assets into local government financing vehicles (LGFVs), or using expected land revenue as debt repayments for LGFVs, the statement said.
It also said LGFVs could not accept guarantees from local governments when thy issue debt, and authorities would strictly prohibit illegal debt issuance by local governments through public-private partnership projects.
The agencies ordered an inspection of local governments' financing and guarantee situation to "fully correct irregularities" by the end of July, the statement, posted on the finance ministry's official website, said.
(Reporting by Yawen Chen and Kevin Yao; Editing by Shri Navaratnam and Nick Macfie)
rewrite:
On May 3, the Chinese government announced enhanced regulatory measures concerning local government debt issuance and financing. In a joint statement issued by six agencies, including the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Finance, the People’s Bank of China, and the securities and banking regulators, authorities underscored a commitment to strengthening financial risk controls. This initiative forms part of a broader effort to address vulnerabilities within the financial system, following heightened regulatory scrutiny and calls from senior officials to mitigate elevated leverage levels.

The directive mandates a clearer delineation between local governments and their associated financing vehicles (LGFVs). It explicitly prohibits local governments from capitalizing LGFVs with public assets or pledging anticipated land sale revenues for debt servicing. Furthermore, LGFVs are barred from obtaining local government guarantees for debt issuance, and authorities will strictly forbid illicit debt raising via public-private partnership arrangements. To ensure compliance, an inspection of local government financing and guarantee practices has been ordered, with instructions to rectify all identified irregularities by the end of July. The statement was disseminated through the official website of the Ministry of Finance.

This drunk driving suspect says she’s just a follower of Christ.
After allegedly boozing behind the wheel Sunday night, Nicole Ann Mintner defended herself to police by telling arresting officers that “Jesus drank wine and so did I,” The Village News reported.
Deputies said they found the 45-year-old asleep at the wheel inside a silver Dodge with her hazard lights activated and engine running in Sumter County, Fla.
During police interviews, Mintner reportedly refused to take off her sunglasses and slapped an officer twice on the shoulder.
She told officers that she had taken Xanax then later admitted to drinking alcohol after four empty sangria bottles were found in her center console.
Mintner was placed under arrest and into the back of a patrol car where she “continuously” screamed and threatened to urinate while en route to Sumter County Detention Center, according to deputies.
When they arrived at the jail, officers attempted to perform field sobriety tests on Minter but she kept talking over them and began singing “Amazing Grace,” according to the Village News.
She also reportedly threw her socks at a camera recording the tests and exposed herself to the officers.
“The defendant removed her right breast from her shirt and completely revealed it to the camera and jail staff,” according to the police report obtained by the newspaper.
Mintner was booked on charges of driving under the influence, battery on a law enforcement officer and resisting an officer. She was released Monday on $6,000 bond, according to court records.

During subsequent questioning, Mintner reportedly declined to remove her sunglasses and struck an officer on the shoulder twice. She initially stated she had consumed Xanax but later acknowledged drinking alcohol after four empty sangria bottles were located within her vehicle’s center console. Following her arrest, Mintner was placed in a patrol car, where she allegedly screamed continuously and threatened to urinate while being transported to the Sumter County Detention Center.

Upon arrival, officers attempted to administer field sobriety tests. However, Mintner repeatedly interrupted the procedures by speaking over the instructions and singing “Amazing Grace.” She also reportedly threw her socks at a recording camera and exposed her right breast to both the camera and jail staff, as documented in the official police report obtained by the newspaper. Mintner was formally charged with driving under the influence, battery on a law enforcement officer, and resisting an officer. Court records indicate she was released on Monday after posting a $6,000 bond.

Outside view of the plant of gold refiner and bar manufacturer Argor-Heraeus SA in the southern Swiss town of Mendrisio, March 1, 2012. REUTERS/Pascal Lauener
HAMBURG German precious metals group Heraeus [HRHLD.UL] said on Monday it had taken full control of Swiss gold and silver processor Argor-Heraeus.
The German group has raised its shareholding in Argor-Heraeus to 100 percent from about 33 percent previously.
No financial details are being released about the deal, which still requires approval from relevant authorities.
The sellers were Germany's Commerzbank (CBKG.DE), Austrian state mint Muenze Oesterreich and Argor-Heraeus management, Heraeus said.
Argor-Heraeus has around 300 employees with operations in Switzerland, Germany, Italy and South America.
It is involved in refining gold ore, recycling of precious metals and industrial processing of bars, coins, alloys and semi-finished products.
"With the full takeover of the shareholdings, Heraeus is now in the position to fully profit from Argors competence and capacity for gold and silver," Heraeus CEO Jan Rinnert said in a statement.
(Reporting by Michael Hogan; editing by Jason Neely)

Labour MP Chris Hipkins says he didn't know his question to officials about citizenship was in any way linked to questions about Australia's Barnaby Joyce's eligibility for parliament there.
But had he known he might have given it a second thought.
Deputy Prime Minister Joyce's position in Australia's federal parliament is under scrutiny after he revealed the New Zealand High Commission had contacted him last week with the "shocking" information that he could be a New Zealander.
Joyce's father was born in New Zealand and it has been confirmed that he is a citizen by descent. That would rule him ineligible to serve in Australia's Parliament.
Advertisement
Labour leader Jacinda Ardern said today that Hipkins shouldn't have been prioritising questions about citizenship.
"We've had a discussion about [it] and as I said to her, had I known this was where it was going to land up I wouldn't have got involved," Hipkins said.
"I had no intention of getting involved in Australian domestic politics."
Hipkins, who has a keen interest in the rights of Kiwis living in Australia, said he asked the citizenship question out of personal interest.
A spokesman for Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne says Australian media had also lodged specific questions about Joyce at or about the same time as Hipkins' general question.
The requests had led to Joyce being informed, he said.
Joyce is the fifth Australian MP to have their citizenship questioned since last month, after senators Scott Ludlam, Larissa Waters, Matthew Canavan and Malcolm Roberts.
- NZN
rewrite:
Labour Member of Parliament Chris Hipkins has stated that he was unaware his inquiry to officials regarding citizenship provisions was connected in any manner to questions concerning the eligibility of Australia’s Deputy Prime Minister, Barnaby Joyce, to serve in that nation’s parliament. He indicated that, had he been cognizant of this linkage, he would have reconsidered the matter.

Mr. Joyce’s tenure in the Australian federal parliament is presently under examination following his disclosure that the New Zealand High Commission contacted him last week with what he described as “shocking” information suggesting he may hold New Zealand citizenship. As his father was born in New Zealand, it has been confirmed that Mr. Joyce is indeed a citizen by descent, a status which would render him ineligible to sit in the Australian Parliament.

Labour Leader Jacinda Ardern remarked that Mr. Hipkins ought not to have prioritized such questions of citizenship. In response, Mr. Hipkins stated, “We have discussed the matter, and as I conveyed to her, had I known this would be the eventual outcome, I would not have become involved. I had no intention of intervening in Australian domestic politics.” He clarified that his question arose from personal interest, given his focus on the rights of New Zealanders residing in Australia.

A spokesperson for Internal Affairs Minister Peter Dunne noted that Australian media had submitted specific inquiries regarding Mr. Joyce contemporaneously with Mr. Hipkins’ more general question. These combined requests ultimately led to Mr. Joyce being notified of his citizenship status. Mr. Joyce represents the fifth Australian parliamentarian to face scrutiny over citizenship qualifications in recent months, following Senators Scott Ludlam, Larissa Waters, Matthew Canavan, and Malcolm Roberts.

The number of building permits issued this April compared to last April was up by 14.4%, data released by the Cyprus Statistical Service show. At the same time, an increase of 6.6% is recorded during the first four months of this year.
The number of building permits issued by local authorities this April was 469, compared to 410 in April 2017, recording an increase of 14.4%. The total value of these permits was up by €17 million reaching €105.6 million compared to €89.6 million in April last year.
The total area of the properties reached 101,500 square metres compared to 87,600 square metres last April.
The permits issued this April concern the construction of 418 residential units compared to 289 last April. During the period of January – April 2018, 1,984 building permits were issued compared to 1,861 in the same period of 2017, recording an increase of 6.6%.
The total value of these permits was up by 27.5% and their total area by 24.5%. The number of residential units to be built was up by 22.3%.
Building permits constitute an important indicator for future activity in the building sector, the Statistical Service says.
rewrite:
Data released by the Cyprus Statistical Service indicate a notable year-on-year increase in building permit issuance for April. Specifically, 469 permits were authorized in April 2018, a rise of 14.4% from the 410 permits issued in April 2017. This growth is further reflected in the total permit value, which increased by €17 million to €105.6 million, and the total permitted area, which expanded to 101,500 square metres from 87,600 square metres. The number of residential units approved for construction in April saw a significant increase to 418, compared to 289 in the corresponding month of the previous year.

Examining the cumulative period from January to April 2018 reveals a broader upward trend, with 1,984 permits issued—a 6.6% increase from the 1,861 issued in the same interval of 2017. The aggregate value of these permits rose by 27.5%, while the total area increased by 24.5%. Furthermore, the number of residential units slated for construction grew by 22.3%. The Statistical Service emphasizes that building permits serve as a critical leading indicator for forthcoming activity within the construction sector.

Amazon, which operates Lovefilm By Post, is predictably pushing subscribers in the direction of Prime Video, and is sweetening the deal with £15 off the cost of a Fire TV Stick. DVD and Blu-ray rentals will still be available up until the end of October, though, and Amazon won't be billing subscribers for that final month. The service is also shutting down in Germany, the only other European country it still serves, on the same day.
I guess it's been a long time coming but @lovefilm by post service to close 31st October pic.twitter.com/Vq1rpFX0l1 — Robertie (@Clert) August 14, 2017
In a way, Lovefilm is partly responsible for the demise of its own postal option. Many moons ago, Lovefilm used to run a streaming service in parallel with its rental offering. It became a relatively big player through various acquisitions, even relieving Amazon of its DVD rental arm in 2008. The house that Bezos built returned the favour in 2011, purchasing Lovefilm in its entirety. A few years later, the streaming side of things was absorbed into Amazon Prime Video, making the rental service a separate subscription and the last thing bearing the Lovefilm name.
The idea of getting your movie fix by post might seem seriously old fashioned now, but the demise of Lovefilm actually leaves something of a hole in the market. There's a reason streaming services like Netflix don't carry the latest titles. Studios want to make sure they're squeezing as much money as they can out of new films through purchases and rentals before selling blanket streaming licenses. You can buy digital copies of movies as soon as they are released on DVD/Blu-ray, or pay a couple of quid to rent them for a watch or two.
Lovefilm By Post, however, was an unlimited service. The top, £12 per month tier (£10 for Prime subscribers, naturally) offered unlimited rentals, which is something that simply isn't replicated by streaming services these days -- the way streaming licences work makes this impossible. It was inevitable Lovefilm By Post wasn't going to be viable forever, but come October 31st, we're not just losing a forgotten rental service, but the last unlimited movie subscription of its kind.
rewrite:
Amazon, the operator of the Lovefilm By Post service, is predictably incentivizing subscribers to transition to its Prime Video platform, offering a £15 reduction on the purchase of a Fire TV Stick as an inducement. DVD and Blu-ray rentals will remain available until the service’s cessation on October 31st, with Amazon waiving subscription fees for that final month. Concurrently, the service will be discontinued in Germany, the only other European nation where it remained operational, on the same date. Public reaction to the announcement, exemplified by a social media post from August 14, 2017, acknowledges the closure as an anticipated, if belated, development.

The decline of the postal rental option can be partially attributed to Lovefilm’s own strategic evolution. Historically, Lovefilm operated a streaming service alongside its physical rental business. Through a series of acquisitions, it expanded its market position, notably acquiring Amazon’s DVD rental division in 2008. Amazon subsequently purchased Lovefilm in its entirety in 2011. Several years later, Lovefilm’s streaming assets were fully integrated into Amazon Prime Video, leaving the postal rental service as a standalone subscription and the final entity carrying the Lovefilm brand.

While the concept of receiving physical media by post may now appear anachronistic, the closure of Lovefilm By Post creates a discernible gap in the home entertainment market. This gap exists due to the prevailing release window economics in the film industry. Major studios typically maximize revenue from new releases through sequential distribution channels: first via cinema, then digital purchase and rental, and finally through broader streaming licenses. Consequently, streaming platforms like Netflix do not immediately offer the latest titles. Consumers can purchase or rent new releases digitally upon their home media debut, but Lovefilm By Post provided a distinct model.

Its premium subscription tier, priced at £12 monthly (£10 for Amazon Prime subscribers), offered unlimited physical rentals. This stands in contrast to contemporary streaming services, where licensing agreements with content owners preclude such an all-encompassing, immediate-access model for new releases. Although the economic unsustainability of Lovefilm’s postal service was ultimately inevitable, its termination on October 31st represents more than the end of a niche operation. It marks the disappearance of the last remaining unlimited movie rental subscription of its kind, eliminating a unique consumer option within the media landscape.

Unlike the Martian desert in the original Destiny, Helles Basin is an arctic region where players will fight the frozen Hive faction Grasp of Nokris on the way to confront Rasputin, the rogue Warmind. The region will host a new horde-like public event called Escalation Protocol where groups of Guardians face seven waves of Hive capped by a unique boss -- one of five that will rotate every week. The elite foe drops custom gear so folks will have to wait over a month to collect them all; Since players activate the event, at least it won't be random.
PvP is getting two ranked modes, one for casual (Valor) and competitive (Glory), though the latter will move players up and down the rank ladder as they win and lose games. Every season will introduce a new gun exclusive to PvP for players to earn.
Fans already knew that tweaks were coming for their favorite exotic guns, including Sturm/Drang, Graviton Lance, Skyburner's Oath and Rat King, but the stream also showed off changes to Fighting Lion, Riskrunner, Crimson and the infamous Hard Light.
There will be two new strikes, Strange Terrain and Will of the Thousands, and one coming exclusively for PS4 players: The Insight Terminus. The Leviathan raid will get a second lair called Spire of the Stars, which will arrive after Warmind launches. Finally, the prestige version of Curse of Osiris' raid, Eater of Worlds, will arrive when the game's third season starts.

The current Renault Twingo dates back to 2014, and new spy shots reveal that a styling update is on the way for the little hatchback. The changes appear to maintain the Twingo's cute, friendly aesthetic.
The biggest changes to the front are in the lower fascia. There are new intakes in each corner, which lend a somewhat sporty aesthetic. The center section appears to be a little more rounded, too. There's lots of camouflage, but there don't appear to be major changes elsewhere. The upper grille and headlights appear to have same shapes as on the current Twingo.
At the back, there are revised tailights that appear to have a rounder shape and a different layout with a rectangular white section in the center. The bumper appears to have a completely different shape. It has a new taper that adds some visual interest to the tail, rather than the current design that's fairly flat.
These photos don't provide a look at the cabin but expect Renault to take the opportunity to update things in there. Material changes and infotainment improvements are the most likely tweaks.
This test mule also has an exhaust the pokes out of the rear corner, instead of the semi-hidden layout from most trims of the existing model. This could indicate that Renault is evaluating some powertrain changes for the hatchback.
The existing Twingo is available with a range of tiny, rear-mounted engines. The base unit is a 1.0-liter naturally aspirated three-cylinder with 70 horsepower (52 kilowatts). There's also a turbocharged 900cc three-cylinder with 90 hp (67 kW). The range-topping GT model gets a 110-hp (82 kW) version of this tiny engine.
Source: CarPix
rewrite:
The Renault Twingo, initially launched in its current iteration in 2014, is undergoing a mid-cycle styling revision, as evidenced by recent photographic documentation. The forthcoming modifications are anticipated to preserve the model's established approachable and amiable visual character.

Alterations to the vehicle's front fascia are most pronounced in its lower section. Newly designed air intakes positioned at each corner impart a subtly more athletic appearance, while the central area exhibits a slightly more rounded contour. Despite extensive camouflage cladding, the principal forms of the upper grille and headlight assemblies remain consistent with the extant model, suggesting no fundamental architectural changes in these areas.

The rear section receives more substantive updates. The tail lamp clusters feature a revised, rounder silhouette and an altered internal graphic, incorporating a rectangular white central element. Furthermore, the rear bumper assembly is entirely redesigned, introducing a tapered profile that provides enhanced visual depth compared to the comparatively planar design of the current vehicle.

Although the cabin is not visible in these images, it is reasonable to anticipate that Renault will implement interior refinements concurrent with the exterior updates. Probable enhancements include upgrades to material quality and improvements to the infotainment system.

Notably, the observed prototype features a conspicuously positioned exhaust outlet at the rear corner, deviating from the partially concealed design prevalent on most current variants. This detail may indicate the evaluation of potential powertrain revisions. The existing Twingo lineup employs a series of compact, rear-mounted engines, including a base 1.0-liter naturally aspirated three-cylinder generating 70 horsepower (52 kilowatts), a turbocharged 0.9-liter three-cylinder producing 90 horsepower (67 kW), and a range-topping GT variant equipped with a 110-horsepower (82 kW) iteration of this engine.

LEGAZPI CITY, Albay: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) would lower from 3 to 4 the alert level for Mount Mayon in the next few weeks if the volcano’s waning activity continued.
Ed Laguerta, Phivolcs chief volcanologist in the Bicol Region, on Saturday said Mayon was showing low abnormal activity in the last 24 hours but no conclusive proof would support that such activity was weakening.
Thus, according to Laguerta, alert level 4 and the eight-kilometer danger zone stay.
He, however, believes that the volcano may still generate explosions as it did in 1984 when Mayon exploded after being quiet for a week.
“We are closely studying the sudden change and decrease of [sulfur dioxide gas emission]of Mayon to 1,583 tons per day from the more than 3,000 tons two days ago,” Laguerta said in a news briefing.
With Alert Level 4 in place, the public is strongly advised to not enter the eight-kilometer danger zone and to be vigilant against pyroclastic currents, lahars and sediment-laden stream flows.
rewrite: The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs) anticipates a potential reduction of Mount Mayon's alert status from Level 4 to Level 3 within the coming weeks, contingent upon the continuation of its current declining activity. This statement was issued by Ed Laguerta, Phivolcs' chief volcanologist for the Bicol Region. He noted that while the volcano exhibited low abnormal activity over the preceding 24-hour period, this observation does not yet constitute conclusive evidence of a sustained weakening trend. Consequently, Alert Level 4 and the enforced eight-kilometer radius danger zone remain in effect. Laguerta cautioned that explosive eruptions, analogous to the 1984 event which occurred after a week of quiescence, remain a possibility. He emphasized that scientists are closely monitoring a significant decrease in sulfur dioxide emissions, which have dropped to approximately 1,583 tons per day from over 3,000 tons recorded two days prior. Under the prevailing Alert Level 4, the public is strictly advised to avoid the designated danger zone and to maintain vigilance against pyroclastic density currents, lahars, and sediment-laden stream flows.

New Zealand completed a 240-run thumping of the West Indies in the second test at Seddon Park today.
Spinner Mitchell Santner took the last two wickets on consecutive balls shortly before tea on the fourth day, the West Indies being dismissed for 203.
The result ensured a clean sweep, winning the series 2-0 after their innings and 67-run win at the Basin Reserve in the first test.
Read more:
Who is New Zealand's greatest test batsmen?
Advertisement
The West Indies had started the fourth day at 30 for two, requiring an improbable 444 to win.
They lost stand-in captain Kraigg Brathwaite in the sixth over of the day, caught at gully off Trent Boult, giving the left armer his 200th test wicket, just the fifth such bowler to that mark.
Neil Wagner dismissed Roston Chase for 64. Photo / Photosport
He is also the sixth New Zealand bowler to 200, after Richard Hadlee, Dan Vettori, Chris Martin, Chris Cairns and current team mate Tim Southee.
Shai Hope was struck on an arm by Neil Wagner and hooked the next ball straight to fine leg.
Sunil Ambris took a blow on his left wrist and after battling on a few minutes, retired hurt on five. A check revealed a broken bone and he is out of the ODI squad.
Shane Dowrich was caught by Henry Nicholls. Photo / Photosport
Wicketkeeper Shane Dowrich popped a catch to short leg but Roston Chase and Ray Reifer battled solidly to lunch and well into the second session, before they departed in quick order.
Chase completed his fifth half century, 64, while Reifer made 29 before falling to a fine low catch by captain Kane Williamson at gully.
Wagner finished with three for 42 and there were two wickets apiece for Southee, Boult and Santner.
The three-game ODI series starts in Whangarei next Wednesday, before which the tourists' have a one-day fixture against a New Zealand XI on Saturday.
The squad is significantly different from their test group, with the likes of batting heavyweights Chris Gayle and Marlon Samuels and Evin Lewis arriving this week.
The ODI series continues in Christchurch on December 23 and Boxing Day.
rewrite:
New Zealand secured a comprehensive 240-run victory over the West Indies in the second Test match at Seddon Park, concluding the match shortly before tea on the fourth day. The West Indies, resuming their second innings at 30 for two in pursuit of an unattainable target of 444, were ultimately dismissed for 203. Spinner Mitchell Santner claimed the final two wickets on consecutive deliveries, ensuring a 2-0 series clean sweep for New Zealand, following their innings and 67-run victory in the first Test at the Basin Reserve.

The West Indies' innings encountered early difficulties on the fourth day. Stand-in captain Kraigg Brathwaite fell in the sixth over, caught at gully off the bowling of Trent Boult. This dismissal marked Boult’s 200th Test wicket, making him the fifth left-arm bowler and the sixth New Zealander overall to achieve this milestone, following Richard Hadlee, Dan Vettori, Chris Martin, Chris Cairns, and current teammate Tim Southee. Subsequent batsmen struggled against persistent bowling. Shai Hope, after being struck on the arm by Neil Wagner, hooked the subsequent delivery directly to fine leg. Sunil Ambris sustained a blow to his left wrist, retired hurt on five, and was later diagnosed with a fracture, ruling him out of the forthcoming One-Day International series.

A partnership developed between Roston Chase and Ray Reifer, who batted resolutely through to lunch and into the second session. Chase compiled a resilient 64, his fifth Test half-century, while Reifer contributed 29 before falling to a sharp low catch by captain Kane Williamson at gully. Their dismissals in quick succession precipitated the innings' conclusion. Wagner concluded with figures of three for 42, with Southee, Boult, and Santner each claiming two wickets.

Attention now turns to the limited-overs segment of the tour. The West Indies, fielding a significantly altered squad featuring notable inclusions such as Chris Gayle, Marlon Samuels, and Evin Lewis, will play a one-day fixture against a New Zealand XI this Saturday. The three-match ODI series commences next Wednesday in Whangarei, with subsequent matches scheduled for Christchurch on December 23 and Boxing Day.

FILE PHOTO: An Apple logo is seen in a store in Los Angeles, California, U.S., March 24, 2017. REUTERS/Lucy Nicholson/File Photo
Apple Inc (AAPL.O) has hired a team of biomedical engineers as part of a secret initiative, initially envisioned by late Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, to develop sensors to treat diabetes, CNBC reported citing three people familiar with the matter.
An Apple spokeswoman declined to comment.
The engineers are expected to work at a nondescript office in Palo Alto, California, close to the corporate headquarters, CNBC said.
The news comes at the time when the line between pharmaceuticals and technology is blurring as companies are joining forces to tackle chronic diseases using high-tech devices that combine biology, software and hardware, thereby jump-starting a novel field of medicine called bioelectronics.
Last year, GlaxoSmithKline Plc (GSK.L) and Google parent Alphabet Inc (GOOGL.O) unveiled a joint company aimed at marketing bioelectronic devices to fight illness by attaching to individual nerves.
U.S. biotech firms Setpoint Medical and EnteroMedics Inc (ETRM.O) have already shown early benefits of bioelectronics in treating rheumatoid arthritis and suppressing appetite in the obese.
Other companies playing around the idea of bioelectronics include Medtronic Plc (MDT.N), Proteus Digital Technology, Sanofi SA (SASY.PA) and Biogen Inc (BIIB.O).
The company's shares were marginally up after the bell on Wednesday.
(Reporting by Divya Grover in Bengaluru; Editing by Sandra Maler and Lisa Shumaker)
rewrite:
According to a CNBC report citing three informed sources, Apple Inc. has recruited a team of biomedical engineers for a confidential project focused on developing sensors for diabetes treatment. This initiative is reportedly rooted in a vision originally held by the company's late co-founder, Steve Jobs. The engineers are said to be operating from an unassuming office in Palo Alto, California, situated near Apple's corporate headquarters. An Apple spokesperson declined to comment on the report.

This development occurs within a broader industrial trend where the demarcation between the pharmaceutical and technology sectors is increasingly indistinct. Companies are forming collaborations to address chronic diseases through advanced devices that integrate biological, software, and hardware components. This convergence is catalyzing the emergence of the novel medical field of bioelectronics. Illustrative of this trend, GlaxoSmithKline and Alphabet Inc., Google's parent company, last year established a joint venture dedicated to commercializing bioelectronic devices designed to modulate nerve activity for therapeutic purposes. Early clinical benefits of such technology have been demonstrated by U.S. firms Setpoint Medical and EnteroMedics Inc., in treating conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and managing obesity. Other significant entities exploring bioelectronics include Medtronic Plc, Proteus Digital Health, Sanofi SA, and Biogen Inc. Following the report, Apple's share price experienced a slight increase in after-hours trading on Wednesday.

Veteran fly fishing guide Michael “Rocky” Cox will speak Thursday, Feb. 8, at a free, public meeting of the Clinch River Chapter, Trout Unlimited. His presentation starts at 7 p.m. in the parish hall of St. Francis Episcopal Church, 158 W. Norris Road, Norris.
Cox, owner of Rocky Top Anglers, is a Knoxville native who has guided more than 1,000 fishing trips professionally since he started in 2001. He says his upbringing in East Tennessee “allowed me to grow up with wonderful places to play right in my own back yard. Countless miles of mountain streams and cold tailwaters provided endless playgrounds. I never realized how much those years of playing in the water would influence my adult life.
“I’ve always loved the peaceful excitement of fly fishing and always found myself thinking about that next big trip to the mountains. When my leisure time came, I was fly fishing. I was captivated by the old guides, rowing their anglers downriver and finding those special places only accessible by driftboat. I knew that guiding others and showing them the places I treasure would be a very rewarding career.”
Clinch River Chapter TU works to preserve and protect the Clinch River tailwater and its watershed through conservation projects and through education of children and adults in aquatic natural resources. For more information, visit http://crctu.org.
rewrite:
The Clinch River Chapter of Trout Unlimited will host a public presentation by veteran fly fishing guide Michael “Rocky” Cox on Thursday, February 8. The event, which is free and open to the public, will commence at 7:00 p.m. in the parish hall of St. Francis Episcopal Church, located at 158 West Norris Road in Norris.

Mr. Cox, a Knoxville native and proprietor of Rocky Top Anglers, has professionally guided over one thousand fishing excursions since commencing his career in 2001. He attributes his professional path to his formative years in East Tennessee, noting that the region’s extensive mountain streams and cold tailwaters provided a formative natural environment. He reflects that these early experiences, which he did not initially recognize as influential, profoundly shaped his adult life and vocation.

Cox describes a longstanding passion for the contemplative engagement of fly fishing, consistently anticipating expeditions into mountainous regions. His leisure time was invariably devoted to the pursuit. He recalls being particularly inspired by observing seasoned guides navigating driftboats to access remote fishing locations. This inspired his realization that a career guiding others to these cherished landscapes would be deeply fulfilling.

The Clinch River Chapter of Trout Unlimited is dedicated to the conservation and protection of the Clinch River tailwater and its watershed. This mission is advanced through direct conservation initiatives and educational outreach focused on aquatic natural resources for both youth and adults. Further information is available at the organization’s website, http://crctu.org.

Wealth and health are definitely connected. But race is also a significant factor, with black residents facing health outcomes that lag behind those of white New Jerseyans — often significantly — over the span a lifetime.
Those are among the conclusions of data released last week as part of the annual County Health Rankings, a national report produced by the New Jersey-based Robert Wood Johnson Foundation and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute. The findings compare counties across the nation on measures like low birth-weight babies, poor health days, and early death — as well as factors that impact these outcomes, including smoking, education levels, and obesity.
Racial disparities in health have become a growing focus in recent years, and Dr. Shereef Elnahal, the acting commissioner of the state Department of Health, has made it a priority to reduce these gaps, which he called “embarrassingly high” at a recent hearing. “Needless to say, we have much work ahead to improve New Jersey’s public health,” he told the Senate Judiciary committee earlier this month.

rewrite:
A clear association exists between wealth and health, yet race also constitutes a significant determinant. In New Jersey, Black residents experience health outcomes that persistently lag behind those of their White counterparts throughout the lifespan, often to a substantial degree.

These conclusions emerge from data published last week within the annual County Health Rankings, a national report compiled by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, based in New Jersey, and the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute. The report compares counties nationwide on metrics such as rates of low birth-weight infants, self-reported days of poor health, and premature mortality. It also analyzes contributing factors, including smoking prevalence, educational attainment, and obesity.

Addressing racial health disparities has become an increasing focus in recent years. Dr. Shereef Elnahal, Acting Commissioner of the state Department of Health, has prioritized reducing these gaps, which he recently described as "embarrassingly high" during a legislative hearing. He affirmed to the Senate Judiciary Committee earlier this month, "Needless to say, we have much work ahead to improve New Jersey’s public health."

Kathrine Herzer has been an actress since she was 10 years old, but her role as Allison McCord on the CBS hit political drama Madam Secretary changed her life. While the California native had small roles in movies such as Mr. and Mrs. Smith and A Lot Like Love, her recurring role alongside stars such as Tea Leoni and Keith Carradine took her career to the next level.
“Madam Secretary is the best,” Herzer told CBS Local in a recent studio interview. “I got the part when I was a junior in high school and I would commute back and forth to New York when we started filming. It’s the best group of people to work with and we have these amazing scripts that create this great energy.”
In addition to her work on Madam Secretary, Herzer is also a full time student at New York University. While her schedule has its challenges, the 20-year-old rising star wouldn’t change anything.
“It’s a lot to balance, but I wouldn’t have it any other way,” Herzer said. “There’s so much that I get from working and going to school at the same time.”
Season Four of the show will be a big one for the McCord family, as Allison is on her way to college. The new season, which premieres Sunday, October 8th at 10pm eastern on CBS, will feature a more mature and empowered Allison McCord.
“Allison is in such a crazy time in her life because she is going to college. She’s venturing into her own world, but the McCord family is so close that it just means that they are all branching out into this new area. I think this bit of independence will give her a lot of power, its an exciting season for her.”

LAWRENCE, Kan. — Kansas forward Udoka Azubuike withdrew his name from the NBA draft on Wednesday, choosing to return for his junior season after participating in the combine.
The 7-footer from Nigeria started 34 games last season, averaging 13 points and seven rebounds. He shot 77 per cent from the field, a Big 12 record and the best mark in the nation.
Azubuike is a traditional back-to-the-basket big man, and scouts have wondered how his skills would transfer to the NBA. Josh Gordon says Packers CB Demarious Randle ‘couldn’t hold my jock strap’
Josh Gordon looked like he could be in for a monster day after he caught two big passes in the first quarter of Sunday’s game, but Green Bay Packers cornerback Demarious Randall did a solid job covering him the rest of the way. Did Randle earn the right to brag about it? That depends on who you ask.
After the game, Randle was asked about his performance against Gordon. He was beaming with confidence.
How well did #Packers CB Damarious Randall cover #Browns WR Josh Gordon? “He had one catch,” Randall said. “Any more questions?” https://t.co/xXwCq9JWOi — Packers News (@PGPackersNews) December 11, 2017
Gordon wasn’t all that impressed. While he complimented the Packers for grinding out an overtime win, he hinted that he would torch Randall if the Cleveland Browns were a better team overall.
Great Win for them but let’s be serious.. Considering several of our disadvantages as a team, this kid couldn’t hold my jock strap on my worst day lol..@RandallTime https://t.co/ennvwjTMUH — Flash Gordon (@JOSH_GORDONXII) December 11, 2017
After seeing Gordon’s tweet, Randall didn’t hold back.
“You must be on that s— again,” he replied.
Gordon ended up with three catches for 69 yards, including one that was an extremely acrobatic touchdown reception early on. Just one of those catches came when Randall was covering him.
Obviously, Gordon would be far more difficult to cover if he had a better quarterback than DeShone Kizer throwing to him. Still, Randall deserves credit for shutting him down in man coverage. Gordon has looked as athletic as ever in his first two games back.
rewrite:
In the aftermath of the December 11, 2017, contest between the Green Bay Packers and Cleveland Browns, a public exchange ensued between Packers cornerback Damarious Randall and Browns wide receiver Josh Gordon regarding Randall’s defensive performance. Gordon demonstrated significant early potential, securing two substantial receptions in the first quarter, including an acrobatic 69-yard touchdown. However, for the remainder of the game, Randall provided effective coverage in man-to-man situations, limiting Gordon to only a single additional catch.

When questioned post-game, Randall expressed clear satisfaction with his performance, pointedly noting, “He had one catch. Any more questions?” Gordon, while acknowledging the Packers’ overtime victory, offered a starkly different assessment via social media. He suggested that systemic disadvantages for the Browns were a mitigating factor and dismissively stated of Randall, “this kid couldn’t hold my jock strap on my worst day.” Randall’s retort was a pointed insinuation regarding Gordon’s past off-field issues.

Analytically, Randall’s coverage was notably successful, particularly given Gordon’s evident athletic prowess in his initial games returning from suspension. The broader context, however, includes the significant limitation posed by Browns quarterback DeShone Kizer’s inconsistent play, which undoubtedly impacted Gordon’s overall opportunity. Consequently, while Randall merits credit for a well-executed defensive assignment, Gordon’s contention that his individual potential was constrained by team-wide deficiencies remains a plausible counterpoint to a purely statistical evaluation of the matchup.

Cypriot television networks may face fierce competition from a planned new Russian-language channel which could attract a considerable number of advertisers.
Even though no formal complaint has yet been submitted to the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority, there is a lot of behind-the-scenes pressure on authorities to drop the condition of Greek subtitles in Russian-language broadcasts. In this way, they hope to limit the Russian channel’s number of viewers and hence the interest of Cypriot businesses in advertising.
The Russian-language channel has only recently secured a temporary broadcast licence, subject to the rule that its broadcasts will have Greek subtitles. This term was applied because the Cyprus Radio Television Authority needed to be able control the channel’s broadcasts without hiring additional personnel fluent in Russian.
This channel’s licence, as well the licences of all other non-subscription channels in Cyprus, expired on 30 June 2018. The Cyprus Radio Television Authority is currently reviewing applications submitted for new temporary licences which will be valid until 30 June 2019.
Shareholders of the company behind the creation and operation of the Russian-language channel network were willing to abide with the directives of the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority from the start and have already approached companies with relevant experience in subtitling.
According to sources, members of the Board of Directors of Cyprus Broadcasting Authority are considering withdrawing the demand for subtitles. Overall, it appears that the broadcasting Authority is heading towards a partial withdrawal of the term: in particular, it is probable that some of the broadcasts and not all of them will be subtitled.
rewrite:
Cypriot television networks may encounter significant competitive pressure from a proposed new Russian-language channel, which is anticipated to attract a substantial share of advertising revenue. Although no formal complaint has been lodged with the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority, considerable behind-the-scenes influence is being exerted on regulatory bodies to eliminate the requirement for Greek subtitles on Russian-language broadcasts. This move is intended to restrict the channel’s viewership and, consequently, diminish its appeal to Cypriot advertisers.

The Russian-language channel has recently obtained a provisional broadcasting licence, contingent upon the inclusion of Greek subtitles in its programming. This condition was imposed to enable the Cyprus Radio Television Authority to monitor the channel’s content without the need to employ additional Russian-speaking staff. The licences for this channel, along with all other non-subscription channels in Cyprus, expired on 30 June 2018. The Authority is presently evaluating applications for new temporary licences, which will remain valid until 30 June 2019.

From the outset, shareholders of the company responsible for establishing and operating the Russian-language channel have expressed willingness to comply with the Cyprus Broadcasting Authority’s directives and have already engaged firms with expertise in subtitling. According to informed sources, members of the Authority’s Board of Directors are contemplating revoking the subtitle mandate. Overall, indications suggest that the Authority is moving toward a partial relaxation of this requirement, whereby only certain broadcasts, rather than all, may be subject to subtitling.

input: Looks like Mayor Fred Eisenberger's puppy, Dash, will have a new friend to visit when he heads to work with the mayor this summer. Pictured here is Ralph, the creation of the City of Hamilton's horticultural staff. The approximately 15-foot sculpture was developed using Carex buchananii (leatherleaf sedge), a sage grass native to New Zealand and grown in the city greenhouses this spring. The grasses were rooted into a frame created by local metal artist Trevor McInytre with the internal infrastructure designed and implemented by the horticultural staff. This includes soil and a watering system inside the sculpture to keep Ralph's "fur" healthy and growing throughout the hot summer. The whimsical garden's designs were initiated by Marcia Monaghan, superintendent of horticulture for the city. She says her inspiration came from seeing Mosaic Culture, a huge horticultural display in Ottawa last year. Monaghan says that despite all the significant dog references — including the mayor's dog, the OHL-winning Bulldogs and the fact that it is the Year of the Dog in Chinese culture — none of these were actually the inspiration for the sculpture. Monaghan says, "We just thought it would be fun." The gardens, which also include a huge butterfly, will be completed midday Friday.
rewrite: Mayor Fred Eisenberger’s dog, Dash, will soon have a new companion to encounter during visits to the mayor’s workplace this summer. This companion is Ralph, a sculptural form created by the City of Hamilton’s horticultural staff. The approximately 15-foot sculpture is composed primarily of Carex buchananii (leatherleaf sedge), a sage grass indigenous to New Zealand that was cultivated in municipal greenhouses this spring. The grasses were affixed to a metal framework fabricated by local artist Trevor McInytre, while the internal infrastructure—including soil and an integrated irrigation system—was designed and installed by horticultural personnel to sustain the plant material throughout the summer season. The concept for this whimsical garden installation originated with Marcia Monaghan, the city’s Superintendent of Horticulture, who drew inspiration from viewing Mosaic Culture, a major horticultural exhibition in Ottawa last year. Monaghan clarifies that, despite numerous contextual canine associations—such as the mayor’s pet, the OHL-winning Bulldogs, and the Chinese zodiac’s Year of the Dog—these did not directly influence the sculpture’s design. Instead, she states, “We just thought it would be fun.” The garden, which also features a large butterfly sculpture, is scheduled for completion by midday on Friday.

VICTORIA — Here are questions Attorney General David Eby has recommended to cabinet for a referendum this fall on British Columbia’s electoral system:
1. Which should British Columbia use for elections to the legislative assembly (Vote for only one):
— The current first-past-the post voting system.
— A proportional representation voting system.
2. If British Columbia adopts a proportional representation voting system, which of the following voting systems do you prefer? (Vote for the voting systems you wish to support by ranking them in order of preference. You may choose to support one, two or all three of the systems):
— Dual-member proportional.
— Mixed-member proportional.
— Rural-urban.
——
Here is a look at the three systems of proportional representation that have been recommended:
— Dual-member proportional would take most of the province’s existing single-member electoral districts and amalgamate them with a second neighbouring district to create two-member districts. The largest rural districts could remain unchanged as single-member districts. Parties could nominate up to two candidates in each district. They would appear on the ballot in an order determined by the party. The first seats would be won by the first candidates of the party that received the most votes in each electoral district. The second seats would be allocated based on provincewide voting results and individual district results.
— A mixed-member system would combine single-member electoral districts, where members are elected under first past the post, with seats also allocated on a regional or provincial level and based on a list of candidates running for proportional representation seats prepared by the parties.
— A rural-urban option is also a mixed system that elects members of the legislature two ways. In urban and semi-urban areas, a single transferable vote would be used to rank candidates by preference. In rural areas, single-member electoral districts would elect their representative using the first-past-the-post system, while a small number of proportional representation seats would also be allocated from a list prepared by the parties based on election results.
rewrite:
The Attorney General of British Columbia, David Eby, has submitted the following questions for cabinet consideration, to be posed in a provincial referendum on electoral reform scheduled for the autumn. The referendum will present voters with two distinct queries.

The first question will be: "Which electoral system should British Columbia use for elections to the legislative assembly? (Vote for only one.)" The options provided will be the existing first-past-the-post system or a proportional representation voting system.

Should the electorate endorse a move to proportional representation, a second question will be presented: "If British Columbia adopts a proportional representation voting system, which of the following voting systems do you prefer? (Vote for the voting systems you wish to support by ranking them in order of preference. You may choose to support one, two, or all three of the systems.)" The specific systems listed for preferential ranking are Dual-Member Proportional, Mixed-Member Proportional, and the Rural-Urban system.

Three distinct models of proportional representation have been recommended for consideration. The Dual-Member Proportional model would primarily combine existing single-member electoral districts into larger, two-member districts, though the most extensive rural districts could remain single-member. Parties would nominate ranked pairs of candidates in each district. The first seat in a district would be awarded to the leading candidate of the party receiving the most votes, with the second seat allocated subsequently to correct for provincial disproportionality.

A Mixed-Member Proportional system would retain single-member districts elected by first-past-the-post, while supplementing these with additional members elected from regional or provincial party lists to ensure overall proportionality between seat share and vote share.

Finally, the Rural-Urban Proportional model employs a hybrid approach. In urban and semi-urban areas, members would be elected using the Single Transferable Vote, a preferential system facilitating proportional outcomes within multi-member districts. In rural areas, the model would maintain first-past-the-post elections for local representatives, augmented by a limited number of top-up seats allocated from party lists to enhance proportionality.

eClinicalWorks launches telehealth solution on healow mobile app
eClinicalWorks, a provider of healthcare IT solutions, has made its telehealth solution available on its Health & Online Wellness (healow) mobile app.
This service will provide patients with live video visits.
The TeleVisits feature has been integrated within the eClinicalWorks electronic health records (EHR) Platform.
All information, submitted or shared by patients using this solution, can be imported into the HER, which in turn supports workflow, clinical research and boosts patient satisfaction as they will have access to care whenever and wherever it is required.
Further, telehealth is becoming mainstream, several providers are making investments in third-party services instead of offering it as a standard service integrated with the practice’s existing technology.
This in turn leaves patients with the trouble of downloading additional apps, remembering login information and then experiencing the inconvenience of not having their telehealth summaries linked with their personal health records.
healow TeleVisits offers a seamless experience for patients and providers with EHR integration being in place.

“In today’s digital health age, patients are interested in care solutions that offer quicker delivery and flexibility. Additionally, providers are seeing benefits with increased patient engagement and streamlined workflow.”

A critical feature of this offering is its native integration with the eClinicalWorks electronic health record (EHR) platform. All data generated during these virtual encounters is seamlessly incorporated into the patient's EHR. This integration is designed to support clinical workflows, aid in research initiatives, and enhance patient satisfaction by enabling access to care without temporal or geographic constraints.

WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court ruled Tuesday that thousands of victims of terrorist attacks overseas cannot sue a foreign bank under a U.S. law dating from the 1700s.
By a 5-4 vote, the court refused to revive lawsuits, dismissed by the lower courts, that sought to hold Arab Bank, which is headquartered in Jordan, responsible for attacks against foreign nationals in the Middle East. More than 6,000 survivors and relatives of those killed in the West Bank and Gaza claimed that officials of the bank were complicit in the attacks.
Beginning in 2004, the victims filed a series of lawsuits accusing the bank of helping to finance Hamas and other terror organizations. The legal action was filed in the U.S. and aimed at Arab Bank through its branch in New York. The lead plaintiff in the case before the Supreme Court, Joseph Jesner, lost his 19-year-old son to a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv.
The lawsuits invoked one of the first laws ever passed by Congress, the Alien Tort Statute of 1789, known as ATS, intended to be a forum for resolving claims of piracy. But Tuesday's ruling said the law did not allow lawsuits of the kind filed by the terror victims.
"Absent further action from Congress, it would be inappropriate for courts to extend ATS liability to foreign corporations," wrote Justice Anthony Kennedy for the court's majority.
"Courts are not well suited to make the required policy judgments that are implicated by corporate liability in cases like this one."
rewrite:
In a 5-4 decision issued on Tuesday, the United States Supreme Court ruled that victims of overseas terrorist attacks are precluded from pursuing litigation against foreign corporations under the Alien Tort Statute (ATS) of 1789. The ruling definitively bars the revival of lawsuits, previously dismissed by lower courts, which sought to hold Jordan-based Arab Bank liable for attacks against foreign nationals in the West Bank and Gaza. These suits, representing over 6,000 claimants comprising survivors and relatives of the deceased, alleged the bank's complicity in facilitating terrorist activities.

The litigation originated in 2004 with a series of actions filed in U.S. courts, targeting Arab Bank through its New York branch. Plaintiffs accused the institution of providing financial support to Hamas and other terrorist organizations. A representative case was brought by Joseph Jesner, the lead plaintiff before the Supreme Court, whose nineteen-year-old son was killed in a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv. The plaintiffs sought recourse under the ATS, an eighteenth-century statute originally intended to address claims of piracy and provide a judicial forum for certain violations of international law.

The Court's majority, in an opinion authored by Justice Anthony Kennedy, concluded that the ATS does not provide a cause of action against foreign corporations. The opinion emphasized the judicial branch's limited institutional capacity in this domain, stating, "Courts are not well suited to make the required policy judgments that are implicated by corporate liability in cases like this one." The ruling explicitly deferred to the legislative branch, noting that "absent further action from Congress, it would be inappropriate for courts to extend ATS liability to foreign corporations." This decision thus forecloses this avenue of civil remedy for international terrorism victims under the current statutory framework.
