* North American pharma customers reluctant to place orders
* 2017 revenue seen at lower end of guidance range
* Shares drop almost 6 percent (Adds details on outlook, shares, analyst comment)
FRANKFURT, April 6 German drugs-packaging firm Gerresheimer on Thursday said its major pharmaceutical customers had been more cautious in placing orders due to uncertainty over the new U.S. administration's policies, sending its shares lower.
Revenues at Gerresheimer's business division that makes glass bottles and vials for drugs fell 2.9 percent in its fiscal first quarter through the end of February as sales in North America slipped.
"Greater uncertainty with regard to the new U.S. government triggered a relatively pronounced reticence among a number of large pharma customers to place orders," Gerresheimer said in a statement, adding that European cosmetic glass sales had risen.
President Donald Trump has promised to increase competition in the pharmaceutical industry without giving details, while promised healthcare reform has been delayed, leaving drugmakers uncertain as to how pricing and demand may be affected.
Overall, Gerresheimer's revenues were down more than 5 percent at 302.8 million euros ($323.1 million) in the quarter, missing analyst consensus of 307 million euros in a Reuters poll.
The group said it expected full-year revenues at the lower end of its forecast range of 1.405 billion to 1.455 billion euros. Analysts on average see 2017 revenues of 1.43 billion euros.
Shares in Gerresheimer fell 5.9 percent in early trading to the bottom of the German mid-cap index, which slipped 0.4 percent.
"The fact that the management currently sees just the lower end of the FY revenue guidance should not come as a major negative surprise after the expected slow start to the year," said DZ Bank analyst Sven Kuerten, reiterating his "buy" rating.
Gerresheimer reiterated that adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) should rise to around 320 million euros this year from 308 million in 2016, after a 6 percent slide in the first quarter. ($1 = 0.9366 euros) (Reporting by Maria Sheahan and Georgina Prodhan; Editing by Victoria Bryan)
rewrite:
On April 6, the German pharmaceutical packaging firm Gerresheimer indicated that heightened caution among its major North American clients, attributed to policy uncertainties under the new U.S. administration, had adversely impacted order volumes and consequently its financial performance. This announcement precipitated a decline in the company's share price.

For the fiscal first quarter ending in February, Gerresheimer reported a 2.9 percent revenue decline within its primary business division, which manufactures glass bottles and vials for pharmaceuticals. This decrease was driven primarily by a contraction in North American sales. The company attributed this trend to a "pronounced reticence" among several significant pharmaceutical customers to place orders, a direct consequence of the greater uncertainty surrounding the regulatory and healthcare policy direction of the new U.S. government. This cautious stance among drugmakers persists despite unfulfilled promises of healthcare reform and stated intentions to increase industry competition by President Donald Trump, leaving the sector unclear on future implications for drug pricing and demand. Conversely, the company noted an increase in sales within its European cosmetic glass segment.

Gerresheimer's total quarterly revenue fell by over 5 percent to 302.8 million euros ($323.1 million), falling short of the 307 million euro analyst consensus forecast in a Reuters survey. As a result, the company stated it now anticipates full-year revenues to align with the lower end of its previously guided range of 1.405 billion to 1.455 billion euros, compared to an average analyst projection of 1.43 billion euros. Concurrently, the company's shares declined by 5.9 percent in early trading, underperforming the broader German mid-cap index, which saw a 0.4 percent decrease.

Analyst commentary suggested the revised outlook was anticipated. DZ Bank analyst Sven Kuerten, reiterating a "buy" rating, noted that the management's expectation for revenues at the lower end of the annual guidance range should not be a major surprise following an expected slow start to the year. Despite a 6 percent decline in adjusted EBITDA for the first quarter, Gerresheimer reaffirmed its full-year forecast for this metric to rise to approximately 320 million euros, up from 308 million euros in 2016.

Johnstone has had numerous loans in the EFL Championship, including spells at Aston Villa, Preston North End and Doncaster Rovers, but failed to make a Premier League appearance for United.
And the 25-year-old will now have a chance to continue building his reputation at West Brom, who are reported to have paid an initial £6.5m.
Johnstone has signed a four-year deal at The Hawthorns and is keen to get started at his new club.
"I'm happy to be here. I've spoken to a lot of people about the club and heard nothing but good things," Johnstone told the West Brom website.
"It's good to get through the door. I've played Championship games and won a promotion from League One with Preston but always seemed to end up back at Manchester United or going somewhere else.
"Now it's time to settle down and take my game up to the next level which I believe I can do here."
Head coach Darren Moore said: "Sam is young and determined to be the best keeper he can possibly be - he's hungry to do that with us at Albion.
"We've had him targeted from the outset and we're all delighted to have him on board. He buys into exactly what we are trying to achieve and will hopefully represent the shape of things to come."
Johnstone's arrival could hasten the departure of another ex-United goalkeeper, Ben Foster.
Former England international Foster has been linked with a switch to Watford, while United are reportedly ready to replace Johnstone with Stoke City goalkeeper Lee Grant.
rewrite:
Sam Johnstone has undertaken multiple loan assignments within the EFL Championship, featuring for clubs such as Aston Villa, Preston North End, and Doncaster Rovers, yet he did not secure a first-team appearance for Manchester United in the Premier League. Now aged 25, the goalkeeper has the opportunity to further develop his professional standing at West Bromwich Albion, which is understood to have remitted an initial fee of £6.5 million for his services. Johnstone has committed to a four-year contract at The Hawthorns and expressed eagerness to commence this new chapter. In a statement published on the club’s official website, he remarked, “I am pleased to finalise this move. My inquiries about the club yielded consistently positive feedback. Having gained extensive experience in the Championship and achieved promotion from League One with Preston, my career has previously involved returns to Manchester United or further loan spells. I now aim to establish stability and elevate my performance, which I am confident this environment will facilitate.”

Head coach Darren Moore provided his assessment, stating, “Sam possesses a youthful determination to maximize his potential as a goalkeeper and is keen to pursue that ambition with us. He was a primary transfer target, and his acquisition is a source of satisfaction for the club. His philosophy aligns with our strategic objectives, and we anticipate he will exemplify the future direction of the team.” Johnstone’s signing may accelerate the exit of another former Manchester United goalkeeper, Ben Foster. The former England international has been associated with a potential transfer to Watford. Concurrently, reports suggest Manchester United are prepared to recruit Stoke City’s Lee Grant as Johnstone’s replacement.

Smoke rises behind a supermarket near Lisbon after a small plane crashed. Portuguese officials say a small plane has crashed beside a supermarket near Lisbon, killing four people on board the aircraft and one on the ground. Four people were slightly injured. (Ramiro Ribeiro via AP)
LISBON, Portugal (AP) — A small plane crashed Monday beside a supermarket near Lisbon, killing four people on board the aircraft and one on the ground. Four people were slightly injured, emergency services said.
The dead included the Swiss pilot, three French passengers on the plane and a Portuguese truck driver, emergency services operational commander Miguel Cruz told The Associated Press.
The Swiss-registered plane crashed shortly after a noon takeoff from the small Tires airfield, 20 kilometers (12 miles) west of the Portuguese capital, Cruz said. Officials said the crash happened amid clear skies and a light wind.
The Tires airfield said the plane was a twin-engine Piper PA-31 Navajo aircraft. The airfield was closed as authorities opened an investigation.
The truck driver was offloading his cargo at the supermarket's rear cargo bay, about 2 kilometers (just over 1 mile) from the runway, when the plane crashed near him. His truck was set ablaze.
Authorities declined to identify those killed in the plane until their identities could be compared with the flight plan.
The injured were shopping inside the supermarket and were treated for shock and smoke inhalation. The crash occurred about 150 meters (yards) from an elementary school.
About three dozen firefighting vehicles rushed to the scene, arriving within six minutes, according to officials. Nearby houses were blackened by smoke, with nine people forced to evacuate their homes.
rewrite:
On Monday, a fatal aviation accident occurred adjacent to a supermarket in the vicinity of Lisbon, Portugal, resulting in five fatalities and four minor injuries. According to emergency services, the crash involved a small, twin-engine Piper PA-31 Navajo aircraft, which was registered in Switzerland. The aircraft departed from Tires airfield, located approximately 20 kilometers west of the capital, shortly after noon under reported conditions of clear skies and light wind. It subsequently crashed near the commercial establishment.

Operational commander Miguel Cruz of the emergency services confirmed the casualties to The Associated Press. The deceased comprised the Swiss pilot, three French passengers aboard the aircraft, and a Portuguese truck driver who was present on the ground. The driver was in the process of unloading cargo at the supermarket's rear bay, situated roughly two kilometers from the airfield's runway, when the incident occurred; the impact ignited his vehicle. The four individuals who sustained minor injuries were inside the supermarket at the time and received treatment for shock and smoke inhalation. Authorities have withheld formal identification of the aircraft's occupants pending verification against the submitted flight plan.

The crash site, which was approximately 150 meters from a local elementary school, prompted a significant emergency response. Officials reported the deployment of approximately three dozen firefighting vehicles, which arrived at the scene within six minutes. The incident produced substantial smoke, which blackened nearby residences and necessitated the precautionary evacuation of nine individuals from their homes. In the aftermath, Tires airfield was temporarily closed as relevant authorities initiated an investigation into the cause of the crash.

(Adds background)
By Dan Levine
SAN FRANCISCO, March 30 The U.S. Justice Department on Thursday appealed a ruling by a federal judge in Hawaii extending a suspension of President Donald Trump's revised restrictions on travel from some Muslim-majority countries.
The appeal will be considered by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco, which last month upheld a suspension of Trump's first travel order.
Trump signed the revised ban earlier this month in a bid to overcome legal problems with a January executive order that caused chaos at airports and sparked mass protests before a Washington judge stopped its enforcement in February.
Trump has said the travel ban is needed for national security.
U.S. District Judge Derrick Watson on Wednesday turned an earlier temporary restraining order into a preliminary injunction in a lawsuit brought by the state of Hawaii.
The case challenged Trump's travel directive as unconstitutional religious discrimination. Hawaii and other opponents of the ban claim it is based on Trump's election campaign promise of "a total and complete shutdown of Muslims entering the United States."
"The court will not crawl into a corner, pull the shutters closed, and pretend it has not seen what it has," Watson wrote on Wednesday.
The Justice Department on Thursday also asked a Seattle federal judge to suspend separate litigation filed by Washington state against Trump's travel restrictions until after the 9th Circuit rules on the Hawaii appeal.
In addition, the Justice Department earlier this month appealed a ruling from a Maryland judge against Trump's revised executive order. That case will be heard by the 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Virginia. (Reporting by Dan Levine; Editing by Richard Chang)
rewrite:
On March 30, the United States Department of Justice filed an appeal contesting a ruling issued by a federal district judge in Hawaii. This ruling had converted a temporary restraining order into a preliminary injunction, thereby extending the suspension of President Donald Trump’s revised executive order imposing travel restrictions on nationals from several Muslim-majority countries. The appeal will be adjudicated by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in San Francisco, which previously upheld a suspension of the administration’s initial travel order in February.

The revised executive order was issued in March as an effort to address legal deficiencies identified in the January directive, which had provoked widespread disruption at airports and public demonstrations before being halted by a federal judge in Washington state. The administration maintains the policy is essential for national security. The state of Hawaii, in its lawsuit, contends the order constitutes unconstitutional religious discrimination, citing as evidence campaign statements in which President Trump advocated for “a total and complete shutdown of Muslims entering the United States.” In his Wednesday opinion, U.S. District Judge Derrick Watson asserted the court must consider this contextual background, stating, “The court will not crawl into a corner, pull the shutters closed, and pretend it has not seen what it has.”

Concurrently, the Justice Department has requested a federal judge in Seattle to suspend parallel litigation initiated by the state of Washington pending the Ninth Circuit’s decision on the Hawaii appeal. Separately, the Department has also appealed a ruling from a federal district judge in Maryland that blocked the revised order; that case is pending before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit in Virginia.

Breaking News Emails Get breaking news alerts and special reports. The news and stories that matter, delivered weekday mornings.
The “Ambien defense” has been used by people trying to excuse themselves for violent crime, for driving under the influence and even for sexual assault. Actress Roseanne Barr took it into a whole new territory on Wednesday when she used the sleeping aid as an excuse for a racist tweet that got her popular ABC television show canceled.
Roseanne’s Ambien defense got immediate blowback from Sanofi, which makes Ambien. “While all pharmaceutical treatments have side effects, racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication,” the company tweeted from its official account.
Doctors active on social media weighed in, too.
“Dear @therealroseanne Ambien does not make you racist, being racist makes you racist,” tweeted Dr. Jennifer Gunter, an outspoken obstetrician/gynecologist who practices at the San Francisco Medical Center.
“To be fair, Ambien might disinhibit, letting the unspoken racism out to be expressed publicly,” answered Dr. David Gorski, a surgeon at the Barbara Ann Karmanos Cancer Institute in Detroit.
Sleep specialists agree.
“Taking Ambien doesn’t take care of sleep deprivation. So the combination of sleep deprivation and medication side effects might result in disinhibited or bizarre behavior," said Azizi Seixas, who studies sleep behavior at New York University.
rewrite:
The "Ambien defense" has been invoked by individuals seeking to mitigate culpability for offenses including violent crime, driving under the influence, and even sexual assault. This strategy entered a novel domain when actress Roseanne Barr attributed a racist tweet—which resulted in the cancellation of her popular ABC television program—to the influence of the sedative medication. The manufacturer of Ambien, Sanofi, issued a prompt rebuttal via its official social media account, stating, "While all pharmaceutical treatments have side effects, racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication."

Medical professionals on social media platforms subsequently contributed to the discourse. Dr. Jennifer Gunter, an obstetrician-gynecologist at the San Francisco Medical Center, explicitly noted, "Ambien does not make you racist, being racist makes you racist." Dr. David Gorski, a surgeon at the Barbara Ann Karmanos Cancer Institute, offered a more nuanced perspective, suggesting that while Ambien may produce disinhibition, it merely allows pre-existing prejudices to be expressed publicly.

This view aligns with expert consensus on sleep pharmacology. Researchers, such as Azizi Seixas of New York University, clarify that sedative medications like Ambien do not address underlying sleep deprivation. The confluence of sleep deficiency and pharmacological side effects may precipitate disinhibited or otherwise aberrant behaviors, but these do not generate de novo racist ideation.

[India], Mar. 20 (ANI): The unidentified object recovered from a train in Uttar Pradesh's Hapur was not a bomb, experts said while giving due clearance.
Following an assessment by experts, the police administration cleared Sangam Express to ply further.
Speaking on the same, Hemant Kutiyal, Superintendent of Police (SP) Hapur, said, "We have checked everything, it seems like some kind of mischief by someone. The train will be sent off now. The watch that we have found is a normal watch."
Earlier, the Northern Railway had confirmed that they recovered an unidentified package from a coach of 14164 Sangam Express at a time it was stationed at Haripur. The concerned authorities, in a missive, had confirmed the news and said that the situation was being monitored. "A torch like-object, with wires attached to it, was found in a toilet of the train. Security forces are present here and the area has been cordoned off. We are taking all the necessary precautions," the police had said. The Northern Railway PRO had stated that the officers and staff of the railway were already on the site for a thorough checking. "We are ensuring that there is no threat to the passengers. The situation is being monitored by senior officers. We are taking this matter very seriously. All actions are being taken to ensure the safety of passengers," read the statement. (ANI)
rewrite:
On March 20, an unidentified object discovered aboard a train in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh, was determined by explosive experts not to be an explosive device, leading to official clearance for the train's departure. Following a security assessment, authorities permitted the 14164 Sangam Express to resume its journey. Hemant Kutiyal, Superintendent of Police for Hapur, subsequently stated that a comprehensive inspection had been conducted, indicating the incident was likely an act of mischief. He confirmed the recovered item was a standard wristwatch and announced the train's imminent release.

The incident originated when Northern Railway officials identified an unattended package within a coach of the stationary Sangam Express at Hapur station. Initial reports from police described the object as torch-like with attached wires, located in a train toilet. In response, security forces cordoned off the area and implemented precautionary measures. A Northern Railway spokesperson confirmed the immediate deployment of railway officers and staff for a thorough inspection. An official statement emphasized that senior officials were monitoring the situation with utmost seriousness, asserting that all necessary actions were being undertaken to ensure passenger safety and that no threat remained.

A photographer is appealing for holiday stories for a new arts and heritage project in Morecambe.
Johnny Bean and wife Carol are looking for memories and stories of Morecambe for the project, ‘High Teas and Holidays.’
Working in partnership with the Exchange Creative Community in West Street, memories, postcards, holiday memorabilia, guest house salvage and ephemera will be used as inspiration for new artworks.
The project will explore Morecambe’s heritage as a seaside holiday resort in the first half of the 20th century, paying homage to the hard-working seaside landlady and the role of the humble seaside postcard.
To begin the project the artists will be researching the history of local guest houses, particularly in the West End.
To find out more about the project you can meet Carol, Johnny and members of the Exchange for an informal chat at The Exchange on Wednesday February 7 from 1-4pm or at Morecambe Central library on Saturday February 10 from 11-2pm.
You can also engage with the project by emailing highteas@beanphoto.co.uk. Picture shows from left, Diana Heyes, Irena Vettese, Claire and Morgane Cozler, Emma Thornton, Kay Dickinson, Angela Palmer, Jane Upton, Kathryn MacDonald and Paul Kondras.
rewrite:
A photographer is issuing a call for contributions to a new arts and heritage initiative in Morecambe. Johnny Bean, in collaboration with his wife Carol, is soliciting personal recollections and narratives pertaining to Morecambe for the project, entitled ‘High Teas and Holidays.’ This endeavour is being conducted in partnership with the Exchange Creative Community on West Street. Found materials, including memories, historical postcards, holiday memorabilia, items salvaged from guest houses, and various ephemera, will serve as source material and inspiration for the creation of new artworks.

The project aims to examine Morecambe’s historical identity as a coastal resort during the early-to-mid twentieth century. It will pay particular tribute to the diligent seaside landlady and acknowledge the cultural significance of the traditional seaside postcard. Initial research will focus on the history of local guesthouse accommodation, especially within the West End district.

Further information can be obtained through informal consultations with the artists and Exchange representatives at The Exchange on Wednesday, February 7th (1-4pm) or at Morecambe Central Library on Saturday, February 10th (11am-2pm). Contributions may also be submitted via email to highteas@beanphoto.co.uk. (Photograph caption, from left: Diana Heyes, Irena Vettese, Claire and Morgane Cozler, Emma Thornton, Kay Dickinson, Angela Palmer, Jane Upton, Kathryn MacDonald, and Paul Kondras).

Taraji P. Henson's dog of 16 years has died.
The 47-year-old actress has been left heartbroken after her beloved pet pooch Uncle Willie - who is believed to be a Yorkshire Terrier and Maltese cross breed - sadly lost his life on Thursday (05.10.17) following a long, happy and healthy life for her.
Taking to her Instagram account, the 'Empire' star uploaded a photograph of her furry friend alongside the caption: "Although I understand NOTHING lasts forever the pain is still very real. #RipUncleWillie He made it 16 long years. He truly was #BenjaminButton I will miss you soooooooooo much!!! (sic)."
The brunette beauty then shared a series of collages - featuring her and her canine having a cuddle - made by her fans and thanked them for their sweet messages.
The 'No Good Deed' star then dug through her archive to find a picture of her and Uncle Willie posing in an anti-animal abuse campaign for the animal rights organisation PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals) back in 2013.
Speaking at the time, she said: "Dogs, to me, are like children. They are the closest thing to God. They are so pure in their love, and all they do is aim to please."
This isn't the first time Taraji has shown just how much she loves animals either, as she previously stripped completely named for an anti-fur advert for the organisation.
She said of her campaign: "We're not just even talking about a full-length fur coat.
"I'm talking about just, like, fur on your gloves or on your jacket or--what goes into making that little piece of fur ripped my heart out."
Meanwhile, it's not known whether Taraji will get another dog to replace Uncle Willie.
rewrite:
The death of Taraji P. Henson’s canine companion, Uncle Willie, has occasioned profound grief for the actress. The pet, a Yorkshire Terrier and Maltese crossbreed believed to be sixteen years of age, passed away on October 5, 2017, following what is described as a lengthy and healthy life. Ms. Henson, aged forty-seven at the time, publicly expressed her sorrow via the social media platform Instagram. Accompanying a photograph of the animal, her caption read: “Although I understand NOTHING lasts forever the pain is still very real. #RipUncleWillie He made it 16 long years. He truly was #BenjaminButton I will miss you soooooooooo much!!! (sic).”

Subsequently, the performer, known for her role in the television series *Empire*, shared a collection of fan-created collages depicting her with the dog, expressing gratitude for the supportive messages received. LKM Recycling, a leading waste management company in the UK, offers shredding services to businesses that have confidential waste paper like old medical records, obsolete legal and financial documents and personal data of former employees.

Wichita Falls Police have confirmed to Newschannel 6 a WFISD employee is facing a charge of Failure to Report.
Texas state law requires a person in an official capacity to notify police and Child Protective Services within 48 hours of learning about or suspecting an incident involving any abuse of a child.
WFPD says its Crimes Against Juvenile detectives did reach out to the WFISD Police Chief and made them aware of the situation before these warrants were issued.
The WFISD has confirmed Haynes Elementary Principal Cindy Underwood has been placed on administrative leave but police have not released the name on the arrest warrant.

According to the WFPD, detectives from the Crimes Against Juvenile unit contacted the WFISD Police Chief to inform them of the situation prior to the issuance of warrants. While the WFISD has confirmed that Cindy Underwood, principal of Haynes Elementary, has been placed on administrative leave, the police have not disclosed the name listed on the arrest warrant. This incident represents the second such alleged offense involving a WFISD principal within the current year.

DENMARK – There are far more questions than answers in the disappearance of journalist Kim Wall, who hasn’t been heard from since she boarded Peter Madsen’s now-sunken submarine Thursday night on Denmark’s Refshaleoen island.
The sub has since been raised, and Wall’s body wasn’t in it. Madsen isn’t contesting a court decision to keep him in custody for up to 24 days as Danish police investigate, and while he has been charged with killing Wall by unknown means, his lawyer has denied he had anything to do with her vanishing.
The Local quotes a Sunday press conference with the Copenhagen Police deputy chief inspector, who said Madsen’s story has changed, from initially telling officials he dropped Wall off at 10:30pm Thursday night on the island to another unspecified explanation since.
The Guardian reports Madsen says they spent about three hours on his Nautilus sub, the largest privately made one in the world at the time of its 2008 launch; the Swedish journalist, who divides her time between New York and Beijing, was doing a profile on Madsen.
The Local also picks up a report from a Swedish tabloid that cites a witness who said Madsen’s sub was seen sailing without its lights on some two hours before Wall’s partner reported the vessel as missing around 2:30am Friday.
“There was very nearly a collision” between the sub and a freighter, per the witness. The Washington Post describes Wall as accomplished—the London School of Economics and Columbia University grad wrote for the New York Times, Guardian, and Atlantic, among others—and recounts her travels to Pyongyang, Sri Lanka, and the Marshall Islands for stories.
Journalist Kim Wall remains missing: "Denmark should not be considered a dangerous assignment for journalists." https://t.co/GO8bBuK5RP — CPJ (@pressfreedom) August 12, 2017
This article originally appeared on Newser: She Vanished After Boarding His Sub. Now, His Story Changes
More From Newser:
rewrite:
The disappearance of journalist Kim Wall, who was last seen boarding inventor Peter Madsen’s privately-built submarine on the evening of Thursday, August 10, 2017, near Refshaleoen island in Denmark, remains an unresolved and developing investigation. Despite the subsequent raising of the sunken vessel, Wall’s body was not recovered from within it. Madsen, who has been charged with the killing of Wall by unspecified means, is not contesting a court order for his custody to be extended for up to 24 days to facilitate the ongoing police inquiry. His legal counsel has formally denied any involvement in her disappearance.

Authorities have indicated inconsistencies in Madsen’s account of events. During a press conference, Copenhagen Police deputy chief inspector noted that Madsen’s initial statement—claiming he disembarked Wall safely at approximately 10:30 p.m. on Thursday—has since been replaced by an alternative, undisclosed version. According to reports from *The Guardian*, Madsen stated that he and Wall spent roughly three hours aboard the *Nautilus*, a submarine notable for being the largest privately constructed vessel of its kind upon its 2008 launch. Wall, a Swedish journalist residing intermittently in New York and Beijing, was reportedly conducting an interview profile of Madsen at the time.

Further complicating the timeline, a witness cited in a Swedish tabloid report, referenced by *The Local*, observed the submarine navigating without its lights approximately two hours prior to Wall’s partner reporting it missing at 2:30 a.m. on Friday. The witness described a near-collision with a commercial freighter during this period. Wall is recognized as an accomplished correspondent, holding degrees from the London School of Economics and Columbia University, and her work has appeared in publications including *The New York Times*, *The Guardian*, and *The Atlantic*. Her professional assignments had previously taken her to diverse locations such as Pyongyang, Sri Lanka, and the Marshall Islands. The case has prompted commentary from press freedom organizations, with the Committee to Protect Journalists noting on social media that Denmark is not typically regarded as a high-risk environment for journalistic work.

A federal judge on Monday ordered LinkedIn Corp. to allow a startup company to scrape data publicly posted by LinkedIn users.
The decision marked a potentially precedent-setting defeat for the Microsoft Corp. MSFT, +1.50% -owned social-networking site in a case with deep implications for the growing industry of data analytics.
The ruling came in a lawsuit brought by hiQ Labs, a San Francisco company founded in 2012 that mines and analyzes publicly available personal data on LinkedIn to predict whether individual employees are likely to leave their jobs. HiQ sued LinkedIn in June after LinkedIn ordered hiQ to stop accessing its site and accused the startup of violating a federal antihacking law.
On Monday, U.S. District Judge Edward M. Chen in San Francisco granted a preliminary injunction giving hiQ access to LinkedIn, for now. In a 25-page opinion, Judge Chen said the 1986 Computer Fraud and Abuse Act wasn’t meant to outlaw the data the collection of online public information.
An expanded version of this report appears on WSJ.com.

rewrite:
On Monday, a federal judge mandated that LinkedIn Corporation permit a startup firm to extract, or "scrape," data publicly posted by users on its platform. This ruling represents a potentially significant legal setback for the social-networking service, owned by Microsoft Corp., and may establish a precedent with profound consequences for the expanding field of data analytics. The litigation was initiated by hiQ Labs, a San Francisco-based enterprise established in 2012, which utilizes publicly accessible personal data from LinkedIn to analyze employee attrition risks. HiQ filed suit in June after LinkedIn demanded it cease accessing the site, alleging violations of the federal Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA).

U.S. District Judge Edward M. Chen of the Northern District of California issued a preliminary injunction, temporarily restoring hiQ's access to the public data. In a 25-page opinion, Judge Chen contended that the 1986 CFAA was not designed to prohibit the collection of publicly available online information. This decision underscores a critical judicial interpretation regarding the limits of anti-hacking statutes in the context of publicly accessible web data.

The Mark Anthony De Simone homicide trial is back on track, only a few days behind schedule. Jury selection is scheduled to begin Wednesday.
A prosecution witness testified during a pre-trial evidentiary hearing Tuesday in Juneau Superior Court about a comment De Simone allegedly said to him immediately after the May 2016 shooting of Duilio Antonio “Tony” Rosales.
The witness said he later passed on the information to the Alaska State Trooper investigator in charge of the case.
The investigator testified he had no record of that particular conversation with the witness.
Judge Philip Pallenberg didn’t believe it was a discovery violation or there was any misconduct involved with disclosure of the new information.
De Simone’s defense doesn’t need a continuance or delay to review the witness’ statements, and Pallenberg scheduled the trial’s jury selection to begin Wednesday morning.
De Simone is accused of shooting Rosales at a hunting cabin in Excursion Inlet. Trial was scheduled to begin Monday until the witness revealed De Simone’s alleged comment Friday.
Pallenberg asked Lemon Creek Correctional Center staff Tuesday to allow De Simone to change into clean civilian or street clothes for each day of the trial.
During previous trials, defendants were forced to wear dirty civilian clothes or prison-issued slip-on shoes, which could be prejudicial in the jury’s eyes.
Pallenberg referred to a 1974 Alaska Supreme Court case that specified “every defendant should have the appearance and dignity of an innocent man,” and they should be clean and presentable with an opportunity to shave and shower.
rewrite:
The homicide trial of Mark Anthony De Simone has resumed, experiencing a delay of only several days. Jury selection is now scheduled to commence on Wednesday.

During a pre-trial evidentiary hearing held Tuesday in Juneau Superior Court, a prosecution witness provided testimony regarding an alleged statement made by De Simone to him following the May 2016 fatal shooting of Duilio Antonio “Tony” Rosales. This witness stated that he subsequently relayed this information to the lead Alaska State Trooper investigator assigned to the case. The investigator, in his own testimony, indicated he possessed no documentation of this specific exchange with the witness.

Presiding Judge Philip Pallenberg determined that the recent disclosure of this information did not constitute a discovery violation nor involve prosecutorial misconduct. Given that the defense did not request a continuance to examine the witness's account, Judge Pallenberg ordered jury selection to proceed on Wednesday morning.

De Simone stands accused of shooting Rosales at a hunting cabin in Excursion Inlet. The trial was originally set to begin on Monday, but was delayed following the witness's disclosure of the alleged statement on Friday.

In a separate procedural matter, Judge Pallenberg directed staff at the Lemon Creek Correctional Center on Tuesday to ensure De Simone is provided with clean civilian attire for each day of the trial. This instruction references concerns from prior proceedings where defendants appeared in soiled clothing or prison-issued footwear, which may create prejudicial perceptions among jurors. Pallenberg cited a 1974 Alaska Supreme Court ruling which holds that defendants are entitled to maintain the appearance and dignity of an innocent person, including being clean, presentable, and afforded opportunities for grooming.

WASHINGTON (Sputnik) - The Trump administration is expected to announce on Thursday that the United States will impose steel and aluminum tariffs on EU states after Washington was unable to win concessions, media reported.
US negotiators failed to reach a deal on the tariffs with EU counterparts ahead of a Friday deadline, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday citing people familiar with the situation.
In March, the Trump administration imposed 10 percent tariffs on imported steel and 25 percent aluminum. The European Union was granted temporary exemption due to expire on Friday. However, the bloc insisted that it should be permanently exempted from them.
Meanwhile, European Union Ambassador to the United States David O’Sullivan said earlier that the EU will likely respond with "counterbalancing" tariffs on US products.
"If tariffs are imposed, I fear we will exercise our right under the World Trade Organization (WTO) to have rebalancing tariffs," O’Sullivan told a meeting at the Woodrow Wilson Center. "We really don't understand the logic of this."
"We are not happy with the prospect of tariffs on steel on and aluminum. We feel it is not legitimate to export additional tariffs on legitimate European exports of steel and aluminum… They're not even produced here [in the United States] in many cases," O’Sullivan said.
Earlier on Wednesday, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire warned that if the European Union was attacked by the proposed US tariffs, the bloc would have to act to defend its own interests.
rewrite:
According to media reports, the Trump administration is anticipated to declare on Thursday that the United States will implement tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from European Union member states, following unsuccessful negotiations to secure concessions. As reported by the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday, citing informed sources, U.S. negotiators did not achieve an agreement with their EU counterparts prior to a Friday deadline. These tariffs, initially imposed in March at rates of 25 percent on aluminum and 10 percent on steel, had temporarily exempted the EU; this exemption is scheduled to lapse on Friday. The European bloc has consistently maintained that it should receive a permanent exemption from these measures.

In response, David O’Sullivan, the European Union’s Ambassador to the United States, indicated that the EU would likely enact "counterbalancing" tariffs on U.S. goods if the measures proceed. Speaking at an event hosted by the Woodrow Wilson Center, O’Sullivan stated the EU would consider exercising its World Trade Organization rights to implement rebalancing tariffs, expressing confusion over the rationale behind the U.S. action. He emphasized the EU's opposition, arguing that imposing additional tariffs on legitimate European exports is unjustified, particularly for products not widely manufactured within the United States. Echoing this stance, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire cautioned earlier on Wednesday that the EU would be compelled to take defensive actions to protect its interests if confronted by the proposed U.S. tariffs.

Plan Now for Salem's Night Out Against Crime
The registration deadline is July 21, 2017.
Image: www.nightoutsalem.com
(SALEM, Ore.) - The Salem Police Department is now accepting registrations for National Night Out block parties in Salem.
National Night Out is an evening dedicated to bringing residents and police together to stand united against crime through neighborhood block parties.
NNO is celebrated across the nation each year on the first Tuesday in August making August 1 the date for 2017. Block parties occur, generally, between 6 p.m. and 9 p.m.
"In Salem, it's our chance to demonstrate community unity against crime," said community relations analyst Angie Hedrick.
"Neighbors have block parties in the street with activities for children. And, sometimes it's just an ice cream social in the front yard or a barbecue potluck in the cul-de-sac.
"The point is the neighbors are reinforcing their watch out for each other atmosphere which helps keep crime off their block."
Block parties wishing to receive a visit from a special police team should register early as the slots for officer visits fill quickly.
"The highlight of our year is visiting block parties to just say hello to neighbors and thank them for being our partners in keeping Salem safe," said Hedrick.
The registration deadline is July 21, 2017. Register online and find more information at www.cityofsalem.net/nno. #nationalnightout #salemnightout
Source: News Release from Salem Police Dept.

rewrite:
The Salem Police Department announces the commencement of registration for National Night Out (NNO) block parties within the city. National Night Out is an annual nationwide event, observed on the first Tuesday of August—August 1 in 2017—dedicated to fostering community solidarity and partnership between residents and law enforcement in the collective effort to deter crime. Neighborhood gatherings are typically scheduled between 6:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m.

Community Relations Analyst Angie Hedrick emphasized the event’s local significance, stating, “In Salem, it is an opportunity to demonstrate communal unity against criminal activity.” She described the varied nature of these gatherings, which range from organized children’s activities in closed-off streets to informal social events such as front-yard ice cream socials or cul-de-sac barbecue potlucks. “The fundamental objective,” Hedrick noted, “is for neighbors to reinforce a mutual surveillance and care atmosphere, a dynamic that contributes directly to crime prevention within the neighborhood.”

Block party organizers seeking a visit from a police unit are advised to register promptly, as the schedule for officer appearances is limited and fills rapidly. Hedrick identified these visits as a departmental priority, remarking, “A highlight of our year is the opportunity to greet residents personally and express gratitude for their essential role as partners in maintaining Salem’s safety.”

The registration deadline is July 21, 2017. Complete registration and obtain further information via the official city website at www.cityofsalem.net/nno.

Benje Choucroun turned up at the White House briefing on Wednesday, catching everyone's attention when he asked Press Secretary Sarah Sanders about school shootings.
"At my school, we recently had a lockdown drill," Choucron, 13, said, reading from a piece of paper. "One thing that affects mine and others' mental health is the worry that we or our friends could get shot at school."
Choucron, a student at Marin Country Day School in California, continued: "Specifically, can you tell me what the administration has done and will do to prevent these senseless tragedies?"
Sanders appeared to tear up during her response.

"I think that as a kid and certainly as a parent, there is nothing more terrifying than for a kid to go to school and not feel safe, so I'm sorry that you feel that way," she said. "This administration takes it seriously and the school safety commission that the president convened is meeting this week, again, an official meeting, to discuss the best ways forward and how we can do every single thing within our power to protect kids within our schools and to make them feel safe and to make their parents feel good about dropping them off."

rewrite:
During Wednesday's White House press briefing, Benje Choucroun, a thirteen-year-old student, attracted notable attention by directing a question to Press Secretary Sarah Sanders concerning the issue of school shootings. Reading from a prepared statement, Choucroun, who attends Marin Country Day School in California, stated, "At my school, we recently had a lockdown drill. One thing that affects mine and others' mental health is the worry that we or our friends could get shot at school." He proceeded to inquire, "Specifically, can you tell me what the administration has done and will do to prevent these senseless tragedies?"

In her response, Sanders appeared visibly moved. She replied, "I think that as a kid and certainly as a parent, there is nothing more terrifying than for a kid to go to school and not feel safe, so I'm sorry that you feel that way." She further outlined administrative actions, noting, "This administration takes it seriously and the school safety commission that the president convened is meeting this week, again, an official meeting, to discuss the best ways forward and how we can do every single thing within our power to protect kids within our schools and to make them feel safe and to make their parents feel good about dropping them off."

Choucroun was present in Washington, D.C., to report on the White House Sports and Fitness Day for *Time for Kids* magazine. The exchange was subsequently highlighted on social media, drawing public focus to the student's question and the administration's stated commitment to school safety.

President Donald Trump’s lawyer Rudy Giuliani spoke to reporters Wednesday, encouraging Special Counsel Robert Muller to wrap up the special investigation at the risk of affecting the midterm elections.
“People should have an answer, even if they put together whatever the heck they have, interview or no interview. By September 1 the public should have an explanation of what Mueller has,” Giuliani told Breitbart News. “I really want that because I really don’t think he has much.”
Giuliani made his impromptu comments to a few reporters as he attended an event promoting sports and fitness. He compared the Muller investigation to former FBI Director James Comey’s handling of the Hillary Clinton e-mail investigation, describing it as “meddling” in the election.
“If he doesn’t file his report by September 1, mid-September, he’s clearly going to pull a Comey,” Giuliani said.
He denied that Trump was going to fire Mueller.
When asked if he thought Democrats wanted to see the investigation stretch out pasted the midterms, he agreed.
“Damn right they do,” he said. “It might be a mistake. It may be the American people have concluded that impeachment is not proper.”
rewrite:
On Wednesday, Rudy Giuliani, legal counsel to former President Donald Trump, addressed members of the press, urging Special Counsel Robert Mueller to conclude his inquiry promptly to avoid potential influence on the upcoming midterm elections. In remarks provided to Breitbart News, Giuliani stated, “The public deserves a resolution, irrespective of whether an interview is conducted. By September 1, there should be a public accounting of Mueller’s findings.” He added, “I strongly believe this is necessary, as I am skeptical that the investigation has yielded substantial evidence.” Giuliani offered these extemporaneous comments while attending a sports and wellness promotion event.

He drew a parallel between Mueller’s probe and former FBI Director James Comey’s management of the Hillary Clinton email investigation, characterizing both as electoral “meddling.” Giuliani asserted, “Should he fail to issue a report by early to mid-September, he will essentially be replicating Comey’s actions.” He further denied any intention by Trump to dismiss Mueller. When questioned on whether he believed Democratic lawmakers preferred to prolong the investigation beyond the midterms, Giuliani concurred, responding, “Absolutely. However, this could prove misguided, as the public may have already determined that impeachment proceedings are unwarranted.”

James Alex Fields Jr., the suspect accused of killing one woman by ramming his car into a group of protesters demonstrating against a downtown Charlottesville white nationalist rally Saturday afternoon, was denied bond during his initial appearance in court Monday, according to reports.
CNN reports the 20-year-old Maumee, Ohio, native appeared via video in front of a Charlottesville judge wearing a black and white jumpsuit.
Fields is being held on charges of second-degree murder, malicious wounding and failure to stop in an accident that resulted in death.
Derek Weimer, who taught Fields history at Randall K. Cooper High School in Kentucky, told the Toledo Blade that Fields expressed white-supremacy ideologies in school. Weimer added that he and other educators tried to change the student’s way of thinking.
“I felt it my mission to explain how vile the Nazis were,” Weimer said.
According to The Chicago Tribune, Weimer recalled that Fields wrote a paper about the Nazi military during World War II for a class called America’s Modern Wars. The teacher said the project was well-written and researched but appeared to be a “big lovefest for the German military and the Waffen-SS.”
“It was obvious that he had this fascination with Nazism and a big idolatry of Adolf Hitler,” Weimer told the newspaper. “He had white supremacist views. He really believed in that stuff.”
When he heard about the Charlottesville attack, the teacher felt guilty.
“My first feeling: I failed, we failed,” he told the Toledo Blade.
At least 26 people were taken to a local hospital from the rally and counter-protests, the Northwest Herald reports. At least 19 of those victims are believed to be injured in the car crash, according to the New York Times.
Charlottesville Mayor Michael Signer identified the fatal victim as 32-year-old Heather Heyer during an appearance on Meet The Press Sunday morning, according to NBC News.
“Heather was such a sweet soul, she did not deserve to die,” Marissa Blair, who was at the rally and friends with Heyer, told The New York Times.
rewrite:
James Alex Fields Jr., the individual charged in connection with the fatal vehicular assault on counter-protesters in Charlottesville, Virginia, was denied bond during his initial court appearance on Monday. The incident occurred on Saturday afternoon when a vehicle allegedly driven by Fields struck a crowd demonstrating against a white nationalist rally. According to judicial reports, the 20-year-old defendant from Maumee, Ohio, appeared via video link before a Charlottesville judge, attired in a black-and-white jumpsuit. The charges against him include second-degree murder, malicious wounding, and failure to stop at an accident resulting in death.

Historical context regarding the defendant’s background has emerged through interviews with former educators. Derek Weimer, who instructed Fields in a history course at Randall K. Cooper High School in Kentucky, informed the Toledo Blade that Fields had expressed white-supremacist ideologies during his schooling. Weimer stated that he and other faculty members actively attempted to counter these views. “I felt it my mission to explain how vile the Nazis were,” Weimer remarked. He further recalled to The Chicago Tribune that Fields had submitted a meticulously researched paper on the Nazi military for a class titled “America’s Modern Wars.” While academically sound, the project was described by Weimer as exhibiting a pronounced admiration for the German military and the Waffen-SS. “It was obvious that he had this fascination with Nazism and a big idolatry of Adolf Hitler,” Weimer noted, adding, “He had white supremacist views. He really believed in that stuff.” Upon learning of the Charlottesville attack, Weimer expressed a sense of professional failure, telling the Blade, “My first feeling: I failed, we failed.”

The aftermath of the rally and subsequent violence resulted in significant casualties. The Northwest Herald reported that at least twenty-six individuals were transported to a local hospital, with the New York Times indicating that no fewer than nineteen of these injuries stemmed from the vehicular incident. The fatality was publicly identified by Charlottesville Mayor Michael Signer on NBC’s *Meet the Press* as 32-year-old Heather Heyer. A friend and fellow rally attendee, Marissa Blair, memorialized Heyer to the New York Times, stating, “Heather was such a sweet soul, she did not deserve to die.”

FILE PHOTO: The logo of commodities trader Glencore is pictured in front of the company's headquarters in Baar, Switzerland, September 30, 2015. REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann/File Photo
LONDON Global diversified natural resource company Glencore (GLEN.L) has closed a $7.335 billion (£5.6 billion), one-year revolving credit facility that refinances an existing $7.7 billion, one-year revolver that was agreed in February 2016, the company said on Wednesday.
The one-year loan, which finances Glencore's trading operations, is part of a bigger loan package that also includes an existing US$6.8bn medium-term loan.
The unsecured facility has a 12-month extension option and a 12-month term-out option, which extends the final maturity until May 2019. The facility has no financial covenants.
The financing was launched at $5 billion and closed substantially oversubscribed after raising $8.55 billion in syndication from Glencore’s wide and supportive group of relationship banks.
A total of 56 banks committed to the facility, including 31 mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners.
Due to the low average utilisation of the company’s combined short and medium term facilities, the one-year facility was reduced to $7.335 billion.
Citigroup, Commerzbank, Standard Charted and UniCredit were active bookrunners on the financing.
(Editing by Tessa Walsh)
rewrite:
Glencore plc (GLEN.L), a global diversified natural resources group, announced the closure of a one-year, unsecured revolving credit facility totalling $7.335 billion. This arrangement refinances a prior one-year facility of $7.7 billion established in February 2016. The facility, which supports the company's trading activities, constitutes one component of a broader financing package that also incorporates a separate, existing medium-term loan of $6.8 billion. It features both a 12-month extension option and a 12-month term-out option, thereby potentially extending the final maturity date to May 2019, and carries no financial covenants.

Initially launched at $5 billion, the syndication process raised $8.55 billion in commitments, resulting in substantial oversubscription. A consortium of 56 relationship banks participated, with 31 institutions acting as mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners. Active bookrunning duties were performed by Citigroup, Commerzbank, Standard Chartered, and UniCredit. The finalized facility size was reduced from the committed amount to $7.335 billion, a decision attributed to the historically low average utilisation across Glencore's combined short and medium-term credit facilities.

Home prices in 20 U.S. cities grew in February at the fastest pace since mid-2014, underscoring the persistent scarcity of inventory amid strong demand, according to S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller data released Tuesday.
Highlights of Home Prices (February) 20-city property values index increased 6.8% y/y (est. 6.4%) after rising 6.4%; fastest gain since June 2014
National home-price gauge rose 6.3% y/y
Seasonally adjusted 20-city index rose 0.8% m/m (est. 0.7%); index level of 209.29 is highest in records back to 2000
Key Takeaways
The data showed monthly gains in all 20 cities, including strong advances in expensive areas such as Seattle and Los Angeles, along with cheaper regions including Cleveland and Detroit. Sales are getting a boost from the strong labor market and borrowing costs that are still relatively low, though they’ve been edging up in recent weeks.
At the same time, a shortage of available and affordable listings, especially of previously-owned houses, is sending prices higher and limiting purchases. Growth in property values continues to outpace wages, another hurdle for younger or first-time buyers looking to enter the housing market. Meanwhile, the ongoing price gains are translating into rising home equity for owners.
Official’s View
“With expectations for continued economic growth and further employment gains, the current run of rising prices is likely to continue,” David Blitzer, chairman of the S&P index committee, said in a statement.
Other Details
All 20 cities in the index showed year-over-year gains, led by a 12.7 percent increase in Seattle and an 11.6 percent advance in Las Vegas; Washington was slowest at 2.4 percent
After seasonal adjustment, Cleveland had the biggest month-over-month rise at 1.6 percent, followed by Detroit and Seattle with a 1.4 percent increase
Separate report from the Federal Housing Finance Agency showed its home-price index climbed 0.6 percent in February from a month earlier after a revised 0.9 percent increase
FHFA price index advanced 7.2 percent from February 2017
— With assistance by Kristy Scheuble
rewrite:
According to data released Tuesday by S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller, residential property values across twenty major U.S. metropolitan areas accelerated in February, registering the most rapid annual appreciation since mid-2014. This trend underscores the sustained pressure on housing inventories amidst robust demand. The 20-City Composite Index advanced by 6.8 percent year-over-year, exceeding the median estimate of 6.4 percent and accelerating from a 6.4 percent increase in the prior month. Concurrently, the broader National Home Price Index rose by 6.3 percent from the previous year. On a monthly basis, the seasonally adjusted 20-city index increased by 0.8 percent, marginally above the projected 0.7 percent, reaching a record index level of 209.29, the highest since the inception of the series in the year 2000.

The report indicated monthly price gains across all twenty constituent cities. Significant advances were observed in high-cost markets such as Seattle and Los Angeles, as well as in more moderately priced regions including Cleveland and Detroit. This widespread appreciation is being fueled by a resilient labor market and historically favorable, though recently rising, mortgage financing costs. A critical constraining factor remains a pronounced shortage of available and affordably priced listings, particularly within the existing home segment. This supply limitation continues to exert upward pressure on values and curtail transactional volume. Furthermore, the pace of home-price growth continues to exceed wage gains, presenting an additional barrier for younger and first-time buyers seeking market entry. Conversely, established homeowners are experiencing commensurate increases in housing equity.

David Blitzer, Chairman of the S&P Index Committee, noted in an accompanying statement, "Given expectations for sustained economic expansion and further employment gains, the current trajectory of rising prices is likely to persist." All cities posted annual gains, led by Seattle at 12.7 percent and Las Vegas at 11.6 percent, with Washington, D.C. recording the slowest growth at 2.4 percent. Following seasonal adjustment, Cleveland experienced the largest monthly increase at 1.6 percent, followed by Detroit and Seattle at 1.4 percent. In a separate report, the Federal Housing Finance Agency indicated its purchase-only home price index increased 0.6 percent in February from January, and advanced 7.2 percent from February 2017.

Keeping tabs on a tabby's tail can help pet owners understand their cat's behaviour much better.
But you also must take into account the cat's body language to fully understand what they are thinking about, University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine's Carlos Siracusa tells National Geographic.
A tapping tail while a cat is napping is "relaxed overall but paying attention to something happening around him, a sound or movement," said Siracusa. If the cat is actually sleeping, it could mean the cat is dreaming.
However, an alert cat that is whipping its tail could suggest nervousness and potential aggression. You would be wise to not touch the cat, Siracusa said.
A tail that is straight up with a curved tip means a cat is being friendly, while an aggressive cat may have its tale straight up.
A relaxed cat will "carry his tail in a neutral or low position," adds Siracusa, while a downward curve can mean defensiveness.
Although figuring out tail movements and what they mean can be a bit tricky, cat's legs tell owners what is really going on.
When a cat darts from one room to another for no apparent reason, sometimes called "the zoomies," it may be due to accumulated arousal, frustration, fear, or pent-up energy, said Siracusa.
In their natural habitat, cats would be climbing trees and chasing prey if they weren't cooped up inside a home, which is low on stimulation.
And cats are more active at dawn and dusk, while the rest of the day they are storing up energy, usually by sleeping or dozing off.
rewrite:
Observing feline tail positioning provides valuable insight into a cat’s behavioral state, according to Carlos Siracusa of the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine, who emphasizes that tail signals must be interpreted within the broader context of overall body language for accurate understanding. As reported by National Geographic, Siracusa notes that a gently tapping tail during rest indicates a relaxed yet attentive state, possibly in response to environmental stimuli; if the cat is asleep, such movement may correspond to dreaming. Conversely, a rapidly whipping tail in an alert cat often signals nervousness or potential aggression, during which physical contact should be avoided.

A vertically raised tail with a curved tip typically denotes a friendly disposition, whereas a fully erect, stiff tail may indicate aggression. A neutral or low tail carriage generally reflects relaxation, while a tail curved downward can suggest defensiveness. Although tail movements require careful interpretation, other behaviors, such as sudden bursts of activity—colloquially termed “the zoomies”—may reveal underlying states of accumulated arousal, frustration, fear, or pent-up energy. Siracusa explains that in domestic settings, cats often lack the stimulation provided in natural habitats, where activities like climbing and hunting would normally expend such energy. Furthermore, cats are crepuscular by nature, meaning they are most active at dawn and dusk; during other periods, they conserve energy primarily through rest or sleep.

HUNTSVILLE, Texas (AP) - Attorneys for a Texas inmate want the U.S. Supreme Court to halt his scheduled execution for the shooting deaths of a 5-year-old girl and her grandmother during a birthday party 10 years ago outside a Fort Worth apartment.
Former Fort Worth street gang member Erick Davila is set for lethal injection Wednesday evening.
This undated photo provided by the Texas Department of Criminal Justice shows Erick Davila. Attorneys for the Texas death row inmate want the U.S. Supreme Court to halt his scheduled execution this week for the shooting deaths of a 5-year-old girl and her grandmother during a birthday party 10 years ago outside a Fort Worth apartment. The former Fort Worth street gang member is set for lethal injection Wednesday, April 25, 2018. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice via AP)
Lawyers for the 31-year-old Davila argue it's improper for the elected Tarrant County district attorney to be involved in the case because she was the judge at Davila's 2009 trial. They also contend evidence that Davila may have been high on drugs at the time of the shooting improperly was withheld from defense attorneys.
State lawyers are contesting the arguments.
Davila was convicted of killing Queshawn Stevenson and her 48-year-old grandmother, Annette Stevenson.
rewrite:
Attorneys representing Texas death row inmate Erick Davila have petitioned the United States Supreme Court for a stay of his execution, which is scheduled for the evening of Wednesday, April 25, 2018. Davila was convicted for the fatal shootings of five-year-old Queshawn Stevenson and her 48-year-old grandmother, Annette Stevenson, a decade ago outside a Fort Worth apartment during a birthday celebration. A former member of a Fort Worth street gang, Davila is slated to receive a lethal injection.

His legal counsel advances two primary arguments in their appeal. First, they assert that the involvement of the elected Tarrant County District Attorney in the case constitutes a procedural impropriety, as she previously presided over Davila’s 2009 trial in her prior capacity as a judge. Second, they contend that exculpatory evidence suggesting Davila may have been under the influence of narcotics at the time of the offenses was improperly withheld from the defense team during trial proceedings. State prosecutors are currently contesting these claims before the Court.

Kate Upton is 24 years old and has as many banners as LeBron James.
And for Upton’s third year on the cover, Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition decided to honor the feat with a trifecta of its own. Upton will get three different covers in the 2017 edition, as was revealed Tuesday on Jimmy Kimmel Live.
The 2017 SI Swimsuit Covers have been revealed. Welcome back, @KateUpton! Follow the link for more photos and video https://t.co/4cszjybbVp pic.twitter.com/y7TguJdPVD — SI Swimsuit (@SI_Swimsuit) February 15, 2017
The cover of the Swimsuit Edition is a closely guarded secret, and Upton hadn’t even seen the images before Kimmel revealed them on TV.
Upton also was on the cover in 2012 and 2013. Last year’s edition featured three separate cover models: Ronda Rousey, Hailey Clauson and Ashley Graham.
Elle Macpherson is the only model with more cover appearances than Upton; she has five, mostly from the 1980s. Upton joins Christie Brinkley, Cheryl Tiegs, Kathy Ireland and Daniela Pestova with her third cover.
rewrite: At age twenty-four, model Kate Upton has now appeared on the cover of the *Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue* as many times as athlete LeBron James has been featured on the cover of the magazine’s regular edition. To commemorate this milestone and her third overall cover appearance, the 2017 edition will feature Upton on three distinct covers, a decision announced on February 15, 2017, during *Jimmy Kimmel Live!* and subsequently confirmed via the publication’s official social media channels. The selection of the Swimsuit Issue cover model is traditionally confidential; Upton herself had not viewed the final images prior to their televised revelation. Her prior covers were in 2012 and 2013, following the 2016 edition, which showcased three separate models: Ronda Rousey, Hailey Clauson, and Ashley Graham. Among all models, only Elle Macpherson, with five covers primarily from the 1980s, has more appearances than Upton. With this third cover, Upton joins the ranks of Christie Brinkley, Cheryl Tiegs, Kathy Ireland, and Daniela Pestova, who have also achieved this distinction.

Dive Brief:
In a new Berkeley IGS/EdSource poll of registered voters, California residents say that creating a safe and positive school environment is more important than standardized test scores, Ed Source reports.
Voters were concerned primarily about bullying and cyberbullying, though they also felt more school resources should be directed to addressing the needs of homeless children and families threatened with deportation
Most voters (57%) support the state’s current “multiple measure” approach to evaluating schools, which de-emphasizes test scores in favor of other measures ,such as graduation rates, safety and school discipline.
Dive Insight:
In many education circles, success is primarily measured by standardized achievement test scores, whether they be national or state assessments. The fate of students, teachers, administrators, schools and school districts often rise and fall by this measure, and producing good test results often becomes the end game of education.
However, in the wider societal context, this poll indicates that tests scores are not the most important consideration for many parents or voters. Though parts of this poll are more specific to California — the immigration question, for instance — the overall priorities for schools ring true across the nation. Earlier polls, for instance, reveal that concerns over school environment and safety are the main reasons parents leave public education for private schools or for homeschooling. Since bullying and cyberbullying now impact about 25% of students, this seems a valid concern.
Achievement test scores have their place in measuring academic success because they provide numerical data that is easy to compare. However, achievement tests do not tell the whole story when it comes to student success or teacher effectiveness. Studies show that grit—a combination of passion and perseverance—may be the stronger indicator of student success. Perhaps quantifying the “grit factor” for students and teachers could provide a better measure in the future.
rewrite:
According to a recent Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) poll conducted in partnership with EdSource, a majority of registered voters in California prioritize the establishment of safe and positive school climates over standardized test performance. The survey indicates that voter concerns are predominantly focused on issues of bullying and cyberbullying. Additionally, respondents expressed support for directing increased school resources toward assisting homeless children and families facing potential deportation. A substantial majority, 57 percent, endorse the state’s existing "multiple measure" accountability framework, which shifts emphasis away from standardized assessments toward alternative indicators such as graduation rates, school safety, and disciplinary records.

Within educational policy and administration, institutional and student success is frequently gauged primarily through standardized achievement test results. These metrics often disproportionately influence evaluations of students, educators, administrators, and entire districts, thereby riskin g the reduction of educational objectives to test score optimization. The poll findings, however, suggest that within the broader societal context, test scores are not the paramount consideration for many parents and voters. While certain elements of the survey, such as questions regarding immigration, reflect California-specific issues, the overarching priorities identified appear consistent with national sentiments. Prior polling data, for instance, reveals that concerns regarding school environment and safety are primary motivators for parents to transition their children from public to private schools or to homeschooling. Given that approximately one-quarter of students are affected by bullying or cyberbullying, this concern is substantively warranted.

While standardized achievement tests offer a quantifiable and comparable metric for assessing certain academic outcomes, they provide an incomplete portrait of student success or educator efficacy. Research suggests that non-cognitive factors, such as grit—defined as a combination of passion and perseverance for long-term goals—may be more predictive of student achievement. Consequently, future accountability systems might benefit from developing methodologies to quantify such psychosocial attributes, thereby creating a more holistic and valid measure of educational quality.

ST. ALBERT, Alta. — Memorial scholarships are being set up to honour four Alberta hockey players who were killed in the Humboldt Broncos bus crash.
Logan Hunter, Jaxon Joseph, Conner Lukan and Stephen Wack were among the 16 people killed on April 6 when the junior hockey team’s bus and a semi-trailer collided at a rural Saskatchewan intersection.
Each of the four had played minor hockey in the community northwest of Edmonton.
The deaths led to the establishment of the St. Albert Humboldt Remembrance Committee in mid-May.
The committee says it will honour the legacy of each young man by installing memory plaques on four benches in St. Albert.
They are also raising money for memorial scholarships named for the four players.
“The tragedy of the Humboldt Broncos has been felt very deeply here in St. Albert and across Canada,” said Nolan Crouse, chairman of the committee. “We have supported one another as we collectively mourned, and now we plan to do something positive to honour the memories of these young men.”
Another 13 players were injured in the crash.
rewrite: In St. Albert, Alberta, memorial scholarships are being established to honor four local hockey players who perished in the Humboldt Broncos bus collision. Logan Hunter, Jaxon Joseph, Conner Lukan, and Stephen Wack were among the sixteen individuals fatally injured on April 6 when the junior hockey team’s bus and a semi-trailer collided at a rural Saskatchewan intersection. All four had participated in minor hockey within the community northwest of Edmonton. Following the tragedy, the St. Albert Humboldt Remembrance Committee was formed in mid-May. The committee intends to commemorate each individual’s legacy by installing memorial plaques on four benches in St. Albert, while concurrently fundraising for scholarships named after the players. Committee Chairman Nolan Crouse stated, “The Humboldt Broncos tragedy has been profoundly felt in St. Albert and across Canada. We have supported each other in collective mourning, and now we aim to undertake a positive initiative to honor these young men’s memories.” The collision also resulted in injuries to thirteen additional players.

DNA testing at Forensic Laboratory to be a reality soon
DPI, Guyana, Monday, December 11, 2017
Speaking recently with media operatives, Minister of Public Security Khemraj Ramjattan revealed that the procurement process to acquire equipment for Forensic Laboratory has been approved. The Minister disclosed the equipment costs fall within the vicinity of US$1M and was provided for by Citizen Security Strengthening Programme (CSSP) of the Ministry of Public Security.
Minister Ramjattan also disclosed that over the next six to seven months, the laboratory, located at Turkeyen, will have its security upgraded to safeguard the integrity of the exhibits, ventilation works completed and the certified training of staff who will be conducting various forensic tests.
Minister Ramjattan explained, “The Americans experts, through their ambassador indicated that we haven’t as yet reached the stage for that quality of DNA testing. And we had to wait until we get all the other things fixed, the infrastructural work, the integrity system and the ventilation system because these exhibits have to be maintained at a certain temperature and also the design of that original lab wasn’t there yet.”
The Public Security Minister said it is disappointing that this was not yet achieved. He, however, emphasised that the “accreditation and the certification, will come when we get it one hundred percent fixed.”
Minister Ramjattan opined that much of the laboratory’s ‘design work’ was incorrectly done previously. This resulted in the government being forced to recall the Barbadian expert, to conduct an assessment of the facility as it currently stood. Subsequent to her findings, he added, reconstructive works began.
The Guyana Forensic Science Laboratory (GFSL) is a government initiative with the long-term goal of providing quality laboratory service to support forensic and non-forensic investigations. The GFSL offers forensic analysis on samples related to criminal investigations in the areas of toxicology, questioned documents analysis, trace evidence and chemical analysis and non-forensic laboratory testing relating to matters not associated with criminal investigations.
By: Natasha Smith
For more photos, click on the link to the DPI’s Flickr Page
https://www.flickr.com/photos/142936155@N03/
rewrite:
The establishment of operational DNA testing capabilities at the Guyana Forensic Science Laboratory (GFSL) is anticipated in the near future. This development was detailed by the Minister of Public Security, Khemraj Ramjattan, during a recent engagement with members of the media. Minister Ramjattan confirmed that the procurement process for essential laboratory equipment, funded through the Ministry of Public Security’s Citizen Security Strengthening Programme (CSSP) at an approximate cost of US$1 million, has received official approval.

The Minister further outlined a timeline of six to seven months for critical preparatory work at the Turkeyen-based facility. This period will be dedicated to enhancing physical security protocols to ensure exhibit integrity, completing necessary ventilation system upgrades, and providing certified training for personnel tasked with conducting forensic analyses. Minister Ramjattan clarified that, according to assessments communicated by American experts, the laboratory has not yet met the requisite standards for accredited DNA testing. He stated, “We had to wait until we get all the other things fixed, the infrastructural work, the integrity system and the ventilation system because these exhibits have to be maintained at a certain temperature and also the design of that original lab wasn’t there yet.” While expressing disappointment over the delay, the Minister stressed that full accreditation and certification are contingent upon the complete rectification of these infrastructural and procedural prerequisites.

Minister Ramjattan attributed part of the delay to previously flawed design work, which necessitated a re-evaluation of the facility. This reassessment was conducted by a recalled Barbadian expert, whose findings subsequently initiated corrective reconstructive efforts. The GFSL is a governmental initiative established with the long-term objective of delivering quality laboratory services to support both forensic and non-forensic investigations. Its forensic functions include toxicology, questioned document analysis, trace evidence, and chemical analysis pertaining to criminal cases, while its non-forensic services address matters unrelated to criminal investigations.
