Former Florida wide receiver Antonio Callaway, who some personnel evaluators consider as talented as any wide receiver in this week's draft, tested positive for marijuana at the combine, NFL sources said.
Callaway's new agent, Malki Kawa, said Tuesday that it was for a diluted sample. A diluted sample is treated as a positive test result under the NFL's Policy and Program on Substances of Abuse.
Kawa did not represent Callaway during the combine; he was hired two weeks ago.
Shortly after Callaway was informed that he tested positive, he and his former agent, Melvin Bratton, parted ways.
Callaway was viewed by some teams as a potential second-day pick, and that was only because of his previous incidents off the field.
In December 2015, a female Florida student accused Callaway of sexually assaulting her, but a Title IX hearing officer cleared him of wrongdoing in August 2016. The woman and her witnesses boycotted the hearing because the university appointed an attorney who was also a Gators football booster to hear the case. Callaway was never criminally charged in the incident.
According to the hearing officer's ruling, Callaway testified that he was "high on marijuana" during the encounter with the woman and stated that he was "so stoned I had no interest in having sex with anyone."
Callaway also was one of nine Florida players last season who allegedly used stolen credit card information to fund bookstore accounts, and he was cited for misdemeanor marijuana possession and possession of drug equipment during a traffic stop by Gainesville police in May 2017.
One talent evaluator said Callaway had enough talent "to one day wear a gold jacket." Now it might be a challenge for Callaway to get drafted.
Asked recently about his past mistakes, Callaway said: "I mean, I matured. I'm past that. I don't dwell on it or nothing. It happened. It happened, so I can't cry over spoiled milk. I was young. I was dumb. I was immature. I've grown a lot, actually. Got a beautiful girl [his daughter, Aulani, was born in February] to look after, so I ain't got no choice but to be a man."
Information from ESPN's Mark Schlabach was used in this report.
rewrite:

Kawa, who was engaged only two weeks prior, did not represent Callaway during the combine. Following notification of the positive test, Callaway and his former representative, Melvin Bratton, terminated their professional relationship.

Prior to this development, some teams considered Callaway a potential selection on the draft’s second day, a projection tempered significantly by his history of off-field incidents. In December 2015, a female student accused him of sexual assault; a Title IX hearing officer subsequently cleared him of wrongdoing in August 2016. The complainant and her witnesses boycotted that proceeding due to the university’s appointment of a hearing officer who was also a Florida Gators football booster. No criminal charges were filed. During the Title IX hearing, Callaway testified that he was “high on marijuana” during the encounter, stating he was “so stoned I had no interest in having sex with anyone.”

Further, Callaway was among nine Florida players implicated last season in the alleged use of stolen credit card information to fund bookstore accounts. Additionally, in May 2017, he received citations for misdemeanor marijuana possession and possession of drug paraphernalia during a traffic stop by Gainesville police. Despite these issues, one talent evaluator suggested Callaway possesses the ability to eventually merit Hall of Fame consideration (“wear a gold jacket”), though his draft prospects are now uncertain.

When questioned recently about his past, Callaway reflected, “I matured. I’m past that. I don’t dwell on it… It happened, so I can’t cry over spoiled milk. I was young. I was dumb. I was immature. I’ve grown a lot, actually. Got a beautiful girl [his daughter, born in February] to look after, so I ain’t got no choice but to be a man.” This report incorporates information from ESPN’s Mark Schlabach.

ZURICH The risk of extremist attacks in Switzerland remains elevated, the Swiss spy agency said on Tuesday, and more attacks by the Islamic State militant group and its sympathisers were expected across Europe.
"In Switzerland, the terrorist threat remains at a heightened level," the Federal Intelligence Service (FIS) said in its annual assessment of risks faced by Switzerland.
"The most likely terrorist threat in Europe and thus also in Switzerland will continue to come from jihad-motivated terrorism," it said. "Further attacks must be expected."
The assessment was released as Europe still comes to terms with attacks in London and Paris linked to Islamist extremism.
The FIS said the greatest danger was that individuals or small groups inspired by Islamic State would carry out attacks in Switzerland or use it as a base to plot other attacks.
FIS said it had identified more than 500 internet users with Swiss connections who were using social media to spread jihadist ideas.
Concerns about extremism and potential attacks led to Swiss voters last year backing a law extending the national spy service's authority to monitor internet traffic, deploy drones and hack foreign computer systems.
Switzerland has so far not been targeted directly in an Islamist attack, but it has had several links to attacks that elsewhere in Europe last year.
Two men who took hostages and killed a priest in northern France last July had travelled via airports in Geneva and Zurich.
Another man who killed at least 12 people when he drove a lorry into a crowded Berlin Christmas market had also visited Switzerland and may also have obtained a gun there.
"It is not yet clear whether these links to Switzerland played any role in the attack," the FIS report said.
With no indication the fight against Islamic State was coming to a close, there "remains the considerable risk that the aggressive battle for the survival of the caliphate, fought using every means at their disposal, will increasingly be carried to Europe", the FIS report said.
Radicalised individuals returning from war zones were the most likely perpetrators, although the number of people leaving Switzerland to fight in Syria and Iraq had declined.
(Reporting by John Revill; Editing by Paul Tait)
rewrite:
The threat of extremist attacks within Switzerland persists at an elevated level, according to an assessment issued on Tuesday by the Swiss Federal Intelligence Service (FIS). The agency further anticipates additional attacks across Europe perpetrated by the Islamic State militant group and its adherents. In its annual risk evaluation, the FIS stated, "In Switzerland, the terrorist threat remains at a heightened level." The report concludes that "the most likely terrorist threat in Europe and thus also in Switzerland will continue to come from jihad-motivated terrorism," and that "further attacks must be expected."

This assessment is published amidst a European context of recent attacks in London and Paris linked to Islamist extremism. The FIS identifies the primary danger as stemming from individuals or small cells, inspired by Islamic State ideology, who may execute attacks within Swiss territory or utilize the country as a logistical base for plotting operations abroad. The service has identified over five hundred internet users with Swiss connections who are actively disseminating jihadist propaganda via social media platforms. These security concerns contributed to a 2016 referendum in which Swiss voters endorsed legislation expanding the national intelligence service's powers to include monitoring internet traffic, deploying surveillance drones, and conducting cyber intrusions into foreign computer systems.

While Switzerland has not experienced a direct Islamist attack on its soil, several connections to attacks elsewhere in Europe have been established. For instance, two perpetrators of a July 2016 hostage-taking and murder of a priest in northern France had transited through Geneva and Zurich airports. Additionally, an individual who killed at least twelve people by driving a lorry into a Berlin Christmas market in December 2016 had previously visited Switzerland and may have acquired a firearm there. The FIS report notes, however, that "it is not yet clear whether these links to Switzerland played any role in the attack."

The report underscores that, with no imminent conclusion to the conflict against Islamic State, "there remains the considerable risk that the aggressive battle for the survival of the caliphate, fought using every means at their disposal, will increasingly be carried to Europe." It identifies radicalised individuals returning from conflict zones in Syria and Iraq as the most probable perpetrators, even though the number of Swiss residents departing to engage in these conflicts has declined.

There’s a way to slash congestion in the Big Apple’s clogged streets, and the name of the game is “carpooling”.
If that sounds obvious enough, a team of scientists at MIT just published a study to prove the point.
It found that app-based carpool services could reduce overall traffic in Manhattan by 300 percent — and eliminate the need for 75 percent of all taxis.
New Yorkers are increasingly getting the hang of carpooling options like Uber’s UberPool, Lyft’s Lyft Line and Via, all of which use computer algorithms in real time to pick up and drop off multiple passengers along single routes.
The MIT study, however, found that existing algorithms still have room for improvement. Some, for example, require all requests to be submitted before creating a route.
A new system devised by MIT scientists allows requests to be rematched to different vehicles. It also takes into account which size vehicle makes the most sense for a given group of ride requests.
“A key challenge was to develop a real-time solution that considers the thousands of vehicles and requests at once,” says Professor Daniela Rus of MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.
A team of researchers led by Rus developed an algorithm that found that 3,000 four-person cars could serve 98 percent of demand in New York City, with an average wait-time of only 2.7 minutes.
Currently, there are more than 13,500 taxicabs on the streets of New York City, according to the city’s Taxi and Limousine Commission.
The MIT algorithm also crunched the numbers with two-person and ten-person vehicles, finding that 3,000 two-person cars could serve 94% of demand and only 2,000 ten-person vehicles could serve 95% of demand.
The final product is what Rus calls an “anytime optimal algorithm,” which means that it gets better the more times you run it.
Transportation studies put the annual cost of congestion at $160 billion, which includes 7 billion hours of time lost to sitting in traffic and an extra 3 billion gallons of fuel burned, according to MIT.
rewrite:
A significant reduction in traffic congestion within New York City is achievable through the strategic adoption of shared mobility services, specifically app-based carpooling. Research from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology substantiates this proposition. A recently published study concludes that such services possess the potential to decrease overall vehicular traffic in Manhattan by as much as three hundred percent, thereby obviating the need for approximately seventy-five percent of the current taxi fleet.

The proliferation of services such as UberPool, Lyft Line, and Via, which utilize real-time algorithmic routing to consolidate multiple passengers onto single journeys, reflects growing public adoption. The MIT investigation, however, identifies considerable potential for optimization beyond current industry practices. Existing algorithms often operate under limitations, such as requiring all ride requests to be submitted prior to route generation.

In response, MIT researchers have devised a novel system featuring enhanced dynamic matching capabilities. This system allows for the continuous reassignment of requests to different vehicles and intelligently determines the most appropriate vehicle size for a given set of ride requests. Professor Daniela Rus of MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory notes that a principal challenge was “to develop a real-time solution that considers the thousands of vehicles and requests at once.”

The algorithm developed under Professor Rus’s direction demonstrates that a fleet of just 3,000 four-passenger vehicles could satisfy ninety-eight percent of taxi demand in New York City, with an average wait time of 2.7 minutes. This stands in contrast to the more than 13,500 taxicabs currently licensed. The model was further applied to fleets of two-passenger and ten-passenger vehicles, indicating that 3,000 two-passenger cars could meet ninety-four percent of demand, while merely 2,000 ten-passenger vehicles could address ninety-five percent.

This methodology constitutes what Rus terms an “anytime optimal algorithm,” meaning its performance improves with successive iterations. The implications for urban mobility are substantial, particularly given the severe economic costs of congestion. MIT cites transportation studies estimating these annual costs at $160 billion, encompassing 7 billion hours lost to delays and an additional 3 billion gallons of fuel consumed.

Members of the Church of Freedom in Christ Ministries stood at the main entrance of the parade holding signs that offered apologies for how the LGBT community has been treated by Christians.
(CNN) — Religion has often been used to put down the LGBT community. But at a pride parade this past weekend in Marikina, a city just east of the Phillipines’ capital of Manila, a group of Christians gathered to say something different: I’m sorry.
Members of the Church of Freedom in Christ Ministries stood at the main entrance of the parade holding signs that offered apologies for how the LGBT community has been treated by Christians.
Their banners read, “We’re here to apologize for the ways that we as Christians have harmed the LGBT community.”
Some of the signs had more personal sentiments.
One man’s stated, “Can we hug you?”
According to parade-goer Kohlin Lallabban, many took the group up on the offer.
“It was so genuine and most of us got teary eyed when we saw them,” Lallabban said.
The demonstration was part of the church’s “I’m Sorry” campaign, through which members seek to apologize on behalf of their fellow Christians for the way biblical writings have been used against the LGBT community.
In a statement on its Facebook page, the church wrote, “We do not need the recognition of people but the heart-warming response of those who accepted our sincere apologies motivates and encourages us to continue doing this mission of our church.”
Lallaban thinks the act means an exceptional amount to the Filipino LGBT community, which has often been at odds with the nation’s heavily Catholic culture.
“It was just so empowering to have that kind of support from the very people who shunned us away.”

rewrite:
At the principal entrance to a pride parade held this past weekend in Marikina, a city situated east of Manila, the capital of the Philippines, congregants from the Church of Freedom in Christ Ministries assembled bearing placards expressing contrition for the historical treatment of the LGBT community by Christian institutions. This demonstration presented a notable contrast to the frequent invocation of religious doctrine to marginalize LGBT individuals. The participants articulated a collective apology through their signage, with one banner explicitly stating, “We’re here to apologize for the ways that we as Christians have harmed the LGBT community.” Other messages conveyed more personal overtures, such as one individual’s sign inquiring, “Can we hug you?”

This public act of reconciliation constituted a component of the church’s designated “I’m Sorry” campaign, an initiative through which its members seek to atone for the adversarial application of biblical texts against LGBT persons. According to an account from parade attendee Kohlin Lallabban, the gesture was met with a profoundly emotional reception, eliciting tears from many and resulting in numerous accepted offers of embrace. The church elaborated on its motivation in an official statement, noting that while public recognition was not its objective, the heartfelt responses received served as a significant impetus to persist in its mission.

For the Filipino LGBT community, which has historically navigated a complex relationship with the nation’s predominantly Catholic cultural framework, such a display of solidarity carries considerable symbolic weight. Lallabban reflected that receiving support from a group traditionally associated with exclusion was uniquely empowering. The event thus underscores a transformative moment of bridge-building within a socio-religious context often characterized by division.

Football Association of Malawi (FAM) has said the verdict involving Nchalo United officials over the alleged match-fixing scandal will be determined today in Blantyre.
The case came to light when four Mzuzu-based referees were found guilty of allegedly pocketing a K15, 000 bribe to manipulate the result of the Carlsberg Cup round of 16 match between Chitipa United and Nchalo United which took place at Mzuzu Stadium on 13 July 2017.
The four referees, namely Limbani Chisambi, Aziz Nyirenda, Stefano Gomani and Jimmy Phiri, were found guilty and eventually handed a life ban by the National Referees Association (NRA).
FAM has come under pressure from several quarters, including the NRA, over its delay to act on the newly-promoted Super League side’s Nchalo United involvement in the scandal.
NRA General Secretary, Chris Kalichero, is on record to have told the media that FAM is setting a bad precedent by not acting on the matter, six months after the incident.
FAM General Secretary Alfred Gunda said the association could not be drawn to make a conclusion due to other circumstances surrounding the case.
“The case is not as easy as some may look at it. It involves several parties. The NRA already made a ruling on the referees with a life ban. At the same time, we also want the banned referees to come as witnesses to the case during our hearing.
“It has taken us time to resolve the matter because we have also been consulting the legal team on the way forward. We strongly believe that rules of natural justice should prevail in this case for the betterment of the game,” he told YFM online in an interview.
Gunda said the case has dragged because the legal team was pre-occupied with other duties; hence the delay to come up with a determination on the matter. He then expressed the hope that the case will be concluded by 3 February 2018.- YFM Online
rewrite:
The Football Association of Malawi (FAM) has announced that a verdict concerning officials of Nchalo United, in relation to an alleged match-fixing scandal, will be delivered today in Blantyre. This case originated from an incident during the Carlsberg Cup round of 16 match between Chitipa United and Nchalo United at Mzuzu Stadium on 13 July 2017. Subsequently, four referees from Mzuzu—Limbani Chisambi, Aziz Nyirenda, Stefano Gomani, and Jimmy Phiri—were adjudged guilty of accepting a bribe of K15,000 to manipulate the match outcome. The National Referees Association (NRA) imposed a lifetime ban on these individuals.

FAM has faced considerable criticism from various entities, including the NRA, for its perceived delay in addressing the involvement of the newly-promoted Super League side, Nchalo United, in the scandal. NRA General Secretary Chris Kalichero has publicly stated that FAM is establishing an unfavorable precedent by failing to act promptly, noting that six months had elapsed since the incident. In response, FAM General Secretary Alfred Gunda explained that the association’s ability to reach a conclusion has been hindered by the complexity of the case and surrounding circumstances. He emphasized that the matter involves multiple parties and noted that while the NRA has already sanctioned the referees, their testimony is required as part of FAM’s ongoing hearings.

Gunda further indicated that the resolution has been protracted due to consultations with legal advisors to ensure an appropriate course of action. He stressed the necessity for the principles of natural justice to be upheld to safeguard the integrity of the sport. The delay in reaching a determination was also attributed to the legal team’s involvement with other professional obligations. Gunda expressed optimism that the proceedings would be concluded by 3 February 2018. This statement was provided during an interview with YFM Online.

Scotland skipper Greig Laidlaw has been ruled out for the rest of the RBS 6 Nations , the Scottish Rugby Union has announced.
The Gloucester scrum-half suffered an ankle injury just before half-time as the Dark Blues lost 22-16 to France in Paris in Saturday.
He left the Stade de France on crutches and was sent back to the Kingsholm Stadium on Monday to be assessed by his club medics.
But Scots head coach Vern Cotter has now been given the bad news that Laidlaw will miss the remainder of the tournament.
It is a considerable blow for a side who have come to rely on Laidlaw, not only for his leadership skills but also his goal-kicking abilities. Ali Price took over at nine at the weekend and looks likely to keep the jersey when Scotland welcome Wales to Murrayfield next Saturday.
However, Cotter must now decide who will take over the captaincy duties.
Flanker John Barclay took over the armband when Laidlaw limped off against Les Bleus, but was soon himself replaced after suffering a head knock.
Jonny Gray became the Scots' third skipper of the day when Barclay was replaced and has long been tipped as a future national team captain.
rewrite:
The Scottish Rugby Union has announced that national team captain Greig Laidlaw will be unavailable for the remainder of the RBS 6 Nations tournament. The Gloucester scrum-half sustained an ankle injury shortly before halftime during Scotland's 22-16 defeat to France in Paris on Saturday. Departing the Stade de France on crutches, Laidlaw returned to Kingsholm Stadium on Monday for assessment by his club's medical staff. Head coach Vern Cotter has subsequently been informed that Laidlaw will miss the tournament's remaining fixtures.

This development represents a significant setback for the side, which has depended considerably on Laidlaw both for his leadership and his goal-kicking proficiency. Ali Price, who assumed the scrum-half position following the injury, is anticipated to retain the role for the upcoming match against Wales at Murrayfield. A pressing decision for Cotter is the reassignment of the captaincy. Flanker John Barclay initially assumed the role after Laidlaw's departure against France but was later substituted due to a head injury. Leadership subsequently passed to Jonny Gray, who is widely regarded as a future national captain, making him a plausible candidate for the permanent role during Laidlaw's absence.

A bloody prison riot in Brazil’s northern province of Amazonas has claimed the lives of at least 60 people, Brazilian authorities say.
According to the province’s public security office, the violent rebellion occurred at the Anisio Jobim penitentiary complex in the provincial capital Manaus on Sunday afternoon and but was quelled on Monday morning.
The violence was triggered by a fight between inmates belonging to rival drug gangs, Sergio Fontes, the head of the security office, told a press conference on Monday, adding that the death toll might rise as authorities get a clearer idea of the incident.
He further said that prison officials were counting the inmates to determine how many had managed to escape.
The massacre was the latest deadly clash to break out between prisoners loyal to the Sao Paulo-based First Capital Command (PCC) drug gang, the country’s most powerful drug cartel, and those aligned with a local Manaus criminal group known as the North Family.
Fontes went on to say that a number of prisoners had exchanged gunfire with police forces and held a dozen of prison guards hostage late on Sunday, adding that 74 inmates had also been taken hostage during the riot, with some murdered and some others released.
A video posted on the website of the Manaus-based newspaper Em Tempo showed the aftermath of the massacre and depicted dozens of bloodied and mutilated bodies piled atop each other on the prison floor as other prisoners milled around.
Brazil is under fire by international watchdog groups for the overcrowding of its prisons, which is the norm in the biggest South American country, and deadly riots routinely erupt there. Brazil has the largest prison population after the United States, China and Russia. Horrific conditions and inter-gang hostilities are widely seen in many facilities of the country.
Back in 1992, a deadly riot at the Carandiru Penitentiary in Sao Paulo in Sao Paulo, killed 111 prisoners, nearly all of them by police as they regained the control of the jail.
rewrite:
A violent uprising at a penitentiary complex in the northern Brazilian state of Amazonas has resulted in the deaths of at least sixty individuals, according to official reports. The disturbance commenced on Sunday afternoon within the Anisio Jobim Penitentiary Complex, located in the state capital of Manaus, and was subdued by authorities by Monday morning, as confirmed by the state's public security department. Sergio Fontes, the head of that department, stated at a Monday press conference that the conflict originated from hostilities between inmates affiliated with rival drug trafficking factions. He further cautioned that the fatality count remains provisional and may increase as the investigation proceeds.

Fontes elaborated that the clash constitutes the most recent in a series of lethal confrontations between members of the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), a dominant cartel based in São Paulo, and inmates aligned with a local criminal organization known as the Family of the North. During the uprising, a number of prisoners engaged in armed exchanges with security forces and held several correctional officers hostage. Additionally, seventy-four inmates were themselves taken hostage by opposing factions; some were subsequently executed while others were later released. An official inventory of the prison population is underway to ascertain the number of potential escapees.

Graphic footage disseminated by the Manaus-based publication *Em Tempo* documented the aftermath, depicting numerous deceased and mutilated bodies within the facility. This incident underscores systemic critiques from international monitoring organizations regarding Brazil's penal system, which is characterized by severe overcrowding and recurrent violent disturbances. Brazil maintains the world's fourth-largest incarcerated population, following the United States, China, and Russia. Its correctional facilities are widely noted for their inhumane conditions and pervasive inter-gang warfare.

The event evokes historical precedent, most notably the 1992 massacre at São Paulo's Carandiru Penitentiary, where 111 inmates were killed, predominantly by state forces during the reassertion of institutional control.

Alan Hairston of Allen,TX had just been laid off from his job at a local grocery where he worked as a meat cutter for 9 years. He and his wife were barely making it by. After borrowing $1200 from his wife’s parents to make rent, he decided to make one gamble with some of that money that has possibly turned out very well for him and his family. Alan bid on a storage bin in Plano,TX and won it for about $330. But what was inside they couldn’t believe.
There were several boxes inside that contained an extensive mint collection of Sports Illustrated magazines that ranged from the first issue in 1954 to the last in 2015. Not knowing anything about the collection and if they were worth anything he had an auctioneer at Heritage Auctions that he knew examine the collection. After a close inspection of the collection, it was estimated that the collection of mint magazines could be worth anywhere from $55,000 to $100K. As a precaution, he told them that Heritage would insure the lot for a total value of $105,000.
“This is going to jump-start the rest of out lives,” his wife Jacqui said. “We will be able to have a future that is better than I thought. We may be able to pay off our vehicles, get a house and take a trip.” “This is a dream come to life,” said Alan. “Everybody hopes to win the lottery. I have to believe we just did.”
rewrite:

Consequently, he and his wife were experiencing significant financial strain. After securing a $1,200 loan from his wife’s parents to cover their rent, Mr. Hairston elected to allocate a portion of those funds toward a speculative purchase. He successfully bid approximately $330 on a storage unit located in Plano, Texas. The contents of the unit proved extraordinary.

Within the unit were multiple boxes containing an extensive, mint-condition collection of *Sports Illustrated* magazines, encompassing every issue from the inaugural publication in 1954 through the final issue of 2015. Unfamiliar with the potential value of such a collection, Mr. Hairston engaged a contact at Heritage Auctions to conduct an appraisal. Following a meticulous examination, the auction house estimated the collection's value to be between $55,000 and $100,000. As a protective measure, Heritage Auctions agreed to insure the lot for a total of $105,000.

His wife, Jacqui, remarked that this discovery would fundamentally alter their circumstances, stating, “This is going to jump-start the rest of our lives. We will be able to have a future that is better than I envisioned, potentially allowing us to pay off our vehicles, purchase a home, and take a vacation.” Mr. Hairston characterized the event as “a dream come to life,” adding, “Everybody hopes to win the lottery. I have to believe we just did.”

DAVIE COUNTY, N.C. -- A dog picked up and thrown across the road in a tornado is now spending his first week at home.
Lewis Vannoy says his dog, Duke, was thrown about 1,000 feet when a tornado came through Davie County in North Carolina almost three weeks ago.
“Picked up in the mass of the swirling wind, picked up and tossed just like a ragdoll,” Vannoy said.
The 12-year-old Australian Shepard survived.
“When I got to him, he was across the road in the pasture,” Vannoy said. “He could hardly walk. He was in severe pain. He was lethargic and crying.”
Vannoy said Duke’s right leg was broken in multiple places and his retina was damaged. The dog had multiple surgeries and spent some time at the vet.
“He’s going to have a full recovery,” said Vannoy.
As Duke makes himself comfortable at home, Vannoy is still processing his loss.
“Thirty-five years to build it, 35 seconds to destroy it,” Vannoy said. “Home, barns, garage, tractors, lawn mowers, there's nothing here that doesn't have damage on it.”
Vannoy says his home is too damaged to fix.
“I’ll build another house and we will make more memories,” Vannoy said.
He says cleaning his property will likely take between a year and a half to two years.
“I ain't giving up,” Vannoy said.
He is happy to be alive.
“It makes you hold on to your children and your grandchildren a little longer,” Vannoy said.
He’s also happy to have Duke with him.
“You really become attached,” Vannoy said.
Vannoy said he also had a horse that was thrown by the tornado and survived.
What he wants people to know to now is that if you get a tornado warning, take cover. He says his situation could have been much worse.
rewrite:
The following account details the survival of a domestic animal amidst significant property destruction resulting from a tornado event in Davie County, North Carolina. Approximately three weeks prior, an Australian Shepherd named Duke, aged twelve, was displaced an estimated one thousand feet by tornadic winds. His owner, Lewis Vannoy, described the dog as being lifted and propelled by the swirling vortex in a manner analogous to a ragdoll. Discovered in a pasture across a roadway from the property, the animal presented with severe injuries, including multiple fractures to its right leg and retinal damage, which rendered it largely immobile and in evident distress.

Following extensive surgical intervention and a period of veterinary hospitalization, Duke has now been discharged and is reportedly expected to achieve a full recovery. His return home coincides with his owner’s ongoing assessment of substantial material losses. Vannoy notes that structures including his primary residence, barns, and garage, alongside equipment such as tractors and lawn mowers, sustained universal damage, rendering the home itself beyond repair. He characterized the devastation as the destruction of thirty-five years of accumulation within a span of thirty-five seconds. The process of clearing the property is anticipated to require approximately eighteen to twenty-four months.

Despite these circumstances, Vannoy expresses a resolve to rebuild and create new memories. His primary sentiments are of gratitude for personal survival, which has reinforced the value of familial bonds, and for the preservation of his companion animal, to which he acknowledges a profound attachment. He further reports that a horse on the property also survived being thrown by the tornado. Vannoy concludes with a cautionary statement, emphasizing that his situation could have been more severe and underscoring the critical importance of seeking immediate shelter upon the issuance of a tornado warning.

Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko and the National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Belarus have helped the Sports and Physical Training Society Dinamo celebrate their 95th anniversary.
"Throughout its history, this organisation has been serving as a basis for the development of physical education, big-time sports, and professional training of Belarusian law enforcement officers," Lukashenko said, according to Belarusian Telegraph Agency, the country's official news agency.
"Many decorated Belarusian athletes are members of Dinamo, among them are [Olympic medallists] Ivan Tikhon, Alexander and Andrei Bogdanovich, Darya Domracheva, Nadezhda Skardino, and others.
"Their achievements symbolise a fierce will to win, make us feel proud for the country, and contribute to the patriotic education of young people.
"Marking the anniversary, we pay tribute to the coaches, specialists, and athletes who originated the sports club, protected the motherland during the Great Patriotic War [Second World War], and served their country across the globe."
The National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Belarus held an event to celebrate the Dinamo sports club's 95th anniversary ©National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Belarus
The President went on to wish current Dinamo employees and veterans good health, happiness, prosperity, great victories, and new records.
The society's 95th anniversary was also celebrated by the National Olympic Committee with renowned athletes and coaches attending an event at the organisation's headquarters in the country's capital Minsk.
Speaking at the ceremony NOC Belarus secretary general George Katulin said: "Dinamo covered themselves with the unfading glory of victories, and many of them are owed to those present here.
"It is noteworthy that all 95 years passed under the motto 'Strength in motion'.
"The National Olympic Committee is thankful to Dinamo for high achievements you have attained throughout our history."
rewrite:
The ninety-fifth anniversary of the Sports and Physical Training Society Dinamo has been commemorated with the support of Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko and the National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Belarus (NOC RB). In a statement disseminated by the state-owned Belarusian Telegraph Agency, President Lukashenko emphasized the organization’s historical role as a foundational institution for advancing physical education, elite sport, and the professional preparation of personnel within Belarusian law enforcement agencies. He highlighted that numerous distinguished Belarusian athletes, including Olympic medalists such as Ivan Tikhon, Alexander and Andrei Bogdanovich, Darya Domracheva, and Nadezhda Skardino, are affiliated with Dinamo. According to the president, their accomplishments exemplify a resolute competitive spirit, foster national pride, and significantly contribute to the patriotic upbringing of youth.

In observance of this milestone, tribute was paid to the coaches, specialists, and athletes who established the sports club, defended the nation during the Great Patriotic War, and have represented the country internationally. President Lukashenko extended his wishes for good health, happiness, prosperity, and further athletic triumphs to both current members and veterans of the Dinamo society.

Concurrently, the National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Belarus hosted a ceremonial event at its Minsk headquarters to mark the anniversary, which was attended by notable athletes and coaches. Addressing the gathering, NOC RB Secretary General George Katulin remarked that Dinamo has accrued enduring prestige through its victories, many of which are attributable to the individuals present. He observed that the society’s entire ninety-five-year history has been guided by the motto “Strength in motion.” Katulin concluded by expressing the National Olympic Committee’s gratitude to Dinamo for the high level of sporting achievement it has sustained throughout its history.

FORDLAND, Mo. — Officials say they have no estimate for how long it will take to restore Ozarks Public Television service to all viewers after a TV tower collapse in southwest Missouri that left one person dead.
Missouri State University spokeswoman Suzanne Shaw said Monday she did not know when viewers who use antennas to get channels would be able to watch KOZK Ozarks Public Television. The university is looking at teaming up with another broadcaster to put its equipment on their tower, but no plans have been finalized.
The Springfield News-Leader reports sine viewers with AT&T U-verse, Mediacom and DirecTV should now be able to watch Ozarks Public Television.
The 1,980-foot (600-meter) tower that collapsed Thursday was used by the university to broadcast Ozarks Public Television. One man, 56-year-old Steve Lemay, died.

MIAMI (AP) — The brother of the teen charged with killing 17 people at a Florida school was arrested Monday afternoon for trespassing at the same school, authorities said.
Zachary Cruz, 18, was arrested at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School and charged with trespassing on school grounds, a Broward Sheriff’s Office report said.
The teen was recorded by security cameras riding his skateboard at the school around 4:30 p.m. though he had received prior warnings from school officials to stay away from the campus, the report said.
Zachary Cruz told the arresting deputy that he was there to “reflect on the school shooting and to soak it in,” according to the report. It added that the teen had “surpassed all locked doors and gates and proceeded to ride his skateboard through school grounds.”
The youth’s brother, 19-year-old Nikolas Cruz, has been charged with 17 counts of first-degree murder in connection with the Feb. 14 shooting.
The Associated Press reported Sunday that documents show some officials recommended in September 2016 that Nikolas Cruz be involuntarily committed for a mental evaluation, though the recommendation was never acted upon. Such a commitment would have made it more difficult, if not impossible, for Cruz to have legally obtained a gun such as the AR-15 assault-style rifle used in the shooting.
Jail records didn’t immediately list an attorney for Zachary Cruz.

According to the official sheriff’s office report, Zachary Cruz was observed via security surveillance riding a skateboard on the campus at approximately 4:30 p.m., despite having received prior warnings from school officials to refrain from entering the property. The report further indicates that he bypassed locked doors and gates to gain access. Upon arrest, he stated his purpose was to “reflect on the school shooting and to soak it in.”

This incident follows recent reporting by The Associated Press which revealed that, in September 2016, certain officials had recommended the involuntary commitment of Nikolas Cruz for a mental health evaluation—a recommendation that was never implemented. Had such a commitment been enacted, it would have presented a significant legal barrier, potentially preventing him from later purchasing the AR-15 style rifle used in the attack. As of the arrest report, no legal representation for Zachary Cruz was listed in jail records.

A feast of fun will be served up at the coast this weekend in a showcase of local food and drink.
The Proper Food and Drink Festival takes place in Whitley Bay, offering music, food and bars.
And organisers say it will make the perfect outing for a Father’s Day treat.
Founder Mark Deakin said: “If you’re struggling to know what to do for your dad, bring him along.
“There’s music, fantastic food, plenty of bars, and of course, entrance is free. What more could you want?”
More than 60 stalls will set up on the Spanish City Plaza, offering the best in locally produced food and drink.
It is the second event of its kind to visit North Tyneside this year, with the festival attracting a record number of visitors when it was held in North Shields in April.
It is the fourth year it has come to the coast and the event has grown in popularity every year since Mark and his wife Shelley first introduced it to North Shields in 2012.
The pair have now added more towns to the tour and in addition to their six Proper Food and Drink Festivals, they run the North East Chilli Fest and in August will launch the Great North Feast in South Shields.
Shelley said: “It all makes for a busy summer, but judging by the number of people who come along, we think we have the recipe just about right.”
The Whitley Bay event runs on Saturday and Sunday, from 10am to 5pm each day.
The North East Chilli Fest, featuring live music from Heaven 17, Smoove and Turrell and the Baghdaddies, takes place beside Gloucester Lodge Farm, near Seaton Sluice, from June 30 to July 2, and the Cramlington food festival runs from July 29-30.
It is at Saltwell Park, Gateshead, on August 5 and 6, and at Ridley Park, Blyth, the following weekend.
The Great North Feast will be held in Bents Park, from August 25-28.

DUBAI May 2 Kuwait's Zain Group and Saudi Telecom Co (STC) have both applied to become the third mobile operator in Oman as the country's regulator looks to award its first licence since 2004.
Zain announced on the Kuwait bourse on Tuesday that it had submitted an offer to bid for the licence. Rival STC had confirmed its application a day earlier.
The shortlist of qualified applications will be announced on Aug. 14, with the winning bid to be announced on Sept. 4, according to statements from the companies.
Oman's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) said last year that it was inviting bids for what will be the first mobile network operator licence Oman has awarded since Ooredoo Oman, then branded Nawras in Oman, started operations in the country in 2004.
Oman Telecommunications (Omantel) and Ooredoo Oman each have a market share of about 41 percent, with virtual mobile network operators holding about 17 percent, the regulator says.
Like neighbouring Gulf Arab states, Oman has a significant young, tech-savvy population that is viewed as a significant driver of growth in the region's telecoms and IT services sector.
The sector is expected to be worth more than $700 million in Oman next year, up from $590 million in 2015, research company IDC says.
"Despite the economic woes and oil price fluctuation, the Omani telecoms market has witnessed relatively healthy growth," said Dubai-based IDC lead analyst Paul Black.
Oman, with a population of about 4.55 million, had a mobile penetration rate of 151 percent with 6.87 million users in the fourth quarter of 2016, the regulator says. The vast majority of users were pre-pay customers.
Zain operates in eight countries in the Middle East and Africa, while Saudi Arabia-based STC has subsidiaries and joint ventures in the Middle East and Asia.
Omantel, which has operated in the country since 1970, and Ooredoo Oman both reported declining first-quarter profit, citing higher royalty and tax rates. (Additional reporting by Hadeel Al Sayegh; Editing by David Goodman)
rewrite:
On May 2, in Dubai, it was reported that Kuwait’s Zain Group and Saudi Telecom Company (STC) have formally submitted applications to become the third mobile network operator in the Sultanate of Oman. This follows an initiative by Oman’s Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) to issue its first new mobile licence since 2004. Zain publicly disclosed its bid submission via a filing on the Kuwait stock exchange on Tuesday, while its competitor, STC, had confirmed its application the preceding day. According to corporate statements, a shortlist of qualified applicants will be announced on August 14, with the final award scheduled for September 4.

The TRA had previously announced the invitation for bids, marking the first such licensing opportunity since Ooredoo Oman—originally operating under the Nawras brand—commenced operations in 2004. The Omani telecommunications market is currently characterized by a duopoly, with Oman Telecommunications Company (Omantel) and Ooredoo Oman each holding approximately 41 percent market share. Virtual mobile network operators account for the remaining 17 percent. The market serves a notably young and technologically adept population, a demographic profile consistent with neighbouring Gulf Arab states and considered a primary catalyst for expansion within the regional telecommunications and information technology services sector.

Industry projections indicate substantial growth for the sector. Research firm International Data Corporation (IDC) estimates the Omani telecom market will exceed $700 million in value next year, rising from $590 million in 2015. According to Dubai-based IDC lead analyst Paul Black, "Despite economic challenges and oil price volatility, the Omani telecoms market has experienced relatively robust growth." Regulatory data further illustrates high mobile adoption, with a penetration rate of 151 percent equating to 6.87 million subscribers in the fourth quarter of 2016, within a population of approximately 4.55 million. The majority of these subscribers utilize pre-paid services.

The two bidders bring extensive regional experience. Zain operates across eight countries in the Middle East and Africa, while STC, based in Saudi Arabia, maintains subsidiaries and joint ventures throughout the Middle East and Asia. Incumbent operators Omantel, established in 1970, and Ooredoo Oman both reported declines in first-quarter profit, attributing the results to increased royalty and tax obligations.

Do you suck at Fortnite on PC? Are you baffled by other players’ ability to magic together amazing forts while you’ve accidentally locked yourself into a brick box prison? Here’s a trick: Remap your damn key bindings.
Fortnite’s default key bindings are awful. To build anything, you need to reach all the way up to F1 through F4 when, generally, your fingers are going to be on W, A, S and D. When bullets are raining down, you’re bleeding out health every fraction of a second it takes for your finger to get all the way up there.
Pros all have different setups, which the site BestFortniteSettings.com documents. Twitch streamer Ninja, for example, has bound his building inputs onto his Logitech G502 mouse’s thumb buttons, which a lot of people rave about. Dr. Lupo has bound his all around his keyboard—the wall build on Q, the platform build on ‘ and the ramp build on F. I can see the merits of that, since building a ramp while running along would feel way more comfortable.
What worked for me—and consequently dragged me out of the lower echelons of Fortnite play—is binding my building inputs to Z, X, C and V, right below my movement keys. That way, I don’t have to move my wrist to construct my basic fort: four tall walls surrounding several staircases. To do that, I need to jump right after building a ramp, which, frankly, feels bad when the ramp key is on the other side of the keyboard.
How have you tinkered with your Fortnite settings? How has it changed the game for you? We’d love to hear in the comments.
rewrite:
Mastering Fortnite on PC presents a significant challenge for many players, particularly regarding the rapid construction mechanics essential for competitive play. A common point of frustration arises from the game's default key bindings, which are inefficiently positioned. The primary building commands are assigned to the F1 through F4 keys, located far from the central movement keys (W, A, S, D). This spatial separation proves detrimental during combat, where every fraction of a second spent relocating one's hand can result in critical health loss.

Examining the configurations of elite players reveals a consensus on customizing these controls. Professional streamers universally employ personalized key bindings to optimize speed and ergonomics. For instance, Ninja assigns building commands to the thumb buttons on his Logitech G502 mouse, a method praised for its intuitive access. Conversely, Dr. Lupo utilizes keys clustered around the movement area, placing wall construction on Q, platform on the apostrophe key, and ramp on F. This proximity allows for seamless integration of movement and building actions.

A highly effective strategy involves remapping the four core building inputs to the Z, X, C, and V keys. Positioned directly beneath the movement keys, this arrangement minimizes hand displacement and enables the swift execution of complex structures, such as a protective enclosure with internal staircases. This configuration is especially advantageous for techniques like the "ramp rush," which requires immediate jumping after placing a ramp—an action cumbersome when the relevant key is distantly located.

Customizing key bindings is therefore not a minor adjustment but a fundamental step toward improving performance. It transforms building from a clumsy, deliberate process into a fluid extension of player movement, fundamentally altering the gameplay experience.

"Provenance" is lighter fare than the Radch trilogy, but it introduces us to some interesting new characters, cultures and technologies.
Frankenstein Dreams: A Connoisseur's Collection of Victorian Science Fiction
Ed. by Michael Sims
(Bloomsbury, 400 pages, $29)
The publication of Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein" in 1818 is usually regarded as the beginning of science fiction, but the genre then took another hundred years to arrive at its present form. In this anthology of stories and novel excerpts from the nineteenth century, editor Michael Sims tracks the process of this shaping, collecting some of the earliest explorations of what would become staple themes such as time travel, robotics and space exploration.
The major difference between SF then and now is perhaps not so much our greater knowledge of the universe as it is the evolution in style. It's the flavour of the writing here, so distinct from our own, that makes this a collection for the connoisseur.
Machine Learning
By Hugh Howey
(Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, 352 pages, $22.50)
While self-publishing via Amazon hasn't led to a total transformation of the book business, there have been some amazing success stories. Hugh Howey, author of the bestselling Silo series of novels, is one of the most notable of these.
The Silo novels are the work of an author skilled in long-form narrative, and it's surprising to turn to the stories collected in "Machine Learning" and find them just as accomplished. Howey's highly original take on such standard SF themes as aliens, artificial intelligence and virtual reality are lively and thoughtful, with several of the stories, including "The Walk Up Nameless Ridge" and "The Plagiarist" being real standouts. "Machine Learning" is a good place to catch Howey at his best.

*Frankenstein Dreams: A Connoisseur's Collection of Victorian Science Fiction*
Edited by Michael Sims
(Bloomsbury, 400 pages, $29)
Although the 1818 publication of Mary Shelley’s "Frankenstein" is conventionally cited as the genesis of science fiction, the genre required approximately a further century to evolve into its contemporary configuration. This anthology, curated by Michael Sims, assembles nineteenth-century short stories and novel excerpts to trace this developmental arc. It features early literary forays into themes that would become central to the genre, including time travel, robotics, and space exploration. The principal distinction between this foundational science fiction and its modern counterpart lies less in humanity’s expanded cosmological knowledge than in the evolution of literary style. The distinctive prose aesthetic of the Victorian period, markedly different from contemporary norms, renders this volume a collection of particular interest to the literary connoisseur.

*Machine Learning*
By Hugh Howey
(Houghton Mifflin Harcourt, 352 pages, $22.50)
The phenomenon of self-publishing via digital platforms such as Amazon has not precipitated a complete transformation of the publishing industry, yet it has yielded several notable commercial successes. Author Hugh Howey, renowned for his bestselling Silo novel series, ranks among the most prominent of these. The Silo narratives demonstrate considerable skill in sustained, novel-length storytelling, making the equally accomplished short fiction assembled in "Machine Learning" a pleasantly surprising counterpart. Howey’s treatments of established science fiction tropes—including extraterrestrial life, artificial intelligence, and virtual reality—are both inventive and intellectually engaging. Several stories within the collection, notably "The Walk Up Nameless Ridge" and "The Plagiarist," are particularly distinguished. Consequently, "Machine Learning" serves as an excellent primer to the author’s most proficient work.

Here's what we've been told about passwords:
Make them complicated.
Use numbers, question marks and hash marks.
Change them regularly.
Use different passwords for each app and website.
Of course, these guidelines often leave users frustrated and struggling to remember them all.
Now, the National Institute of Standards and Technology is about the make all of our lives much easier. The organization recently revised its guidelines on creating passwords, and the new advice sharply diverges from previous rules.
"The traditional guidance is actually producing passwords that are easy for bad guys and hard for legitimate users," says Paul Grassi, senior standards and technology adviser at NIST, who led the new revision of guidelines.
The organization suggests keeping passwords simple, long and memorable. Phrases, lowercase letters and typical English words work well, Grassi tells NPR's Audie Cornish. Experts no longer suggest special characters and a mixture of lower and uppercase letters. And passwords never need to expire.
"We focus on the cognitive side of this, which is what tools can users use to remember these things?" Grassi says. "So if you can picture it in your head, and no one else could, that's a good password."
While these rules may seem suspiciously easy, Grassi says these guidelines help users create longer passwords that are harder for hackers to break. And he says the computer security industry in both the public and private sectors has received these new rules positively.
"It works because we are creating longer passwords that cryptographically are harder to break than the shorter ones, even with all those special character requirements," Grassi says. "We are really bad at random passwords, so the longer the better."
Previously, security experts recommended the use of password manager apps to ensure users' accounts were protected. Grassi says these apps are useful because they completely randomize the password, but he says they aren't necessary to maintain security.
Grassi stands by these new guidelines because he says previous tips for passwords impacted users negatively and did not do much to boost security. When users change their passwords every 90 days, they often aren't dramatically changing the password, Grassi says.
"I'm pretty sure you're not changing your entire password; you're shifting one character," he says. "Everyone does that, and the bad guys know that."
rewrite:
Conventional wisdom regarding password creation has long emphasized complexity. Standard advice includes the incorporation of numerals, symbols such as question marks and hash marks, and the routine expiration and replacement of credentials. Furthermore, users are frequently instructed to maintain unique passwords for each distinct application and website. In practice, however, these directives often result in user frustration and difficulty in recall, potentially undermining security compliance.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has recently promulgated revised guidelines that substantially alter this paradigm, aiming to reduce user burden while enhancing effective security. The new recommendations represent a significant departure from prior established rules. According to Paul Grassi, the senior standards and technology adviser at NIST who led the revision process, “The traditional guidance is actually producing passwords that are easy for bad guys and hard for legitimate users.”

The updated guidance advocates for passwords that are simple, lengthy, and memorable. As Grassi explains, passphrases composed of lowercase letters and common English words are now considered effective. The revised standards explicitly retire previous suggestions mandating special characters, arbitrary capitalization, and forced periodic expiration. This shift in focus is deliberate. “We focus on the cognitive side of this, which is what tools can users use to remember these things?” Grassi states. “So if you can picture it in your head, and no one else could, that’s a good password.”

Although these prescriptions may appear deceptively lenient, they are designed to encourage the creation of longer passphrases that are cryptographically more resilient against automated cracking attempts than shorter, complex passwords. Grassi notes that the computer security community across both public and private sectors has responded favorably to these new rules. “It works because we are creating longer passwords that cryptographically are harder to break than the shorter ones, even with all those special character requirements,” he observes. “We are really bad at random passwords, so the longer the better.”

While password manager applications, which generate and store completely randomized credentials, remain a useful tool for ensuring account protection, Grassi indicates they are not an absolute necessity for maintaining security under the new framework. The rationale for this comprehensive revision is grounded in an assessment of past practices. Grassi asserts that previous password policies negatively impacted user experience without delivering commensurate security benefits. For instance, mandatory 90-day password changes often result in only minor, predictable alterations. “I’m pretty sure you’re not changing your entire password; you’re shifting one character,” he notes. “Everyone does that, and the bad guys know that.”

Police in Belgium arrest driver who tried to ram haredi man and child who were walking to synagogue in Antwerp.
Police in Belgium have arrested a man who is suspected of trying to ram with his car an Orthodox man and a child on a street in Antwerp, JTA reported Saturday.
The incident occurred on Saturday morning while the man and the child were walking to synagogue and was filmed by security cameras.
The footage shows a black Seat Ibiza car swerving sharply while speeding on Isabellalei, a central street in Antwerp, toward the alleged victim and a boy, who is the man’s son, according to the Antwerp-based Joods Actueel Jewish monthly.
The car is seen intersecting a bike path, apparently while speeding. The car then climbs the curb as the two alleged victims are walking toward it, prompting them to jump away from the curb and toward the safety of the building facades.
They jump behind a lamp post. The car swerves back wildly, returning to the road from its incursion into the sidewalk. The father ran after the car as it sped away.
Joods Actueel reported that witnesses said the driver had foreign origins. While their report did not name the man or offer any additional information on his identity, Israel's public broadcaster Kan News reported that the driver was of Muslim origin.
The suspect was tracked down through the footage of the license plate. He is to be arraigned Sunday on suspicion of attempted manslaughter.
In September, a Jewish man in Antwerp was physically assaulted as he made his way home from synagogue on a Friday night. The victim was accosted by a local youth, who hurled anti-Semitic epithets at him.
The assailant, who apparently is a recent convert to Islam, then physically assaulted the haredi man, punching him in the face and leaving him injured.
About 12,000 of Belgium's 40,000 Jews live in Antwerp, which also is the location of two thirds of the country's synagogues and a significant hasidic community.
rewrite:
On Saturday, authorities in Antwerp, Belgium, apprehended a driver suspected of intentionally attempting to strike an Orthodox Jewish man and a child with his vehicle. The incident, which was captured by municipal security cameras, occurred in the morning as the two individuals were proceeding to a local synagogue. According to a report from the Jewish Telegraphic Agency (JTA), the event transpired on Isabellalei, a central thoroughfare in the city.

Video evidence disseminated by the Antwerp-based monthly publication *Joods Actueel* depicts a black Seat Ibiza vehicle swerving sharply at high speed toward the alleged victims, identified as a father and his son. The automobile is seen crossing a designated bicycle path while accelerating, subsequently mounting the curb directly in the path of the pedestrians. This action compelled the two individuals to leap away from the curb toward the relative safety of adjacent building facades, positioning themselves behind a lamppost. The vehicle then swerved erratically back onto the roadway before departing the scene at speed; the father is reported to have pursued the car briefly.

While *Joods Actueel* cited witness accounts suggesting the driver had foreign origins, the publication did not disclose the suspect's identity. However, subsequent reporting by Israel's Kan News indicated the individual is of Muslim origin. Law enforcement officials successfully identified and located the suspect through analysis of the vehicle's license plate footage. He is scheduled for arraignment on Sunday, facing allegations of attempted manslaughter.

This event follows a separate antisemitic assault in Antwerp in September, wherein a Jewish man was accosted and physically attacked by a local youth while returning from synagogue on a Friday evening. The assailant, reported to be a recent convert to Islam, directed antisemitic slurs at the victim before inflicting physical injuries. Antwerp is home to approximately 12,000 of Belgium's estimated 40,000 Jewish residents, hosting two-thirds of the nation's synagogues and a substantial Hasidic community.

Actress Cynthia Nixon, who won a 2004 Emmy award for playing single lawyer Miranda Hobbes in HBO’s “Sex and the City,” is reaching for a new role. She plans to challenge New York Governor Andrew Cuomo in a Democratic primary election this year.
I love New York, and today I'm announcing my candidacy for governor. Join us: https://t.co/9DwsxWW8xX pic.twitter.com/kYTvx6GZiD — Cynthia Nixon (@CynthiaNixon) March 19, 2018
Nixon, 51, announced her candidacy on Monday in a news release and video highlighting her family, which includes her wife and two children. A lifelong New Yorker, she is a friend of Mayor Bill de Blasio, who has been feuding with Cuomo for about four years. For more than 10 years, she has been pushing for more city and state spending on public schools and for gender equality and gay rights.
“We want our government to work again, on healthcare, ending mass incarceration, fixing our broken subway,” she said in the video. “We are sick of politicians who care more about headlines and power than they do about us.”
Nixon has been an actor since she was 12 years old. She attended New York City public schools and is a graduate of Barnard College in northern Manhattan at Columbia University.

In her announcement, she emphasized her deep ties to the state, her family—including her wife and two children—and her advocacy record.

She is politically aligned with New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio, a noted rival of Governor Cuomo. She outlined policy priorities including healthcare reform, ending mass incarceration, and addressing the systemic failures of the New York City subway system. Her campaign frames this bid as an effort to restore functional and responsive government.

A Wisconsin McDonald’s manager is facing a felony theft charge after being accused of stealing thousands of dollars from her employer by issuing fake refunds on Big Macs that customers never returned.
According to the Greenfield Patch, Mary Ruelle, a manager who worked at a McDonald’s restaurant in Greenfield, Wis., has been accused by her supervisor of stealing money from the franchise location from mid-January to March 24.
MCDONALD’S SWITCHING UP THE MCFLURRY?
According to a criminal complaint, Ruelle would select food items that had been sold at the location that day and issue refunds using a code only certain employees could access. To maximize the amount of cash refunded, the supervisor says Ruelle chose higher-ticket, popular items like Big Macs.
After reviewing the store’s surveillance video, Ruelle’s supervisor told police that he witnesses his employee authorizing refunds for the food and then take money directly from the register– but no customers were present.
Normally, refunds issued at McDonald’s are just a couple of dollars but the supervisor noticed something was off when refunds were coming in for $31.32 on Jan. 14 to $132.62 on March 24, with some refunds over $200.
FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK FOR MORE FOX LIFESTYLE NEWS
In all Ruelle stole $3,827.17 — the equivalent of 1,071 Big Mac burgers.
If convicted, the former manager now faces up to a year and a half in prison or up to $10,000 in fines.

A criminal complaint details the alleged method: Ruelle purportedly selected food items sold that day and processed refunds using an access-restricted code reserved for managerial staff. To increase the illicit cash withdrawals, her supervisor asserts that she focused on higher-priced, popular menu items such as Big Macs. Surveillance footage reviewed by the supervisor reportedly showed Ruelle authorizing these refunds and then removing cash directly from the register without any customers present.

In total, the alleged embezzlement amounted to $3,827.17, a sum equivalent to the cost of approximately 1,071 Big Mac sandwiches. If convicted, Ruelle could face a sentence of up to eighteen months imprisonment or fines of up to $10,000.

There was no end of intrigue at the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show this year.
Rumor, the German shepherd who narrowly lost at last year's show, had come close to simply hanging up her leash and retiring. Instead, she stormed back to win her category again this year — and then, to top it all off, beat out more than 2,800 dogs to take Best in Show on Tuesday, as well.
The triumph makes her only the second German shepherd to win the top prize in Westminster's 141-year history. Considering Westminster is the second-longest continuously running sporting event in the U.S. — second only to the Kentucky Derby — the redemptive win for the 5 1/2-year-old female is no mean feat.
Not only that, but as NPR's Merrit Kennedy noted earlier this month, Westminster also played host to another rarity at this year's dog show: cats. The featured felines shared a showcase with the dogs called Meet & Compete.
Still, whatever words we can offer on the event seem a little beside the point. The dogs — big and small, noble and loony — are the main event.
So, without further throat-clearing, here's what you came for: A few of our very favorite images from the competition.
rewrite:
The 2023 Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show was marked by significant intrigue. Notably, Rumor, a German shepherd who had narrowly missed victory in the previous year's competition, nearly retired. However, she returned decisively, first securing her breed category and then prevailing over more than 2,800 contestants to claim the Best in Show title on Tuesday. This achievement establishes her as only the second German shepherd to earn this top honor in the event's 141-year history. Given that Westminster is the second-longest continuously running sporting event in the United States, trailing only the Kentucky Derby, this redemptive victory for the five-and-a-half-year-old female represents a considerable accomplishment.

Further distinguishing this year's show was the inclusion of cats in a "Meet & Compete" showcase, a notable rarity as reported by NPR. While such details provide context, the central focus remains the dogs themselves—of all sizes and temperaments. The following selection presents several exemplary images from the competition.

The stars seem to be aligning for the New England Patriots.
Even with a suspension to Tom Brady at the start of the season and an injury to Rob Gronkowski towards the end of it, the team snagged the AFC’s top seed at a relative stroll. Now, with the winner of the injury-decimated Raiders-Texans game seemingly awaiting them, it looks like New England’s best case scenario is unfolding before them.
There’s only one team that can spoil everything: The Miami Dolphins.
Here are the seedings and match ups for this year’s playoffs.
Looking at the current landscape, the Patriots will undoubtedly be rooting against any potential upsets. If all the higher seeds prevail, Pats fans will watch Brady take on either Savage or Osweiler at home (good luck with that, Houston) while the Chiefs and Steelers are busy beating each other up.
But the Steelers, dangerous though they are, can also be streaky. They’ve lost five times this season and have relied on late scores to win a number of other games, like against the Ravens two weeks ago. The team that so many picked for the Super Bowl ahead of the season has shown it’s prone to odd results, and the Dolphins, which beat the Steelers earlier in the season (albeit in Miami) may well hand them a season-ending upset this time.
And if it does, that could be a headache for New England.
A Miami upset would pit them against the Dolphins, a team which has won three of its last seven games against the Patriots. Yes, those were all in Miami, but the point remains: Rather than its cushy Raiders-Texans game, it’d take on a fired-up divisional rival off a huge upset.
At this point, the Raiders or the Texans are divisional match ups both of the top two AFC seeds will want. If Miami gets hot and takes out the Steelers, they could play the ultimate spoiler against the Pats, with the Chiefs awaiting them the Conference Championship at the end of it all. The Patriots are still the better team, of course, and they should prevail, but its pathway has became more fraught. Injuries and fatigue are suddenly in play in a way they weren’t before. And that, at this point in the season, is that last thing that any team wants.
rewrite:
The New England Patriots appear poised for a favorable postseason trajectory. Despite commencing the season with the suspension of quarterback Tom Brady and concluding it with a significant injury to tight end Rob Gronkowski, the team secured the American Football Conference’s top playoff seed with notable ease. Presently, with the victor of the Wild Card matchup between the injury-depleted Oakland Raiders and Houston Texans ostensibly awaiting them in the divisional round, New England’s optimal playoff scenario appears to be materializing. However, one franchise possesses the capacity to disrupt this advantageous path: the Miami Dolphins.

An examination of the playoff bracket reveals that the Patriots will undoubtedly prefer outcomes wherein higher-seeded teams prevail. Should the seeding hold, New England would host a divisional round game against either Houston’s Tom Savage or Brock Osweiler—a decidedly favorable matchup—while the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers, both formidable contenders, would be tasked with eliminating one another. Nevertheless, the Steelers, while dangerous, have demonstrated inconsistency throughout the season. The team has suffered five defeats and relied upon late-game scoring to secure several victories, including a recent contest against the Baltimore Ravens. This preseason Super Bowl favorite has proven susceptible to anomalous results. The Dolphins, who defeated Pittsburgh earlier this season in Miami, are precisely the type of opponent capable of delivering a season-ending upset in the Wild Card round.

Such an outcome would introduce considerable complication for New England. A Miami victory would force the Patriots to face a divisional rival that has triumphed in three of the last seven meetings between the clubs, rather than a presumably overmatched opponent from the Raiders-Texans contest. While those Dolphins victories occurred in Miami, the psychological and competitive dynamics would shift markedly. The Patriots would confront an emboldened division opponent riding the momentum of a significant road upset, thereby forfeiting a comparatively manageable matchup.

Consequently, both the Patriots and Chiefs would strongly prefer to encounter either Oakland or Houston in the subsequent round. A scenario in which Miami defeats Pittsburgh and advances to face New England would position the Dolphins as a potential spoiler, with the victor then likely confronting Kansas City in the AFC Championship Game. While the Patriots remain the superior team and should ultimately prevail, their pathway to the Super Bowl would become markedly more arduous. Factors such as cumulative fatigue and the heightened physical toll of a more competitive contest would become salient concerns in a manner previously avoided. At this advanced stage of the season, such added complications are precisely what any championship aspirant seeks to circumvent.

Bangladesh's government condemned an attack on New York City's subway system, as it emerged that the suspect is an immigrant from the South Asian nation.
"Bangladesh is committed to its declared policy of 'Zero Tolerance' against terrorism, and condemns terrorism and violent extremism in all forms or manifestations anywhere in the world, including Monday morning's incident in New York City," the government statement said in a statement.
Police in Bangladesh said Tuesday that they were not in a position to comment on the suspect, identified by U.S. authorities as Akayed Ullah, a 27-year-old Bangladeshi immigrant. Ullah is accused of strapping a crude pipe bomb to his body and detonating it during rush hour Monday in an attack in which only he was seriously wounded.
Ullah arrived in the United States in 2011 and the Department of Homeland Security said he's a lawful permanent resident of the U.S. who was living in Brooklyn. He came to the U.S. on a visa issued to him based on a family connection to a U.S. citizen.
Law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation said Ullah had looked at Islamic State group propaganda online and told investigators he was retaliating against U.S. military aggression, but had no direct contact with the group. The people spoke to The Associated Press on the condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak publicly about the blast.
Ullah's family in the U.S. said in a statement that it was heartbroken and deeply saddened by the suffering the attack has caused.
———
Associated Press writer Colleen Long in New York contributed to this report.
rewrite:
The government of Bangladesh issued a formal condemnation of an attack on the New York City subway system following revelations that the individual suspected of perpetrating the act is an immigrant originating from Bangladesh. An official statement affirmed the nation’s adherence to a declared policy of "Zero Tolerance" regarding terrorism, expressing condemnation for "terrorism and violent extremism in all forms or manifestations anywhere in the world, including Monday morning's incident in New York City." Concurrently, law enforcement authorities in Bangladesh indicated on Tuesday that they were not prepared to comment on the suspect, whom U.S. officials have identified as Akayed Ullah, a 27-year-old immigrant from Bangladesh. Ullah is alleged to have affixed an improvised explosive device to his person and detonated it during Monday's rush hour, an incident in which he alone sustained serious injury.

Ullah entered the United States in 2011 as a lawful permanent resident residing in Brooklyn, having obtained a visa through a familial connection to a U.S. citizen, according to the Department of Homeland Security. Law enforcement officials with knowledge of the investigation, who spoke to The Associated Press under condition of anonymity due to lack of authorization to discuss the case publicly, indicated that Ullah had consumed online propaganda from the Islamic State group. He reportedly informed investigators that his actions constituted retaliation for U.S. military interventions, though he had no direct contact with the organization. Separately, Ullah’s family in the United States released a statement expressing profound sorrow and heartbreak over the suffering caused by the attack.
