Nwosu Optimistic Nigeria Will Qualify For 2019 AFCON Despite Matchday-One Setback
By Izuchukwu Okosi:
Onetime Super Eagles midfielder, Henry Nwosu, is optimistic that the Super Eagles will bounce back strongly after a woeful losing start at home to their 2019 AFCON, and will finally make it to the final tournament in Cameroon, Completesportsnigeria.com reports.
To start a qualifying campaign on a losing note is bad," Nwosu told Completesportsnigeria com of the Super Eagles 2-0 loss to Bafana Bafana in Uyo.
"I will not like to single out anybody for blame but I want to emphasize that it would be catastrophic should they lose their next game in the qualifiers.
"This result means that they must win all their remaining matches, and that's a big task, but unfortunately must be so now.
"What happened was unfortunate, but in Nigeria, we love surprises and can still beat South Africa in their home in the reverse fixture."
He would also react on the talks that the experience of the likes of John Mikel Obi and Victor Moses would have made the difference for the Eagles against Bafana.
"Any player wearing Nigeria's colours could have helped the team win. South Africa were simply better in the match," Nwosu who was the revelation at the Maroc '88 Africa Cup of Nations where he scored a goal that was ruled out in the final against Cameroon stated.
The post Nwosu Optimistic Nigeria Will Qualify For 2019 AFCON Despite Matchday-One Setback appeared first on Complete Sports Nigeria.

“Initiating a qualification series with a loss is decidedly unfavorable,” Nwosu remarked. He declined to assign individual blame for the result but emphasized the critical nature of the upcoming fixtures. “It would be catastrophic should they lose their next qualifying match,” he stated. “This outcome necessitates victory in all remaining matches, which constitutes a considerable challenge, yet it has become an imperative following the opening defeat.”

While characterizing the loss as unfortunate, Nwosu highlighted the unpredictable nature of football, particularly within the Nigerian context. “In Nigeria, we are accustomed to surprises and remain capable of defeating South Africa in the return fixture on their home ground,” he asserted.

Addressing commentary suggesting that the experience of absent players such as John Mikel Obi and Victor Moses might have altered the match’s outcome, Nwosu offered a pragmatic assessment. “Any individual selected to represent Nigeria is expected to contribute to a positive result,” he noted. “In this instance, South Africa simply demonstrated superior performance on the day.” Nwosu, who was a notable figure at the 1988 Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco—where a goal he scored in the final against Cameroon was disallowed—spoke from a position of considerable international experience.

His commentary underscores a belief in the team’s capacity for resilience despite the significant pressure now imposed by the initial setback. The focus, according to Nwosu, must shift unequivocally to securing maximum points from the remaining qualification matches to ensure progression to the 2019 AFCON finals.

A Kilgore woman has pleaded guilty to killing her mother and has accepted a 35-year prison sentence.
Kayla Ann Wheeler, 29, entered the plea in Judge David Brabham’s courtroom Monday. She had been scheduled for jury selection.
Wheeler was arrested in November 2016 after police responded to a body call in Hidden Hills Apartments in Longview. Police say the body of Elizabeth Jane Wheeler, 52, had been in the apartment for several days and officers were notified by the apartment complex management team.
According to a probable cause for arrest, Wheeler initially arrived at the location asking about her mother. She voluntarily agreed to be interviewed.
During the course of that interview, Wheeler "admitted to stabbing her mother in the neck with a knife following a physical altercation with her mother," the document reads.
She told detectives, "It was me. I killed her."

rewrite: On Monday, Kayla Ann Wheeler, a 29-year-old resident of Kilgore, entered a guilty plea in the courtroom of Judge David Brabham to the charge of killing her mother, accepting a 35-year prison sentence. This plea occurred prior to the scheduled commencement of jury selection. The case originated in November 2016 when law enforcement, responding to a request from the management of the Hidden Hills Apartments in Longview, discovered the deceased body of 52-year-old Elizabeth Jane Wheeler, who had been deceased for several days. According to the probable cause affidavit, the defendant initially arrived at the scene inquiring about her mother and voluntarily submitted to an interview. During that interview, Wheeler confessed to stabbing her mother in the neck with a knife following a physical altercation, explicitly stating to detectives, "It was me. I killed her."

The shipwreck found off Auckland’s west coast has been identified as looters were warned again that they could face a fine of $60,000 for stealing any part of the wreck, which is classified as an archaeological site.
The wreck was identified as the Daring, a 17m long schooner that was driven ashore by wild gales in 1865.
Vandals were warned about damaging Daring, with the wreck protected under the provisions of the Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga Act, with someone taking to the timbers with a chainsaw since 1 NEWS first visited the site on Tuesday.
The vessel, which was built in Mangawhai in 1863, had been carrying grass seed from Taranaki to Onehunga. No one died as it was beached intact.
Experts believe the wreck is well preserved because it appears to have been buried in sand since it was driven ashore.
The New Zealand Maritime Museum alerted Auckland Council’s heritage department to a Facebook post showing the discovery.
Robert Brassey, Auckland Council’s Principal Specialist in Cultural Heritage and maritime history expert, says it’s an astounding discovery.
“It’s extremely rare for a wreck of this age to have survived in such good condition; it is a significant part of our maritime heritage,” he said.
“However what’s even more astounding is that someone has been selfish enough to have damaged the ship within days of it being exposed by scavenging timber off it.”
Any person damaging or destroying the wreck is liable for a fine up to $60,000.
rewrite:
The shipwreck located off the west coast of Auckland has been formally identified. Concurrently, warnings have been reissued that individuals removing material from the site, which holds protected archaeological status, face penalties of up to $60,000. The vessel has been confirmed as the *Daring*, a seventeen-meter schooner driven ashore during a severe gale in 1865. Constructed in Mangawhai in 1863, the schooner was transporting grass seed from Taranaki to Onehunga at the time of its loss; it beached intact, resulting in no fatalities.

Maritime experts indicate the wreck is exceptionally well-preserved, likely due to having remained buried in sand since its stranding. The New Zealand Maritime Museum initially notified the Auckland Council’s heritage department after the discovery was highlighted in a social media post. Robert Brassey, Principal Specialist in Cultural Heritage for Auckland Council and a maritime history expert, described the find as astounding. He noted the rarity of a wreck from this period surviving in such condition, emphasizing its significance as a maritime heritage asset. Brassey further expressed dismay that an individual had deliberately damaged the vessel by removing timber with a chainsaw shortly after its exposure, an act he characterized as profoundly selfish.

The site is protected under the Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga Act, and any person damaging or destroying the wreck is liable to prosecution and a fine not exceeding $60,000.

An event which treats guests to a slap-up meal before they watch a human dissection is coming to Sussex.
After a series of sell-out tours across the UK, Anatomy Lab Live will arrive at the Hilton Brighton Metropole, on March 9 next year.
Anatomy Lab
The spine-tingling experience invites guests to sit down to dinner while watching trained anatomists disect a semi-synthetic human body.
And to top it off, visitors can have a go at dissecting body parts themselves.
Anatomist Sam Piri said the show was aimed at healthcare professionals and students, as well as those with a strong interest in the human body.
He added: “I wanted to give people something that is real, to see, touch, feel and smell. I wanted to give people something that is real, to see, touch, feel and smell.
“After a very successful tour earlier this year we’re back bigger and better than before.
“You’ll have the chance to dissect the specimens guided by myself and my team to really enhance your understanding of anatomy, physiology and the clinical pathology.”
To begin with two anatomists will dissect VIVIT – which is claimed to be the world’s only semi-synthetic human corpse with real organs.
They will carry out an in-depth observation of various disease states before mortuary technicians bring samples out to the audience for a closer look.
The organs – which all come from pigs because of the anatomical similarity with humans – include the brain, spinal cord, stomach, liver and rectum.
Guests will be given mortuary wear including protective surgical hats, masks and aprons as well as scalpels, scissors, forceps and bone saws to help with their own dissection attempt.
They can look closer inside a real head and brain sample, dissect the heart and blood vessels, and observe the structure of the limbs.
Sam added: “Together we’ll experience the physiology of clinical pathology comparing healthy and diseased samples.
“We’ll learn how the human body is built and how a post-mortem is conducted.”
There will also be time for questions to the team about different pathology.
Standard tickets cost £79 with reductions for NHS staff, students and groups.
All ticket-holders must be over 16.
For more information on Anatomy Lab Live go to anatomylablive.co.uk.
rewrite:
A forthcoming event in Sussex will offer attendees a formal dinner followed by an observational human dissection. Following a series of sold-out presentations across the United Kingdom, *Anatomy Lab Live* is scheduled to occur at the Hilton Brighton Metropole on 9 March of the coming year. This distinctive experience involves a seated dinner during which trained anatomists perform a dissection upon a semi-synthetic human cadaver. Furthermore, participants will be afforded the opportunity to undertake guided dissection of anatomical specimens themselves.

Anatomist Sam Piri, the event’s lead, states that the presentation is designed for healthcare professionals, medical students, and individuals with a dedicated interest in human anatomy. He elaborates: “My objective was to provide an authentic, multisensory encounter—to see, touch, feel, and smell real anatomical structures. After a highly successful tour earlier this year, we are returning with an expanded and enhanced programme. Under the guidance of myself and my team, you will have the chance to dissect specimens, thereby deepening your understanding of anatomy, physiology, and clinical pathology.”

The proceedings will commence with two anatomists dissecting a subject known as VIVIT, described as the world’s sole semi-synthetic human cadaver incorporating genuine organic matter. They will conduct a detailed examination of various pathological states, after which mortuary technicians will distribute tissue samples to the audience for closer inspection. These organs, which are porcine in origin due to their anatomical similarity to human structures, include the brain, spinal cord, stomach, liver, and rectum.

Participants will be provided with appropriate mortuary attire, including protective surgical caps, masks, and aprons, alongside dissecting instruments such as scalpels, scissors, forceps, and bone saws for their practical engagement. Activities will include the examination of a real cephalic and cerebral specimen, dissection of cardiac and vascular tissues, and observation of the structural anatomy of the limbs. Mr. Piri adds: “Collectively, we will explore the physiology of clinical pathology by comparing healthy and diseased samples. We will learn about the construction of the human body and the methodology of a post-mortem examination.” A dedicated question-and-answer session with the anatomical team will also be included.

Standard admission is priced at £79, with discounted rates available for National Health Service staff, students, and groups. All attendees must be aged sixteen or above. Further details regarding *Anatomy Lab Live* are available at anatomylablive.co.uk.

A NSW police officer said "do what you want" when her colleague asked if he could film them having sex, a Sydney court has been told.
Giving evidence in the Downing Centre Local Court on Tuesday, Timothy Michael Patterson said the woman had consented to him filming them having sex at a Sydney hotel in July 2017.
But he said she didn't know he was posting the videos to a Snapchat group - which he did to boast to his mates.
Camera Icon Timothy Patterson Picture: AAP
Patterson said he asked if the woman minded if he filmed them and she replied: "Yeah, I don't care. Do what you want."
The 28-year-old has pleaded not guilty to three counts of filming the woman in a private act without her consent for the purposes of sexual gratification and of using a carriage service to menace, harass or offend.
Patterson described the encounter as "exciting" saying he wanted to make the video for them both.
But prosecutor Mardi Cartwright suggested he had covertly filmed his colleague for the sexual gratification of himself and other male police officers who were members of a Snapchat group called "No Snitches".
The now-suspended senior constable said the purpose was not sexual gratification but to boast to his mates.
"As juvenile as it was (I did it to) boast to the guys I was having sex and they weren't," he said.

MGM Holdings Inc said it would acquire the 81 percent of premium U.S. channel Epix it does not already own from two of its partners, Viacom Inc and Lionsgate Entertainment Corp, for about $1 billion.
The deal is expected to boost MGM's TV business as it seeks to build a stronger platform to distribute its content.
Viacom currently owns half of Epix, while Lionsgate has a 31.2 percent stake.
Epix, whose shows include "Berlin Station" and "Graves," has about 14 million subscribers, according to research firm SNL Kagan.
Paramount Pictures and Lionsgate will continue to provide their first-run theatrical releases to Epix under multi-year agreements, the companies said in a joint statement.
The deal is expected to close by the end of this month.
Famous for its library that includes James Bond, Rocky and other classics, MGM also co-produces and distributes television shows such as "Teen Wolf" on MTV, "Vikings" on A&E and "Fargo" on FX.
It also owns MGM-branded U.S. channels that largely play its films and international networks.
MGM, which emerged from bankruptcy six years ago, is controlled by hedge funds including Anchorage Capital Partners and Highland Capital Partners.
LionTree Advisors was financial adviser to Viacom and Lionsgate. Shearman & Sterling LLP was legal adviser to Viacom, while O'Melveny & Myers LLP served as Lionsgate's legal adviser. Latham & Watkins LLP was MGM's legal adviser.
(Reporting by Laharee Chatterjee and Nikhil Subba in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva)

Ethiopian Airlines lands Airbus in Abuja Tuesday
The Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport will be open for traffic from Tuesday and Ethiopian Airlines says it will land a brand new Airbus A350-900 to mark the official reopening of the airport on Wednesday.
The Airline’s Traffic and Sales Manager, Mrs. Firiehiwot Mekonnen, made this known, on Monday, in Abuja.
Mekonnen said that the aircraft would land in Abuja on its first day of operation from Addis Ababa and that it would remain on Abuja route.
The airline launched its first A350-900 Airbus on the London Heathrow route August last year. It has three of the plane in its fleet and awaits the delivery of nine more before 2019.
She said that the decision to celebrate the inaugural flight to Abuja was because of the airline’s commitment to the Nigerian market.
According to the manager, the 313-passenger capacity aircraft is expected to land at 11.15 am to be the first aircraft to land at the newly rehabilitated Abuja runway.
“The Ethiopian’s brand new Airbus A350-900 is landing in Abuja airport tomorrow (Tuesday) as the first aircraft to land on the newly rehabilitated runway and first airbus to land in Abuja.
“From now on, we are going to operate Airbus on Abuja route,’’ she said.
When Abuja Airport was closed on March 8 for repairs on its runway and flight operations were diverted to Kaduna International Airport, Ethiopian Airlines was the first to land its new Boeing 787 in Kaduna.
The airline, being the only international carrier that agreed to operate at Kaduna, had maintained consistent operation at the airport in the last six weeks.
Governor Nasir el-Rufai of Kaduna State had also requested that the airline maintained its Kaduna operation even after the reopening of Abuja airport.
Mokennen said that the airline “is seriously considering the governor’s request”. (NAN)

The St. Vincent De Paul pharmacy in Biloxi reached a big milestone with a 20th anniversary celebration at the downtown Biloxi facility.
Twenty years ago, the Catholic Diocese of Biloxi saw a need to help those who couldn't help themselves with pharmaceuticals. More than 203,000 prescriptions have since been filled by the St. Vincent De Paul Pharmacy.
“Many of our clients are here sometimes for just a stop gap, they've lost their job, or they've recently lost their home,” said Sam Burke, pharmacy executive director. “Whatever it might be, hopefully we can just bridge that gap for them. We're trying to give them the medicines they need for some semblance of a good quality of life, a much better quality of life if they did not have them."
Burke added that the facility has come a long way since its humble beginnings in a trailer, which was eventually destroyed by Hurricane Katrina.
"There's a lot of folks that would not be able to have the kind of medications they have and need without this group here,” said Bishop Louis Kihneman, Diocese of Biloxi. “They do wondrous work, and we're blessed to have them. There are some people, that without this medication, they would not be able to survive."
The pharmacy already has satellite locations in Bay. St. Louis and Moss Point. Coming in October, they'll have another location in the northern part of the Diocese in Hattiesburg.

rewrite:
The St. Vincent De Paul Pharmacy in Biloxi recently commemorated a significant milestone: its twentieth anniversary, observed at its downtown Biloxi facility. Two decades prior, the Catholic Diocese of Biloxi identified a critical need to provide pharmaceutical assistance to individuals unable to secure such resources independently. Since its inception, the pharmacy has dispensed in excess of 203,000 prescriptions.

Sam Burke, the pharmacy’s executive director, noted that the clientele often includes individuals experiencing temporary crises, such as job loss or displacement. “Our objective is to bridge that gap,” Burke stated, “by providing necessary medications to afford them a semblance, or a significantly improved quality of life, which would be unattainable otherwise.” He reflected on the institution’s evolution from its modest origins in a trailer, a structure later destroyed by Hurricane Katrina.

Bishop Louis Kihneman of the Diocese of Biloxi emphasized the pharmacy’s vital role, asserting, “Many individuals would lack essential medications without this service. The work performed is remarkable, and its presence is a blessing to the community. For some, this access is a matter of survival.”

In addition to its primary site, the pharmacy currently operates satellite locations in Bay St. Louis and Moss Point. Further expansion is planned, with an additional location scheduled to open in Hattiesburg, within the northern region of the Diocese, in October.

China is taking their restrictions to the next level, now working to bar people from transportation like flights and planes due to bad “social credit.” According to Reuters, “people who would be put on the restricted lists included those found to have committed acts like spreading false information about terrorism and causing trouble on flights, as well as those who used expired tickets or smoked on trains.”
The National Development and Reform Commission also claimed that people who had “financial wrongdoings, such as employers who failed to pay social insurance or people who have failed to pay fines” would also face these travel restrictions as well. This new plan will go into effect on May 1, and is part of China’s ongoing (but still unofficial) plan to measure their citizens’ “social credit” based on the principle of “once untrustworthy, always restricted.” In a very Black Mirror move, there are also plans for a system that would allow for government organizations to disclose data on their citizens’ trustworthiness and issue penalties and additional restrictions based on people’s social credit score.
This may not be a totally new move, though, as 6.15 million Chinese citizens have been banned from various modes of transportation due to their “social misdeeds” back in early 2017.

Furthermore, the National Development and Reform Commission has indicated that those engaged in financial misconduct, including employers neglecting social insurance payments or individuals failing to settle fines, will also be subject to these travel limitations. Scheduled to take effect on May 1, this policy forms part of China's broader, though not formally codified, initiative to assess citizen trustworthiness under the principle of "once untrustworthy, always restricted." This development is not entirely unprecedented, as approximately 6.15 million citizens were already prohibited from using various transport services in early 2017 due to recorded social misconduct.

A plane carrying 35 diplomats expelled from the United States over Russia's alleged meddling in the U.S. presidential election arrived in Moscow early Monday, Russian state television reported.
A Russian Il-96 plane carrying the diplomats and their families landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at 2:05 am local time after having taken off from Washington on Sunday, state television said.
U.S. intelligence says the Kremlin ordered a hack-and-release of Democratic Party and Hillary Clinton campaign staff emails in a bid to put Donald Trump in the White House.
Moscow has repeatedly dismissed the allegations.
The expulsions of the diplomats -- described as intelligence operatives based at the Russian embassy in Washington and the consulate in San Francisco -- were part of a package of sanctions ordered by President Barack Obama Thursday in the final weeks of his administration.
Obama also ordered the closure of two Russian compounds in New York and Maryland that the United States says were used "for intelligence-related purposes."
Russian President Vladimir Putin last week rebuked the outgoing president for "unfriendly steps" amounting to "a provocation aimed at further undermining Russian-American relations."
The Kremlin strongman warned that Russia reserved the right to respond but refrained from ordering the tit-for-tat expulsion of American diplomats from Russia, saying that Moscow's next move will be "based on the policies pursued by the administration of president Donald Trump."
Putin's decision has been interpreted as a sign he is looking to Trump to rebuild U.S.-Russian ties after he is inaugurated as president later this month.
rewrite:
Early on Monday, Russian state media reported the arrival in Moscow of an aircraft transporting thirty-five diplomatic personnel expelled from the United States. This action was a direct response to allegations of Russian interference in the U.S. presidential election. The Il-96 aircraft, carrying the diplomats and their families, landed at Vnukovo Airport at 2:05 a.m. local time following its departure from Washington on Sunday.

According to U.S. intelligence assessments, the Russian government orchestrated cyber intrusions and the subsequent dissemination of emails from the Democratic Party and the Hillary Clinton campaign, ostensibly to influence the electoral outcome in favor of Donald Trump. Russian authorities have consistently denied these accusations. The expulsions, targeting individuals identified as intelligence operatives stationed at the Russian embassy in Washington and the consulate in San Francisco, constituted a component of sanctions authorized by President Barack Obama during the final weeks of his term. Concurrently, President Obama mandated the closure of two Russian facilities in New York and Maryland, asserted by the U.S. to have served intelligence-gathering functions.

In reaction, Russian President Vladimir Putin criticized these measures as "unfriendly steps" and a "provocation" detrimental to bilateral relations. While asserting Russia's right to retaliate, President Putin notably declined to implement immediate reciprocal expulsions of American diplomats. Instead, he indicated that subsequent Russian actions would be contingent upon the foreign policy trajectory of the incoming administration of President-elect Donald Trump. This posture has been widely interpreted as signaling a strategic pause, with Moscow anticipating an opportunity to recalibrate relations under the new U.S. presidency.

HARARE, Zimbabwe (AP) — Pakistan had five balls to spare when it beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets on Wednesday and eliminated the African host from the Twenty20 tri-series tournament.
Solomon Mire missed out on the chance to become Zimbabwe's first century-maker in a T20 international as his 94-run knock carried Zimbabwe to 162-4 after captain Hamilton Masakadza lost his first toss in the tri-series and his team was put in to bat.
Opener Fakhar Zaman (47) and Hussain Talat (44) led Pakistan to 163-3 in 19.1 overs against an inexperienced bowling attack as Pakistan registered its second win against Zimbabwe.
It was Zimbabwe's third straight loss.
Australia plays against Pakistan on Thursday before both teams meet in Sunday's final.
Mire stood tall against Pakistan's full-strength attack as left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Amir (1-25) got his first game of the series and replaced Usman Khan.
Mire and Cephas Zhuwao (24) provided a solid opening partnership of 49 runs before Tarisai Musakanda (33) added 64 runs for the third wicket with Mire.
Mire, who hit six sixes and six fours, reached his half-century off 32 balls when he hoisted left-arm spinner Mohammad Nawaz for a six over long off in the 11th over.
Pakistan struggled for wickets despite seamer Faheem Ashraf (1-24) and leg-spinner Shadab Khan (1-28) bowling a decent four overs each in the middle overs.
Mire looked set to become the first Zimbabwe batsman to score a century in a Twenty20 before he holed out at deep mid-wicket off seamer Talat in the 18th over — only a ball after Asif Ali missed a sitter at deep square leg.
Mire also featured in two dismissals during Pakistan's innings as he took a fine catch in the deep to dismiss Haris Sohail. He then denied Zaman a half century through his medium pace when the left-hander was caught at mid-on.
Captain Sarfraz Ahmed (38 not out) and experienced Shoaib Malik (12 not out) kept their composure and carried Pakistan home.
Ahmed was not happy with his bowlers, saying it "was not up to the mark, they have to work hard."
rewrite:
In a Twenty20 tri-series match in Harare on Wednesday, Pakistan secured a seven-wicket victory over Zimbabwe with five deliveries remaining, thereby eliminating the host nation from the tournament. Zimbabwe, having been sent in to bat after captain Hamilton Masakadza lost the toss, posted a total of 162-4. This innings was anchored by Solomon Mire, whose 94-run performance narrowly missed establishing him as Zimbabwe’s first centurion in T20 international cricket. Pakistan, in response, achieved the target of 163 in 19.1 overs, guided by opener Fakhar Zaman (47) and Hussain Talat (44), registering their second win against Zimbabwe and condemning the hosts to a third consecutive defeat in the series. The result sets the stage for Pakistan’s upcoming match against Australia on Thursday, with both teams scheduled to contest the final on Sunday.

Mire’s innings constituted a resilient effort against a full-strength Pakistani attack, which featured the return of left-arm fast bowler Mohammad Amir (1-25). He formed a solid opening partnership of 49 with Cephas Zhuwao (24) and later added 64 for the third wicket with Tarisai Musakanda (33). Demonstrating aggressive strokeplay, Mire struck six sixes and six fours, reaching his half-century off 32 balls. Despite disciplined spells from seamer Faheem Ashraf (1-24) and leg-spinner Shadab Khan (1-28), Pakistan struggled to take wickets during the middle overs. Mire appeared poised for a historic century until his dismissal in the 18th over, caught at deep mid-wicket off the bowling of seamer Hussain Talat, immediately after a dropped chance by Asif Ali.

Mire also contributed in the field during Pakistan’s chase, taking a catch to dismiss Haris Sohail and later removing Fakhar Zaman with his medium pace to deny the opener a half-century. The Pakistani innings was ultimately guided to completion by captain Sarfraz Ahmed (38 not out) and the experienced Shoaib Malik (12 not out), who maintained their composure to secure the win. Reflecting on the performance, Captain Ahmed expressed dissatisfaction with his bowling unit, stating it was not up to the required standard and emphasizing the need for greater effort.

FRANKFURT The head of Germany's central bank would be happy to see the European Central Bank buying bonds at a lower pace in a year's time, he told German weekly Die Zeit.
Bundesbank President Jens Weidmann said in the interview the time to reduce the ECB's monetary stimulus to the economy was approaching as the recovery gained pace.
"The time to keep the foot no longer on the metal, but to take it off slightly ... is approaching in my view," Jens Weidmann said in the interview, due to be appear in Die Zeit's Thursday edition.
Asked whether he sided with his Dutch colleague Klaas Knot in expecting that ECB bond purchases would not be running at their current pace a year from now, Weidmann said: "I would welcome that."
"But generally I don't speculate on the future decisions of the ECB's Governing Council," he added.
Weidmann's remarks in the interview were slightly different than in a preview published earlier, in which it was said Weidmann would welcome it if there were no ECB purchase sat all a year from now.
(Reporting by Francesco Canepa; Editing by Alison Williams)
rewrite: In an interview with the German weekly publication Die Zeit, Bundesbank President Jens Weidmann indicated his approval of a prospective reduction in the European Central Bank’s bond-buying pace within the coming year. Weidmann stated that, as economic recovery accelerates, the appropriate moment to begin scaling back the ECB’s monetary stimulus measures is drawing nearer. “The time to keep the foot no longer on the metal, but to take it off slightly ... is approaching in my view,” he remarked in the interview, scheduled for publication in the Thursday edition. When questioned whether he agreed with Dutch central bank governor Klaas Knot’s expectation that ECB asset purchases would not continue at their present rate in a year’s time, Weidmann responded, “I would welcome that.” He further clarified, “But generally I don’t speculate on the future decisions of the ECB’s Governing Council.” It is noted that these comments differ slightly from an earlier preview of the interview, which had suggested Weidmann would welcome a complete cessation of ECB purchases within a year.

NASHVILLE — Tennessee quarterback Marcus Mariota will be a game-time decision for Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins.
Mariota was listed Friday as questionable for the game in Miami after being limited in practice for the third consecutive day with a left hamstring injury suffered last week in a 57-14 loss at Houston.
"I've been able to get out there for a little bit, but the majority of practice I do a lot of rehab. My first and foremost goal is to get healthy, and that's what I've been working on," Mariota said Friday.
Mariota said he needs to have some mobility in order to be able to play. The Titans (2-2) are talking about letting him take part in Saturday's walk-through. But a final decision might not be reached until 90 minutes before kickoff Sunday when the list of inactives is due.
"I think if I'm able to move around and am able to hand the ball off, and am able to drop back, then I'll definitely play," Mariota said. "It's a tough decision. It's a decision that was made this past Sunday in Houston. It's never easy for an athlete. To that point, I'm going to do my best to get healthy, and hopefully, I'll be ready to go."
Titans coach Mike Mularkey said he didn't want Mariota doing much in practice, preferring the quarterback to heal up.
"We're not putting him to a point where he could make it any worse, so he actually feels pretty good right now," Mularkey said.
If Mariota is unable to start, then backup Matt Cassel will start. He took the bulk of the first-team reps in practice this week after struggling last week coming off the bench. Cassel was intercepted twice with one returned for a touchdown and stripped of the ball when sacked.
Brandon Weeden, signed Tuesday as insurance, would be the backup if Mariota does not play.
Both wide receiver Corey Davis and safety Johnathan Cyprien as out again this week. Both players have missed multiple weeks with hamstring injuries of their own.
rewrite:
The availability of Tennessee Titans quarterback Marcus Mariota for Sunday’s contest against the Miami Dolphins will be determined at game time. Mariota was officially listed as questionable on the injury report following his third consecutive day of limited participation in practice. The limitation stems from a left hamstring injury sustained during the previous week’s 57-14 loss to the Houston Texans.

In a statement issued Friday, Mariota emphasized his ongoing rehabilitation efforts. “I have been able to participate on a limited basis, but the majority of my practice time has been devoted to rehabilitation. My primary objective is to regain full health, which has been the focus of my work,” he stated. Mariota further clarified that sufficient mobility is a prerequisite for his participation. The Titans organization is considering involving him in Saturday’s walk-through session, though a definitive decision regarding his status may be deferred until 90 minutes prior to kickoff on Sunday, coinciding with the deadline for submitting the inactive player list.

Mariota elaborated on his criteria for playing, noting, “If I demonstrate the ability to move effectively, execute handoffs, and drop back to pass, I will certainly play. The decision is a challenging one, originating from the injury event in Houston. Such determinations are invariably difficult for any athlete. Accordingly, I am dedicating my efforts to recovery with the hope of being prepared to play.” Head coach Mike Mularkey corroborated this cautious approach, indicating that the practice restrictions are intentional to prevent aggravation of the injury. “We are avoiding situations that could potentially worsen the condition. At present, he is reporting positive progress,” Mularkey affirmed.

Should Mariota be unable to start, backup quarterback Matt Cassel is prepared to assume the role. Cassel received the majority of first-team repetitions during practice this week following a difficult relief appearance in the previous game, during which he threw two interceptions—one returned for a touchdown—and lost a fumble on a sack. Recently signed quarterback Brandon Weeden would serve as the backup in this scenario.

Additionally, the Titans will be without wide receiver Corey Davis and safety Johnathan Cyprien for another week. Both players continue to recover from their respective hamstring injuries, having now missed multiple consecutive games.

Coca-Cola's began selling Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, a reformulated replacement for Coca-Cola Zero, in 20 markets last year. It reported a "double-digit" growth during the quarter Tuesday. The company has also been moving its Honest and Smartwater brands into more international markets.

The world's largest drink maker reported a 3 percent boost in volume and a 4 percent jump for concentrates, with its namesake brand contributing the most. Concentrate sales rose in every region but Latin America, where they were flat.
"We're encouraged with our first quarter performance as we continue our evolution as a consumer-centric, total beverage company," said CEO James Quincey.

You might have caught the news that Opera is killing its Opera Max VPN service. That's a bummer, but there are plenty of VPN apps out there if you don't absolutely need the data compression features of Max. For example, the newly released Kaspersky Secure Connection app. It's in beta and only has limited data, but it's free.
Kaspersky Secure Connection is designed to prompt you to turn it on whenever you connect to an unsecured public WiFi hotspot. The functionality when you're connected is about what you'd expect from any other VPN app. Your traffic is routed through the encrypted connection to the VPN server, then out to its destination. This prevents eavesdropping and logging of your data, but the VPN can see everything you do. Kaspersky says it will not keep any logs of your activity, so it's up to you if you believe that.
The app is currently free with no in-app purchases. There will be IAPs, though. Eventually, you'll be able to spend $6.49-38.99 on subscriptions to the premium VPN service with unlimited data. Right now, you're limited to 200MB of daily traffic in the beta version of the app. That's reasonably generous compared to other VPN apps. If you just need a VPN to do a few sensitive things on public WiFi, that could be all you need.
rewrite:
Opera has announced the discontinuation of its Opera Max VPN service. While this development may be disappointing for some users, numerous alternative VPN applications remain available, particularly for those whose requirements do not specifically include the data compression functionality offered by Max. One such alternative is the recently launched Kaspersky Secure Connection application, currently in a beta phase. Although it provides a limited data allowance, it is offered free of charge.

This application is engineered to automatically prompt the user to activate the VPN upon connecting to an unsecured public WiFi network. Its core operational principle aligns with standard VPN protocols: user traffic is encrypted and routed through a secure VPN server before proceeding to its final destination. This process mitigates risks associated with data interception and local logging on the public network. It is important to note, however, that the VPN provider itself retains the technical capacity to monitor user activity. Kaspersky asserts a strict no-logging policy, leaving the evaluation of this claim to the discretion of the individual user.

The beta version is presently free and devoid of in-app purchases, though a premium subscription model is planned for future implementation. Projected pricing for unlimited data ranges from $6.49 to $38.99. The current beta imposes a daily data limit of 200MB, a comparatively generous allocation relative to other free VPN services. For users whose needs are confined to occasional, sensitive tasks on public networks, this provision may prove entirely sufficient.

Petitioners ignorant— Sole Administrator
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
ABUJA—Staff of ABUJA—Staff of Ajaokuta Steel Company in Kogi State have petitioned the Federal Government over alleged refusal of the Sole Administrator, Mr Joseph Isah, to retire after completing his tenure.The staff, in the petition sent through Acting Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Mrs. Habibat Lawal, to Acting President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo; and Minister of Mines and Steel Development, Dr. Kayode Fayemi, asked for Federal Government’s urgent intervention.
In the said petition, Isah allegedly refused to hand over to the most senior management staff after completing his 35 years as stipulated by the Nigerian Civil Service Rules.In the petition by Mr. Salifu Oguche Usman Esq, Principal Partner at Abbluent Partners, Abuja, on behalf of the Ajaokuta Steel Company staff, it was claimed that Isah should have retired on August 3, 2017, having completed the statutory 35 years of service.
He was said to have been employed on August 3, 1982, as a Process Engineer in the company.The staff accused him of re-appointing himself to remain in office beyond his tenure and asked for his immediate exit.Isah was also accused of contravening financial and administrative regulations of government as he was alleged to have diverted workers’ promotion allowances to other uses.However, Isah told Vanguard on phone that the petitioners acted out of ignorance.“I was appointed sole administrator in November 2012. Technically, by that appointment, my civil service career ended because my appointment is a political appointment. I earn a political appointee’s salary. My appointment letter is there for anyone to see,” he said.
The staff urged the SGF not to only direct the Sole Administrator to proceed on retirement but also investigate the allegations on financial impropriety and other infractions raised by them against the Sole Administrator.
rewrite:
Staff members of the Ajaokuta Steel Company Limited in Kogi State have formally petitioned the Federal Government of Nigeria concerning the alleged refusal of the Sole Administrator, Mr. Joseph Isah, to retire following the completion of his statutory tenure. The petition, submitted through the Acting Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Mrs. Habibat Lawal, and addressed to the Acting President, Professor Yemi Osinbajo, and the Minister of Mines and Steel Development, Dr. Kayode Fayemi, requests urgent federal intervention.

The petition, prepared by Mr. Salifu Oguche Usman, Esq., Principal Partner at Abbluent Partners in Abuja, asserts that Mr. Isah was obligated to retire on August 3, 2017, having completed the mandatory 35 years of service as stipulated under Nigerian Civil Service Rules, following his initial employment as a Process Engineer on August 3, 1982. It is alleged that instead of handing over to the most senior management staff, he has effectively reappointed himself to remain in office. Furthermore, the petition accuses him of contravening governmental financial and administrative regulations, specifically by diverting funds allocated for staff promotion allowances to other purposes.

In response to these allegations, Mr. Isah, contacted by telephone, stated that the petitioners are misinformed. He clarified that his civil service career concluded upon his appointment as Sole Administrator in November 2012, which he characterizes as a political appointment. He emphasized that he receives a political appointee’s salary and indicated that his appointment letter is available for verification.

The staff have appealed that the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation not only direct the Sole Administrator to proceed on retirement but also institute a comprehensive investigation into the allegations of financial impropriety and other administrative infractions detailed in the petition.

Norway and Romania each enjoyed victories as Ivory Coast confirmed their withdrawal from the Women's Junior World Handball Championship in Debrecen.
Ivory Coast did not turn up for their opening matches in Group A and have now confirmed their non participation.
"On July 4, the 2018 International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Junior World Championship Competition Management received the official notice that the Ivory Coast team will not be able to travel to Hungary for the event and will therefore not participate," a statement confirmed.
"This information came following the delayed travel of the team, after which the Group A schedule was adjusted in the hope of avoiding the cancellation of other matches.
"In accordance with the corresponding decision of the Competition Management following the relevant IHF Regulations, the team of Ivory Coast will be removed from the match schedule of the event.
"This means that all other teams in Group A will only play four preliminary round matches."
Norway, who missed their first match against the Ivorians, triumphed 25-20 against Brazil in their first encounter at the Főnix Hall.
Romania overcame Paraguay elsewhere today ©HungaryHandball2018
In Group B, defending bronze medallists Romania progressed in a 41-25 win over Paraguay at the Hódos Imre Sports Hall.
Romania only led 16-13 at the halfway point before pressing ahead.
Andrada-Bianca Berbece scored 10 goals for the European side.
Hungary also beat Portugal 33-20 today in Group A.
in Group C, Japan were beaten 33-23 by defending champions Denmark while The Netherlands beat Angola 37-21.
rewrite:
The opening day of the 2018 International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Junior World Championship in Debrecen was marked by competitive matches and a significant withdrawal. The Ivory Coast national team formally confirmed its non-participation in the tournament. According to an official statement, the IHF Competition Management received notification on July 4th that the team would be unable to travel to Hungary. This decision followed earlier travel delays, which had initially prompted a rescheduling of Group A matches in anticipation of the team's arrival. In accordance with IHF regulations, the Competition Management subsequently removed Ivory Coast from the event schedule. Consequently, all remaining teams in Group A will now play only four preliminary round matches instead of five.

In the ensuing competition, Norway secured a 25-20 victory over Brazil in Group A at the Főnix Hall, a match originally slated against Ivory Coast. Meanwhile, in Group B, the defending bronze medalists, Romania, achieved a 41-25 win against Paraguay at the Hódos Imre Sports Hall. After leading narrowly 16-13 at halftime, Romania extended its advantage in the second period, with Andrada-Bianca Berbece contributing ten goals. In other results, Hungary defeated Portugal 33-20 in Group A. Group C saw defending champions Denmark overcome Japan 33-23, while the Netherlands triumphed over Angola with a score of 37-21.

For the second summer in succession Cheltenham Town face a battle to retain the services of Harry Pell.
A rival League Two club are keen to sign the 26-year-old, who was close to joining Blackpool in a £200,000 move last August.
On that occasion the Robins accepted the bid, but with a two year deal on the table Pell failed to agree personal terms with the newly-promoted League One side.

Chesterfield were also keen on the 6ft 5in midfielder last summer, but a different club from the fourth tier have now made an approach to capture his signature ahead of 2018/19.
Pell signed a two-and-a-half year contract extension in January 2017, keeping him at Whaddon Road until the end of next season.
He joined Cheltenham ahead of their National League title winning campaign of 2015/16, instantly becoming a fans' favourite and he has made more than 120 starts for the club.
Born in Essex, Pell started out in the youth set-up at Charlton Athletic before spells at Bristol Rovers, Hereford, AFC Wimbledon and Eastleigh.
A specialist central midfielder, Pell has also been used as a wide forward and a central striker in his three years with the Robins.
He has scored three goals in his last five games, including a brace in the 5-3 win at Crawley Town on March 24.
But he missed Saturday's 4-3 defeat at Cambridge United after having two wisdom teeth removed.
When he is on song he is undoubtedly one of Cheltenham's most influential players, regularly catching the eye of opposition managers and fans alike.

The Binghamton Central School District has been awarded a $29 million grant from the New York State Office of Child and Family Services. They will receive $577,000 each year for the next five years in order to provide long-term afterschool programming to more than 400 students from Kindergarten through Seniors in high school.
"We know that when we're able to support our students outside of the school day as well as throughout the summer months, they will succeed both academically as well as socially, emotionally, and physically," said Tonia Thompson, Binghamton Central School District Superintendent.
We have been very successful at getting money into communities that experience high levels of poverty through the Empire State Poverty Reduction Initiative, which has also targeted the City of Binghamton and the surrounding urban areas. — Assemblywoman Donna Lupardo
The grant is funded by a $35 million appropriation in the 2018 State Budget, which helps "high-needs" schools.
"The $35 million dollars is targeting some of the poorest communities in the state," said Lupardo.
The Binghamton program will focus on sustainability and will consist of STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) related activities. The day-to-day operations will be run by district staff, high school students, and the Cornell Cooperative Extension of Broome County.
"You're going to see young people engaging in a variety of activities every day after school, which accentuates what's happening in the classroom," said Victoria Giarratano, Cornell Cooperative Extension Executive Director.
Organizers say the program will begin shortly and take place over the course of the next 30 weeks plus four weeks during the summer.
rewrite:

This funding, distributed as $577,000 annually, will establish sustained afterschool programming for over 400 students spanning kindergarten through twelfth grade. The grant is sourced from a $35 million appropriation within the 2018 State Budget, designated for supporting "high-needs" schools. As noted by Assemblywoman Donna Lupardo, "The $35 million dollars is targeting some of the poorest communities in the state." This aligns with broader efforts, such as the Empire State Poverty Reduction Initiative, which has previously directed resources to Binghamton and adjacent urban regions experiencing significant poverty.

District Superintendent Tonia Thompson emphasized the holistic benefits of extended learning opportunities, stating, "We know that when we're able to support our students outside of the school day as well as throughout the summer months, they will succeed both academically as well as socially, emotionally, and physically." The program will prioritize sustainability and center on STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) activities. Operational management will be conducted by district personnel, high school students, and the Cornell Cooperative Extension of Broome County. According to the Extension's Executive Director, Victoria Giarratano, "You're going to see young people engaging in a variety of activities every day after school, which accentuates what's happening in the classroom." The initiative is scheduled to commence imminently and will operate over thirty weeks during the academic year, supplemented by an additional four weeks in the summer.

Currently, Nantong is part of the Savelugu municipality called Savelugu/Nantong, while Yunyoo is tied to the Bunkprugu district named Bunkprugu/Yunyoo.
Interestingly, Savelugu/Nantong and Bunkprugu /Yunyoo witnessed political upheavals by some irate youth of the governing New Patriotic (NPP) during the nomination of Municipal, Metropolitan and District Chief Executives.
Whereas those in Savelugu/Nantong finally backed down their protest, the Bunkprugu/Yunyoo nominee was rejected after three unsuccessful confirmation by members of the assembly.
President Nana Addo’s announcement of the creation of those two new districts gave residents there a sigh of relief.
They applauded government’s decision, and pledged their commitment to deepen peaceful coexistence to make the proposal feasible.
President Nana Addo revealed that government has secured $45.7 million for the rehabilitation and expansion of water systems across three regions of the country.
He assured the Nayiri that a chunk of the said amount will be spent on rehabilitating the water systems in Gambaga, Nalerigu and Walewale.
He said works on the water rehabilitation and expansion systems will commence before the end of 2017.
He reaffirmed government’s endeavour to connect several communities in the north to the national electrification grid.
The Nayiri commended government for implementing pro-poor policies needed to improve the well-being of Ghanaians.
He emphasized the need for government to lobby investors to explore the large lime deposit in Mamprugu land.
He said several communities within his jurisdiction lacked electricity and therefore called for the construction of a sub power station in Nalerigu to feed the deprived communities.
He further decried the deplorable road network in Mamprugu which requires rapid attention.

On October 7, 2017, President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo announced a governmental initiative to elevate six districts within the Northern Region to municipal status, as part of ongoing local government reforms. This declaration was made during an address to the chiefs and citizens of the Mamprugu traditional area at the Nayiri palace forecourt in Nalerigu, as part of the President’s three-day regional tour. The districts specified for upgrade include East and West Mamprusi, with Nantong and Yunyoo also identified for elevation.

Presently, Nantong is administered as part of the Savelugu municipality, designated Savelugu/Nantong, while Yunyoo is incorporated within the Bunkprugu district, known as Bunkprugu/Yunyoo. Notably, both of these existing administrative units experienced political disturbances during the nomination processes for Municipal, Metropolitan, and District Chief Executives. These protests were led by dissatisfied youth affiliated with the governing New Patriotic Party (NPP). Although protests in Savelugu/Nantong were eventually withdrawn, the nominee for Bunkprugu/Yunyoo was rejected following three unsuccessful confirmation attempts by the district assembly. Consequently, the President’s announcement regarding the creation of separate districts for these areas was met with considerable relief by local residents, who expressed approval for the decision and pledged to support peaceful coexistence to facilitate the proposal's implementation.

In a related development, President Akufo-Addo disclosed that the government has secured funding totaling $45.7 million for the rehabilitation and expansion of water supply systems across three regions of the country. He assured the Nayiri, the traditional ruler, that a significant portion of these funds would be allocated to water system projects in Gambaga, Nalerigu, and Walewale, with commencement of works anticipated before the end of 2017. The President further reaffirmed the government's commitment to extending the national electricity grid to numerous communities in the northern territories.

In response, the Nayiri commended the administration for implementing policies aimed at poverty alleviation and improving citizen welfare. He concurrently emphasized the necessity for the government to attract investment for the exploitation of substantial lime deposits within the Mamprugu area. Highlighting infrastructural deficits, the Nayiri noted the absence of electricity in many communities under his jurisdiction and advocated for the construction of a substation in Nalerigu to service these deprived areas. He also drew attention to the deteriorated condition of the road network in Mamprugu, urging prompt remedial action.

The National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) has revised its standard on how to properly install nonmetallic-sheathed cable (NM-B) and underground feeder and branch circuit (UF-B) cables and systems. NEMA RV 2-2016 Application and Installation Guidelines for Nonmetallic-Sheathed Cable and Underground Feeder and Branch Circuit Cable provides comprehensive guidance to installers and code enforcement personnel including guidelines on bend radius, markings, securing, supporting and terminating, and maintaining the integrity of the grounding system.
According to Randy Kummer, of Southwire Company, and a member of the NEMA Building Wire and Cable Section Technical Committee, “The release of this new edition of RV 2 is timely as it aligns with the 2017 National Electrical Code® and recognizes the most current installation practices. Electricians and authorities having jurisdiction should download a copy to review and reference.”
NEMA RV 2-2016 is available for $82 in hard copy and as an electronic download for no cost on the NEMA website.

This includes specifications for bend radius, cable markings, securing and supporting methods, termination procedures, and the maintenance of grounding system integrity.

April 28 Qualcomm Inc said on Friday Apple Inc will not pay royalties to its contract manufacturers, that are owed to the chipmaker, for sales made in the first quarter of 2017.
Qualcomm, the largest maker of chips used in smartphones, also said the iPhone maker will withhold further payments until the ongoing legal dispute with Qualcomm is resolved.
Apple sued Qualcomm in January accusing Qualcomm of overcharging for chips and refusing to pay some $1 billion in promised rebates.
Shares of Qualcomm fell 4.3 percent to $50.91 in premarket trading, while shares of Apple were up marginally at $143.92.
Qualcomm also slashed its profit and revenue forecasts for the current quarter, to exclude royalty revenue from Apple's contract manufacturers.
The company said it now expects current-quarter revenue of $4.8 billion-$5.6 billion, down from the $5.3 billion-$6.1 billion it had expected previously.
Qualcomm also cut its forecast for current-quarter adjusted profit to 75-85 cents per share, from 90 cents-$1.15 per share. (Reporting by Anya George Tharakan in Bengaluru; Editing by Sai Sachin Ravikumar)
rewrite:
On April 28, Qualcomm Inc. announced that Apple Inc. has directed its contract manufacturers to withhold first-quarter 2017 royalty payments owed to the chipmaker. Qualcomm, the predominant manufacturer of smartphone semiconductors, further stated that Apple will continue suspending such payments until the resolution of their ongoing legal dispute. This litigation was initiated by Apple in January, alleging that Qualcomm engaged in overcharging for its chips and withheld approximately $1 billion in committed rebates.

Concurrently, Qualcomm revised its financial projections downward for the current quarter, explicitly excluding all anticipated royalty revenue from Apple’s manufacturing partners. The company now forecasts revenue between $4.8 billion and $5.6 billion, a reduction from its prior guidance of $5.3 billion to $6.1 billion. Additionally, Qualcomm adjusted its projected adjusted earnings per share to a range of $0.75 to $0.85, down from the previous $0.90 to $1.15. Following this announcement, Qualcomm's shares declined 4.3 percent to $50.91 in premarket trading, whereas Apple's shares experienced a marginal increase to $143.92.

COLLEEN LONG, Associated Press
NEW YORK (AP) — A pipe bomb strapped to a man went off in the New York City subway near Times Square on Monday, injuring the suspect and another person at the height of the morning rush hour, law enforcement officials said.
The man and the other person were being treated for non-life-threatening injuries. The officials spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the incident.
The explosion triggered a massive emergency response by police and fire both above and below ground, tangling subway and bus service at the nearby Port Authority bus terminal.
Video from above the “Crossroads of the World” showed lines of police and emergency vehicles, their lights flashing, lining the streets and no other vehicle traffic moving.
Everything around the Port Authority area was shut down — a surreal scene of still at what would ordinarily be a bustling rush hour.
New Jersey Transit buses headed to the Port Authority were diverting to other locations. NJ Transit said buses were taking passengers to Secaucus and Hoboken, where they could take trains into the city.
White House Press Secretary Sarah Sanders tweeted that President Donald Trump had been briefed on the explosion.
Copyright 2017 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten or redistributed.
Comments
comments
rewrite:
On Monday morning, during the peak of rush hour, an explosive device affixed to an individual detonated within the New York City subway system in proximity to Times Square, according to law enforcement officials. The incident resulted in injuries to the suspect and one additional person, both of whom received treatment for wounds not considered life-threatening. These officials provided information to The Associated Press under condition of anonymity, as they lacked authorization to discuss the matter publicly.

The detonation prompted an extensive multi-agency emergency response from police and fire departments both above and below ground level. This response significantly disrupted public transportation, entangling subway and bus operations, particularly at the adjacent Port Authority Bus Terminal. Aerial footage of the vicinity, often described as the "Crossroads of the World," depicted numerous stationary police and emergency vehicles with activated lights, while all other vehicular traffic was halted. The normally bustling Port Authority area was rendered inactive, presenting a surreal tableau of stillness during a typically congested period.

Consequently, New Jersey Transit buses destined for the Port Authority were rerouted to alternate locations, including Secaucus and Hoboken, where passengers could transfer to rail services for entry into Manhattan. The White House Press Secretary, Sarah Sanders, confirmed via social media that President Donald Trump had been briefed on the explosion.

The controversial World Cup in Qatar has been plunged into major doubt over "political risks".
FIFA handed the 2022 tournament to the Arab country in 2010 ahead of fellow contender Australia, sparking uproar over alleged corruption, The Sun reports.
But according to the BBC, a report suggests "Western diplomats have privately stated they do not know whether or not the tournament will take place as planned".
That is because there have been allegations of corruption during the bidding process and the building of the state-of-the-art stadiums.
Advertisement
Not only that, Qatar are currently in a political fallout with neighbouring countries with increasing risk that they will fail to secure contracts over infrastructure.
They have a £153 billion ($257 billion) infrastructure program that is deemed a "high-risk project".
If Qatar were forced to pull out of hosting it could open the door for Australia, who lost out to the Gulf State in the 2022 bid.
Thousands of workers are building the stadiums with basic health and safety and have been subjected to life-threatening heat.
According to Human Rights Watch, hundreds of migrant workers have died in the process of trying to get the country prepared for the tournament.
But Qatar have remained bullish in their own statement by claiming the report is "laughable".
They said: "The intention to create doubt regarding the tournament, while attempting to cause resentment among Qatari citizens and anxiety among foreign businesses and residents, is as transparent as it is laughable.
"Despite the ambitious title of this report, there is absolutely no risk to the future of the first World Cup in the Middle East."
rewrite:
The hosting of the 2022 FIFA World Cup by Qatar is now subject to significant uncertainty due to heightened geopolitical and reputational risks. Originally awarded the tournament in 2010 over rival bidder Australia—a decision that itself sparked allegations of corruption—the event faces potential disruption. According to diplomatic sources cited in a BBC report, Western officials have privately expressed doubts about whether the competition will proceed as scheduled. These concerns are multifaceted, stemming from persistent allegations of misconduct during the initial bidding phase and throughout the construction of the tournament's infrastructure.

Further compounding the uncertainty is Qatar's strained diplomatic relations with several neighboring states, which increases the risk of disruptions to essential infrastructure contracts. The nation is undertaking an extensive infrastructure program, valued at approximately £153 billion, which external analysts have categorized as a high-risk venture. Should Qatar be compelled to relinquish hosting duties, Australia has been cited as a potential alternative. Concurrently, the preparation for the event has raised serious human rights concerns. Reports indicate that thousands of migrant laborers, working under perilous heat conditions with inadequate health and safety protections, are constructing the stadiums. Human Rights Watch has documented hundreds of migrant worker fatalities linked to these projects.

In response to these challenges, Qatari authorities have issued a robust dismissal of the reported uncertainties, characterizing them as baseless. An official statement asserts that the aim of such reports is to foster doubt and resentment, a motive described as "transparent" and "laughable." It further contends that, notwithstanding the alarming nature of external assessments, there is no credible threat to the successful staging of the first World Cup in the Middle East.

Ross’s unconditional love for Rachel; Rachel’s incessant confusions; Monica’s competitiveness for winning at life; Phoebe’s uncanny chatter and optimism; Chandler’s sense of humor; Joey’s love for pizza – don’t we already miss being a part of their lives?
If one thing that we have learnt from the longest and most loved show of the 90s is that – no matter what you do, no matter where you live – friendship is the best kind of love there is, because it’s only with friends that you can get through anything and everything.
Who doesn’t love F.R.I.E.N.D.S?
What’s the perfect way to pay tribute to the show that defined love, friendship, and heartaches in the most beautiful way possible? It’s not building a fort, it’s not running the roads with life-size banners, and it’s definitely not yelling your lungs out from the 100th floor of the tallest building in the world. It’s as simple as having a t-shirt that can display your love for six friends who seemed just as much closer as your real friends.
“You know we all have had moments where we felt just…One of Them”
T-shirts are your Best Friend, for Life!
Take a trip down memory lane with the huge selection of exclusive Friends t shirts that you can shop online here and flaunt the Friends style legacy.
Show off Joey Tribbiani’s popular catchphrase “Joey doesn’t share food”, hangout with your friends flaunting your love for everything that goes in and around the infamous Central Perk, or celebrate the king of sarcasm with friends tees sporting Chandler’s punchlines – we bet, each one of you will find something to appease your fandom.
rewrite:
The enduring appeal of the television series *Friends* lies in its nuanced portrayal of its central characters: Ross Geller’s unwavering devotion to Rachel Green; Rachel’s own perennial uncertainties; Monica Geller’s intensely competitive nature; Phoebe Buffay’s idiosyncratic wisdom and persistent optimism; Chandler Bing’s defensive yet resonant wit; and Joey Tribbiani’s simple, heartfelt passions. Collectively, these attributes foster a profound sense of familiarity and loss among the audience, underscoring a pervasive cultural nostalgia for the fictional community. A primary thematic conclusion from this seminal and widely cherished program of the 1990s is that friendship constitutes a paramount form of love. The narrative consistently demonstrates that, irrespective of circumstance or geography, genuine camaraderie provides the foundational support necessary to navigate life's varied challenges.

In light of the show’s significant cultural impact, which redefined contemporary portrayals of affection, fellowship, and tribulation, the question arises regarding an appropriate tribute. Such homage need not be grandiose—it is neither a physical monument nor a public spectacle. Rather, it can be effectively realized through the acquisition of merchandise that allows for a personal and continuous celebration of the series. A curated selection of officially licensed t-shirts facilitates this connection, enabling individuals to commemorate the program’s legacy. These garments feature iconic elements such as Joey Tribbiani’s memorable dictum, “Joey doesn’t share food,” motifs from the Central Perk coffeehouse, or signature examples of Chandler Bing’s sarcastic humor. This mode of engagement permits fans to express their affiliation, subtly invoking the shared sentiment of having, at times, felt like “one of them,” and thereby extending the show’s communal ethos into daily life.

MINNEAPOLIS (WCCO) – While the Minnesota Vikings’ season didn’t end the way they or the fans hoped it would, they can take solace in the fact that they pulled off one of the greatest football plays of all time in the Minneapolis Miracle.
Or at least the best play of the year. That’s the award the Minneapolis Miracle received at the NFL Honors Saturday night.
KEENUM.
DIGGS.
GAME OVER. The Minneapolis Miracle is the @Bridgestone Elite Performance Play of the Year! #NFLHonors pic.twitter.com/b0ImnRYZk5 — NFL (@NFL) February 4, 2018
The play – also known as Buffalo Right Seven Heaven – shocked the Saints (and, probably, the Vikings too) as Case Keenum heaved a pass to Stefon Diggs, who caught it and – thanks to a whiffed tackle by Saints safety Marcus Williams – took it to the house for a walk-off touchdown.
Let’s not talk about what happened one week later – for now, let’s bask in the glow of the Minneapolis Miracle, the NFL’s Play of the Year.
rewrite: Despite concluding in a manner that fell short of expectations for both the team and its supporters, the Minnesota Vikings' season is distinguished by the execution of a historically significant play, colloquially termed the Minneapolis Miracle. This play was formally recognized as the Bridgestone Elite Performance Play of the Year at the NFL Honors ceremony on February 3, 2018. The sequence, diagrammed as "Buffalo Right Seven Heaven," resulted in a game-winning touchdown during the final seconds of a playoff contest. Quarterback Case Keenum delivered a pass to wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who, following an unsuccessful tackle attempt by New Orleans Saints safety Marcus Williams, advanced into the end zone. While the team's postseason journey ended the following week, the play itself remains a singular achievement, celebrated as the league's premier play of that year.

Adele isn’t the only artist who thinks Beyoncé should have won big at the 2017 GRAMMY Awards. Beyoncé’s sister, Solange, has voiced her opinion on her sister’s loss Sunday (February 12) in a since-deleted post on Twitter.
Related: Adele Thanks Beyoncé in Her Record, Album of the Year Speeches
“There have only been two black winners in the last twenty years for album of the year,” she wrote in a later deleted tweet. “There have been over 200 black artist who have performed.”

Interestingly, three of those Album of the Year winners over the past 20 years were by women: Lauryn Hill for The Miseducation Of Lauryn Hill, Whitney Houston for the Bodyguard Soundtrack and Natalie Cole for Unforgettable… With Love.

SARASOTA, Fla. (WFLA) – Two people in Sarasota are facing charges after carfentanil was delivered to a home over the weekend.
Sarasota County Sheriff’s Office detectives were contacted by the Department of Homeland Security about a package believed to contain fentanyl being shipped internationally to an address in Sarasota.
The package was intercepted and taken for forensic testing, where a clear bag containing a white, powdery substance tested positive for carfentanil.
The package was delivered to an address in the 4000 block of Proctor Road.
Michael Bennett, 39, and Trisha Steffes, 36, took the package inside while detectives watched.
A search warrant was served minutes later.
Bennett and Steffes admitted to knowing the package contained carfentanil.
More than seven grams of fentanyl were found in a false electrical outlet in the home, as well as other drugs and paraphernalia.
Bennett and Steffes are charged with delivery of carfentanil, possession for fentanyl with intent and possession of paraphernalia.
Both were released over the weekend on bond.
WHAT OTHERS ARE CLICKING ON-
>>BACK TO TOP STORIES
rewrite: Two individuals in Sarasota, Florida, have been formally charged following the delivery of carfentanil to a residential address. The investigation originated when detectives from the Sarasota County Sheriff’s Office were notified by the Department of Homeland Security regarding an internationally shipped parcel, suspected to contain fentanyl, destined for a Sarasota location. Upon interception, forensic analysis confirmed the presence of carfentanil within a clear bag containing a white powdery substance. The parcel was subsequently delivered under law enforcement surveillance to a residence on the 4000 block of Proctor Road, where Michael Bennett, 39, and Trisha Steffes, 36, retrieved it. A search warrant was promptly executed. Both suspects acknowledged awareness of the package's contents. The subsequent search yielded over seven grams of fentanyl concealed within a false electrical outlet, alongside additional controlled substances and paraphernalia. Bennett and Steffes face charges including delivery of carfentanil, possession of fentanyl with intent to deliver, and possession of paraphernalia. Each was released on bond following their arrest.

AM expelled from Plaid Cymru for misconduct
South Wales Central AM, Neil McEvoy, has been excluded from Plaid Cymru for 18 months.
The party's disciplinary panel heard four complaints against him which they say were either damaging to Plaid Cymru's reputation, or breached confidentiality.
Neil McEvoy was found guilty of misconduct over his conduct in party meetings, "intimidating" correspondence, and causing distress among party members.
The AM has criticised the decision saying the inquiry was "flawed from the very beginning".
"The so-called inquiry has been completely flawed from the very beginning.
“There has been no due process or natural justice, just a sustained effort by lobbyists to undermine me.
“Having to wait over a year since the complaints were first made is unacceptable.
"I will obviously be appealing this disgraceful decision.”
A spokesperson for Plaid Cymru says: "The exclusion reflects the gravity of the cases put before the Panel.
"Neil McEvoy will have the right to appeal the decision."
rewrite:
Neil McEvoy, the Assembly Member for South Wales Central, has been expelled from Plaid Cymru for a period of eighteen months following a disciplinary hearing. The party's panel adjudicated four separate complaints, determining that his actions had either damaged the party's public standing or constituted a breach of confidentiality. The findings of misconduct pertained to his behaviour during internal meetings, the sending of correspondence deemed intimidating, and the causation of distress among fellow party members.

Mr. McEvoy has publicly condemned the verdict, characterising the investigative process as fundamentally flawed and alleging an absence of due process and natural justice. He further contends that the prolonged timeline since the initial complaints were lodged is unacceptable and has stated his intention to appeal the decision.

A spokesperson for Plaid Cymru stated that the severity of the exclusion corresponds to the gravity of the cases presented, while confirming Mr. McEvoy’s right to initiate an appeal.

Jack Preece is on the hunt for a double promotion with both Old Centralians and Coventry.
The openside-flanker has had strong starts to the season both playing with Coventry and coaching Old Cents.
The Old Centralians product wants promotion to the Championship with the midlands outfit and to see the Gloucester side step back into the national leagues.
Preece said: “It would be really nice to win promotion with both teams and just tick both of those boxes.
“With both Coventry and Cents there is still a long season ahead so we’ll reassess our goals after Christmas.
“But it is all going well and to plan so far.”
Old Centralians have won three of their opening five games and sit seventh in South West One East – they are looking to jump back up to the national leagues to the South West Premier with promotion.
Coventry have 24 points from a possible 25 at the start of the National One season with five wins. They are hoping to follow Hartpury up to the Championship from National One.
Preece added: “We are hoping to make the step back up to the national leagues in the next few years.
“At the moment I don’t think we are quite ready and are really pushing for promotion next year.
“But if it comes this time around, we would certainly take it and see how we went in the league above.”

Coventry, meanwhile, have secured 24 points from a possible 25 at the outset of the National One season, with five victories, aspiring to follow Hartpury’s path into the Championship.

Regarding Old Centralians’ longer-term aspirations, Preece added, “Our aim is to return to the national leagues within the next few years. Presently, I believe we are not entirely prepared and are more realistically targeting promotion next season. Should it occur this season, however, we would undoubtedly accept it and evaluate our performance in the higher division.”
