Visitor fees will be waived at all Adventure Pass areas except the Santa Ynez Recreation Area
Los Padres National Forest officials announced Tuesday that Saturday has been designated as a “Fee Free Day” for visitors to the forest.
In all areas of the forest where an Adventure Pass is normally required, the fee will be waived in celebration of National Public Lands Day, which is held each year on the last Saturday in September.
An Adventure Pass is typically required for day-use activities and camping at many recreational facilities in the forest. This weekend’s Fee Free Day applies to all Adventure Pass areas except the Lower Santa Ynez Recreation Area on the Santa Barbara Ranger District, where the fee remains in effect. Other fees such as reservation fees and group site fees also will still apply. Forest visitors who validate a daily Adventure Pass on Fee Free Day can have the pass replaced free of charge at most Forest Service offices.
“National Public Lands Day is the perfect opportunity to get outdoors and enjoy the natural wonders of our public lands,” Los Padres National Forest Supervisor Peggy Hernandez said. “This affords visitors the chance to see what we have to offer free of charge.”
National Public Lands Day began in 1994 with three federal agencies and 700 volunteers. Last year, 150,000 volunteers assisted with projects at more than 2,000 locations across the country.
For more information on current conditions and how you can get involved, call one of these offices:
» Monterey District Office — King City at 831.385.5434
» Santa Lucia District Office — Santa Maria at 805.925.9538
» Santa Barbara District Office — Santa Barbara at 805.967.3481
» Ojai District Office — Ojai at 805.646.4348 or Mt. Pinos Ranger District/Frazier Park at 661.245.3731
— Joe Pasinato is a spokesman for the Los Padres National Forest.

Toledo police say a 4-year-old boy is in the hospital after jumping out of a second-story window on Tuesday.
The incident happened at a home on Clifton Boulevard around 11:30 a.m.
Fire crews responded to the home to check on the well-being of a child who jumped out of a window.
Crews spoke to a witness who said they saw 4-year-old Landyn Williamson standing on the windowsill on the second story of the home with his arms out like he was trying to fly before jumping out of the window face first.
The witness said the boy landed on his side in the driveway.
EMS took the Williamson youth to the hospital with unspecified injuries.
Police say the boy's mother, Jessica Gusky, and her boyfriend, Brian Miller, weren't home at the time of the incident.
The two told police they went to the store around the corner and the boy was sleeping when they left. They told police they were only gone for a few minutes.
As the witness ran across the street to check on the boy, Gusky and Miller were coming up the street, the witness said.
Gusky was charged with child endangerment and is being held in the Lucas County Jail.
Miller was given a summons with a court date of June 11.
Copyright 2018 WTOL. All rights reserved.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, a four-year-old male child was transported to a medical facility following an incident in which he descended from a second-story window at a residential property on Clifton Boulevard. The event occurred at approximately 11:30 a.m. Emergency fire service personnel were dispatched to the location to assess the welfare of the juvenile. According to witness testimony provided to responding crews, the child, identified as Landyn Williamson, was observed standing on the interior windowsill of the second floor with his arms extended in a manner suggestive of an attempt to fly, prior to propelling himself from the window in a forward-facing orientation. The witness reported that the child subsequently landed on his side upon the residential driveway.

Emergency Medical Services transported the juvenile to a hospital for treatment of unspecified injuries. Investigative authorities indicate that the child’s mother, Jessica Gusky, and her cohabiting partner, Brian Miller, were absent from the residence during the incident. Both individuals stated to police that they had departed to a nearby retail establishment while the child was asleep, asserting an absence of only several minutes’ duration. The witness reported encountering Gusky and Miller returning to the residence as the witness proceeded to assist the child.

As a result of the investigation, Jessica Gusky was charged with child endangerment and is currently detained at the Lucas County Jail. Brian Miller was issued a summons with a scheduled court appearance on June 11.

DALLAS -- The State Fair of Texas is right around the corner and it means Big Tex and the gang are already kicking off preparations.
Not only is securing those corn dog stands important, but securing the security is the bigger issue!
Every year Dallas Police Department sends over 200 of their officers to guard the fairgrounds. With a recent shortage in staffing, DPD has found themselves in a funnel.
"We have reduced the number of officers we put down there in an 'on-duty' capacity and we're increasing the number of officers we're hiring in an 'off duty' capacity," explained interim Chief David Pughes.
The state fair will have to bring in other agencies to make sure they have enough security. This will include Dallas Independent School District, the Dallas County Sherriff's office, and DART Police.
If an off-duty Dallas Police officer wants to spend his or her free time keeping people safe at the fair, he or she will be able to apply through The State Fair.
"Security at the Fair is a priority for us, Pughes added. "But, greater than that, we have to ensure that the people that are coming and going and living and playing in the city are safe too!"

× Tribe, groups to sue Navy over ship cleaning in Puget Sound
SEATTLE (AP) — The Suquamish Tribe and two environmental groups have sued the U.S. Navy, alleging the Navy cleaned a decommissioned aircraft carrier in Puget Sound in violation of federal clean-water laws.
The mothballed 60,000-ton USS Independence was cleaned in waters near Bremerton, Washington, in January and February before it was towed to Brownsville, Texas, this month to be dismantled.
The tribe, Washington Environmental Council and Puget Soundkeeper Alliance say the Navy scraped the ship’s hull and sent toxic copper-based paint, zinc and other pollutants into the water. They say Navy should have obtained permits under the Clean Water Act authorizing such discharges.
They want to ensure that other decommissioned ships are not scraped in the same way in the future.
A Navy spokeswoman did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The complaint was filed Wednesday in federal court in Tacoma.
rewrite: The Suquamish Tribe, in conjunction with the Washington Environmental Council and the Puget Soundkeeper Alliance, has initiated legal proceedings against the United States Navy. The litigation alleges that the cleaning of the decommissioned aircraft carrier USS Independence in the waters of Puget Sound near Bremerton, Washington, during January and February violated the Clean Water Act. According to the complaint, the process of scraping the vessel’s hull released toxic substances, including copper-based antifouling paint, zinc, and additional pollutants, into the marine environment without the requisite federal discharge permits. The plaintiffs seek judicial intervention to prevent similar unauthorized cleaning activities for other decommissioned vessels in the future. The lawsuit was formally filed in the United States District Court in Tacoma on Wednesday. A representative for the Navy has not yet provided a public statement regarding the allegations.

NBC 7's Alex Presha reports an investigation involving a trash collector being crushed by his own vehicle. (Published Thursday, Oct. 5, 2017)
David James Strobridge was known as “DJ” by those close to him.
Strobridge was working a collection route Monday when he was pinned by his empty truck and died on the job.
Emergency workers were called to an alley near Hershel Avenue and Torrey Pines Road in La Jolla.
NBC 7 wanted to know a little bit more as to why Strobridge was operating this truck alone -- or even if that's normal.
The general manager at Tayman Industries, the company Strobridge worked for, told NBC 7 it has been a tough week. He said he and his employees miss DJ.
The general manager said Strobridge was working a recycle route on Monday and it is normal for employees to go out alone if they're emptying 120 bins or less.
San Diego Police Department Lt. Charles Lara said it’s likely Strobridge was trying to stop the moving truck when he was pinned.
“A dumpster may have gotten loose,” Lara said. “Ultimately the truck was moving and he attempted to stop the moving truck by getting into the cab. And he unfortunately was pinned between the truck and the wall.”
Cal OSHA has no other incidents recorded for Tayman Industries though the company does have a log of an employee placed on restricted duty back in 2015 for a similar type incident.
Cal OSHA's investigation into Monday's incident could last up to 6 months.
rewrite:
An investigation into a fatal industrial incident involving a refuse collector was reported by NBC 7 on October 5, 2017. The victim was identified as David James Strobridge, referred to familiarly as “DJ” by acquaintances. The incident occurred on Monday during a routine collection route in La Jolla, when Strobridge was fatally pinned by his own empty vehicle. Emergency services responded to the location in an alley proximate to Hershel Avenue and Torrey Pines Road.

Inquiries were made regarding the operational circumstances, specifically whether it was standard procedure for an employee to work alone. The general manager of Tayman Industries, Strobridge’s employer, confirmed that operating solo is normative for routes involving 120 bins or fewer, and characterized the week following the event as difficult for the company. According to San Diego Police Department Lieutenant Charles Lara, preliminary reconstruction suggests Strobridge was attempting to halt the moving vehicle, potentially after a dumpster became dislodged, which resulted in him being trapped between the truck and a wall.

Records from the California Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal OSHA) indicate no prior formal incidents for Tayman Industries, though a 2015 log notes an employee assigned to restricted duty following a similar event. The regulatory investigation into Monday’s fatality is anticipated to require up to six months for completion.

The man, who has been identified by relatives, is believed to have lived in the tower for 30 years and was seen praying at his window as he waited for help on the 11th floor.

filmed him as he waved a jumper as a makeshift SOS flag and cried out for help from his 11th-floor flat.

New Mexico man gets 170-year prison term in child porn case
LAS CRUCES, N.M. (AP) — A New Mexico man has been sentenced to 170 years in federal prison for producing and possessing child pornography and conspiring to transport people illegally into the country.
Prosecutors say 34-year-old Samuel Elliott of Columbus also was ordered to pay more than $210,000 in restitution to each of the three children victimized by the child porn production scheme.
They say Elliott got 30 years in prison on each of three child porn counts to run consecutive for 90 years. He also got 20 years in prison for each of four porn possession counts to run consecutive for 80 years and a concurrent 15-month term for the transporting charge.
Prosecutors say the child porn crimes occurred between December 2012 and July 2013 while Elliott conspired to transport immigrants in August 2013.
rewrite: A federal court in New Mexico has imposed a 170-year prison sentence upon a Columbus man convicted of producing and possessing child sexual abuse material and conspiring to transport individuals unlawfully into the United States. Samuel Elliott, 34, was ordered to pay restitution exceeding $210,000 to each of the three child victims identified in the production scheme. The sentence structure includes consecutive 30-year terms for three production counts, totaling 90 years, and consecutive 20-year terms for four possession counts, totaling 80 years. A separate 15-month term for the conspiracy to transport charge will be served concurrently. According to prosecutors, the offenses involving child sexual abuse material occurred from December 2012 through July 2013, while the transportation conspiracy took place in August 2013.

০ = 0, ১ = 1, ২ = 2, ৩ = 3, ৪ = 4, ৫ = 5, ৬ = 6, ৭ = 7, ৮ = 8, ৯ = 9
্ = See example (Hasant/Viram) ় = * (Nukta) ʼ = ' (Urdhacomma) ঽ = & (Avagrah) ৺ = ~ (Isshar) ৹ = a~ (Bengali ana sign) ৲ = Rs~ (Bengali Rupee sign) ৳ = T~ (Taka sign) । = | (Devanagari danda) ॥ = || (Devanagari double danda) ₹ = Rs (Indian Rupee sign) 卐 = +~ (Swastika sign) Zero Width Joiner = ^ Zero Width Non Joiner = ^^
These symbols will type Bengali characters first but if "~" will be followed, it will remove previously typed Bengali character and then type the symbol.
Symbols & ~ * : ^ | ' have special meaning. You can type this way & = &~ ~ = ~~ * = *~ : = :~ ^ = ^~ | = |~ ' = '~
The English symbols [ ] { } ( ) < > - + / = ; . , " ? ! % \ _ $ @ # translate into the same symbols.
Example নমস্কার can be written by typing "namaskaar"
As per Rule # 3, ligature will be rendered. ZWJ and ZWNJ characters are used to produce alternate rendering of ligature.
A consonant followed by ZWJ character will produce half-formed consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‍ন = prash^n
A consonant followed by ZWNJ character will produce dead consonant character.
Example
প্রশ্ন = prashn
প্রশ্‌ন = prash^^n
If two english characters are making one Bengali Vowel (i.e. ai, au), then
ZWJ character is used to separate them into two different vowels. It will not
add ZWJ character but only considered as the separator between two
vowels.
rewrite:
The following delineates a systematic transliteration scheme for generating Bengali script from Roman characters. The foundational mappings are as follows: the numerals ০ through ৯ correspond to 0 through 9. Specific diacritics and punctuation are represented by designated symbols: ্ (Hasant/Viram) is contextual; ় (Nukta) by `*`; ʼ (Urdhacomma) by `'`; ঽ (Avagrah) by `&`; ৺ (Isshar) by `~`; ৹ (Bengali ana sign) by `a~`; ৲ (Bengali Rupee sign) by `Rs~`; ৳ (Taka sign) by `T~`; । (Devanagari danda) by `|`; ॥ (Devanagari double danda) by `||`; ₹ (Indian Rupee sign) by `Rs`; and 卐 (Swastika sign) by `+~`. The Zero Width Joiner (ZWJ) and Zero Width Non-Joiner (ZWNJ) are represented by `^` and `^^`, respectively.

A critical operational rule is that a trailing tilde (`~`) functions as an override, deleting the immediately preceding Bengali character and replacing it with the intended symbol. Consequently, the symbols `&`, `~`, `*`, `:`, `^`, `|`, and `'` possess special syntactic meaning. To produce these symbols literally, they must be escaped by appending a tilde (e.g., `&~` for `&`, `~~` for `~`). Standard English punctuation and symbols—including `[ ] { } ( ) < > - + / = ; . , " ? ! % \ _ $ @ #`—translate directly without modification.

The system adheres to standard Bengali ligature formation. The ZWJ (`^`) and ZWNJ (`^^`) characters provide granular control over glyph rendering. A consonant followed by ZWJ yields a half-formed consonant (e.g., `prashn` produces প্রশ্ন, while `prash^n` produces প্রশ্‍ন). A consonant followed by ZWNJ produces a dead consonant, or *hasanta* (e.g., `prash^^n` yields প্রশ্‌ন).

Furthermore, when two Roman characters represent a single Bengali vowel diphthong (e.g., 'ai', 'au'), the ZWJ character serves as a logical separator to parse them as distinct vowel entities. In such cases, the ZWJ is not rendered as a visible character but instructs the system to inhibit diphthong formation. For illustration, the Bengali word নমস্কার is generated by the input sequence "namaskaar".

A man was shot and killed near Twain Avenue and Swenson Street Friday night, Metro Police said. (Austin Turner / FOX5)
Police arrested a man for shooting and killing another man near Twain Avenue and Swenson Street on Friday, April 20, Metro Police said.
The shooting was reported at 9:21 p.m. on the 3700 block of Hazelwood Street.
Mark Salazar, 47, was found in an alley with a single gunshot wound to his chest, according to the Clark County Coroner and police. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Police found an empty cell phone case in his possession. Police said they believed the shooter may have taken Salazar's phone.
During the investigation, police found a surveillance camera in a nearby building. The property manager said an unknown person had been squatting in the laundry room. She later admitted, it was her son, Gonzalo Rivera. In that laundry room, police found paperwork with Rivera's name on them. Investigators also found blood in the room, according to an arrest report.
In the surveillance video, Rivera was seen "hurriedly moving through the alley carrying a trash bag towards a dumpster, and putting unknown items into a dumpster," police said.
Rivera's brother later admitted he was there during the shooting that "happened quickly after an argument ensued." Rivera's brother said Rivera did not plan to shoot Salazar. The brother said he did help clean up the scene before he called 911, according to Rivera's arrest report.
Gonzalo Rivera agreed to speak with detectives, denied being involved in Salazar's death, and claimed someone else pulled the trigger. He later admitted to cleaning up the scene, taking Salazar's phone and carrying a blood-soaked shirt to his car before leaving the area. He was arrested on April 25 for murder with a deadly weapon.
Metro said anyone with information on the case should contact them at 702-828-3521.
Copyright 2018 KVVU (KVVU Broadcasting Corporation). All rights reserved.
rewrite:

Authorities were dispatched to the 3700 block of Hazelwood Street following a report received at 9:21 p.m. The victim, identified by the Clark County Coroner’s Office as 47-year-old Mark Salazar, was discovered in an alley with a solitary gunshot wound to the thoracic region and was pronounced deceased at the scene. Investigative notes indicate that an empty cellular telephone case was recovered from Salazar’s person, leading police to postulate that the perpetrator may have appropriated the victim’s phone.

Subsequent investigation led officers to a nearby residential building, where surveillance footage was obtained. The property manager initially reported an unidentified individual residing unlawfully within the laundry facility but later conceded this person was her son, Gonzalo Rivera. The aforementioned video recording depicted an individual, alleged to be Rivera, moving with haste through the alley while carrying a refuse sack toward a dumpster and depositing unspecified items within it.

According to the arrest report, Rivera’s sibling, who was present during the incident, stated that the shooting transpired rapidly following a verbal altercation and was not premeditated. The sibling further acknowledged assisting in the cleanup of the scene prior to contacting emergency services. When interviewed, Gonzalo Rivera initially denied any involvement in the homicide, asserting that another individual discharged the firearm. USA Curling(NEW YORK) — At 6’4 and 250 lbs, Washington Redskins tight end, Vernon Davis, is not a typical curling player or fan.
Well, the word ‘fan’ may actually be an understatement. In 2010, Davis was awarded the title of “honorary captain” of Team USA Curling and has attended every winter Olympics since. He says he plans to attend the 2018 Games in South Korea too.
“I love the sport of curling because it’s just you and the stone and the broom,” Davis told ABC News and ESPN’s Undefeated in a joint video interview. “You have to have a still mind, a calm mind. Just like anything else, like when it comes to football. The mindset has to be still.”
As the story goes, back in 2009, a football reporter covering the San Francisco 49’ers, for whom Davis was playing at the time, dared Davis to give the winter sport a try.
“I was like, ‘Curling? What is that?'” he said. “[The reporter] was like ‘Just come on out, you’ll love it, you’ll love it.’ So I went out on the ice and I was probably on the ice for maybe an hour and a half, and I fell in love with it.”
A few months later, Team USA invited Davis to join them as their ceremonial captain to “give them encouragement and support,” Terry Davis, the director of communications for USA Curling told ABC News and ESPN’s Undefeated. “Vernon also took part in media opportunities at both [2010 and 2014] Games to help curling gain more exposure.”
In addition to bringing general awareness to the sport, the African American two-time Pro Bowler said he also hopes his role as honorary captain can help attract more African Americans to the pastime. “Right now, I feel like a lot of African Americans don’t really know too much about the game of curling. But it can be different… and that can change through promoting,” he said.
“I’m an art studio major so I’m all about doing something different and just trying to see what else is out there, exploring, and just thinking outside the box and opening up my mind.”
This is a joint project between ABC News and ESPN’s The Undefeated.
Copyright © 2017, ABC Radio. All rights reserved.
rewrite:
Vernon Davis, a 6’4”, 250-pound tight end for the Washington Redskins, represents an unconventional figure within the sphere of curling fandom and participation. Indeed, the term “fan” proves insufficient; since 2010, Davis has held the ceremonial title of honorary captain for Team USA Curling and has attended every Winter Olympic Games since that appointment, with plans to extend that streak to the 2018 Games in PyeongChang, South Korea.

In a joint video interview with ABC News and ESPN’s *The Undefeated*, Davis articulated his appreciation for the sport’s psychological demands. “I love the sport of curling because it’s just you and the stone and the broom,” he stated. “You have to have a still mind, a calm mind. Just like anything else, such as football, the mindset must be still.” His introduction to curling occurred in 2009, when a reporter covering the San Francisco 49ers—Davis’s team at the time—challenged him to try the winter sport. Davis recalled his initial reaction: “I was like, ‘Curling? What is that?’” He accepted the invitation, however, and after approximately ninety minutes on the ice, he “fell in love with it.”

Shortly thereafter, USA Curling extended an invitation for Davis to serve as honorary captain. Terry Davis, USA Curling’s director of communications, explained to the same outlets that the role was designed for Davis to “give [the team] encouragement and support.” He further noted that Davis participated in media engagements during both the 2010 and 2014 Olympic Games, efforts aimed at increasing the sport’s visibility.

Beyond general promotion, Davis, a two-time Pro Bowl selection who is African American, expressed a specific aspiration for his involvement. He hopes his profile can help attract more African Americans to curling. “Right now, I feel like a lot of African Americans don’t really know too much about the game of curling,” he observed. “But it can be different… and that can change through promotion.” Davis connected this outreach goal to his personal disposition, noting his background as an art studio major: “I’m all about doing something different and just trying to see what else is out there, exploring, and just thinking outside the box and opening up my mind.”

This report is a collaborative effort between ABC News and ESPN’s *The Undefeated*.

Leandro Bacuna could make his Reading debut against his former club after joining the Royals on Sunday when Aston Villa visit the Madejski Stadium.
Midfielder Garath McCleary (groin) will hope to feature for the first time this season after returning to training.

Aston Villa manager Steve Bruce told BBC WM:
"Playing away from home has been our Achilles heel since I arrived and, to be brutally honest, I haven't been able to address it in the six months I've been here.
"I can't address it quickly enough. We've shown flashes of it so far this season, but when we're away from home, we just haven't got enough.
"The one thing that my teams have had over the years to be successful is resilience."

LOS ANGELES: Floyd Mayweather has shot down rumors of a deal to fight martial arts star Conor McGregor, insisting he is content to remain retired.
The 39-year old American took to his social media Instagram account late Tuesday, telling his fans that he wanted to set the record straight.
“There seems to be several rumors floating around media recently however, let the record show, there hasn’t been any deals made in regards to a fight between myself and any other fighters. I am happily retired and enjoying life at this time. If any changes are to come, be sure that I will be the first to let the world to know.”
Mayweather’s statement may be sincere or it may not be. He has been know in the past to often stretch the truth announcing several times that the fight of the moment would be his last only to use that ploy as a bargaining tool to try and sell more tickets.
The possibility of a fight between boxer Mayweather and McGregor appeared to get a boost as Ultimate Fighting Championship boss Dana White said he’d pay $25 million to each.
White, president of the popular UFC mixed martial arts brand in which Ireland’s McGregor stars, seemed to indicate in his comments on a Fox radio broadcast that the two would meet in a boxing ring, not the UFC octagon.
Mayweather, who retired in 2015 with a perfect 49-0 record, is considered one of the greatest fighters of all-time. McGregor has never fought a professional boxing match.
McGregor became the first man to simultaneously hold UFC titles in two weight divisions when he beat Eddie Alvarez in New York on November 12.
At the end of November he was issued a California boxing license in a development that fueled speculation about a showdown between the two. AFP
AFP/CC

I am contentedly retired and relish my present circumstances. Should any developments arise, I will assuredly be the primary source to inform the public.”

The authenticity of Mayweather’s declaration remains ambiguous, given his historical propensity for strategic public pronouncements. On previous occasions, he has declared impending contests to be his final professional engagement, a tactic often interpreted as a mechanism to enhance promotional leverage and ticket sales.

Prospects for a crossover contest between the undefeated boxer and the UFC champion received notable impetus following comments from Ultimate Fighting Championship President Dana White, who publicly proposed a financial offer of twenty-five million dollars to each athlete. White, overseeing the organization in which the Irish McGregor is a preeminent star, suggested during an interview on Fox radio that such an encounter would likely occur under standard boxing regulations rather than within the UFC’s octagonal enclosure.

Mayweather, who concluded his professional career in 2015 with an unblemished record of 49 victories, is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished pugilists in history. Conversely, McGregor possesses no prior experience in professional boxing. McGregor achieved an unprecedented feat in UFC history on November 12 by securing championship titles in two distinct weight divisions concurrently following his victory over Eddie Alvarez in New York. The subsequent issuance of a California boxing license to McGregor in late November further intensified conjecture surrounding a potential confrontation between the two athletes.

SANTA ANA, Calif. (AP) — Actor Harrison Ford had a potentially serious run-in with an airliner at a Southern California airport, NBC-TV reported Tuesday.
Ford, 74, was told to land his single-engine plane on a runway at John Wayne Airport in Orange County on Monday, but he mistakenly landed it on a parallel taxiway, passing over an American Airlines jet holding nearby, NBC reported.
“Was that airliner meant to be underneath me?” Ford is heard asking air traffic controllers in a recording, NBC reported.
American Airlines Flight 1456, with 110 passengers and six crew, departed safely for Dallas a few minutes later.
Ford’s publicist, Ina Treciokas, declined comment Tuesday afternoon.
Federal Aviation Administration spokesman Ian Gregor couldn’t confirm that Ford was piloting the Aviat Husky that overflew the Boeing 737, but he said the pilot received and had read back the proper landing instructions.
The FAA is investigating, Gregor said.
Ford collects vintage planes and has a long and good record as an aviator. But he has had several close calls.
In March 2015, Ford suffered a broken arm and a gashed forehead when his World War II-era trainer crashed on a Los Angeles golf course when it lost power shortly after takeoff.
In 1999, Ford crash-landed his helicopter during a training flight in which he and an instructor were practicing auto rotations in Ventura County, northwest of Los Angeles. Ford and the instructor were unhurt.
Ford was flying a Beechcraft Bonanza in 2000 when wind shear forced him to make an emergency landing at Lincoln Municipal Airport in Nebraska. Ford and his passenger were uninjured when the plane clipped the runway, but its wing tips were damaged, officials said.

However, he erroneously landed instead on a parallel taxiway, overflying an American Airlines Boeing 737 jet that was holding in position nearby. In an audio recording cited by NBC, Ford is heard inquiring of air traffic control, “Was that airliner meant to be underneath me?” American Airlines Flight 1456, carrying 110 passengers and six crew members, subsequently departed safely for Dallas several minutes later.

Federal Aviation Administration spokesman Ian Gregor stated that, while he could not confirm the pilot’s identity, the pilot of the involved Husky had received and correctly read back the proper landing instructions. The FAA has initiated an investigation into the incident. Ford’s representative, Ina Treciokas, declined to comment.

An experienced aviator with a collection of vintage aircraft, Ford has maintained a generally favorable flying record. Nevertheless, his history includes several notable incidents. In March 2015, he sustained a broken arm and a head laceration when his World War II-era trainer aircraft experienced engine failure after takeoff and crashed on a Los Angeles golf course. During a 1999 training flight in Ventura County, Ford performed an emergency autorotation and crash-landed a helicopter; neither he nor his instructor was injured. Furthermore, in 2000, wind shear necessitated an emergency landing of his Beechcraft Bonanza at Lincoln Municipal Airport in Nebraska. Although the aircraft sustained damage to its wing tips upon contacting the runway, Ford and his passenger emerged unharmed.

GORDEN Tallis will soon come face-to-face with Queensland’s three NRL coaches, but the man dubbed the “Raging Bull” is not afraid to tell them that a Sydney team will win this year’s premiership.
The rugby league great will be part of The Courier-Mail’s 2018 NRL season launch luncheon on February 27, alongside Broncos coach Wayne Bennett, Cowboys mentor Paul Green and Titans newcomer Garth Brennan.
Secure your tickets to the launch here
And while the former Broncos and Maroons legend would never turn his back on his state, Tallis believes these men will this year be trumped by a foe from down south – Roosters coach Trent Robinson.
Tallis said the Sydney club’s time had come to hold the trophy high, but a Queenslander will still play an influential part in getting them there.
“Cooper Cronk is more than a fair purchase,” Tallis said.
Camera Icon Gorden Tallis believes the Roosters’ time is nigh. Picture: News Corp Australia
“The Roosters have been at the pointy end of the competition for the last few years now, but Cronk and (fellow new recruit) James Tedesco, those two guys will make a massive difference.”
Tallis said that while question marks still lingered over how Cronk would fare without long-time Melbourne, Queensland and Australian teammates Cameron Smith and Billy Slater, he had no doubt the gifted halfback would succeed.
“You know Alf (Langer) wasn’t as good without Kevin Walters, Brett Kenny wasn’t the same without Peter Sterling and Laurie Daley wasn’t as good without Ricky Stuart,” he said.
“These three are going to realise for the first time what that’s like. But they’re so classy.
“People say that Billy Slater’s the greatest ever fullback to play the game, Cam Smith is the greatest No.9 to play. Cooper’s never been held in that high of a regard.
“This is his chance to jump out of the shadow.”
Tallis will share more of his season predictions at the NRL launch at Suncorp Stadium when The Courier-Mail and Sunday Mail’s chief sports reporter Robert Craddock hosts a Q&A panel with him and fellow Broncos great Darren Lockyer.

Nothing says the holiday season is over like the sight of a dead Christmas tree sitting in your living room.
You know the look. The strong and slender twigs which until a few days ago held your perfectly decorated tree together have started to sag, leaving perky ornaments looking rather dull.
The once luscious and green tree is now starting to look and feel dry with needles falling off faster than you can sweep them off your floor.
Wait too long and getting the tree out of your home will make you regret you ever purchased a real one in the first place.
But why wait when the City of Ottawa is collecting Christmas trees every week in January.
“Christmas trees will be collected on your regular scheduled collection day,” said deputy mayor Bob Monette in a gentle reminder posted on Facebook.
Just make sure to take down the ornaments along with all that tinsel and throw it to the curb.
For those of you sneaking the tree out of your apartment or condo building (where they are forbidden in the first place), just remember: trees wrapped in plastic bags will not be picked up by the city.
If you’re still having a hard time parting with your tree, consider this:
A dried out Christmas tree is not only an eyesore, it’s also a fire hazard as demonstrated by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission in a video circulating on social media:
If you have other uses for your Christmas tree, let us know!

twitter.com/susanamas

The initially vibrant green foliage transitions to a brittle, arid state, shedding needles at a rate that exceeds routine maintenance. Procrastination in the removal of the tree compounds the inconvenience, potentially fostering regret regarding the initial decision to procure a natural specimen.

However, such delay is unnecessary, as the City of Ottawa facilitates weekly collection services for Christmas trees throughout the month of January. As Deputy Mayor Bob Monette noted in a public advisory, "Christmas trees will be collected on your regular scheduled collection day." For individuals residing in multi-unit dwellings where such trees are typically prohibited, it is imperative to note that trees enclosed in plastic bags will not be accepted for municipal collection.

For those reluctant to dispose of their tree, it is worth considering that a desiccated tree constitutes both an aesthetic detriment and a significant fire hazard, a point demonstrated by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission in widely circulated public service materials. Alternative applications for retired Christmas trees may be suggested to the provided contact.

MADRID, March 31 Spanish engineering company Isolux said on Friday it had activated the formal process aimed at avoiding insolvency, as it battles to secure enough money to remain in business.
Under Spanish law, companies can enter into debt restructuring proceedings that give them up to four months to reach an agreement with creditors to avoid a full-blown insolvency process and a potential bankruptcy.
Isolux has over 2 billion euros ($2.1 billion) in restructured debt, according to an update on its restructuring process published in December.
Spanish engineering companies have been struggling to meet debt obligations and shrink their businesses after more than a decade of debt-fueled expansion projects worldwide.
Renewable energy firm Abengoa narrowly avoided filing for Spain's biggest ever bankruptcy last year after it secured backing from creditors for a restructuring plan to cut its debt of over 9 billion euros.
Isolux said on Friday the decision taken by the board would not affect its capacity to carry out operations, in particular any projects started in recent months.
Last December, Isolux agreed to a debt restructuring deal with bondholders and banks, such as Banco Santander, Caixabank and Bankia, taking 95 percent of the company in a debt for equity swap.
Isolux said on Friday it was trying to sell its concession assets and had begun to look for an investor for the holding company that groups the engineering and construction business.
The company, which has over 5,200 workers, carries out infrastructure and energy projects in 35 countries. It has delayed the publication of its results until negotiations are concluded.
($1 = 0.9360 euros) (Reporting By Andrés González; Writing by Jesús Aguado; Editing by Angus Berwick and Mark Potter)

Under Spanish insolvency law, such proceedings afford a company a period of up to four months to negotiate an agreement with its creditors, thereby averting a full declaration of insolvency and potential bankruptcy. This action follows a protracted period of difficulty for Spain's engineering sector, which has been compelled to scale back operations and manage debt obligations following an extended era of leveraged international expansion. Isolux itself carries restructured debt exceeding €2 billion, as detailed in a December update on its financial restructuring.

The company’s board affirmed that this decision does not impair its operational capacity, particularly concerning projects commenced in recent months. This development occurs in the context of a challenging environment for major Spanish engineering groups, exemplified by renewable energy firm Abengoa, which narrowly avoided the nation's largest bankruptcy last year through a creditor-approved restructuring of its over €9 billion debt. Isolux had previously agreed to a debt-for-equity swap in December, wherein bondholders and banking entities, including Banco Santander, Caixabank, and Bankia, acquired a 95 percent stake. Concurrently, the firm is pursuing the sale of its concession assets and has commenced a search for an investor for the holding company encompassing its core engineering and construction divisions. Employing over 5,200 individuals and executing infrastructure and energy projects across 35 countries, Isolux has postponed the publication of its financial results pending the conclusion of these ongoing negotiations.

FEES RISE: Residents will soon be hit with a fee hike when Bundaberg Regional Council implements a rise in dumping costs at the region's waste facilities.
DUMPING your rubbish at the region's waste facilities is about to cost even more.
From July 1, getting rid of a trailer load of waste will cost $15, $3 more than the current fee.
Dumping a car load of rubbish will cost residents $11 and a wheelie bin amount of waste will be $7 to dump.
Bundaberg Regional Council fee waste and recycling spokesman Scott Rowleson said the fee hike was due to the expected approval of a dump voucher scheme for ratepayers at today's budget meeting, which will also adopt new fees and charges for local waste facilities.
Cr Rowleson said the two vouchers would provide ratepayers two free visits to a waste disposal facility at a time of their choosing.
"The free voucher message has been a constant in the conversation around waste service delivery for a long time and this is something council has heard loud and clear," he said.
"Residents do need to realise that this initiative comes at a cost to council with a potential loss of $1.3 million in revenue.
"Our waste facilities, through stringent environmental requirements, are expensive to maintain and anyone utilising these facilities will need to pay an appropriate charge."
But it's not all hikes.
Cr Rowleson said domestic green waste disposal had dropped 50c to $7.50 a load while the $5 individual charge for the disposal of e-waste including televisions and monitors had been dropped completely.
He said 70% of council waste charges would remain unchanged or decrease and only 30% would increase.
Cr Rowleson said he would be disappointed if residents turned to illegal dumping in the wake of the increases.
"Apart from the fines that are imposed on those caught engaging in illegal dumping, the perpetrators simply put more financial pressure back on the rest of the community who ultimately fund the clean-up of their mess," he said.
Dump fees:
Sedan or station wagon: Current $10, from July $11
Van, ute or trailer (all other waste): Current $12, from July $15
Sedan, station wagon, van, ute or trailer (green waste only): Current $8, from July $7.50
rewrite:
The Bundaberg Regional Council is set to implement revised fee structures for waste disposal at its regional facilities, effective July 1. These adjustments will result in increased costs for several categories of general waste disposal. Specifically, the fee for disposing of a trailer load of waste will rise from $12 to $15. Similarly, the cost for a standard car load will increase from $10 to $11, while the fee for an amount equivalent to a wheelie bin will be set at $7.

According to Councillor Scott Rowleson, the Council's spokesperson for waste and recycling, these increases are directly linked to the anticipated approval of a new dump voucher scheme for ratepayers. This scheme is scheduled for consideration during the current budget meeting, which will also formalize the new fee schedule. Cr Rowleson explained that the approved scheme will provide each ratepayer with two vouchers, each permitting a free visit to a waste disposal facility at a time of the ratepayer's choosing. He stated, "The request for free vouchers has been a persistent theme in community discussions regarding waste services, and the Council has acknowledged this feedback." However, he emphasized that "this initiative entails a significant financial impact on the Council, with a projected revenue loss of approximately $1.3 million. Maintaining our waste facilities in compliance with stringent environmental regulations is costly, and it remains necessary for users of these services to contribute appropriate charges."

Conversely, not all fee categories will experience increases. The disposal cost for domestic green waste will decrease by fifty cents to $7.50 per load. Furthermore, the previous $5 individual charge for disposing of electronic waste, such as televisions and computer monitors, will be eliminated entirely. Cr Rowleson noted that approximately 70% of the Council's waste charges will either remain unchanged or decrease, with only 30% subject to increase.

In response to potential concerns, Cr Rowleson expressed hope that residents would not resort to illegal dumping as a consequence of the revised fees. He cautioned, "Beyond the substantial fines levied against individuals caught illegally dumping, such actions ultimately impose additional financial burdens on the broader community, which must fund the cleanup of unlawfully disposed waste."

The revised fee schedule is as follows: for a sedan or station wagon (general waste), the fee will increase from $10 to $11; for a van, utility vehicle, or trailer (general waste), from $12 to $15; and for any vehicle containing only green waste, the fee will decrease from $8 to $7.50.

PITTSBURGH — Chicago Cubs right-hander Yu Darvish has inflammation in his right triceps but no structural damage, and could start a throwing program as soon as the weekend.
Darvish, signed to a $126 million, six-year contract in February as a free agent, underwent an MRI on Tuesday in Chicago. The Cubs announced the results before playing the Pittsburgh Pirates on Wednesday night.
The Cubs also placed right-handed reliever Carl Edwards Jr. on the 10-day disabled list with right shoulder inflammation, and recalled right-hander Cory Mazzoni from Triple-A Iowa. Edwards felt discomfort in his shoulder Tuesday night after pitching one scoreless inning in an 8-6 victory over the Pirates.
Darvish got his first win with the Cubs in his previous start at Cincinnati on May 20, holding the Reds to one run and two hits in six innings. In eight starts, he is 1-3 with a 4.95 ERA.

However, "a sizeable" number of its units are below the 13sq metres for double rooms set out in legislation drawn up in 1992 and last modified in 2009.
All accommodation in Northern Ireland, from hotels to airbnb properties, must be certified by tourism officials in order to operate legally.

The forthcoming easyHotel on Howard Street in Belfast, part of a United Kingdom-based budget accommodation chain, is scheduled to commence operations in August. However, its opening is now contingent upon certification, as a significant proportion of its double rooms do not meet the minimum size requirements stipulated by Northern Irish legislation. Consequently, the hotel chain has formally contacted the Permanent Secretary at the Department for the Economy and the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, Karen Bradley, to seek urgent clarification. The statement further characterized the certification as a discretionary matter, emphasizing that the impending opening hinges on resolving this legislative discrepancy.

LONDON May 2 Commodities trader Vitol has agreed to buy an 85,000 barrel per day (bpd) condensate splitter in the Netherlands from Koch Supply and Trading, a subsidiary of U.S. conglomerate Koch Industries, Vitol said in a statement on Tuesday.
The world's largest oil trader has been expanding in the downstream and retail sectors over the last few years as it seeks outlets for its growing traded volumes.
Such assets also allow the trader to access new markets and to forge longer-term supply deals as opposed to ad hoc ones, the traditional base of its business.
Vitol's traded oil volume grew by 16 percent to over 7 million bpd last year.
The splitter, located in Rotterdam, is a specialised refining asset that processes very light oil, known as condensate, into higher value products such as naphtha that is used in the petrochemical industry and gasoline blending.
Vitol did not disclose the value of the deal.
"The splitter is a well-run asset in a good strategic location at the heart of Rotterdam's oil and petchem industry. Its acquisition will enhance our offering to our customers across the region," Russell Hardy, Vitol CEO for Europe, Middle East and Africa, said in the statement.
Vitol has a refining capacity of 390,000 bpd through various joint venture investments in northern Europe, Australia and the Middle East. It owns and operates the Cressier and Bayernoil refineries via subsidiary Varo Energy and has a majority stake in a refinery in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. (Reporting by Julia Payne and Bengaluru Newsroom; Editing by Mark Potter)
rewrite:
On Tuesday, May 2, Vitol, the world’s leading independent commodities trader, announced an agreement to acquire an 85,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) condensate splitter located in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, from Koch Supply and Trading, a subsidiary of Koch Industries. The transaction underscores Vitol’s ongoing strategic expansion within downstream and retail sectors, a move driven by the need to secure outlets for its increasing traded volumes. Such physical assets facilitate entry into new markets and enable the formation of longer-term supply arrangements, thereby diversifying beyond the ad hoc transactions that have traditionally constituted the core of its operations. Vitol’s traded oil volumes rose by 16 percent in the preceding year, exceeding 7 million bpd.

The Rotterdam splitter is a specialized refining unit that processes condensate, a very light crude oil, into higher-value products including naphtha for the petrochemical industry and components for gasoline blending. Russell Hardy, Vitol’s Chief Executive Officer for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, noted in the statement that the asset is well-operated and occupies a strategically advantageous position within Rotterdam’s integrated oil and petrochemical complex, asserting that its acquisition will enhance the company’s regional customer offerings. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Vitol maintains an aggregate refining capacity of approximately 390,000 bpd through various joint venture investments in Northern Europe, Australia, and the Middle East. This includes ownership and operation of the Cressier and Bayernoil refineries via its subsidiary Varo Energy, as well as a majority stake in a refinery in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates.

MADRID The Basque parliament on Thursday urged ETA to disarm as soon as possible, focusing attention on a pledge by the separatist group to surrender its entire arsenal two days before that handover is due to take place.
ETA declared the end of its bid to establish an independent Basque state in northern Spain and southern France in 2011 but has only handed over part of its weapons cache to authorities.
It has said it will give up the rest in the French city of Bayonne on Saturday.
However, it is not yet clear how the handover will be organised and if it will be formally accepted by the Spanish and French governments.
The Basque regional parliament in Vitoria-Gasteiz voted by 65 to 9 in support of a motion urging ETA to "carry out a single act of unilateral, complete, definitive and verified disarmament as soon as possible".
It also called for an international verification commission, which was set up when ETA declared a ceasefire in 2011, to continue supporting the process.
Spain's ruling Popular Party (PP) refuses to negotiate with ETA, instead calling for its total dissolution.
Its representative in the Basque parliament, Alfonso Alonso, said the planned handover was "a dramatisation of surrender".
"ETA lasted such a long time because it had social and political support. The process of socially disarming ETA is not over," Alonso said.
The Spanish state prosecutor has asked the High Court to examine any arms cache for murder weapons used in unresolved cases, but the judge has yet to give a ruling, a court spokeswoman said.
(Additional reporting by Inmaculada Sanz; Editing by Sonya Dowsett and John Stonestreet)
rewrite:
On Thursday, the Basque Parliament issued a formal appeal for the immediate disarmament of the separatist organization ETA. This legislative action underscores a pledge made by the group to surrender its remaining arsenal, scheduled for two days following the parliamentary motion. ETA declared a definitive cessation of its armed campaign for an independent Basque homeland in northern Spain and southern France in 2011, yet has previously relinquished only a portion of its weaponry. The group has announced its intention to surrender the remainder this Saturday in the French city of Bayonne. Significant uncertainty persists, however, regarding the logistical organization of this event and whether it will receive formal acceptance from the Spanish and French governments.

In a session held in Vitoria-Gasteiz, the regional parliament approved a motion by a vote of 65 to 9, urging ETA to execute "a single act of unilateral, complete, definitive and verified disarmament as soon as possible." The motion further advocated for the continued involvement of the international verification commission, established following ETA’s 2011 ceasefire declaration, to oversee the process. The Spanish national government, led by the Popular Party (PP), maintains a policy of non-negotiation with ETA, demanding instead the group's total dissolution. Alfonso Alonso, the PP’s representative in the Basque parliament, characterized the planned handover as "a dramatisation of surrender," noting that "ETA lasted such a long time because it had social and political support. The process of socially disarming ETA is not over."

In a related judicial development, the Spanish state prosecutor has petitioned the High Court to inspect any surrendered arms for potential evidence in unresolved homicide investigations. A court spokeswoman confirmed that a presiding judge has not yet issued a ruling on this request.

By JENNIFER McDERMOTT
Associated Press
PROVIDENCE, R.I. (AP) - A Rhode Island company is going to build a wind farm that will be 10 times the size of the nation's first offshore wind farm.
Deepwater Wind says the new 400-megawatt wind farm will also create more than 800 jobs in Rhode Island.
Democratic Gov. Gina Raimondo and other officials visited the Port of Providence on Wednesday for the announcement.
Massachusetts and Rhode Island announced offshore wind projects last week aimed at delivering 1,200 megawatts of energy, enough to power about 600,000 homes.
The company also built the nation's first offshore wind farm off Block Island, Rhode Island. It has five turbines. This latest project will have up to 50 turbines south of Martha's Vineyard.
Deepwater Wind's CEO says it will be "an enormous clean energy machine."

rewrite:
On May 30, 2018, Deepwater Wind announced plans to construct a 400-megawatt offshore wind farm, a project an order of magnitude larger than the nation's inaugural installation. The company, which developed the first U.S. offshore wind farm featuring five turbines near Block Island, Rhode Island, in 2016, intends to deploy up to fifty turbines south of Martha's Vineyard. This initiative follows recent commitments by Massachusetts and Rhode Island to procure 1,200 megawatts from offshore wind, a capacity sufficient to power approximately 600,000 residences.

The announcement was made at the Port of Providence, with Rhode Island Governor Gina Raimondo and other officials in attendance. The project is projected to generate over 800 employment opportunities within the state. The chief executive officer of Deepwater Wind characterized the forthcoming development as a substantial contributor to renewable energy infrastructure.

Previous spy shots have caught a new generation of the Escape (Kuga in Europe) under development, and now photos have revealed that a plug-in hybrid variant could be part of the lineup. Given the Blue Oval's decision to drop most of the cars from its lineup, a PHEV version of the crossover would be a way to get back some of the possible drop in average fuel economy across the whole range.
This test mule looks nearly identical to the ones in previous spy photos, except for the additional flap on the driver side fender that hides the spot for plugging in the Escape. Powertrain details for the PHEV remain a mystery at this point. We expect the model to use something new, though, due to the age of the tech driving the C-Max Energi and Fusion Energi.
Up front, the new Escape appears to retain the current model's broad grille and narrow lower fascia. The headlights continue to run up the fenders, too, but they seem more angular here. At the rear, Ford's engineers use panels to hide the shape rear, but it appears that there is a far sleeker shape back there that would lend the model a lot more style.
There aren't details about the next-gen Escape's cabin but expect it to share tech with the latest Focus because they ride on the same platform. A more advanced infotainment system and better driver assistance are among the likely improvements. Ford also intends to offer a three-row version, but so far details are sketchy about whether this version would be physically larger or just have extra seating in the back at the expense of less cargo room.
There are more concrete rumors about the non-PHEV Escape's powertrain. It would reportedly come standard with the 1.5-liter EcoBoost with cylinder activation that comes in 148-horsepower (110-kilowatt) and 180-hp (134 kW) tunes in the new Focus. Range-topping versions would allegedly get a turbocharged 2.0-liter.
Ford will reportedly unveil the new Escape in 2019, and it'll be on sale for the 2020 model year in the United States.
Source: Automedia
rewrite:
Recent photographic evidence has documented a next-generation iteration of the Ford Escape (marketed as the Kuga in Europe) undergoing development. These latest images indicate the potential inclusion of a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variant within the model lineup. This strategic introduction could serve to mitigate potential declines in corporate average fuel economy, a consideration particularly salient following Ford's strategic shift away from numerous traditional passenger car models.

The observed test vehicle is largely consistent with prior prototypes, with the principal distinction being a supplementary flap integrated into the driver-side fender, concealing the charging port for the PHEV system. Specific details regarding the plug-in hybrid powertrain remain undisclosed. However, it is anticipated that the system will constitute a new development, given the aging technology employed in existing models such as the C-Max Energi and Fusion Energi.

Exterior styling, as partially revealed, suggests the forthcoming Escape will maintain the current generation's prominent grille and narrowed lower fascia. The headlight design, while continuing to extend along the fenders, appears to adopt a more angular profile. Although rear sections remain obscured by camouflage, the contours imply a sleeker overall silhouette, potentially enhancing the vehicle's aesthetic appeal.

Interior specifications for the next-generation Escape are not yet available. Nevertheless, given its shared platform with the latest Ford Focus, the model is expected to incorporate similar technological features. Probable enhancements include a more advanced infotainment interface and upgraded driver assistance systems. Ford has also indicated plans for a three-row configuration, though precise details—whether this entails increased exterior dimensions or a repackaged interior sacrificing cargo space for additional seating—remain unconfirmed.

Powertrain information for conventional, non-hybrid variants is subject to more substantiated speculation. Reports suggest a standard 1.5-liter EcoBoost engine with cylinder deactivation technology, offered in multiple output configurations as seen in the new Focus. Allegedly, range-topping models will feature a turbocharged 2.0-liter powerplant.

Industry reports indicate an anticipated unveiling of the new Escape in 2019, with market availability in the United States commencing for the 2020 model year.

To the Editor:
Re “Keep ICE Arrests Out of Court” (Op-Ed, Nov. 27):
As César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández points out, equal access to justice — a founding principle of our country — is threatened when Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents seize suspected undocumented immigrants from our courthouses.
These actions discourage immigrants from coming to court as witnesses, plaintiffs and defendants and undermine the country’s promise of justice for all. That’s why the American Bar Association House of Delegates adopted a resolution in August calling on Congress to add courthouses to the list of “sensitive locations” in which immigration enforcement actions can be taken only in emergency circumstances.
Schools, hospitals and churches are already considered sensitive locations. Free and unfettered access to courthouses is essential to the administration of justice. Do we really want to discourage domestic violence victims or witnesses of crime from visiting our institutions of justice?
HILARIE BASS, MIAMI
The writer is president of the American Bar Association.
rewrite:
To the Editor:
In response to the opinion piece "Keep ICE Arrests Out of Court" (Nov. 27), César Cuauhtémoc García Hernández correctly asserts that the foundational principle of equal access to justice is compromised when Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents detain individuals suspected of lacking documentation within courthouses. Such enforcement actions deter immigrant participation in the legal system, whether as witnesses, plaintiffs, or defendants, thereby eroding the nation's commitment to justice for all. Consequently, the American Bar Association’s House of Delegates adopted a resolution in August urging Congress to designate courthouses as "sensitive locations," where immigration enforcement would be permitted only under exigent circumstances. This designation already applies to schools, hospitals, and churches. Unimpeded access to courthouses is indispensable for the proper administration of justice. We must consider whether it is prudent to dissuade victims of domestic violence or witnesses to crimes from engaging with our judicial institutions.

HILARIE BASS, MIAMI
The writer is president of the American Bar Association.

NEW YORK, April 28 U.S. interest rate futures were steady to marginally lower on Friday as traders saw the Federal Reserve as being on track to raise interest rates further despite news the U.S. economy grew at its weakest pace in three years in the first quarter.
Analysts and traders brushed off government data showing gross domestic product expanded at a 0.7 percent annual rate, blaming the below-forecast reading on a statistical anomaly and seasonal factors.
Instead they said they were confident in an economic rebound in the current quarter together with signs of accelerating employment costs, which would allow the Fed to raise rates as early as June.
The Federal Open Market Committee, the U.S. central bank's policy-setting group, meets next Tuesday and Wednesday and traders see little chance it will raise rates from its current target range of 0.75 to 1.00 percent .
"Wage gains are unambiguously accelerating. Meanwhile, the trend in the unemployment rate still appears to be downward. These data will keep pressure on the Fed to keep tightening," Jim O'Sullivan, chief U.S. economist at High Frequency Economics, wrote in a research note.
Earlier Friday, the Labor Department said its employment cost index (ECI), which measures wages and benefits, grew at a 0.8 percent annualized pace in the first three months of 2017, faster than the 0.6 percent rate seen among economists polled by Reuters.
U.S. rates futures fell almost immediately on the GDP and ECI data before turning flat as traders awaited a vote in Washington to try to avert a government shutdown.
Federal funds futures implied traders saw a 71 percent chance the Fed would raise rates to 1.00-1.25 percent at its June policy meeting, unchanged from late on Thursday, CME Group's FedWatch program showed.
They suggested traders priced in an 84 percent probability the Fed would make such a move at its September meeting, little changed from Thursday's close.
Fed funds contracts implied traders saw a 54 percent chance the Fed would raise rates to 1.25-1.50 percent in December , up slightly from 51 percent late Thursday, according to CME's FedWatch.
(Reporting by Richard Leong; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama and James Dalgleish)
rewrite:
U.S. interest rate futures exhibited stability with a marginal downward bias on Friday, April 28, as market participants maintained expectations for further monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve. This sentiment persisted despite the release of data indicating that U.S. economic growth, measured by gross domestic product, had decelerated to an annualized rate of 0.7 percent in the first quarter, its most subdued pace in three years. Financial analysts and traders largely dismissed the significance of this below-forecast GDP figure, attributing the weakness to transient statistical distortions and seasonal adjustment factors.

Market focus remained firmly on indicators supportive of continued Federal Reserve action. Participants expressed confidence in an anticipated economic rebound during the current quarter, coupled with emerging signs of accelerating labor costs. These conditions were viewed as providing the necessary justification for the central bank to implement an increase in the federal funds rate as early as its June policy meeting. The immediate focus, however, was on the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for the following Tuesday and Wednesday, with consensus expecting no change to the current target range of 0.75 to 1.00 percent at that session.

Supporting the case for policy normalization, the Labor Department reported that its Employment Cost Index (ECI), a comprehensive measure of wages and benefits, rose at an annualized pace of 0.8 percent in the first quarter. This acceleration exceeded the 0.6 percent gain forecast by economists in a Reuters poll. "Wage gains are unambiguously accelerating. Meanwhile, the trend in the unemployment rate still appears to be downward. These data will keep pressure on the Fed to keep tightening," noted Jim O'Sullivan, chief U.S. economist at High Frequency Economics, in a research commentary.

Market pricing, as derived from federal funds futures contracts, reflected this outlook. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, futures implied a 71 percent probability of a June rate hike to a 1.00-1.25 percent target range, a level unchanged from the previous day. The probability assigned to a subsequent increase in September stood at 84 percent, also largely steady. Expectations for a further hike in December, to a 1.25-1.50 percent range, were priced at a 54 percent likelihood, a slight increase from 51 percent on Thursday. Following an initial decline upon the release of the GDP and ECI data, rates futures trading stabilized as market attention shifted to legislative proceedings in Washington aimed at averting a potential government shutdown.

Police opened fire after a man pointed a gun at them during an attempted robbery at 7-Eleven in Kalihi (Image: Hawaii News Now)
Honolulu police arrested a man suspected of trying to rob a 7-Eleven store and then pointing a gun at officers on Sunday night.
Police said the suspect, 35-year-old David Kinikini, was armed when he entered the store at the intersection of Dillingham Boulevard and North King Street at around 8:50 p.m. That’s when customers and employees ran out of the store and called police.
Police arrived within minutes to find Kinikini trapped inside the store.
HPD said Kinikini then pointed his gun at the officers, prompting them to fire two shots.
He was not hit by a bullet, but he did faint, authorities said.
Police arrested Kinikini on two counts of first-degree attempted murder on a law enforcement officer and one count of first-degree robbery.
No injuries were reported.
The 7-Eleven store has since reopened.
Copyright 2018 Hawaii News Now. All rights reserved.
rewrite: On Sunday evening, Honolulu police officers discharged their firearms in response to a suspect aiming a weapon at them during an attempted commercial robbery at a 7-Eleven convenience store in the Kalihi district. The suspect, identified as 35-year-old David Kinikini, allegedly entered the establishment located at the intersection of Dillingham Boulevard and North King Street at approximately 8:50 p.m. while armed. This action prompted customers and employees to evacuate the premises and contact law enforcement. Officers arrived shortly thereafter, locating Kinikini confined within the store. According to the Honolulu Police Department, Kinikini subsequently directed his firearm at the officers, which precipitated the discharge of two rounds by police. Although not struck by gunfire, the suspect lost consciousness and was taken into custody. Kinikini faces formal charges, including two counts of first-degree attempted murder of a law enforcement officer and one count of first-degree robbery. No injuries were sustained during the incident, and the business has resumed normal operations.

Under the current cosmology model, known as λCDM, dark matter, which makes up a vast majority of the known universe, creates a sort of gravitational framework, influencing the movement of our galaxies and other large objects in space. Cosmologists love this model, because it answers a lot of questions and works well.
© AP Photo/ Isaac Gomez/INAH 'Floating' Stone Sanctuary Allegedly Representing Universe Uncovered in Mexico
However, one of the consequences of the λCDM model is that so-called dwarf, or ‘satellite,' galaxies, should orbit a host galaxy like a cloud, a ball, or, for a better scientific analogy, like electrons around the nucleus of an atom.
But they don't. According to a review by Ars Technica, two closely observed galaxies — our Milky Way and our nearest galactic neighbor the Andromeda Galaxy — have their smaller satellite galaxies arranged like a disc. Yes, those satellite galaxies more or less orbit their hosts in a plane, like planets orbit the stars.
Scientists used to dismiss these two occurrences as a statistical quirk. But then a third was noted: Centaurus A, whose satellite galaxies are also seemingly aligned in a single plane.
Why does it happen? Cosmologists admit: they don't know.
"There is no obvious answer, unfortunately, or maybe expectedly — otherwise planes of satellite galaxies would not be seen as a problem and we wouldn't talk about them as much," said astrophysicist Marcel Pawlowski of the University of California, Irvine, who co-authored the study with fellow astrophysicist Oliver Müller of the University of Basel and other colleagues.
Astrophysicists say more data is needed. Either observations of the known universe are playing a bad joke on our statistics, or our entire cosmology model must be reviewed. But, surprisingly, the scientific community is not quite ready to do that, yet.
"It would take very strong evidence of an insurmountable problem to give up on λCDM, or at least a model that looks very much like it," said astrophysicist Mike Boylan-Kolchin of the University of Texas, who commented on the study.
"My money is on λCDM, but it would be thrilling to find out that it is wrong," Boylan-Kolchin added.
rewrite:
The prevailing cosmological framework, known as the Lambda Cold Dark Matter (λCDM) model, posits that dark matter—constituting the predominant mass-energy content of the observable universe—establishes a gravitational scaffold that governs the dynamics of galaxies and other large-scale structures. This model is widely favored within cosmology for its explanatory power and empirical consistency.

A consequential prediction of the λCDM paradigm is the distribution of dwarf, or satellite, galaxies around a primary host galaxy. Simulations suggest these satellites should be dispersed in a roughly spherical halo, analogous to a cloud or, in a more precise physical analogy, akin to electrons occupying a diffuse orbital cloud around an atomic nucleus. Observational evidence, however, contradicts this expectation. As detailed in a review by Ars Technica, the satellite galaxies of the Milky Way and the Andromeda Galaxy are not spherically distributed but are instead arranged in a thin, rotating plane, reminiscent of planetary orbits within a stellar system.

Initially, these two instances were considered potential statistical anomalies. This interpretation has been challenged by the discovery of a similar configuration around Centaurus A, a third galaxy whose satellites also appear aligned in a coherent plane. The underlying mechanism for this planar alignment remains unexplained. As astrophysicist Marcel Pawlowski of the University of California, Irvine, a co-author of a relevant study, notes: "There is no obvious answer, unfortunately, or maybe expectedly—otherwise planes of satellite galaxies would not be seen as a problem and we would not discuss them as extensively."

The scientific consensus indicates a need for further data. The present discrepancy suggests one of two possibilities: either current observations represent a statistical fluke, or the λCDM model requires significant revision. Notably, the cosmological community exhibits reluctance to abandon the established paradigm without compelling evidence. Astrophysicist Mike Boylan-Kolchin of the University of Texas, commenting on the issue, stated: "It would require very strong evidence of an insurmountable problem to relinquish λCDM, or at least a model that closely resembles it." He further added, "My confidence remains with λCDM, though it would be profoundly exciting to discover it is fundamentally incorrect." This tension underscores a critical juncture in cosmology, where accumulating observational data may necessitate a refinement of our most fundamental models of the universe.

ADVERTISING agencies are joining a new campaign pledging not to accept work promoting the ‘no’ campaign for marriage equality.
Some of Australia’s biggest advertisers are involved in the Say No to No campaign, as well as smaller agencies and freelancers, Huffington Post has reported.
Many LGBTI advocates and mental health experts have said a plebiscite and public debate will be harmful to the LGBTI community.
“A plebiscite would give anti-gay campaigners the biggest stage they have ever had,” said Australian Marriage Equality.
“I’ve been in ads for over 30 years and it’s a great community,” said Nick Cummins, creative partner at The Royals agency and one of the campaign’s organisers.
“Sometimes we have to make messages or ads for things we don’t necessarily believe in 100 percent, but when it comes to these sorts of issues, it’s an opportunity for us to have an impact. This is something we can make a difference.
“We know there are going to be those hurtful and harmful messages which will hurt a lot of Australians, so this is us having the ability to say ‘not on our watch’. It’s like refusing to work on tobacco advertising, I see it as similar.
“This is not about stopping people voting no, it’s just us saying we won’t create hurtful messages.”
Say No to No has already been joined by hundreds of advertisers who refuse to promote the anti–marriage equality message, despite the millions of dollars in potential revenue.
“Imagine if every agency, production company, sound designer or illustrator said no to working on these harmful ads,” said the campaigners in a statement.
“Imagine then our friends in media also standing up and saying no to the no campaign. And brands also joining in to pledge that no harmful ads will appear on their sites or channels.
“Yes, the no campaigners will find a way to make their hurtful divisive messages. But we can make it difficult for them.
“And more importantly, we as an industry can show our friends in the non-heterosexual community that we still believe in them and in fairness.”
rewrite:
A coalition of advertising agencies has initiated a new campaign, pledging to decline any creative work that promotes the opposition to marriage equality. As reported by the Huffington Post, this "Say No to No" initiative includes participation from several of Australia's largest advertising firms, alongside smaller agencies and freelance professionals. The movement emerges amid concerns raised by numerous LGBTI advocates and mental health experts, who argue that a public plebiscite and the accompanying national debate would inflict harm upon the LGBTI community. Australian Marriage Equality has echoed this sentiment, stating that such a plebiscite would provide "anti-gay campaigners the biggest stage they have ever had."

Nick Cummins, a creative partner at The Royals agency and one of the campaign's organisers, contextualised the decision within broader industry ethics. He noted that while advertising professionals often create messages for products or causes they may not personally endorse, certain social issues present a clear opportunity for positive impact. "This is something we can make a difference on," Cummins stated. He drew a parallel to the industry's widespread refusal to work on tobacco advertising, framing the current pledge as a similar ethical stand. "We know there are going to be those hurtful and harmful messages which will hurt a lot of Australians," he said, "so this is us having the ability to say 'not on our watch'." He emphasised that the objective is not to prevent individuals from voting according to their conscience, but rather for the industry to refuse to craft explicitly damaging communications.

Hundreds of advertisers have already joined the pledge, foregoing substantial potential revenue by refusing to promote the anti-marriage equality message. Campaign organisers have issued a statement envisioning a broader collective refusal, asking stakeholders to imagine if every agency, production company, and media supplier declined to participate in such advertisements. They further called upon media outlets and brands to pledge that no harmful ads would appear on their platforms. The campaign acknowledges that opponents of marriage equality will likely find alternative avenues to disseminate their messages. However, the primary aim is to significantly raise the practical and financial barriers to doing so. Ultimately, the initiative seeks to demonstrate solidarity, signalling to the non-heterosexual community that the advertising industry supports them and remains committed to principles of fairness and equality.
