MONTGOMERY, Ala. (AP) - Alabama officials were ordered Wednesday to release information about the state's lethal injection procedure as a federal judge granted news organizations' request to unseal records in the wake of an aborted execution.
U.S. Judge Karon O. Bowdre ruled that the public has a "common law right of access to the sealed records relating to Alabama's lethal injection protocol." However, Bowdre said the state can keep some information secret in the interest of security, such as the names of low-level prison employees involved in executions.
The judge ordered the state to tell her by June 7 if there is identifying information in any of the records that the court plans to make public.
Alabama for years has released scant details about its execution process or where it obtains the drugs used.
A spokesman for Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall said the office is reviewing the order.
The Associated Press, The Montgomery Advertiser and the Alabama Media Group had filed a motion seeking the release of the protocol.
The motion was filed in federal court in a lawsuit brought by death row inmate Doyle Lee Hamm. Alabama halted Hamm's execution in February when the execution team could not connect an intravenous line to Hamm, who had damaged veins because of lymphoma, hepatitis and past drug use.
"It may also help the public to understand how the same scenario might be repeated or avoided under the protocol as it currently stands," Bowdre wrote of the release of the information.
rewrite:
On Wednesday, a federal judge mandated that Alabama state officials disclose information pertaining to the state's lethal injection protocol, granting a motion by several news organizations to unseal records following a recently halted execution. U.S. District Judge Karon O. Bowdre ruled that a "common law right of access" applies to the sealed documents concerning Alabama's execution procedures. The ruling permits the state to redact specific security-sensitive details, including the identities of lower-level correctional personnel involved in carrying out executions. Judge Bowdre further directed the state to identify by June 7 any personally identifiable information contained within the records slated for public release.

For years, Alabama has maintained a policy of minimal disclosure regarding its execution methods and the sourcing of lethal injection drugs. A spokesperson for Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall stated the office is presently reviewing the judicial order. The motion to unseal was filed in federal court by The Associated Press, The Montgomery Advertiser, and the Alabama Media Group within the context of a lawsuit brought by death row inmate Doyle Lee Hamm. The state aborted Hamm's execution in February after the execution team repeatedly failed to establish an intravenous line, complications attributed to Hamm's compromised vascular health due to lymphoma, hepatitis, and prior intravenous drug use.

In her opinion, Judge Bowdre noted that public disclosure of the protocol could aid understanding of how similar procedural failures might be either repeated or prevented under the existing framework.

The World Health Organization supports the consideration of Government of South Africa of introduction of a tax on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) to help reduce excessive sugar intake. This is one of interventions proposed in the Strategy for the prevention and control of obesity in South Africa 2015-2020.
WHO has supported introduction of such taxes since it was proposed by the National Treasury in August 2016.WHO’s Representative to South Africa, Dr. Rufaro Chatora, took part in a parliamentary hearing held on January 31, 2017, to discuss the proposed SSB tax. During his presentation, Dr. Chatora highlighted the evidence and the impact of SSB tax. Experience from other countries which implemented the same tax demonstrates its potential to reduce consumption of sugar and raise revenues that can be used to prevent and control diabetes, obesity and other noncommunicable diseases (NCDs).
In recent days, the WHO Executive Board was held, during which Board members asked the WHO Secretariat for more information on a range of policy options and cost-effective interventions proposed by WHO to prevent and control NCDs, including the use of taxation on SSBs, before the next World Health Assembly (22-31 May).
There has been no “veto” of such interventions proposed by WHO or its Executive Board, including SSBs, despite industry statements and media reporting based on such statements. WHO Member States have asked for more information on these interventions ahead of the upcoming World Health Assembly.
“WHO stands ready to support the Republic of South Africa, and as well as other countries, in protecting and improving the health their citizens and offering effective, technically sound and feasible measures to promote health for all people, no matter age, gender or background,” says Chatora.
Taxation on SSB is just one of a range of cost-effective measures proposed by WHO to curb the threat of NCDs, responsible for the deaths of 16 million people every year before the age of 70. Other interventions targeting obesity include nutrition labelling; marketing restrictions of unhealthy foods and beverages to kids; fruit and vegetable subsidies; physical activity policies and social marketing campaigns. WHO member states around the world, including South Africa, have committed to halt the rise of obesity and diabetes, reduce premature deaths from NCDs by 25 per cent by 2025 and one-third by 2030, the latter target in line with the Sustainable Development Goals.
rewrite:
The World Health Organization endorses the consideration by the Government of South Africa to implement a fiscal levy on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) as a mechanism to mitigate excessive sugar consumption. This intervention forms part of a suite of measures outlined in the national *Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Obesity in South Africa 2015-2020*. WHO support for such fiscal policy commenced following its initial proposal by the South African National Treasury in August 2016. The Organization’s commitment was further demonstrated by the participation of its Representative to South Africa, Dr. Rufaro Chatora, in a parliamentary hearing convened on 31 January 2017 to deliberate the proposed tax. In his address, Dr. Chatora underscored the empirical evidence and anticipated public health impact of an SSB levy. International precedent from jurisdictions that have enacted analogous taxes indicates their efficacy in reducing dietary sugar intake and in generating government revenue, which can be strategically reinvested in initiatives to prevent and control diabetes, obesity, and other noncommunicable diseases (NCDs).

The subject was also deliberated during the recent session of the WHO Executive Board. Board members requested the WHO Secretariat to provide additional information on a spectrum of policy options and cost-effective interventions, including the taxation of SSBs, proposed by the Organization for NCD prevention and control, in advance of the forthcoming World Health Assembly (22-31 May). Contrary to assertions from certain industry quarters and subsequent media reports, there has been no veto of these proposed interventions, including SSB taxation, by either WHO or its Executive Board. Rather, Member States have sought further technical details on these measures prior to the Assembly.

Dr. Chatora affirmed, “WHO stands ready to support the Republic of South Africa, alongside other nations, in safeguarding and enhancing the health of their populations by advocating for effective, evidence-based, and feasible measures to promote health for all people, irrespective of age, gender, or socioeconomic background.”

Taxation of SSBs constitutes one component of a broader array of cost-effective measures recommended by WHO to address the NCD burden, which accounts for approximately 16 million premature annual deaths globally among persons under 70 years of age. Complementary interventions targeting obesity encompass mandatory nutrition labelling, restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy foods and beverages to children, subsidies for fruits and vegetables, physical activity policies, and social marketing campaigns. WHO Member States worldwide, including South Africa, have committed to halting the rise in obesity and diabetes, and to reducing premature mortality from NCDs by 25% by 2025 and by one-third by 2030, the latter target aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals.

Michael Cohen scrubbed the reference “personal attorney to President Donald J. Trump” from his Twitter biography on Wednesday just days after he went on television to declare that his first loyalty is to his family.
Cohen, who once famously said he’d “take a bullet” for the president, made the change on his Twitter page but still describes himself as “Personal Attorney to President Donald J. Trump” on his LinkedIn page.
Cohen, who’s under criminal investigation by federal prosecutors in Manhattan, told ABC News in an interview that “my wife, my daughter and my son have my first loyalty and always will. I put my family and country first.”
The change on Cohen’s Twitter page was first reported by Newsweek.
The interview, which aired Monday, was the first time he’s spoken publicly since FBI agents, acting on a referral from special counsel Robert Mueller, raided his office, apartment and hotel room in search of documents related to his hush-money payment to porn star Stormy Daniels less than two weeks before the 2016 election.
Cohen paid Daniels $130,000 as part of a non-disclosure agreement to keep her silence about an affair she alleges she had with Trump in 2006.
The Trump Organization turned over 1.3 million items seized during the raid to the federal government after examining them to determine whether they contained information protected by attorney-client privilege.
The items can now be used by prosecutors in the Southern District of New York who are investigating Cohen for possible bank and wire fraud, and campaign finance violations.
Cohen has not been charged.

On Wednesday, Michael Cohen removed the descriptor “personal attorney to President Donald J. Trump” from his Twitter biography. This alteration followed a televised interview, aired Monday, in which Cohen asserted that his primary loyalty resides with his family. Notably, the designation remains unchanged on his LinkedIn profile. Cohen, who is the subject of a federal criminal investigation by prosecutors in the Southern District of New York, stated to ABC News, “my wife, my daughter and my son have my first loyalty and always will. I put my family and country first.”

The interview marked his first public commentary since Federal Bureau of Investigation agents, acting upon a referral from Special Counsel Robert S. Mueller III, executed search warrants at his office, apartment, and hotel room. This raid sought documents pertaining to a $130,000 payment made to adult film actress Stormy Daniels. The payment, facilitated through a non-disclosure agreement, was intended to secure her silence regarding an alleged 2006 affair with Donald Trump and occurred shortly before the 2016 presidential election.

Following the searches, the Trump Organization conducted a review of the approximately 1.3 million seized items to ascertain attorney-client privilege claims before surrendering them to federal authorities. These materials are now available to prosecutors examining potential bank fraud, wire fraud, and campaign finance violations involving Cohen. To date, no criminal charges have been filed against him. The initial report of the biographical modification was published by Newsweek.

Our audience’s strong views on how much danger drones present to our flying
In the past couple of weeks drones have been a hot topic in aviation as news broke of a drone-helicopter collision over New York City and the FAA banned drones from operating at a number of federal landmarks. The question that has been on the minds of personal flyers for years, though, is this: how much risk do recreational and other light drones present to our small airplanes?
The voice of our audience was overwhelming in expressing concern about these remotely controlled or autonomous flying contraptions. A full 71 percent of respondents voiced concern that drones were either a “great risk” (31 percent) or they posed some real risk (41 percent) to light GA.
A minority felt the opposite, that drones either didn’t present “much risk” (17 percent) or they posed “effectively zero risk” to light GA.
Just one precent of respondents voiced the opinion that drones are a positive factor in GA safety.
rewrite: Recent discourse within aviation has been significantly shaped by incidents involving unmanned aerial systems, notably a drone-helicopter collision in New York City and subsequent Federal Aviation Administration restrictions around federal landmarks. This has amplified a longstanding concern among general aviation participants: the degree of risk posed by recreational and lightweight drones to small aircraft. Survey data from this community reveals a predominant apprehension. Specifically, 71 percent of respondents indicated that drones constitute either a "great risk" (31 percent) or "some real risk" (41 percent) to general aviation. A minority dissented, with 17 percent perceiving "not much risk" and a further portion assessing the risk as "effectively zero." Notably, only one percent of respondents viewed drones as a net positive for aviation safety. The collective sentiment thus underscores a pronounced concern regarding drone integration into shared airspace.

BRUSSELS (Reuters) - European Union officials have proposed removing eight jurisdictions from the blacklist of tax havens the bloc adopted in December, in what critics may see as a blow to its campaign against tax avoidance.
EU states decided last month to draw up the list in a bid to discourage the most aggressive tax dodging practices.
But eight of the 17 jurisdictions currently listed are set to be quickly removed from the list after they offered to change their tax rules, according to EU documents seen by Reuters.
Panama, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, Barbados, Grenada, Macao, Mongolia and Tunisia are the jurisdictions that EU officials have recommended be delisted.
The removal of Bahrain was also initially considered, but its delisting was eventually not recommended, the documents show.
The proposal will be discussed at a meeting of EU ambassadors on Wednesday and is expected to be adopted by EU finance ministers when they meet next week in Brussels for monthly talks.
Jurisdictions set to remain on the blacklist are American Samoa, Bahrain, Guam, the Marshall Islands, Namibia, Palau, Saint Lucia, Samoa, and Trinidad and Tobago.
The proposal for the delisting was made by the so-called Code of Conduct Group, which gathers tax experts from the 28 EU member states. It monitors countries’ commitments to abide by EU standards on tax matters.
If the recommendation were confirmed by EU ministers, the eight jurisdictions will be moved to a so-called gray list which includes those who have committed to change their rules on tax transparency and cooperation. The gray list currently includes 47 jurisdictions.
The shrinking of the blacklist is likely to be criticized by tax transparency groups. In December some activists denounced the listing process as a whitewash and had called for the inclusion in the blacklist of some EU countries accused of facilitating tax avoidance, like Luxembourg, Malta, Ireland and the Netherlands.
The recommended removal of Panama may cause particular outcry, as it has been at the center of one of the largest disclosures of offshore schemes, the so-called Panama Papers.
EU officials have said the purpose of the blacklist is to convince jurisdictions to become more transparent. Having fewer on the list means more countries have committed to changes, they say.
rewrite:
European Union officials have proposed the removal of eight jurisdictions from the bloc’s tax haven blacklist, which was formally adopted in December. This development may be perceived by critics as undermining the EU’s broader initiative to combat tax avoidance. The list was originally established following a decision by EU member states last month, with the objective of deterring aggressive tax planning practices.

According to EU documents reviewed by Reuters, eight of the seventeen currently listed jurisdictions are slated for rapid removal after making commitments to amend their tax regulations. The jurisdictions recommended for delisting are Panama, South Korea, the United Arab Emirates, Barbados, Grenada, Macao, Mongolia, and Tunisia. Although the removal of Bahrain was initially contemplated, the documents indicate that its delisting was ultimately not advised.

This proposal is scheduled for discussion at a meeting of EU ambassadors on Wednesday and is anticipated to be endorsed by EU finance ministers during their forthcoming monthly deliberations in Brussels next week. Jurisdictions that would remain on the blacklist include American Samoa, Bahrain, Guam, the Marshall Islands, Namibia, Palau, Saint Lucia, Samoa, and Trinidad and Tobago.

The recommendation for delisting originates from the Code of Conduct Group, a body comprising tax experts from all twenty-eight EU member states, which is responsible for monitoring compliance with EU standards on taxation. Should EU ministers approve the recommendation, the eight jurisdictions would be transferred to a “gray list,” which encompasses territories that have pledged to enhance tax transparency and cooperation. Presently, forty-seven jurisdictions are included on this gray list.

The prospective reduction of the blacklist is likely to attract criticism from tax transparency advocacy groups. During the list’s initial publication in December, some activists condemned the process as inadequate, arguing for the inclusion of certain EU member states—such as Luxembourg, Malta, Ireland, and the Netherlands—that have been accused of enabling tax avoidance. The proposed removal of Panama may provoke particular controversy, given its central role in the “Panama Papers” leak, one of the most significant disclosures of offshore financial arrangements.

EU officials have maintained that the blacklist’s primary aim is to encourage jurisdictions to adopt greater transparency. They contend that a shorter list reflects increased commitments to reform among a wider array of countries.

NEW YORK (CBSNewYork) — The NYPD is taking extra security precautions after learning about Wednesday’s shooting that occurred at a congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia.
Deputy Commissioner of Intelligence and Counterterrorism John Miller said the NYPD sprang into action determining where any members of congress might be in New York City and whether they were attending any public events.
“Out of an abundance of caution we moved resources to City Hall, to Gracie Mansion, to other government locations and as we learned more we were able to adjust that,” Miller said. “We will have additional resources at some public events where elected officials are attending today.”
PHOTOS: Gunfire Erupts At Congressional Baseball Practice
Members of the NYPD’s Critical Response Command and Strategic Response Group have been deployed to government locations.
Miller noted, “We are seeing globally with increasing frequency either terrorist attacks or incidents involving deranged active shooters.”
Five people were shot when a man opened fire on members of the Republican Congress as they were practicing for an annual charity baseball game, which is scheduled to go on as planned Thursday.
The shooting suspect, identified by law enforcement sources as James T. Hodgkinson, 66, of Belleville, Illinois, was fatally shot by police.
The FBI is working to identify a motive for the shooting.
rewrite:
In response to the shooting that occurred during a congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia on Wednesday, the New York Police Department has implemented enhanced security protocols. Deputy Commissioner for Intelligence and Counterterrorism John Miller stated that the department immediately initiated efforts to ascertain the locations of any congressional members within New York City and their potential participation in public events. Miller explained that resources were preemptively deployed to sites including City Hall and Gracie Mansion, with subsequent adjustments made as more information became available. He confirmed that additional personnel would be present at certain public events involving elected officials.

Units from the NYPD's Critical Response Command and Strategic Response Group have been assigned to secure government locations. Miller observed a global trend of increasing frequency in both terrorist attacks and incidents involving disturbed active shooters. The Virginia incident resulted in five individuals being shot when a gunman opened fire on Republican members of Congress practicing for an annual charity baseball game, which authorities have confirmed will proceed as scheduled. The alleged assailant, identified by law enforcement as 66-year-old James T. Hodgkinson of Belleville, Illinois, was fatally wounded by police. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is currently investigating the motive behind the attack.

Those who voted for The Apprentice star Donald Trump in the 2016 election because they wanted an entertaining presidency that would mirror their favorite NBC reality TV show are probably not experiencing any voter’s remorse just yet. Trump’s tumultuous administration has already seen over a dozen high level firings and resignations, and it’s only eight months into his first term. The latest White House drama of course involves Secretary of State Rex Tillerson, who was already at odds with the president before it came out this week that he allegedly called Trump an “f-ing moron” back in July, threatening to resign his post.
Now, Axios is reporting that Trump is entertaining the idea of replacing Tillerson with CIA Director Mike Pompeo. (In other words, expect an announcement by the end of the day.) One especially telling excerpt of the report alleges Trump’s real problem with Tillerson, and not surpringly it involves the amount of media attention the former Exxon CEO is getting from his beloved cable news programs.
Sources tell us Trump recognizes that a Cabinet shuffle would bring bad press. White House Chief of Staff John Kelly wants stability, and so is discouraging high-level departures before next year. And yet, insiders say Trump’s relationship with Tillerson is broken beyond repair. We’re told Trump was furious that Tillerson didn’t try to blunt the story about him calling the president a “moron,” by just going out and denying it (whether or not it actually occurred). After what Trump considered a strong trip to Vegas, he seethed when he got back and saw Tillerson’s gaffe dominating cable-news coverage. Everywhere he flipped, there was Tillerson’s face instead of his.
Given Trump’s obsession with the NBC News exclusive this week even in light of the mass shooting in Las Vegas and a humanitarian crisis in Puerto Rico (and like, everything we know about his character), it certainly doesn’t seem unfathomable.
rewrite:
The electorate that supported Donald Trump, formerly of *The Apprentice*, in the 2016 presidential election, ostensibly desiring a presidency as entertaining as the NBC reality program, likely remains without significant regret. This assessment persists despite an administration marked by turbulence, including over a dozen high-level dismissals and resignations within its initial eight months. The prevailing White House narrative presently centers on Secretary of State Rex Tillerson. Tensions between Tillerson and the president, which were previously established, intensified following reports this week that the Secretary allegedly referred to Trump as an “f-ing moron” in July and subsequently contemplated resignation.

According to an Axios report, President Trump is now considering replacing Tillerson with Central Intelligence Agency Director Mike Pompeo, a move that could be imminent. A particularly revealing element of the report suggests Trump’s primary grievance involves the substantial media attention Tillerson, the former ExxonMobil CEO, commands from cable news networks—a domain of particular significance to the president. Sources indicate that while Trump acknowledges a cabinet reshuffle would generate negative publicity, and while Chief of Staff John Kelly advocates for stability by discouraging further high-level departures before the coming year, the relationship between the president and his Secretary of State is perceived as irreparably damaged.

Furthermore, following what the president deemed a successful trip to Las Vegas, he returned to find cable news coverage dominated by Tillerson’s diplomatic misstep, thereby supplanting his own media presence. Considering Trump’s demonstrated preoccupation with media narratives—evidenced by his focus on an NBC News exclusive this week amidst the aftermath of the Las Vegas shooting and the Puerto Rico humanitarian crisis—this course of action appears entirely plausible. The president’s well-documented character and priorities render such a decision far from unfathomable.

The U.S. stock market has been in a pronounced uptrend of late, with a number of companies seeing particular gains on the back of strong quarterly earnings. However, the stocks that have lagged the market ahead of quarterly results could be the ones offering the most opportunity, Goldman Sachs wrote on Wednesday.
In a note written by options strategist Katherine Fogertey, Goldman recommended buying call options on stocks that had underperformed the broader market by at least 3% in the two weeks ahead of their quarterly earnings release. “We have found that over the past 20 years, stocks that underperform have had a tendency to stage relief rallies on reported earnings,” the note said. “This bias in the market has made buying calls on these stocks particularly profitable.”
For the fourth-quarter earnings season, investors who bought the closest out-of-the-money call five days ahead of the earnings date, and closed it the day after, returned 24% on such stocks. “This is above the 1996 [to] present average of 18%,” Goldman wrote.
The investment bank wrote that this method was one of “our two favorite earnings strategies,” along with buying straddles—wherein an investor buys a bullish call option and a bearish put option at the same strike price, betting that a stock will move by a certain amount, rather than in a particular direction.
Goldman named five companies that fit the criteria for the “underperformer” trade: Kroger Co. KR, +0.17% , Southern Co. SO, -0.94% , Alexion Pharmaceuticals Inc. ALXN, +0.36% , Charter Communications Inc. CHTR, +0.30% and Stillwater Mining Co. SWC, +0.15% .
In the case of Kroger, Goldman expects the company’s earnings to top expectations due to a stock-repurchase program, it said. The bank also said the grocery-store chain’s outlook would be “better than feared.”
Thus far this year, Kroger shares are down 4.2%, compared with a 4.4% gain for the S&P 500 SPX, +0.11% .

NICOSIA, Cyprus (AP) - The Cyprus Cooperative Bank says it's looking for investors to buy up the lender either in whole or in part.
The bank said Monday it has appointed Citigroup Global Markets to look for investors as part of its strategic plan.
The deadline for expressions of interest is March 29.
The bank is 77-percent state-owned and is the leader in the amount of deposits held by Cypriots.
But it's weighed down by bad loans - more than 58 percent of the total.
That was a consequence of a 2013 banking crisis that forced Cyprus to accept a rescue deal that included a seizure of unsecured deposits in the country's two largest lenders.
Finance Minister Harris Georgiades said the move would help rebuild confidence and credibility in the bank.

Although the state holds a 77-percent ownership stake and the bank maintains the largest share of deposits in Cyprus, it remains burdened by a non-performing loan ratio exceeding 58 percent. Finance Minister Harris Georgiades stated that this initiative aims to restore confidence and credibility in the institution.

On February 15, 2017, His Excellency Eng. Sultan bin Saeed Al Mansoori, Minister of Economy of the United Arab Emirates, convened a meeting with H.E. Dauren Abayev, Minister of Information and Communications of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The primary objective of the discussions was to advocate for enhanced bilateral cooperation between the two nations, with a specific focus on the fields of information systems, innovation, and smart city development. The dialogue centered on establishing joint institutional mechanisms to facilitate the exchange of expertise and foster collaborative initiatives within these strategic sectors.

The meeting was attended by a delegation of senior officials from both nations. Representing the UAE were Eng. Mohammed Ahmed Bin Abdulaziz Al-Shehhi, Undersecretary for Economic Affairs; Humaid bin Butti Al Muhairi, Assistant Undersecretary for the Corporate Sector and Consumer Protection; and Essam Al Falasi, Director of the Information Technology Department at the Ministry of Economy. The Kazakh delegation included Arman Issagaliyev, Consul General of Kazakhstan in the UAE, alongside other high-ranking representatives.

In the context of accelerating global technological advancement, both parties recognized the increasingly critical role of information and communications technology (ICT) as a driver of innovation, knowledge-based economic growth, and sustainable development. Consequently, they emphasized the multitude of opportunities for collaborative engagement and mutual learning within the vital ICT sector. This strategic alignment is anticipated to elevate bilateral relations to a more substantive level.

H.E. Al Mansoori attributed the strength of UAE-Kazakhstan relations to a mutual commitment to deepening economic and trade linkages, as well as a shared intent to leverage their respective strategic geographic positions, inherent strengths, and developmental potentials. He provided empirical data to underscore the existing economic engagement, noting that bilateral trade volume exceeded USD 270 million in 2015 and surpassed USD 180 million within the first three quarters of 2016. The Minister projected further growth in these figures, contingent upon continued joint efforts across several foundational sectors. He specifically identified ICT and smart cities as domains offering considerable potential for cooperation, particularly in the transfer of knowledge and expertise, the augmentation of investments, and the formation of joint ventures.

For his part, H.E. Abayev expressed Kazakhstan’s keen interest in fortifying its ties with the UAE and in studying the Emirates’ trajectory toward becoming a preeminent global hub for investment and commerce. He further noted that Kazakhstan is actively reinforcing its business environment and legislative framework pertaining to ICT, in alignment with its national growth objectives. Minister Abayev concluded by reiterating his nation’s desire to pursue a substantive exchange of ICT expertise and experiences with the United Arab Emirates.

BROWNING — A torso found in the Illinois River in November soon will be buried, although authorities say they are still unable to identify the victim.
Schuyler County Sheriff Bill Redshaw said the torso is being stored in Adams County and will be buried soon, although time and location have not been determined.
The investigation was turned over to Illinois State Police in December, but there have been no leads as to the identity.
“It was a tough one,” Redshaw said. “We’d like to get closure and I’m sure there’s someone out there who wants closure. We haven’t given up on it.”
Redshaw said attempts to match DNA to records on file turned up nothing. He said some people who have had a family member missing have called, but nothing panned out.
There have been several homeless people who have not been located for some time but that avenue did not provide any clues. One, in particular, involved a missing homeless man who had often camped along the Illinois River. He was thought to be a possible match but ultimately was not.
Illinois State Police authorities continue to investigate but had no new information Tuesday.
Coroner Terry Millslagle said in December that it appeared the limbs had been removed from the body and that he did not believe the death to be accidental. An autopsy revealed little except that the amputated sections were smooth.
The cause of death has yet to be determined.
The body had been in the river for at least seven to 10 days before it was noticed, according to a report by the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. The body was found in Sugar Creek but it is unknown where the body entered the river.

According to Schuyler County Sheriff Bill Redshaw, the remains are currently held in Adams County, with the precise timing and location of burial yet to be finalized. Jurisdiction over the case was transferred to the Illinois State Police in December; however, the investigation has yielded no substantive leads regarding the victim’s identity.

Sheriff Redshaw characterized the case as particularly challenging, noting the shared desire for resolution both by law enforcement and presumed family members. He emphasized that investigative efforts persist. Attempts to identify the deceased through DNA comparison with existing databases have proven unsuccessful. While several individuals have contacted authorities regarding missing relatives, none of these inquiries have produced a match. Investigative avenues included examining records of missing persons, including several long-term unlocated homeless individuals. One specific line of inquiry focused on a missing homeless man known to frequent areas along the Illinois River, but this potential lead was ultimately excluded.

As of Tuesday, Illinois State Police officials reported no new developments in the ongoing investigation. In a December statement, Coroner Terry Millslagle indicated that the limbs appeared to have been deliberately removed from the torso, suggesting the death was not accidental. Autopsy findings were limited, noting only that the amputations were smoothly executed. The official cause of death remains undetermined.

A report from the Illinois Department of Natural Resources estimated the remains had been submerged in the river for a period of seven to ten days prior to discovery. Although the torso was found in Sugar Creek, the precise point of entry into the river system is unknown.

"Illicit alcohol" was found and seized from 31 different resorts, restaurants and nightclubs in Mexico, ABC News reports.
More than 10,000 gallons of alcohol was found from an unnamed company with "bad manufacturing practices." Some of the alcohol was found at a resort where a 20-year-old Wisconsin woman drowned in January after drinking in the hotel lobby.
Abbey Conner, 20, was pulled from a pool at an Iberostar resort near Playa del Carmen, according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. After Conner's death, the paper received numerous reports from others who said they got sick and experienced blackouts at resorts in Cancun and Playa del Carmen.
Rick and Diana Neuenschwander of Symmes Township, Ohio said they found tainted alcohol in their margaritas from the Secrets Akumal Riviera Maya resort for a getaway over Independence Day. The resort is close to the resort where Conner drowned.
“It was just a little odd. They were different colors,” Rick said. “We ... just blacked out ... We just don't remember what happened.”
Allegations of tainted or substandard alcohol that resulted in illness or blacking out became serious enough that the State Department updated its Mexico page in July, warning travelers to take extra caution when consuming alcohol.
“We're standing in the pool, got our little floatie out, and we had some drinks. We were drinking some margaritas,” Rick said. “They were blowing bubbles in the pool. You got people dancing. It was Fourth of July in Mexico ... It was a lot of fun.”
Hours after having the "odd"-looking margaritas, Rick said he and Diana regained consciousness in their hotel room. He said they had no memory of what happened.
“We weren't drunk. We were out — completely different. If we stumbled, we have no idea that we stumbled. We don't know what happened,” Rick said, adding that he woke up with scratches on his face and that his wife had bruised shoulders. “My wife felt like she was maybe held down.”
Read more about the Neuenschwander's story in this I-Team report.
Problems found by Mexican authorities included expired alcohol, water leakage, lack of documentation and a lack of disinfectant, the Journal Sentinel reported.
There's no word from officials on criminal charges, any connection to Conner's death, or any efforts to crack-down on alcohol violations, the Journal Sentinel reported.

As reported by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, Conner was recovered from a pool at an Iberostar resort near Playa del Carmen. Her death prompted the newspaper to investigate, leading to numerous accounts from individuals who reported becoming ill or experiencing memory loss after consuming alcohol at resorts in the Cancun and Playa del Carmen regions.

One such account comes from Rick and Diana Neuenschwander of Symmes Township, Ohio, who allege they were served adulterated alcohol in their margaritas during a July Fourth holiday at the Secrets Akumal Riviera Maya resort, located proximate to where Conner died. Health officials are warning the public to watch for measles’ symptoms after an infected person flew into Vancouver on June 23.
According to the B.C. Centre for Disease Control, the infected person flew from New Delhi to Guangzhou on China Southern flight CZ 3028 and then from Guangzhou to Vancouver on China Southern flight CZ 377 on June 23.
The CDC believes that travellers on those flights, as well as anyone who might have gone through Vancouver International Airport that day.
The centre said that travellers on the affected flights could infect others even outside of YVR.
Measles is a high infectious disease that is spread by coughing and sneezing.
READ MORE: Langley school district plans to keep a list of unvaccinated children
Although the CDC believes that most travellers are immune to measles, all travellers on those flights are asked to check if they have been vaccinated.
Infants less than a year old are, and others who haven’t been vaccinated, are considered especially at risk.
Most people born after 1970 have likely received the measles, or MMR (a combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine) and are protected. Many of those born before 1970 are likely to be immune due to prior measles infections.
Symptoms, which can take between one to three weeks to develop, include:
Fever
Cough
Runny nose
Red eyes
Rash that starts centrally including on the face, spreads to the limbs and lasts at least three days

rewrite:
Public health authorities have issued an advisory regarding potential measles exposure following the arrival of an infected individual at Vancouver International Airport (YVR) on June 23. The British Columbia Centre for Disease Control (BCCDC) reports that the individual traveled from New Delhi to Guangzhou on China Southern Airlines flight CZ 3028, subsequently connecting to Vancouver aboard China Southern Airlines flight CZ 377 on the same date. The BCCDC indicates that passengers on these specific flights, as well as individuals present in areas of YVR traversed by the infected person, may have been exposed. There exists a further risk of secondary transmission from exposed passengers beyond the airport environment.

Measles is a highly contagious viral illness transmitted via respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing. While the BCCDC notes that a majority of travelers are likely immune, all passengers on the identified flights are advised to verify their vaccination status. Particular risk is posed to infants under one year of age and other unvaccinated individuals. Most persons born after 1970 have likely received the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine, conferring protection. Many individuals born prior to 1970 are presumed immune due to previous infection.

The incubation period ranges from 7 to 21 days. Initial symptoms typically include fever, cough, coryza (runny nose), and conjunctivitis (red eyes). This is followed by a characteristic maculopapular rash, which often begins on the face and spreads centrifugally to the trunk and limbs, persisting for a minimum of three days.

Ashley Young insists his hunger for the game remains strong despite admitting uncertainty over his Manchester United future.
The former England international has started only 13 games for United this season and was linked with a move to the Chinese Super League in January and February.
But with eight of those starts coming in United's last 13 games, Young is back in the fray and wants to concentrate on events on the pitch.
The 31-year-old said: "There was of course, and there is always, speculation and especially when there is a transfer window and you are not playing.
"But I have always said that I want to play as much as possible. What the future holds I am not too sure. I am just concentrating on each game and when the manager calls on me I will give 100 per cent and look to play as well as I can.
"I am looking to play as many games as I can between now and the end of the season. That is what I am concentrating on now. That is the main focus for me and then we will see what happens.
"I have fire and hunger in my belly. I want to succeed. I work hard. When you have such competition in a fantastic squad it pushes you on every day.
"If you watched training there are no challenges that are not like in a game. Everybody wants to pull on the shirt and I am no different."
Young insisted he "was concentrating on Manchester United" when the rumours of a move to China surfaced and has not yet looked beyond the end of his current deal at Old Trafford.
Young, who joined United from Aston Villa in 2011, said: "I have another year left on my contract and an option after that so if there is anything there to be discussed you would have to ask the manager."

SUNRISE, Fla. - The pain of the parents of the Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School students killed in the Valentine's Day massacre was familiar to Sybrina Fulton. Her unarmed 17-year-old son Trayvon Martin was killed in Sanford, Fla., six years ago.
The former Miami Jackson Senior High School teacher and program coordinator for the Miami-Dade Housing Authority now works for the Trayvon Martin Foundation. Like the parents in Parkland, the grieving mother said she decided to do everything in her power to prevent another tragedy.
"We want to move forward and we want to keep on putting the pressure on to make sure that we get these laws changed," Fulton said Monday during a news conference in Sunrise.
Fulton was standing next to Fred Guttenberg, a real estate broker who lost his 14-year-old daughter Jaime in the Valentine's Day massacre that left 17 dead at the school in Parkland. The tragedy prompted a wave of activist now known as the "Never Again" movement.
"I am desperate to go wherever I can to have this conversation to bring about rational, sane, common-sense gun safety measures," Guttenberg said.
Fulton worked as a program coordinator for the Miami-Dade Housing Authority and as a Miami Jackson Senior High School teacher. Nothing prepared her for the life of activism that has involved regular meetings with politicians and co-authoring a book.
Although Zimmerman used a Kel-Tec PF-9 9mm pistol, and the circumstances of her son's death were different, Fulton supports Guttenberg's mission. The parents met with Rep. Debbie Wasserman Shultz, who said there is a need for legislation, to prevent young people from dying in shootings.
Wasserman Schultz said their goal is to push for legislation to ban assault rifles and high-capacity magazines, and to get rid of the "loopholes" of the federal background check system.
The Never Again movement is planning events in Washington, D.C., and around the nation March 24.

Fulton, formerly a teacher at Miami Jackson Senior High School and a program coordinator for the Miami-Dade Housing Authority, is now an employee of the Trayvon Martin Foundation. Mirroring the resolve of the Parkland parents, Fulton, as a grieving mother, has committed to utilizing all available resources to avert future tragedies.

During a Monday news conference in Sunrise, Florida, Fulton stated, “We want to move forward and we want to keep on putting the pressure on to make sure that we get these laws changed.” She appeared alongside Fred Guttenberg, a real estate broker whose fourteen-year-old daughter, Jaime, was among the seventeen individuals killed in the Parkland school shooting. Although the circumstances of Trayvon Martin’s death—involving a Kel-Tec PF-9 9mm pistol wielded by George Zimmerman—differ from the Parkland shooting, Fulton endorses Guttenberg’s mission. The parents jointly met with Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz, who affirmed the necessity of legislative action to prevent further shooting deaths among youth.

Wasserman Schultz outlined their objective to advocate for legislation prohibiting assault rifles and high-capacity magazines, while also addressing perceived deficiencies, or “loopholes,” in the federal background check system. In support of these aims, the Never Again movement has scheduled coordinated events in Washington, D.C., and across the United States for March 24.

LONDON (Reuters) - British aerospace and defense electronics group Cobham said on Friday it has agreed to sell its AvComm and Wireless test businesses to Viavi Solutions for $455 million, as part of the latest stage of a turnaround plan.
Cobham, which had said in August that it may divest the units, plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt, further strengthening its balance sheet after a string of profit warnings forced it into a rights issue last year.
The company said it would be able to pay down about 440 million pounds ($627 million) of debt by combining the proceeds from the deal with existing cash.
The Wireless unit, which does 5G mobile network testing, and communications equipment maker AvComm, together account for around 10 percent of Cobham’s revenue. The group acquired AvComm through its ill-fated Aeroflex acquisition in 2014, which increased its debt burden.
Chief Executive David Lockwood, who took over in 2016 to lead a turnaround, had said there was little overlap between the Wireless and AvComm units and the rest of the business and the sale followed a competitive process.
“We can now focus on delivering value-add technology and capabilities to our defense, aerospace and space customers, supported by a more resilient balance sheet,” he said.
AvComm is based in the U.S., while the Wireless unit, is based in Britain, said Cobham, adding that the deal is expected to complete in the first half of this year.
Shares in Cobham closed at 124.8 pence on Thursday, valuing the company at 3 billion pounds.

This transaction constitutes a key element of the group’s ongoing strategic turnaround plan. Cobham, which had initially indicated a potential divestment of these units in August, intends to allocate the proceeds toward debt reduction, thereby further consolidating its balance sheet. This follows a series of profit warnings that necessitated a rights issue last year.

The combined proceeds from the sale, alongside existing cash reserves, are projected to facilitate debt repayment of approximately £440 million ($627 million). The Wireless unit, which specialises in 5G mobile network testing, and the communications equipment manufacturer AvComm collectively contribute roughly 10% of Cobham’s total revenue. Notably, AvComm was integrated into the group via the 2014 acquisition of Aeroflex, a transaction that subsequently increased Cobham’s debt burden.

Chief Executive David Lockwood, appointed in 2016 to lead the corporate recovery, stated that the divestment followed a competitive process and reflected the limited operational synergy between these units and Cobham’s core defence, aerospace, and space activities. Lockwood emphasised that the move will enable the company to intensify its focus on delivering value-added technologies for its core customer base, supported by a more resilient financial structure. Cobham confirmed that AvComm is U.S.-based, while the Wireless unit is headquartered in Britain, with the transaction anticipated to close in the first half of this year. Cobham’s shares closed at 124.8 pence on Thursday, resulting in a market capitalisation of approximately £3 billion.

input: You probably read our first-drive review of the Chevy Corvette ZR1. (But ICYMI, check it out .) But there was a pretty astonishing video at the bottom of the post that you might have overlooked.In our review, one thing's for sure, we did not drive the ZR1 at 212 mph. But Chevy did, in two flying-mile test runs at the Papenburg test track in Germany, an outing that set a track record. The video is above, and like last week's video of the Porsche GT3 RS sub-7-minute lap of the Nürburgring , it's well worth your time. (And it won't take much of your time, as the Corvette video is a mere, action-packed 3:14.)The ZR1 hit 214.88 mph in its first, downwind run — the car's limiter is set to 215. It hit 210.20 mph in the second run into the wind, and the two are averaged at 212. At those speeds, the ZR1 is not only this year's Indy 500 pace car , it could practically compete.The best part of the video, apart from the sound, is the grit-in-your-teeth camera angle that's seemingly at road level, which makes the action seem that much faster.
rewrite:

The footage, comparable in significance to recent documentation of a Porsche GT3 RS completing a sub-seven-minute Nürburgring lap, is concise yet compelling, with a duration of three minutes and fourteen seconds.

During the initial downwind run, the ZR1 reached 214.88 mph, approaching its electronically limited top speed of 215 mph. A subsequent upwind run yielded 210.20 mph, resulting in an averaged speed of 212 mph. This performance caliber not only justifies the model's role as the Indianapolis 500 pace car but also suggests potential competition viability. Beyond the auditory experience, the most impactful element of the video is a low, road-level camera perspective that intensifies the perception of velocity.

Luke Shaw’s Manchester United career is over and he is a transfer target for Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, according to the Daily Star.
The England international, aged 22, was substituted at half-time in the FA Cup quarter-final win over Brighton & Hove Albion, then given a public dressing down by Jose Mourinho.
United boss Mourinho claimed Shaw had let him down by failing to follow simple tactical instructions in the first 45 minutes of the 2-0 victory.
That was reportedly the final straw for the Portuguese coach, who has had a series of run-ins with Shaw over the past two seasons.
Mourinho is said to believe he will never be able to fully trust the former Southampton player and is ready to offload him.
Tottenham and Chelsea are both reported to be keen on Shaw. With Mourinho having earmarked Spurs left-back Danny Rose as his preferred replacement for Shaw, the north Londoners might have the edge.
Leicester City and Shaw’s former club Southampton are also tracking him.

Mayor Michelle De La Isla announced the “Mayor’s Task Force against Domestic Violence” for Topeka and Shawnee County Monday morning.
“The Mayor’s Task Force against Domestic Violence is a project that is very close to my heart. The YWCA helped me get out of an abusive relationship and I believe that this task force will help many other women get out of harmful situations,” Mayor De La Isla said. “I believe that stopping domestic violence and abuse is key to improving people’s lives and improving the City of Topeka. Together with our partners we can all help to end domestic violence in this community.”
The task force is made up of representatives across the criminal justice system as well as community service agencies including Topeka Police Department, Shawnee County Sheriff’s Office, the YWCA Center for Safety and Empowerment, Shawnee County District Attorney’s Office, Shawnee County Court Services, local Batterer’s Intervention Programs, Washburn University, Department of Children and Families, Valeo Behavioral Health, and
Stormont Vail Hospital.
These agencies join together with the purpose of increasing victim safety, offender accountability, and community awareness. These agencies are committed to eradicating the problem of domestic violence and are willing to hold themselves and each other accountable.
Kathleen Marker “We know our communities are safer when we work together,” said the YWCA’s Kathleen Marker.
“The YWCA Northeast Kansas is proud to be a part of this large collaborative effort to ensure women, children and families are guaranteed access to justice and services that keep them safe.”

NEW YORK (AP) — The New York Jets have signed former Lions linebacker Brandon Copeland and re-signed defensive lineman Xavier Cooper.
Copeland missed last season after tearing a pectoral muscle during the preseason. He had 30 tackles and one forced fumble in 32 games the previous two seasons with the Lions. The 26-year-old Copeland will be a backup on defense and be a key part of the Jets' special teams unit.
He signed with Baltimore as an undrafted free agent out of Penn in 2013 and spent time later that season on Tennessee's practice squad. After signing with Orlando of the Arena Football League in 2015, Copeland impressed Detroit after participating in the NFL Veterans Combine.
Cooper was not tendered as a restricted free agent, but was brought back after he had 16 tackles and one sack in eight games. His play increased when Muhammad Wilkerson was benched at the end of the season.

He is anticipated to serve in a defensive reserve capacity and contribute significantly to special teams. His performance at the 2015 NFL Veterans Combine, after a stint in the Arena Football League, led to his signing with Detroit. Cooper, who was not tendered as a restricted free agent, returns after registering 16 tackles and one sack in eight games, with his role expanding following the benching of Muhammad Wilkerson late in the season.

West Brom midfielder Chris Brunt admits he’s surprised Michael O’Neill wasn’t targeted by top Premier League clubs after the success he’s enjoyed with Norther Ireland.
Brunt plans to speak with O’Neill in the coming weeks about his own international future but said it was a pleasant surprise to see the Ballymena man commit to a new contract.
“I have really enjoyed every minute of it and Michael has done a fantastic job,” Brunt explained, “It’s a really big feat for the IFA to keep him on.
“To be honest I’m very surprised he wasn’t linked with a lot of bigger jobs purely based on the success he had with us because when he took over we were 125th or so in the world and he took us up to 20th. That’s down to the way he does things.
“He knows what to do to get the best out of the lads that are there in order to try and win a game. He leaves no stone unturned concerning the opposition.
“My future is obviously something I will have to think about over the next few weeks. Before the next international break I’ll definitely speak to him about it. I’m not making any decisions just yet.”
Brunt also described last year’s heartbreaking World Cup play-off defeat to Switzerland as more difficult to take than missing Euro 2018 through injury.
“I knew straight away I was going to miss the Euros so it was a little easier to take in that sense.
“Missing out on the World Cup hit me harder than I was expecting. Playing international football has, a lot of times, been quite difficult but the last couple of years, leading up to the Euros and the World Cup qualifying campaign, have been really great,” he added.

Brunt elaborated on his surprise, remarking, "In all honesty, I am very surprised he was not linked with more prominent positions, based solely on the success he has achieved with us. When he assumed the role, the team was ranked approximately 125th in the world; he has since elevated us to 20th. This progress is attributable to his meticulous methodology." DALLAS — A Texas jury has found a neurosurgeon guilty Tuesday of maiming patients who had turned to him for surgery to resolve debilitating injuries.
The verdict of the Dallas County jury on a first-degree felony charge of injury to an elderly person means 44-year-old Christopher Duntsch of Plano could be sentenced to five to 99 years or life in prison. He also could be given probation. The penalty phase of his trial began Tuesday afternoon.
The Dallas Morning News reports the jury deliberated about four hours before deciding on its verdict. The indictment accused Duntsch of wide-ranging malpractice that included improper placement of screws and plates along patients’ spines, a sponge left in another patient and a major vein cut in another. Records also showed that he operated on the wrong part of a patient’s spine, damaged nerves and left one woman with chronic pain and dependent on a wheelchair.
Prosecutors had accused Duntsch of maiming four patients and causing the death of at least two between July 2012 and June 2013. They say Duntsch’s hands and surgical tools amounted to “deadly weapons” contended that Duntsch “intentionally, knowingly and recklessly” harmed up to 15 of his patients.
Prosecutors said Duntsch said in a 2011 email to his girlfriend that he would “become a cold-blooded killer.”
But Duntsch’s attorneys argued that Duntsch was not a criminal but just a lousy surgeon committing malpractice in chaotic operating rooms in hospitals in Dallas and its northern suburbs. They also said the tone of the email to his girlfriend was unclear could have been meant as sarcasm.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, a jury in Dallas, Texas, rendered a guilty verdict against neurosurgeon Christopher Duntsch for the felony offense of maiming patients who had sought surgical treatment from him for debilitating conditions. The conviction on the first-degree felony charge of injury to an elderly individual carries a potential sentence for the 44-year-old Plano resident ranging from five to ninety-nine years, up to life imprisonment, with probation remaining a possibility. The penalty phase of the trial commenced Tuesday afternoon following the jury's decision, which was reached after approximately four hours of deliberation, as reported by The Dallas Morning News.

The indictment detailed extensive alleged malpractice, including the improper placement of spinal hardware, leaving a surgical sponge within a patient, severing a major vein, operating on an incorrect spinal segment, causing nerve damage, and rendering one patient permanently wheelchair-bound with chronic pain. Prosecutors asserted that between July 2012 and June 2013, Duntsch's actions maimed four patients and resulted in the death of at least two others. They contended his surgical conduct was so egregious that his hands and instruments constituted "deadly weapons," and that he "intentionally, knowingly and recklessly" harmed as many as fifteen patients. Prosecutors further referenced a 2011 email in which Duntsch purportedly told his girlfriend he would "become a cold-blooded killer."

The defense argued that Duntsch was not a criminal but an incompetent surgeon whose malpractice occurred in chaotic operating room environments in Dallas-area hospitals. They also suggested the cited email may have been intended sarcastically and that its tone was ambiguous.

SOCHI, Russia President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday that Russia's relationship with Turkey had fully recovered after what he called a crisis caused by Ankara's shooting down of a Russian warplane near the Syrian border in 2015.
Russia retaliated against Turkey at the time with a slew of economic sanctions and Ankara later took measures which made life difficult for Moscow too.
Speaking after holding talks with Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan in the Black Sea Russian resort of Sochi, Putin said relations were finally getting back to normal and that trade had stopped falling.
"Some time ago our bilateral ties, as it well known, were tested. Now we can say with certainty remark that the recovery process in Russo-Turkish ties is complete," Putin told a news conference. "We are getting back to a normal cooperative partnership."
Putin said Russia would launch a joint investment fund with Turkey with funds of up to $1 billion and said Moscow stood ready to help Turkey improve security measures at its tourist resorts.
(Reporting by Denis Pinchuk in Sochi and Andrey Ostroukh and Vladimir Soldatkin in Moscow; Editing by Andrew Osborn)
rewrite:
During a joint press conference in Sochi on Wednesday, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the full restoration of bilateral relations with Turkey, following a period of tension precipitated by the 2015 downing of a Russian military aircraft near the Syrian border by Turkish forces. This incident had prompted a series of Russian economic sanctions and reciprocal measures from Ankara, which significantly strained diplomatic and economic ties. Speaking after discussions with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Black Sea resort, Putin stated that relations have now normalized and that the decline in mutual trade has been arrested.

Putin explicitly noted, "Our bilateral ties were, as is widely recognized, subjected to a serious test. We can now definitively state that the recovery process in Russian-Turkish relations is complete, and we are returning to a normative partnership based on cooperation." As a tangible step forward, he disclosed plans to establish a joint investment fund with a capitalization of up to one billion dollars. Furthermore, Putin expressed Russia's readiness to assist Turkey in enhancing security protocols at its tourist destinations.

BEIJING May 3 China's state-owned refiner China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) said it has loaded the first crude oil through its Myanmar-to-China pipeline, the latest step towards supplying crude to its new refinery in Yunnan province.
Some 1,150 cubic meters per hour of crude flowed into the 770-kilometre (480 mile) pipeline from Tuesday, CNPC said in a statement on Tuesday.
The move comes almost a month after the first tanker carrying 140,000 tonnes of crude started discharging into the pipeline following the official launch.
CNPC's PetroChina plans to import overseas oil and pump it through the pipeline to supply its new 260,000-barrels-per-day Anning refinery in landlocked Yunnan province.
The pipeline starts at Kyauk Phyu in Myanmar's west and enters China at the border city Ruili and is a joint investment by CNPC and the Myanmar Oil and Gas Enterprise. (Reporting by Josephine Mason; Editing by Christian Schmollinger)
rewrite: On May 3, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) announced the commencement of crude oil loading into the Myanmar-China pipeline, marking a significant advancement in supplying its newly operational refinery in Yunnan province. According to a CNPC statement issued Tuesday, the flow rate into the 770-kilometer pipeline initiated at approximately 1,150 cubic meters per hour. This development follows the official pipeline launch nearly one month prior, when an initial tanker discharged 140,000 tonnes of crude. The pipeline, a joint venture between CNPC and Myanmar Oil and Gas Enterprise, originates at Kyauk Phyu on Myanmar’s western coast and crosses into China at Ruili. It is designed to transport imported crude to PetroChina’s Anning refinery in Yunnan, which has a capacity of 260,000 barrels per day.

The ongoing sage of Stormy Daniels‘ alleged affair with Donald Trump continues, with new details emerging on a near-constant basis. Trump’s personal lawyer and fixer Michael Cohen has been a major player in the story of the consensual affair and the subsequent fallout. Cohen sat down with Vanity Fair and laid out his side of the events, addressing claims from Daniels (real name Stephanie Clifford) and her lawyer Michael Avenatti.
Cohen claims that his attempts to silence Daniels have nothing to do with Trump’s presidential campaign: “If she would have come to me a month before, or three months before, I would have done the same thing. People are mistaking this for a thing about the campaign. What I did defensively for my personal client, and my friend, is what attorneys do for their high-profile clients. I would have done it in 2006. I would have done it in 2011. I truly care about him and the family—more than just as an employee and an attorney.” It also seemed that Cohen was surprised with Trump’s win, saying that it seemed “that you can’t beat the Clinton machine.”
He also addressed Avenatti’s claims that someone close to Trump threatened Daniels, saying “unlike Mr. Avenatti, we are not handling this matter through the court of public opinion. We are handling it through a court of competent jurisdiction.” He also reiterated that he personally was not behind that claim.
“In fact, I have never spoken to her. I have never e-mailed her. I have never met her. I have never texted her. Every interaction with Ms. Clifford was always through her previous attorney. I can only speak for myself,” he said. “I reiterate: I have never threatened her in any way and I am unaware of anyone else doing so.”
When asked about why he used his personal home equity line to pay Daniels’ settlement, Cohen explains that “he did it for his own reasons and it’s irrelevant if people believe him or not.” However, he does take offense at CNN implying that he is a “less sexy version” of Ray Donovan.
(Via Vanity Fair)

SMALL hatchbacks, crossovers and pickup-based SUVs may dominate the Philippine auto market, but a few car makers still include in their lineup an executive sedan model.
Chevrolet Philippines is one of such companies. It introduced the 2018 Chevrolet Malibu earlier this month, bringing back the latest version of a nameplate it first released locally in 2014. The new Malibu, according to the company, is lighter, leaner and longer than the model it replaced — itself a dynamic performer. So no “Yank Tank” this new car is.
“The all-new 2018 Chevrolet Malibu delivers more efficiency, connectivity and advanced safety features than ever, along with more rear legroom and interior space,” Chevrolet said in a statement. It added the model was named the 2017 Best Midsize Car in the U.S. News and World Report’s annual Best Cars for Families survey.
Among the car’s features are an inductive mobile charger that allows for wireless connection to mobile devices, a nine-speaker Bose audio system, and Chevrolet’s Mylink, which integrates phone functions and provides access to some apps via an eight-inch touch screen panel. The system also offers voice-command functions.
Semi-automatic parallel and perpendicular parking, adaptive cruise control, and ventilated front seats are some of the car’s premium items.
Meanwhile, included in the new Malibu’s list of safety-related technologies are lane-keep assist, lane departure warning, front collision alert, front pedestrian detection, forward automatic braking, side blind zone alert and rear cross traffic alert. The car also packs eight air bags around the cabin.
In 2018 new-generation form the Malibu (in the Philippines, at least) is powered by a smaller — but gutsier — engine than that found in the previous model. Where the old car was propelled by a 165-hp, 225-Nm, 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine, the new one relies on a 2.0-liter four-pot mill that, through turbo-charging, makes 250hp and 353Nm. Paired to this engine is a six-speed automatic transmission.
Now sold solely in LTZ trim level, the Malibu is priced at P2,131,888. — BMA
rewrite:
While small hatchbacks, crossovers, and pickup-based sport utility vehicles constitute the dominant market segments within the Philippine automotive industry, several manufacturers continue to offer models in the executive sedan category. Among these is Chevrolet Philippines, which recently reintroduced the Chevrolet Malibu nameplate to the local market in its 2018 iteration. This launch marks the return of a model first introduced domestically in 2014. According to the manufacturer, the latest generation Malibu exhibits a reduction in weight, a more streamlined profile, and an increase in length compared to its predecessor, which was itself recognized for dynamic performance, thereby distancing the new vehicle from historical perceptions of cumbersome American automobiles.

In an official statement, Chevrolet asserted that the 2018 Malibu provides enhanced efficiency, connectivity, and advanced safety features, accompanied by increased rear-seat legroom and interior volume. The company further noted that the model was designated the 2017 Best Midsize Car in the U.S. News & World Report’s annual Best Cars for Families ranking.

Notable amenities include an inductive wireless charging pad for mobile devices, a premium nine-speaker Bose audio system, and the Chevrolet MyLink infotainment system. This system integrates smartphone functionality and provides application access via an eight-inch color touchscreen, supplemented by voice-command capabilities. Additional premium features comprise semi-automatic parallel and perpendicular parking assistance, adaptive cruise control, and ventilated front seats.

The vehicle’s comprehensive suite of safety technologies encompasses lane-keep assist, lane departure warning, forward collision alert with pedestrian detection, automatic emergency braking, side blind zone alert, and rear cross-traffic alert. Passenger protection is further augmented by eight airbags strategically positioned throughout the cabin.

In its Philippine specification, the 2018 Malibu is equipped with a smaller displacement, turbocharged engine that generates superior output relative to the prior model. It replaces a naturally aspirated 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine producing 165 horsepower and 225 Newton-meters of torque with a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder unit delivering 250 horsepower and 353 Newton-meters. Power is transmitted to the front wheels via a six-speed automatic transmission. Currently offered exclusively in the high-grade LTZ trim, the vehicle carries a manufacturer’s suggested retail price of ₱2,131,888.

Canada has taken steps to make its national anthem “O Canada” more inclusive.
Lawmakers passed a bill this week changing the line “true patriot love in all thy sons command,” to “true patriot love in all of us command.”
“It’s a kind of inclusive, embracing turn of phrase,” says former Prime Minister Kim Campbell. She’s one of several famous Canadian women who started a campaign to change the lyrics in 2013.
Some Canadians have pushed back, citing tradition. But “people have been tinkering with the anthem throughout the century,” says Campbell.
In 1908, Robert Stanley Weir first wrote the lyric in "O Canada" as “true patriot love thou dost in us command,” and changed it to “in all thy sons command” in 1913. In the 1970s, Parliament changed two other lines.
The “us” in the national anthem explicitly includes women and immigrants in a way that “sons” didn’t, says Campbell.
“It's a tile in the mosaic of progress. It alone, of itself, is not going to make a difference, but it's a piece of the puzzle.”
From PRI's The World ©2017 PRI
rewrite: The Canadian government has enacted legislation to render the national anthem, "O Canada," more inclusive. This measure alters the lyric from "true patriot love in all thy sons command" to "true patriot love in all of us command." Proponents, including former Prime Minister Kim Campbell, characterize the revision as an inclusive and embracing modification. Campbell, who helped initiate a campaign for this change in 2013, notes that while some citizens oppose the alteration on traditional grounds, the anthem's lyrics have undergone periodic revision throughout the past century. The original 1908 version by Robert Stanley Weir read "thou dost in us command," which was amended to "in all thy sons command" in 1913; further changes were implemented by Parliament in the 1970s. Campbell argues that the term "us" explicitly encompasses women and immigrants in a manner that "sons" did not. She describes the amendment as a single tile within a broader mosaic of social progress, suggesting that while its impact alone may be limited, it constitutes a meaningful component of a larger puzzle.

In order to further simplify accessibility to foreign exchange by the Small and Medium Scale Enterprises (SMEs) the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced a newly designed form to facilitate minimal documentation.
Confirming this new development on Monday, the apex Bank spokesman, Mr Isaac Okorafor said the motive behind the new form is “to provide for the foreign exchange needs of SMEs, including those in retail business and to reduce the rigour of too much documentation.”
According to him, the Bank has decided to ease the difficulty usually experienced by these category of businesses.
Mr okorafor further explained that “henceforth, all SMEs seeking to obtain foreign exchange for eligible transactions shall now fill the newly designed form with basic documentation only for the importation of goods and services.”
With this, the SMEs would be accommodated under the SME Foreign Exchange regime recently introduced by the apex Bank at the prevailing rate to import eligible visible and invisible items, he noted.
This new measure will take immediate effect and importers in this category would no longer be required to fill Form M.
rewrite:
In an effort to enhance access to foreign exchange for Small and Medium Scale Enterprises (SMEs), the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has introduced a newly designed form intended to streamline documentation requirements. Confirming this development, the Bank’s spokesman, Mr. Isaac Okorafor, stated that the initiative aims to address the foreign exchange needs of SMEs, including those in retail, while alleviating the administrative burden associated with extensive paperwork. He indicated that this measure is a direct response to the difficulties historically encountered by this sector.

Mr. Okorafor elaborated that, effective immediately, all SMEs seeking foreign exchange for eligible transactions will be required to complete the new form, which necessitates only basic documentation for the importation of goods and services. Consequently, these enterprises will be integrated into the recently established SME Foreign Exchange regime, allowing them to import eligible visible and invisible items at prevailing rates. This policy supersedes the previous requirement for such importers to complete Form M, with the new procedures taking effect without delay.

NEW YORK — Baltimore linebacker Za’Darius Smith and Washington cornerback Bashaud Breeland have been fined $18,231 by the NFL for hits last weekend.
Smith was called for roughing the passer after hitting Pittsburgh’s Ben Roethlisberger in the Ravens’ loss to the Steelers.
Breeland made a horsecollar tackle of Kansas City running back Kareem Hunt in the third quarter of the Redskins’ loss to the Chiefs last Monday night.
Oakland punter Marquette King was docked $9,115 by the league after he threw a football at a Denver Broncos player following a failed fake punt. He was penalized 15 yards for unsportsmanlike conduct.
Jacksonville linebacker Paul Posluszny was fined $9,115 for taunting Jets linebacker Dylan Donahue after Donahue got hurt during a punt when he hit the Jaguars veteran.
Philadelphia’s Vinny Curry and Indianapolis’ Jonathan Hankins were also fined $9,115 — both for unnecessary roughness.
——
For more NFL coverage: http://www.pro32.ap.org and http://www.twitter.com/AP–NFL
rewrite: The National Football League has levied fines against several players for infractions occurring during recent contests. Baltimore Ravens linebacker Za’Darius Smith was fined $18,231 for roughing the passer following a hit on Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger. Similarly, Washington Redskins cornerback Bashaud Breeland received an identical fine for a horsecollar tackle on Kansas City Chiefs running back Kareem Hunt. Additional fines of $9,115 were issued to Oakland Raiders punter Marquette King for unsportsmanlike conduct, Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Paul Posluszny for taunting an injured opponent, and to Philadelphia Eagles defensive end Vinny Curry and Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle Jonathan Hankins for unnecessary roughness. These disciplinary actions underscore the league's enforcement of player conduct regulations.

FILE PHOTO: An Boeing 777 aircraft lands at the Charles de Gaulle International Airport in Roissy, near Paris, October 27, 2015. REUTERS/Christian Hartmann/File Photo
Boeing Co (BA.N) said on Thursday it delivered 169 jetliners in the first quarter, down from 176 in the same period a year earlier.
The company said deliveries of the single-aisle 737 slipped to 113 in the quarter, from 121 a year earlier, as it readies a newer version of its most popular plane.
Boeing said deliveries of its twin-aisle 777 jetliner fell to 21 from 23, while those of the 787 Dreamliner increased to 32 from 30.
The company has said it expects to deliver between 760 and 765 commercial aircraft in 2017, more than the 748 in 2016.
The world's biggest planemaker said it booked net orders of 198 aircraft in the first quarter.
(Reporting by Ankit Ajmera in Bengaluru; Editing by Savio D'Souza)
rewrite: Boeing Company (BA.N) reported on Thursday that it delivered 169 commercial aircraft during the first quarter, a decrease from the 176 units delivered in the same period of the preceding year. This figure includes a decline in deliveries for the single-aisle 737 model, which fell to 113 from 121 a year earlier, as the company prepares for a newer version of this prominent aircraft. Deliveries of the twin-aisle 777 jetliner also decreased, moving from 23 to 21. In contrast, deliveries of the 787 Dreamliner increased to 32 from 30. The company has maintained its full-year delivery guidance for 2017, projecting between 760 and 765 commercial aircraft, which would exceed the 748 delivered in 2016. Additionally, Boeing recorded net new orders for 198 aircraft in the first quarter.
