American Lexi Thompson built on her success at the ANA Inspiration with a third-round five-under-par 67 on Saturday to grab a two-shot lead heading into the final round. Thompson completed the final 10 holes of her delayed second round early in the day, carding a 67, and then returned to make six birdies and one bogey in her third round to reach 13-under.
Norwegian Suzann Pettersen shot a third-round 68 and was two back at 11-under.
At 10-under 206 were South Koreans Hur Mi-jung, Park In-bee and Ryu So-yeon and Minjee Lee of Australia.
Tied at eight-under 208 were Cristie Kerr, Michelle Wie, Ariya Jutanugarn of Thailand and Karine Icher of France.
The 22-year-old Thompson has twice held the 54-hole lead in this event, going on to win in 2014, and is looking for her second Major victory.
"Yeah, well, that experience always helps me out, but I'm just going to focus on tomorrow, focus on one shot at a time, relax out there between shots and just focus on doing my routine," Thompson told reporters. Pettersen is a 15-time winner on the LPGA Tour but has never won a major. She has finished as the runner-up three times at the event at the Mission Hills Country Club course.
"I'm driving the ball well and that's a major key on this golf course," Pettersen said. "And if you do, you can kind of attack it as well. So far, so good. I've got a big job to do tomorrow.
"I mean, the leaderboard is packed behind me as well. You've got to expect to go out there and shoot low. There's a lot at stake, but I'm all in for it."
(Writing by Jahmal Corner in Los Angeles; editing by Sudipto Ganguly)

Subsequently, in her third round, she registered six birdies against a single bogey, advancing her total score to thirteen-under-par.

Norwegian competitor Suzann Pettersen remains in close contention, two strokes behind at eleven-under following a third-round 68. A group of four players, comprising South Koreans Hur Mi-jung, Park In-bee, and Ryu So-yeon, alongside Australia’s Minjee Lee, are tied at ten-under 206. An additional cohort, including Americans Cristie Kerr and Michelle Wie, Thailand’s Ariya Jutanugarn, and France’s Karine Icher, are positioned at eight-under 208.

Thompson, aged 22, has previously held the 54-hole lead in this event on two occasions, notably converting one into a victory in 2014, and now seeks her second major championship title. Reflecting on her position, Thompson indicated to reporters that prior experience is beneficial but emphasized her strategy of focusing on each shot individually and maintaining her pre-shot routine. She identified effective driving as a critical component for success on the Mission Hills Country Club course, enabling a more aggressive approach. Acknowledging the densely packed leaderboard, Pettersen conceded that a low final-round score will be necessary, stating she is prepared for the challenge.

The gruesome killing of an elderly women, who was murdered by a 34-year-old local, has shocked villagers. He was discovered sucking blood from her cut throat with a pot of blood nearby, but fled the scene.
In a Zimbabwean village, the police have arrested a man suspected of killing an elderly woman and sucking her blood. As Chronicale, a local outlet, reported, the 34-year-old local, Cristopher Sibanda, attacked the victim on her way from a local hospital in broad daylight, hitting her several times with a log and cutting her throat.
Passers-by reportedly discovered him by the road near the hospital, allegedly sucking the victim’s blood. They tried to detain the man, but he fled the scene. A pot with some blood, presumably from the victim’s wound, was found nearby.

After the gruesome discovery, the villagers launched a manhunt, eventually catching the perpetrator and bringing him to the local police. The policemen confirmed that he was detained and in custody.
A representative of the local community, Edward Marijeni, shocked by the killing, said that they had known Sibanda “sometimes seemed to lose his mind,” but he had never been violent. He also hadn’t undergone treatment for any mental health condition, according to the locals.

According to a report by the local outlet *Chronicle*, the suspect, identified as Cristopher Sibanda, allegedly attacked the victim in broad daylight as she returned from a hospital. The assault involved repeatedly striking her with a log before cutting her throat.

Passers-by reportedly discovered Sibanda by the roadside near the medical facility, where he was allegedly sucking blood from the victim’s wound. Although these witnesses attempted to detain him, he fled the scene. Authorities later recovered a pot containing blood, presumed to be from the victim, nearby. Subsequently, community members organized a search, which led to the suspect’s apprehension and his subsequent handover to police custody, where he remains detained.

In the aftermath, a community representative, Edward Marijeni, expressed profound distress over the incident. He noted that while Sibanda was known to occasionally exhibit signs of psychological disturbance, he had no prior history of violent behavior. Furthermore, local sources indicate the suspect had not received any formal diagnosis or treatment for a mental health condition prior to the attack.

SYDNEY, Australia — Raelene Castle will take over as chief executive officer at Rugby Australia next month, becoming the first woman to lead one of the major national unions in world rugby.
Castle, who has been CEO at Netball New Zealand and at the Canterbury Bulldogs in Australia's National Rugby League, will replace Bill Pulver on Jan. 15.
Rugby Australia Chairman Cameron Clyne announced the appointment Tuesday, saying Castle was the standout applicant among more than 200 candidates.
"I am especially looking forward to getting out into the rugby communities across Australia and meeting the diverse range of people that make the game tick," Castle said in a statement. "Having followed rugby closely for over 30 years and having worked in the New Zealand and Australian sporting environments for the past 10, there is no doubt Australian rugby has a clear international and domestic offering for both male and female athletes that can be further developed and strengthened."
Castle's other governance roles in sport have included serving as a board director of the International Federations of Netball Associations and as chair of the NRL club CEOs leadership group.
Clyne said Castle would bring "a fresh set of eyes to the challenges and opportunities at Rugby Australia, bringing to us her learnings from other codes."
"Through her most recent roles as CEO of the Bulldogs and Netball New Zealand, Raelene has led sporting organizations at both a national and club level, giving her an in-depth understanding of what it takes to run a national sporting body as well as the unique challenges for clubs and the importance of building strong relationships and a unity of purpose within," the sport, Clyne said. "Raelene is an extremely impressive executive who covered every base as far as what the board was looking for in a chief executive officer to lead our game into an important new chapter."
Castle was born in Australia and moved to New Zealand as a child, returning to Sydney in 2013 to take the job at the Bulldogs.
Castle is the first woman to lead one of Australia's four national football governing bodies, and Rugby Australia said she is the first woman to lead one of the world's top-tier rugby national governing bodies.
By The Associated Press
rewrite:
Raelene Castle is to commence the role of Chief Executive Officer at Rugby Australia in January, thereby becoming the inaugural woman to lead a major national union within world rugby. The appointment, announced by Rugby Australia Chairman Cameron Clyne, concludes a search process involving over two hundred candidates, from whom Castle was identified as the preeminent applicant. She will succeed Bill Pulver on the fifteenth of January.

Castle’s professional background includes executive leadership roles as CEO of Netball New Zealand and, more recently, of the Canterbury Bulldogs in Australia’s National Rugby League. Her governance experience extends to serving as a board director for the International Federation of Netball Associations and as chair of the NRL club CEOs leadership group. In announcing the appointment, Chairman Clyne emphasized the breadth of Castle’s experience, noting her leadership of organizations at both national and club levels. He stated this provides her with a comprehensive understanding of the operational demands of a national sporting body, as well as the distinct challenges faced by constituent clubs. Clyne further indicated that Castle would apply a fresh perspective to the challenges and opportunities confronting Rugby Australia, informed by her learnings from other sporting codes. He described her as an extremely impressive executive who comprehensively met the board’s criteria for a CEO to guide the sport into a significant new chapter.

In a public statement, Castle expressed particular anticipation for engaging with rugby communities across Australia and meeting the diverse individuals integral to the sport. She noted that, having followed rugby closely for over three decades and worked within the New Zealand and Australian sporting landscapes for the past ten years, she recognizes Australian rugby possesses a clear offering for both male and female athletes domestically and internationally—an offering with potential for further development and strengthening.

Castle, born in Australia before moving to New Zealand as a child, returned to Sydney in 2013 for her role with the Bulldogs. Her appointment is historically significant on two fronts: she is the first woman to lead one of Australia’s four major national football governing bodies, and, according to Rugby Australia, she is also the first woman to assume the leadership of a top-tier national rugby union globally.

Migdal murder survivor Natan Atiya, thanks 'the nation of Israel for everything' and thanks G-d for saving him.'
Natan Atiya, 10, survived the murder of his 11-year-old brother Nahman and his neighbors two weeks ago by pretending to be dead.
In an interview with Channel 20, Natan's father, Yisrael, said, "Thank G-d, after the customary week of mourning, we are trying to get back into our routine. People still come to comfort us. We have a lot of help, and are receiving a lot of warmth and love.
"My children, thank G-d, are filled with emuna (belief in G-d). They know this world is only temporary, and they know that we returned the deposit G-d gave us. They know their brother Nahman was a righteous person, and they know they can talk about him and that he's still here - we just can't see him anymore. But they know he hears us and that he's with us.
"They've already begun dreaming about him, so his presence is very tangible. Right now everything is fresh in our memories, and thank G-d the children are smart and understand a lot. The younger ones don't understand everything, but those who are old enough to understand are doing very well.
"Just like Natan was saved by a miracle, his physical and spiritual recovery is also a miracle."
Natan said, "I thank the entire nation of Israel for everything - for the love, the hugs, the prayers, the blessings and the gifts. Thank you, G-d, for giving me strength and saving me."
The Atiya family is still paying a lot of money for Natan's treatments.
rewrite:
Natan Atiya, a survivor of the Migdal attack, has expressed profound gratitude to both the nation of Israel and to God for his survival. The ten-year-old boy endured the murder of his eleven-year-old brother, Nahman, and neighbors two weeks prior by feigning death. In a subsequent interview with Channel 20, his father, Yisrael Atiya, described the family's process of navigating grief and recovery. He stated, “Following the customary week of mourning, we are, thank God, attempting to resume our routine. We continue to receive visitors offering comfort, and we are beneficiaries of considerable assistance, warmth, and love.”

Yisrael Atiya further elaborated on his children’s spiritual resilience, noting, “My children, thank God, are imbued with *emuna* (faith in God). They comprehend the transient nature of this world and that we have returned the deposit God entrusted to us. They recognize their brother Nahman as a righteous individual, and they understand they may speak of him, for he remains present—merely unseen. They are assured that he hears them and is with them.” He observed that the children have already begun dreaming of Nahman, making his presence palpably felt. While the memories remain vivid, Yisrael Atiya expressed gratitude for the children’s discernment, noting the older ones are coping remarkably well despite the profound trauma.

He characterized not only Natan’s initial survival but also his ongoing physical and spiritual recuperation as miraculous. Natan himself conveyed his appreciation, declaring, “I extend thanks to the entire nation of Israel for everything—for the love, embraces, prayers, blessings, and gifts. Thank you, God, for granting me strength and delivering me.” The Atiya family continues to bear significant financial burdens associated with Natan’s medical treatments.

While almost every major retailer has some form of a return policy, a growing number of stores are keeping track of who makes returns and whether or not they should be allowed to continue to do so in the future. This is all in an effort to help cut down on return fraud which accounts for about six percent of all returns.
Retail fraud is a broad category and includes things such as wardrobing, receipt fraud and price arbitrage. Wardrobing is the practice of purchasing items with the intent of using them for a short time and then immediately returning them, receipt fraud is using fake receipts to attempt to return products for profit, and price arbitrage is the practice of purchasing a cheap item and returning it in the place of a similar, more expensive item.
Industry estimates put loses due to retail fraud in the tens of billions of dollars so naturally, companies are looking to do whatever they can to help stop this. Ten of the top 100 retailers, including Best Buy and Home Depot, have turned to a company called The Retail Equation for help. The Retail Equation maintains a database of consumer behaviors such as how often a consumer makes returns and for what value. They then create a report for the customer as described on their website:
A Return Activity Report is a history of your return and exchange transactions posted in stores using Verify Return Authorization. The report lists return activity information including the stores you have returned to and, for each return, the date and time, whether it was receipted or non-receipted, and the dollar amount.
Using predictive analytics, the company attempts to determine if the return is likely to be fraudulent and whether or not to permit it. This will prevent stores from having to implement stricter return policies. The hope is to ban consumers who return more items than they should but retailers aren't saying much about this policy yet.
As with all emerging technologies, there are many reports of false positives but that is something that will hopefully improve with time.
rewrite:
While the vast majority of major retailers maintain established return policies, an increasing number are implementing systems to monitor customer return behavior and assess the future privilege of returns. This strategic shift is primarily aimed at mitigating return fraud, which industry analyses indicate constitutes approximately six percent of all merchandise returns.

Return fraud encompasses several specific practices, including wardrobing, receipt fraud, and price arbitrage. Wardrobing refers to the purchase of items with the premeditated intent of using them temporarily before seeking a refund. Receipt fraud involves the utilization of counterfeit receipts to return merchandise for illicit gain. Price arbitrage is the practice of buying a less expensive item and subsequently attempting to return it as a similar, higher-priced product to obtain undue credit.

Given that industry estimates project annual losses from retail fraud in the tens of billions of dollars, corporations are actively pursuing countermeasures. Notably, ten of the top one hundred retailers, such as Best Buy and Home Depot, have engaged the services of a firm called The Retail Equation. This company maintains a proprietary database tracking individual consumer return patterns, including frequency and monetary value. As outlined on its website, The Retail Equation generates a Return Activity Report for consumers, which provides a detailed transaction history. This report catalogs return and exchange activities at participating stores, listing for each transaction the location, date, time, receipt status, and dollar amount.

Leveraging predictive analytics, the firm evaluates the likelihood of fraudulent intent for each return transaction, thereby informing the retailer’s decision to authorize or deny it. A stated objective of this system is to enable retailers to avoid enacting universally stricter return policies by selectively restricting privileges. The goal is to curtail returns from consumers who demonstrably exceed normative patterns, though retailers have thus far been reticent to elaborate on the specific thresholds or criteria employed.

As with many nascent technological solutions, there have been documented instances of false positives, wherein legitimate returns are incorrectly flagged. It is anticipated that the refinement of analytical models and data inputs will enhance accuracy over time.

iCarly alum Nathan Kress and his wife London Elise will be adding some more pink to their family when they welcome their first child early next year — the couple is expecting a daughter.

“You can find me on my porch, in my rocking chair, polishing my shotgun, for the next 18 to 40 years,” Nathan, 24, quipped in the caption.

The South Nodaway R-IV Board of Education met in open and closed sessions on January 17 to handle the following school district business:
In closed session, the retirement of K-12 Principal Darbi Bauman was accepted and the decision was made to promote from within SN ranks to fill her position. Bauman has been with the district for 32 years.
For the 2018-19 school year, Assistant Principal Aaron Murphy will be the elementary principal and Athletic Director Dustin Skoglund will be the secondary principal.
The district will be searching for a physical education instructor to replace Murphy and Skoglund for next year.
At the end of the 2017-18 school year, Wanda Bloom, first grade teacher, and Vikki Spire, speech, are retiring. Kara Davis, paraprofessional, resigned as of January 19.
Board members Macia Kemper and Brian Flora have filed for the two open board positions.
A bid for $4,665.52 was accepted from Game Time Athletics, Weston, for a batting cage and outfield fence for the Guilford Sports Complex.
Superintendent Johnnie Silkett is looking into placing a SN directional sign on US Highway 71 and Highway M. He discussed MoDOT requirements for the sign. The board encouraged him to pursue the matter.
The district has received a $10,000 Pathways for Teachers grant in conjunction with Jefferson C-123. The districts will use the grant for teacher personal development. Phase I will include a kick-off introductory day followed by three days of Project Based Learning (PBL) training this spring.
The focus of the grant is health science, advanced manufacturing and science, technology, engineering and mathematics or STEM.
The school district is looking at five- and 10-year plans, which will incorporate PBL instruction to make SN students job competitive in the 21st century.
The 2018-19 school calendar had its first reading.
rewrite:
The South Nodaway R-IV Board of Education convened in both open and closed sessions on January 17 to conduct district business. During a closed session, the board accepted the retirement of K-12 Principal Darbi Bauman, who has served the district for thirty-two years. It was determined that her position would be filled through internal promotion. Consequently, for the 2018-19 academic year, Assistant Principal Aaron Murphy will assume the role of elementary principal, while Athletic Director Dustin Skoglund will become the secondary principal. The district will initiate a search for new personnel to fulfill the physical education responsibilities previously held by Murphy and Skoglund.

The board acknowledged several additional staffing changes effective at the conclusion of the 2017-18 school year: the retirements of first-grade teacher Wanda Bloom and speech instructor Vikki Spire, alongside the resignation of paraprofessional Kara Davis, effective January 19. Regarding board composition, members Macia Kemper and Brian Flora have filed for candidacy in the upcoming election for two open positions.

In facilities matters, a bid of $4,665.52 from Game Time Athletics of Weston was accepted for the procurement and installation of a batting cage and outfield fence at the Guilford Sports Complex. Furthermore, Superintendent Johnnie Silkett reported on preliminary investigations into erecting a South Nodaway directional sign at the intersection of US Highway 71 and Highway M, including Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT) requirements. The board authorized continued pursuit of this initiative.

The district, in collaboration with Jefferson C-123, has been awarded a $10,000 Pathways for Teachers grant aimed at professional development. Phase I of the grant program will commence with an introductory day followed by three days of Project Based Learning (PBL) training this spring. The grant focuses on enhancing instruction in health science, advanced manufacturing, and STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) fields. This initiative aligns with the district’s development of five- and ten-year strategic plans, which integrate PBL methodologies to improve student competitiveness in the 21st-century workforce. Finally, the 2018-19 school calendar underwent its first reading.

Palestinian Authority Chairman Mahmoud Abbas publicly mourned the passing of Archbishop Hilarion Capucci, 94.
Capucci, who died on Sunday in Rome, was an active supporter of the PLO and later the Palestinian Authority and Hamas terror organization.
In 1974 Capucci was caught using his diplomatic protection to smuggle guns for the PLO and sentenced to 12 years in prison. Capucci was released four years later, however, after the Pope made a special request on his behalf.
Following the Islamic Revolution in 1979, Capucci maintained ties with the Iranian regime and later became a support of the Hamas terror group backed by Iran.
Abbas called Capucci a "great warrior," and in 2013 presented him with a medal of honor in Rome.
Terrorist organization Fatah said Capucci's death pained "every Palestinian's heart" and expressed pride in "militant" Cappuci and his activities.
In 2002, Capucci participated in a pro-Palestinian parade in Rome and said, "Greetings to the sons of the Intifada and to the martyrs who go and fight as if they were going to a party... We want our land, or we will die with dignity... Intifada till victory."
Eight years later, Capucci participated in the failed attempt to run the Israeli security blockade of Gaza on board the Mavi Marmara, the Turkish vessel whose seizure sparked six years of diplomatic tensions between Jerusalem and Ankara.
rewrite:
Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas issued a public statement expressing condolences upon the death of Archbishop Hilarion Capucci at the age of ninety-four. Capucci, who passed away in Rome, was a noted supporter of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and, subsequently, both the Palestinian Authority and the Hamas organization, designated as a terrorist group by several nations. In 1974, he was apprehended for utilizing his diplomatic status to smuggle weapons for the PLO, resulting in a twelve-year prison sentence. His release occurred after four years following a papal intercession.

Subsequent to the 1979 Islamic Revolution in Iran, Capucci sustained relations with that government and later endorsed Hamas, which receives support from Iran. Abbas conferred upon him the title of "great warrior" and awarded him a medal of honor in a 2013 ceremony in Rome. The Fatah organization, also designated as terrorist by some states, described his death as a profound loss and praised his militant activities. In a 2002 pro-Palestinian demonstration in Rome, Capucci delivered a speech extolling the participants of the Intifada and martyrs, declaring, "We want our land, or we will die with dignity... Intifada till victory." Furthermore, in 2010, he participated in the attempted breach of the Israeli maritime blockade of Gaza aboard the Mavi Marmara, a Turkish vessel whose interception precipitated a prolonged diplomatic dispute between Israel and Turkey.

Q. It seems like my hangovers are much worse now that I am older, 42, to the point I can’t even have one drink without feeling listless the next day. What can I do, besides drinking water while drinking alcohol, to improve the situation?
A. The real “problem” might be that you’re drinking less as you age, which reduces your tolerance for alcohol, said Lara Ray, a professor of clinical psychology at the University of California, Los Angeles, who researches alcoholism. Someone with the self-image of a partying twentysomething but the lifestyle of a responsible 42-year-old may simply have lost the tolerance for a lot of alcohol, she said.
“Age may be a proxy for regularity of drinking,” Dr. Ray said. “If you haven’t gone to a party for two to three weeks, it might be less about being 40 and more about your drinking history.”
Also, as we age, we lose muscle mass, replacing it with fat. The same drink will cause more intoxication in a body with a higher fat content compared to a leaner one, she said. But this tends to be true more for people over 65 than over 40, she said.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
Dr. Ray suggests drinking more slowly to compensate for this change in body composition, and to drink more water or other liquids to dilute the alcohol. A quick spike in blood alcohol levels followed by a quick drop make hangovers more likely, she said, so avoiding those sudden changes should help.

The biological basis of hangovers is still unclear, said Dr. Marc Schuckit, a professor of psychiatry at the University of California, San Diego. Some people think being hung over is a mild form of alcohol withdrawal; others think hangovers are caused by dehydration or an imbalance of electrolytes like sodium, potassium or magnesium, he said.
rewrite:
The apparent increase in hangover severity with age, particularly the experience of pronounced listlessness following even a single drink at age 42, is a recognized phenomenon. According to Dr. Lara Ray, a professor of clinical psychology at the University of California, Los Angeles, whose research focuses on alcoholism, a primary factor may be a reduction in overall alcohol consumption that often accompanies midlife. This decreased regularity of drinking leads to a diminished physiological tolerance. Dr. Ray posits that age itself may serve as a proxy for drinking patterns; an individual who perceives themselves as a frequent social drinker but whose actual lifestyle has become more moderate may be experiencing the effects of a reduced drinking history rather than age per se.

Furthermore, physiological changes associated with aging can influence alcohol metabolism. A gradual loss of muscle mass and a corresponding increase in adipose tissue alter body composition. Since alcohol is water-soluble and not distributed into fat tissue, a higher proportion of body fat results in a higher concentration of alcohol in the bloodstream and other lean tissues for a given dose, leading to greater intoxication. Dr. Ray notes, however, that this effect is typically more pronounced in individuals over age 65 than in those over 40.

To mitigate these effects, Dr. Ray recommends several behavioral adjustments. Consuming alcoholic beverages at a slower pace allows the body more time for metabolism, compensating for changes in body composition. Concurrent hydration with water or other non-alcoholic liquids serves to dilute alcohol concentration. These practices help prevent a rapid peak and subsequent precipitous decline in blood alcohol concentration, a pattern strongly correlated with more severe hangover symptoms.

The precise biological mechanisms underlying hangovers remain an area of scientific inquiry. As explained by Dr. Marc Schuckit, a professor of psychiatry at the University of California, San Diego, several hypotheses exist. Some researchers conceptualize a hangover as a mild form of alcohol withdrawal, while others attribute symptoms primarily to dehydration or to an imbalance in key electrolytes such as sodium, potassium, and magnesium. The consensus is that multiple interrelated pathways are likely involved.

March 19 (UPI) -- South Korean boy band Wanna One returned with new music Monday.
The K-pop group released the EP 0+1=1 (I Promise You) and an energetic music video for the single "Boomerang."
The "Boomerang" video shows Yoon Ji-sung, Ha Sung-woon, Hwang Min-hyun, Ong Seong-wu, Kim Jae-hwan, Daniel Kang, Park Ji-hoon, Park Woo-jin, Bae Jin-young, Lee Dae-hwi and Lai Kuan-Lin wearing all-black studded ensembles as they perform choreographed dance numbers.
"Wanna One I 'BOOMERANG' M/V The beginning of the golden age! Wanna One 2nd Mini Album '0+1=1 (I PROMISE YOU),'" the boy band announced on Twitter.
Wanna One said at a press conference Monday in Seoul that it hopes to make 2018 its "golden age," according to The Korea Herald.
"Fans would be able to see different sides of us on the new album. We got more powerful and mature," Kang said.
Wanna One was previously known for its mellow and youthful image. The group released the EP 1-1=0 (Nothing Without You) in November, which was a re-release of its EP 1x1=1 (To Be One).

NEW DELHI — India’s main opposition Congress party on Monday named Rahul Gandhi, the scion of the country’s Nehru-Gandhi political dynasty, as party president.
Gandhi was elected to the post unopposed and succeeds his mother, Sonia Gandhi, for the top job in the party.
The party had governed India for decades before the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata party swept to power in 2014. Gandhi faces the difficult task of resurrecting a crumbling Congress party, a task made harder by a series of crushing defeats in state elections over the last year.
Gandhi, 47, entered politics in 2004 and is a member of India’s Parliament. He was appointed party vice-president in 2013.
Sonia Gandhi has led the party for 19 years. She has had health problems over the last few years, but the family and party have released little information about them.
Rahul Gandhi becomes the sixth member of the Nehru-Gandhi family to lead Congress. His father, Rajiv Gandhi, his grandmother Indira Gandhi and his great-grandfather Jawaharlal Nehru have served as prime minister since India’s independence from British colonialists in 1947.
rewrite: On Monday, the Indian National Congress, the nation's principal opposition party, formally appointed Rahul Gandhi as its president. Mr. Gandhi, a scion of the influential Nehru-Gandhi political dynasty, was elected to the position unopposed, succeeding his mother, Sonia Gandhi. This transition occurs as the Congress party, which governed India for decades prior to the Bharatiya Janata Party's electoral victory in 2014, confronts significant organizational and electoral challenges. Mr. Gandhi, aged 47 and a sitting member of India’s Parliament since 2004, faces the formidable task of revitalizing the party following a series of decisive defeats in recent state elections. He previously served as party vice-president beginning in 2013. Sonia Gandhi concluded a nineteen-year tenure as party president, a period during which her health concerns, though sparingly detailed in official communications, were acknowledged. Rahul Gandhi now becomes the sixth member of his family to lead the Congress party, following a lineage that includes his father, Rajiv Gandhi, his grandmother, Indira Gandhi, and his great-grandfather, Jawaharlal Nehru, all of whom served as Prime Minister of India following independence in 1947.

Workers clean windows outside the Cape Town headquarters of Anglo-South African financial services company Old Mutual, March 7, 2016. REUTERS/Mike Hutchings
Britain's Old Mutual Plc (OML.L) said it would sell its 26 percent stake in Kotak Mahindra Old Mutual Life Insurance Ltd to Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd (KTKM.NS) for about 12.93 billion rupees ($201.7 million)(£156.28 million).
The sale will end Old Mutual's joint venture with Kotak Mahindra Bank, the company said late Thursday.
The net consideration after tax is 11.7 billion rupees, Old Mutual said.
The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to be completed in the second half of the year.
Old Mutual is in the midst of breaking up its business in four parts by the end of next year. The firm aims to list or sell its emerging markets business and is sharpening focus on its sub-Saharan Africa business.
(Reporting by Abinaya Vijayaraghavan in Bengaluru; Editing by Gopakumar Warrier)

The transaction, disclosed late Thursday, will terminate the longstanding joint venture between the two entities. Old Mutual specified the net post-tax consideration at 11.7 billion rupees. Pending regulatory approvals, completion is anticipated in the latter half of the year. This divestment aligns with Old Mutual's broader strategic restructuring, which involves separating its operations into four distinct units by the end of the forthcoming year. The firm intends to list or sell its emerging markets segment while concentrating its strategic focus on its sub-Saharan African operations.

Sean Hannity welcomed Fox News The Five host Jesse Watters (formerly of The O’Reilly Factor segment “Watters’ World”) and liberal political commentator Jessica Tarlov on Thursday night to discuss the Devin Nunes memo, which Trump approved for release on Friday. Like the president, both Hannity and Watters seem confident that the contents of the “cherry-picked memo” — which FBI Director Christopher Wray is “raising hell” over — will serve to discredit the Russia probe.
Watters even went so far as to quote Barack Obama, in that “if you don’t want the truth to come out, you have something to hide,” insinuating that Democrats have a reason to fear details of the FBI’s surveillance of Trump campaign advisor Carter Page.
Hannity then went on to suggest that the infamous “pee-pee tape” was a made up story to obtain a FISA warrant, which Watters unsurprisingly agreed with. “And you know it’s not true,” he chimed in, presenting the most astounding argument against the existence of the salacious evidence so far. “If someone pees in the bed, where are you gonna sleep?”
Watters claim was received incredulously by a stunned Tarlov. “Well I don’t think he’s having a sleepover, I think it’s transactional, I don’t think it’s a cuddle-fest,” she retorted. Indeed, Tarlov. I don’t think Russian hookers work the way Jesse Watters think they work — but we’ll leave it at that.
rewrite:
On the evening of Thursday, February 1st, Fox News host Sean Hannity facilitated a discussion concerning the impending release of the classified memorandum authored by House Intelligence Committee Chairman Devin Nunes. His guests were fellow Fox News host Jesse Watters, of *The Five*, and liberal political commentator Jessica Tarlov. The conversation centered on the anticipated content of the document, which President Donald Trump had authorized for public disclosure the following day. Mirroring the president’s stated position, both Hannity and Watters expressed confidence that the selectively compiled information within the memo would significantly undermine the credibility of the ongoing investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election, a perspective reportedly contested by FBI Director Christopher Wray.

Watters further invoked a quotation from former President Barack Obama—"if you don’t want the truth to come out, you have something to hide"—to insinuate that Democratic opposition to the memo’s release stemmed from a desire to conceal purported procedural overreach. This specifically alluded to the Federal Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) warrant obtained for former Trump campaign advisor Carter Page.

The discourse then turned to the unverified allegation involving compromising material, colloquially termed the "pee-pee tape." Hannity posited the theory that this narrative was fabricated to justify the FISA surveillance, a contention with which Watters readily concurred. Watters offered a literalistic critique of the allegation’s plausibility, questioning its logistical particulars, which was met with evident astonishment by Tarlov. She countered that the hypothetical scenario was transactional rather than social, implicitly challenging the underlying assumptions of Watters’ remark. The segment concluded without further elaboration on the point.

President Donald Trump ’s nominee to lead the Veterans Affairs Department, White House physician Ronny Jackson, plans to pursue confirmation despite a review that a Senate committee opened into allegations of improper behavior and management lapses, two people familiar with the matter said.
The two people described Jackson’s intentions following an Oval Office meeting he had late Tuesday afternoon with Trump.
Trump said earlier in the day at a news conference with French President Emmanuel Macron Tuesday that he had advised Jackson to withdraw.
"I said to Dr. Jackson, what do you need it for?” Trump said. “I don’t want to put a man through a process like this. It’s too ugly and disgusting.” He later added, “I really don’t think personally he should do it, but it’s totally his, I would stand behind him, totally his decision."
The president spoke hours after Senator Johnny Isakson, chairman of the Veterans Affairs Committee, said he and the panel’s ranking Democrat, Jon Tester, decided to delay a hearing on Jackson’s nomination that had been scheduled for Wednesday and sent a letter to Trump seeking more information.

These individuals clarified Jackson’s stance following a meeting with the President in the Oval Office on Tuesday afternoon. Earlier that day, during a joint press conference with French President Emmanuel Macron, President Trump stated he had counseled Jackson to withdraw from consideration, expressing reluctance to subject him to a contentious confirmation process. Trump characterized the proceedings as “too ugly and disgusting,” and while he personally advised against continuation, he affirmed he would respect and support Jackson’s ultimate decision. No one was injured late Monday night in a smokey fire at a multi-story senior housing apartment building, according to the Santa Maria Fire Department.
Firefighters were called out at about 10:45 p.m. to Union Plaza, 120 N. Broadway, and found fire alarms ringing and four smoke detectors activated on the third floor, Battalion Chief Scott Johnson said.
“Fire crews were assigned to the second, third, and forth floors to assist with locating the fire, removing occupants and sheltering in place,” Johnson said. “Fire crews were able to locate the source of smoke, which was burnt food in one of the occupancies.”
Firefighters ventilated the smoke from the third floor, and all the residents were allowed to return to their units, Johnson said.
There was no damage to the structure, Johnson said.

Image copyright Reuters Image caption Foreign Affairs Minister Chrystia Freeland said trade deals must help workers at home and abroad
Canada will push for environmental and labour protections during trade talks with the US and Mexico on Wednesday.
Canada's Minister of Foreign Affairs Chrystia Freeland outlined Canada's goals for the North American Free Trade Agreement on Monday in parliament.
US President Donald Trump is an outspoken critic of the agreement, and initiated the renegotiation in May.
The US is expected to push for more access to Canada's agricultural market, and an end to trade deficits.
Ms Freeland said Canada will push for the agreement to become more "progressive", and include more environmental and labour protections, as well as sections on gender equality and indigenous rights.
She also said Canada would seek a formal mechanism to ending trade disputes as they arise.
"We must pursue progressive trade agreements that are win-win, helping workers both at home and abroad to enjoy higher wages and better conditions," Ms Freeland said.
In her address to the committee on international trade, Ms Freeland laid out six main goals for the negotiations:
modernise the agreement for the technology sector
include provisions for the environment, labour, gender equality and indigenous rights
cut red tape
open up government-procurement processes
make it easier for professionals to work throughout North America
create a formal dispute mechanism to fight countervailing and anti-dumping duties
Canada is the America's largest export market and second-largest trading partner after China.
In 2016, more than $540bn (£416bn) of goods passed over the border between Canada and the US.
But tensions have been mounting under Mr Trump, who made tough-on-trade talk a hallmark of his campaign.
He has slapped tariffs on Canadian lumber and slammed Canadian pricing of dairy products, taking aim at Canada's system of supply management.
The US government has said trade deficits and market access will top its agenda during renegotiations.
Mexico wants to continue free access to goods and services, and strengthen the energy sector, according to a document leaked to Reuters.
rewrite:
On Monday, Canada’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Chrystia Freeland, articulated the nation’s principal objectives for the forthcoming renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) before a parliamentary committee. These negotiations, set to commence on Wednesday with the United States and Mexico, will see Canada advocating for the integration of enhanced environmental and labour safeguards, alongside provisions addressing gender equality and Indigenous rights. Minister Freeland emphasized the pursuit of “progressive” trade agreements designed to generate mutual benefits, asserting that such frameworks should elevate wages and improve working conditions for labour forces domestically and internationally.

In her address to the Committee on International Trade, Minister Freeland delineated six core priorities for the modernization of NAFTA. These include updating the agreement to reflect advancements in the technology sector, incorporating robust chapters on environmental and labour standards as well as gender and Indigenous rights, reducing bureaucratic impediments to commerce, liberalizing government procurement processes, facilitating the mobility of professionals across North America, and establishing a formalized mechanism for the resolution of trade disputes, particularly concerning countervailing and anti-dumping duties.

The renegotiation process was initiated in May following sustained criticism of NAFTA by U.S. President Donald Trump, for whom stringent trade rhetoric has been a defining feature of his administration. The United States is anticipated to prioritize the reduction of its trade deficit and seek greater access to Canada’s agricultural market, notably taking issue with Canada’s supply management system for dairy. Recent bilateral tensions have been exacerbated by the imposition of U.S. tariffs on Canadian softwood lumber.

Canada remains the United States’ largest export destination and its second-largest trading partner after China, with bilateral goods trade exceeding $540 billion in 2016. Meanwhile, according to a document obtained by Reuters, Mexico’s negotiating aims will focus on preserving unfettered access for goods and services while seeking to reinforce its energy sector. The upcoming trilateral discussions will thus confront a complex array of national priorities within a pivotal economic partnership.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Puerto Rico’s new governor has been sworn in as the U.S. territory prepares for what many believe will be new austerity measures and a renewed push for statehood to haul the island out of a deep economic crisis.
Ricardo Rossello was sworn in Monday and proposed several measures aimed at alleviating the crisis. Among them is a proposal to hold a referendum that would ask voters whether they prefer statehood or independence.
“The United States cannot pretend to be a model of democracy for the world while it discriminates against 3.5 million of its citizens in Puerto Rico, depriving them of their right to political, social and economic equality under the U.S. flag,” Rossello said in his inaugural speech, delivered in Spanish. “There is no way to overcome Puerto Rico’s crisis given its colonial condition.”
The new governor said he would hold elections to choose two senators and five representatives and send them to Washington to demand statehood, similar to what Tennessee did in the 1790s in its push for statehood.
Rossello also aims to boost public-private partnerships and use that revenue to save a retirement system that faces a $40 billion deficit. Rossello has pledged to work closely with a federal control board that U.S. Congress created to oversee Puerto Rico’s finances. He said he supports negotiations with creditors to help restructure a nearly $70 billion public debt.
Rossello announced that he has already signed six executive orders, among them are efforts to promote bilingual education and to eliminate the wage gap for female government employees.
Supporters rallied outside the Capitol on Monday cheering the new governor, many waving U.S. flags.
rewrite:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — Ricardo Rosselló was inaugurated as Governor of Puerto Rico on Monday, assuming leadership of the United States territory amid a profound economic crisis. His administration is anticipated to introduce stringent austerity measures and to vigorously renew initiatives aimed at achieving U.S. statehood for the island.

In his inaugural address, delivered in Spanish, Governor Rosselló framed the territory’s political status as a fundamental impediment to recovery. “The United States cannot pretend to be a model of democracy for the world while it discriminates against 3.5 million of its citizens in Puerto Rico, depriving them of their right to political, social and economic equality under the U.S. flag,” he stated. “There is no way to overcome Puerto Rico’s crisis given its colonial condition.” To address this, he proposed a referendum allowing voters to express a preference between statehood and independence.

Furthering the statehood initiative, Rosselló outlined a plan to hold elections for two senators and five representatives, who would be dispatched to Washington, D.C., to petition for admission to the union—a strategy he compared to that employed by Tennessee in the 1790s.

Concurrently, the governor announced several economic measures. These include fostering public-private partnerships, with generated revenue directed toward stabilizing a public retirement system confronting a $40 billion deficit. He pledged cooperation with the federal financial oversight board established by the U.S. Congress and expressed support for restructuring negotiations regarding the island’s nearly $70 billion public debt. Additionally, Rosselló confirmed the signing of six executive orders, which encompass initiatives to promote bilingual education and to eliminate gender-based wage disparities for government employees.

The inauguration was met with support from crowds gathered outside the Capitol, many of whom waved U.S. flags.

By Eamon Quinn
Eir has told its investors its next big decision on its future plans won’t be revealed until later this spring when the deal involving its new French owners is expected to be completed.
It comes as another business group, Isme characterised the telecom firm’s plan announced this week to pull out of the Government’s National Broadband Plan as disastrous and which will likely delay the introduction to 2023. It said it has serious reservations about the contract process run by the Department of Communications after what Isme said was Eir securing “low hanging fruit” in its existing installation of broadband.
Outgoing Eir chief Richard Moat in its latest quarterly report blamed the complexity of the National Broadband Plan contract and identified pricing issues “outside of the National Broadband Plan process” for it quitting the tender.
Underlying earnings of €125m in the three months to end December were up 4% from a year earlier on reduced costs, even as revenues fell 2% to €322m, leaving it on target to hit full-year earnings growth targets, it said. Storm- related costs came to €3m in the quarter. Mr Moat had no other news on the company’s strategy. Eir has changed hands more times than any other European national telecom. It is being bought by French entrepreneur Xavier Niel via NJJ and Iliad.
He will buy a 64.5% stake in Eir for an estimated €1bn, while two US hedge funds remain as minority shareholders. The firm has net debts of €2.16bn. Fitch Ratings analyst Damien Chew said Eir’s latest earnings were “broadly in line with what we expected”. He said the effects of the change of ownership won’t be known until the deal is completed, probably in April.

Don't Miss

Eir has informed its investors that its forthcoming strategic decisions will not be disclosed until later this spring, pending the anticipated completion of its acquisition by new French owners. This development follows criticism from the Irish Small and Medium Enterprises Association (Isme), which characterized the telecommunications firm’s recent withdrawal from the Government’s National Broadband Plan as disastrous, likely delaying the initiative’s introduction until 2023. Isme expressed serious reservations regarding the procurement process administered by the Department of Communications, alleging that Eir had secured advantageous "low-hanging fruit" through its existing broadband infrastructure.

In Eir’s latest quarterly report, outgoing chief executive Richard Moat attributed the withdrawal to the complexity of the National Broadband Plan contract and cited pricing concerns external to the formal process. The company reported underlying earnings of €125 million for the quarter ending December, a 4% year-on-year increase driven by reduced costs, despite a 2% decline in revenue to €322 million. This performance reportedly keeps Eir on track to meet full-year earnings targets. The quarter also included €3 million in storm-related costs. Mr. Moat provided no further updates on corporate strategy.

Eir, which has undergone more ownership changes than any other European national telecommunications operator, is being acquired by French entrepreneur Xavier Niel through NJJ and Iliad. The transaction involves an estimated €1 billion for a 64.5% stake, with two US hedge funds retaining minority shares. The company carries net debt of €2.16 billion. According to Fitch Ratings analyst Damien Chew, Eir’s recent earnings are "broadly in line with expectations," though the implications of the ownership transition will remain uncertain until the deal finalizes, likely in April.

GM Extends Summer Shutdown at Two Car Plants as Demand Falls
by Darryl Hood
General Motors is extending the normal two-week summer shutdown at two U.S. car factories because of slumping demand.
Union officials say the Lordstown, Ohio, plant near Cleveland and the Fairfax plant in Kansas City, Kansas, will close for as long as five weeks in June and July. The summer shutdown normally lasts two weeks.
Lordstown makes the Chevrolet Cruze compact while Fairfax builds the Chevrolet Malibu midsize car.
Cruze sales are up 36 percent due largely to fleet sales. Sales to individual buyers are down 3 percent. Malibu sales are down 30 percent through May.
Spokesman Jim Cain confirms that some car plants will see more down weeks but wouldn’t give specifics. He says GM is adjusting as the market shifts from cars to trucks and SUVs.
(Copyright 2017 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten or redistributed.)
rewrite: In response to declining market demand, General Motors has announced an extension of the customary two-week summer production hiatus at two of its United States automotive assembly facilities. According to union officials, the plants in Lordstown, Ohio, and Fairfax, Kansas, will suspend operations for a period of up to five weeks during June and July. The Lordstown facility manufactures the Chevrolet Cruze compact vehicle, while the Fairfax plant produces the Chevrolet Malibu midsize sedan. Notably, while Cruze sales have increased by 36 percent year-to-date—primarily driven by fleet purchases—retail sales for the model have declined by 3 percent. Malibu sales have decreased by 30 percent through May. Company spokesman Jim Cain acknowledged that certain plants would experience additional idle weeks, without providing specific details, attributing the production adjustments to a broader market transition from passenger cars to trucks and sport utility vehicles.

The lead changed hands eight times before the Bears went on a 15-0 run over a 2:12 span early in the second half. Baylor had three 3-point plays during the spurt, including one that resulted in a five-point trip after Iowa State coach Steve Prohm was hit with a technical foul.
''We wanted to come out and you want to get the crowd going, and we wanted to get some momentum,'' Baylor coach Scott Drew said. ''We were able to get some separation and get the crowd into the game. That really helps, especially with the zone and different things like that, because now they're trying to score quicker and it's harder to score quicker against (the zone).''
Baylor (13-10, 3-7 Big 12 Conference) led 51-38 at that point and the Cyclones never got closer than eight the rest of the way.
''When we went into halftime they told us to be very aggressive and take the ball to the basket,'' said Maston, who was 9-of-11 shooting. ''I know I was shooting a couple of fadeaway jumpers, and they told me to get in there and basically force my will into the paint and get easy buckets. So that's what I did, and it ended up working out great.''
Manu Lecomte added 14 points for the Bears, who won despite shooting 2 for 14 from 3-point range. Baylor made up for that with a 43-35 edge in rebounds and 52-28 in points in the paint. The Bears shot 62 percent in the second half and 50 percent for the game.
Jo Lual-Acuil Jr. added 10 points and 14 rebounds for Baylor.
''I think it was just determination. We knew coming into the game we had to win,'' Lual-Acuil said. ''T.J. (Maston) did a great job playing with energy and we didn't want to leave here without a win.''

SAN FRANCISCO — Tesla dropped a standard new-car braking test it saw as unnecessary as it pushed to make an elusive production target for its Model 3 sedans last week.
The so-called "brake and roll" test was halted early on June 26, according to Business Insider.
"I can't even figure out a good reason to ever bypass this," Dave Sullivan, manager of product analysis for AutoPacific, said in an email to USA Today. "For a company that is under such immense scrutiny for safety, there is zero reason to bypass anything related to brakes now."
Tesla, based south of San Francisco in Palo Alto, Calif., has faced scrutiny for a series of accidents involving its Autopilot system, which handles some of the driving chores but requires driver oversight.
Tesla spokesperson Dave Arnold said that the test was redundant because the company drives every Model 3 on its test track, where it checks brakes, alignment and other aspects of the car that would impact its overall safety.
"Every car we build goes through rigorous quality checks and must meet exacting specifications, including brake tests," Arnold said in a statement. "There are no exceptions."
Investors were buoyed by the news earlier in the week that CEO Elon Musk had hit his long-promised output of 5,000 Model E's — the $35,000-and-up Model 3 is considered critical to the company's financial success — by Musk's second quarter deadline. But some analysts warned that the level, which included Tesla setting up a tent for additional production, wasn't sustainable.
CFRA Research downgraded Tesla stock to "sell."
In a note Tuesday, GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives called the "brake and roll" news "a potential gut punch to the bulls that now worry about sustainability and speed bumps ahead on the Model 3 front."
Ives still rates the stock a buy with a $375 target due largely to the recent positive news about Model 3. But, he said, "the knee jerk reaction from the Street's perspective is clearly a concern that neutralizes some of the long awaited good news from reaching the key 5,000 per week goal."

This procedure typically verifies brake function and ensures wheels rotate freely after vehicles roll off the assembly line.

Commenting on the decision, Dave Sullivan, manager of product analysis at AutoPacific, expressed significant concern in a correspondence with USA Today, stating, "I cannot identify a valid rationale for ever bypassing this test. For a corporation subject to intense safety scrutiny, there is no justification for circumventing any protocol related to brake systems at this juncture." The Palo Alto-based automaker has previously faced regulatory and public examination following a series of incidents involving its driver-assistance Autopilot system.

Daniel Ives, an analyst at GBH Insights, characterized the braking test news in a Tuesday note as "a potential gut punch to the bulls," introducing concerns about production sustainability. It’s been seven years since Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore ended their marriage — and by default — broke up their landmark noise rock band Sonic Youth. The dissolution of alt rock’s only surviving power couple came as a blow to anyone who thought there was something special about the healing and sustaining power of experimental noise rock. Now, as if to underline and punctuate the finality of the break, former drummer Steve Shelley is selling off some of the band’s effects pedals on eBay.
Sonic Youth was known for anarchic, dissonant soundscapes and their heavy reliance on particular effects pedals and customized instruments in order to achieve their aesthetic. They famously had to cancel a tour once after their custom gear had been stolen because it was impossible to re-create their sound live with factory instruments. Clearly, these pedals represent more than your usual stompbox. And by all indications, the band is on board with this sale. Their still active official twitter account actually tweeted out a link to the sale. So it’s safe to assume this sale is sanctioned by the band or at least whoever runs their social.
You can peruse the items and bid on them for yourself over on eBay, but bear in mind that they come with a disclaimer on the listings themselves:
“It cannot be said with certainty when or by whom each particular pedal was used.”
There are currently only four items up and the prices are already in the hundreds of dollars. Expect to pay a high price for an authentic lo-fi sound.
rewrite:
Seven years have passed since the dissolution of both the marriage between Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore and, consequently, their seminal noise rock band Sonic Youth. The separation of alternative rock’s preeminent and enduring creative partnership represented a significant loss for those who perceived a unique, restorative quality in the band’s experimental sonic explorations. The finality of this rupture now appears underscored by former drummer Steve Shelley’s decision to auction a selection of the band’s effects pedals via eBay.

Sonic Youth’s aesthetic was defined by anarchic, dissonant soundscapes, achieved through a heavy reliance on specific effects pedals and extensively customized instrumentation. Their dependence on this tailored equipment was such that the theft of their gear once necessitated a tour cancellation, as reproducing their complex live sound with standard instruments proved impossible. Thus, these devices transcend the function of ordinary stompboxes, embodying integral components of the band’s artistic identity. The sale appears to have the group’s endorsement, as their active official Twitter account has publicized the auction link, suggesting authorization by the band or its representatives.

Prospective bidders may examine the listings on eBay, though they are cautioned by a seller’s disclaimer noting that definitive historical usage for each individual pedal cannot be verified. With only four items currently available and bids already reaching several hundred dollars, acquiring these artifacts promises to command a considerable premium for a tangible connection to an authentic lo-fi legacy.

input: Clouds have been stubborn lately across south Florida and the region. On Monday they persisted much of the day although only a few favored locations actually received rain from them. The wettest, by far, was the Lower and Middle Florida Keys. Looking ahead, brief rain showers will remain possible as we tap into some moisture off the ocean. High pressure is at the heart of our weather pattern. It’s anchored south of Bermuda in the western Atlantic (and likely to stay stationary into the middle of the week). For us, that means a continued onshore flow with comfortable temperatures and a nice breeze. Later in the week, the high should weaken further and ease southward. Local winds, in turn, will probably start veering more out of the south by the upcoming weekend. Expect a rise in temperature, into the middle 80’s with higher levels of humidity. Early next week looks a bit more interesting, by the way. Long range forecast maps show a cold front crossing the Gulf of Mexico and moving our way by late Sunday or Monday. Rain and thunderstorm chances will likely increase ahead of the boundary… if the front holds together. Right now, it’s too far off to say with any confidence (and fronts this time of the year can be especially weak, if not fickle).
rewrite:
Persistent cloud cover has characterized recent conditions across southern Florida and the surrounding region. On Monday, overcast skies endured throughout much of the day, though precipitation was limited to only a few localized areas. The Lower and Middle Florida Keys recorded the most significant rainfall by a considerable margin. In the short term, brief isolated showers remain possible as modest moisture is drawn from the adjacent ocean. The dominant meteorological feature is a high-pressure system anchored south of Bermuda in the western Atlantic, which is forecast to remain quasi-stationary through midweek. This pattern sustains a consistent onshore flow, resulting in seasonable temperatures and moderate breezes for the region.

Later in the week, a gradual weakening and southward displacement of this high-pressure system is anticipated. Consequently, local wind patterns are expected to shift, becoming more southerly by the upcoming weekend. This shift will likely bring elevated temperatures, reaching the mid-80s Fahrenheit, alongside increased atmospheric humidity. Early next week may introduce more dynamic conditions. Long-range model projections indicate a cold front traversing the Gulf of Mexico, potentially approaching the region by late Sunday or Monday. An associated increase in showers and thunderstorms is probable ahead of this frontal boundary, contingent upon the system maintaining its integrity. However, given the considerable lead time and the typical weakness of frontal systems during this season, considerable forecast uncertainty remains.

Chris Christie chowed down with President Trump at the White House Tuesday amid speculation that the New Jersey governor might join the administration as it grapples with growing pains.
Christie and wife Mary Pat had a Valentine’s Day’s lunch with the commander in chief the day after Trump ousted his national security adviser, Michael Flynn, and amid chatter among Trump allies that more shakeups are coming.
A source close to Christie told The Post that possible ­administration positions were discussed.
“I heard it was about chief of staff,” the source said.
But the White House said the conversation was about curbing opioid abuse, a major priority for the governor, and the chief-of-staff issue “didn’t even come up.”
“They talked about combating drugs briefly,” White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer told The Post.
Spicer pushed back on speculation that Christie would be drafted to beef up the White house staff.
“I think Governor Christie said he has a year left of his administration and he intends to fully serve it out,” Spicer said.
“So we’re not discussing one month in what we intend to do in a year and a half. Let’s get there first.”
Christie, an early and effective surrogate for Trump during the election race, was previously passed up for vice president and was also replaced by VP Mike Pence to head up the White House transition team.
But Christie remained a loyal friend to Trump and blamed early White House problems, such as the botched immigration executive-order rollout, on staff that ­“ill-served” the president.
Christie’s office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The closed-door meeting occurred as Trump allies were openly questioning Reince Priebus’ ability to serve as chief of staff.
The public complaints started Sunday when Christopher Ruddy, CEO of Newsmax Media, said Priebus was “in way over his head” and should be canned. Ruddy later softened his tone after talking with Priebus and reported that the White House has full confidence in the chief of staff.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, Governor Chris Christie of New Jersey joined President Donald Trump for a private lunch at the White House. This meeting occurred amidst ongoing speculation that Governor Christie might assume a formal role within the administration, which is currently navigating significant operational challenges. The luncheon, which included the Governor’s wife, Mary Pat Christie, took place on February 14th, merely one day after President Trump dismissed National Security Advisor Michael Flynn. Concurrently, discussions among the President’s allies suggested further potential personnel changes.

An anonymous source familiar with Governor Christie’s perspective indicated to The Post that various administrative positions were considered during the conversation, specifically mentioning the role of Chief of Staff. However, White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer offered a contradictory account, asserting that the discussion focused primarily on strategies to combat opioid abuse—a policy area of longstanding importance to Governor Christie—and that the subject of the Chief of Staff position was not raised. Spicer further downplayed the speculation regarding Christie’s recruitment, noting the Governor’s stated commitment to completing the final year of his term in New Jersey.

Governor Christie, who was an early and prominent supporter of President Trump during the campaign, was previously considered for Vice President and initially led the presidential transition team before being replaced by Vice President Mike Pence. Despite these developments, Christie has maintained his allegiance to the President, attributing early administrative difficulties, such as the problematic implementation of an executive order on immigration, to staff who he believed inadequately served the President. Christie’s office did not provide an immediate comment regarding the meeting.

This private gathering coincided with public doubts expressed by some Trump allies concerning the efficacy of Reince Priebus in his capacity as Chief of Staff. These concerns were notably voiced by Christopher Ruddy, CEO of Newsmax Media, who initially suggested Priebus was unqualified and should be replaced. Ruddy later moderated his criticism after a discussion with Priebus, subsequently reporting that the White House retains full confidence in its Chief of Staff.

Apple likes to add new features and data points into Maps, the latest of which is the addition of bike sharing data for more than 175 cities across 36 countries.
You can search for the specific bike share system in your city in the search field in Apple Maps, search for “bike sharing”, or ask Siri.
Apple has partnered with Ito World to provide the bike data; this is the first bike-sharing dataset provided as a single feed.
The schemes have a total of more than 12,810 "points of interest", each one a place where you can pick up or drop off a cycle.
Cities and services added in the UK are:
Bath (nextbike Bath)
Belfast (Coca-Cola Zero Belfast Bikes)
Exeter (co bikes)
Glasgow (nextbike Glasgow)
London (Santander Cycles/Boris Bikes)
Milton Keynes (Santander Cycles MK)
Stirling (nextbike Stirling)
University of Warwick (UniCycles)
Apple’s original woes with Apple Maps are well documented, but the company has improved the app phenomenally over the last few years, adding in much more accurate detail.
Public transport information continues to be extended as well, while lane guidance for navigation has also recently launched in Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Austria, South Africa and Poland.
Apple Maps recently added more than 30 detailed indoor airport maps for major international airports including London Heathrow, JFK, LaGuardia, LAX, Hong Kong International, Chicago O’Hare, Amsterdam, Schiphol, Geneva, Toronto Pearson, and the remarkably-still-open Berlin Tegel.
Check out Indoor Maps for Apple Maps: What are they and how can you use them?
rewrite:
Apple has integrated bicycle-sharing data into its Maps application, extending coverage to over 175 cities across 36 countries. Users may locate specific local bicycle-sharing systems by entering a query in the Apple Maps search field, searching for the generic term “bike sharing,” or issuing a voice command via Siri. This bicycle-sharing dataset, supplied through a partnership with Ito World, represents the first instance of such information being consolidated into a single feed. The aggregated schemes encompass more than 12,810 distinct points of interest, each corresponding to a bicycle docking or rental station.

In the United Kingdom, the newly incorporated cities and their respective services include: Bath (nextbike Bath), Belfast (Coca-Cola Zero Belfast Bikes), Exeter (co bikes), Glasgow (nextbike Glasgow), London (Santander Cycles), Milton Keynes (Santander Cycles MK), Stirling (nextbike Stirling), and the University of Warwick (UniCycles). This enhancement is part of a broader, sustained effort to advance the functionality and accuracy of Apple Maps, an application that has undergone significant improvement since its problematic initial release. Further developments include the ongoing expansion of public transit information and the recent introduction of lane guidance for navigation in Canada, Australia, Switzerland, Austria, South Africa, and Poland.

Additionally, Apple Maps has recently incorporated detailed indoor maps for more than thirty major international airports. Notable examples include London Heathrow, John F. Kennedy International, LaGuardia, Los Angeles International, Hong Kong International, Chicago O’Hare, Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Geneva Airport, Toronto Pearson International, and Berlin Tegel. These indoor maps provide detailed layouts to assist with navigation within terminal buildings.

(CBS Local) – Gun owners around the country are blowing up expensive coolers after the NRA accused outdoor lifestyle company Yeti of joining a nationwide boycott of the gun-rights organization.
According to a letter from Marion P. Hammer of the NRA’s Institute for Legislative Action, Yeti has cut ties with the NRA and is refusing to do business with the NRA Foundation or offer discounts to members. “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities,” Hammer claims in the April 20 statement.
In response to the news, NRA members and supporters have begun taking their frustrations out on the company’s hottest item: outdoor coolers. In a number of online videos boycotting Yeti, gun owners are seen destroying the expensive containers by loading them with explosives and shooting them. “This Yeti ain’t ready,” South Carolina resident Bryan Atkinson declared before obliterating his cooler.
The pricey coolers reportedly cost anywhere between $250 and $1,300; making a discount on Yeti camping and hunting gear very helpful to consumers. “If Yeti can’t stand behind the NRA, I ain’t standing behind Yeti no more,” Atkinson added in a Facebook post.
Yeti is disputing the NRA’s claims that they’ve joined a boycott against pro-gun Americans. “Yeti notified the NRA Foundation, as well as a number of other organizations, that we were eliminating a group of outdated discounting programs,” the company wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. The outdoor lifestyle supplier added that they’re offering business partners like the NRA alternative programs and called claims that Yeti was turning their backs on young gun owners untrue.
Several organizations including airlines and rental car companies have cut ties with the National Rifle Association in the wake of the deadly Parkland, Florida school shooting which killed 17 people in February. Since the shooting, many Americans have lashed out at the NRA for their stance on assault rifles and lobbying efforts against tighter gun laws.
Although Yeti says that their policy change on discounts is not related to the boycott, the decision was made less than two months after groups began to cut ties with the pro-gun group. Bank of America joined the movement in mid-April when the company announced that it would no longer lend money to companies which produce assault-style weapons for civilians.
rewrite:

The controversy originated from a letter issued by Marion P. Hammer of the NRA’s Institute for Legislative Action, which asserted that Yeti had severed its business relationship with the NRA Foundation and discontinued member discounts. In a statement dated April 20, Hammer contended, “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities.”

This declaration prompted a retaliatory response from numerous NRA members and supporters, who have expressed their dissatisfaction through the highly visible destruction of Yeti coolers. A series of videos circulated online depict individuals employing firearms and explosives to demolish the containers, which are retail priced between approximately $250 and $1,300. One participant, Bryan Atkinson of South Carolina, proclaimed prior to destroying his cooler, “This Yeti ain’t ready,” later reinforcing his position in a social media post by stating, “If Yeti can’t stand behind the NRA, I ain’t standing behind Yeti no more.”

In an official statement released via Facebook, the company clarified that it had notified the NRA Foundation, along with several other organizations, of the discontinuation of a specific set of legacy discount programs. Yeti emphasized that it is offering alternative partnership arrangements to affected groups and explicitly rejected the assertion that it is abandoning young firearm enthusiasts. The company maintains that its policy revision is unrelated to any political boycott.

This incident occurs within a broader context of corporate disengagement from the NRA following the February 2018 school shooting in Parkland, Florida, which resulted in seventeen fatalities. In the subsequent months, multiple entities, including several airlines and rental car companies, have dissolved institutional ties with the gun-rights organization. Public criticism of the NRA’s lobbying against stricter firearm regulations and its stance on military-style assault weapons has intensified significantly. Although Yeti denies any connection between its decision and this wider movement, its policy change was enacted less than two months after other corporations began distancing themselves. This period also saw financial institutions such as Bank of America announce they would cease lending to manufacturers of assault-style weapons for civilian use.

Sleaford First XI came agonisingly close to winning at second-placed Grantham on Saturday, eventually losing the Lincs ECB Premier League fixture by just a single run.
Grantham batted first after winning the toss but after a solid start, some determined bowling saw the innings interestingly poised at 126-5 with Andrew Jones and Adi Sreedharan each claiming two victims.
Home captain Daniel Webb helped his side post a competitive total, supervising the rest of the innings with an important knock of 66 to take the hosts to 224 from their allotted overs.
At 90-4 in Sleaford’s reply the game was in the balance, but a stand between Andy Hibberd and Shaun Morris swung the game in favour of the visitors who took themselves to within 18 runs of victory with five wickets in hand.
But Sleaford finished just short of the target despite Hibberd’s contribution of 93.
* In the South Lincs and Border League Premier, Sleaford Seconds took maximum points against Frieston to stay top.
Batting first, Sleaford posted 201-7 with Charlie Roberts (67) the principal contributor. The visitors never threatened in reply and were all out for 74, with spinners Angus Youles, Sumit Puri and Ben Hutson claiming eight wickets between them.
Sunday’s game for Sleaford Academy, sponsored by Turnbulls, brought a comprehensive 10-wicket win against Boston who were dismissed for only 39.
* Sleaford Firsts, sponsored by Baker Plant Hire, host Market Deeping on Saturday, while on Sunday, Revesby visit London Road in the Lincoln Sunday League Premier. Matchball sponsor is Michael Shaw.
