Share This: Nintendo Fans Are Still Waiting For That Pokémon RPG Announcement Jess
It feels like it’s been years since Nintendo sent Switch players the survey that revealed an upcoming, currently unnamed “Pokémon RPG” game; since dangling this respective carrot in the faces of all Pokémon fans, Nintendo has been constantly in the news for everything but the reputed Switch game—first with their announcement of a new Mario movie, and then with Pokémon Go’s release of generation 3 Pokémon. At every turn, Nintendo refuses to give fans the information we want to hear.
The last fresh Pokémon titles released were Ultra Sun and Moon—games that (according to IGN) will be the last Pokémon RPG games made for the 3DS console. Having allegedly pushed the old handhelds to the limits of their capabilities, Nintendo aims to transfer the beloved series to the Switch. Still, aside from knowing it’s “in development,” fans have heard virtually nothing about the next game in the series.
With the crowd holding their breath, it’s no surprise that the Pokémon GO’s Pokémon additions were met with frustrated sighs. We can only hope that this RPG finds ways to break whatever limits Nintendo saw in the 3DS with the Switch, a console that has already been proven to be amazing.
rewrite:
Nintendo enthusiasts continue to await an official announcement regarding the previously indicated Pokémon role-playing game (RPG) for the Switch console. This anticipation stems from a user survey distributed by Nintendo, which referenced an unnamed Pokémon RPG project. Since that initial disclosure, however, corporate communications have focused on other ventures, such as an upcoming animated film featuring the Mario franchise and the incremental addition of third-generation Pokémon to the mobile application *Pokémon GO*. Consequently, the lack of subsequent information pertaining to the purported Switch title has become a source of ongoing frustration for the fan community.

The most recent core series entries, *Pokémon Ultra Sun* and *Ultra Moon*, were released for the Nintendo 3DS. Industry analysis, including reports from IGN, suggests these titles represent the final RPG iterations for that handheld platform, having ostensibly reached its technical limitations. Nintendo’s stated intent is to migrate the primary Pokémon series to the more advanced Switch system. Beyond a confirmation that such a project is in development, substantive details remain conspicuously absent.

This protracted silence has heightened expectations, leading to a perception that ancillary updates, such as those for *Pokémon GO*, are inadequate substitutes for news of the core RPG. The collective hope is that the eventual title will leverage the Switch's demonstrated capabilities to transcend the constraints identified in the previous hardware, thereby delivering a commensurate evolutionary step for the franchise.

By ARTHUR L. MACK
Staff Writer
In anticipation of expected heavy rains, the result of a tropical disturbance that formed a few days ago and is expected to reach the Gulf Coast this weekend, the cities of Saraland and Satsuma are distributing sandbags for residents in those respective cities.
The city of Saraland will distribute sandbags at its Public Works Department, located at 150 Station Street, from 9 a.m. until 3 p.m. today (Thursday, May 24), and from 9 a.m. until 3 p.m. on Friday. Residents can receive anywhere from 10-15 bags, and depending on the weather, from 10-20 bags.
According to Warren Stephens of the Saraland Public Works Department, since the tropical system appears to be heading toward the Gulf Coast the demand for sandbags has been great.
“We’ve been kind of active this morning,” he told the Call News.
The city of Satsuma started distributing sandbags today as well, with the hours of distribution from 7 a.m. until 3:30 p.m. at the city’s Public Works facility at 5668 Second Street, located behind the police department.
According to Bridget Nolan of the city’s Public Works Department, if residents need bags after regular hours, they should call the department’s number at 251-331-1514 and ask to speak with her. As with the city of Saraland, sandbags will be distributed to residents of the city of Satsuma only. Each household will be provided up to 20 bags of sand.
“We’ll give sandbags out today, Friday, and if necessary, Saturday,” Nolan said. “If residents are elderly or disabled, we’ll deliver the sandbags to them.”
So far, the city of Chickasaw has not made a decision to distribute sandbags, as officials were still monitoring the weather. A decision is expected later this afternoon.
rewrite:
In anticipation of significant precipitation from a tropical disturbance forecasted to impact the Gulf Coast this weekend, the municipalities of Saraland and Satsuma have initiated sandbag distribution programs for their residents. The proactive measures are a direct response to the anticipated heavy rainfall associated with this meteorological system.

The City of Saraland will distribute sandbags at its Public Works Department, located at 150 Station Street. Distribution hours are scheduled from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. on Thursday, May 24, and again on Friday during the same timeframe. The quantity provided will range from ten to fifteen bags per resident, with a potential increase to twenty bags contingent upon worsening weather conditions. Warren Stephens of the Saraland Public Works Department noted a substantial demand for sandbags, attributing it to the storm’s projected path toward the Gulf Coast.

Concurrently, the City of Satsuma commenced distribution today at its Public Works facility, situated at 5668 Second Street behind the police department. Hours of operation are from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Bridget Nolan of the Satsuma Public Works Department indicated that distribution will continue through Friday and, if necessary, Saturday. Each eligible household may receive up to twenty sandbags. The city has also arranged for delivery to elderly or disabled residents upon request. For assistance outside standard hours, residents are instructed to contact the department directly. As in Saraland, this service is restricted to Satsuma residents.

Conversely, the City of Chickasaw has not yet finalized plans for sandbag distribution, with officials continuing to monitor the developing weather system. A decision is anticipated later this afternoon.

Beijing 2022 organisers have prepared a list of more than 2,000 questions to ask at next week's Pyeongchang 2018 Winter Olympic de-brief.
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) will gather in the Chinese capital from Monday (June 4) to assess this year's Winter Games which took place in South Korea in February.
It will be a key chance for Beijing to learn before their hosting duties in four years time, with IOC President Thomas Bach due to hear a report from the Chinese Organising Committee during the five-day event.
Yan Cheng, the human resources director for Beijing 2022, told China Daily the list of questions would be shared with members of the IOC delegation as well as officials from Pyeongchang.
They relate to areas including snow sport operations, he said.
"This marks the handover of Olympic hosting expertise from Pyeongchang to Beijing," said Yan.
"The share of knowledge and transfer of expertise from the Pyeongchang Organising Committee will enlighten us about the complexity of hosting the Winter Olympic Games and provide us with proven experience to facilitate our work."
Beijing 2022 leaders have already announced plans to attract more skilled international workers to play a part in the Winter Olympics and Paralympics.
The de-brief for Pyeongchang 2018 will be held next week ©Getty Images
Organisers hope to attract people to work in areas including sports management and volunteer services.
Yan told ECNS that international talent was needed as China's winter sports industry is still "relatively underdeveloped".
He also said the Organising Committee would strenghten its contact and cooperation with similar bodies overseas.
This could include attracting staff who worked at Pyeongchang 2018.
Fourteen experts from foreign countries have reportedly already helped Beijing address issues including venue planning, track design and overall logistics.
Beijing 2022 began their first extensive recruitment drive in April of last year.
It has so far led to 31 out of 3,894 applicants being appointed to various roles.
The Winter Olympics are due to run between February 4 and 20 in 2022.
The Paralympics are scheduled to follow between March 4 and 13.
Beijing itself will share the sporting action with clusters in Zhangjiakou and Yanqing.
The capital hosted the Summer Olympics and Paralympics in 2008 and will become the first city to also host the Winter editions.
rewrite:
The Beijing 2022 Organising Committee has prepared a comprehensive list exceeding two thousand questions for the forthcoming debriefing session on the PyeongChang 2018 Winter Olympic Games, scheduled for next week. This session, convened by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), will assemble in the Chinese capital commencing Monday, June 4, to conduct a formal review of the Winter Games held in South Korea this past February. The event represents a critical opportunity for Beijing to acquire operational insights prior to assuming its hosting responsibilities in four years. IOC President Thomas Bach is expected to receive a report from the Chinese Organising Committee over the course of the five-day meeting.

Yan Cheng, Human Resources Director for Beijing 2022, indicated to China Daily that the catalogue of inquiries will be disseminated to members of the IOC delegation and officials from PyeongChang, encompassing domains such as snow sport operations. Yan characterised this exchange as signifying "the handover of Olympic hosting expertise from Pyeongchang to Beijing," noting that "the share of knowledge and transfer of expertise from the Pyeongchang Organising Committee will enlighten us about the complexity of hosting the Winter Olympic Games and provide us with proven experience to facilitate our work."

Concurrently, Beijing 2022 leadership has articulated plans to recruit a greater number of skilled international personnel to contribute to both the Winter Olympics and Paralympics. Organisers aim to attract expertise in fields including sports management and volunteer services. Yan explained to ECNS that this international recruitment is necessitated by the fact that China's winter sports industry remains "relatively underdeveloped." He further stated the Committee's intention to strengthen contact and cooperation with analogous overseas bodies, a initiative that may involve attracting staff formerly employed for PyeongChang 2018. To date, fourteen foreign experts have reportedly assisted Beijing in addressing areas such as venue planning, track design, and overall logistics.

The inaugural extensive recruitment drive for Beijing 2022 commenced in April of the previous year, resulting thus far in the appointment of thirty-one individuals from 3,894 applicants to various positions. The XXIV Olympic Winter Games are scheduled for February 4 to 20, 2022, followed by the Paralympic Winter Games from March 4 to 13. Events will be hosted across Beijing and the clustered zones of Zhangjiakou and Yanqing. Having hosted the Summer Olympics and Paralympics in 2008, Beijing is poised to become the first city to host both the Summer and Winter editions of the Games.

(From L) French presidential election candidate for the far-right Front National (FN) party, Marine Le Pen, French journalist Christophe Jakubyszyn, French journalist Nathalie Saint-Cricq and French presidential election candidate for the En Marche ! movement, Emmanuel... REUTERS/Eric Feferberg/Pool
PARIS French far-right leader Marine Le Pen and her centrist rival Emmanuel Macron clashed on security in a heated debate ahead of Sunday's presidential election run-off, with Le Pen accusing Macron of being complacent on Islamist fundamentalism.
"You have no plan (on security) but you are indulgent with Islamist fundamentalism," Le Pen said during the televised debate, accusing Macron of being soft on security.
Macron retorted that terrorism would be his priority if he is elected on Sunday and accused Le Pen of being simplistic. "What you are proposing is snake oil," he said, referring to her proposals to close France's borders.
"You are telling lies," he said when Le Pen alleged he had links with controversial Muslim radicals. He accused her of sowing "civil war".
(Reporting by Ingrid Melander and Michel Rose; Editing by Adrian Croft)

Macron countered by declaring terrorism his foremost priority if elected and dismissed Le Pen’s proposals, such as closing national borders, as simplistic and ineffective. He further accused her of disseminating falsehoods by suggesting he maintained associations with controversial Muslim figures, warning that her rhetoric risked inciting civil discord. The debate highlighted the stark ideological divisions between the two candidates on issues of security and immigration ahead of the decisive vote.

Swoon all you want about that time the Mother of Dragons first met the King in the North. For a certain subset of Game of Thrones fans, Daenerys’ most important Season 7 moment took place in Sunday’s episode, when she and Ser Jorah once more breathed the same air.
“You look strong. You found a cure?” she asked, beaming. “I wouldn’t be here if I hadn’t,” he answers, equally over the moon before once more offering himself for her service.
If you want a refresher on the man who bent the knee to Dany long before anyone else did, here’s a quick backgrounder on Khaleesi and her knight. Back in Season 1, Ser Jorah Mormont attended Daenerys’ wedding to Khal Drogo. The exiled knight vowed to serve her as he’d served her father, and he stuck with her through the death of her husband and her rise to power among the Dothraki. Along the way, Jorah also fell into a deep well of admiration/romantic love for the young queen. Sadly, she didn’t feel the same.
Then there was a little jealousy, a little revealed treachery, a little banishment, a little uncurable illness and a lot of undying devotion, which brings us to this week’s “Eastwatch” and the touching reunion of two of our favorite Thrones characters.
We were so into the idea of Jorah’s return to #TeamDaenerys that we thought we’d pull together a dragon’s flight down memory lane, all the better to savor the ser’s return to his sovereign — especially if that whole Eastwatch mission goes awry. Click on the photo gallery above to revisit key moments from the ballad of Jorah and Daenerys.

Their dialogue upon his return—her noting, "You look strong. You found a cure?" and his reply, "I wouldn't be here if I hadn't,"—conveys mutual affection and renewed commitment to her service.

To contextualize this relationship: Ser Jorah Mormont first pledged fealty to Daenerys Targaryen at her wedding to Khal Drogo in Season 1, vowing to serve her as he had her father. He remained a steadfast advisor through her husband's death and her ascendance within the Dothraki culture. During this period, Jorah developed profound admiration and romantic feelings for the queen, which were not reciprocated. The subsequent narrative involved his jealousy, revealed treachery, temporary banishment, and a struggle with a greyscale infection, all underpinned by his enduring loyalty. This complex history culminates in their emotional reunion in "Eastwatch."

In anticipation of Jorah’s reinstatement to Daenerys’s counsel and given the perilous nature of the mission to Eastwatch, it is pertinent to revisit pivotal interactions between these characters. The following retrospective examines key moments in the enduring, though unrequited, devotion of Ser Jorah Mormont to his queen.

A wide group of youngsters from across the Leighton Buzzard area will be just a crazy bunch of guys and dolls when they perform one of the most popular musicals of all time.
Leighton Buzzard Youth Theatre is staging the much loved Guys and Dolls at the town’s library theatre from Friday to Saturday, November 17 to 18.
It follows on from the success the group had with previous productions Joseph and Treasure Island.
The group will take the audience back to 1950s New York with a riotous premise and plenty of laughter.
The whole area has issues with illegal gamblers and the Salvation Army is trying to make the world a more respectable place and the cops are always one step behind.
A spokesman for the group has described Guys and Dolls as a fabulous show for all the family, with toe tapping tunes all the way.
Expect to hear tunes including Luck be a Lady, Sit Down You and Rockin’ the Boat which will be tackled with the flair, energy and talent that have been showcased in previous productions by the group.
Performances start at 7.30pm each night with a matinee production taking place at 2pm on Saturday, November 18.
Tickets for the show are £9 with concession tickets available for £6.50. To book call 0300 300 8125 or visit www.leightonbuzzardlibrarytheatre.co.uk.

(Adds Finance Ministry's comments, background details)
MEXICO CITY, March 31 Mexico's finance ministry on Friday cut its 2017 growth outlook for Latin America's no. 2 economy, flagging uncertainty over U.S. policy, and said it saw inflation ending the year nearly a full percentage point above the central bank's target range.
It expects the economy to grow between 1.3 and 2.3 percent in 2017 and then rebound to expand 2.0-3.0 percent in 2018. The ministry had previously projected gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 2.0-3.0 percent in 2017 and 2.5-3.5 percent for 2018.
"Although weakness in global growth has started to dissipate, uncertainty about the new U.S. government's policy direction poses downside risks for the Mexican economy," the ministry said.
The finance ministry also said it saw annual inflation ending 2017 at 4.9 percent, above the central bank's target range, before subsiding to 3.0 percent by year-end 2018.
Mexico's central bank raised its benchmark interest rate for the fifth time in a row on Thursday, taking borrowing costs to an eight-year high to anchor inflation expectations. But policymakers slowed the pace of hikes on the back of a rally in the peso.
The finance ministry projected the peso would end 2017 at 19 per dollar and 19.1 per dollar in 2018.
It sees a fiscal deficit of 2.4 of projected gross domestic product this year and a deficit of 2.0 percent for 2018.
After running primary budget deficits since 2009, the government said it would post a primary surplus of 0.5 percent of GDP next year.
Total public sector borrowing requirements will amount to 2.5 percent of GDP in 2018, the finance ministry estimated, 0.4 percentage points lower than its 2017 level.
Mexico's central bank said on Wednesday it had transferred 321.7 billion pesos ($17 billion) of its 2016 surplus to the federal government, which will help the country pay down debt this year. (Reporting by Anthony Esposito and Veronica Gomez; Editing by Alistair Bell)
rewrite:
On March 31, the Mexican Ministry of Finance revised its economic growth projections for 2017 downward, citing policy uncertainty emanating from the United States as a principal risk factor. The Ministry further indicated that annual inflation is anticipated to conclude the year significantly above the central bank's target band. The revised forecast anticipates Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth within a range of 1.3 to 2.3 percent for 2017, a reduction from the previous estimate of 2.0 to 3.0 percent. A rebound to a range of 2.0 to 3.0 percent is projected for 2018, which also represents a downward adjustment from the earlier 2018 forecast of 2.5 to 3.5 percent. In an official statement, the Ministry noted that while weakness in global growth has begun to dissipate, "uncertainty about the new U.S. government's policy direction poses downside risks for the Mexican economy."

Concurrently, the inflation outlook for 2017 was raised to 4.9 percent, nearly a full percentage point above the upper limit of the central bank's target range, before an expected moderation to 3.0 percent by the conclusion of 2018. This revision follows a series of monetary policy adjustments, wherein the central bank increased its benchmark interest rate for a fifth consecutive time to an eight-year high, albeit at a decelerated pace following a recovery in the peso's exchange rate. The Ministry projects the peso to trade at 19.0 per U.S. dollar at the end of 2017 and 19.1 per dollar in 2018.

Regarding public finances, the Ministry forecasts a fiscal deficit equivalent to 2.4 percent of GDP for the current year, narrowing to 2.0 percent in 2018. Notably, after a sustained period of primary budget deficits since 2009, the government anticipates achieving a primary surplus of 0.5 percent of GDP in the coming year. Total public sector borrowing requirements are estimated at 2.5 percent of GDP for 2018, a reduction of 0.4 percentage points from the 2017 level. These fiscal conditions are partially supported by a transfer of 321.7 billion pesos from the central bank's 2016 surplus to the federal government, a measure intended to facilitate debt reduction.

Qatar withdraws peacekeepers from Djibouti-Eritrea border
Qatar has withdrawn its peacekeeping troops from the Djibouti-Eritrea border, the foreign ministry said on Wednesday, after years of mediating in a territorial dispute between the two African states.
“The state of Qatar informed the government of Djibouti that it has withdrawn all its troops deployed on the border line in Djiboutian territory,” a ministry statement said.
The ministry said Qatar had been an “impartial diplomatic mediator” in the dispute between Djibouti and Eritrea, which led to armed clashes in 2010.
The decision by Qatar to withdraw its troops comes as the Gulf emirate is locked in a bitter dispute with Saudi Arabia and its allies over alleged ties to Islamist extremists, a charge it denies.
Both Djibouti and Eritrea have good relations with Qatar’s leading opponents Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and have taken their side in the Gulf split.
Qatar has also played the role of mediator in other African conflicts.
It brokered a peace deal between the Khartoum government and rebels in the Red Sea coast region of Sudan, which borders Eritrea. It has tried to do the same in the conflict in Sudan’s western region of Darfur.

Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern has promised the new Government will work in partnership with Maori to solve the problems they face.
Ms Ardern was speaking today at Karetu Marae in Northland, the home marae of the new Crown-Maori Relations, Corrections and Tourism Minister, Kelvin Davis.
1 NEWS political reporter Katie Bradford reports the message from people at Karetu Marae today is that clear they want the Government to keep listening to them, visiting them and working with them to solve the problems in Northland, and facing Maori.
Ms Ardern told reporters she thinks those on the marae and the Government "absolutely agree".
"As I said yesterday with the iwi chairs, as we said when we met with members of regional and local government, we've got a lot of things that we want to achieve. And we can't do it alone, and I think we're only going to make the gains we'd like to make if we work in partnership," she said.
Asked how the Government will do that, with economic development much needed in Northland," Ms Ardern said: "Absolutely. Well firstly, by listening."
She said she and her team talked with local mayors yesterday about many issues they and local MPs see.
"And it's about uss not dictating what happens, but working together to identify the problems. Regional roads, regional employment are great examples."
The Prime Minister said the Government's provincial growth fund is a key opportunity "to say to local government what things in your area would unleash jobs? So rather than us dictating, sitting down and finding out what the opportunities are".
She said a "great and obvious example" in Northland is that the region is prime for forestry which not only creates employment opportunities, "it helps us tick off environmental goals as well".
Asked about a four-lane road to Whangarei, Ms Ardern said NZTA is looking at safety issues and she has heard the mayors when they say people's access to the region is key".
She said she's sure ministers will be sitting down with mayors to ensure access is key, but would not make a decision on such a road today.

Reporting indicates a consistent message from the community at Kēretu Marae, emphasizing a continued desire for governmental engagement through active listening, consultation, and cooperative problem-solving, particularly concerning issues prevalent in Northland and among Māori populations broadly. In response, Prime Minister Ardern affirmed a shared perspective between the Government and the marae community, stating, “As I indicated yesterday in discussions with iwi chairs, and as was echoed in our meetings with regional and local government representatives, we have substantial objectives to accomplish. These cannot be achieved in isolation; meaningful progress will be realized only through genuine partnership.”

When questioned on the mechanisms for this partnership, especially given Northland’s pressing economic development needs, the Prime Minister emphasized listening as a foundational step. She noted recent consultations with local mayors and Members of Parliament to understand regional priorities. “The approach is not one of imposition, but of collaboration to identify key challenges. Infrastructure, such as regional roads, and regional employment serve as pertinent examples,” she elaborated.

Ardern highlighted the Government’s Provincial Growth Fund as a pivotal instrument in this cooperative framework, designed to empower local governance. “It is an opportunity to inquire of local government: which initiatives in your area would catalyze job creation? The process involves joint deliberation to identify opportunities, rather than top-down prescription,” she stated. She cited forestry development in Northland as a salient example, noting its dual potential to generate employment and advance environmental sustainability objectives.

Regarding specific infrastructure, such as a proposed four-lane highway to Whangārei, the Prime Minister acknowledged that the New Zealand Transport Agency is conducting safety assessments. She recognized the emphasis local leaders place on regional accessibility, confirming that ministers will engage further with mayors to ensure this remains a priority. However, she declined to announce an immediate decision on the project, indicating that deliberations are ongoing.

By Chinedu Adonu
ENUGU – ENUGU police command on Wednesday arrested the leader of Biafra Zionists Federation, BZF, Barr. Benjamin Onwuka and 20 others who attempted to take over Enugu Government House.
The self-acclaimed President of Biafra, Barr. Benjamin Onwuka stormed the Government House as early as 7 am with Biafra flags.
The group had earlier vowed to be at the Government House today, Wednesday May 30 for the purpose of declaration of Biafra Republic.
Our correspondent reports that upon their arrival at the Government House gate, they were rounded up by security operatives. They marched from the Bissala Road axis to the area.
A combined team of security operatives made up of the DSS, anti-terrorism squad, mobile policemen, SARS, among others carried out the operation.
Onwuka and about 20 other members of the group were arrested, while others fled.
Deputy leader of the group, Mazi Ambrose Ugwu, who confirmed the arrest, said the Southeast governors would be held responsible for whatever happened to their members.
“Peace loving Zionists were today treated like common criminals by the police, who were doing the bidding of Southeast governors.
They beat our members, including our commander, like criminals.
“What happened today is very condenmable. We hold South east governors responsible. There is a collaborating among the five of them to crush Biafra agitators.
“But we are not going be cowed.
We are giving them ultimatum to release them immediately. Failure to do so, they will have the United States and other of our international allies to contend with,” Ugwu boasted.
Confirming Onwuka’s arrest the Enugu state command of the Nigeria Police Force said he was nabbed within the Enugu metropolis alongside his members based on the intelligence information.
In a statement signed by the PPRO Ebere Amaraizu, the police said
“Onwuka has been standing trial in the court of competent court of jurisdiction over his alleged role of murder,Armed Robbery and unlawful possession of firearms before he resurfaced today but fell into the hands of the eagle eyed security operatives of the command.
“Suspects are helping the operatives in their investigations,” the statement reads.
rewrite:
On Wednesday, May 30, the Enugu State Police Command arrested Barrister Benjamin Onwuka, the leader of the Biafra Zionists Federation (BZF), along with approximately twenty of his followers. The arrests occurred following an attempt by the group to forcibly enter the Enugu State Government House. Onwuka, who declares himself the President of Biafra, led the assembly to the Government House premises at approximately 7:00 a.m., carrying flags associated with the Biafran separatist movement. The group had previously publicly declared its intention to proclaim a Republic of Biafra from that location on that date.

According to eyewitness reports, upon the group's arrival at the gates of the Government House, they were apprehended by a coordinated security detail. The operatives comprised personnel from multiple agencies, including the Department of State Services (DSS), anti-terrorism units, mobile police forces, and the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS). The individuals were detained as they marched from the Bissala Road axis toward the Government House. While Onwuka and an estimated twenty others were taken into custody, a number of additional participants reportedly fled the scene.

In a subsequent statement, the Enugu State Police Public Relations Officer, Ebere Amaraizu, confirmed the arrests. The statement indicated that Onwuka was apprehended within the Enugu metropolis based on intelligence reports. It further noted that Onwuka was already undergoing trial in a court of competent jurisdiction for alleged charges including murder, armed robbery, and unlawful possession of firearms prior to this incident. The police statement concluded by asserting that the suspects are currently assisting with ongoing investigations.

A response was issued by Mazi Ambrose Ugwu, the deputy leader of the BZF, who confirmed the arrests and condemned the security forces' actions. Ugwu characterized the treatment of the group’s members, whom he described as peaceful, as akin to that of common criminals. He accused the five state governors of Nigeria’s southeastern region of collaborating to suppress Biafran agitation and held them directly responsible for the welfare of the detained individuals. Ugwu issued an ultimatum for their immediate release, warning of potential diplomatic repercussions involving the United States and other unspecified international allies, and vowed that the group would not be intimidated.

The Remains of the Day ★★★★★
6.20-9.00pm Sony Movie Channel
One of Merchant/Ivory’s best, this clever adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel. It’s told in flashback as Anthony Hopkins, the butler at stately Darlington Hall, drives to meet the hall’s former housekeeper, Emma Thompson, after many years. What unfolds is a tale of two relationships – an unstated romantic one between Hopkins and Thompson, and a master-servant one between Hopkins and the late Lord Darlington (James Fox). In the late 1930s, the well-meaning but misguided Fox, though not a fascist, was an appeaser, who – along with more sinister men – sympathised with Germany and sought to keep Britain out of the war. The almost fanatically loyal Hopkins realised too late what was going on and realised, too, that he had wasted his life in the service of an undeserving man. A brilliantly understated, unemotional performance by Hopkins is well supported by Thompson and Fox. 1930s Darlington Hall is Britain in microcosm – a feudal state ruled by the aristocracy where the working classes knew their place.
For more of today’s free-to-air films, see our TV listings
Order your copy of the Radio Times Guide to Films 2017
rewrite: A masterful adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro's novel by Merchant Ivory Productions, *The Remains of the Day* is presented in a flashback narrative. The story follows Stevens, a butler portrayed by Anthony Hopkins, as he journeys to reunite with the former housekeeper of Darlington Hall, played by Emma Thompson, after a prolonged separation. The film intricately explores two central relationships: the restrained, unspoken romantic connection between the two servants, and the complex master-servant dynamic between Stevens and his late employer, Lord Darlington (James Fox). Set against the backdrop of the late 1930s, Lord Darlington is depicted as a well-intentioned yet politically misguided aristocrat. While not a fascist, he espoused appeasement policies, sympathizing with Germany and collaborating with more malevolent figures in an effort to prevent British involvement in the impending war. Hopkins delivers a brilliantly understated performance, capturing Stevens's tragic realization of his employer's flawed character and the profound personal sacrifice of a life spent in loyal service. The microcosm of Darlington Hall reflects the broader British class structure of the era—a feudal society where the aristocracy maintained rigid control and the working classes adhered to prescribed social roles.

Melbourne Storm utility back Young Tonumaipea will quit the NRL club in July to follow his faith and become a missionary.
Storm player Young Tonumaipea in action against the New Zealand Warriors. Source: Photosport
Tonumaipea, a devout Christian, told his teammates of his plans to embark on the two-year mission and will leave after the State of Origin period.
The 25-year old premiership player will travel to Germany in July where he will teach his faith and conduct service in communities.
The Victorian has played 40 games for Melbourne since making his first-grade debut and has been a trailblazer for the game in the state.
Tonumaipea became just the second Victorian to pull on the Storm jersey back in 2014, developing through the club's underage age systems.
He has also represented his native Samoa at international level on five occasions, culminating at last year's Rugby League World Cup.
"As I have matured I've come to learn that football is not everything in my life," Tonumaipea said.

The 25-year-old premiership player is scheduled to travel to Germany, where he will engage in missionary work, including teaching and community service.

Why it matters to you Buried landmines injure tens of thousands of civilians every year. This innovative technique may help detect the explosives before they detonate.
A team of researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem have developed an innovative new method for detecting buried land mines, and it combines two unconventional tools: lasers and fluorescent bacteria.
Civilians around the world are continually impacted by live land mines left over from wartime. Detecting the land mines is difficult and removing them is obviously dangerous. And every year, between 15,000 and 20,000 people are hurt or killed by the devices. As many as 110 million buried land mines have been laid in more than 70 countries since the 1960s, according to the United Nations. Millions are still buried and unexploded.
Over the past few years, a number of creative methods have emerged for detecting and detonating land mines, including Massoud Hassani’s windblown device and drone-based system called Mine Kafon.
The new Hebrew University method is inspired by the fact that soils collect trace amounts of explosive vapors that leak out of land mines. Detecting the vapors helps detect the land mine.
The researchers genetically engineered bacteria to give off a fluorescent signals when contacted by the explosive vapors. They then packed the bacteria into small beads and sprinkled them across the top layer of a test site that had land mines buried underneath. From a safe distance, they scanned the site with a laser and successfully detected the location of the land mines. A paper detailing the study was published last week in the journal Nature Biotechnology.
“Our field data show that engineered biosensors may be useful in a land mine detection system,” said Shimshon Belkin, who was in charge of engineering the bacteria.
However, he pointed out there were a few more obstacles ahead: “For this to be possible, several challenges need to be overcome, such as enhancing the sensitivity and stability of the sensor bacteria, improving scanning speeds to cover large areas, and making the scanning apparatus more compact so it can be used on board a light unmanned aircraft or drone.”
rewrite:
The persistent global threat posed by buried landmines, which injure or kill an estimated 15,000 to 20,000 civilians annually, underscores the critical need for improved detection technologies. Since the 1960s, as many as 110 million landmines have been deployed across more than 70 nations, with millions remaining active and unexploded, according to United Nations estimates. Conventional detection and removal are fraught with difficulty and extreme danger. In response, researchers have pursued various innovative approaches, including wind-driven and drone-based systems. A recent advancement from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem introduces a novel detection methodology that integrates laser scanning with genetically engineered bacterial biosensors.

This technique exploits the phenomenon whereby buried landmines release trace explosive vapors that accumulate in the surrounding soil. Researchers, led by Professor Shimshon Belkin, genetically modified bacteria to emit a fluorescent signal upon contact with these vapors. These sensor bacteria were encapsulated into polymeric beads and distributed across the surface of a controlled test site containing buried landmines. Subsequently, the area was scanned remotely with a laser system, which successfully identified the mines’ locations by detecting the bacterial fluorescence. The study detailing this proof-of-concept was recently published in the journal *Nature Biotechnology*.

Belkin notes that the field data indicate engineered biosensors hold potential for integration into practical landmine detection systems. However, he cautions that significant technical challenges must be addressed before widespread deployment is feasible. Key obstacles include enhancing the sensitivity and environmental stability of the sensor bacteria, increasing the speed of laser scanning to survey large areas efficiently, and miniaturizing the detection apparatus for deployment on lightweight unmanned aerial vehicles or drones. Overcoming these hurdles would represent a substantial step toward a safer, more effective means of mitigating this enduring humanitarian crisis.

EpiPen auto-injection epinephrine pens manufactured by Mylan NV pharmaceutical company for use by severe allergy sufferers are seen in Washington, U.S. August 24, 2016. REUTERS/Jim Bourg/File Photo
Generic drugmaker Mylan NV said on Friday that its manufacturing partner for EpiPen devices had expanded a recall of the life-saving allergy shot in the United States and other markets.
The announcement comes a week after Mylan said it had recalled about 81,000 EpiPen devices in countries outside the United States following two reports of the company's allergy treatment failing to work in emergencies.
The recall is being initiated in the United States and will extend to Europe, Asia, North and South America, Mylan said.
The recalled product was manufactured by Meridian Medical Technologies, a Pfizer Inc company, and distributed by Mylan between December 2015 and July 2016.
Mylan, which is the focus of multiple federal investigations, has come under fire for staggering price increases on the emergency shot in the United States.
Mylan has also been heavily criticized for classifying EpiPen as a generic rather than a branded product, which led to much smaller rebates from the company to state Medicaid programs.
(Reporting by Akankshita Mukhopadhyay in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel)

On August 24, 2016, EpiPen auto-injectors, manufactured by Mylan NV for the treatment of severe allergic reactions, were documented in Washington, U.S. This image is credited to REUTERS/Jim Bourg. This action follows a prior recall initiated one week earlier, wherein approximately 81,000 EpiPen devices were withdrawn from markets outside the United States. The current recall, commencing in the United States, is slated to extend to regions including Europe, Asia, and North and South America. This classification resulted in markedly reduced rebates provided to state Medicaid programs.

Netflix is trialling an expensive new membership tier that will anger those already paying for Premium access. That's because it removes high dynamic range support from Premium and charges more per month for HDR and Dolby Vision video under a new Ultra tier. Potentially, a lot more.
In addition, in some trial locations, Premium subscribers have had the number of concurrent devices able to view Netflix halved.
At present, the Premium tier, which is priced at £9.99 per month in the UK, allows for viewing on up to four screens at once, plus gives access to 4K HDR content - in Dolby Vision too if your TV supports it.
If the Ultra tier is rolled out after the trials, Premium subscribers will no longer get HDR support. They will still get Ultra HD resolutions where applicable, but supporting shows and films won't display the better contrast and colour range on offer with HDR.
To get HDR, subscribers would have to pay extra. The Ultra tier is being tested at €16.99 in Europe, which equates to £14.99 in the UK.
The trial version of the Ultra tier also offers access for up to four devices at once, and in some regions that has pushed Premium down to just two. And those on the Standard tier found their access limited to just the one device at a time, down from two.
A Netflix spokesperson told CNET that the new tier tests are part of a usual process to understand its customer needs: "We continuously test new things at Netflix and these tests typically vary in length of time," said Smita Saran.
"In this case, we are testing slightly different price points and features to better understand how consumers value Netflix."
She also said that there is a chance the new tier may never fully roll out.
rewrite:
Netflix is currently conducting trials of a new, higher-priced subscription tier, a move likely to frustrate existing Premium subscribers. This is because the trial involves removing high dynamic range (HDR) support, including Dolby Vision, from the Premium tier and placing it within a proposed "Ultra" tier at a significantly increased monthly cost. Concurrently, in certain test markets, the number of simultaneous streams permitted for Premium subscribers has been reduced by half.

Presently, the Premium tier, priced at £9.99 monthly in the United Kingdom, permits viewing on up to four devices simultaneously and includes access to 4K Ultra HD content with HDR and Dolby Vision, where supported by the user's display. Should the Ultra tier be implemented following these trials, Premium subscribers would retain Ultra HD resolution but would lose access to HDR. Consequently, compatible films and series would no longer display the enhanced contrast and expanded colour gamut characteristic of HDR technology. To regain this feature, subscribers would be required to pay an additional fee; the Ultra tier is being tested in Europe at €16.99, approximately £14.99 in the UK.

The experimental Ultra tier also allows for four concurrent streams. However, its introduction in some regions has resulted in the Premium tier being downgraded to only two simultaneous streams. Furthermore, subscribers on the Standard tier in these test areas have seen their allowance reduced from two streams to just one. A Netflix spokesperson, Smita Saran, informed CNET that these tests are part of standard operations to gauge customer preferences, stating, "We continuously test new things at Netflix and these tests typically vary in length of time. In this case, we are testing slightly different price points and features to better understand how consumers value Netflix." Saran also noted that there remains a possibility the new Ultra tier may not be launched widely following the trial period.

The trade in illegal drugs contributes an estimated 0.1 percent of France's GDP, earning 2.7 billion euros, according to the national statistical institute, Insee.
The figures are based on the findings of a government agency poll and could be an underestimate, according to Insee statisticians, since some respondents may have distrusted the pollsters.
An estimated 3.1 billion euros-worth of drugs are consumed in France each year, according to the findings, but 400 million euros represent imports and so must be subtracted and credited to the GDP of the exporting countries, leaving a balance of 2.7 billion euros.
France's trade in cannabis is worth a billion euros and that in cocaine 800 million euros, according to the estimates.
The statistics are the first ever produced in France on the contribution of drug trafficking to the economy.
Refusal to count prostitution
They arise from a request from the EU's Eurostat institute to include the proceeds of the drug trade and prostitution in GDP figures, because they are legal in some countries, such as the Netherlands, and so already included in those countries' official statistics.
The change has been responsible for a considerable rise in the official GDP of some countries, espacially Italy and Spain.
Eurostat defined the drug trade and prostitution as commercial transactions that have been freely entered into.
President Emmanuel Macron's government has ended prison terms for cannabis use, on the grounds that they were ineffective, but has not legalised consumption or sale of the drug.
Insee has refused to include prostitution in its figures, arguing that "street prostitution is notoriously practiced by people who are usually undocumented, often minors and controlled by secret networks that have brought them to France".
A 33-year-old man was shot dead on Tuesday night in Menton, a town on the Italian border, in what is believed to be a drug-related killing.
Another man, who went to a hospital with injuries to his legs, has been detained as his role in the shooting is clarified.
rewrite:
According to the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (Insee), the illicit drug trade contributes an estimated 0.1 percent to France’s Gross Domestic Product, representing approximately 2.7 billion euros. These figures, derived from a government agency survey, are potentially an underestimate, as Insee statisticians acknowledge that respondent distrust of pollsters may have compromised data accuracy. The analysis indicates an annual consumption of drugs valued at 3.1 billion euros within France. However, 400 million euros of this total constitutes imports, which are subtracted from the domestic calculation and attributed to the exporting nations' GDP, resulting in the net balance of 2.7 billion euros. The estimates further specify that the cannabis trade accounts for one billion euros, while cocaine accounts for 800 million euros. This constitutes the first official statistical evaluation in France of the economic contribution of drug trafficking.

The production of these statistics originates from a directive by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union, which requested member states to incorporate the proceeds of both the drug trade and prostitution into national GDP calculations. This harmonization effort is justified on the grounds that such activities are legal in certain member states, such as the Netherlands, and are therefore already included in their official economic accounts. The methodological adjustment has precipitated a significant increase in the reported GDP of several countries, notably Italy and Spain. Eurostat classifies both the drug trade and prostitution as voluntary commercial transactions.

The French government under President Emmanuel Macron has discontinued prison sentences for cannabis use, deeming them ineffective, though it has not legalized either consumption or sale. Insee has, however, declined to incorporate prostitution into its economic figures. The institute justifies this exclusion by arguing that street prostitution is predominantly conducted by individuals who are typically undocumented, frequently minors, and controlled by covert networks responsible for their presence in France. In a related incident underscoring the violent dimensions of the illicit drug market, a 33-year-old man was fatally shot in Menton, a town on the Italian border, on Tuesday night in a suspected drug-related homicide. A second individual, who presented at a hospital with leg injuries, has been detained as authorities investigate his potential involvement in the shooting.

Nearly 40 years after the Summer Olympics brought festive crowds and top athletes from all over the world to Soviet Moscow, the Russian capital is again in the spotlight, hosting another major sports event, the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Check out Sputnik's gallery to discover how these epic tournaments have changed the city.
On June 14, the 2018 FIFA World Cup kicked off in Russia for the first time in the country's history with a colorful opening ceremony at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium. Football matches will be played all throughout the country until July 15, when the final takes place. At this very stadium, on July 19, 1980, the Olympic flame was lit, commencing the 1980 Summer Games. This is not the only thing that these two sports festivals have in common, although a lot has changed over the last four decades – even the country's name is different. From happy fans to top athletes and celebrations — Sputnik's has picked the highlights.
rewrite: Four decades after the 1980 Summer Olympics drew international athletes and celebratory crowds to Soviet Moscow, the Russian capital has returned to the global stage by hosting the 2018 FIFA World Cup. This presentation examines the city's transformation through these two landmark sporting events. The World Cup commenced on June 14 at Moscow’s Luzhniki Stadium, with matches scheduled across the nation until the final on July 15. Notably, this same venue hosted the opening ceremony of the 1980 Summer Games on July 19 of that year. While these spectacles share a common scale and setting, the intervening forty years have brought profound change, including the nation’s very designation. The following gallery curates defining moments, from athletic excellence to public festivity, illustrating both continuity and evolution.

LONDON — Alexis Sanchez is off the mark for Manchester United.
On his Old Trafford debut, the recruit from Arsenal tapped in the rebound after his penalty was saved to seal United's 2-0 victory over Huddersfield in the English Premier League on Saturday.
Romelu Lukaku also netted for United, which seized the chance to close the gap on Manchester City to a still-vast 13 points after the leader was held by Burnley to 1-1.
City defender Danilo looked like proving an unlikely match-winner but after a glaring miss for a second by Raheem Sterling, Johann Berg Gudmundsson levelled late.
City has dropped points only four times, but three of those games were the most recent away trips.
It will still take a monumental collapse for City manager Pep Guardiola to miss out on his first English title.
The tussle to stay in the Premier League is far tighter.
Southampton escaped the relegation zone after winning at West Bromwich Albion 3-2 to end a 13-match winless run in the league. Swansea is out of the danger zone only on goal difference after drawing with Leicester 1-1.
But Stoke sunk back into the bottom three after Bournemouth followed up recent fine wins against Arsenal and Chelsea by beating the less illustrious opposition 2-1. Bournemouth climbed to ninth ahead of Everton, which was at Arsenal in the late game.
Brighton ended West Ham's six-match unbeaten run by winning 3-1 to move three points clear of the drop zone.
rewrite:
Alexis Sanchez registered his inaugural goal for Manchester United during the club’s Premier League fixture against Huddersfield Town on Saturday. Making his home debut at Old Trafford, the recent acquisition from Arsenal converted on the rebound after his initial penalty kick was saved, thereby securing a 2-0 victory for his side. Romelu Lukaku also scored for United, which capitalized on an opportunity to reduce the deficit behind league leaders Manchester City to thirteen points. This followed City’s 1-1 draw with Burnley, a match in which defender Danilo nearly emerged as an unexpected match-winner. A late equalizer from Johann Berg Gudmundsson canceled out City’s advantage after Raheem Sterling had missed a clear opportunity to extend the lead. Although Manchester City has dropped points on only four occasions this season, three of those instances have occurred in their most recent away matches. Nevertheless, it would require a substantial collapse for manager Pep Guardiola to be deprived of his first English league title.

The contest to avoid relegation remains considerably more competitive. Southampton exited the relegation zone by defeating West Bromwich Albion 3-2, ending a thirteen-match winless streak. Swansea City moved out of the bottom three only on goal difference following a 1-1 draw with Leicester City. Conversely, Stoke City fell back into the relegation places after a 2-1 loss to Bournemouth, which built upon recent victories over Arsenal and Chelsea. Bournemouth’s win elevated them to ninth position, surpassing Everton. Meanwhile, Brighton & Hove Albion concluded West Ham United’s six-match unbeaten run with a 3-1 victory, moving three points clear of the relegation zone.

Logo of Tencent is displayed at a news conference in Hong Kong, China March 22, 2017. REUTERS/Tyrone Siu
HONG KONG Chinese tech giant Tencent Holdings has signed a $4.65 billion loan deal, Basis Point reported, amid a flurry of fund-raising by China's internet giants.
Tencent, which had an original target of about $2 billion for the loan, inked the deal on March 24 following commitments from a dozen banks, Thomson Reuters publication Basis Point reported, citing sources.
The loans for general corporate purposes comprise a $2.79 billion term loan and a $1.86 billion revolving credit. Citigroup was the coordinator, mandated lead arranger and bookrunner of the facility.
Tencent, best known for its WeChat mobile app, has been on an investment drive in a wide array of sectors such as gaming, entertainment, cloud computing and online financing.
It reported net profit of 41.1 billion yuan ($5.97 billion) last year on Wednesday, up 43 percent, on revenue that rose 48 percent to 151.94 billion yuan.
Tencent raised $7.94 billion in two syndicated loans in the past nine months, including $3.5 billion in October to back a deal for a majority stake in Finnish mobile game developer Supercell Oy.
Tencent did not immediately respond to requests for comment when contacted by Reuters.
(Reporting by Carol Zhong and Sijia Jiang; Writing by Sijia Jiang; Editing by Stephen Coates)
rewrite:
On March 22, 2017, the corporate logo of Tencent Holdings was displayed at a press conference in Hong Kong, China. According to a report from the Thomson Reuters publication Basis Point, the Chinese technology conglomerate Tencent Holdings has finalized a syndicated loan agreement valued at $4.65 billion. This transaction occurs amidst a period of substantial capital raising initiatives undertaken by major Chinese internet corporations. Basis Point, citing unnamed sources, indicated that the agreement was signed on March 24, following commitments from approximately twelve financial institutions, exceeding an initial target of approximately $2 billion.

The financing facility, designated for general corporate purposes, consists of a $2.79 billion term loan and a $1.86 billion revolving credit facility. Citigroup acted as the coordinator, mandated lead arranger, and bookrunner for this arrangement. Tencent, widely recognized for its WeChat mobile application, has pursued an expansive investment strategy across diverse sectors including gaming, entertainment, cloud computing, and online finance. The company's recent financial performance, reported on Wednesday, showed a 43 percent increase in net profit to 41.1 billion yuan ($5.97 billion), with revenue rising 48 percent to 151.94 billion yuan.

This latest financing follows two prior syndicated loans within the preceding nine months, which collectively raised $7.94 billion. One such prior facility, a $3.5 billion loan arranged in October, supported the acquisition of a majority stake in the Finnish mobile game developer Supercell Oy. Reuters reported that Tencent did not provide an immediate response to requests for comment regarding the current loan agreement.

Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester takes part in a panel convened to speak about the health of the U.S. economy in New York November 18, 2015. REUTERS/Lucas Jackson
A Federal Reserve policymaker on Thursday repeated her call for further rate hikes and a trimming of the central bank's balance sheet later this year, as the U.S. economy is expected to rebound from what looks like a weak first quarter.
"If economic conditions evolve as anticipated, I believe further removal of accommodation via increases in the fed funds rate will be needed," said Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester, a hawkish policymaker who regains a vote on interest rates next year. "I would (also) be comfortable changing our reinvestment policy this year."
The Fed raised rates in mid-March, its second policy tightening in three months. The central bank has also been topping up a $4.5 trillion portfolio of bonds amassed in the wake of the financial crisis, but plans to eventually begin shrinking it by letting the assets mature.
While the economy has been expanding at a 2-percent rate over the last few years, the Atlanta Fed's GDPNow forecast predicts it dipped to 1 percent in the first three months of the year.
Yet the "underlying fundamentals supporting the economic expansion are sound," Mester added in prepared remarks to a financial risk conference in Chicago. "While growth in the first quarter may come in on the weak side, I think this largely reflects transitory factors and residual seasonality in the data."
(Reporting by Jonathan Spicer; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama)
rewrite:
In a panel discussion concerning the condition of the U.S. economy held in New York on November 18, 2015, Cleveland Federal Reserve President Loretta Mester delivered remarks. REUTERS/Lucas Jackson

On Thursday, a Federal Reserve official reiterated her advocacy for additional increases to the benchmark interest rate and for initiating a reduction of the central bank’s balance sheet later in the year. This position is predicated on an anticipated economic rebound following an apparently weak first quarter. Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester, a policymaker with a hawkish stance who will regain a vote on the Federal Open Market Committee next year, stated, “If economic conditions evolve as anticipated, I believe further removal of accommodation via increases in the federal funds rate will be required.” She further indicated, “I would also be comfortable changing our reinvestment policy this year.”

The Federal Reserve implemented a rate increase in mid-March, representing its second monetary policy tightening within a three-month period. The central bank has maintained a $4.5 trillion portfolio of securities acquired following the financial crisis through reinvestment, though it intends to eventually commence balance sheet normalization by ceasing reinvestments and allowing assets to mature.

Although the economy has grown at approximately a two percent annual rate in recent years, the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model projects growth decelerated to about one percent in the first quarter. Nonetheless, in prepared remarks for a financial risk conference in Chicago, Mester asserted that the “underlying fundamentals supporting the economic expansion are sound.” She added, “While growth in the first quarter may come in on the weak side, I think this largely reflects transitory factors and residual seasonality in the data.”

(Reporting by Jonathan Spicer; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama)

A last-minute try to All Blacks Sevens speedster Joe Ravouvou has handed a sub-par All Blacks Sevens side a 17-12 victory over Argentina and guaranteed them top spot in their Hamilton Sevens pool.
New Zealand's Regan Ware in action against France on day one of the Hamilton Sevens. Source: Photosport
It was all looking a bit grim for the Kiwis heading into the dying moments of their Waikato showdown until Ravouvou broke down the right to crash over.
They had been trailing 12-5 after first-half Luciano Gonzalez and Felipe del Mestre tries handed a valiant Argentinian side the ascendancy.
But tries to Vilimoni Koroi and Ravouvou turned it around late on.
Undefeated across Saturday's pool play, the All Blacks Sevens will now go on to face England in Sunday's quarter-final after the latter's loss to South Africa.
It was a solid day for Clark Laidlaw's troops.
In Saturday's earlier matches, the Kiwis demolished France 52-7, while a Koroi playmaking masterclass guided them to a 24-5 win over Scotland.
The Otago-based teen was in stunning form against the Scots, setting up first-half tries to Tim Mikkelson and captain Scott Curry before scoring his own.
Scotland eventually beat out Argentina and France to a quarter-final berth via head-to-head after all three sides finished pool play on five points.
They'll play the fearsome Blitzbokke, who made light work of the English in Pool B's afternoon crunch match with a 28-7 triumph.
Elsewhere, Australia failed to secure top spot in Pool A after going down 26-15 in a winner-takes-all clash with Olympic gold medallists Fiji.
In a seesawing clash, the two sides traded tries until Fiji pulled away in the second half with a long-range Jasa Veremalua effort and an Eroni Sau clincher.
They'll go on to face Pacific neighbours Samoa in Sunday's quarter-finals, while the Sydney Sevens-winning Australians will take on Kenya.
SUNDAY'S HAMILTON SEVENS QUARTER-FINALS:
- Fiji vs Samoa
- South Africa vs Scotland
- New Zealand vs England
rewrite:
A last-minute try by All Blacks Sevens speedster Joe Ravouvou secured a 17-12 victory for a below-par New Zealand side over Argentina, guaranteeing them top position in their pool at the Hamilton Sevens. The outcome appeared uncertain for the New Zealand team until the final moments of the match at Waikato Stadium, when Ravouvou broke down the right flank to score. Argentina had established a 12-5 lead following first-half tries from Luciano Gonzalez and Felipe del Mestre, demonstrating determined play. However, subsequent tries by Vilimoni Koroi and Ravouvou in the latter stages overturned the deficit.

Having remained undefeated throughout Saturday’s pool matches, the All Blacks Sevens will advance to a quarter-final encounter with England on Sunday, following England’s loss to South Africa. The team, under the guidance of coach Clark Laidlaw, experienced a successful opening day. In earlier fixtures, New Zealand delivered a commanding 52-7 victory over France, while a playmaking masterclass from Koroi guided them to a 24-5 win against Scotland. The teenage player from Otago was particularly impressive versus Scotland, contributing to first-half tries for Tim Mikkelson and captain Scott Curry before crossing for one himself.

Scotland ultimately progressed to the quarter-finals ahead of Argentina and France via a head-to-head tiebreaker, after all three sides concluded pool play with five points. They will face South Africa’s formidable Blitzboks, who dispatched England 28-7 in the decisive Pool B afternoon match. Meanwhile, in Pool A, Australia failed to secure top position after a 26-15 defeat in a winner-takes-all contest against Olympic gold medallists Fiji. In a closely contested encounter, the teams exchanged tries until Fiji secured the result in the second half through a long-range effort from Jasa Veremalua and a decisive score by Eroni Sau. Fiji will now meet Pacific neighbours Samoa in the quarter-finals, while Australia, the recent Sydney Sevens champions, will face Kenya.

[India], Mar. 20 (ANI): The fear of failure is so high among students taking the Uttar Pradesh Board examinations that some of them turned to desperate measures like attaching notes on their answer sheets.
Currency notes of Rs 100, Rs 50 and Rs 500 were found in answer sheets during the checking of 12th board examination papers in Firozabad district.
The teachers said, "Students, whose exams did not go well, are attaching currency notes in the examination papers to bribe us. We are giving marks only on merit. None of us are accepting the money found in the answer sheets."
Another thing that came to light was that the CCTV cameras that were installed inside the examination centres were not working as their connection wires were damaged. When teachers were asked about the same, they refused to comment on it. Recently, in a related but different episode, a video went viral, wherein a miscreant brandishing gun can be seen inside an examination hall for facilitating the students to cheat. The incident took place at Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar University in Agra. Vice-Chancellor Dr Arvind Kumar Dixit said that the matter would be probed with the help of administration and police force. (ANI)
rewrite:
On March 20, reports emerged from India detailing significant malpractice surrounding the Uttar Pradesh Board examinations. A profound fear of academic failure has compelled some students to resort to bribery, with currency notes of various denominations discovered attached to answer sheets during the evaluation of twelfth-grade papers in Firozabad district. Invigilators confirmed that these funds were intended as illicit inducements for higher marks. They emphasized, however, that all grading is conducted strictly on merit and that no bribes have been accepted.

Concurrently, it was revealed that surveillance systems within certain examination centers were non-operational due to damaged wiring, a point on which staff declined to elaborate. This follows a separate but related incident at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University in Agra, where a viral video depicted an individual wielding a firearm inside an examination hall, allegedly to facilitate cheating. University Vice-Chancellor Dr. Arvind Kumar Dixit has stated that the matter will be formally investigated in coordination with administrative and police authorities.

MIAMI (CBSMiami) – Former athletes and a Florida developer are teaming up for a good cause.
Furniture and household items are being moved out from the Estates at Acqualina, a Sunny Isles Beach resort undergoing a massive renovation, and donated to two Florida foundations.
Laura and Jorge Posada’s foundation for Puerto Rico have joined Derek Jeter’s Turn2 foundation to get the donated household items to hurricane victims in Puerto Rico, Miami and Key West.
Posada and Jeter were teammates for years while playing baseball for the New York Yankees.
“Now I can also say that I am Derek Jeter’s teammate because we are working together to benefit all those who were affected by the natural disasters,” Laura said.
“I’m going to donate furniture to families who were affected in the keys and also donate furniture to families from Puerto Rico to a newly located to the Miami area,” added Jeter said.
“Now we want to construct, and how about people who have lost it all?” Jorge said. “So this is another step in our rebuilding part.”
More than 125 pieces are being donated by the estates at Acqualina.
This as the developers begin demolition to build the new estates on property where another Yankees legend, Babe Ruth, vacationed and put on the map.
“It’s only fitting that these two modern day legends continue a Yankee tradition by leading us all to community service consistent with the values of their organizations,” said Jules Trump, Developer at Acqualina.
Furniture and appliances are being moved out and sorted, and they are going to be shipped out to Puerto Rico.
Families should be receiving them by the beginning of next year.
rewrite:
A collaborative philanthropic initiative involving former professional athletes and a Florida-based developer is currently underway. The Estates at Acqualina, a resort in Sunny Isles Beach undergoing extensive renovation, is donating its surplus furniture and household items. These goods are being allocated to two charitable foundations: the Turn2 Foundation, established by Derek Jeter, and the foundation for Puerto Rico led by Laura and Jorge Posada. The collective aim is to distribute these items to assist households impacted by recent hurricanes in Puerto Rico, Miami, and Key West.

The partnership leverages a pre-existing relationship, as Jorge Posada and Derek Jeter were formerly teammates on the New York Yankees baseball team. Laura Posada emphasized the continuation of this collaborative spirit, stating, “Now I can also say that I am Derek Jeter’s teammate because we are working together to benefit all those who were affected by the natural disasters.” Jeter outlined the distribution plan, noting furniture will be provided to affected families in the Florida Keys and to displaced Puerto Rican families now residing in the Miami area. Jorge Posada framed the effort as a component of broader reconstruction, posing the question, “how about people who have lost it all? So this is another step in our rebuilding part.”

In total, over 125 pieces are being donated. This charitable action coincides with the commencement of demolition on the property, a site historically associated with another Yankees legend, Babe Ruth. Jules Trump, the developer for Acqualina, remarked on the symbolic continuity, noting it is “only fitting that these two modern day legends continue a Yankee tradition by leading us all to community service consistent with the values of their organizations.” The donated furniture and appliances are presently being organized for shipment, with delivery to recipient families anticipated by the start of the coming year.

WASHINGTON — The Environmental Protection Agency plans to restrict research used in developing regulations, the agency said Tuesday, a change that could affect rules governing everything from household products to power-plant emissions.
The proposal follows years of complaints by conservatives that regulations such as emissions restrictions under the Obama administration sometimes went beyond what science could prove. The new proposal would exclude the many research studies that don’t make their raw data public and limit the use of findings that can’t be reproduced by others. The EPA said this would boost transparency.
“When you have studies that you actually publish from third parties, but you don’t publish the methodology, and you don’t publish the data, you only publish the conclusions, that presents problems to those that want to offer comment on the veracity, the authenticity, the ability to assess and evaluate the conclusions that have been drawn,” Administrator Scott Pruitt said before signing the proposed rule.
The proposal is subject to a public-comment period of at least 30 days and is likely to see legal challenges, which could delay or prevent its implementation. The move prompted an uproar from scientists who say it would exclude so much research that the resulting rules would endanger Americans’ health. Ahead of the announcement, a coalition of 985 scientists issued a statement decrying the plan.
An expanded version of this report appears on WSJ.com.
Also popular on WSJ.com:
Amazon to start offering in-car deliveries.
How to dress like a billionaire.
rewrite:
The Environmental Protection Agency announced on Tuesday its intention to implement new restrictions on the scientific research utilized in the formulation of regulatory policy. This shift could significantly influence a broad spectrum of rules, encompassing standards for household chemicals as well as emissions from industrial facilities such as power plants.

This initiative responds to longstanding criticisms from conservative circles, which have argued that certain past regulations, including emissions limits established during the Obama administration, were at times predicated on scientific evidence deemed insufficiently transparent. The proposed policy would predominantly exclude from consideration epidemiological and other studies that do not publicly disclose their underlying raw data. Furthermore, it would constrain the reliance on scientific findings that cannot be independently replicated. The agency contends that these measures will enhance the transparency and accountability of the regulatory process.

Administrator Scott Pruitt, prior to endorsing the draft rule, emphasized concerns regarding the evaluation of research where only conclusions, and not methodologies or primary data, are available for public scrutiny. The proposal will now undergo a mandatory public-comment period of no less than thirty days. It is anticipated to face legal challenges, which may obstruct or delay its enactment. The announcement has provoked strong opposition from segments of the scientific community. A coalition of 985 scientists, in a preemptive statement, condemned the plan, arguing that it would disqualify a substantial body of vital public health research, thereby potentially leading to weaker regulations and increased health risks for the American public.

Puebla, Mexico, October 6, 2017 ( venezuelanalysis.com ) – Venezuelan electoral authorities completed Friday an audit of voting infrastructure, ahead of elections later this month.
According to state media outlet AVN, the National Electoral Council was set to complete its checks of Venezuela’s voting booths and other voting equipment, as the October 15 regional vote draws closer. The previous day, the CNE said it had audited their software, along with servers used by the country’s electronic voting system.
The final preparations were being made amid an ongoing controversy over last minute changes to ballots. The opposition has accused the CNE of failing to remove candidates who lost their primaries last month. Critics have warned that if the candidates remain on the ballots, opposition supporters could cast votes for candidates that aren’t technically in the race anymore, leaving their ballots null.
The controversy has even pulled in Canada, which issued a statement demanding the CNE scrub the null candidates from ballots.
“All political parties must be allowed to replace candidates according to the law ... Canada calls on the CNE to make decisions in full respect of the electoral law,” Canada’s embassy said.
On Wednesday the Supreme Court's Electoral Tribunal ruled that the CNE should accept candidate changes and modifications up to ten days before the elections. However, the decision has been criticised by opposition spokespeople as too little too late. They say that there is no longer time to make the substitutions, while the CNE has yet to officially comment.
But the candidate replacement issue isn’t the only controversy. The opposition has also accused the CNE of quietly shuttering 77 voting stations. Opposition leaders claim the closures were concentrated in areas that typically vote against the government.
Thought the CNE has not responded to the allegations, the President of the Council of Electoral Experts [CEELA] Nicanor Moscoso said Thursday that Venezuela’s voting system remains one of the best in the world.
“It is the safest method, and nobody can manipulate the information given by the voting machine,” he said.
According to teleSUR, Moscoso also praised the automated system as “extraordinary”.
The CNE signed an agreement with CEELA Thursday, and confirmed that the body will formally observe the country's upcoming elections.
The vote will take place on October 15, and will see the election of new governors and state legislators.
rewrite:
On October 6, 2017, in Puebla, Mexico, Venezuelan electoral authorities concluded an audit of the nation's voting infrastructure in preparation for regional elections scheduled for October 15. According to the state media outlet Agencia Venezolana de Noticias (AVN), the National Electoral Council (CNE) finalized its verification of voting booths and associated equipment. This procedural step followed an audit conducted the previous day, which examined the software and servers integral to the country's electronic voting system.

These final preparations occurred amidst significant controversy regarding last-minute modifications to electoral ballots. Opposition groups have alleged that the CNE failed to remove candidates who were unsuccessful in primary elections held the previous month. Critics contend that retaining these candidates on the ballot risks invalidating votes, as supporters may inadvertently select individuals who are no longer formally contesting the elections. This dispute has attracted international attention, with the Canadian embassy issuing a statement urging the CNE to adhere to electoral law and facilitate the lawful replacement of candidates.

On Wednesday, October 4, the Supreme Court's Electoral Tribunal issued a ruling permitting the CNE to accept candidate changes and modifications up to ten days prior to the election. However, opposition spokespeople have criticized this decision as insufficient and untimely, arguing that the window for implementing such substitutions has effectively closed. The CNE has not provided an official response to these criticisms.

Beyond the candidate replacement issue, further allegations have emerged from opposition leaders, who accuse the CNE of closing 77 voting stations. They assert these closures are disproportionately concentrated in regions with historically strong opposition support. While the CNE has not publicly addressed these specific claims, Nicanor Moscoso, President of the Council of Electoral Experts of Latin America (CEELA), offered commentary on Thursday. Moscoso affirmed that Venezuela's voting system remains among the most robust globally, describing the automated process as "extraordinary" and emphasizing that the information from voting machines is secure from manipulation.

The CNE formalized its relationship with CEELA through an agreement signed on Thursday, confirming that the international body will serve as an official observer for the upcoming elections. These elections, set for October 15, will determine the selection of new governors and state legislators across Venezuela.
