KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- It has been nearly five months since a massive fire burned a historic church near Truman and Troost. On Sunday, the congregation came together for a special Easter service.
The congregation met at their temporary new location in Neiman Elementary School in Shawnee.
"We brought in some screens and some different things just make it a little different. And being a gymnasium like this is challenging but it's been good," said John Crane, the Senior Pastor at Evangelistic Center Church.
Pastor Crane is a third generation pastor and grew up spending Easter at Evangelistic Center Church. He said the community has really come together to support the church since the fire in November.
"I just believe in this process, as difficult as it has been, that there is a greater purpose in it and we are going to find that out as we seek it," said Crane.
Easter last year was spent in the historic church built more than 50 years ago on Troost and Truman.
Crane said they are now actively looking at different properties and pursuing new locations. They hope to be out of the temporary location by next Easter.
rewrite:
A significant fire occurred nearly five months ago at the historic Evangelistic Center Church, located near the intersection of Truman Road and Troost Avenue in Kansas City, Missouri. This past Sunday, the congregation assembled for a dedicated Easter service at their provisional venue within Neiman Elementary School in Shawnee. Senior Pastor John Crane, a third-generation minister who observed Easter at this church throughout his upbringing, noted the adaptive measures undertaken for the occasion. He acknowledged the challenges of convening in a gymnasium but affirmed the community's supportive response following the November incident.

Pastor Crane expressed a theological perspective on the adversity, stating a belief in a greater purpose emerging from the difficult process, which the congregation intends to discern through continued seeking. The previous year's Easter observance was held within the original church structure, which had stood for over fifty years. Currently, the church is actively evaluating potential properties and pursuing permanent relocation options. The objective is to transition from the temporary facility by the time of the next Easter celebration.

Shocking pictures reveal the devastating effect prosecco can have on your teeth.
Everyone’s favorite fizz turns teeth into a “chalk like powder” according to an alarming new study.
Dental scientists from the Oral Health Foundation left healthy human molars and incisors in the Italian sparkling wine for 14 days.
Prosecco is known for having a triple threat to your pearly whites for acidic bubbles, alcohol and a high sugar content.
And as we enter the party season more and more people will be knocking back the fizz.
But the study might make drinkers think again after the tooth was completely destroyed after being immersed in prosecco for a fortnight.
Dr. Ben Atkins told the Daily Mail: “If I were to pick the tooth up, it would likely turn to a chalk-like powder in my hand.”
“This could be extremely painful, leading to a need for extensive restoration or extraction.”
“Prosecco’s high sugar [and acid] content hits drinkers with a double whammy of erosion and decay. At Christmas, if we are sipping a drink throughout the day, our teeth are under constant attack.”
Cola was also tested in the study and was shown to have an “extreme” and “shocking” effect on teeth.
Worries over the soft beverage lead to it being banned from school vending machines and cafeterias in a bid to keep kids’ teeth healthy.
Atkins said: “Apart from the extensive staining, turning the tooth brown after only two days, it has also completely cracked in half owing to the huge extent of demineralization which has made it weak.
“The effects on young teeth can very quickly become extreme, devastating future oral health. With 12 spoons of sugar in a typical can of a cola-like drink, the decay potential is almost off the scale.”
Back in August the worries of the “prosecco smile” were revealed by a top London dentist.
Dr. Mervyn Druian said: “It is acidic and it has sugar in it so, while a few glasses are fine, if you drink too much of it you are going to have a problem. The signs of prosecco smile are where the teeth come out of the gum.”
“It starts with a white line just below the gum, which if you probe it is a little bit soft and that is the beginning of tooth decay which can lead to fillings and dental work.”
rewrite:
A recent investigation has documented the considerable dental damage associated with regular consumption of prosecco. Research conducted by the Oral Health Foundation demonstrates that this popular sparkling wine poses a significant risk to dental integrity. In the experimental protocol, sound human molars and incisors were immersed in prosecco for a period of fourteen days. The beverage presents a triple threat to enamel due to its combination of carbonation, acidity, alcohol, and a substantial sugar content. These factors collectively accelerate the processes of erosion and decay.

The findings indicate severe deterioration following prolonged exposure. Dr. Ben Atkins, commenting on the results to the Daily Mail, noted that the affected tooth structure became so compromised that it could potentially disintegrate into a chalk-like powder upon handling. Such advanced degradation would likely result in considerable pain and necessitate extensive restorative treatment or possibly extraction. Dr. Atkins further emphasized that the high sugar and acid content creates a compounded damaging effect. During extended social periods, such as the holiday season, frequent sipping can subject the dentition to sustained attack, significantly increasing the risk of harm.

For comparative purposes, the study also examined the impact of cola, which exhibited similarly extreme and deleterious effects on dental specimens. Concerns regarding such soft drinks have previously prompted their removal from school vending machines and cafeterias to protect juvenile oral health. Dr. Atkins observed that cola not only caused pronounced staining, darkening the tooth within two days, but also induced severe structural weakness. The resultant demineralization was so advanced that the tooth fractured. He cautioned that the high sugar content—approximately twelve teaspoons per typical serving—poses a decay risk of considerable magnitude, with particularly rapid and devastating consequences for developing dentition.

These concerns echo earlier professional warnings. In August, Dr. Mervyn Druian, a prominent London dentist, highlighted the phenomenon termed "prosecco smile." He explained that the acidic and sugary composition of the drink can, with excessive consumption, lead to observable pathology at the gingival margin. The initial sign is a softened, white line just below the gum, indicative of early decay that may progress, necessitating fillings and other dental interventions. This evidence collectively underscores the importance of moderation and oral hygiene practices when consuming acidic and sugar-rich beverages.

LAGOS, April 13 Nigerian interbank lending rates rose sharply by around 100 percentage points on Thursday, as commercial lenders scrambled for cash to pay for bond purchases and cover their positions, traders said.
Overnight lending rates rose to around 300 percent from 200 percent at the end of Wednesday, as naira liquidity dried up in the banking system and some banks were forced to borrow from the central bank.
Nigeria raised 105.32 billion naira ($345 million) from bond sales this week, and payment for the debt sale was due on Thursday, draining liquidity in the market and pushing further up the cost of money in the market.
"The market is currently short of funds with major placers asking for a higher rate on their money as a result of pressure from those who need cash to cover their positions," one trader said.
The central bank has consistently sold dollars at both the spot and forward markets, and required banks to pay for the purchase. This has drained liquidity in the market.
The bank said authorised dealers bought $45 million out of $100 million it made available on the spot market.
"There are strong indications that the demand for foreign exchange by authorized dealers has slumped," it said in a statement.
Nigeria's financial markets will be closed until April 18 for a public holiday. ($1 = 305.1000 naira) (Reporting by Oludare Mayowa; Writing by Oludare Mayowa and Alexis Akwagyiram; Editing by Toby Chopra)
rewrite:
According to a central bank statement, interbank lending rates in Nigeria experienced a significant surge, increasing by approximately one hundred percentage points on Thursday. Market traders attributed this sharp rise to commercial lenders actively seeking liquidity to fulfill obligations related to bond purchases and to cover their financial positions. Specifically, overnight lending rates escalated to roughly 300 percent, a substantial increase from the 200 percent recorded at the close of trading on Wednesday. This spike coincided with a severe contraction of naira liquidity within the banking system, compelling several institutions to secure funds through borrowing from the central bank.

The liquidity strain was exacerbated by a government bond sale this week, which raised 105.32 billion naira (equivalent to $345 million). The settlement for this debt issuance, due on Thursday, effectively withdrew substantial liquidity from the market, thereby elevating the general cost of borrowing. One trader noted that the market faced a pronounced shortage of funds, with major liquidity providers demanding higher rates due to pressure from entities requiring cash to cover positions. Furthermore, the central bank's consistent sales of US dollars in both spot and forward markets, for which immediate payment from banks is mandated, has contributed to the persistent drainage of naira liquidity. The bank reported that authorized dealers purchased $45 million of the $100 million offered in the spot market, while also observing a notable decline in foreign exchange demand from these dealers. Nigerian financial markets are scheduled to remain closed until April 18th for a public holiday.

Awareness alone is insufficient; we must continue, instigate, and compel change.” The specific beneficiary organizations will be disclosed upon conclusion of the fundraising effort.

By Scott T. Sterling
Lin-Manuel Miranda and Ben Platt have teamed up for a cause.
The Broadway stars have united to create “Found/Tonight,” a mashup of “You Will Be Found” from Dear Evan Hanson and “The Story of Tonight” from Hamilton.
Related: Lin-Manuel Miranda Shares ‘Almost Like Praying ft Artists for Puerto Rico (Salsa Remix)’
The song comes with a new music video. Watch it below. Sheet music for “Found/Tonight” is made available for free here.
The song was inspired by the thousands of students across the country who mobilized following the Stoneman Douglas High School shooting in Parkland, FL just last month. A portion of all proceeds will go towards the March For Our Lives Initiative. Platt and Miranda are also united in encouraging other artists to help spark a viral campaign by explaining why they march using the hashtag #IWillMarch.
“In the wake of Parkland, I was awestruck by the strength and leadership of the students and their ability to speak truth to power,” Miranda explained in a press statement. “In the midst of their grief, they mobilized the youth of our nation and created a movement. This is their moment. Not just for themselves, but for all of us. This song is my way of helping to raise funds and awareness for their efforts, and to say Thank You, and that we are with you so let’s keep fighting, together.”
“When Lin called me to be a part of this mashup, I couldn’t say no,” Platt added. “Better gun control is something that all Americans should be passionate about. These students are paving the way for future generations and it’s so inspiring to see young people standing up for what is probably the most important cause right now in this country, and demanding action. I hope that this song can play some small part in bringing about real change.”
Find more information about the March For Our Lives Initiative here.
rewrite:
A collaborative musical work has been released by prominent Broadway figures Lin-Manuel Miranda and Ben Platt. The composition, titled “Found/Tonight,” is a musical amalgamation of “You Will Be Found” from the production *Dear Evan Hansen* and “The Story of Tonight” from *Hamilton*. The release is accompanied by an official music video. In a philanthropic gesture, the sheet music for this piece has been made publicly available without cost.

The initiative is a direct response to the student-led activism that emerged following the recent shooting at Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida. A segment of the revenue generated by this project will be directed to the March For Our Lives Initiative. Furthermore, the artists are advocating for broader participation, urging fellow creators to contribute to a digital awareness campaign by articulating their support through the hashtag #IWillMarch.

In an official statement, Miranda elaborated on the motivation behind the project: “In the wake of Parkland, I was awestruck by the strength and leadership of the students and their ability to speak truth to power. In the midst of their grief, they mobilized the youth of our nation and created a movement. This is their moment. Not just for themselves, but for all of us. This song is my way of helping to raise funds and awareness for their efforts, and to say Thank You, and that we are with you so let’s keep fighting, together.”

Platt provided additional commentary, stating, “When Lin contacted me to participate in this mashup, I felt compelled to agree. The pursuit of more effective firearm regulation is an issue that should concern every American. These students are establishing a precedent for future generations, and it is profoundly inspiring to witness young people advocating for what is arguably among the most critical contemporary national issues and insisting upon legislative action. It is my hope that this musical work may contribute in some modest capacity to facilitating substantive change.”

Further details regarding the March For Our Lives Initiative are accessible through its official channels.

rewrite:
On Tuesday, April 12, Mediatel SA announced it has convened an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for May 8. The primary agenda item is a vote on a proposal to reduce the company’s share capital by 65.4 million zlotys (approximately $16.32 million) to offset accumulated losses from prior fiscal years. This reduction will be effected by lowering the nominal value of each existing share from 1 zloty to 0.5 zloty.

Concurrently, the company plans a capital increase through the issuance of 130.8 million Series C shares, each with a nominal value of 0.5 zloty. These shares will be offered via a private subscription, excluding pre-emptive rights for existing shareholders. Furthermore, Mediatel intends to issue up to 138.3 million Series D shares, also with a nominal value of 0.5 zloty per share, through a private placement without pre-emptive rights.

The company stated these resolutions are strategically designed to protect the Hawe group, specifically Hawe Telekom, from a potential hostile takeover attempt by its principal creditor, Agencja Rozwoju Przemysłu SA.

SPRINGFIELD, Ill. -- A Medal of Honor recipient says he's humbled by the appreciation he's been shown by the people in Illinois.
The State Journal-Register reports 71-year-old James McCloughan (mih-KLOO'-uhn) of South Haven, Michigan was the keynote speaker during the main program of the Veterans and Gold Star Family Day Event at the Illinois State Fair on Sunday.
McCloughan, who was accompanied on stage by Gov. Bruce Rauner and Springfield Mayor Jim Langfelder, called all of the veterans and current service members his heroes.
McCloughan received the Medal of Honor from President Donald Trump at the White House on July 31. He's the first Medal of Honor recipient under Trump.
McCloughan, a combat medic, is credited with saving the lives of 10 members of his company during a Vietnam War battle despite his own serious wounds.
___

rewrite: During the Veterans and Gold Star Family Day Event at the Illinois State Fair in Springfield, Medal of Honor recipient James McCloughan expressed profound humility regarding the appreciation shown to him by the state’s residents. The 71-year-old combat medic from South Haven, Michigan, served as the keynote speaker for the main program. On stage with Governor Bruce Rauner and Springfield Mayor Jim Langfelder, McCloughan identified all veterans and active service members as his personal heroes. President Donald Trump presented McCloughan with the nation’s highest military award at the White House on July 31, making him the first service member to receive the Medal of Honor under the current administration. This recognition follows his heroic actions during a Vietnam War battle, where, despite sustaining serious injuries, he is credited with saving the lives of ten members of his company.

CAIRO — Two passenger trains collided on Friday just outside Egypt's Mediterranean port city of Alexandria, killing at least 36 people and injuring about 123, according to two medical officials.
A statement by the Egyptian Railways Authority said a train traveling to Alexandria from Cairo, Egypt's capital, crashed into the back of another train, which was waiting at a small station in the district of Khorshid, just east of Alexandria.
A general view of people by the wreckage after two passenger trains collided in Alexandria, Egypt, on Friday. Hazem Gouda / EPA
The stationary train had just arrived from Port Said, a Mediterranean city on the northern tip of the Suez Canal, when it was hit, according to the statement.
The statement did not say what caused the accident, saying only that the authority's experts would be investigating.
Associated Press video footage from the scene showed mangled train coaches on the tracks as hundreds of onlookers and victims' relatives gathered around on both sides of the tracks.
Ambulances were standing by and riot police were deployed to keep the onlookers away from the scene of the disaster.
Egypt's railway system has a poor safety record, mostly blamed on decades of badly maintained equipment and poor management.
Friday's collision was the latest in a series of deadly accidents that have claimed hundreds of lives over the years. Figures recently released by the state's statistics agency show that 1,249 train accidents took place last year, the highest number since 2009 when the number reached 1,577.
Friday's accident was the deadliest rail accident since 2006, when at least 51 people were killed when two commuter trains collided near Cairo.
Two trains are seen after they collided just outside Egypt's Mediterranean port city of Alexandria, Friday. Ravy shaker / AP
And earlier, in 2002, a massive fire engulfed a train filled with local holiday travelers. The train sped for miles, with flames engulfing one carriage after another, killing more than 370 people.
In November 2012, a speeding train crashed into a bus carrying Egyptian children to their kindergarten in the country's south, killing more than 50 — mostly children between the ages of four and six. Two months later, at least 19 people died and more than 100 were injured in a train derailment south of Cairo.
rewrite:
On Friday, a collision involving two passenger trains occurred near the Mediterranean port city of Alexandria, Egypt, resulting in significant casualties. According to statements from two medical officials, the incident claimed at least 36 lives and injured approximately 123 individuals. The Egyptian Railways Authority released a report indicating that a train originating from Cairo, the nation's capital, and bound for Alexandria struck the rear of another train. The stationary train, which had recently arrived from Port Said—a city situated at the northern terminus of the Suez Canal—was awaiting departure at the Khorshid district station, located east of Alexandria. The authority's statement did not specify a cause for the accident, noting only that an official investigation would be conducted by its experts.

Visual documentation from the scene, including Associated Press footage, depicted severely damaged carriages on the tracks, with hundreds of onlookers and relatives of victims assembled alongside the railway. Emergency services, including ambulances, were present at the location, while riot police were deployed to maintain perimeter security and control crowd access to the wreckage.

This event underscores longstanding concerns regarding the safety record of Egypt's railway infrastructure. Systemic issues, widely attributed to decades of inadequate maintenance and managerial deficiencies, are frequently cited as contributing factors. The collision represents the most recent in a sequence of fatal railway incidents that have accumulated a substantial death toll over previous years. Recent data published by the state statistics agency recorded 1,249 train accidents during the preceding year, the highest annual figure since 2009, when 1,577 accidents were documented.

Friday's accident constitutes the most severe rail disaster since 2006, when a collision between two commuter trains near Cairo resulted in at least 51 fatalities. Historical precedents include a catastrophic fire in 2002 that engulfed a train carrying holiday travelers, leading to over 370 deaths as the burning train continued for several miles. More recently, in November 2012, a high-speed train collided with a bus transporting children to a kindergarten in southern Egypt, killing more than 50 individuals, predominantly children aged four to six. This was followed two months later by a derailment south of Cairo that caused at least 19 fatalities and over 100 injuries.

TOKYO, April 6 JERA Co said on Thursday that it had struck a memorandum of understanding with Dubai Supply Authority (DUSUP) on cooperation in the liquefied natural gas (LNG) business.
JERA, the world's top LNG importer, has been forming alliances with other big LNG buyers to secure more flexible supply contracts in a move which shifts power to importers from producers as oversupply grows.
JERA, a fuel joint venture between Tokyo Electric Power and Chubu Electric Power, said it and DUSUP would discuss opportunities for mutual collaboration in the LNG business, including joint procurement of LNG and opportunities for cooperation related to LNG shipping and storage capacity.
DUSUP procures natural gas through national and international pipelines and through the development of an LNG import facility called a floating storage regasification unit (FSRU) in Jebel Ali.
"JERA believes that strengthening its relationship with DUSUP will contribute to expanding business opportunities for both companies," JERA said in a statement.
The Tokyo-based firm last month signed a similar agreement with two of the world's biggest LNG buyers, Korea Gas Corp (KOGAS) and China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) to exchange information and cooperate in the joint procurement of LNG. (Reporting by Osamu Tsukimori. Editing by Jane Merriman)
rewrite:
On Thursday, April 6, JERA Co. announced the execution of a memorandum of understanding with the Dubai Supply Authority (DUSUP) concerning cooperative efforts within the liquefied natural gas sector. As the world's foremost LNG importer, JERA—a fuel procurement joint venture between Tokyo Electric Power Company and Chubu Electric Power Company—has been actively forming alliances with other major buyers. This strategy aims to secure more flexible supply contracts, a development that shifts market leverage toward importers and away from producers amid conditions of growing oversupply.

According to its statement, JERA and DUSUP will explore mutual collaboration opportunities. These include the potential for joint LNG procurement and cooperation related to LNG shipping logistics and storage capacity. DUSUP currently procures natural gas via national and international pipelines and is developing an LNG import facility utilizing a floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) at Jebel Ali. JERA indicated that strengthening this relationship is expected to expand business opportunities for both entities.

This agreement follows a similar strategic pact signed last month by JERA with two other leading LNG importers, Korea Gas Corporation (KOGAS) and China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), focusing on information exchange and joint procurement initiatives.

Image caption The 1983 film made the phone box in the Aberdeenshire village of Pennan famous
A musical based on the classic 1983 film Local Hero will have its world premiere in Edinburgh next year.
The Royal Lyceum will be the first to perform the musical, which has been adapted by the theatre's artistic director David Greig and Bill Forsyth.
The Scottish filmmaker wrote and directed the original movie.
International music star Mark Knopfler has written the music and lyrics for the new production, which will open in Spring 2019.
Knopfler, who rose to fame in multi-million selling band Dire Straits, wrote the score for the 1983 film.
It tells the story of an American oil company representative who is sent to the fictional Ferness on the west coast of Scotland to buy the village and its land in order to build a refinery.
Image caption The inn in the village of Pennan was the setting for many scenes in the film
However, "Mac" MacIntyre adapts to Scottish village life and becomes worried the deal will ruin the place he has come to love.
It was made in several locations around Scotland but most of the Ferness village scenes were filmed in Pennan on the Aberdeenshire coast.
The red phone box on the village's main street where Mac makes phone calls to his boss in Texas, played by Burt Lancaster, became one of the most famous images of Scottish cinema.
Image copyright Mihaela Bodlovic Image caption Bill Forsyth and David Greig at the Royal Lyceum Theatre in Edinburgh
Glasgow writer and director Forsyth's other films include Gregory's Girl and Comfort and Joy.
David Greig, an acclaimed playwright as well as theatre director, said: "Local Hero is one of those great Scottish stories that has captured the imaginations of people across the world, it has been one of my favourite films since I first saw it as a teenager.
Local Hero is due to open at The Lyceum in Spring 2019 before transferring to The Old Vic in London.
rewrite:
The 1983 cinematic release *Local Hero* achieved particular renown for featuring the telephone box situated in the village of Pennan, Aberdeenshire. A musical adaptation of this classic film is scheduled for its world premiere in Edinburgh next year. The inaugural production will be staged at the Royal Lyceum Theatre, under the artistic adaptation of the theatre’s own artistic director, David Greig, in collaboration with Bill Forsyth, the Scottish filmmaker who authored and directed the original motion picture. The music and lyrics for this new theatrical production have been composed by internationally acclaimed musician Mark Knopfler, with its opening slated for Spring 2019. Knopfler, who gained prominence as a member of the multi-million-selling band Dire Straits, also composed the original score for the 1983 film.

The narrative follows an American oil company representative dispatched to the fictional Scottish west coast village of Ferness with the objective of purchasing the entire settlement and its surrounding land for the construction of a refinery. However, the protagonist, "Mac" MacIntyre, gradually assimilates into the local community and develops profound concerns that the proposed deal will irrevocably damage the environment and culture he has grown to cherish. Although filming occurred across multiple Scottish locations, the majority of scenes depicting the village of Ferness were shot in Pennan, on the Aberdeenshire coast. A prominent iconic image from Scottish cinema emerged from these sequences: the red telephone box on the village’s main street, from which Mac places calls to his Texas-based supervisor, portrayed by Burt Lancaster.

Bill Forsyth, the Glasgow-based writer and director, is further recognized for films such as *Gregory’s Girl* and *Comfort and Joy*. David Greig, an esteemed playwright and theatre director, has remarked, "*Local Hero* stands as one of those quintessential Scottish narratives that has captivated a global audience. It has remained a personal favourite since my initial viewing in adolescence." Following its debut at The Lyceum in Spring 2019, the musical production of *Local Hero* is anticipated to transfer to The Old Vic in London.

LSU head coach Ed Orgeron celebrates with his players after a win over Texas A&M in an NCAA football game at Kyle Field on Thursday, Nov. 24, 2016, in College Station, Texas. LSU won the game 54-39. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News)
Texas coach Tom Herman has desperately tried to find a way into Louisiana for a satellite camp this summer.
And on three different occasions, Herman and his staff were told that plans changed and the Longhorns were no longer welcomed at the host college, according to Sports Illustrated.
Why? LSU doesn't want Herman -- or really any Power Five peer, for that matter -- snooping around Louisiana for young talent at satellite camps. According to SI's Pete Thamel, Arkansas, Texas A&M and Houston were all disinvited to a camp at Southeastern Louisiana this summer.
While recent news of a Texas-Belhaven camp fallout made waves Tuesday, LSU's mindset isn't a new one under Ed Orgeron, who was promoted from interim coach to head coach at the end of last season.
Last year, former LSU coach Les Miles was incredibly upset with Tulane for its camp agreement with Texas A&M. When LSU hosted satellite camps this summer, the Tigers invited essentially everybody but Tulane.
rewrite: Following a 54-39 victory over Texas A&M in an NCAA football game at Kyle Field on November 24, 2016, LSU head coach Ed Orgeron is depicted celebrating with his players. Concurrently, Texas coach Tom Herman has encountered significant obstacles in his efforts to conduct a satellite football camp within Louisiana this summer. According to a report from Sports Illustrated, Herman and his staff received notification on three separate occasions that their planned camps at host colleges were canceled, effectively barring the Longhorns from participation. This exclusion stems from a deliberate policy by LSU, which aims to prevent rival Power Five conference programs, including Texas, from recruiting within its home state. As detailed by SI reporter Pete Thamel, other programs such as Arkansas, Texas A&M, and Houston were similarly disinvited from a camp scheduled at Southeastern Louisiana University. Although a recent canceled camp arrangement between Texas and Belhaven University attracted attention, this protective stance predates Coach Orgeron’s official appointment as head coach at the conclusion of the previous season. The strategy mirrors actions taken under former LSU coach Les Miles, who objected strongly to Tulane’s camp partnership with Texas A&M last year. Subsequently, when LSU organized its own satellite camps this summer, it extended invitations broadly but pointedly excluded Tulane.

The Santa Barbara County Sheriff’s Office has detained two men suspected in the Thursday night burglary of a home in Montecito.
Franke James Showell, 25, of Lancaster and Donyae Lamonte Dixon, 29, of Los Angeles are in custody at Santa Barbara County Jail on suspicion of burglary and conspiracy, with Showell also suspected of false impersonation. Both men are being held on $50,000 bail.
Just after 9 p.m. Thursday, a resident in the 200 block of Gould Lane, in Montecito, said he heard “strange noises coming from a child’s bedroom inside his residence,” according to the sheriff’s office.
The man, a father of two young children, investigated and “upon entering a hallway between bedrooms, he immediately saw a male suspect dressed in dark clothing.”

The sheriff’s office said the man yelled at the suspect, who fled back into the bedroom and out the window, which allegedly was used to enter the home.
“The suspect was last seen fleeing down an embankment to a wooded area,” according to the sheriff’s office.
In the wake of the Montecito mudslide, deputies have conducted increased patrols in the area. Within minutes of the 911 call, deputies located Showell, one of the suspected intruders, fleeing in a vehicle. Dixon, the other suspected intruder, was found “hiding in the bushes alongside the roadway.”
The sheriff’s office said a K-9 team tracked the scent from the window of the home to the patrol car where Showell was detained.

They face charges of burglary and conspiracy, with Showell additionally suspected of false impersonation. Bail for each has been set at $50,000.

The resident confronted the individual, who subsequently retreated into the bedroom and exited through a window that appeared to have been used for entry. The suspect was last observed fleeing down an embankment into a wooded area.

Due to enhanced patrols implemented following the Montecito mudslide, deputies responded promptly to the 911 call. Showell was located and detained minutes later while attempting to flee in a vehicle. Dixon was discovered concealed in roadside vegetation. A Sheriff’s Office K-9 unit corroborated the suspects’ path, tracing a scent from the point of entry at the residence to the patrol vehicle where Showell was held.

KANSAS CITY, Kan. — Tensions between the KCK Fire Department and the city’s former mayor are flaring once again.
An investigation by the KCK Fire Department determined some firefighters set of a firetruck siren early Tuesday morning near former mayor Mark Holland’s house. The department said the firefighters were returning to the station from a medical call when they set off the siren.
After they had passed his home, Holland said they turned the siren off. The former mayor posted surveillance video of the firefighters’ actions, which he called harassment, on his Facebook page.
The department said in a statement the firefighters involved “will be dealt with as necessary to ensure that activation of sirens and lights will only be done in compliance with current policies.”
The former mayor and KCK firefighters have a contentious relationship. The firefighters’ union, which backed David Alvey for mayor in last year’s election, fell into a back-and-forth mud slinging with Holland that ended with the resignation of the KCK fire chief and Holland’s accusations of corruption in the fire department.

In a formal statement, the department indicated the involved firefighters “will be dealt with as necessary to ensure that activation of sirens and lights will only be done in compliance with current policies.” This episode reflects the enduring contentious relationship between Holland and the department. The conflict has historical precedent, notably during the previous election cycle when the firefighters’ union endorsed Holland’s opponent, David Alvey. That period featured public accusations between Holland and the union, culminating in the fire chief’s resignation and allegations by Holland of corruption within the department.

[India], December 11 (ANI): India's first Electronic Manufacturing Cluster (EMC) will be coming to Andhra Pradesh.

What do you do when you need to get in some last-minute preparation for the U.S. Women’s Open but the U.S. Women’s Open course is closed? You improvise.
With the remnants of subtropical storm Alberto dumping more than four inches of rain the last two days at Shoal Creek Golf Club, USGA officials kept players and spectators off the Birmingham, Ala., course on Tuesday . So reigning U.S. Women’s Open champion Sung Hyun Park sought out another place to practice, and showed up early Tuesday afternoon at the Topgolf Birmingham.
Chris Stevenson, a writer for The Athletic Ottawa, happened to go to the facility as well to pass the time, and stumbled upon Park hitting balls in a bay. He then shared Park’s swing on his Twitter account.
“People here and there were stopping to watch her,” Stevenson told GolfChannel.com. “I would hit two balls and turn around and watch her hit two. I asked her if I could take a video. She was gracious enough to say yes.”
With Shoal Creek still closed through Wednesday morning, fans might want to head to Topgolf to see who else shows up.

WASHINGTON (AP) — A chartered train carrying dozens of GOP lawmakers to a Republican retreat in West Virginia struck a garbage truck south of Charlottesville, Virginia, on Wednesday. No lawmakers were believed injured, but it at least one person in the truck was said to be seriously injured.
"We're fine, but our train hit a garbage truck. Members with medical training are assisting the drivers of the truck," Rep. Greg Walden, R-Ore., wrote on Twitter.
A GOP aide said the train is partially derailed.
Oklahoma GOP Rep. Tom Cole says a person on the truck may have been seriously injured.
Cole said he's not aware of any injuries on the train. A GOP aide speaking on condition of anonymity says no lawmakers were injured.
Cole said he believes the accident occurred south of Charlottesville, Virginia. The train was en route to the Greenbrier resort in White Sulfur Springs for a three-day issues retreat featuring appearances by President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence.
Rep. Bradley Byrne, R-Ala., tweeted: "The train carrying GOP members to our retreat had a collision, but Rebecca and I are both okay. Security and doctors on board are helping secure the scene and treat injuries."
Cole said he felt "a tremendous jolt" when the accident occurred at about 11:15 a.m. EST, nearly two hours after it left Washington headed to the Greenbrier resort in White Sulphur Springs, W.Va.
He said the train stopped quickly after impact. He said several GOP lawmakers who are doctors got off the train to assist, including Rep. Brad Wenstrup, R-Ohio, who was also at last June's shooting of Republicans at a baseball practice in nearby Alexandria, Virginia, and treated some of the victims.
Other doctor-lawmakers who helped included Reps. Michael Burgess, R-Texas, Phil Roe, R-Tenn., and Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La.
Cole said the front of the train hit a vehicle that appeared to be a trash truck, which he said was torn in half. He said the accident apparently occurred at or near a crossing because he could see railroad crossing gates.
He said lawmakers had not been told when they would resume their trip to their retreat.
rewrite:
On Wednesday, a chartered train transporting numerous Republican members of Congress to a policy retreat in West Virginia was involved in a collision with a garbage truck south of Charlottesville, Virginia. Preliminary reports indicate that no lawmakers sustained injuries, although at least one individual in the truck is believed to have been seriously injured. According to a Republican aide, the train subsequently experienced a partial derailment.

Representative Greg Walden (R-Ore.) stated via social media, "We're fine, but our train hit a garbage truck. Members with medical training are assisting the drivers of the truck." This account was corroborated by Representative Tom Cole (R-Okla.), who confirmed the serious injury of a person in the truck while noting no known injuries among the train's passengers. An anonymous GOP aide also affirmed that no legislators were harmed.

The incident occurred at approximately 11:15 a.m. Eastern Standard Time, nearly two hours after the train's departure from Washington, D.C. The destination was the Greenbrier resort in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, the site of a scheduled three-day retreat featuring planned appearances by President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence. Representative Cole described experiencing "a tremendous jolt" upon impact, after which the train came to a rapid stop. The collision, which appeared to take place at or near a railroad crossing, involved the front of the train striking a vehicle resembling a trash truck; the vehicle was reported to have been torn in half.

Following the accident, several members of Congress with medical training disembarked to provide assistance. Among them was Representative Brad Wenstrup (R-Ohio), who had previously aided victims during the June 2017 congressional baseball practice shooting in Alexandria, Virginia. Other physician-lawmakers who rendered aid included Representatives Michael Burgess (R-Texas), Phil Roe (-R-Tenn.), and Senator Bill Cassidy (R-La.). Representative Bradley Byrne (R-Ala.) publicly confirmed his and his wife's safety, noting that security personnel and doctors on board were managing the scene and treating injuries. As of the initial reports, lawmakers had not been informed of a timeline for resuming their journey to the retreat.

NEW YORK Two Russian nationals arrested in the United States last October on charges of conspiring to export sensitive military technology from the United States to Russia were sentenced to time served on Friday, a spokesman for U.S. prosecutors said.
Dmitrii Aleksandrovich Karpenko, 33, and Alexey Krutilin, 27, both pleaded guilty on March 8 and were sentenced by U.S. District Judge Leo Glasser in Brooklyn. They have agreed to immediate deportation to Russia, where both live, the spokesman said.
U.S. prosecutors said the men planned to obtain microelectronics from manufacturers and suppliers in the United States and export them to Russia while evading government controls on high-tech exports.
The technology at issue included devices used in radar and missile guidance systems, prosecutors said. The United States restricts the export of items it believes could contribute to weapons proliferation and undermine U.S. national security.
Karpenko and Krutilin were arrested in Denver on Oct. 5 in a sting operation arranged by U.S. Department of Homeland Security agents posing as sellers, according to court filings.
In briefs filed in the Brooklyn court, lawyers for Karpenko and Krutilin said while the two men knew the purpose of their trip was illegal, they had been sent by their employer, a Russian company called Aelek, and did not plan the purchases themselves.
"We're grateful that Judge Glasser recognised the limited role that Mr. Karpenko and Mr. Krutilin played in the conspiracy," said Richard Levitt, a lawyer for Karpenko.
Raymond Granger, a lawyer for Krutilin, said his client was "extremely gratified" by the decision.
Prosecutors said last October that Karpenko and Krutilin conspired with Alexey Barysheff, a U.S. citizen living in Brooklyn who was also arrested. Prosecutors say Barysheff set up front companies to buy and export electronics.
Barysheff also has pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced on June 17, court records show.
(Reporting by Brendan Pierson in New York; Editing by Jonathan Oatis and Bill Trott)

The spokesperson confirmed that both defendants have consented to immediate deportation to their home country of Russia.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants engaged in a scheme to procure controlled microelectronics from U.S. manufacturers and suppliers for illicit export to Russia, thereby circumventing federal regulatory controls governing the transfer of advanced technologies. The items in question included components utilized in radar and missile guidance systems. Such exports are restricted by the United States on grounds that they could contribute to weapons proliferation and consequently pose a threat to national security.

The arrests of Karpenko and Krutilin occurred in Denver on October 5 following a covert operation conducted by agents of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, who posed as equipment vendors. Legal filings submitted to the court by defense counsel contended that while the defendants were aware their mission violated U.S. law, they were acting under the direction of their employer, a Russian entity identified as Aelek, and were not the architects of the procurement plan. Attorney Richard Levitt, representing Karpenko, expressed gratitude that the court acknowledged the limited role played by his client and Mr. Krutilin in the conspiracy. Raymond Granger, counsel for Krutilin, stated his client was profoundly gratified by the court’s disposition.

Prosecutors had previously indicated that the defendants conspired with Alexey Barysheff, a U.S. citizen residing in Brooklyn who was also arrested. Barysheff is alleged to have established front companies to facilitate the purchases and exports. Court records show that Barysheff has likewise pleaded guilty and is scheduled for sentencing on June 17.

Saudi Arabia’s powerful heir apparent, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, is visiting Washington and other American cities this week promoting his image as an enlightened reformer out to modernize his conservative country and encourage foreign investment.
That image is stained by his chief foreign policy initiative, the humanitarian catastrophe that is the war in Yemen, in which at least 10,000 civilians have been killed, many as a result of indiscriminate airstrikes by the Saudis and their Persian Gulf partners. Other legislative efforts would block military aid to Saudi Arabia, including millions of dollars in arms sales.

Legislators plan to introduce legislation on Wednesday that would require the Department of Transportation to implement a residential parking permit system in designated parts of the city — including much of northern Manhattan.
One proposed bill would cover all areas between 60th Street and Inwood and would allow the DOT to reserve as many as 80 percent of the parking spaces in certain areas for local residents.
Manhattan City Council members Mark Levine, Helen Rosenthal and Keith Powers said the measure is needed because so many park-and-ride commuters from outside the borough take up spots in residential neighborhoods and then hop on the subway.
“For too long suburban commuters have taken advantage of free street parking in Northern Manhattan and crowded out the people who actually live in our neighborhoods,” said Levine, a co-chair of the Manhattan delegation.
“Whether you live in Washington Heights or the Upper East Side, parking in our borough is an incredible challenge for so many who live here,” he added. “We can’t afford to continue as one of the only big cities in America that doesn’t have a residential parking permit system–this policy is long overdue.”
The legislation would limit permits to those with a New York State driver’s license, one permit per driver, and would be attached to a specific license plate.
Another bill, by Council Transportation Committee Chair Ydanis Rodriguez (D- Upper Manhattan), would seek a citywide residential permit parking system. It would require permit holders to pay yet-to-be-determined fees to park in their designated areas.
Rodriguez did not immediately return messages.
Both bills leave the determination of the parking hours and locations where parking would be reserved for permit-holders to the DOT, which in the past has expressed resistance to such programs.
A spokesperson for Council Speaker Corey Johnson said he’s reviewing the bills.
Reps for DOT and Mayor de Blasio’s office said they would review the legislation when introduced.
The bills faces at least one major hurdle — by some officials’ reckoning, Albany would have to give its permission to implement the program.
City DOT officials say they believe residential permit parking would require state approval.
Additional reporting by Danielle Furfaro
rewrite:
On Wednesday, legislators intend to introduce proposed legislation mandating the Department of Transportation (DOT) to establish a residential parking permit system within specified city zones, encompassing a significant portion of northern Manhattan. One legislative proposal would apply to all areas situated between 60th Street and Inwood, authorizing the DOT to designate up to eighty percent of parking spaces in certain neighborhoods for the exclusive use of local residents. Manhattan City Council members Mark Levine, Helen Rosenthal, and Keith Powers assert that this measure is necessary due to the prevalence of park-and-ride commuters from outside the borough, who occupy parking spots in residential neighborhoods before utilizing subway transit.

Council Member Levine, a co-chair of the Manhattan delegation, stated, “For an extended period, suburban commuters have exploited the availability of free street parking in Northern Manhattan, thereby displacing the residents of these communities.” He further emphasized, “Parking within the borough, whether in Washington Heights or the Upper East Side, presents a considerable difficulty for numerous residents. We can no longer persist as one of the few major American cities lacking a residential parking permit system; this policy is substantially overdue.”

The proposed legislation would restrict permits to individuals possessing a valid New York State driver’s license, limited to one permit per driver, and would be associated with a specific vehicle license plate. A separate bill, introduced by Council Transportation Committee Chair Ydanis Rodriguez (D- Upper Manhattan), advocates for the implementation of a citywide residential permit parking program. This proposal would necessitate that permit holders pay fees, which remain to be determined, for parking within their assigned zones. Council Member Rodriguez was not immediately available for comment.

Both legislative proposals delegate the authority to establish specific parking hours and designate reserved locations for permit holders to the DOT, an agency that has historically indicated resistance to such programs. A spokesperson for Council Speaker Corey Johnson confirmed that the legislation is under review. Representatives from the DOT and Mayor de Blasio’s office similarly indicated they would evaluate the bills upon formal introduction.

A significant potential obstacle for the legislation is the requirement, as noted by some officials, for approval from the state legislature in Albany to enact the program. City DOT officials have concurred, stating their belief that implementing residential permit parking would necessitate state authorization.

SEOUL, South Korea (AP) " South Korea has called up English Premier League stars Son Heung-min and Ki Sung-yeung for vital 2018 World Cup qualifiers against Iran and Uzbekistan.
South Korea needs at least four points from matches against Iran in Seoul on Aug. 31 and Uzbekistan in Tashkent five days later to be sure of heading to Russia next summer.
There have been injury concerns over both players. Son, who scored 21 goals last season for Tottenham Hotspur, fractured his arm for his country in a 3-2 loss in Qatar in June. Ki, the national team's captain, picked up a knee injury in the same game.
"There is more possibility of Ki playing in the second game," recently-appointed head coach Shin Tae-yong told a news conference Monday. "I have been in regular contact with him and with some new players in the squad, we need players like Ki."
Advertisement
Ki did not feature for Swansea City in its opening league 0-0 draw at Southampton on Saturday.
There was better news regarding Son, who appeared as a second-half substitute for Spurs in an opening day 2-0 win at Newcastle, wearing a bandage on his arm.
Shin, in charge for his first game after Uli Stielike was fired in June following a third loss in five qualifying matches, also recalled 38-year-old striker Lee Dong-gook in his 26-man roster.
South Korea sits second in Group A in the third round of Asian qualifying, seven points behind the already-qualified Iran and just a point ahead of Uzbekistan.
Only the top two in both six-team groups progress automatically to Russia. The third-place teams from Groups A and B will meet in an October two-match Asian elimination game for the right to enter a final play-off against CONCAFAF's fourth-placed team.

Securing a minimum of four points from the fixture against Iran in Seoul on August 31st and the subsequent match in Tashkent against Uzbekistan five days later is imperative for South Korea to guarantee qualification for the tournament in Russia.

Both players have been subject to recent injury concerns. Son Heung-min, who recorded twenty-one goals for Tottenham Hotspur in the previous season, sustained an arm fracture during South Korea’s 3-2 defeat to Qatar in June. National team captain Ki Sung-yueng incurred a knee injury in the same match. At a Monday press conference, newly appointed head coach Shin Tae-yong indicated a greater likelihood of Ki’s participation in the second qualifying match, stating, “I have been in regular contact with him, and with some new players in the squad, we need players like Ki.” Ki was absent from Swansea City’s season-opening draw against Southampton. Conversely, Son featured as a second-half substitute for Tottenham Hotspur in their victory over Newcastle, albeit with a protective arm bandage.

Coach Shin, overseeing his first match since replacing the dismissed Uli Stielike in June, has also included veteran striker Lee Dong-gook, aged 38, in a 26-player roster. In the Asian Football Confederation’s third round of qualifying, South Korea currently occupies second position in Group A. The third-place teams from Groups A and B will contest a two-match playoff in October, the winner of which will advance to an intercontinental playoff against the fourth-placed team from the CONCACAF region.

BERLIN A 90th-minute goal from Benjamin Huebner gave Hoffenheim a last-gasp 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday and moved them up into third place with three matches left in the season.
The top three teams win an automatic Champions League group-stage spot with the fourth going into the competition's qualifying rounds.
Bayern Munich secured their fifth successive league title on Saturday after crushing VfL Wolfsburg 6-0 to leave them 10 points clear with three games left as RB Leipzig, in second place on 63, drew 0-0 against Ingolstadt.
Nadiem Amiri hit the post for Hoffenheim early in the game and the hosts kept up the pressure throughout but could not score until Huebner rose high to drill in his header from a corner.
The win sent Hoffenheim into third, one point ahead of Borussia Dortmund, who drew 0-0 against Cologne on Saturday. Hoffenheim and Dortmund meet next week.
Veteran Halil Altintop scored twice as Augsburg crushed Hamburg SV 4-0 in their relegation derby to climb out of the drop zone.
The 34-year-old former Turkey international struck twice in the first half as Augsburg rose to the big occasion, leaving Hamburg, the only team to have played in the Bundesliga every season since the top league's creation in 1963, in the relegation playoff spot on 33 points.
Altintop fired in for the lead in the 28th minute and then tapped in at the far post 14 minutes later as Augsburg also hit the woodwork twice in a dominant performance.
Philipp Max made sure of the three points that lifted hosts Augsburg to 13th on 35, with a low shot, and substitute Raul Bobadilla added the fourth goal in the 85th minute.
(Reporting by Karolos Grohmann, editing by Pritha Sarkar and Clare Fallon)
rewrite:
A ninetieth-minute goal from Benjamin Huebner secured a dramatic 1-0 victory for Hoffenheim over Eintracht Frankfurt on Sunday, a result that elevated the side to third position with three fixtures remaining in the Bundesliga season. The top three finishers qualify automatically for the UEFA Champions League group stage, while the fourth-placed team must enter the competition’s qualifying rounds.

This pivotal win followed Bayern Munich’s confirmation of a fifth consecutive league title on Saturday, achieved through a 6-0 defeat of VfL Wolfsburg. That result established a ten-point lead at the summit, as second-placed RB Leipzig, on 63 points, were held to a 0-0 draw by Ingolstadt. In Sunday’s match, Hoffenheim applied sustained pressure, with Nadiem Amiri striking the post early on, before Huebner finally broke the deadlock by powerfully heading in a corner kick. The three points place Hoffenheim one point ahead of Borussia Dortmund, who drew 0-0 with Cologne on Saturday; the two teams are scheduled to meet next week.

In a significant relegation encounter, Augsburg delivered a commanding 4-0 victory over Hamburg SV, propelled by a brace from veteran forward Halil Altintop. The 34-year-old former Turkish international scored twice in the first half, establishing a lead in the 28th minute and adding another from close range 14 minutes later. Augsburg’s dominant performance, which included striking the woodwork twice, was capped by further goals from Philipp Max and substitute Raul Bobadilla. The result lifts Augsburg to 13th place with 35 points, while Hamburg—the only club to have participated in every Bundesliga season since its 1963 inception—remains in the relegation playoff position with 33 points.

Galway Bay fm newsroom – Galway’s unemployment figure is continuing its downward trend.
The latest statistics from the CSO reveal that there are currently 12,323 people on the Live Register across the city and county – a drop of over 10% since last year
Last month, Galway’s Live Register figure dropped by 55 on th figure for October.
The biggest decrease in unemployment was in the city, where 114 people came off the register.
There are currently just over 6,100 people out of work in the city.
In Loughrea, 22 people came off the Live Register in November, leaving the area’s jobless figure at just over 1,200.
In Ballinasloe, the unemployment figure dropped by 15 to just over 1,400 last month.
However, Clifden, Gort and Tuam experienced slight increases in unemployment during November.
Clifden saw an extra 85 people join the register last month, leaving its jobless figure at 802.
Gort and Tuam saw very slight increases of 9 and 2 – leaving their unemployment figures at 913 and 1,793 respectively.
rewrite: Recent data from the Central Statistics Office (CSO) indicate a continuation of the downward trend in unemployment within Galway city and county. The total number of individuals listed on the Live Register currently stands at 12,323, representing a decline of more than 10 percent compared to the previous year. A month-on-month analysis shows a reduction of 55 persons from October to November. The most significant decrease occurred within Galway city, where 114 persons were removed from the register, resulting in a current total of approximately 6,100 unemployed. Similar reductions were observed in Loughrea, with a decrease of 22 persons to just over 1,200, and in Ballinasloe, with a decrease of 15 persons to slightly above 1,400. Conversely, the towns of Clifden, Gort, and Tuam recorded marginal increases in their Live Register figures during November. Clifden experienced an addition of 85 persons, raising its total to 802, while Gort and Tuam saw minor increases of 9 and 2 persons, resulting in totals of 913 and 1,793, respectively.

Regarding annual raises, it is common practice to apply annual percentage increase to base pay only, not total compensation.

If you speak to the board instead of your friend you will burn more than bridges, baby — you’ll create a scene straight out of a Hollywood disaster flick! Picture this instead: Two besties at Sunday brunch. You tell her that the only thing that dwarfs your love of the arts is your love of your friendship — and you fear the gig is getting in the way. You talk it over, cry, hug, clink glasses and resolve the tension. Break a leg!

This strategy prioritizes preserving the personal relationship while seeking a professional understanding, thereby aiming for an amicable resolution to the managerial conflict.

Lela Rose is all about occasion dressing. That doesn’t strictly mean black tie fare, though she’ll argue her dresses have a formal enough quality to make a pass. She designs for work-to-dinner, luncheons, dinner parties; in a nutshell, her lifestyle. What she’s gravitated toward personally is a sense of unfussy elegance. “Pieces that you throw on and don’t feel too buttoned-up or restricted in,” the designer said in her showroom. Her designs toe the line of polished, elegant femininity; for pre-fall, she also drew from men’s wear.
It all started with a scrap piece of glen plaid Rose has always kept but hasn’t been able to use. Her customers want flirty and romantic, so the challenge has been translating the plaid into something feminine and approachable. She delivered on some great light and airy plaid dresses in chiffon, ripstop taffeta and slipdresses with little ties — in a soft palette of pink, green, blue and lavender. A fluid gown bringing in all the colors had great motion and drawstring ties to adjust the waistline. Most modern was a wide-shouldered wrap top paired with embroidered pants; it was a cool take on less formal evening.
Elsewhere, feminine touches provided some novelty. There were little bow details running up the back of a gown or dangling as playful earrings, removable dickey collars on a shift dress, dimensional soutache embroidery on a peplum top and dress, and guipure lace inserts on the balloon sleeves of a button-down.

GENEVA Five migrants are believed to have died when a rubber boat sank off the coast of Libya on Tuesday, aid groups said on Friday, adding that reports earlier this week that many more had been killed were wrong.
Probably still in shock after he was taken to the Italian island of Lampedusa, a 16-year-old Gambian boy told humanitarian workers on Wednesday he was the only survivor of the wreck, Cecile Pouilly, a spokeswoman for the UNHCR, told reporters.
When 140 others disembarked at a different port on Thursday, several identified the boy as having been on the same boat.
"So we have pretty good information that this tragedy didn't occur as was initially reported," said Joel Millman, spokesman for the International Organization for Migration.
"We try to be as conservative as possible and only report what we know. This was not one of those cases."
Some 650 migrants are estimated to have died trying to reach Europe by crossing the Mediterranean so far this year, and arrivals in Italy are up about 30 percent from the same period last year.
(Reporting by Stephanie Ullmer-Nebehay; writing by Steve Scherer; editing by Andrew Roche)
rewrite:
A tragic maritime incident off the Libyan coast on Tuesday is now confirmed to have resulted in five migrant fatalities, according to statements from aid organizations released on Friday. These reports correct earlier, unverified accounts that had suggested a significantly higher death toll. A spokesperson for the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), Cecile Pouilly, informed reporters that a 16-year-old Gambian boy, rescued and brought to the Italian island of Lampedusa, provided a critical account on Wednesday. The survivor stated he was the sole survivor from a sunken rubber dinghy. This testimony was corroborated on Thursday when several individuals among a group of 140 migrants arriving at a separate port identified the adolescent as having been aboard the same vessel.

Joel Millman, a spokesman for the International Organization for Migration (IOM), emphasized the importance of verified reporting, stating, "We try to be as conservative as possible and only report what we know. This was not one of those cases." The incident occurs within a broader context of ongoing peril on the Mediterranean migration route. Current IOM estimates indicate approximately 650 migrant deaths have occurred during crossings to Europe this year, while arrivals in Italy have increased by roughly thirty percent compared to the same period in the prior year.

The Boys and Girls Club of Southwest Missouri will wrap up their participation in the Graduate for Más. Throughout the year, teen members of the Boys and Girls Club completed nine volunteer events and toured 10 community colleges and universities in the four states area where they learned about various degree programs. These opportunities were made possible through a $9,540.00 grant from the Taco Bell® Foundation.
The Boys and Girls Club hosted a graduation celebration in May for the Class of 2017. The event was to honor local high school students who graduated in the Class of 2017 and to celebrate rising upperclassmen.
“Graduation season is our favorite time of year. We’ve watched the young men and women in our community work so hard to get to this point and it’s a thrill to share in their joy of earning that diploma,” said Megan Williams, Teen Coordinator of Boys and Girls Club of Southwest Missouri. “We appreciate the Taco Bell® Foundation for recognizing and celebrating our new grads and committing to our future ones through the Foundation’s long-term support right in Joplin.”
The grant to Boys and Girls Club of Southwest Missouri is part of a partnership between the Taco Bell® Foundation and Boys & Girls Clubs of America to support more young people through high school graduation and beyond.
“We founded the Taco Bell Foundation to invest in youth and to ignite their futures, starting with graduation. These youth are our customers, friends, families, employees and our future leaders,” said Frank Tucker Chief People Officer at Taco Bell and President for the Taco Bell Foundation. “Our partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America provides an opportunity to deliver on our commitment to ensure youth are empowered to graduate from high school and go onto pursue their dreams. We’re proud of the effort put forth by every youth being honored at this wonderful event.”

Taiwanese hiker Liang Sheng Yueh, who was lost in the Himalayas for over a month, smiles as he celebrates his 21st birthday at a hospital after being rescued, in Kathmandu, Nepal April 28, 2017. REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar
Taiwanese hiker Liang Sheng Yueh, who was lost in the Himalayas for over a month, celebrates his 21st birthday at a hospital after being rescued, in Kathmandu, Nepal April 28, 2017. REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar
KATHMANDU A Taiwan hiker rescued 47 days after disappearing in the foothills of the Himalayas and just days after his girlfriend died is recovering well in hospital in the Nepali capital of Kathmandu, his doctor said on Friday.
Liang Sheng-yueh, who turned 21 on Friday, went missing with girlfriend Liu Chen-chun, 19, in early March while they were trekking in the remote Ganesh Himal area in northwestern Nepal.
Liang, his feet riddled with maggots and his hair infested with lice, was picked up by a rescue helicopter on Wednesday. The body of Liu, who died this week, was taken to hospital for a post mortem.
"I feel very happy now," a confused-looking Liang, his head shaved, told reporters after cutting a birthday cake from his hospital bed, adding that he had not lost hope during his ordeal.
The trekkers lost their trail after a snowstorm. They had no local guide or porter. Liang and Liu survived on snow, water and salt he was carrying, but Liu eventually died from starvation.
"He has started taking normal food and is walking with the help of physiotherapists," said Chakra Raj Pandey, medical director at the Grande International Hospital.
Tens of thousands of foreign hikers who visit Nepal every year are a key source of income in the cash-strapped nation that is home to Mount Everest.
(Reporting by Gopal Sharma; Editing by Nick Macfie)
rewrite:
On April 28, 2017, Taiwanese trekker Liang Sheng-yueh marked his twenty-first birthday from a hospital bed in Kathmandu, Nepal, following his rescue after being missing for over a month in the Himalayan region. The occasion was documented in a photograph distributed by Reuters, in which Liang is depicted smiling.

Medical personnel reported on that Friday that Liang was recuperating satisfactorily at a medical facility in the Nepalese capital. His rescue concluded a forty-seven-day ordeal that began in early March when he and his girlfriend, nineteen-year-old Liu Chen-chun, disappeared during a trek in the remote Ganesh Himal area of northwestern Nepal. Tragically, Liu perished shortly before the rescue operation. Liang was located and extracted by helicopter on April 26; he presented with severe maggot infestation in his feet and lice in his hair. Liu’s remains were transported to the hospital for post-mortem examination.

From his hospital bed, Liang, whose head had been shaved, expressed to reporters a sense of happiness and maintained that he had retained hope throughout his harrowing experience. According to his account, the pair lost their route following a snowstorm. Trekking without a local guide or porter, they subsisted on snow, water, and salt that Liang carried until Liu ultimately succumbed to starvation. Dr. Chakra Raj Pandey, Medical Director at Grande International Hospital, stated that the patient had commenced a regular diet and was ambulating with assistance from physiotherapists.

This incident underscores the risks associated with trekking in Nepal’s remote high-altitude regions, which attract tens of thousands of foreign visitors annually. Tourism constitutes a vital source of revenue for the nation, which hosts Mount Everest and other peaks within the Himalayan range.

Mumbai: Australian pacer Billy Stanlake has been ruled out of the remainder of the Sunrisers Hyderabad campaign in the ongoing Indian Premier League (IPL) after he suffered a finger injury while fielding in a match against Chennai Super Kings two days back.
"Sunrisers Hyderabad fast bowler Billy Stanlake has been ruled out of the remainder of the eleventh"edition of the ongoing IPL," a media release from the Sunrisers Hyderabad said.
Indian and Australian orthopaedic specialists have advised Stanlake against playing the remaining tournament owing to an injury that he sustained in the match against Chennai Super Kings played at Hyderabad on April 22, it added.
"Billy sustained a displaced fracture on the fifth finger of his right hand whilst fielding. Surgical reduction and fixation was required to restore the function to that finger," the release said.
According to the release,"the pacer"has flown back to Australia for further treatment.
The 23-year-old fast bowler had taken five wickets in the four games, which he played for Hyderabad in this IPL.
rewrite: Australian fast bowler Billy Stanlake has been excluded from participation in the remaining fixtures of the Sunrisers Hyderabad franchise in the ongoing Indian Premier League (IPL) due to a finger injury. The injury was sustained while fielding during a match against the Chennai Super Kings in Hyderabad on April 22. A formal release from the team stated that Stanlake incurred a displaced fracture to the fifth finger of his right hand, necessitating surgical intervention for reduction and fixation to restore functionality. Following consultations with orthopaedic specialists in both India and Australia, it was advised that he withdraw from the tournament. Consequently, the player has returned to Australia to continue his treatment. The 23-year-old pacer had secured five wickets across the four matches he played for Hyderabad in this eleventh edition of the IPL.

rewrite:
On Monday, Cynthia Nixon, an actress widely recognized for her portrayal of Miranda Hobbes on the television series *Sex and the City*, formally declared her candidacy for Governor of New York. In an announcement video, she positioned her campaign as a direct challenge to the political establishment in Albany, articulating a vision for a state government that serves the broader populace rather than a privileged minority. “I love New York. I’ve never lived anywhere else,” Nixon states in the video, which depicts scenes of her domestic life with her wife, Christine Marinoni, and their children. “But something has to change. We want our government to work again, on healthcare, ending mass incarceration, fixing our broken subway. We are sick of politicians who care more about headlines and power than they do about us. It can’t just be business as usual anymore.”

Nixon will contest the Democratic primary against the incumbent, Governor Andrew Cuomo. Recent electoral data, however, indicates a significant challenge for her candidacy. A Siena College poll released Monday shows Cuomo maintaining substantial leads over two potential Republican opponents, Dutchess County Executive Marc Molinaro (57% to 29%) and State Senator John DeFrancisco (57% to 28%). More critically for Nixon, the same poll finds Democratic registered voters favoring Cuomo over her by a margin of 66 percent to 19 percent.

Nixon, a 51-year-old liberal activist and longtime supporter of New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio—a fellow Democrat frequently at odds with Governor Cuomo—enters the race with considerable name recognition from her acting career, though her political profile is less established. Siena pollster Steven Greenberg noted, “She is far from a household name in New York, though she is better known than either Molinaro or DeFrancisco.” Her personal narrative is deeply rooted in New York; raised by a single mother in a modest Manhattan walk-up apartment, she began acting at age twelve to fund her education. She subsequently worked her way through Barnard College at Columbia University. A product of New York City’s public school system, she is also the parent of three children who are either current students or graduates of that system. If elected, Cynthia Nixon would become both the first woman and the first openly LGBTQ individual to hold the office of Governor of New York.

What makes a good Christmas? Friends and family get-togethers, presents and those special festive foods which are delicious, look tempting and are almost impossible to resist. Christmas comes once a year, so why shouldn’t you have turkey with all the trimmings, Christmas pudding, mince pies, cream, cheese, trifle, pork pie, chocolates, nuts and a glass or two? Well, a typical Christmas dinner will probably be 1,000 calories alone and the day’s intake could tot up to 6,000! All that food is hard to stomach and the most likely consequence is indigestion. When you eat, your stomach produces acid as part of the digestion process but this acid can sometimes irritate the lining of the stomach, the top part of the bowel or the oesophagus. Large amounts of food can also stretch the stomach causing acid reflux known as heartburn, so called because of the burning pain behind your breastbone. So, what can be done? Antacids – can provide immediate relief by neutralising stomach acid, which reduces irritation and discomfort. Alginates – are helpful with acid reflux and help prevent stomach acid getting into the oesophagus, causing heartburn. Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) – these restrict the acid produced by the stomach and are taken as tablets. Formerly only available on prescription, but now in the pharmacy. H2-receptor antagonists – like PPIs used to be prescription-only, but some are now available over the counter from your pharmacy. They work by interacting with the stomach cells which release acid, lowering the acidity level in your stomach.
It’s definitely worth making sure that you ‘have something in’ for indigestion, especially at Christmas time. If you are taking prescribed medication, or suffer from a long-term condition, always speak to your pharmacist before buying. If you have persistent or recurring indigestion, you should seek advice from your GP.
If you do indulge, there’s always that New Year’s resolution to be more active – oh, and you’ll only have to walk for 21.5 hours to burn off those Christmas Day calories.
Have a Happy Christmas!
rewrite:
The quintessential Christmas experience is often characterized by convivial gatherings of friends and family, the exchange of gifts, and the consumption of distinctive festive cuisine renowned for its palatability, visual appeal, and near-irresistible nature. Given the annual occurrence of the holiday, indulgence in a traditional meal—featuring turkey with accompaniments, Christmas pudding, mince pies, cream, cheese, trifle, pork pie, chocolates, nuts, and alcoholic beverages—is frequently perceived as justifiable. However, a typical Christmas dinner may alone approximate 1,000 calories, with total daily intake potentially reaching 6,000 calories. Such substantial consumption poses significant digestive challenges, with indigestion being a probable consequence. During digestion, the stomach naturally secretes acid; this acid can, at times, irritate the gastric mucosa, the duodenum, or the esophageal lining. Furthermore, voluminous meals can induce gastric distension, leading to acid reflux and the symptomatic retrosternal burning pain colloquially termed heartburn.

Several pharmacological interventions can ameliorate these conditions. Antacids offer immediate symptomatic relief by neutralizing gastric acid, thereby reducing mucosal irritation and discomfort. Alginates are particularly beneficial for acid reflux, forming a protective barrier that inhibits the regurgitation of stomach acid into the esophagus. Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs), available in tablet form, function by substantially suppressing gastric acid secretion. Once exclusively prescription-based, certain PPIs are now obtainable from pharmacies. Similarly, H2-receptor antagonists, which were also formerly prescription-only, are accessible over the counter; they operate by antagonizing the histamine receptors on parietal cells, thereby diminishing acid production.

It is prudent to ensure the availability of such remedies for dyspepsia, particularly during the festive period. Individuals taking prescribed medications or managing chronic health conditions should consult a pharmacist prior to purchasing any treatment. Persistent or recurrent indigestion necessitates consultation with a general practitioner.

For those who partake liberally, the prospect of a New Year's resolution to increase physical activity remains—a pertinent consideration given that expending the caloric intake from Christmas Day would require approximately 21.5 hours of walking.
