The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association (TSSAA) Board of Control approved the addition of a Unified Track & Field event at their recent meeting on Monday, August 14, 2017. This competition, which will initially begin as an Invitational Championship, is to be first implemented during the 2018 Spring Fling Championships. The decision marks the beginning of a partnership between TSSAA and Special Olympics Tennessee in Unified Sports.
Dedicated to promoting social inclusion through shared sports training and competition experiences, Unified Sports joins students with and without intellectual disabilities on the same team. It was inspired by the principle that practicing and competing together promotes inclusion and understanding to help break down stereotypes.
TSSAA member schools with existing Unified Track & Field programs will have until October 1 to notify Special Olympics Tennessee of their desire to participate. For the inaugural year, eight teams will be invited by Special Olympics Tennessee to take part in the event. The TSSAA desires to officially sanction the sport of Unified Track & Field in subsequent years, involving more schools and implementing qualifying sectionals.
Bernard Childress, Executive Director of the TSSAA, expressed excitement over the partnership with Special Olympics Tennessee. “Special Olympics Tennessee has done amazing work in our state for a long time and we are thrilled to be working with them to enhance our State Championship experience. The addition of Unified Sports and the relationship we have begun with Special Olympics will have an extremely positive impact on athletics and student-athletes across our state. Whenever we can make a decision that provides opportunities for more student-athletes, that is a direction we want to go.”
Alan Bolick, President of Special Olympics Tennessee, stated his appreciation to the Board of Control and staff of TSSAA and echoed similar sentiments. “The establishment of this unique partnership will no doubt have a positive influence on creating more inclusive environments in our public and private schools as well as the communities in Tennessee where these athletes live.”
Events included in the inaugural TSSAA Unified Track & Field Invitational will be the 100 meter Dash, 400 meter Run, 4×100 meter Relay, Shot Put, and Long Jump. The Unified Track & Field events will be incorporated into the existing Spring Fling Track & Field schedule, with individual medals awarded and a Unified Track & Field Champion and Runner-up team decided.

rewrite:
The white elephant gift exchange constitutes a festive tradition wherein a group of individuals—such as friends, family members, or colleagues—gather to exchange whimsical and often impractical gifts during a holiday celebration. The procedure typically commences with participants either adopting a Secret Santa framework or drawing numbers to establish a sequential order. The individual assigned the first number selects an unopened gift, unveiling it for the assembly. Each subsequent participant faces a choice: to appropriate an already revealed gift from a preceding participant or to select a new, unopened parcel.

Should a gift be appropriated, the individual from whom it was taken then selects a replacement from the pool of unopened gifts. This cycle of selection and appropriation continues until every participant has taken a turn. To prevent indefinite circulation, a conventional rule limits any single gift to a maximum of three appropriations; the fourth individual to claim the item retains it permanently.

As the primary objective of this exchange is communal amusement rather than material value, participants are encouraged to prioritize humor and novelty over monetary expenditure. Consequently, the most successful gifts are frequently those deemed eccentric or humorous. RICHMOND HEIGHTS, Ohio (KRON/CNN) — A nurse in Ohio is now out of a job after deciding she was too sick to work.
She says the hospital she worked for fired her after she got the flu.
We know this flu season is worse than normal, and when one “fill-in” nurse at University Hospitals said she was too sick to work two times over the course of a few days, it violated hospital policy.
Just after Christmas Theresa Puckett was hardly a picture of good health.
She called out sick once at the end of 2017, and when she came back, a superior sent her home early because she was still fighting off the flu.
“I was putting in my cough drops, I was drinking my water, I was putting in my Mucinex,” Puckett said. “I mean, the whole nine yards just to patch myself up enough to go to work.”
That led to another sick day, opening her up to being fired because of UH’s policy that temporary nurses called PRNs, like Theresa, may be dismissed after two non-approved absences over 60-days.
Theresa says it speaks to the nursing and hospital culture, keeping hospitals staffed no matter what the consequences.
“But when it happened to me, and I really truly was too sick to go to work, I was punished for that,” Puckett said. “I was punished for staying home with a doctor’s note.”
UH has a “no-fault” attendance policy, where the hospital says “notes from a physician do not ‘excuse’ an occurrence of absence.”
The policy says only approved leaves of absence, workplace illnesses or injuries, scheduled paid time off–like vacation time or doctors appointments–or jury duty or bereavement leave are considered excused.
That means even Theresa’s note from her own doctor saying she shouldn’t interact with people who are already sick wasn’t enough.
rewrite:
In Richmond Heights, Ohio, a nurse employed on a contingent basis was terminated from her position at University Hospitals following two occurrences of influenza-related absence within a brief period during the 2017-2018 flu season. The nurse, Theresa Puckett, reported first calling in sick at the end of December 2017. Upon her return, a supervisor determined she remained visibly ill and sent her home early. After attempting to mitigate her symptoms, Puckett called in sick a second time. These two absences, occurring within a 60-day window, constituted a violation of the hospital’s attendance policy for per diem or “PRN” staff, which permits termination following two unapproved absences.

Puckett contends her dismissal highlights a problematic institutional culture within healthcare that prioritizes maintaining staffing levels above all else, even when it conflicts with employee health and sound public health practice. She asserts she was legitimately incapacitated and provided a physician’s note recommending isolation to avoid exposing immunocompromised patients. However, the hospital’s formal “no-fault” attendance policy does not accept medical documentation to excuse an absence occurrence. According to the policy, only pre-approved leaves, workplace injuries or illnesses, scheduled paid time off, jury duty, or bereavement leave are considered excused absences.

Consequently, Puckett’s documented medical condition and physician’s advice were deemed insufficient grounds for an excused absence under the policy’s strict parameters. This case raises questions regarding the balance between rigid attendance protocols, the welfare of healthcare workers, and the potential public health implications of compelling contagious staff to report for duty.

Related Coverage Brewin’ up with Coal Yard Coffee
INDIANAPOLIS (WISH) — We’re talking this java morning.
24-Hour News 8’s Dick Wolfsie is on a tour of local coffee shops.
First up, he headed down to the south side to check out Strange Brew Coffee in Greenwood.
The locally-owned shop has been open for about 14 years. Owner Daniel Carr says it is the oldest coffee shop in Greenwood and is all about creating a community feel.
“We have local artists that we give space to,” Carr said. “We don’t take profits from their sales. What they sell is what they get. And we rotate them out every once and a while. So, we like to support the local art community.”
What do customers think of the shop?
“People from all sorts of walks of life come in here, they enjoy their products,” said Andrew Dills. “It’s just wonderful place for drinks and gathering and a sense of oneness.”
Next up, Dick popped up to Rabble Coffee on the east side just near 10th and Rural streets.
General Manager Josie Hunckler highlighted what the shop is doing for the community.
“We have a pay-it-forward system,” Hunckler said. “There’s a lot of scarcity in our neighborhood and we’re just trying to, like, help feed people and get people coffees. So what you can do here is you can buy a burrito or a medium coffee for someone else.”
The company has a token system to help with their pay-it-forward system.
rewrite:
This segment of a local news feature examines two Indianapolis-area coffee establishments, highlighting their distinct approaches to fostering community engagement. The first destination visited was Strange Brew Coffee in Greenwood, a locally-owned operation that has been serving the community for approximately fourteen years. According to proprietor Daniel Carr, this tenure establishes the shop as the oldest of its kind in Greenwood, with a central mission of cultivating a communal atmosphere. This is achieved in part through a dedicated support of local artists. Carr explained, “We provide display space for local artists and do not take any commission from their sales; they retain all proceeds. We rotate the featured artists periodically, which is our way of supporting the local arts community.” Patron Andrew Dills characterized the environment as a welcoming gathering place, noting, “Individuals from diverse backgrounds frequent the shop, enjoy the products, and appreciate the venue as a wonderful space for beverages and fostering a sense of unity.”

The subsequent visit was to Rabble Coffee, located on the city’s east side. General Manager Josie Hunckler detailed the shop’s specific initiative to address local needs, stating, “We operate a pay-it-forward system. Recognizing the economic scarcity present in our neighborhood, we aim to help provide meals and coffee. Customers have the option to purchase a burrito or a medium coffee for a future patron in need.” To facilitate this program, the shop utilizes a token system.

The unprecedented flow of leaks coming out of the American intelligence community about President Donald Trump and members of his inner circle does not appear to be stemming anytime soon. Tonight, the New York Times published a report based on the account of anonymous U.S. intelligence officials detailing how “phone records and intercepted calls show that members of Donald J. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign and other Trump associates had repeated contacts with senior Russian intelligence officials in the year before the election.” The Times notes that U.S. intelligence “intercepted the communications around the same time that they were discovering evidence that Russia was trying to disrupt the presidential election by hacking into the Democratic National Committee.”
The National Security Agency, which monitors the communications of foreign intelligence services, initially captured the communications between Mr. Trump’s associates and Russians as part of routine foreign surveillance. After that, the F.B.I. asked the N.S.A. to collect as much information as possible about the Russian operatives on the phone calls, and to search through troves of previous intercepted communications that had not been analyzed.
…
But the intercepts alarmed American intelligence and law enforcement agencies, in part because of the amount of contact that was occurring while Mr. Trump was speaking glowingly about the Russian president, Vladimir V. Putin. At one point last summer, Mr. Trump said at a campaign event that he hoped Russian intelligence services had stolen Hillary Clinton’s emails and would make them public.
The officials said the intercepted communications were not limited to Trump campaign officials, and included other associates of Mr. Trump. On the Russian side, the contacts also included members of the Russian government outside of the intelligence services, the officials said. All of the current and former officials spoke on the condition of anonymity because the continuing investigation is classified.
rewrite:
The ongoing dissemination of unauthorized disclosures from within the United States intelligence community concerning former President Donald Trump and his associates shows no indication of abating. In a recent report, *The New York Times*, citing anonymous U.S. intelligence officials, detailed that obtained telephone records and intercepted communications indicate repeated contacts between members of Donald J. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, along with other Trump associates, and senior Russian intelligence officials during the year preceding the election. The report further notes that these communications were intercepted contemporaneously with the discovery of evidence indicating Russian efforts to disrupt the presidential election through the cyber intrusion of the Democratic National Committee.

These communications were initially collected by the National Security Agency (NSA), which conducts routine surveillance of foreign intelligence services. Subsequently, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) requested the NSA to expand its collection efforts regarding the Russian operatives involved and to conduct retrospective analyses of previously unexamined intercepted communications.

The content of these intercepts generated significant concern within U.S. intelligence and law enforcement agencies. This concern was compounded by the frequency of the contacts occurring alongside public statements by then-candidate Trump expressing admiration for Russian President Vladimir V. Putin. Notably, during a campaign event in the summer of 2016, Mr. Trump publicly stated he hoped Russian intelligence services had procured Hillary Clinton’s emails and would release them.

According to the officials, the intercepted communications were not confined to formal campaign staff but encompassed a wider circle of Mr. Trump’s associates. On the Russian side, contacts extended beyond intelligence personnel to include other Russian government officials. All sources, both current and former officials, provided this information under conditions of anonymity due to the classified nature of the ongoing investigation.

Portia Woodman scored eight tries as New Zealand hammered Hong Kong 121-0, while there were also wins for Canada, England, USA, Ireland and France on day two of the Women’s World Cup in Dublin.
Playing with pace and power, the Blacks Ferns steamrolled Hong Kong, with Woodman at the centre of the 19-try rout. New Zealand ran in nine first-half tries for a commanding 57-0 lead at the break and they more than doubled that tally with 10 tries in the second stanza. The bonus-point victory takes New Zealand top of the log in Pool A.
Canada ground out 15-0 win against Wales with Lori Josephson and Magali Harvey dotting down. The result means Canada are now one point behind New Zealand in the standings.
In Pool B, England registered a comfortable 56-13 bonus-point win over Italy. Danielle Waterman, Lydia Thompson and Emily Scarratt scored two tries each.
The USA also collected maximum log points with a 43-0 triumph against Spain. The bonus-point win puts the USA and England are level on 10 points apiece and means the forthcoming match between the sides will be a straight shootout for a spot in the semi-finals.
Ireland needed a strong second half performance to beat a gallant Japan outfit 24-14. Japan led 14-0 at half time, but the hosts came to life in the last 25 minutes to the win.
France lashed Australia 48-0 in the last game of the day. The win takes the French two points clear of Ireland at the summit of the Pool C standings.
Photo: World Rugby
rewrite:
On the second day of the Women’s Rugby World Cup in Dublin, New Zealand delivered a commanding performance, defeating Hong Kong 121-0. Portia Woodman was instrumental in the victory, scoring eight of her side’s nineteen tries. Demonstrating considerable pace and power, the Black Ferns established a 57-0 lead by halftime with nine tries, before adding a further ten in the second half. This bonus-point win places New Zealand at the top of Pool A.

In the same pool, Canada secured a 15-0 victory over Wales, with tries from Lori Josephson and Magali Harvey, positioning them one point behind New Zealand in the standings. Meanwhile, in Pool B, England achieved a comfortable 56-13 bonus-point win against Italy, featuring two tries each from Danielle Waterman, Lydia Thompson, and Emily Scarratt. The United States also earned maximum points with a 43-0 triumph over Spain, placing them level with England on ten points. Consequently, their upcoming match will determine which team advances to the semi-finals.

Ireland overcame a resilient Japanese team, who led 14-0 at halftime, by mounting a strong second-half comeback to win 24-14. In the final match of the day, France dominated Australia with a 48-0 victory, moving two points clear of Ireland at the summit of Pool C. These results set a competitive stage for the remainder of the tournament’s pool phase.

Newlywed actress Jessica Chastain is in talks to take on a villain role in the next X-Men film.
Producer/screenwriter Simon Kinberg will make his directorial debut on X-Men: Dark Phoenix, and according to Deadline.com, Chastain has been tapped to tackle the character Shi’ar Empress Lilandra.
Franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence, Michael Fassbender, James McAvoy, and Nicholas Hoult will all return for the next movie, as will Sophie Turner, Tye Sheridan, and Kodi Smit-McPhee, who joined the cast for 2016’s X-Men: Apocalypse.
Kinberg is also producing the project, alongside Hutch Parker and Lauren Shuler Donner. He has long been involved with the X-Men franchise and wrote 2006’s X: Men: The Last Stand, in addition to writing and producing X-Men: Days of Future Past and X-Men: Apocalypse. He also produced X-Men: First Class and Deadpool, while he is involved in its upcoming sequel, and is working on X-Men: The New Mutants, which comes out next year.
X-Men: Dark Phoenix will focus on Game of Thrones’ Turner as powerful young mutant Jean Grey, also known as Dark Phoenix. It is set for release in November, 2018.
Lawrence previously ruled herself out of returning to the X-Men franchise, but admitted she would reconsider if she was allowed to play Mystique alongside Chris Pratt’s Star-Lord in a Guardians of the Galaxy film.
“I won’t be Mystique in the X-Men movies, but I would love to be Mystique in Guardians Of The Galaxy,” she said. “I wonder if I could do that?”
Meanwhile, one person who will not be returning to the franchise is Hugh Jackman. The actor recently completed his last run as Wolverine in spin-off film Logan.

Conversely, Hugh Jackman has definitively concluded his tenure as Wolverine, following his final performance in the 2017 film *Logan*.

PINELLAS COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) — On Saturday, U.S. Representative Charlie Crist (D – St. Petersburg) will meet with community leaders, parents and teenagers to try and find a solution for the growing problem of teens stealing cars in Pinellas County.
The Pinellas County Sheriff has called this issue an epidemic.
Crist will also sit down with non-profit and community leaders for a panel discussion on how to get young people more engaged.
This comes after local, county and state leaders met over the summer with parents and teens to try and identify why this is happening.
“The takeaway from our meeting last summer was that kids are hungry for programs aimed at their interests. It was also clear we need to do a better job letting them know what’s currently available. With that in mind, our office will be hosting a local youth program expo this Saturday,” said Crist. “It will bring together non-profits working with at-risk youth, so they can share information on what’s being offered to children, their parents, and community leaders. I’m hopeful it might also lead to some synergy and partnerships between the organizations participating.”
The event Saturday is free and open to the public. It will be held at the Childs Park Recreation and Fitness Center in St. Petersburg from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Teen vehicle thefts have been a problem in Pinellas County for months now.
On Feb. 1, four teenagers were arrested after police say they tried to hit officers with a minivan they had stolen in St. Petersburg.
Last August, three teens with lengthy criminal records died in a crash in Palm Harbor while playing a game of “cat and mouse” in two stolen vehicles. In a news conference after the crash, Pinellas County Sheriff Bob Gualtieri described the incident as “an unfortunate continuation of the epidemic of juveniles engaging in the deadly game of auto burglary and auto thefts.”
Back in March of 2016, three teenage girls were found dead inside a car that drove into a St. Pete pond. All three girls had criminal histories which included grand theft auto.

LIVERPOOL, England (Reuters) - Everton manager Ronald Koeman said Wayne Rooney, who scored on his return to the club in the 1-0 win over Stoke on Saturday, was far from a spent force and showed exactly why he was the right signing for the club.
Rooney's move back to his boyhood club, after 13 successful years at Manchester United, divided opinion between those who viewed it as a welcome romantic return and those who felt he was not the right player for Koeman's new-look side.
But in his first Premier League outing Rooney not only scored the winner with a beautifully executed header from a Dominic Calvert-Lewin cross, but he also exuded quality and composure throughout.
"There was one player in an Everton shirt today who was, from the first second to the last, comfortable on the pitch," said the Dutch manager.
"He made every decision the right one and he scored a great goal from a great cross from Dominic.
"In difficult moments, he showed his experience. That is why we signed Wayne -- expecting to show his team-mates all that experience, and it was really important," he said.
Rooney last scored a goal for Everton at Goodison on March 13, 2004 when he claimed the winner against Portsmouth.
That gap of 4,869 days is the longest between goals for the same club in the Premier League. The header was his 300th involvement in a goal in the Premier League, with 101 assists to add to his 199 goals. Only Alan Shearer, with 324, has more.
And he joined Shearer and Frank Lampard with the most goals on the league's opening day - eight.
Koeman not only believes that Rooney fits perfectly into his plans at Everton, but he also thinks he is far from the faded force that many felt he was becoming at United.
"Wayne showed he is still one of the best players in his position and he showed today the player that we expected," said Koeman.
"A lot of cleverness on the pitch and a great goal and a great header. We can't ask for more than he showed today."

In a post-match commentary following Everton Football Club’s 1-0 victory over Stoke City on Saturday, manager Ronald Koeman asserted that Wayne Rooney’s performance decisively countered narratives of the player being a diminished force, thereby validating the strategic rationale behind his acquisition. Rooney’s return to his formative club, after a thirteen-year tenure at Manchester United marked by considerable success, had elicited divergent perspectives. While some framed the transfer as a sentimentally resonant homecoming, others questioned its tactical suitability for Koeman’s evolving squad blueprint.

However, during his inaugural Premier League appearance for Everton in this campaign, Rooney not only secured the match-winning goal—a precisely directed header from a Dominic Calvert-Lewin delivery—but also demonstrated sustained technical quality and tactical composure throughout the fixture. Koeman observed, “There was one player in an Everton shirt today who was, from the first second to the last, comfortable on the pitch. He made every decision the right one and he scored a great goal from a great cross from Dominic.” The Dutch manager further emphasized the value of Rooney’s seasoned influence, stating, “In difficult moments, he showed his experience. That is why we signed Wayne—expecting him to show his team-mates all that experience, and it was really important.”

The goal marked a significant personal milestone for Rooney, being his first for Everton at Goodison Park since March 13, 2004, when he scored the winner against Portsmouth. The intervening period of 4,869 days constitutes the longest interval between goals for the same club in Premier League history. Furthermore, the header represented Rooney’s 300th direct goal involvement in the competition, combining 199 goals with 101 assists—a tally exceeded only by Alan Shearer’s 324. Additionally, Rooney equaled the records of Shearer and Frank Lampard by scoring his eighth goal on a Premier League opening day.

Koeman’s assessment extends beyond the immediate match impact, contending that Rooney integrates seamlessly into Everton’s strategic framework and remains a player of considerable caliber, contrary to perceptions of decline during his latter period at Manchester United. “Wayne showed he is still one of the best players in his position and he showed today the player that we expected,” Koeman concluded. “A lot of cleverness on the pitch and a great goal and a great header. We cannot ask for more than he showed today.”

All 6 suspects are facing criminal charges after authorities recovered 890 kilos of shabu worth P3 million
MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Justice (DOJ) will begin its preliminary investigation into the criminal charges filed against 6 suspects involved in a major drug bust operations in San Juan City on Tuesday, January 3.
The suspects – Chinese nationals Shi Gui Xiong alias "Xiong," Che Wen De aka "Jacky Tan," and Wu Li Yong alias David Go, as well as their alleged Filipino cohorts Abdullah Mahmod Jahmal, Salim Cocodao Arafat, and Basher Tawaki Jama – will be facing prosecutors at 10:30 am for violation of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.
The 6 suspects were arrested following several raids in houses in Mangga Street, Barangay Little Baguio and Bonifacio Street in San Juan.
Charges were filed against them before the DOJ for the manufacture and sale of illegal drugs on December 27. Inquest proceedings were conducted before Assistant State Prosecutors Mary Jane Sytat and Ethel Rhea Suril.
The drug busts in San Juan City were part of a 4-month long operation led by the National Bureau of Investigation.
The operation, considered as the biggest so far under President Rodrigo Duterte’s term, led authorities to recover 890 kilos of shabu with a street valued pegged at around P3 million.
Assisted by their legal counsels, the suspects have all agreed to file their counter-affidavits during the prelimineray investigation. They, however, have waived their right to immediate resolution of charges for their immediate release. – Rappler.com
rewrite:
On Tuesday, January 3, a preliminary investigation will commence by the Department of Justice (DOJ) into criminal charges filed against six individuals apprehended during a significant narcotics operation in San Juan City. The suspects comprise three Chinese nationals—Shi Gui Xiong (alias "Xiong"), Che Wen De (alias "Jacky Tan"), and Wu Li Yong (alias David Go)—along with three Filipino associates: Abdullah Mahmod Jahmal, Salim Cocodao Arafat, and Basher Tawaki Jama. They are scheduled to appear before prosecutors at 10:30 a.m. to address allegations of violating the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

Their arrest ensued from coordinated raids at residences on Mangga Street, Barangay Little Baguio, and Bonifacio Street in San Juan. Formal charges pertaining to the manufacture and sale of illegal substances were lodged with the DOJ on December 27, with inquest proceedings subsequently overseen by Assistant State Prosecutors Mary Jane Sytat and Ethel Rhea Suril. This enforcement action was the culmination of a four-month investigation spearheaded by the National Bureau of Investigation.

Deemed the largest seizure of its kind under President Rodrigo Duterte's administration, the operation resulted in the confiscation of 890 kilograms of shabu, with an estimated street value of approximately three million Philippine pesos. While assisted by legal counsel, the accused have elected to submit counter-affidavits during the preliminary investigation. They have, however, formally waived their right to seek an immediate resolution of the charges for the purpose of provisional release.

The Borussia Dortmund team bus is seen after an explosion near their hotel before their Champions League quarter-final first leg game against AS Monaco in Dortmund, Germany. REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach/Livepic
BERLIN German prosecutors have doubts about the authenticity of letters that suggested Islamist militants attacked soccer team Borussia Dortmund's bus and a newspaper cited an investigator as saying right-wing extremists were probably behind the bomb attack.
Three identical letters printed in German found near the scene of Tuesday's attack in Dortmund had stated it was carried out "in the name of Allah", broadcaster ARD reported, citing other media. The letters referred to the use of Tornado reconnaissance planes in Syria, which Germany has deployed as part of the military campaign against Islamic State.
But a report commissioned by investigators said there were "significant doubts" about the letters and suggested they had been written to trick people into thinking there was an Islamist militant motive, ARD added.
"That's accurate," Frauke Koehler, a spokeswoman for the federal public prosecutor's office, said when asked to comment on the ARD report.
"It is indeed doubtful," she said of the letters.
Asked why there were doubts, she said she could not give any more information as the investigation was ongoing.
Bild newspaper cited an investigator as saying: "The overall circumstances lead us to believe it's most likely that the perpetrators have a right-wing background."
Koehler declined to comment on that report.
German newspaper Tagesspiegel said on its website on Friday it had received an anonymous far-right email claiming responsibility for Tuesday's attack. It said the email referred to Adolf Hitler, railed against multiculturalism and suggested another attack might occur on April 22.
Koehler said prosecutors had received a copy of the letter but she could not comment further.
The Borussia Dortmund players' bus was heading to their stadium for a Champions League match against AS Monaco on Tuesday when three explosions occurred, injuring Spanish defender Marc Bartra.
Experts have been expressing scepticism for days about the origins of the letters claiming responsibility. Security sources have said investigators are looking at whether left or right-wing extremists may have carried out the attack.
A day after the attack, the interior minister of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia described the letters as "unusual".
(Reporting by Michelle Martin; Editing by Alison Williams)
rewrite:
Following an explosive incident targeting the Borussia Dortmund team bus en route to a UEFA Champions League quarter-final fixture against AS Monaco on Tuesday, German federal prosecutors have raised serious questions regarding the authenticity of claimed Islamist militant responsibility. The attack, which resulted in injuries to Spanish defender Marc Bartra, was initially accompanied by three identical letters discovered near the scene. These documents, written in German and cited by broadcaster ARD, purported to justify the act “in the name of Allah” and referenced Germany’s deployment of Tornado reconnaissance aircraft in Syria as part of the coalition against Islamic State.

However, an investigative report has cast significant doubt on the legitimacy of these communications. A spokeswoman for the federal public prosecutor’s office, Frauke Koehler, confirmed the assessment, stating, “It is indeed doubtful,” and indicated the letters may constitute a deliberate attempt to mislead authorities by suggesting an Islamist militant motive. Koehler declined to elaborate further, citing the ongoing nature of the investigation.

In a development pointing toward an alternative line of inquiry, the Bild newspaper quoted an investigator suggesting the perpetrators likely possessed a right-wing extremist background, based on an evaluation of the overall circumstances. While Koehler refrained from commenting on this specific report, further potential evidence emerged on Friday. The Tagesspiegel newspaper reported receiving an anonymous far-right email claiming responsibility for the attack. This communication allegedly contained references to Adolf Hitler, denounced multiculturalism, and hinted at the possibility of a subsequent attack on April 22. Prosecutors have acknowledged receipt of a copy of this email but have offered no additional commentary.

This skepticism regarding the initial claims aligns with broader expert opinion and official statements in the days following the event. Security sources have indicated that investigators are examining potential involvement from across the extremist spectrum, including both left and right-wing groups. The interior minister of North Rhine-Westphalia, the state where Dortmund is located, previously characterized the physical letters as “unusual,” underscoring the perplexing nature of the evidence. The investigation thus remains focused on unraveling the precise ideological motivations and identities of those responsible for the violent disruption.

March 31 Royal Dutch Shell Plc plans to double the capacity of its liquefied natural gas import facility at Hazira on India's west coast to 10 million tonnes a year, a top company executive said on Friday.
Shell Gas B.V, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell Plc, owns a 74 percent stake in Hazira LNG Ltd, while Total Gaz Electricite France, a unit of France's Total SA, holds the rest.
"We've done all the work, now it's sort of taking a look at when is the right timing in terms of demand that's available," Nitin Prasad, chairman of Shell Companies in India, told Reuters, without giving a timeline for the expansion.
A government panel said in a report in April 2015 that Hazira LNG will look to expand the capacity of its LNG terminal in the western state of Gujarat by 50 percent to 7.5 million tonnes per annum in the fiscal year to March 2017.
Shell on Friday opened a new technology centre in Bengaluru, the capital of the southern state Karnataka. The technology hub, Shell's third in the world, is aimed at expanding the company's research and development activities in Asia.
India aims to raise the share of natural gas in its energy mix to 15 percent in the next three years from about 6.5 percent at present, as it attempts to achieve energy security while keeping pollution levels down.
India's gas imports in April 2016-February 2017 rose 16.4 percent to 22.53 billion cubic metres, according to government data. (Reporting by Arathy S Nair and Tanvi Mehta in Bengaluru; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)
rewrite:
On March 31, a senior executive of Royal Dutch Shell Plc announced the company's intention to double the annual capacity of its liquefied natural gas import terminal at Hazira, on India's western coast, to 10 million tonnes. The Hazira facility is operated by Hazira LNG Ltd, in which Shell Gas B.V., a subsidiary of Royal Dutch Shell Plc, holds a 74 percent equity stake; the remaining 26 percent is held by Total Gaz Electricite France, a subsidiary of France's Total SA. Nitin Prasad, Chairman of Shell Companies in India, informed Reuters that preparatory studies for the expansion are complete, stating, "We've done all the work, now it's sort of taking a look at when is the right timing in terms of demand that's available." He did not, however, provide a specific timeline for the project's execution.

This proposed expansion follows a prior governmental assessment. An April 2015 report by a government panel indicated that Hazira LNG was expected to increase its terminal capacity in Gujarat by 50 percent, to 7.5 million tonnes per annum, within the fiscal year ending March 2017. The announcement coincided with the inauguration of Shell's new technology centre in Bengaluru, Karnataka. This hub, the company's third globally, is designed to augment its research and development operations within Asia.

This infrastructure development aligns with India's broader energy policy objectives. The government aims to elevate the proportion of natural gas in the national energy mix from approximately 6.5 percent to 15 percent within three years, a strategy intended to enhance energy security while mitigating pollution. Supporting this shift, government data indicates that India's gas imports for the period April 2016 to February 2017 increased by 16.4 percent, reaching 22.53 billion cubic metres.

Scrooge is transported to Kelowna in New Vintage Theatre’s new holiday play, opening Wednesday
Head to the Rotary Centre For The Arts this week for a classic Christmas play with a promised Kelowna twist.
New Vintage Theatre’s new holiday play brings the holiday’s infamous Scrooge to the streets of Kelowna.
Adapted for the stage by Artistic Director Bonnie Gratz, A Kelowna Christmas Carol incorporates the beloved elements of Dickens’s original story; Scrooge, the Cratchits and an adorable Tiny Tim, and places them in Kelowna at a pivotal period of the city’s history.
“Our play looks at the character of Scrooge in a very unique way. I have incorporated stories of Kelowna historical figures such as one of the city’s first doctors Dr. Benjamin Boyce and his wife, Mary; Countess Bubna, the exotic first owner of The Eldorado, then called The Eldorado Arms Hotel; Frank and Nell DeHart and Mar Jok. Arthur Knox, the land magnet that owned almost all of Kelowna from Water Street to The Mission, plays an important role, too,” said Gratz.
Another surprising element of this production will be the community members that are set to take part in the play as hosts.
Those hotsts include: Dom Rampone, Mayor Colin Basran, Councillor Maxine DeHart, Marianna DeHart and Linda Digby of Kelowna Museums, who assisted New Vintage in the research stage of play development.
Gratz said the play has already received a huge response from the community and there are just a few tickets remaining for evening and matinee shows.
Tickets are available from www.rotarycentreforthearts.com or The Rotary Centre For The Arts Box Office.
A Kelowna Christmas Carol by Bonnie Gratz runs Dec.13-21 at The Rotary Centre For The Arts.
Public shows are at 7 p.m. on Dec.14, 15, 16 and 21 with a matinee on Dec.17 at 2 p.m.
For more about New Vintage, check out their website at www.newvintage.ca.
To report a typo, email:
newstips@kelownacapnews.com.
@carmenweld
carmen.weld@bpdigital.ca
Like us on Facebook and follow us on Twitter.
Graham Daley and Vince Walzak in A Kelowna Christmas Carol. Photo Credit: Alison Beaumont
rewrite:
New Vintage Theatre inaugurates its seasonal production this Wednesday with a localized adaptation of a classic narrative, transporting the iconic Ebenezer Scrooge to the setting of Kelowna. The performance will be staged at the Rotary Centre for the Arts, offering a traditional Christmas tale reimagined with distinct regional elements. Under the direction of Artistic Director Bonnie Gratz, *A Kelowna Christmas Carol* retains the fundamental characters and structure of Charles Dickens’s original work—including Scrooge, the Cratchit family, and the endearing figure of Tiny Tim—while situating the narrative within a historically significant era of Kelowna’s development.

Gratz notes that the production presents a distinctive interpretation of Scrooge’s character, integrating narratives of notable local historical figures. These include among the city’s earliest medical practitioners, Dr. Benjamin Boyce and his wife Mary; Countess Bubna, the inaugural proprietor of the establishment known then as The Eldorado Arms Hotel; Frank and Nell DeHart alongside Mar Jok; and the prominent landholder Arthur Knox, whose holdings once encompassed much of the area from Water Street to The Mission. An additional notable feature of this staging is the participation of several community members who will serve as hosts during the performance. This group comprises Dom Rampone, Mayor Colin Basran, Councillor Maxine DeHart, Marianna DeHart, and Linda Digby of Kelowna Museums, the latter having provided research assistance during the play’s developmental phase.

The production has, according to Gratz, elicited considerable community interest, with limited ticket availability remaining for both evening and matinee presentations. *A Kelowna Christmas Carol*, written by Bonnie Gratz, will be performed at the Rotary Centre for the Arts from December 13th through December 21st. Public evening performances are scheduled for 7:00 p.m. on December 14th, 15th, 16th, and 21st, with a matinee on December 17th at 2:00 p.m. Tickets may be acquired via the venue’s official website or directly through its box office. Further information regarding New Vintage Theatre is accessible through its institutional website.

Manta rays are some of the sea’s most graceful creatures, capable of gliding almost effortlessly and able to swim efficiently even in turbulent water. Now, researchers at the National University of Singapore have created a robot that mimics the manta.
Dubbed “MantaDroid,” the cute little bot is about 14 inches long and 25 inches wide and weighs 1.5 pounds. Using its pair of flexible pectoral fins, each powered by a single electric motor, it’s able to swim for up to 10 hours.
“Manta rays are known to be extremely efficient swimmers,” Chew Chee Meng, an associate professor in the university’s department of mechanical engineering, told NBC News MACH in an email. “We wanted to explore an alternative solution to traditional propeller-based thrusters that are used by most autonomous underwater vehicles.”
The robot could be used for search and rescue operations, as well as to perform underwater surveys and inspections, like those conducted by environmental groups. It could even be deployed in swarms for faster, more efficient searches and surveys, according to the researchers.
The engineers spent two years testing 40 different fin designs, aiming to recreate how real-life manta rays thrust forward by flapping their fins to drive water backwards. They say the MantaDroid achieved “good maneuverability” when tested in a pool. The bot was able to swim at a top speed of 2.3 feet per second — equivalent to almost 1.6 miles per hour.
Like its real-life counterpart, the MantaDroid has a wide, flat body, which means it could be equipped with multiple sensors on its “belly.” And the fins seem to have big benefits over propellers, Meng said. In addition to being less likely to get tangled in aquatic plants, they cause less turbulence than props.
“As a whole, MantaDroid tends to have less environmental impacts on marine ecosystems,” Meng said.
Meng and his colleagues want to test the MantaDroid in a marine environment to study its swimming ability at various depths, and to gauge its ability to handle currents.
The engineers are also working to make the bot autonomous.
“We plan to incorporate sensors and implement perception algorithms on the current prototype to make MantaDroid autonomous after we have completed the maneuverability study and design optimization,” Meng said.
rewrite:
Manta rays, recognized for their exceptional grace and hydrodynamic efficiency, represent a model of effective aquatic locomotion, even within turbulent marine environments. Researchers at the National University of Singapore have successfully engineered a bio-inspired robotic platform that emulates this species. This device, designated the "MantaDroid," measures approximately 35 centimeters in length and 63 centimeters in width, with a mass of 0.7 kilograms. It is propelled by a pair of flexible pectoral fins, each actuated by a singular electric motor, enabling operational endurance of up to ten hours.

Associate Professor Chew Chee Meng of the Department of Mechanical Engineering explained the project's rationale, noting that manta rays demonstrate remarkable swimming efficiency. The research initiative sought to investigate an alternative propulsion methodology to the conventional propeller-based thrusters commonly employed in autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The potential applications for such a platform are considerable, including deployment in search and rescue operations, underwater environmental surveyance, and structural inspection. Furthermore, researchers suggest that coordinated deployment in swarms could significantly enhance the speed and efficiency of such tasks.

The engineering team dedicated two years to hydrodynamic development, experimentally evaluating forty distinct fin designs to accurately replicate the biomechanical mechanism by which biological manta rays generate thrust through posteriorly directed water displacement via fin undulation. Pool-based testing demonstrated that the MantaDroid attained favorable maneuverability, achieving a maximum velocity of 0.7 meters per second, equivalent to approximately 1.6 miles per hour.

Anatomically analogous to its biological counterpart, the robot possesses a broad, planar body. This morphology provides substantial surface area for the integration of multiple sensory instruments on its ventral side. Professor Chew further highlighted the functional advantages of the fin-based propulsion system over traditional propellers. Specifically, the fins exhibit a reduced propensity for entanglement in aquatic vegetation and generate significantly less hydrodynamic turbulence. Consequently, Professor Chew stated, "As a whole, MantaDroid tends to have less environmental impacts on marine ecosystems."

Future research directions include open-water testing to evaluate the platform's swimming performance across a range of depths and its capacity to navigate oceanic currents. Concurrently, the engineering team is developing autonomous operational capabilities. Professor Chew indicated that following the completion of ongoing maneuverability studies and design optimization, the integration of sensors and implementation of perception algorithms on the current prototype are planned to facilitate fully autonomous operation.

A safety warning has been voiced by police after a rise in incidents involving drones.
Northumbria Police are issuing a safety message to all drone users after an increase in popularity.
Superintendent Sarah Pitt.
Officers say they are causing concerns and could cause hold ups and risks to plane journeys of they are flown close.
They have also warned about the legality of using them in crowded areas.
Superintendent Sarah Pitt, Northumbria Police’s operations department, said: “The public need to be aware that if we identify them as flying in restricted areas then they could be prosecuted.
“Some users don’t realise these types of aircraft are subject to rules and legislation.
"We need to ensure we do our part to keep the public safe and informed.
“You should always keep your drone within your line of sight and always fly your drone away from helicopters, aircrafts, airports and airfields; those found violating these rules could face prosecution.
“Flying these types of aircraft within 150 metres of a crowded area is a criminal offence and may infringe air safety legislation.
“Not only could flying drones in the flight paths of aircrafts cause major delays, some of which come at a great cost, but it could also put members of the public at risk and it will not be tolerated.”
rewrite:
Northumbria Police have issued a formal safety advisory in response to a growing number of incidents involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones. This warning follows a significant increase in their public usage. Superintendent Sarah Pitt of the Operations Department emphasized that irresponsible drone operation raises serious concerns, posing potential risks to aviation safety and causing disruptive delays to air travel.

The public is reminded that UAVs are subject to specific rules and legislation. Individuals must be aware that flying in restricted zones, including near airports, airfields, and aircraft, is unlawful. Operators are legally required to maintain direct visual line of sight with their drone and to avoid aviation infrastructure. Crucially, piloting a drone within 150 metres of a crowded area constitutes a criminal offence under air safety regulations.

Such breaches not only endanger public safety but also carry the risk of substantial financial penalties due to flight disruptions. Northumbria Police underscore that violations will be met with prosecution, as the force is committed to upholding these regulations to ensure community safety and the integrity of national airspace.

While one’s home oral hygiene routine provides defence against tooth decay and gum disease, regular professional care from the Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist is also a necessity.
[LONDON, 4/7/2018] – A Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist can provide the full range of oral health care. Cosmetic dentistry, urgent repairs and restorations, and regular preventive treatments are all on offer from the Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist.
Different kinds of treatment
The twice-yearly visit to the Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist is a crucial part of good oral health. When gum disease and tooth decay begin to take hold, the early signs are too discreet for the patient to notice at home. The skill and experience of a Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist means they can intervene with treatment before disease causes unnecessary harm. The Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist can also advise the patient on how to adjust their tooth brushing regime to maximise its effectiveness.
Aesthetic reasons often cause people to visit the Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist. Chipped teeth and tooth discolouration are common occurrences that can negatively affect the way a person feels about their appearance. Treatment for these conditions is speedy and effective.
The teeth whitening process turns a funny-looking smile into one that’s fresh and bright. Patients can select the particular shade of white they want for their smile, and the straightforward procedure leaves them with a fresh-feeling mouth.
Improvements
When a person has one or more teeth missing in London, they can have legitimate oral health concerns as well as cosmetic dissatisfaction. Gaps in the smile are usually not pleasant to look at. A Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist has a range of tooth replacement methods including bridges and dentures. Dental implants are joined with the patient’s jawbone to provide properly anchored replacement teeth that do their jobs with natural stability.
Looking ahead
A Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist can enhance the alignment of a patient’s teeth to improve their effectiveness as well as their appearance. Modern-day braces and aligners are designed to be nearly invisible, so the patient avoids the social discomfort associated with traditional metal braces.
A Harley Street Dental Clinic dentist aims to improve a person’s overall health by professionally caring for their teeth and gums.

While a diligent personal oral hygiene regimen constitutes a primary defence against dental caries and periodontal pathologies, the adjunct of regular professional care, as provided by the Harley Street Dental Clinic, remains an essential component of comprehensive oral health management. Ducati MotoGP rider Andrea Dovizioso of Italy rides during the Japanese Grand Prix at the Twin Ring Motegi circuit in Motegi, north of Tokyo, Japan, October 11, 2015.
(Reuters) - Ducati's Andrea Dovizioso held off MotoGP points leader Marc Marquez to claim his third victory of the season at the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday.
Italian Dovizioso, who started on a soft rear tyre, took the lead with seven laps to the finish line and maintained a slender advantage over Honda riders Marquez and Dani Pedrosa, who completed the podium.
Dovizioso's team mate Jorge Lorenzo finished fourth despite taking an early lead in dry conditions at the Red Bull Ring, while Johann Zarco finished fifth.
Yamaha endured a disappointing afternoon with Maverick Vinales and Valentino Rossi taking the sixth and seventh spot, respectively.
Alvaro Bautista secured an eighth-placed finish for Aspar Ducati, with Avintia Ducati's Loris Baz ended ninth.
KTM wildcard Mika Kallio beat last year's winner Andrea Iannone to the 10th spot.
Marquez leads the championship standings with 174 points, 16 ahead of second-placed Dovizioso. Vinales slipped to third spot with 150 points, followed by Rossi on 141.
rewrite: On October 11, 2015, Italian Ducati MotoGP rider Andrea Dovizioso participated in the Japanese Grand Prix at the Twin Ring Motegi circuit, located north of Tokyo. In subsequent competition, Ducati rider Andrea Dovizioso secured his third victory of the season at the Austrian Grand Prix, successfully defending against championship leader Marc Marquez. Starting the race on a soft rear tyre, Dovizioso assumed the lead with seven laps remaining, maintaining a narrow margin over Honda riders Marc Marquez and Dani Pedrosa, who completed the podium in second and third place respectively. Despite an early lead in dry conditions at the Red Bull Ring, Dovizioso's teammate Jorge Lorenzo finished fourth, followed by Johann Zarco in fifth. The Yamaha team experienced a disappointing result, with Maverick Viñales and Valentino Rossi finishing sixth and seventh. Álvaro Bautista placed eighth for Aspar Ducati, while Loris Baz of Avintia Ducati finished ninth. KTM wildcard entry Mika Kallio claimed tenth position, ahead of the previous year's winner, Andrea Iannone. In the championship standings, Marquez leads with 174 points, holding a sixteen-point advantage over Dovizioso. Viñales occupies third position with 150 points, followed by Rossi with 141.

The last of the area sprinkles ended Monday afternoon, but we are still waiting for cooler, drier air to roll in from the west and northwest. That will occur Monday night and very early Tuesday morning as the second of a pair of cold fronts sweeps east of the viewing area.
Expect a Tuesday morning start for the Red Stick around 50° to the lower 50s under generally fair skies. You'll notice a nice drop in the humidity too. We may not have entirely clear skies for Tuesday as wraparound flow brings clouds from the north, but you can look forward to fair skies through most of the day. Tuesday will be cooler in the afternoon too, with highs topping out in the 60s for most WAFB neighborhoods. And don’t forget Tuesday is the official first day of spring (astronomical spring - Spring Equinox). The official time for the change in seasons is 11:15 a.m. CDT.
The First Alert Forecast into the weekend looks like a great one! A warming trend will begin on Wednesday and continue into the weekend. The warm up will be accompanied by lots of sunshine for the work week with a mainly dry weekend on the way as well. Our forecast calls for highs in the Capital region around 70° for Wednesday, in the 70s for Thursday and Friday, and into the 80s for the weekend.
In the extended outlook, we are posting spotty showers for Sunday afternoon with a 30 percent chance of rain on Monday. Don’t let that ever so slight rain chance on Sunday change any weekend plans!
The Mississippi River is cresting along its stretch through the WAFB area, but we can expect extra high water to persist for Ole’ Man River for the next five to seven days before we start to see river levels fall. There's still a bit of a rise to come for the lower Atchafalaya (Morgan City), but the upper and middle stretches of that river are at/near crest and should show slow falls this week.

rewrite:

Conditions for Tuesday morning in the Baton Rouge area are projected to commence with temperatures approximately 50°F to the lower 50s under predominantly fair skies. A marked reduction in humidity levels is also anticipated. While cloud cover associated with northerly wraparound flow may preclude completely clear conditions, skies are expected to remain largely fair throughout the majority of the day. Afternoon highs will be cooler, generally reaching the 60s°F across most WAFB communities. Tuesday also marks the vernal equinox, denoting the astronomical commencement of spring at 11:15 a.m. CDT.

The extended forecast through the upcoming weekend indicates favorable conditions. A warming trend is anticipated to initiate on Wednesday and persist through the weekend. This period of rising temperatures will be accompanied by abundant sunshine during the workweek, with a predominantly dry weekend also expected. Projected high temperatures are near 70°F for the Capital region on Wednesday, ascending into the 70s°F for Thursday and Friday, and reaching the 80s°F over the weekend.

In the extended outlook, isolated showers are possible by Sunday afternoon, with a 30 percent probability of precipitation extending into Monday. This minimal rainfall chance is not expected to necessitate alterations to weekend plans.

Regarding area hydrology, the Mississippi River is currently at crest stage along its reach through the WAFB coverage area. Elevated water levels are forecast to persist for the subsequent five to seven days before a gradual recession begins. The lower Atchafalaya River near Morgan City may experience a slight additional rise, while the upper and middle segments are at or near crest and should begin a slow decline this week.

A new Golden Fisherman monument will be dedicated outside the Biloxi Maritime and Seafood Museum. (Photo Source: WLOX)
The world will soon get its first look at the new Golden Fisherman when the monument is dedicated just outside the Biloxi Maritime and Seafood Museum.
Wednesday work crews installed the stand where statue will permanently live. He remains shrouded in secrecy until Thursday night.
For now, the base of the statue, which like the old one, contains 811 names of Biloxi families that established the city's rich seafood history and heritage along with past shrimp kings and queens.
"Everyone is honored on the base, and the fisherman is on top," said Addison Riemann, who’s with the group of monument designers. He's 6-foot-tall and weighs 1,000 pounds. "He's lifelike. There's a lot of definition with his arms, and you'll see his veins popping out. You'll see a lot of definition, even in his knuckles."
The statue made its way to the Coast from Europe, much like the journey many of those families he represents have made over the years.
“This Golden Fisherman made the same exact voyage as so many of our ancestors did,” said Kim Ross Bush, president of the museum’s board of directors. “He came across the same Atlantic Ocean they did from Italy. He's beautiful, he's significant, and he means so much to all of us and he stands for all of us."
Copyright 2018 WLOX. All rights reserved.
rewrite:
A new monument entitled *The Golden Fisherman* is scheduled for dedication at the Biloxi Maritime and Seafood Museum. The installation marks the first public presentation of this work. Preparatory work concluded on Wednesday with the installation of the permanent pedestal, though the statue itself will remain concealed until the Thursday evening ceremony.

The monument’s base, consistent with its predecessor, is inscribed with 811 names. These commemorate Biloxi families foundational to the region’s seafood heritage, alongside former Shrimp Kings and Queens. Addison Riemann, a member of the design collective, explained the symbolic arrangement: "Everyone is honored on the base, and the fisherman is on top." The statue itself is a six-foot-tall, one-thousand-pound bronze figure. Riemann emphasized its detailed verisimilitude, noting the defined musculature of the arms, prominent veins, and even the articulation of the knuckles.

The statue’s journey from its European foundry to the Mississippi Coast intentionally mirrors the historical transatlantic passage of many local families. Kim Ross Bush, President of the Museum’s Board of Directors, underscored this parallel: “This Golden Fisherman made the same exact voyage as so many of our ancestors did, crossing the Atlantic from Italy. He is beautiful, significant, and deeply meaningful; he stands for all of us.” The monument thus serves as both an artistic tribute and a historical homage to the community’s origins.

The EFF urged South Africans to down tools and support the national strike against the R20 minimum wage hourly rate. Picture:Ayanda Ndamane/African News Agency/ANA
Johannesburg - The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) on Tuesday urged South Africans to down tools and support the national strike against the R20 minimum wage hourly rate.
"Government has already imposed VAT, sugar tax, fuel levy and all other manner of taxes to resolve an economic crisis that the workers did not create," the EFF said in a statement.
"The very same government proposes that the national minimum wage for all workers should be R20 per hour, even less than the minimum living wage that was in the findings of a research from UCT in 2014."
Read more: #SAFTUstrike: Saftu rallies forces for strike over minimum wage
The party said the proposed minimum wage will further entrench poverty and cause the present inequalities to remain a permanent feature of the country, even though the ruling African National Congress "claimed it advocates for radical economic transformation".
Also read: How Saftu's strike will affect Durbanites
Congress of South African Trade Unions' rival, the South African Federation of Trade Unions (Saftu) will embark on a general strike on Wednesday over what it termed "the biggest attacks on working-class people, trade unions and the poor" since the end of apartheid.
Saftu has slammed the planned national minimum wage of R20 per hour, or R3 500 a month, as well as amendments to labour laws. The union federation is also angry over economic hardships facing workers and the poor.
Cosatu has distanced itself from the strike, saying that it supports the minimum wage tabled.
African News Agency/ANA
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) issued a public appeal for a nationwide cessation of labor in protest against the proposed national minimum wage of R20 per hour. The political party articulated its position through an official statement, which contended that the government, having already implemented various fiscal measures such as Value-Added Tax, a sugar tax, and a fuel levy to address an economic crisis not of workers’ making, was now advancing a remuneration standard deemed insufficient. The EFF criticized the R20 hourly rate as falling below the minimum living wage benchmark established in a 2014 University of Cape Town study, arguing that such a policy would perpetuate poverty and cement existing socioeconomic inequalities. This outcome, the statement asserted, would persist despite the ruling African National Congress’s professed commitment to radical economic transformation.

Concurrently, the South African Federation of Trade Unions (Saftu), a rival to the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu), has organized a general strike for Wednesday. Saftu describes the proposed wage and accompanying amendments to labor legislation as the most severe assaults on the working class, trade unions, and the impoverished since the end of apartheid. The federation has denounced the monthly equivalent of approximately R3,500, citing the broader economic hardships confronting workers and the poor. In contrast, Cosatu has formally dissociated itself from the industrial action, expressing its support for the tabled minimum wage legislation.

Merck CEO Kenneth Frazier is leaving President Trump's American Manufacturing Council, saying, "I feel a responsibility to take a stand against intolerance and extremism."
The resignation came after Trump was criticized for his response to the violence at white supremacist events in Charlottesville, Va., over the weekend. The president, famous for his ability to be direct and forceful, was faulted for condemning violence "on many sides."
Within an hour of Merck announcing Frazier's withdrawal, Trump retorted on Twitter, "Now that Ken Frazier of Merck Pharma has resigned ... he will have more time to lower ripoff drug prices!"
In a statement on his resignation, Frazier said, "America's leaders must honor our fundamental values by clearly rejecting expressions of hatred, bigotry and group supremacy, which run counter to the American ideal that all people are created equal."
Frazier, who is African-American, said he was acting as both the CEO of Merck and "as a matter of personal conscience."
The rift did not seem to harm Merck's stock: The drug company's shares rose by nearly a full percentage point in the first hour of trading, to nearly $63.
Members of his own party have called on Trump to condemn Saturday's killing of a woman who had been protesting white supremacists as an act of domestic terrorism. The White House later stated that Trump was including "white supremacists, KKK Neo-Nazi and all extremist groups" in his remarks about the violence.
Frazier's departure is the latest high-profile exit from a White House advisory council since Trump took office in January.
After Trump announced in June that the U.S. would be leaving the Paris climate accord, both Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Disney CEO Bob Iger left his business advisory council.
Months earlier, in February, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick left the same panel during the fallout from Trump's executive order that banned immigrants from seven Muslim countries.
"The executive order is hurting many people in communities all across America," Kalanick said at the time.
rewrite:
Kenneth Frazier, Chief Executive Officer of Merck & Co., has resigned from President Donald Trump’s American Manufacturing Council, citing a moral obligation to oppose intolerance and extremism. His decision follows widespread criticism of the President’s initial response to the violent clashes at white supremacist rallies in Charlottesville, Virginia. President Trump, whose rhetoric is often characterized by directness, faced bipartisan reproach for broadly condemning violence “on many sides” without initially singling out the white nationalist groups involved. Within an hour of Merck’s public announcement, President Trump responded via Twitter, stating, “Now that Ken Frazier of Merck Pharma has resigned … he will have more time to lower ripoff drug prices!”

In an official statement explaining his resignation, Frazier asserted, “America’s leaders must honor our fundamental values by clearly rejecting expressions of hatred, bigotry and group supremacy, which run counter to the American ideal that all people are created equal.” Frazier, who is African-American, indicated he was acting both in his capacity as Merck’s CEO and pursuant to his personal conscience. The departure did not appear to negatively impact Merck’s market valuation; the company’s stock price increased by nearly one percent in early trading, reaching approximately $63 per share.

Frazier’s resignation occurred amid mounting pressure from members of the President’s own party urging him to explicitly denounce the fatal vehicular attack on a counter-protester in Charlottesville as an act of domestic terrorism. Subsequently, the White House clarified that the President’s condemnation of violence was intended to encompass “white supremacists, KKK Neo-Nazi and all extremist groups.”

This exit represents the most recent high-profile departure from a White House advisory council since President Trump’s inauguration. Preceding this, Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Disney CEO Bob Iger resigned from a separate business advisory council following the June announcement of U.S. withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement. Several months earlier, in February, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick left the same business council in the wake of President Trump’s executive order restricting immigration from seven predominantly Muslim nations, which Kalanick stated was “hurting many people in communities all across America.”

A Syracuse University professor recently urged students and colleagues to help “finish...off” the “fascists” who were demonstrating against Sharia law.
According to NPR, the Syracuse rally was marked by tensions between the anti-Sharia protesters—many of whom reportedly dressed in military-style fatigues—and self-styled “anti-fascist” (a.k.a., “antifa”) counter-protesters wearing face masks and carrying flags.
"We almost have the fascists in [sic] on the run...come down to the federal building to finish them off."
[RELATED: Twitter threats land Rutgers prof in loony bin]
“We almost have the fascists in [sic] on the run,” Professor Dana Cloud tweeted Saturday, referring to the local “March Against Sharia” demonstration taking place that day. “Syracuse people come down to the federal building to finish them off.”
A self-proclaimed socialist, Cloud has been featured on Turning Point USA’s Professor Watchlist for blaming the U.S. for 9/11 and for rewriting the Pledge of Allegiance to the people of Iraq, Palestine and Afghanistan.
The “March Against Sharia” protests, organized by a pro-Donald Trump organization called ACT for America, have been met with resistance from “antifa” groups who contend that the group is using the threat of Sharia as a pretext to stoke anti-Muslim bias, though ACT maintains that it is merely drawing attention to the threat of incorporating elements of Sharia into the American justice system.
[RELATED: Drexel prof claims white genocide tweet was merely satire]
Lisa Joseph, who organized the ACT event in Syracuse, asserted that while she is not aware of any specific instances in which Sharia law has been implemented in this country, ACT is committed to “guarding against it” in order to ensure that “radical Islamist ideology [does] not hijack the peaceful Muslims here in this country”—a sentiment echoed by Syracuse student Ryan Dunn.
“People think it’s a legal system that Muslims are trying to impose on Americans,” Dunn told Campus Reform. “However, no one wants America governed by Sharia law, including American Muslims.”
The Syracuse Post-Standard reports that no violence took place at the local demonstration, though demonstrators on both sides engaged in a prolonged shouting match from opposite sides of a street.
Campus Reform reached out to professor Cloud, but did not get a response in time for publication.
Follow Campus Reform on Twitter: @CampusReform
rewrite:
A professor at Syracuse University recently issued a public call for students and colleagues to assist in decisively confronting demonstrators protesting against Sharia law, whom she characterized as “fascists.” National Public Radio (NPR) reported that the rally in Syracuse was defined by heightened tensions between two groups: the anti-Sharia protesters, many of whom were attired in military-style fatigues, and a contingent of counter-protesters identifying as “anti-fascist” (commonly referred to as “antifa”), who wore face coverings and carried flags.

In a social media post, Professor Dana Cloud explicitly referenced the local “March Against Sharia” demonstration, stating, “We almost have the fascists in [sic] on the run...Syracuse people come down to the federal building to finish them off.” Professor Cloud, who identifies as a socialist, has previously been listed on Turning Point USA’s Professor Watchlist for assertions holding the United States responsible for the September 11 attacks and for composing an alternative pledge of allegiance directed toward the populations of Iraq, Palestine, and Afghanistan.

The “March Against Sharia” protests are organized by ACT for America, a group supportive of former President Donald Trump. These demonstrations have consistently faced opposition from antifa organizations, which argue that ACT for America employs the concept of a Sharia threat as a mechanism to promote anti-Muslim sentiment. ACT for America maintains that its objective is solely to highlight concerns regarding the potential incorporation of elements from Sharia law into the American judicial framework.

Lisa Joseph, the organizer of the Syracuse ACT event, clarified that while she is not cognizant of any specific instances of Sharia law being implemented in the United States, the organization is dedicated to “guarding against it.” This stance is intended to prevent what she termed “radical Islamist ideology” from undermining the peaceful Muslim community within the country. This perspective was echoed by Syracuse student Ryan Dunn, who noted to Campus Reform that a common misconception is that Muslims seek to impose Sharia law on Americans, whereas, in reality, American Muslims do not desire governance by Sharia law.

According to The Syracuse Post-Standard, the local demonstration concluded without physical violence, although participants from both factions engaged in an extended verbal confrontation across a divided street. Campus Reform attempted to contact Professor Cloud for comment but did not receive a response prior to publication.

There's a new face fronting Homes Under The Hammer and her name is Martell Maxwell.
The freelance television and radio presenter, journalist and author steps in to fill Lucy Alexander's shoes, after she left in 2016.
But who is Martell? And where have you seen her before?
Who is Martell Maxwell?
Scottish native Martell Maxwell is a journalist, author, radio and TV presenter with a degree in Law from Edinburgh University and a stellar career in newspapers under her belt.
She first popped up working for The Sun, where she wrote for the Bizarre column in her early days working as a journalist.
Since then she's written a novel based on her experiences as a showbiz reporter and gone on to appear on TV and radio throughout the UK, interviewing some of the biggest names in entertainment and championing her beloved Scotland from time to time too.
Where have I seen her before?
Everywhere, really. Martell presents segments on The One Show, steps in for special showbiz slots on ITV's Lorraine, and chances are you'll also have spotted her offering her views on the big entertainment issues on the likes of Daybreak and Sky News.
She's also worked for BBC3 and Channel 5 too.
rewrite:
Martell Maxwell has been appointed as the new presenter of the television programme *Homes Under The Hammer*, succeeding Lucy Alexander, who departed in 2016. Maxwell is a freelance television and radio presenter, journalist, and author. A native of Scotland, she holds a law degree from the University of Edinburgh and has established a notable career in journalism, beginning with her work for *The Sun* newspaper, where she contributed to the Bizarre column. Subsequently, she authored a novel informed by her experiences as a showbusiness reporter. Her broadcasting career encompasses appearances across British television and radio, featuring interviews with prominent entertainment figures and occasional advocacy for Scottish culture.

Maxwell’s prior television presence is extensive. She regularly contributes segments to BBC One’s *The One Show* and occasionally hosts entertainment features on ITV’s *Lorraine*. Additionally, she has provided commentary on entertainment news for programmes such as *Daybreak* and Sky News. Her professional credits also include work for BBC Three and Channel 5.

rewrite: On Tuesday, June 13, emergency services successfully rescued a horse named Jack after it fell into a ditch in Heath Lane, Willaston, having reportedly suffered a seizure. Similar to Prime Day, the first-ever Way Day is intended to be a new “retail holiday” like Black Friday, and will feature major discounts site wide. That includes thousands of furniture, décor, outdoor living and home improvement items, according to a release from the brand.

NEW YORK — Stocks are rallying Monday morning as the tensions between the U.S. and North Korea that flared last week appeared to ease. Technology companies and banks are making some of the largest gains as stocks bounce back from their losses with some of the biggest gains the market has seen this year. All 11 industrial groups in the Standard & Poor's 500 index are moving higher.
KEEPING SCORE: The S&P 500 jumped 24 points, or 1 percent, to 2,466 as of 11:15 a.m. Eastern time. The Dow Jones industrial average gained 147 points, or 0.7 percent, to 22,005. The Nasdaq composite added 73 points, or 1.2 percent, to 6,329. The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies climbed 14 points, or 1.1 percent, to 1,388.
Last week was the worst for stocks since late March, as the S&P 500 fell more than 1.4 percent. Rising tensions between the U.S. and North Korea startled investors out of the complacency that has weighed on the stock market for most of this year. That eased Monday after officials said fighting is not imminent. The top U.S. military officer said the country wants to resolve the standoff peacefully.
Thursday was the worst day for stocks since mid-May, and Monday is shaping up to be the best day since late April.
Advertisement Continue reading the main story
LEADERS: Technology stocks rose in early trading. Apple added $1.88, or 1.2 percent, to $159.36 and Microsoft picked up $1.07, or 1.5 percent, to $73.57. Western Digital advanced $2.77, or 3.5 percent, to $82.67.
rewrite:
U.S. equity markets advanced decisively on Monday, recovering from the prior week's losses as geopolitical tensions between the United States and North Korea showed signs of abating. This resurgence was broadly based, with all eleven industrial sectors within the Standard & Poor's 500 index trading higher. Technology and financial equities were among the leading gainers, contributing to one of the most substantial single-day rallies witnessed this year.

As of 11:15 a.m. Eastern Time, key benchmarks reflected this upward momentum. The S&P 500 index rose 24 points, or 1.0 percent, to 2,466. The Dow Jones Industrial Average increased by 147 points, or 0.7 percent, reaching 22,005. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index gained 73 points, or 1.2 percent, to 6,329, while the Russell 2000 index of smaller-capitalization companies climbed 14 points, or 1.1 percent, to 1,388.

This rally followed the market's worst weekly performance since late March, during which the S&P 500 declined more than 1.4 percent. The sell-off was precipitated by heightened diplomatic and military rhetoric between the U.S. and North Korea, which disrupted a prolonged period of investor complacency. Sentiment improved markedly on Monday following reassurances from officials that armed conflict was not imminent, including a statement from the top U.S. military officer emphasizing a preference for a peaceful resolution to the standoff. Consequently, Monday's trading session was poised to be the strongest since late April, a sharp reversal from Thursday, which had been the worst day for equities since mid-May.

Notable individual performers in the technology sector included Apple, which gained $1.88 (1.2%) to $159.36; Microsoft, which advanced $1.07 (1.5%) to $73.57; and Western Digital, which rose $2.77 (3.5%) to $82.67.
