Leeds United head coach Thomas Christiansen says that if the axe falls at Elland Road he will leave with his head held high, following the Whites' 4-1 home crushing against Cardiff City.

There was no end of intrigue at the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show this year.
Rumor, the German shepherd who narrowly lost at last year's show, had come close to simply hanging up her leash and retiring. Instead, she stormed back to win her category again this year — and then, to top it all off, beat out more than 2,800 dogs to take Best in Show on Tuesday, as well.
The triumph makes her only the second German shepherd to win the top prize in Westminster's 141-year history. Considering Westminster is the second-longest continuously running sporting event in the U.S. — second only to the Kentucky Derby — the redemptive win for the 5 1/2-year-old female is no mean feat.
Not only that, but as NPR's Merrit Kennedy noted earlier this month, Westminster also played host to another rarity at this year's dog show: cats. The featured felines shared a showcase with the dogs called Meet & Compete.
Still, whatever words we can offer on the event seem a little beside the point. The dogs — big and small, noble and loony — are the main event.
So, without further throat-clearing, here's what you came for: A few of our very favorite images from the competition.

Rumor, a German shepherd who narrowly missed victory in the previous year's competition, nearly retired from the show circuit. However, she returned decisively, first securing her breed category and then prevailing over more than 2,800 competitors to be awarded Best in Show on Tuesday. Given that Westminster is the second-longest continuously running sporting event in the United States, trailing only the Kentucky Derby, this redemptive victory for the five-and-a-half-year-old female represents a considerable accomplishment.

Further distinguishing this year's show was the inclusion of cats, a notable rarity, which shared a "Meet & Compete" showcase with the canine participants. Ultimately, however, analytical commentary remains secondary to the central spectacle: the dogs themselves, in all their varied majesty and eccentricity. After the concert, interested participants will march from the lawn of the Bit and Spur to the Canyon Community Center where they will gather for a drum circle. A wave has started to weld across the United States as many cities and states have renamed Columbus Day to "Indigenous People's Day”
As another October arrives, the debate continues in the United States about whether to continue recognizing Christopher Columbus as the “discoverer” of America.
Columbus Day remembers the landing of Christopher Columbus to the Americas on October 12, 1492.
It was unofficially celebrated in a number of cities and states as early as the 18th century but did not become a federal holiday until 1937.
It is celebrated every year on the second Monday of October.
Italian-Americans consider Columbus a symbol of progress. However, Native Americans reject the notion and condemn his atrocities towards indigenous peoples.
Many cities in the U.S. namely, Seattle, Minneapolis, Portland, Albuquerque, Tulsa and states like Alaska, Minnesota and Vermont have renamed Columbus Day to “Indigenous People’s Day” to honor the Native Americans whose home was invaded in the aftermath of Columbus’ arrival.
We spoke to Brian Cladoosby, president of the National Congress of American Indians, who said the U.S. doesn’t teach the true history of Columbus’ intent in coming to the Americas and also shed light on some of the atrocities he committed towards Native Americans.
Watch the video above to learn more about topic.
Read More Dear America, Columbus Was A Genocidal Maniac Not An Icon
Banner/Thumbnail Credit: Reuters
rewrite:
A significant shift is underway across the United States, as numerous municipalities and states have moved to rename the federal holiday of Columbus Day as "Indigenous Peoples' Day." With the annual arrival of October, a persistent national debate continues regarding the commemoration of Christopher Columbus as the purported discoverer of the Americas. The holiday, observed on the second Monday of October, marks the anniversary of Columbus's landing on October 12, 1492. Although locally celebrated in some areas since the 18th century, it was not formally established as a federal holiday until 1937.

For many Italian-Americans, the figure of Columbus represents heritage and progress. Conversely, Native American communities and their advocates strongly reject this narrative, condemning the violence and atrocities inflicted upon indigenous populations following European contact. In response, jurisdictions including the cities of Seattle, Minneapolis, Portland, Albuquerque, and Tulsa, as well as the states of Alaska, Minnesota, and Vermont, have adopted the designation "Indigenous Peoples' Day." This change seeks to honor Native American histories and cultures, recognizing the invasion and displacement that commenced with Columbus's voyages.

Brian Cladoosby, President of the National Congress of American Indians, has criticized the prevailing historical narrative, arguing that U.S. education often fails to address the full scope of Columbus's intentions and the consequent suffering inflicted upon indigenous peoples. This ongoing reevaluation reflects a broader effort to confront colonial legacies and acknowledge a more complex national history.

A young American man trying an under-arm serve while cramping during a five-setter at the French Open.
Seen that before?
Except, unlike for 1989 champion Michael Chang, the unusual strategy didn't help result in a victory for Jared Donaldson against Grigor Dimitrov on Wednesday.
The fourth-seeded Dimitrov came back to beat the 21-year-old 6-7 (2-7) 6-4 4-6 6-4 10-8 in a second-round marathon that lasted four hours, 19 minutes on Court 18 at Roland Garros.
When it ended, Dimitrov leaned forward while raising each knee to give it a kiss - perhaps thanking his legs for carrying him to the win while Donaldson's gave way.
Donaldson, who is ranked 57th, was actually two points from winning when he led 6-5 in the fifth and got to love-30 on Dimitrov's serve. But Dimitrov took the next four points to hold for 6-all.
Dimitrov broke to lead 8-7 and served for the victory, but Donaldson broke right back.
Camera Icon Jared Donaldson proved the under-arm serve isn’t dead. Picture: Getty Images
In the next game, though, Donaldson could barely stand, let alone move well.
He double-faulted. Then he tried an under-arm serve - not his first of the match, either - and lost the point.
Dimitrov hit a winner to break for a 9-8 edge, Donaldson slowly limped to the sideline for the changeover, and soon enough, it was over.
Chang famously used an under-arm service motion while cramping during a fourth-round win against Ivan Lendl on the way to the French Open title 29 years ago.
rewrite:
During a protracted five-set encounter at the French Open, a young American competitor, experiencing severe cramping, resorted to an under-arm service motion. This tactical choice evoked a famous historical precedent from the 1989 tournament, wherein champion Michael Chang successfully employed a similar strategy. However, in Wednesday's second-round match on Court 18 at Roland Garros, this unconventional approach did not yield a victorious outcome for Jared Donaldson against fourth-seeded Grigor Dimitrov. In a marathon contest lasting four hours and nineteen minutes, Dimitrov ultimately prevailed with a score of 6-7 (2-7), 6-4, 4-6, 6-4, 10-8.

The conclusion of the match saw Dimitrov ceremoniously acknowledge his physical endurance, while Donaldson’s capacity for movement deteriorated significantly. Despite being ranked 57th globally, Donaldson had positioned himself advantageously, standing within two points of victory at 6-5 in the decisive set with a love-30 advantage on Dimitrov’s serve. Dimitrov, however, secured the next four points to hold serve and level the set. Although Dimitrov subsequently achieved a break to lead 8-7 and served for the match, Donaldson immediately broke back. In the following game, Donaldson’s mobility was profoundly compromised, resulting in a double fault and a failed under-arm service attempt. Dimitrov capitalized with a winning shot to break for a 9-8 lead, and Donaldson, visibly debilitated, could not recover. This incident demonstrates that the under-arm serve, while a rare strategic artifact, remains within the contemporary tactical repertoire, albeit one whose efficacy is contingent upon specific physical and competitive circumstances, as historically illustrated by Chang’s iconic use of the maneuver twenty-nine years prior.

Under the scheme 'Gram Swarajya Yojna,' where the state government aims to reach out over 50,000 village panchayats in Uttar Pradesh, the Chief Minister was also seen holding a chaupal (meeting) with the family and the locals at the village, while reviewing various development projects. "WADA is responsible for the integrity of the anti-doping system. From my understanding… old bottles will be used to avoid any problems… we are very confident in that system," Adams told a press conference.
The decision was taken after on Friday, WADA issued a recommendation for the IOC to use the earlier models of bottles for doping probes during the 2018 Games, as it had been revealed that the new generation of security bottles could be opened without evidence.

Investigation

Demand for global air freight rose 8.4 percent in February, accelerating after a 6.9 percent rise in January and reflecting improving world trade, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Wednesday.
Demand, measured in freight tonne kilometres, also grew faster than capacity, which shrank 0.4 percent. That meant load factors improved 3.5 percentage points to 43.5 percent and gave yields a boost, IATA said.
Adjusted for the extra day from 2016's leap year, demand in February rose 12 percent, the association added. Demand was also driven by increased shipments of semiconductor materials used in consumer electronics
"February further added to the cautious optimism building in air cargo markets," IATA Director General Alexandre de Juniac said in a statement. "While there are signs of stronger world trade, concerns over the current protectionist rhetoric are still very real."
(Reporting by Bartosz Dabrowski; Editing by Victoria Bryan)
rewrite: Global air freight demand increased by 8.4 percent in February, according to data released by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) on Wednesday. This represents an acceleration from the 6.9 percent growth recorded in January and aligns with broader indicators of recovering international trade. Measured in freight tonne kilometres, demand growth outpaced capacity, which contracted by 0.4 percent. Consequently, the load factor improved by 3.5 percentage points to 43.5 percent, providing a positive impetus for yield performance. When adjusted for the leap year effect from 2016, February demand exhibited a 12 percent increase. This expansion was partly driven by heightened shipments of semiconductor materials for consumer electronics. IATA Director General Alexandre de Juniac noted that the results contribute to a cautiously optimistic outlook, while also acknowledging persistent concerns regarding protectionist trade policies.

INCREASED patrols and heightened community awareness at Mon Repos beach have led to a man being charged.
Senior Constable Cameron Graham said a man being charged with wilful exposure following overwhelming response from the community after an alleged incident at Mon Repos on Friday last week.
"A 62-year-old male person was charged with wilful exposure after a number of witnesses came forward with reports," Sen-Const Graham said.
"The man will face court next month."
Sen-Const Graham said police made it a priority to patrol all beaches in general, but patrols of the Mon Repos specifically had increased over the past week.
"He obviously didn't read the NewsMail article because he was caught just a few days after the story appeared in the paper," he said.
Last week the NewsMail published the story of reporter Tahlia Stehbens' uncomfortable experience at the beach.
Senior Constable Nigel Schultz said people had historically been charged with offences committed along the Mon Repos strip with people sometimes behaving inappropriately.
"It happens mostly away from the walking tracks, in the bushland area," Sen-Const Schultz said.
"Unfortunately, some websites give false information about it being a meeting point.
"The Mon Repos area is patrolled daily down Moores Rd and we do motorbike patrols through the bike path.
"We also walk through the bushland behind and check licence plates of cars to ensure they aren't wanted for anything."
Sen-Const Schultz said there had been problems with people exposing themselves on the beach but it was mostly due to the fact they thought it was a nudist beach.
"We can usually encourage those people to move on and not come back," Sen-Const Schultz said.
Sen-Const Schultz said people should phone PoliceLink on 131 444 if they saw anything suspicious, or call 000 if they were in immediate danger.
"People should be aware of their surroundings," he said.
"We've never had anybody actually attacked there but I wouldn't advise females to walk alone, especially in this day and age, and use the tracks available."
rewrite:
Enhanced police surveillance and elevated community vigilance at Mon Repos beach have resulted in criminal charges being laid against an individual. According to Senior Constable Cameron Graham, a 62-year-old man has been charged with wilful exposure following numerous witness reports stemming from an alleged incident at the location on the preceding Friday. The accused is scheduled to appear in court next month. Senior Constable Graham noted that while general beach patrols remain a policing priority, there has been a specific increase in patrols at Mon Repos over the past week. He suggested the individual may have been unaware of recent media coverage, stating the arrest occurred shortly after a related article was published.

That article detailed an uncomfortable experience encountered by reporter Tahlia Stehbens at the beach. Senior Constable Nigel Schultz added that there is a history of individuals being charged for offences along the Mon Repos strip, often involving inappropriate behaviour. He indicated such incidents predominantly occur away from designated walking tracks, within bushland areas. Senior Constable Schultz also addressed the circulation of misinformation, noting that some websites inaccurately promote the area as a meeting point. To counter these issues, he outlined ongoing patrol strategies, including daily vehicle patrols along Moores Road, motorbike patrols on the bike path, and foot patrols through the bushland, supplemented by vehicle licence plate checks.

A recurring problem involves individuals exposing themselves under the mistaken belief that Mon Repos is a nudist beach. In such cases, police typically intervene to instruct the individuals to leave and not return. Authorities advise the public to remain aware of their surroundings and to report any suspicious activity by contacting PoliceLink on 131 444, or dialling 000 in an emergency. While Senior Constable Schultz confirmed there have been no recorded attacks at the location, he recommended against solitary walks, particularly for women, advising instead that pedestrians utilise the established tracks.

MINNEAPOLIS (WCCO) — It’s always great to bring encouraging updates from the patients profiled in Kylie’s Kids, and this week Kylie Bearse has two to share.
Jazzy
When we last saw her, 13-year-old Jazzy was waiting for a new heart, and she finally got it. However, the day after the surgery she experienced some complications. Jazzy’s body was rejecting her new heart and we asked all of you to send a lot of love and prayers.
It’s now been two months since Jazzy’s transplant and her health scare. Her family says she’s getting a little stronger every day.
She’s still not quite able to stand on her own, but her appetite is back and she’s in good spirits.
Next week she’ll be transferring to rehab at Gillette’s Children’s Hospital. This August marks 10 months in the hospital.
Nathalia
We introduced you to Nathalia in December. She’s from Duluth, but travels down to Masonic Children’s Hospital for cancer treatment. She had surgery on her legs, and was working on walking again.
Her family loves to explore, usually in the form of hiking. Recently they got to go on a whole new adventure. Nathalia got to go on a helicopter ride with Love Your Melon over the city of Minneapolis.
Her mom says she’s doing well, with no more chemo treatments planned as of now. She’s on clinical trial, which is outpatient.
And that she loved the helicopter ride.
rewrite:
This week's installment of Kylie's Kids presents two encouraging updates concerning previously featured patients.

The first concerns Jazzy, a thirteen-year-old who was awaiting a heart transplant. That procedure has now been successfully completed. However, a significant postoperative complication arose the following day when her body initiated a rejection response, necessitating a period of critical concern. Now two months post-transplant, her family reports steady, incremental progress in her strength each day. While she has not yet regained the ability to stand independently, her appetite has returned and her spirits remain positive. The next phase of her recovery will involve a transfer to the rehabilitation unit at Gillette Children’s Hospital next week. By August, her cumulative hospitalization will reach ten months.

The second update pertains to Nathalia, a Duluth resident receiving cancer treatment at Masonic Children’s Hospital. Following leg surgery, she has been engaged in rehabilitative efforts to walk again. Recently, she participated in a distinctive experience: a helicopter tour over Minneapolis, facilitated by the Love Your Melon organization. Her mother reports that Nathalia is currently doing well, with no further chemotherapy scheduled. She is now participating in an outpatient clinical trial. The family, which enjoys exploration through hiking, shared that Nathalia greatly appreciated the aerial adventure.

Morton, 3 Astros Relievers Combine to 5-hit Angels, 3-0
HOUSTON (AP) _ Charlie Morton and three relievers combined for a five-hitter,
Jose Altuve drove in two runs and the Houston Astros beat the Los Angeles Angels
3-0 on Monday night for their fifth straight win.
Morton (1-1) worked in and out of trouble over five innings, allowing five hits
and two walks with three strikeouts. He had runners on in every inning,
including stranding the bases loaded in the second when he got Ben Revere to fly
out. Morton has allowed three runs or fewer in each of his three starts this
season.
Chris Devenski followed Morton with two perfect innings, Luke Gregerson threw a
perfect eighth and Ken Giles pitched the ninth for his third save. Astros
pitchers retired the last 14 batters.
Jesse Chavez (1-2) allowed two runs and seven hits over a season-high seven
innings. He struck out five and rebounded after allowing five runs in 4 1/3
innings in his last outing.
rewrite: In a Monday evening contest, the Houston Astros secured a 3-0 victory over the Los Angeles Angels, marking their fifth consecutive win. The triumph was anchored by a collective pitching performance from starter Charlie Morton and relievers Chris Devenski, Luke Gregerson, and Ken Giles, who combined to limit the Angels to five hits. Morton (1-1) pitched five innings, yielding five hits and two walks while striking out three. He consistently worked out of potential scoring situations, most notably by stranding the bases loaded in the second inning. Following Morton, Devenski and Gregerson each delivered perfect relief innings, and Giles completed the shutout in the ninth for his third save. Collectively, Astros pitchers retired the final fourteen batters. Offensively, Jose Altuve contributed two runs batted in. For the Angels, Jesse Chavez (1-2) delivered a season-high seven innings, allowing two runs and seven hits, an improvement from his previous start.

Philippine ports must expand capacity to allow entry of larger containers, in order to provide direct service and eliminate transhipment of goods, American shipping company APL said on Friday.
Advertisements
“The vessel couldn’t enter the port and that’s something extremely important for development,,” APL Chief Executive Officer Nicolas Sartini said in a press briefing.
“Today, Manila and Philippines cannot take direct service, so we offer transhipment service,” he said.
The APL chief executive noted that a direct service will lessen transportation cost, compared with conducting transhipment where goods are off-loaded from one ship in a certain location, then transferred to another ship before reaching the final destination.
“Once you offer direct service, we immediately see the volumes of markets growing,” Sartini said, citing that the port in Jakarta, Indonesia, offers direct service which helped the city’s economy to grow. According to the Sartini, APL seeks to discuss the said matter with the Department of Transportation and maritime leaders to help resolve the issue.
Sartini said good infrastructure is important to increase trade within a region.
“Trade is bringing in income,” Sartini said, and “we have to facilitate the trade by all means.”
In the Philippines, APL serves the ports of Manila north and south, Subic, Davao, General Santos, Cebu and Cagayan. Its export markets are Japan, the United States, Hong Kong, China and Singapore. The import markets it serves are US, China Japan, Thailand, Korea and Singapore.
Sartini said APL seeks to introduce new routes and services in the Intra-Asian region, after it has launched a shipment route between Philippines and India last week.
“We are connecting the Philippines with every single market in Intra-Asia. We have 150 million containers moving in the world. One out of six of them is in Intra-Asia,” Sartini said.
“We continue to open new services. It would be the Intra-Asia scope. We continue to grow the regional network. We are taking new origins in the Philippines, opening new goods market for the Philippine goods to be sold anywhere else in the world,” he added.
APL could also acquire local shipping companies to further grow its business.
rewrite:
On Friday, the American shipping company APL emphasized the necessity for Philippine ports to enhance their infrastructure capacity to accommodate larger container vessels. This expansion is deemed critical to establishing direct shipping services and eliminating the current reliance on transhipment. Nicolas Sartini, Chief Executive Officer of APL, underscored this point during a press briefing, stating, “The vessel couldn’t enter the port and that’s something extremely important for development.” He elaborated that, at present, Manila and the Philippines overall are unable to receive direct services, necessitating the provision of transhipment alternatives.

Sartini explained that direct service would significantly reduce transportation costs. Transhipment, which involves unloading cargo from one vessel at an intermediate port and transferring it to another for final delivery, incurs additional handling expenses and time delays. In contrast, “Once you offer direct service, we immediately see the volumes of markets growing,” he asserted, citing the economic growth observed in Jakarta, Indonesia, following the implementation of direct port services. APL intends to engage with the Philippine Department of Transportation and maritime industry leaders to address this infrastructural limitation.

The executive highlighted the fundamental role of robust infrastructure in stimulating regional trade, noting, “Trade is bringing in income,” and “we have to facilitate the trade by all means.” APL currently operates within several Philippine ports, including Manila North and South, Subic, Davao, General Santos, Cebu, and Cagayan. Its export markets encompass Japan, the United States, Hong Kong, China, and Singapore, while key import origins include the U.S., China, Japan, Thailand, Korea, and Singapore.

Looking forward, APL is focused on expanding its Intra-Asian network. Following the recent launch of a Philippines-India route, the company plans to introduce additional services within the region. Sartini emphasized the strategic importance of Intra-Asia trade, noting that it accounts for one out of every six containers moved globally, representing approximately 150 million containers. “We are connecting the Philippines with every single market in Intra-Asia,” he said, adding that the company continues to grow its regional network by establishing new origins within the Philippines and opening markets for Philippine goods worldwide. Furthermore, APL is considering the acquisition of local shipping companies as a potential strategy for business growth.

A judge set bail for a 19-year-old girl suspected in a deadly DUI crash in the northwest part of the Valley at $250,000.
Nina Gateley appeared in a Las Vegas courtroom Friday morning. Court records show she faces one count of driving under the influence, above the legal limit, resulting in death.
According to Las Vegas Metro police, Gateley was behind the wheel of a 2003 Chevrolet Silverado that was heading southbound on Sky Pointe when the truck exited the roadway. She steered back onto the roadway and the truck overturned.
[RELATED: Teen killed, driver charged after suspected DUI crash in northwest Las Vegas]
Of five people in the truck, four were ejected, police said. Two were taken to a hospital. Makenzzi Lea Nix, 16, was pronounced dead at Mountain View Hospital.
[RELATED: Mother of valley teen killed in rollover crash speaks out]
Four of the five people involved in the crash were between the ages of 16 and 17, police said.
According to Gateley's arrest report, officers at the scene discovered several bottles of alcohol in backpacks at the scene. Three passengers told police they were drinking in the desert before the crash and confirmed Gateley was the driver.
Gately is scheduled to appear in court again on June 13 for a preliminary hearing.

rewrite:
On Friday morning, Nina Gateley, aged 19, appeared in a Las Vegas courtroom where a judge set bail at $250,000. She faces a formal charge of driving under the influence with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding the legal limit, resulting in a fatality. The charges stem from a single-vehicle rollover crash in the northwest region of the Las Vegas Valley.

According to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, Gateley was operating a 2003 Chevrolet Silverado southbound on Sky Pointe Drive when the vehicle departed the roadway. Upon her attempt to steer back onto the road, the truck overturned. Of the five occupants, four were ejected. Two individuals required hospitalization, and one, 16-year-old Makenzzi Lea Nix, was pronounced deceased at Mountain View Hospital. Police noted that four of the five vehicle occupants were between 16 and 17 years of age.

The arrest report indicates that responding officers located multiple bottles of alcohol within backpacks at the scene. Three passengers subsequently confirmed to authorities that they had been consuming alcohol in a desert area prior to the incident and identified Gateley as the driver. A preliminary hearing in the case is scheduled for June 13.

NEW YORK -- A woman climbed the base of the Statue of Liberty on the Fourth of July and seven people have been arrested on Liberty Island, all of whom are believed to be protesters, law enforcement sources told CNN.
The woman is affiliated with Rise and Resist, Martin Joseph Quinn, an organizer for the group, told CNN. But Quinn added her climb was not part of the planned protest today. "She climbed without our knowledge. It was not part of our action. We are deeply concerned for her safety," Quinn said.
At one point, the woman walked back and forth under Lady Liberty's sandal and then sat down and appeared to unfurl a small flag or banner. The other protesters, also with Rise and Resist, held a banner over the railing at the base of the statue.
Law enforcement officials were seen mounting a ladder to the base of the statue and talking to the woman, who was sitting in the folds of the statue's gown.
The NYPD is building a rope rescue system to help bring the woman down from the base, because officers don't believe she will come down on her own, a police source told CNN.
Liberty Island has been evacuated while they attempt to get her down, according to Jerry Willis with the National Park Service.
The NYPD says three of its emergency service units and a harbor unit are on scene.

On the Fourth of July, a woman ascended the base of the Statue of Liberty, leading to the arrest of seven individuals on Liberty Island. Law enforcement sources indicate that all those detained are believed to be affiliated with protest activities. According to Martin Joseph Quinn, an organizer for the group Rise and Resist, the woman is a member of that organization. Quinn clarified, however, that her climb was not a component of the group’s planned demonstration for the day, stating, “She climbed without our knowledge. It was not part of our action. We are deeply concerned for her safety.”

During the incident, the individual was observed moving beneath the statue’s sandal before sitting down and apparently deploying a small flag or banner. Concurrently, other protesters associated with Rise and Resist displayed a banner over the railing at the statue’s base. Law enforcement personnel were documented accessing the pedestal via a ladder to engage with the woman, who was positioned within the folds of the statue’s gown.

A police source reported that the New York Police Department is constructing a rope rescue system to facilitate her extraction, as officers anticipate she will not descend voluntarily. In response to the situation, Liberty Island has been evacuated, according to Jerry Willis of the National Park Service. The NYPD has deployed three emergency service units and a harbor unit to the scene.

Despite criticism that the President has still not condemned white supremacy after a self-proclaimed member of the fringe group drove a car into a crowd of counter protestors at a white supremacy rally this weekend, Attorney General Jeff Sessions defended the President saying he made a “very strong statement.”
“He said what happened in Charlottesville is unacceptable and we need to find out what happened, that it’s wrong and we need to study it and see what as a nation we can do to be more effective against this kind of extremism and evil,” he said on the “Today” show Monday. “It was a good statement delivered just a few hours after the event. The next day, yesterday, they explicitly called out the Nazis and the KKK.”
The hosts of the show pushed back, saying that statement came from an unnamed White House spokesperson, not President Donald Trump himself. Sessions said the name on the statement was irrelevant.
“I’m sure he will talk again about it soon. He will be speaking to the people today. I’m not sure what he will say, but that’s my understanding. He’s been firm on this from the beginning. He is appalled by this,” Sessions said.
Sessions’ rhetoric is similar to Vice President Mike Pence’s defense of the President, who said Trump “clearly and unambiguously condemned the bigotry, violence and hatred” and questioned why the media was spending more time criticizing the President’s words than “criticizing those who perpetrated the violence to begin with.”
Watch the interview below:
rewrite:
Following a weekend incident in which an individual associated with a fringe white supremacist group drove a vehicle into a crowd of counter-protesters at a rally, the President has faced criticism for not explicitly condemning white supremacy. In response, Attorney General Jeff Sessions defended the administration's position during a Monday appearance on the "Today" show, asserting that the President had issued a "very strong statement" promptly after the event. Sessions quoted the statement, which characterized the events in Charlottesville as unacceptable and wrong, emphasizing a national need to understand and effectively counter such extremism. He further noted that the following day, the administration explicitly denounced the Nazis and the Ku Klux Klan.

The interview hosts challenged this defense by pointing out that the specific condemnation was attributed to an unnamed White House spokesperson rather than to President Donald Trump directly. Sessions dismissed the significance of the attribution, maintaining the statement reflected the President's views. He expressed confidence that the President would address the matter again, stating, "He’s been firm on this from the beginning. He is appalled by this."

This rhetoric aligns with defenses offered by other administration officials, including Vice President Mike Pence, who previously stated that Trump had "clearly and unambiguously condemned the bigotry, violence and hatred." Pence, like Sessions, questioned media focus on the President's wording rather than on the perpetrators of the violence.

input: JEDDAH: Enhancing regional integration through tourism will be the theme when the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) holds the 10th session of the Islamic Conference of Tourism Ministers (ICTM) in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Feb. 5-7.During this session, OIC Secretary-General Yousef Al-Othaimeen will present his report to the ministers of tourism of the OIC member states. The report includes the implementation of the OIC Framework for Development and Cooperation in the field of tourism in terms of promoting Islamic tourism; celebratory activities of Islamic tourism capitals; promotional tourism activities; organizing tourist exhibitions; establishing a tourism portal; tourism capacity-building programs; tourism publications; and tourism statistics and studies.The ICTM will also discuss the development of Islamic cultural and heritage tourism; the plan for the development and promotion of Islamic tourism; and a study on branding Muslim-friendly tourism in the global market.Participants will also review the progress in tourism projects such as the Regional Project for Sustainable Tourism Development in a Network of Cross Border Parks and Protected Areas in West Africa.The forthcoming ICTM is also expected to address challenges faced by the OIC on the successful organization of various tourism fairs and the development of a joint strategy for the successful organization of Islamic tourism exhibitions.The session will also select the two Islamic tourism capitals of 2019 and 2020, and review programs to facilitate the diverse celebration of this year-long event.
rewrite:
The tenth session of the Islamic Conference of Tourism Ministers (ICTM), convened by the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), will convene in Dhaka, Bangladesh, from February 5 to 7. The central theme of the ministerial meeting will be the advancement of regional integration through tourism initiatives. OIC Secretary-General Yousef Al-Othaimeen will present a comprehensive report to the assembled ministers, detailing the implementation of the OIC Framework for Development and Cooperation in Tourism. This report encompasses progress in key areas, including the promotion of Islamic tourism, the designation and celebratory activities of Islamic tourism capitals, promotional campaigns, the organization of tourist exhibitions, the establishment of a dedicated tourism portal, capacity-building programs, publications, and the compilation of tourism statistics and studies.

The conference agenda will further include deliberations on the development of Islamic cultural and heritage tourism, a strategic plan for the development and promotion of Islamic tourism, and a study concerning the branding of Muslim-friendly tourism within the global marketplace. Participants will review the status of ongoing projects, such as the Regional Project for Sustainable Tourism Development in a Network of Cross-Border Parks and Protected Areas in West Africa. The session will also address organizational challenges related to tourism fairs and formulate a joint strategy for future Islamic tourism exhibitions. Additional items for consideration include the selection of the Islamic tourism capitals for 2019 and 2020, alongside a review of programs designed to facilitate the year-long celebrations for these capitals.

ROXANA, Ill. - Some parents are complaining about a pair of math questions written by an Illinois high school teacher on a classroom whiteboard.
The parents said the questions were not only in bad taste but gave the impression the teacher was making light of drug use, according to KTVI.
On Thursday, the Roxana School District superintendent confirmed these questions appeared during a freshman math class.
The first question: "You take 600mg of cocaine, your body filters out 40% per hour, how high are you in three hours?"
The second question: "Unfortunately, you can't pay your dealer, so she sets up a payment. You owe her $1,000 at 25% daily, how much do you owe one year later?"
The district said this was an example of poor judgment. A statement from the district reads, in part:
"The district is addressing the matter with the faculty member and those impacted by this incident. The faculty member has apologized to students and parents for this lapse in judgment and has reiterated the intent was never to promote or make light of illicit drug use. The district is taking the necessary measures to ensure that the damage is repaired. The district is addressing this issue as a personnel matter according to district policy."

“The way large U.S. firms are taxed in the European Union is posing major challenges for France, the country’s finance minister told CNBC Thursday,” Silvia Amaro and Karen Tso report for CNBC. “Bruno Le Maire, the recently appointed French finance minister, is at the forefront of an initiative to impose an ‘equalization tax’ for tech companies across the EU — a potential new policy that is set to disrupt the way companies operate in Europe.”
“One of the biggest proposals is to tax companies on their revenues rather than on their profits. Taxing the latter would usually culminate in a smaller number. The idea with an ‘equalization’ tax is to avoid firms taking advantage of different tax codes across the 28 European member countries, which has allowed many of them to pay little tax in some countries,” Amaro and Tso report. “Many large U.S. tech firms base their European headquarters in EU nations with favorable tax regimes, that often means they book the majority of their European profits in those countries.”
Amaro and Tso report, “Paul Gambles, managing partner at MBMG Group, told CNBC that it seems that the European Union is backing rising protectionism and thus helping its own companies against competition from U.S. firms.”
Read more in the full article here.
rewrite:
In a CNBC report published Thursday, Silvia Amaro and Karen Tso detail significant challenges for France arising from the European Union’s taxation framework for major U.S. corporations. French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire, recently appointed to his position, is leading an effort to institute an “equalization tax” targeting technology firms operating within the EU. This proposed policy represents a substantial shift that could fundamentally alter corporate operations across Europe.

A central component of the proposal involves levying taxes based on corporate revenues instead of profits, the latter typically yielding a lower tax liability. The objective of the equalization mechanism is to prevent firms from exploiting divergent tax codes among the EU’s 28 member states, a practice that has enabled numerous companies to minimize their tax burdens in certain jurisdictions. As noted in the report, many large U.S. technology firms establish their European headquarters in nations with favorable tax regimes, thereby attributing the bulk of their European profits to those countries.

Furthermore, the report cites commentary from Paul Gambles, managing partner at MBMG Group, who suggested to CNBC that the European Union appears to be endorsing a trend toward increased protectionism, thereby advantaging its domestic companies against competition from U.S. firms.

Fabinho has left little room for doubt that he intends to leave Monaco as the Ligue 1 champions look set to lose another star player.
Bernardo Silva, Benjamin Mendy and Tiemoue Bakayoko have already left, while Kylian Mbappe, Thomas Lemar and Fabinho have also been linked with departures.
For his part, Fabinho - a reported target for Manchester United - has made no secret of his desire to secure a transfer and he reaffirmed that after Monaco's 4-1 win over Dijon.
"I feel good, there is nothing to say about my situation, the club knows my will," said the 23-year-old. "I hope we will continue this way and that Monaco will still be okay."
The principality club's vice-president Vadim Vasilyev said last month that they would not sell Lemar or Fabinho in this transfer window.
He said: "We have kept all of the key players that we intended to keep.
"Fabinho is a must-have player in midfield who was being courted by all the major clubs. I will also address speculation about Lemar: he is staying with us. We have discussed this.
"Both these players have tremendous talent and are essential for our team.
"We must not await further departures, rather arrivals."

He explicitly confirmed Lemar would remain, stating, "We have discussed this. Both these players have tremendous talent and are essential for our team." Vasilyev concluded by indicating the club's focus is now on acquisitions, not further departures.

rewrite:
The implementation of 4-D sensory effects in theatrical screenings, as exemplified by the presentation of *Captain America: Civil War*, represents a superfluous technological augmentation that elevates cost without enhancing narrative substance. This is evidenced by a viewing experience wherein the audience's reaction to the extraneous stimuli proved more engaging than the film itself. Such gimmickry underscores a broader industry trend toward prioritizing spectacle over content, a trend most prominently embodied by the persistent use of 3-D filmmaking. A critical reassessment of this practice is warranted, as 3-D technology frequently functions as a financial imposition on audiences rather than a meaningful artistic tool, often failing to justify its premium pricing.

Historical and contemporary applications of the format further illustrate its problematic nature. Its use ranges from the artistically questionable, as in Gaspar Noé's *Love*, where it serves primarily to accentuate graphic content, to the commercially exploitative, as seen in films like the 2015 *Vacation*, which contribute to rising ticket prices without corresponding qualitative merit. Notably, the technical effort required for post-production 3-D conversion, such as the extensive process undertaken for *The Wizard of Oz*, often results in a visually impressive but fundamentally unnecessary alteration of the original work.

The decline of 3-D as a dominant cinematic format is a development met with approval by many film critics, who have long questioned its artistic validity beyond a narrow subset of genres. This skepticism stands in contrast to the productive application of three-dimensional printing technology in fields like pharmacology, where the FDA's approval of a 3-D-printed drug signifies a substantive advancement. The dichotomy between these applications highlights that the value of a technology is derived from its purposeful integration rather than its mere novelty. The film industry's continued reliance on such formats as a default, rather than a deliberate creative choice, risks diminishing the artistic integrity of the medium.

The Ohio State Senate has eliminated a lead provision from the Ohio budget.
The provision would have weakened Toledo’s ability to enforce the recently passed Lead Safe Law.
This law serves to prevent lead poisoning of children in rental properties and home day care centers.
“I am gratified that our State Senators so far have seen the wisdom in permitting local jurisdictions to monitor and enforce more proactive lead safety measures. We expect other Ohio communities to follow Toledo regarding lead poisoning prevention,” said Toledo Mayor Paula Hicks-Hudson.
In the Lead Safe Law, landlords are given instructions on how to prepare their properties to pass inspections and to maintain safe rental properties for families.
Home day-care centers are also required to be inspected and certified.
The city of Toledo has moved to file both criminal and civil charges against landlords which blatantly disregard orders to repair lead hazards or to vacate properties.

Furthermore, Toledo has initiated both criminal and civil proceedings against landlords who willfully fail to comply with orders to remediate lead hazards or vacate non-compliant properties.

When President Trump makes his first return to his New York City home since the inauguration, he will be greeted by a rat.
A New York artist created a massive inflatable "Trump rat" which he presented in front of the Plaza Hotel on Tuesday.
John Post Lee, owner of Bravin Lee art galleries in NYC/LI said he commissioned 7ft "Trump Rat" to express "disgust" pic.twitter.com/t5ONR9G354 — Laura Figueroa (@Laura_Figueroa) August 14, 2017
John Post Lee, of the Bravin Lee gallery, said he modeled his Trump rat after the blow-up rats labor unions often use to protest businesses.
"I was amazed at how effective [the rats] were. I marveled at how disgusting they were," Lee told the New York Daily News.
The large rat features Trump's signature hairstyle, a Russian flag lapel pin and cufflinks styled after the Confederate Stars & Bars.
Additional barricades were seen in front of Trump Tower, as the president plans to travel there from his golf course near Bernardsville, N.J. later Monday.
The rat joins its Washington, D.C. counterpart, an inflatable "Trump rooster" now positioned near the White House.

rewrite:
During a press conference, President Donald Trump and CNN correspondent Jim Acosta engaged in a contentious exchange regarding the 2017 Charlottesville rally, with Acosta asserting the President had disseminated misinformation. In his remarks, Trump explicitly denounced white supremacist groups, including the Ku Klux Klan and neo-Nazis, by name.

Concurrently, ahead of the President's first scheduled return to his New York City residence since the inauguration, a significant protest artifact was deployed. A New York artist commissioned a seven-foot inflatable effigy, colloquially termed the "Trump rat," which was installed outside the Plaza Hotel. John Post Lee, proprietor of the Bravin Lee galleries, stated the installation was intended to convey profound disapproval. Modeled after the large rodents traditionally utilized by labor unions in protests, Lee noted he was struck by their visceral impact. The effigy incorporates distinctive features: the President's characteristic hairstyle, a lapel pin resembling the Russian flag, and cufflinks patterned after the Confederate battle flag.

Security preparations, including additional barricades, were observed at Trump Tower in anticipation of the visit. This installation parallels a similar protest piece in Washington, D.C.—an inflatable "Trump rooster" situated near the White House. These events unfolded alongside commentary from figures such as Lawrence Jones, who emphasized the necessity of explicitly identifying ideological adversaries, and a report detailing the Charlottesville suspect's mother expressing disbelief following her son's arrest.

British-born, New York raised-and-based music producer Karsh Kale says there is no software that can come close to replacing the chemistry between musicians when they come together to create music.
“The years have proven one thing to me — that there is no software, controllers, loopers, or other gear on this planet that can come close to replacing the chemistry that happens when musicians come together to make music,” Kale, who has roots in India, said in a statement.
“The ideas always remain human. I think young artistes need to be less concerned with what gear they are using and more about gaining more human experience,” he added.
Kale features in a new episode of Red Bull Music Academy’s “Studio Science” which looks inside the laboratories of some of the creative minds, offering tips and tricks for aspiring musicians.
The series has featured musicians like Disclosure, Four Tet and Suzanne Ciani.
Now, “Studio Science” turns its attention to the tabla star and celebrated multi-instrumentalist Kale, in the episode shot in India.
The episode premieres on Red Bull Music Academy’s YouTube channel on Wednesday, and features him alongside the Karsh Kale Collective.
“I love the idea of bringing people into the intimate details of our unique studio approaches and set-ups. Each artiste figures their own way to navigate the infinite possibilities of the studio and Red Bull Music Academy’s ‘Studio Science’ is a great platform to open that door for aspiring artistes and producers,” said Kale.
The collective includes guitarist Warren Mendonsa, flute player Ajay Prasanna, Jai Row Kavi on drums, Karan Deshmukh on percussions, Apeksha Dandekar on vocals, Nathan Thomas on bass and Delhi-based live act Shadow & Light (Anindo and Pavithra).

The foundational ideas remain inherently human. Consequently, I believe emerging artists should focus less on the specific gear they employ and more on cultivating richer human experiences.” Kale presents these views in a new installment of the Red Bull Music Academy’s “Studio Science” series, which examines the creative methodologies of various artists to provide guidance for aspiring musicians. Previous episodes have featured notable figures such as Disclosure, Four Tet, and Suzanne Ciani.

Lionel Messi played down Argentina's chances at the World Cup, though the hat-trick hero insisted the South American giants are a great team.
Runners-up at the 2014 World Cup, Argentina stepped up their preparations for next month's Russia showpiece with a routine 4-0 victory over Caribbean minnows Haiti in Buenos Aires on Tuesday.
Messi was the hero at La Bombonera – the Argentina captain and Barcelona superstar scoring three goals and assisting Sergio Aguero in the international friendly.
Argentina will face Israel on June 9 before going head-to-head with Iceland, Croatia and Nigeria in Group D at the World Cup, where reigning champions Germany, Brazil, France and Spain are among the favourites.
And Messi said Argentina are not among the candidates to lift the trophy as Jorge Sampaoli's men seek to win their third World Cup and first since 1986.
"I am very grateful to all the people, we always feel the affection of all, not like other times that we received insults," said Messi, who took his international tally to 64 goals.
"We all go to Russia for the same reason, the World Cup is the dream of us, of the country. We are not candidates but we are very good, training and improving day by day.
"We have good players and we are getting stronger to fight as an equal with anyone."
The five-time Ballon d'Or winner added: "In a World Cup, logic is almost never given. We have to aim to win the first game, which is the most important because it will give us peace of mind.
"Let no one have doubts that we are going to try everything, as people always ask us.
"We are going with a great squad that is becoming strong at the team and individual level. We are facing a beautiful possibility and we are looking for that."
rewrite:
Lionel Messi has tempered expectations regarding Argentina’s prospects at the forthcoming FIFA World Cup, despite having delivered a standout performance in a preparatory match and affirming the squad’s quality. Argentina, who were finalists in the 2014 tournament, continued their preparations for the competition in Russia with a 4-0 victory over Haiti in an international friendly held in Buenos Aires. Messi, the team’s captain and a globally renowned footballer, was instrumental in the result, scoring three goals and providing an assist for teammate Sergio Aguero.

The Argentine national team is scheduled to play a final friendly against Israel on June 9th before commencing their World Cup campaign in Group D, where they will face Iceland, Croatia, and Nigeria. While nations such as defending champions Germany, along with Brazil, France, and Spain, are widely considered favorites for the title, Messi explicitly stated that Argentina should not be counted among the primary contenders. The team, under the management of Jorge Sampaoli, aims to secure a third World Cup title, their first since 1986.

Reflecting on public support, Messi expressed appreciation for the positive reception, contrasting it with past criticisms. He noted that his recent goals have brought his international tally to 64. Regarding Argentina’s ambitions, Messi emphasized a collective focus on the tournament, stating, "We all go to Russia for the same reason; the World Cup is the dream of us, of the country. We are not candidates but we are very good, training and improving day by day." He further highlighted the squad’s developing strength, asserting that the team possesses the quality to compete effectively against any opponent.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner also addressed the unpredictable nature of the tournament, noting that logic seldom prevails. He stressed the importance of a positive start in the opening match to establish momentum. A woman has died in south London in a hit-and-run involving a number of vehicles after she was struck by two trucks and two cars.
The victim, thought to be in her late 20s or early 30s, was initially hit by a HGV as the crossed Norwood Road in Tulse Hill on a pedestrian crossing, but the driver failed to stop, the Daily Mail reports.
Three other drivers - two cars and one lorry - subsequently hit her, but none of them stopped at the scene this morning.
Police were called by the London Ambulance Service at 6.48am to reports of a woman injured after a road traffic collision.
Advertisement
Paramedics treated her at the scene, but she sadly died at 7.21am.
Acting Detective Sergeant Alastair Middleton, said: "I am appealing for anyone who witnessed the collision and the moments afterwards to contact us.
"I would also urge the drivers of all four vehicles to come forward and speak with my team."
Formal identification is yet to take place and enquiries to trace next of kin are ongoing.
A post-mortem examination will be held in due to course and detectives from the Met's Roads and Transport Policing Command are investigating.
A Metropolitan Police spokesman said: "Officers have established that the woman was struck by an HGV as she crossed the road at a pedestrian crossing.
"The driver failed to stop at the scene.
"Officers believe that the woman was subsequently struck by a second lorry and two cars - none of these drivers stopped."
rewrite:
A fatal multi-vehicle collision occurred in south London, resulting in the death of a female pedestrian in a hit-and-run incident. The victim, believed to be aged between her late twenties and early thirties, was initially struck by a heavy goods vehicle (HGV) while utilizing a pedestrian crossing on Norwood Road in Tulse Hill. According to reports, the driver of this vehicle failed to remain at the scene. Subsequently, the individual was struck by three additional vehicles: a second lorry and two cars. None of these drivers stopped following the collisions.

The Metropolitan Police were alerted by the London Ambulance Service at 06:48 hours following reports of a casualty from a road traffic incident. Despite treatment administered by paramedics at the location, the woman was pronounced deceased at 07:21 hours. A formal identification process is pending, and efforts to locate next of kin are ongoing. A post-mortem examination will be conducted in due course, with the investigation led by detectives from the Met's Roads and Transport Policing Command.

Acting Detective Sergeant Alastair Middleton has issued a public appeal for witnesses to the collision and its immediate aftermath to make contact. The drivers of all four vehicles involved are also urged to come forward and speak with investigators. Police have confirmed the sequence of events, noting the initial impact by an HGV at the crossing and the subsequent collisions with a second lorry and two cars, all of which constituted fail-to-stop offences.

COLUMBUS, Ga — It’s something a person would never want to see after logging into the nation’s number one social media site.
Facebook was rocked Sunday after an Ohio man uploaded a video of himself randomly shooting an elderly pedestrian. The suspect Steve Stephens remains on the run.
Users across the internet say they are frightened, concerned, and even disturbed by what they saw in Stephens’ video.
Thomas Waynic is the CEO and Executive Director of the Pastoral Institute. He says monitoring what you view on social media is very important. He adds incidents like this could put people in a vulnerable place.
News 3’s Ken Martin asks Waynic how this could impact those who may have watched the deadly encounter on social media.
“It can therefore disturb me internally have an affect on my sleep, have an affect on my sense of safety, have an affect on my overall general feeling about the world.” Waynic says. “We experience some kind of vicarious trauma to it and depending on our resilience level it can accumulate to a point where it begins to disturb us internally.”
rewrite:
On Sunday, the social media platform Facebook was the site of a deeply disturbing incident when an Ohio man, Steve Stephens, uploaded a video depicting the seemingly random fatal shooting of an elderly pedestrian. Stephens remains at large. The graphic nature of the content has generated widespread concern among users, many of whom report feeling frightened and disturbed after viewing the video.

Thomas Waynic, CEO and Executive Director of the Pastoral Institute, emphasizes the critical importance of monitoring one's exposure to such material on social media. He warns that incidents of this nature can profoundly impact viewers, potentially inducing a state of vulnerability. Waynic explains that exposure can lead to vicarious trauma, adversely affecting an individual's sleep, sense of safety, and general worldview. The cumulative psychological effect, he notes, is contingent upon personal resilience and can reach a threshold where it causes significant internal disturbance. This event underscores the potential for violent online content to inflict secondary psychological harm on its audience.

[India], July 4 (ANI): Reacting to the Supreme Court judgement in Delhi Government-LG power tussle case, Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Nalin Kohli said that there is no reason for the Delhi Government calling it a victory, as their demand for statehood to Delhi has been rejected by the top court.
"I don't understand how Delhi Government is claiming this to be a victory? Their main plank was that this is a state whereas Court has unequivocally said it's not a state. They said they had the exclusive executive control that was rejected too. This is a UT (Union Territory), Centre has a role to play," Nalin Kohli said.
The Supreme Court, in its judgement, said that the Lieutenant Governor must work harmoniously with the state but also added that Delhi cannot be granted statehood, citing an earlier judgement. Chief Justice of India Dipak Misra, who headed the five-judge bench comprising A.K. Sikri, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud and Ashok Bhushan said, "LG cannot act independently unless where the Constitution allows. LG cannot be an obstructionist." "L-G cannot act independently unless where the Constitution allows. L-G cannot be an obstructionist, he must take advice from the Council of Ministers. The Council has to inform the L-G of its decisions. The L-G must work harmoniously with the state, the L-G and council of ministers have to be constantly aligned. There is no space for anarchy," the CJI said. The power tussle between the Delhi government and the Lieutenant Governor has been on since the formation of the AAP government in the state. Recently, Kejriwal, along with Delhi's Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia and others, sat on a nine-day sit-in strike against Delhi Lieutenant Governor Anil Baijal at the latter's office-cum-residence. (ANI)
rewrite:
On July 4, Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Nalin Kohli responded to the Supreme Court's judgment concerning the administrative power tussle between the Delhi Government and the Lieutenant Governor. Kohli contended that the Delhi Government had no basis for declaring the ruling a victory, given that the apex court had explicitly rejected its principal demand for full statehood. He stated, "I fail to comprehend the claim of victory by the Delhi Government. Their fundamental position was that Delhi is a state, whereas the Court has unequivocally declared it is not. Their assertion of exclusive executive control was also rejected. Delhi remains a Union Territory, in which the Central Government retains a legitimate role."

The Supreme Court, in its ruling, emphasized the necessity for harmonious collaboration between the Lieutenant Governor and the elected government, while simultaneously affirming that Delhi cannot be accorded statehood, a position consistent with prior jurisprudence. Chief Justice of India Dipak Misra, presiding over a five-judge constitutional bench, articulated that the Lieutenant Governor is not empowered to act independently except in constitutionally specified domains and must not adopt an obstructionist stance. The Chief Justice elaborated, "The Lieutenant Governor cannot act independently unless permitted by the Constitution. He cannot be an obstructionist and is obligated to consider the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Council must keep the Lieutenant Governor informed of its decisions. A harmonious relationship is essential, requiring constant alignment between the Lieutenant Governor and the council of ministers; there is no room for anarchy." This protracted conflict over administrative authority has persisted since the Aam Aadmi Party assumed governance. Notably, Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, alongside Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia and other ministers, recently conducted a nine-day sit-in protest at the official residence of Lieutenant Governor Anil Baijal.

NEW YORK, March 29 Trading volume for emerging market debt rose 9 percent last year to $5.167 trillion, according to a survey of 45 leading investment and commercial banks in 90 emerging market countries.
The survey from EMTA, the emerging markets debt trading and investment industry trade association, found that debt trading volume fell in the fourth quarter of 2016 to $1.132 trillion.
That number was down 18 percent from trading during the third quarter of 2016 and 2 percent lower than trading in the fourth quarter of 2015.
EMTA said that emerging markets debt trading volume in 2015 was the lowest recorded since 2009.
The growth in 2016 was the result of "strong inflows, volatility related to global political events (Brexit, U.S. elections), and idiosyncratic market developments within emerging markets," Hongtao Jiang, head of emerging market credit strategy at Deutsche Bank, said in a statement with the release.
He also noted that India and Argentina were the largest contributors to idiosyncratic country risk.
"However, this masks a multi-year declining trend in trading volumes as 2016 total turnover remains substantially lower than 2013 and 2014 levels," he said, "reflecting the impact of tighter regulation across banks on their ability in providing liquidity." (Reporting by Dion Rabouin; Editing by Grant McCool)
rewrite:
According to a survey encompassing 45 leading investment and commercial banks across 90 emerging market countries, annual trading volume for emerging market debt increased by nine percent in 2016, reaching a total of $5.167 trillion. The survey, conducted by EMTA—the trade association for the emerging markets debt trading and investment industry—indicated that trading volume declined to $1.132 trillion during the fourth quarter of 2016. This figure represents an eighteen percent decrease from the third quarter of 2016 and a two percent reduction compared to the fourth quarter of 2015. EMTA noted that the 2015 annual volume was the lowest recorded since 2009.

Hongtao Jiang, Head of Emerging Market Credit Strategy at Deutsche Bank, attributed the 2016 annual growth to substantial capital inflows, volatility associated with global political events such as Brexit and the U.S. elections, and idiosyncratic developments within specific emerging markets. Jiang identified India and Argentina as the most significant contributors to country-specific risk. He cautioned, however, that this annual increase obscures a persistent multi-year downtrend, as the 2016 total turnover remains substantially below the levels observed in 2013 and 2014. This longer-term decline reflects the impact of heightened regulatory constraints on banks, which have curtailed their capacity to provide market liquidity.

Around The World In 80 Days comes to Nottingham’s Theatre Royal from July 11-15.
Adapted from the Jules Verne story by Laura Eason and directed by Theresa Heskins, in this play the mysterious and fabulously wealthy Phileas Fogg wagers his life’s fortune that he can circumnavigate the globe in just 80 days.
Join him and his loyal valet Passepartout, as they voyage from the misty alleys of Victorian London to the exotic subcontinent and the Wild West in a race against the clock.
Theresa Heskins’s celebrated production is on six month UK tour including a summer season in London and a Christmas engagement at the Lowry.
A cast of eight play over 125 characters in this imaginative, high-spirited escapade including six trains, five boats, four fights, three dances, two circus acts and an elephant!

Accompanied by his devoted valet Passepartout, Fogg embarks on a perilous journey from Victorian London to the Indian subcontinent and the American frontier. This acclaimed staging, currently on a six-month national tour, features a versatile ensemble of eight performers portraying more than one hundred and twenty-five characters. The inventive staging incorporates numerous scenic elements, including six trains, five boats, and an elephant. Ticket prices range from £12.50 to £27.50, available through the venue's official website or box office.

TAMPA -
A new season of theater, dance, music and learning is underway at the Straz Center in downtown Tampa.
The premiere performing arts center on the eastern shore of the Hillsborough River is the epicenter for outstanding performances by professionals and amateurs.
“We inspire students to dream, reach, create and discover,” said Matthew Belopavlovich, the lead theater teacher at the Straz Center's Patel Conservatory.
The conservatory in an arts learning center for more than 70,000 students on stage, in classrooms and in the community each year. It offers classes in music, theater and dance, said Belopavlovich, who also teaches outreaches and is directing Peter Pan Jr.
Classes range from drumming at MacDill Air Force Base to screenwriting to taking a theater outreach class a Pepin Academy.
Applications are available by emailing communityprograms@strazcenter.org or go to the community programs on the PatelConvervatory.org website.
Anyone who want to take a class at Patel Conservatory also can apply for a scholarship. The center offers merit and need based scholarships.
Applications are open through April 6.

Integral to its mission is the Patel Conservatory, an arts education center engaging over 70,000 students annually through stage, classroom, and community-based instruction. Matthew Belopavlovich, lead theater teacher at the conservatory, emphasized its role in inspiring students “to dream, reach, create and discover.” The curriculum encompasses diverse offerings, from music and dance to specialized courses such as screenwriting and outreach programs at locations including MacDill Air Force Base and Pepin Academy. Interested participants may obtain application materials via email at communityprograms@strazcenter.org or through the community programs section of the PatelConservatory.org website. rewrite:
The i.MX6ULL System on Module (SOM), based on the NXP i.MX 6ULL processor, integrates a power-efficient, high-performance ARM Cortex-A7 CPU core. This processor family is designed for cost- and power-optimized applications, featuring an advanced implementation of a single ARM Cortex-A7 core operating at speeds up to 528 MHz. It incorporates an integrated power management module, which reduces external power supply complexity and simplifies power sequencing. The processor supports various memory interfaces, including 16-bit LPDDR2, DDR3, DDR3L, along with NAND flash, NOR flash, eMMC, and Quad SPI. It also provides a wide range of peripheral interfaces for connectivity options such as WLAN, Bluetooth, GPS, displays, and camera sensors.

This specific SODIMM-form-factor SOM leverages the i.MX 6ULL to offer a compact, cost-optimized solution. It is integrated with on-board power management (PMIC), Flash memory, DDR3, and a dual Ethernet PHY. Pre-loaded with a Linux operating system, the module is ideally suited for general embedded and industrial applications where power efficiency and cost are critical. Key technical specifications include the ARM Cortex-A7 core running at 528 MHz with 128 KB L2 cache, support for a parallel LCD display up to WXGA resolution (1366×768), and an 8/10/16/24-bit parallel camera sensor interface. It also features an electrophoretic display controller for direct drive of E-Ink EPD panels. Memory support encompasses 16-bit LP-DDR2 and DDR3/DDR3L, parallel NOR flash, dual-channel Quad-SPI NOR flash, and 8-bit raw NAND flash with 40-bit ECC. Connectivity is facilitated through dual MMC/SDIO ports, dual USB 2.0 OTG ports with PHY, multiple audio interfaces (I2S/SAI, S/PDIF), dual 10/100 Ethernet with IEEE 1588 support, and two 12-bit ADCs with integrated resistive touch screen controller support.

Initial contact regarding airline service issues should be directed to the carrier. Should the airline fail to provide a resolution, complaints may be filed with the U.S. Department of Transportation.

**Attorneys**
Legal practitioners often specialize in specific fields. The Louisiana State Bar Association offers guidance for selecting appropriate legal counsel.

**Automotive Purchases**
Resources are available to assist consumers with the vehicle acquisition process within the state of Louisiana.

**Automotive Recalls**
Consumers may investigate open safety recalls for their vehicles by entering the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) into the database maintained by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

**Consumer Disputes**
The Louisiana Attorney General’s Office intervenes in matters where business practices are alleged to be unfair or deceptive.

**Credit Reports**
A complimentary credit report is available to consumers annually through the designated, industry-sanctioned website.

**Credit Scores**
While consumers possess multiple credit scores, the substantive content of the credit report is generally considered more significant than the numerical score itself.

**Medical Practitioners**
The licensure status of physicians may be verified through state records. Complaints regarding medical practice should be submitted to the relevant state authority.

**Healthcare Standards**
Grievances concerning licensed healthcare providers may be filed with the Louisiana Department of Health.

**Insurance Fraud**
Insurance agents in Louisiana are required to maintain a valid state-issued license. Allegations of fraudulent activity may result in legal penalties.

**Landlord-Tenant Relations & Evictions**
A comprehensive guide to Louisiana statutes governing landlord and tenant obligations, including eviction procedures, is available for reference.

**Lemon Law Protections**
Consumers who purchase new vehicles with substantial defects may seek recourse under the Louisiana Lemon Law.

**Lottery Scams**
Individuals are advised to exercise caution against fraudulent schemes that exploit the premise of lottery winnings to illicitly obtain funds or personal information.

ESPN reporter Chris Haynes caused a minor meltdown on Twitter Thursday when he wrote that LeBron James would be willing to sit down with the Golden State Warriors this summer as he explores free agency, citing “league sources.”
Within hours, the James report was the biggest story on ESPN, and commentator Stephen A. Smith declared that James would destroy his legacy if he considered joining the Warriors.
James apparently saw Smith’s comments, and responded to the ESPN report Friday. LeBron denied that said he would meet with any team in the league this summer, and said the report was a “discredit” to his team.
“The first thing I did is start laughing, actually. It’s nonsense, and it’s a non-story, and I think it’s a discredit to what I’m trying to do here. It’s a discredit to my teammates and the coaching staff here. My only focus right now is trying to figure out how we can become a championship-caliber team in these next few months. There’s been so many stories about me in the last few months and the last few days about where I’m going and where I’m at and what place I’m in… I’m right here. I’m right now, and this is my present and this is where I’m at. If you don’t hear something coming from my voice, then it’s not true.”
James also seemed to respond to Stephen A. Smith, and stated that it bothers him that the rumor become the news of the day in sports media.
rewrite:
On Thursday, ESPN journalist Chris Haynes, citing unnamed league sources, reported that LeBron James would be open to a meeting with the Golden State Warriors during the upcoming free agency period. This report precipitated significant discourse on social media platform Twitter. The story rapidly ascended to become a leading item across ESPN’s platforms, where commentator Stephen A. Smith asserted that any consideration by James of joining the Warriors would irreparably damage his professional legacy.

James subsequently addressed the report publicly on Friday, having evidently become aware of Smith’s commentary. He explicitly refuted the central claim, denying any plans to meet with other franchises during the summer and characterizing the reporting as a "discredit" to his current organization. “My initial reaction was actually to laugh,” James stated. “It is nonsense and a non-story. I believe it is a discredit to what I am trying to accomplish here, a discredit to my teammates and the coaching staff. My sole focus at present is determining how we can evolve into a championship-caliber team in the coming months. There have been numerous narratives circulating recently regarding my future destination and my current state of mind. I am here, focused on the present. This is my current situation. If a statement does not originate from me directly, it is not factual.”

James further appeared to respond indirectly to Smith’s remarks, expressing his frustration that an unsubstantiated rumor had dominated the day’s sports media cycle, thereby diverting attention from his and his team’s competitive objectives.

Speculation that powerhouse prop Alex Walmsley is to leave Saints has been nailed on the head ... by the player himself.
The 27-year-old former Batley forward, whose existing contract ends at the end of the 2018 season, insisted yesterday: “I’m not going anywhere unless there is something being talked about above my head.
“The club have not spoken to me and neither have I talked to Castleford. I love St Helens, the players and all the staff and it has been the same since I first arrived.”
Ironically, he has been linked with the club which Saints face in the opening fixture of the Super 8s at the Jungle tonight and Big Al will be hoping he can help reverse the results of the previous two fixtures this year at the same venue - a 53-10 drubbing in the Ladbrokes Challenge Cup and a 16-12 Super League setback a few weeks later.
He said: “Castleford current top the table and there is a reason why they are 10 points clear of their nearest rivals, Leeds Rhinos ... they have been the most consistent side in the competition so far and we will have to be at our best to pick up what are two vital points.
“It is a tough test for us but we are not going there just to make up the numbers.”
Walmsley feels Saints are in the kind of form to earn a top four spot, especially with players like James Roby, Matty Smith and Jon Wilkin, who have big match experience, in their ranks.
Success will also enhance his own chances of making the England squad for the end of season World Cup - and hopes his performance in a Saints shirt catches the eye of international boss Wayne Bennett.
“It is a dream of mine to represent my country and there is no bigger stage to play on than a World Cup tournament,” he said.
rewrite:
Speculation regarding the potential departure of prominent prop forward Alex Walmsley from St Helens has been definitively addressed by the player himself. Walmsley, aged 27 and formerly of Batley, whose current contract concludes at the end of the 2018 season, explicitly stated, “I have no intention of leaving unless discussions occur without my involvement. The club has not approached me, and I have held no talks with Castleford. I maintain a strong affinity for St Helens, including the players and staff, a sentiment consistent since my arrival.”

This clarification is particularly notable as the rumour connected him to Castleford, the very opponent St Helens faces in their opening Super 8s fixture at the Jungle. Walmsley will undoubtedly aim to contribute to reversing the outcomes of the two previous encounters at that venue this season: a decisive 53-10 defeat in the Ladbrokes Challenge Cup and a subsequent 16-12 Super League loss. Assessing the challenge, he acknowledged Castleford’s position at the summit of the table, noting, “Their ten-point lead over Leeds Rhinos is a consequence of being the competition’s most consistent side. Securing these two vital points will require our utmost performance. While it is a rigorous test, our objective extends beyond mere participation.”

Walmsley expressed confidence that St Helens possesses the requisite form to secure a top-four finish, a prospect bolstered by the presence of experienced players such as James Roby, Matty Smith, and Jon Wilkin. Furthermore, team success would augment his personal aspirations for international selection. Strong performances for St Helens could enhance his prospects of inclusion in the England squad for the forthcoming World Cup, thereby attracting the attention of national coach Wayne Bennett. “Representing my country is a personal ambition,” Walmsley affirmed, “and the World Cup represents the ultimate stage upon which to do so.”
