A 'Black Panther' roars. A whale says "hello." And a groundhog silently decides our winter fate. It's time for this week's politics-free side of the news.
Scroll for more content...
A 'Black Panther' roars
It's still two weeks away from hitting theaters. But 'Black Panther' is already outselling every superhero film in pre-sales!
A whale says 'hello'
Wikie the whale is able to repeat a handful of words. Scientists believe she's the first orca in the world to mimic human speech. Way to go, Wikie!
A groundhog ruins everyone's day
Punxsutawney Phil scurried out of a marmot hole and saw his shadow. Which means more winter. Thanks, Phil.
A cosmic event dazzles
A lunar eclipse, a blood moon and a super moon? It was all of those things! If you missed it, another one will be visible next year.
A teen lights the way
Nearly half a million Puerto Ricans still don't have power. He wanted to do something about that. Now he delivers hundreds of solar lamps throughout the island.
A woman mobilizes a community
She asked. They answered. Social media steps in to ease the Cape Town water crisis.
rewrite:
This week's news features several notable developments beyond the political sphere, spanning entertainment, science, and community action.

The forthcoming film 'Black Panther' has achieved record pre-sales, surpassing all previous superhero films two weeks prior to its theatrical release. In scientific news, an orca whale named Wikie has demonstrated the ability to mimic human speech, representing a potential first in observed cetacean vocal learning. Regarding tradition, the groundhog Punxsutawney Phil emerged and observed his shadow, an event folklore interprets as predicting six additional weeks of winter.

Astronomically, a rare celestial convergence of a lunar eclipse, a supermoon, and a blood moon recently occurred; a similar event will be visible next year. In humanitarian efforts, a teenager in Puerto Rico is addressing ongoing power shortages by distributing hundreds of solar lamps to affected residents. Concurrently, in Cape Town, a community organizer has effectively utilized social media to mobilize collective action in response to the severe regional water crisis.

“Last week, a story went viral that claimed Apple was intentionally slowing down older iPhones to push people to buy its latest models,” Futuremark reports. “The claim was based on data which shows Google searches for ‘iPhone slow’ spiking dramatically with the release of each new model.”
“And while plenty of reputable sites debunked the logic of that claim, no one looked at actual performance data to tell the true story,” Futuremark reports. “Fortunately, we have plenty of real-world data we can use. Since 2016, we have collected more than a hundred thousand benchmark results for seven different iPhone models across three different versions of iOS.”
“These benchmark results provide a unique insight into the everyday performance of each iPhone model over time,” Futuremark reports. “Our benchmarking data shows that, rather than intentionally degrading the performance of older models, Apple actually does a good job of supporting its older devices with regular updates that maintain a consistent level of performance across iOS versions.”
Read more in the full article – recommended – here.
MacDailyNews Take: Sorry, conspiracy theorists, there’s no conspiracy here.
[Thanks to MacDailyNews Reader “Fred Mertz” for the heads up.]
rewrite:
According to a report by Futuremark, a widely circulated narrative emerged last week alleging that Apple deliberately slows down older iPhone models to incentivize purchases of newer devices. This assertion was purportedly supported by data indicating significant spikes in Google searches for "iPhone slow" coinciding with each new model release. Futuremark notes that while numerous credible sources critiqued the reasoning behind this claim, an analysis of empirical performance data was absent. The organization addresses this gap by drawing upon its own extensive dataset, comprising over one hundred thousand benchmark results collected since 2016 across seven iPhone models and three iOS versions.

This benchmark data offers a distinct perspective on the longitudinal performance of each model. Futuremark's analysis indicates that, contrary to allegations of intentional degradation, Apple effectively supports older devices through software updates that sustain consistent performance levels across iOS iterations. The findings thus challenge the premise of planned obsolescence in this context. The full article is recommended for further detail. An accompanying editorial comment dismisses the allegations as unfounded.

Rangers chairman Dave King faces possible contempt of court proceedings after failing to comply with a Takeover Panel order.
A document released by the independent body indicates that papers were served on King last month.
The South African-based businessman has so far failed to launch a compliant offer for the remainder of the club’s shares, after the Takeover Panel ruled he had acted in concert with other investors ahead of boardroom regime change in March 2015.
The chairman of the Takeover Panel hearings committee, Michael Crane QC, rejected King’s request to convene a hearing to review a decision to refuse to grant him more time to produce proof of funds.
Rangers’ biggest shareholder has previously claimed his offer had been delayed amid difficulties in securing clearance from the South African authorities to move money needed to underwrite his £10.75million bid to the United Kingdom.
The decision states: “In the event, process in the contempt proceedings appears to have been served on Mr King in South Africa on 8 June 2018.
“This seems to have prompted Mr King’s request of 11 June 2018 to have the committee convened for a review of the Executive’s refusal to grant an extension of time.
“In the meantime, Mr King had produced no evidence to show that he had instructed Investec to seek the necessary exchange control consents or to confirm its willingness to receive the consideration monies into a UK account with a view to giving the requisite cash confirmation.
“It is noteworthy that, in his submissions of 18 June 2018 Mr King does not maintain that he has now instructed Investec to do this.”
King earlier lost two challenges to the panel’s order in the Court of Session in Edinburgh.
Meanwhile, Bruno Alves appears to be edging towards a Rangers exit after reports in Italy claimed he had arrived at Serie A newcomers Parma for a medical.
The 36-year-old Portugal defender made 25 appearances for Rangers after joining from Cagliari.
rewrite:
Mr. David King, the Chairman of Rangers Football Club, is confronting potential contempt of court proceedings due to his non-compliance with an order issued by the Takeover Panel. Documentation released by this independent regulatory body confirms that legal papers were served upon Mr. King last month. This situation arises from his failure to initiate a mandatory offer for the remaining shares in the club, a requirement triggered after the Panel determined he had acted in concert with other investors prior to a change in boardroom control in March 2015.

The Chairman of the Takeover Panel’s hearings committee, Michael Crane QC, has subsequently denied a request from Mr. King to convene a review hearing concerning the Executive’s refusal to grant an extension for providing proof of funds. The club’s largest shareholder had previously cited delays in obtaining necessary clearance from South African authorities to transfer the funds required to underwrite his £10.75 million offer to the United Kingdom. The committee’s decision notes that the initiation of contempt proceedings, with process served in South Africa on 8 June 2018, appears to have prompted Mr. King’s request for a review on 11 June 2018.

The ruling further observes that Mr. King had submitted no evidence demonstrating he had instructed Investec to seek the requisite exchange control consents or to confirm its willingness to receive the consideration into a United Kingdom account for the purpose of providing a cash confirmation. It is also noted that in his subsequent submissions of 18 June 2018, Mr. King did not assert that he had since issued such instructions to Investec. This development follows two unsuccessful legal challenges by Mr. King against the Panel’s order in the Court of Session in Edinburgh.

In a separate matter pertaining to the club’s squad, defender Bruno Alves appears to be nearing a departure from Rangers. Italian media reports indicate the 36-year-old Portugal international, who made 25 appearances for the club after joining from Cagliari, has arrived at Serie A newcomers Parma to undergo a medical examination.

Consultations vital to end ethnic crisis – Osinbajo
Acting President Yemi Osinbajo has said consultation with ethnic leaders is vital to end crisis in the country.
He disclosed this at a summit on promoting peace, democracy and stability organized by Journalists for Democratic Rights (JODER) held on Wednesday in Abuja.
Osinbajo, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters, Senator Babafemi Ojudu, said the presidency has commenced intensive consultations with stakeholders to douse tension created by some ethnic associations through their utterances.
He added that the nation should see its socio-cultural differences as a source of strength rather than weaknesses, adding that any form of breakup will be costly.
He said the Igbos had invested so much outside the Igboland and war is not the solution.
“Nigerians should deepen social interactions and appreciate the positive sides of each other,” the acting President said.

Acting President Yemi Osinbajo has emphasized the critical importance of consultations with ethnic leaders as a necessary mechanism for resolving the nation’s ongoing ethnic tensions. This statement was delivered during a summit focused on the promotion of peace, democracy, and stability, organized by Journalists for Democratic Rights (JODER) in Abuja on Wednesday. Represented by Senator Babafemi Ojudu, the Special Adviser to the President on Political Matters, Osinbajo indicated that the presidency has initiated intensive dialogues with key stakeholders. The objective of these engagements is to mitigate the heightened tensions resulting from recent pronouncements by certain ethnic associations.

Furthermore, Osinbajo articulated that the nation’s socio-cultural diversity should be regarded as a source of collective strength rather than a point of division. He cautioned that any movement toward national dissolution would entail significant costs. Illustrating this point, he noted the substantial investments made by the Igbo community outside their indigenous region, arguing that conflict cannot serve as a viable solution. The Acting President urged citizens to enhance social interactions and foster a mutual appreciation of each other’s positive attributes. He concluded that through sustained dialogue and a commitment to unity, the current crises can be effectively addressed, thereby preserving national integrity and stability.

CHARLOTTE, S.C. — Zane Najdawi scored 28 points, grabbed 10 rebounds and Frankie Johnson drove for one layup to force overtime and another to give The Citadel the lead for good in the extra period on Saturday and the Bulldogs defeated Furman 100-92 to cap an intense three-win home stand.
Languishing near the bottom of the Southern Conference standings four games ago, The Citadel (9-14, 4-7) took undefeated conference leader ETSU to overtime, losing by two on the road when a last-second 3 rimmed out. Once home, the Bulldogs defeated Mercer for the first time in 91 years a week ago, rallied to bump off Wofford, one of the conference leaders, on Thursday, and did it again to Furman (16-8, 7-4) Saturday.
The Paladins held a 17-point lead with 9:13 remaining when Devin Sibley hit a 3-pointer. The Citadel marched back, making its last seven field-goal attempts with Johnson driving to the hoop to tie 88-88 with 4.8 seconds remaining.
The rally continued into the overtime as Johnson drove for the go-ahead and kissed it off the glass for a 90-88 lead, the Bulldogs first since 25-24 of the first half, and they never let Furman come back, making 10 of 11 free throws.
rewrite:
On Saturday, The Citadel Bulldogs concluded a demanding three-game home stand with a 100-92 overtime victory over the Furman Paladins. The win was propelled by a standout performance from Zane Najdawi, who recorded 28 points and 10 rebounds, and by critical plays from Frankie Johnson. Johnson’s driving layup with 4.8 seconds remaining in regulation forced the overtime period, and he subsequently scored another layup to secure a permanent lead for the Bulldogs in the extra session.

This victory extends a notable resurgence for The Citadel (9-14, 4-7 Southern Conference). Having languished near the conference bottom recently, the team previously took undefeated league leader ETSU to overtime on the road before narrowly losing. The home stand then featured a historic win over Mercer, ending a 91-year drought, followed by a comeback victory against conference leader Wofford on Thursday, culminating in the defeat of Furman (16-8, 7-4).

Furman had established a 17-point advantage with 9:13 remaining, but The Citadel mounted a decisive rally, making its final seven field-goal attempts in regulation. The Bulldogs continued their momentum into overtime, seizing a 90-88 lead—their first since the first half—and secured the win by converting 10 of 11 free throws while preventing any Furman response.

The Diamondbacks are paying for their coach’s Apple Watch, just like the Red Sox did last month.
MLB announced Friday it was fining the Diamondbacks and coach Ariel Prieto each for Prieto’s decision to wear the electronic device in the dugout during Wednesday night’s win over the Rockies in the NL wild-card game.
An investigation into Prieto’s fashion choice revealed no illegal actions, such as stealing signs, during the game in Phoenix, but MLB has a rule against wearing such devices in the dugout and handed down punishment accordingly. On Thursday, Prieto called wearing the watch on game night a “simple oversight and honest mistake.”
“MLB forensically examined Mr. Prieto’s Apple Watch and his cell phone and interviewed Mr. Prieto,” the league said in a statement. “MLB found no evidence that Mr. Prieto used the Apple Watch or cell phone for any purpose in the dugout, nor any baseball-related communication on either device, during Wednesday’s game.
“Despite these findings, Mr. Prieto violated MLB’s on-field regulation by having this device in the dugout. As a result, Mr. Prieto and the D-backs have each been fined an undisclosed amount.”
Commissioner Rob Manfred plans to take the Diamondbacks’ money and donate it to hurricane relief efforts in Puerto Rico, MLB added in the statement.
The Red Sox ignited the discussion around the use of high-tech devices when the Yankees believed they caught them using a coach’s Apple Watch to steal signs during a game in August. Boston admitted to the violation and was fined an undisclosed amount.
At the time, Manfred warned teams that any future offense of this type would be met with harsher sanctions.
rewrite:
Major League Baseball announced on Friday that it has levied fines against the Arizona Diamondbacks organization and coach Ariel Prieto for Prieto’s possession of an Apple Watch in the dugout during Wednesday’s National League wild-card victory over the Colorado Rockies. This action mirrors a prior incident involving the Boston Red Sox, who were similarly penalized last month for a coach’s use of such a device. Following an investigation, the league stated that forensic examination of Prieto’s watch and cell phone, along with an interview, uncovered no evidence of illicit activity, such as sign-stealing, or any baseball-related communication during the contest in Phoenix. Prieto characterized the incident as an unintentional oversight.

Nevertheless, MLB determined that Prieto’s actions constituted a violation of on-field regulations prohibiting electronic devices in the dugout. Consequently, both the coach and the club received undisclosed financial penalties. Commissioner Rob Manfred intends to direct the funds from the Diamondbacks’ fine toward hurricane relief efforts in Puerto Rico. The issue of electronic devices gained prominence after an August incident in which the New York Yankees accused the Red Sox of utilizing an Apple Watch to decode signs. Boston admitted to the violation and was fined. Following that case, Commissioner Manfred issued a warning that future infractions would result in more severe sanctions, underscoring the league’s commitment to enforcing its rules despite the absence of proven competitive advantage in this instance.

Warning: This article contains a major spoiler from The Originals‘ upcoming fourth season finale. Proceed at your own risk!
Hope Mikaelson is about to hit another growth spurt.
Though neither The CW nor Warner Bros. TV are commenting, sources confirm to TVLine that The Originals is bracing for a significant time jump, setting the stage for a much older Hope — think late teens — to be introduced in Season 5. The time jump could arrive as soon as the June 23 season finale (The CW, 8/7c); casting for the “new” role, currently being portrayed by the phenomenal Summer Fontana, is now underway.
We also hear there’s potential for adult Hope to snag her own spinoff, though neither The CW nor Warner Bros. TV would comment on that either. Of course, if Hope does end up at the center of a third series in the Vampire Diaries universe, it would be sort of like a prophecy coming to fruition — albeit one foretold by executive producer Julie Plec.
“I think there are future shows down the line that can be spawned out of this world and could tell good stories,” Plec told TVLine back in March while discussing the letter Klaus sent to Caroline in the series finale of The Vampire Diaries. “It’s a hope for the future if nothing else.”
As for what else the future might hold for Hope, Plec reminded TVLine that “the idea of [Caroline and Alaric’s] school as a safe haven for young supernatural beings certainly has a lot of relevance for Hope,” leading many viewers — including the one currently typing this — to believe that Hope will relocate from New Orleans to Mystic Falls by the end of the season.
What are your thoughts on Hope time-jumping her way to a potential spinoff? Drop ’em in a comment below.

Thanks to a dinger from Jay Bruce, the Cleveland Indians have a 1-0 lead in their ALDS against the New York Yankees.
The Indians’ Twitter account used the moment he hit that fourth-inning home run to reminded the world that the acquisition of Bruce happened thanks to a smart front office and …
Jay Bruce is on our team because our owner wrote a check that competitors for Jay wouldn't. pic.twitter.com/nIIff4RMcZ — AL Central champs! (@Indians) October 6, 2017
Hmmm. “Competitors for Jay,” eh? Which competitors for Bruce’s services wouldn’t write a check for the slugger?
Here’s a report from the New York Post in August:
After being mostly shunned at the non-waiver deadline, Jay Bruce was pursued by two AL teams with playoff aspirations and more. The Yankees were not only one of those teams, they had agreed to send the two prospects requested by the Mets in exchange for the Mets eating a piece of the roughly $5 million Bruce was owed the rest of the season … It was the Indians who ultimately landed Bruce, with a source saying the Yankees never got a chance to bid again.
Perhaps it was because Cleveland was willing to assume all the money that Bruce was owed.
Maybe that was revenge for the Yankees’ tweet that reminded the world that LeBron James once rooted for the Pinstripes.
rewrite:
A fourth-inning home run by Jay Bruce provided the Cleveland Indians with a 1-0 lead in their American League Division Series against the New York Yankees. The organization’s official Twitter account utilized the event to highlight the strategic front-office acquisition of Bruce, implicitly crediting ownership’s financial commitment. The accompanying tweet stated, “Jay Bruce is on our team because our owner wrote a check that competitors for Jay wouldn't,” suggesting other suitors were unwilling to match the financial terms.

This allusion to “competitors” invites inquiry into which teams declined to assume Bruce’s remaining salary. Reporting from the New York Post in August detailed the circumstances: following limited interest at the non-waiver trade deadline, Bruce was pursued by multiple American League contenders, including the Yankees. The Yankees had reportedly agreed to send two prospects to the New York Mets, contingent on the Mets absorbing a portion of Bruce’s approximately $5 million remaining obligation. However, the Indians ultimately secured the player. A source indicated the Yankees were not afforded a subsequent opportunity to bid, implying Cleveland’s willingness to assume the full financial burden was a decisive factor.

This transaction may be viewed within a broader context of competitive exchanges between the franchises, perhaps even as a retaliatory gesture following a prior Yankees social media post referencing LeBron James’s childhood support for the team.

TEHRAN, Iran — Iran’s Foreign Ministry said Monday it will raise the case of a detained British-Iranian woman with the judiciary “out of humanitarian concerns” following a visit by Britain’s foreign secretary.
Ministry spokesman Bahram Ghasemi said the final decision on whether to release Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe, who is serving a five-year sentence for allegedly plotting to overthrow the government, rests with the judiciary.
Zaghari-Ratcliffe “is considered an Iranian national and should serve her prison conviction according to the judicial system of Iran,” he added.
British Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson raised the case during a two-day visit to Iran that concluded Sunday. Zaghari-Ratcliffe, a charity worker, was detained in April 2016. Her family has denied the allegations against her.
She is among several dual nationals held in Iran, where the judiciary and security forces are dominated by anti-Western hard-liners. It’s unclear whether Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif, a relative moderate, can secure her release.
Johnson recently complicated efforts to free her by saying incorrectly that she was training journalists when arrested. He has since apologized.
Britain and Iran have discussed the release of some 400 million pounds ($530 million) held by London, a payment Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi made for Chieftain tanks that were never delivered. The shah abandoned the throne in 1979 and the Islamic Revolution soon installed the clerically overseen system that endures today.
Authorities in London and Tehran deny the payment has any link to Zaghari-Ratcliffe.
However, the United States made a $400 million transfer to Iran in January 2016 when Iran freed Washington Post journalist Jason Rezaian and three other Iranian-Americans. That money too involved undelivered military equipment from the shah’s era. Some U.S. politicians criticized the transfer, calling it a ransom payment.
rewrite:
On Monday, the Iranian Foreign Ministry announced that, following a visit by the British Foreign Secretary, it would refer the case of a detained British-Iranian woman to the judiciary on humanitarian grounds. Ministry spokesman Bahram Ghasemi stated that any final decision regarding the release of Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe—currently serving a five-year sentence for alleged involvement in plots to overthrow the government—rests solely with the judicial authorities. Ghasemi further emphasized that Zaghari-Ratcliffe is considered an Iranian national and is therefore subject to the rulings of Iran’s judicial system.

The case was raised directly by British Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson during a two-day diplomatic visit to Iran concluding Sunday. Zaghari-Ratcliffe, a charity worker, was initially detained in April 2016, with her family consistently denying all charges against her. She is one of several dual nationals currently held in Iran, where the judiciary and security apparatus are largely controlled by factions skeptical of Western engagement. The capacity of the comparatively moderate Foreign Minister, Mohammad Javad Zarif, to secure her release remains uncertain.

Complicating diplomatic efforts, Foreign Secretary Johnson recently made inaccurate remarks suggesting Zaghari-Ratcliffe had been training journalists at the time of her arrest, for which he has since apologized. Concurrently, broader negotiations between the United Kingdom and Iran have involved discussions concerning approximately £400 million (equivalent to $530 million) held by London. These funds originate from a payment made by the former Shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, for Chieftain tanks that were never delivered, prior to his ouster in the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Officials from both nations deny any connection between this financial dispute and Zaghari-Ratcliffe’s case.

Nevertheless, observers note a precedent: in January 2016, the United States transferred $400 million to Iran coincident with Tehran’s release of Washington Post journalist Jason Rezaian and three other Iranian-Americans. Those funds also pertained to undelivered military equipment from the pre-revolutionary era. The transfer drew criticism from some U.S. legislators, who characterized it as a ransom payment.

'Game of Thrones', starring Kit Harington, is the most pirated show in TV history (AFP Photo/Neilson Barnard)
Mumbai (AFP) - Four people have been arrested in India for leaking an episode from HBO's "Game of Thrones" television series before it was aired in the country, police said Monday.
Already the most pirated show in TV history, the popular fantasy drama -- which tells the story of noble families vying for the Iron Throne -- has been plagued by leaks in recent weeks following the premiere of the seventh season.
After receiving a complaint for a company "we investigated the case and have arrested four individuals for unauthorised publication of the fourth episode from season seven," Deputy Commissioner of Police Akbar Pathan told AFP.
He said the four -- accused of criminal breach of trust and computer-related offences -- would be detained until August 21 amid an investigation.
The case was filed by a Mumbai-based company responsible for storing and processing the TV episodes for an app, local media said.
The four arrested were company employees who possessed official credentials giving them access to the episodes, the reports added.
Game of Thrones has more Emmy Awards than any narrative show in history and airs in 170 countries, with viewership figures shattering records across the world.
As well as being a hit globally, it has a massive fan base in South Asia.
Showrunners David Benioff and D.B. Weiss last year announced the shortened run of seven and six episodes for the final two seasons and confirmed the summer return for season seven, a departure from the usual April premieres.
The show has been teasing winter's arrival since its pilot episode in 2011, and in the latest episode preview "Death Is The Enemy" has finally moved closer to showcasing a battle between a horde of undead "White Walkers" from the frozen North and a troop of warriors led by hero Jon Snow (Kit Harington).

NEWARK, N.J. (AP) - "Jersey Shore" star Michael "The Situation" Sorrentino and his brother pleaded not guilty Monday to additional tax fraud charges after federal prosecutors say they filed fake tax returns and claimed luxury car and clothing purchases were business expenses.
Michael and Marc Sorrentino entered their pleas during an arraignment in federal court in Newark.
"This is a complicated case - Michael is not a complicated person," Michael Sorrentino's attorney, Henry Klingeman, told reporters outside the courthouse after the hearing had concluded.
Marc Sorrentino's attorney declined to comment on the proceedings.
In 2014, the brothers pleaded not guilty to charges they filed bogus tax returns on nearly $9 million and claimed millions in personal expenses as business expenses.
Michael Sorrentino was indicted this month on charges including tax evasion, structuring bank deposits to avoid reporting requirements and falsifying records. Marc Sorrentino was charged with falsifying records to obstruct a grand jury investigation.
Prosecutors allege Michael Sorrentino didn't pay federal income tax owed on the $8.9 million he earned from 2010 to 2012, failed to file a personal tax return for 2011 and filed fake corporate returns for one of the companies the brothers set up after he gained fame on the show. Prosecutors say he also made a series of bank deposits of under $10,000 to avoid bank reporting requirements.
After the brothers were served with grand jury subpoenas seeking records from their companies, prosecutors allege Marc Sorrentino falsified records to reclassify taxable payments to himself as nontaxable payments and business deductions.
"The Situation" appeared on all six seasons of the MTV reality show, which followed the lives of rowdy housemates on New Jersey's famed Atlantic shore and ran from 2009 to 2012.
Copyright 2017 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten or redistributed.
rewrite:
On Monday, in a federal court in Newark, New Jersey, Michael Sorrentino—known for his role on the television program "Jersey Shore"—and his brother, Marc Sorrentino, entered pleas of not guilty to new charges of tax fraud. Federal prosecutors allege that the brothers submitted fraudulent tax returns and improperly categorized expenditures for luxury vehicles and apparel as legitimate business deductions. This recent arraignment follows an initial indictment in 2014, in which both individuals similarly pleaded not guilty to charges of filing false returns concerning nearly nine million dollars in income and misrepresenting millions in personal expenses as business costs.

The current superseding indictment accuses Michael Sorrentino of multiple offenses, including tax evasion, structuring bank deposits to circumvent federal reporting mandates, and falsifying financial records. Specifically, prosecutors contend that he failed to pay federal income tax on approximately $8.9 million earned between 2010 and 2012, neglected to file a personal return for the 2011 tax year, and submitted a fraudulent corporate return for an entity established by the brothers. It is further alleged that he engaged in structuring by making a series of bank deposits each under the $10,000 reporting threshold. Marc Sorrentino faces charges of falsifying records to obstruct a grand jury investigation, purportedly altering documents to reclassify taxable disbursements to himself as non-taxable or as business deductions following the issuance of subpoenas.

Legal representation for Michael Sorrentino, attorney Henry Klingeman, characterized his client outside the courtroom, stating, “This is a complicated case—Michael is not a complicated person.” Counsel for Marc Sorrentino declined to comment on the proceedings. Michael Sorrentino gained prominence through his participation in all six seasons of the MTV reality series "Jersey Shore," which aired from 2009 to 2012 and depicted the activities of a group residing on the New Jersey coastline.

As 400,000 people come to Las Vegas for EDC, Project Neon will begin closures. (FOX5)
Bonnie Hawkins has lived on Washington near Martin Luther King Boulevard, and said she's used to traffic, but not the amount she'll be seeing this weekend.
"Sometimes the traffic is so heavy I can't get out of my driveway," she said. "That's hard enough. Then having the Electric Daisy Carnival come, it is not going to be nice at all," she said exasperated.
Hawkins said living close to the Spaghetti Bowl, she's familiar with Project Neon, but this weekend, it'll be even worse. As 400,000 people come to Las Vegas for EDC, Project Neon will begin closures.
Beginning at 10:00 p.m. Friday, through Monday at 5:00 a.m., the US 95 will be closed in both directions where it connects to I-15. MLK will also be shut down.
"We could not avoid this," Tony Illia with Nevada Department of Transportation said. "We plan our construction years in advance."
That means people heading to EDC will have to potentially get off and take side streets through neighborhoods. NDOT said side streets nearby the Spaghetti Bowl will also be affected including Bonanza, Rancho, Eastern, Valley View and Decatur.
As bad as that traffic will be for people like Bonnie Hawkins, NDOT said it'll be nothing compared to when the festival wraps up.
"The big concern is Monday morning. When all that [EDC] traffic exits and mingles with the morning commute traffic," Illia said.
Bonnie Hawkins said she planned to avoid the added traffic as much as she can, and if she doesn't have to leave her house early morning or late at night, she won't.
"We have no choice but to deal with it."
Project Neon was 65 percent complete as of Monday and was scheduled to wrap up in summer 2019.
Copyright 2018 KVVU (KVVU Broadcasting Corporation). All rights reserved.
rewrite:
The convergence of the Electric Daisy Carnival (EDC), an event attracting approximately 400,000 attendees to Las Vegas, with planned closures for the Project Neon highway improvement initiative is anticipated to create significant traffic disruptions. Local resident Bonnie Hawkins, whose residence on Washington Avenue near Martin Luther King Boulevard is proximate to the Interstate 15/U.S. Highway 95 interchange known as the "Spaghetti Bowl," expressed concern regarding the compounded congestion. While accustomed to existing traffic volumes, Hawkins anticipates severe difficulties, stating, "Sometimes the traffic is so heavy I can't get out of my driveway. That's hard enough. Then having the Electric Daisy Carnival come, it is not going to be nice at all."

The Nevada Department of Transportation (NDOT) confirmed that the scheduled Project Neon closures cannot be postponed. "We could not avoid this," explained NDOT spokesman Tony Illia. "We plan our construction years in advance." The closures are set to commence at 10:00 p.m. on Friday and continue through 5:00 a.m. on Monday, involving a full shutdown of U.S. 95 in both directions at its connection with I-15, as well as the closure of Martin Luther King Boulevard. Consequently, festival traffic will be diverted onto local arterial streets, including Bonanza, Rancho, Eastern, Valley View, and Decatur, which are also expected to experience substantial impacts.

NDOT officials indicate that the most severe congestion is likely to occur post-festival. "The big concern is Monday morning, when all that [EDC] traffic exits and mingles with the morning commute traffic," Illia noted. In response to the anticipated gridlock, Hawkins plans to minimize travel, venturing out only if absolutely necessary. "We have no choice but to deal with it," she concluded. As of the report date, Project Neon was reported as 65 percent complete, with a projected completion date set for summer 2019.

SALEM, Ore. (AP) — Reindeer are supposed to pull Santa Claus' sleigh, but in Oregon recently, a red-suited man on a sled wound up pushing a deer.
The reverse-reality Christmas-season tale played out when a deer wandered onto a frozen golf course pond in Sunriver, Oregon, on Friday and then lost its footing.
Try as it might, it couldn't get all its legs underneath him. It skidded and slithered, and its legs buckled.
Along came firefighter Jeff "JJ" Johnston, astride a new ice-rescue sled that was as bright red as the suit he wore, and as the nose on Rudolph the reindeer, which guided Santa's sleigh one foggy Christmas Eve.
Benjamin O'Keefe, a captain in the fire department of the resort and residential community, had his camera rolling. His video has become a sensation, garnering millions of views and picked up by broadcasters in the United States and overseas.
The young deer's hind legs began pumping, but it couldn't get up on its front legs. It was on an icy treadmill, going nowhere.
Johnston got close, spoke calming words to the deer and — slipping a bit himself as a tried to gain traction — gently pushed it with the front of the sled to the edge of the pond. Even then, the deer needed some coaxing. It seemed to have enjoyed the slippery ride.
Johnston tapped it on the head with the back of his gloved hand, then scratched the top of its head and ears, like you'd pet a dog.
The deer tried to get onto the sled before it turned around. Pushed once more to the snowy ground, it gained solid footing and, with a wave from Johnston, scampered off, presumably to join its mates in some deer games.
"JJ was talking to it the whole time," said Tammie Waters, office manager for the Sunriver Fire Department. "The deer played along pretty good."
It was the inaugural rescue mission for the sled, which was purchased with a grant from Firehouse Subs, a sandwich restaurant chain, she said. She hopes it never happens, but when someone falls through the ice or is stuck on thin ice, the sled will be put to use.
"It was a great way to get training, and rescue a deer," Waters said.
rewrite:
A recent incident in Sunriver, Oregon, presented an inversion of traditional Christmas imagery: rather than a reindeer pulling a sleigh, a firefighter in a red suit pushed a stranded deer to safety using a bright red rescue sled. The event occurred on the afternoon of Friday, December 22, when a young deer ventured onto the frozen surface of a golf course pond, lost its footing, and became incapacitated. Despite repeated efforts, the animal could not regain a stable stance; its legs buckled and slid outward, leaving it effectively immobilized on the ice.

Firefighter Jeff “JJ” Johnston responded to the scene utilizing a newly acquired ice-rescue sled, notable for its vivid red coloration. The entire episode was recorded on video by Captain Benjamin O’Keefe of the Sunriver Fire Department. The footage has since achieved widespread circulation, accumulating millions of views and receiving coverage from various domestic and international media outlets.

In the recording, the deer’s hind legs are observed moving involuntarily, yet it remained unable to position its forelegs securely beneath its body, resulting in a futile scrambling motion. Johnston carefully approached the animal, offering calm verbal reassurance. After briefly struggling for traction on the ice himself, he gently used the front of the sled to guide the deer toward the pond’s edge. Even upon reaching solid ground, the deer required additional encouragement to stand. Johnston subsequently engaged in brief tactile reassurance, tapping and then gently scratching the animal’s head and ears with a gloved hand.

Following a momentary investigation of the sled, the deer was guided onto the snowy bank. Once on stable footing, it promptly departed the area. According to Tammie Waters, office manager for the Sunriver Fire Department, Johnston maintained a continuous, calming dialogue with the deer throughout the interaction, and the animal exhibited a cooperative demeanor.

The rescue served as the inaugural operational use of the specialized sled, which was procured through a grant from the Firehouse Subs restaurant chain. Waters noted that while the primary intended application of the equipment is for human ice-rescue scenarios, this event provided valuable practical training while simultaneously facilitating a successful animal rescue.

A derailed freight train is currently causing some problems on the railways in the East Midlands.
The train has derailed between Peterborough and Ely disrupting trains on the Liverpool Lime Street / Nottingham / Norwich route.
It is though the train derailed at around 2.30pm but no injuries are being reported
The line is currently closed between Peterborough and Ely.
East Midlands Trains are unable to run between Peterborough and Ely and a spokeman said this disruption will continue for the rest of the evening.
There is the potential that the disruption to services may last a couple of days.
A statement from East Midlands trains said:
"In order to get you to where you need to be we have arranged for the following alternative routes to be available to you.
"These routes remain the most comfortable and quickest journey options:
"You can travel on GTR Great Northern services via Liverpool Street to / from Norwich. Greater Anglia are running trains between Ely and Norwich in both directions which you can use your ticket on.
"You are also able to travel on Virgin Trains East Coast, Hull trains, via Kings Cross and Liverpool Street to go to / from Norwich.
"Cross Country are accepting East Midlands Trains customers on any reasonable route and Virgin Trains West Coast are accepting our tickets for customers travelling to / from Norwich to Liverpool Lime Street and the North West.
"We are running replacement buses between Peterborough and Ely in both directions.
"Advance purchase tickets may be used on other trains, than booked on the affected route.
"These arrangements will remain in place until the line re-opens and the train service recovers."
rewrite:
A freight train derailment is currently causing significant disruption to rail services in the East Midlands region. The incident occurred on the line between Peterborough and Ely at approximately 14:30, resulting in the closure of that section. No injuries have been reported. This closure is directly affecting services operating on the Liverpool Lime Street to Norwich route via Nottingham.

East Midlands Trains has confirmed that all services between Peterborough and Ely are suspended, with a company spokesperson indicating that this disruption will persist throughout the evening. Furthermore, there exists a possibility that service alterations may continue for several days.

In response, East Midlands Trains has issued a statement outlining comprehensive contingency arrangements for affected passengers. The company has established reciprocal ticket acceptance agreements with several other rail operators to facilitate alternative travel. Specifically, tickets are being accepted on GTR Great Northern services via London Liverpool Street to and from Norwich, and on Greater Anglia services between Ely and Norwich. Additionally, Virgin Trains East Coast and Hull Trains services via London Kings Cross and Liverpool Street are available for Norwich-bound passengers. CrossCountry is accepting passengers on any reasonable route, and Virgin Trains West Coast is accepting tickets for travel between Norwich, Liverpool Lime Street, and the Northwest.

To provide a direct connection, replacement bus services are operating in both directions between Peterborough and Ely. The company has also confirmed that advance purchase tickets for the affected route may be used on alternative services. These contingency measures will remain in effect until normal rail service is restored following the reopening of the line.

PERTH (miningweekly.com) – ASX-listed Emmerson Resources has struck a deal with Territory Resources to develop a Tennant Creek processing hub in the Northern Territory.
Emmerson has agreed to sell its Warrego Mill lease to Territory to construct and commission a central processing facility with a proposed capacity of 300 000 t/y that will be the hub for feed from Emmerson’s small mines, which would have priority over third party ores.
Advertisement
First gold production from the processing facility is targeted for late 2018, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals.
Territory will pay an initial A$100 000 deposit to Emmerson, with further payments subject to final negotiations and the transfer of liabilities.
Advertisement
Territory will also assess Emmerson’s small mines for future mining and processing on a profit share or royalty basis, with the company to enter into an earn-in and potential joint venture (JV) over Emmerson’s southern tenements, subject to the two companies reaching commercial agreements.
The southern tenements is the most gold endowed portion of the Tennant Creek mineral field, and contains the historical Nobles Nob and Juno deposits, which are owned by Territory, as well as gold tailings from these projects, which will provide a source of feed to the central processing facility.
Under the proposed earn-in and JV, Emmerson will conduct exploration aimed at making further discoveries or extensions to these historic mines.
Emmerson MD Rob Bills said on Thursday that the development of a modern, centralized processing facility was a major step forward in establishing an integrated exploration, mining and processing hub in the Tennant Creek mineral field.
“This is something Emmerson has been championing for some time as it has the potential to unlock stranded gold assets in the region and is consistent with our strategy of monetizing our smaller, high grade resources.”
Bills said that it would generate additional funding for Emmerson’s exploration programmes, which was aimed at discovering high-grade gold, copper and cobalt, similar to the Edna Beryl and Jasper Hills discoveries.
rewrite:
ASX-listed Emmerson Resources has entered into an agreement with Territory Resources for the establishment of a centralised processing hub within the Tennant Creek mineral field of Australia’s Northern Territory. Under the terms of the agreement, Emmerson will transfer its Warrego Mill lease to Territory, which will undertake the construction and commissioning of a processing facility. This facility is proposed with an annual capacity of 300,000 tonnes and is intended to serve as the primary hub for ore sourced from Emmerson’s portfolio of smaller mining operations. Feedstock from these Emmerson-owned mines will be granted priority access over third-party ores. The project targets initial gold production by late 2018, contingent upon securing all requisite regulatory approvals.

Financial considerations include an initial deposit of A$100,000 payable by Territory to Emmerson, with subsequent payments to be determined through final negotiations and the transfer of associated liabilities. Furthermore, Territory will evaluate Emmerson’s smaller mines for potential future mining and processing under profit-sharing or royalty-based arrangements. The agreement also provides for an earn-in and potential joint venture structure over Emmerson’s southern tenements, pending the finalisation of commercial terms between the two entities. These southern tenements represent the most gold-endowed segment of the Tennant Creek field, hosting the historical Nobles Nob and Juno deposits—assets owned by Territory—as well as gold-bearing tailings from these projects, which will constitute a supplementary feed source for the central facility. Within the proposed earn-in and joint venture framework, Emmerson would be responsible for conducting exploration programmes aimed at delineating new discoveries or extensions to these historic mineralised systems.

Emmerson Managing Director Rob Bills characterised the development of a modern, centralised processing facility as a significant advancement toward creating an integrated exploration, mining, and processing hub in the Tennant Creek region. He stated that this initiative, long advocated by Emmerson, holds potential to unlock stranded gold assets and aligns with the company’s strategic objective of monetising its smaller, high-grade resources. Bills further noted that the arrangement is expected to generate additional funding for Emmerson’s ongoing exploration programmes, which are focused on the discovery of high-grade gold, copper, and cobalt deposits analogous to previous discoveries such as Edna Beryl and Jasper Hills.

Parliament has approved the Customs Amendment Bill 2017 that will allow for the removal of import duty on vehicular spare parts.
The bill was passed after a protracted debate, with the minority insisting the bill is unconstitutional and a breach of the ECOWAS treaty.
They also questioned why government did not remove all duties on spare parts as promised in the 2017 budget statement.
Deputy Minority Leader James Avedzi said the move will only benefit spare part importers and not the ordinary Ghanaian.
“The government must ensure that you are reducing the duty on the parts. As the importers enjoy the reduction in duties they must reduce the prices of the parts but there is no mechanism to ensure that.
“They will go and get the reduction, enrich their pockets but they will not reduce the prices of the parts,” he said.
He added if the buyers will not benefit from the reduction, then there is no point in implementing the policy.
The protest by the Minority follows a major policy announcement by the government to reduce taxes and duties it described as nuisance.
As part of the 2017 budget statement that was read on the floor, the Finance Minister Ken Ofori Atta announced that import duties had been removed on spare parts a major policy decision which got spare parts dealers at Abossey Okai in Accra and other parts of the country jubilating.
Despite passing the budget, there was the need to amend the country’s laws to allow for the import duties on the spare parts to be removed.
With the law amended and the duties removed it is yet to be seen if the prices of spare parts will reduce.
rewrite:
The Parliament of Ghana has enacted the Customs Amendment Bill 2017, legislation that authorizes the elimination of import duties on automotive spare parts. The bill's passage followed an extended parliamentary debate, during which the Minority caucus maintained that the legislation is unconstitutional and constitutes a violation of the ECOWAS treaty. Furthermore, the Minority raised objections regarding the government's failure to comprehensively remove all duties on spare parts, as had been initially pledged in the 2017 budget statement. Deputy Minority Leader James Avedzi contended that the policy would primarily advantage importers of spare parts rather than the general populace. He argued that while importers would benefit from reduced duties, there exists no enforceable mechanism to guarantee that these savings are transferred to consumers through lower retail prices. Avedzi cautioned that importers might simply retain the financial benefit, thereby negating the intended economic relief for buyers and rendering the policy ineffective.

This parliamentary opposition emerged in response to a significant government policy initiative aimed at abolishing certain taxes and duties characterized as nuisance imposts. Within the 2017 budget statement delivered to Parliament, Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta had announced the removal of import duties on spare parts, a declaration that was met with approval by spare parts dealers in commercial districts such as Abossey Okai in Accra and elsewhere. However, despite the budget's approval, a specific legislative amendment was required to formally enact this fiscal change. Now that the legal amendment has been ratified and the duties officially removed, the critical question remains whether this regulatory adjustment will ultimately translate into reduced market prices for vehicular spare parts, thereby fulfilling the policy's stated objective of providing tangible economic benefits to consumers.

(Reuters) - An experimental Roche Holding AG drug, added to standard therapy, led to a far higher rate of remission and helped patients with an advanced, aggressive blood cancer live significantly longer than the standard treatment alone, according to data from a mid-stage trial released at a medical meeting on Sunday.
FILE PHOTO: The logo of Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche is seen outside their headquarters in Basel, Switzerland, January 30, 2014. REUTERS/Ruben Sprich/File Photo
In the trial of 80 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) whose disease had progressed despite several treatment regimens, the addition of Roche’s polatuzumab vedotin raised the complete response rate to 40 percent. That compared with 15 percent who achieved a complete response with just the standard drugs - Roche’s Rituxan and Teva’s Treanda chemotherapy. Complete response indicates no detectable signs of cancer.
There was a 65-percent reduction of risk of death with polatuzumab, researchers reported at the American Society of Hematology meeting in Atlanta. Median overall survival was 11.8 months for the polatuzumab combination versus 4.7 months for patients who received standard therapy.
“These results exceeded our expectations both for the complete response rate, because this is a heavily pre-treated population, and also that we were able to detect an overall survival benefit of this magnitude,” said Sandra Horning, Roche’s chief medical officer and head of product development.
Roche needs new cancer drugs as it begins to face competition from cheaper biosimilar versions of its longtime blockbuster oncology medicines Avastin and Herceptin.
Polatuzumab is a newer type of medicine called antibody drug conjugates designed to link therapeutic antibodies to cancer cell-killing agents while minimizing the effect on normal cells.
Polatuzumab, which targets a specific protein expressed in the majority of B-cell lymphomas, has received breakthrough therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration the priority medicines tag from European regulators, indicating that it is widely viewed as a potentially important advance.
It is also being tested in combination with other newer Roche medicines.
Average duration of response improved from 3.7 months with the standard therapy to 8.8 months with the three-drug combination in the Phase II study.
No unexpected safety signals were observed with the addition of polatuzumab, the company said.
DLBCL is a fast growing and the most common form of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma.
rewrite:
Data presented at a medical conference on Sunday indicate that the addition of an investigational agent from Roche Holding AG to standard therapy substantially increased remission rates and significantly extended survival for patients with an advanced and aggressive form of blood cancer, compared to standard treatment alone. These findings emerged from a mid-stage clinical trial.

The Phase II study enrolled 80 patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) whose disease had progressed following multiple prior treatment regimens. When Roche’s polatuzumab vedotin was combined with standard therapy—comprising Roche’s Rituxan (rituximab) and bendamustine chemotherapy—the complete response rate reached 40 percent. This contrasts with a 15 percent complete response rate observed in patients receiving only the standard two-drug regimen. A complete response denotes the absence of detectable cancer.

Researchers reported these results at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in Atlanta. The analysis further demonstrated a 65 percent reduction in the risk of death for the polatuzumab combination arm. Median overall survival was 11.8 months for patients receiving the three-drug combination, compared to 4.7 months for those on standard therapy alone.

Sandra Horning, M.D., Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development, stated, “These results exceeded our expectations, both in terms of the complete response rate—given this is a heavily pre-treated population—and in the magnitude of the overall survival benefit observed.”

Polatuzumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate, a class of therapeutics designed to deliver a cytotoxic agent selectively to cancer cells by linking it to a targeted antibody. It binds to a protein expressed on the surface of most B-cell lymphomas. The compound has received Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and a Priority Medicines (PRIME) designation from European regulators, reflecting its potential as a significant therapeutic advance.

The development of new oncology agents is strategically important for Roche, as it anticipates biosimilar competition for established blockbuster therapies such as Avastin and Herceptin. In this trial, the addition of polatuzumab also improved the median duration of response from 3.7 months to 8.8 months, without raising unexpected safety concerns. Further studies evaluating polatuzumab in combination with other novel Roche therapies are ongoing.

DLBCL is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma and is characterized by rapid progression.

Straight seam high-frequency erw steel pipe has been continuously improved due to advances in technology for more than ten years, so that its application range has been rapidly expanded. Its main advantages are:
a. It does not add any chemical components during the welding process, and its welding quality depends mainly on the quality of the base metal. In recent years, due to the continuous improvement of the quality of hot rolled coils, the quality of the welds has been improved in the pipe making process. Even if the quality of the welds is slightly insufficient, the quality of the entire steel pipe will not be affected.
b. In recent years, due to the advancement of automation technology, the main parameters of resistance welding can be optimized by computer control, so that the welding quality is greatly improved.
c. Has a small residual stress and a high strength.
d. High geometric accuracy, easy to install on site, butt welds and anti-corrosion construction.
e. Short weld bead, which means improved reliability.
f. It has a price advantage, and its price is much lower than that of straight seam double-sided submerged arc welded steel pipe. However, due to the lack of weld quality in straight seam high-frequency electric resistance welded steel pipes, external anti-corrosion treatment is required.
In recent years, straight seam high-frequency electric resistance welded steel pipes have developed rapidly in China, and can produce DN400 steel pipes.
rewrite:
Over the past decade, technological advancements have driven the continuous improvement of straight-seam high-frequency electric resistance welded (HFW) steel pipe, leading to a significant expansion of its application scope. The principal advantages of this product are as follows:

a. The welding process does not introduce additional chemical elements; weld quality is primarily dependent on the base metal. Recent enhancements in hot-rolled coil quality have consequently elevated weld integrity during pipe manufacturing. Even in instances of marginally insufficient weld quality, the overall performance of the steel pipe remains uncompromised.

b. Progress in automation technology now enables computer-controlled optimization of key resistance welding parameters, resulting in substantially improved welding quality.

c. The pipes exhibit low residual stress and high mechanical strength.

d. They offer high geometric accuracy, facilitating on-site installation, field butt-welding, and anti-corrosion construction.

e. The weld bead is short, which enhances structural reliability.

f. HFW pipe holds a considerable price advantage, being significantly less costly than straight-seam double-sided submerged arc welded (SAW) steel pipe. However, due to inherent limitations in weld quality, external anti-corrosion treatment is typically required.

In recent years, the production of straight-seam HFW steel pipe has advanced rapidly within China, with manufacturing capabilities now extending to pipes of DN400 diameter.

For seven months, writers J.H. Williams and Wendy Wright-Williams worked to piece together a 331-page collection of art work that explores the Las Vegas mass shooting and the days following. (Abby Theodros/FOX5)
For seven months, writers J.H. Williams and Wendy Wright-Williams worked to piece together a 331-page collection of art work that explores the Las Vegas mass shooting and the days following.
“We’ve been working on this since a week after the incident took place,” curator and contributor J.H. Williams said.
Williams, a professional comics artist, is known for his work on titles including Batwoman and The Sandman: Overture.
His latest project is a collaboration with his wife Wendy. “It was a unique thing we could do that we knew how to do and bring help to those impacted,” Williams said.
The comic anthology is titled “Where We Live,” and features more than 70 stories, illustrations, poems, and essays. More than 150 artists contributed, according to Williams.
The collection includes fictional and real-life experiences. Some of the stories were told by 1 October survivors.
“The main goal is to raise as much money as we can but we’re hoping to do it in a meaningful way,” Wendy said.
The book, which hits shelves Wednesday, cost $20. The proceeds will go to the non-profit Route 91 Strong. The organization is dedicated to raising awareness and funds for survivors and victims of gun violence.
Wendy said she hopes the book also sparks dialogue about the frequency in which mass shootings in America occur.
“The tragedy took place in our back yard and this is where we live, I want people to think about that,” Wendy said. “What if this was where you lived?”
Williams said the book is available on Amazon and in Valley book stores.
The couple will host a book signing on Saturday at Alternate Reality Comics. Sixteen local contributors and creators are set to attend the event.
Copyright 2018 KVVU (KVVU Broadcasting Corporation). All rights reserved.
rewrite:
Over a period of seven months, writers J.H. Williams and Wendy Wright-Williams compiled a 331-page anthology of artwork examining the 2017 Las Vegas mass shooting and its immediate aftermath. J.H. Williams, who served as both a curator and contributor to the project, stated, “We’ve been working on this since a week after the incident took place.” Williams is a professional comics artist, recognized for his work on publications such as *Batwoman* and *The Sandman: Overture*. This latest endeavor represents a collaboration with his wife, Wendy Wright-Williams. Williams explained their motivation, noting, “It was a unique thing we could do that we knew how to do and bring help to those impacted.”

The resulting comic anthology, entitled *Where We Live*, comprises more than seventy individual pieces, including stories, illustrations, poems, and essays. According to Williams, the volume features contributions from over 150 artists. The collection integrates both fictional narratives and documented real-life experiences, with several accounts provided directly by survivors of the October 1st shooting. Wendy Wright-Williams emphasized the project’s dual objectives: “The main goal is to raise as much money as we can but we’re hoping to do it in a meaningful way.”

Priced at twenty dollars and released on a Wednesday, the book directs all proceeds to the nonprofit organization Route 91 Strong, which is dedicated to raising awareness and generating funds for survivors and victims of gun violence. Wendy Wright-Williams further expressed a hope that the publication would stimulate discourse concerning the prevalence of mass shootings in the United States. She remarked, “The tragedy took place in our back yard and this is where we live; I want people to think about that. What if this was where you lived?”

The anthology is available for purchase through Amazon and at various bookstores within the Las Vegas Valley. The couple scheduled a book signing event for that Saturday at Alternate Reality Comics, which was to be attended by sixteen local contributors and creators associated with the project.

THE IRISH PENAL Reform Trust has called for solitary confinement and restricted regimes to be banned in prison.
A new report from the IPRT calls for an end to these practices, which it says can have a severe negative effect on prisoners’ mental health.
Solitary confinement involves a prisoner being kept in their cell without proper human contact for more than 22 hours a day.
Restricted regimes are the same practice, but for in the region of 19 hours a day.
Commenting on the launch of the report today, executive director of the IPRT Deirdre Malone said that the group wanted to ensure a minimum out-of-cell time of eight hours per day.
“We recognise the challenge for any prison service in balancing prisoner safety on the one hand, while at the same time providing prisoners with a reasonable and humane regime,” said Malone.
She said that prisoners may be placed on ‘protection’ in lock up after having asked for it.
“Yet those regimes are significantly impoverished as prisoners face restricted access to education, physical activities and fresh air; limitations on family visits and phone contact; and difficulties in accessing health and addiction support.
Such restrictions can have a serious negative impact on effective reintegration upon release.
The report is based on a major evidence-based research project led by the IPRT, and contains 25 key recommendations.
These include:
The placement in solitary confinement of adults with mental health difficulties or mental or physical disabilities should be prohibited
Where a prisoner requests to be kept on protection for an extended period, this should be kept under constant review
The Irish Prison Service should research and develop a range of initiatives to address violence in prisons
“It is our view that Ireland should be leading by example on this issue and set a high bar regarding the protection of human rights, especially for people in some of the most vulnerable positions – those who are detained,” said Malone.
rewrite:
The Irish Penal Reform Trust (IPRT) has issued a call for the prohibition of solitary confinement and restricted regimes within the prison system. A newly published report from the organisation advocates for the cessation of these practices, citing their potential to inflict severe detrimental effects on the psychological well-being of incarcerated individuals. Solitary confinement is defined as the isolation of a prisoner in a cell with minimal meaningful human contact for periods exceeding 22 hours per day. Restricted regimes constitute a comparable practice, typically involving confinement for approximately 19 hours daily.

Upon the report’s launch, IPRT Executive Director Deirdre Malone articulated the organisation’s objective to establish a statutory minimum of eight hours daily out-of-cell time for all prisoners. “We acknowledge the inherent challenge for any prison service in balancing institutional safety with the provision of a reasonable and humane daily regime,” stated Malone. She noted that prisoners may voluntarily request placement on ‘protection’ status, resulting in such lockdowns. “However, these regimes are profoundly impoverished, as individuals experience severely restricted access to education, physical exercise, and outdoor space; limitations on familial visits and telephone communication; and barriers to obtaining healthcare and addiction support services. Such conditions can substantially undermine prospects for effective reintegration post-release.”

The report is the product of a substantial evidence-based research initiative led by the IPRT and presents twenty-five principal recommendations. Key proposals include: the explicit prohibition of placing adults with mental health difficulties or mental or physical disabilities into solitary confinement; the implementation of constant, regular review for any prisoner who voluntarily requests an extended period on protective lockdown; and a mandate for the Irish Prison Service to research and develop a comprehensive suite of initiatives aimed at addressing violence within prisons.

Malone concluded, “It is our firm position that Ireland should assume a leadership role on this issue, establishing a high standard for the protection of human rights. This is particularly imperative for those in highly vulnerable circumstances, including individuals who are detained.”

PARIS (Reuters) - Holders France ran into a spot of bother as they split the opening day’s singles matches to finish locked at 1-1 with Netherlands in the first round of their Davis Cup World Group tie after being hit by injuries on Friday.
French number one Jo-Wilfried Tsonga had been ruled out of the tie with a knee problem and Lucas Pouille, who was scheduled to play the first singles rubber, pulled out injured on Friday.
That meant world number 25 Adrian Mannarino had to step in at the 11th hour and he ended up being outclassed 7-6(4) 6-3 6-3 by world number 369 Thiemo De Bakker.
Richard Gasquet drew France level with a 6-4 7-6(3) 3-6 7-5 win against Robin Haase.
Pouille, who gave France the winning point against Belgium in the 2017 final last November, pulled out suffering from a stiff neck.
“Gasquet was solid. He went for the points, especially near the end of the game. It’s a good sign for the team,” said France captain Yannick Noah.
Tennis - Davis Cup - First Round - France vs Netherlands - Halle Olympique, Albertville, France - February 2, 2018 Netherlands' Thiemo de Bakker with Adrian Mannarino of France after winning their match REUTERS/Emmanuel Foudrot
Noah said he was not sure Pouille would be able to play on Sunday.
“I hope he can play but the medical staff will need to work miracles,” added Noah.
Slideshow (5 Images)
Belgium got off to a commanding start in Liege against Hungary as Ruben Bemelmans and David Goffin won the opening singles. Switzerland, without 20-times grand slam champion Roger Federer and Stanislas Wawrinka, were 2-0 down against Kazakhstan in Astana.
Britain, without the services of Andy Murray who led them to the title in 2015, were surprisingly tied at 1-1 with Spain. World number 114 Cameron Norrie upset Roberto Bautista Agut, 23rd in the ATP rankings, in a five-set thriller.
Serbia were on the brink of being eliminated after falling 2-0 behind against the United States. Sam Querrey and John Isner won their singles against Laslo Djere and Dusan Lajovic respectively.
Alexander Zverev needed five sets to tame unheralded Alex de Minaur to give Germany 1-0 lead against Australia before Nick Kyrgios overwhelmed Jan-Lennard Struff in straight sets to level the tie in Brisbane.
rewrite:
PARIS (Reuters) – The French Davis Cup team, defending the title it secured in 2017, encountered significant adversity on the opening day of its World Group first-round tie against the Netherlands on Friday, ultimately concluding the singles matches with a 1-1 draw after being hampered by injuries. The squad’s preparations were disrupted by the absence of its top-ranked player, Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who was ruled out due to a knee injury. Further complication arose when Lucas Pouille, initially designated for the first singles match, withdrew on the day of competition citing a stiff neck.

This last-minute alteration necessitated the inclusion of world number 25 Adrian Mannarino. Mannarino, however, was defeated in straight sets, 7-6(4), 6-3, 6-3, by the Netherlands’ Thiemo de Bakker, who is ranked 369th globally. France subsequently restored parity through Richard Gasquet, who secured a four-set victory over Robin Haase with a scoreline of 6-4, 7-6(3), 3-6, 7-5. French captain Yannick Noah praised Gasquet’s performance, noting, “Gasquet was solid. He went for the points, especially near the end of the game. It’s a good sign for the team.” Regarding Pouille’s availability for the remainder of the tie, Noah expressed uncertainty, stating, “I hope he can play but the medical staff will need to work miracles.”

Concurrent Davis Cup matches elsewhere produced varied results. In Liege, Belgium established a commanding position against Hungary, with Ruben Bemelmans and David Goffin winning their opening singles matches. Conversely, Switzerland, competing without its leading players Roger Federer and Stanislas Wawrinka, fell to a 2-0 deficit against Kazakhstan in Astana. The British team, absent 2015 title-winning captain Andy Murray, achieved a surprising 1-1 standoff with Spain in Marbella, following an upset victory by world number 114 Cameron Norrie over 23rd-ranked Roberto Bautista Agut in a five-set encounter.

Serbia faced potential elimination after losing both of its opening singles matches to the United States, with Sam Querrey and John Isner defeating Laslo Djere and Dusan Lajovic, respectively. In Brisbane, the tie between Germany and Australia was leveled at 1-1. Alexander Zverev required five sets to overcome Alex de Minaur, granting Germany an initial lead, which was promptly negated by Nick Kyrgios’s straight-sets victory over Jan-Lennard Struff.

LOS ANGELES — Tobias Harris scored 24 points in his Clippers debut, leading Los Angeles to a 113-103 victory over the Chicago Bulls on Saturday.
Danilo Gallinari also had 24 points, Lou Williams added 21 points and six assists, and Montrezl Harrell scored 14 to help the Clippers win for the third time in four games.
Zach LaVine lhad 21 points and nine rebounds to led six Bulls players scoring in double figures in their sixth straight loss.
Chicago missed its first seven field goals of the game and finished shooting 36.1 per cent.
Harris, Avery Bradley and Boban Marjanovic came to the Clippers on Monday in the trade that sent Blake Griffin to Detroit.
Center DeAndre Jordan, also rumoured to be in trade conversations, led the Clippers with 16 rebounds but scored only three points on 1-for-6 shooting.
The Bulls never led, but remained within striking distance throughout most of the game. The Clippers outscored Chicago in the paint, 52-36.
TIP-INS
Bulls: Coach Fred Hoiberg said newly acquired Omer Asik, Jameer Nelson and Tony Allen did not suit up because they had yet to take their physicals. ... Sent an assistant trainer to Chicago to check on the progress of G Kris Dunn (concussion). Said Hoiberg: "He's still on the concussion protocol. As he continues to feel better, hopefully he can cross off the steps to get out of it. Then he'll need a couple of practices before he's cleared." ... F Lauri Markkanen remained home for the birth of his first child but Hoiberg said he may rejoin the team for their next game in Sacramento.
Clippers: C Doc Rivers said G Austin Rivers (right ankle) should return when the team starts to play seven consecutive road games on Feb. 9. He's missed 17 games with what was originally called a strained Achilles.

In a contest held in Los Angeles on Saturday, the Clippers secured a 113-103 victory over the Chicago Bulls. Tobias Harris, making his debut for the Clippers following a trade acquisition from Detroit earlier in the week, contributed a team-high 24 points. He was joined in scoring by Danilo Gallinari, who also tallied 24 points, while Lou Williams added 21 points and six assists. Montrezl Harrell provided 14 points off the bench, supporting the Clippers in achieving their third win across four games.

For the Bulls, Zach LaVine recorded 21 points and nine rebounds, leading six Chicago players who scored in double figures. Despite this balanced offensive effort, the team suffered its sixth consecutive defeat. Chicago’s shooting proved inefficient, as the team missed its initial seven field goal attempts and concluded the game with a 36.1 percent success rate from the field. Although remaining competitively engaged for much of the contest, the Bulls never held a lead and were outscored by the Clippers in the paint, 52-36.

Notable performances included Clippers center DeAndre Jordan, who gathered a game-high 16 rebounds amidst ongoing trade speculation, though he scored only three points. Regarding team personnel, Bulls coach Fred Hoiberg indicated that recently acquired players Omer Asik, Jameer Nelson, and Tony Allen were inactive pending physical examinations. He also noted that guard Kris Dunn remains in the concussion protocol, while forward Lauri Markkanen was absent for the birth of his child but may rejoin the team subsequently. For the Clippers, coach Doc Rivers stated that guard Austin Rivers, having missed 17 games with a right ankle injury, is anticipated to return upon the commencement of a seven-game road trip on February 9.
