DURHAM, N.C. (WNCN) — The families of two people killed in the September crash of a Duke Life Flight helicopter in rural northeastern North Carolina have filed a lawsuit against the makers of the helicopter and its engines and the estate of the pilot.
The lawsuit contends that a combination of pilot error and a known problem with the engines contributed to the crash, which killed all four people aboard the flight.
The families of Mary Susan White Bartlett, the patient on the flight, and Kristopher Harrison, a flight nurse, are the plaintiffs.
The pilot, Jeffrey Burke, died in the crash, as did flight nurse Crystal Sollinger, whose family and estate are not involved in the lawsuit.
“All evidence points to a blocked engine drain line,” said the plaintiff’s attorney, Gary C. Robb, in a news release.
Robb is a Missouri-based expert in helicopter-related litigation.
Robb said the plaintiffs believe the blocked line led to an engine fire, and then engine shutdown. He said a crash in January 2017 first brought the engine problem to regulatory and company officials’ attention.
The FAA released a bulletin describing the engine problem last month, specifically referencing both the South Dakota crash and the North Carolina crash.
“This was absolutely a preventable crash,” Robb said in the news release.
The suit also contends that Burke, the pilot, should have continued forward flight and executed an autorotation landing maneuver.
A National Transportation Safety Board preliminary report days after the Sept. 8 crash said witnesses saw dark smoke streaming from the helicopter before it crashed in a field.
The French engine maker Safran, and the European helicopter company, Airbus Helicopter, as well as their American distributors, are named in the suit. None of them immediately responded to requests for comment.
rewrite:
A lawsuit has been filed by the families of two individuals who perished in the September crash of a Duke Life Flight helicopter in rural northeastern North Carolina. The defendants named in the litigation include the manufacturers of the helicopter and its engines, as well as the estate of the deceased pilot. The suit alleges that the fatal accident, which resulted in the deaths of all four persons aboard, was caused by a confluence of pilot error and a previously identified engine defect.

The plaintiffs are the families of Mary Susan White Bartlett, a patient being transported, and flight nurse Kristopher Harrison. The pilot, Jeffrey Burke, and a second flight nurse, Crystal Sollinger, also died in the crash; their respective families and estates are not party to this legal action.

According to the plaintiffs' legal representative, Gary C. Robb—a Missouri-based attorney specializing in aviation litigation—available evidence indicates a blocked engine drain line precipitated the event. Robb asserts this blockage led to an engine fire and subsequent shutdown. He further stated that this specific engine issue was initially brought to the attention of both regulatory authorities and the involved companies following a separate crash in January 2017. The Federal Aviation Administration subsequently issued a bulletin last month detailing the engine problem, explicitly referencing both the South Dakota and North Carolina incidents. Robb characterized the crash as "absolutely preventable."

The complaint also contends that Pilot Burke failed to execute appropriate emergency procedures, specifically alleging he should have maintained forward flight and initiated an autorotation landing maneuver. This account is partially corroborated by a preliminary report from the National Transportation Safety Board, which cited witness observations of dark smoke emanating from the aircraft prior to its impact in a field.

The defendants enumerated in the suit are the French engine manufacturer Safran, the European helicopter manufacturer Airbus Helicopter, and their American distributors. None of these entities provided an immediate response to requests for comment.

TALLAHASSEE (CBSMiami/AP) — The State of Florida is making a change on a subject that has been a hot topic of late.
Florida’s governor has ordered a statue of a Confederate general at the U.S. Capitol to be removed and replaced with one of an African-American woman.
Gov. Rick Scott signed the bill (SB 472) making that step official Monday.
The bill removes a statue of Confederate Gen. Edmund Kirby Smith and replaces it with a statue of Mary McLeod Bethune.
She founded a school that would eventually become historically black Bethune-Cookman University in Daytona Beach, Florida.
Bethune’s statue would be the first African-American woman in Statuary Hall.
Congress allows each state two statues in Statuary Hall.
Florida’s other one is of John Gorrie, whose inventions led to modern-day air conditioning.
(© Copyright 2018 CBS Broadcasting Inc. All Rights Reserved. The Associated Press contributed to this report.)
rewrite: On Monday, Governor Rick Scott of Florida formally enacted legislation (SB 472) mandating the replacement of the state’s contribution to the National Statuary Hall Collection in the U.S. Capitol. The statute orders the removal of the likeness of Confederate General Edmund Kirby Smith. It will be succeeded by a statue honoring the educator and activist Mary McLeod Bethune, founder of the institution that evolved into Bethune-Cookman University in Daytona Beach. Upon its installation, this tribute will represent the first statue of an African-American woman in Statuary Hall. Each state is permitted two statues in the hall; Florida’s other honoree is John Gorrie, recognized for his pioneering work in refrigeration and air conditioning. This legislative action addresses ongoing national discourse regarding historical commemoration.

LEXINGTON, Ky. (AP) - An explosion damaged a UPS freight hub Wednesday morning in Kentucky's second-largest city, sending multiple people to the hospital in what fire officials described as an accidental blast.
Lexington Battalion Chief Jason Wells said a truck and trailer with an acetylene tank exploded in the building, news outlets reported. The cause of the explosion was not yet known, but the blast wasn't suspicious.
"Nothing leads us to believe this is anything other than an accidental explosion," the fire department tweeted.
The building on Blue Sky Parkway sustained significant damage, which was visible in the back of the building. The facility had been evacuated and everyone was accounted for, fire officials said.
Eight people received medical attention following the blast, Wells said. Two people taken to the hospital suffered from burns and possible concussions, and six others in the vicinity of the explosion were taken to the hospital for observation as a precaution, Wells said. Fire officials initially said about a dozen people received medical attention.
Lexington fire department spokeswoman Jessica Bowman said the building's structural stability was being checked as part of an effort to determine what happened and how.
Businesses near the site reported a loud explosion shortly before 8 a.m. EDT. Emergency crews rushed to the scene and restricted access to the area.
The blast was felt inside other buildings.
rewrite:
On the morning of Wednesday, an accidental explosion occurred at a United Parcel Service freight facility in Lexington, Kentucky, resulting in structural damage and multiple hospitalizations. According to Lexington Battalion Chief Jason Wells, as reported by news outlets, the detonation originated from a truck and trailer containing an acetylene tank within the building. The precise cause remains undetermined, though authorities have stated the incident is not considered suspicious. The Lexington Fire Department publicly affirmed via social media that all available evidence indicates an accidental event.

The facility, located on Blue Sky Parkway, sustained considerable damage, particularly to its rear section. All personnel were successfully evacuated and accounted for. Medical attention was provided to eight individuals following the blast. Two of those transported to a hospital were treated for burns and potential concussions, while six others in the vicinity were taken for precautionary observation. Initial estimates from fire officials had indicated approximately a dozen individuals required medical evaluation. Jessica Bowman, a spokeswoman for the Lexington Fire Department, noted that assessments of the building's structural integrity are underway as part of the ongoing investigation.

Nearby businesses reported a loud explosion shortly before 8:00 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time. Emergency responders promptly arrived at the scene and secured the area. The force of the blast was perceptible within adjacent structures.

Good Governance: S’African Academy To Honour 8 Nigerian Govs
BY BODE GBADEBO, Abuja
A leadership development organisation based in Pretoria, Leadership Academy South Africa (LASA) has nominated eight deserving state governors in Nigeria for its maiden Leadership Awards for Excellence (LAE) slated for Thursday, July 13, 2017.
According to a press release by the Nigerian partners of the event, Abuja-based Bulfol Services Venture and signed by its managing director, Mr. Segun Abdulsalam, the award ceremony, which will take place at the Heartfelt Arena in Pretoria, South Africa, is conceptualised “to recognise and reward leaders in government and business, who have distinguished themselves in different areas of good governance and leadership.”
The statement further named the awardees to include the chairman of the Nigerian Governors Forum (NGF) and Zamfara state governor, Alh. Abdulaziz Yari (Good Leadership); Ogun state governor, Senator Ibikunle Amosun (Infrastructural Development and Housing); and Abia state governor, Okezie Ikpeazu (Urban Renewal and Commerce).
Others are Kebbi state governor, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu (Agriculture and Food Security); Akwa Ibom state governor, Dr. Udom Emmanuel (Good Governance); Adamawa state governor, Senator Jubrilla Bindow (Road Infrastructure and Poverty Reduction); Plateau state governor, Rt. Hon. Simon Lalong (Peace Ambassador); and Kogi state governor, Alh. Yahaya Bello (Security).
The organisers also said the international event will be televised live on the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) television station for worldwide audience even as they congratulate the governor-awardees for delivering on their respective mandates in the different specified areas of development amid dwindling revenues accruing to their states.

YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (WYTV) –
You can enjoy jelly beans that taste like banana, cherries and lemons but also black pepper, earwax, worms and worse….rotten egg, skunk spray and canned dog food.
How can companies such as Jelly Belly do that?
Jelly Belly uses a machine called a gas chromatograph.
Let’s say you want a rotten egg tatse…the scientists put a rotten egg into the machine and the machine disolves it or heats it and analyzes the chemical makeup of the gas that comes out.
It can then create a tastate modeled on that gas.
The company decideda few years ago to add a new bean called Stinky Socks…so one scientist aged his own socks in a sealed plastic bag for a couple of weeks, put the socks in the gas chromatograph, which came up with the socks’ flavor makeup.
Once a new jelly bean flavor is ready, it goes through taste testing trials to get the flavor just right, and adjustments are made based on that feedback.
The vomit tasting bean actually came from spoiled cheese on an old pizza.
Did you miss an episode of Daybreak or want to re-visit a previous ‘Nugget’? View previous ‘Nugget of Knowledge’ entries on WYTV.com .
If you have an idea for a ‘Nugget of Knowledge,’ send your idea in an email to Len.Rome@wytv.com .
rewrite:
The process by which companies such as Jelly Belly develop unconventional jelly bean flavors, ranging from banana and cherry to black pepper, earwax, and even rotten egg or skunk spray, relies on sophisticated analytical technology. A key instrument in this flavor creation is the gas chromatograph. To replicate a specific aroma, such as that of a rotten egg, scientists introduce the source material into the device. The machine then heats or dissolves the sample, analyzing the chemical composition of the resulting vapors. This data allows for the synthesis of a flavor compound modeled on that gaseous profile.

For instance, in developing a "Stinky Socks" flavor, a scientist aged socks within a sealed plastic bag for several weeks before subjecting them to gas chromatograph analysis to derive their distinct flavor signature. Similarly, the vomit-flavored bean originated from the analysis of spoiled cheese on discarded pizza. Once a prototype flavor is formulated, it undergoes rigorous sensory evaluation trials. Feedback from these tastings informs precise adjustments to achieve the desired flavor profile. This methodical approach enables the accurate simulation of a vast array of unusual tastes.

ZAGREB, Croatia (AP) — Hundreds of people, including two government ministers, attended a commemoration ceremony Monday to honor a Croatian general who died after apparently taking poison at a United Nations tribunal that confirmed his war crimes conviction.
Bused in from other Croatian towns and from Bosnia, admirers of Slobodan Praljak filled the main concert hall in Zagreb, the capital. The gathering, organized by a Croatian generals' association, displayed the resurging nationalism in the European Union's newest member state.
Miroslav Tudjman, the son of Croatia's late president Franjo Tudjman, denounced the tribunal in The Hague, Netherlands. Tudjman described Praljak as a "big man no one can match."
"Slobodan Praljak wouldn't live as a war criminal for a minute because he wasn't one," Tudjman told a clapping crowd. "His conviction is an insult for justice."
Advertisement
Praljak gulped what he said was poison after judges at the Yugoslav war crimes court confirmed his 20-year sentence in an appeals hearing last month. Despite medical attention, he died soon after.
Many in Croatia consider Praljak a hero despite his conviction for war crimes — including murder, persecution and inhumane treatment — against Muslims in Bosnia during the 1992-95 war. For days, Praljak's photo was on display at Zagreb's main square where people lit candles.
Dutch authorities and the court have opened investigations into how Praljak, who had been in custody, obtained the substance.
Croatian officials have criticized the ruling against Praljak and five other former Bosnian Croat officials because it linked Croatia's wartime leadership with Bosnian Croat efforts to carve out a mini-state in Bosnia.
Tudjman, whose late father was named in the verdict as having been involved in the plot, described the ruling as "unjust" and "staged" as a result of anti-Croat bias by the Hague court.
Croatia has faced criticism internationally and from liberals at home for its heated reaction to The Hague ruling and Praljak's death, amid the surge in right-wing sentiments, including death threats against some liberal politicians.
Praljak was reportedly cremated last week in a private ceremony.
rewrite:
A commemoration ceremony was held in Zagreb, Croatia, on Monday, attended by several hundred individuals, including two state ministers, to honor the late Croatian General Slobodan Praljak. Praljak died last month after ingesting a substance he identified as poison immediately following the confirmation of his war crimes conviction by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague. The event, organized by an association of Croatian generals and drawing attendees bused in from various Croatian towns and Bosnia, filled the capital’s main concert hall, illustrating a resurgence of nationalist sentiment within this newest European Union member state.

During the ceremony, Miroslav Tudjman, son of Croatia’s late President Franjo Tudjman, publicly denounced the ICTY, characterizing its proceedings as unjust and asserting that Praljak was “a big man no one can match.” Addressing an applauding audience, Tudjman stated, “Slobodan Praljak wouldn't live as a war criminal for a minute because he wasn't one,” and labeled the conviction “an insult for justice.” Praljak’s death occurred shortly after the appellate hearing, despite receiving prompt medical attention.

Notwithstanding his conviction for war crimes—including murder, persecution, and inhumane treatment against Bosnian Muslims during the 1992-95 conflict—many within Croatia regard Praljak as a national hero. In the days following his death, his photograph was displayed in Zagreb’s central square, accompanied by public candlelight vigils. Concurrently, Dutch authorities and the ICTY have initiated investigations into how Praljak, while in custody, obtained the lethal substance.

The Croatian government has criticized the ICTY’s appellate verdict, which upheld sentences against Praljak and five other former Bosnian Croat officials. Officials object particularly to the judgment’s linkage of Croatia’s wartime leadership to efforts by Bosnian Croats to establish an autonomous entity in Bosnia. Miroslav Tudjman, whose late father was implicated in the verdict as participating in the conspiracy, described the ruling as “unjust” and “staged,” alleging systemic anti-Croat bias within the Tribunal.

Croatia’s vehement reaction to the verdict and Praljak’s death has drawn international criticism and censure from domestic liberal circles. This response occurs amidst a notable rise in right-wing sentiments within the country, which has included death threats directed at some liberal politicians. Praljak was reportedly cremated in a private ceremony last week.

MILAN Italian fashion house Roberto Cavalli said on Thursday direct sales had stabilised in the first months of the year thanks to its reorganisation efforts, after overall revenue plunged 13.6 percent annually in 2016.
The Florence-based group, popular with celebrities, reported net revenues of 155 million euros (131.71 million pounds) for last year and a loss before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of 26 million euros. Restructuring costs contributed to a net loss of 55 million euros.
But CEO Gian Giacomo Ferraris, who launched a deep overhaul of the group six months ago, including cutting almost a third of Cavalli's jobs, said in a statement direct sales were "stabilised, if not slightly growing in the first quarter of 2017."
The fashion label, which has been going through an overhaul since Italian private equity firm Clessidra bought it in April 2015, confirmed a return to profitability in 2018.
(Reporting by Giulia Segreti, editing by Valentina Za)
rewrite: The Italian fashion house Roberto Cavalli announced on Thursday that its direct sales have stabilized during the initial months of the current year, attributing this development to ongoing corporate reorganization. This follows a reported 13.6 percent annual decline in overall revenue for 2016. The Florence-based group, which is favored by numerous celebrities, disclosed net revenues of 155 million euros for the preceding year. It also recorded a loss before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation of 26 million euros, with restructuring costs contributing to a net loss totaling 55 million euros. Chief Executive Gian Giacomo Ferraris, who initiated a comprehensive restructuring six months ago involving a reduction of nearly one-third of the workforce, stated that direct sales in the first quarter of 2017 were "stabilised, if not slightly growing." The label, undergoing transformation since its acquisition by the Italian private equity firm Clessidra in April 2015, reaffirmed its objective of returning to profitability by 2018.

So the worst kept secret in the East Midlands has now been confirmed and Frank Lampard has been announced as the new manager of Derby County.
Some may be surprised at what route that the club has gone down. Lampard has achieved much in theme, both as a Chelsea legend and England International of some 106 caps, but he is a complete rookie in the management game.
Derby have tried many different approaches in addressing the management situation and all have fallen short in their aim of reaching the Premier League.
Lampard has ambitions to make it as a manager and this is a very big gig at which to start this period of his footballing career.
He will have to be shown patience and given time.
Those expecting instant success may have to reassess their hopes for the next season as Derby will have to make adjustments to their team budget after years of spending money by past bosses.
Perhaps with Lampard having gained much respect during his playing days, he will be able to pull off some good loan deals?
Whatever anyones thoughts are about this appointment, it will ensure that the club remain under the spotlight by the national media. He will be scrutinised heavily by the red tops.
Derby County fans will have to take the following into consideration too when they make their own minds up about him - Rookie boss, reduced budget, learning his trade.
We will need to get behind him from day one! Whoever is appointed it never satisfies everyone.
Welcome to Pride Park Frank Lampard, I hoe your stay is a long and successful one.
rewrite:
The long-anticipated appointment in the East Midlands has now been formally confirmed, with Frank Lampard assuming the role of manager at Derby County Football Club. This decision may elicit surprise regarding the strategic direction chosen by the club. While Lampard’s distinguished playing career is unquestionable, marked by legendary status at Chelsea and 106 international caps for England, he enters this position without prior managerial experience. Derby County has employed varied managerial strategies in recent years, yet each has ultimately fallen short of the overarching objective: promotion to the Premier League.

Lampard’s stated ambition to forge a successful managerial career begins with a significant challenge at this level. His tenure will necessitate patience and time, as institutional and fiscal realities impose constraints. Expectations of immediate success may require recalibration, particularly as the club adjusts to a more restrained budgetary framework following periods of considerable expenditure under previous regimes. It is plausible that Lampard’s considerable stature and networks within the game could facilitate advantageous loan arrangements for the squad.

Regardless of individual perspectives on this appointment, it guarantees sustained national media attention focused on the club, with Lampard’s performance subject to intense scrutiny. Supporters evaluating this development must consider several factors: the manager’s inexperience, a reduced operational budget, and the inherent process of acquiring managerial proficiency. Collective support from the outset is imperative, acknowledging that no appointment universally satisfies all constituencies. Frank Lampard is welcomed to Pride Park, with the hope that his tenure proves both enduring and successful.

But employing teachers is not one of Utah's strengths.
The state's school districts are currently facing a staffing shortage, with low wages and large class sizes — a product of worst-in-the-nation funding levels — combining to make Utah classroom jobs noncompetitive, and contributing to high turnover rates among school faculty.
That's why Bailey supports Our Schools Now, a proposed ballot initiative that seeks to lift the state's income tax rate from 5 percent to 5.875 percent.
If successful, Our Schools Now would generate roughly $750 million for the state's public education system, including $1.8 million for Corner Canyon High School.
The money, to be distributed on a per-student basis, would mean higher salaries, additional teaching positions, new classroom technology or any other item on the wish lists of administrators and policymakers.
"If we could have more teachers, then we could reduce the stress on the teachers already in the classroom," Bailey said. "There would be more job satisfaction and better retention."
The initiative, expected to reach voters in 2018, is not without its detractors.
Tax-wary advocacy groups bristle at writing schools a $750 million check, while Utah lawmakers object to circumventions of the legislative process.
Critics point to the hundreds of millions of dollars added to school budgets since the Great Recession, which led to incremental and disputed improvements in school performance.
Others, like Sutherland Institute education policy analyst Christine Cooke, cite Utah's above-average graduation rate and best-in-the-nation science scores as evidence that Utah schools are succeeding despite low funding levels.
"More money is not necessarily reform," said Cooke, also a former educator. "Real education reform requires innovations, new ideas, asking big, bold questions and opportunities for personalization."
Lawmakers, who deflated an elections-related ballot initiative in 2014 by passing a compromise bill, plan to hold several hearings on Our Schools Now.
The initiative's organizers, among the most notable and influential business leaders in the state, say they're willing to strike a deal with the Legislature. But they also believe the public is with them, and the initiative won't be satisfied or called off without a significant boost to school coffers.
"We are full steam ahead," said Education First co-chairman Bob Marquardt. "We've gotten quite a bit of attention since our announcement a month ago and a lot of interest."
rewrite:
Utah faces significant challenges in the recruitment and retention of qualified educators. The state’s public school districts are currently contending with a pronounced staffing shortage, a situation exacerbated by noncompetitive compensation structures and elevated student-to-teacher ratios. These conditions are direct consequences of Utah’s position as the state with the lowest per-pupil funding in the nation, which collectively renders teaching positions unattractive and contributes to high rates of faculty turnover. In response to this crisis, Bailey endorses the Our Schools Now ballot initiative, a measure proposing an increase in the state income tax rate from 5 percent to 5.875 percent.

If approved by voters, this initiative is projected to generate approximately $750 million in additional annual funding for public education statewide. For individual institutions such as Corner Canyon High School, this would translate to an estimated $1.8 million in new resources. Allocated on a per-student basis, these funds could be directed toward increasing educator salaries, creating new teaching positions, acquiring instructional technology, or addressing other priorities identified by school administrators and policymakers. Bailey argues that such investments would alleviate current systemic pressures, stating, "If we could have more teachers, then we could reduce the stress on the teachers already in the classroom. There would be more job satisfaction and better retention."

Scheduled for the 2018 ballot, the initiative has nevertheless attracted criticism. Fiscal conservative groups oppose the substantial financial commitment, while some state legislators object to the use of a ballot measure to circumvent the standard budgetary process. Critics also note that hundreds of millions of dollars have been added to education budgets since the Great Recession, resulting in only incremental and debated gains in student outcomes. Furthermore, analysts such as Christine Cooke of the Sutherland Institute contend that Utah’s educational system, evidenced by its above-average graduation rates and leading national science scores, is already performing effectively despite limited funding. Cooke, a former educator, emphasizes that "More money is not necessarily reform. Real education reform requires innovations, new ideas, asking big, bold questions and opportunities for personalization."

The state legislature, which previously neutralized a 2014 ballot initiative through a compromise bill, plans to hold multiple hearings on the proposal. The initiative’s organizers, a coalition of prominent Utah business leaders, have expressed a willingness to negotiate with lawmakers. However, they maintain strong public support and insist they will not withdraw the measure without securing a substantial and guaranteed increase in education funding. As Education First co-chairman Bob Marquardt affirmed, "We are full steam ahead. We've gotten quite a bit of attention since our announcement a month ago and a lot of interest."

Vienna, 23 April 2018
DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG is switching to the mid market segment with effect from today. The shares of the German property developer have been tradable on the exchange-regulated “Third Market” since 7 December 2017. With this upgrade, the company offers its investors a plus in information. By being included in the “mid market”, the company is contractually bound to comply with increased transparency, quality and publicity criteria. DWH Deutsche Werte Holding is supported by Capital Lounge GmbH as Capital Market Coach. As market maker, ICF BANK AG Wertpapierhandelsbank ensures sufficient liquidity in continuous trading between 9:00 and 17:30 hours.
This example shows how important the exchange-regulated “Third Market” is as a starting point for the first step on the Vienna Stock Exchange. An easily accessible stock exchange segment promotes the further development of companies on the domestic capital market. Only recently, the Ministry of Finance announced that the existing obstacles for domestic companies would be removed. The government plans to enable bearer shares of Austrian companies to be traded on the Third Market again. The Vienna Stock Exchange hopes for a rapid legal implementation and is already in the starting blocks with a new, attractive offer for companies. This means that Austrian companies will again be able to profit from an easy access to the stock exchange in the future.
rewrite:
Effective 23 April 2018, DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG has transitioned to the mid market segment of the Vienna Stock Exchange. The shares of this German property developer had been listed on the exchange-regulated Third Market since 7 December 2017. This segment upgrade entails enhanced informational provisions for investors. Specifically, inclusion in the mid market obligates the company contractually to adhere to elevated standards of transparency, quality, and public disclosure. In this process, DWH Deutsche Werte Holding is advised by Capital Lounge GmbH in the capacity of Capital Market Coach. Furthermore, ICF BANK AG Wertpapierhandelsbank acts as the designated market maker, thereby ensuring sufficient liquidity through continuous trading between the hours of 9:00 and 17:30.

This case underscores the significance of the exchange-regulated Third Market as an initial listing platform and a preparatory stage for companies entering the Vienna Stock Exchange. Such an accessible segment facilitates corporate development within the domestic capital market. This development aligns with recent policy announcements; the Austrian Ministry of Finance has declared its intention to eliminate existing barriers for domestic companies. Notably, the government plans to reinstate the eligibility of bearer shares from Austrian companies for trading on the Third Market. The Vienna Stock Exchange anticipates prompt legislative implementation and is prepared to launch a revised, attractive offering for companies. Consequently, Austrian firms are expected to regain the benefit of streamlined access to public equity markets in the foreseeable future.

TAMPA BAY, Fla. — A dog named ‘Scarface’ sent two people to the hospital after its owner tried to put a sweater on him, the Tampa Bay Times reported.
The incident occurred around 2:30 p.m. on Friday when 52-year-old Brenda Guerrero tried to put a sweater on the dog and it attacked her. Her husband, 46-year-old Ismael Guerrero, tried to pull the dog off of his wife and it turned and began attacking him.
Warning: Graphic video
Please enable Javascript to watch this video
That's when their 22-year-old son got a knife and began stabbing the pit bull in the head and neck, the newspaper reported.
All three were able to escape the house and leave the dog in the backyard.
"Officers responding said the dog was pretty aggressive," said Eddy Durkin with the Tampa Bay police, according to WTFS. "When they Tased the dog, the dog was still pulling away and was able to release the prongs from the Taser."
Officials said there were two children in the house when they entered, but they were uninjured.
Brenda and Ismael were taken to the hospital. Brenda's injuries are serious but not life-threatening.
rewrite:
According to a report by the Tampa Bay Times, an incident in Tampa Bay, Florida, resulted in two individuals being hospitalized following an attempted intervention by a dog's owner. On Friday at approximately 2:30 p.m., Brenda Guerrero, aged 52, was attacked by the pit bull, named 'Scarface,' while attempting to dress the animal in a sweater. Her spouse, 46-year-old Ismael Guerrero, intervened and was subsequently attacked by the dog as well. The couple's 22-year-old son then used a knife to stab the dog in the head and neck, enabling all three adults to exit the residence and confine the animal to the backyard.

Tampa Bay police officers, as cited by WTFS, described the dog as highly aggressive, noting that it resisted a Taser deployment by pulling the prongs free. Upon entering the home, officials confirmed the presence of two unharmed children. Both Brenda and Ismael Guerrero required hospital transport; Brenda sustained serious but non-life-threatening injuries.

Villagers have freed 15 riot police they were holding over a land dispute in the suburban district of Vietnam's capital and authorities were trying to persuade the villagers to free the 20 remaining police and local officials, state media said Tuesday.
The standoff began Saturday when police clashed with villagers who allege their land was illegally taken for sale by a military-run telecoms firm. Some villagers who were arrested have been released. The state-run online newspaper Vnexpress reported Tuesday that three of those being held had managed to escape.
The newspaper quoted Maj. Gen. Bach Thanh Dinh, deputy Hanoi police chief, as saying the release of the villagers was not a compromise with the instigators of the standoff who illegally held police and officials.
"We will handle everything in accordance with the law," he said "Those who intentionally instigated, illegally detained people will be dealt with seriously."
On Monday, Hanoi Mayor Nguyen Duc Chung talked via telephone with the villagers' representatives and pledged to have direct talks with them the next day, according to lawyer Tran Vu Hai who helped to arrange the talk. The lawyer posted the pledge on his Facebook page but said Tuesday that Chung disputed it, indicating the talks would not go ahead.
"It's his right," the lawyer said.
State-run Tuoi Tre newspaper cited the Hanoi Communist Party Organization's propaganda department as saying the land had been reserved to build a military airfield since 1980 and was recently given to military-run telecommunications company Viettel, the country's largest mobile phone operator.
Viettel is to build a large project which is of "special significance on defense and security of the military and the country," it said.
The paper said some villagers had illegally occupied some of the land given to Viettel to do their farming.
Land disputes are common in Vietnam, where residents often claim that their land was taken for infrastructure or other industrial or residential projects and they not properly compensated.
rewrite:
A confrontation between residents and authorities in a suburban district of Vietnam’s capital has resulted in the release of 15 detained riot police officers, though 20 other police and local officials remain in custody, according to state media reports from Tuesday. The standoff originated on Saturday following clashes between police and villagers who assert that their land was unlawfully appropriated for sale by a military-affiliated telecommunications corporation. While some arrested villagers have been released, the state-operated online publication Vnexpress noted on Tuesday that three of the individuals held by villagers had successfully escaped.

Major General Bach Thanh Dinh, Deputy Chief of the Hanoi Police, was quoted as stating that the release of the detained villagers did not constitute a compromise with those who instigated the standoff and illegally confined officials. “We will handle everything in accordance with the law,” he asserted. “Those who intentionally instigated [the conflict] and illegally detained people will be dealt with seriously.” In a related development, Hanoi Mayor Nguyen Duc Chung engaged in a telephone conversation with village representatives on Monday, facilitated by lawyer Tran Vu Hai. The mayor reportedly committed to holding direct discussions the following day, a pledge publicly shared on the lawyer’s Facebook page. However, on Tuesday, the attorney indicated that Mayor Chung had contested the account, suggesting the planned talks would not proceed. “It’s his right,” the lawyer remarked.

Official reporting from the state-run Tuoi Tre newspaper cited the Hanoi Communist Party Organization’s propaganda department, which clarified that the land in question had been designated for a military airfield since 1980 and was recently allocated to Viettel, a military-run telecommunications firm and the nation’s largest mobile operator. The publication stated that Viettel is to develop a major project possessing “special significance for the defense and security of the military and the country.” It further noted that some villagers had illegally occupied portions of the land assigned to Viettel for agricultural use.

Such land disputes occur frequently in Vietnam, where residents often allege that property has been seized for infrastructure, industrial, or residential developments without adequate compensation.

ERIN, Wisconsin | Steve Stricker didn’t get the automatic exemption he wanted. The Edgerton native had to play his way into the 117th U.S. Open. Playing in this year’s major at Erin Hills was paramount for Stricker. After all this is the first time in the 117 years of the U.S. Open it’s being playing in the state of Wisconsin. Stricker would like nothing more that to be near the top of the leader board during Sunday’s final round.
“It’s very exciting to be here,” said Stricker during Tuesday’s news conference. “I wasn’t sure if I was going to be here but I’m very excited and relieved. I worked hard to get here. Put a lot of extra effort in playing in different tournaments to get here so all in all it worked out. It should be a great event. I go into every tournament expecting to play well so this is really no different. I’m going in trying to compete best I can and hopefully get in contention. That’s my goal is to contend and see what happens.”

The 50-year old Stricker has played well lately. He won a 36-hole sectional qualifier in Memphis, Tennessee to make it into the U.S. Open field. He’s playing in his 20th U.S. Open. And the 12-time PGA Tour winner is certainly a crowd favorite. He received a loud ovation from the Erin Hills crowd during Tuesday’s practice rounds.
“It’s overwhelming at times the number of people that are coming up to me wishing me luck. I get a pretty nice round of applause just during the practice round so it was pretty cool!”

OAKLAND — For four straight years, the NBA Finals have featured the Warriors and the Cavaliers.
And Guillermo.
“Four years in a row,” confirmed the affable sidekick from Jimmy Kimmel Live!
Guillermo Rodriguez, 47, was back at Oracle Arena for NBA Finals media day on Wednesday, accompanied by a team of handlers, producers and cameramen, interviewing players and lending his quirky approach to the proceedings.
He showed up wearing a cast on his right arm, which he asked players to sign.
“Is it real?” a TV reporter asked him.
“Yes, it’s real. Touch it right there,” he suggested, before yelping, “Ow!”
The cast was real, the injury was not. In fact, Guillermo pulled the cast off and coaxed Warriors rookie forward Jordan Bell into sliding it on his right arm.
Bell, sensitive to causing panic about the state of his health, quickly yanked it off.
Guillermo was feeling good about his relationship with the players after securing an interview with LeBron James at the NBA All-Star Game.
“Everybody loves me,” he said. “LeBron loves me.”

MIAMI (CBSMiami) – Researchers are now testing Botox injections, typically for cosmetic use, to see if they can treat depression and social anxiety.
Army Veteran Vivian Cooke has long struggled with debilitating depression. She has tried alternative therapies and medication to cope with her symptoms.
“It wasn’t effective. Some side effects would be headaches or stomachache,” said patient Vivian Cooke.
Three years ago, she tried something different after hearing about a study testing Botox to treat depression
“We don’t believe it has anything to do with looks,” said Dr. Eric Finzi with the Chevy Chase Cosmetic Center.
Finzi said facial expressions are part of the circuit of the brain related to mood.
“Fear, anger, and sadness all go through this muscle so Botox basically inhibits the muscle and calms it down. So it becomes more difficult to feel those negative emotions.
The makers of Botox announced the final phase of testing for depression will begin. Dr. Finzi says previous studies show between 50 to 60 percent of patients benefit from the treatment.
“Our hope is, eventually, it will form a place as one of the tools to treat depression,” said Finzi.
The doctor is also studying whether Botox can treat social anxiety.
Vivian says she noticed a change in her depression almost immediately.
“I found, overall, my mood was better on a day to day basis. I had less problems with depression,” she said.
Even though the study Vivian took part in is over, she says she will continue to get the injections.
Botox is temporary and typically wears off after three months.
Researcher are also testing Botox to see if it can help patients with bipolar disorder.
rewrite:
Investigations are underway to assess the therapeutic potential of Botulinum Toxin Type A (Botox), commonly utilized for cosmetic purposes, in the treatment of major depressive disorder and social anxiety. This research is noted by sources including CBS Miami. A pertinent case is that of U.S. Army veteran Vivian Cooke, who has experienced protracted and debilitating depressive episodes. Cooke reports having pursued various pharmacological and alternative therapeutic interventions with limited efficacy and undesirable side effects, including headaches and gastrointestinal discomfort.

Approximately three years ago, Cooke enrolled in a clinical trial exploring Botox for depression. Dr. Eric Finzi of the Chevy Chase Cosmetic Center, a researcher involved, emphasizes that the proposed mechanism is neurological rather than aesthetic. He posits that facial musculature is integrated into the neural circuitry governing mood. Specifically, the corrugator supercilii muscle, involved in expressions of fear, anger, and sadness, is targeted. By inhibiting muscular activity via Botox, the afferent feedback signaling associated with negative emotions may be attenuated, thereby potentially reducing the subjective experience of those states.

The pharmaceutical manufacturer has announced the commencement of a final-phase trial for depression. Preliminary studies, according to Dr. Finzi, indicate a positive response rate of approximately 50 to 60 percent among participants. The objective is to establish Botox as a viable adjunctive tool within the broader therapeutic arsenal for depression. Concurrently, research is exploring its application for social anxiety disorder.

Patient-reported outcomes from the initial trial are promising. Cooke describes a rapid and sustained improvement in her daily mood and a significant reduction in depressive symptoms. Consequently, she plans to continue receiving injections despite the conclusion of the formal study period. It is noted that the effects of Botox are transient, typically lasting three months, necessitating repeated administration. Further investigations are also examining the efficacy of Botox in managing symptoms associated with bipolar disorder.

Amuru man taken to court, cautioned for keeping tortoise
Amuru man cautioned over keeping protected animal species
The newly created Uganda Standards, Utilities and Wildlife Court has sentenced Dennis Omoni to a caution for unlawful possession of a tortoise. This after convict Omoni, a resident of Amuru District, pleaded guilty to a charge of being in possession of protected species, before Grade one magistrate Gladys Kamasanyu.
Omoni told court in Kampala that the tortoise which was found at his home had invaded his fish pond and it was disrupting his farming business.
However the Magistrate cautioned him never to endanger these protected species as he will be denying a chance to the young generation to see them.

A resident of Amuru District, Dennis Omoni, has been formally cautioned by the Uganda Standards, Utilities and Wildlife Court for the unlawful possession of a protected tortoise species. The ruling was delivered by Grade One Magistrate Gladys Kamasanyu in Kampala, following Omoni’s guilty plea to the charge. In his testimony, Omoni explained that the tortoise had been discovered at his residence after it encroached upon his fish pond, thereby disrupting his aquaculture operations.

Magistrate Kamasanyu issued a cautionary statement, emphasizing that endangering protected species deprives future generations of the opportunity to encounter them. The court’s decision underscores the legal protections afforded to wildlife under Ugandan law and demonstrates the operational mandate of the newly established specialized court in adjudicating such violations. This case illustrates the intersection of rural livelihood activities with wildlife conservation statutes, highlighting the judiciary’s role in enforcing environmental protections while considering individual circumstances. BEIJING A senior Uighur official in China's restive western region of Xinjiang has admonished other Communist Party "cadres" from the mostly Muslim Uighur minority for failing to pull their weight in the fight against terrorism, state media said.
China has increased security in Xinjiang to fight what it sees as a grave threat from Islamist extremists stirring up ethnic tension.
Rights groups say that party restrictions on the religion and culture of the Uighurs create simmering resentment of the state and of policies that encourage the majority Han people to move to the region in vast numbers.
"I have become deeply aware, in these severely complicated circumstances, that we Uighur cadres have not taken on the bulk of the work (in fighting terrorism)," said Mehmet Emin Bekri, a top official in south Xinjiang's Kashgar city, according to a post on an official city account on WeChat, a popular social media app.
"(Our) work ethic is superficial, (our) stability measures half-hearted, and there is a clear gap between (our) security work and the demands of the central, regional and prefectural party committees," he said.
A former trading post, Kashgar is central to China's One Belt, One Road initiative, President Xi Jinping's signature foreign and economic policy that aims to create a new "Silk Road" of trade and infrastructure links between China and the developing nations of Euroasia.
But the city and nearby towns in southern Xinjiang are also among the most unstable in the region, creating a threat to plans that the party is combating with mass police rallies and a raft of new "anti-terror" measures.
"We must be soberly aware that... the infiltration of religious extremist thought is intense, the group influence is large, the scope wide, the level of poison deep, especially among people born in the 1980s and 1990s," Bekri said.
Bekri's remarks were published alongside photos of him meeting with white-bearded elderly Uighurs wearing traditional hats over meals of flat bread.
The party encourages ethnic minorities to become cadres, but Uighurs still number far fewer than Han officials in the region, and as all party employees are expected to be atheist, they are often seen by fellow Uighurs as having abandoned their culture.
(Reporting by Christian Shepherd; Editing by Nick Macfie)
rewrite:

The remarks were published on an official municipal account on the WeChat social media platform.

The Chinese government has intensified security protocols within Xinjiang, framing this as a necessary response to a significant threat posed by Islamist extremism and its potential to exacerbate ethnic tensions. Conversely, human rights organizations contend that state-imposed restrictions on Uighur religious and cultural practices, alongside policies encouraging substantial Han Chinese migration to the region, generate underlying resentment that may contribute to instability.

Bekri’s commentary, articulated within what he described as "severely complicated circumstances," highlighted specific deficiencies. He noted that the work ethic was "superficial," stability measures were "half-hearted," and identified a "clear gap" between local security efforts and the directives issued by central, regional, and prefectural party committees. Kashgar, a historically significant trading hub now central to President Xi Jinping’s Belt and Road Initiative, occupies a strategically vital position. This initiative seeks to establish enhanced trade and infrastructure networks across Eurasia. However, the city and surrounding areas in southern Xinjiang are also noted for experiencing considerable instability, which presents a challenge to these economic and strategic plans. The state response has included large-scale police demonstrations and a series of newly implemented counter-terrorism measures.

Further elaborating on the nature of the perceived threat, Bekri warned of the "intense" infiltration of religious extremist ideology, describing its influence as broad, its reach wide, and its effects particularly deep among individuals born in the 1980s and 1990s. The publication of his remarks included photographic documentation of his engagements with elderly, white-bearded Uighur men wearing traditional headwear during meals featuring flatbread.

While the Communist Party promotes the inclusion of ethnic minorities within its cadre system, Uighur officials remain significantly outnumbered by their Han counterparts in the region. Furthermore, as party membership requires adherence to atheism, Uighur cadres can often be perceived by their co-ethnics as having distanced themselves from traditional cultural and religious practices.

Two Kenyan runners, both of them making their Boston Marathon debut, have won the prestigious race.
Edna Kiplagat, a Kenyan policewoman and two-time world champion marathoner, finished first in the women's race with a time of 2:21:52. Rose Chelimo, a Kenyan-born Bahraini runner, placed second.
Geoffrey Kirui, also of Kenya, won the mens' race at 2:09:37 — his first-ever marathon victory. He edged out Portland runner Galen Rupp by 21 seconds.
It was a big day for debut runners at Boston, according to Runner's World.
In the women's race, 25-year-old Jordan Hasay ran her first-ever marathon in 2:23:00 to place third. It was the fastest-ever debut by an American woman, Runner's World says.
And in the men's race, 26-year-old Suguru Osako of Japan — also competing in his first marathon — placed third with 2:10:28.
Meanwhile, competitors in the wheelchair race finished in world-best times, The Associated Press reports:
"Manuela Schar of Switzerland finished in 1 hour, 28 minutes, 17 seconds — shattering the world best by more than five minutes. Fellow Swiss Marcel Hug took the men's race in 1:18:04, also the fastest time ever. "The winners' times are considered a world best and not a world record. The straight-line Boston course doesn't qualify for world records because of the possibility of a supportive tailwind like the one on Monday."
The athletes had a tailwind of 13 mph, the AP reports.
rewrite:
The 121st Boston Marathon was distinguished by the victories of two Kenyan athletes, each marking their inaugural participation in the event. Edna Kiplagat, a Kenyan police officer and two-time world champion, secured the women's title with a time of 2:21:52, followed by Kenyan-born Bahraini runner Rose Chelimo in second place. The men's division was won by Geoffrey Kirui, also of Kenya, in 2:09:37, representing his first marathon victory; he finished 21 seconds ahead of American athlete Galen Rupp.

The event proved notable for several debut performances. In the women's race, 25-year-old American Jordan Hasay achieved a third-place finish in 2:23:00, which Runner's World identifies as the fastest marathon debut for an American woman. Similarly, 26-year-old Suguru Osako of Japan placed third in the men's race with a time of 2:10:28 in his first marathon.

Concurrently, the wheelchair divisions witnessed historically rapid performances. As reported by The Associated Press, Manuela Schär of Switzerland completed the course in 1:28:17, surpassing the previous world best by over five minutes. Her compatriot, Marcel Hug, won the men's race in 1:18:04, also establishing a fastest-ever time. These marks are classified as world bests rather than official world records, as the Boston Marathon's point-to-point course and elevation drop render it ineligible for record ratification, particularly given the potential for advantageous tailwinds. Such conditions were present, with a reported tailwind of 13 mph assisting competitors.

AUSTIN -- For five years, Esperanza Herrera lived with her 93-year-old mother in her southeast Austin home of more than a quarter-century and served as her full-time caretaker.
They followed the same morning routine on March 12: Herrera cooked her mother’s breakfast, and Mary Moreno would sit for hours in her favorite chair in her kitchen.
Moreno had just finished her eggs and bacon when her daughter noticed a package near the front door. She assumed it was her mother’s mail-order medication.
Instead, it was a near-fatal bomb.
RELATED:
Austin bombing victim undergoes several surgeries, feels 'blessed to be alive'
Moreno said she at first could not fathom that her home had been a target of the bomber.
“I was screaming 'the water heater burst,'” Moreno said in her first interview since the blast. “I started to hear her screaming, ‘Take my mother out,’ and I was going to walk. And I saw all the glass."
She soon realized something more dangerous had happened.
It was the second of two explosions in a series of blasts that rocked Austin that day. The other killed 17-year-old Draylen Mason.
In the nearly 10 weeks since the bomber killed himself with an explosive device as police closed in, none of the survivors have agreed to talk about their recovery. Moreno’s daughter is still recovering, and she and her other daughters say they are healing emotionally.
“It’s like, ‘Why here? Why my sister?’” said Zulema Prado, who lives in California but has been in Texas to help care for her mother.
For weeks, Moreno was unable to live in her home. Law enforcement officials had to clear it as a crime scene, and several repairs had to be made.
The family says they are now hoping Herrera recovers enough to return to the family home.
© 2018 KVUE

Their established morning routine on March 12 proceeded typically: Herrera prepared her mother’s breakfast, after which Moreno would sit for an extended duration in her preferred kitchen chair. Shortly after Moreno completed her meal of eggs and bacon, her daughter observed a parcel near the front entrance, initially presuming it to contain her mother’s mail-ordered pharmaceuticals.

The package, however, contained an explosive device that detonated with nearly lethal consequences. In her first interview since the incident, Moreno recounted an initial inability to comprehend that her residence had been deliberately targeted. “I was screaming ‘the water heater burst,’” Moreno stated. “I began to hear her screaming, ‘Take my mother out,’ and I attempted to walk. I then observed the shattered glass.” She subsequently recognized that a more perilous event had transpired.

This explosion constituted the second in a series of detonations that occurred in Austin that day; a separate blast resulted in the death of 17-year-old Draylen Mason. In the approximately ten weeks following the perpetrator’s suicide via an explosive device as law enforcement approached, none of the surviving victims had publicly discussed their recuperation. Herrera remains in recovery, and both she and her sisters report ongoing emotional healing. “It prompts the question, ‘Why here? Why my sister?’” remarked Zulema Prado, who, though residing in California, has been in Texas assisting with her mother’s care.

For several weeks, Moreno was displaced from her home as law enforcement processed the location as a crime scene and necessary repairs were undertaken. The family now expresses hope that Herrera’s recovery will progress sufficiently to permit her return to the familial residence.

ORANGEBURG, S.C. — Trey Samuel ran for 153 yards and three touchdowns on 15 carries and South Carolina State scored 28 unanswered points in a 35-14 victory over Morgan State on Friday night.
The first six possessions of the second half ended in two safeties, two fumbles, a blocked field goal and an interception. Morgan State took a 14-7 lead after its two safeties but South Carolina State tied it on Quan Caldwell's 29-yard catch with 4:41 left in the third quarter.
S.C. State opened the fourth with 21 points in less than three minutes.
Two plays after Morgan State's fourth turnover, on a fumbled punt return, Samuel ran for a 15-yard touchdown to take a 21-14 lead. Darius Leonard intercepted a pass on Morgan State's next possession and ran it back 12 yards to extend the Bulldogs' lead and Samuel capped the scoring with an 89-yard TD run.

The Bulldogs then dominated the fourth quarter, scoring 21 points within three minutes. This surge included a 15-yard touchdown run by Samuel after a fumbled punt return, a 12-yard interception return for a touchdown by Darius Leonard, and finally, an 89-yard touchdown run by Samuel to conclude the scoring.

If you’re seeking relationship bliss circa 2017, look no further than your phone.
It seems emojis, those expressive pictures all over texts and Instagram, could actually help our love lives. In his new book, “The Emoji Code,” to be published in the U.S. in August by MacMillan Picador, British linguist Vyv Evans argues that emojis are making us better communicators.
Evans calls emojis a “near-universal form of communication,” replacing internet slang like LOL with the popular “face with tears of joy” emoji.
And while he says some see the little glyphs as “little more than an adolescent grunt,” Evans says those people couldn’t be more wrong.
Evans’ research found that 72 percent of 18- to 25-year-olds find it easier to express their emotions if they’re using emojis. And 80 percent of people in the U.K. said they use them.
There’s a reason for that: Digital communication has stripped away important context like gestures, facial expressions and tone of voice. Emails and texts often come across as more ambiguous — or mean-spirited — than intended.
Enter the emoji. Adding a little smiley face or winking eye can convey joking or sarcasm. A text that says “Sure, go ahead!” with a kissy face could read more like “sure … go ahead” without one.
A Match.com survey of singles in America found that people who use emojis went on more dates and were more likely to have sex than those who didn’t. More than half of singles who used emojis had sex in 2014, compared to 31 percent of singles who didn’t, according to the survey.
NBC News /
If this leaves you with a confused face, and you don’t even know how to express that in emoji, check out this quick primer of definitions from Emojipedia.
rewrite:
In the contemporary pursuit of relational fulfillment, one's mobile device may hold significant potential. Research suggests that emojis—the expressive pictographs ubiquitous in digital messaging and social media platforms such as Instagram—can positively influence romantic interactions. This perspective is advanced by British linguist Vyv Evans in his forthcoming volume, *The Emoji Code* (MacMillan Picador, August 2017), wherein he contends that emojis enhance communicative efficacy.

Evans characterizes emojis as a "near-universal form of communication," noting their displacement of earlier internet slang, such as "LOL," with symbols like the widely adopted "face with tears of joy." Although some critics dismiss these glyphs as trivial or immature, Evans argues this assessment is fundamentally mistaken. Empirical findings underpinning his work indicate that 72 percent of individuals aged 18 to 25 report greater ease in expressing emotions when employing emojis, a practice corroborated by 80 percent of the surveyed population in the United Kingdom.

This utility arises from a deficit inherent to digital communication: the absence of paralinguistic cues, including gesture, facial expression, and vocal tone. Consequently, emails and text messages are frequently perceived as more ambiguous or inadvertently harsh than intended. Emojis function to mitigate this issue. The strategic insertion of a smiling or winking face, for instance, can clarify intent, signaling humor or sarcasm. A message stating "Sure, go ahead!" may be interpreted as passive-aggressive without an accompanying affectionate symbol, whereas its inclusion can alter the perceived tone entirely.

Supporting data from a Match.com survey of American singles reveals a correlation between emoji usage and romantic success. Participants who regularly used emojis reported a higher frequency of dates and a greater likelihood of sexual activity. Specifically, over half of emoji-using singles were sexually active in 2014, compared to only 31 percent of non-users. Thus, these digital symbols appear to facilitate not only clearer communication but also tangible social outcomes.

TORONTO Canadian clean technology companies are struggling to stay afloat and falling behind global peers even as Ottawa promises to boost the sector and move the country toward a low carbon future, a report released on Thursday showed.
Analytica Advisors said in its seventh annual report that despite years of publicly funded support for research and development, losses for clean tech companies widened to C$3.56 billion ($2.64 billion) in 2015 from C$3.18 billion in 2014, and shareholder returns limped in below the Canadian average. Figures for 2016 are not yet available.
Those metrics have made it difficult to convince pension funds and other investors to put money into the sector even as Ottawa has made a string of promises designed to boost the green economy.
"In short, Canada's clean-technology industry is awash in red ink" and its companies vulnerable to foreign takeover, the report said adding that Canada's share of the global clean tech export market slipped to 1.4 percent in 2015 versus 1.6 percent in 2008, while Malaysia and China have taken much larger chunks over that period.
Canadian clean tech revenue rose 8 percent to C$13.27 billion in 2015 versus the prior year, but the cost of financing projects has increased, adding to the pressure on companies looking to increase their scale.
One profitable company that nevertheless highlights the dilemma is Northland Power Inc (NPI.TO), which has developed several offshore wind projects in Europe but is seeking a buyer to fund its next stage of growth.
Other publicly listed Canadian renewable energy companies include TransAlta Renewables Inc (RNW.TO) and Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp (AQN.TO).
The federal Liberal government has imposed a national price on carbon and sought to boost the use of renewable energy, promising C$1.8 billion of federal funding over the next three years to support clean technology projects.
Canadian dollar issuance accounted for less than $1 billion of the fast-growing global green bond market which totaled $82 billion last year, an earlier report by RBC Capital Markets showed.
($1 = 1.3473 Canadian dollars)
(Reporting by Alastair Sharp; Editing by Lisa Shumaker)

These deteriorating financial metrics have hindered efforts to attract investment from institutional investors, such as pension funds, even as the federal government has announced a series of policy initiatives intended to stimulate the green economy. The report concludes that “Canada’s clean-technology industry is awash in red ink” and its constituent companies are increasingly vulnerable to foreign acquisition. It further notes that Canada’s portion of the global clean technology export market declined to 1.4 percent in 2015 from 1.6 percent in 2008, a period during which competitors such as Malaysia and China captured substantially larger market shares.

Although industry revenues increased by 8 percent to C$13.27 billion in 2015 compared to the previous year, the rising cost of project financing has intensified pressures on firms attempting to scale operations. The case of Northland Power Inc. exemplifies this challenge; while profitable and active in developing European offshore wind projects, the company is reportedly seeking a buyer to finance its subsequent growth phase. Other publicly traded entities in the sector include TransAlta Renewables Inc. and Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp.

Concurrently, the federal Liberal government has implemented a national carbon pricing mechanism and promoted renewable energy adoption, pledging approximately C$1.8 billion in federal funding over a three-year period for clean technology initiatives. However, Canada’s participation in the global green bond market remains modest. A prior RBC Capital Markets report indicated that Canadian dollar-denominated issuance constituted less than $1 billion of the total $82 billion global green bond market last year, a market that is experiencing rapid growth.

Super Eagles coach, Gernot Rohr has continued to rue his loss to South Africa’s Bafana Bafana in the African Cup Nations qualifiers in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.
It was the first only loss the German-born coach has suffered so far in competitive football contest since taking over the Super Eagles in 2016.
Rohr who was speaking in an interview with Soccer Laduma said the South Africans were lucky to run away with a 2-0 win after his side did most of the playing.
“I did regret the defeat, but I think South Africa were very lucky. We had more possession.
“We had the better chances. South Africa scored with only their second shot – that was quite fortunate. “Perhaps they celebrated the victory too much, because they hardly won any other game after- wards. One always has to remain modest even in victory,” Rohr said.
After the World Cup tournament the AFCON qualifiers will resume with Nigeria playing away to Seychelles in September. Libya topping group E will play the Super Eagles in October.
rewrite: Super Eagles coach Gernot Rohr continues to reflect on his team's defeat to South Africa's Bafana Bafana during the African Cup of Nations qualifiers in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State. This remains the sole competitive loss the German-born manager has incurred since assuming leadership of the Nigerian national team in 2016. In an interview with Soccer Laduma, Rohr suggested that the South African side benefited from fortune in securing a 2-0 victory, despite his team demonstrating superior control of the match. He stated, "I regretted the defeat, but I believe South Africa were very fortunate. We maintained greater possession and created the more significant opportunities. Their second shot resulted in a goal, which was quite lucky." Rohr further commented, "Perhaps they celebrated excessively, as they subsequently won hardly any other matches. One must always remain modest, even in victory." Following the World Cup, the AFCON qualifiers will resume with Nigeria facing Seychelles away in September, followed by a match against Group E leaders Libya in October.

Less than six months after the “Unite the Right” rally on the campus of the University of Virginia led to a white supremacist running over counter-protesters with lethal results, a new report indicates that white supremacist fliers are popping up on the grounds of more and more college campuses across the country.
Since September 1, 2016, the Anti-Defamation League has recorded 346 instances of white supremacist propaganda everywhere from community colleges to Ivy League schools. Fliers, stickers, banners and posters qualified as instances of propaganda.
The propaganda contain hateful messages attacking Jews, blacks, Muslims, immigrants and the LGBT community, according to the ADL, while promoting an urgent need to "save" the white race.
© REUTERS/ Rex Curry Over 2,000 People Attend Rally Against White Supremacy in US Dallas
Texas, California, Pennsylvania, Florida, Virginia and Ohio have been the hardest hit, the ADL said January 29.
Identity Evropa, Patriot Front, Vanguard America, a group called The Right Stuff, neo-Nazi group Atomwaffen Division, the Daily Stormer and the American Renaissance were the most prolific propagandizers, according to ADL.
The Unite the Right group at Charlottesville, Virginia chanted slogans like "white lives matter," "Jews will not replace us" and "blood and soil" while walking through the campus with torches to protest the removal of a Robert E. Lee statue by the city government. Lee was the commander of the Army of Northern Virginia, one of the primary armies of the secessionist Confederacy during the American Civil War and was a slave owner.
Ironically, the "patriotic" effort to uphold Lee's legacy leaves out the fact that Lee effectively renounced his US citizenship to fight for the Confederate Army in 1861, before eventually surrendering in 1865. After the war, and until Lee died, his US citizenship was not restored.
rewrite:
In the wake of the “Unite the Right” rally at the University of Virginia—an event that culminated in a white supremacist fatally striking counter-protestors with a vehicle—a recent report documents a proliferation of white supremacist propaganda materials on an increasing number of college campuses nationwide. According to data compiled by the Anti-Defamation League (ADL), there have been 346 documented instances of such propaganda at institutions ranging from community colleges to Ivy League universities since September 1, 2016. These instances encompass the distribution of fliers, stickers, banners, and posters.

The ADL reports that this propaganda frequently disseminates hateful rhetoric targeting Jewish, Black, Muslim, immigrant, and LGBTQ+ communities, while simultaneously advocating for the purported preservation of the white race. As of January 29, the states most affected by these activities are Texas, California, Pennsylvania, Florida, Virginia, and Ohio. The primary groups identified as responsible for this output include Identity Evropa, Patriot Front, Vanguard America, The Right Stuff, the neo-Nazi Atomwaffen Division, the Daily Stormer, and American Renaissance.

This activity echoes the ideologies displayed during the Charlottesville rally, where participants marched with torches across campus, chanting slogans such as "white lives matter," "Jews will not replace us," and "blood and soil" to protest the municipal removal of a statue of Robert E. Lee. Lee, a slaveholder, served as commander of the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia during the American Civil War. Ironically, efforts to valorize Lee’s legacy often omit the historical detail that he effectively renounced his U.S. citizenship to lead Confederate forces in 1861. His citizenship remained unreinstated until after his death, despite his surrender in 1865.

NEW YORK — American Girl’s newest doll is a boy.
The beloved toy maker known for its 18-inch female figurines that hail from different eras in American history is about to release its first male doll.
His name is Logan Everett, and he’s part of a “new series of contemporary” characters that will be up for sale starting Thursday. Logan’s character plays drums for Tenney Grant, a girl trying to make it big in Nashville’s music scene.
Logan has a couple of looks including a leather jacket over gray T-shirt or a T-shirt that says “Play Loud” under an unbuttoned plaid shirt.
“A boy character has been a top request from our fans for decades,” American Girl spokesperson Julie Parks said in a statement Tuesday.
“We do an enormous amount of research with girls and their parents, and the one thing we’ve heard loud and clear is a desire for more—specifically more characters and stories from today—with more experiences, more diversity, and more interests,” Parks said. Thursday will also mark the return of one of the classic American Girl dolls — Felicity Merriman, a young colonial girl who was archived in 2011.
In addition, American Girl will begin offering two new dolls later in 2017. A contemporary doll named Z Yang, who’s a filmmaker, will be released in the Spring. And Nanea, a historical doll who lives in Hawaii during World War II, will be released this fall.
The 18-inch figures sell for $115 each, or about $140 for the doll, a collection of accessories and the doll’s book.
rewrite:
American Girl, the esteemed toy manufacturer renowned for its 18-inch historical dolls depicting girls from various periods in American history, is poised to introduce its inaugural male doll. The new character, named Logan Everett, represents a departure from the company's traditional offerings and heralds the launch of a contemporary character series available beginning Thursday. Logan is portrayed as the drummer for Tenney Grant, an aspiring musical artist in Nashville. His attire includes options such as a leather jacket worn over a gray T-shirt, as well as a "Play Loud" T-shirt paired with an unbuttoned plaid shirt.

According to a statement issued Tuesday by American Girl spokesperson Julie Parks, the introduction of a male character fulfills a longstanding consumer demand. "A boy character has been a top request from our fans for decades," Parks noted. She further explained that extensive research conducted with girls and their parents consistently indicated a desire for expanded product lines, emphasizing contemporary narratives, greater diversity of experiences, and a broader range of interests. Concurrently, the company will reintroduce one of its archived historical characters, Felicity Merriman—a colonial-era doll originally retired in 2011—on Thursday.

Additional releases scheduled for 2017 include two further dolls. A contemporary doll named Z Yang, characterized as a filmmaker, is planned for spring. Subsequently, a historical doll named Nanea, whose story is set in Hawaii during World War II, will be released in the fall. Each 18-inch doll retails for $115, while a bundled set comprising the doll, a collection of accessories, and a corresponding narrative book is priced at approximately $140.

FOR Bundaberg woman Skye Dempsey, necessity truly was the mother of invention.
Unable to find any canine clothes that were quite right for her foxy chihuahua cross Lily, she decided to make her own.
"I could not find a pair of PJs in Bundaberg that fit her,” she said, adding that commercial dog pyjamas often didn't come long enough to cover her pet's body.
Soon Miss Dempsey found herself making pyjamas and dresses for other dogs, and Skye's Puppy PJs was born.
"I learnt to sew from mum and I got into it because of Lily,” she said.
"I was just like, 'why aren't I selling these?'.
Starting to sell them at the end of winter last year, Miss Dempsey said she had stitched about 80 outfits last year alone.
Skye Dempseys dog Rollee models dog pyjamas. Mike Knott BUN020117PYJAMAS5
"One lady bought eight - four summer pairs and four winter pairs,” she said.
"Her dog is allergic to grass so she bought a whole wardrobe.”
Miss Dempsey said with the garments being made to order, she could either take measurements or let owners do it if they lived in another location.
"I've sent some to Melbourne and Sydney and a few on the Gold Coast,” she said.
"They can measure their own dog and I'll send it to them.
"I'll send them photos of materials and they can select what they want.”
Miss Dempsey said there were different reasons for owners dressing their dogs, ranging from allergies to making sure their furbabies kept warm.
Pet owners can check out Miss Dempsey's Facebook group, "Hand Made Puppy PJ's” or call 0421 738 170.
