BELGRADE Germany supports Serbia on its path to the European Union membership but the Balkan country must work on reforms and sort out ties with its former province Kosovo, German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel said on Wednesday .
Speaking before a meeting with Serbian president-elect Aleksandar Vucic, Gabriel said: "You have a responsibility to continue reforms and to continue to develop better relations with Kosovo. That is an essential precondition for accession to the European Union."
Gabriel said he could not give a precise date when Serbia could enter EU.
Earlier on Wednesday, Gabriel who will visit Kosovo on Thursday and Albania on Monday on his Balkan tour, urged Balkan states to overcome their divisions to integrate into the European Union.
Six countries in the Western Balkan region, which is still recovering from a decade of wars and economic turmoil in the 1990s, aim to join the European Union - Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia, Bosnia, Kosovo and Albania.
Gabriel said Serbia, the biggest market, has "a good bit of work" to do to meet the requirements for EU membership, including improving transparency, governance and rule of law, and fighting corruption.
Those steps were also important for Serbia to be able to attract small- and medium-sized businesses, who needed stable conditions, he said.
He said it was good that daily protests by thousands of people after Vucic's election on April 2 had been allowed to proceed without government intervention.
"If you want to get into the EU, you must know that demonstrations and protests against democratically elected governments and president are possible, permitted and within the EU, quite common," Gabriel said.
Vucic, who won a presidential election on April 2 in a landslide, said: "As far as we are concerned we are on the European Union path and whether it will happen or not it does not only depend on us."
Gabriel said he remained concerned about developments elsewhere in the region, where "demons of the past" were arising once again.
Tensions have flared in recent months between Kosovo and Serbia, as well as between three ethnics groups in Bosnia, as nationalist sentiment grows across the region.
(Reporting by Andrea Shalal)
rewrite:
In a statement delivered in Belgrade on Wednesday, German Foreign Minister Sigmar Gabriel affirmed Germany's support for Serbia's European Union accession ambitions, while simultaneously underscoring the requisite for substantive reforms and the normalization of relations with Kosovo. Gabriel, who met with Serbian President-elect Aleksandar Vucic, articulated that Serbia bears a distinct responsibility to advance its reform agenda and foster improved relations with Kosovo, describing this as an essential precondition for EU membership. He declined, however, to provide a precise timeline for Serbia's potential accession.

As part of a broader Balkan tour that includes subsequent visits to Kosovo and Albania, Gabriel emphasized the imperative for Western Balkan states to reconcile historical divisions to facilitate regional integration into the European Union. Six nations from the region—Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Albania—maintain aspirations for EU membership, despite the enduring legacy of 1990s conflicts and economic instability.

Gabriel identified Serbia, as the region's largest market, as having a considerable amount of work ahead to satisfy EU criteria. Key areas for improvement include enhancing transparency, governance, and the rule of law, alongside intensifying efforts to combat corruption. He noted that such reforms are not only critical for accession but are equally vital for attracting small- and medium-sized enterprises, which require a stable and predictable operating environment.

The Foreign Minister also commented on the ongoing public protests following the April 2 presidential election, viewing the government's non-intervention as a positive sign. He stated that within the EU, demonstrations against democratically elected leadership are permissible and commonplace, a standard Serbia must embrace.

President-elect Vucic, who secured a decisive electoral victory, reiterated Serbia's commitment to its European path while acknowledging that the ultimate outcome depends on factors beyond Serbia's sole control. Gabriel concluded by expressing concern over resurgent nationalist sentiments elsewhere in the region, referencing renewed tensions between Kosovo and Serbia and among ethnic groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina as manifestations of what he termed "demons of the past."

× Cheap Wine Is About to Get a Lot More Expensive
The price of wine is going up.
Global wine production slumped to its lowest level in 60 years in 2017, according to data from the International Organisation of Vine and Wine.
The most recent harvest produced 25 billion liters of wine, a decrease from 26.7 billion in 2016 and 27.6 billion in 2015. The decline was driven by weak harvests in key markets including Europe and South Africa.
The shortage has caused the wholesale price of basic wine in Italy to skyrocket 74% over the previous year, according to the European Commission. Prices are up 45% in Spain and over 10% in France.
Analysts said that producers, dealers and retailers will absorb some of the price hikes, but consumers will end up paying more — especially for cheaper bottles.
“The wine companies that are targeting very low prices … will be hit the worst, because their margins are very low,” said Stephen Rannekleiv, a global beverages strategist at Rabobank. “When prices go up, it puts a lot of strain on them.”
Reduced supply will also hurt quality.
“There will be, in some cases, lower quality wines getting blended into slightly higher value products, so everyone kind of goes down a tier in quality,” said Rannekleiv.
Related: Forget craft beer. The next craze is non-alcoholic brew
Producers were hardest hit in Europe, where heavy hailstorms and harsh frosts damaged vineyards in early 2017 before a summer drought took its toll. The continent accounts for 65% of global wine production, and 57% of consumption.
European production dropped 15% in 2017. Production fell 21% in Italy, 18% in France and 15% in Spain, according to the Commission.
Other regions had problems, too.
Wildfires destroyed or tainted some of the harvest in California, and drought harmed vineyards in South Africa. Warm weather can cause grapes to ripen early and be smaller in size.
Rannekleiv said the result was a global harvest that was even worse than analysts had feared.
Related: Coke is launching an alcoholic drink in Japan
The pain could spread to other industries.
Rannekleiv said the slump in production means there will be less wine to divert for use in other products. Brandy and vinegar makers could be hurt, for example.
rewrite:
Global wine production has declined to its lowest level in six decades, precipitating a substantial increase in wholesale prices, particularly for entry-level wines. According to data from the International Organisation of Vine and Wine, the 2017 harvest yielded approximately 25 billion liters, a notable reduction from the 26.7 billion liters produced in 2016 and 27.6 billion liters in 2015. This contraction is largely attributable to diminished harvests in several key producing regions, most notably within Europe and South Africa.

The European Commission reports that the resulting supply shortage has driven a dramatic 74 percent year-over-year increase in the wholesale price of basic wine in Italy, with prices rising 45 percent in Spain and over 10 percent in France. While industry analysts anticipate that producers, distributors, and retailers will absorb a portion of these cost increases, a significant share is ultimately expected to be passed on to consumers. This effect will be most pronounced for lower-priced offerings. Stephen Rannekleiv, a global beverages strategist at Rabobank, notes that companies operating on narrow margins in the value segment will be under considerable strain. Furthermore, the constrained supply is projected to adversely affect overall quality, as some producers may blend lower-quality wines into higher-value products, effectively causing a downward shift in quality tiers across the market.

Adverse climatic conditions were the primary driver of the production shortfall. European vineyards, which account for 65 percent of global production, were severely impacted by a sequence of heavy hailstorms, frosts in early 2017, and subsequent summer droughts. Official data indicates European production fell by 15 percent overall, with declines of 21 percent in Italy, 18 percent in France, and 15 percent in Spain. Concurrently, other regions faced similar challenges: wildfires compromised portions of the California harvest, while drought conditions in South Africa stunted grape development. Unseasonably warm weather in several areas also led to premature ripening and smaller berry size. Rannekleiv observes that the cumulative global harvest result was more severe than initial analyst projections.

The ramifications of this supply contraction may extend beyond the wine sector itself. With less wine available for alternative uses, industries reliant on wine as a base material—such as brandy and vinegar production—could face sourcing difficulties and increased costs. This underscores the broad economic sensitivity to agricultural volatility within the global wine supply chain.

Sooty the possum was lucky to escape from a combustion stove at a Pimlico house.
Sooty the possum was lucky to escape from a combustion stove at a Pimlico house. Jeanette Dundas
WHEN Pimlico man Brian lit the fire in his slow combustion stove, smoke poured out into the room.
The flue was obviously blocked.
But, almost immediately after, a possum dropped into the fire.
Brian acted quickly and got the possum out, but was unsure if it had sustained burns, so he called WIRES for help.
Sooty, as the young possum was named, was extremely lucky.
After rescue and examination it turned out that she had sustained minimal damage as she had avoided the hot part of the fire box. Her main concern was smoke inhalation.
Possums, gliders and many bird species use hollows as homes. Sadly, as human habitat expands, these are no longer as easy to find. A chimney or flue looks very much like a hollow log and clearly this possum had been seeking shelter in this man-made home.
Sooty is fairly young and should most certainly have still been with her mum, but she was not in good body condition, indicating she may have lost her mum some time prior to sheltering in Brian's flue.
She has now been in care with WIRES for a week and is doing well.
Shortly she will be transferred to a large aviary till she is ready to be released back to the wild.
If you have a fireplace it is a good idea to ensure you have an adjustable stainless steel chimney cap.
It is the only way to prevent animals from entering your chimney or flue.
Please call WIRES on 66281898 should you find a native animal in trouble.
rewrite:
A young common brushtail possum narrowly avoided severe injury after entering a combustion stove in a residence in Pimlico. The incident occurred when the homeowner, Brian, ignited the stove only to discover the flue was obstructed, causing smoke to fill the room. Shortly thereafter, a possum fell into the firebox. Brian promptly extracted the animal and contacted the wildlife rescue organization WIRES for assistance, concerned it may have been burned. The possum, subsequently named Sooty, was found to have been remarkably fortunate. Upon rescue and veterinary examination, it was determined she had sustained only minimal physical trauma, having largely avoided direct contact with the hottest areas of the combustion chamber. Her primary injury was related to smoke inhalation.

Arboreal mammals such as possums and gliders, alongside numerous bird species, are dependent on tree hollows for shelter and nesting. The ongoing expansion of urban and suburban developments has significantly reduced the availability of these natural cavities. Consequently, artificial structures like chimneys and stove flues, which superficially resemble hollow logs, are increasingly identified as substitute refuges. Sooty’s case exemplifies this perilous adaptation. Although a juvenile typically still dependent on maternal care, her poor body condition suggests she may have been orphaned prior to seeking shelter in the flue.

Following a week of specialized care from WIRES, Sooty has recovered satisfactorily. Her rehabilitation will continue in a large aviary until she attains the requisite condition and skills for release back into a suitable natural habitat. To prevent similar incidents, homeowners with chimneys or flues are strongly advised to install an adjustable stainless steel chimney cap, which serves as an effective barrier against animal intrusion. Members of the public encountering native wildlife in distress are encouraged to contact WIRES for professional assistance.

Nigerian Lady narrates her hilarious experience living in Canada and how she was arrested crossing a rail track
A Nigerian lady identified as “Blackmigrantgirl” on twitter took to the microblogging platform to share how she got a ticket for crossing “ordinary railtrack”
Read her hilarious ordeal below;
The logical side of me understands why I got the ticket but I am still unhappy about it. Let me explain what happened.
I had to travel by bus and by train from the venue of a job interview I attended today, back to the home of my hosts on the other side of town- in Stouffville. My bus arrived the train station with very little time to spare for the departure time of the train to Stouffville. Unfortunately for me, the closest route from the bus terminal to the train platform is now blocked off due to ongoing construction. I then had to make a dash for it across from the bus to the train station, following the longer route, down the stairs and then up another flight of stairs to the departure platform.
Only for me to get to the departure platform to discover that I was on the wrong platform and the train was on the far side of the station.
Adrenalin had already kicked in from all the running and I gave it free rein to cross the train track to get on my train. I didn’t even have enough time to think about the consequences of what I was doing.
Of course I got caught ????
Next thing I know, a security guard is walking up to me and asking me to step out of the train. Everyone was looking at me like I stole. Chai! My father in heaven oh.
Long story short, to my utter disbelief, th4e security guard wrote me a ticket for 180 Canadian dollars. All my explanation of being late, being new to Canada, not knowing I was violating a bye-law fell on deaf ears.
Now I have to call the courthouse tomorrow, to beg for a lesser fine.
Honestly, I’m just tired???????. I just hope I am hired for the job that brought me downtown today”
Do you have similar experience? Share with us in the comment section below
rewrite:
A Nigerian national residing in Canada, who identifies as “Blackmigrantgirl” on the social media platform X (formerly Twitter), has recounted an incident in which she received a citation for unlawfully crossing railway tracks. The following is her detailed narrative.

While the rational aspect of my comprehension acknowledges the justification for the penalty, I remain disconcerted by the event. I shall elucidate the circumstances. Following a job interview, I needed to return via bus and train from the interview location to my hosts’ residence in Stouffville, a community on the opposite side of the metropolitan area. Upon arriving by bus at the train station, I had minimal time before the scheduled departure of my Stouffville-bound train. Compounding this difficulty, the most direct access from the bus terminal to the appropriate train platform was obstructed due to active construction. Consequently, I was compelled to take a significantly longer route, necessitating a hurried descent down one staircase and an ascent up another to reach the departure platform.

Upon arrival, I discovered I was on the incorrect platform; my train was stationed on the opposite side of the facility. The adrenaline precipitated by my earlier sprint influenced my subsequent decision. I proceeded to cross the active railway tracks to board the train, an action undertaken without sufficient deliberation regarding its potential repercussions.

Unsurprisingly, the act resulted in interception. A security official approached and instructed me to disembark from the train. The attention from fellow passengers was profoundly mortifying, as their gazes conveyed a judgment akin to my having committed a theft. To summarize the outcome, and to my considerable astonishment, the security officer issued a monetary penalty of 180 Canadian dollars. All appeals for leniency—citing my tardiness, recent arrival in Canada, and ignorance of the specific municipal bylaw—were disregarded.

I am now obligated to contact the local courthouse to formally petition for a reduction of the fine. The experience has been profoundly fatiguing. My sole consolation is the potential of securing the employment position that necessitated my travel into the city center. This account raises broader questions regarding the acclimatization challenges faced by new immigrants and the sometimes abrupt enforcement of local ordinances.

Halifax Regional Police responded to a home on Acadia Street shortly before 2 a.m. Tuesday after receiving a report that two men had forced their way inside.
Police say the men had their faces covered, were dressed in black, and one was armed with a knife. The suspects fled the scene in a vehicle, which was spotted by a responding officer not far from the home.
The vehicle was stopped and four suspects were arrested. They were held in police custody overnight.
A resident of the home was sent to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries and has since been treated and released.
Police say the investigation has revealed that the victim and suspects are not known to each other, and the victim was not the intended target.
Shaquean James Bowden, 21, and Anthony Alfrado Corradini, 19, both of Halifax, and Darcy Raymond Delbert Caldwell, 28, and Kerry Lee Sampson, 31, both of Windsor, have all been charged with one count each of break and enter, assault with a weapon, assault causing bodily harm, and possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose.
Corradini has also been charged with one count of disguise with intent and three counts of breach of probation.
All four men are due to appear Wednesday in Halifax provincial court.
rewrite:
Halifax Regional Police have charged four individuals in relation to a residential invasion in Halifax that resulted in non-life-threatening injuries to a male occupant, who authorities have determined was not the intended victim of the incident. Police were dispatched to a residence on Acadia Street shortly before 2:00 a.m. on Tuesday following reports of two males forcibly entering the premises. According to official statements, the suspects, whose faces were concealed and who were attired in black clothing, fled the scene in a vehicle subsequent to the incident. One of the individuals was reportedly armed with a knife. A responding officer located the vehicle in proximity to the residence, leading to a traffic stop and the arrest of four suspects, who remained in custody overnight.

The injured resident was transported to a hospital for treatment and has since been released. The ongoing investigation indicates no prior acquaintance between the victim and the suspects, confirming the victim was not the intended target. The accused have been identified as Shaquean James Bowden, 21, and Anthony Alfrado Corradini, 19, both of Halifax, along with Darcy Raymond Delbert Caldwell, 28, and Kerry Lee Sampson, 31, both of Windsor. Each faces charges of break and enter, assault with a weapon, assault causing bodily harm, and possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose. Corradini faces an additional charge of disguise with intent and three counts of breach of probation. All four individuals are scheduled for an initial appearance in Halifax Provincial Court on Wednesday.

Antivirus Giant McAfee Acquires VPN Provider TunnelBear
Internet security company McAfee has bought VPN provider TunnelBear. McAfee hasn't announced how much the deal is worth, but in a statement the company said it plans to integrate TunnelBear's services into its own VPN service, Safe Connect.
"We're confident this acquisition will serve both our end users and partners by embedding its best-in-class, hardened network into our Safe Connect product," said McAfee CEO Christopher Young.
The End of Free VPN?
There's a chance this acquisition could spell the end of TunnelBear's free service. It's currently first in our roundup of the best free VPNs , but that could all change when it's integrated into McAfee Safe Connect, which has a different pricing model.
McAfee Safe Connect offers a free seven-day trial, but after that there's a subscription fee of $7.99 per month, or $47.88 per year.
There could also be a change in TunnelBear's terms. The Canadian company is known for its clear privacy policy, which explains every piece of data it collects from its users and why, but once the McAfee purchase is complete, it'll need to abide by US laws. If you currently use TunnelBear, it's well worth keeping an eye out for anything new.
What's Next for McAfee
The start of 2018 has been a busy time for McAfee. At last month's Mobile World Congress, it demonstrated a new feature for Amazon Alexa that lets you check the security of your home network and change its settings with just your voice. For example, you can see how many devices are connected, set a time limit for your child's iPad, and disconnect any devices you don't recognize.
Last month, the company also announced a deal with European internet provider Telefonica, providing security software for home and mobile networks. McAfee Secure Home Platform will be integrated with Telefonica's broadband routers, with extra protection for users' phones when they're out and about.
Could we soon see a voice-activated VPN from McAfee, or routers with TunnelBear tech built in? We'll be keeping an eye out.

In a strategic expansion of its cybersecurity portfolio, the prominent internet security corporation McAfee has announced the acquisition of the virtual private network (VPN) provider TunnelBear. The financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. According to an official statement, McAfee intends to integrate TunnelBear’s technological assets into its existing VPN product, McAfee Safe Connect. Christopher Young, Chief Executive Officer of McAfee, elaborated on the rationale, stating, “We are confident this acquisition will serve both our end users and partners by embedding its best-in-class, hardened network into our Safe Connect product.”

This corporate merger raises pertinent questions regarding the future availability of TunnelBear’s complimentary VPN tier, which is currently highly ranked among free VPN services. The integration process may precipitate the discontinuation of this free offering, as McAfee Safe Connect operates on a distinct commercial model. That service provides a seven-day trial period, subsequently requiring a subscription fee of either $7.99 monthly or $47.88 annually. Furthermore, operational changes are anticipated in TunnelBear’s governance and privacy policies. The Canadian firm has been recognized for its transparent data practices, meticulously detailing its data collection purposes. Post-acquisition, TunnelBear will be subject to United States legal jurisdiction, necessitating vigilance from existing users regarding potential modifications to its terms of service.

McAfee’s activities in early 2018 indicate a period of concerted corporate development. During the recent Mobile World Congress, the company previewed a novel integration for Amazon Alexa, enabling voice-command security assessments and management of home networks. This functionality includes auditing connected devices, imposing parental controls on specific hardware, and disconnecting unrecognized endpoints. Concurrently, McAfee established a partnership with the European telecommunications provider Telefonica to deploy its security software across residential and mobile networks. This collaboration will embed the McAfee Secure Home Platform within Telefonica’s broadband infrastructure, extending enhanced protection to mobile devices outside the home environment.

These initiatives collectively suggest a broader corporate strategy toward integrated, multi-platform security solutions. Future developments may include voice-activated VPN capabilities or the incorporation of TunnelBear’s technology into network hardware. The industry will monitor the integration’s progression and its implications for both product offerings and user privacy standards.

According to Irish Water this evening a burst has occurred on the pipeline serving the Staleen Water Treatment Plant which serves Drogheda & East Meath.
A repair crew is on site to assess the burst and begin repairs. The burst is close to the same location as the burst which occurred last year.
The treated drinking water reservoir serving Drogheda and East Meath has enough water to maintain a water supply to customers for the present.
Irish Water are asking all customers to conserve water until they can can confirm a timeline for resumption of a normal water supply.
"We will provide a further update in the morning and during tomorrow as the picture becomes clearer.
"While we are hopeful that the repair on this occasion will be achieved in a shorter timeframe we are nevertheless mobilizing our full Crisis Management Team so that we will have contingency measures in place to respond to whatever circumstances arise.
"Irish Water has approved the budget and design for a new pipeline to replace the existing lines. We are in the final stages of resolving all of the contractual issues to begin mobilization of construction of this pipeline within weeks."
rewrite:
Irish Water has reported that a pipeline supplying the Staleen Water Treatment Plant, which serves the Drogheda and East Meath regions, sustained a rupture this evening. A repair team is currently on-site to evaluate the damage and initiate necessary repairs. Notably, this incident has occurred in proximity to the site of a similar pipeline failure last year.

Presently, the treated drinking water reservoir for these areas retains sufficient capacity to maintain supply to customers. However, Irish Water is advising all consumers to practice water conservation until a definitive timeline for the restoration of normal service can be established. A further update will be provided tomorrow morning and throughout the day as assessments progress.

While officials express optimism that repairs on this occasion may be completed more swiftly, the full Crisis Management Team has been mobilized as a precautionary measure. This ensures contingency plans are prepared to address any potential developments. Concurrently, Irish Water has confirmed the approval of both budget and design for a new pipeline to replace the existing infrastructure. The organization is in the final stages of resolving contractual matters, with construction mobilization anticipated to commence within weeks.

Boeung Kak community members protest outside of the Council of Ministers office in Phnom Penh yesterday. Heng Chivoan
Authorities thwart Boeung Kak event
Some 30 Boeung Kak land activists yesterday were blocked by 50 Daun Penh district security guards from delivering a petition to the Council of Ministers seeking Prime Minister Hun Sen’s intervention in helping release fellow activist Tep Vanny.
The group of women claimed they were travelling by tuk-tuk to deliver the petition when they were stopped by security forces from leaving their neighbourhood.
The petition asks the premier to help free Vanny, who was arrested in August for taking part in a cursing ceremony. Since then, the court decided to revive two long-dormant cases against her, convicting her in one of them for allegedly using violence during a protest near Hun Sen’s house in 2013.
The petition also asks Hun Sen to stop arresting Boeung Kak women, and to help resolve the community’s land disputes.
“We are disappointed. This is the first time that authorities came and picked up the petition at the community,” said community representative Bov Sophea. “I think they tried to negotiate to avoid any problems.”
Kong Chamroeun, a representative of Hun Sen’s cabinet, picked up the petition and said it would be forwarded to the premier.
rewrite:
On Thursday, members of the Boeung Kak community assembled to deliver a petition to the Council of Ministers in Phnom Penh, seeking the intervention of Prime Minister Hun Sen. Their demonstration was obstructed by approximately fifty security personnel from Daun Penh district, who prevented a group of roughly thirty female land rights activists from departing their neighborhood. The activists reported that they were halted while traveling by tuk-tuk.

The petition formally requests the Prime Minister's assistance in securing the release of fellow activist Tep Vanny. Ms. Vanny was initially arrested in August for participating in a cursing ceremony. Subsequently, the judicial system revived two previously dormant legal cases against her, resulting in a conviction in one instance for alleged acts of violence during a 2013 protest near the Prime Minister's residence. Furthermore, the document appeals for an end to the arrest of Boeung Kak women and for governmental assistance in resolving the community's ongoing land disputes.

Community representative Bov Sophea expressed disappointment, noting it was the first instance authorities had collected a petition directly from the community, a move she interpreted as an effort to negotiate and prevent potential disturbances. Kong Chamroeun, a representative from the Prime Minister's cabinet, accepted the petition and confirmed it would be forwarded for consideration.

A man dressed only in his pyjamas when seen by police outside his car failed to provide a breath test.
Kenneth Roberts, 53, explained how he had earlier gone in the Landrover to take his dog for a walk.
When they returned to the vehicle it would not start, so he walked home, a court in Mold was told.
Later in the pub he was warned of the danger of leaving his vehicle and walked back to ensure it was locked.
But he got soaked from the rain and was in the process of changing his overalls, with his pyjamas underneath, when the police arrived.
Roberts told Flintshire Magistrates Court that he did not provide a breath specimen at St Asaph police station on October 28 because he did not think he had done anything wrong.
He admitted failing to provide a breath specimen when suspected of being ‘in charge’ of the Landrover.
Roberts escaped a driving ban following a plea by barrister Owen Edwards, defending, that it would cause him exceptional hardship.
Roberts, of Main Road in Ffynnongroyw, was fined £650 with £85 costs and a £65 surcharge.
Magistrates said they believed it was a deliberate refusal, but they accepted that to ban him would mean the loss of his job.
That would mean the loss of his home and the effect that would have on his wife and his daughter.
His father-in-law and his sister also relied upon him being able to drive.
Magistrates said they accepted there was no suggestion that he intended to drive and the fact that the Landrover would not start at the time had influenced their decision.
rewrite:
Kenneth Roberts, aged 53, of Main Road, Ffynnongroyw, was convicted for failing to provide a breath specimen when suspected of being in charge of a motor vehicle. According to evidence presented at Flintshire Magistrates Court in Mold, Mr. Roberts had initially driven his Land Rover to walk his dog. Upon returning to the vehicle, he found it would not start and consequently proceeded home on foot. Later, while at a public house, he was advised of the risks associated with leaving his vehicle unattended and returned to secure it. During this return journey, he became drenched by rain. When police officers arrived at the scene, he was in the process of changing his outer clothing, wearing pyjamas beneath. Mr. Roberts subsequently declined to provide a breath test at St Asaph police station on October 28th, stating he did not believe he had committed an offence.

Despite magistrates determining the refusal to be deliberate, a driving ban was not imposed following a plea of exceptional hardship by his defence barrister, Owen Edwards. The court accepted that disqualification would result in the loss of Mr. Roberts’ employment, which would in turn jeopardise his home and adversely affect his wife, daughter, father-in-law, and sister, all of whom rely on his ability to drive. Magistrates also noted the absence of any evidence that he intended to drive, a conclusion influenced by the fact that the Land Rover was inoperable at the material time. Mr. Roberts was fined £650, with £85 in costs and a £65 victim surcharge.

MOGADISHU, Somalia (AP) — A Somali police officer says a suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a security checkpoint near Mogadishu's international airport, killing at least three people.
Capt. Mohamed Hussein says the bomb detonated Monday as security forces were searching cars at the checkpoint, a few hundred meters (yards) from the main base of the African Union peacekeeping mission.
The checkpoint is close to United Nations offices and the Peace Hotel, which is often frequented by foreigners and officials. The powerful blast blew roofs off nearby buildings.
A second blast and heavy gunfire could be heard at the checkpoint after the attack, but there were no immediate details.
The al-Qaida-linked Islamic extremist group al-Shabab, which often carries out such attacks, quickly claimed responsibility for Monday's attack through its radio arm, Andalus.
Despite being ousted from most of its key strongholds across large parts of south and central Somalia, the homegrown group continues to wage deadly attacks across the country.
Somalia's capital has seen frequent bomb attacks at hotels and military checkpoints. In July, two al-Shabab suicide bombers detonated explosives-laden cars outside the office of the U.N.'s mine-clearing agency and an army checkpoint near the African Union's main base, killing 13.
The assaults have threatened this Horn of Africa nation's attempts to rebuild from decades of chaos. The country's presidential election, a key step toward recovery, already has been delayed multiple times because of security and other concerns.
rewrite:
On Monday, a suicide bomber detonated a vehicle laden with explosives at a security checkpoint in close proximity to Mogadishu's international airport, resulting in a minimum of three fatalities. According to Captain Mohamed Hussein, a Somali police officer, the detonation occurred as security personnel were conducting inspections of vehicles. The checkpoint is situated several hundred meters from the primary base of the African Union peacekeeping mission and is adjacent to United Nations offices and the Peace Hotel, an establishment commonly frequented by international personnel and officials. The force of the explosion was sufficient to damage nearby structures, displacing roofs from buildings. Subsequent to the initial blast, reports indicated sounds of a second explosion and sustained gunfire in the vicinity, though further details were not immediately available.

Responsibility for the assault was promptly claimed by the al-Qaida-affiliated Islamic extremist group al-Shabab via its radio broadcast network, Andalus. Although largely dislodged from its principal strongholds across southern and central Somalia, this indigenous insurgent faction persists in executing lethal attacks nationwide. The capital has experienced recurrent bombings targeting hotels and military checkpoints. A notable precedent occurred in July, when two al-Shabab operatives detonated vehicular bombs outside the United Nations mine-clearing agency's office and an army checkpoint near the African Union's main base, killing thirteen individuals.

These persistent attacks jeopardize Somalia's efforts to achieve stability following decades of conflict. The nation's presidential election, a critical component of its political reconstruction, has already been postponed on multiple occasions due to security challenges and related logistical concerns.

Every day, 144 people are killed in the United States from opioid overdoses, according to the Center for Disease Control.
Courts within the criminal justice system are on the frontline of the epidemic, seeing adults with substance use disorders and children in families with opioid addiction.
That's why a conference is being held in Coronado this week to bring awareness of what is going on in the juvenile justice system and how judges can take leadship roles in helping families and children through the court system.
This coming in light of President Donald Trump's announcement Monday calling for stiffer penalties for drug traffickers, including embracing the death penalty.
The multi-day conference will feature guest speakers discussing current juvenile justice issues, solutions and judiciary actions for future solutions.
The meeting will be an educational opportunity for judges, family law attorneys, probation officers and those interested in the juvenile justice system.
The conference will highlight new programs and current research having to do with the opioid epidemic in connection to the court and justice system.
There will also be film screenings, topics of technology and teen dating violence, child sex trafficking informational meetings and brain science lectures.
Guests at the conference will include Judge Tony Capizzi of Montgomery County Juvenile Court in Dayton Ohio, Joey Ordunda Hastings, the CEO of the National Council of Juvenile and Family Court Judges in Reno, Nevada, and others.
The conference will take place at Loews Coronado Bay Resort from March 18-21.
rewrite:
According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the United States experiences approximately 144 fatalities daily due to opioid overdoses. The criminal justice system, and particularly its courts, operate at the forefront of this public health crisis, routinely adjudicating cases involving adults with substance use disorders and children from families impacted by opioid addiction. In response, a multi-day conference is being convened in Coronado this week to elevate awareness of the epidemic’s effects within the juvenile justice system and to examine the capacity of judges to assume leadership roles in assisting affected families through judicial mechanisms. This gathering occurs following President Donald Trump’s recent announcement advocating for enhanced penalties, including capital punishment, for drug traffickers.

The conference aims to provide an educational forum for judges, family law attorneys, probation officers, and other juvenile justice stakeholders. Programming will feature expert presentations on contemporary juvenile justice issues, alongside discussions of potential solutions and judicial actions for future implementation. A specific focus will be placed on emerging programs and current research pertaining to the opioid epidemic’s intersection with court systems. The agenda further includes film screenings, sessions on technology and teen dating violence, informational meetings on child sex trafficking, and lectures on relevant brain science. Notable participants will include Judge Tony Capizzi of the Montgomery County Juvenile Court in Dayton, Ohio, and Joey Orduña Hastings, CEO of the National Council of Juvenile and Family Court Judges in Reno, Nevada. The event is scheduled to take place at the Loews Coronado Bay Resort from March 18th through the 21st.

The organization has already found and interviewed the operator of a drone that hit an Army Black Hawk
The NTSB has issued a statement saying that it will investigate the September 21 collision of a civilian drone and an Army UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter east of Staten Island, New York. The Army is conducting a separate investigation, but because the drone was a civilian aircraft, it falls to the NTSB to conduct its own inquiry. Drone manufacturer DJI and the FAA will be participating in the NTSB’s investigation.
The helicopter sustained damage to its main rotor blade, window frame and transmission deck. The DJI Phantom 4 drone was destroyed by the impact. According to the NTSB, they have been able to identify and interview the operator of the drone. The drone operator also provided the NTSB with the drone’s flight data logs. The investigation is ongoing and the NTSB has stated that it is reviewing flight data from both drone and helicopter and FAA airspace and temporary flight restriction documents.
Learn more at the NTSB.
rewrite: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has announced it will investigate the September 21st collision between a civilian unmanned aerial system (drone) and a U.S. Army UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter, which occurred in airspace east of Staten Island, New York. While the Army is conducting a parallel inquiry, the NTSB holds primary investigative authority as the involved drone was a civil aircraft. The investigation will include participation from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the drone’s manufacturer, DJI. The impact resulted in damage to the helicopter’s main rotor blade, window frame, and transmission deck, while the DJI Phantom 4 drone was destroyed. Investigators have successfully identified and interviewed the drone’s operator, who subsequently provided the device’s flight data logs. The ongoing investigation entails a comprehensive review of flight data from both vehicles, alongside relevant FAA airspace and temporary flight restriction documentation. Further details are available through the NTSB.

Ioan Ficior, 89, a Romanian communist-era labour prison commander is escorted by police at the end of his trial in Bucharest, Romania, March 29, 2017. Inquam Photos/Liviu Florin Albei via REUTERS
Ioan Ficior, 89, a Romanian communist-era labour prison commander is escorted by police at the end of his trial in Bucharest, Romania, March 29, 2017. Inquam Photos/Liviu Florin Albei via REUTERS
BUCHAREST An 89-year-old communist-era labour prison commander faces the rest of his life in prison after Romania's top court ruled on Wednesday he must stay 20 years behind bars for murder and crimes against humanity.
Ioan Ficior was sentenced for involvement in the deaths of 103 inmates at the Danube delta prison labour colony of Periprava, the second case of its kind since the collapse of Nicolae Ceausescu's dictatorship in December 1989.
Ficior was accused of subjecting political inmates to beatings and starvation and denying them medical treatment and heating. He was in charge of the prison from 1958 to 1963.
The court ruling, quoting the prosecutors, said: "The biggest death toll - 53 - occurred in 1960. The youngest inmate who died was 19 years old and the oldest was 71."
The former commander protested his innocence, saying: "I did not get involved in such deeds that I'm accused of."
Prosecutors have said detainees were subjected to water and food shortages, beatings with steel wire, lack of medicines and long working hours in maize fields.
Former detainee Gheorghe Tomici recalled: "Personally I have been forced by guards to pluck grass with my teeth."
"I remember a lawyer who left a blade of grass behind during the manual weeding of the maize fields. He was forced by security guards to pluck the weed with his mouth. I remember seeing his dentures in the ground," he said.
According to the Institute for Investigation of Communist Crimes (IICCMER), up to 2 million Romanians were estimated to have been killed, imprisoned, deported, relocated or otherwise victimized between 1945 and 1989.
(Reporting by Radu Marinas; Editing by Tom Heneghan)
rewrite:
On March 29, 2017, Ioan Ficior, an 89-year-old former commander of a communist-era labour prison, was escorted by police following his trial in Bucharest, Romania. Subsequently, on a Wednesday, Romania’s Supreme Court ruled that Ficior must serve a 20-year prison sentence for murder and crimes against humanity, a verdict that effectively ensures he will remain incarcerated for the remainder of his life. This conviction pertains to his involvement in the deaths of 103 inmates at the Periprava labour colony in the Danube delta, representing only the second prosecution of its kind since the collapse of Nicolae Ceaușescu’s regime in December 1989.

Ficior, who commanded the prison from 1958 to 1963, was found guilty of subjecting political prisoners to systematic abuse, including beatings, starvation, denial of medical care, and exposure to extreme cold. Prosecutors documented that detainees endured severe shortages of food and water, were beaten with steel wire, deprived of medicine, and forced into prolonged labour in maize fields. The court cited prosecution evidence indicating the highest mortality occurred in 1960, with 53 fatalities among inmates ranging from 19 to 71 years of age.

Throughout the proceedings, Ficior maintained his innocence, asserting, “I did not get involved in such deeds that I'm accused of.” Testimonies from survivors, however, detailed extreme brutality. Former detainee Gheorghe Tomici recounted being compelled to pluck grass with his teeth, while describing an incident in which a fellow prisoner was forced to remove a weed with his mouth, resulting in his dentures being left on the ground.

This case occurs within the broader historical context documented by the Institute for the Investigation of Communist Crimes in Romania (IICCMER), which estimates that up to two million Romanians were killed, imprisoned, deported, forcibly relocated, or otherwise victimized between 1945 and 1989. The prosecution of Ficior constitutes a significant, albeit belated, judicial reckoning with this legacy of systematic repression.

Lawyer demands N200, 000 for emergency adjournment
Mr. David Emagun, counsel to Law Union and Rock Insurance Plc, on Wednesday, demanded a cost of N200,000 from another counsel for serving an emergency application for adjournment on him.
The insurance company was sued by its former branch manager, Mr. John Johnson, contesting his alleged dismissal, entitlements and other terminal benefits.
At a resumed hearing of the suit at the National Industrial Court, Abuja, Emagun said he was served the application from the claimant’s counsel that morning.
He, therefore, prayed the court to grant him cost, explaining it was for travelling expenses and accommodation for himself and two other witnesses from Lagos.

Black Stars captain Asamoah Gyan and President-elect Akufo-Addo
In the absence of Asamoah Gyan and Andre Ayew stand-in Black Stars captain Emmanuel Agyemang-Badu says his teammates are poised to end Ghana’s long wait for a major title by winning the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations to make President-elect Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo Addo proud.

“Secondly, the team is poised for action when the tournament starts on the 14th of January. We started our training three days ago and so far there’s no injury in camp, everything is going on well.
”We are leaving here tomorrow to Dubai as president (Kwesi Nyantakyi) said to continue our intense training programmes.
”With the quality in camp, the cohesion and team spirit, I think Nana will be proud of us by the time the tournament ends.”
@NATIONAL ACCORD/Myjoyonline.com

This achievement, he asserted, would honor President-elect Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. The Udinese midfielder addressed the media on behalf of the squad following a meeting with a two-person delegation representing the incoming president.

Agyemang-Badu extended congratulations to the president-elect for his electoral success and his efforts throughout the year. He subsequently confirmed the team's readiness for the tournament commencing on January 14th, noting that training had begun three days prior without any current injuries, and that preparations were proceeding positively. The order, issued by Transportation Secretary Arthur Tugade, is a response to the security scare springing from the continuing crisis in Marawi
Published 6:10 PM, June 13, 2017
MANILA, Philippines – Transportation Secretary Arthur Tugade on June 5 ordered the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) to intensify security over the country's waters.
Through Department Order (DO) No. 2017-008, the PCG was directed "to take over the security supervision of ports and shipping, whether public or private, including the egress and ingress to all waterways from the Maritime Industry Administration (Marina) and Philippine Ports Authority (PPA)."
The order is a response to the security scare springing from the continuing crisis in Marawi City which led to the declaration of martial law over the entire island region of Mindanao.
In line with its mandate under Republic Act 5173, the PCG will be controlling movement of all vessels in seaports and harbors and designating security zones around at least 1,600 ports of the country.
The PCG will also strictly enforce maritime security communications; supervise, regulate, and control port police and private security guards, K9 entities, divers and underwater operations in all maritime-related facilities and infrastructure.
In addition, it will enforce the ports and ships identification system and inspect cargoes to restrict travel of suspicious individuals and to prevent the transport of contraband.
The PCG may arrest, seize, or detain persons, cargo, and vessels found violating maritime security and other pertinent laws, and file the necessary charges.
Over Mindanao waters, the PCG may set and enforce security measures within the bounds of the International Ships and Ports Security Code and the Philippine Constitution's provisions on martial law.
Only persons "judicially charged for rebellion or offenses inherent in or directly connected with the invasion" are deprived of the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus. (READ: Martial Law 101: Things you should know)
The order will be effective until July 22 when martial law hits its 60th day. If the President requests or if public safety calls for it, martial law may be extended by Congress.
Read the full order here:
D.O. No. 2017-008 Control and Supervision of Ports and Ships Security Operations by the PCG by Ram Talabong on Scribd
– Rappler.com
rewrite:
On June 5, 2017, Philippine Transportation Secretary Arthur Tugade issued Department Order No. 2017-008, directing the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) to enhance maritime security nationwide. This directive constitutes a formal response to security concerns arising from the ongoing conflict in Marawi City, which precipitated the declaration of martial law across the Mindanao region. The order explicitly transfers primary security oversight of all public and private ports, shipping operations, and waterway access points from the Maritime Industry Administration (MARINA) and the Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) to the PCG.

In accordance with its statutory mandate under Republic Act 5173, the PCG is thereby authorized to assume comprehensive control. This includes regulating vessel movement within all seaports and harbors, establishing designated security zones encompassing approximately 1,600 ports, and rigorously enforcing maritime security communication protocols. Furthermore, the PCG is charged with the supervision, regulation, and control of all security personnel operating within maritime facilities. This extends to port police, private security details, K-9 units, and divers conducting underwater operations.

Additional measures under the order involve the strict enforcement of port and vessel identification systems and the inspection of cargo. These actions are intended to restrict the mobility of individuals deemed security threats and to interdict the transportation of contraband materials. The PCG is empowered to arrest individuals, seize cargo, and detain vessels found in violation of maritime security laws, with subsequent legal charges to be filed as necessary.

For waters surrounding Mindanao, the PCG will implement and enforce specific security measures. These operations will be conducted within the legal frameworks established by the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code and the pertinent provisions of the Philippine Constitution regarding martial law. It is noted that the suspension of the writ of habeas corpus applies solely to individuals judicially charged for rebellion or related offenses directly connected to invasion.

This enhanced security regime is scheduled to remain in effect until July 22, 2017, coinciding with the initial 60-day period of martial law. An extension beyond this date is contingent upon a formal request by the President and subsequent congressional approval, should public safety requirements necessitate prolonged measures.

(CBS Local) – Gun owners around the country are blowing up expensive coolers after the NRA accused outdoor lifestyle company Yeti of joining a nationwide boycott of the gun-rights organization.
According to a letter from Marion P. Hammer of the NRA’s Institute for Legislative Action, Yeti has cut ties with the NRA and is refusing to do business with the NRA Foundation or offer discounts to members. “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities,” Hammer claims in the April 20 statement.
In response to the news, NRA members and supporters have begun taking their frustrations out on the company’s hottest item: outdoor coolers. In a number of online videos boycotting Yeti, gun owners are seen destroying the expensive containers by loading them with explosives and shooting them. “This Yeti ain’t ready,” South Carolina resident Bryan Atkinson declared before obliterating his cooler.
The pricey coolers reportedly cost anywhere between $250 and $1,300; making a discount on Yeti camping and hunting gear very helpful to consumers. “If Yeti can’t stand behind the NRA, I ain’t standing behind Yeti no more,” Atkinson added in a Facebook post.
Yeti is disputing the NRA’s claims that they’ve joined a boycott against pro-gun Americans. “Yeti notified the NRA Foundation, as well as a number of other organizations, that we were eliminating a group of outdated discounting programs,” the company wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. The outdoor lifestyle supplier added that they’re offering business partners like the NRA alternative programs and called claims that Yeti was turning their backs on young gun owners untrue.
Several organizations including airlines and rental car companies have cut ties with the National Rifle Association in the wake of the deadly Parkland, Florida school shooting which killed 17 people in February. Since the shooting, many Americans have lashed out at the NRA for their stance on assault rifles and lobbying efforts against tighter gun laws.
Although Yeti says that their policy change on discounts is not related to the boycott, the decision was made less than two months after groups began to cut ties with the pro-gun group. Bank of America joined the movement in mid-April when the company announced that it would no longer lend money to companies which produce assault-style weapons for civilians.

The letter characterizes this action as a withdrawal of support for youth outdoor recreational programs, stating, “YETI should be ashamed. They have declined to continue helping America’s young people enjoy outdoor recreational activities.”

Subsequent to this announcement, segments of the NRA membership and its supporters have expressed their dissatisfaction through demonstrations targeting Yeti’s premium coolers, which retail for approximately $250 to $1,300. Online footage depicts individuals employing explosives and firearms to destroy these containers. The world’s third-largest financial technology (fintech) company, Finastra, has been officially launched, following the union announced in March between Canada’s D+H and London-based Misys.

The big number in the reveal of the plug-in hybrid and all-electric versions of the Honda Clarity models was the 42-mile electric range for the PHEV and the 25.5-kWH battery in the EV. But there's another number that was revealed at the New York Auto Show that we should all be aware of: a mid-$30s price tag. Honda wouldn't give out the exact MSRP just yet (both of these vehicle will go on sale later this year, with the EV coming to select market first and then the PHEV getting nationwide availability at some point), but the official word is somewhere around $35,000 for either one.
This is a whole lot less than the Clarity Fuel Cell, which is only available for lease at $369 a month (plus $2,499 due at signing) for 36 months. There's no announced MSRP for the fuel cell, but a price tag of around $60,000 was bandied around in the past. You get $15,000 worth of "free" hydrogen over the course of the lease, and Honda VP of Environmental Business Development Office, Steve Center, says that Honda may move as many hydrogen units as all-electric models. "Maybe the fuel cell would [sell] more," Center said. "I think people are going to start to realize that a) it's an electric car, and b) you don't have any of the battery car limitations in terms of charge time or range. 'Cause that car won't have a 366 mile EPA range, and you don't have to have home to charge it."
The PHEV will outsell them both, obviously, because it will be available across the U.S., and not just in green car hot spots like the other powertrain options. If you want a deeper dive into the Clarity series, check out our full interview with Center here.

Honda has not yet released precise manufacturer's suggested retail prices, as both vehicles are scheduled for market introduction later this year. The battery-electric model will launch in select regional markets first, followed by the nationwide availability of the plug-in hybrid. Official estimates place the price for either model at approximately $35,000.

This represents a substantial reduction compared to the Clarity Fuel Cell vehicle, which is currently offered only through a lease program at $369 per month for 36 months, with $2,499 due at signing. While no MSRP has been announced for the fuel cell model, previous discussions suggested a price near $60,000. The lease includes an estimated $15,000 worth of hydrogen fuel. According to Steve Center, Vice President of the Environmental Business Development Office at Honda, sales volumes for the hydrogen fuel cell model may potentially match those of the battery-electric version. "Perhaps the fuel cell model will achieve higher sales," Center stated. "I believe consumers will begin to recognize that a) it is fundamentally an electric vehicle, and b) it eliminates typical battery-electric limitations regarding refueling duration and driving range. That vehicle will not have a 366-mile EPA range, nor does it require a home charging setup."

The plug-in hybrid variant is anticipated to outsell both the fuel cell and battery-electric models, attributable primarily to its planned availability across the entire United States, rather than being restricted to specific regional markets like the other powertrain options.

Dive Brief:
An independent school in Potomac, MD, gives seniors the option of completing a capstone project that not only allows them to integrate what they’ve learned in the lower grades, but also to conduct research on something they feel passionate about, Lisa Vardi, a teacher at the school, writes for EdSurge .
. Mentors are assigned to help students narrow their topics, set goals and conduct research for their year-long projects, and they include faculty members and members of the community.
The projects culminate with a symposium — attended by students, faculty members, parents and others in the community — at which the seniors can present their projects, and it has evolved over the years from a small evening gathering to a full-day event.
Dive Insight:
The capstone project at this particular school is available to honors-level students and lasts over the course of the year. While not all schools may be able to allow students to devote that much time to a project, educators are finding that there is value in letting students choose the topics they want to research or present as long as they demonstrate that they are meeting standards in their work. Not reserving such projects for high-achieving students might also be a way to motivate and engage students who might be struggling or hard to reach.
This post provides several suggestions for incorporating more student inquiry into existing classrooms and schedules, such as having a design challenge or a genius hour. While schools frequently ask students to work together on group projects, students can also benefit by pursuing something more personal. Such projects might also allow for more engagement with family and community members and help students learn more about their strengths. In this piece, Anne Keith, a former Montana teacher of the year talks about how passion projects are a way to increase engagement and teach skills, such as problem-solving, creativity, innovation and communication.

An independent school in Potomac, Maryland, offers its senior students the option to undertake a capstone project. According to Lisa Vardi, a teacher at the school writing for EdSurge, this initiative enables participants to synthesize knowledge acquired in earlier grades while conducting independent research on a subject of personal passion. Each student is paired with a mentor, drawn from either the faculty or the local community, who assists in refining the research topic, establishing objectives, and guiding the investigative process throughout the academic year. The project culminates in a symposium, attended by students, faculty, parents, and community members, where seniors present their work. This event has expanded significantly over time, evolving from a modest evening gathering into a comprehensive day-long occasion.

At this institution, the capstone is available primarily to honors-level students and spans the entire school year. Although not all schools may possess the resources to allocate such extensive time to individual projects, educators increasingly recognize the pedagogical value of permitting students to select their own research or presentation topics, provided they demonstrate adherence to academic standards. Furthermore, expanding access to such inquiry-based projects beyond only high-achieving students could serve as a means to motivate and engage those who may be struggling or otherwise disengaged.

Several strategies exist for integrating greater student-directed inquiry into existing curricula and schedules without major structural overhaul. Examples include implementing design challenges or dedicating specific periods, such as a “genius hour,” to independent exploration. While collaborative group projects remain common in schools, there is significant benefit in allowing students to pursue more individualized work. Such personal projects can also foster increased engagement with family and community resources and help students identify their own strengths and interests. Supporting this view, Anne Keith, a former Montana Teacher of the Year, notes in the article that passion-based projects are an effective method to enhance student engagement while cultivating essential skills, including problem-solving, creativity, innovation, and communication.

INDIANAPOLIS (WISH) — Indy Eleven diehard Mike Obremski gets interesting looks on game day, thanks to some unique company.
“Finally the team told the security staff, there is a guy coming in with a bag of bricks,” Obremski said.
Since 2014, Obremski has delivered personalized bricks to any Indy Eleven goal score or if the team’s goalie posts a shutout.
“It started with the phrase ‘Brick by Brick’ and it’s continued to gain steam over the last couple of seasons,” Obremski said. “Don Smart once asked me how he was going to get his through customs back to Jamaica.”
As for the Eleven’s leading scorer, forward Justin Braun, the bricks continue to add up at home.
“I have quite the pile going in my garage right now,” Braun said. “Once I figure out what to do with them, maybe it will turn into a sports memoribila room or something.”
Obremski’s love for this tradition and this team is as solid as the 100-year-old clay.
And for the past few years he needed it.
Just after moving to Indianapolis, Obremski suddenly lost his best friend. It was his mom, Marie.
“Before she passed away, she would see pictures of me in the stands and she would chuckle. She would be really excited,” Obremski said.
It’s apparent that this discovery of this afternoon oasis is no coincidence.
“Wife, daughter and Indy Eleven. That is just kind of how it goes.”
Sometimes, the roar of the crowd, really does reach the heavens.
Just ask the guy with the guy with the bricks.
rewrite:
In Indianapolis, a dedicated supporter of the Indy Eleven soccer club, Mike Obremski, attracts notable attention on match days due to an unusual practice. As Obremski explains, “Finally the team informed the security staff that there is a guy coming in with a bag of bricks.” Since 2014, Obremski has presented personalized bricks to any Indy Eleven player who scores a goal or to the goalkeeper upon achieving a shutout. This tradition originated from the club’s “Brick by Brick” motto and has grown in prominence over recent seasons. Obremski notes that former player Don Smart once inquired how he would transport his brick through customs to Jamaica.

For the team’s leading scorer, forward Justin Braun, the accumulating bricks are stored at his residence. Braun states, “I have quite the pile going in my garage right now. Once I figure out what to do with them, maybe it will turn into a sports memorabilia room or something.” Obremski’s commitment to this ritual and to the club remains as steadfast as the century-old clay from which the bricks are formed.

This tradition has also provided meaningful personal solace. Shortly after relocating to Indianapolis, Obremski experienced the sudden loss of his mother, Marie, who was his closest confidant. He recalls, “Before she passed away, she would see pictures of me in the stands and she would chuckle. She would be really excited.” For Obremski, this weekly sporting engagement represents a discovered refuge, intricately woven into his life alongside his family. He summarizes, “Wife, daughter, and Indy Eleven. That is just kind of how it goes.” At times, the communal fervor of the stadium seems to transcend the ordinary, a sentiment perhaps best understood by the individual bearing the bricks.

NEWCASTLE, England (AP) — Burnley struck late to extend Newcastle's winless run at home in the Premier League with a 1-1 draw on Wednesday.
Substitute Sam Vokes' header rebounded in off Newcastle goalkeeper Karl Darlow with five minutes remaining after new signing Kenedy appeared to have inspired the Magpies to victory.
The Brazilian, who has joined on loan from Chelsea until the end of the season, won a penalty that was subsequently missed, before setting up Jamaal Lascelles for the opening goal in the 65th minute.
Newcastle has now failed to win at St James' Park in eight Premier League games and is one of four teams just one point clear of the relegation zone.
Kenedy made an immediate impact as he won a penalty just 34 minutes into his Newcastle career, drawing a foul from Phil Bardsley only for Joselu to see his tame effort saved by Nick Pope.
It was Newcastle captain Lascelles who was the eventual beneficiary of Kenedy's persistence, heading home a perfectly placed corner.
Just five minutes from the end, Newcastle was unlucky to be denied its first home league victory since October. Vokes' header hit the crossbar, before bouncing in via a deflection off the helpless Darlow.
Burnley hasn't won in eight Premier League games, but ended a three-match losing streak and moves up to seventh in the table.
rewrite:
On Wednesday, a late equalizer from Burnley resulted in a 1-1 draw at St James' Park, thereby extending Newcastle United's winless run in home Premier League fixtures. The match appeared destined for a home victory following the decisive influence of debutant Kenedy, on loan from Chelsea. The Brazilian midfielder won a penalty, which was subsequently missed by Joselu in the first half, before providing the assist for captain Jamaal Lascelles's 65th-minute headed goal from a corner. However, with merely five minutes of regulation time remaining, substitute Sam Vokes secured a point for the visitors. His headed effort struck the crossbar and fortuitously rebounded into the net via Newcastle goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

This result prolongs Newcastle's concerning home form to eight league matches without a victory, situating the club just one point above the relegation zone. Conversely, the draw concludes a three-match losing streak for Burnley, elevating them to seventh position in the league table, despite their own parallel run of eight games without a win. The encounter ultimately underscored the fine margins defining outcomes in the Premier League, with Newcastle denied a pivotal victory by a late and somewhat unfortunate deflection.

Art curator Diana Larrea has been called the “Princess of Miami Street Art” because of her role in the increasingly relevant urban art movement. The Peruvian born photographer documents the street art scene of Miami and, according to her, “the walls have become the news.”
Larrea began photographing the street art in her city in 2010 and over time she came to know the artists behind the murals and paste-ups as well. Their stories and where they came from jumped out at her and held her attention. Now, she can’t go anywhere in Miami without craving fresh art.
“I’m always discovering new murals,” Larrea says. “It’s the best when I discover them running.”
A regular runner through the sunny streets of Miami, Larrea finds something new to love about her city every time she laces up her shoes. It’s her favorite way to get inspired, even if it doesn’t lead to the most cohesive runs.
“Sometimes I have to stop running to read something,” she explains. “It just gets your attention. ”
Currently, Larrea is particularly interested in raising the voices of females in the street art community. She views it as her duty. Women are having their day in the street art world and if Larrea can show how hard they work she feels she’ll be doing her part for the betterment of everybody. Join us as we follow her through the streets of Miami — and get acquainted with her bold mission.
rewrite:
Art curator Diana Larrea, recognized as the “Princess of Miami Street Art” for her significant role within the burgeoning urban art movement, is a Peruvian-born photographer dedicated to documenting Miami’s street art scene. She posits that “the walls have become the news,” framing public art as a vital medium for contemporary discourse. Commencing her photographic documentation in 2010, Larrea has since cultivated relationships with the artists behind the murals and paste-ups, finding herself captivated by their personal narratives and origins. This engagement has fostered a persistent attentiveness; she now navigates Miami with a constant desire to encounter new artistic expressions.

“I am always discovering new murals,” Larrea notes, “and it is most rewarding when I encounter them while running.” As a regular runner traversing Miami’s sunlit streets, she finds each outing reveals novel appreciations for the city. This practice serves as her primary source of inspiration, albeit one that disrupts the continuity of her exercise. “Occasionally, I must halt my run to engage with a text-based piece,” she explains. “It simply commands attention.”

Presently, Larrea is particularly focused on amplifying the voices of women within the street art community, which she considers a professional imperative. As women gain prominence in this domain, she believes highlighting their dedicated labor contributes to the broader advancement of the field. This examination follows Larrea through Miami’s urban landscape to elucidate her determined mission.

FREMANTLE has already received a huge boost from its top draft pick, with talented young midfielder Andrew Brayshaw signing a two-year contract extension with the Dockers.
The deal is on top of the initial two-year contract Brayshaw signed when he was recruited to Fremantle via last month’s national draft and will keep the teenager at the club until 2021.
The Dockers claimed Brayshaw with Pick 2 at the draft, with the midfielder emerging as one of the best junior prospects following a promising TAC Cup season with Sandringham.
A prolific ball winner who uses the footy effectively, he impressed with his spread from stoppages and averaged 25 disposals and 6.6 tackles per game with the Dragons.
“I heard that the club was interested in re-signing me and I’ve been treated really well here and everyone’s been really welcoming, so I just snatched it up as quickly as I could,” Brayshaw said.
“I definitely feel there’s something special going on at the club and I’m really excited for the next few years and I definitely want to be a part of that.”
Brayshaw was Fremantle’s first of two top-five selections at the draft, with the Dockers also claiming fellow Vic Metro midfielder Adam Cerra with Pick 5.
Brayshaw is the brother of Melbourne midfielder Angus, while his other brother Hamish was recruited to West Coast with Pick 68 in last month’s national draft.
rewrite:

This agreement extends the initial two-year contract Brayshaw entered upon his recruitment in the recent national draft, thereby binding the promising midfielder to the club until the conclusion of the 2021 season. Fremantle utilised the second overall selection to acquire Brayshaw, a player widely regarded as an elite junior prospect following an outstanding TAC Cup campaign with the Sandringham Dragons. Demonstrated by an average of 25 disposals and 6.6 tackles per game, his effectiveness as a prolific ball-winner and his capacity to spread effectively from stoppages were particularly notable.

Brayshaw expressed immediate enthusiasm for the extension, stating, “Upon learning of the club’s interest, I seized the opportunity without hesitation, having been treated exceptionally well and feeling genuinely welcomed. I am convinced a special culture is developing here, and I am eager to contribute to the club’s trajectory in the coming years.” Brayshaw represented the first of Fremantle’s two top-five draft acquisitions, with the club also selecting Victorian midfielder Adam Cerra with the fifth pick. The Brayshaw family exhibits a strong presence in the Australian Football League; Andrew’s brother, Angus, plays for Melbourne, while another brother, Hamish, was selected by West Coast with pick 68 in the same draft.

HONG KONG, March 31 Hong Kong's private home prices climbed for an 11th straight month in February, hitting another record high, a government index released on Friday showed.
In February, Hong Kong's private home prices index rose 1.1 percent from the previous month, to 312.8 from 309.4, according to data from the Rating and Valuation Department. The February figure was 14.3 percent higher than a year earlier.
The Asian financial hub has the world's least affordable private housing and flats cost 18.1 times the gross annual median income, according to a survey by Demographia, a private firm.
Hong Kong's newly-selected leader Carrie Lam, who will take office in July, said on Tuesday she was "very determined" to tackle the high cost of housing, one of the top concerns of foreign business executives about the city.
The government has vowed to increase housing supply and has raised stamp duties to try to rein in prices, but to little effect.
Property developers from mainland China have been submitting record-breaking bids in Hong Kong land auctions, which is likely to keep driving housing prices up. (Reporting by Venus Wu; Editing by Richard Borsuk)
rewrite:
According to data released on Friday, March 31, by the Hong Kong Rating and Valuation Department, the territory's private residential property price index increased for an eleventh consecutive month in February, reaching a new historic peak. The index rose by 1.1 percent month-on-month, from 309.4 in January to 312.8 in February, representing a year-on-year increase of 14.3 percent. This sustained appreciation occurs within a market already characterized by extreme unaffordability; a survey by the private firm Demographia indicates Hong Kong's private housing costs are 18.1 times the gross annual median income, the highest such ratio globally.

In response to this critical issue, which ranks among the foremost concerns for foreign business executives in the city, Chief Executive-elect Carrie Lam stated on Tuesday that she is "very determined" to address high housing costs upon assuming office in July. While the government has pledged to augment housing supply and implemented elevated stamp duties to moderate prices, these measures have thus far yielded limited effect. Concurrently, record-breaking bids from mainland Chinese property developers in Hong Kong land auctions are exerting further upward pressure on the market, suggesting continued price escalation.
