By Margaret Matibiri
A Nigerian couple reportedly teamed up with a Bluffhill man and went on shopping spree of expensive phones and groceries using cloned American Visa Cards.
Oluwaseya Ajibala Ogbechi (43), Ruth Ruramai Ogbechi (28) and Olga Tapiwa Tapambwa (29) reportedly duped supermarkets and gadgets shops of groceries and Apple iPhone 7 plus phones worth over $20 000.
The trio appeared before Harare magistrate Ms Barbra Chimboza facing seven counts of fraud which is defined as unauthorised use or possession of credit or debit card.
The trio will appear before the same magistrate today for bail ruling.
Prosecuting, Ms Linda Gadzikwa alleged that on May 8, the trio used a cloned ATM Visa Card belonging to a customer of Chase Bank of United States of America (USA) to buy groceries worth $5 627.60 at SPAR Supermarket in Ballantyne suburb, Harare.
The court heard that Chase Bank discovered that the card was being fraudulently used in Zimbabwe and alerted the complainant, CABS Bank.
It is alleged that the trio was captured on CCTV camera in the shop while transacting with the Visa Card.
It is the State’s case that on April 12, the three accused persons used a cloned ATM Visa Card belonging to a customer of National Association a USA company to transact.
The trio allegedly bought groceries in supermarkets around Harare, and also food at Chang Thai Restaurant all of which was worth $1 349.54.
In total, they spent $21 687.63 The Herald
rewrite:
A Nigerian couple, in collaboration with a resident of Bluffhill, allegedly engaged in a series of fraudulent transactions utilizing cloned United States-issued Visa cards to procure high-value electronics and groceries. The accused individuals—Oluwaseya Ajibala Ogbechi (43), Ruth Ruramai Ogbechi (28), and Olga Tapiwa Tapambwa (29)—are reported to have defrauded various retail establishments, obtaining goods including Apple iPhone 7 Plus devices and supermarket provisions with a total value exceeding US$20,000. The trio appeared before Harare Magistrate Ms. Barbra Chimboza, facing seven counts of fraud, legally defined as the unauthorized possession or use of a credit or debit card. Their bail ruling is scheduled before the same magistrate today.

According to the prosecution, led by Ms. Linda Gadzikwa, the defendants allegedly employed a cloned ATM Visa card, issued to a customer of the United States-based Chase Bank, to purchase groceries valued at US$5,627.60 from a SPAR Supermarket in Harare’s Ballantyne suburb on May 8. The court was informed that Chase Bank detected the fraudulent activity occurring in Zimbabwe and subsequently notified the complainant, CABS Bank. Prosecution evidence indicates the transactions were captured by the supermarket’s closed-circuit television system. Furthermore, the State alleges that on April 12, the accused utilized another cloned ATM Visa card, belonging to a customer of the National Association, a U.S. company. This card was used for transactions totaling US$1,349.54 across various Harare supermarkets and the Chang Thai Restaurant. The cumulative value of the alleged fraudulent acquisitions amounts to US$21,687.63.

Image caption Wiltshire Council said the trees were in a "poor condition"
A town which had its trees chopped down in a council blunder the night before being judged for Britain in Bloom has been awarded a gold.
Volunteers were left "horrified" when Wiltshire Council cut down trees in the Market Place in Melksham ahead of a South West Britain in Bloom bid.
Despite the tree stumps and "enormous mess" left, the town was given its highest award to date by judges.
Kathy Iles, chair of Melksham Bloomers, said it was "absolutely amazing".
The trees in the town's Market Place were removed by the council as part of a planned redevelopment.
Ms Iles said she had been walking "the route for a last check" when she saw contractors cutting them down and making an "enormous mess".
Despite trying to get them to stop, the area was left with just a tree stump and a half-felled tree with "Christmas lights dangling from it".
Image caption The trees were removed from Melksham's Market Place by the council as part of a planned redevelopment
"It wasn't possible to hide it and there was no way we could cover it up, it was just really unfortunate," said Ms Iles.
"But there's an RHS judging rule that any areas under redevelopment are not judged.
"When they announced we got the gold, I'm surprised they didn't hear me scream in Melksham. It was the most incredible feeling."
Wiltshire Council apologised but said the trees had been in poor condition and were removed as "part of ongoing investment in Melksham".
rewrite:
In an incident preceding a Britain in Bloom competition, the town of Melksham in Wiltshire was awarded a gold award despite the untimely removal of trees in its Market Place by the local council. Wiltshire Council had undertaken the removal as a component of a scheduled redevelopment initiative, stating the trees were in a state of poor condition and characterizing the action as part of ongoing investment in the town. Volunteers from the Melksham Bloomers group, however, were reportedly horrified to discover contractors felling the trees on the eve of the South West Britain in Bloom judging, leaving behind tree stumps and what was described as an enormous mess.

Kathy Iles, chair of Melksham Bloomers, recounted discovering the contractors during a final inspection of the judging route, noting the unsuccessful attempt to halt the work. The area was left with a visible stump and a partially felled tree adorned with dangling Christmas lights, a situation Ms. Iles deemed unfortunately impossible to conceal. Nevertheless, under Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) judging guidelines, areas under active redevelopment are exempt from assessment. Consequently, the town received its highest award to date. Ms. Iles described the announcement of the gold award as eliciting an incredible feeling of amazement. While Wiltshire Council has apologized for the mishap, it reiterated that the removal was conducted due to the trees' poor condition and aligns with broader improvement plans for Melksham.

I urge everyone to visit the memorial to see it for themselves.

Shields, and new housing is being developed at the Avenue, High Point and Whisky Bends sites in Whitley Bay.

Our young people are always so passionate and enthusiastic about playing an active part in our community, and I hope they all have a great experience during the week.
rewrite:
It is a great pleasure to engage with constituents from across North Tyneside, and I was particularly gratified by the substantial attendance at my public listening event in Wallsend during September. Such forums provide a valuable opportunity for residents to directly communicate the local issues of greatest concern to them. I extend a cordial invitation to all interested parties to attend the subsequent event, scheduled for Saturday, November 18, at The Beacon Centre in North Shields.

Last month, I was honoured to attend the unveiling of the Fiddler’s Green memorial in North Shields. This aesthetically accomplished sculpture serves as a profoundly fitting tribute to the many fishermen who lost their lives in the course of their occupation. Witnessing hundreds of individuals gather on the Fish Quay to commemorate our maritime heritage and honour those lost at sea was a deeply moving experience. I would encourage everyone to visit the memorial personally. I reiterate my congratulations to all who contributed to the fundraising efforts required to realise this commendable project.

Regeneration initiatives throughout the borough are progressing rapidly. Planning permission has been secured for new residential developments at Northumberland Square in North Shields, with additional housing projects advancing at the Avenue, High Point, and Whisky Bends locations in Whitley Bay.

The forthcoming Local Democracy Week will involve young people across North Tyneside in educational activities designed to explore the meaning and practice of democracy. The consistent passion and enthusiasm demonstrated by our youth in seeking active civic participation is most encouraging, and I hope their engagements during the week are both informative and rewarding.

Alfa Romeo Sauber F1 Team driver Marcus Ericsson has predicted that tyre management will be crucial in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
Degradation has been a notable factor in the first two races at the Baku City Circuit, however this year sees a different challenge, with the event moved forward from its usual June slot. Early weather forecasts suggest cooler temperatures, something that may ease the Swede’s worries.
“Tyre management will be a key factor, as the degradation of the tyres is quite high during the race,” said Ericsson. “It is quite a cool track, with a good mix of high-speed sectors and challenging corners.”
Ericsson looked at the additional challenges posed by Formula 1‘s newest street circuit, putting particular emphasis on the narrowest corner on the calendar – known colloquially as the ‘castle chicane’, or Turns 8 and 9. The uphill right hander is just 7.6 metres wide, and was the site of a red flag inducing crash in FIA Formula 2‘s feature race.
“The race in Baku will be our first street race of the season,” added Ericsson. “What is special about the track is that it features some twisty parts, mainly around the castle.
“The track is very narrow there, and you must be very precise as a driver.”
Baku also boasts the longest straight on the Formula 1 calendar, a 2.2 kilometre long stretch along Neftchilar Avenue, where the pits are located. Mixed with several slow corners, the circuit demands a lot of different strengths from the car, making car setup a fine balance.
“Another challenge will be to set up the car to suit the demands of the circuit,” the 27-year-old noted. “I look forward to going to Baku, and continuing our strong performance from the first three races of the year.”
Courtesy of Ericsson at the Bahrain Grand Prix, Sauber scored their earliest points finish in three years – when Ericsson and then team-mate Felipe Nasr both finished in the top ten at the 2015 Australian Grand Prix.

Preliminary meteorological projections indicate potentially cooler ambient temperatures, a condition which may alleviate some concerns regarding thermal degradation.

Ericsson elaborated, stating, "Tyre management will be a key factor, as the degradation of the tyres is quite high during the race. It is quite a cool track, with a good mix of high-speed sectors and challenging corners." He further examined the unique demands of Formula 1's newest street circuit, highlighting the notably narrow castle chicane, comprising Turns 8 and 9. This uphill right-hand turn, measuring merely 7.6 metres in width, previously caused a red flag incident during an FIA Formula 2 feature race. "The race in Baku will be our first street race of the season," Ericsson added. "What is special about the track is that it features some twisty parts, mainly around the castle. The track is very narrow there, and you must be very precise as a driver."

The circuit also incorporates the championship's longest straight, a 2.2-kilometre section on Neftchilar Avenue adjacent to the pit lane. This high-speed segment, combined with several technical, low-speed corners, imposes a wide array of performance requirements on the car, necessitating a carefully calibrated setup compromise. "Another challenge will be to set up the car to suit the demands of the circuit," noted the 27-year-old driver.

Ericsson expressed optimism for the event, citing the team's positive start to the season. His point-scoring finish at the Bahrain Grand Prix marked Sauber's earliest points achievement in three years, a precedent last set when Ericsson and former teammate Felipe Nasr both finished within the top ten at the 2015 Australian Grand Prix. He concluded, "I look forward to going to Baku, and continuing our strong performance from the first three races of the year."

An East Texas church is going the extra mile to help those in need this Super Bowl Sunday.
As a part of Souper Bowl of Caring the First Presbyterian Church in Tyler has been collecting canned goods since the beginning of January.
A competition among Sunday School Classes has led to the collection of over 7,000 cans.
“This is a very tangible way for them to help and to see what their hard work promoting and pushing this can do,” says Neil McKown, the youth minister at First Presbyterian. “Just by putting their minds to it, by asking by talking to people and by sharing that there are real issues in our community.”
The cans will be picked up by PATH, People Attempting To Help, on Sunday.
First Presbyterian has collected enough cans to stock the food pantry for one week and feed 440 families.
For more information about the Souper Bowl of Caring or to make a donation head to their website.
rewrite: In observance of the upcoming Super Bowl Sunday, the First Presbyterian Church in Tyler, Texas, is undertaking a significant charitable initiative. The congregation is participating in the Souper Bowl of Caring, a national movement, and has been gathering canned food donations since early January. A coordinated effort among its Sunday School classes, framed as a friendly competition, has resulted in the accumulation of more than 7,000 canned items. According to youth minister Neil McKown, this project offers participants a tangible means of assisting others and witnessing the direct impact of their advocacy and labor. He emphasizes that through dedicated focus and community dialogue regarding local needs, substantial support can be mobilized. The collected donations will be distributed this Sunday by PATH (People Attempting To Help), a local organization. This contribution is sufficient to supply the affiliated food pantry for one week, providing for approximately 440 families. Further details regarding the Souper Bowl of Caring campaign and donation procedures are available through its official website.

BELLEVILLE TOWNSHIP, N.J. (CBSNewYork) — Talk about a good old fashioned blossom battle.
When people think about cherry blossoms, they naturally will think of Washington D.C.
But you don’t need to head down I-95 to find the very best blossom bloom this spring.
Just head to Belleville, New Jersey — right on the border of Newark.
“People come from all over to see these cherry blossoms,” one woman told CBS2’s Scott Rapoport.
Right in Essex County — far away from inside the Beltway — you’ll find a burgeoning bumper crop of cherry trees. There are over 4,000 in Branch Brook Park alone, either in bloom or about to bloom.
“It’s just like something out of a painting,” Belleville historian Michael Perrone says. “It’s a living painting. That’s how I’d describe it.”
Perrone says throughout the town you can find almost 8,000 cherry blossom trees — more than double the 3,700 that grace the streets of our nation’s capital.
According to Perrone, the numbers simply don’t lie.
“There’s no question that Belleville is the cherry blossom capital of America,” he said.
Perrone says the town’s cherry blossom bonanza began in 1927, when 2,000 were first planted as a gift from Caroline Bamberger — one of the founders of the once famous Bamberger’s department store.
Since then, more and more have been planted. In turn, the town’s collection has grown and grown.
“There’s just a feeling of calmness when you see them,” one woman said.
The famed blossoms are featured on the township’s seal, flags, and even the police patches of Belleville’s finest.
“It’s something we’re proud of,” Police Chief Mark Minichini tells CBS2. “We want to show it to the world.”
It’s a source of inspiration to both those who live in the town, and those who come from far and wide to visit what’s known around the area as the “Cherry Blossom Capital of America.”
If you plan on seeing the blossoms in bloom, Perrone says some trees in the park and most trees in the town will be blooming later this week or next.
rewrite:
While Washington, D.C., is widely recognized for its celebrated cherry blossoms, a lesser-known but arguably more significant collection exists in Belleville, New Jersey, situated adjacent to Newark. This Essex County township presents a compelling alternative to the famed Tidal Basin displays. Branch Brook Park alone contains over 4,000 cherry trees, currently in or approaching peak bloom, contributing to a total of nearly 8,000 such trees throughout the municipality. This figure more than doubles the approximately 3,700 trees adorning the nation’s capital.

According to local historian Michael Perrone, this distinction is unambiguous. “There’s no question that Belleville is the cherry blossom capital of America,” Perrone asserts. The origin of this extensive arboreal collection dates to 1927, when Caroline Bamberger, a co-founder of the former Bamberger’s department store, donated and planted 2,000 trees. Subsequent plantings have steadily expanded the town’s inventory. The cultural significance of the blossoms is deeply embedded in local identity, featuring prominently on the township seal, municipal flags, and even the patches of the Belleville Police Department. Police Chief Mark Minichini notes, “It’s something we’re proud of. We want to show it to the world.”

Residents and visitors alike describe the bloom as a profoundly aesthetic experience, with Perrone likening the spectacle to “a living painting” and others citing the pervasive sense of tranquility it inspires. The phenomenon has established Belleville as a regional destination, attracting individuals specifically to witness its springtime display. For those planning a visit, phenological reports indicate that blossoms in the park and throughout the town will reach peak bloom in the coming week. Thus, Belleville substantiates its claim as a preeminent center for cherry blossom appreciation in the United States, offering an accessible and quantitatively superior display to the more traditionally recognized location.

Many have learned the hard way that if you kick the beehive and mess with Beyonce, you’re gonna get stung. Well, now you can add a young brewer in Brooklyn to Beyonce’s list of persona non grata.
Katarina Martinez is an up-and-coming brewmaster in Brooklyn. Her Lineup Brewing puts out the usual list of IPAs, pale ales, and stouts that have become the backbone of many a microbrewery. Martinez’s twist is that she names her beers based on what inspires her in life. So Lineup’s session IPA is called “In the Defense of Ghosting.” Their cream ale is called “Shame.” The East-coast IPA is called “Notorious.” You get the (millennial) drift.
Tonight’s release was brilliant! Cannot wait for Saturday at @beerkarma.bstc 🙏🏼 photo by: @grassowhat A post shared by Lineup Brewing (@lineupbrewing) on Nov 30, 2017 at 7:53pm PST
Martinez’s latest inspiration was Queen Bey herself. It was pretty simple for Martinez — Beyonce inspires her and she wanted to honor that with a beer. So a pilsner called “Bïeryoncé” was born. But, according to Pitchfork, Beyonce didn’t see it that clearcut. Nor was she flattered. The pop star’s legal team issued a cease and desist order to Lineup to immediately stop making the beer. So, now, “Bïeryoncé” will be relegated to the ranks of other misfires like “John Lemon” and all those DoughP puns.
Martinez had hoped Beyonce would have taken the beer in stride. “We’re disappointed she didn’t take it as a compliment, but oh well,” Martinez lamented before moving on, “It was fun while it lasted!”
If you’re in the New York City area, you still might be able to snag a can or two of “Bïeryoncé” while supplies last. Who knows, they may be a collector’s item one day. And if not, at least you can drink that tasty pilsner inside.
🤫 *shh* did you guys know we’re having our first can release next week? #bïeryoncé A post shared by Lineup Brewing (@lineupbrewing) on Nov 22, 2017 at 10:57am PST
(Via Pitchfork)
rewrite:
Numerous parties have discovered through experience that provoking Beyoncé Knowles-Carter incurs significant repercussions. A recent addition to those who have encountered her disfavor is a novice brewer based in Brooklyn. Katarina Martinez, an emerging brewmaster and founder of Lineup Brewing, produces a standard portfolio of India pale ales, pale ales, and stouts typical of many microbreweries. Martinez’s distinctive approach involves naming her beers after personal inspirations. Consequently, the brewery’s session IPA is titled “In the Defense of Ghosting,” its cream ale is named “Shame,” and its East Coast IPA is called “Notorious,” reflecting a millennial sensibility.

Martinez’s most recent inspiration derived from the iconic performer Beyoncé. Her intention was straightforward: to pay homage through a beer named in her honor. Thus, a pilsner labeled “Bïeryoncé” was created. However, as reported by Pitchfork, Beyoncé’s interpretation diverged markedly; she was not flattered. Legal representatives for the entertainer issued a cease-and-desist order demanding the immediate discontinuation of the beer. Consequently, “Bïeryoncé” joins a catalog of unsuccessful naming ventures, such as “John Lemon” and various “DoughP” puns.

Martinez expressed hope that Beyoncé would have received the tribute favorably. “We are disappointed she did not interpret it as a compliment, but such is the situation,” Martinez stated, adding philosophically, “It was an enjoyable endeavor while it persisted.” For consumers in the New York City vicinity, limited quantities of “Bïeryoncé” may remain available. These products could potentially attain collectible status; if not, they at least offer the consumption of a well-crafted pilsner.

This incident underscores the legal and reputational risks associated with employing celebrity names or likenesses for commercial purposes without authorization, even when intended as tribute. It further illustrates the challenges small businesses face when navigating intellectual property law against entities possessing considerable legal resources. The episode serves as a cautionary tale regarding the boundaries of artistic inspiration and brand protection in contemporary commerce.

Dead and dismembered goats, chickens and other animals were found in a San Antonio-area home Friday night after police responded to calls of a suspected animal sacrifice ritual, authorities said.
At least a dozen people were arrested and charged with animal cruelty, the San Antonio Express-News reported.
“There’s a misunderstanding but we’re not going to talk about it,” a woman at the home told Fox 29 San Antonio.
Bexar County sheriff’s deputies found the group inside a garage where a woman was cutting up animal parts and another person was draining the blood of a chicken into a container, Sgt. Elizabeth Gonzalez said.
“It appears that they were having some sort of unknown ritual,” Gonzalez said.
Officers found 11 of the suspects gathered in a circle, officials told the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.
Deputies additionally found multiple dead and mutilated animals in the residence, including goats and chickens.
As many as 14 people, men and women ages 23 to 65, were arrested and will face misdemeanor charges of cruelty to non-livestock animals, authorities said. The offense is a Class A misdemeanor, unless it is enhanced because of previous related offenses, they said.
Bexar County Animal Control Services removed several live animals from the scene, the report said.
Authorities identified 11 of the suspects: Alexander Gene Campos, 23; Ivan Felipe Gonzalez, 24; Carmen Maria Gonzalez-Trujillo, 41; Cynthia Gabriell Martinez, 29; Liza Mercado, 46; Marie Galan Murcia, 65; Ramon Patino Jr., 65; Luiz Rodriguez Ortiz, 41; Robert Talamantez, 55; Irma Garza Talamantez, 64; and Arteaga Ariel Torres, 39.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
rewrite:
On Friday evening, law enforcement authorities in the San Antonio area responded to reports of a suspected animal sacrifice ritual, discovering deceased and dismembered goats, chickens, and other animals within a residence. According to official statements, Bexar County sheriff’s deputies encountered a group inside a garage where one individual was segmenting animal remains while another drained blood from a chicken into a container. Sergeant Elizabeth Gonzalez indicated the activity appeared to constitute an unspecified ritual. Officers reported locating eleven individuals gathered in a circle within the property.

Deputies subsequently found multiple deceased and mutilated animals at the location. As many as fourteen individuals, ranging in age from 23 to 65, were arrested and face misdemeanor charges of cruelty to non-livestock animals. The offense is classified as a Class A misdemeanor, subject to enhancement based on prior related offenses. Bexar County Animal Control Services removed several living animals from the premises.

Authorities publicly identified eleven of those apprehended: Alexander Gene Campos, 23; Ivan Felipe Gonzalez, 24; Carmen Maria Gonzalez-Trujillo, 41; Cynthia Gabriell Martinez, 29; Liza Mercado, 46; Marie Galan Murcia, 65; Ramon Patino Jr., 65; Luiz Rodriguez Ortiz, 41; Robert Talamantez, 55; Irma Garza Talamantez, 64; and Arteaga Ariel Torres, 39. A representative present at the scene declined to comment substantively, stating only, “There’s a misunderstanding but we’re not going to talk about it.”

ROCKWALL, Texas (WFLA) — A high school soccer coach in Texas has been placed on leave after a team photo surfaced that some are calling offensive.
The photo shows Marco Duran, the varsity girls soccer coach at Rockwall Heath High School, and his team posing with their middle fingers up.
“Even if the kids are 18, that should not be happening in school at all,” one parent, Todd Christian, said. “I believe the man should be fired on the spot.”
Coach Duran, who is also a sign language teacher, is now on paid leave per district policy. According to the school’s website, he has been a coach and a teacher for 16 years.
“I would have to say looking at the photo and looking at the man smiling he absolutely had to not be using judgment,” Christian said.
Many parents agree with Christian, saying they’re upset about the picture. And even the parents who said it was much ado about nothing admitted they questioned the coach’s judgment.
“Because of course, social media, everybody sees everything,” parent Ashanti Wright said. “All it takes is one post and it’s gone everywhere. Obviously, he didn’t care enough about his job or his students to not let them post something like that.”
Others weighed in on social media, according to CNN affiliate KTVT, and defended the coach saying he photobombed the picture and didn’t know what the girls were doing with their hands.
The school says it’s also taken action against the students in the photo, but did not say what the action was.
rewrite:
A varsity girls’ soccer coach at Rockwall Heath High School in Texas has been placed on administrative leave following the circulation of a team photograph deemed inappropriate. The image depicts coach Marco Duran posing alongside team members, all of whom are displaying raised middle fingers. The incident has prompted significant concern among parents and community members regarding professional conduct within an educational setting.

Parental response has been largely critical. One parent, Todd Christian, asserted that such behavior is unacceptable in a school environment, regardless of the students’ age, and called for immediate termination. He further questioned the coach’s judgment, citing Duran’s apparent smile in the photograph. While some parents dismissed the controversy as exaggerated, they concurrently acknowledged a lapse in professional discernment. Concerns were also raised regarding the dissemination of the image on social media, with one parent, Ashanti Wright, suggesting the posting indicated a disregard for both professional standing and student welfare.

In contrast, some commentary reported by CNN affiliate KTVT has defended the coach, claiming he inadvertently entered the photograph and was unaware of the gesture being made by the students. Coach Duran, who also serves as a sign language instructor and has sixteen years of tenure within the district, has been placed on paid leave pending investigation, in accordance with standard district policy. The school district has confirmed that disciplinary measures have also been taken against the students involved, though the specific nature of those actions has not been disclosed.

rewrite:

A 60-year-old would-be paedophile has been jailed after being tricked into meeting a non-existent schoolgirl for sex in a car park.
Douglas Thorpe, of St John’s Bank in South Chailey, in Lewes near Brighton, was sentenced to three years and four months in prison at a hearing yesterday at Bolton Crown Court.
The court heard how Thorpe drove 250 miles to meet Kim, a “14-year-old girl” at Tesco in Hindley, before being apprehended by a man called Darren Minto who runs a paedophile hunting site called “creep catchers.” Judge Timothy Stead heard how Thorpe had sent explicit messages, including a picture of his penis, to Kim before grooming “her” and meeting up for sex.
Once he had been caught, police searched the would-be paedophile, finding condoms and lubricant in his pockets. Thorpe initially denied the charges but later admitted his intentions. Prosecution barrister, Justin Hayhoe, told Judge Stead how the two had begun talking on a social media site called “Scout”.
“During that time it was established how old she was,” he said. “The girl (Minto) confirmed he was a girl aged 14 from Wigan. His response to that was “I could get into trouble for chatting to you lol, I’m older than you.”
“He then continued to start about grooming what he believed to be a 14-year-old girl. He told her he loved her.”
Mr Hayhoe read out messages from Thorpe calling his potential victim a “sexy girl” and saying it was a “pity” he couldn’t see her in school uniform.
The messages became more explicit over a series of weeks.
The pair arranged to meet up, Thorpe also told “Kim” that he had bought her an iPhone 5 for her 14th birthday, which was later found in his car following his arrest. Defending Thorpe, Ms Janet Ironfield said: “I hope i don’t speculate, at the time of his offending he was approaching a crisis in his personal life or mental health. He recognises a need for professional help of varying kinds.”
rewrite:
A sixty-year-old man has been imprisoned following his attempt to meet a fictitious minor for sexual purposes. Douglas Thorpe, of St John’s Bank, South Chailey, Lewes, was sentenced to three years and four months’ imprisonment at Bolton Crown Court. The court was informed that Thorpe had travelled approximately 250 miles to a Tesco car park in Hindley to meet “Kim,” whom he believed to be a 14-year-old girl. He was instead apprehended by Darren Minto, an individual operating a group known as “creep catchers” which targets suspected child predators.

Evidence presented to Judge Timothy Stead detailed that Thorpe had engaged in explicit online communication with the decoy profile, including transmitting an indecent image of himself. He subsequently engaged in grooming behaviour and arranged a meeting for sexual activity. Upon his detention, police discovered condoms and lubricant in his possession. Thorpe initially denied the allegations but later pleaded guilty to attempting to engage in sexual communication with a child and arranging a child sex offence.

Prosecuting barrister Justin Hayhoe outlined that contact originated on the social platform “Scout,” where the decoy’s age was explicitly stated as 14. Thorpe’s response acknowledged the legal risk, stating, “I could get into trouble for chatting to you lol, I’m older than you.” Notwithstanding this, he proceeded to express affection and initiate grooming. Mr. Hayhoe read messages in which Thorpe referred to the decoy as a “sexy girl” and lamented not seeing her in school uniform. The exchanges grew increasingly explicit over several weeks, culminating in the arranged meeting. In mitigation, defence counsel Janet Ironfield submitted that her client was experiencing significant personal and potential mental health difficulties at the time of the offences and acknowledges a requirement for professional intervention. The sentence reflects the seriousness of the planned offending.

Zimbabwe’s wildlife agency said on Tuesday it was investigating allegations that a South African national bribed officials to allow a Colorado-based tourist to take the ivory tusks of an elephant illegally shot in a Zimbabwe game park.
Their inquiry comes after U.S. prosecutors accused the South African, who was with a hunting party in Gonarezhou National Park in southern Zimbabwe, of paying up to $8,000 in bribes to Zimbabwean government officials to kill the elephant inside the park and to have the animal’s ivory released.
“We are investigating the matter,” said Tinashe Farawo, spokesman for the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority. He gave no further details.
A government official, who declined to be named because he was not authorised to speak to the media, said Zimbabwean authorities had contacted the South African but he was not forthcoming with information.
A statement by the U.S. Department of Justice in Colorado dated May 21 said the South African conspired with the unidentified Colorado hunter to export the tusks by falsely saying in official documents the hunter was a South African resident and that the elephant was shot outside Gonarezhou.
It is illegal under Zimbabwean law for hunters to shoot animals inside a state game park.
In 2015, a U.S. dentist touched off a global storm when he killed a rare black-maned lion named Cecil with a bow and arrow outside Hwange National Park in western Zimbabwe, forcing the United States to suspend importation of elephant trophies from Africa.-Reuters
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority announced it has initiated an investigation into allegations that a South African national bribed officials to facilitate the illegal export of ivory tusks from an elephant shot within a Zimbabwean national park by a hunter from Colorado, United States. This inquiry follows charges by U.S. prosecutors that the individual, part of a hunting party in Gonarezhou National Park in southern Zimbabwe, disbursed up to $8,000 in bribes to government officials to authorize both the elephant's killing inside the park and the subsequent release of its ivory. Tinashe Farawo, a spokesperson for the authority, confirmed, "We are investigating the matter," while declining to provide additional details.

An unnamed Zimbabwean government official, unauthorized to speak publicly, indicated that authorities had contacted the South African suspect but had not received cooperative information. According to a May 21 statement from the U.S. Department of Justice in Colorado, the South African conspired with the unidentified Colorado hunter to export the tusks by falsely declaring in official documentation that the hunter was a South African resident and that the elephant was killed outside Gonarezhou's boundaries. Zimbabwean law expressly prohibits hunting within state game parks.

This incident recalls the 2015 international controversy involving a U.S. dentist who killed Cecil, a rare black-maned lion, outside Hwange National Park, which subsequently led the United States to suspend imports of African elephant trophies.

MADINAH: Prince Sultan bin Salman, president of the Saudi Commission for Tourism and National Heritage, will launch “Madinah, the capital of Islamic Tourism 2017” festival on Saturday in King Fahd Central Park.
Spokesperson for the organizers of the event, Khalid Al-Shahrani, said the organizing committee has finalized preparations for hosting Madinah’s guests from all over the Islamic world. He said the countdown for the first-of-its-kind event in the member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).
Al-Shahrani said the event will be attended by ministers, intellectuals, writers and media personalities. He said the festival will be shown live on large screens in certain Madinah areas, such as the Zuhoor alley in the King Fahd garden, the Hijra Road and Al-Rashed mall compound.
Al-Shahrani added that many activities and programs will be held with the launching of the event, which will attract more tourists to Madinah.
Waheeb Al-Sahli, the undersecretary of the Madinah Governorate and head of the Executive Committee of the “Madinah: Islamic Tourism capital” event, has overseen preparations for the inauguration event in King Fahd Central Park. Assisting are Munir bin Mohammed Nasser, director of the Madinah Branch of the Tourism and National Heritage, and Wafi Al-Qahtani, executive manager of the organizing company.
Over 700 people are employed to run the event.

Image copyright Google/Church of England Image caption The Very Reverend Martin Thrower, rector of Hadleigh, Layham and Shelley, has now admitted two charges of voyeurism
A clergyman who held his mobile phone over the top of a public toilet cubicle and filmed a 17-year-old boy has admitted voyeurism.
The Very Reverend Martin Thrower, 56, had denied two charges of voyeurism, but changed his pleas to guilty after the first witness gave evidence.
Norwich Crown Court heard Thrower was arrested at a shopping centre in Ipswich in August.
Judge Katharine Moore adjourned the case for reports.
Thrower will be sentenced on 3 August.
Image copyright PA Image caption At interview, Martin Thrower said he had been taking such footage "for a couple of years since 2014"
The court was told the boy heard a noise above him while on the toilet at the Buttermarket shopping centre.
The teenager looked up and could see someone's hand holding a mobile phone.
William Carter, prosecuting, said: "He [the 17-year-old] reacted by getting up smartly and grabbing the phone. Unsurprisingly, he was pretty shocked and upset by what had happened."
'Weird kind of desire'
He said the teenager took the phone to a security officer who detained Thrower until police arrived and arrested him.
Mr Carter said police found three further videos recorded that day, 4 August 2016. including two of other men who had not noticed they were being filmed.
Thrower, of Church Street, Hadleigh, Suffolk, is rector of Hadleigh, Layham and Shelley.
Officers seized computer equipment from his home and found 589 still images of "hundreds of different men", Mr Carter said.
At interview, Thrower said he had been taking such footage "for a couple of years" at places including supermarkets and service stations.
Thrower, who is on bail, is suspended from all roles by the Diocese of St Edmundsbury in Ipswich.
The church has launched a disciplinary process against him which could conclude with him being removed from office and banned from all clergy roles.
rewrite:
The Very Reverend Martin Thrower, the 56-year-old rector of Hadleigh, Layham and Shelley, has pleaded guilty to two counts of voyeurism. He had initially denied the charges but changed his plea following the testimony of the first witness at Norwich Crown Court. The court heard that Thrower was apprehended in August 2016 at the Buttermarket shopping centre in Ipswich after filming a 17-year-old male from over a toilet cubicle partition.

According to the prosecution, presented by William Carter, the victim became aware of a noise from above while using the facilities. Upon looking up, he observed a hand holding a mobile phone over the cubicle wall. The teenager responded by quickly standing and seizing the device. He was described as being profoundly shocked and distressed by the incident. The victim subsequently delivered the phone to a security officer, who detained Thrower until the arrival of police officers, at which point he was arrested.

An examination of the mobile phone revealed three additional videos recorded on the same date, 4 August 2016, two of which depicted other unaware male victims. Following his arrest, computer equipment was seized from Thrower’s residence in Hadleigh, Suffolk. Forensic analysis uncovered a cache of 589 still images featuring, as described by the prosecutor, “hundreds of different men.” During police interview, Thrower admitted to having engaged in this clandestine filming activity “for a couple of years,” citing locations such as supermarkets and service stations.

Judge Katharine Moore adjourned the case for the preparation of reports, with sentencing scheduled for 3 August. Thrower is currently on bail but has been suspended from all ecclesiastical duties by the Diocese of St Edmundsbury and Ipswich. The Church of England has initiated a separate disciplinary process which may result in his removal from office and a permanent prohibition from holding any clerical position.

Manchester City star Raheem Sterling has suggested he would like to make a move to Spain.
The England international, aged 22, has been one of the best performers for Pep Guardiola’s table-topping team.
Before his resurgence this season, he had been tipped for a move to Arsenal in the last transfer window.
But Sterling has ruled out joining the Gunners. He says that a return to his hometown of London and having his childhood friends nearby is not an option, hinting that it would be too much of a distraction for his career.
Sterling, who turns 23 on Friday, says he has happy at City at the moment, but clearly has thoughts of moving on to play overseas at some stage.
According to the Daily Mail, the former Liverpool youngster said: “I’m happy at Man City at the moment. But nobody knows what the future brings so one day, definitely, it would be nice to play abroad. It would be a great experience.
“Spain’s attractive. Anywhere the weather is nice really! Can’t be in London. I can’t be near my friends. They got to stay down there.”
Sterling is under contract at the Etihad Stadium until June 2020. City are tipped to open talks about an extension this summer.

TRENTON, N.J. (AP) — New Jersey's new Democratic governor ordered the state to rejoin a regional environmental pact on Monday, reversing a decision by former Republican Gov. Chris Christie.
Gov. Phil Murphy signed an executive order to put New Jersey back in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative. It mandates that the state Department of Environmental Protection and the Board of Public Utilities begin negotiations with the initiative's nine current member states to determine how the New Jersey should re-enter.
The RGGI is a cap-and-trade program of nine New England and mid-Atlantic states whose aim is to reduce carbon emissions from power plants. The money it raises is distributed to participating states to finance clean energy programs.
Christie had announced in 2011 that the state would leave the initiative, saying the pact didn't effectively reduce greenhouse emissions and amounted to a tax on utility customers.
Murphy said Christie's decision led New Jersey to fall behind on the critical goals of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating the impacts of global climate change. By withdrawing from RGGI, Murphy said New Jersey has foregone an estimated $279 million in revenue that could have been realized by participating in the pact's carbon budget trading program.
"New Jersey has not been a partner to our neighbor states in advancing the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions since pulling out of RGGI," Murphy said. "Pulling out of RGGI slowed down progress on lowering emissions and has cost New Jerseyans millions of dollars that could have been used to increase energy efficiency and improve air quality in our communities. With this executive order, New Jersey takes the first step toward restoring our place as a leader in the green economy."
rewrite:
On Monday, New Jersey's newly inaugurated Democratic Governor, Phil Murphy, issued an executive order directing the state to rejoin the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI). This action reverses the 2011 withdrawal executed by his predecessor, Republican Governor Chris Christie. The order mandates the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection and the Board of Public Utilities to commence negotiations with the initiative's nine current member states to formalize the terms of re-entry.

RGGI is a cooperative cap-and-trade program among nine states in the New England and mid-Atlantic regions, designed to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel-powered electricity generation. The program establishes a regional cap on emissions, requires power plants to hold allowances for their emissions, and auctions those allowances. The resulting revenue is allocated to participating states to fund renewable energy and energy efficiency initiatives.

Governor Christie had justified the state's exit by contending the pact functioned as an ineffective tax on utility ratepayers without meaningfully curtailing greenhouse gases. In contrast, Governor Murphy argued that the withdrawal caused New Jersey to fall behind in critical efforts to mitigate climate change and resulted in significant economic and environmental opportunity costs. He estimated the state forfeited approximately $279 million in potential auction revenue, funds which could have been invested in clean energy programs.

"New Jersey has not been a partner to our neighbor states in advancing the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions since pulling out of RGGI," Murphy stated. He further asserted that the departure impeded progress on emission reductions and cost residents millions in potential investments for energy efficiency and air quality improvements. The executive order, therefore, represents an initial step toward repositioning New Jersey as a participant in regional climate policy and the green economy.

Feist has joined the ranks of Kelis, Coolio, Patti LaBelle, Dolly Parton and Grizzly Bear’s Chris Taylor. She’s now a musician with a cookbook to her name.
In Pleasures: The Meals of an Album, the Canadian singer-songwriter shares more than 40 vegetarian recipes. The dishes are arranged “song-by-song, day-by-day,” and represent the meals that fuelled the recording sessions for Feist’s latest album, Pleasure.
For example, on day one, Feist recorded I’m Not Running Away. Co-author and chef for the Pleasure sessions, Adrienne Amato, prepared tostadas with fried bananas and coconut for breakfast, following by root vegetable and lentil soup for lunch and vegan cauliflower pizza for dinner.
“The making of an album is a communal process on many levels, and that extended to the community of the kitchen while we were recording,” Feist said in a statement. “We hope this book will embolden you to expand your repertoire, stock up on simple staples and invite friends into your kitchen to cook some of these meals with them.”
The book is available exclusively via Feist’s online store ($25; feiststore.com) and is expected to ship on December 11. All proceeds will be donated to Community Food Centres Canada, a non-profit dedicated to promoting “health, belonging and social justice in low-income communities across Canada through the power of food.”

When seemingly every troubling report of current affairs is followed by frantic shrieks of “Fake news!,” we seek sources we can trust, like Facebook posts from Moby.
Earlier today, the producer logged on to share some big-if-true info sourced from unnamed “friends who work in D.C.,” and it would seem the guy who wrote “South Side” knows a few things most of us don’t. Among his assertions: The infamous, unverified intelligence dossier about Donald Trump is legit; the president is in cahoots with the Russian government; his administration is attempting to start a war with Iran; influential Republican operatives want to unseat him; and so do multiple domestic and international intelligence agencies. Here, read for yourself:
It should be noted that Moby isn’t entirely off-base here. On Friday, CNN reported that U.S. investigators have corroborated some of the conversations described in the Trump-Russia dossier. (Nothing related to piss, though.) This morning, the New York Times reported that members of Trump’s National Security Council were considering intercepting an Iranian ship and searching it for weapons last week. Influential right-wing mega-donors the Koch brothers haven’t made a secret of their disapproval for Trump’s immigration policy.
But who’s supposedly feeding deep-state insider intel to Moby, of all people? Guys… it’s time for some game theory.
rewrite:
In an era where distressing developments in current affairs are frequently met with accusations of "fake news," identifying reliable information sources becomes paramount. Some individuals turn to figures such as the musician Moby for such insight. Earlier today, the producer utilized social media to disseminate significant, albeit unverified, claims attributed to anonymous "friends who work in D.C." These assertions suggest a privileged awareness of confidential matters. Specifically, Moby contended that the unverified intelligence dossier concerning Donald Trump is authentic; that the President is colluding with the Russian government; that his administration is seeking to initiate a conflict with Iran; and that influential Republican operatives, alongside various domestic and international intelligence agencies, are working to remove him from office.

It is noteworthy that certain elements of these claims find parallels in established reporting. For instance, CNN recently indicated that U.S. investigators have corroborated some conversations detailed in the Trump-Russia dossier. Separately, The New York Times has reported that members of the National Security Council contemplated intercepting an Iranian vessel last week. Furthermore, prominent conservative donors like the Koch brothers have publicly expressed dissent regarding presidential policies. Nevertheless, the mechanism by which such ostensibly sensitive intelligence would reach a public figure like Moby invites skepticism and warrants analytical scrutiny.

The Hornets went to the playoffs twice in Clifford's five seasons, never winning a playoff series.
"The NBA isn't about winning — the NBA is about winning in the playoffs," Clifford said at the end of Charlotte's season.
Clifford is coming to a franchise that has lost more games than any other NBA club over the past six years — 335. That's four more than Philadelphia, a franchise that was openly tanking for years before turning things around this season.
The Magic weren't tanking. They've just been bad.
Orlando hasn't had longer than a five-game winning streak at any time over the last six seasons. But over that same span, the Magic have had 23 losing streaks of at least five games. On their way to a 25-57 record that left them 18 games out of a playoff spot, the Magic had two seven-game slides and two other nine-game skids.
Since Van Gundy left, the Magic have gone through a series of resets.
There have been 62 players in uniform over the last six seasons — none of them an All-Star while in Orlando — and now five different coaches. Van Gundy was replaced by Jacque Vaughn, who was let go after 2 1/2 seasons and replaced on an interim basis by James Borrego. Scott Skiles then took over for one year, and Vogel ran things the last two seasons.
Clifford now gets his chance.
By Tim Reynolds, The Associated Press
rewrite:
During his five-season tenure, the Charlotte Hornets qualified for the playoffs on two occasions under Coach Steve Clifford, though they failed to advance beyond the first round in either appearance. Reflecting on the team’s performance, Clifford emphasized the distinction between regular-season success and postseason achievement, stating, “The NBA isn't about winning — the NBA is about winning in the playoffs.” Clifford now assumes leadership of the Orlando Magic, a franchise that has accumulated the most losses in the NBA over the past six years, totaling 335 defeats. This figure surpasses even that of the Philadelphia 76ers, an organization that engaged in a deliberate, multi-year strategy of roster depletion prior to its recent competitive resurgence.

Unlike Philadelphia, Orlando’s prolonged struggles cannot be attributed to intentional tanking; rather, the team has simply performed poorly. Across the last six seasons, the Magic have never achieved a winning streak exceeding five games, while simultaneously enduring 23 separate losing streaks of at least five games. Their most recent campaign resulted in a 25-57 record, finishing 18 games outside of playoff contention and featuring two seven-game losing streaks and two nine-game skids. This period of sustained inefficacy followed the departure of Coach Stan Van Gundy and has been characterized by organizational instability. The franchise has cycled through five head coaches and utilized 62 different players over this six-year span, none of whom earned All-Star honors while with Orlando. The coaching carousel included Jacque Vaughn, interim coach James Borrego, Scott Skiles, and most recently, Frank Vogel. Clifford now steps into this context, tasked with reversing the franchise’s entrenched losing trajectory.

Indiana State Police say the incident happened just before 9:00 p.m. Tuesday.
Police responded to the Chuckle’s Gas Station on Old Decker Road, on the south side of Vincennes.
Indiana State Police say officers were attempting to serve a felony warrant to the 35-year-old male at the time of the shooting.

Herdsmen attacks: Delta lawmaker alleges threat to life
By Perez Brisibe
ABRAKA—THE lawmaker representing Ethiope East in Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evance Ivwurie, has raised alarm that his life was under threat owing to his campaign against armed Fulani herdsmen in his constituency.
Chief Ivwurie, in a statement yesterday, explained that some individuals from the northern part of the country were using the security agencies to muzzle him in an attempt to silence him.
He said: “A Kaduna State-based group petitioned the Minister of Interior and National Security Adviser accusing me and the Deputy Speaker of Delta State House of Assembly, Mr Friday Osanebi, of alleged proclamation of genocide against the Fulani and Hausa in our constituencies.
“The threat I am currently facing is as a result of my decision to champion and stand in the gap for the people of my constituency who are killed and maimed daily by suspected armed Fulani herdsmen.
“I have been invited by the Delta State Police Command on several occasions and I made it clear to them that as a law abiding citizen, with respect for the Nigerian constitution, I will not make such unscrupulous statement against any section of the country.”
On his part, the Deputy Speaker, through his media aide, Agbanashi Obinna, said: “The allegation by the group is not true and should be treated as a figment of the imagination of the authors.”
Confirming the investigation by the police on the lawmakers, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr. Zanna Ibrahim said: “A civil rights movement reported the duo to the National Security Adviser over their utterances.
“We (police) have been tasked to investigate and report back to the Inspector General of Police but they both denied the allegations. Investigation is still ongoing.”
The post Herdsmen attacks: Delta lawmaker alleges threat to life appeared first on Vanguard News.

This assertion is directly linked to his vocal opposition to the activities of armed Fulani herdsmen within his electoral district. In an official statement released recently, the lawmaker contended that certain individuals from northern Nigeria are utilizing state security apparatuses to intimidate and silence him.

Chief Ivwurie provided specific details regarding the origins of the threat. He reported that a group based in Kaduna State submitted a petition to both the Minister of Interior and the National Security Adviser. This petition accused him and the Deputy Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Mr. Friday Osanebi, of allegedly inciting genocide against Fulani and Hausa communities residing within their constituencies. The lawmaker refuted these accusations, stating that the perceived threat stems solely from his commitment to advocate for his constituents, whom he claims are subjected to daily violence and fatalities perpetrated by suspected armed herdsmen.

In response to these allegations, Chief Ivwurie confirmed that he has been summoned on multiple occasions by the Delta State Police Command. During these interactions, he maintained his innocence, asserting his adherence to the law and the Nigerian constitution, and denying any involvement in making inflammatory statements against any ethnic group.

The office of the Deputy Speaker, through a media aide named Agbanashi Obinna, also issued a rebuttal. The aide characterized the group’s allegations as entirely fictitious and a product of the petitioners’ imagination, urging that they be dismissed as such.

The Delta State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Zanna Ibrahim, verified that an investigation into the matter is proceeding. He clarified that the inquiry was initiated following a report from a civil rights movement to the National Security Adviser concerning the lawmakers’ public remarks. The police have been instructed to investigate and report their findings to the Inspector General of Police. Commissioner Ibrahim confirmed that both legislators have denied the accusations and stated that the investigative process remains ongoing.

“When Apple released the cellular-capable Apple Watch Series 3 in September, it didn’t realize that a tiny component — its next-generation embedded SIM card (eSIM) — would lead China to quickly and abruptly cut off Apple Watch phone service within its borders,” Jeremy Horwitz writes for VentureBeat. “This morning, the cellular Apple Watch belatedly became available to order in China’s Hong Kong territory… spotlighting the surprising challenges eSIM faces as it becomes critical to next-generation wearables and 5G devices, replacing the 25-year-old traditional SIM card.”
“Nothing about eSIMs would appear to justify governmental panic. Physical SIM cards spent decades shrinking from full-sized to mini, micro, and nano cards before the GSM Association approved eSIM, an even smaller, trayless, permanently installed successor,” Horwitz writes. “The innovation enabled Apple Watch Series 3 to gain only 0.25mm of thickness despite integrating a complete cellular communications system.”
“eSIMs also enable seamless network switching: You can change carriers as needed, including during international travel. Indeed, eSIMs are eventually expected to end international roaming charges,” Horwitz writes. “Since cellular Apple Watches and iPads have set the stage for eSIMs, it’s highly likely that 2019 iPhones and 5G smartphones from other manufacturers will be eSIM-only. So get ready — pretty soon, you’ll be able to kiss carrier lock-ins and international roaming fees goodbye.”
Read more in the full article here.
[Thanks to MacDailyNews Readers “Fred Mertz” and “Dan K.” for the heads up.]
rewrite:
The September 2017 release of the cellular-enabled Apple Watch Series 3 inadvertently precipitated a swift suspension of its phone functionality in mainland China, a consequence of its incorporation of a next-generation embedded SIM (eSIM). As reported by Jeremy Horwitz for VentureBeat, the subsequent availability of the cellular model in Hong Kong underscores the unexpected regulatory complexities eSIM technology encounters as it becomes integral to next-generation wearables and 5G devices, thereby displacing the traditional, quarter-century-old SIM card.

The eSIM specification, ratified by the GSM Association, represents an evolutionary progression from the successive miniaturization of physical SIM cards. Its trayless, permanently embedded design presents no apparent rationale for regulatory concern. This innovation permitted the Apple Watch Series 3 to integrate a full cellular system while adding a mere 0.25mm to its thickness.

Functionally, eSIMs facilitate seamless network switching, allowing users to change carriers as needed, including during international travel, with the potential to eliminate roaming charges. With cellular Apple Watches and iPads establishing an early precedent, it is highly probable that subsequent iPhones and 5G smartphones from various manufacturers will adopt eSIM-only configurations. This transition portends a significant shift away from carrier lock-in policies and the traditional fees associated with international roaming.

Kirui finished in two hours nine minutes and 37 seconds after holding off a challenge by American Galen Rupp in the race's final stretch down Boylston Street, the site of the deadly 2013 bombing attack.
Kirui repeatedly tested Rupp in the closing miles, with the American Olympic bronze medalist eventually unable to match the Kenyan's pace.
"He put in several surges and I was able to cover a few of them," Rupp told reporters after the race.
Kiplagat, a 38-year-old mother of two whose resume includes marathon wins in London, Moscow, New York and Daegu, ran alone for the final miles of the race and finished in 2:21:52, almost a minute ahead of Bahrain's Rose Chelimo.
The Kenyan maintained her comfortable lead despite briefly stopping in the final miles when she realized she had grabbed a rival's water bottle from an aid station and went back to return it.
"I had to put back something which was not mine," Kiplagat told reporters. "I was afraid, because you know, if you miss water it can affect you."
American Jordan Hasay set a record for an American women's debut marathon, coming in third in 2:23:00. Japan's Suguru Osako finished third among the men.
Security was high along the course, which begins in Hopkinton, Massachusetts, and passes through Boston's suburbs to the finish line, where a pair of ethnic Chechen brothers on April 15, 2013 set off two homemade bombs, killing three people and injuring more than 200.
Meb Keflezighi, who in 2014 became the first American to win the race in over three decades, finished 13th in his final Boston Marathon.
Keflezighi, who plans to retire from racing after the New York City marathon in November, stopped after his victory to touch the hand of Bill Richard, whose 8-year-old son Martin was the youngest person to die in the bombing.
"In 2013, I was a spectator just like the three victims and when I saw the 8-year-old ... the first thing in my mind was that could have been my daughter," said Keflezighi.
Tens of thousands of people packed the streets for Boston's largest sporting event, held on the Patriots Day holiday, which commemorates the start of the American Revolution.
To search for individual finishers, visit the marathon's results page.
rewrite:
Geoffrey Kirui secured victory in the Boston Marathon with a time of 2:09:37, ultimately prevailing over American contender Galen Rupp in the concluding segment along Boylston Street—a location infamously associated with the lethal bombing incident of 2013. In the final miles, Kirui executed a series of tactical surges to test Rupp, the Olympic bronze medalist, who proved unable to sustain the Kenyan’s accelerated pace. Reflecting on the race, Rupp acknowledged to reporters, “He put in several surges and I was able to cover a few of them.”

In the women’s division, Edna Kiplagat, a 38-year-old mother of two and a veteran champion of marathons in London, Moscow, New York, and Daegu, completed the course in 2:21:52. She maintained a solitary lead for much of the latter stage, finishing nearly one minute ahead of Bahrain’s Rose Chelimo. Notably, Kiplagat’s margin was preserved despite an interruption in the final miles when she realized she had inadvertently taken a rival’s water bottle from an aid station; she returned to replace it. “I had to put back something which was not mine,” Kiplagat explained. “I was afraid, because you know, if you miss water it can affect you.” American Jordan Hasay achieved a third-place finish in 2:23:00, setting a record for an American woman’s debut marathon. Among the men, Japan’s Suguru Osako placed third.

The event was conducted under heightened security measures along the traditional route from Hopkinton, Massachusetts, through Boston’s suburbs to the finish line on Boylston Street, where on April 15, 2013, two ethnic Chechen brothers detonated homemade explosives, resulting in three fatalities and over two hundred injuries. Meb Keflezighi, who in 2014 became the first American man to win the Boston Marathon in over thirty years, concluded his final Boston appearance in thirteenth place. Following his victory in 2014, Keflezighi paused to clasp the hand of Bill Richard, father of eight-year-old Martin Richard, the youngest victim of the bombing. Keflezighi, who plans to retire after the New York City Marathon in November, recalled, “In 2013, I was a spectator just like the three victims and when I saw the 8-year-old … the first thing in my mind was that could have been my daughter.”

The race, held on the Patriots’ Day holiday commemorating the onset of the American Revolution, attracted tens of thousands of spectators lining the streets for Boston’s premier sporting event. Official results for all participants are accessible via the marathon’s designated results page.

TURANGI, New Zealand — New Zealanders still don’t know who will next lead their country after a final vote count from a general election held two weeks ago tightened the close race between liberals and incumbent conservatives.
Election officials on Saturday released the final 17 per cent of the vote tally, including votes cast by people who were outside of their district or overseas during the election. The conservative National Party ended with 44 per cent of the vote, while the liberal bloc of the Labour Party and the Green Party ended with a combined 43 per cent.
Negotiations to form the next government will now begin in earnest.
Both sides will need to talk with the small New Zealand First party, led by maverick 72-year-old lawmaker Winston Peters. That party finished with 7 per cent of the vote, leaving it holding the balance of power.
Peters hasn’t indicated which of the larger parties he favours. A former National Party lawmaker, Peters has formed coalitions in the past with both National and Labour.
In the 120-seat parliament, the votes translate to 56 seats for National, 46 for Labour, nine for New Zealand First and eight for the Green Party. The final vote count gave both Labour and the Green Party one extra seat apiece over their election night tally. Those came at the expense of the National Party, which lost two seats.
Prime Minister Bill English said voters had clearly favoured National over Labour and he looked forward to engaging with Peters so National could lead a strong and stable government.
The National Party has held power for the past nine years.
“Not since 1969 has the National Party finished ahead of the Labour opposition at four successive elections, and I want to thank everyone involved in this historic achievement,” English said in a statement.
Labour leader Jacinda Ardern said she welcomed the final tally.
“Today’s final election count has strengthened the mandate for change,” she said in a statement.
Peters has said he plans to make a decision this week.
His policies are eclectic. He wants to drastically reduce immigration and stop foreigners from buying farms. He opposes plans by the National Party to increase the pension age and plans by the Labour Party to tax certain water users.
Until negotiations are complete, English will remain as caretaker prime minister.

The National Party secured 44 percent of the vote, while the combined Labour and Green Parties attained 43 percent.

Formal negotiations to establish a governing coalition are now commencing. Both major blocs must engage with the New Zealand First party, which holds the balance of power after obtaining 7 percent of the vote. The party is led by Winston Peters, a 72-year-old veteran and politically independent figure. Peters has not signaled a preference for either major party. A former National Party parliamentarian, he has previously entered into coalition agreements with both National and Labour governments.

Within the 120-seat Parliament, the distribution of seats stands at 56 for the National Party, 46 for Labour, nine for New Zealand First, and eight for the Green Party. The final count awarded Labour and the Green Party one additional seat each compared to the preliminary election-night figures, while the National Party’s total decreased by two seats.

Prime Minister Bill English asserted that voters had delivered a clear preference for the National Party over Labour and expressed his intention to commence discussions with Peters to form a strong and stable government. The National Party has been in government for the past nine years. English noted in a statement, “Not since 1969 has the National Party finished ahead of the Labour opposition at four successive elections, and I want to thank everyone involved in this historic achievement.”

Labour leader Jacinda Ardern welcomed the final results, stating, “Today’s final election count has strengthened the mandate for change.” Peters has indicated he intends to reach a decision within the week. His policy platform is eclectic, advocating for a substantial reduction in immigration, restrictions on foreign ownership of farmland, opposition to the National Party’s proposed increase to the pension age, and resistance to Labour’s plan to tax certain water users. Until coalition negotiations are concluded, Bill English will continue in a caretaker capacity as Prime Minister.

DECATUR, Ga. (AP) – Another major highway in metro Atlanta has been closed, this one because an underground gas leak caused the fast lane to buckle.
DeKalb County spokeswoman Sarah Page says the pavement on Interstate 20 buckled in the HOV lane Monday morning, several miles southeast of downtown Atlanta. All westbound lanes are closed until further notice.
WXIA-TV reports the large bump in the interstate is about 3 feet high.
It’s the second time a major highway in the Southeast’s largest city has become defective in the past few weeks. A large fire allegedly set by a man smoking crack cocaine caused overpass on Interstate 85 to collapse a few miles north of downtown Atlanta on March 27.

Police have identified a 44-year-old homicide victim whose body was discovered near a rec centre in Port Coquitlam over the weekend.
Shawn Curtis George, a resident of the tri-cities area, was found dead on a trail not far from the Hyde Creek Recreation Centre shortly before 10 p.m. Sunday.
The cause of death hasn't been released, but police said George appears to have met with foul play, and the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team is handling the case.
"Mr. George was known to police," Cpl. Meghan Foster said in a news release. "Investigators are working to determine the motive. Anyone who knew Mr. George is asked to contact police."

Police: Des Plaines man set fire to neighbor's gas meter, lawn
hello
A Des Plaines man was charged Monday with aggravated arson after authorities said he poured gasoline on a neighbor's natural-gas meter and lawn and set them on fire last week.
Jason G. John, 36, of the 1000 block of Rose Avenue, was denied bond during an initial court appearance and is in custody at the Cook County jail awaiting trial.
Police said John poured gasoline and set fire to the house's gas meter and front lawn about 10:30 p.m. Thursday.
Firefighters were able to quickly extinguish the fire, according to a news release.
Police said all of the home's residents were inside at the time of the fire, though no one was injured. John appeared to be intoxicated at the time, police added.
The homeowner, Henry Krol, said Monday most of his family was upstairs asleep, as he saw the orange glow of flames from his window. Police said he and John were involved in an argument several weeks earlier.
"I'm trying to figure out why someone would want to kill me over a swear word," Krol said. "We were in this house and we could have died."
There was some fire damage to the siding on the house, authorities said.
An investigation into last week's fire led to John as a suspect, and a search warrant executed at his house uncovered evidence tying him to the arson, authorities said.
rewrite:
A resident of Des Plaines has been formally charged with aggravated arson following an incident in which he allegedly doused a neighbor’s natural gas meter and front lawn with gasoline and ignited them. Jason G. John, 36, of the 1000 block of Rose Avenue, was denied bond during an initial court appearance and remains detained at the Cook County Jail pending trial. According to authorities, the event occurred at approximately 10:30 p.m. on Thursday. Fire department personnel promptly extinguished the flames.

Police reports indicate all occupants of the residence were inside at the time of the fire, though no injuries were sustained. Authorities noted that John appeared to be intoxicated during the incident. The homeowner, Henry Krol, stated that most of his family was asleep upstairs when he observed an orange glow from his window. Investigators disclosed that Krol and John had been engaged in a dispute several weeks prior. Krol expressed bewilderment, remarking, “I’m trying to figure out why someone would want to kill me over a swear word. We were in this house and we could have died.” Officials confirmed minor fire damage to the home’s exterior siding.

The investigation into the fire identified John as a suspect. Subsequently, evidence linking him to the arson was recovered during the execution of a search warrant at his residence.

Thermal refuges protect trout on Housatonic
Photo: H John Voorhees III / Hearst Connecticut Media Image 1 of / 1 Caption Close Image 1 of 1 Buy photo The Housatonic River in Gaylordsville, Conn. August, 2017. The Housatonic River in Gaylordsville, Conn. August, 2017. Photo: H John Voorhees III / Hearst Connecticut Media Buy this photo Thermal refuges protect trout on Housatonic 1 / 1 Back to Gallery
Spots along several area rivers serve as cooling spots for trout in the summer months when the trouts’ regular streams and rivers get too hot.
Anglers are not allowed to fish at these thermal refuges until after September 15. They are marked by signs, noting that fishing must be done at least 100 feet away.
“Summer can be a very difficult time for trout here in Connecticut,” according to the state Department of Energy and Environmental Protection. “Many of our waters warm well into the stressful and often deadly range. To beat the heat, trout will seek out places where groundwater and cold tributaries enter.”
Some of these spots are along the Housatonic, Naugatuck and Shetucket rivers.
“Please do not disturb the trout seeking refuge,” DEEP said in its fishing newsletter. “Even walking along the bank can cause the fish to scatter back out into the main channel where the water temperatures can have significant consequences.”
rewrite:
Thermal refuges serve as critical habitats for trout populations within the Housatonic River watershed and other regional waterways. During summer months, when ambient river temperatures rise to stressful or lethal levels, these discrete areas provide cooler conditions essential for fish survival. They are typically formed by the influx of groundwater or cooler tributary streams. In response, trout congregate in these refuges to mitigate thermal stress.

Recognizing their ecological importance, the Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) has established protective regulations. Angling is expressly prohibited within designated refuge zones until after September 15. These areas are demarcated with signage instructing that fishing activities must occur no closer than 100 feet. The policy aims to minimize disturbance, as even proximate human activity, such as walking along the bank, can displace trout back into warmer main channel waters, with potentially severe physiological consequences.

Key rivers containing these protected thermal refuges include the Housatonic, Naugatuck, and Shetucket. DEEP emphasizes in its public communications that preserving the integrity of these habitats is vital, urging the public to avoid disturbing trout seeking respite from elevated summer temperatures.
