Authorities identify Algonquin women killed in crash
hello
The two Algonquin women killed Sunday in a three-vehicle crash have been identified as 58-year-old Elizabeth A. Jay and 78-year-old Louise J. Schreiner.
Jay was driving eastbound on Route 62 in Algonquin about 3:12 p.m. when her vehicle crossed the centerline and struck two oncoming vehicles, one of which was being driven by Schreiner, McHenry County Coroner Anne Majewski said.
Jay was taken to Centegra Hospital-Huntley, where she died at 3:48 p.m. from blunt trauma to the chest, according to an autopsy conducted Monday. Schreiner, whose car was hit head-on, suffered blunt trauma to the head, neck and chest, Majewski said. She was pronounced dead at the scene.
The driver of a third vehicle was taken to the hospital with nonlife-threatening injuries, Algonquin Deputy Police Chief Ryan Markham said.
Algonquin police are still investigating the cause of the crash, which occurred just west of Sandbloom Road. Witnesses told police they saw Jay's vehicle suddenly swerve to the right and strike a curb before veering to the left and accelerating quickly into oncoming traffic, Markham said.
"It sounds like there was some very sudden erratic driving on the part of the one driver," he said. "She drove head-on into westbound traffic at a very high rate of speed."
Authorities do not believe drugs or alcohol played a role in the crash, Markham said. Police are considering other factors, such as a medical issue, distracted driving or a mechanical failure.
rewrite:
The two Algonquin women fatally injured in a three-vehicle collision on Sunday have been identified as Elizabeth A. Jay, 58, and Louise J. Schreiner, 78. According to McHenry County Coroner Anne Majewski, the incident occurred at approximately 3:12 p.m. on Route 62 in Algonquin. Jay, who was traveling eastbound, crossed the centerline and collided with two oncoming vehicles, one of which was operated by Schreiner.

Jay was transported to Centegra Hospital-Huntley, where she was pronounced deceased at 3:48 p.m. An autopsy performed Monday determined the cause of death to be blunt chest trauma. Schreiner, whose vehicle sustained a head-on impact, succumbed to blunt force injuries to the head, neck, and chest and was pronounced deceased at the scene. The driver of the third involved vehicle sustained non-life-threatening injuries and was hospitalized.

The Algonquin Police Department continues to investigate the causation of the crash, which occurred west of Sandbloom Road. Witness statements indicate that Jay’s vehicle swerved abruptly to the right, struck a curb, then veered left and accelerated rapidly into opposing traffic. Deputy Police Chief Ryan Markham noted the operation involved sudden erratic maneuvering and a high rate of speed at the point of impact. Preliminary investigation suggests that alcohol and drugs were not contributing factors. Authorities are examining alternative explanations, including potential medical emergencies, driver distraction, or vehicular mechanical failure.

A 33-year-old man faces charges of attempted murder and malicious damage to property after he is alleged to have randomly opened fire outside a flats on Woodville Road, striking a 27-year-old woman in the head.
Wentworth SAPS communications officer, Cpt MP Gumede said, “The incident unfolded at about 5am along Major Calvert and Woodville Road near the flats. The police were alerted and were informed that the known suspect fired random shots at the flats. A 27-year-old woman was hit by a stray bullet in the head and was rushed to Wentworth Hospital.”
He added, “The victim was in a stable condition and was discharged the same day after receiving stitches. Durban Flying Squad members on duty responded to the scene. Sgt Ogle heard the shots being fired and walked up to the flats. The police officer noticed the suspect and commanded him to stop. The suspect fired another shot and ran away. The police member pursued the suspect who disappeared into Woodville flats but he could not be found.”
“Through the assistance of informers the suspect was tracked and arrested. He was detained at the police station for attempted murder and malicious damage to property. Sgt Ogle and Cst Karsen from Durban Flying Squad are commended for effecting the arrest,” said Cpt Gumede.
rewrite:
A 33-year-old male has been charged with attempted murder and malicious damage to property following an alleged random shooting incident outside residential flats on Woodville Road, which resulted in a 27-year-old female sustaining a gunshot wound to the head. According to Wentworth SAPS communications officer Captain MP Gumede, the event occurred at approximately 05:00 at the intersection of Major Calvert and Woodville Road. Police were notified that a known suspect had discharged a firearm indiscriminately at the flats. The victim, struck by a stray bullet, was transported urgently to Wentworth Hospital.

Captain Gumede further reported that the victim, having received sutures, was in stable condition and discharged later that same day. Members of the Durban Flying Squad responded, with Sergeant Ogle proceeding toward the flats upon hearing gunfire. The officer observed the suspect and issued a command to halt, at which point the suspect fired an additional round and fled. A pursuit ensued, but the suspect evaded capture within the Woodville flats complex.

Subsequently, through information provided by informants, the suspect was located and apprehended. He is currently detained on the aforementioned charges. Captain Gumede commended Sergeant Ogle and Constable Karsen of the Durban Flying Squad for their role in effecting the arrest.

The robber was after oxycondone and wanted it badly enough to risk entering a Walgreens wearing a black ski mask to get it.
Douglas Wayne Diemer, 51, of the 1200 block of Fairfield Avenue, is charged with robbery and resisting law enforcement.
Several people called police to report the robbery and pointed the first responding officer in the direction of Diemer’s green 2000 Chevy Impala making an escape near Cass Street and West State Boulevard. The witnesses were yelling, “that’s him!” court documents said.
Diemer confronted the female pharmacist while keeping one hand in his pocket, as though he had a weapon. The pharmacist said she was afraid for her safety and handed over three bottles of oxycodone with acetaminophen, the documents said.
The detective who answered the call tried to pull Diemer’s car over, but he continued to flee. While in pursuit with several police cars, Diemer’s car had a flat tire and he stopped in the 1200 block of Fairfield Avenue near his home. He threw a white prescription bottle from the passenger compartment, later picked up by another officer. The bottle was oxycodone with acetaminophen, the documents said.
Diemer appeared to have chewed or eaten several of the white pills because there was a white powdery substance stuck to his lips and mouth, court records said. He was being held in lieu of $12,500 bail.

rewrite:
Douglas Wayne Diemer, a 51-year-old resident of the 1200 block of Fairfield Avenue, has been charged with robbery and resisting law enforcement following an incident in which he allegedly entered a Walgreens pharmacy wearing a black ski mask with the intent to acquire oxycodone. According to court documents, multiple witnesses contacted law enforcement to report the robbery and directed the initial responding officer toward a green 2000 Chevrolet Impala, operated by Diemer, which was fleeing the vicinity of Cass Street and West State Boulevard. Witnesses were reported to have identified the suspect by exclaiming, “that’s him!”

The documents further state that Diemer approached a female pharmacist while keeping one hand concealed in his pocket, simulating the presence of a weapon. Fearing for her safety, the pharmacist complied with his demand and provided three bottles of oxycodone combined with acetaminophen. A detective subsequently attempted to initiate a traffic stop, but Diemer refused to comply and led multiple police vehicles on a pursuit. The chase concluded in the 1200 block of Fairfield Avenue, near his residence, after his vehicle sustained a flat tire. During the incident, Diemer discarded a white prescription bottle from the passenger compartment, which was later recovered by an officer and confirmed to contain oxycodone with acetaminophen.

Court records indicate that Diemer exhibited evidence of having ingested several pills, as a white powdery residue was observed around his lips and mouth. He is currently detained in lieu of $12,500 bail.

BRUSSELS The Muslim and Jewish communities in Flanders have criticised a proposal by the Belgian region to ban the unstunned slaughter of small animals, which they say would contravene their rules for ritual killing.
Under the draft law, animals like Sheep and poultry will have to be stunned electrically before being killed, which most animal rights campaigners say is more humane than the Islamic halal and Jewish kosher rituals. Both require that butchers swiftly slaughter the animal by slitting its throat and draining the blood.
"Unstunned slaughter is outdated," Ben Weyts, regional minister of animal welfare, said in a statement. "In a civilised society, it is our damn duty to avoid animal suffering where possible."
The bill has broad support in the predominantly Catholic region, and the opposition from Flanders' religious minorities illustrates the difficulties facing some European countries as they struggle to integrate immigrant populations.
The issue could play with a wider audience, including right wing politicians and animal rights campaigners, who generally support the legislation.
As stunning larger animals is not possible without also fatally wounding them, the proposed law requires animals such as cattle be stunned immediately after their throats are cut if slaughtered in a ritual manner.
Belgium's Muslim community said its religious council has previously expressed its opposition to stunned slaughter and there had been no change in its stance since then.
"Muslims are worried about whether they can eat halal food ... in conformity with their religious rites and beliefs," the Belgian Muslim Executive said.
The Flemish Jewish community said it was studying the proposal and that stunned slaughter was not in line with Jewish religious laws.
While the proposed law would only apply to the Dutch-speaking region of Flanders in the north of Belgium, other Belgian regions are planning similar moves.
Countries including Denmark, Switzerland and New Zealand already prohibit unstunned slaughter.
(Reporting by Robert-Jan Bartunek, additional reporting by Tom Heneghan; editing by Richard Lough)
rewrite:
In the Flemish region of Belgium, a legislative proposal mandating the pre-slaughter stunning of small animals has drawn criticism from local Muslim and Jewish communities, who contend that such a requirement would contravene their respective religious prescriptions for ritual slaughter. The draft legislation stipulates that animals such as sheep and poultry must be rendered unconscious via electrical stunning prior to slaughter, a practice widely advocated by animal welfare organizations as a more humane alternative to traditional Islamic halal and Jewish kosher methods. Both religious rituals necessitate that the animal be killed by a swift incision to the throat, ensuring rapid blood drainage.

Ben Weyts, the Flemish Minister for Animal Welfare, defended the proposal, stating, "Unstunned slaughter is outdated," and asserting that "in a civilised society, it is our damn duty to avoid animal suffering where possible." The bill enjoys considerable support within the predominantly Catholic region. The opposition from religious minorities underscores the broader socio-political challenges facing several European nations as they navigate issues of integration and cultural accommodation. This matter also resonates with a wider constituency, including right-wing political groups and animal rights activists, who largely endorse the legislative initiative.

Recognizing that stunning larger animals without causing fatal injury is not feasible, the proposed law includes a provision for cattle: if slaughtered ritually, they must be stunned immediately after the throat is cut. The Belgian Muslim Executive has reiterated its religious council's established opposition to pre-slaughter stunning, noting no change in this position. It expressed concern regarding the ability of Muslims to access halal food in accordance with their religious rites. Similarly, the Flemish Jewish community indicated it is reviewing the proposal, emphasizing that stunned slaughter is incompatible with Jewish religious law.

Although the legislation would apply solely to the Dutch-speaking region of Flanders, other Belgian regions are reportedly considering analogous measures. This move aligns with existing prohibitions on unstunned ritual slaughter in several countries, including Denmark, Switzerland, and New Zealand.

SHE’S a real Donaldganger.
Dolores Leis Antelo, a Spanish farmer, is taking the internet by storm thanks to her uncanny resemblance to US President Donald Trump.
A photo of Dolores, who is from La Coruna, a port city in Spain, has gone viral online with thousands of retweets.
It shows her clutching a hoe and gazing into the distance in a pose that resembles that of Trump wielding a golf club on the green.
Camera Icon You’d be forgiven for mixing them up. Picture: Supplied, Reuters/David Moir
Antelo has since been dubbed the “Donald Trump of the Costa da Morte,” according to the original report in La Voz de Galicia.
“My photo seems to have travelled far. I say it is because of the colour of my hair,” she told the Spanish news outlet.
Her daughter Ana said: “Imagine if we were in Donald Trump’s family!”
But Dolores has spent her whole life in Cabana de Bergantiños with her husband of 40 years and has never been interested in the digital world and does not even own a mobile phone
“I have never been curious to have one but I do look at what my daughters show me. They say this picture will make me famous but I don’t get why,” she said.
This story originally appeared in the New York Post and has been republished with permission.
rewrite:
A Spanish agriculturalist, Dolores Leis Antelo, has garnered significant online attention due to her striking physical resemblance to former United States President Donald Trump. A photograph of Antelo, a resident of the port city of La Coruña, has been widely circulated, accruing thousands of social media engagements. The image depicts her holding a hoe and looking into the distance, a posture notably similar to Trump’s frequent stance while holding a golf club on a course. This visual parallel has led to her being humorously referred to as “the Donald Trump of the Costa da Morte” in regional media.

When contacted by the Spanish publication *La Voz de Galicia*, Antelo remarked that her photograph had achieved unexpected reach, speculating that her hair colour may be a contributing factor. Her daughter, Ana, quipped about the familial implications of the resemblance. Despite the sudden notoriety, Antelo maintains a traditional lifestyle in Cabana de Bergantiños with her husband of four decades. She expresses no personal engagement with digital technology, not even possessing a mobile telephone. While her daughters show her the online reactions, she professes puzzlement over the photograph’s viral fame, stating she does not comprehend the reason for its popularity. This account was initially reported by the *New York Post* and is reproduced here under permission.

The duo of Kwan Shing Dee and Neil Uy combined for 160 Stableford points to emerge as the overall champion in the 40th Jose Yulo Memorial Tournament last January 27 and 28 at the Canlubang Golf and Country Club in Canlubang, Laguna.
The tandem of Christopher Yam and Jerboa Go finished second with 157 points while Tommy Sliman and Joe Sullivan finished third with 154.
Mari Hechanova and Jun Jun Plana, meanwhile, bagged the team lowest gross plum after scoring 297.
Individual low gross winners Aniceto Mandanas and Jonas Magcalayo had 142 and 144 points to finish first and second, respectively.
Jr Brillantes, on the other hand, sizzled with 133 net points to snare the individual low net title followed by Paul Shenck at second with 135.
The daily winners on North course were Toshikatsu Oka and Yuji Tokunaga (77- first day), and Rupert Manhit and Bert Dela Rama (80- second day). Finishing second at the same course were Kazuaki Omi and Masahito Nonaka (76- first day), and Rolly Viray and Kristine Torralba (77- second day).
In the South course, the top golfers were the tandem of Rudy Fulo and Jaime Bautista (82), and Chie-Fu Yeh and Robert Yao (82) while Shoichi Hoshi and Koji Yasuma (81), and Dave Hernandez and Mark Viray (81) placed second and third, respectively.
Antonio Oliver won a brand new Mitsubishi Mirage in the raffle draw during the awarding ceremonies.
The tournament was held in honor of former Supreme Court Chief Justice and late businessman Jose Yulo, who acquired Canlubang together with the Sugar Estate in 1948.

Yari, Lalong pledge improved workers’ welfare
The welfare of civil servants in Zamfara State in 2017 will be top priority.
Governor Abdulaziz Yari made the promise in his statewide broadcast yesterday.
He said that although there were hitches in the outgone year, “there will be better things to come in this new year and no one will be left behind.’’
He added that under his watch as the state governor, no civil servant was owed salary and promised that this would continue.
He explained that the government would continue to provide conducive atmosphere and encouragement for the people to engage in businesses to improve self-reliance and economic growth in the state.
The governor also expressed happiness in the outcome of dialogue with bandits in the state that resulted in some of them repenting and surrendering their arms.
He appreciated Federal Government’s efforts in setting up an army and air force brigades in the state, saying this will continue to guarantee the safety of lives and property.
He then wished the people a happy new year and urged them to continue to pray for the success of the administration.
Also in the spirit of the New Year, Governor Simon Bako Lalong of Plateau State has reassured the citizens of the state of his administration’s determination to deliver on his mandate. He gave the assurance in a broadcast to the people of the state yesterday on the Plateau Radio Television Corporation (PRTVC) to mark the New Year.
He said: “The year 2017 now offers hope and better opportunities for service. We are determined to take advantage of this offer, to make life better for our people and our state greater than before.
“We are a part of Plateau project, and for this, I count on your partnership to make 2017 a prosperous year for Plateau State.”

The U.S. Air Force has sent a number of F-35 stealth fighters to Europe as a message to Russia that it stands behind its NATO allies.
The F-35As arrived on Saturday in the United Kingdom. The jets from Hill Air Force Base in Utah will conduct training with other U.S. and NATO aircraft over the next several weeks.
It is the F-35A’s first training deployment to Europe. “As we and our joint F-35 partners bring this aircraft into our inventories, it’s important that we train together to integrate into a seamless team capable of defending the sovereignty of allied nations,” Gen. Tod D. Wolters, commander of US Air Forces in Europe, said in a statement. The aircraft “will help maintain the fundamental sovereignty rights of all nations,” the USAF noted.
The deployment is in support of what the U.S. calls the European Reassurance Initiative. That was initiated in 2014 by the White House in response to Russian actions in the Crimea and Ukraine.
rewrite: The United States Air Force has deployed a contingent of F-35A Lightning II stealth fighter aircraft to Europe, a move interpreted as a demonstration of resolve and commitment to its NATO allies in the context of regional security. The aircraft, originating from Hill Air Force Base in Utah, arrived in the United Kingdom on Saturday. Over the ensuing weeks, they will participate in integrated training exercises with other U.S. and allied NATO forces. This event marks the inaugural training deployment for the F-35A variant in the European theater. General Tod D. Wolters, commander of U.S. Air Forces in Europe, emphasized the necessity of such joint training to achieve seamless integration and a collective defense capability, stating it is vital for "defending the sovereignty of allied nations." The deployment supports the European Reassurance Initiative, a policy framework established by the U.S. administration in 2014 in direct response to Russian military activities in Crimea and eastern Ukraine.

John Kane

-- The Art of John Kane, an exhibition of Oil Paintings, Prints and Charcoals.'As an artist I am interested in the 19th Century Romantic Movement's concerns during the the industrial revolution about the loss of communities and the potential reduction of emotions through mechanisation. Hence their great interest in the "sublime" power of landscapes and heightened emotions.As we experience de-industrialisation and the infinite growth of computer systems, I question if we too, as they were, should be concerned with a loss of our emotional well being and the importance we should place on this. As such, I am drawn to the latent power in beach-scapes or still industrial landscapes, which exist in contrast to the the turmoil of the power of nature or the resonance of past industrial activity. This was the subject of my MA in Fine Art in 2004 at The Wimbledon School of Art and influences my work today, represented in oil paintings, prints and charcoals.From the shores of Newlyn, Cornwall to Bristol or Big Pit in South Wales, we should celebrate those men and women who worked in our agricultural or heavy industries.'Visit http://www.hours- space.com/2017/ 05/08/contemporary- romant... for details
rewrite:
The artistic practice of John Kane is profoundly engaged with the aesthetic and social legacy of industrialisation, drawing explicit parallels with the concerns of the 19th-century Romantic Movement. Kane’s work interrogates the historical loss of communities and the perceived diminution of human emotion through mechanisation, themes that preoccupied Romantic artists and writers. In the contemporary context of de-industrialisation and the pervasive expansion of digital systems, he posits a critical question: whether modern society should similarly be concerned with a potential erosion of emotional well-being and what priority should be accorded to its preservation.

Consequently, Kane is drawn to the latent power and historical resonance embedded within landscapes marked by past industrial activity, as well as to quieter beach-scapes. These environments stand in deliberate contrast to the overt turmoil of sublime natural forces, yet possess their own potent, lingering presence. This thematic focus formed the core of his Master’s research in Fine Art at Wimbledon School of Art in 2004 and continues to fundamentally inform his current practice, which is realised through oil paintings, prints, and charcoal drawings.

His work also serves as a form of commemoration, seeking to celebrate the individuals who laboured within Britain’s agricultural and heavy industries, from the shores of Newlyn in Cornwall to locations in Bristol and South Wales. An exhibition of these works, titled ‘The Art of John Kane’, is currently on view.

PHILADELPHIA — The Philadelphia 76ers have started an investigation into tweets linked in a report to team president Bryan Colangelo that criticized Sixers players Joel Embiid and Markelle Fultz, among other NBA figures.
The burner accounts also took aim at former Sixers general manager Sam Hinkie, Toronto Raptors executive Masai Ujiri and former Sixers players Jahlil Okafor and Nerlens Noel, according to a report by The Ringer website.
"The allegations are serious and we have commenced an independent investigation into the matter," the Sixers said Wednesday in a statement. "We will report the results of that investigation as soon as it is concluded."
The website asked the team about five Twitter accounts it suspected Colangelo was operating. He said in a statement that he used one of the accounts to monitor the NBA industry and other current events, but that he was "not familiar with any of the other accounts" brought to his attention and that he didn't know who was "behind them or what their motives may be in using them."
Embiid, the 24-year-old All-Star centre, tweeted that he didn't believe the report.
"I don't believe the story. That would just be insane," he wrote.
Colangelo was hired as president of basketball operations for Philadelphia in April 2016. He served as Toronto's general manager from 2006-2013.
Colangelo, the son of longtime sports executive Jerry Colangelo, stepped in with the Sixers after Hinkie resigned. He lost his GM job in Toronto after the Raptors missed the playoffs for the fifth consecutive season, and Ujiri took over basketball operations.
According to The Ringer, one of the Twitter accounts it connected to Colangelo downplayed Hinkie's role in the franchise's turnaround. It also lamented in another post that Ujiri hadn't done anything to make the Raptors better.
Another account accused Embiid of "playing like a toddler having tantrums," and one criticized Fultz for his work with his "so called mentor/father figure."
rewrite:
The Philadelphia 76ers organization has initiated an independent investigation following a report by The Ringer website alleging that team president Bryan Colangelo is linked to anonymous social media accounts that criticized numerous individuals associated with the National Basketball Association. According to the report, these purported accounts targeted current 76ers players Joel Embiid and Markelle Fultz, former general manager Sam Hinkie, Toronto Raptors executive Masai Ujiri, and former players Jahlil Okafor and Nerlens Noel.

In an official statement released Wednesday, the franchise acknowledged the gravity of the allegations, stating, "The allegations are serious and we have commenced an independent investigation into the matter. We will report the results of that investigation as soon as it is concluded." The inquiry was prompted after The Ringer presented the team with evidence concerning five specific Twitter accounts suspected of being operated by Colangelo. In his own responsive statement, Colangelo admitted to utilizing one account for professional monitoring of league affairs but denied involvement with the others, asserting he was "not familiar with any of the other accounts" and had no knowledge of who was "behind them or what their motives may be in using them."

The report details that one of the accounts in question disparaged the legacy of former executive Sam Hinkie regarding the franchise's rebuilding efforts, while another criticized Masai Ujiri's tenure with the Raptors. Additional posts contained personal critiques of players, including a characterization of Joel Embiid as "playing like a toddler having tantrums" and a comment disparaging Markelle Fultz's relationship with a personal mentor. Embiid, the team's All-Star center, publicly dismissed the report via social media, writing, "I don't believe the story. That would just be insane."

Colangelo, son of renowned sports executive Jerry Colangelo, was appointed president of basketball operations for Philadelphia in April 2016, succeeding Hinkie. His prior tenure as general manager of the Toronto Raptors concluded in 2013 following five consecutive playoff absences, after which Ujiri assumed control of basketball operations. The ongoing investigation seeks to ascertain the validity of the reported connections and the provenance of the critical social media commentary.

Riyadh is ready to provide Iranian Hajj pilgrims with favorable services and solve any problem they may face, an official with Saudi Arabia Hajj Ministry told an Iranian delegation.
Saudi Arabian Deputy Hajj Minister Abdolrahman Bijavi in a meeting on Sunday with Iran’s consular delegation in Medina, reaffirmed his country’s adherence to offering suitable services to the ‘Guests of the Compassionate’, IRNA reported.
He further said, “My colleagues and I are ready round the clock to hear views of Hajj headquarters and solve pilgrims’ possible problems.”
During the meeting, both sides were unanimous about respecting pilgrims’ rights and their dignity and also full implementation of the agreement earlier signed between Iran’s Hajj and Pilgrimage Organization and Saudi Hajj Ministry.
Foreign Ministry’s 10-member consular delegation arrived in Medina on August 2 to render consular services to the Iranian pilgrims in Mecca and Medina, two major Saudi cities home to holy shrines.
Iran stopped sending pilgrims to Hajj over security concerns after two deadly incidents claimed the lives of more than 470 Iranian pilgrims during the Hajj rituals in 2015 when some 4,700 people lost their lives in a human stampede in Mina, near Mecca.
Earlier, a massive construction crane had collapsed into Mecca's Grand Mosque, killing more than 100 pilgrims, including 11 Iranians, and injuring over 200 others, among them 32 Iranian nationals.
Iran announced that it would not send its pilgrims to the annual Islamic gathering unless the Saudi officials guarantee their security, safety and dignity.
No Iranians attended Hajj congregation in 2016 due to Saudis' failure to provide the necessary conditions for their participation. However, the situation is now different in 2017 after the Iranian and Saudi officials reached an agreement upon which the latter became committed to provide necessary grounds for the presence of the Iranian pilgrims in this year's Hajj rituals.
rewrite:
Saudi Arabian authorities have affirmed their readiness to extend favorable services and address any potential challenges for Iranian pilgrims participating in the Hajj pilgrimage. This commitment was conveyed by Deputy Hajj Minister Abdolrahman Bijavi during a meeting on Sunday with an Iranian consular delegation in Medina, as reported by the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA). Minister Bijavi reiterated his nation's dedication to providing suitable services to what are termed the ‘Guests of the Compassionate,’ emphasizing that he and his colleagues are prepared to receive feedback from Hajj officials and resolve pilgrim issues at all times. The discussions resulted in a mutual consensus on upholding the rights and dignity of pilgrims and ensuring the complete implementation of the existing bilateral agreement between Iran’s Hajj and Pilgrimage Organization and the Saudi Ministry of Hajj.

This diplomatic engagement follows the arrival of a ten-member consular delegation from Iran’s Foreign Ministry in Medina on August 2, tasked with providing consular services to Iranian nationals in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Iranian participation in the Hajj had been suspended following two tragic incidents in 2015. The first involved the collapse of a construction crane into Mecca's Grand Mosque, resulting in over 100 fatalities, including 11 Iranians, and more than 200 injuries, among them 32 Iranian nationals. Subsequently, a human stampede in Mina, near Mecca, claimed approximately 4,700 lives, including more than 470 Iranian pilgrims. Citing these security failures, Iranian officials declared they would not authorize pilgrim travel until Saudi authorities could guarantee safety, security, and dignified treatment. Consequently, no Iranian pilgrims attended the 2016 Hajj due to the unmet conditions.

The resumption of pilgrim travel for the 2017 season follows a renewed agreement between Iranian and Saudi officials. This accord commits Saudi Arabia to establishing the necessary provisions to facilitate the secure and dignified participation of Iranian pilgrims in the annual Islamic gathering, marking a shift from the preceding years of diplomatic impasse.

Even as Trump’s most loyal allies condemned the white supremacists groups engaging in violence in Charlottesville, Fox News didn’t.
A rally in Charlottesville, Virginia, left one anti-racism activist and two police officers dead and several others injured.
It was, beyond doubt, a spectacle meant to incite hate and violence — and it did more than just that by claiming three innocent lives.
President Donald Trump didn't call out white supremacists, even as criticism built over his wishy washy statement, from ordinary Americans and from within his own party. Most of his allies condemned the white supremacists groups engaging in violence in Charlottesville.
Well, most allies, excluding the ones working at Fox News.
The “Fox & Friends” panel, somehow, found a way to justify the actions of the torch and weapons-carrying white supremacists and in doing so, they also defended Trump’s first statement, which, for the record, lacked any mention whatsoever of white supremacy.
Read More If Trump Plans To Fight White Nationalism, He Should Start With Bannon
“I think the president nailed it,” said Pete Hegseth, a co-host. “He condemned in the strongest possible terms hatred and bigotry on all sides as opposed to immediately picking a side out the gate.”
And then Hegseth went on understand the “grievance underneath” the rally, which included marchers from alt-right, neo-Nazi groups as well as the Ku Klux Klan.
“You can call [violence] out, and then — but still also listen, say, on Black Lives Matter, to the grievances of young African-American males in urban cores who feel like they are looked at differently by police. That discussion still should be had,” he said, adding a lot of white men “feel like, ‘Hey, I’m treated differently in this country than I feel like I should have. I’ve become a second-class citizen. None of it — they tell me I have white privilege.’”
Coming from Fox News, which has always considered Black Lives Matter a hate group, this statement is not surprising — but it does not make it any less shocking.
The only “grievance” white supremacists have held since time immemorial is hate and bigotry — and anyone who attempts to justify hate and bigotry is complicit in hate and bigotry.
rewrite:
In the aftermath of the violent rally in Charlottesville, Virginia—an event that resulted in the deaths of one counter-protester and two state police officers, alongside numerous injuries—a clear consensus emerged among political leadership condemning the white supremacist groups responsible. President Donald Trump’s initial statement, however, was broadly criticized as equivocal for its failure to explicitly identify and denounce these groups, drawing rebuke from both the public and members of his own party. While the president’s most loyal allies subsequently issued unambiguous condemnations of the white supremacists involved, one prominent outlet aligned with his administration notably abstained: Fox News.

Contrary to the prevailing political response, commentators on Fox News programming, notably the “Fox & Friends” panel, engaged in rhetoric that served to contextualize and, to a degree, legitimize the actions of the demonstrators, many of whom were affiliated with alt-right, neo-Nazi, and Ku Klux Klan factions and were witnessed carrying torches and weapons. In doing so, they also defended the president’s initial, non-specific remarks. Co-host Pete Hegseth asserted, “I think the president nailed it… He condemned in the strongest possible terms hatred and bigotry on all sides as opposed to immediately picking a side out the gate.” Hegseth proceeded to advocate for an understanding of the “grievance underneath” the rally, drawing a parallel to the need to listen to grievances within the Black Lives Matter movement.

This rhetorical framing is particularly notable given Fox News’s historical portrayal of Black Lives Matter as a hate group. The attempt to establish a moral equivalence between the grievances of white supremacists and those of racial justice movements is a profound distortion. The foundational ideology of white supremacy is intrinsically rooted in hatred and bigotry; its central “grievance” is the rejection of racial equality. Any discursive effort to rationalize or legitimize this ideology, irrespective of the platform, constitutes complicity in its propagation. The events in Charlottesville constituted a stark manifestation of hate-fueled violence, and the subsequent media discourse revealed not only a failure in moral clarity but also the perils of providing ideological cover for movements fundamentally opposed to democratic and egalitarian principles.

The simulator will allow developers to test programs and debug code with their own computers, which is necessary since there really aren't any quantum computers for them to test their work on yet. Microsoft is also offering a more powerful simulator -- one with over 40 logical qubits of computing power -- through its Azure cloud computing service. And because the kit is integrated into Microsoft's Visual Studio developer tool suite, many aspects of the new kit will be familiar.
"What you're going to see as a developer is the opportunity to tie into tools that you already know well, services you already know well," Todd Holmdahl, Microsoft's VP in charge of its quantum effort, said in a statement. "There will be a twist with quantum computing, but it's our job to make it as easy as possible for the developers who know and love us to be able to use these new tools that could potentially do some things exponentially faster – which means going from a billion years on a classical computer to a couple hours on a quantum computer."

The simulator enables developers to test and debug quantum programs using conventional computers, a necessity given the current absence of widely accessible quantum hardware for practical experimentation. In a statement, Todd Holmdahl, Microsoft’s corporate vice president for quantum, emphasized the approach: “Developers will have the opportunity to leverage tools and services with which they are already proficient. While quantum computing introduces novel concepts, our objective is to minimize complexity, allowing developers to utilize these tools that promise exponential performance gains—potentially reducing tasks from billions of years on classical systems to mere hours on quantum computers.”

Rory McIlroy admits he will have "no excuses" for not performing well in this week's Dubai Duty Free Irish Open.
McIlroy won the title in 2016 but has missed the cut in four of the last five years, during which time he has had to juggle his duties as tournament host of the £5.3million event.
"I've cut back from a few things off the golf course," McIlroy said in his pre-tournament press conference at Ballyliffin. "It's not that we're not doing them, I'm just maybe not as involved in some of the stuff.
"There's been a couple of times where I just haven't felt as prepared as I could have been walking on to the first tee on Thursday. So I got here Monday morning, practised Monday afternoon and all day yesterday.
"I've done my work. So there's no excuse about not being prepared or not, and I've learned that as I went along. I felt I was underprepared at County Down [in 2015]. I felt OK at The K Club I guess. I've learnt as I went along and I feel this year I'm right where I need to be."
rewrite: Rory McIlroy has acknowledged that he will have “no excuses” for any potential underperformance at this week’s Dubai Duty Free Irish Open. Despite having claimed the title in 2016, McIlroy has missed the cut in four of the last five editions of the tournament, a period during which he has also balanced his responsibilities as host of the £5.3 million event. Speaking at a pre-tournament press conference at Ballyliffin, McIlroy explained that he has reduced certain off-course commitments. “It is not that these activities have ceased,” he clarified, “but rather that my personal involvement in some areas has been scaled back.” He reflected on previous occasions when he felt insufficiently prepared upon beginning play. To address this, he arrived on Monday morning, undertaking practice sessions that afternoon and throughout the following day. “My preparation is complete,” McIlroy stated. “Consequently, there can be no justification related to a lack of readiness. Through experience—feeling underprepared at County Down in 2015 and somewhat more adequate at The K Club—I have adapted my approach. This year, I believe my preparation aligns precisely with the requirements.”

Floral tributes have been left at the scene where a teenager fell to her death from a multi-storey car park.
The 19-year-old, named locally as Murron McDermid, died in the early hours of Saturday after the incident on Longsmith Street.
Since hearing the news, people have headed there to pay their respects and bunches of flowers have been laid against the car park wall.
One card, from Julie and Ellie, read: "To Murron, to a beautiful lady. We will miss you my dear."
Another message simply read: "Gonna miss u Murron."
The young artist exhibited her paintings at the city’s hub Jolt in King’s Square, where staff remember her fondly.
Jason Smith, chief executive of Marketing Gloucester which runs it, called her a “sweet” girl.
“This was a complete shock to us,” he said.
“She was such a character, full of energy. This will be a shock for the arts community in Gloucester.
“She was a lovely girl, with a lot of enthusiasm. She was one of those who would always come over and say hello.”
Police said the death is being treated as unexplained but not suspicious and her next of kin have been informed.
It is understood she is a former pupil of Chosen Hill School in Churchdown, The Crypt School in Gloucester and SGS College in Stroud. She had been working at The Grape Tree in Gloucester.

Attached sentiments include a card from Julie and Ellie, which stated, "To Murron, to a beautiful lady. We will miss you my dear," and another message that read, "Gonna miss u Murron."

Ms. McDermid was a young artist who had exhibited her work at Jolt, an arts hub in King’s Square. Staff there recalled her positively, with Jason Smith, chief executive of the managing organization Marketing Gloucester, describing her as a “sweet” and enthusiastic individual. He further remarked on her amiable nature, stating she was one who would consistently offer greetings.

Authorities have indicated that the death is currently treated as unexplained but not suspicious, and her next of kin have been notified. Educational and employment records show she attended Chosen Hill School in Churchdown, The Crypt School in Gloucester, and SGS College in Stroud, and was most recently employed at The Grape Tree in Gloucester.

"I thought it'd be a good idea to have a dog that's not law enforcement, a non law enforcement canine that doesn't do apprehension or anything like that where it's safe to have them among the students, so I had started it," Ray McCarty says.
Parents can rent the K9 to see whether or not their kids have drugs hidden in their rooms.
"The times that we find things, it's basically just confirming the parent's suspicions and it's nice when we don't find things," McCarty says.
Read more here.

Metro K9 Services provides inspections conducted by canines with specialized training in narcotics detection. According to company representative Ray McCarty, the initiative originated from the perceived utility of deploying dogs that are not affiliated with police agencies and are trained exclusively for detection, thereby ensuring a non-threatening presence in environments such as schools. This service enables parents, among other clients, to utilize canine sweeps to investigate suspected drug possession by minors within domestic settings. McCarty notes that while positive detections serve to confirm parental suspicions, negative outcomes are also viewed favorably. This development represents a commercialization of surveillance techniques traditionally reserved for official use.

A weather warning lasting for an astonishing 34 hours is in place for the West Midlands, lasting from Thursday 11am until 9pm on Friday.
Thunderstorms could bring "torrential rain" with 40mm forecast to fall in one hour in some areas of the West Midlands.
Frequent lightning and large hail are possible, forecasters warned.

Swearing, stage fighting and winner speech strops – the Brit Awards have had it all over the years, but whether there will be the same histrionics from 2017's music stars remains to be seen.
Here's everything you need to know about the 2017 Brit Awards, from how to watch to who's performing.
What time are the 2017 Brit Awards on TV?
The Brits will be shown live on ITV on Tuesday 22 February from 7.30pm.
Clara Amfo, Laura Jackson and Alice Levine will host coverage of the red carpet on ITV2 from 6.30pm - 7.30pm and will then go backstage from 10pm to 11pm.
Who are the Brits hosts this year?
Dermot O'Leary and Emma Willis will be trying to maintain order as the show gets underway, taking over from last year's hosts Ant and Dec. The pair have been brought in after original host Michael Bublé was forced to pull out after it was revealed his young son had liver cancer.
“Firstly, my immediate thoughts and prayers are with Michael and his family at such a difficult time," said O'Leary as the news was announced. "Michael is an effortless showman, so those patent shoes will not be easy to fill, but it's an honour to be asked to step in with Emma to host the Brits."
Who are the Brit Award nominees?
David Bowie is up for two posthumous awards on the night, while the current crop of British talent is represented by Skepta and Little Mix with three nominations apiece. Check out the full shortlist here.
Can I vote for the winner?
You can vote now to decide who wins Best British Video and Best British Breakthrough Act – head to this link to find out more. Voting closes on the 17th February.
Who is performing at this year's Brit Awards?
The full line-up has now been confirmed. Expect performances from Katy Perry, Ed Sheeran, Bruno Mars, The 1975, Little Mix, Emeli Sandé and Skepta.
Brit Icon Robbie Williams will also be performing on the night.
Did you say Brit Icon?
Yes, it's a special award for "artists whose writing, recording and performances have made a lasting impact on British culture". Robbie Williams is being given the honour this year, following in the footsteps of Elton John and David Bowie.

TORONTO – Friday, June 30 (two weeks and two days from now) will be the last chance a resident of Ontario will have to take a road test for an Ontario CDL (or A/Z, as it’s known in the province) without first taking a mandatory training training.
Good luck getting an appointment. Extended lineups were being reported more than a month ago.
After July 1, prospective drivers will have to register with one of the province’s more than 80 certified schools. The bare minimum training will involve 103 hours of training, broken down as 36.5 hours in class and 67 hours in or at the truck, with at 17 of those in the yard; 50 holding the steering wheel; with 32.5 of them on the road and 17.5 hours in the yard, backing up and doing other maneuvers.
Air brake training will add another 12 hours, minimum.
The lowest price school will be $6,000.
Ontario is the first province to make truck-driving-training obligatory. Other jurisdictions are expected to follow suit.
The switch to mandatory training will indeed be game-changing. While about 9,000 Class A road tests are delivered each year in Ontario, just 2,500 people went through a Private Career College, public college, or Ministry of Transportation-approved driver certification program in 2014.
rewrite:
Effective June 30, residents of Ontario will face a final opportunity to undertake a road test for a Commercial Driver’s Licence (CDL), classified provincially as Class A/Z, without prior completion of mandatory training. Securing an examination appointment, however, is anticipated to be challenging, given that extended wait times were documented over a month in advance.

Commencing July 1, all prospective commercial drivers must enroll in one of the province’s eighty-plus certified training institutions. The mandated curriculum requires a minimum of 103.5 hours of instruction. This total comprises 36.5 hours of in-class education and 67 hours of practical training. The practical component is further delineated into 50 hours of hands-on vehicle operation, with 32.5 hours conducted on public roads and 17.5 hours dedicated to yard maneuvers such as backing. An additional minimum of 12 hours is required for specialized air brake endorsement training. The associated cost for these programs begins at approximately $6,000.

Ontario represents the first Canadian jurisdiction to implement compulsory commercial driver training, a regulatory shift expected to influence other provinces. This policy constitutes a significant transformation for the industry. Historically, while roughly 9,000 Class A road tests are administered annually in Ontario, only an estimated 2,500 individuals completed formal, approved training programs in a recent benchmark year.

By MacDonald Dzirutwe | Reuters |
Zimbabwe’s wildlife agency said on Tuesday it was investigating allegations that a South African national bribed officials to allow a Colorado-based tourist to take the ivory tusks of an elephant illegally shot in a Zimbabwe game park.
Their inquiry comes after U.S. prosecutors accused the South African, who was with a hunting party in Gonarezhou National Park in southern Zimbabwe, of paying up to $8,000 in bribes to Zimbabwean government officials to kill the elephant inside the park and to have the animal’s ivory released.
“We are investigating the matter,” said Tinashe Farawo, spokesman for the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority. He gave no further details.
A government official, who declined to be named because he was not authorised to speak to the media, said Zimbabwean authorities had contacted the South African but he was not forthcoming with information.
A statement by the U.S. Department of Justice in Colorado dated May 21 said the South African conspired with the unidentified Colorado hunter to export the tusks by falsely saying in official documents the hunter was a South African resident and that the elephant was shot outside Gonarezhou.
It is illegal under Zimbabwean law for hunters to shoot animals inside a state game park.
In 2015, a U.S. dentist touched off a global storm when he killed a rare black-maned lion named Cecil with a bow and arrow outside Hwange National Park in western Zimbabwe, forcing the United States to suspend importation of elephant trophies from Africa.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Management Authority (ZPWMA) announced it is investigating allegations that a South African national bribed officials to facilitate the illegal export of elephant ivory. The inquiry follows U.S. federal charges alleging the individual paid approximately $8,000 in bribes to Zimbabwean government officials. These payments were intended to secure permission for an elephant to be unlawfully hunted within Gonarezhou National Park and for the subsequent release of its tusks to a hunter based in Colorado.

Tinashe Farawo, a spokesman for the ZPWMA, confirmed the investigation was underway but declined to provide further details. An unnamed government official, unauthorized to speak publicly, stated that Zimbabwean authorities had contacted the South African suspect but had received insufficient cooperation.

According to a May 21 statement from the U.S. Department of Justice in Colorado, the South African conspired with the unidentified Colorado hunter to export the tusks by falsifying official documentation. The documents falsely declared the hunter to be a South African resident and misrepresented the elephant as having been shot outside the protected boundaries of Gonarezhou National Park. Hunting within Zimbabwe's state game parks is prohibited by national law.

This incident recalls the 2015 international controversy involving a U.S. dentist who killed a protected lion named Cecil near Hwange National Park. That case prompted the United States to temporarily suspend imports of African elephant hunting trophies.

Several N.F.L. teams determined cheerleading programs had a scarcity problem on game days. If cheerleaders were on the sideline dancing, none were available to serve as scantily clad hostesses who could mingle with fans high up in the cheap seats or in the luxury suites, where teams catered to big-money customers.
To address that shortcoming, some teams created a different kind of cheerleading team — one whose members did not do any cheering or require any dance training. They were hired mainly for their appearance. Their visits with male fans, the teams believed, produced a better game-day experience, akin to the approach of the Hooters restaurant chain.
In interviews with a dozen women who have worked for N.F.L. teams as noncheering cheerleaders and six others who had direct knowledge of the noncheering squads, they described minimum-wage jobs in which harassment and groping were common, particularly because the women were required to be on the front lines of partying fans. The fans had no reason to believe these women were not actual cheerleaders because the women often dressed exactly like the cheerleaders dancing on the field or nearly the same.
“It’s a really big secret, and now you know about it,” said Jackie Chambers, 33, a model with more than a decade of experience who worked as a Houston Texans noncheering cheerleader last season. “But teams don’t want fans to know about it. All of the cheerleaders are supposed to blend in with each other.”
rewrite:
Several National Football League franchises identified a deficiency in their cheerleading programs on game days, finding that when cheerleaders were performing on the sidelines, they were unavailable to act as hospitality ambassadors. These roles involved interacting with spectators in the less expensive upper-level seating areas and in premium luxury suites, where teams focus on catering to high-value patrons. To remedy this gap, certain teams established a distinct category of cheerleading squad—one whose members neither performed cheers nor required dance training. Recruitment prioritized physical appearance. Management operated under the belief that these women’s interactions with predominantly male fans enhanced the game-day atmosphere, mirroring a marketing strategy employed by establishments such as the Hooters restaurant chain.

In interviews conducted with twelve women who have served as non-cheering cheerleaders for NFL teams and six additional individuals with direct knowledge of these squads, subjects described minimum-wage positions where harassment and unwanted physical contact were frequent occurrences. This environment was exacerbated by the requirement to engage directly with celebratory fans. Spectators often could not distinguish these employees from performing cheerleaders, as their attire was identical or nearly identical to that of the sideline dancers. "It's a really big secret, and now you know about it," stated Jackie Chambers, a 33-year-old model with over ten years of experience who worked in this capacity for the Houston Texans. "But teams don't want fans to know about it. All of the cheerleaders are supposed to blend in with each other."

(Portland, OR) – Governor Kate Brown today announced that she is reaffirming her commitment to pursue gun violence prevention measures. In the wake of the Las Vegas shooting, the largest mass shooting in United States history, and the two-year anniversary of the mass shooting at Umpqua Community College, Governor Brown will be working with Oregon lawmakers to develop legislation for the 2018 legislative session that will keep guns out of the wrong hands and help protect Oregonians from gun violence.
“My thoughts and prayers are with the families suffering from gun violence in Oregon and across the country. But, I know my condolences will never be enough to keep families safe from violence,” said Governor Brown. “We, as lawmakers, must put politics aside and work together to keep our communities safe. I look forward to working with the Legislature to finish what we started last session and close the Charleston and Boyfriend Loopholes for good. These policies will keep guns out of the wrong hands and help keep our promise to families across the state to keep our communities safe.”
Closing the “Charleston Loophole” will keep a person who is prohibited from purchasing firearms unless and until the Oregon State Police can determine they are eligible. Closing the “Boyfriend Loophole” will update the definition of a domestic violence offender to match the definition already in Oregon law, and will also add persons convicted of misdemeanor stalking to those prohibited from purchasing firearms.
rewrite:
(Portland, OR) – Governor Kate Brown has formally reaffirmed her commitment to advancing gun violence prevention measures. This announcement follows the recent mass shooting in Las Vegas, now recorded as the deadliest such incident in United States history, and coincides with the two-year commemoration of the mass shooting at Umpqua Community College. Governor Brown will collaborate with the Oregon State Legislature to craft specific legislation for the 2018 session, with the stated objectives of preventing firearms from reaching prohibited individuals and enhancing protections for Oregon residents against gun violence.

Governor Brown stated, “While my deepest sympathies remain with the families in Oregon and nationwide affected by gun violence, condolences alone are insufficient to ensure public safety. It is incumbent upon us as legislators to transcend political divisions and collaborate on meaningful measures to secure our communities.” She further expressed her intent to work with the Legislature to complete initiatives from the previous session, specifically to permanently close the so-called Charleston and Boyfriend loopholes. “These policies are designed to restrict firearm access from unauthorized individuals and are integral to fulfilling our commitment to safeguard communities statewide,” she added.

Legislatively, closing the Charleston Loophole would prohibit a firearm transfer unless and until the Oregon State Police complete a background check confirming eligibility. Closing the Boyfriend Loophole involves revising the statutory definition of a domestic violence offender to align with existing Oregon law, thereby expanding prohibitions to include individuals convicted of misdemeanor stalking offenses.

Poultry samples from markets in Metro Manila were found to be contaminated with drug-resistant Campylobacter bacteria, a cause of acute gastroenteritis, a soon to be published study by University of the Philippines researchers found.
The research team from the UP Institute of Biology and Natural Sciences Research Institute tested 265 samples of chicken parts from 15 wet markets and 15 supermarkets in Metro Manila, and found 202 of them, or about 76 percent, contaminated with either Campylobacter jejuni or Campylobacter coli bacteria, both of which can cause gastroenteritis.
Acute gastroenteritis from Campylobacter infection causes 400 million to 500 million cases of diarrhea annually, the researchers said. Data from the US National Institutes of Health (NIH) indicate that gastroenteritis is responsible for 1.5 million to 2.5 million deaths annually, mainly among children in developing countries. In a 2010 study, NIH researchers said that up to 12 percent of deaths among children under five years old could be attributed to gastroenteritis.
In addition, the UP researchers found that most of the bacteria in the contaminated samples were resistance to the common antibiotics used to fight them. “Nearly all of the isolates were resistant to clindamycin (98.6 percent), erythromycin (98.6 percent), nalidixic acid (98.1 percent), and tetracycline (94.2%), while resistance to chloramphenicol (52.7 percent) and gentamicin (65.2 percent) were not as prevalent,” the study’s findings said.
The researchers said that samples from chicken skin and chicken liver had the highest levels of contamination.
The study also pointed out that the levels of contamination in samples from Metro Manila were apparently higher than in similar earlier studies conducted in Laguna and Nueva Ecija, and that samples taken from wet markets showed higher levels of drug resistance than those taken from supermarkets.
“The presence of drug resistant Campylobacter in the samples tested is also a public health concern,” the study concluded. “Further monitoring of chicken products is suggested since the level and type of contamination represents a significant risk to consumers, unless food safety management strategies and pathogen reduction performance standards are implemented strictly in key production points to lower pathogen carriage in public markets.”
The study, an advance version of which has been made available online, will be published in a forthcoming issue of the Japanese Journal of Infectious Diseases.
rewrite:
A forthcoming study by researchers from the University of the Philippines has identified a high prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant *Campylobacter* species, causative agents of acute gastroenteritis, within poultry products sampled from Metro Manila. The investigation, to be published in the *Japanese Journal of Infectious Diseases*, analyzed 265 chicken part samples procured from 15 wet markets and 15 supermarkets. Results indicated that 202 samples (76.2%) were contaminated with either *Campylobacter jejuni* or *Campylobacter coli*.

The public health implications of this contamination are substantial. As noted by the researchers, *Campylobacter* infection results in an estimated 400 to 500 million cases of diarrheal disease globally each year. Citing data from the U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH), the study further contextualizes the burden of gastroenteritis, which is associated with 1.5 to 2.5 million annual fatalities, predominantly affecting children in developing nations. Prior NIH research has suggested that gastroenteritis may account for up to 12 percent of mortality in children under five years of age.

A critical finding of this study is the widespread antimicrobial resistance observed among the bacterial isolates. Susceptibility testing revealed extremely high resistance rates to several common antibiotics: clindamycin (98.6%), erythromycin (98.6%), nalidixic acid (98.1%), and tetracycline (94.2%). Resistance to chloramphenicol (52.7%) and gentamicin (65.2%) was also documented, though at comparatively lower levels. Analysis identified chicken skin and liver samples as having the highest contamination loads.

The research also provided comparative insights, noting that contamination levels in Metro Manila exceeded those reported in earlier studies conducted in Laguna and Nueva Ecija. Furthermore, isolates recovered from wet market samples demonstrated higher levels of drug resistance than those from supermarket samples.

The study concludes that the presence of drug-resistant *Campylobacter* in retail poultry constitutes a significant public health concern. It advocates for enhanced, continuous monitoring of chicken products, emphasizing that the current contamination profile poses a considerable consumer risk. The authors stress that this risk can only be mitigated through the stringent implementation of food safety management systems and pathogen reduction performance standards at critical points in the production chain, thereby lowering pathogen prevalence in public markets. An advance version of the manuscript is currently available online.

The numbers are really beginning to add up for West Bromwich Albion 's leading schemer Matt Phillips.
Assists number seven and eight (discounting his EFL Cup contribution) turned the Hull game on its head.
It also pushed Phillips, a ludicrously cheap £5 million acquisition from QPR, into esteemed company.
Yet not even the country's most celebrated conspirators - Adam Lallana, Alexis Sanchez, Mesut Ozil and Christian Eriksen - can match the flying Scotsman's tally of assists.
Only one can.
Manchester City's Kevin De Bruyne, who cost 11 TIMES more than Phillips, has nine assists.
But the big name Belgian has half as many goals as Phillips, who, lest we forget, has bagged four in his last nine.
The turnaround in fortunes since he was dropped for the game against De Bruyne's City in October is incomprehensible.
Yet it's not just Phillips' stats that stand out.
Arguably the most impressive aspect of his performance today was his willingness to want the ball and to make things happen when Albion were struggling to move out of first gear.
With the crowd growing impatient at Albion's lack of offensive cohesion and Hull's dominance, Phillips was the one man who offered a ray of hope, showing real character and maturity in the process.
International fixtures don't resume until March and a lot can happen between now and then.
But Scotland boss Gordon Strachan surely faces one of the easiest decisions when the World Cup qualifying campaign returns.
With limited resources to work with (Hull's Robert Snodgrass is among the leading lights) Strachan simply has to recall Phillips, even if his form tails off a touch.
There's a good chance of that, because, let's be honest, Phillips can't surely maintain the red hot streak he's on right now.
He's a confidence player, and he's playing with more confidence now than at any point in his career.
rewrite:
The statistical contributions of West Bromwich Albion's principal creative force, Matt Phillips, are accumulating to a significant degree. His seventh and eighth assists in league competition, which precipitated a decisive turnaround in the match against Hull City, further enhance his standing. This output elevates Phillips—acquired from Queens Park Rangers for a notably modest fee of five million pounds—into a notable echelon of playmakers. Indeed, the current tally of assists from several of the nation's most celebrated creators, including Adam Lallana, Alexis Sánchez, Mesut Özil, and Christian Eriksen, is surpassed by that of the Scottish international.

Only a single player, Manchester City's Kevin De Bruyne, who commanded a transfer fee approximately eleven times greater, has provided more assists this season, with nine. It is noteworthy, however, that the Belgian international has scored half as many league goals as Phillips, who has registered four in his previous nine appearances. The reversal in his fortunes since being omitted from the squad for the fixture against Manchester City in October is particularly striking.

Beyond the raw statistics, the most compelling feature of Phillips' recent performance was his demonstrative willingness to demand possession and instigate attacking play during a period when his team was struggling to establish any offensive rhythm. As spectator impatience grew in response to Hull's dominance and Albion's disjointed play, Phillips provided a singular source of potential, exhibiting considerable character and maturity in the process.

With international fixtures not scheduled until March, the immediate future remains uncertain. Nevertheless, Scotland manager Gordon Strachan is presented with what appears to be a straightforward selection decision when World Cup qualification resumes. Given the limited pool of resources at his disposal—with Hull City's Robert Snodgrass representing another key figure—a recall for Phillips seems imperative, even allowing for the possibility of a slight diminution in his current form. Such a regression is plausible, as maintaining his present exceptional standard may prove unsustainable. Phillips is demonstrably a player whose performance is closely linked to confidence, and he is currently operating with a greater degree of self-assurance than at any prior point in his career.

Gene Simmons, KISS frontman and master capitalist, has filed a trademark application for a hand gesture that looks an awful lot like the heavy metal horns, the “rock on” hands–whatever you want to call them. It would be ridiculous for Simmons to claim such an iconic and widely used symbol as his own, but also understandable on some level, since the horns are within his purview as a hard rocker. But the gesture that he’s trying to trademark has little if anything to do with sex, drugs, or rock n roll: It’s the American Sign Language symbol for “I love you.”
Everyone, of course, knows the devil horns: Index and pinky extending toward the sky; thumb, middle, and ring fingers tucked into a little ball. As The Hollywood Reporter notes, Simmons filed a trademark application with the USPTO on June 9 for a gesture that’s similar, but with one crucial difference. It’s right there in his application (emphasis ours): “The mark consists of a hand gesture with the index and small fingers extended upward and the thumb extended perpendicular.”
The application also includes a drawing:
No self-respecting metalhead would show up to a concert with thumb extended perpendicular! But as you can see from the photo above, and the many more available online showing Simmons’ message of devotion to the ASL-speaking community, he is evidently no self-respecting metalhead.
Simmons’ application only covers use of the sign for uses of “entertainment, namely, live performances by a musical artist; personal appearances by a musical artist,” THR notes, so the ASL community needn’t worry about having to pay the guy a fee every time they want to get cute with their boyfriends and girlfriends. Read the full story–which includes a very funny anecdote about Jay Z, the pro wrestling great Diamond Dallas Page, and the garish electro duo 3OH!3–here.
rewrite:
Gene Simmons, the frontman of the band KISS and a figure noted for his commercial acumen, has submitted a trademark application to the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) for a specific hand gesture. This gesture bears a strong resemblance to the widely recognized "devil horns" or "rock on" hand sign prevalent in heavy metal culture. While any attempt to claim exclusive rights over such an iconic and ubiquitously employed symbol appears fundamentally untenable, it is perhaps contextually unsurprising given Simmons’ longstanding association with hard rock. However, the particular configuration detailed in his application diverges significantly from its cultural referent. According to the filing from June 9, as reported by *The Hollywood Reporter*, the mark consists of “a hand gesture with the index and small fingers extended upward and the thumb extended perpendicular.” This specific articulation—with the thumb extended outward—corresponds not to the traditional metal salute, but to the established American Sign Language (ASL) symbol for “I love you.”

The classic metal horns gesture is characterized by the index and pinky fingers extended skyward, with the thumb, middle, and ring fingers curled inward. The inclusion of a perpendicular thumb, as specified by Simmons, fundamentally alters the sign’s semantic meaning, transforming it from a symbol of rock affiliation to one of affection within ASL. The application includes a drawing that clearly depicts this configuration. As noted by *The Hollywood Reporter*, the sought trademark is narrowly scoped, applying only to uses within “entertainment, namely, live performances by a musical artist; personal appearances by a musical artist.” Consequently, this legal action does not purport to restrict the use of the ASL sign in its primary communicative context, thereby alleviating concerns within the Deaf community regarding everyday usage. The broader report on this matter includes further contextual commentary involving other public figures.

Conservation officers had to euthanize approximately one bear in every 30 complaints.
British Columbia’s Conservation Officer Service reports more than 20,000 conflicts between humans and wildlife around the province between January and October of this year.
Environment Ministry spokesman Mike Badry says about 14,000 of those complaints involve confrontations with black bears.
He says 469 bruins, or approximately one bear in every 30 complaints, had to be destroyed.
Spring and early summer produced the greatest number of complaints about bears, but Badry says the confrontations have tailed off, making 2017 an average year for complaints about wildlife.
RELATED: Bear complaints nearly double across B.C.
He warns that confrontations could increase because bears are now focused on finding as much food as possible before they hibernate.
Homeowners are urged to secure all food sources, such as garbage or compost and to ensure fruit trees are picked clean.
RELATED: Conservation investigating after having to euthanize bear
“These bears are trying to put on weight for denning throughout the winter, so they are highly motivated to find food,” Badry says.
“That is where we really put the emphasis on attractant management.”
The Canadian Press
rewrite:
Data from British Columbia’s Conservation Officer Service indicate that over 20,000 human-wildlife conflicts were recorded across the province between January and October of this year. According to Mike Badry, a spokesman for the Ministry of Environment, approximately 14,000 of these incidents involved encounters with black bears. Of these, 469 bears—representing roughly one bear per thirty complaints—were euthanized by conservation personnel. While the spring and early summer months yielded the highest volume of bear-related complaints, Badry notes that the frequency subsequently declined, rendering 2017 an average year for overall wildlife conflict reports.

Badry cautions, however, that encounters may rise as bears enter a hyperphagic state, intensifying foraging efforts to accumulate fat reserves prior to winter hibernation. He emphasizes that attractant management is critical during this period, urging residents to secure potential food sources such as garbage, compost, and fruit from trees. “These bears are highly motivated to find food to support weight gain for denning,” Badry states, underscoring the importance of preventive measures to reduce conflict.

U.S. President Barack Obama listens as he participates in his last news conference of the year at the White House in Washington, U.S., December 16, 2016. REUTERS/Carlos Barria
By Jeff Mason
HONOLULU (Reuters) - U.S. President Barack Obama will deliver a farewell address on Jan. 10 to reflect on his time in office and say thank you to his supporters, he said in an email statement released on Monday.
Obama, noting that the first president of the United States, George Washington, had penned a farewell address in 1796, said he would deliver his speech in his hometown of Chicago.
"I'm thinking about (the remarks) as a chance to say thank you for this amazing journey, to celebrate the ways you've changed this country for the better these past eight years, and to offer some thoughts on where we all go from here," he said.
Republican Donald Trump will be sworn in to office on Jan. 20. During his campaign for the White House, Trump pledged to undo many of Obama's signature policy measures, including his healthcare law.
Obama, who campaigned hard for Trump's Democratic opponent Hillary Clinton, has sought to ensure a smooth transition of power despite major policy differences with his successor. He also leaves his party without a clear figurehead as he leaves the White House.
"Since 2009, we've faced our fair share of challenges, and come through them stronger," Obama said in the email, likely foreshadowing a theme for his speech.
"That's because we have never let go of a belief that has guided us ever since our founding - our conviction that, together, we can change this country for the better."
(Reporting by Jeff Mason; Editing by Paul Tait)
rewrite:
On December 16, 2016, U.S. President Barack Obama concluded his annual schedule of press engagements with a final news conference at the White House in Washington. In an official email statement released on Monday, President Obama announced his intention to deliver a farewell address on January 10. The purpose of this address, as articulated in the statement, is to reflect upon his tenure in office and to express gratitude to his supporters. President Obama noted the historical precedent for such an address, referencing the farewell message delivered by the nation's first president, George Washington, in 1796. He plans to deliver his remarks in his hometown of Chicago.

In the statement, President Obama framed the upcoming address as an opportunity "to say thank you for this amazing journey, to celebrate the ways you've changed this country for the better these past eight years, and to offer some thoughts on where we all go from here." The political context for this valedictory speech is defined by the imminent inauguration of Republican President-elect Donald Trump on January 20. Throughout his campaign, Trump pledged to dismantle several of Obama's signature policy achievements, most notably the Affordable Care Act. Despite these profound policy differences, President Obama has worked to facilitate a smooth transition of power, having campaigned vigorously for Trump's Democratic opponent, Hillary Clinton. His departure also leaves the Democratic Party without a clear successor as its national leader.

Anticipating a central theme of his farewell remarks, President Obama’s statement reflected on the challenges faced during his administration, asserting, "Since 2009, we've faced our fair share of challenges, and come through them stronger." He attributed this resilience to a foundational national belief, stating, "That's because we have never let go of a belief that has guided us ever since our founding - our conviction that, together, we can change this country for the better."
