Treasury Secretary Steve Mnuchin said Monday the Trump administration’s target date to get tax reforms through Congress and on President Trump’s desk was “not realistic at this point.”
Mnuchin said in an interview with the Financial Times that the August deadline is set to falter following setbacks with Congress over health care.
“It is fair to say it is probably delayed a bit because of the healthcare,” Mnuchin told the paper.
Mnuchin added that he agreed with Trump that the dollar’s strength was hurting exports, but said he saw the strength of the dollar as a positive thing over the long term, according to Reuters.
“As the world’s currency, the primary reserve currency, I think that over long periods of time the strength of the dollar is a good thing,” he told the Financial Times.
Mnuchin said last month that the administration was planning to turn quickly to tax reform with the goal of getting a program approved by Congress by August. He said he had been overseeing work on the administration’s bill over the past two months and it would be introduced soon. He said it would be one proposal that would cover both cutting individual and corporate taxes in the same legislation.
Mnuchin added that if the timeline was delayed, he still expected a proposal to pass by the fall.
Press secretary Sean Spicer also acknowledged last month that the August deadline was an “ambitious one” for such a comprehensive and complicated project, but he said it’s a goal the administration “is going to try to stick to.”
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Click for more from Reuters.
rewrite:
In an interview with the Financial Times on Monday, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin stated that the Trump administration’s previously stated objective of enacting comprehensive tax reform legislation by August is “not realistic at this point.” Secretary Mnuchin attributed this anticipated delay primarily to legislative setbacks concerning healthcare reform, noting, “It is fair to say it is probably delayed a bit because of the healthcare.” He reaffirmed, however, that he expects a proposal to be passed by the fall.

Mnuchin further addressed economic policy in remarks reported by Reuters, concurring with President Trump’s assessment that the current strength of the U.S. dollar is detrimental to exports. Nevertheless, he emphasized a long-term positive view, telling the Financial Times, “As the world’s currency, the primary reserve currency, I think that over long periods of time the strength of the dollar is a good thing.”

The Treasury Secretary had previously outlined an accelerated timeline for tax reform. Last month, he indicated that the administration intended to swiftly pivot to tax legislation following healthcare, with the aim of Congressional approval by August. He reported overseeing the development of a unified legislative proposal over the preceding two months, designed to simultaneously reduce both individual and corporate tax rates within a single bill.

Administration officials have acknowledged the ambitious nature of the initial timeline. Press Secretary Sean Spicer remarked last month that the August deadline was an “ambitious one” for a policy initiative of such complexity but stated it remained a goal the administration “is going to try to stick to.”

The see-saw battle of temps will be on full display this weekend.
THIS EVENING: Temps will stay fairly steady as cold air mass starts to depart. Temps will fall only into the upper teens, with wind chill values near 10.
RISING TEMPS OVERNIGHT: As warmer air starts to return, temps will climb after midnight into the low 20s by Daybreak.
MILD SATURDAY: Temps will climb into the upper 30s and lower 40s Saturday, with a brisk SW wind. Snow, and even some rain / snow chances will hold off until around Midnight of after.
SUNDAY SNOW: We will see many hours of snowfall off and on Sunday, but temperatures are going to be key. Most of the day Sunday will see temps at or near 32°. This will cut down on the snowfall totals during those hours, in my opinion. After about 4pm, as colder air arrives, that will be the highest chance of more snow accumulation. Having said that, it looks to be a light snowfall total event. Most places will see 1″-3″ of snow, but I am leaning towards the low-end in most places. Southern Indiana looks to see 1″ or less.
8-DAY FORECAST…WINTER STORM TUESDAY / WEDNESDAY: The next storm system to keep a very close eye on will be Tuesday into Wednesday. This system could bring heavy snow, ice, or even some rain depending on track. Way to early to say who will get what, but keep checking in to the blob over the weekend, for updates and by Monday, should have a pretty good grasp of what may take place. Another clipper looks to arrive late next week.

A pronounced fluctuation in temperatures will be evident this weekend. This evening, temperatures will remain relatively stable as the incumbent cold air mass begins to recede. Overnight lows will only descend into the upper teens, with wind chill values approximating ten degrees. Subsequently, a warming trend will commence overnight, with temperatures rising after midnight and reaching the low twenties by dawn.

Saturday will be comparatively mild, with temperatures ascending into the upper thirties to lower forties amid a brisk southwesterly wind. Precipitation, including potential snow or a rain-snow mix, is expected to hold off until approximately midnight or later.

Intermittent snowfall is anticipated throughout much of Sunday. Temperature will be a critical determinant, however, with values expected to remain at or near freezing for most of the day. This is likely to suppress snow accumulation rates during these hours. A higher probability for more substantive accumulation will arrive after approximately 4:00 PM, as colder air infiltrates the region. Overall, this is forecast to be a light snowfall event, with most areas receiving between one and three inches. Current guidance suggests accumulations will tend toward the lower end of this range, with southern Indiana likely to see one inch or less.

Looking ahead, the next significant system to monitor will approach from Tuesday into Wednesday. This system possesses the potential to deliver heavy snow, ice, or rain, with specific impacts highly dependent on its eventual track. While precise details remain uncertain this far in advance, forecasts will solidify over the coming days. Another, weaker clipper system may arrive late in the upcoming week.

Kuskokwim Bay villages were battered by an autumn storm that intensified Wednesday night, and lasted through Thursday. Local leaders in Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk reported strong winds in the region. “My house was shaking,” said Roland Andrew, Kongiganak’s Tribal Administrator, with a laugh. “My family was kind of freaked!” Particularly, he said, his grandchildren.
The three communities also reported high water that flooded the lowlands. In Kwigillingok, the river overflowed its banks and filled nearby lakes, but the water didn’t threaten any homes or local infrastructure and the flooding was thankfully minor. “I’m hoping there’s none after this,” said Tribal Adminstrator Darrel John, who says that floods in Kwig can threaten the village’s homes and bridges. None of the three communities reported significant erosion.
The weather is getting colder and stormier and if your village is affected by any flooding, erosion, or wind damage by major storms, we want to hear from you. You can message news tips to KYUK on Facebook or email us at news@kyuk.org.

Local authorities in Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk documented severe wind conditions. Roland Andrew, the Tribal Administrator for Kongiganak, noted the structural shaking of his residence, remarking that his family, particularly his grandchildren, were considerably alarmed.

These three villages additionally reported elevated water levels inundating low-lying areas. In Kwigillingok, the river exceeded its banks, replenishing adjacent lakes; however, this flooding remained minor and did not endanger homes or critical infrastructure. Tribal Administrator Darrel John expressed concern, stating that such events in Kwigillingok historically pose risks to residential structures and bridges, and he voiced hope for no subsequent incidents. Significant erosion was not reported in any of the communities.

As seasonal conditions become increasingly cold and turbulent, KYUK solicits reports from villages experiencing flooding, erosion, or wind damage from major storms. News tips may be submitted via message to KYUK on Facebook or by email to news@kyuk.org.

SYDNEY (AP) — Raelene Castle will take over as chief executive officer at Rugby Australia next month, becoming the first woman to lead one of the major national unions in world rugby.
Castle, who has been CEO at Netball New Zealand and at the Canterbury Bulldogs in Australia's National Rugby League, will replace Bill Pulver on Jan. 15.
Rugby Australia Chairman Cameron Clyne announced the appointment Tuesday, saying Castle was the standout applicant among more than 200 candidates.
"I am especially looking forward to getting out into the rugby communities across Australia and meeting the diverse range of people that make the game tick," Castle said in a statement. "Having followed rugby closely for over 30 years and having worked in the New Zealand and Australian sporting environments for the past 10, there is no doubt Australian rugby has a clear international and domestic offering for both male and female athletes that can be further developed and strengthened."
Castle's other governance roles in sport have included serving as a board director of the International Federations of Netball Associations and as chair of the NRL club CEOs leadership group.
Clyne said Castle would bring "a fresh set of eyes to the challenges and opportunities at Rugby Australia, bringing to us her learnings from other codes."
"Through her most recent roles as CEO of the Bulldogs and Netball New Zealand, Raelene has led sporting organizations at both a national and club level, giving her an in-depth understanding of what it takes to run a national sporting body as well as the unique challenges for clubs and the importance of building strong relationships and a unity of purpose within," the sport, Clyne said. "Raelene is an extremely impressive executive who covered every base as far as what the board was looking for in a chief executive officer to lead our game into an important new chapter."
Castle was born in Australia and moved to New Zealand as a child, returning to Sydney in 2013 to take the job at the Bulldogs.
Castle is the first woman to lead one of Australia's four national football governing bodies, and Rugby Australia said she is the first woman to lead one of the world's top-tier rugby national governing bodies.
rewrite:

This appointment marks a historic milestone, as Castle becomes the first woman to lead one of the major national unions within world rugby. The announcement was made Tuesday by Rugby Australia Chairman Cameron Clyne, who stated that Castle emerged as the preeminent candidate from a field exceeding two hundred applicants.

Castle brings extensive executive experience from prominent sporting organizations, having previously served as CEO of both Netball New Zealand and the Canterbury Bulldogs in Australia’s National Rugby League. In a statement, Castle expressed her anticipation of engaging with rugby communities across Australia, noting, “Having followed rugby closely for over 30 years and having worked in the New Zealand and Australian sporting environments for the past 10, there is no doubt Australian rugby has a clear international and domestic offering for both male and female athletes that can be further developed and strengthened.” Her governance background includes roles as a board director for the International Federations of Netball Associations and as chair of the NRL club CEOs leadership group.

Chairman Clyne emphasized the strategic value of Castle’s appointment, highlighting that she will provide “a fresh set of eyes to the challenges and opportunities at Rugby Australia, bringing to us her learnings from other codes.” He further elaborated on her qualifications, stating, “Through her most recent roles… Raelene has led sporting organizations at both a national and club level, giving her an in-depth understanding of what it takes to run a national sporting body as well as the unique challenges for clubs and the importance of building strong relationships and a unity of purpose within the sport.” Clyne characterized Castle as an “extremely impressive executive” who comprehensively fulfilled the board’s criteria for a CEO to guide the organization into a significant new phase.

Born in Australia, Castle moved to New Zealand as a child before returning to Sydney in 2013 for her role with the Bulldogs. Her appointment is doubly historic: she is not only the first woman to lead one of Australia’s four major national football governing bodies, but, according to Rugby Australia, is also the first woman to assume leadership of a top-tier national rugby union globally.

Three members of Grantham Running Club participated in the seventh annual Brass Monkey 10K race on Sunday.
The race was held at Rockingham Motor Speedway in Northamptonshire, in support of Lakelands Hospice, Corby. In warmer than expected temperatures and under a blue sky, any hope of personal bests was soon dashed due to the high winds in the exposed location.
Paul Rushworth with the newest addition to his family post-race at Helsby.
There was a large turnout of more than 550 runners and some wheelchair racers for this event around the banked speedway circuit.
Travelling at somewhat less than the lap record of 215mph, Stuart Baty came home in 134th place in a time of 50min 44sec, with Simon Hartley finishing in 62:29 and Lucinda Gamble in 68:50.
All three were members of last year’s very popular and successful 10 weeks to 10K programme run by Grantham Running Club and have participated in a number of events since their graduation.
l Grantham Running Club’s Paul Rushworth travelled to Helsby, near Chester, to take part in the Four Villages Half Marathon last Sunday.
The race visited Dunham-on-the-Hill, Mouldsworth and Manley before returning to Helsby along quiet country lanes. This year’s event was run in extreme conditions with wintery sleet showers blowing across the course for the duration of the event.
Despite the tough conditions, Paul finished in a creditable 1:35:50, making full use of the final three-mile steady downhill sections to increase his speed to the finish.
Paul also took the opportunity to introduce the new arrival in his family to the world of running.

The race was hosted at the Rockingham Motor Speedway in Northamptonshire, organized in support of Lakelands Hospice in Corby. Although conditions featured warmer than anticipated temperatures and clear skies, prospects for achieving personal best times were hindered by strong winds across the exposed circuit. The event attracted a substantial field of over 550 runners, alongside several wheelchair athletes, who completed laps of the banked speedway course. Representing the club, Stuart Baty finished in 134th position with a time of 50 minutes and 44 seconds, followed by Simon Hartley in 62:29 and Lucinda Gamble in 68:50. All three athletes are graduates of the club’s well-regarded "10 Weeks to 10K" programme from the previous year and have since continued their involvement in numerous competitive events.

Separately, club member Paul Rushworth competed in the Four Villages Half Marathon in Helsby, near Chester, on the same weekend. The course traversed Dunham-on-the-Hill, Mouldsworth, and Manley before concluding in Helsby via quiet rural lanes. This year’s race was conducted under severe weather conditions, with persistent wintry sleet showers throughout. Despite the challenging environment, Rushworth delivered a commendable performance, finishing in 1 hour, 35 minutes, and 50 seconds. He effectively utilized a steady three-mile downhill segment in the final segment to accelerate toward the finish. Additionally, Rushworth marked the occasion by introducing his newborn child to the running community post-race.

AKRON, Ohio — Malcolm Duvivier hit 6 of 9 from 3-point range and scored 24 and Daniel Utomi added a double-double to propel Akron to a 94-89 victory over Appalachian State on Saturday night in a game that tipped off three hours late because of weather conditions.
Utomi finished with 18 points and 10 rebounds and the sophomore buried two late 3-pointers to help the Zips (5-2) hold off the Mountaineers (5-6) in the first meeting between the schools.
Griffin Kinney poured in a career-high 28 points for Appalachian State. The senior made 9 of 13 shots from the floor and 9 of 11 free throws. Ronshad Shabazz scored 18 of his 26 points in the second half and added five assists, while Justin Forrest scored 13 with five assists.
Virshon Cotton and Duvivier hit back-to-back 3-pointers to key a 14-7 run and the Zips led 47-38 at the half.
The Mountaineers battled back and led 77-76 on two Kinney free throws with 4:32 remaining in the game, but Cotton hit two free throws, Duvivier made a jumper and Utomi hit back-to-back 3s to push the lead 86-79 and the Zips held on from there.
rewrite:

The Akron Zips ultimately secured a 94-89 victory. Teammate Daniel Utomi contributed a double-double with 18 points and 10 rebounds, and his two critical three-pointers in the game's closing moments helped solidify the win for Akron, which improved its record to 5-2.

Appalachian State (5-6) was led by Griffin Kinney, who achieved a career-high 28 points on efficient shooting, making 9 of 13 field goal attempts and 9 of 11 free throws. Ronshad Shabazz added 26 points, 18 of which occurred in the second half, alongside five assists. Justin Forrest also contributed 13 points and five assists.

Akron established a 47-38 halftime lead, aided by a 14-7 scoring run featuring consecutive three-pointers from Virshon Cotton and Duvivier. Appalachian State mounted a second-half comeback, briefly taking a 77-76 lead with 4:32 remaining. However, a sequence of free throws by Cotton, a jumper by Duvivier, and Utomi's consecutive three-pointers extended Akron's advantage to 86-79, a margin they maintained for the remainder of the contest.

A tower block in London where at least 12 people died is still burning this morning - over 24 hours later.
No one is expected to have made it out alive from the top two floors of the tower.

Paul Littlejohn live nearby

In close proximity to the site, the Al-Manaar mosque has been established as a temporary relief centre, receiving supplies from across the region. Prime Minister Theresa May has publicly expressed condolences to the victims of the catastrophic fire.

Applications for a further three Russian athletes to compete as neutrals have been filed to the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).
According to Russia's state news agency TASS, the Russian Athletics Federation (RusAF) has sent the appeals of Daniil Kotov, Yegor Nikolayev and Anatoliy Ryapolov to the global governing body.
RusAF remains banned from international athletics competitions due to doping allegations, pending its completion of reinstatement criteria.
Athletes are permitted to compete neutrally if they can demonstrate they have been operating in an "effective testing system".
The ban, which has been in place since November 2015, was maintained by the IAAF Council last month.
RusAF spokesperson Natalia Yukhareva told TASS that there were still 50 applications which have not yet been filed.
In total this year, 47 applications have been approved, of which nine were specifically for the World Under-18 Championships in Kenya’s capital Nairobi and two were specifically for the European Under-20 Championships in Italian city Grosseto.
A total of 109 applications have been declined.
Yegor Nikolayev is among those hoping to be able to compete as a neutral athlete ©Getty Images
Nineteen Russians competed as Authorised Neutral Athletes at this year's IAAF World Championships in London.
They won a total of six medals, including one gold, and would have placed ninth overall, above Germany.
RusAF President Dmitry Shlyakhtin said earlier this month that he expects Russia to have to participate as neutrals at the World Indoor Championships in Birmingham in March.
Long jumper Ryapolov claimed the gold medal at the 2014 Youth Olympic Games in Nanjing and won the world youth title in Donestk in 2013.
He also topped the podium at the 2015 European Junior Championships.
Kotov won a silver medal in the pole vault event at the 2014 World Championships in Eugene in the United States.
Nikolayev, a middle distance runner, was part of the Russian team which was second at the European Team Championships in Stockholm in 2012.
He has also finished fourth at the 2013 and 2015 editions of the Summer Universiade.
rewrite:
The International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF) has received applications for a further three Russian athletes—Daniil Kotov, Yegor Nikolayev, and Anatoliy Ryapolov—to obtain eligibility to compete as Authorised Neutral Athletes. According to reports from the Russian state news agency TASS, these appeals were submitted by the Russian Athletics Federation (RusAF). RusAF itself remains suspended from international competition due to doping violations, a ban upheld by the IAAF Council last month and originally instituted in November 2015. Its reinstatement is contingent upon satisfying specific criteria. Under the prevailing regulations, individual athletes may apply for neutral status provided they can substantiate that they have been subject to an effective anti-doping testing system outside the suspended federation’s framework.

A RusAF spokesperson, Natalia Yukhareva, indicated via TASS that approximately fifty applications from Russian athletes are still pending submission. To date in the current year, the IAAF has approved forty-seven applications for neutral athlete status. Of these, nine were specifically for the World Under-18 Championships in Nairobi and two for the European Under-20 Championships in Grosseto. Conversely, a total of one hundred and nine applications have been declined. The precedent for such participation was set at the recent IAAF World Championships in London, where nineteen Authorised Neutral Athletes from Russia competed, securing six medals, including one gold. This collective performance would have ranked ninth in the overall medal table, ahead of Germany. RusAF President Dmitry Shlyakhtin has subsequently expressed anticipation that Russian athletes will again participate as neutrals at the forthcoming World Indoor Championships in Birmingham.

The three athletes in question have established competitive records. Anatoliy Ryapolov, a long jumper, secured gold at the 2014 Youth Olympic Games in Nanjing and won the world youth title in 2013, in addition to topping the podium at the 2015 European Junior Championships. Daniil Kotov earned a silver medal in the pole vault at the 2014 World Championships in Eugene, Oregon. Middle-distance runner Yegor Nikolayev was a member of the Russian team that placed second at the 2012 European Team Championships in Stockholm and has also achieved fourth-place finishes at the 2013 and 2015 Summer Universiade.

BATTLEFORD, Sask. — A Saskatchewan farmer who was acquitted last month in the fatal shooting of a young Indigenous man is to be back in court April 16 to face gun charges.
Gerald Stanley was charged in November 2016 with two counts of unsafe storage of firearms and his case was up Monday in a Battleford, Sask., courtroom.
The charges relate to the police investigation that began after 22-year-old Colten Boushie was shot and killed on Stanley’s farm in August 2016.
Some of Boushie’s family were outside court holding signs that read “Justice Against Institutional Racism” and “Blood On Your Hands.”
Stanley wasn’t in court nor was his lawyer, Scott Spencer, who called in for the proceeding.
The Crown asked for more time in the case.
Penalties for unsafe storage of a firearm range from a conditional discharge — which means no criminal record — to a fine, to a prison sentence.
Last month, a jury found Stanley not guilty of second-degree murder in Boushie’s death.
Boushie was one of five young people who drove onto Stanley’s farm near Biggar in 2016. His friends testified they were looking for help with a flat tire.
Stanley told the trial he thought they were trying to steal an all-terrain vehicle. He testified he fired warning shots to scare them away and the gun accidentally went off again when he went to pull the keys from their SUV.
(CTV Saskatoon, The Canadian Press)
rewrite:
In Battleford, Saskatchewan, a farmer previously acquitted in the fatal shooting of an Indigenous man is scheduled to reappear in court on April 16 to address separate firearms charges. Gerald Stanley, who was charged in November 2016 with two counts of unsafe storage of firearms, had his case called in a Battleford courtroom. These charges stem from the police investigation initiated after 22-year-old Colten Boushie was shot and killed on Stanley’s property in August 2016.

Outside the courthouse, members of Boushie’s family demonstrated, holding signs with messages such as “Justice Against Institutional Racism” and “Blood On Your Hands.” Neither Stanley nor his legal counsel, Scott Spencer, were physically present; Spencer participated in the proceedings via telephone. The Crown prosecution requested an adjournment to allow further preparation. Convictions for unsafe firearm storage can result in penalties ranging from a conditional discharge—which carries no criminal record—to monetary fines or incarceration.

Last month, a jury found Stanley not guilty of second-degree murder in connection with Boushie’s death. The incident occurred when Boushie and four others drove onto Stanley’s farm near Biggar. According to trial testimony from his companions, the group was seeking assistance for a flat tire. Stanley testified that he believed they were attempting to steal an all-terrain vehicle. He stated that he discharged warning shots to deter them and that the firearm accidentally discharged a second time as he moved to remove the keys from their vehicle.

(Source: CTV Saskatoon, The Canadian Press)

By Lloyd Gumbo
Parliament has urged the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education to improve its communication, so that members of the public and other stakeholders can buy into its new initiatives.
Members of the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Education, Sport, Arts and Culture told Primary and Secondary Education Minister Dr Lazarus Dokora that poor communication was his ministry’s greatest let down.
They said this when Minister Dokora appeared before the committee last week.
Mutasa Central MP Mr Trevor Saruwaka (MDC-T) said it was important for the ministry to improve on its communication strategies if its programmes were to be supported.
“Your tenure as the Minister of Education has been riddled or characterised by controversies, for instance on incentives, e-enrolment, new curriculum or on the National Pledge,” said Mr Saruwaka.
“Don’t you think there is a problem with communication between your ministry and your stakeholders and the nation at large? When you present your issues, they seem quite clear, but it appears there is a disconnection between what you know and what you want to do and the communication with the rest of the nation, where you end up being fought from all angles? Don’t you think you need to do something about communication from your ministry to the nation?”
Zanu-PF MP for Pelandaba-Mpopoma, Cde Joseph Tshuma added: “The minister and his ministry are lacking one thing and its communication. Let me give you an example of STEM, when it came in, I remember when it was first implemented, even Cabinet had not approved it, but because of jingles and talking, people started buying into it”, he said.
Dr Dokora acknowledged that his ministry had not done enough to communicate its initiatives.
“On communication, I agree with you,” he said.
“My biggest challenge is having bodies in the communication system who cannot perform the task.
This ministry has raised expectations, we must be able to communicate. The Herald
rewrite:
The Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Education, Sport, Arts and Culture has formally advised the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education to enhance its external communications to foster greater public and stakeholder support for its policy initiatives. This recommendation was directed to the Minister, Dr. Lazarus Dokora, during a committee session last week, where legislators identified deficient communication as a principal shortcoming of the ministry.

In his remarks, Mr. Trevor Saruwaka, the Member of Parliament for Mutasa Central (MDC-T), emphasized the critical need for the ministry to refine its communication strategies to secure broader endorsement for its programmes. He noted that the minister’s tenure has been marked by public controversies regarding policies such as teacher incentives, electronic enrolment systems, curricular reforms, and the introduction of a national pledge. Mr. Saruwaka posed a series of rhetorical questions, suggesting a significant disconnect between the ministry’s internal understanding of its objectives and the public’s perception thereof, which has resulted in widespread opposition. He urged the minister to address this communicative gap.

This sentiment was echoed by Cde Joseph Tshuma, the Zanu-PF MP for Pelandaba-Mpopoma, who cited the example of the STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) initiative. He observed that public acceptance of the programme was initially cultivated through promotional jingles and discourse, even prior to formal Cabinet approval, thereby illustrating the power of effective outreach.

In response, Minister Dokora conceded the validity of these criticisms, acknowledging that the ministry’s communication efforts have been insufficient. He attributed part of the challenge to capacity constraints within the ministry’s communications unit, stating that personnel tasked with this function have underperformed. The minister recognized the elevated public expectations placed upon the ministry and affirmed the necessity of improving communication, specifically referencing the potential role of *The Herald* newspaper in this endeavour.

Image copyright Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire Image caption The 65,000-tonne ship set sail from Rosyth dockyard in June
The UK's new £3bn aircraft carrier will arrive in its home port on Wednesday, the Royal Navy has confirmed.
HMS Queen Elizabeth is due to sail into Portsmouth at about 07:10 BST following extensive preparations at the naval base.
Weather conditions meant the exact date could not be confirmed until Monday.
The 65,000-tonne ship has been undergoing sea trials since setting sail from Rosyth dockyard in Fife, where it was built, in June.
The 900ft (280m) long carrier cannot currently deploy planes but flying trials are due to begin next year, with 10 F-35 Lightning II jets and 120 aircrew preparing for the task in the US.
It is expected to be the Navy's flagship for the next 50 years.
Preparations for the arrival of the future flagship of the fleet, and its 700 staff, saw more than 20,000 items ranging from a human skull to sea mines dredged up from Portsmouth Harbour.
The Ministry of Defence said specialist dredging vessels had removed 3.2m cubic metres of sediment - the equivalent to 1,280 Olympic swimming pools - during the dredging operation carried out to deepen the harbour mouth to enable the Queen Elizabeth to reach Portsmouth naval base.
In a statement earlier this month, Defence Secretary Sir Michael Fallon heralded the ship's impending arrival, and declared it would be deployed "across the seven seas, using her strike power to deter our enemies".
rewrite:
The United Kingdom’s new aircraft carrier, HMS Queen Elizabeth, is scheduled to arrive at its home port of Portsmouth on Wednesday, as confirmed by the Royal Navy. The £3 billion vessel is expected to enter the harbour at approximately 07:10 British Summer Time, following comprehensive preparatory work at the naval base. Adverse weather conditions had previously prevented confirmation of the precise arrival date until this Monday.

Constructed at the Rosyth dockyard in Fife, the 65,000-tonne carrier commenced sea trials in June after departing from its construction site. Measuring 280 metres in length, the ship is not yet equipped to deploy aircraft; however, flying trials are planned to initiate next year. In preparation, ten F-35 Lightning II jets and 120 associated aircrew are currently training in the United States. HMS Queen Elizabeth is projected to serve as the Royal Navy’s flagship for the next half-century.

Extensive harbour preparations for the carrier and its 700 personnel involved the removal of over 20,000 items from Portsmouth Harbour, ranging from historical artefacts such as a human skull to obsolete sea mines. The Ministry of Defence reported that specialist dredging vessels extracted 3.2 million cubic metres of sediment—equivalent to the volume of 1,280 Olympic swimming pools—to deepen the harbour entrance sufficiently for the vessel’s access.

In a statement earlier this month, Defence Secretary Sir Michael Fallon heralded the imminent arrival, asserting that the carrier would be deployed globally to utilise its strike capabilities as a deterrent against adversaries.

A new £1 million fund to tackle drug and crime will be set by the Labour West Midlands mayor if elected later this year.
It is the latest pledge from Labour candidate Siôn Simon who is placing the war on "everyday crime" at the centre of his campaign.
He is teaming up with the West Midlands Police Commissioner David Jamieson to put £1 million on the table for a new drugs and gangs task force if he is installed in the mayor's office in May.
Mr Simon will also demand new powers from London to tackle the scourge of crime.
He said: "Unreported gang and drug-related crimes, or so-called everyday crime, needn't be a reality for us.
"But we can't rely on politicians in London who tell us crime isn’t going up.
"Because, for many people I speak to across the West Midlands, that couldn't be further from the truth.
"With a new West Midlands mayor, someone from here who understands the problems that we face, we can finally do something about it. It's time for us to get tough on crime."
He said the task force would limit the supply of young people to gangs and drug dealers by creating initiatives and activities to prevent them being tempted by a life of crime.
He said: "We need to find diversions for these at-risk young people before they are drawn into gangs and crime."
Last week, he also pledged to defend police numbers in the region.
Police commissioner David Jamieson last year ran a drugs and violence commission to look into the issue and the task force will follow through on its recommendations.
Mr Simon is one of five candidates currently bidding to become West Midlands mayor.
rewrite:
Siôn Simon on Crime and Funding Cuts to Police Forces in the West Midlands

Labour candidate Siôn Simon has positioned the reduction of "everyday crime" as a central pillar of his campaign for the West Midlands mayoralty, an election scheduled for later this year. In collaboration with the current West Midlands Police and Crime Commissioner, David Jamieson, Mr. Simon has pledged to establish a new £1 million fund dedicated to a drugs and gangs task force, contingent upon his election in May. This initiative represents his latest policy commitment on the issue.

Mr. Simon argues that unreported gang and drug-related offences, often categorised as everyday crime, constitute a pervasive reality that must be confronted. He has expressed scepticism towards political narratives originating from London which suggest crime is not increasing, stating that for many residents across the region, such assertions are profoundly disconnected from their lived experience. He contends that a mayor from the West Midlands, possessing direct understanding of local challenges, is essential for implementing effective solutions. "It is time for us to get tough on crime," he asserted.

The proposed task force would aim to disrupt criminal supply lines and, critically, implement preventative measures. Mr. Simon emphasised the strategy of creating targeted initiatives and activities designed to divert at-risk young people from gang involvement and criminal exploitation before they are drawn into such networks. "We need to find diversions for these at-risk young people," he stated, framing intervention as a key mechanism for limiting the recruitment pool for gangs and drug dealers.

Furthermore, Mr. Simon has recently committed to defending police officer numbers within the region against potential reductions. His proposed task force is intended to build upon the work of a drugs and violence commission chaired by Commissioner Jamieson last year, by enacting its subsequent recommendations. Mr. Simon is one of five candidates currently seeking the position of West Midlands Mayor.

One Council Bans Bouncy Castles After Norfolk Death
A council in the South of England has banned bouncy castles following the death of a three-year-old girl in Gorleston on Sunday.
Ava-May Littleboy from Suffolk died from a head injury after being thrown from an inflatable trampoline.
In a statement issued on Wednesday, Havant Borough Council, which is near Portsmouth, said no incidents or concerns had been raised in the area.
But in the wake of the incident in Norfolk, a council spokesman said: "It has been decided that until the reason for the explosion of the bouncy castle has been identified, such that the risk can be properly managed by the event organiser, Havant Borough Council will not permit the use of bouncy castles or inflatables at any events taking place on its land.
"The position will be reviewed once the outcome of the inquiry into the cause of the explosion of the bouncy castle is known."
Experts are examining the equipment on the beach in Gorleston.
Police said witnesses reported hearing a "loud bang" before the inflatable "apparently burst" at the seaside site.
The incident has led to calls for the Government to consider a temporary ban on inflatables in public spaces.
The regulations surrounding inflatables has also been raised in the Commons today by the MP for Harlow, where 7 year old Summer Grant from Norwich died in 2016, when the bouncy castle she was on blew away.
Robert Halfon said action was needed after "two horrific tragedies".
rewrite:
In response to a fatal incident in Norfolk, a local authority in southern England has prohibited the use of inflatable amusement structures, including bouncy castles, on its property. The decision by Havant Borough Council, located near Portsmouth, follows the death of a three-year-old girl, Ava-May Littleboy of Suffolk, who sustained a fatal head injury after being ejected from an inflatable trampoline in Gorleston on Sunday. Although the council confirmed no prior local incidents or concerns had been reported, it has enacted a precautionary suspension pending the investigation's findings. A council spokesman stated that the prohibition will remain until the cause of the inflatable's failure is identified and appropriate risk management protocols can be assured for event organizers. The policy will be reassessed upon conclusion of the official inquiry.

Authorities are currently examining the equipment involved in the Gorleston beach incident, with police reports indicating witness accounts of a loud noise preceding the apparatus's apparent rupture. This event has prompted calls for governmental consideration of a temporary nationwide ban on such inflatables in public areas. Furthermore, the regulatory framework governing these structures was raised in parliamentary discussion, notably by Robert Halfon, Member of Parliament for Harlow. He referenced this incident alongside the 2016 death of seven-year-old Summer Grant in Norwich, who was killed when a bouncy castle became airborne, urging legislative action in light of these two tragedies.

Mohamed Salah has become the first player to score 10 goals in Europe in a single season for Liverpool.
The Egypt star struck twice in the first half of Tuesday's Champions League semi-final first leg with Roma at Anfield.
Salah curled home a spectacular opening goal 35 minutes in, before a delightful chipped second made it 2-0 at the break.
It means the 25-year-old is the first Reds player to reach double figures for goals in a European campaign, while he is also the first African player to score at least nine in a single Champions League tournament.
Salah, who was crowned the PFA Players' Player of the Year on Sunday for his Premier League performances, has now hit 43 goals in all competitions in his first season with Liverpool.
He is just four goals short of equalling the record for goals in a season, set by Ian Rush in 1983-84.
rewrite: Mohamed Salah has achieved the distinction of becoming the inaugural Liverpool player to score ten goals in European competition within a single season. The Egyptian forward accomplished this feat by scoring twice during the first half of the UEFA Champions League semi-final first leg against AS Roma at Anfield on Tuesday. His opening goal, a precisely curled finish in the 35th minute, was followed by an adeptly chipped effort to establish a 2-0 lead by halftime. Consequently, the 25-year-old is also the first African footballer to register a minimum of nine goals in a singular Champions League tournament. Having recently been awarded the PFA Players' Player of the Year for his domestic performances, Salah has now tallied 43 goals across all competitions in his debut Liverpool campaign. He currently trails the club's single-season scoring record, held by Ian Rush since the 1983-84 season, by only four goals.

A blaze on Saddleworth Moor which fire crews have been fighting for more than a week is being treated as arson.
Police say witnesses reported that people were lighting a bonfire on the moorland above Stalybridge, Greater Manchester, on the early evening of Sunday June 24 - about 50 minutes before the first emergency call to raise the alarm.
The fire on land at Buckton Vale, east of Manchester, later led two days later to the evacuation of dozens of homes in the village of Carrbrook as flames threatened to engulf properties and continued to spread as fire crews from across the country, with the assistance of the Army, successfully battled to keep the area safe.
On Wednesday with the fire still burning, although under control, Greater Manchester Police said the bonfire sighting was being pursued as a possible line of inquiry.
(Image: PA)
Chief Superintendent Neil Evans said: "The moorland fire is now being investigated as arson following information from local witnesses and initial inquiries.
"The scale of this fire is exceptional and we are treating it with the utmost seriousness.
"That said, we are under no illusion that solid evidence as to where the fire started and what was the cause will not be easy to establish."
rewrite:
A wildfire on Saddleworth Moor, which fire services have been combating for over a week, is now being investigated as a case of arson. According to police, witnesses reported individuals igniting a bonfire on the moorland above Stalybridge, Greater Manchester, during the early evening of Sunday, June 24. This sighting occurred approximately fifty minutes prior to the initial emergency call alerting authorities. The blaze, located on land at Buckton Vale east of Manchester, escalated over the subsequent days. By Tuesday, it necessitated the evacuation of dozens of homes in the village of Carrbrook as advancing flames threatened residential properties. Fire crews from across the nation, assisted by the Army, worked to contain the spread and protect the area.

On Wednesday, with the fire still burning but under control, Greater Manchester Police confirmed that the reported bonfire incident constituted a significant line of inquiry. Chief Superintendent Neil Evans stated that the moorland fire is officially being investigated as arson based on information from local witnesses and preliminary investigations. He emphasized the exceptional scale of the incident and the seriousness with which it is being treated. However, he also acknowledged the investigative challenges, noting that securing definitive evidence regarding the fire's precise origin and cause will be difficult to establish.

We are still more than a week away from the famed total solar eclipse of 2017. The event, which will be experienced in some way across much of the U.S., is rare but thankfully, it won’t go uncelebrated.
Now, just to put it in perspective, this eclipse will take place on August 21 over a period of a few minutes and will be most impacting and visible across a swath of the U.S. that is less than 100 miles wide. So, yes, it will get dark that day – for a few minutes. But there is certainly a load of prepublicity and, of course, savvy marketers that are promoting travel to the heaviest impacted areas – also known as the area of totality.
You can buy special eclipse glasses, t-shirts and other memorabilia. Experts have been all over the media with predictions on animal behavior with bird and insects and reptiles going into night mode during the event.
The bottom line is that there is a load of attention being placed on the eclipse that will only last a few brief minutes, but has captured the attention of the country. So, prepare for at least a little darkness unless you have made travel plans to make it to the prime viewing area. Hopefully, this novel event will distract the country for a little while from political strife and international challenges. And hopefully, Mother Nature will cooperate and it will be a clear day – because nothing ruins an eclipse more than clouds. Happy eclipse watching, East Texas!

Substantial public anticipation has been generated, accompanied by commercial initiatives promoting travel to regions within the path of greatest obscuration. Imagine that you’ve been struggling with a serious and fairly embarrassing personal problem. Putting aside a longstanding reluctance to address it, you finally consult a therapist. The therapist is friendly and welcoming and promises to protect your privacy. Gaining a sense of trust, you bare your soul, describing the issue you are struggling with in all of its painful detail.
Only later do you realize, to your horror, that your confessions were being recorded and retained by the therapist. It turns out that your therapist, to supplement his income, has gotten into the advertising business: He takes data gleaned from his patients and offers it to advertisers (or any other interested party) for a fee.
Everyone would be outraged by this; it is professionally unethical and a serious breach of trust. Yet what I’ve described is not so different from our relationship with businesses like Google, Facebook, Quora and Amazon. They hold themselves out as trustworthy, enticing us to share our information with them — from the banal details of our lives to our most intimate secrets — without making it very clear that everything is being recorded, kept and used for advertising.
The Europeans find this kind of thing distasteful, which is why last Friday they instituted a strict online privacy law — the General Data Protection Regulation. The law’s approach is, for want of a better word, European: broad, rule-driven and administered by regulators. Under the G.D.P.R., any company that gathers or processes personal data is defined as a “data controller” and is subject to a raft of new rights and duties that are enforced by Europe’s member states.
rewrite:
Consider a scenario in which an individual grapples with a significant and personally sensitive issue. After overcoming a prolonged hesitation to seek help, they finally engage a therapist. This professional presents as congenial and trustworthy, explicitly assuring confidentiality. Consequently, the patient, feeling secure, divulges the intricate and distressing details of their private struggle. Subsequently, however, they discover with alarm that their disclosures were systematically recorded and archived. The therapist, it is revealed, has monetized this confidential data by selling it to advertisers or other third parties to supplement personal income. Such conduct would universally be deemed an egregious ethical violation and a profound betrayal of fiduciary duty.

This analogy is not far removed from contemporary digital interactions. Corporations such as Google, Facebook, Quora, and Amazon position themselves as reliable services, encouraging users to entrust them with information ranging from mundane daily details to profoundly intimate secrets. Often, the extent to which this data is perpetually recorded, retained, and leveraged for targeted advertising is not made sufficiently transparent. European regulatory bodies have explicitly condemned this model as objectionable, leading to the implementation of the stringent General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) last Friday.

The GDPR embodies a characteristically European regulatory philosophy: comprehensive, rule-based, and overseen by centralized authorities. It designates any entity collecting or processing personal data as a "data controller," subjecting them to an extensive array of new obligations and user rights. Enforcement is delegated to the member states, establishing a robust legal framework intended to redress the power imbalance between individuals and data-intensive enterprises.

It seems like every time you visit your favorite watering hole, the same bartenders are there. It’s almost like they don’t even go home or take a break, right? Well, bartenders aren’t superhuman cyborgs from the future bent on global domination who don’t require sleep, rest, and relaxation. Just like you, they need a break or a day off every now and then. And just because they mix up drinks all day, that doesn’t mean they don’t enjoy throwing back a few cocktails in their time off. This is especially true on a sunny, warm, summer day. That’s why we asked ten bartenders to tell us what they like to drink on those rare occasions they aren’t standing behind the bar concocting your favorite cocktails.
Zach Rivera, Beverage Director at Headquarters Beercade in Chicago and Nashville
Shutterstock
“My favorite (on a warm day) and also the most annoying to make is probably a mojito. It’s refreshing, delicious, and easy to drink.”
Tara Shadzi, Lead Bartender at BOA Steakhouse in Santa Monica, California
Shutterstock
“The best cocktail to drink outside in the Southern California sunshine has got to be the pina colada. Yes, it’s overplayed, but so delicious. Try it with real coconut, aged Zacapa rum, pineapple, and agave. Or better yet, try the mescal BOA version called the “Fire and Smoke.” A smoky, spicy, pineapple mescal drink is just calling your name for a summer patio happy hour session.”
rewrite:
It may appear to the frequent patron that bartenders are perpetually present at their establishments, seldom departing or taking respite. However, bartenders are not superhuman entities devoid of need for rest, relaxation, or personal time. Like all individuals, they require periodic breaks and days away from their professional duties. Furthermore, the fact that their occupation involves mixing beverages does not preclude their enjoyment of consuming cocktails during their leisure time. This inclination is particularly pronounced on warm, sunny summer days. To explore this subject, ten bartenders were consulted regarding their preferred drinks during those intervals when they are not professionally engaged in cocktail preparation.

Zach Rivera, Beverage Director at Headquarters Beercade in Chicago and Nashville, stated: "My preferred warm-weather beverage, which is also notably labor-intensive to prepare, is likely the mojito. It is refreshing, flavorful, and easily consumed."

Tara Shadzi, Lead Bartender at BOA Steakhouse in Santa Monica, California, remarked: "The optimal cocktail for outdoor consumption in Southern California sunshine is undoubtedly the piña colada. While arguably commonplace, it remains exceptionally palatable. I recommend its preparation with fresh coconut, aged Zacapa rum, pineapple, and agave. Alternatively, one might sample BOA's mescal variation, the 'Fire and Smoke.' This smoky, spicy pineapple and mescal concoction is ideally suited for a summer patio happy hour."

Joachim Low praised his players for a job well done after Germany clinched a place at next year's World Cup with a commanding 3-1 victory over Northern Ireland.
The reigning world champions secured a ninth straight win in qualifying on Thursday to guarantee they will finish top of Group C and play at the showpiece tournament for the 19th time in their history.
Bayern Munich midfielder Sebastian Rudy gave Germany a superb start with a long-range strike inside two minutes before former Hoffenheim team-mate Sandro Wagner added a second goal in the 21st minute.
Joshua Kimmich volleyed in a third in the closing minutes and although Northern Ireland found the net in injury time through Josh Magennis, Low refused to let conceding at the death dampen his mood.
"​I am satisfied," Low told reporters afterwards in Belfast.
"We doubled the lead very quickly. In the Czech Republic we took the lead early too but then lost control. That did not happen today.
"We felt on the pitch that we had everything under control in the second half. That's when we slowed down a little bit."
Rudy's stunning opener was crucial against a Northern Ireland side who had not conceded a goal in qualifying since losing the reverse fixture 2-0 in Hannover last October.
The 27-year-old's effort – his first in international football – put Germany on their way to Russia - and now they can focus on retaining the World Cup.
"The goal was extremely important. We dominated the match the whole time," Rudy said.
"We're going to Russia to win something. We want to defend the title."
rewrite:
Following a decisive 3-1 victory over Northern Ireland that secured qualification for the forthcoming World Cup, Germany’s head coach Joachim Löw commended his squad’s performance. The reigning world champions, having now achieved nine consecutive qualifying victories, ensured they will finish at the summit of Group C and will participate in the tournament for a nineteenth occasion. The match commenced with an exceptional long-range strike from Bayern Munich midfielder Sebastian Rudy within two minutes, a lead which was extended in the 21st minute by Sandro Wagner, Rudy’s former Hoffenheim teammate. A third goal was volleyed home by Joshua Kimmich in the final minutes. A late consolation goal from Northern Ireland’s Josh Magennis during injury time did not diminish Löw’s overall satisfaction, as expressed in his post-match remarks in Belfast.

Löw indicated particular satisfaction with the team’s sustained control following the rapid establishment of a two-goal advantage, contrasting it with a previous match against the Czech Republic where an early lead was relinquished. He noted that the team deliberately moderated its tempo in the second half while maintaining full command of proceedings. Rudy’s early goal proved particularly critical against an opponent that had maintained an unbreached defense throughout qualifying since the reverse fixture in October 2016. This inaugural international goal for the 27-year-old set the foundation for the victory and subsequent qualification. Rudy emphasized the goal’s significance in establishing immediate dominance and articulated the team’s ambition for the forthcoming tournament, stating the objective is not merely to participate but to successfully defend the World Cup title.

Roma must now replicate its extraordinary quarter-final performance against Barcelona to overturn the deficit in this tie. On that occasion, it recovered from a 4-1 first-leg defeat by securing a 3-0 victory at the Stadio Olimpico to advance to the semi-finals. Although Liverpool was arguably outplayed during the initial thirty minutes, a superb strike from Salah against his former club initiated the scoring for Jürgen Klopp’s side. Salah added a second goal shortly before halftime, becoming the first Liverpool player to reach ten goals in a single European campaign. He then turned provider for Mané and Firmino as Roma struggled defensively. Firmino headed in a fifth goal from a standard set-piece, but Eusebio Di Francesco’s team secured two valuable away goals in the closing minutes, preserving a measure of hope for the second leg.

The Swedish prime minister has addressed anti-semitic sentiments growing in the country amid the recent US decision on Jerusalem, which caused a negative reaction of Muslims worldwide.
"I am outraged by the attack on the synagogue in Gothenburg yesterday and that violence against Jews was incited at a demonstration in Malmo. There is no place for anti-Semitism in Swedish society. The perpetrators must be held to account. All democratic forces must now work together to build a tolerant and open society in which everyone feels safe," Swedish Prime Minister Stefan Lofven in a statement on Sunday, commenting on the recent attack on a synagogue in the city of Gothenburg and an anti-Jewish rally in the city of Malmo.
On Saturday, a group of masked people firebombed a synagogue in Sweden's second-largest city, Gothenburg. No people have been injured in the incident and the fire was quickly extinguished. On the same day, Malmo, Sweden's third biggest city, witnessed an anti-Semitic rally. The Jewish Agency for Israel spokesperson Avi Mayer expressed on Sunday his concern over the events in Sweden.
READ MORE: Jewish Agency for Israel Alarmed Over Growing Anti-Semitic Sentiment in Sweden
The recent anti-Jewish sentiments in Sweden intensified three days after the announcement of the US decision to recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and relocate the US embassy from Tel Aviv, which prompted a negative reaction of Muslims worldwide.
On December 10, President Emmanuel Macron urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to negotiate with the Palestinians on the controversial US decision, after Israel's top official had urged the Palestinians to agree that Jerusalem is the capital of the Jewish state, claiming that the sooner they "come to grips with this reality," the faster the sides would move toward a peace settlement.
READ MORE: Netanyahu Calls on Palestinians to Agree Jerusalem is 'Israel's Capital'
The international community believes that the status of East Jerusalem, a holy site for three religions, should be determined based on an agreement with the Palestinians, who seek to create their own state with the capital in the Holy City.

The Prime Minister explicitly referenced an attack on a synagogue in Gothenburg and an anti-Jewish demonstration in Malmo, declaring, “I am outraged by the attack on the synagogue in Gothenburg yesterday and that violence against Jews was incited at a demonstration in Malmo. PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds, 2017’s most successful game launches on Xbox One tomorrow, but in some parts of the world, they already have their hands on the Battle Royale experience that’s hooked over 24 million people on PC. Unfortunately, it looks like there may be some optimization problems. Early streams and video captures are showing stuttering and an inconsistent framerate for the Xbox version of the game, with some saying the game dipped into the single-digits.
This isn’t good, at all. PUBG is a fast-paced, kill or be killed game in which one wrong move in your battle to survive inside a shrinking battlefield against 99 other players needs the most precise movement possible. With no aim-assist on the analog controls of a console joypad, every frame matters, and right now it seems like people trying to survive are having a tough time. The rooms inside houses seem extremely dark, which will affect looting (especially in the early game rush for tools of survival), and textures are popping in and out. How will players know if that’s a bush or a person they need to shoot?
And it’s not the absolute most crucial part of the game, but beginning a match by parachuting out and landing in a safe area, or maneuvering away from a zone in which a host of people who want to kill you with anything they can get your hands on await, is important. In the below clip (cued at the appropriate timestamp) we see how choppy it is landing, looking like it’s way under the reported 30FPS the game was supposed to run at. Additionally, look at those shadows popping in and out. That’s going to get people killed. It’s not completely game-breaking, but this isn’t something that makes me excited to step away from my gaming rig anytime soon.
rewrite:
PlayerUnknown’s Battlegrounds, the most commercially successful game launch of 2017, will be released on the Xbox One console tomorrow. However, in certain regions, players have already gained access to the Battle Royale experience that has captivated over 24 million users on PC. Initial indications, unfortunately, suggest potential optimization issues. Early streaming footage and video captures of the Xbox version display noticeable stuttering and an inconsistent framerate, with reports of performance occasionally dropping into single-digit frames per second.

Such performance shortcomings are particularly concerning given the game’s design. PUBG is a high-stakes, competitive survival game where precise movement and timing are critical. Players must outmaneuver 99 opponents within a dynamically contracting play area, where a single error can result in elimination. The absence of aim-assist for console analog controls further heightens the importance of fluid and responsive performance; every frame counts for situational awareness and accurate targeting. Current reports indicate that players are struggling with these technical impediments. Additionally, environmental rendering appears problematic: interiors are excessively dark, hindering the crucial early-game activity of looting for equipment, while textures and objects, such as foliage, manifest abruptly, creating visual ambiguity that can obscure threats.

Another significant, though not absolutely core, gameplay element is also affected: the initial parachute descent and subsequent positional maneuvering. Successfully landing in a secure location or navigating away from high-density combat zones is a vital strategic phase. In available footage, this sequence exhibits severe choppiness, appearing to operate well below the targeted 30 frames per second. The erratic rendering of shadows further compounds these visual inconsistencies. While these issues may not completely invalidate the gameplay experience, they represent substantial technical deficiencies that detract from playability. Consequently, these performance problems diminish the incentive for players to transition from the established PC version to the console platform in its current state.

DETROIT — Ten years after leaving Michigan, the PGA Tour is bringing a new tournament to Detroit.
Detroit-based Quicken Loans has signed an agreement to host a PGA Tour event in the Motor City starting next summer. Still to be determined is the name of the tournament and when it will be played, though it likely would be two weeks after the U.S. Open.
It is expected to be held at Detroit Golf Club, a century-old course designed by Donald Ross.
As part of the agreement, the company will retain its title sponsorship of the Quicken Loans National this year, which is held at the TPC Potomac and run by the Tiger Woods Foundation. The foundation will not be involved in the Detroit tournament.
Intersport will operate the tournament, along with other attractions that will take place in Detroit during the event.
One of the selling points for bringing the PGA Tour to Detroit was taking part in revitalizing the city.
"Professional golf belongs in Detroit," Quicken Loans chief executive Jay Farner said. "The Motor City — and the entire state of Michigan — have long served as a premier golf destination with some of the best courses in the country. We will be working with the PGA Tour to make the Detroit stop one of the most exciting and engaging events on the professional golf calendar."
Michigan had the Buick Open from 1958 through 2009, with a brief hiatus in the early 1970s. Woods won the tournament three times, including the final edition.
Quicken Loans stepped in as the title sponsor of Woods' tournament in Washington in 2014 after AT&T did not renew the contract. It moved to different courses and struggled to get a strong field, not helped by injuries to Woods that kept him from playing the last two years.
Quicken Loans also has a personal endorsement contract with Rickie Fowler.
rewrite:
A decade following the PGA Tour’s departure from Michigan, professional golf will return to the state with a new tournament in Detroit. Quicken Loans, a corporation headquartered in Detroit, has finalized an agreement to serve as host for a PGA Tour event in the city, commencing in the summer of the forthcoming year. While the specific designation of the tournament and its precise dates remain pending official confirmation, preliminary indications suggest it will be scheduled approximately two weeks subsequent to the U.S. Open. The anticipated venue is the historic Detroit Golf Club, a century-old course originally designed by Donald Ross.

Pursuant to this new arrangement, Quicken Loans will maintain its title sponsorship of the existing Quicken Loans National for the current year, an event held at TPC Potomac and operated by the Tiger Woods Foundation. The foundation, however, will not be affiliated with the Detroit tournament. Event operations will be managed by Intersport, which will oversee the competition as well as ancillary attractions scheduled to coincide with the tournament in Detroit. A principal rationale for establishing the event involved contributing to the ongoing revitalization of the city.

Quicken Loans Chief Executive Jay Farner emphasized the alignment, stating, "Professional golf belongs in Detroit. The Motor City—and the entire state of Michigan—have long served as a premier golf destination with some of the nation’s finest courses. We intend to collaborate with the PGA Tour to ensure the Detroit stop becomes one of the most compelling and interactive events on the professional golf calendar." Michigan previously hosted the Buick Open from 1958 through 2009, with a brief interruption in the early 1970s; Tiger Woods secured victory in that tournament on three occasions, including its final iteration.

Quicken Loans assumed title sponsorship of Woods’ Washington-based tournament in 2014 following AT&T’s decision not to renew its contract. That event subsequently relocated among various courses and encountered challenges in attracting a consistently robust field, a situation exacerbated by Woods’ injuries, which precluded his participation in the last two editions. Additionally, Quicken Loans maintains a personal endorsement agreement with professional golfer Rickie Fowler.

Foes Reconcile after Downtown Fight Video Goes Viral
by Ellis Eskew
Two Montgomery foes make amends after video of a brutal fight in downtown goes viral.
The fight broke out at one o’clock Saturday morning in downtown Montgomery.
The two sides were brought together Monday night at Rell’s Kitchen to reconcile.
They shook hands and apologized to the city and to each other.
They also prayed together.
Ja’Mel Brown organized the event.
He says, “we all know it was an embarrassment what happened Friday downtown. It was embarrassing. It went viral. But what ways can we find to make something positive out of it? So over the weekend, I was thinking and I said let’s do like they used to do back in the old days. Those who had a fist fight, they put them in one room and we mediate,” said Brown.
Increased police patrols in that area are expected now.

The involved parties convened on Monday evening at Rell’s Kitchen for a mediated resolution. Brown characterized the widely disseminated incident as an embarrassment, proposing that a constructive outcome be derived from it. He cited historical community mediation practices as his inspiration for facilitating the dialogue. In response to the event, authorities are anticipated to augment police patrols within the affected area.

SYDNEY FC's ebullient approach to the A-League semi-finals has continued, with defender Michael Zullo claiming the Sky Blues can top Melbourne Victory for strength and technique.
Insisting that his side was already the fittest in the league, Zullo said the weekend off - while Victory shaded Adelaide 2-1 in the elimination final - had given Sydney another layer of advantage before Saturday's game.
Zullo's words underscored Sydney's confidence, a day after captain Alex Brosque said that losing the last seven encounters would be playing on Victory's minds.
"The break gives us a huge advantage," Zullo said. "They played a tough 90 minutes but more importantly it's given us a chance to reach full fitness, and a few extra days to recover and prepare.
"Physically we've been the strongest team in the league all year and this will add to our advantage as well.
"(Victory's) game is based on physicality but we're a physically superior side. When you look at it in that way, we've turned their strength into our strength. The quality we have in our front third this year has really been the difference.
Zullo has the job of containing Victory star Leroy George.
"Also, the fact we defend as a team, and everyone plays a part defensively, has led to our team coming out on top."
Zullo's personal battle will be with Victory's freewheeling winger Leroy George, whose header brought his side level with Adelaide, but the Sydney leftback insisted he had the answer to come out on top.
"I watched the game, and Adelaide defend differently to the way we do," he said. "We have each other's back and fill in for each other when we need to.
"For me personally, the best way to contain an attacker is to defend. It's a cliche but something that seems to have worked for us.
"To be honest, for us it didn't matter. We knew whoever it was we'd beaten them this year and put in really good performances as well. We weren't too fazed, and it's Melbourne so we're ready."

February 2, 2018- Elizabethtown Area High School seniors Scyla Crozier and Erin Kraskewicz won awards in the 2018 Lancaster County Regional Scholastic Writing Awards sponsored by the Lancaster County Library. Kraskewicz was honored with a silver key in the poetry category for her entry Purple Daffodils and an honorable mention for her Personal Essay/Memoir entry titled The Girl. Crozier received an honorable mention for her Flash Fiction entry Breaking News: Man Dies In House Fire Caused By Gas Leak.
The prestigious recognition program provides an avenue for students in local middle and high schools to express themselves through writing. The student entries were judged at the local level by a panel of distinguished writers and journalists. Students could enter their writings into various categories such as dramatic script, humor, journalism, poetry and science fiction.
This is the third year in a row Kraskewicz has earned awards in the competition. She received a silver key and two honorable mentions in the 2017 competition to go along with a gold key she received her sophomore year in the Poetry category.
Founded in 1923, the Scholastic Art and Writing Awards are the oldest, longest-running, most prestigious recognition program for creative teenagers in the United States. The program is open to students in grades 7-12. This year, nationwide more than 140,000 works of art and writings were submitted to the competition

TOKYO Bank of Japan board member Takehiro Sato said labour market reform and other measures to boost Japan's growth potential must accompany monetary easing to raise the country's low long-term inflation expectations.
Prolonged economic stagnation has pushed down long-term inflation expectations to around zero percent, and it is not easy to raise them even through massive monetary stimulus if monetary policy is the "only game in town," Sato said in a speech at Yale University on Tuesday.
"Given that monetary policy on its own has limited effects, it is vital to make steady efforts, such as through labour market reform ... to change Japan's conservative inflation expectations," Sato said in the text of his speech posted on the BOJ's website on Wednesday.
Japanese companies and labour unions have traditionally prioritised job security over pay rises, a practice that has restrained wage increases and worked to push down long-term inflation expectations, Sato said.
By changing such practices and increasing job flexibility, Japan can boost labour productivity and potential growth. That would, in turn, increase corporate profits and household income, helping to accelerate inflation and strengthen the effect of monetary easing, he said.
"Given that there is an increasing sense of labour shortage caused by Japan's population decline, now is an ideal time to take a step forward in labour market reform," Sato said.
(Reporting by Leika Kihara; Editing by Eric Meijer)
rewrite:
In a recent address, Bank of Japan Policy Board member Takehiro Sato emphasized that monetary easing alone is insufficient to elevate Japan’s subdued long-term inflation expectations, which have declined to approximately zero percent amid prolonged economic stagnation. He argued that such expectations cannot be easily raised through aggressive monetary stimulus if it remains the sole policy tool. Instead, structural reforms—particularly in the labour market—are essential to complement monetary policy and enhance the nation’s growth potential.

Sato noted that traditional practices, wherein Japanese firms and labour unions prioritize job security over wage increases, have historically suppressed pay growth and contributed to lower inflation expectations. Reforming these practices to improve labour market flexibility would, he contended, boost productivity and potential economic growth. This structural improvement would subsequently elevate corporate profits and household incomes, thereby fostering inflationary pressures and amplifying the efficacy of monetary accommodation.

He further observed that demographic decline in Japan is intensifying perceptions of labour shortage, presenting an opportune moment to advance labour market reforms. Sato concluded that sustained efforts in this domain are vital to shifting entrenched, conservative inflation expectations and achieving durable economic revitalization.

Bitcoin and its brethren have taken a beating over the past seven days. While no one knows exactly why that is—and don’t believe anyone who claims otherwise—two particularly troublesome events certainly haven’t helped.
Buzzkills: At 2:57 a.m. in Tokyo last Friday, hackers swiped more than half a billion dollars’ worth of cryptocurrency tokens from the Japanese exchange Coincheck. Then on Tuesday, it came to light that U.S. financial regulators had subpoenaed Bitfinex, one of the world’s most popular exchanges, and Tether, a cryptocurrency company that claims its tokens are pegged to the U.S. dollar.
There will be ramifications: Coincheck’s executives have admitted that they neglected to use basic security measures. That isn’t comforting financial regulators, who were already worried about how cryptocurrency exchanges operate. As for Bitfinex and Tether, the New York Times reports growing concern that the former has been using the latter to prop up the price of Bitcoin—which may explain why it’s taken a tumble as well.
Subscribe to Chain Letter, our twice-weekly newsletter focused on cryptocurrencies and blockchains. It’s free!

A man who told police he was selling drugs to pay child support and legal fees was arrested following a traffic stop.
That arrest also led to a child neglect complaint against his girlfriend.
Police Sgt. Matthew Whittington stopped a car Friday at the intersection of Southwest 7th Street and Lee Boulevard. K-9 Officer Brittany Schulte arrived as backup and her dog indicated drugs might be present, according to Whittington's report, and officers found a dark-colored backpack with three bags of marijuana, a Xanax pill, a scale, and multiple plastic bags.
During an interview, the driver said he had been selling marijuana for approximately two years in order to help pay child support and legal fees, according to the police report. He also told officers he had approximately 6 ounces of marijuana, guns and $3,000 in cash at home, where he lived with his girlfriend and two children.
Detectives Kim Morton and Jeff Hall who were watching the man's home in the 300 block of Northwest 40th Street saw a woman leave the house and put a child in a vehicle, according to the police report. When she returned, they told her that her boyfriend had been arrested and asked about the whereabouts of the other child. She told them she had left her 4-year-old daughter in the house asleep while she took her other child to school.

PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) – A 27-year-old woman faces a federal charge of attempted sex trafficking of a child after the FBI interviewed an Eugene man in a child pornography investigation.
Kelsey Christine Wheeler was arrested Friday by the FBI and is likely to make her first appearance in federal court in Portland Monday.
The FBI interviewed the man at his Eugene home on April 13. He told agents he responded to a sex ad online and met with a woman in January, then reportedly went from Eugene to Portland on a Monday night, documents show.
Using an alias, Wheeler told the man she could arrange an “encounter” between him and a 3-year-old who is known to her, the man told the FBI.
Last Friday, the FBI and Portland police got hold of Wheeler to check on the child. Documents showed she admitted using the alias the man said she used and that she’d been a prostitute off-and-on since she was 15.
