2016 Rio Olympics - Equestrian - Victory Ceremony - Jumping Individual Victory Ceremony - Olympic Equestrian Centre - Rio de Janeiro, Brazil - 19/08/2016. Gold medalist Nick Skelton (GBR) of Britain poses with his national flag in front of the Olympic rings. REUTERS/Pilar Olivares
LONDON Britain's Olympic show jumping double gold medallist Nick Skelton announced his retirement at the age of 59 on Wednesday, saying he was not getting any younger and it was good to go out at the top.
Skelton, a team gold medallist in London in 2012, won his first individual Olympic title with Big Star at last year's Rio Games.
The oldest British gold medallist since 1908, he competed in seven Olympics despite being advised by his surgeon to give up riding after a fall in 2000 snapped vertebra in his neck in two places.
"It has come to a point, after months of thought and consideration, that myself and my partner Big Star have decided to retire from competition," Skelton said on his website (www.nickskelton.com).
"We feel that Big Star has done everything that a rider could ask and it is time for him to relax and enjoy his stallion duties. As for myself, I have always stated that when Big Star was finished I would be as well.
"This sport has given me more than I could have ever hoped over the past 43 years and it is such a difficult decision to make, but I'm not getting any younger and it is nice for the two of us to end on the highest note possible."
Skelton and Big Star's farewell appearance will be at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on May 14.
(Reporting by Alan Baldwin, editing by Neil Robinson)
rewrite:
On August 19, 2016, at the Olympic Equestrian Centre in Rio de Janeiro, British equestrian Nick Skelton celebrated his individual show jumping gold medal victory at the Rio Olympic Games. The athlete was photographed posing with the British flag before the iconic Olympic rings. On Wednesday, the 59-year-old Skelton publicly announced his retirement from competitive sport, stating a desire to conclude his career at its pinnacle.

Skelton, who secured a team gold medal at the London 2012 Olympics, earned his first individual Olympic title aboard his horse, Big Star, in Rio. His career is notable for its longevity and resilience; having competed in seven Olympic Games, he is the oldest British athlete to win gold since 1908. This achievement is particularly remarkable given a severe injury in 2000, wherein a fall resulted in a neck vertebra fractured in two places, leading surgical advice to cease riding.

In a formal statement published on his official website, Skelton declared, “It has come to a point, after months of thought and consideration, that myself and my partner Big Star have decided to retire from competition.” He elaborated that Big Star had accomplished all attainable goals and would now transition to stallion duties. Skelton affirmed a prior commitment to retire concurrently with his equine partner, stating, “I have always stated that when Big Star was finished I would be as well.” He expressed profound gratitude for a 43-year career, acknowledging the difficulty of the decision but emphasizing the appropriateness of concluding at the highest possible level.

Skelton and Big Star are scheduled for a final public appearance at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on May 14.

WILMINGTON, NC (WWAY) — If you’ve received a call from a company wanting to buy a timeshare take heed.
The Better Business Bureau is investigating a possible scam in the area.
The BBB of Coastal Carolina says it has received a large number of calls from people contacted by Hope Mills Timeshares.
The BBB says the Fayetteville business is telling them they have a buyer for their timeshare. However, they’re requesting money first for the transaction.
The BBB says there’s no record of the business, no real estate license for the business, and it’s not listed with the secretary of state.
Better Business Bureau Serving Coastal Carolina (BBB) is here to tell consumers what they can do to stop these calls for good:
First and foremost, do not answer calls from numbers you do not recognize. If it’s a legitimate contact, they will leave a message. Even if a scammer leaves a message, this will give you time to think about what is being asked of you.
Be cautious of those automated messages asking you to “Press 9” to be taken off of their call list. It’s best to just hang up. Pressing your keypad is another way to alert the caller that they have reached an active number, and they will continue to call and sell your number to other scammers as well.
Be aware that scammers are calling and impersonating legitimate businesses, organizations, and charities. The best thing you can do to prevent yourself from falling victim is to hang up, find the appropriate phone number, and call them directly to speak to a representative.
Join the Do Not Call Registry (gov) to cut down on legitimate telemarketing and sales calls. Although it won’t stop scammers, you’ll get fewer calls, making it easier to spot the fraudulent ones.
Write down the phone number of those callers violating the Do Not Call Registry and file a scam report with BBB Scam Tracker and the FTC’s Do Not Call List.
There’s an app for that! Nomorbo.com takes you off any phone call that comes in as a robo call (an automated or machine-made call). The best part? Nomorobo is free for your landline and only $1.99 for cell phones.
rewrite:
Residents of the Wilmington, North Carolina, area are advised to exercise heightened caution regarding unsolicited communications from entities proposing to purchase timeshare properties. The Better Business Bureau (BBB) Serving Coastal Carolina has issued an alert concerning a potential fraudulent scheme operating locally. According to the BBB, a significant volume of consumer complaints has been lodged against an organization identified as Hope Mills Timeshares, based in Fayetteville. The entity reportedly contacts timeshare owners, claiming to have secured a buyer for their property but subsequently requests an upfront fee to facilitate the transaction. Investigations reveal no legitimate business registration, absence of a real estate license, and no filing with the Secretary of State for this organization, all hallmarks of a deceptive operation.

To mitigate such risks, the BBB provides the following formal recommendations for consumer protection. First, refrain from answering calls from unrecognized numbers. Legitimate entities will typically leave a voicemail, which allows the recipient time to assess the request without pressure. Second, exercise extreme caution with interactive voice response systems, particularly those instructing recipients to press a key to be removed from a calling list. Engaging with these prompts often confirms the number as active, potentially increasing call frequency and leading to the number being sold to other malicious actors. The recommended action is to terminate the call without interaction.

Third, remain vigilant regarding caller impersonation of authentic businesses, charities, or organizations. The most effective defense is to disconnect, independently verify the official contact information for the institution being represented, and initiate contact directly. Fourth, enrollment in the National Do Not Call Registry, managed by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), is advised. While this registry does not deter unlawful scammers, it reduces the volume of legitimate telemarketing calls, thereby making fraudulent communications more conspicuous. Consumers should document the phone numbers of any registry violators and report them via the BBB Scam Tracker and the FTC’s complaint system.

Finally, technological solutions such as Nomorobo offer an additional layer of defense by automatically blocking identified robocalls. This service is provided free of charge for landline users and is available for a nominal monthly fee for cellular devices. Proactive adoption of these measures can significantly reduce vulnerability to telecommunications fraud.

LONDON: Chelsea boss Antonio Conte insisted he remains the best man to lead the Londoners despite an alarming dip in form from the Premier League champions in his second season in charge.
Wednesday’s shock 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth left Chelsea down in fourth, 18 points off runaway league leaders Manchester City, and fighting just to qualify for next season’s Champions League.
Conte has also repeatedly voiced his frustrations at his lack of input over the club’s transfer policy, further fuelling speculation he won’t remain in charge at Stamford Bridge beyond the end of the season.
“I trust in my work and this is the only way that brought me to be one of the best managers,” said Conte, who won three Serie A titles in a glorious three-year spell in charge at Juventus.
“I don’t trust in anything else, only in my work and my job.”
Conte labelled his preparations for Wednesday’s defeat as “disastrous” as Chelsea finally landed Olivier Giroud from Arsenal as a striking alternative to the injured Alvaro Morata, whilst the out of favour Michy Batshuayi was allowed to join Borussia Dortmund.
However, Conte is wary of throwing Giroud straight into his starting line-up for Monday night’s trip to Watford.
“We are working with him and we have to check his physical condition. It won’t be easy for him to start against Watford,” added Conte.
AFP
rewrite:
Amidst a significant decline in form during his second season, Chelsea manager Antonio Conte has asserted that he remains the most suitable individual to oversee the Premier League champions. This declaration follows a surprising 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Wednesday, a result which positioned Chelsea in fourth place, eighteen points behind the dominant league leaders, Manchester City, and intensified the club's struggle to secure qualification for the subsequent UEFA Champions League campaign. Conte has additionally expressed repeated dissatisfaction regarding his limited influence over the club's transfer policy, thereby amplifying speculation that his tenure at Stamford Bridge may conclude at the season's end. The manager, who secured three Serie A titles during a successful period at Juventus, grounded his confidence solely in his professional methodology, stating, "I trust in my work and this is the only way that brought me to be one of the best managers. I don’t trust in anything else, only in my work and my job."

Conte characterized the preparations for the recent defeat as "disastrous," a period which coincided with the acquisition of striker Olivier Giroud from Arsenal to provide an alternative to the injured Álvaro Morata, while Michy Batshuayi was permitted to join Borussia Dortmund. Nevertheless, Conte expressed caution regarding the immediate integration of Giroud into the starting lineup for the forthcoming match against Watford, noting the necessity to assess the player's physical readiness and indicating that an immediate start would present a considerable challenge.

MUNCY TOWNSHIP -- Our online shopping habits could be affecting more than just stores this time of year.
Newswatch 16 spoke with a few bell ringers hoping to collect donations from shoppers at the Lycoming Mall near Muncy.
You'd expect to see shoppers around the mall carrying bags filled with gifts, but when we caught up with Tony Perotta from the Salvation Army, he was carrying a red kettle. Year after year, volunteers with the Salvation Army collect money.
"They always say nickels, dimes, quarters, dollars. It doesn't really matter. All is very much appreciated as we raise money through the Christmas season and throughout the year," Perrotta said.
With two anchor stores gone and Sears closing after the new year, the mall has fewer storefronts open this holiday season. Perrotta says it hasn't affected donations.
"I'm surprised at how busy it was. Saturday was one of best days at the mall," Perrotta said. "The weekends it's a little busier, but on the weekdays it's pretty slow."
On the other side of the mall, Joseph Reifsnyder set up camp next to an American Rescue Workers chimney. Reifsnyder says he would stand, but he has multiple sclerosis. He volunteered with the nonprofit last year, too.
"This year seems to be a little slow in the mall because of the store closing," Reifsnyder said.
"We had some concerns about being here at the mall, but I'm presently surprised again with the generosity," said Mike Kane, American Rescue Workers.
American Rescue Workers relies on money and toy donations from the community, especially this time of the year.
In the next few weeks, the group will hand out hundreds of meals and thousands of presents for the holiday.
"We give toys to over 1,100 children. It's a huge operation. It brings a lot of Christmas joy to a lot of families who otherwise would not have it," Kane added.
Both nonprofits will be at the mall most days collecting donations until the end of the month.
rewrite:
The proliferation of online retail may be exerting an influence beyond commercial establishments during the holiday season, as suggested by observations at the Lycoming Mall near Muncy Township. Despite the expectation of shoppers bearing gift-laden bags, representatives from charitable organizations were observed conducting seasonal fundraising efforts.

Tony Perrotta of the Salvation Army, overseeing the traditional red kettle campaign, noted the consistent importance of public contributions. "All donations, whether nickels, dimes, quarters, or dollars, are sincerely appreciated as we raise essential funds throughout the Christmas season and the year," Perrotta stated. He reported that despite the mall's diminished occupancy following the departure of two anchor stores and the impending closure of Sears, donation levels have remained resilient. "I was surprised by the volume; Saturday represented one of our most successful days at this location," he remarked, while acknowledging that weekday traffic is typically slower than weekends.

Conversely, Joseph Reifsnyder, a volunteer with the American Rescue Workers stationed beside a donation chimney, offered a differing assessment. Reifsnyder, who volunteers despite managing multiple sclerosis, suggested that mall traffic has declined. "This year seems to be a little slow in the mall because of the store closings," he observed. However, Mike Kane of the American Rescue Workers countered this perspective, expressing initial concerns about the venue but noting positive results: "I am presently surprised again by the generosity." The organization is heavily dependent on community donations of funds and toys during this period to support its annual holiday distribution, which encompasses hundreds of meals and thousands of gifts. "We provide toys to over 1,100 children. It is a significant operation that brings Christmas joy to many families who would otherwise go without," Kane added.

Both nonprofit entities will maintain a presence at the mall through the end of the month to collect donations, illustrating the ongoing role of physical retail spaces in facilitating community philanthropy even as shopping patterns evolve.

New Delhi: The Central government on Tuesday told the Supreme Court that death by hanging is not as "barbaric, inhuman and cruel" as an execution by firing squad or lethal injection.
Supporting a legal provision that a death row convict would only be hanged to death, the Ministry of Home Affairs told a bench headed by Chief Justice Deepak Misra that death by hanging was "quick, simple" and free from anything that would unnecessarily sharpen the poignancy of the prisoner.
"Execution, as contemplated under section 354(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, is not barbaric, inhuman and cruel as well as in compliance with safeguard no. 9 of the resolutions adopted by the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)," said the affidavit filed by the ministry.
The affidavit came while responding to a PIL filed by advocate Rishi Malhotra challenging the constitutionality of hanging to death as a mode of execution. Section 354 (5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure mandates that a person sentenced to death shall "be hanged by the neck till he is dead". The apex court had termed the Constitution as a "compassionate and organic" guiding book and asked it to consider changing the law so that a convict, facing death penalty, dies in peace and not in pain. The affidavit of the ministry further stated: "Lethal injection, which is believed to be painless, has also been contested on the ground that it may lead to uncomfortable death wherein the convict is unable to express his/her discomfort because of paralysis by the paralytic agent injected. It is believed by many that lethal injection, as is practised currently, is designed to create only an appearance of serenity and painless death." It added that such injections, if made available, can be misused, and also ruled out the option of execution by a firing squad contending that it was not "fail-safe" and can be extremely painful if shooters miss the heart by accident or by intention. "Hanging with more advanced procedures is far safer than techniques such as lethal injections. The procedure by which a death sentence is to be executed is dependent upon a variety of factors such as economic feasibility, availability of skilled and technical personnel, equipment and resources, rate of botched executions," the affidavit said, adding that the mode of execution is a "matter of legislative policy".
rewrite:
On Tuesday, the Central Government of India presented its position before the Supreme Court, asserting that execution by hanging cannot be characterized as "barbaric, inhuman and cruel" when compared to alternative methods such as firing squads or lethal injection. This submission was made in an affidavit filed by the Ministry of Home Affairs before a bench presided over by Chief Justice Deepak Misra. The ministry was responding to a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) initiated by advocate Rishi Malhotra, which challenges the constitutional validity of hanging as a mode of execution under Section 354(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).

The affidavit defended the existing legal provision, which mandates that a condemned prisoner "be hanged by the neck till he is dead." It contended that this method is "quick, simple," and devoid of elements that might "unnecessarily sharpen the poignancy of the prisoner." Furthermore, the government argued that execution as contemplated under Section 354(5) of the CrPC is not in violation of fundamental rights and is consistent with safeguard number nine of the resolutions adopted by the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC).

The ministry's response also engaged with the Court's earlier observation that the Constitution is a "compassionate and organic" document, which had prompted judicial inquiry into potential reforms to ensure a death sentence is carried out with minimal suffering. In this context, the affidavit provided a critical analysis of proposed alternatives. It questioned the purported humaneness of lethal injection, noting that it has been contested on grounds that paralytic agents may prevent a convict from expressing significant discomfort, thereby creating only an "appearance of serenity and painless death." The affidavit also raised concerns about the potential misuse of such drugs.

The option of execution by firing squad was similarly dismissed as not being "fail-safe," with the observation that it could result in extreme pain if shooters miss the heart, whether by accident or intention. The government concluded that hanging, particularly with advanced procedures, presents a safer and more reliable alternative. It emphasized that the selection of an execution methodology involves considerations of "economic feasibility, availability of skilled and technical personnel, equipment and resources, and the rate of botched executions," ultimately characterizing the choice of mode as a "matter of legislative policy" for Parliament to decide.

Emmanuel Macron, head of the political movement En Marche !, or Onwards !, and candidate for the 2017 French presidential election, attends a news conference at his campaign headquarters in Paris, France, March 28, 2017. REUTERS/Charles Platiau
PARIS French centrist Emmanuel Macron is on course to come out on top of the first round of France's presidential election next month and go on to win in the May 7 runoff against far right leader Marine Le Pen, an Elabe poll showed on Wednesday.
Macron, a popular independent who served as economy minister under President Francois Hollande, would win 25.5 percent of the vote in the April 23 first round while Le Pen would get 24 percent, according to the poll for BFM TV.
Both of their scores were down 0.5 percentage points from the last time the poll was conducted a week ago, Elabe said.
The poll also showed that conservative Francois Fillon's score rose to 18 percent from 17 percent in what was the first increase since he was engulfed by a scandal over payments to family members for work they may not have done.
That would still not be enough to get him into the May runoff, which Macron was seen winning with 63 percent of the vote to Le Pen's 37 percent.
The poll, which was conducted on March 28-29, also showed far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon making further gains, with his first round score reaching 15 percent, up from 13.5 percent a week earlier.
His gains came at the expense of Socialist candidate Benoit Hamon whose share of the vote slipped to only 10 percent from 11.5 percent.
Hamon, a hardline Socialist who wants to legalise cannabis and create a basic monthly state income for all, has struggled to win support from centre-left Socialists like former prime minister Manuel Valls who said on Wednesday he would vote for Macron.
(This version of the story corrects first name of far left candidate in para 6)
(Reporting by Leigh Thomas; Editing by Richard Balmforth)

According to this survey conducted for BFM television, Macron, a former economy minister under President François Hollande, would secure 25.5 percent of the vote in the April 23 first round, while Le Pen would garner 24 percent. Both figures represented a decline of 0.5 percentage points from the previous iteration of the poll conducted one week earlier.

The poll, fielded on March 28-29, further indicated a shift in support for other candidates. Conservative candidate François Fillon saw his first-round projection rise to 18 percent from 17 percent, marking his first increase since becoming embroiled in a scandal concerning alleged payments to family members for fictitious employment. Despite this gain, the poll suggested he would not qualify for the second-round runoff. In that hypothetical contest, Macron was forecast to defeat Le Pen decisively, with 63 percent of the vote to her 37 percent.

Meanwhile, far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon continued to gain traction, with his first-round support rising to 15 percent from 13.5 percent the prior week. This increase appeared to come at the expense of Socialist Party candidate Benoît Hamon, whose projected share declined to 10 percent from 11.5 percent. Hamon, a hardline Socialist advocating for policies such as the legalization of cannabis and the establishment of a universal basic income, has faced difficulties consolidating support from the center-left wing of his own party. This was exemplified by former Prime Minister Manuel Valls, who stated on Wednesday that he would cast his ballot for Macron in the election.

ABUJA An outbreak of meningitis in Nigeria has killed 269 people in recent weeks, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control said, as Africa's most populous country and aid organizations attempt to tackle the surge in infections.
As of Monday, 1,828 suspected cases of meningitis were reported with 269 deaths in 15 of the country's 36 states, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) said on Twitter late on Tuesday.
The center said on its website that 33 people died of meningitis in 2016.
More than 2,000 people died from an outbreak of the disease in Nigeria in 2009, with basic healthcare limited in rural parts of the country, where most people live on less than $2 a day, despite the country's huge oil resources.
Meningitis is the inflammation of tissue surrounding the brain and spinal cord which can be caused by viral or bacterial infections. It spreads mainly through kisses, sneezes, coughs and in close living quarters.
The NCDC said it was now working with the World Health Organisation, the U.N. Children's Fund and Medecins Sans Frontieres, also known as Doctors Without Borders, to try to control the outbreak.
(Reporting by Sharon Ogunleye, Paul Carsten and Alexis Akwagyiram, editing by Ed Osmond)
rewrite:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) has reported a significant meningitis outbreak, resulting in 269 fatalities in recent weeks. As of Monday, 1,828 suspected cases and these confirmed deaths have been recorded across 15 of Nigeria's 36 states, according to a statement released by the NCDC via Twitter on Tuesday. This current surge in infections is being addressed by national authorities and international aid organizations. Historical context indicates the severity of such outbreaks; while 33 meningitis-related deaths were recorded in 2016, a 2009 epidemic resulted in over 2,000 fatalities. This recurrent public health challenge persists despite Nigeria's substantial oil revenues, as basic healthcare remains limited in rural areas where a significant portion of the population subsists on less than two dollars per day.

Meningitis, an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord caused by viral or bacterial agents, is transmitted primarily through respiratory secretions via actions such as coughing and sneezing, as well as through close contact in communal living spaces. In response to the current crisis, the NCDC is coordinating containment efforts in collaboration with the World Health Organisation, the United Nations Children's Fund, and Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders).

BARTON COUNTY -The Kansas Court of Appeals reversed a district court judge’s decision to set aside the identity theft conviction of a woman who moved to Kansas from Mexico in 2003 without proper documentation to join her husband, according to court documents.
Following a jury trial, Melissa Valles was convicted of illegally using the social security number of a Colorado resident to obtain employment at several Great Bend businesses, according to a media release from the court.
However, the judge who heard the case granted a motion to arrest judgement, essentially ruling that the court did not have jurisdiction over the case.
The Barton County Attorney’s Office appealed that decision, and the Court of Appeals agreed that the trial judge was incorrect in his decision. Arguing the State’s case to the three-judge panel on the Court of Appeals, then-County Attorney Doug Matthews contended that a change in the law allowed the case to continue even though the language used in the complaint to charge Valles was technically incorrect.
The judges on the Court agreed, holding that the complaint was sufficient since it alleged facts that, if proven beyond a reasonable doubt, would show that Valles had committed a crime in Kansas.
Because Valles understood the charges being brought against her, she was able to present a defense, even though that defense was unsuccessful.
The Court of Appeals panel concluded that the trial judge erred by granting the motion. The case will now be returned to Barton County for sentencing before a different judge
rewrite:
In Barton County, the Kansas Court of Appeals has reversed a district court judge’s decision to set aside an identity theft conviction for Melissa Valles, according to judicial records. Valles, who relocated from Mexico to Kansas in 2003 without legal documentation to reunite with her spouse, was convicted by a jury for unlawfully utilizing a Colorado resident’s Social Security number to secure employment at multiple businesses in Great Bend.

Subsequent to the trial, the presiding judge granted a motion in arrest of judgment, determining the court lacked jurisdiction over the matter. The Barton County Attorney’s Office appealed this ruling. The Court of Appeals concurred with the prosecution, finding the trial judge’s decision erroneous. During proceedings before a three-judge appellate panel, then-County Attorney Doug Matthews asserted that a statutory modification permitted the case to proceed, notwithstanding technically imprecise language in the charging complaint.

The appellate judges upheld this argument, ruling the complaint was legally sufficient as it alleged facts which, if proven beyond a reasonable doubt, would establish Valles committed a crime within Kansas. The panel noted Valles comprehended the charges against her, enabling her to mount a defense, albeit unsuccessfully. Consequently, the Court of Appeals concluded the trial judge erred in granting the motion. The case has been remanded to Barton County for sentencing, which will be conducted before a different judge.

**Breaking News** @richforever new album "Rather You Than Me" in stores March 17, 2017 A post shared by Chris Rock (@chrisrock) on Feb 14, 2017 at 9:33pm PST
Rick Ross must have something on Chris Rock. That’s the only thing that makes sense in this particular situation. Otherwise, why would Rock be doing album promos for Rozay and calling the Maybach Music head honcho the best to ever do it?
As far as marketing tactics go, it’s a brilliant move by Ross, who had the comedian to announce the news that Ross’ new studio album, Rather Me Than You, will now officially be released on March 17th. Early Wednesday morning, Rock put the word out in a video posted to his Instagram in which he said “I wanna say whats up to my man Ricky Ross, Ricky Rozay. The greatest rapper alive and he’s got a new album coming out called ‘Rather You Than Me’ that drops March 17th with the hit single ‘I Think She Like’ featuring Ty Dolla $ign.” No, there didn’t appear to be anyone holding him against his will either so maybe he really does like Ross’ music or he was paid handsomely for the quick mention.
Whatever the case, it’s welcome news to hear that The Bawse will officially makes his return in March. Just last week he dropped off the new track “Summer 17” as a warm-up and he’s been spotted in the studio with Jay Z in recent weeks in what’s likely a new collab between the two of them. Those two usually create magic together so that alone is enough reason to anticipate the project.

This promotional strategy represents a calculated marketing tactic by Ross, leveraging Rock's considerable public profile and credibility to generate anticipation. The uncoerced nature of the endorsement, as evidenced by the video, suggests either a genuine appreciation for Ross's musical output or a structured promotional agreement. Regardless of the specific motivation, the announcement successfully signals Ross's official return to the music industry.

This news follows other strategic releases, including the recent track "Summer Seventeen," which functions as a preliminary offering. Furthermore, documented studio sessions with fellow rapper and entrepreneur Jay-Z imply a potential collaboration on the new project. Given their history of critically and commercially successful partnerships, this prospect alone provides substantial grounds for heightened anticipation surrounding "Rather You Than Me."

NEW BEGINNINGS: Sandra Smith with grandsons Leyland, Brighton and Preston Smith picking up the keys for their new Mitsubishi Pajero from Black Toyota sales representative Lauren Wilson.
IT WAS a very happy Easter for Warwick woman Sandra Smith who had her wish for a new car granted just before the holy holiday.
The grandmother-of-five had wanted a new vehicle to be able to drive her five grandchildren - Preston, Bright, Leyland, Zara and Lara - left in her care.
After a slow start to donations on her GoFundMe page, Mrs Smith said she was thrilled to pick up the keys to a brand new Mitsubishi Pajero from Black Toyota last Thursday.
She said the seven-seater car was just what the family had in mind.
"I would like to thank the comedy duo Women Like Us, Mandy Nolan and Ellen Briggs, because without them this would not have been possible,” Mrs Smith said.
"They helped with my GoFundMe and to raise $5790 to make up the $15,000 we needed to get the car.
"The rest I put in from selling some items and saving up for a while.”
Mrs Smith had the help of donations from 90 people in two months.
After hearing her story, Black Toyota also helped Mrs Smith secure the car by selling at cost price.
"Thank you too to Black Toyota for dropping the price on the vehicle by about $5000 and helping us secure the car in time for the new school term,” she said.
Mrs Smith said she and her grandkids had already been able to enjoy trips together to Leslie Dam and Killarney Falls at the weekend, and headed to Toowoomba yesterday to pick up some new school supplies.
"The kids are loving it,” she said.
"Getting them to daycare and school each day had previously taken me a few trips so I'm grateful this will make things a lot easier for us all.
Black Toyota sales assistant Lauren Wilson said she was thankful the business was able to help a local family in need.
"We're thankful they came to us and we were able to help them out,” MsWilson said.
rewrite:

This development fulfilled a specific need for Mrs. Smith, a grandmother responsible for five grandchildren—Preston, Brighton, Leyland, Zara, and Lara—who required reliable transportation for their care. The procurement of a seven-seat Mitsubishi Pajero was finalized last Thursday through Black Toyota, with sales representative Lauren Wilson facilitating the key handover. Mrs. Smith indicated the vehicle was precisely suited to the family’s requirements.

The purchase was enabled through a collaborative financial effort. A public fundraising campaign initiated on the GoFundMe platform garnered $5,790 from ninety individual donors over a two-month period. Comedic duo Women Like Us, comprising Mandy Nolan and Ellen Briggs, were instrumental in promoting this campaign. Mrs. Smith supplemented these funds with personal savings accrued over time and proceeds from the sale of personal items, collectively meeting the required total of approximately $15,000. Furthermore, Black Toyota contributed significantly by offering the vehicle at cost price, effectively reducing the final amount by an estimated $5,000. Mrs. Smith expressed gratitude for this commercial concession, which ensured timely delivery for the commencement of the new school term.

The vehicle’s immediate utility was demonstrated through several familial excursions over the weekend, including visits to Leslie Dam and Killarney Falls. A subsequent trip to Toowoomba was undertaken to procure school supplies. Mrs. Smith emphasized the practical benefits, noting that the logistical challenges of transporting multiple children to their respective educational and care facilities, which previously necessitated several journeys, are now greatly alleviated. The grandchildren have reportedly responded with enthusiasm to the new arrangements.

Lauren Wilson of Black Toyota reflected on the transaction, stating the dealership was thankful for the opportunity to assist a local family in achieving a solution to their transportation needs. The collective outcome underscores the impact of community support paired with corporate social consideration in addressing specific familial requirements.

HARVEY Fresh owner Parmalat is planning a series of meetings this month with its WA dairy farmer suppliers to discuss new contracts from October.
It is understood Parmalat is also seeking a variation to existing contracts which would relieve it of having to pay final growth incentive payments for May.
The company also wants to discuss a cost-sharing proposal which could see farmers contributing to the cost of trucking surplus WA milk interstate.
Last spring, when it was receiving more milk than it needed, Parmalat at its own cost, began trucking milk 80,000-100,000 litres at a time in triple road train tankers, 4200 kilometres from the Harvey Fresh factory to a Parmalat bottling plant in Darwin.
It also trucked excess milk to South Australia.
The moves are believed to have cost the company at least $1 million.
Most of Parmalat’s current standard contracts with its 64 suppliers are due to end in October.
The three-year contracts, paying up to 52 cents a litre plus growth incentive payments for times of the year when seasonal conditions usually cause milk production volumes to reduce, were presented to farmers in 2014 after Parmalat purchased Harvey Fresh.
The contracts were aimed at securing supply because Harvey Fresh at the time was processing high-volume, low-margin private brand $1-a-litre milk for Coles supermarkets.
However since the Parmalat takeover, Coles has shifted its private brand processing from Harvey Fresh to Lion Dairy & Drinks for a lower price, but only three suppliers transferred over to Lion, leaving Harvey Fresh with a contracted supply of more milk than it needs.
Plans to expand exports to soak up the surplus milk were thwarted last year by the European Union dumping of dairy products on Asian markets due to trade restrictions with Russia.
Parmalat has honoured its three-year contracts but is understood to be keen to renegotiate with farmers.
It is understood Parmalat wants to return to 12-month supply contracts.
rewrite:
Parmalat, the parent company of HARVEY Fresh, has scheduled a series of meetings with its Western Australian dairy supplier base this month to deliberate on new contractual terms commencing in October. The company is reportedly seeking an amendment to existing agreements that would absolve it from remitting final growth incentive payments for the month of May. Furthermore, Parmalat intends to propose a cost-sharing model wherein farmers would partially subsidize the transportation expenses for surplus Western Australian milk shipped to other states.

This initiative follows logistical measures undertaken by the company last spring. Faced with a milk surplus, Parmalat independently financed the interstate transportation of excess volumes. This involved shipping batches of 80,000 to 100,000 litres via triple road train tankers over 4,200 kilometres from the Harvey Fresh facility to a Parmalat bottling plant in Darwin, with additional volumes redirected to South Australia. These operations are estimated to have incurred costs exceeding one million dollars.

The majority of Parmalat’s standard contracts with its sixty-four suppliers are set to expire in October. These three-year agreements, established in 2014 following Parmalat’s acquisition of Harvey Fresh, offered payments up to 52 cents per litre, supplemented by growth incentives during seasonal production declines. The contracts were initially designed to secure milk supply for Harvey Fresh, which was then processing high-volume, low-margin private label milk for Coles supermarkets at one dollar per litre. Subsequent to the acquisition, Coles relocated its private label processing to Lion Dairy & Drinks under more favorable pricing. Only three suppliers followed this transition, resulting in Harvey Fresh retaining contractual milk volumes in excess of its operational requirements.

Plans to mitigate this surplus through expanded export channels were impeded last year by the European Union’s diversion of dairy products into Asian markets, a consequence of trade restrictions with Russia. While Parmalat has fulfilled the terms of its three-year contracts, the company is now positioned to pursue renegotiations. It is understood that Parmalat aims to revert to a system of annual supply contracts moving forward.

BUENOS AIRES, Argentina (AP) — President Mauricio Macri said Monday that government employees in Argentina won't receive pay raises this year as part of a string of measures aimed at cutting spending.
Macri also announced the elimination of 1,000 "political positions" and the firing of family members appointed as advisers by government ministers. The measure is expected to save the government about $75 million.
Macri came into office in December 2015 promising to revive Argentina's economy and fight entrenched corruption. Although he is credited with ending a longstanding dispute that returned Argentina to global credit markets after more than 14 years, he has struggled to attract badly needed foreign investment.
At home, the government's austerity move comes just as Argentines are facing increases in fuel, utilities and transportation costs that have harmed Macri's popularity ratings. His government also faced violent protests in December over a pension overhaul bill that was ultimately approved by Congress.
"If Argentines chip in, all of us who are part of politics must make twice the effort and lead by example," Macri said at the presidential palace after returning from Europe, where he met with potential investors.
The pay freeze and other moves are expected to have a limited impact on the annual budget. But Macri said he hopes it can be followed by mayors and governors to reduce Argentina's high deficit.
rewrite:
In a statement issued on Monday, Argentine President Mauricio Macri announced a series of fiscal austerity measures, including a pay freeze for all government employees for the remainder of the year. Further actions involve the elimination of approximately 1,000 political appointments and the dismissal of family members who had been appointed as ministerial advisers. These combined steps are projected to yield budgetary savings of roughly $75 million.

Elected in December 2015 on a platform of economic revitalization and anti-corruption, President Macri has achieved some successes, notably resolving a protracted sovereign debt dispute that restored Argentina’s access to international credit markets. However, his administration has faced challenges in attracting the substantial foreign investment required for sustained growth. The announcement of these austerity measures coincides with domestic increases in the costs of fuel, utilities, and public transportation, which have adversely affected public approval ratings. The government also contended with significant public protests in December regarding a pension reform bill, which was subsequently ratified by Congress.

Speaking at the presidential palace upon his return from a trip to Europe, where he engaged with potential investors, Macri emphasized the necessity of shared sacrifice, stating that political officials must "lead by example." While the direct fiscal impact of the pay freeze and related actions on the annual budget is considered limited, the President expressed his intention for these measures to serve as a model for provincial governors and municipal mayors, aiming to collectively address the nation's elevated fiscal deficit.

A busy junction ground to a halt after a collision between a car and a tipper truck.
Emergency services were called to the crossroads in the middle of Standish after the incident involving a blue Ford Focus and a red skip loader just before noon on Friday.
Following the impact the car ended up colliding with the railings outside Winnard and Brown estate agents.
A 50-year-woman who was in the car was trapped in her vehicle and had to be rescued by the fire and ambulance services.
She was checked over by paramedics but had sustained no injuries.
The driver of the truck was also unhurt.
The incident, where High Street, Market Street, Preston Road and School Lane all meet, caused some disruption to motorists travelling in the middle of the day.
Rectory Lane was blocked for a time with emergency services vehicles as crews helped the woman and made the scene safe.
Officers from Greater Manchester Police (GMP) directed traffic around the scene, which was still ongoing at around 12.45pm.
rewrite: A significant traffic disruption occurred at a major intersection following a collision between a private vehicle and a commercial tipper truck. Emergency services were dispatched to the crossroads in central Standish after the incident, which involved a blue Ford Focus and a red skip loader, shortly before 12:00 on Friday. The impact caused the car to subsequently strike the railings outside the premises of Winnard and Brown estate agents. A 50-year-old female occupant of the car was extricated from the vehicle by fire and ambulance personnel. Although assessed at the scene by paramedics, she sustained no injuries, and the truck driver was also unharmed. The junction of High Street, Market Street, Preston Road, and School Lane experienced considerable disruption during the midday period. Rectory Lane was temporarily obstructed by emergency service vehicles during the response and recovery operation. Officers from Greater Manchester Police managed traffic flow around the scene, with the incident ongoing until approximately 12:45.

NBC 7's Consumer Bob reports on a new kind of convenience: how companies are working to deliver groceries directly to the kitchens of consumers. (Published Friday, Sept. 22, 2017)
Companies May Soon Be Delivering Food Straight to Your Kitchen
Amazon Prime Now customers can get free two-hour delivery on groceries over $35 from Whole Foods in San Diego, the companies announced Tuesday.
Customers can choose from bestselling items in the Whole Foods stores ranging from everyday staples to fresh meat or seafood, company officials said.
Customers with an Amazon Prime membership will get two-hour delivery for free on orders over $35. Anyone wanting their order within an hour will be charged $7.99 on orders of $35 or more.
The service is being offered to customers within the city of San Diego. Hours are daily from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Items for purchase include a selection of alcohol.
More information is available through the Prime Now app.
It's one of many new shopping services being offered to consumers looking to save time and effort when it comes to their household chores. Vons will deliver your groceries. Walmart wants to put groceries in your refrigerator.
San Diego State University Marketing Professor Miro Copic called the rush to change up how we shop "the next frontier in retail" in a previous interview with NBC 7.
Copic said less than five percent of grocery shoppers use a delivery service. Even so, companies know it is the future of the industry.
Amazon bought Whole Foods in a deal valued at $13.7 billion in June 2017.
rewrite:
A recent consumer report highlights the expansion of direct-to-consumer grocery delivery services, exemplified by a new initiative from Amazon and Whole Foods Market. On September 22, 2017, it was announced that Amazon Prime Now members in San Diego could receive complimentary two-hour delivery for Whole Foods grocery orders exceeding thirty-five dollars. This service, operational daily from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., provides access to a curated selection of bestselling items, including everyday staples, fresh meats, seafood, and a range of alcoholic beverages. For a fee of $7.99, one-hour delivery is available for orders meeting the same minimum. This model is part of a broader retail trend aimed at maximizing consumer convenience by minimizing the time and effort required for household procurement.

Industry analysts posit that such services represent a significant evolution in retail strategy. Marketing Professor Miro Copic of San Diego State University has characterized this shift as "the next frontier in retail," noting that while current adoption rates for grocery delivery remain below five percent, corporations are strategically investing in this channel as the anticipated future of the industry. This perspective is reinforced by Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods in June 2017 for approximately $13.7 billion, a move that facilitated this integrated service. The proliferation of similar offerings from other major retailers, such as Vons and Walmart, underscores a competitive race to dominate the home delivery market and embed services directly into the consumer's domestic environment.

Image copyright Getty Images Image caption Jesse Duplantis said the jet would not be for his personal use, but instead "belong to the ministry"
A US televangelist has asked his followers to help fund his fourth private jet - because Jesus "wouldn't be riding a donkey".
Jesse Duplantis said God had told him to buy a Falcoln 7X for $54m (£41m).
He added he was hesitant about the purchase at first, but said God had told him: "I didn't ask you to pay for it. I asked you to believe for it."
Although preachers owning private jets is not unusual, this particular appeal has caused controversy.
Twitter users responded to the request with disbelief, with many quoting Bible verses warning against greed and "false prophets", or suggesting that the money could be better used to help the poor.
In a video address posted on his website, 68-year-old Mr Duplantis explained: "You know, I've owned three different jets in my life, and I've used them and just burning them up for the Lord Jesus Christ.
"Now, some people believe that preachers shouldn't have jets. I really believe that preachers ought to go on every available voice, every available outlet, to get this Gospel preached to the world."
Standing beside framed pictures of his current fleet, he said that the jet he bought 12 years ago was no longer sufficient for his ministry because he could not fly non-stop, meaning he had to pay "exorbitant" refuelling costs.
Another picture which appeared in the video showed the preacher standing with the three aircraft, above the caption: "It's not about possessions, it's about priorities."
Mr Duplantis justified the request by saying that Jesus had told people to "go into the world and preach the Gospel to every creature, now how we gonna do that? I can't live long enough to travel by car or by ship or by train, but I can do it by an aeroplane".
In 2015, Mr Duplantis appeared in a video with another preacher, Kenneth Copeland, in which Mr Copeland described travelling on commercial airlines as being "in a long tube with a bunch of demons".
rewrite:
The request by American televangelist Jesse Duplantis for financial contributions from his followers to acquire a fourth private aircraft has generated notable controversy. Duplantis, aged 68, has publicly stated that divine instruction prompted him to purchase a Falcon 7X jet, valued at approximately $54 million. He rationalizes this appeal by asserting that the aircraft is essential for his evangelical ministry, arguing that efficient global travel is a prerequisite for fulfilling the biblical directive to spread the Gospel. In a video address, Duplantis countered critics who question clergy owning private jets, contending that ministers should utilize every available means of communication and transportation to achieve their missionary objectives.

He specifically referenced the limitations of his current jet, acquired twelve years prior, noting its inability to complete long-haul flights without refueling stops, which he characterizes as incurring "exorbitant" costs. While acknowledging his initial hesitation regarding the substantial expenditure, Duplantis claims he received further spiritual reassurance: "I didn't ask you to pay for it. I asked you to believe for it." He further defended the request by contrasting air travel with slower alternatives, stating that traveling by car, ship, or train would be impractical given the scope of his perceived mission.

Public reaction, particularly on social media platforms such as Twitter, has been largely critical. Many respondents have expressed skepticism, citing scriptural admonitions against greed and false prophecy, and suggesting that the funds could be more ethically directed toward charitable aid for the impoverished. This incident occurs within a broader context where ownership of private jets by prominent evangelical figures is not uncommon, yet the explicit solicitation for a fourth such asset has intensified scrutiny. The controversy is further underscored by Duplantis's prior public statements, including a 2015 video in which he appeared alongside preacher Kenneth Copeland, who disparaged commercial air travel as being akin to confinement "in a long tube with a bunch of demons." Throughout his appeal, Duplantis maintains a distinction between personal luxury and ministerial necessity, exemplified by a caption in his video stating, "It's not about possessions, it's about priorities," and his assertion that the jet would belong to the ministry rather than for his personal use.

BOGOTA — Colombian authorities are seeking to re-arrest a former hit man for late drug lord Pablo Escobar for violating his parole after he was caught partying with a major trafficker wanted by the U.S., prosecutors said Saturday.
Jhon Jairo Velasquez, known by his nickname Popeye, was paroled in 2014 after confessing to hundreds of murders and spending 22 years in jail for plotting the murder of an ex-presidential candidate. Since being released, Velasquez has gained notoriety as an author and YouTube celebrity who delivers angry diatribes against leftist rebels, corrupt politicians and Venezuela’s socialist government.
His presence at a raucous birthday party for Juan Carlos Mesa, one of Colombia’s most-wanted drug traffickers, constituted a “very serious” offence, said the country’s chief prosecutor’s office. The U.S. had been offering a $2 million bounty for Mesa’s capture.
Police raided the party on Friday at a country house near Medellin where they arrested Mesa, alias Tom, who was celebrating his 50th birthday in almost stereotypical narco form: surrounded by armed bodyguards, young women, bountiful alcohol and lots of gambling.
It was unclear what Velasquez was doing at the party. El Tiempo newspaper reported that police seized more than $40,000 in cash, jewelry and seven luxury cars.
Velasquez took advantage of his time behind bars to obtain a number of academic degrees and to seek forgiveness from his victims. He also provided prosecutors with testimony that led to the conviction of a former justice minister close to Escobar.
But even while expressing regret about his crimes, he continued to demonstrate admiration for his former boss.
“If Pablo Escobar were to be reborn I’d go with him without thinking,” he told El Tiempo newspaper in 2013.
rewrite:
Colombian judicial authorities announced on Saturday their intention to petition for the re-incarceration of a former assassin for the late narcotics trafficker Pablo Escobar, following his violation of parole conditions. The individual, Jhon Jairo Velasquez—infamously known as "Popeye"—was found to have attended a social gathering with a high-profile drug trafficker sought by the United States. Velasquez had been released on parole in 2014 after serving twenty-two years of a sentence for his role in orchestrating the assassination of a former presidential candidate, having confessed to involvement in hundreds of homicides. Post-release, he has cultivated a public persona as an author and online commentator, frequently issuing vehement critiques against left-wing guerrilla factions, corrupt political figures, and the Venezuelan government.

The Office of the Attorney General of Colombia characterized his attendance at a boisterous birthday celebration for Juan Carlos Mesa, a principal target of Colombian and U.S. drug enforcement agencies, as a "very serious" infraction. The United States has offered a reward of two million dollars for information leading to Mesa's capture. A police operation conducted on Friday at a rural estate near Medellín resulted in Mesa's arrest. The event exemplified stereotypical narco-trafficker extravagance, reportedly featuring armed security personnel, numerous attendees, abundant alcohol, and gambling activities. Authorities also confiscated over forty thousand dollars in currency, assorted jewelry, and seven high-end vehicles. While Velasquez's specific purpose at the event remains undetermined, his presence alone prompted the legal response.

During his imprisonment, Velasquez pursued several academic qualifications and offered public apologies to his victims. His cooperation with prosecutors also contributed to the conviction of a former justice minister with ties to Escobar. Notwithstanding these expressions of remorse and assistance to judicial authorities, Velasquez has persistently voiced admiration for his former employer. In a 2013 interview with El Tiempo newspaper, he stated, "If Pablo Escobar were to be reborn I’d go with him without thinking."

A two-car crash on Long Island killed three people and injured four, police say.
According to Suffolk County police, the driver of a red Honda Civic lost control of the car and crossed the double yellow line and slammed into a Nissan Pathfinder in Medford just before 4:30 p.m. on Monday.
The two passengers inside the Honda, 20-year-old Dominick Lopez of Shirley, and 23-year-old Derek Buffa of Mastic Beach were ejected and were pronounced dead at the scene, police said. A passenger inside the Nissan, 67-year-old Aida Cardenas of Selden, was taken to an area hospital, where she died, officials said.
The driver of the Nissan and his wife were taken to an area hospital to be treated for non-life threatening injuries, authorities said. The couple’s 11-year-old son and 1-year-old son were also in the car and were taken to the hospital, where they are being treated for non-life threatening injuries, police said.
Both vehicles were impounded for safety and checked and police say they continue to investigate.
Meanwhile, earlier on Monday, a Long Island woman was killed in a hit-and-run crash in Lindenhurst in the early hours -- three months after her sister-in-law died in a crash there and less than two years after her brother met the exact same fate.
rewrite:
A fatal two-vehicle collision in Medford, Long Island, on Monday afternoon resulted in three fatalities and four individuals sustaining injuries, according to Suffolk County police authorities. The incident occurred at approximately 4:30 p.m. when the operator of a red Honda Civic reportedly lost control, crossed a double yellow line, and collided with a Nissan Pathfinder. Two passengers within the Honda, identified as Dominick Lopez, 20, of Shirley, and Derek Buffa, 23, of Mastic Beach, were ejected and pronounced deceased at the scene. A passenger in the Nissan, Aida Cardenas, 67, of Selden, was transported to a local hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.

The driver of the Nissan and his spouse were transported for treatment of non-life-threatening injuries. Their two children, ages 11 and 1, were also present in the vehicle and hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Both vehicles were impounded for safety inspections as the investigation remains ongoing. Separately, earlier on Monday, a female pedestrian was killed in a hit-and-run incident in Lindenhurst. This tragedy follows the death of her sister-in-law in a collision at the same location three months prior, and her brother’s fatal crash there less than two years ago.

By SHERRI RUGGIERI
Bergen County Executive Jim Tedesco presented to the Bergen County Board of Chosen Freeholders his 2018 budget proposal that contains no county tax increase. Even though Bergen County is the most populous county in New Jersey, it continues to have the second lowest county tax rate. County Executive Tedesco explained, “Despite what some may say, government should not be run like a business, because government does not exist to turn a profit. Government exists to the serve the people.” The 2018 budget will fund infrastructure investments and improvements, education, and programs for Bergen County’s veterans, seniors, and children. Furthermore, the budget has been designed to keep full-time county workers earning $15 an hour to adjust to increases in the cost of living.
“By bringing business principles to the management of the county, we are delivering a budget that keeps taxes flat while meeting the needs of the people of Bergen County today and providing the foundation to continue building a better Bergen County for years to come,” stated Tedesco. Under Tedesco’s Administration, Bergen County has received the Moody’s Investors Service’s highest rating because of its strong financial management and future strategic planning.
Sherri Ruggieri is the managing editor of Empire State News. A practicing attorney for over 20 years, Ms. Ruggieri is also chairperson of Edison Township’s Planning Board. Additionally, she has served as a college professor, with nearly a decade of experience in teaching law and political science courses.

Bergen County Executive Jim Tedesco presented his 2018 budget proposal to the Bergen County Board of Chosen Freeholders, a plan which proposes no increase in the county tax levy. Notably, Bergen County, while the most populous in New Jersey, maintains the second lowest county tax rate. In his remarks, County Executive Tedesco articulated a philosophical distinction between governance and commerce, stating, “Despite what some may say, government should not be run like a business, because government does not exist to turn a profit. Government exists to serve the people.” The proposed budget allocates funds for critical infrastructure investments and improvements, educational initiatives, and programs supporting the county’s veterans, senior citizens, and children. A further provision ensures that all full-time county employees will earn a minimum wage of fifteen dollars per hour, an adjustment responsive to rising living costs.

Tedesco emphasized that the application of sound business principles to county management has yielded a fiscally responsible budget. “We are delivering a budget that keeps taxes flat while meeting the needs of the people of Bergen County today and providing the foundation to continue building a better Bergen County for years to come,” he stated. This approach to financial stewardship has resulted in Bergen County, under Tedesco’s administration, receiving the highest possible credit rating from Moody’s Investors Service, a recognition of its robust financial management and strategic long-term planning.

WALSENBURG/ GARDNER — Huerfano County native Sherry Gomez has been on RE-1 school board since Nov. 2013. She was appointed for two years when the vacancy for District B was not filled. In 2015 she was formally elected and has been an active school board member for RE-1 school district for the last four years.
As a present school board member she has supported present administration and teachers in the developed improvement plan for Peakview School to move out of priority status. She also was a strong activist for passing the mill levy override to help improve finances to assist in obtaining better salaries and tools for teachers to help with recruitment and retention and the change in student release time from 3 pm to 4:30 pm to allow for one on one tutoring. Sherry is a strong advocate for maintaining the operation of Gardner School as an option for community member’s children for education Pre-K to 8th grade.
Her objectives for re-election are to continue to advocate for the operation of Gardner school and to bring parent awareness to the public to stress how important a child’s achievement includes active participation from home. A Facebook page, “Be the Change you want to see” has been created to guide and support parents who are busy and need easy access to information so they can help their children be successful, along with bridging the communication between the public and teachers.
rewrite:
Sherry Gomez, a native of Huerfano County, has served on the RE-1 School District Board of Education since November 2013. Her initial appointment to the District B seat, which followed an unfilled vacancy, spanned a two-year term. In 2015, she was formally elected to the position and has maintained an active role on the board for the subsequent four years.

During her tenure, Gomez has consistently supported the district’s administration and teaching staff. Notably, she endorsed the developed improvement plan for Peakview School aimed at moving the institution out of state priority status. She was also a prominent advocate for the successful mill levy override, which was designed to improve district finances. These additional funds are intended to support more competitive teacher salaries and provide enhanced instructional tools, thereby aiding in recruitment and retention efforts. Furthermore, she supported extending the student release time from 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM to facilitate one-on-one tutoring sessions. Gomez remains a staunch proponent of maintaining the operation of Gardner School as an educational option for community children from pre-kindergarten through eighth grade.

Her objectives for re-election include continuing to advocate for Gardner School’s operation and raising parental awareness regarding the critical role of home involvement in student achievement. To this end, she has helped establish a Facebook page titled “Be the Change You Want to See.” This resource is designed to guide and support busy parents by providing accessible information to help their children succeed, while also serving to bridge communication between the public and teaching staff.

Negão the dog was abandoned at a gas station in Mogi das Cruzes, Brazil. He was left with nothing. But thanks to the kindness of the station’s owners, he would soon have a new family and a job to boot.
It was two years ago when Negão was left at the Shell gas station. Luckily, co-owner Sabrina Plannerer and her partner wasted no time taking in the abandoned dog and giving him a loving home.
“We adopted him immediately and got him all the care animals need,” Plannerer told The Dodo. “We took him to the vet to get vaccinated and de-wormed. We bought him food, a dog house and a leash to take him on walks.”
They also gave him a job as a greeter at the gas station. He even has his own employee ID badge.
“Negão waits for people to arrive, and then goes up to say hello, winning them over with his charms,” Plannerer told The Dodo. “Customers love him. Some people even bring him toys.”
He’s definitely the cutest gas station employee we’ve ever seen!
rewrite:
A canine later named Negão was abandoned at a Shell fuel station in Mogi das Cruzes, Brazil, approximately two years ago. The proprietors of the establishment, Sabrina Plannerer and her partner, promptly intervened by providing the dog with sanctuary and subsequently adopting him. According to Plannerer’s account to The Dodo, they ensured comprehensive veterinary care, including vaccination and deworming, and supplied essential provisions such as nourishment, shelter, and a leash.

Beyond securing a permanent residence, Negão was assigned a formal role as a greeter at the station, complete with an identification badge. In this capacity, he approaches patrons upon their arrival, engaging with them in a manner described as charming and endearing. This conduct has reportedly garnered significant affection from the clientele, some of whom bring him toys. The integration of the animal into the commercial environment has thus proven successful, transforming an instance of abandonment into a narrative of stable employment and social inclusion within a community setting.

LAS VEGAS (AP) — The Latest on civil trial involving Las Vegas Strip headliner David Copperfield and a British tourist who claims he was seriously hurt in a fall while taking part in a signature Copperfield illusion in 2013 (all times local):
12:30 p.m.
A judge in Las Vegas has rejected a call by David Copperfield's attorney for a mistrial based on the amount of media coverage that a civil negligence lawsuit involving the world-famous illusionist is getting.
Attorney Elaine Fresch complained Tuesday about interviews involving plaintiff Gavin Cox's attorney, Benedict Morelli.
Fresch noted that one interview aired on CBS-TV just hours before proceedings resumed.
Under questioning by Nevada state court Judge Mark Denton, three jurors said they turned off broadcasts when they saw references to the case on the news during a five-day break in the civil trial.
The judge allowed the trial to resume.
Copperfield is on the stand answering questions from Morelli about whether Copperfield knew of anyone besides Cox who was injured taking part in the magician's audience-volunteer illusion over nearly 20 years he has performed it.
____
9 a.m.
Las Vegas Strip headliner David Copperfield is due to return to the witness stand in a lawsuit by a British tourist who claims he was seriously hurt in a fall while taking part in one of Copperfield's signature illusions in 2013.
The magician resumes testimony Tuesday after last week revealing secrets behind a trick that appears to make volunteer audience members vanish onstage and appear a few moments later in the back of the theater.
Plaintiff Gavin Cox of Kent, England, alleges he fell after being hurried by stagehands through an MGM Grand hotel alleyway coated with a powdery residue near a trailer-sized trash bin.
Copperfield's lawyers lost pretrial bids to close proceedings to the public to avoid revealing performance secrets
Cox and his wife are seeking unspecified damages.
rewrite:
In a civil negligence trial underway in Las Vegas, world-renowned illusionist David Copperfield faces allegations from a British tourist who claims to have sustained serious injuries during a signature audience participation illusion in 2013. Presiding Nevada state court Judge Mark Denton denied a motion for a mistrial filed by Copperfield’s legal counsel, attorney Elaine Fresch. The motion was predicated on concerns regarding extensive media coverage of the proceedings. Fresch specifically cited a televised interview featuring the plaintiff’s attorney, Benedict Morelli, which aired on CBS shortly before the trial reconvened following a five-day recess.

During judicial inquiry, three jurors affirmed they had discontinued viewing news broadcasts upon encountering references to the case. Based on this finding, Judge Denton permitted the trial to proceed. Copperfield subsequently resumed his testimony, undergoing cross-examination by Attorney Morelli. The line of questioning focused on whether Copperfield had prior knowledge of any injuries, beyond those alleged by the current plaintiff, sustained by participants in the long-running audience volunteer illusion over its approximate twenty-year performance history.

The plaintiff, Gavin Cox of Kent, England, asserts that he fell while being directed by stagehands through a service alleyway at the MGM Grand hotel. The alleged incident occurred near a large waste container, with Cox citing a powdery residue on the ground as a contributing factor. In a related development from prior testimony, Copperfield disclosed certain methodological details of the illusion in question, which typically involves volunteers disappearing from the stage and reappearing elsewhere in the theater. Pre-trial motions by Copperfield’s legal team to seal the proceedings, intended to protect proprietary performance secrets, were previously denied by the court. Cox and his spouse are seeking compensatory damages, the specific amount of which remains unspecified at this stage in the litigation.

MILAN, April 28 Saipem has teamed up with Italy's state railways to bid for work on a Russian high-speed train project as the Italian oil engineering and contracting firm seeks new business to offset an ongoing slump in the energy industry.
Oil service groups like Saipem have been hit by a sharp fall in oil prices since mid-2014 that has led energy majors to cut billions of dollars in costs and delay investments.
Oil and gas exploration and development firms spent just 400 billion euros ($436 billion) on projects last year compared to 700 billion euros in 2014, according to Saipem CEO Stefano Cao.
"We've signed a memo of understanding with Ferrovie dello Stato (Italy railways) to make a joint bid for a part of the Moscow-Kazan project," Cao told shareholders at a meeting on Friday.
The Moscow–Kazan project, first proposed in 2009, is a 770-km (480-mile) high-speed rail link between the two Russian cities.
If the bid with Ferrovie was successful, the work could be worth a total of about $3 billion, Cao said.
To offset the slump in the oil and gas sector, Saipem has said it plans to grow business lines in areas like engineering, renewable energy and energy platform dismantling.
But Cao said no talks with the Russians were underway yet about the rail project and he did not expect the work to be booked in the company's backlog in the short term.
Italy's state railways, which has plans to list on the Milan market, is looking to expand its business abroad.
It has operations in Germany and Greece and is looking to bid in tenders in the Britain.
($1 = 0.9177 euros) (Reporting by Stephen Jewkes; Editing by Edmund Blair)
rewrite:
On April 28, the Italian engineering and contracting firm Saipem announced a collaboration with Ferrovie dello Stato, Italy’s state-owned railway operator, to jointly submit a bid for a segment of a Russian high-speed rail project. This initiative represents a strategic effort by Saipem to diversify its operations and mitigate the adverse effects of the protracted downturn in the global energy sector. Companies specializing in oilfield services, including Saipem, have faced significant challenges following the pronounced decline in crude oil prices that commenced in mid-2014. This downturn has prompted major energy corporations to implement substantial cost reductions and defer capital expenditures.

Stefano Cao, Chief Executive Officer of Saipem, provided context by noting that exploration and development spending within the oil and gas industry fell to approximately 400 billion euros ($436 billion) last year, a notable decrease from the 700 billion euros recorded in 2014. During a shareholder meeting, Cao confirmed the execution of a memorandum of understanding with Ferrovie dello Stato pertaining to the Moscow-Kazan high-speed railway project. Initially proposed in 2009, this infrastructure initiative entails the construction of a 770-kilometer (480-mile) line connecting the two Russian cities. Cao indicated the potential value of the contract could reach an estimated $3 billion, should the consortium’s bid prove successful.

In response to sectoral pressures, Saipem has articulated a strategy to expand its activities in domains such as engineering, renewable energy, and the decommissioning of energy platforms. However, Cao clarified that substantive discussions with Russian authorities regarding the rail project have not yet commenced, and he does not anticipate the work being added to the company’s order backlog in the immediate future. Concurrently, Ferrovie dello Stato, which has expressed intentions to pursue a listing on the Milan stock exchange, is seeking to broaden its international portfolio. The operator currently maintains activities in Germany and Greece and is also evaluating tender opportunities in the United Kingdom.

Lawyer Lorenzo Gadon on Tuesday claimed that Chief Justice Maria Lourdes Sereno gave cash to officials of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), sourcing the money from the judiciary’s funds.
Gadon, who filed the impeachment complaint against Sereno who is on leave, said the chief justice gave allowances to the IBP officers, which is why they supported her in connection with the impeachment complaint and the quo warranto petition filed against her by Solicitor General Jose Calida.
“The reason why I filed an impeachment case against Chief Justice Sereno was because of her own fault and it is obvious from the results of the House committee on justice that she had committed so many corrupt acts,” Gadon said in a speech during the conference on empowering women law enforcers held in Camp Aguinaldo, the headquarters of the Philippine military.
Gadon has accused Sereno of not acting on petitions to provide survivors’ benefits to the families of judges who died.
“Majority of those judges are female, 95 percent are female, and their age was at about 80 years old. They failed to receive benefits even if it was under the law,” he said.
Gadon claimed that the “Sereno Supreme Court” provided allowance to IBP officials. “You can see that the IBP officials have been siding with her,” he added.
Jojo Lacanilao, one of the lawyers of Sereno, disputed Gadon’s claims.
“He is again lying and perjuring himself,” Lacanilao told reporters in a text message.
“Attorney Gadon is full of lies just like the impeachment complaint he filed. He also has no evidence on the accusations he was hurling against CJ Sereno,” he added.
On Monday, Jover Laurio of Pinoy Ako Blog filed a disbarment case against Gadon for allegedly violating his oath as a lawyer and the Code of Professional Responsibility when he filed the “baseless unactionable criminal complaint” against Sereno.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, attorney Lorenzo Gadon alleged that Chief Justice Maria Lourdes Sereno disbursed cash to officials of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP), asserting that the funds originated from judiciary resources. Gadon, the complainant in the impeachment case against the currently leave-taking chief justice, contended that these monetary allowances were provided to IBP officers, thereby securing their support for her amidst the impeachment proceedings and the separate quo warranto petition submitted by Solicitor General Jose Calida. Gadon articulated these accusations during a speech at a conference on empowering women law enforcers, held at Camp Aguinaldo, the headquarters of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. He stated that his impetus for filing the impeachment complaint stemmed from Sereno’s purported misconduct, citing the findings of the House committee on justice as indicative of numerous corrupt acts.

Further, Gadon accused the chief justice of failing to act upon petitions seeking survivors’ benefits for the families of deceased judges, noting that a significant majority of these judges were female, approximately 95 percent, and around 80 years of age. He emphasized that these families were deprived of legally mandated benefits. Gadon linked this inaction to a broader pattern, alleging that the "Sereno Supreme Court" financially accommodated IBP officials, which he posited explained their consistent alignment with her position.

These claims were vigorously disputed by Jojo Lacanilao, a member of Chief Justice Sereno’s legal team. In a text message to reporters, Lacanilao denounced Gadon’s statements as false and perjurious, characterizing the attorney as "full of lies" and noting a consistent absence of evidence for his allegations. This controversy follows a recent disbarment complaint filed against Gadon by blogger Jover Laurio of Pinoy Ako Blog. The complaint, submitted on Monday, charges Gadon with violating his attorney’s oath and the Code of Professional Responsibility by initiating what is described as a "baseless unactionable criminal complaint" against Chief Justice Sereno.
