Schaeffler is the main sponsor of the Audi Sport ABT Formula E team, so the company has access to the appropriate hardware. It took four electric motors from the FE01 race car and stuffed them into the RS3. The motors produce a combined 1,180 horsepower. That makes the 400 hp produced by the RS3’s stock 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-five seem positively timid.
Dubbed 4ePerformance, the electric RS3 can reach 124 mph from a standstill in 7 seconds, according to Schaeffler. The company didn’t mention a 0 to 60 mph time, but we reckon the 4ePerformance can do the job a bit quicker than Audi’s claim of 3.9 seconds for the stock RS3.
Besides the raw power, the electric RS3 should possess decent agility. Two motors power each axle, giving the car all-wheel drive (this is an Audi, after all) and gearboxes at both axles enable torque vectoring. This means power can be shifted side to side to help nudge the car around corners. Two battery packs with a total capacity of 64 kilowatt hours power the car, and Schaeffler appears to have used the bodywork from the Audi RS3 LMS race car as well.
Audi previously tried to build and market its own all-electric performance car, the R8 e-tron, but production ended after just a few examples were built. The German automaker is now focusing its attention on the more practical e-tron SUV, which is expected to launch later this year. Audi will likely introduce additional all-electric models after that as part of parent Volkswagen Group’s electrification push.
Formula E is attracting more manufacturers. The field already includes the likes of Audi, BMW, and Jaguar, with Mercedes-Benz and Porsche set to join the series as well. Nissan will also replace its alliance partner Renault in Formula E. As automakers also launch more electric road cars, Formula E will likely grow in importance as a marketing tool.

Investigators determine the blaze to be accidental and related to a passing train
Firefighters responded Monday afternoon to a small vegetation fire near Gaviota, according to the Santa Barbara County Fire Department.
The blaze burned along the railroad tracks south of Highway 101, near Mariposa Reina, according to Fire Department spokesman Mike Eliason.
Capt. David Sadecki said Tuesday that the cause of the fire was most likely related to a passing train and was considered accidental.
Several engine crews and at least one water-dropping helicopter were dispatched to the fire, which broke out at about 3:45 p.m.
The fire, which charred about an acre, was burning in grass and light chaparral, Eliason said.
At the time of the blaze, there were sustained winds of 15 to 20 mph, with gusts to 25 mph, Eliason said.
“It was putting up some pretty good flames, but it just ran out of real estate,” Eliason said.
— Noozhawk executive editor Tom Bolton can be reached at .(JavaScript must be enabled to view this email address) . Follow Noozhawk on Twitter: @noozhawk, @NoozhawkNews and @NoozhawkBiz. Connect with Noozhawk on Facebook.
rewrite: On Monday afternoon, a vegetation fire occurred near Gaviota, adjacent to the railroad tracks south of Highway 101 in the vicinity of Mariposa Reina. According to the Santa Barbara County Fire Department, the incident commenced at approximately 3:45 p.m. and consumed approximately one acre of grass and light chaparral. Firefighting resources included multiple engine crews and at least one helicopter equipped for water drops. Conditions at the time featured sustained winds of 15 to 20 miles per hour, with gusts reaching 25 miles per hour, which contributed to the fire's intensity. Captain David Sadecki stated on Tuesday that investigators have determined the cause was most likely linked to a passing train and have classified the blaze as accidental. The fire was ultimately contained due to limited fuel availability within the affected area.

A Church Warsop man who was stranded in Mansfield after losing his wallet on a drunken night out, borrowed a car to get home and argued with police when he was stopped, a court heard.
Samuel Billyeald was stopped in his pal’s BMW, on Albert Street, at 1.15am, on November 25, because he was driving without any lights.
“He was arrested because there was no attempt to provide a specimen,” said prosecutor Daniel Pietryka.
“One minute he was compliant and the next he refused to cooperate. He was being difficult and had to be restrained.”
Billyeald, 22, of Laurel Avenue, admitted driving without insurance, or a licence, and failing to cooperate with a preliminary test or to provide a specimen for analysis, when he appeared at Mansfield Magistrates Court, on Monday.
Abbie Edwards, mitigating, said: “This is totally out of character. He went out socialising in Mansfield town centre. He had consumed too much alcohol to drive.
“He lost his wallet and house keys and had no way to find his way home. Regretably, he decided to borrow a friend’s car. He did think about walking but it was very cold.
“He panicked when the police pulled him over and that’s why he refused to give a breath sample. He was clearly affected by the alcohol. He is very remorseful and ashamed.”
Ms Edwards said Billyeald has “quite severe mental health issues.”
He has one previous conviction for threatening behaviour, from April this year, which puts him in breach of a suspended sentence, the court heard.
Probation officer Sarah Alderton said: “He knew that the offence would put him in breach of a suspended sentence order. He chose to make a foolish mistake.”
She said he claimed to be a social drinker, but acknowledged that both offences were committed when he was drunk.
Billyeald was given a 12 month community order, with a two month curfew, from 7pm to 7am, and the operational period of his suspended sentence was extended by two months.
He was banned from driving for 12 months. He must pay £85 court costs and an £85 victim surcharge.
rewrite:
The case of Samuel Billyeald, a 22-year-old resident of Laurel Avenue in Church Warsop, was heard at Mansfield Magistrates' Court on Monday. Mr. Billyeald pleaded guilty to multiple driving offences, including operating a vehicle without insurance or a valid licence, failing to cooperate with a preliminary roadside test, and refusing to provide a specimen for analysis. The court was informed that the incident occurred in the early hours of November 25th, when police stopped a BMW being driven by Mr. Billyeald on Albert Street, Mansfield, at approximately 1:15 a.m., due to the vehicle's headlights being inactive.

Prosecutor Daniel Pietryka stated that Mr. Billyeald was subsequently arrested following his refusal to provide a specimen. Mr. Pietryka described the defendant's conduct as inconsistent, noting an initial compliance that shifted to a refusal to cooperate, necessitating physical restraint by officers.

In mitigation, legal representative Abbie Edwards explained that the events were highly uncharacteristic for her client. Mr. Billyeald had been socialising in Mansfield town centre, consuming a quantity of alcohol that rendered him unfit to drive. After misplacing his wallet and house keys, thereby losing his means of returning home, he made the regrettable decision to borrow a friend's vehicle, having considered but dismissed walking due to the low temperature. Ms. Edwards submitted that Mr. Billyeald panicked upon being intercepted by police, leading to his non-compliance with the breath test procedure, and that he now expresses considerable remorse and shame. She further informed the court that Mr. Billyeald experiences significant mental health difficulties.

The court noted a previous conviction for threatening behaviour from April of this year, which placed Mr. Billyeald in breach of a suspended sentence order. Probation Officer Sarah Alderton reported that the defendant was aware his actions constituted a breach, describing his decision as a "foolish mistake." While Mr. Billyeald identifies as a social drinker, Ms. Alderton acknowledged that both recorded offences were committed while he was under the influence of alcohol.

The magistrates imposed a 12-month community order with a two-month curfew, stipulating confinement between the hours of 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. The operational period of the suspended sentence was extended by two months. Additionally, Mr. Billyeald was disqualified from driving for 12 months and ordered to pay £85 in court costs alongside an £85 victim surcharge.

HONG KONG, March 29 (IFR) - Asian credit markets continued on a constructive path on Wednesday, though there was volatility in Fosun International's notes following surprising news of a management reshuffle at the Chinese conglomerate.
"Market sentiment remained positive today with spreads slightly tighter. However, we also saw a bit of profit taking," said a Hong Kong-based investment-grade credit trader.
The iTraxx Asia investment-grade index, which has rolled into Series 27, was 1.7bp tighter at 93.8/95.3bp. China Cinda's 3.0% 2020 notes were 3bp tighter at 129.3bp over US Treasuries.
In the high-yield sector, another credit trader observed that there was some initial selling in Fosun International's recent 2022s in the morning, but that the notes later recovered to cash price of around 101.5.
Fosun International announced last night the resignation of two top managers after reporting 2016 net profit growth of 28% year on year.
Liang Xinjun resigned as vice chairman and chief executive of the company for health reasons, while senior vice-president Ding Guoqi also stepped down.
Property developer China Evergrande's 2018s were bid at a cash price of around 104, according to Tradeweb. The developer reported that its 2016 core profit jumped 89% year on year to Rmb20.81bn, thanks to strong increases in property prices and volumes.
(Reporting by Ina Zhou; editing by Dharsan Singh)
rewrite:
Asian credit markets maintained a constructive trajectory on Wednesday, albeit with isolated volatility. Notably, notes issued by Fosun International experienced price fluctuations subsequent to an unexpected announcement of senior management changes at the conglomerate. A Hong Kong-based investment-grade credit trader noted, "Overall market sentiment remained positive, evidenced by marginally tighter spreads, though some profit-taking activity was observed."

The iTraxx Asia ex-Japan investment-grade index, having rolled into its Series 27, tightened by 1.7 basis points to 93.8/95.3bp. Similarly, China Cinda's 3.0% bonds maturing in 2020 tightened by 3bp, trading at a spread of 129.3bp over US Treasuries. Within the high-yield sector, a separate trader reported initial selling pressure on Fosun International's 2022 notes during the morning session, which later recovered to a cash price approximating 101.5.

This activity followed Fosun International's disclosure, released the prior evening, of the resignations of two senior executives. Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Liang Xinjun resigned citing health reasons, and Senior Vice-President Ding Guoqi also stepped down. The announcement coincided with the company's report of a 28% year-on-year increase in 2016 net profit. Elsewhere, property developer China Evergrande's 2018 bonds were bid at a cash price near 104. The developer attributed an 89% annual rise in its 2016 core profit, to RMB20.81 billion, to robust increases in both property prices and sales volume.

St. Rose Health Center provides cardiac rehabilitation for patients after a heart-related event but they also realize the importance of preventing problems from occurring in the first place.
Since February is American Heart Month, Shannon Deines, imaging supervisor, shared information on the three cardiovascular screenings available at St. Rose. She encourages the community to take advantage of these screenings to help prevent a variety of concerns.
“Each non-invasive test takes less than 30 minutes and the cost is very affordable,” Deines said. “Anyone concerned about cardiovascular disease is encouraged to call for an appointment.
“When screens detect a problem, we refer patients to their primary-care physicians,” she added. “When a problem is not detected, the patient can enjoy peace of mind.”
One screen checks for peripheral arterial disease (PAD) to help determine the risk of blockages in leg arteries.
“Those who are wondering about PAD might consider a few questions,” Deines suggested. “For example, do you have leg cramping, aching or fatigue when you walk? Do you have poorly healing ulcers on your feet or toes? Do you smoke, or have hypertension, diabetes or high cholesterol?”
A stroke scan also is available at St. Rose. This is an ultrasound test to see inside the carotid arteries in the neck. It can detect early signs of plaque build-up.
And the third screening involves a scan for an abdominal aortic aneurysm, which is a ballooning of the arterial wall that may cause the artery to burst.
A doctor’s referral is not necessary for any of these screenings, and the fee for each is $30. However, if someone chooses to have all three at the same time, the total cost is $75. Cash and checks are accepted.
“When screening results are available, we mail them to the patients,” Deines noted. “They can share results with their doctors.
“If any concerns are detected,” she elaborated, “we will recommend they follow up with their doctor for further testing. This type of preventive health care can go a long way to preventing or alleviating more serious conditions in the future.”
rewrite:
St. Rose Health Center offers comprehensive cardiac rehabilitation services for patients recovering from cardiac events, while also emphasizing the critical role of preventive care in mitigating cardiovascular disease. In observance of American Heart Month this February, Shannon Deines, Imaging Supervisor at the facility, has detailed three cardiovascular screenings available to the public. She advocates for community utilization of these services as a proactive measure against a spectrum of potential health concerns.

"Each non-invasive screening requires less than thirty minutes to complete and is offered at a highly accessible cost," stated Deines. "Individuals with any concerns regarding cardiovascular disease are encouraged to schedule an appointment." She further explained the dual benefit of the screenings: "If a screening detects a potential issue, we refer the patient to their primary care physician for further evaluation. Conversely, a negative result provides valuable reassurance and peace of mind."

The first screening assesses for Peripheral Arterial Disease (PAD), evaluating the risk of arterial blockages in the lower extremities. Deines suggested that individuals consider specific indicators: "Potential candidates might inquire if they experience leg cramping, aching, or fatigue during ambulation; have poorly healing ulcers on the feet or toes; or possess risk factors such as a history of smoking, hypertension, diabetes, or high cholesterol."

A second option is a stroke risk assessment, utilizing ultrasound imaging to visualize the carotid arteries in the neck. This scan can identify early-stage plaque accumulation, a precursor to cerebrovascular events. The third screening is an abdominal aortic aneurysm scan, which detects abnormal ballooning of the aortic wall that carries a risk of rupture.

A physician referral is not required for any of these screenings. The fee for each individual test is thirty dollars; however, a bundled rate of seventy-five dollars is available for clients opting to undergo all three screenings concurrently. Payment is accepted via cash or check. "Results are mailed directly to patients upon availability," Deines noted, "enabling them to share the findings with their physicians. Should any abnormalities be detected, we will recommend prompt follow-up with a doctor for further diagnostic testing. This model of preventive healthcare is instrumental in forestalling or mitigating more severe future conditions."

GLENDALE, AZ - Arizona twins are going to have a unique story to tell for the rest of their lives after they were born in different years.
Holly and Brandon Shay weren’t expecting their boys to arrive for another few weeks, however, they were shocked when Banner Hospital in Glendale admitted them on New Year’s Eve.
After six exhausting hours of labor, their first son, Sawyer, was born at 11:51 p.m.
“I wanted to make sure he was OK, and they had to keep reminding me that I had to push," Holly said.
Just one minute after midnight on January 1, 2017, their second baby, Everett, was born.
The boys who previously shared nine months in the same space won’t be sharing a birthday -- or even their birth year.
“I think Sawyer might give his brother a hard time,” Brandon said. “I think it’s mostly going to be Sawyer teasing Everett over him being the eldest.”
rewrite: A pair of twins in Glendale, Arizona, possess a distinctive narrative for their lifetimes, having been born in separate calendar years. Holly and Brandon Shay anticipated the arrival of their sons several weeks later, yet were surprised by an admission to Banner Hospital in Glendale on December 31, 2016. Following six hours of labor, their first son, Sawyer, was delivered at 11:51 p.m. Holly noted her concern for the infant's welfare required staff to repeatedly remind her to continue pushing. Precisely one minute after midnight on January 1, 2017, their second son, Everett, was born. Consequently, the twins, who previously occupied a shared gestational space for nine months, will not share a common birth date or even year. Brandon Shay speculated that Sawyer may later jest with Everett regarding his status as the elder sibling.

DALLAS (AP) - Two Dallas police officers were critically wounded in a shooting Tuesday outside a home improvement store, authorities said.
Police Chief U. Renee Hall said a store loss-prevention officer also was shot in the incident about 4:15 p.m. outside a Home Depot in northern Dallas.
In a tweet about the shooting Tuesday evening, the Dallas Police Department said the officers were critically wounded. During a news conference Tuesday night at Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Dallas, Hall declined to give an update on their conditions, citing consideration for the privacy of the officers' families.
"We're asking you to continue praying for our officers," Hall said.
The two police officers went to the store to assist an off-duty police officer with taking a man into custody and then the shooting happened.
A 29-year-old man is being sought as a person of interest. Hall said the man left the scene in a white pickup truck.
"I continue to be upset at the lack of respect of our police in this city and in our country," said Mayor Mike Rawlings, who also attended the hospital news conference.
In 2016, four Dallas police officers and a transit officer were shot dead by a sniper in an ambush that came toward the end of a peaceful protest over the police killings of black men that had occurred in other cities.
___
This story has been corrected to show that the fatal shooting of five officers in Dallas was during a protest in 2016, not 2006.

rewrite:
On the afternoon of Tuesday, April 24, 2018, two Dallas police officers were critically wounded in a shooting incident outside a Home Depot store in northern Dallas. According to authorities, the event occurred at approximately 4:15 p.m. A loss-prevention officer from the store was also shot during the altercation. The officers had initially responded to the location to provide assistance to an off-duty officer who was in the process of apprehending an individual.

Police subsequently launched an extensive search for a 29-year-old male identified as a person of interest, who was reported to have fled the scene in a white pickup truck. Law enforcement personnel concentrated their efforts in the vicinity of the Home Depot, near an ExtraSpace Storage facility. Concurrently, a security presence was established at the emergency room entrance of Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Dallas, where the wounded officers were receiving treatment.

During a news conference held at the hospital Tuesday evening, Dallas Police Chief U. Renee Hall declined to provide specifics regarding the officers' medical conditions, citing a need to respect the privacy of their families. She did, however, confirm the critical nature of their injuries and requested public support. "We're asking you to continue praying for our officers," Chief Hall stated. Dallas Mayor Mike Rawlings, who also attended the briefing, expressed his dismay, remarking, "I continue to be upset at the lack of respect for our police in this city and in our country."

The incident evoked memories of a prior tragedy in Dallas. In 2016, during a peaceful protest, a sniper ambush resulted in the fatal shooting of five law enforcement officers: four from the Dallas Police Department and one transit officer. That protest had been organized in response to police-involved shootings of black men in other U.S. cities.

This report clarifies that the aforementioned fatal 2016 shooting occurred during a protest in that year, not in 2006. The information is based on official statements and reports from the associated press.

RUSSIAN TIME heads into the 13th GP2 season with a new line-up comprising 22-year-old Russian Artem Markelov and Italian 21-year-old Luca Ghiotto.
Markelov and Ghiotto were both top 10 championship finishers in the 2016 series, with Artem winning the Monaco feature race and finishing on the podium in the season finale at Yas Marina. Luca, meanwhile, finished runner-up in the Hockenheim feature event and claimed four podiums in all, including a win at Sepang en route to his 111 points.
Both men have impressive records in the junior racing categories, with Markelov a former runner-up in the German F3 championship and Ghiotto vice-champion in both Formula Abarth and Formula Renault 2.0 before taking pole position at Spa on his GP3 debut. His 2015 GP3 campaign saw him finish runner-up to current Force India F1 driver Esteban Ocon, beaten by eight points despite five victories and eight podiums.
"We made an important step last year," Markelov said, "with a win and a top 10 finish in the championship. The GP2 series is highly competitive and I’m looking forward to doing even better in 2017 and challenging for more wins and hopefully becoming a consistent front-runner."
Speaking about the season ahead, Ghiotto said: "Let me firstly thank all at RUSSIAN TIME for the great opportunity they have offered me. Having crossed their cars a few times in 2016, I know how good they are! I think we have great potential to develop together. I’m looking forward to working with my new team mate Artem, and can’t wait to hit the track in March to start work."
Team principal Svetlana Strelnikova added: "I’m delighted to be able to announce such a promising line-up that will hopefully allow us to challenge for the teams’ championship that we won in 2013. The fact that four different teams have claimed the title in the past four seasons is a good illustration of just how competitive the series is. We are all hugely looking forward to it."

Ghiotto secured vice-champion status in both Formula Abarth and Formula Renault 2.0, and subsequently took pole position at Spa-Francorchamps on his GP3 Series debut. Senator Cynthia Villar quashed fears on Thursday that she would be proposing a ban on the serving of unlimited rice or unli-rice in restaurants and food outlets.
“I am not planning to make a law banning ‘unli-rice.’ Not at all,” Senator Cynthia Villar said in a statement.
Villar issued the statement amid reports that she wanted to ban unli rice.
ADVERTISEMENT
“I just voiced out my concern that eating too much rice is one of the main causes of high blood sugar that leads to diabetes,” the senator said.
“I cannot prevent people from eating unlimited amount of rice. It is their choice. It was just a genuine expression of concern on my part,” she added.
The unli-rice issue came up during Wednesday’s hearing of the Senate committee on agriculture and food, which Villar chairs.
“Unlimited rice is bad for the health. We should learn how to eat more vegetables,” the senator said during the hearing.
READ: Unli-rice is unhealthy, says Villar
In Thursday’s statement, Villar recognized that it would be difficult to stop Filipinos from eating rice “as the Philippines is a nation or rice eaters.”
“But to decrease health risks, cutting down on rice is still a good idea,” she said.
The senator cited a study, which showed that eating one plate of white rice everyday increases the risk of developing diabetes by 11 percent. Health experts, she said, also recommend adding 20% of brown rice to the daily white rice consumption as it can reduce the risk of diabetes by around 16%.

“Rice causes an increase in the level of sugar in the blood, which makes pancreas produce more insulin and cause frequent spikes in blood sugar level leading to diabetes. When not managed, diabetes may cause organ malfunction leading to death,” Villar said.
The senator earlier urged concerned government agencies such as the Department of Agriculture, Department of Social Welfare and Development, and the Department of Health (DoH) to align their programs in order to promote better nutrition and health among the young Filipinos.
“I have recommended to the government departments and they are doing it in some areas already to incorporate vegetable gardening in schools in the feeding program, for instance. In a statement released on Thursday, Senator Cynthia Villar, Chairperson of the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Food, categorically dispelled concerns regarding any proposed legislative prohibition on the service of unlimited rice, commonly termed "unli-rice," within Philippine dining establishments. The senator explicitly clarified, “I am not planning to make a law banning ‘unli-rice.’ Not at all.” This clarification was issued in response to circulating reports suggesting her support for such a ban.

Senator Villar explained that her remarks, which originated during the committee’s hearing on Wednesday, were intended solely to express a public health concern. “I just voiced out my concern that eating too much rice is one of the main causes of high blood sugar that leads to diabetes,” she stated. She emphasized the autonomy of individual dietary choices, noting, “I cannot prevent people from eating unlimited amount of rice. It is their choice. It was just a genuine expression of concern on my part.” During the hearing, she had advocated for dietary moderation, asserting, “Unlimited rice is bad for the health. We should learn how to eat more vegetables.”

Acknowledging the cultural significance of rice consumption in the Philippines, Villar conceded that persuading Filipinos to reduce intake is challenging, describing the nation as one of "rice eaters." Nevertheless, she maintained that “to decrease health risks, cutting down on rice is still a good idea.” To substantiate this position, she cited scientific research indicating that daily consumption of one plate of white rice elevates diabetes risk by approximately eleven percent. Furthermore, she referenced expert recommendations to integrate twenty percent brown rice into the daily diet, a modification associated with a potential sixteen percent reduction in diabetes risk.

Villar elaborated on the physiological mechanism, explaining that rice consumption elevates blood sugar levels, thereby stimulating increased insulin production from the pancreas. This process can lead to frequent glycemic spikes, a pathway to developing diabetes, which, if unmanaged, may result in organ dysfunction and mortality.

Beyond dietary advice, the senator outlined a policy-oriented approach to improving national nutrition. She reported urging relevant government agencies—including the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Social Welfare and Development, and the Department of Health—to synchronize their programs to promote better health among Filipino youth. One specific recommendation involves integrating vegetable gardening into school feeding programs. “They can also source the ingredients locally, particularly the perishable produce, to help the small farmers and cooperatives,” Villar added, highlighting the dual benefits of enhancing nutritional education and supporting local agricultural economies.

YOUNGSTOWN, Ohio (AP) -- Cole Gentry scored 21 points and Mark Hughes added 15 points on 5-of-10 shooting from 3-point range to power Wright State to an 83-57 romp over Youngstown State on Saturday.
Gentry connected on 8 of 13 shots from the floor to help the Raiders (18-7, 10-2 Horizon League) finish 29 of 51 (57 percent). Gentry hit 3 of 6 shots from distance as Wright State shot 41 percent (9 of 22) from beyond the arc. The Raiders held the Penguins (6-19, 4-8) to 31-percent shooting from the floor (20 of 65) and 18 percent (3 of 17) from long range.
Braun Hartfield was the lone Penguin in double figures with 20 points. He added six rebounds and three steals. Naz Bohannon had 13 rebounds to go along with nine points.
Hartfield scored seven as the Penguins jumped out to a 9-2 lead, but Hughes hit two 3s in a 14-0 run and Wright State, which led 40-25 by halftime, never trailed again.

Cole Gentry led all scorers with 21 points, converting 8 of 13 field goal attempts, while Mark Hughes contributed 15 points, including 5 successful three-point shots out of 10 attempts. Collectively, the Raiders (18-7, 10-2) shot 57 percent from the field (29 of 51) and 41 percent from three-point range (9 of 22). Defensively, they limited Youngstown State (6-19, 4-8) to 31 percent shooting overall (20 of 65) and 18 percent from beyond the arc (3 of 17). For the Penguins, Braun Hartfield recorded a team-high 20 points, along with six rebounds and three steals, while Naz Bohannon secured 13 rebounds and added nine points. Despite an early 9-2 lead for Youngstown State, fueled by seven points from Hartfield, Wright State responded with a 14-0 run—featuring two three-pointers from Hughes—and maintained a 40-25 halftime advantage, never relinquishing the lead thereafter.

BANGKOK, March 30 Mudman Pcl, which runs cafes and restaurants such as Au Bon Pain and Dunkin' Donuts in Thailand, plans to raise 1.1 billion baht ($32 million) in an initial public offering (IPO) to help repay debt and fund expansion.
The company plans to sell about 211 million new shares at 5.25 baht each, parent firm Sub Sri Thai (SST) said in a statement to the stock exchange on Thursday.
Of the total, up to 41.44 million shares will be offered to SST's existing shareholders on March 29-31 and the rest will be sold to the public on April 3-5, it said.
Maybank Kim Eng Securities (Thailand) is the IPO lead underwriter and Siam Commercial Bank is the financial adviser.
Mudman also runs the Baskin Robbins franchise in Thailand as well as its own brand Greyhound Cafe.
Overall, it has 439 branches of Au Bon Pain, Dunkin Donuts, Baskin Robbins and Greyhound restaurants and cafes in Thailand and is planning to open its first Greyhound Cafe in London this year. ($1 = 34.4 baht) (Reporting by Wirat Buranakanokthanasan; writing by Orathai Sriring; editing by David Clarke)
rewrite: On March 30, Mudman Public Company Limited, the operator of Au Bon Pain and Dunkin' Donuts franchises in Thailand, announced its intention to raise 1.1 billion baht (approximately $32 million USD) through an initial public offering (IPO). The capital will be allocated towards debt repayment and expansion initiatives. According to a statement issued by its parent company, Sub Sri Thai Public Company Limited (SST), to the stock exchange, the offering involves approximately 211 million new shares priced at 5.25 baht per share. The allocation includes up to 41.44 million shares for existing SST shareholders from March 29 to 31, with the remainder offered to the public from April 3 to 5. Maybank Kim Eng Securities (Thailand) serves as the lead underwriter, with Siam Commercial Bank acting as financial adviser. Mudman's portfolio also includes the Baskin Robbins franchise and its proprietary Greyhound Cafe brand. The company currently operates 439 outlets across its brands within Thailand and plans to inaugurate its first Greyhound Cafe in London within the current fiscal year.

The Blue Jays challenged two safe calls with the same batter up in the third — one at second on a steal attempt and the other at the home with a runner looking to score when a pitch bounced away. Both were overturned.

Cora is excited to get his World Series ring before Thursday's series opener in Houston.

He plans to bring a jersey he wore last season as the team's bench coach, have it signed by the Astros and hang it "probably at home."

rewrite:
The Toronto Blue Jays were without third baseman Josh Donaldson for a second consecutive game due to right calf soreness. The Boston Red Sox continued to miss outfielder Mookie Betts for a fourth straight contest owing to left side tightness that originated during batting practice on Sunday. Manager Alex Cora indicated that Betts would likely return to the lineup the following day if he felt adequately recovered. Second baseman Dustin Pedroia was also granted a scheduled day of rest.

During the third inning, the Blue Jays successfully challenged two safe calls involving the same batter. The first pertained to a stolen base attempt at second, while the second concerned a play at home plate following a wild pitch. Both initial rulings were overturned following video review.

Cora expressed anticipation for receiving his World Series ring prior to Thursday's series opener in Houston, reflecting on the championship season as "an amazing ride." He intends to bring a jersey from his tenure as the team's bench coach last season, have it signed by members of the Astros organization, and display it, likely in his home.

Home plate umpire Jerry Layne remained in the game after being struck in the chest by a foul ball, though he was momentarily dazed and required steadying by Boston catcher Christian Vazquez.

Regarding upcoming pitching assignments, Toronto left-hander Jaime Garcia (2-3, 5.52 ERA) is scheduled to start Friday's series opener in Detroit. Boston left-hander Drew Pomeranz (1-2, 6.75 ERA) is slated to start Thursday's opener of a four-game series in Houston. Pomeranz has struggled recently, posting an 0-1 record with a 9.53 ERA and failing to complete more than four innings in any of his last three appearances.

WorkSafeBC wants you to keep safe while hanging those Christmas lights this year
On average more than 930 workers in British Columbia are seriously injured each year due to falls from ladders and many of those incidents were preventable.
With the holiday season in full swing, WorkSafe BC wants you to know that using a ladder around the house has risks too.
WorkSafeBC has released six new ladder-safety videos to remind workers, employers and homeowners to use ladders safely, both on the job and while decorating at home for the holidays.
“Last year, more than 1,000 workers were seriously injured in falls from height, including while using step ladders, extension ladders and scaffolding,” says Dan Strand, Director of Prevention Field Services for WorkSafeBC.
“The new videos and our ladder safety resources illustrate how the right ladder, the correct positioning and hazard assessments could prevent a life-changing serious injury or death.”
From 2012 to 2016, six workers died and there were 4,920 accepted time-loss claims — including 1,634 serious injuries — as a result of falls from ladders across all industries in B.C.
It’s time to use ladders safely:
Select the right ladder for the job and ensure the ladder is long enough to extend one metre above the upper landing
Place the ladder on a firm, level surface and inspect it before each use to ensure it’s in good working condition, looking for issues such as cracks or loose rungs
Always maintain three points of contact while climbing a ladder: two feet and one hand or two hands and one foot
Don’t carry heavy or bulky objects while climbing up or down a ladder
Don’t work from the top two rungs of the ladder or have more than one worker on a ladder at once
Wind, rain, and snow may pose additional hazards that need to be mitigated
Check for power lines and ensure a minimum distance of three metres can be maintained at all times before starting work

rewrite:
WorkSafeBC emphasizes the importance of safety during the installation of seasonal decorations, specifically Christmas lighting. Annually, an average of over 930 workers in British Columbia sustain serious injuries from falls involving ladders, a significant portion of which are avoidable. As holiday activities intensify, WorkSafeBC underscores that domestic ladder use also entails considerable risk.

To reinforce safe practices, WorkSafeBC has published six new instructional videos aimed at workers, employers, and homeowners. These resources are intended to promote ladder safety in both occupational and residential contexts, particularly during holiday decorating. Dan Strand, Director of Prevention Field Services at WorkSafeBC, notes, “Last year, more than 1,000 workers suffered serious injuries in falls from height, including incidents involving step ladders, extension ladders, and scaffolding.” He adds, “These new videos, along with our existing safety materials, demonstrate how appropriate ladder selection, correct positioning, and thorough hazard assessments can prevent severe, life-altering injuries or fatalities.”

Statistical data from 2012 to 2016 indicate that falls from ladders across all industries in British Columbia resulted in six fatalities and 4,920 accepted time-loss claims, which included 1,634 serious injuries. To mitigate such incidents, adherence to the following safety protocols is essential:

1. Select a ladder suitable for the task, ensuring it is of sufficient length to extend one metre above the intended upper landing point.
2. Position the ladder on a firm, level surface and conduct a pre-use inspection to confirm it is in good condition, checking for defects such as cracks or loose rungs.
3. Maintain three points of contact (e.g., two feet and one hand, or two hands and one foot) while ascending or descending.
4. Avoid carrying heavy or bulky items when climbing.
5. Refrain from using the top two rungs and ensure only one person uses a ladder at a time.
6. Account for environmental hazards such as wind, rain, or snow, which require additional precautions.
7. Prior to commencing work, identify nearby power lines and maintain a minimum clearance of three metres at all times.

These guidelines are integral to reducing the incidence of ladder-related injuries and fatalities. For further reference, ladder safety resources are available through official channels.

Gunning for a return ticket to the zonal playoffs, Ceres Negros FC takes on Home United FC in the final match day of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Cup 2018 Asean zone group stage today at the Panaad Park and Stadium in Bacolod City.
The defending champion Yellow Busmen square off with the Protectors at 6 p.m.
Ceres Negros leads Group F with 13 points on an unbeaten record of four wins and a draw.
The Philippine titlist only needs a stalemate to enter the knockout phase for the second consecutive year.
Last season, Ceres beat Home United to emerge as the first Filipino club to rule the Asean zone. Head coach Risto Vidakovic wants to make history anew.
“We are not playing against Home United. We’re playing because we want to make history. We have the opportunity to make an excellent finish on the group stage and be on top of the group,” said Vidakovic.
Home, on the other hand, stands at No. 2 with 10 points on a 3-3-1 win-draw-loss record.
The Singaporean booters need to win by five goals or more to edge out the Filipino squad in the race to the playoffs.
Mentor Aidil Sharin, who is eager to steer his Protectors to an upset victory, reminds his wards to keep their transition defense sturdy.
“Our mind is to win and get three points. That’s the main objective to come here. But we have to be smart in how we’re going play and of course be very tight during the counter-attack,” said Sharin.
The first meeting between the two regional powerhouse teams ended in a 1-1 draw at the Jala Besar Stadium last February 27.
Shahril Ishak scored the opening goal via a penalty kick for Home but Super Herrera hit an equalizer for Ceres late in the game.
Meanwhile, Global Cebu FC looks to close its campaign on a bright note against Bali United FC in a non-bearing match at the Kapten I Wayan Dipta Stadium in Indonesia.
The People’s Club and the Tridatu Warriors battle for pride at 7 p.m.
rewrite:
Ceres Negros FC will face Home United FC in the concluding match of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Cup 2018 ASEAN zone group stage this evening at Panaad Park and Stadium in Bacolod City, with progression to the zonal knockout playoffs at stake. The defending champions, Ceres Negros, will compete against Home United, colloquially known as the Protectors, commencing at 6:00 PM.

Ceres Negros currently occupies first position in Group F, having accrued 13 points from an undefeated campaign comprising four victories and one draw. The Philippine titleholders require only a draw from this fixture to secure qualification for the knockout phase for a second consecutive year. Having defeated Home United last season to become the first Filipino club to win the ASEAN zone, head coach Risto Vidakovic has expressed ambition to achieve another historic milestone. Vidakovic stated, “Our objective extends beyond the opponent; we are motivated by the opportunity to make history. We aim to conclude the group stage optimally and finish at the summit of the group.”

Conversely, Home United holds second place with 10 points, derived from a record of three wins, three draws, and one loss. The Singaporean side must secure a victory by a margin of five or more goals to surpass Ceres Negros and advance to the playoffs. Their head coach, Aidil Sharin, emphasized the necessity of a disciplined defensive approach in pursuit of an upset. Sharin noted, “Our primary objective is to win and obtain three points. However, we must execute intelligently and maintain particular solidity in transition to counter-attacks.”

The previous encounter between these two regional contenders concluded in a 1-1 draw at the Jala Besar Stadium on February 27. Shahril Ishak opened the scoring for Home United from a penalty kick, but Ceres Negros secured a late equalizer through striker Bienvenido Marañón, commonly referred to as ‘Super’.

In a simultaneous but inconsequential Group F match, Global Cebu FC will conclude its campaign against Bali United FC at the Kapten I Wayan Dipta Stadium in Indonesia at 7:00 PM, with both teams competing for pride.

The PFL finalizes the venue of the Global Cebu vs Ceres-Negros finals match
Published 8:28 PM, December 11, 2017
MANILA, Philippines – The Philippines Football League (PFL) announced on Monday, December 11, that the finals knockout match between Global Cebu FC and Ceres-Negros FC will be held at the Pana-ad Stadium in Bacolod on Saturday, December 16.
Prior to the announcement, Global Cebu FC sent an appeal to the PFL that stated they were "exercising their right to host the PFL final" based on the argument that they were included in the fixture whose winner had the right to host the final.
(READ: Global Cebu FC wants to host PFL finals in Cebu City Sports Complex)
According to the statement released by the PFL, the league arrived at a decision after the second finals series meeting with the clubs. In their first meeting held on Wednesday, November 29, 2017, the top 4 clubs were "invited to signify their intention to host the Finals," but are still subjected to the PFL "making the final decision in accordance with Article 2.11 of the PFL Tournament Regulations."
Only FC Meralco Manila and Ceres signified their intent to host the final match, where the Manila team would have hosted it in Rizal Memorial Stadium. Cebu City Sports Complex was not available due to the "pitch and lighting" conditions, while University of the Makati "would not be able to host back-to-back matches."
The PFL also cited that they arrived at the decision to host it at Pana-ad due to "a variety of factors including, but not limited to, venue availability, commercial, marketing, and financial considerations."
The finals match will kick off at 6 pm on Saturday, while the 3rd and 4th place match between Meralco and Kaya FC will take place on Friday, December 15 at the Rizal Memorial Stadium but the time is yet to be finalized. – Rappler.com
rewrite:
On Monday, December 11, 2017, the Philippines Football League (PFL) finalized the venue for its inaugural championship match, selecting Pana-ad Stadium in Bacolod as the host site for the final knockout contest between Global Cebu FC and Ceres-Negros FC on Saturday, December 16. This announcement followed a formal appeal from Global Cebu FC, which asserted its right to host the final. The club’s claim was based on its participation in a specific fixture where the victorious team was granted hosting privileges under the league’s framework.

According to an official PFL statement, the decision was reached during a second finals series meeting with the involved clubs. An initial meeting on Wednesday, November 29, 2017, had invited the top four clubs to express their intent to host the final, though the league retained ultimate authority per Article 2.11 of the PFL Tournament Regulations. Only FC Meralco Manila and Ceres-Negros FC submitted formal hosting proposals, with Meralco nominating Rizal Memorial Stadium. Potential venues in Cebu City and Makati were deemed unsuitable; the Cebu City Sports Complex was unavailable due to inadequate pitch and lighting conditions, while the University of Makati could not accommodate back-to-back matches.

The league cited a comprehensive assessment of multiple factors in selecting Pana-ad Stadium, including venue availability alongside commercial, marketing, and financial considerations. The championship match is scheduled for 6:00 PM on December 16. Preceding the final, the third-place playoff between FC Meralco Manila and Kaya FC will be held at Rizal Memorial Stadium on Friday, December 15, with the kickoff time to be determined.

With the Dunlop MSA British Touring Car Championship returning for rounds four, five and six this weekend at Donington Park. Team Shredded Wheat Racing with Gallagher hope that this is the circuit to kick off their 2018 silverware collection following a topsy-turvy meeting at Brands Hatch earlier this month.
The damp conditions played havoc with the assured competitive nature of the Motorbase prepared Ford Focus RS, therefore Brands Hatch was seen as a bit of a disappointment for the team during both qualifying and the races. The highest placed finish over the weekend went the way of Tom Chilton who finished fifth at the first race of the day.
Considering the success that Motorbase have had previously at Donington where they have scored victories in 2011, 2012 and 2016, the team is confident that the trend for good results at the circuit will continue.
Oly Collins Team Manager commented on why he believed the team should have a better weekend than they did at Brands, “On paper, Donington should suit the RS better than the Brands Indy circuit.
“It’s a little faster and the aero and chassis improvements that we’ve made to the Focus should make a big difference there.
“We went well at the media day test last month and it’s been a happy hunting ground for us in the past, so we’re aiming to continue that trend this weekend and hopefully bag ourselves some new silverware to take home on Sunday night!”
Chilton also echoed these sentiments, “I was second fastest there on media day and we showed at Brands Hatch that we have the pace to be challenging for wins.
“I can’t wait to shake off the run of bad luck we had at Brands Hatch and get our championship challenge off the ground this weekend.”
Whilst James Cole, driver of the #20 Focus RS is assured by the speed shown by the car during the early stages of this year, “I think the pace we’ve shown so far during pre-season and also at Brands demonstrates the potential of where we should be.
“We’ve reset after the bad luck we had during the opening rounds and it’s time to show what were capable of this weekend.”
rewrite:
The Dunlop MSA British Touring Car Championship resumes this weekend at Donington Park for its fourth, fifth, and sixth rounds. Team Shredded Wheat Racing with Gallagher anticipates that this circuit will provide the opportunity to commence its 2018 podium campaign, following an inconsistent meeting at Brands Hatch earlier this month.

Adverse weather conditions significantly disrupted the typically assured competitive performance of the Motorbase-prepared Ford Focus RS. Consequently, the Brands Hatch event proved disappointing for the team across both the qualifying sessions and the races. The highest finish achieved over the weekend belonged to Tom Chilton, who secured fifth position in the day’s opening race.

Given Motorbase Performance’s prior success at Donington Park, where the team secured race victories in 2011, 2012, and 2016, there is confidence that this trend of strong results at the circuit will continue. Team Manager Oly Collins elaborated on the rationale for expecting an improved performance relative to Brands Hatch: “Theoretically, the Donington circuit should be better suited to the Focus RS than the Brands Hatch Indy layout. It is a somewhat faster circuit, and the aerodynamic and chassis enhancements we have implemented on the Focus should yield a more pronounced benefit there. Our performance was strong during the media day test last month, and historically, this has been a successful venue for our team. Our objective is to maintain that trajectory this weekend and, ideally, secure new silverware by Sunday evening.”

Driver Tom Chilton expressed congruent sentiments: “I recorded the second-fastest time there on media day, and our pace at Brands Hatch demonstrated our potential to contend for victories. I am eager to move beyond the unfortunate circumstances encountered at Brands Hatch and properly initiate our championship challenge this weekend.”

Meanwhile, James Cole, driver of the #20 Focus RS, draws assurance from the car’s demonstrated speed in the early phase of the season: “The pace exhibited during pre-season testing and, in glimpses, at Brands Hatch, indicates our potential competitive level. We have recalibrated following the misfortunes of the opening rounds and are prepared to demonstrate our capabilities this weekend.”

An award-winning board game café in Sharnbrook is inviting families to enjoy some quality time together next weekend (Saturday and Sunday, July 14/15) at a Teenage Appreciation event.
Ready Steady Roll, at Ivy Lodge Farm off the A6, says teenagers who visit with their parents will get a free slice of cake while they play any board games from their more than 300 game collection.
Ready Steady Roll
Darrell Cannon, owner of Ready Steady Roll, said: “It may be a hard sell to get a teenager to play board games if their memories of board games are marathon sessions of Monopoly ending with arguments
“But there is a whole world of games that are fun, interesting and much less rage inducing!
“We pride ourselves on finding a game for everyone, even people who think they don’t like board games - plus we have delicious homemade cake made by my wife Charlotte!
“Parents are always looking for ways to get their teenagers off the latest technological fad, from Snapchat to Fortnite, and board games are the perfect remedy.
“I love it when a family come in with a sceptical teenager and within minutes they are sat around a table, laughing and having a great time together.
“Teenagers have a lot of stress in their lives, from exams to social media pressures, so spending quality time together as a family, whether that’s by playing a board game or going on a walk in so important everyone’s wellbeing.”
Ready Steady Roll started life as a monthly Pop Up event in Sharnbrook Village Hall. It is based at Ivy Lodge, in Sharnbrook, 10 minutes down the A6 from Rushden.
Anyone can visit from Wednesday to Sunday during the day with booking recommended either on 07584 484101 or info@readysteadyroll.co.uk
Visit www.readysteadyroll.co.uk for more.
rewrite:
Ready Steady Roll, an award-winning board game café situated at Ivy Lodge Farm off the A6 in Sharnbrook, will host a Teenage Appreciation event next weekend, on Saturday the 14th and Sunday the 15th of July. The establishment extends an invitation to families, encouraging them to partake in shared recreational time. As part of the initiative, teenagers accompanied by a parent will receive a complimentary slice of homemade cake while accessing the café’s collection of over three hundred board games.

Darrell Cannon, proprietor of Ready Steady Roll, acknowledges the potential challenge of engaging adolescents with board games, particularly if prior experiences are associated with protracted and contentious sessions such as Monopoly. He emphasises, however, the existence of a diverse array of contemporary games designed to be engaging and enjoyable without fostering frustration. The café prides itself on curating selections to suit all preferences, including those who may initially express disinterest in the medium. Cannon further notes that the event offers families a constructive alternative to digital pursuits, such as social media and video games, by facilitating direct interpersonal interaction and cooperative play. He observes that even initially sceptical teenagers often quickly become immersed in the social experience, resulting in shared laughter and familial bonding.

Cannon also highlights the broader significance of such activities for adolescent wellbeing, contending that in an era marked by academic pressures and the demands of social media, dedicated family time—whether through board games or other shared pursuits—is vital for collective mental health.

Originally operating as a monthly pop-up event in Sharnbrook Village Hall, Ready Steady Roll is now permanently based at Ivy Lodge, approximately ten minutes from Rushden via the A6. The café is open from Wednesday to Sunday; advance booking is recommended via telephone (07584 484101) or email (info@readysteadyroll.co.uk). WELLS, ME (CBS Local) – A friendly dog’s “thank you” to the firefighter who rescued him from a roof has gone viral.
The pup in Wells, Maine got himself into a rough situation over the Memorial Day weekend when he escaped out the second floor window of his owner’s home and was trapped on a small porch roof.
“We received numerous calls but one concerned citizen, Phil Burke, discovered him early on and notified us. Another awesome citizen stood by with the dog until we could arrive on scene!” Wells Police wrote on Facebook.
When a firefighter climbed up to help the dog get back inside, the grateful pup became more interested in showing his appreciation than getting off the roof. Police on the ground recorded the friendly dog circling Fire Department Captain Jeff Nawfel and giving him a bunch of kisses on the face before getting a final nudge back into his home.
The dog’s “thank you” was posted on May 27 and has already been viewed over 16,000 times. “Thank you to all that called and helped save him,” officers wrote on Facebook.
rewrite: In Wells, Maine, a canine's expression of gratitude toward a firefighter who assisted it gained significant attention online. Over the Memorial Day weekend, the dog escaped through a second-story window of its owner's residence, becoming stranded on a narrow porch roof. The Wells Police Department reported receiving multiple calls regarding the incident. A concerned citizen, Phil Burke, initially located the dog and alerted authorities, while another individual remained with the animal until first responders arrived. Upon scaling the roof to facilitate the rescue, Fire Department Captain Jeff Nawfel was met with an affectionate response from the dog. As documented by officers on the scene, the dog circled Captain Nawfel and repeatedly licked his face before being gently guided back inside the home. The police department's social media post detailing the event, which included a note of thanks to all who assisted, was published on May 27 and has since accumulated over 16,000 views.

Police are warning people intending to tramp the Tongariro Alpine Crossing to be fully prepared after an English tourist plunged 100m down rocks and ice this morning.
Senior Constable Barry Shepherd of Taupō Police said trampers should carry an ice axe and crampons - and know how to use them.
Taupō's Greenlea helicopter this morning flew a paramedic and Land Search and Rescue volunteer to Mt Tongariro to rescue an English woman who had slipped on ice at Red Crater and fallen 100m down the mountain into a ravine.
She was "pretty beaten up" by the fall down through rocks and ice, including a knocking her head and suffering bruises and cuts, Mr Shepherd said.
Advertisement
The woman, 30, who has been living and working in New Zealand, set out from the Mangatepopo carpark this morning at 4am with a young Austrian woman as a companion.
The fall occurred at about 7.30am and the alarm was raised 10 minutes later.
The helicopter flew from Taupō Airport to Mt Tongariro and dropped off a paramedic near Emerald Lakes, who made his way to the woman.
It then unloaded the SAR volunteer who used an ice axe and crampons to reach the Austrian woman perched on the icy slope below the summit of Red Crater, where she had remained.
She had been in voice contact with her friend, although she could not see her, and initially feared she had been killed in the fall.
Shepherd said both women did the right thing in staying put and calling for help but there was always ice on the Tongariro Alpine Crossing at this time of year and people needed to be properly prepared.
"It's icy up there, that whole Red Crater summit was icy.
"It'll thaw and soften around late morning but freezes overnight and will be frozen in the mornings, and if you get a bit of cloud and it stays under cloud, it won't thaw out at all."
If people did not know how to use an ice axe and crampons, they should use a guiding service across the crossing, he added.
The injured woman was flown to Rotorua Hospital.
rewrite:
Authorities are issuing a stern warning to individuals planning to traverse the Tongariro Alpine Crossing, following a serious incident this morning in which an English tourist fell approximately one hundred meters down a rocky and icy section of the mountain. Senior Constable Barry Shepherd of the Taupō Police emphasized that trampers must be adequately equipped with an ice axe and crampons, and possess the requisite skills to utilize this equipment effectively.

The emergency response was initiated when a thirty-year-old English woman, currently residing and employed in New Zealand, slipped on ice at the Red Crater summit at approximately 7:30 a.m. She subsequently fell into a ravine. The woman had commenced her trek from the Mangatepopo carpark at 4:00 a.m., accompanied by a young Austrian woman. The alarm was raised ten minutes after the fall. Taupō's Greenlea helicopter was dispatched from Taupō Airport, transporting a paramedic and a Land Search and Rescue (SAR) volunteer to the site. The paramedic was deployed near Emerald Lakes and proceeded to the injured tramper, while the SAR volunteer, employing an ice axe and crampons, reached the Austrian companion who had remained stationary on the icy slope below the summit.

Senior Constable Shepherd reported that the victim sustained significant injuries from the descent over rocks and ice, including head trauma, bruising, and lacerations. He commended both individuals for their appropriate response in remaining in place and summoning assistance. However, he underscored the persistent hazardous conditions on the crossing during this season, noting that ice is consistently present. "The entire Red Crater summit was icy," Shepherd stated. He further explained that while surfaces may thaw and soften by late morning, overnight freezing ensures icy conditions persist in the early hours. The presence of cloud cover can inhibit thawing entirely, prolonging the danger.

Shepherd reiterated that trampers lacking proficiency with ice axes and crampons should strongly consider engaging a professional guiding service for the crossing. The injured woman was ultimately airlifted to Rotorua Hospital for medical treatment. This incident serves as a critical reminder of the inherent risks of alpine environments and the non-negotiable necessity of proper preparation and equipment.

Severe thunderstorm watch canceled for this evening
hello
The severe thunderstorm watch originally scheduled to last until 8 p.m. was canceled early as the storms moved out of the area.
Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry, Lake, Will and many other northern Illinois counties were part of the watch from the National Weather Service in Chicago. There also was a warning for DuPage, Will and parts of Kane and Cook counties that lasted until 5:45 p.m.

Crystal Palace have gone down in Brondby manager Alexander Zorniger's estimations, following a second collapsed move for goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow.
The goalkeeper was the subject of a deadline day bid on Wednesday for the Eagles and was believed to be all set for the move to London, having seen a deal to Palace fall through last summer, too.
It was initially understood Brondby pulled out of the deal late on, but the Danish club seem to have their side of the story, too.
Boss Zorniger has been quoted by Danish newspaper, BT, and is happy to have kept Ronnow - for now - but is isn't happy with the treatment received by Palace.
"Frederik was in the same situation last summer. The same club would have the same player on the last day of the transfer window," he said, as quoted by BT.
"I don’t know if anyone can understand what they do, I’m not able to do. But he is still here and we’re very happy.
"Maybe they think it’s professional, but from my point of view it’s unprofessional. It’s disrespectful to another club."
Ronnow, himself, is gutted his Premier League dream has been crushed twice in the space of five months.
He was quoted: "I’m obviously annoyed, but also clear and motivated.
"I could choose to go and cry in the corner, but I wouldn’t get anything out of it."
rewrite:
Crystal Palace Football Club has diminished in the esteem of Brondby manager Alexander Zorniger, following a second unsuccessful attempt to secure the transfer of goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow. The goalkeeper was the subject of a deadline-day proposal from the Premier League club on Wednesday and appeared poised to complete a move to London, having also seen a potential transfer to Palace collapse the previous summer.

Initial reports suggested Brondby withdrew from negotiations at a late stage; however, the Danish club has presented its own perspective. As quoted by the Danish publication BT, Manager Zorniger expressed satisfaction at retaining Ronnow for the present, but conveyed significant displeasure with Crystal Palace’s conduct. "Frederik was in the same situation last summer. The same club would have the same player on the last day of the transfer window," he stated. "I don’t know if anyone can understand what they do; I’m not able to. But he is still here and we’re very happy. Maybe they think it’s professional, but from my point of view it’s unprofessional. It’s disrespectful to another club."

For his part, Ronnow has expressed profound disappointment that his aspiration to play in the Premier League has been thwarted twice within five months. He remarked, "I’m obviously annoyed, but also clear and motivated. I could choose to go and cry in the corner, but I wouldn’t get anything out of it."

Last week, footage was released of a schizophrenic man writhing on the floor of his cell until he dies as California sheriff’s deputies laugh and smirk.
The Tribune of San Luis Obispo posted the approximately eight-minute-long video of Andrew Holland's death on January 22, 2017, last week. Holland, who was in jail for minor offenses, died after an embolism traveled to his brain. Blood clots, which typically cause embolisms, often occur after an extended period of sitting or lying down.
The footage contradicts the county officials' version of how Holland died. Contrary to what police stated, Holland was not "found unconscious and unresponsive" and was not "under the continual care of a physician" at the time of his death.
Holland was pronounced dead in his cell at 5:36 p.m. on January 22, 2017, only about an hour after he was released from being strapped to a plastic restraint chair for two days for hitting himself.
In an email Thursday, County Administrative Officer Wade Horton said the video was "extremely painful to watch."
​"What happened to Andrew Holland was a tragedy that impacts our entire community," Horton wrote.
"Although we can't bring Andrew back, our county has made, and continues to make, changes in response to this terrible event."
Some of the reforms implemented including banning the use of restraint chairs, hiring an independent contractor to audit county procedures and establishing the Stepping Up initiative to reduce the number of mentally ill patients in prisons.
In July 2017, Holland's family was awarded a $5 million settlement from the county. They plan to use the settlement money to establish a nonprofit organization to advocate for civil rights of mentally ill people in jail.
"We had hope that his life would improve, but on January 22nd of this year, our son Andrew died a brutal and tortured death at the hands of the custodial staff at San Luis Obispo County jail," Holland's mother, Sharon, told reporters last July.
Although Horton did admit that the county is partly responsible for Holland's death, he did not specify whether any officials would face consequences over Holland's death.
rewrite:
Last week, video evidence was publicly released depicting the final moments of Andrew Holland, an individual diagnosed with schizophrenia, who expired while writhing on the floor of a San Luis Obispo County jail cell as sheriff’s deputies observed with apparent amusement. The San Luis Obispo Tribune published this approximately eight-minute recording, dated January 22, 2017. Holland, who was incarcerated for minor infractions, succumbed to a fatal embolism that traveled to his brain. Such vascular events, commonly caused by blood clots, are frequently associated with prolonged periods of immobility.

This footage directly contradicts the official account provided by county authorities. Contrary to initial statements, Holland was not discovered “unconscious and unresponsive,” nor was he “under the continual care of a physician” at the time of his death. Official records indicate he was pronounced deceased in his cell at 5:36 p.m. on January 22, 2017, approximately one hour after being released from a restraint chair. He had been confined in that apparatus for a period of two days following an incident of self-harm.

In a statement issued last Thursday, County Administrative Officer Wade Horton described the video as “extremely painful to watch” and acknowledged the event as “a tragedy that impacts our entire community.” Horton further noted that while Andrew Holland cannot be restored, the county has enacted, and continues to implement, systemic reforms in response. These measures include a prohibition on the use of restraint chairs, the engagement of an independent contractor to audit county procedures, and the establishment of the Stepping Up initiative, which aims to reduce the incarceration of individuals with mental illness.

In July 2017, Holland’s family reached a $5 million settlement with the county. The family intends to allocate these funds toward founding a nonprofit organization dedicated to advocating for the civil rights of mentally ill persons within the carceral system. As his mother, Sharon Holland, stated to reporters at that time, “We had hope that his life would improve, but on January 22nd of this year, our son Andrew died a brutal and tortured death at the hands of the custodial staff.” While Administrator Horton conceded partial institutional responsibility for the tragedy, his statement did not specify whether any personnel would face disciplinary or legal consequences.

More of the same is expected this entire week, although high temperatures will be close to normal and very high dew points will result in unusually warm morning lows. Showers and thunderstorms are likely to erupt each day, dependent on a combination of daytime heating and an old frontal boundary lurking just north of here, plus minor disturbances on a smaller scale. Activity may again be rather isolated today, but scattered the rest of the week with a bit more coverage expected.
An early look at next Monday’s weather for the solar eclipse indicates we may be able to see it fairly well with partly cloudy skies. Later forecasts will pin it down with more precision.

Kano State government has approved N4 billion for the construction of underpass and flyover that will connect Zaria Road/Silver Jubilee and Zoo Road in the metropolis.
In a statement in Abuja on the outcome of the 11th State Executive Council, SEC, meeting presided over by Governor Abdullahi Ganduje, the Commissioner for Information, Youth and Culture, Malam Muhammad Garba, said the project was aimed at reducing carbon emission and road accidents and to beautify the state capital.

MADISON — The bad news keeps coming for the Wisconsin basketball team.
On the same day guard D’Mitrik Trice was to undergo surgery on his foot that will keep him out indefinitely, Wisconsin announced Monday that freshman guard Kobe King will have season-ending knee surgery.
Advertisement
King injured his left knee during practice on Friday. After not being present during the first half of Saturday’s game against Marquette, the La Crosse native sat behind the bench during the second half of that loss.
“I’m disappointed that I’m not able to finish the season with my teammates,” King said in a tweet sent by UW. “But following my surgery, I plan to attack my rehab as aggressively as possible & come back stronger than ever. While I’m out, I look forward to watching our team continue to grow this season”
A prized recruit in the 2017 class, King was averaging 5.2 points and 1.4 rebounds for the Badgers over the first 10 games of the season. King is eligible to apply for a medical hardship waiver after the season. If granted, he would still have four years of eligibility remaining.
“I feel awful for D’Mitrik and Kobe,” coach Greg Gard said in a tweet sent by UW. “Fortunately, there is a silver lining that we were right under the minimum number of games to apply for a (medical hardship).”
The loss of King, combined with the uncertainty around Trice, is a significant hit for a team that was struggling to find its way even with that duo on the floor. As of now, the only true guards Wisconsin has coming off its bench are junior T.J. Sclundt, who played a career-high 13 minutes against Marquette, and true freshman walk-on Walt McGrory, who was expected to redshirt this season.
The Badgers are just 4-7 on the year, a mark that has them at three games under .500 for the first time since 2001. They’ll host Western Kentucky on Wednesday.

On the same day that guard D’Mitrik Trice was scheduled for foot surgery, which will sideline him for an indeterminate period, the program disclosed that freshman guard Kobe King will undergo season-ending surgery on his left knee. King sustained the injury during a practice session last Friday. Notably absent during the first half of Saturday's contest against Marquette University, the La Crosse native was observed seated behind the bench for the duration of the second half in what resulted in a loss for the Badgers.

In a statement disseminated via the university's official communications, King expressed his disappointment at being unable to complete the season alongside his teammates. He affirmed his intention to pursue postoperative rehabilitation with diligence, aiming to return at an enhanced level of performance. Concurrently, he conveyed his support for the team's continued development in his absence. A highly-regarded recruit from the 2017 class, King was contributing averages of 5.2 points and 1.4 rebounds per game through the season's initial ten contests. Following the season's conclusion, he will be eligible to apply for a medical hardship waiver. Should this petition be approved, he would retain four full years of collegiate eligibility.

Head coach Greg Gard, also quoted through official university channels, communicated his sympathy for both Trice and King. He noted a mitigating circumstance, indicating that the timing of King's injury occurred prior to the threshold that would preclude a medical hardship application. The absence of King, coupled with the indefinite loss of Trice, represents a substantial setback for a squad that has faced difficulties even with both players available. This depletion leaves the backcourt depth notably compromised. Presently, the only reserve guards at Wisconsin's disposal are junior T.J. Schlundt, who logged a career-high thirteen minutes against Marquette, and true freshman walk-on Walt McGrory, who was previously anticipated to redshirt this season.

The team's record currently stands at four wins and seven losses, placing them three games below a .500 winning percentage for the first time since the 2001 season. The Badgers are scheduled to host Western Kentucky University in their next outing on Wednesday.

How far would you go to save a life? Would you donate your gently used clothes or household items? Do you have items that have been sitting in your house for a long time, meaning to get rid of them? If the answer to any of these is yes, then why not donate them to The Salvation Army and be our partner in Doing The Most Good.
Winter is the hardest season for The Salvation Army for clothing donations. We are asking residents to open their closets and donate clothes and shoes and help us fund the Adult Rehabilitation Center. Since the ARC doesn’t solicit government funding, the ministry runs solely on the generosity of individuals, organizations and businesses who donate goods to be sold in our Family Stores. Please consider making a donation today by calling 800-SA-TRUCK for a free pickup. Or drop your donation at a store, donation center or donation box near you.
Bil Moriarty, donation development coordinator
The Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center
Portland

SAO PAULO, April 10 Shareholders of Brazil's BNDES have approved a statute guaranteeing the state development bank will keep at least 40 percent of its earnings, capping dividends to the federal government for the first time, newspaper Valor Economico reported on Monday.
The new statute calls for the bank to pay the government 25 percent to 60 percent of its adjusted annual profit, Valor reported. In recent years, the government took all available earnings to cover its fiscal deficit.
Media representatives for the bank did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Previously, BNDES had no defined dividend policy, its legal director, Marcelo de Siqueira Freitas, told Valor. The paper said the bank's technical staff saw the policy as helping to guarantee capital levels and reduce the need for the repeated funding that the government provided in recent years.
The move is another step toward curbing political influence in strategic planning at BNDES. Under the leftist Workers Party's 13-year administration, the bank became a tool for economic policies that contributed to a huge fiscal deficit.
Since the party lost power last year, the new center-right government has encouraged BNDES to write stricter bylaws curbing political intervention in lending decisions and demanding better corporate governance from borrowers. (Writing by Brad Haynes and Guillermo Parra-Bernal; Editing by Daniel Flynn and Lisa Von Ahn)
rewrite:
On April 10, shareholders of Brazil’s National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES) ratified a statutory amendment establishing, for the first time, a formal dividend policy. As reported by the newspaper Valor Econômico, the new statute mandates the retention of a minimum of forty percent of the bank’s annual earnings, thereby instituting a ceiling on dividend distributions to the federal government. Specifically, it stipulates that dividends shall range from twenty-five to sixty percent of BNDES’s adjusted annual profit. This represents a significant departure from recent practice, wherein the federal government claimed all available profits to address fiscal shortfalls.

According to Valor, the bank’s legal director, Marcelo de Siqueira Freitas, confirmed that BNDES previously operated without a defined dividend policy. Technical staff within the institution view the new policy as a mechanism to bolster capital reserves and diminish reliance on the repeated capital injections provided by the government in preceding years. This statutory change constitutes a further measure to insulate the bank’s strategic planning from political influence. During the thirteen-year administration of the leftist Workers’ Party, BNDES was frequently utilized as an instrument for economic policy, a role that contributed substantially to the national fiscal deficit. Since the accession of a new center-right government, BNDES has been encouraged to adopt stricter governance bylaws aimed at curtailing political intervention in lending decisions and enforcing enhanced corporate governance standards among its borrowers. Representatives of BNDES did not immediately respond to requests for commentary.
