DURHAM, N.C. (WNCN) – A crowd of protesters gathered outside the old Durham County courthouse on Main Street Monday evening in opposition to a Confederate monument in front of the government building.
Around 7:10 p.m. a woman using a ladder climbed the statue of a soldier and attached a rope around the statue.
Moments later, the crowd pulled on the rope and the statue fell. One man quickly ran up and spat on the statue and several others began kicking it.
It’s not clear where law enforcement officers were during the protest.
Previous story: Haslam: Nathan Bedford Forrest should not be honored at State Capitol
In 1924, the Confederate statue was dedicated to Durham.
Engraved on the front of the monument is “The Confederate States of America.”
Above it, is a statue representing a soldier who fought in the civil war.
“It needs to be removed,” Loan Tran, an organizer, said earlier Monday. “These Confederate statues in Durham, in North Carolina, all across the country.”
There are similar monuments in several cities around North Carolina.
Tran doesn’t want to see it anymore.
“When I see a Confederate statue in downtown Durham, or really anywhere, it fills me with a lot of rage and frustration,” she said.
Organizers say tonight’s protest is a reaction to the events in Charlottesville this past weekend.
“People can be mobilized and people are angry and when enough people are angry, we don’t have to look to politicians to sit around in air conditions and do nothing when we can do things ourselves,” said Takiyah Thompson, a protester.
The statue is on county property.
In an email to CBS North Carolina, Durham County spokeswoman Dawn Dudley says:
“Due to a North Carolina state law passed a few years ago, Durham County is prohibited from removing or making substantive alteration to historical monuments and memorials. I share this to say that there is a statute in place making the efforts you mention below difficult to move forward. I would assume that the only thing possible are steps to reverse the law.”
This statue has been the center of controversy before after graffiti was spray painted on it a few years ago.
The group that met Monday say their purpose is to “smash white supremacy.”
rewrite:
On the evening of Monday, August 14, 2017, a group of demonstrators assembled outside the former Durham County courthouse on Main Street in Durham, North Carolina. Their gathering constituted a protest against a Confederate monument situated on the grounds of the government building. At approximately 7:10 p.m., an individual utilized a ladder to ascend the statue, which depicts a soldier from the Civil War, and secured a rope around it. The assembled crowd then pulled the rope, toppling the monument. Following its descent, one individual approached and spat upon the fallen statue, while several others proceeded to kick it. The whereabouts of law enforcement personnel during these events remain unclear.

The monument in question was originally dedicated in Durham in 1924. Its base bears the inscription “The Confederate States of America,” surmounted by the figure of a Confederate soldier. The protest was organized, in part, as a direct response to the violent events that had transpired in Charlottesville, Virginia, the preceding weekend. Organizer Loan Tran articulated the motivation for the action earlier that Monday, stating, “It needs to be removed. These Confederate statues in Durham, in North Carolina, all across the country.” Tran further expressed that encountering such monuments elicits profound anger and frustration. Another participant, Takiyah Thompson, framed the event as an act of popular mobilization, suggesting that public anger can precipitate direct action when political processes are perceived as ineffective.

The statue is located on county property. However, in a statement issued via email, Durham County spokeswoman Dawn Dudley cited a North Carolina state law that prohibits local governments from removing or substantively altering historical monuments and memorials. This statute effectively constrains the county’s ability to address such monuments through official channels, with legislative reversal presented as the probable requisite course for any formal change.

This incident was not the first instance of controversy surrounding the monument; it had previously been defaced with graffiti. The organizing group explicitly stated their purpose as the dismantling of white supremacy, framing the statue’s removal as a symbolic act toward that goal. The protest and subsequent toppling of the monument occurred within a broader national debate concerning the public display of Confederate iconography and its historical implications.

Disaster assistance will be provided to people affected by Cyclone Marcus after it smashed the Top End last weekend.
Around 6000 households still without power will be eligible to receive an immediate cash payment of $250 and possibly further funding for damage to their homes and to replace household contents, Northern Territory Chief Minister Michael Gunner says.
"We have now opened five relief centres for residents to apply for immediate payments if they are still without power," Mr Gunner said.
The category two cyclone battered the territory over the weekend, bringing flooding, road closures and winds in excess of 130km/h.
At its peak, 30,000 homes were without power and schools and other government services were forced to remain closed on Monday.
The funding is provided through the jointly-funded Commonwealth-State Natural Disaster Relief and Recovery Arrangements.
Mr Gunner said further assistance would be considered once damage assessments and cost estimates became available in coming days.

July 4 (UPI) -- An Ecuadorian court ordered the arrest of former President Rafael Correa over his alleged involvement in a failed plot to kidnap a political rival in 2012.
Judge Daniella Camacho of the National Justice Court of Ecuador said she alerted Interpol of a request to extradite Correa, who lives in Belgium with his wife.
Prosecutors accuse the former president of being behind the brief kidnapping of Fernando Balda in Bogota, Colombia, where the former lawmaker fled to avoid tensions with Correa. Balda said five men attempted to kidnap him but Colombian police halted the plot.
Balda traveled to Colombia to avoid charges of being involved in a failed coup against Correa in 2010. Balda was sentenced to one year in prison.
The former president, who led Ecuador from 2007 to 2017, denied the charges and said there was no evidence against him.
"How much success will this farce have at the international level?" Correa said. "Don't worry, everything is a matter of time. We will overcome!"

Judge Daniella Camacho of the National Justice Court confirmed that Interpol has been notified of an extradition request for Correa, who currently resides in Belgium. Prosecutors assert Correa orchestrated the brief kidnapping attempt of former legislator Fernando Balda in Bogotá, Colombia, where Balda had relocated amid political tensions. According to Balda, the attempt was thwarted by Colombian police. Balda had initially fled to Colombia to evade charges related to an alleged 2010 coup attempt against Correa, for which he later received a one-year prison sentence. Correa has publicly denied all allegations, stating there is no evidence against him and dismissing the proceedings as a "farce," while expressing confidence that the matter will be resolved in his favor over time.

CHARLESTON, WV – The West Virginia Department of Agriculture (WVDA) will begin aerial treatment for gypsy moth in early May. The spraying will occur across approximately 5,298 acres within Grant, Hardy, Nicholas and Pendleton counties. The goal is to reduce impacts of the gypsy moth in West Virginia’s forested lands. The WVDA proposed to treat these acres under the WVDA Cooperative State-County-Landowner (CSCL) suppression program.
“The gypsy moth is the most serious forest pest currently in West Virginia. This is a non-native, invasive insect that feeds on over 300 species of trees and shrubs, including West Virginia hardwoods,” said Commissioner of Agriculture Kent Leonhardt. “Defoliation by gypsy moth caterpillars can kill trees or weaken them substantially, making them more susceptible to other pests and diseases.”
Landowners in the CSCL Program have signed a contract, paid a deposit and share the final cost with the WVDA to complete treatment for their gypsy moth problem. Landowners then select the spray material to be used on their property. The spray materials offered for 2018 are Foray 48B (Btk) or Mimic (Tebufenozide). Egg mass densities on non-residential forested lands must contain 500 egg masses per acre or higher to qualify for treatment.
“This treatment program is a safeguard to one of our most important natural resources. Homeowners, as well as our timber and tourism industries, benefit from this program,” Leonhardt said. “Without control measures, our water quality, recreation experiences, wildlife habitat and timber production could all be negatively impacted.”
WVDA officials caution against the transport of firewood into or out of the state. Owners of RVs and campers are asked to thoroughly inspect and wash their equipment before moving it.
If there are any concerns, please contact Quentin “Butch” Sayers, Assistant Director or G. Scott Hoffman, GMCS Coordinator at 304-788-1066 or via e-mail to ghoffman@wvda.us.
Comments
rewrite:
The West Virginia Department of Agriculture (WVDA) has announced the forthcoming commencement of aerial treatment operations targeting the gypsy moth (*Lymantria dispar*), scheduled to initiate in early May. These suppression activities are planned for approximately 5,298 acres across Grant, Hardy, Nicholas, and Pendleton counties. The objective is to mitigate the detrimental impacts of this defoliator on the state’s forest ecosystems. This intervention is conducted under the auspices of the WVDA Cooperative State-County-Landowner (CSCL) suppression program.

Commissioner of Agriculture Kent Leonhardt emphasized the severity of the threat, stating, “The gypsy moth represents the most serious extant forest pest in West Virginia. As a non-native, invasive insect, it feeds on over 300 species of trees and shrubs, including ecologically and economically vital West Virginia hardwoods.” He further noted that defoliation by gypsy moth caterpillars can cause direct tree mortality or significantly weaken specimens, thereby increasing their susceptibility to secondary pests and pathogens.

Participation in the CSCL Program requires landowners to execute a contract, provide a deposit, and share the final treatment cost with the WVDA. Participants subsequently select the approved spray material for application on their property, with the 2018 options being Foray 48B (Btk) or Mimic (Tebufenozide). Eligibility for treatment on non-residential forested lands is contingent upon a minimum egg mass density of 500 per acre.

Commissioner Leonhardt underscored the program’s broader significance: “This treatment initiative serves as a safeguard for a critical natural resource. It confers benefits to homeowners, as well as to the timber and tourism sectors.” He warned that absent such control measures, negative repercussions could extend to water quality, recreational opportunities, wildlife habitat, and timber production.

The WVDA also advises the public to refrain from transporting firewood into or out of the state and recommends that owners of recreational vehicles and campers thoroughly inspect and clean their equipment prior to relocation.

For inquiries or concerns, individuals may contact Quentin “Butch” Sayers, Assistant Director, or G. Scott Hoffman, Gypsy Moth Control Program Coordinator, at 304-788-1066 or via email at ghoffman@wvda.us.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry has addressed the recently released US Nuclear Posture Review, which designates Iran, China, Russia and North Korea as potential threats to US national security.
In the Nuclear Posture Review (NPR), released on February 2, 2018, US President Trump has delineated the country's stance on nuclear weapons: in general, the president decided to follow Obama's plan for modernizing the country's nuclear arsenal in three directions: new bomber aircraft, submarines and land-based missiles.
Commenting on the document, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif described the possible consequences it might bring to the world.
The US Nuclear Posture Review reflects greater reliance on nukes in violation of the #NPT, bringing humankind closer to annihilation. No wonder the Doomsday Clock is at its most dangerous since 1953. Trump’s obduracy in killing the #JCPOA stems from the same dangerous imprudence. — Javad Zarif (@JZarif) 3 февраля 2018 г.
According to how the document depicts Iranian policy in the Middle East, the country views US influence in the region as a threat to its goal to become the dominant regional power. The NPR speculates that Iran continues to fund the largest missile program in the Middle East and could, in the future, threaten or deliver weapons, developing increasingly long-range ballistic missile capabilities, and pursuing its alleged "aggressive efforts" to undermine neighboring governments, casting doubt on its "long-term commitment to foregoing nuclear weapons capability."

Commenting on Washington's position, the minister described it as "ignorance of Iran and the region".
Trump again confirms his ignorance of Iran & region. Everyone knows where he stands; and it's certainly not with Iranians. His 'virtuous', ‘democratically- elected' clients in our region may cheer, but not those on receiving end of their tyranny & weapons, incl Yemeni children. — Javad Zarif (@JZarif) 31 января 2018 г.​
US nuclear forces are said to contribute to the "deterrence of nuclear and non-nuclear attack," "assurance of allies and partners," "achievement of US objectives if deterrence fails," and "capacity to hedge against an uncertain future." The Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has issued a formal response to the recently published United States Nuclear Posture Review (NPR), a document which identifies Iran, alongside China, Russia, and North Korea, as a potential threat to U.S. national security. Released on February 2, 2018, under the administration of President Donald Trump, the NPR outlines the strategic direction for the nation’s nuclear weapons policy. In broad terms, the review commits to continuing the modernization program for the U.S. nuclear arsenal initiated under the previous administration, focusing on three primary delivery systems: new strategic bomber aircraft, ballistic missile submarines, and intercontinental ballistic missiles.

In his commentary on the document, Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif articulated concerns regarding its global implications. Through a statement posted on the social media platform Twitter on February 3, 2018, Minister Zarif contended that the U.S. Nuclear Posture Review indicates a heightened and unlawful dependence on nuclear arms in violation of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), thereby advancing humanity closer to potential catastrophe. He noted that this posture is reflected in the setting of the Doomsday Clock at its most perilous position since 1953. Zarif further asserted that President Trump’s determination to abrogate the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) originates from the same perilous lack of judgment.

The NPR itself characterizes Iranian foreign policy in the Middle East as perceiving U.S. influence as an obstacle to its own regional hegemony. It posits that Iran maintains the most extensive missile program in the region and may, in future contingencies, utilize or threaten to employ such systems. The document suggests Iran is advancing its long-range ballistic missile capabilities and engaging in what it terms "aggressive efforts" to destabilize neighboring governments, thereby raising questions regarding its "long-term commitment to foregoing nuclear weapons capability."

In a separate critique of Washington’s stance, issued via Twitter on January 31, 2018, Foreign Minister Zarif described the U.S. position as demonstrating "ignorance of Iran and the region." He argued that while certain regional allies of the United States might endorse this posture, it is not aligned with the interests of the Iranian people or those suffering from regional conflicts, explicitly mentioning Yemeni children.

Conversely, the U.S. Nuclear Posture Review frames its nuclear forces as essential for multiple strategic objectives: deterring nuclear and non-nuclear attacks, assuring allies and partners, achieving U.S. aims should deterrence fail, and providing a hedge against an uncertain future. This rationale was echoed by then-Secretary of Defense James Mattis, who stated that a credible nuclear deterrent exists to prevent a war that can never be won from ever being fought.

SAN DIEGO – Leaders of a plan to erect industrial-sized tents to house San Diego’s burgeoning homeless population announced Monday that more than 200 people have endorsed the proposal, including many civic leaders.
Peter Seidler, part of the Padres ownership team, and restaurateur Dan Shea describe their plan as a bridge to the “Housing First” model being adopted across the country to address the homelessness problem.
In Housing First, the homeless not only get off the streets but are also provided necessary social services like substance abuse treatment, health care and job counseling.
Seidler and Shea first announced their plan last month. Among those announcing their backing of the proposal were philanthropist Malin Burnham, San Diego Regional Economic Development Corp. President and CEO Mark Cafferty, developer Doug Manchester and Kris Michell, who heads the Downtown San Diego Partnership.
Rep. Scott Peters, D-San Diego, and county Supervisor Ron Roberts also signed on to the plan.
In January’s annual tally of the area’s transient population, 5,619 homeless individuals were counted in the city of San Diego, a 10.3 percent increase from last year. Of those, 3,231 were living on the streets.
City and county officials have responded recently with a series of proposals on how to address both homelessness and a lack of affordable housing.
The city of San Diego funded a cold-weather shelter in a tented structure in Barrio Logan for around 30 years. It was shut down for the last time two years ago in favor of a permanent facility run by Father Joe’s Villages.
rewrite:
In San Diego, proponents of a proposal to construct large-scale industrial tents as shelter for the city's expanding homeless population reported on Monday that the initiative has garnered the endorsement of over two hundred individuals, among them numerous prominent civic figures. The plan, introduced last month by Peter Seidler, a member of the Padres ownership group, and restaurateur Dan Shea, is characterized by its architects as an interim measure bridging toward the nationally recognized "Housing First" model. This model prioritizes providing unhoused individuals with immediate stable housing coupled with comprehensive support services, including substance abuse treatment, healthcare, and employment counseling.

The list of declared supporters includes philanthropist Malin Burnham, San Diego Regional Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Mark Cafferty, developer Doug Manchester, and Kris Michell, President and CEO of the Downtown San Diego Partnership. Additionally, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (D-San Diego) and County Supervisor Ron Roberts have endorsed the proposal.

This initiative emerges against a backdrop of increasing need. The January point-in-time count identified 5,619 homeless individuals within the city of San Diego, reflecting a 10.3 percent increase from the previous year, with 3,231 of those individuals unsheltered. In response, municipal and county officials have recently advanced various proposals aimed at addressing both homelessness and the affordable housing shortage. Historically, the city operated a seasonal cold-weather shelter in a tented structure in Barrio Logan for approximately three decades; this facility was permanently closed two years ago following the establishment of a permanent shelter operated by Father Joe’s Villages.

In a rather shocking development, the Supreme Court recently pulled up Tamil star Rajinikanth's wife Latha for failing to pay the Rs 6.20 Crore she owes a noted advertising company. While rebuking the former playback singer, the Supreme Court also asked her to either clear her dues or face trial. The SC has given her nearly a week to make it clear whether she plans to clear the dues. The advertising firm was associated with the highly ambitious 2014 release Kochadaiiyaan and had given nearly Rs 10 Crore to Latha's company.
The lady's company was supposed to refund the amount and pay an additional Rs 1.2 Crore as 'guaranteed profit'.
Latha's troubles started when a trial court asked the Police to look into the matter. In 2016, the Karnataka High Court quashed the order. Following this, the advertising company approached the Supreme Court. Earlier this year, the 'apex court' made it clear that she would have to clear the dues.
In case you did not know, Kochadaiiyaan was directed by Soundarya Rajinikanth and marked her directorial debut. Shot using motion capture technology, it featured Rajinikanth and Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone in the lead. The supporting cast featured names such as Jackie Shroff, Nassar and R Sarathkumar. Released on May 23, 2014, it opened to a good response at the box office but ultimately failed to live up to the expectations. Its distributors suffered losses and this proved to be an embarrassment for 'Thalaiva'.
Interestingly, this controversy involving Latha comes at a time when the Superstar is busy with his political commitments. On the film front, he currently has 2.0 and a film with Karthik Subbaraj in his kitty. 2.0 is a Shankar directorial and will see Rajini reprise his Chitti character from the 2010 hit Enthiran. Recently, it was reported that the makers of 2.0 are in a fix because of the unsatisfactory performance of Kaala. As such, it is not very clear when the sci-fi thriller will ultimately hit the screens.
rewrite:
In a significant legal development, the Supreme Court of India has issued a stern admonition to Mrs. Latha Rajinikanth, spouse of prominent Tamil film actor Rajinikanth, for her failure to settle a debt of ₹6.20 crore owed to a prominent advertising firm. The court explicitly directed her to either discharge the outstanding amount or face criminal proceedings, granting a period of approximately one week to declare her intention regarding the repayment. This financial obligation originates from an agreement associated with the 2014 film *Kochadaiiyaan*, for which the advertising company had advanced approximately ₹10 crore to a firm owned by Mrs. Rajinikanth. The contractual terms stipulated that her company was to refund this sum along with an additional ₹1.2 crore designated as a 'guaranteed profit'.

The litigation commenced following a trial court order directing police investigation into the matter, which was subsequently quashed by the Karnataka High Court in 2016. The aggrieved advertising firm then petitioned the Supreme Court, which earlier this year upheld the liability, mandating the clearance of dues. The film in question, *Kochadaiiyaan*, marked the directorial debut of Soundarya Rajinikanth. Utilizing motion capture technology, it featured Rajinikanth and Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone in lead roles, with a supporting cast including Jackie Shroff, Nassar, and R. Sarathkumar. Released on 23 May 2014, the film initially garnered a positive box office response but ultimately underperformed relative to expectations, resulting in financial losses for its distributors and considerable professional embarrassment for Rajinikanth.

This legal controversy emerges concurrently with Rajinikanth's active engagement in political commitments. Regarding his cinematic projects, he is currently associated with two films: *2.0*, a science-fiction thriller directed by Shankar in which he reprises his role as Chitti from the 2010 film *Enthiran*, and an untitled project with director Karthik Subbaraj. The release schedule for *2.0* has reportedly become uncertain due to the underwhelming commercial performance of his recent film *Kaala*, leaving its theatrical debut date indeterminate.

Can't work out what to watch on Netflix UK? Not sure what's new to the service or where to find the best box sets on Netflix?
Well, hopefully this updated guide to the best TV shows available right now should be a good start.
From top Netflix original series like Stranger Things and House of Cards, great British dramas like Sherlock, Doctor Who and Peaky Blinders to brilliant US and UK comedy, here are the best TV shows to watch on Netflix right now.
And if you still can't work out what to watch, why not check out our guide to the Top 50 Netflix movies available now?
There's a reason why everyone's talking about it; this brilliantly scary horror series following four normal 1980s kids and one telekinetic super-girl is packed with heart. And an inter-dimensional monster that walks through walls. Oh, and an unmissable soundtrack too. Just watch it.
This Cillian Murphy-starring crime epic has won acclaim all over the world, with everyone from Tom Cruise to the late David Bowie singing its praises. That's quite a broad fanbase, but the Brummie-based 1920s gang series really does have something for everyone. Sharp suits, sharper razor blades, and performances that cut through all the usual bingewatching dross.
The series follows naïve, middle-class Piper Kerman (Taylor Schilling) as she embarked on a 15-month sentence. With its brilliant ensemble cast of strong, funny and racially diverse women, the four seasons of Orange contradict every "women behind bars" stereotype.

It all began here as when a charismatic cop (Lennie James) found himself under investigation by anti-corruption officers. New investigations come every series, with the threads all coming together at the climax of series three. Unmissable British crime.
Gavin & Stacey co-creator and Late Late Show host James Corden proves he still has a gift for narrative comedy alongside breakout star Mathew Baynton. rewrite:
For viewers seeking guidance on programming selections within the Netflix UK library, particularly regarding new additions or curated recommendations, this updated guide to currently available television series serves as a substantive starting point. It encompasses a broad spectrum of content, from acclaimed Netflix original productions such as *Stranger Things* and *House of Cards*, to esteemed British dramas including *Sherlock*, *Doctor Who*, and *Peaky Blinders*, alongside distinguished comedy series from both the United States and the United Kingdom. Should further assistance be required in selecting content, a complementary guide to the top fifty films currently available on the platform is also recommended.

This critically lauded horror series, which follows a group of adolescents and a psychokinetic girl in the 1980s, skillfully combines genuine emotional resonance with supernatural terror, notably featuring a trans-dimensional entity. Its period-specific soundtrack further enhances the atmospheric narrative, solidifying its status as essential viewing.

Across its four seasons, the series utilizes a skilled ensemble cast of diverse, complex female characters to effectively subvert the entrenched stereotypes commonly associated with the women-in-prison genre.

The narrative foundation is established with the investigation of a charismatic police officer (Lennie James) by an anti-corruption unit. In *The Wrong Mans*, James Corden—co-creator of *Gavin & Stacey* and television host—alongside Mathew Baynton, demonstrates a sustained aptitude for narrative comedy. The series transcends the situational comedy format to function as a full-scale comedic thriller, depicting its protagonists as ordinary individuals inadvertently entangled in a criminal and espionage conspiracy.

Without Thomas Szajko’s testimony, alleged shooter Afshin Ighani could get off on that charge
Afshin Maleki Ighani, 45, was arrested in April in Princeton and is facing several charges including attempted murder in connection to a shooting that took place in Oliver. Ighani could get off on the charges, after the alleged shooting victim died last week. (Western News file photo)
A man accused of an April crime spree in the South Okanagan and Similkameen areas may get off on allegedly shooting an Oliver man, after the key witness died last week.
Afshin Maleki Ighani is accused of shooting Thomas Szajko in Oliver on Apr. 19 this year, and has been going through the court system, leading up to a trial on the matters. But Szajko was the Crown’s key witness on that matter, and he died in his home on Dec. 1 of unspecified causes.
Related: Oliver shooting victim reportedly dies months later
Asked how the trial could go forward without testimony of Szajko, Crown lawyer John Swanson only said “That’s a problem.”
Though Szajko may have made a statement to the police, no testimony would mean the defence has no opportunity to cross-examine Szajko.
Swanson said he is working with police to review evidence and attempt to build up the case without testimony from Szajko.
“We’re working on it,” he said in a brief interview with the Western News.
Related: Alleged Oliver shooter elects trial by judge
Though Ighani may get off without a trial on that matter, he will still need to stand trial over the alleged kidnapping of a woman later that week, as police entered a regional manhunt for him.
Police had surrounded an RV they believed Ighani to be living in at Szajko’s property on the evening of Apr. 19, but after entering the vehicle did not find Ighani.
Later that week, police received reports of a man having kicked another man out of a vehicle and taking a woman with him, leading the police to the Similkameen Valley.
Related: RCMP hunt for alleged shooter
Ighani was later found in a mobile home park in Princeton, where he was arrested and charged on all alleged incidents.
Ighani’s next court appearance is set for Dec. 18 for a preliminary inquiry.
@dustinrgodfrey
dustin.godfrey@pentictonwesternnews.com
Like us on Facebook and follow us on Twitter.
rewrite:
The potential exists for the charges pertaining to an alleged shooting to be dismissed against Afshin Maleki Ighani, following the death of the key witness. Ighani, aged 45, was arrested in Princeton in April and faces multiple charges, including attempted murder, in connection with a shooting incident that occurred in Oliver on April 19. The Crown’s case has been significantly compromised by the death of the alleged victim, Thomas Szajko, at his residence on December 1 from unspecified causes. As Szajko was the primary witness for the prosecution, his absence presents a substantial obstacle to proceeding with a trial on the shooting allegation.

When questioned regarding the feasibility of a trial without Szajko’s testimony, Crown counsel John Swanson acknowledged the difficulty, stating, “That’s a problem.” While Szajko may have provided an initial statement to law enforcement, the inability to present him for cross-examination by the defense fundamentally weakens the evidentiary basis for the charge. Swanson indicated that the Crown is collaborating with police to reassess the available evidence in an effort to construct a viable case absent the witness’s direct testimony, noting, “We’re working on it.”

Notwithstanding the potential dismissal of the shooting charge, Ighani remains subject to judicial proceedings for other alleged offenses. He is scheduled to stand trial for the alleged kidnapping of a woman, which occurred in the days following the Oliver incident. This event precipitated an extensive regional search by police. Initial efforts to apprehend Ighani on the evening of April 19, involving the containment of a recreational vehicle on Szajko’s property, were unsuccessful. Subsequent reports later that week described a man forcibly ejecting another individual from a vehicle and abducting a female passenger, directing police attention to the Similkameen Valley. The investigation culminated in Ighani’s arrest at a mobile home park in Princeton, where he was charged in relation to all alleged incidents.

A preliminary inquiry for Ighani is scheduled for December 18. The progression of the shooting charge, however, is now contingent upon the Crown’s capacity to substantiate its case through evidence independent of the deceased witness’s account.

A teenager was rescued from train tracks after he fell following a night out in Lancashire, say police.
Concerned family members contacted the police after he was discovered on the tracks by Nancy Street in Darwen at around 2.30am on Monday.
The 18-year-old was rescued by fire services and taken to hospital with a serious head injury.
A police spokesman said: "It seems a lad coming home from a night out has fallen from a railway bridge onto tracks.
"We had a call from a concerned family member who had gone to collect him. He was then found on the tracks.
"The lad was rescued by firefighters and taken to hospital.
"He is believed to have fractured his skull, but is conscious, breathing and talking.
"The lad had been out for quite a while on a very cold night by the time he was found so there were some initial concerns.
"But the fire service and paramedics came out quickly and although it was a serious injury, he was obviously a lot better when he was found."
The teenager remains in hospital in what is believed to be a none life threatening condition.
rewrite:
An eighteen-year-old male was successfully extracted from railway tracks in Darwen, Lancashire, in the early hours of Monday morning, following an apparent fall from a railway bridge. According to police reports, the incident occurred after the individual had been socializing during the evening. A concerned family member, who had arrived to collect him, discovered him on the tracks near Nancy Street at approximately 02:30 and subsequently alerted authorities. Emergency services, including the fire brigade and paramedics, responded promptly to the scene.

The individual sustained a serious head injury, preliminarily assessed as a skull fracture, and was transported to a hospital for treatment. Police indicated that, given the extended duration of exposure to cold nighttime temperatures prior to his discovery, there were initial welfare concerns. However, upon arrival, emergency personnel found the patient to be conscious, breathing, and communicative. His condition, while serious, was subsequently described as non-life-threatening. He remains hospitalized for further observation and care.

* India imposes tax after 4-mth gap -govt sources
* Some had expected tariff of as much as 25 pct
* Country is world's No.2 wheat producer
* Also brings in import tax on variety of pulse
NEW DELHI, March 28 India on Tuesday imposed a 10 percent import tax on wheat with immediate effect, government sources said, reinstating the tariff after a gap of nearly four months that saw large overseas purchases.
The government wants to curb imports when Indian farmers are starting to harvest their crops, said three sources directly involved in deciding on the issue. They declined to be identified as they were not authorised to speak on the matter.
Earlier this month, government sources had said New Delhi could impose a 25 percent import tax on wheat.
India, the world's second-biggest wheat producer, lowered the import tax wheat to 10 percent from 25 percent last September and scrapped the duty on Dec. 8.
On Tuesday, the government also imposed a 10 percent tax on Tur, a variety of pulse, after a crash in local prices.
Waves of farmers have stepped up local production of pulses to help the government cut a hefty import bill.
The permission for duty-free imports had encouraged private traders to buy more than 5 million tonnes of wheat since mid-2016 to meet a supply shortfall left by two years of drought.
Most flour millers and biscuit makers imported wheat from France, Ukraine and Australia.
Both large imports and forecasts of a bumper crop prompted the government to impose the tax, the sources said.
The farm ministry last month forecast wheat output at 96.64 million tonnes in 2017, up from 92.29 million tonnes last year. (Reporting by Mayank Bhardwaj; Editing by Joseph Radford)
rewrite:
On March 28, the Government of India reinstated a 10 percent import tariff on wheat with immediate effect, according to official sources. This decision concludes a duty-free period of nearly four months, during which significant volumes of wheat were procured from international markets. The primary objective of the tariff is to regulate import levels coinciding with the commencement of the domestic harvest season, as stated by three government sources directly involved in the policy decision. These individuals requested anonymity, as they were not authorized to speak publicly on the matter.

This reinstated duty is notably lower than the 25 percent rate that some officials had indicated earlier in the month as a potential measure. India, ranking as the world's second-largest wheat producer, had originally reduced the import levy from 25 percent to 10 percent in September of the previous year before eliminating it entirely on December 8. Concurrently, the government imposed a 10 percent import duty on Tur, a specific variety of pulse, in response to a decline in local market prices. Increased domestic cultivation of pulses, encouraged to reduce a substantial import bill, had contributed to this price decrease.

The interim duty-free regime had facilitated private traders in importing over 5 million tonnes of wheat since mid-2016 to address supply deficits resulting from consecutive drought years. Primary importers, including flour millers and biscuit manufacturers, sourced this wheat largely from France, Ukraine, and Australia. Government sources cited the combination of these substantial imports and projections of a robust domestic harvest as key factors prompting the tariff's reintroduction. The Ministry of Agriculture forecasted a 2017 wheat output of 96.64 million tonnes, an increase from the 92.29 million tonnes produced the previous year.

AS THE populations of Australia's big cities soar, the number of people calling Bundaberg home rose by 405 people in the year to June 2017, new figures show.
And the growth comes on the back of a big increase in overseas migrants to the Rum City.
For the first time the Australian Bureau of Statistics yesterday released data showing the components driving population change in Australia's capital cities and regions.
These showed without overseas people moving here, population growth would have been relatively stagnant - a net increase of just 13.
Bundaberg's natural increase, births minus deaths, was 96, much lower than neighbouring Gladstone which recorded more than 600.
However, 1090 people left Gladstone in the year from June 2016, compared to just 83 in the Rum Capital.
The net total of 392 new overseas migrants delivered the bulk of the population's 405 new residents and took Bundaberg's total to 94,858. This is 9140 less than Fraser Coast's population.
A spokesman for the bureau said for the purposes of the report, the numbers didn't include backpackers and only those who had, or planned to live in the community for more than a year were counted.
Ratsel Sanderson, 34, moved to Bundaberg from the Philippines four years ago and plans to raise a family here.
She lives with her Australian husband, who she met online. They now have a six-month-old son Jacob (pictured).
Ms Sanderson said she loved the quiet nature of Bundaberg and that the lifestyle was so "easy going”.
"At the moment I am happy,” she said.
"I used to work at the Coffee Club before I had my baby. Now I am a stay-at-home mum.”
She migrated alone, but had met a lot of people who speak the language from her hometown area.
And while people are migrating from overseas to Bundaberg, the numbers are nowhere near as big as the big cities.
Together, Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane accounted for more than 70 per cent of Australia's population growth in 2016-17.
In Melbourne, net overseas migration was the major contributor to population growth, adding 80,000 people.
Natural increase contributed 29 per cent, while net internal migration accounted for 7.3 per cent of population growth.
rewrite:
Recent demographic data reveals that while Australia's major metropolitan centers continue to experience substantial population expansion, regional areas such as Bundaberg also recorded growth. In the period concluding June 2017, Bundaberg’s population increased by 405 individuals, reaching a total of 94,858. This growth is primarily attributable to net overseas migration, which contributed 392 new residents. In contrast, natural increase—calculated as births minus deaths—accounted for only 96 persons, a figure notably lower than that of the adjacent Gladstone region, which recorded over 600. However, Gladstone experienced a significant net loss of 1,090 persons through internal migration during the same interval, compared to a minimal outflow of 83 from Bundaberg. Without the influx of international migrants, Bundaberg’s population growth would have been relatively stagnant, with a net increase of merely 13 persons.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics recently disseminated, for the first time, detailed components of population change for both capital cities and regional areas. According to a bureau spokesperson, these estimates exclude transient populations such as backpackers, counting only individuals who have established, or intend to establish, residence for a minimum of twelve months. The data underscore that overseas migration is a dominant driver of national demographic trends. Collectively, Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane accounted for over seventy percent of Australia’s population growth in 2016–17. In Melbourne specifically, net overseas migration was the predominant contributor, adding 80,000 persons, whereas natural increase constituted 29 percent and net internal migration 7.3 percent of growth.

While Bundaberg’s migration figures are modest relative to these major capitals, the impact on the community is tangible. Illustrative of this trend is the case of Ratsel Sanderson, a 34-year-old migrant from the Philippines who relocated to Bundaberg four years ago. Now residing with her Australian husband, whom she met online, and their six-month-old son, Ms. Sanderson expresses appreciation for the region’s tranquil and easygoing lifestyle. Although she initially migrated alone, she has since connected with others from her linguistic and regional background. Her experience, transitioning from employment at a local café to being a stay-at-home parent, reflects the personal dimensions underlying the statistical narrative of regional population change.

input: The beta releases are available today of Wayland 1.15 and the Weston 4.0 reference compositor. Wayland 1.15 is another relatively modest cycle. Wayland 1.15 pulls in libwayland-egl where as before that library was part of Mesa, making some semantics of Wayland more clear in the documentation, improvements to wayland-scanner, and some minor API additions.The Wayland 1.15 Beta release today has mostly wayland-egl fixes along with some other very minor alterations.Weston 4.0 Beta is out today and as usual that compositor-side work is much more exciting. Weston 4.0 will have initial support for atomic mode-setting, initial support for the input-timestamps protocol, dropping of the older XDG-Shell v5, and a variety of other feature additions/improvements and bug fixes.The Weston 4.0 Beta brings support for its OpenGL renderer to create high priority contexts support for GPUs , various DRM compositor fixes, support for multiple back-ends with simple-dmabuf-drm, and other minor fixes/improvements.More details on the Wayland mailing list . The stable Wayland 1.15.0 / Weston 4.0.0 releases are expected in April.
rewrite:
Beta releases of Wayland 1.15 and the Weston 4.0 reference compositor are now available. Wayland 1.15 represents a relatively modest development cycle. Its primary changes include the integration of libwayland-egl, which was previously part of Mesa, thereby clarifying certain semantic details within the documentation. Additional updates encompass improvements to the wayland-scanner utility and minor API additions. The current beta release focuses predominantly on wayland-egl corrections alongside other minimal alterations.

Conversely, the Weston 4.0 beta introduces more substantial compositor-side developments. Notable features comprise initial support for atomic mode-setting and the input-timestamps protocol, the deprecation of the legacy XDG-Shell v5 interface, and various other enhancements and bug resolutions. This beta also enables the OpenGL renderer to establish high-priority GPU contexts, includes multiple DRM compositor fixes, and supports multiple back-ends via simple-dmabuf-drm, among other minor refinements. Further details are accessible through the Wayland mailing list. The stable releases of Wayland 1.15.0 and Weston 4.0.0 are anticipated in April.

Staff and volunteers at a Borders school are celebrating after being recognised for their efforts to give youngsters a sporting chance.
Denholm Primary School has been given a prestigious national award for innovation and achievement in delivering physical education and extra-curricular sport.
Euan Amos at Denholm Primary School.
It has been handed a Sportscotland silver school sport award for its commitment to engaging all pupils in sporting activity.
Funded by the National Lottery, the award is a nationwide initiative intended to encourage schools to continuously improve physical education and sport.
The award also encourages sporting links between schools and the communities around them.
Stewart Harris, chief executive of Sportscotland, said: “Congratulations to all the staff and pupils at Denholm Primary School.
“They should be extremely proud of this fantastic achievement.
“Not only have they put physical education and sport at the heart of their school and local community, but they have managed to do so in a way that encourages all pupils to engage in physical activity whilst having fun at the same time.
“Sportscotland is committed to building a world-class sporting system for everyone, and a crucial part of that is putting young people at the heart.
“Working with our partners in local authorities and governing bodies of sport, we are creating closer links between physical education, school sport and club sport, which benefits young people by providing more and better opportunities to take part in sport.” With more applications than ever before, there are currently 212 Sportscotland gold award schools, 336 silver ones and 84 given bronze.
Morag McCreadie, headteacher at Denholm Primary, said the award was an honour, adding: “Our staff work incredibly hard to deliver a variety of sports across the year and to all stages in the school. We believe that physical education, physical activity and sport are important factors in the school curriculum, and without our committed staff and volunteer coaches working alongside sports specialists, it would not be possible to achieve as we do.”
rewrite:

The school has received a prestigious national accolade, the Sportscotland Silver School Sport Award, in acknowledgement of its innovation and achievement in delivering physical education and extracurricular sporting programmes. This award, funded by the National Lottery, forms part of a nationwide initiative designed to encourage schools to pursue continuous improvement in physical education and sport, while also fostering stronger sporting links between schools and their surrounding communities.

Stewart Harris, Chief Executive of Sportscotland, extended his congratulations, stating: “All staff and pupils at Denholm Primary School should be extremely proud of this accomplishment. They have successfully positioned physical education and sport at the heart of the school and local community, achieving this in a manner that engages every pupil in physical activity in an enjoyable way. Sportscotland is committed to developing a world-class sporting system for all, with young people central to this vision. By collaborating with partners in local authorities and sports governing bodies, we are strengthening the connections between physical education, school sport, and community club sport. This integrated approach benefits young people by expanding and enhancing their opportunities for participation.” Currently, the award scheme includes 212 gold, 336 silver, and 84 bronze recipients, reflecting a high level of engagement from schools across Scotland.

Morag McCreadie, Headteacher at Denholm Primary, described the award as an honour. She emphasised: “Our staff work diligently to provide a diverse range of sports throughout the year to all pupil stages. We consider physical education, physical activity, and sport to be vital components of the school curriculum. This achievement would not be possible without the commitment of our staff and volunteer coaches, who work in partnership with sports specialists to deliver these programmes effectively.”

A man was taken to hospital after being assaulted on a Dundee street by two men — who then fled in a taxi.
Emergency services, including police and an ambulance, were called to Lochee High Street around 6.30pm on Thursday.
The victim, who suffered facial injuries, was taken to Ninewells Hospital after the attack, which happened near the Farmfoods store.
Police have now launched an investigation into the incident, after which the attackers left in a taxi.
A Police Scotland spokesman said: “Police Scotland is following positive lines of inquiry after a man was assaulted by two other men in Lochee High Street around 6.30pm on Thursday.
“It is understood the men then left the area in a taxi.
“The victim was taken to Ninewells Hospital where he was treated for facial injuries.”
The spokesman added: “Inquiries are ongoing and anyone with information relating to the incident is asked to call 101 or speak to any police officer. Quote the reference number CR/20909/17.”
Ann Marie Allan, 58, of Kelly’s Bar, said she saw the police and ambulance coming up the street.
She said: “Apparently the guy was lying out on the street before a girl called for them.
“From what we heard, there was quite a lot of blood but we didn’t see exactly.
“There had supposedly been folk arguing out there for most of the day before that.
“The police were there for quite a few hours after it happened.”
A Scottish Ambulance Service spokesman said: “We received a call at 6.38pm on Thursday August 10 to attend an incident on High Street.
“We dispatched one ambulance to the scene.
“One male patient in his 30s was taken to Ninewells Hospital.”
rewrite:
On the evening of Thursday, August 10, a male individual was assaulted by two men on Lochee High Street in Dundee. The incident, which occurred in the vicinity of a Farmfoods retail outlet at approximately 6:30 p.m., resulted in the victim sustaining facial injuries. Following the assault, the perpetrators departed the scene via taxi. Emergency services, including Police Scotland and the Scottish Ambulance Service, were alerted. According to an ambulance service spokesperson, a call was received at 6:38 p.m., prompting the dispatch of one ambulance to the location. The male victim, reported to be in his thirties, was subsequently transported to Ninewells Hospital for medical treatment.

Police Scotland have initiated a formal investigation into the assault. A police spokesperson confirmed that positive lines of inquiry are being pursued and appealed to the public for information, requesting that any witnesses contact the police via the non-emergency number 101, quoting reference CR/20909/17. Local accounts provided additional context. Ann Marie Allan, a 58-year-old resident of the area, reported observing the arrival of emergency services. She indicated that, according to local reports, the victim was lying on the street prior to assistance being summoned, and that a significant amount of blood was present. Allan further noted that there had reportedly been ongoing disputes in the area for much of that day and that police remained at the scene for several hours following the incident.

In his multibook series They Drew as They Pleased: The Hidden Art of Disney’s Late Golden Age, Disney historian Didier Ghez has performed his own Indiana Jones act, delving into the recesses of the Mouse House’s storied animation archives to unearth the rarest of cinematic treasures. With the third volume coming out next week, Ghez gave Yahoo Entertainment a sneak preview of his archaeology, stunning artwork created for Disney features and shorts in the 1940s, including such masterpieces as Dumbo, Fantasia, Bambi, and Alice in Wonderland.
“Half of the pieces in the book come from the Disney vault and half from the collection of the families of Disney artists. More than 90 percent of them had never been seen before in book form,” Ghez says. “Most of them had not been seen by anyone outside of the Disney Studio in more than 75 years.
“Rescuing these pieces of art created by some of the most talented artists of the 20th century is immensely rewarding.”
Contained here are illustrations for “The Mouse’s Tale,” a scene from Dumbo that was ultimately cut from the film, as well as the image Ghez calls “the most exceptional document featured in the book.” Click through to see.
They Drew as They Pleased: The Hidden Art of Disney’s Late Golden Age: The 1940s — Part Two (Chronicle Books, $45) will be available on Oct. 10.
rewrite:

With the third volume scheduled for release next week, Ghez provided Yahoo Entertainment with an exclusive preview of his findings, showcasing previously unpublished artwork developed for Disney features and short films during the 1940s. This collection includes material related to such canonical works as *Dumbo*, *Fantasia*, *Bambi*, and *Alice in Wonderland*.

Ghez notes that approximately half of the artworks featured in the volume originate from the Disney archives, while the remainder are drawn from the private collections of Disney artists' families. He emphasizes that over ninety percent of these pieces have never been reproduced in book form, and most have remained unseen by anyone outside the Disney Studio for more than seventy-five years. “The recovery of these artworks, created by some of the most talented artists of the twentieth century, is immensely rewarding,” Ghez states.

Among the highlights is concept art for a deleted sequence from *Dumbo* titled “The Mouse’s Tale,” alongside an image Ghez describes as “the most exceptional document featured in the book.” *They Drew as They Pleased: The Hidden Art of Disney’s Late Golden Age: The 1940s — Part Two* (Chronicle Books, $45) will be available on October 10.

MOUNT PLEASANT, S.C. (AP) — It wasn’t the Easter bunny that startled a South Carolina homeowner and his family. It wasn’t even a burglar.
The Post and Courier of Charleston reports Susie and Steve Polston were worried that someone was trying to get into their home on Sunday. Instead, Polston’s 16-year-old son found the intruder: a nine-foot alligator crawling on their second-story porch.
The family says the alligator climbed a back stairwell to the porch, crunched through the aluminum screen door and nestled between a sofa and a swinging bench.
State law requires a nuisance-trapped alligator to be killed, but the family didn’t want that. The other choice was to wait it out, but the alligator was eventually euthanized.
Last year, an alligator rang a doorbell, while another fell asleep on a porch.

rewrite: In Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, a homeowner and his family experienced a disturbance originating not from a festive Easter visitor nor a criminal intruder. According to a report from *The Post and Courier* of Charleston, Susie and Steve Polston became concerned that an individual was attempting to enter their residence on Sunday. The source was identified by their sixteen-year-old son: a nine-foot alligator situated on their second-story porch. The reptile had ascended a rear stairwell, breached an aluminum screen door, and positioned itself between a sofa and a swinging bench. While state statute mandates the euthanization of nuisance alligators following capture—an outcome the family wished to avoid—the alternative of waiting was ultimately untenable, resulting in the animal's death. Such incidents are not unprecedented; in the prior year, an alligator was documented activating a doorbell, while another was found sleeping on a porch.

March 31 Australian shares were trading flat with a downward bias on Friday as basic material and financial stocks fell, but were still on track to log their best month since December.
The S&P/ASX 200 index was down 0.2 percent at 5,883.3 in lacklustre trading at 0101 GMT. The index is on track to log its best week since Nov. 25.
"It's the last day of the quarter. The market had a pretty strong rally yesterday and it's just repositioning today," said Bill Keenan, general manager equities and researcher at Lonsec. Miner BHP BIlliton lost 0.3 percent while gold miner Newcrest Mining declined 0.7 percent and was on track for a fourth straight session of losses. Dalian Commodity Exchange Iron ore futures erased gains on Thursday, while gold dipped as the dollar strengthened.
Financial stocks, which had been gaining for the past six sessions, fell on Friday with the 'Big 4' banks losing between 0.2 percent and 0.9 percent.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commision (ACCC) on Friday denied authorization for banks to collectively bargain with Apple and boycott Apple Pay.
Meanwhile, banking watchdog Australian Prudential Regulatory Authority said it would place limits on interest-only residential loans to reinforce sound mortgage lending practices in a hot property market.
Bendigo and Adelaide Bank, included in the ACCC report, was up 0.8 percent.
Energy stocks in the region fell with Woodside Petroleum Ltd losing 0.5 percent.
Among gainers, telecom and utility sectors rose as Telstra Corporation Ltd gained nearly one percent and AGL Energy Ltd added 1.8 percent.
New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index rose a marginal 14.61 points to 7,183.72 and was set for its fourth straight day of gains as consumer stocks rose.
Fletcher Building Ltd rose 0.8 percent, while a2 Milk Company Ltd added 1.4 percent. For more individual stocks activity click on (Reoprting by Susan Mathew in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Christina Martin; Editing by Vyas Mohan)

Rehabilitation of Kariba Dam is expected to start in May after Zimbabwe and Zambia signed off a $ 300 million financing deal with the European Union and World Bank.
The project, which is also being co-financed by the Swedish Government and African Development Bank (AfDB) through a mix of loans and grants, entails reshaping the plunge pool and refurbishment of the six spillway gates.

Happy Fourth of July! Celebrate Independence Day with this fruity star-spangled sangria from lifestyle blog Heart and Seam.
From fashion and beauty to wellness and recipes Heart and Seam founder Janet Cooke shares real-life experiences on her blog from her home in New Hampshire -- including her festive and tasty summer sangria recipe.
Heart and Seam Lifestyle Blog
"This is a fun festive spin on a classic sangria recipe," Cooke told "GMA." "The best part about this recipe is that you can make it in large batches so it's perfect for a Fourth of July cookout where there will be lots of family and friends to enjoy."
Check out the full recipe and pour this red, wine and blueberry beverage all day for friends and family.
Heart and Seam Lifestyle Blog
Ingredients
1 bottle red wine (I like Pinot Noir or Shiraz)
1-1/2 cups cranberry juice
1 cup brandy
juice from one large orange
2 cups fresh blueberries
8 ounces fresh strawberries cut in quarters
Club soda
Directions
To a large pitcher add wine, cranberry juice, brandy and orange juice.
Add blueberries and strawberries. Chill for a few hours.
To serve, fill glasses half full with ice and use a slotted spoon to add fruit from the pitcher to each glass. Pour liquid over ice and fruit, top with club soda and serve.
Tips
Add raspberries, blackberries and even apples to create even more of a festive drink.
Be sure to add the ice to the glasses and not the pitcher itself. You will dilute the sangria if you add directly to the pitcher.

This digital publication, founded by Janet Cooke from her residence in New Hampshire, disseminates content spanning fashion, beauty, wellness, and gastronomy, often reflecting personal narrative. The included sangria exemplifies this approach, offering a celebratory variation on a conventional formula.

Cooke characterized the recipe to "Good Morning America" as "a fun festive spin on a classic sangria," noting its particular suitability for social gatherings due to its scalability for large batches, thereby accommodating the typical convivial assembly of family and friends on the holiday. The complete instructions yield a red-hued beverage incorporating wine and blueberries.

The formulation requires one bottle of red wine, such as Pinot Noir or Shiraz, combined with one and one-half cups of cranberry juice, one cup of brandy, and the freshly squeezed juice of one large orange. Two cups of fresh blueberries and eight ounces of fresh strawberries, quartered, constitute the primary fruit components, with club soda added later for effervescence.

Preparation involves amalgamating the wine, cranberry juice, brandy, and orange juice in a large pitcher before introducing the blueberries and strawberries. The mixture should be refrigerated for several hours. For service, glasses are half-filled with ice, and fruit is allocated to each using a slotted spoon. The chilled liquid is then poured over the ice and fruit, finished with a topping of club soda.

Suggestions for adaptation include incorporating additional fruits such as raspberries, blackberries, or apples to enhance the festive quality. A critical procedural note advises adding ice solely to individual serving glasses rather than the central pitcher to prevent undesirable dilution of the sangria.

With summer here, chances are that you’ve probably spared a bit of thought for getting that sun-kissed, tanned look often associated with youth and vitality. The sad irony, of course, is that while we might associate suntanned skin with good health, prolonged sun exposure can lead to accelerated skin aging, as well as associated risks like skin cancer.
A new research project published in the journal Cell Reports suggests that things don’t have to remain that way, though. What scientists have discovered is a small molecule that may be able to stimulate the darkening of human skin, without exposing it to potentially harmful UV radiation. This involves inhibiting an enzyme called Salt Inducible Kinase (SIK), which naturally suppresses pigmentation. By inhibiting it, pigment synthesis is instead stimulated.
“Based upon human epidemiology which shows that darkly pigmented people are at significantly lower risk of developing skin cancer, as well as other indications of UV damage to skin, we suspect that the ability to stimulate pigment production [minus] use of damaging UV-rays, may provide the benefits without the damage from UV,” Dr. David Fisher of Massachusetts General Hospital, one of the researchers on the project, told Digital Trends. “In laboratory animals, it has been shown that UV-independent pigment darkening of redhaired mice does provide strong skin protection from UV. However, this has not yet been tested in humans. The current discovery will hopefully make it possible to test this [in people].”
Before this can be rolled out as a summer staple alongside beer coolers and barbecues, however, Fisher explains that it is important to first determine the safety or toxicity of the agent, in order to know how best to apply it to people. If the compounds are found to be safe, the researchers then hope to identify the population of people for whom such darkening would be most helpful, before carrying out initial clinical testing.
“We are currently in discussions with several potential partners for developing the approach toward clinical application,” Fisher said.
rewrite:
A common aspiration during the summer months is to achieve a sun-tanned complexion, which is frequently associated with perceptions of youth and vitality. However, a significant irony exists in this pursuit: while a tan is often mistakenly equated with robust health, prolonged exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation is a well-established cause of accelerated skin aging and a primary risk factor for skin cancer. Recent scientific investigation offers a potential avenue to decouple the desired pigmentation from its damaging cause. Research published in *Cell Reports* identifies a small molecule capable of stimulating cutaneous darkening in human skin without the need for exposure to harmful UV radiation.

The mechanistic basis for this effect involves the inhibition of an enzyme known as Salt Inducible Kinase (SIK), which normally functions to suppress melanin production. By pharmacologically inhibiting SIK, the pathway for pigment synthesis is activated. As explained by Dr. David Fisher of Massachusetts General Hospital, a co-author of the study, this approach is grounded in epidemiological evidence demonstrating that individuals with darker constitutive pigmentation exhibit significantly lower rates of skin cancer and other forms of UV-induced photodamage. The hypothesis, therefore, is that inducing pigmentation independently of UV exposure could confer protective benefits without the associated risks. Supporting this, preclinical studies in red-haired mouse models have shown that UV-independent pigment darkening provides substantial protection against subsequent UV damage. While this protective effect remains to be conclusively demonstrated in humans, the current discovery establishes a foundational tool for such testing.

Before any potential translation to human use, Dr. Fisher emphasizes the necessity of rigorous safety and toxicological profiling of the agent to determine appropriate application parameters. Following the establishment of safety, subsequent research steps would aim to identify candidate populations most likely to benefit from such an intervention, prior to initiating clinical trials. Fisher notes that discussions are currently underway with potential partners to advance this methodology toward clinical application.

Courtesy Columbia County Sheriff’s Office (NEW YORK) — A high school soccer coach who allegedly ran away with a 17-year-old girl is being extradited to Florida, an official told ABC News Monday.
Rian Rodriguez, 27, had been in custody in upstate Onondaga County, New York, on a Florida warrant for alleged custodial interference since 17-year-old Caitlyn Frisina was found safe in New York with him earlier this month. He’s now been released from the Onondaga County Jail to be extradited to Florida, where he lives, said Jon Seeber of the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office.
A spokesperson for the Columbia County Detention Facility in Florida confirmed to ABC News that Rodriguez is heading to the jail, but the spokesperson declined to say when he is expected to arrive due to security reasons.
Frisina was reported missing from her Florida home on Nov. 26, sparking a massive search. She and Rodriguez — a family friend and assistant soccer coach at the teen’s Florida high school — were found in a car together in Syracuse six days later.
Frisina has since been reunited with her parents.
Chuck Keller, the Syracuse-based attorney representing Rodriguez in New York, told ABC News last week, “I can say that my client maintains his innocence of any charges and has consented to be extradited back to Florida as soon as possible so that he can clear up the matters there.”

A gunman killed 4 people at a UPS facility in San Francisco before killing himself on Wednesday, Assistant Police Chief Toney Chaplin said. According to CNN, two other people were also shot and survived.
Police responded to a report of an active shooter around 8:55 AM local time at the UPS San Francisco Customer Centre — package sorting and delivery facility that employs about 850 people.
Officers arrived to learn the suspect was still inside the building, Chaplin said. A police “contact team” soon found him armed with an assault pistol, the assistant chief said.
“The suspect put the gun to his head and immediately discharged the weapon,” he said.
Though the suspect was wearing a UPS uniform, investigators have yet to confirm he was actually an employee, Chaplin said.
Local media quoted witnesses within the warehouse at the time of the incident as saying that the gunman went in through the front entrance and started shooting, without saying anything — once at the back of a victim and then at the heads of some others.
Employees of UPS were evacuated from the facility as officers tried to search for additional victims and witnesses, Xinhua reported.
For a moment, appealing that “don’t put officers at risk,” San Francisco Police Department posted a message on its Twitter social media network account calling for media to “stop showing video and photos of (police) Tactical Units search the roof and other parts of the scene.”
There have been no words on possible motives of the shooter or what led to the workplace shooting.
UPS said in a statement that pending the police investigation, it “cannot provide information as to the identity of persons involved at this time” and that regarding those injured, it is “unsure of their status at this time.”
rewrite:

According to a CNN report, two additional individuals sustained gunshot wounds but survived. Law enforcement authorities were alerted to an active shooter situation at approximately 8:55 AM local time at the UPS San Francisco Customer Centre, a parcel sorting and delivery operation employing roughly 850 individuals.

Upon arrival, officers ascertained that the suspect remained inside the building. A police tactical unit subsequently located the individual, who was armed with an assault-style pistol. Assistant Chief Chaplin stated that the suspect then fatally shot himself. Although the individual was attired in a UPS uniform, investigators have not yet verified his employment status with the company.

Media accounts citing witnesses within the warehouse indicate that the assailant entered through the front entrance and commenced firing without uttering any words, targeting victims from behind and in the head. Following the incident, UPS personnel were evacuated from the premises as officers conducted searches for additional victims and witnesses, a detail reported by Xinhua.

Concurrently, the San Francisco Police Department issued a public appeal via its Twitter account, urging media outlets to refrain from broadcasting imagery of tactical units operating on the roof and other areas of the scene to avoid compromising officer safety. As of the latest reports, no information regarding the shooter’s potential motives or the precipitating factors of the violence has been disclosed.

In an official statement, UPS indicated that, pending the ongoing police investigation, it is unable to disclose the identities of involved parties and remains uncertain of the current medical status of those injured.

Feb. 2 (UPI) -- To hunt successfully, cheetahs must keep their head still and eyes focused on the movements of their prey while running at high speed. How does the fastest animal in the world do it?
New research suggests the feline's inner ear is specially-designed to maintain balance and visual focus while running at speeds upwards of 60 miles per hour.
"If you watch a cheetah run in slow motion, you'll see incredible feats of movement: its legs, its back, its muscles all move with such coordinated power," Camille Grohé, a research fellow at the American Museum of Natural History, said in a news release. "But its head hardly moves at all."
In mammals, the inner ear plays an important role in balance and orientation. For the cheetah, the inner ear must preform these essential functions at high-speeds.
"Until now, no one has investigated the inner ear's role in this incredible hunting specialization," Grohé said.
The mammalian inner ear features three interconnected semicircular canals, each with fluid and sensory hairs that perceive even the slightest movements of the head. Each canal is oriented at a unique angle to detect different directional motions: vertical, horizontal and side-to-side tilt.
To understand how cheetahs evolved a unique iteration of the inner ear, scientists used high-resolution X-ray computed tomography to image semicircular canals in the skulls of modern cheetahs, Acinonyx jubatus, and a close relative, Acinonyx pardinensis, which went extinct 126,000 years ago. The images helped scientists build 3D digital images of the two species' inner ear.
Scientists found the inner ear of modern cheetahs boasts greater volume that the inner ear of other modern felines. Their anterior and posterior semicircular canals are both longer.
"This distinctive inner ear anatomy reflects enhanced sensitivity and more rapid responses to head motions, explaining the cheetah's extraordinary ability to maintain visual stability and to keep their gaze locked in on prey even during incredibly high-speed hunting," said John Flynn, curator of mammalian fossils at the museum.
Acinonyx pardinensis was also without a more voluminous inner ear, suggesting the cheetah's vestibular system is modern specialization.
Researchers published their findings in the journal Scientific Reports.
rewrite:
On February 2 (UPI), a report detailed the critical requirement for hunting cheetahs to maintain head stability and ocular focus on prey while sprinting at extreme velocities. This prompts the question of how the world's fastest terrestrial animal achieves such precise control. Emerging research indicates that the species' inner ear anatomy is uniquely adapted to preserve equilibrium and visual fixation during runs exceeding 60 miles per hour.

Camille Grohé, a research fellow at the American Museum of Natural History, noted in a news release, "If you observe a cheetah running in slow motion, you witness remarkable feats of movement: its legs, back, and muscles operate with coordinated power. However, its head remains remarkably stable." In mammalian physiology, the inner ear is fundamental to balance and spatial orientation. For the cheetah, this vestibular system must execute these essential functions under conditions of immense speed. "Until now, the role of the inner ear in this specialized hunting adaptation had not been examined," stated Grohé.

The mammalian inner ear comprises three interconnected semicircular canals, each containing fluid and sensory hairs that detect minute head movements. Each canal is oriented at a distinct angle to perceive specific directional motions: vertical, horizontal, and rotational tilt. To investigate the evolutionary development of the cheetah's inner ear, researchers employed high-resolution X-ray computed tomography to image the semicircular canals within skulls of the modern cheetah (*Acinonyx jubatus*) and its extinct relative, *Acinonyx pardinensis*, which perished approximately 126,000 years ago. These scans facilitated the construction of detailed three-dimensional digital models of the inner ear structures for both species.

Analysis revealed that the modern cheetah's inner ear possesses a greater overall volume compared to other extant felids. Specifically, its anterior and posterior semicircular canals are elongated. John Flynn, the museum's curator of mammalian fossils, explained, "This distinctive vestibular morphology reflects enhanced sensitivity and accelerated response to head movements, accounting for the cheetah's exceptional capacity to maintain visual stability and a fixed gaze on prey during high-speed pursuits." In contrast, *Acinonyx pardinensis* lacked a similarly voluminous inner ear, indicating that this specialized vestibular adaptation is a more recent evolutionary development in the modern cheetah lineage. The research team has published these findings in the journal *Scientific Reports*.
