An interesting perspective has been recently pointed out that I honestly hadn’t put much thought to until now that “Global Supply Chains Contain Inflation.” This report and a number of others mention that the global supply chain has put persistent downward pressure on prices and therefore, governments around the world that are reconsidering their participation in free trade (sound familiar?) should realize that withdrawal could come at a high cost.
While monetary policy has deservedly been given a lot of the credit for limiting inflation over the past 25+ years, the growth of the global market seems to actually have had a potentially greater impact. In the U.S., government borrowing (i.e., national debt) was supposed to fuel inflation, but it hasn’t. Counteracting this is the abundance of inexpensive consumer goods imported from Asia as well as less expensive raw and intermediate materials sourced globally (and a relatively low price of fuel as an added incentive for global trade).
It is safe to say that international trade leads to competition at a global level and tends to push down prices of domestically produced goods, and even the threat of cheaper imported substitutes keeps a lid on domestic production costs. That can partially explain wage stagnation a bit as, like the cost of any other factor of production, wage growth—and its impact on overall inflation—is also kept in check through this mechanism.
I think that this effect isn’t only due to the availability of global trade, but also a company’s ability to use technology and process improvements, such as Lean and Six Sigma, to improve the agility and efficiency of their supply chains and operations functions. This has enabled global trade to keep growing. So, any activities that can put a damper on these effects—such as artificial trade barriers and other economic uncertainty, significant fuel price increases, environmental disasters and terrorism—could also result in increases in inflation.
rewrite:
A noteworthy perspective has emerged, positing that global supply chains exert a deflationary influence on prices—a consideration that merits greater attention. Recent analyses, including the cited report, indicate that these international networks have consistently applied downward pressure on inflation. Consequently, governments reevaluating their engagement with free trade regimes should recognize that disengagement may entail significant economic costs.

While monetary policy has justifiably received considerable credit for moderating inflation over the past quarter-century, the expansion of global markets appears to have exerted a potentially more substantial effect. In the United States, for instance, substantial government borrowing and national debt accumulation were anticipated to fuel inflationary pressures, yet this outcome has not materialized. This counteraction can be attributed to the influx of low-cost consumer goods from Asia, alongside globally sourced inexpensive raw and intermediate materials, further facilitated by historically low fuel prices that incentivize international trade.

International trade fosters global competition, thereby reducing prices for domestically produced goods. Even the potential availability of cheaper imported alternatives constrains domestic production costs. This mechanism partially explains concurrent wage stagnation, as compensation growth—like other production factors—is similarly moderated, thereby containing its inflationary impact.

This deflationary effect stems not solely from trade accessibility but also from corporate adoption of technological and process innovations, such as Lean and Six Sigma methodologies. These enhancements improve supply chain agility and operational efficiency, thereby sustaining the expansion of global trade. Consequently, any developments that impede these dynamics—including artificial trade barriers, economic uncertainty, sharp increases in fuel prices, environmental disasters, or terrorism—could undermine this deflationary force and contribute to renewed inflationary pressures.

OWING MILLS, Md. – Every year when Santa comes to town children and their parents line-up to meet the jolly big man – but one Maryland toddler wasn’t having it.
Kerry Spencer taught her son the sign for “help” in sign language – and during his photo with Santa he made the sign.
“We taught our baby sign language. This is the sign for ‘help.’ You’re welcome,” Spencer wrote.
We taught our baby sign language. This is the sign for "help." You're welcome. pic.twitter.com/i6NkxBf4KP — Kerry Spencer (@Swilua) December 5, 2017
Spencer tweeted out the hilarious photo on Tuesday and it has since gone viral.
She went on to clear up the specific sign language variant he was taught.
“In baby sign you go with what they do. We showed him the ASL version and this is what he did,” she wrote on Twitter.
In baby sign you go with what they do. We showed him the ASL version and this is what he did. — Kerry Spencer (@Swilua) December 6, 2017
And to all the commenters saying he did it wrong, he was one! Give the poor guy a break! 😂 (This is the actual sign:) pic.twitter.com/0pgfRmbdk7 — Kerry Spencer (@Swilua) December 8, 2017
No word on if the little boy was able to let Saint Nick know what he wanted for Christmas before his parents rescued him.
rewrite:

While such encounters typically involve festive greetings, this particular child utilized a non-verbal form of communication. His mother, Kerry Spencer, had instructed him in infant sign language, specifically the gesture for "help," which he employed during his photograph with Santa.

Spencer disseminated an image of this occurrence via the social media platform Twitter on December 5, 2017, accompanied by the explanatory caption: "We taught our baby sign language. This is the sign for 'help.' You're welcome." The post rapidly achieved widespread circulation online. In subsequent clarifications, Spencer noted that while the American Sign Language (ASL) version of the sign was demonstrated, the infant's approximation was accepted, adhering to the adaptive principles of "baby sign." She further addressed online commentary regarding the technical accuracy of the gesture, humorously defending her one-year-old son's interpretation.

The incident concludes with an unresolved humorous note, as it remains unspecified whether the child successfully communicated his Christmas desires to Santa prior to parental intervention. The episode illustrates both a practical application of early childhood communication strategies and the viral nature of such candid familial moments in digital media.

[India], Apr 24 (ANI): In wake of the violence that gripped West Bengal, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Bairia district, Surendra Singh on Tuesday said the inaction of Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee would soon lead to a situation similar to that of Jammu and Kashmir and the Hindus would be wiped out of the state.

Hindus are unsafe in Bengal. If nothing is done about it, Bengal will face situation like that in Jammu and Kashmir. Hindus will be ousted from Bengal just like it happened in Jammu and Kashmir." Singh told reporters here.
While likening the Chief Minister with mythical demoness Surpanakha, Singh said that the Congress party was playing the role of demon king, Ravana. Singh further alleged torture of Hindus by terrorists entering the TMC-ruled state from adjoining Bangladesh. "Fortunately we have a leader like Modi Ji and we will oust all foreign elements from Bengal," he added. A clash broke out between supporters of Trinamool Congress (TMC) and BJP, during filing of nominations for panchayat elections in Birbhum district, on Monday, which claimed one BJP worker's life. Clashes were reported from other parts of the state as well. Singh is not new to controversial statements. Recently, speaking in defence of BJP MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar who was accused of raping a girl in Unnao, Singh said that no one could rape a mother of three children. (ANI)

TORONTO "Star Trek" fans can now get Starfleet's most famous figures to help deliver their mail, thanks to a new collection of seven stamps issued on Friday by Canada Post, the country's mail operator.
The stamps, a followup to a set released last year for the science-fiction franchise's 50th anniversary, include the captains from each of the five "Star Trek" television series already aired. They are depicted alongside a key nemesis from the series.
The sixth stamp is of the Galileo shuttle craft, which first appeared in the original series in 1966. A holographic foil stamp in the shape of a "Borg" cube is the seventh in the collection.

rewrite:
On April 28, 2017, the Reuters news agency obtained and published an undated handout photograph depicting a set of seven postage stamps issued by Canada Post, the national postal service, featuring imagery from the *Star Trek* science-fiction franchise. The issuance of this commemorative collection was announced on Friday of that week, offering enthusiasts of the series an opportunity to utilize depictions of iconic characters for postal delivery. This set constitutes a subsequent release following a previous series issued in commemoration of the franchise’s fiftieth anniversary the prior year.

The thematic content of the stamps is derived from the central narrative elements of the television series. Five of the stamps portray the commanding officers, or captains, from each of the five principal *Star Trek* television series that had been broadcast to date. Each captain is graphically presented alongside a primary antagonist from their respective narrative arc. A sixth stamp features an illustration of the Galileo shuttlecraft, a vessel that made its inaugural appearance in the original 1966 television series. The seventh and final stamp is distinguished by its specialized production; it is a holographic foil stamp manufactured in the three-dimensional shape of a Borg cube, representing one of the franchise's most formidable collectives.

This philatelic release by Canada Post represents an intersection of popular culture and official postal service commemorative practices, acknowledging the enduring cultural impact of the *Star Trek* narrative universe.

CHICAGO The credit rating for Bridgeview, Illinois, fell into the junk level on Friday after S&P Global Ratings hit the Chicago suburb with a four-notch downgrade to BB-minus.
S&P cited debt pressures on Bridgeview, which issued $135 million of general obligation (GO) bonds in 2005 for a stadium that it owns and manages.
"The downgrade reflects our view that the village will continue to face acute business, financial, and economic uncertainties related to its debt burden, particularly the debt issued for its Toyota Park stadium," S&P analyst Blake Yocom said in a statement.
S&P placed the junk rating on a watch list for a possible further downgrade due to concerns over potentially reduced market access and weakened liquidity for Bridgeview.
Steve Landek, Bridgeview's mayor, said he believed the downgrade was triggered by a plan the suburb was considering to restructure $24.5 million of variable-rate bonds to a fixed-rate mode with a 2047 maturity. He said Bridgeview would come up with a better plan over the next 90 days.
The credit rating agency said it expects Bridgeview, which has used restructurings in the past to ease debt service payments and minimize property tax hikes, to continue the practice, possibly pushing bond maturities out to years beyond the useful life of the stadium.
It added that the "underperforming" stadium has left the suburb with an "extremely high" GO debt burden that totals about $256 million and "very weak" liquidity.
With seating for as many as 28,000, Toyota Park, which opened in 2006, hosts soccer games, concerts and other events in the village of 17,000 located southwest of Chicago.
(Reporting by Karen Pierog; editing by Lisa Shumaker)
rewrite:
On Friday, S&P Global Ratings downgraded the credit rating of Bridgeview, Illinois, by four notches to BB-minus, relegating it to speculative, or "junk," status. The agency cited significant debt pressures confronting the Chicago suburb, stemming primarily from $135 million in general obligation (GO) bonds issued in 2005 to finance the construction of Toyota Park, a stadium owned and managed by the village. In a statement, S&P analyst Blake Yocom indicated the downgrade reflects an assessment that Bridgeview will continue to face acute business, financial, and economic uncertainties related to this debt burden. Furthermore, S&P placed the rating on CreditWatch with negative implications, signaling potential for an additional downgrade due to concerns over potentially reduced market access and weakened liquidity.

Bridgeview Mayor Steve Landek suggested the downgrade was precipitated by the village's consideration of a plan to restructure $24.5 million in variable-rate bonds into a fixed-rate mode with a 2047 maturity. Mayor Landek stated the village intends to formulate an alternative plan within the next ninety days. S&P noted its expectation that Bridgeview, which has historically utilized debt restructurings to ease debt service payments and minimize property tax increases, will continue this practice. This could potentially extend bond maturities beyond the useful life of the stadium. The agency added that the "underperforming" stadium has resulted in an "extremely high" GO debt burden, totaling approximately $256 million, alongside "very weak" liquidity.

Toyota Park, which opened in 2006 with a capacity of 28,000, hosts soccer matches, concerts, and other events. It operates within Bridgeview, a village of approximately 17,000 residents located southwest of Chicago.

Food waste, poverty, and hunger are three realities for many families in Duncan and the Cowichan Valley.
Approximately two thousand children live below the poverty line in Duncan and with Cowichan Valley residents wasting 40 per cent of their food, the Cowichan Food Recovery Project is aiming to address these issues.
Agriculture Minister, Lana Popham stopped by the Cowichan Green Community office in Duncan Friday and announced $84,000 dollars in funding.
Executive Director of the Cowichan Green Community, Judy Stafford says there are both environmental and community impacts tied to this program.
Popham says Vancouver has a great example of what is possible here in the Cowichan Valley from a food recovery standpoint.
The Cowichan Food Recovery Project provides four participants with an opportunity to gain experience before entering the job market.
Stafford says these participants are an integral part of the project.
Popham says this is a great program that will go a long way to reducing food insecurity.
The money will be used to provide four participants with food safety training, WHMIS and first aid certification, along with opportunities to travel to other parts of the island and the province that offer similar programs, and try and replicate them here.

Food insecurity, poverty, and food waste represent interconnected challenges for numerous households in Duncan and the broader Cowichan Valley region. During a visit to the Cowichan Green Community office, British Columbia’s Minister of Agriculture, Lana Popham, announced provincial funding of $84,000 to support the initiative. Judy Stafford, Executive Director of the Cowichan Green Community, emphasizes the program’s dual environmental and social benefits. Minister Popham cited successful food recovery models in Vancouver as a precedent for potential local replication.

The allocated funds will specifically cover participant training in food safety, Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS) protocols, and first aid certification. Furthermore, it will enable travel to examine analogous programs elsewhere on Vancouver Island and across the province, with the objective of adapting effective strategies locally. Minister Popham characterized the program as a significant measure toward alleviating food insecurity in the community.

Grads and apprentices from Ricardo Rail have won the annual Railway Challenge organised by the Institution of Mechanical Engineers (IMechE).
(Credit: @IMeche)
Making its debut in the event, the Ricardo team came out ahead of nine other competitors from across the UK and Germany. Teams were required to design and manufacture a miniature, 10 1/4” gauge railway locomotive, with the trains put through their paces at the Stapleford Miniature Railway in Leicestershire. The competition, which took place from 28 June to 1 July, saw Ricardo named Grand Champions ahead of last year’s winners, SNC Lavalin Rail and Transit.
“This year’s Railway Challenge was the toughest competition yet,” said head judge Bill Reeve, director of Rail at Transport Scotland and an IMechE Fellow.
“For Ricardo to win in the first year it has competed is an outstanding achievement. Good teamwork and project management, with sound system engineering and testing delivered impressive and reliable performance.”
The locomotives were tested in a series of track-based and presentation challenges, including a design report and business presentation, as well as challenges on the locomotive’s traction, ride comfort, noise, maintainability and ability to store energy. This year’s entrants delivered a wide range of solutions for traction and braking systems and suspension designs, with locomotives featuring fuel cells, internal combustion, batteries, super-capacitors, and mechanical energy storage.
“We had a team that worked really well together and benefitted from cross-industry expertise by having railway and automotive team members,” said Benjamin Morley, graduate consultant engineer and project manager of the Ricardo Rail team. “The general design wasn’t overcomplicated, though we did concentrate our efforts on the energy recovery.”

They prevailed over nine other competing teams from the United Kingdom and Germany, including the previous year’s winners, SNC-Lavalin Rail and Transit. The competition requires teams to design and manufacture a functional miniature locomotive to a 10 ¼-inch gauge.

According to head judge Bill Reeve, Director of Rail at Transport Scotland and an IMechE Fellow, “This year’s Railway Challenge was the toughest competition yet.” He emphasised that “For Ricardo to win in the first year it has competed is an outstanding achievement. Good teamwork and project management, with sound system engineering and testing delivered impressive and reliable performance.” The evaluation comprised a series of track-based and presentation-based assessments. These included a formal design report, a business case presentation, and technical challenges evaluating traction, ride comfort, noise emissions, maintainability, and energy storage capabilities. This year’s entries exhibited a diverse array of engineering solutions for traction, braking, and suspension systems, incorporating technologies such as fuel cells, internal combustion engines, batteries, super-capacitors, and mechanical energy storage.

Benjamin Morley, graduate consultant engineer and project manager for the Ricardo Rail team, attributed their success to effective collaboration. “We had a team that worked really well together and benefitted from cross-industry expertise by having railway and automotive team members,” he stated. “The general design wasn’t overcomplicated, though we did concentrate our efforts on the energy recovery system.” The final rankings placed Ricardo Rail first, followed by SNC-Lavalin Rail and Transit in second, and the University of Birmingham in third position.

Call it a cow-beaver.
Ranchers northeast of Regina are shaking their heads after watching a herd of curious bovines slowly follow a beaver across one of their pastures.
Adrienne Ivey and her husband Aaron were out checking their 150 cattle near Ituna, Sask., on Good Friday when they noticed something odd.
The cattle were gathered together and walking slowly behind a beaver, with some of the heifers lowering their heads to get a closer look at the furry cowboy with a funny-looking tail.
When the beaver stopped, the herd would stop, and then follow again when the rodent resumed its stroll.
Ivey says they are used to herding their cows with horses or quads, but nothing like this.
She says young cattle are naturally curious, while the beaver seemed to ignore all the attention.
“We knew that people would get a great chuckle out of it because you cannot get more Canadian than that,” said Ivey, who posted a video of the beaver-bovine cattle drive on Facebook.
“We talk about how awesome our Canadian beef is, but a beaver leading cattle around? It’s the most Canadian thing ever!”
Ivey said the beaver was probably looking around the pasture for a place to build a dam.

rewrite:
A peculiar incident involving bovine curiosity has been documented on a ranch northeast of Regina. Ranchers Adrienne and Aaron Ivey, while inspecting their herd of approximately 150 cattle near Ituna, Saskatchewan, on Good Friday, observed an unusual procession. The cattle were congregated and moving slowly in tandem with a beaver traversing the pasture. Several heifers lowered their heads to scrutinize the rodent at closer proximity. The herd exhibited a synchronized pattern of movement, halting when the beaver paused and proceeding again upon its resumption of travel.

The Iveys, accustomed to managing cattle via conventional means such as horses or all-terrain vehicles, found this spontaneous formation notable. Adrienne Ivey noted that the younger cattle demonstrated innate inquisitiveness, while the beaver appeared largely indifferent to its bovine escort. She remarked that the scene represented a quintessentially Canadian occurrence, prompting her to share a video of the event on social media for its humorous appeal. Ivey further contextualized the incident by humorously juxtaposing the national symbolism of Canadian beef with that of the beaver, suggesting the confluence of the two created an archetypal national moment. She speculated that the beaver was likely surveying the pasture for potential dam construction sites.

On December 12, 2017, Prime Minister Narendra Modi undertook a journey via seaplane from the Sabarmati River in Ahmedabad to Dharoi Dam in Mehsana district, Gujarat. This event marked the inaugural flight of such an aircraft within India. The Prime Minister announced the travel plans at a preceding election rally, stating his intention to proceed to the Ambaji temple following the landing at Dharoi Dam and to return via the same mode of transport. He contextualized the use of seaplanes as a strategic governmental initiative to enhance connectivity in regions where conventional airport infrastructure is not feasible, noting the substitution of a planned roadshow with this aerial journey due to logistical circumstances.

The initiative draws a parallel to prior efforts in other states, notably Kerala. There, a commercial seaplane service was launched in June 2013 under the auspices of Kerala Tourism Infrastructure Limited, with an inaugural flight operated from Kollam by Kairali Aviation. However, the Kerala venture failed to commence sustained commercial operations, primarily due to opposition from local fishing communities. VOL. 41 | NO. 6 | Friday, February 10, 2017
KNOXVILLE (AP) — A federal jury in Knoxville has convicted a Pennsylvania man of charges connected to a multistate bank robbery-kidnapping spree.
The Knoxville News Sentinel (http://bit.ly/2lehEml) reports 44-year-old Michael Benanti of Lake Harmony, Pa., was convicted of 23 charges, including conspiracy to commit bank extortion, and kidnapping, carjacking and extortion. Benanti faces more than 300 years in prison and will be sentenced July 25.
The case involved kidnappings of three East Tennessee bank-connected families as well as an attempted kidnapping and a bank robbery in Pennsylvania, kidnapping of a Connecticut bank employee and his mother and a grocery store robbery in North Carolina.
Benanti's partner, 46-year-old Brian Witham, was given a plea deal that caps his sentence at 42 years. Benanti denied involvement, and defense lawyers tried to convince jurors that Witham was lying.
rewrite: On Friday, February 10, 2017, a federal jury in Knoxville convicted Michael Benanti, a forty-four-year-old resident of Lake Harmony, Pennsylvania, on twenty-three criminal counts. These charges, as reported by the Knoxville News Sentinel, stemmed from a multistate crime spree and included conspiracy to commit bank extortion, kidnapping, carjacking, and extortion. The offenses involved the kidnappings of three bank-affiliated families in East Tennessee, an attempted kidnapping and bank robbery in Pennsylvania, the kidnapping of a Connecticut bank employee and his mother, and a grocery store robbery in North Carolina. Benanti, who faces a potential sentence exceeding three hundred years, is scheduled for sentencing on July 25. His accomplice, forty-six-year-old Brian Witham, accepted a plea agreement limiting his sentence to forty-two years. Throughout the trial, Benanti maintained his innocence, with defense counsel arguing that Witham's testimony was fraudulent.

In an unexpected discovery that shifts how scientists think about the early days of the universe, astronomers have detected a supermassive black hole that they say is the most distant ever observed.
The colossal black hole is so far away that light from the quasar in which it is located was emitted just 690 million years after the Big Bang, which took place 13.8 billion years ago. Quasars are star-like celestial objects made up of a supermassive black hole and surrounding gas, which shines with incredible brilliance as it falls into the black hole.
The newfound object certainly lives up to the supermassive moniker; it’s about 800 million times as massive as the sun. In comparison, the supermassive black hole at the center of our Milky Way galaxy, Sagittarius A*, is about 4.6 million times as massive as the sun.
That stupendous size has astronomers scratching their heads.
“Now that we are seeing it, we have to explain it,” Dr. Eduardo Banados, an astrophysicist with the Carnegie Institution for Science in Pasadena, California, and the lead author of a paper about the discovery, told the Los Angeles Times. “And that is a big challenge for theorists right now.”
The paper was published online Dec. 6, 2017 in the journal Nature.
Larger supermassive black holes have been discovered, Dr. Robert Simcoe, a professor at MIT’s Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research and co-author of the paper, told NBC News MACH in an email. “What’s unprecedented is the combination of large size so early in the history of the universe.”
rewrite:
Astronomers have identified the most distant supermassive black hole yet observed, a finding that challenges existing theoretical frameworks regarding the early universe. This black hole resides within a quasar, an extremely luminous galactic nucleus, whose light was emitted approximately 690 million years after the Big Bang—an event dated to 13.8 billion years ago. Quasars consist of a supermassive black hole accreting surrounding gas, a process that generates extraordinary radiative output.

The newly detected object possesses a mass roughly 800 million times that of the Sun, thereby qualifying as supermassive. This stands in stark contrast to the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A*, which has a mass of only about 4.6 million solar masses. The exceptional mass of this high-redshift black hole presents a significant puzzle for models of early cosmic structure formation.

As stated by Dr. Eduardo Banados of the Carnegie Institution for Science, lead author of the study, "Now that we are seeing it, we have to explain it... That is a big challenge for theorists right now." The research was published online in the journal *Nature* on December 6, 2017. Co-author Dr. Robert Simcoe of MIT’s Kavli Institute for Astrophysics and Space Research noted that while larger supermassive black holes have been documented, "What’s unprecedented is the combination of large size so early in the history of the universe." This discovery thus provides a critical observational constraint for understanding rapid black hole growth in the epoch of reionization.

ORLANDO (CBSMiami/AP) – The companies involved in the design and construction of Florida International University’s pedestrian bridge have been named in the first lawsuit filed since its collapse.
Matt Morgan, of Morgan and Morgan, announced that his firm is representing Marquise Hepburn in a civil suit filed Monday morning out of Miami-Dade County.
Morgan said his client was riding his bike to work when the bridge failed, causing a vehicle that veered to get out of the way of the collapse to hit Hepburn, throwing him from his bicycle.
Hepburn suffered spinal injuries during the incident and is still recovering, the attorney said. He has since been discharged from the hospital.
In a press conference held Monday afternoon, Morgan said there were a number of factors his firm plans to dig into, as the collapse is under investigation.
The negligence lawsuit seeks unspecified damages from the entities involved in building the bridge. They include Munilla Construction Management and FIGG Bridge Engineers. Both companies say they will cooperate with multiple investigations into the collapse.
The lawsuit says cracks in the 174-foot span should have been taken seriously and traffic should have been diverted during any testing.
Gallery: Scene of the FIU Bridge Collapse
Southwest 8th Street remains closed indefinitely between 107th Avenue and 117th Avenue as crews work to clear the bridge debris.
On Monday, the university observed a moment of silence 1:47 p.m., the same time the bridge fell last Thursday, as the first step in healing the community.
A vigil for the six people who died in the collapse is planned for Wednesday.
(© Copyright 2018 CBS Broadcasting Inc. All Rights Reserved. The Associated Press contributed to this report.)

The initial civil litigation concerning the collapse of the pedestrian bridge at Florida International University has been filed, naming the firms responsible for its design and construction. According to the complaint, Mr. Hepburn was bicycling to work when the structure failed. In the ensuing incident, a vehicle swerved to avoid falling debris and struck him, ejecting him from his bicycle. Mr. Hepburn sustained spinal injuries, for which he continues to receive treatment following his discharge from hospitalization.

During a press conference, Attorney Morgan indicated his firm intends to investigate multiple factors contributing to the collapse, which remains under official scrutiny. The negligence suit seeks unspecified damages from the involved entities, notably Munilla Construction Management and FIGG Bridge Engineers. Both companies have publicly stated their commitment to cooperating with the multiple ongoing investigations. The litigation alleges that observed cracks in the 174-foot span constituted a serious warning sign and that traffic should have been diverted from the area during any structural testing.

Recovery efforts continue at the site, with Southwest 8th Street closed indefinitely between 107th and 117th Avenues as crews clear debris. The university community observed a moment of silence at 1:47 p.m. on Monday, marking the precise time of the previous Thursday's collapse, as an initial step in a healing process. A vigil for the six fatalities is scheduled for Wednesday.

THE serial cheat chucked out of an Australia Day ultra-marathon event for cutting out dozens of kilometres of the course, also has a chequered history at home in Britain and in the US it has emerged — including convictions for operating as a landlord without a licence.
Mark Robson has been told he is not welcome at local charity fun runs, after more dishonest behaviour behind the bib came to light this week.
Mr Robson, 46, was exposed after the ultra-marathon organisers caught him failing to complete large parts of the Australind course, before crossing the line to claim a medal.
He was thrown out of the race in disgrace.
The former advertising sales executive had been banned by Australia’s triathlon authorities over similar allegations when he competed in the prestigious Busselton ironman event in 2013.
It has emerged that starting lines are not the only thing Mr Robson has run away from in recent years.
In 2012, Mr Robson was convicted of renting a flat in his native Gateshead, in the north east of England, without a licence.
The flat, in the suburb of Chopwell, was in an area where a landlord licensing scheme operated, meaning it was a criminal offence to operate a privately rented property without a licence.
All the rent, of £5,219 ($9290), was to be repaid.
It was the second such conviction for Mr Robson, who according to local media reports, had not acted after local council officials encouraged him to register for a licence.
Mr Robson has failed to respond to repeated questions about his ban by two major amateur sporting organisations.
There are also questions about his performance in an ultra-endurance race in Florida in 2016.
Authorities there are chasing Mr Robson for defaulted payments on a time-share apartment in the Westgate Vacation Villas complex just outside Orlando.
It emerged yesterday Mr Robson will still be permitted to compete in this year’s Rottnest Swim.
But not in the HBF Run for a Reason, whose organisers have told Mr Robson he was not welcome at the event after issues surrounding his run in 2016.
It is understood Mr Robson ran in the half-marathon under another competitor’s name, who had only paid an entry fee for the 12km race.
rewrite:
Mark Robson, a 46-year-old former advertising sales executive, has been disqualified from an Australia Day ultra-marathon event following the discovery that he circumvented a significant portion of the course. This incident has brought to light a broader pattern of deceptive conduct, extending beyond athletic competitions to include legal infractions in both the United Kingdom and the United States.

Organisers of the event in Australind determined that Mr. Robson failed to complete dozens of kilometres before crossing the finish line to claim a medal, resulting in his removal from the race. This is not an isolated incident in his sporting history; he previously received a ban from Australian triathlon authorities for similar allegations during the 2013 Busselton Ironman event. Consequently, he has been informed he is unwelcome at several local charity running events.

Mr. Robson’s record of misconduct includes convictions in the United Kingdom. In 2012, he was found guilty of operating as an unlicensed landlord in Gateshead, England, specifically for renting a property in Chopwell, an area subject to a mandatory licensing scheme. This constituted a criminal offence, and he was ordered to repay all collected rent, totaling £5,219. Local media reported this as a second conviction, noting he had failed to comply with prior council directives to obtain the necessary licence.

Further allegations have emerged regarding his participation in a 2016 ultra-endurance race in Florida, where questions have been raised about the legitimacy of his performance. Separately, authorities in Florida are pursuing Mr. Robson for defaulted payments related to a timeshare apartment in the Westgate Vacation Villas complex near Orlando.

Despite these issues, it has been confirmed that Mr. Robson remains eligible to compete in this year’s Rottnest Swim. However, he has been explicitly barred from the HBF Run for a Reason. Organisers of that event declared him unwelcome following an incident in 2016, where it is alleged he participated in the half-marathon under another entrant’s name, who had only registered for the shorter 12-kilometre race. Mr. Robson has not responded to repeated requests for comment regarding his bans from these amateur sporting organisations.

View of a sign outside the Imperial Tobacco Seita cigarette plant in Carquefou, near Nantes, April 15, 2014. REUTERS/Stephane Mahe
LONDON Britain's Imperial Brands, the fourth-largest international tobacco company, remains committed to its pursuit of e-cigarettes as the best alternative to smoking, but could pivot quickly with a heated tobacco product within months if proved wrong, a senior executive said on Wednesday.
"Our belief is that the opportunity in e-vapour remains bigger than the opportunity in heated tobacco," said Matthew Phillips, Imperial's chief development officer. He said Imperial was looking at heated tobacco even though it wasn't testing a product like Philip Morris, British American Tobacco and Japan Tobacco International.
So far Japan is the most developed market for heated tobacco products, as it has stricter rules around the nicotine-laced liquids used in e-cigarettes.
"I'm yet to see the kind of traction outside Japan that would make me change that view and start following a heated tobacco strategy more proactively," Phillips said on a conference call with analysts following the company's half-year results.
"If we have to change our mind because it did start getting traction, we would be able to follow with an offering within a number of months."
Phillips said recent innovations in "vaping" and marijuana technology in the United States means that heated tobacco products do not need to be in the format in which they are currently sold.
Phillips said different consumers were using different products, noting that younger "millennial" consumers tended to use e-cigarettes, while the tobacco-based products appealed to older people.
(Reporting by Martinne Geller; Editing by Susan Fenton)

To date, Japan represents the most advanced market for heated tobacco products, partly due to stricter regulations governing the nicotine-containing liquids used in e-cigarettes. “I'm yet to see the kind of traction outside Japan that would make me change that view and start following a heated tobacco strategy more proactively,” Phillips stated during a conference call with analysts following the release of the company’s half-year results. He added, “If we have to change our mind because it did start getting traction, we would be able to follow with an offering within a number of months.”

He also highlighted divergent consumer preferences, noting that younger, millennial consumers tend to favor e-cigarettes, while tobacco-derived products retain greater appeal among older demographics.

* Meeting to take place on Thursday
* Norway PM visiting China on April 7-10, first in decade
* Full diplomatic relations restored after Nobel Peace Prize row (Adds details, background)
By Nerijus Adomaitis
OSLO, April 5 Norway's deputy oil minister will meet top executives of China's biggest offshore oil producer CNOOC on Thursday to discuss possible cooperation ahead of the first visit by a Norwegian prime minister to China in a decade, officials said.
CNOOC, which operates the 140,000 barrels per day Buzzard field offshore Britain via its subsidiary Nexen, said in 2010 it would be interested to come to Norway.
The row over the Nobel Peace Prize award to Chinese dissident Liu Xiaobo, chosen by a Norwegian committee that same year, froze relations between the two countries.
Norwegian Prime Minister Erna Solberg will be in Beijing on April 7-10 to meet President Xi Jinping, Prime Minister Li Keqiang and other Chinese officials, in the first visit by a Norwegian premier since the countries resumed full diplomatic relations in December.
Norway's Ingvil Smines Tybring-Gjedde will meet the number two executive at CNOOC on April 6, the oil ministry and business lobby group Norwegian Energy Partners told Reuters.
"We have had a very good relationship with Chinese oil companies, and we want to get back to the situation before the Nobel peace prize and all the problems with China," said Haakon Skretting from Norwegian Energy Partners.
Solberg will take executives from several top Norwegian companies, including oil firm Statoil, to China.
Statoil, which has had an office in Beijing since 1982, said China was a key market, with sales to its refineries at roughly 100,000 barrels per day, in addition to LPG and other products.
Companies such as Kuwait's Kufpec and Russia's Gazprom have also recently shown an interest in Norwegian oil assets and technology.
"Norway provides opportunities to gain know-how and learn about new technologies in order to bring them back home later," Daniel Rennemo, head of PricewaterhouseCoopers's Norway oil and gas transactions team, told Reuters.
"It remains attractive due to it resource potential, highly qualified workforce, stable geopolitics and attractive tax regime, while companies like Statoil have also managed to cut costs significantly."
(Editing by Gwladys Fouche and Terje Solsvik, editing by David Evans)
rewrite:
On Thursday, April 6, a meeting is scheduled between Norway’s Deputy Minister of Petroleum and Energy, Ingvil Smines Tybring-Gjedde, and senior executives of the China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC). This diplomatic engagement precedes an official state visit to China by Norwegian Prime Minister Erna Solberg from April 7 to 10, her first such visit in a decade. The discussions are anticipated to focus on potential cooperative ventures within the offshore energy sector, signaling a continued thaw in bilateral relations following a prolonged diplomatic rift.

Diplomatic relations between Norway and China were significantly strained in 2010 following the Norwegian Nobel Committee’s decision to award the Peace Prize to Chinese dissident Liu Xiaobo. The subsequent freeze in high-level dialogue and cooperation lasted until December 2016, when full diplomatic relations were formally restored. Prime Minister Solberg’s upcoming itinerary includes meetings with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Keqiang, representing a culmination of this normalization process.

The business delegation accompanying Prime Minister Solberg will include representatives from several major Norwegian firms, notably the state-owned energy company Equinor (formerly Statoil). Equinor has maintained a presence in China since 1982 and identifies the country as a strategic market, with daily crude oil sales to Chinese refineries approximating 100,000 barrels, in addition to liquefied petroleum gas and other products. CNOOC has previously expressed interest in the Norwegian continental shelf, notably in 2010 through its subsidiary Nexen, which operates the Buzzard field in the UK North Sea.

Industry analysts note that Norway remains an attractive partner for international energy investment due to its substantial resource base, highly skilled workforce, political stability, and favorable fiscal terms. Daniel Rennemo, head of the oil and gas transactions team at PricewaterhouseCoopers Norway, observed that the sector offers valuable technological expertise and cost-efficient operations, as demonstrated by Equinor’s significant reductions in operational expenditures. This combination of factors continues to draw interest from global energy entities, including recent attention from firms such as Kuwait’s Kufpec and Russia’s Gazprom.

The concurrent ministerial and executive-level dialogues underscore a mutual intent to rebuild and deepen economic ties, particularly in energy, which had been disrupted by the earlier diplomatic dispute. Officials, including Haakon Skretting of Norwegian Energy Partners, have explicitly stated the objective of returning to the robust cooperative relationship that existed prior to 2010.

And, of course, there’s the small matter of Andy Murray…
Nadal was rather respectful at the news that Federer would go into the tournament as top seed, despite the fact the Swiss currently sits at number two in the world rankings: “For winning so many times here and having so much success on grass, he deserves to be the number one seed for everything he has achieved here.”
When is Roger Federer playing his second round match at Wimbledon?
Federer will next play Lukas Lacko, the world number 73 from Slovakia, in what is likely to be another easy test for the top seed, after he saw off Lajovic 6-1 6-3 6-4 in the first round. Right to declare jihad rests with State, not a mohalla or mosque: Ahsan Iqbal
Interior Minister Ahsan Iqbal said that in an Islamic country only the State had the right to declare jihad, not a mohalla or a mosque, and nobody could issue fatwas calling for killing others.
“We need to curb these trends as they are a threat to our internal security,” the minister said in the National Assembly, media reported.
“The enemy wants Muslims to behead each other. If we continue treading this path of violence and unrest, we wouldn’t even need an [external] enemy to destroy us,” he added.
Iqbal said social networking websites were being used to issue fatwas calling for killing others over blasphemy.
He added that the people issuing such edicts on the internet could not claim ownership of faith. “They will be dealt with sternly under the cyber crime law,” he maintained.
Speaking on the terrorist attack on a shrine in Jhal Masgi a day earlier, the minister said he had sought a report on the incident.
He added that he wanted to send a message to those sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan that such attacks would not help them achieve their nefarious designs.
“We need to unite to defeat terrorism. If we remain at each other’s throats, then we will achieve nothing but self-destruction.”
rewrite:
In an address to the National Assembly, Interior Minister Ahsan Iqbal asserted that within an Islamic state, the exclusive authority to declare jihad resides with the State itself, and not with local neighborhoods (mohallas) or individual mosques. He emphasized that no entity possesses the right to issue fatwas sanctioning the killing of others. The minister identified the proliferation of such unauthorized religious edicts as a significant threat to internal security, stating that these trends must be curbed. He warned that adversarial elements seek to instigate fratricidal conflict among Muslims, and that a continued trajectory of internal violence and unrest would render external enemies superfluous to the nation’s destabilization.

Minister Iqbal specifically noted the misuse of social networking platforms to disseminate fatwas inciting violence, particularly on accusations of blasphemy. He contended that individuals promulgating such decrees online cannot claim authoritative ownership of religious faith. Furthermore, he affirmed that such actors would face stringent legal action under cyber crime legislation. Referencing a recent terrorist attack on a shrine in Jhal Magsi, the minister confirmed he had requisitioned a detailed report on the incident. He directed a message to the sponsors of terrorism within Pakistan, stating that such attacks would not advance their nefarious objectives. Iqbal concluded with a call for national unity against terrorism, arguing that internal discord would lead only to collective self-destruction.

The fan club of the Christian Vertical Centre in Tema is the second to qualify for the semifinal of the ongoing National Junior Graphic Fan Club Spelling Competition.
This brings to two the schools which will represent the Greater Accra Region in the semifinal of the competition which has been slated for March 2017.
Being the first time the school has reached the semifinal stage of the national competition, the contestants and supporters, as well as members of staff present at the contest, wasted no time to sing their school anthem happily after they were declared winners of the knockout contest last week.
Contestants of the Christian Vertical Centre did not have it easy in their group because at the end of the contest they had tied with Happy Kids School at Kwashieman which also wanted to make a debut appearance in the semifinal and proceed to the final stage of the competition.
The two schools both had 41 points so the tie had to be broken.
After spelling three words each, the tie was broken and Christian Vertical Centre amassed 45 points, while Happy Kids followed closely with 44 points.
The other participating schools in the group, Acropolis School at Gbawe and Step-By-Step Montessori School, Dansoman, had 28 and 25 points, respectively.
The other schools which have also qualified for the semifinal are the Nest School Complex Junior Graphic Fan Club, Takoradi, and Holy Trinity Lutheran School Junior Graphic Fan Club in Kumasi.

Consequently, two institutions will now represent the Greater Accra Region in the semifinal stage, scheduled for March 2017. This marks the school’s inaugural advancement to the national semifinals. Following their declaration as winners in last week’s knockout contest, the contestants, alongside their supporters and attending staff members, promptly celebrated by joyfully singing the school anthem.

The path to qualification was arduous for the Christian Vertical Centre contestants. Upon conclusion of the group stage, they were tied with Happy Kids School of Kwashieman, which also sought its first appearance in the semifinals with aspirations of progressing to the final round. Both schools had accumulated 41 points, necessitating a tie-breaking procedure. After each school spelled three additional words, Christian Vertical Centre prevailed with 45 points, narrowly surpassing Happy Kids School, which secured 44 points. The other participating schools in the group, Acropolis School in Gbawe and Step-By-Step Montessori School in Dansoman, attained 28 and 25 points, respectively.

They join previously qualified semifinalists: The Nest School Complex Junior Graphic Fan Club in Takoradi and the Holy Trinity Lutheran School Junior Graphic Fan Club in Kumasi.

Familiar faces return to the N.B.A. finals. Or you can watch two De Niro films.
What’s on TV
N.B.A. FINALS 9 p.m. on ABC. “The Purge” is getting its fourth installment this summer. “Rick and Morty” was just picked up for a fourth season. And now, the Cavaliers and the Warriors will play each other in the finals for the fourth straight year — something that has never happened in any North American sports league. LeBron James will try to even the number of championships over that span at two apiece — but he’ll need help from an underwhelming and injured supporting cast that was brutally mocked by “Saturday Night Live.” The Warriors looked vulnerable against the Rockets, but hope to enter the conversation to be considered one of the best teams ever. And Jimmy Kimmel’s GAME NIGHT leads in at 8, with celebrity guests like Kevin Hart, Robert Downey Jr., Will Ferrell and Snoop Dogg competing in a three-point challenge.
CASINO (1995) 7 p.m. on VH1. Robert De Niro stars in this crime film from Martin Scorsese, playing a handicapper who oversees a lucrative Vegas casino. Sharon Stone earned an Oscar nomination as Ginger McKenna, his scheming wife.
A BRONX TALE (1993) 8 p.m. on AMC. Chazz Palminteri made his Broadway musical debut this month as the gangster Sonny in the surprisingly durable show “A Bronx Tale.” He probably didn’t have to do too much character work, though: He wrote “A Bronx Tale” in 1989 as an autobiographical one-man show, and then played Sonny in this 1993 film, also starring Mr. De Niro. “Mr. Palminteri gives the kind of coolly magnetic performance that makes it easy to see why Mr. De Niro gravitated toward this material in the first place,” Janet Maslin wrote in her review in The New York Times. “And Mr. De Niro is able to lend toughness to an ending that risks becoming overpoweringly sentimental, and instead succeeds in conveying a strong sense of father-son love.”

The National Basketball Association finals feature a historic recurrence of participants, while concurrent television programming offers two films starring Robert De Niro. The following comprises the evening's notable broadcasts.

**N.B.A. FINALS**, 9 p.m. on ABC. The Cleveland Cavaliers and Golden State Warriors are poised to contest the championship series for an unprecedented fourth consecutive year, a feat unmatched in the history of major North American professional sports leagues. This installment continues a modern rivalry, with LeBron James seeking to equalize the championship tally at two titles each over this four-year period. However, his endeavor is complicated by an injury-plagued and oft-criticized supporting cast, a subject of recent satire on *Saturday Night Live*. The Warriors, despite demonstrating vulnerability in the preceding conference finals against the Houston Rockets, aim to secure a third title in four years, thereby strengthening their case for consideration among the greatest teams in league history. Preceding the game at 8 p.m., *Jimmy Kimmel's Game Night* will feature a celebrity three-point shooting contest with participants including Kevin Hart, Robert Downey Jr., Will Ferrell, and Snoop Dogg.

**CASINO (1995)**, 7 p.m. on VH1. This crime drama, directed by Martin Scorsese, stars Robert De Niro as Sam "Ace" Rothstein, a handicapper tasked with overseeing the day-to-day operations of a profitable Las Vegas casino. Sharon Stone received an Academy Award nomination for her performance as Ginger McKenna, Rothstein's manipulative wife.

**A BRONX TALE (1993)**, 8 p.m. on AMC. Chazz Palminteri, who recently debuted in the Broadway musical adaptation of *A Bronx Tale*, originally authored the work as an autobiographical one-man show in 1989. He subsequently reprised his role as the gangster Sonny in this 1993 film, which also stars Robert De Niro. In her contemporaneous review for *The New York Times*, Janet Maslin noted that "Mr. Palminteri gives the kind of coolly magnetic performance that makes it easy to see why Mr. De Niro gravitated toward this material in the first place." She further observed that "Mr. De Niro is able to lend toughness to an ending that risks becoming overpoweringly sentimental, and instead succeeds in conveying a strong sense of father-son love."

April 6 France's PSA Group, the maker of Peugeot, Citroen and DS cars, said on Thursday it had begun offering a car-sharing service in Los Angeles, marking its return to the United States.
PSA also said it had created a new division - PSA North America - that will be led by Larry Dominique, a U.S. auto industry veteran who has worked at General Motors, Chrysler and Nissan Motor.
The automaker is offering the car-sharing service via its Free2Move brand and its partner Travelcar, a French car rental startup that PSA helped break into the U.S. market this year.
The service is currently being offered to travelers from Los Angeles airport, ahead of a wider U.S. rollout, PSA said in a statement. bit.ly/2oIKLji
PSA last month agreed to buy European rival Opel from General Motors. (Reporting by Shashwat Awasthi in Bengaluru; Editing by Sai Sachin Ravikumar)
rewrite: On April 6, the PSA Group, manufacturer of Peugeot, Citroën, and DS automobiles, announced the commencement of a car-sharing service in Los Angeles. This initiative signifies the corporation's re-entry into the United States market. Concurrently, PSA disclosed the establishment of a new operational division, PSA North America, to be headed by Larry Dominique, an experienced executive with a background at General Motors, Chrysler, and Nissan Motor. The car-sharing service is being deployed through the Free2Move brand in collaboration with Travelcar, a French car rental startup that PSA assisted in entering the U.S. market this year. Initially available to travelers from Los Angeles International Airport, the service precedes a broader national rollout, according to a company statement. This development follows PSA's recent agreement to acquire its European rival, Opel, from General Motors.

Law enforcement agencies are seeing an increase in cattle theft in parts of southwest Missouri. The Jasper County Sheriff's Office is getting proactive, taking steps to ensure it doesn't happen to local farmers.
It has happened 2 or 3 times in the past, thieves going on to Roger Hines' property at night and stealing cattle.
“There’s not a lot of profit in the cattle businesses anyway and if you lose a few times like that you're going to go backwards,” Hines, with J-H Cattle, says.
In the last week there have been 3 reports of cattle theft in Barry County, one incident where 16 cows were stolen.
Hines is glad the Jasper County Sheriff's Office is taking measures to keep it from happening here.
“If we see someone pulling farm equipment at 2 o’clock in the morning, we're going to stop them and make contact with them,” says Detective Tim Williams.
That method has worked in the past and since there's been suspicious activity in neighboring counties, Detective Williams says it is completely legal for a deputy to make a stop to identify the driver. Their main goal is simply to protect local farmers.
“So much of our job is reactive, someone has something stolen and we show up after the fact. This is a great chance for us to be proactive and work hand in hand with our farmers and prevent it from ever happening in our county,” says Williams.
One cow can be worth thousands of dollars so when people are coming and not just taking cattle but fuel and equipment too, the loss in revenue will add up.
“It adds up, it really does,” says Hines.
“It’s not only the initial loss of revenue, it’s all that revenue from the calves that they were going to have as well. So that’s potentially their livelihood and you're taking away their livelihood,” says Williams.
And local farmers are appreciative of the preventative measures the Sheriff’s Office is taking.
“I think they're doing a very good job, I think anybody that steals cattle around here, they're going to be sorry,” says Hines.
The Sheriff's Office has also posted tips on how farmers can protect themselves from thieves. To view them visit: https://www.facebook.com/jaspercountymissourisheriff/
rewrite:
Law enforcement agencies in southwestern Missouri are reporting a rise in incidents of cattle theft. In response, the Jasper County Sheriff’s Office has adopted a proactive stance aimed at preventing such crimes from affecting local agricultural operations. Historically, thefts have occurred on multiple occasions; for example, Roger Hines of J-H Cattle has experienced two or three nocturnal intrusions onto his property resulting in the loss of livestock. Hines notes that profit margins in cattle ranching are often narrow, and repeated losses of this kind can significantly set back a farming enterprise. This concern is underscored by recent criminal activity in the adjacent Barry County, where three separate thefts were reported within a single week, including one incident involving sixteen stolen cows.

Detective Tim Williams of the Jasper County Sheriff’s Office explains that deputies are now conducting stops of suspicious vehicles, such as those transporting farm equipment during early morning hours, to verify driver identification and intent. This approach, which has proven effective in the past, is considered a legally justifiable preventive measure, particularly given increased suspicious activity in neighboring jurisdictions. Williams emphasizes that the primary objective is to safeguard local farmers, stating, “So much of our job is reactive… This is a great chance for us to be proactive and work hand in hand with our farmers and prevent it from ever happening in our county.”

The economic impact of these thefts is substantial. Individual cattle can be valued at thousands of dollars, and losses are compounded when fuel and equipment are also taken. Hines observes that the financial consequences accumulate rapidly. Detective Williams further highlights the long-term repercussions, noting that theft deprives ranchers not only of immediate revenue but also of future income from the calves the stolen animals would have produced, thereby threatening the viability of their livelihoods.

Local agricultural producers have expressed appreciation for these preventive initiatives. Hines commended the Sheriff’s Office, remarking, “I think they’re doing a very good job,” and added that perpetrators would likely face consequences. In addition to increased patrols and vehicle stops, the Jasper County Sheriff’s Office has disseminated practical guidance to help farmers enhance security on their properties. These recommendations are publicly accessible through the office’s official social media channels.

During a white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia over the weekend, far-right demonstrators including neo-Nazis and Ku Klux Klan members were involved in violent clashes with counter-protesters.
A woman was killed and 19 other people were injured on Saturday when a car ran into a crowd protesting against the rally.
In the wake of the clashes, U.S. President Donald Trump was criticized from all sides for failing to explicitly condemn the white supremacy groups.
The violence comes at a time when hate groups are experiencing growth and higher prominence. According to research from the Southern Poverty Law Center released earlier this year, 917 hate groups were spread out across the U.S. in 2016 compared to 892 in 2015 and 784 in 2014.
Only 457 hate groups existed in the U.S. back in 1999, and their numbers hit an all-time high of 1,018 in 2011:
You will find more statistics at Statista
The organization identified 193 Black Separatist groups, as well as 130 active Ku Klux Klan groups. That is a sharp increase on 2014 when the country’s most infamous supremacist organization had 72 groups.
Last year, the U.S. also had 101 anti-Muslim and 100 White Nationalist organizations. 99 neo-Nazi groups were also identified, along with 78 categorized as being Racist Skinhead.

On Saturday, a vehicular assault on a crowd opposing the rally caused one fatality and injured nineteen individuals. Following these events, President Donald Trump faced broad criticism for his failure to explicitly condemn the white supremacist factions involved.

This violence occurs amidst a documented resurgence in the prevalence of hate groups. Research published earlier this year by the Southern Poverty Law Center indicates a trend of growth, with 917 such groups active across the United States in 2016, an increase from 892 in 2015 and 784 in 2014. This represents a significant rise from a base of 457 groups in 1999, though the figure remains below the peak of 1,018 recorded in 2011.

The Center's data for 2016 specified 193 Black Separatist groups and 130 active Ku Klux Klan chapters, the latter marking a sharp increase from the 72 chapters identified in 2014. The inventory further included 101 anti-Muslim organizations, 100 White Nationalist groups, 99 neo-Nazi groups, and 78 groups categorized as Racist Skinhead organizations.

Chelsea custodian Asmir Begovic insists that his team have enough experience to hold their nerve and get over the line to win the league title.
The Pensioners surrendered three points to Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, thus opening a window of opportunity for second placed Tottenham Hotspur.
Antonio Conte's team though still hold a four-point lead at the top of the table with six matches still left to be played in the season, and also look to have a more straight forward run-in.
And the 29-year-old goalkeeper feels that there are enough experienced player in the squad to guide them through and the general mood within the team is not nervy.
"It’s not getting nervy. We an experienced group of players who have been there and done this before. We have to just focus on getting better for the next game", Begovic told his club's official website.
"We’ll bounce back.
"There is still lots to play for this season.
"We just have to do our job.
"We still have a four-point advantage which at the beginning of the season we would have taken at this stage."
Chelsea now have four home games against Southampton, Middlesbrough, Watford and Sunderland, along with two away games against Everton and West Brom and Begovic feels that if they can win their games Tottenham's results won't matter.
"We are still in a good position and we just have to concentrate on ourselves.
"If we pick up the points we need it doesn’t matter what Spurs do."
rewrite:
Chelsea goalkeeper Asmir Begovic maintains that his squad possesses the requisite experience to maintain composure and secure the Premier League title. This statement follows Chelsea's defeat to Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, a result which has provided second-placed Tottenham Hotspur with a renewed opportunity. Despite this setback, Antonio Conte's side retains a four-point advantage at the summit of the table, with six fixtures remaining in the season. Furthermore, the team's schedule is perceived to be comparatively favourable.

Begovic, aged 29, emphasises that the squad contains a sufficient number of seasoned players to navigate the concluding phase of the campaign, asserting that the overall atmosphere within the team is not one of anxiety. "It’s not getting nervy. We are an experienced group of players who have been in this situation before. Our focus must simply be on improving for the next match," Begovic stated in an interview on the club's official website. He expressed confidence in the team's capacity to recover, noting, "There is still much to compete for this season. Our task is to fulfil our own responsibilities."

The goalkeeper highlighted that a four-point lead at this juncture would have been considered acceptable at the season's outset. Chelsea's remaining fixtures comprise four home matches against Southampton, Middlesbrough, Watford, and Sunderland, alongside two away fixtures at Everton and West Bromwich Albion. Begovic contends that if Chelsea successfully attain the necessary results, Tottenham's performances become irrelevant. "Our position remains strong, and we must concentrate solely on our own performances. Should we accumulate the required points, Tottenham's results will be immaterial," he concluded.

PERTH (miningweekly.com) – Gold miner Doray Minerals has reported record quarterly production from its Deflector mine, in Western Australia, exceeding company expectations.
Gold production during the March quarter reached 18 551 oz, with 966 t of copper also produced. This compared with the 16 810 oz of gold and 833 t of copper produced in the previous quarter from the Deflector mine.

The increase in production for the March quarter resulted from higher ore grades, as underground development at Deflector continued.
“This quarterly production at Deflector represents an annualised rate in the order of 75 000 oz of gold plus copper credits, which provide approximately 25% additional revenue. This overall performance is exceeding expectations on all metrics and is a significant improvement from what was contemplated in the life-of-mine model,” said Doray MD Leigh Junk on Tuesday.
Advertisement
During the quarter under review, Doray sold 18 240 oz of gold, generating revenues of A$38.7-million.
Junk noted that the quarterly results were further strengthened by Doray’s exploration success at the Da Vinci deposit, as well as new discoveries within the Deflector mine.
“We have successfully executed the turnaround strategy and Doray is now in the strongest position that it has been in recent years with its cash and debt positions,” he added.

Taro Aso speaks during the Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills, California, U.S., May 1, 2017. REUTERS/Lucy Nicholson
LOS ANGELES Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said the yen is vulnerable to rising political tensions over North Korea's missile program and development of nuclear weapons, and warned against extreme instability in the currency.
"We should always think about what the yen would be like if something happens in North Korea," Aso told a forum in Los Angeles on Monday.
The Japanese currency has been perceived as a safe-haven asset in recent years, which tends to be bought by global investors at a time of crisis.
Asked about such a view at the summit, Aso said while "the yen is said to be a safe-haven currency" the situation in North Korea made it "extremely unstable".
Tensions on the Korean peninsula have been high for weeks, driven by concerns that the North might conduct its sixth nuclear test in defiance of pressure from the United States and Pyongyang's sole major ally, China.
The dollar hit a one-month high against the yen, after U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin commented on the possibility of ultra long-term bond issuance. [FRX/]
Aso declined to comment on exchange rates, saying that currencies should be set by markets.
On trade negotiations with Washington, Aso said Japan and 10 other nations should push ahead with the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) trade deal, excluding the United States.
"Now that the U.S. has decided to withdraw from TPP, we are thinking that it might be better for the remaining eleven countries to go ahead with TPP," Aso said.
While expressing a cautious view on the U.S. stance of shifting towards bilateral trade negotiations, Aso said Washington will eventually find it better to rejoin TPP although it will take some time.
"Because the twelve countries worked together, concessions were given to the U.S.," he said. "It's not a fact that the U.S. will be able to gain more from bilateral framework than TPP."
(Reporting by Lawrence Delevingne; Writing by Tetsushi Kajimoto; Editing by Sam Holmes)
rewrite:
At the Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills, California, on May 1, 2017, Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso addressed the vulnerability of the yen to escalating geopolitical tensions surrounding North Korea's missile and nuclear weapons programs, cautioning against the potential for severe currency instability. Speaking at a forum in Los Angeles, Aso emphasized the necessity of considering the yen’s trajectory in the event of further developments in North Korea. Although the Japanese currency has been widely regarded as a safe-haven asset in recent years, attracting investment during periods of global crisis, Aso noted that the specific circumstances posed by North Korea render it "extremely unstable."

Persistent tensions on the Korean peninsula, fueled by concerns over a potential sixth nuclear test by North Korea despite international pressure from the United States and China, have contributed to this financial uncertainty. Concurrently, the U.S. dollar reached a one-month peak against the yen following remarks by U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin regarding the potential issuance of ultra long-term bonds. Minister Aso declined to comment directly on specific exchange rates, reiterating the principle that currency valuations should be determined by market forces.

Regarding international trade policy, Aso advocated for the eleven remaining nations to proceed with the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) agreement following the withdrawal of the United States. He expressed a cautious perspective on the U.S. shift toward bilateral trade negotiations, suggesting that Washington would ultimately find it more advantageous to rejoin the multilateral TPP framework, albeit after a considerable period. Aso argued that the original twelve-nation negotiations involved mutual concessions, and it is not evident that the United States would secure superior terms through bilateral agreements compared to the comprehensive TPP structure.

BERLIN, April 12 American artist Ryan Mendoza, who has moved the former house of late civil rights icon Rosa Parks from Detroit to Berlin, says he would like to return it to the United States one day.
Parks' refusal in 1955 to give up her bus seat in Alabama for a white passenger became a symbol of the U.S. civil rights movement. She later moved to Detroit, where the house she lived in faced demolition until her niece, Rhea McCauley, bought it.
McCauley paid $500 for the two-storey dwelling and in turn handed it over to Mendoza, who painstakingly stripped it into 2,000 pieces and paid $13,000 to move it to Berlin, where he has put it back together again outside his studio.
Now he wants to move the house back to the United States.
"This house really belongs in the United States," he told Reuters. "It doesn't belong here, but since it is here, it encourages more people to think about why it was on the demolition list."
Mendoza would also like to involve former U.S. first lady Michelle Obama in the project.
"It would be the perfect solution if Michelle Obama became the ambassador of this project," he said. "She has the courage and she totally convinced me when she said what was so obvious: that the White House was built by slaves."
Former U.S. President Barack Obama is due to join German Chancellor Angela Merkel in Berlin in May as part of celebrations to mark 500 years of Protestantism in Europe.
(Reporting by Ute Swart; Writing by Paul Carrel)
rewrite:
In an initiative to preserve a significant artifact of American civil rights history, American artist Ryan Mendoza has relocated the former Detroit residence of the late Rosa Parks to Berlin. He has expressed a definitive intention to repatriate the structure to the United States in the future. Rosa Parks’s act of civil disobedience in 1955, when she refused to relinquish her seat on a Montgomery, Alabama bus to a white passenger, established her as a seminal figure in the U.S. civil rights movement. Following her later relocation to Detroit, the house she occupied was slated for demolition. Its preservation was initiated by Parks’s niece, Rhea McCauley, who purchased the property for five hundred dollars.

McCauley subsequently entrusted the two-story dwelling to Mendoza. The artist meticulously deconstructed the house into approximately two thousand components, facilitated its transatlantic shipment at a personal cost of thirteen thousand dollars, and reconstructed it at his Berlin studio site. Mendoza now seeks to return the reassembled house to the United States. He contends, “This house truly belongs in the United States. While its current location in Berlin provokes necessary reflection on why such a historically significant property was ever designated for demolition, its proper context is within its country of origin.”

Furthermore, Mendoza has proposed involving former First Lady Michelle Obama in the preservation project, suggesting she would serve as an ideal ambassador. He cites her demonstrated courage and her poignant historical observation regarding the construction of the White House by enslaved individuals as compelling rationale. This development coincides with the scheduled visit of former President Barack Obama to Berlin in May, where he will join German Chancellor Angela Merkel in commemorating the quincentenary of Protestantism in Europe.

Single mother of two Alaina Chase says running a half-marathon at the Great Wall of China this month helped her overcome major mental health challenges.
Alaina, of Ngāti Kahungunu, was one of around 80 New Zealanders and Australians from the Influence Crew NZ who took part, most of them were Māori or Pasifika.
Chase started training for the event in May last year and says it changed her life.
“It was really hard, it was a struggle. There were times where I wanted to quit but the support from the crew and the trainer, it pushed me along because I went through so many personal life experiences leading up to the event,” says Chase.
“My kids were so proud when they saw their mummy with this big medal and that was the reason why I wanted to do this, to celebrate defeating mental illness and for my children as well”.
Chase completes the half marathon. Source: Alaina Chase
In 2014 Chase suffered from depression, anxiety, and public phobia during her second pregnancy.
“I tried many various therapies like counselling that unfortunately didn’t work and I ended up getting really low on life”.
Her doctor advised her to “give fitness a go” and after two weeks of doing exercise, she says she went back to normal.
“Since then, 2016, I’ve just been training and training, and I wanted to do all these marathons to celebrate that I’ve gotten better and defeated that dark place”.
The Influence Crew NZ performed a haka before the event started. Source: Doug Healy
Before the trip to China the team of 80, led by their trainer Doug Healey, kept in touch over Facebook. After the marathon they left China “as a family,” says Chase.
“Those five short days that I had in China was the best thing that I have ever done in my life. It was a life-changing experience and I’m definitely going back in 2020 to complete the full marathon”.

She commenced training in May of the preceding year, a process she describes as transformative.

Chase characterises the training as profoundly challenging. "The regimen was arduous and represented a considerable struggle. There were instances where I contemplated withdrawal, but the sustained support from the crew and the trainer proved instrumental in maintaining my progress. This was particularly vital given the numerous personal life experiences I navigated in the period leading to the event," she states. A primary motivation was her children: "My children expressed immense pride upon seeing their mother with this substantial medal. This outcome was a fundamental objective—to commemorate conquering mental illness and to achieve this for my children as well."

Her mental health challenges originated in 2014 during a second pregnancy, when she experienced depression, anxiety, and public phobia. "I engaged with multiple therapeutic interventions, including counselling, which unfortunately proved ineffective, culminating in a profoundly low period," Chase recalls. A medical professional subsequently recommended she "give fitness a go." Notably, after two weeks of consistent exercise, she observed a return to her normative state. "From that point in 2016 onward, I have dedicated myself to training. Pursuing these marathon events serves to celebrate my recovery and my departure from that dark period," she explains.

The cohort, led by trainer Doug Healey, maintained communication via Facebook prior to the journey. A significant cultural moment occurred when the Influence Crew NZ performed a haka before the race commenced. Reflecting on the experience, Chase notes the group departed China "as a family." She concludes, "Those five brief days in China represent the most meaningful undertaking of my life. It was a life-changing experience, and I fully intend to return in 2020 to complete the full marathon."
