The number of people in homeless accommodation has fallen slightly, from 6,035 in March to 5,963 in April, according to latest figures from the Department of Housing.
However, the figures represent a 19.9 per cent increase on the April 2017 figure of 4,972. They also come amid ongoing controversy over the removal of 578 people from the March figures compared with the February figures, under a reclassification exercise by the department.
There were also warnings on Wednesday from a number of charities that as many as 20,000 people were living in “hidden homelessness” – in other words, without their own homes and living in overcrowded conditions with families or friends.
The April figures show there were 3,689 children in 1,712 families in emergency homeless accommodation, compared with 3,646 children in 1,720 families in March. These figures represent a 36 per cent increase in the number of homeless children since April 2017, when there were 2,708, and a 31 per cent increase in the number of homeless families in the same year, up from 1,302.
Minister for Housing Eoghan Murphy said: “The report shows a reduction in the number of adults and families accessing emergency accommodation, which is welcome.
“I have said before that monthly reporting makes it difficult to identify any developing trends at an early stage, but from these figures it would seem that the presentation of new families in to emergency accommodation is stabilising.
“That said, while the number of families in emergency accommodation is down this month, a small number of families with a large number of children did present, meaning that the number of dependents has risen by 43.”
Fianna Fáil spokesperson on housing Darragh O’Brien said the State was “encouraging people and families into hidden homelessness by failing to provide pathways towards long-term housing solutions.
“Homelessness is sadly no longer just about those sleeping rough on our streets or the thousands of people living in temporary accommodation but also about the sizeable number hidden from our view and exempt from housing supports.
“Those who have found themselves to be without a place to call home, hidden from official statistics and not receiving support, can find themselves in precarious situations, including couch surfing.
rewrite:
Recent data released by the Department of Housing indicate a marginal decline in the number of individuals residing in homeless accommodation, from 6,035 in March to 5,963 in April. Notwithstanding this short-term decrease, the April 2024 figure represents a substantial 19.9 per cent increase relative to the corresponding period in 2017, when 4,972 persons were recorded. This statistical release occurs against a backdrop of ongoing scrutiny concerning the Department’s reclassification exercise, which resulted in the removal of 578 individuals from the March totals when compared with those reported in February.

Concurrently, several charitable organizations issued warnings on Wednesday that approximately 20,000 individuals may be experiencing "hidden homelessness." This term denotes persons who lack independent housing and instead reside in overcrowded conditions with family or friends, thereby remaining largely absent from official metrics.

A detailed examination of the April statistics reveals 3,689 children within 1,712 families residing in emergency homeless accommodation. This reflects a slight increase from the March figures of 3,646 children across 1,720 families. When assessed longitudinally, these numbers signify a 36 per cent rise in homeless children since April 2017, when 2,708 were documented, alongside a 31 per cent increase in homeless families over the same period, rising from 1,302.

In response to the report, Minister for Housing Eoghan Murphy acknowledged the reduction in adults and families accessing emergency accommodation as a positive development. He cautioned, however, that monthly reporting complicates the early identification of sustained trends. The Minister noted that the entry of new families into emergency accommodation appears to be stabilising, while highlighting a countervailing detail: despite the overall decrease in families this month, the arrival of a small number of families with many children resulted in a net increase of 43 dependents.

Fianna Fáil housing spokesperson Darragh O’Brien offered a more critical perspective, asserting that state policy is effectively channeling individuals and families into hidden homelessness by failing to establish viable pathways to permanent housing. He expanded the conventional definition of homelessness, arguing it now encompasses not only those sleeping rough or in temporary accommodation, but also a significant population obscured from official view and consequently ineligible for housing supports. These individuals, excluded from statistics and assistance, often find themselves in precarious living situations, including recurrent displacement among acquaintances’ residences.

WASHINGTON (AP) — A federal judge ruled Tuesday against the Trump administration's decision to end a program protecting some young immigrants from deportation, calling the Department of Homeland Security's rationale against the program "arbitrary and capricious."
U.S. District Judge John D. Bates in Washington wrote that the decision to rescind the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, known as DACA, "was unlawful and must be set aside."
Bates wrote that DHS' decision "was predicated primarily on its legal judgment that the program was unlawful. That legal judgment was virtually unexplained, however, and so it cannot support the agency's decision."
Bates gave DHS 90 days to "better explain its view that DACA is unlawful." If the department cannot come up with a better explanation, he wrote, it "must accept and process new as well as renewal DACA applications."
Advertisement
DACA allowed immigrants brought to the U.S. illegally as children, known as Dreamers, to stay and work legally under renewable permits. President Donald Trump announced last year that he would end the program started by President Barack Obama. It was officially rescinded in March, but DHS is continuing to issue renewals because of previous court orders.
Bates' ruling Tuesday night comes in a pair of cases whose lead plaintiffs are the NAACP and Princeton University. He is the third judge to rule against administration plans to end the program.
rewrite:
On Tuesday, a United States federal judge issued a ruling opposing the Trump administration's termination of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program. In his decision, U.S. District Judge John D. Bates of Washington, D.C. declared the Department of Homeland Security's (DHS) action "arbitrary and capricious," concluding that the rescission "was unlawful and must be set aside." The court found that DHS predicated its decision primarily on an insufficiently explained legal judgment that the program was unlawful, a rationale deemed inadequate to justify the agency's action.

Judge Bates has remanded the matter to DHS, providing a 90-day period to articulate a more robust justification for its position on DACA's illegality. Should the department fail to do so, the order stipulates that it must resume accepting and processing both new applications and renewal requests. The DACA program, established during the Obama administration, provides temporary protection from deportation and work authorization for certain undocumented immigrants who entered the United States as minors. The Trump administration announced its termination in September 2017, with an official rescission in March 2018, though court injunctions have compelled the continued processing of renewal applications.

This ruling, issued in litigation spearheaded by the NAACP and Princeton University, represents the third judicial decision against the administration's efforts to end DACA, maintaining a legal barrier to its discontinuation.

Another 14 individuals have been added to the list of people who Canada says are among those responsible for the deterioration of democracy in that country under the regime of Nicolas Maduro.
The sanctions essentially prohibit Canadians from doing business with people or entities on the list.

Freeland said the latest sanctions underline Canada's commitment to democracy and its rejection of the "fraudulent" presidential elections.

Preventing holiday buffet horrors! Whether you’re going to a party or hosting one, the last thing you want this season is to let bad food spoil someone’s merry good time.
Newswatch 16’s Ryan Leckey teamed up with experts Monday to take a closer look at food safety around the holidays.
Penn State Extension 4-H Educator Sandi Graham and Registered Dietitian/Author Julia Grocki offered several tips to help while hosting a party as well as which foods keep longer at room temperature vs. others.
The pair teamed up with Ryan at the Vintage Kitchen, a cooking school in Clarks Summit located behind Everything Natural.
The CDC estimates that “each year 48 million people get sick from a food-borne illness, 128,000 are hospitalized, and 3,000 die.”
Registered Dietitian Julia Grocki, who’s the author of “What You’re Looking For Is Not In The Fridge,” also shared tips on mindful eating. She wrote a book after losing 130 pounds.
Julia’s best advice to avoid packing on extra pounds over the holidays is “mindful eating.”
Julia described that as “paying attention to your physical hunger, make sure you’re not eating due to emotions and/or stress, and use all your senses while eating to see if you actually like the food you’re consuming.” For more tips on mindful eating, head here!
rewrite:

Whether one is hosting an event or attending as a guest, attention to proper food handling can avert health risks that may disrupt seasonal celebrations. Experts emphasize the importance of understanding which perishable items require strict temperature control and which foods are more stable at ambient conditions.

Such approaches can help mitigate seasonal weight gain while promoting a more intentional relationship with food.

When severe weather strikes, it's important to have a plan in place to keep everyone safe. That's the goal of a National Weather Service program called “StormReady.”
This Friday, Rhode Island is celebrating, because every city and town has earned the distinction. Rhode Island is the first state in the nation to have all of its cities and towns receive the “StormReady” designation. Friday afternoon, a ceremony was held at the Rhode Island State House with the Governor, National Weather Service officials, and representatives from communities across the state.
Back in 2012, only three of the state's communities had met the requirements. Today, all 39 cities and towns have done it.
Each community met specific storm preparation standards to be declared "StormReady." There are several requirements, all focused on the safety of residents.
Bob Thompson, the Meteorologist In Charge at the National Weather Service Weather Forecast Office in Taunton says, "'StormReady' is a program that the National Weather Service has to help communities to be better prepared in the event of hazardous weather."
The program has been in place for several years, and communities across the country are getting on board. The standards that have to be met for a city or town to be designated "StormReady" are rigorous.
Thompson says, "Requirements in terms of the communications [are] observation equipment in the area for weather information, the ability to disseminate information out when there is a warning or some sort of heads up of hazardous weather, and the plans that they have made for preparedness."
Businesses can also take part in the program. They can choose to become "StormReady Supporters" by developing plans to protect their employees during severe weather.
We here at ABC6 became StormReady Supporters back in 2012, and we are proud to say we are the only StormReady Supporter listed in the state of Rhode Island.
It remains our mission to keep you informed before and during severe weather.
©WLNE-TV / ABC6 2018
rewrite:
According to data from the National Weather Service (NWS), severe weather events in the United States result in an average of 500 fatalities and approximately $15 billion in damages annually. To mitigate these impacts, proactive community planning is essential. The NWS addresses this need through its "StormReady" program, which is designed to enhance public safety by ensuring localities establish robust preparedness protocols. Notably, the state of Rhode Island has achieved a significant milestone, becoming the first state in the nation to have every municipality earn the "StormReady" designation. A ceremony commemorating this accomplishment was held at the Rhode Island State House, attended by the Governor, NWS officials, and municipal representatives.

In 2012, only three Rhode Island communities had satisfied the program's criteria. Presently, all 39 municipalities have met the rigorous standards required for certification. As explained by Bob Thompson, Meteorologist in Charge at the NWS Weather Forecast Office in Taunton, the "StormReady" initiative assists communities in improving their preparedness for hazardous weather. The certification requirements are comprehensive, mandating specific capabilities. These include the deployment of observational equipment for monitoring weather conditions, establishing reliable communication systems to disseminate warnings and emergency information to the public, and formulating detailed preparedness plans.

The program, which has been operational for several years, also extends to private sector participation. Businesses can attain recognition as "StormReady Supporters" by developing and implementing plans to safeguard employees during severe weather. For instance, WLNE-TV/ABC6 obtained this supporter designation in 2012 and remains the only entity listed as such within Rhode Island. The overarching objective of these efforts, shared by both the NWS and participating organizations, is to ensure the timely dissemination of critical information before and during severe weather events, thereby enhancing public safety and resilience.

The makers of Ambien want no part in Roseanne Barr‘s career implosion.
In a series of tweets early Wednesday morning, Barr had blamed the sedative for prompting her to make a racist comment about former President Obama advisor Valerie Jarrett, which ultimately led ABC to cancel Roseanne on Tuesday.
RELATEDRoseanne Barr Blames Ambien for Racist Outburst in Erratic Twitter Spree
Barr’s first tweet read: “guys I did something unforgiveable so do not defend me. It was 2 in the morning and I was ambien tweeting — it was memorial day too — i went 2 far & do not want it defended — it was egregious Indefensible. I made a mistake I wish I hadn’t but…don’t defend it please.”
She cited Ambien again in a later post: “Not giving excuses for what I did(tweeted) but I’ve done weird stuff while on ambien — cracked eggs on the wall at 2am etc.”
Sanofi, the pharmaceutical company that produces Ambien, has since responded to Barr’s claims, stating that “racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication.”
People of all races, religions and nationalities work at Sanofi every day to improve the lives of people around the world. While all pharmaceutical treatments have side effects, racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication. — Sanofi US (@SanofiUS) May 30, 2018
rewrite:
The pharmaceutical manufacturer Sanofi has explicitly distanced itself from Roseanne Barr’s recent professional collapse, rejecting her attribution of racist remarks to the use of its sedative medication, Ambien. Following the cancellation of her television program by ABC on Tuesday, Barr engaged in a series of social media posts in the early hours of Wednesday, asserting that her consumption of Ambien precipitated a racist comment directed at Valerie Jarrett, a former advisor to President Barack Obama. In these posts, Barr described her actions as “unforgiveable” and “egregious,” citing instances of unusual nocturnal behavior while under the influence of the drug, including posting on social media and other erratic activities.

In an official corporate response via Twitter, Sanofi addressed these claims directly. The company emphasized its diverse global workforce and its mission to improve lives worldwide. It categorically stated that while all pharmaceutical treatments carry potential side effects, “racism is not a known side effect of any Sanofi medication.” This rebuttal serves to clearly separate the company’s product from Barr’s conduct and to affirm its stance against the implied connection between its medication and racially prejudiced behavior.

Oregon’s immediate post-Dillon Brooks future got considerably brighter Wednesday.
The Ducks received a commitment from Illinois State graduate transfer MiKyle McIntosh, he announced via social media.
The 6-foot-7 McIntosh was one of the most highly sought after grad transfers on the market after he put up 12.5 points and 5.6 rebounds per game last season for the Redbirds. He shot 41 percent from the field and 34.8 percent from 3-point range while also averaging 1.8 assists per night.
Like many grad transfers in June, McIntosh’s impact may be overstated some given the shallowness of the market and the rapid approach of fall semesters everywhere, but he’ll be able to bring quite a bit to the table for Dana Altman’s group, which is coming off the program’s first Final Four in over 70 years.
With Brooks, along with Jordan Bell and Tyler Dorsey, opting to leave early for the NBA, Oregon will certainly be in reload mode in 2017-18, and having McIntosh, as skilled and experienced player, will help bridge the gap as the program’s high-touted 2017 recruiting class finds its footing.
rewrite: The departure of Dillon Brooks from the University of Oregon's basketball program was followed by a significant development this Wednesday. MiKyle McIntosh, a graduate transfer from Illinois State University, publicly announced his commitment to Oregon via social media. The 6-foot-7 forward, who averaged 12.5 points and 5.6 rebounds per game last season while shooting 41.0 percent from the field and 34.8 percent from three-point range, was among the most pursued graduate transfers available. While the impact of such late-cycle transfers can sometimes be inflated due to limited remaining options and the imminent start of the academic year, McIntosh is positioned to contribute meaningfully to a team, coached by Dana Altman, that is returning from its first Final Four appearance in over seven decades. Following the early exits to the NBA of Brooks, Jordan Bell, and Tyler Dorsey, Oregon will necessitate a roster recalibration for the 2017-18 season. McIntosh, as a skilled and experienced player, will provide vital stability as the program's highly-regarded 2017 recruiting class acclimates to collegiate competition.

A former care home in Ventnor could be turned into ten two-bedroom apartments for over 60s who are ‘looking to downsize’.
Steephill Residential Home, built in 1924 to house nurses from the nearby hospital, closed in 2017. Somerset Care, who ran the home, had accrued losses of £140,000 during its final 12 months.
Planning permission for single house
The property was purchased by Richard Bendy after the home was closed and all the equipment removed.
Permission was granted in January to convert the former care home into a single house.
Revised application
The new application states:
“Since gaining planning permission the applicant has carried out extensive research into local housing need and carried out consultations with estate agents to determine the most appropriate use for the building.”
These investigations concluded there was significant demand for two bedroom apartments in Ventnor.
Over 60s covenant
However, the Isle of Wight Council imposed a covenant on the property which restricts occupation to the over 60s.
The plan will require two ‘relatively small extensions’ to the building.
The ground floor units will have their gardens immediately outside the apartments and the second floor apartments will have their own balconies. A landscaped area will provide a shared garden.
‘Substantial internal alternations’ required
During its time as a care home, the building was altered to provide a number of smaller spaces for toilets and bathrooms so ‘substantial internal alternations’ are required to open up spaces.
Thirteen car park spaces will be provided to compensate for the lack of a bus route through Undercliff Drive, including three spaces for visitors.
Full details can be found on the council’s Planning Website.
This article is from the BBC’s LDRS (Local Democracy Reporter Service) scheme, which OnTheWight is taking part in. Some additions by OnTheWight. Ed
Location map
View the location of this story.
rewrite:
A proposal has been submitted to convert a former residential care home in Ventnor into ten two-bedroom apartments intended for residents aged sixty and above who are seeking to downsize. The property, Steephill Residential Home, was originally constructed in 1924 to accommodate nurses from a neighbouring hospital and ceased operations in 2017. Its previous operator, Somerset Care, reported accumulated losses of £140,000 in the final year of service.

Following the home’s closure and the removal of its fixtures, the site was acquired by Richard Bendy. Initial planning consent was secured in January for the conversion of the building into a single dwelling. A revised application has since been filed, citing subsequent research into local housing needs and consultations with estate agents. This investigation identified a significant demand for two-bedroom apartments within Ventnor.

The proposed development is subject to a covenant imposed by the Isle of Wight Council, restricting occupancy exclusively to persons over sixty years of age. The plans necessitate two relatively modest extensions to the existing structure. The ground-floor apartments would have direct access to private gardens, while second-floor units would feature private balconies. A landscaped communal garden area is also proposed.

Substantial internal alterations are required to reconfigure the layout, as the building was previously adapted to incorporate numerous small en-suite facilities for its care home function. To mitigate the limited public transport access along Undercliff Drive, the proposal includes the provision of thirteen parking spaces, three of which are designated for visitors. Comprehensive details of the application are available on the local authority’s planning portal.

*This report originates from the BBC Local Democracy Reporter Service, with OnTheWight as a participating partner. Additional material has been provided by OnTheWight.*

Neighbors of the London apartment building torched in an inferno have sprung into action to help survivors of the fire, donating clothes, food and water and offering shelter.
Churches such as the Roman Catholic St. Francis of Assisi and a nearby mosque are serving as gathering points for donations for those who raced out of the burning building in the middle of the night, fleeing with little else than the clothes in which they slept.
Social media sites have also joined the effort, with some Londoners offering a space on their sofas for those affected by the blaze.
Marco Antoniades, who owns MGA Autos on Latimer Road, says "like in most places in England, people get together and help each other in times like this. That's what we're trying to do."
At least 12 people have died and 79 others were injured Wednesday in the blaze at Grenfell Tower.

Local business owner Marco Antoniades observed that the community's collective response reflects a broader characteristic of mutual aid during crises. The blaze, which occurred on Wednesday, resulted in a confirmed death toll of at least twelve individuals, with seventy-nine others injured.

SFA Semicon Philippines Corp. (SSPC) on Monday said it received P20.11 million from the government as part of an incentive program that allows for discounted power rates.
In a disclosure to the stock exchange on Tuesday, the local arm of one of Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd.’s South Korean suppliers said the amount is part of a discounted electricity incentive granted under Executive Order No. 856 (EO 856) and its lease agreement with Clark Development Corp.
EO 856 states that the government must support the power infrastructure requirements of Clark Freeport Zone. SSPC’s manufacturing plant is located at the Clark Freeport Zone in Pampanga.
The discounted power rate program is part of government’s efforts to support power-intensive industries to lure foreign investors to invest in the country.
SSPC said the payment will boost its cash and cash equivalents by some $390,000.
The company reported its net income declined by 71% to $1.83 million in 2017, amid stiff competition and a 29% rise in costs.
“The increased direct costs and relatively low average selling prices resulted in the 54% decline in gross profit declined from $15.40 million to $6.70 million during the year in review,” SSPC previously said.
A wholly owned subsidiary of Korea-based firm STS Semiconductor and Telecommunications Co., Ltd., SSPC has a business transaction agreement to supply its products to Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. until May 2019. — Janina C. Lim
rewrite:
SFA Semicon Philippines Corporation (SSPC) announced on Monday that it had received a payment of 20.11 million Philippine pesos from the government. This payment constitutes an incentive under a program providing discounted electricity rates. In a formal disclosure filed with the stock exchange on Tuesday, the company, which is the local subsidiary of a South Korean supplier to Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd., clarified that the incentive is granted pursuant to Executive Order No. 856 (EO 856) and its existing lease agreement with the Clark Development Corporation. EO 856 mandates governmental support for the power infrastructure needs of the Clark Freeport Zone, where SSPC’s manufacturing facility is situated in Pampanga.

This initiative to offer reduced power costs forms part of broader governmental efforts to assist energy-intensive industries and attract foreign direct investment. SSPC stated that the incentive payment would increase its cash and cash equivalents by approximately 390,000 US dollars. The company's financial performance in 2017 was characterized by a 71% decline in net income to 1.83 million US dollars, attributed to competitive pressures and a 29% increase in operational costs. SSPC had previously noted that elevated direct costs coupled with relatively low average selling prices precipitated a 54% reduction in gross profit, from 15.40 million to 6.70 million US dollars for the period under review. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of STS Semiconductor and Telecommunications Co., Ltd. of Korea, SSPC operates under a business transaction agreement to supply products to Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. through May 2019.

× Remembering the Revolutionary War Battle of Wyoming Like it Was Yesterday
WYOMING, Pa. — Part of the fight for our country’s independence took place in Luzerne County.
The Battle of Wyoming killed 300 patriots in 1778. Some of their descendants still live in the area and remember their past every Independence Day.
James Davenport carried on that meaningful family tradition with his 3-year-old son Luke at a special ceremony in Wyoming.
Davenport laid flowers for his great-grandfather times five–and Luke’s great-grandfather times six–who was killed in the Battle of Wyoming in 1778.
“We’re patriotic. We love our country, and people sacrificed to make it the way it is right now. We absolutely love it. We remember them, and we get choked up and we celebrate their sacrifice,” Davenport said.
Hundreds of people, most from Luzerne County, watched as the wreaths were placed at the Wyoming Monument. It really meant a lot for the descendants of revolutionary soldiers.
“Awesome doesn’t even describe it. To know that my ancestors literally died defending this land fighting for our freedom is phenomenal. There’s just no words,” Heather Ruseskas said.
The ceremony has become a family tradition for plenty of people around the Wyoming Valley on Independence Day.
“I’ve been coming here since I was a little kid. My father was bringing me when the Stegmeier men actually used to shoot real .22 blanks at that time,” Bob Chipego of Swoyersville said.
Even though the Battle of Wyoming was 240 years ago, people remembered it like it was just yesterday.
“I think history is our story. If we forget it, that’s a sad thing. I think it’s important to honor the people who fought and died here,” Revolutionary War reenactor Dave Hopfer said.
The actual Battle of Wyoming took place on July 3, 1778. People in Wyoming have been remembering their sacrifice for the last 140 years.
“They didn’t have weapons like we have today. I mean, they were lucky if they had a gun,” Wyoming Monument Association President Marcella Starr said.
No matter your story, people just hope you have a happy Fourth of July.
rewrite:
The Battle of Wyoming, a significant engagement in the American Revolutionary War, occurred in the Wyoming Valley of Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, on July 3, 1778. The conflict resulted in the deaths of approximately three hundred American patriots. Today, descendants of these individuals continue to reside in the region and observe Independence Day with ceremonies honoring this historical sacrifice. One such observance involves the laying of wreaths at the Wyoming Monument, an event that draws hundreds of attendees, predominantly from Luzerne County.

James Davenport, participating with his three-year-old son Luke, exemplifies the perpetuation of this familial tradition. Davenport paid tribute to a direct ancestor, his great-great-great-great-great-grandfather, who fell during the battle. Reflecting on the ceremony, Davenport stated, “We are patriotic. We love our country, and people sacrificed to make it what it is today. We remember them, and we are moved, and we celebrate their sacrifice.” For descendants like Heather Ruseskas, the emotional resonance is profound. “To know that my ancestors literally died defending this land fighting for our freedom is phenomenal. There are just no words,” she remarked.

This commemoration has evolved into an enduring tradition for many families in the Wyoming Valley. Bob Chipego of Swoyersville noted his lifelong attendance, recalling, “My father brought me when participants used to fire .22 caliber blanks.” The event underscores a collective commitment to historical memory. As Revolutionary War reenactor Dave Hopfer observed, “History is our story. If we forget it, that is a sad thing. It is important to honor the people who fought and died here.”

Formal remembrance at the site has been conducted for approximately 140 years. Marcella Starr, President of the Wyoming Monument Association, contextualized the participants’ valor, noting, “They did not have weapons like we have today. They were fortunate to have a gun.” The ceremony serves not only as a specific act of remembrance but also as a broader affirmation of national heritage and gratitude, aligning with the communal spirit of the Fourth of July.

Today, salmon lovers across the country can order sockeye salmon from Pride of Bristol Bay and have it delivered directly to their homes and businesses. A portion of proceeds from every order placed will go directly to efforts to protect Bristol Bay from the Pebble Mine proposal.
"Trout Unlimited is thrilled to partner with Pride of Bristol Bay to bring a little bit of this iconic place into homes and onto grills nationwide," said Nelli Williams of Trout Unlimited. "By purchasing salmon from Pride of Bristol Bay, consumers can feel good about where their salmon comes from, while also supporting critical work to ensure that this national treasure is around for future generations to use and enjoy."
The company, founded by fisherman Matt Luck in 2015, will donate 10 percent of all profits to Trout Unlimited's Save Bristol Bay program. The program works to safeguard Bristol Bay, Alaska's pristine watershed and wild salmon populations from the proposed Pebble Mine, which if built, would be a massive, toxic open-pit mine in the headwaters of Bristol Bay's most productive salmon rivers.
"Whether you fish with a net or a rod and reel, we all understand the importance of clean water and intact fish habitat in Bristol Bay. Pebble is a threat to local communities, the commercial fishing industry and a hunting and fishing paradise," said Williams. "This partnership is one of many examples of commercial and sport fishermen standing together to advocate for Bristol Bay's fisheries and clean water. We hope people will join us by ordering salmon and voting with their forks to safeguard our fisheries and communities."
To learn more about Pride of Bristol Bay and order a box of sustainable Bristol Bay Alaska sockeye delivered to your door, visit: www.prideofbristolbay.com. To learn more about Trout Unlimited's efforts to protect Bristol Bay, Alaska visit: www. savebristolbay.org.
rewrite:
Consumers across the United States may now procure sockeye salmon directly from Pride of Bristol Bay for delivery to residential or commercial addresses. A percentage of revenue from each purchase is allocated to initiatives opposing the Pebble Mine project in Bristol Bay.

Nelli Williams of Trout Unlimited expressed the organization’s enthusiasm for the collaboration: “Trout Unlimited is pleased to partner with Pride of Bristol Bay in making this iconic resource accessible to households nationwide. Consumers who purchase this salmon can derive satisfaction from a transparent sourcing process while concurrently contributing to essential conservation efforts designed to preserve this national treasure for future utilization and enjoyment.”

Founded in 2015 by fisherman Matt Luck, the enterprise commits ten percent of its total profits to Trout Unlimited’s Save Bristol Bay campaign. This program is dedicated to protecting the pristine watershed and wild salmon populations of Bristol Bay, Alaska, from the proposed Pebble Mine. This project entails the construction of an extensive open-pit mine within the headwaters of the region’s most productive salmon rivers, posing a significant threat of toxic contamination.

Williams further noted, “From commercial netters to recreational anglers, there is a shared recognition of the necessity for clean water and undisturbed fish habitat in Bristol Bay. The Pebble Mine represents a direct threat to local communities, the commercial fishing industry, and a renowned sporting paradise. This partnership exemplifies the unified advocacy of commercial and sport fishing interests in defense of Bristol Bay’s fisheries and water quality. We encourage public support through purchasing salmon, thereby casting a consumer vote for the protection of these fisheries and communities.”

For further information on Pride of Bristol Bay and to order sustainably harvested Bristol Bay sockeye salmon, visit www.prideofbristolbay.com. Details regarding Trout Unlimited’s conservation initiatives in Bristol Bay are available at www.savebristolbay.org.

Rahanna Bisseret Martinez, a 13-year-old from Oakland, finished a close second Friday night during the Season 1 finale of “Top Chef Junior.”
Martinez was edged out by 14-year-old Chef Owen Pereira of Baltimore, MD. in the gastronomic showdown.
“Top Chef Junior,” a kid-friendly spin-off of Bravo’s hit show “Top Chef,” debuted in October on the Universal Kids channel and started with some of the best chefs aged 11-14 from across the country. Over the past three months Owen and Rahanna have been put to the test in professional challenges like “restaurant wars” and the “quickfire challenge” as they rose to the top of the pack.
“These young chefs were incredible all season long, cooking their hearts out and giving even seasoned chefs like myself a run for our money with their talent,” said “Top Chef Junior” head judge Curtis Stone. “Owen has shown incredible talent all season long and we’re so proud to name him the first ever ‘Top Chef Junior.'”
The season finale brought Owen and Rahanna together in a head-to-head challenge in which they were required to cook a three-course meal representing their past, present, and future. “Top Chef” winner Brooke Williamson and alum Shirley Chung, along with fellow “Top Chef Junior” Season 1 contestants Henry and Milo, served as the sous chefs for the finalists.
The meal was judged by special guests, including two-Michelin star chef Josiah Citrin, chef Richard Blais, recurring guest judges Gail Simmons, Tiffany Derry, and Antonia Lofaso, as well as host Vanessa Lachey and head judge Stone.
In a close deliberation, Owen was awarded the coveted title of “Top Chef Junior” and a $50,000 cash prize.
According to an NBC online site, Rahanna first learned how to cook by watching American chef and TV personality Julia Child. Child, she says, was an inspiration to her and showed amateur chefs could cook just as well as professionals, something she hopes to do with children her age one day.
Throughout the show she showcased her love and passion for Mexican and Louisiana cuisine, exploring different depths of flavor and complex elegant styles.
“I really liked all the dishes I made because of the way I interpreted them. I wanted to show that Mexican and Louisiana food could be regal and refined,” she said.

OPPORTUNISTIC sports fans are turning parts of East Perth into a makeshift parking lot during Optus Stadium events, prompting anger from some nearby residents.
The Sunday Times photographed cars parked bumper to bumper along Summers Street and surrounds ahead of the Perth Scorchers semifinal BBL clash with Hobart on Thursday.
With few parking restrictions in place, stadium visitors are using the area to stash their cars before walking across the Windan Bridge. City of Vincent chief executive Len Kosova confirmed the council had received “a small number of complaints from residents” regarding the influx of vehicles on event days.
He said rangers were yet to issue any infringement notices but introducing tougher parking restrictions was under consideration.
“The city’s rangers have been monitoring car parking practices during the recent stadium open day, ODI and BBL semifinal,” Mr Kosova said.
“The city will continue to assess the local impact of Optus Stadium events prior to considering if further parking restrictions are warranted.”
Camera Icon Bumper-to-bumper parking in East Perth. Picture: Ross Swanborough
Mr Kosova said he had not raised the issue with either Optus Stadium management or the State Government.
Meanwhile, Transport Minister Rita Saffioti has ruled out adding stops at Perth Stadium station to the regular Transperth timetable in the short term, citing budgetary constraints.
“As part of the stadium budget there was no funding allocated by the former government to make the Perth Stadium station a stop for all services,” she said. “Additional funding would be required to purchase the additional rail cars and to fund the additional costs of operating the station. I would like to see the station open in the future for all services, in particular as activity increases around the stadium.”
Perth Stadium Steering Committee minutes, obtained under the Freedom of Information Act, reveal Perth Stadium station was originally planned to operate year round but that adding the station to the regular timetable would require additional carriages and could result in the closure of a station on the Armadale line.
rewrite:
The precinct surrounding Optus Stadium in East Perth is experiencing ad hoc vehicular congestion during major events, as spectators opportunistically utilize residential streets for parking. This phenomenon, observed prior to events such as the recent Perth Scorchers BBL semifinal, involves vehicles parked contiguously along thoroughfares including Summers Street. Subsequently, attendees proceed on foot via the Windan Bridge to the stadium. This practice has elicited formal complaints from a segment of the local community regarding the influx of vehicles and the resultant disruption.

Municipal authorities have acknowledged the issue. Len Kosova, Chief Executive of the City of Vincent, confirmed receipt of a limited number of resident complaints. While rangers have monitored parking compliance during several major events, including a stadium open day, a One Day International cricket match, and the aforementioned BBL semifinal, no infringement notices have been issued to date. The council is presently evaluating the local impact of stadium events and is considering the potential implementation of more stringent parking controls. Mr. Kosova noted that this matter has not yet been formally escalated to Optus Stadium management or to state-level government officials.

Concurrently, the integration of Perth Stadium station into the standard Transperth rail timetable presents a separate logistical and fiscal challenge. Transport Minister Rita Saffioti has indicated that no immediate changes are planned, citing budgetary limitations inherited from the previous administration. The original stadium budget did not allocate funds for the station to function as a routine stop for all train services. Operationalizing the station year-round would necessitate significant additional expenditure for the procurement of extra rail carriages and ongoing operational costs. Historical planning documents, obtained through Freedom of Information requests, reveal that while year-round operation was initially envisioned, integrating the station into the regular network could potentially necessitate the closure of an existing station on the Armadale line due to operational constraints. Minister Saffioti expressed a desire to see the station fully operational in the future, particularly as development activity in the stadium precinct intensifies.

The Championships have increased the overall prize money for the 7th year in the row, to a whopping £34 million
Wimbledon have increased their overall prize money for the 7th year in the row, to a whopping total of £34 million. The figure is a £2.4 million increase from last year’s total of £31.6 million.
Advertisement
The 7.6 per cent increase also ensures that Wimbledon remains one of the most lucrative tennis grand slams in the world.
How much will the Champions of Wimbledon win?
Competitors in the single titles category have the potential to earn the most. Winners of this year’s Wimbledon singles titles (men’s and women’s) will each pocket a record £2.25 million in prize money, while runners up in the singles title will also take home £1.125 million each.
For each stage you earn a significant chunk more. If you get through from the second round to the fourth round you’ll take home an extra £100,000, with a jump from £63,000 to £163,000. At the third round there’s a cool £100,000 on offer. Quarter-finalists win £281,000, and semi-finalists pocket £562,000.
Winners in the doubles titles will each receive a cheque for £450,000, while the runners up will also win £225,000.
How much do you earn for competing at all?
Even qualifying for a singles title at Wimbledon is lucrative, as competitors who reach the first round of the singles titles know that they’re entitled to at least £39,000 each – even if they fall at the first hurdle. There’s no prize for the first round of the doubles titles, but there’s £11,500 each on offer at the second round.
What about the other titles?
Winners in the Wheelchair event take home £40,000. Competitors must get through to the quarter-finals for the chance of winning any cash – in this case, £8,500.
Mixed Doubles champions get £110,000 for their trouble while the runner’s up take home £55,000.
For a full break down of Wimbledon 2018’s prize money click here.
Advertisement
Wimbledon 2018 will be as usual screened by the BBC, who are screening the tournament in Ultra HD for the first time. This year’s Championships are held from Monday 2nd July – Sunday 15th July.

This represents a £2.4 million rise, or 7.6 per cent, from the 2017 total of £31.6 million. This consistent upward trajectory further cements Wimbledon's status as one of the most financially rewarding Grand Slam tournaments in professional tennis.

The most substantial rewards are reserved for the singles champions. The 2018 men's and women's singles title winners will each receive a record £2.25 million. The runners-up in these categories will be awarded £1.125 million each. Prize money scales progressively through the tournament stages. For instance, progression from the second round to the fourth round yields a significant increase of £100,000, from £63,000 to £163,000. Competitors reaching the third round are awarded £100,000, while quarter-finalists and semi-finalists will earn £281,000 and £562,000, respectively.

In doubles competitions, the winning pair will share £900,000, amounting to £450,000 per player. The runners-up will share £450,000, or £225,000 each. Even initial participation is financially notable; any player qualifying for the main draw of the singles competition is guaranteed a minimum of £39,000 for a first-round appearance. While no prize money is awarded for a first-round exit in the doubles, participants reaching the second round will receive £11,500 each.

Prize allocations extend to other events. The wheelchair singles champions will earn £40,000, with prize money commencing at the quarter-final stage, where participants receive £8,500. In mixed doubles, the champion pair will share £110,000, with the runners-up dividing £55,000.

The 2018 Championships will be held from Monday, 2nd July, to Sunday, 15th July. As in previous years, live coverage will be provided by the BBC, which will broadcast the tournament in Ultra High Definition for the first time.

JACKSONVILLE, N.C. (WNCT) — Out of 20 million asthma sufferers nationwide, seven million are kids who miss dozens of days of school due to their symptoms.
The Onslow County Health Department hopes to change that.
It’s offering a new consultation service using asthma education kits.
The board of commissioners approved the asthma education kits for $4,000 last year.
Inside of them are common allergens that could trigger asthma; everything from dust mites in stuffed animals, to exhaled smoke from a cigarette and roaches.
Nurses with the initiative will travel to local schools and offer private consultations with families to help them put their health back in their own hands.
“Our main goal is to reduce asthma-related hospitalizations, reduce school missed days or work days as well as reduce the medical care costs and emergency visits,” Mary Jane Burlaza, a public health nurse, said.
Health officials say it will also keep the cost of hospital bills down.
In Onslow County in 2014, 137 patients were hospitalized from asthma with a cost per patient of $4,000.
If you’d like to make an appointment for the service call the health department at 910-347-2154.
rewrite:
In the United States, asthma affects an estimated twenty million individuals, including seven million children whose symptoms frequently result in numerous absences from school. The Onslow County Health Department has initiated a program aimed at mitigating this issue through a novel consultation service utilizing specialized asthma education kits. These kits, approved for $4,000 by the county board of commissioners in the preceding year, contain representations of common allergens known to trigger asthma attacks. These range from dust mites, as found in stuffed animals, to tobacco smoke and cockroach allergens.

Public health nurses involved in the initiative will visit local schools to provide private family consultations, empowering individuals to manage their health more effectively. According to Public Health Nurse Mary Jane Burlaza, the primary objectives are to reduce asthma-related hospitalizations, decrease missed days of school or work, and lower associated medical costs and emergency department visits. Health officials further note the program's potential to reduce overall hospitalization expenses. This is particularly relevant for Onslow County, where in 2014 alone, 137 asthma-related hospitalizations occurred at an approximate cost of $4,000 per patient. Families interested in scheduling a consultation may contact the health department at 910-347-2154.

Stidham Named Auburn Starting Quarterback
by Rashad Snell
Jarrett Stidham will be Auburn’s starting quarterback for the opener against Georgia Southern.
Tigers coach Gus Malzahn announced in a Twitter post Monday that he had just informed the team of the decision. Malzahn posted that “the team is excited for Jarrett and ready for the season.”
The 6-foot-3, 214-pound sophomore enrolled in January and beat out returning starter Sean White. Auburn opens Sept. 2 at Jordan-Hare Stadium.
Stidham was the offensive MVP in Auburn’s spring game, when White was sidelined while recovering from surgery to repair a broken right forearm sustained in the Sugar Bowl loss to Oklahoma.
Stidham passed for 1,165 yards and 12 touchdowns as a freshman at Baylor in 2015. He arrived in Auburn after spending last fall at a junior college with no football program.

The 6-foot-3, 214-pound transfer secured the position over returning starter Sean White, having enrolled at Auburn in January. Stidham previously demonstrated his collegiate ability at Baylor University in 2015, passing for 1,165 yards and 12 touchdowns, and spent the intervening fall semester at a junior college without a football program. After firing Slimbridge to an opening day 2-1 victory over Paulton Rovers, Marley Thomas has been challenged by manager Freddy Ward to reach a tally of 20 goals for the season, writes Johnny Morton .
Thomas came off the bench to score two in the space of four minutes to secure all three points for the Swans and kick their Division One West of the Southern League campaign off to the perfect start.
Ward has called on other players who find themselves out of the starting team to follow in Thomas' example and show him why they should be playing.
"He will be very important this season," said Ward.
"I said to him during pre-season that I wanted him to get to 20 goals this season, and he agreed he needed to add more goals to his game.
"He started on the bench because he got a little knock a couple of weeks ago. I asked people who were left out to show me why they should be starting when they come on, and he did exactly that."
The Thornhill Park outfit are one of six local teams in the league, alongside Cinderford Town, Bishops Cleeve, Shortwood United, Cirencester Town and Evesham United.
Ward says the local derbies make for an exciting season.
"A lot of people know each other having played against or with each other before," he added.
"The more local derbies, the better for the area"
It will be Cirencester who provide the opposition on Wednesday night, with Charlie Griffin's side aiming to bounce back from a 2-0 defeat against Taunton Town.
Ward is familiar with The Centurions, having enjoyed a spell with them in the past.
"On paper, they have a very good side," he said.
"I had a couple of seasons with Cirencester and I know a couple of their players that are still there now from when I was there, and I know they will be strong.
"They didn't get off to the best start, but they were playing Taunton who will probably be looking for promotion this season.
"They'll be looking to get some points on the board so it'll be a tough game and we are looking forward to it."

CARDIFF, Wales — When Warren Gatland bumped into Wales Rugby Union chief executive Martyn Phillips on Friday, the coach predicted Wales would beat Scotland by 20 points.
Gatland said Phillips was shocked.
The rest of the rugby world was, too, on Saturday when Gatland’s side whipped Scotland by 27 points, 34-7, to open the Six Nations.
Wales was the bettors’ underdog, but to make up for eight British Lions out injured, Gatland picked 12 Scarlets and started 10.
Almost 10 years to the day after he started 13 Ospreys in his first match as Wales coach and beat England at Twickenham, Gatland’s gamble on the Scarlets also paid off.
Their self-belief, attacking attitude, and understanding made up for more than 500 caps’ worth of talent being injured.
“It was an afternoon I was expecting with the way we have trained the last couple of weeks,” Gatland said.
“There was definitely a quiet confidence in the squad, they have been outstanding in their preparation, and we went into the game expecting to win reasonably comfortably.”
Wales scored four tries, bombed at least three more, and kept Scotland scoreless until the 78th minute.
“Apart from the soft try at the end our defence was outstanding,” he said. “Getting the bonus point was pleasing as well.”
Wales will be the underdog again next week when it goes to Twickenham to face the two-time defending champion but Gatland expects to have at least two of his Lions backs available.
Liam Williams will take a full part in training on Monday after an abdominal problem, and George North should be available after tight hamstrings.
“I’ve said the draw was great for us. We’ve got England and Ireland away (in the next two rounds),” he said.
“We’ve often had pretty tough opening encounters so getting Scotland at home first up for us was a great opportunity. There were a lot of players who were involved last year (in the loss at Murrayfield) and they wanted to make up for that disappointment.
“Next week, we go to a venue where we’ve had a lot of success in the last 10 years.”
At Twickenham, Gatland can count three wins on his watch. But he wasn’t ready to predict the result next Saturday.

Gatland informed Phillips of his prediction that Wales would defeat Scotland by a twenty-point margin, a forecast which reportedly surprised the executive. This sentiment was shared broadly across the rugby community on Saturday, when the Welsh team surpassed that prediction, securing a decisive 34-7 victory, a twenty-seven-point differential, in their opening match of the Six Nations Championship.

Despite entering the contest as underdogs in betting markets, Gatland’s strategic selection compensated for the absence of eight injured British and Irish Lions players. He opted to include twelve players from the Scarlets regional team, with ten in the starting lineup. This decision echoed a similar gamble taken almost precisely a decade prior, when, in his first match as Wales coach, he started thirteen players from the Ospreys region and defeated England at Twickenham. The reliance on the Scarlets contingent proved equally successful. Their collective confidence, offensive mindset, and cohesive understanding effectively offset the loss of over five hundred combined international caps due to injury.

Gatland noted that the performance aligned with expectations developed during a rigorous two-week training period. He described a quiet confidence within the squad, praising their exemplary preparation and stating the team anticipated a reasonably comfortable victory. The match saw Wales score four tries, with several additional opportunities missed, while maintaining a defensive stronghold that prevented Scotland from scoring until the 78th minute. Gatland highlighted the exceptional defensive effort, aside from a conceded try late in the match, and expressed satisfaction at securing a bonus point for scoring four tries.

Wales is anticipated to be the underdog once again in the subsequent round, facing two-time defending champion England at Twickenham. However, Gatland expects to reintegrate at least two of his Lions backs, with Liam Williams returning to full training following an abdominal issue and George North likely available after managing tight hamstrings. Gatland reflected that the tournament draw was favorable, providing an initial home fixture against Scotland—a significant opportunity following a prior loss at Murrayfield—before challenging away matches against England and Ireland. He acknowledged the team’s historical success at Twickenham over the past decade, where he has overseen three victories, but declined to offer a specific prediction for the forthcoming encounter.

INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Andrew Luck threw a 1-yard touchdown pass to Jack Doyle with 9 seconds left Sunday to give the Indianapolis Colts a 24-20 victory over Jacksonville in their season finale.
Indy (8-8) went 75 yards in 84 seconds with no timeouts to avoid its first losing season since 2011, sending retiring linebacker Robert Mathis out with a win in his final NFL game.
Jacksonville (3-13) matched the second-worst record in franchise history after blocking a punt with 1:54 to go and breaking a 17-17 tie with 1:33 left.
Instead, Luck took the Colts right downfield for the score. He finished 24 of 40 with 321 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in a game full of milestones.
Mathis extended his league record of strip-sacks to 41 in the fourth quarter, two days after announcing he would retire.

rewrite: In a dramatic conclusion to the regular season, quarterback Andrew Luck connected with tight end Jack Doyle on a one-yard touchdown pass with nine seconds remaining, securing a 24-20 victory for the Indianapolis Colts over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The decisive drive covered 75 yards in 84 seconds without the benefit of timeouts, allowing Indianapolis (8-8) to avert a losing season for the first time since 2011. The win also marked a triumphant finale for retiring linebacker Robert Mathis. Despite a late surge that included a blocked punt and a go-ahead field goal with 1:33 remaining, Jacksonville (3-13) concluded with one of the poorest records in franchise history. Luck’s performance included 321 passing yards and two touchdowns. Mathis further extended his NFL career record for forced fumbles via sack to 41 during the contest.

TVC E. It was reported via AFP that, Popular independent Gambian radio station Teranga FM was yesterday Sunday (1st of January 2017) ordered to cease operations by national security agents for unspecified reasons.
The station, which translates news from Gambian papers into local languages, has previously been silenced and in 2015 its manager was slapped with sedition and “publication of false news” charges for privately sharing a provocative photo of President Yahya Jammeh.
“Four National Intelligence Agency operatives and one police officer in uniform came to the radio station this afternoon (Sunday) around 2:30 pm and told us to stop broadcasting,” a staff member told AFP on condition of anonymity.
“They said they have been ordered by the director general of NIA, Yankuba Badjie, to tell us to stop broadcasting with immediate effect. We asked them the reason for their action, but they said they are only acting on executive orders and do not know the reason why the radio should stop broadcasting,” he added.
A security source said no one had been arrested but could not say why the radio station was ordered off the air. “We only asked them to stop broadcasting and they cooperated with us. They have stopped broadcasting since in the afternoon,” the source told AFP.
The radio station was not broadcasting Sunday evening, according to an AFP correspondent.
Station manager Alagie Ceesay was arrested by the country’s secret police in July 2015 on charges of sedition and “publication of false news” relating to allegations that he distributed images by mobile phone of a gun pointed at a picture of Jammeh.
Ceesay escaped from hospital where he was being treated in mid-April last year while on trial for sedition.
Jammeh, who has ruled the small west African country with an iron fist since taking power in a bloodless coup in 1994, lost December’s presidential election but has rejected the results and filed a court challenge.
He is regularly accused of rights abuses and repression of the media.
The Gambia ranked 145 out of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders’ 2016 World Press Freedom Index, pointing to “a climate of terror around anything remotely to do with journalism”.
The post Gambia authorities shut independent radio station appeared first on COMPLETE ENTERTAINMENT.
rewrite:
On January 1, 2017, the Gambian independent radio broadcaster Teranga FM was ordered to cease all broadcasting operations by state security personnel, as reported by Agence France-Presse (AFP). The directive, issued without a publicly specified rationale, was delivered on a Sunday afternoon by a contingent comprising four operatives from the National Intelligence Agency (NIA) and one uniformed police officer. According to an anonymous staff member interviewed by AFP, the officials stated they were acting under the direct orders of NIA Director General Yankuba Badjie and could provide no further justification for the shutdown, citing only that they were executing an executive mandate. A separate security source confirmed to AFP that the station complied with the order, halting its broadcasts that afternoon, and that no arrests were made at that time. An AFP correspondent later verified that the station remained off the air that evening.

This incident represents a continuation of state pressure against the station, which is noted for translating news from Gambian newspapers into local languages. Teranga FM had previously been subjected to silencing measures. In July 2015, its manager, Alagie Ceesay, was arrested by secret police on charges of sedition and "publication of false news." The charges stemmed from allegations that he privately distributed via mobile phone a provocative image depicting a firearm aimed at a portrait of President Yahya Jammeh. Ceesay, who was on trial for sedition, subsequently escaped from a medical facility where he was receiving treatment in April 2016.

The context for these actions is the extended authoritarian rule of President Yahya Jammeh, who assumed power in a 1994 coup and has maintained control through repressive measures. Despite losing the presidential election in December 2016, Jammeh contested the results, initiating a legal challenge. His regime has been frequently criticized for human rights violations and the systematic repression of media freedom. This environment is reflected in The Gambia's position at 145 out of 180 countries in Reporters Without Borders' 2016 World Press Freedom Index, which described a pervasive "climate of terror" surrounding journalistic activities in the country.

St. Matthew’s Music Guild opens its 33rd series of concerts with a program of music by Kodaly, Saint-Saens and Mozart at 8 p.m. on Friday, October 13, at St. Matthew’s Church, 1031 Bienveneda.
Internationally renowned pianist Inna Faliks will be the guest soloist. Called “adventurous and passionate” by The New Yorker, the Ukrainian-born pianist has established herself as one of the most exciting, committed, communicative and poetic artists of her generation.
Faliks is professor of piano at the UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music, where she also serves as chair of the Piano Department. After her acclaimed teenage debuts at the Gilmore Festival and with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, she has performed on many of the world’s great stages, with numerous orchestras, in solo appearances, and with conductors such as Leonard Slatkin and Keith Lockhart.
Interim music director and conductor Tomasz Golka won the 2003 Eduardo Mata International Conducting Competition. He has guest-conducted throughout the world, including the Seattle Symphony, Spoleto USA Festival Orchestra, Warsaw Philharmonic, and Baden Baden Philharmonic, among others. He has served as Chief Conductor of the Colombia National Symphony in Bogotà, Music Director of the Lubbock Symphony Orchestra, and is currently Music Director of the Riverside Philharmonic.
The concert will begin with Zoltan Kodaly’s colorful Dances of Galánta, a work from 1933 based on folk music from Galánta (now part of Slovakia) that has become the composer’s most frequently performed piece and remains an audience favorite.
Next on the program is the fiery Second Symphony of Camille Saint-Saëns. Known as the “French Mendelssohn,” Saint-Saëns draws obvious parallels in this work with Mendelssohn’s famous “Italian” Symphony.
The program concludes with Ms. Faliks as soloist in Mozart’s beloved Piano Concerto No. 20, a work that audiences are sure to recognize from the film Amadeus.
Admission is $35 or Music Guild Season Pass. The Music Guild offers season passes which are good for all concerts for as little as $200. For more information, visit the Music Guild website at MusicGuildOnline.org or call (310) 573-7421.

The St. Matthew’s Music Guild inaugurates its thirty-third concert season on Friday, October 13, at 8:00 p.m. The performance will be held at St. Matthew’s Church, located at 1031 Bienveneda, and will feature compositions by Zoltán Kodály, Camille Saint-Saëns, and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.

The distinguished guest soloist for the evening is the internationally acclaimed pianist Inna Faliks. Hailed by *The New Yorker* as “adventurous and passionate,” the Ukrainian-born artist has secured her reputation as one of the most compelling, dedicated, and poetically communicative pianists of her generation. Professor of Piano and Chair of the Piano Department at the UCLA Herb Alpert School of Music, Faliks launched her career with celebrated teenage debuts at the Gilmore Festival and with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra. She has since performed on prestigious international stages, appearing with major orchestras, in solo recitals, and under the baton of conductors including Leonard Slatkin and Keith Lockhart.

The ensemble will be led by interim music director and conductor Tomasz Golka, recipient of the 2003 Eduardo Mata International Conducting Competition. Maestro Golka has guest-conducted widely, with engagements encompassing the Seattle Symphony, Spoleto USA Festival Orchestra, Warsaw Philharmonic, and Baden Baden Philharmonic. His previous appointments include Chief Conductor of the Colombia National Symphony in Bogotá and Music Director of the Lubbock Symphony Orchestra; he currently serves as Music Director of the Riverside Philharmonic.

The program commences with Kodály’s vibrant *Dances of Galánta* (1933), a work rooted in the folk music of Galánta, now in Slovakia, which stands as the composer’s most frequently performed composition and a perennial favorite. This will be followed by Camille Saint-Saëns’s vigorous Symphony No. 2. Often termed the “French Mendelssohn,” Saint-Saëns invites clear comparison in this symphony to Mendelssohn’s renowned “Italian” Symphony. The concert will conclude with Ms. Faliks as soloist in Mozart’s esteemed Piano Concerto No. 20 in D Minor, K. 466, a work familiar to many audiences from its appearance in the film *Amadeus*.

The Hastings Group which has just opened its seventh hotel in the North, the £53 million Grand Central in Belfast, enjoyed a 7.8 per cent jump in sales last year, pushing annual pretax profits to more than £5.2 million.
Latest financial accounts for the family-owned hotel group, which also holds a 50 per cent stake in the five-star Merrion Hotel in Dublin, show that turnover also increased by more than £2.8 million last year to hit a high of £39.6 million.
According to the accounts, the Hastings Group received £647,504 last year from its joint venture in the Landmark Investment Company which holds 100 per cent of the share capital in Hotel Merrion Limited.
Although the hotel group, which employs more than 1,000 people in the North, may have strengthened its financial performance last year, its latest accounts are also tinged with sadness as they mark the passing of Sir William Hastings in December 2017, who had been at the helm of the family business for more than 50 years.
Legacy of William Hastings
The directors state in their report that: “Sir William almost single-handedly built up the group from the 1960s to what it is today. The group was his life and he is sorely missed by the directors and staff.”
The latest set of accounts for the 12 months ending October 2017 show that the value of the Hastings Group’s “tangible assets” jumped by more than £25 million to £77.4 million last year.
This included a value of £32 million placed on the Grand Central Hotel which was under construction at the time.
The 23-storey hotel in the centre of Belfast, which the Hastings Group said was the single biggest investment it has undertaken, opened for business last month.
The level of this investment is also reflected in the latest financial accounts which show the increase in the hotel group’s bank loans and overdraft jumped from £14.8 million in 2016 to more than £33.1 million in 2017.
rewrite:
The Hastings Group, a family-owned hotel enterprise, has reported a 7.8 per cent increase in sales for the previous financial year, elevating its annual pretax profits to over £5.2 million. This performance is documented in the Group’s latest financial accounts, which also record a turnover growth exceeding £2.8 million, culminating in a total of £39.6 million. The Group’s portfolio recently expanded with the inauguration of its seventh Northern establishment, the £53 million Grand Central Hotel in Belfast. Furthermore, the Group maintains a fifty per cent interest in the five-star Merrion Hotel in Dublin through its joint venture involvement. From this venture, conducted via the Landmark Investment Company—which holds the entire share capital of Hotel Merrion Limited—the Hastings Group received £647,504 during the reported period.

These accounts, covering the twelve months to October 2017, are marked by a note of solemnity, recording the passing of Sir William Hastings in December 2017. Sir William had led the family business for over five decades. The directors’ report pays tribute, stating that he “almost single-handedly built up the group from the 1960s to what it is today,” noting his profound legacy and that he is “sorely missed by the directors and staff.”

Financially, the period saw a significant appreciation in the Group’s tangible assets, which rose by more than £25 million to reach £77.4 million. This valuation incorporated an attributed worth of £32 million for the Grand Central Hotel, which was under construction at the time. This 23-storey Belfast property, described by the Group as its single largest investment to date, commenced operations last month. The scale of this undertaking is mirrored in the Group’s financing structure, with bank loans and overdrafts escalating from £14.8 million in 2016 to over £33.1 million in 2017, reflecting the capital commitment required for such a major development. The Group employs more than 1,000 individuals in its Northern operations.

Just in time for summer-like temperatures in October, Allentown is finally opening its multi-million dollar Cedar Beach Pool.
Yes, Allentown residents can take a dip this weekend -- for free.
The city's largest and most popular pool has been dry since 2015, when a leak closed the pool for that summer.
The pool will be open from noon to 7 p.m. Saturday and Sunday for city residents and city employees. Visitors are required to show identification, such as a driver's license, city ID or school ID.
The cover will come off this $3M public pool project soon
Saturday will also include a showing of "Finding Dory" on the city's outdoor movie screen, which is slated to start at dusk.
That project was supposed to be completed by the summer of 2016, but the city ran into a number of problems, including structural issues discovered after the project began.
The delays have led to the project to balloon from $1.3 million to more than $3 million.
Sarah Cassi may be reached at scassi@lehighvalleylive.com. Follow her on Twitter @SarahCassi. Find lehighvalleylive.com on Facebook.
rewrite: Allentown will inaugurate its renovated Cedar Beach Pool, a multi-million dollar public facility, coinciding with unseasonably warm October conditions. The city's largest and most frequented pool, inactive since a 2015 leak forced its closure, will be accessible without charge this weekend exclusively to residents and municipal employees. Operation hours are scheduled from noon to 7 p.m. on Saturday and Sunday, with valid identification required for entry. This opening follows significant delays and cost overruns; initially projected for completion in summer 2016 at an estimated $1.3 million, the project encountered structural complications and other obstacles, ultimately expanding its budget to over $3 million. The inaugural weekend will also feature a dusk screening of "Finding Dory" on the municipal outdoor screen. Further details may be obtained from reporter Sarah Cassi.

A federal judge in Manhattan on Wednesday ordered lawyers for Michael D. Cohen, President Trump’s longtime fixer, to complete within two weeks their review of a huge trove of documents and data that the F.B.I. seized from him last month and that prosecutors are eager to use in their continuing investigation of Mr. Cohen.
The judge, Kimba M. Wood, said that if the lawyers did not meet her June 15 deadline, she would allow the government to take control of the review, which is to determine whether any of the seized paperwork or electronic files should be protected under the lawyer-client privilege belonging to Mr. Trump.
Until now, a court-appointed special master has been overseeing scrutiny of the materials with Mr. Cohen’s lawyers, but Judge Wood suggested in a hearing in Federal District Court that the process was moving too slowly.
“It’s important for the court to balance the slow, deliberate needs of those who are asserting attorney-client privilege,” Judge Wood said, “with the needs for an investigation to go forward.”
rewrite:
On Wednesday, a federal judge in the Southern District of New York directed attorneys for Michael D. Cohen, former personal counsel to President Trump, to conclude their privilege review within a two-week period. The materials in question constitute a substantial volume of documents and data seized from Mr. Cohen by the Federal Bureau of Investigation last month, which federal prosecutors seek to utilize in their ongoing investigation. Presiding Judge Kimba M. Wood stipulated that failure to meet the June 15 deadline would result in the government assuming control of the process. This review is tasked with identifying any items potentially shielded from disclosure by President Trump’s attorney-client privilege.

Previously, a court-appointed special master had supervised the examination alongside Mr. Cohen’s legal team. However, Judge Wood indicated during a hearing that the pace of review was insufficient. She emphasized the judicial obligation to balance the meticulous requirements of privilege assertion against the prosecutorial need for investigative progress.

A schoolboy was rushed to hospital with a serious eye injury after he was attacked by a dog.
It happened on Sunday afternoon outside the Green Bear in Nuneaton.
The eight-year-old, who has not been identified, was taken to the George Eliot Hospital .
But, due to the severity of puncture wounds to one of his eyes, he had to be transferred to the University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire for treatment.
Police say that it has been reported that the dog, which has been described as possibly being an American Bulldog, attacked the boy at 6pm on Sunday (April 22) at The Green Bear pub in Church Road.
Now they want to trace the owners, a man and a woman, who left the scene after the attack, CoventryLive reported .
PC Clayton Kelley said: "We're keen to hear from anyone who can help us to identify the owners of the dog.
"We believe the owners, a man and a woman, went into the pub at around 4pm and were in there for around an hour and a half before the incident happened.
"They left immediately after the incident without speaking to anyone.
"We're hoping that someone else in the pub will have recognised them and be able to help us identify them."
Anyone with information that could help trace the dog and its owners, should call police on 101, quoting incident reference number 311 of April 22.
Details can also be passed on to officers via the Crimestoppers hotline, which is free to call from a landline and confidential, on 0800 555 111.

The incident occurred outside The Green Bear public house on Church Road in Nuneaton at approximately 6pm on Sunday, April 22. The child, whose identity has not been disclosed, was initially transported to George Eliot Hospital. However, due to the severity of puncture wounds to one eye, he was subsequently transferred to University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire for further specialist care.

According to police reports, the dog involved is described as potentially an American Bulldog. The animal’s owners, identified as a man and a woman, reportedly departed the scene following the attack without engaging with witnesses or emergency services. Authorities state the owners had entered the premises around 4pm and remained there for approximately ninety minutes prior to the incident. Investigators are now seeking to trace these individuals and have appealed for public assistance.

Police Constable Clayton Kelley has issued a statement urging anyone with relevant information to come forward, particularly patrons who may have been present at the establishment and could assist in identifying the owners. Individuals possessing information are instructed to contact the police via the non-emergency number 101, citing incident reference 311 for April 22. Information may also be submitted anonymously and free of charge through the independent Crimestoppers hotline at 0800 555 111.
