April 24 (UPI) -- Data from the Department of Education released Tuesday showed black students are disproportionately arrested and disciplined compared to white students.
Thirty-one percent of K-12 students who were arrested or referred to law enforcement were black, while black students accounted for 15 percent of the total student population across U.S. public schools and districts, according to the Civil Rights Data Collection for the 2015-16 school year.
The 16-point disparity between black student enrollment and law enforcement referrals was up from 11 percent in the 2013-14 school year.
Conversely, white students accounted for 36 percent of students who were arrested or referred to police, while representing 49 percent of all enrolled students.
Black students also were disproportionately restrained and secluded, representing 27 percent of all students who were restrained and 23 percent of those secluded.
Black males also accounted for 23 percent of expulsions, while white males accounted for 27 percent. Black and white females each accounted for 10 percent of all expulsions.
Black male students accounted for 25 percent of students who received an out-of-school suspension, while representing 8 percent of enrolled students and black female students, who also represented 8 percent of enrolled students, accounted for 14 percent of students who received an out-of-school suspension.
The data also showed that race was the second most commonly reported reason for bullying among male students at 62 percent, behind disability at 66 percent. A total of 63 percent of female students reported being bullied most often due to their gender.
Black students disproportionately reported being harassed or bullied for their race -- 35 percent reported such incidents.
In a statement released along with the data Education Secretary Betsy DeVos said "protecting all students' civil rights is at the core of the department's mission."
"I want to commend the many educators, school leaders and OCR staff who put in countless hours to produce this data and who work tirelessly to ensure all students are able to learn in a safe and nurturing environment free from discrimination," she said.
rewrite:
Data released on April 24 by the U.S. Department of Education reveals significant racial disparities in school discipline and law enforcement referrals during the 2015-16 academic year. According to the Civil Rights Data Collection, Black students, who constituted 15 percent of the total K-12 public school population, represented 31 percent of those arrested or referred to law enforcement. This 16-percentage-point disparity between enrollment and law enforcement involvement marks an increase from an 11-point gap recorded during the 2013-14 school year. In contrast, white students comprised 49 percent of the student body but accounted for 36 percent of arrests or police referrals.

Further disciplinary measures also showed disproportionality. Black students represented 27 percent of all instances of physical restraint and 23 percent of incidents involving seclusion. Regarding expulsions, Black male students accounted for 23 percent, compared to 27 percent for white male students, while Black and white female students each represented 10 percent of expulsions. Out-of-school suspensions exhibited a pronounced disparity: Black male students, constituting 8 percent of enrollment, represented 25 percent of such suspensions. Similarly, Black female students, also 8 percent of enrollment, accounted for 14 percent of out-of-school suspensions.

The data also indicated that race was a prevalent factor in reported bullying. Among male students, 62 percent cited race as the reason for bullying, second only to disability at 66 percent. For female students, 63 percent reported gender as the most common basis for bullying. Notably, 35 percent of Black students reported experiencing harassment or bullying specifically due to their race.

In a statement accompanying the data release, Education Secretary Betsy DeVos affirmed that “protecting all students' civil rights is at the core of the department's mission.” She commended educators, school leaders, and Office for Civil Rights staff for their work in compiling the data and for efforts to “ensure all students are able to learn in a safe and nurturing environment free from discrimination.”

A verdict has been reached in the Taylor Swift groping trial, a jury in a Denver courtroom ruled that former radio host David Mueller assaulted and battered Taylor Swift at a meet-and-greet photo session in June 2013.
The Judge awarded Swift the $1 she was suing for. Her attorney Doug Baldridge, says the amount “has immeasurable value” in the scheme of things. “She’s trying to tell people out there that you can say no when someone grabs you, no matter who they are.” Swift says in a statement obtained by PEOPLE and EW. “I want to thank Judge William J. Martinez and the jury for their careful consideration, my attorneys Doug Baldridge, Danielle Foley, Jay Schaudies and Katie Wright for fighting for me and anyone who feels silenced by a sexual assault, and especially anyone who offered their support throughout this four-year ordeal and two-year long trial process, I acknowledge the privilege that I benefit from in life, in society and in my ability to shoulder the enormous cost of defending myself in a trial like this. My hope is to help those whose voices should also be heard. Therefore, I will be making donations in the near future to multiple organizations that help sexual assault victims defend themselves.”
rewrite: A jury in a Denver courtroom has delivered a verdict in the civil trial concerning allegations of groping against entertainer Taylor Swift, finding former radio host David Mueller liable for assault and battery during a meet-and-greet photograph session in June 2013. The court awarded Swift the symbolic sum of one dollar, which she had sought in her suit. Her lead attorney, Doug Baldridge, characterized the nominal award as possessing "immeasurable value" within the broader context of the case, indicating its purpose was to affirm the principle that individuals may rightfully object to unwanted physical contact irrespective of the perpetrator's status. In a public statement, Swift expressed gratitude to Judge William J. Martinez and the jury for their deliberation, and to her legal team for their advocacy on her behalf and for others who feel silenced following a sexual assault. She further acknowledged her personal socioeconomic privilege in being able to sustain the considerable expenses of protracted litigation. Stating a hope to amplify voices that might otherwise go unheard, Swift announced her intention to donate to several organizations dedicated to assisting victims of sexual assault.

A 25-year employee was nominated to take over as Northampton County's Director of Corrections, according to a news release issued Monday.
James Kostura is the choice of Northampton County Executive Lamont McClure. McClure hopes county council will confirm his nominee in April, the release says.
Former director Daniel Keen lost his job after County Executive John Brown was voted out last year. Keen was appointed in 2014. The prison is now in the hands of interim director Todd Buskirk.
Kostura has served as deputy warden at the prison since 2013, the news release says.
He began his career as a corrections officer in 1993 and later moved up to shift lieutenant then security operations administrator.
Kostura served in the U.S. Navy/Naval Reserves for 20 years as an active duty SEAL officer providing training in anti-terrorism techniques and defensive tactics.
Rudy Miller may be reached at rmiller@lehighvalleylive.com. Follow him on Twitter @RudyMillerLV. Find Easton area news on Facebook.
rewrite:
On Monday, a news release announced the nomination of a twenty-five-year veteran employee to assume the role of Director of Corrections for Northampton County. County Executive Lamont McClure has selected James Kostura for the position, with the expectation that the county council will confirm the appointment in April. This vacancy follows the departure of former director Daniel Keen, who was appointed in 2014 and left his post subsequent to the electoral defeat of former County Executive John Brown last year. The facility is currently under the interim leadership of Todd Buskirk.

Kostura, who joined the prison as a corrections officer in 1993, has advanced through the ranks to positions including shift lieutenant and security operations administrator. He has served as deputy warden since 2013. Additionally, he completed a twenty-year tenure in the U.S. Navy and Naval Reserves as an active-duty SEAL officer, specializing in anti-terrorism and defensive tactics training.

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J. (AP) - Gov. Phil Murphy on Monday got behind a prospective a 12-acre development project aimed at attracting new technology and other jobs to New Jersey.
The Democratic governor met with officials from Rutgers University, local and state government, private businesses and others at the university to support the project, called the Hub.
Murphy, who met privately with the group of leaders before he spoke to reporters, said the idea for the project goes back at least five years but what's new is "the will" to push the project forward.
"There needs to be a will to pull it together because the interests are quite disparate, and you need to be able to pull a lot of different and perspectives togethers," Murphy said.
The project fits with Murphy's campaign promises to jump-start what he calls the state's innovation economy, though there were few details on the project immediately available.
It's not clear who exactly would fund the project, but the governor said there's broad support in the state and that he hopes the federal government will help finance the effort.
New Brunswick Mayor Jim Cahill, also a Democrat, said a four-acre portion of the project is "shovel-ready" and set to be located near the city's train station, along the corridor connecting New York to Philadelphia.
Democratic Assembly Speaker Craig Coughlin also attended the event and said he plans to introduce legislation but didn't give any details.
In addition to state and local elected officials, Rutgers President Robert Barchi and RWJ Barnabas Health President Barry Ostrowsky also attended the event and sounded supportive.
Barchi said Murphy is the "catalyst" for getting the project kick-started.
Murphy also said later that the New Jersey Economic Development Authority will begin a planning and implementation study of the project. He said the authority is expected to identify partners for the Hub.
rewrite:
On Monday, Governor Phil Murphy of New Jersey publicly endorsed a prospective 12-acre development initiative, designated "the Hub," which is intended to attract technology firms and generate employment within the state. The Democratic governor convened with officials from Rutgers University, alongside representatives from municipal and state government and private sector entities, at the university to express his support. Following a private meeting with this assemblage of leaders, Governor Murphy addressed members of the press, noting that the concept for the project has been under consideration for a minimum of five years. He emphasized that the novel element is the present collective resolve to advance the initiative. "There needs to be a will to pull it together because the interests are quite disparate, and you need to be able to pull a lot of different perspectives together," Murphy stated.

This undertaking aligns with the governor's previously articulated campaign commitment to stimulate what he terms the state's "innovation economy," although specific details regarding the project remain limited at this juncture. While the precise sources of funding have not been definitively identified, Governor Murphy indicated there is extensive support within New Jersey and expressed hope for federal financial assistance. New Brunswick Mayor Jim Cahill, also a Democrat, reported that a four-acre segment of the development, situated near the city's train station along the New York-Philadelphia corridor, is prepared for imminent commencement.

The event was also attended by Democratic Assembly Speaker Craig Coughlin, who announced an intention to introduce supporting legislation, though without providing particulars. Additional notable attendees included Rutgers University President Robert Barchi and RWJ Barnabas Health President Barry Ostrowsky, both of whom voiced approval for the project. President Barchi characterized Governor Murphy as the essential "catalyst" for initiating the endeavor. Governor Murphy further disclosed that the New Jersey Economic Development Authority will undertake a comprehensive planning and implementation study for the Hub and is anticipated to identify appropriate collaborative partners for its execution.

The Fate of the Furious enjoyed an excellent extended opening weekend of 5 days at the box office in India. The 8th installment of the Fast and the Furious franchise has raked in approximately 11.50 crores on Sunday and now stands with a grand total of 47.50 crores.
The film has affected the business of Vidya Balan’s Begum Jaan to a great extent. It’ll be interesting to see whether The Fate of the Furious will be able to remain steady in weekdays or not.
The film has performed better than other Hollywood films which released this year in India.
The previous part of the film, Furious 7 collected 110 crores in India, which very much justifies the expectations related to this part. It’ll be interesting to see whether this part will surpass the collections of its previous installment.
Though Furious 8 has received positive to mixed reviews, there is hardly any impact on its box office business.
Apart from India, the film has created many box office records across the globe, especially in China where it collected $190 million.
Apart from the ensemble cast of Vin Diesel, Dwayne Johnson, Jason Statham, Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Chris Bridges, Nathalie Emmanuel, Kurt Russell, Scott Eastwood and Helen Mirren, Academy Award winner Charlize Theron features as a fierce villain named Cipher, who has the technology to hack into the world’s computerized cars in this 8th installment of action franchise film.
The film has shot around different locations across the world including Mývatn, Havana, Atlanta, Cleveland and New York City.
Written by Chris Morgan and Gary Scott Thompson, The Fate of the Furious is directed by F. Gary Gray, who has previously helmed movies like Straight Outta Compton, Law Abiding Citizen and The Italian Job.
Fast and Furious 8 is produced by Neal H. Moritz, Vin Diesel and Michael Fottrell.
rewrite:
The eighth installment of the *Fast and the Furious* franchise, *The Fate of the Furious*, has demonstrated a robust commercial performance during its extended five-day opening weekend in the Indian market. The film garnered approximately 11.50 crore rupees on Sunday alone, culminating in a cumulative domestic box office total of 47.50 crore rupees. This strong opening has significantly impacted the earnings of concurrently running films, notably Vidya Balan's *Begum Jaan*. Industry observers are monitoring whether the film can maintain its momentum during the ensuing weekdays. Its initial performance has surpassed that of other Hollywood releases in India this year.

Comparisons are inevitably drawn to its predecessor, *Furious 7*, which achieved a substantial 110 crore rupee total in India. This historical benchmark sets a high expectation for the current installment's potential trajectory, raising the question of whether it will exceed the collections of the previous film. Notably, the film's box office performance appears largely unaffected by the spectrum of critical reception, which has ranged from positive to mixed.

Globally, the film has set numerous box office records, with a particularly notable performance in China, where it earned $190 million. The ensemble cast includes Vin Diesel, Dwayne Johnson, Jason Statham, Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Chris Bridges, Nathalie Emmanuel, Kurt Russell, Scott Eastwood, and Helen Mirren. Academy Award winner Charlize Theron joins the franchise as the antagonist Cipher, a character who utilizes advanced technology to hijack computerized vehicles worldwide. Production spanned several international locations, including Mývatn, Havana, Atlanta, Cleveland, and New York City.

The screenplay was written by Chris Morgan and Gary Scott Thompson, with direction by F. Gary Gray, whose prior directorial credits include *Straight Outta Compton*, *Law Abiding Citizen*, and *The Italian Job*. The film is produced by Neal H. Moritz, Vin Diesel, and Michael Fottrell.

Evgeny Buryakov, a former New York banker who was convicted in federal court of conspiring to act in the United States as an agent of the Russian Federation, is shown in this handout photo sitting on a commercial flight, escorted by deportation officers and turned over to... REUTERS
A Russian banker convicted last year in the United States for involvement in a spy ring operating in New York City has been deported to Moscow, a U.S. law enforcement agency said on Wednesday.
Evgeny Buryakov, 42, was escorted to Russia by deportation officers aboard commercial flights and turned over to Russian authorities, the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a statement.
Buryakov was arrested in January 2015 and charged with two others. U.S. prosecutors said they had worked with the Russian intelligence service and conspired to gather economic intelligence on behalf of Russia, including information about U.S. sanctions against Russia, and to recruit New York City residents as intelligence sources.
Buryakov, who worked at Russian state-owned Vnesheconombank, was sentenced in May by a U.S. district judge in Manhattan to 2-1/2 years in prison after pleading guilty to having conspired to act improperly as an agent for the Russian government.
He received credit for 16 months already spent in custody and was in line to be deported after completing his sentence.
(Reporting by Nathan Layne; Editing by Toni Reinhold)
rewrite:
Evgeny Buryakov, a former banker convicted of conspiring to act as an agent of the Russian Federation within the United States, has been deported to Moscow. According to a statement issued on Wednesday by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the 42-year-old was escorted by deportation officers aboard a commercial flight and subsequently transferred to Russian authorities. Buryakov was initially arrested in January 2015, alongside two co-conspirators, on charges of collaborating with Russian intelligence services. Federal prosecutors asserted that the group conspired to collect economic intelligence for Russia, focusing on topics such as U.S. sanctions policy, and attempted to recruit residents of New York City as intelligence assets.

Employed by the Russian state-owned financial institution Vnesheconombank, Buryakov ultimately pleaded guilty to the conspiracy charge. In May of last year, he was sentenced in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to a term of thirty months imprisonment. Having received credit for sixteen months of time already served in pre-trial custody, he became eligible for deportation upon the completion of his sentence. This removal concludes a judicial process concerning espionage-related activities conducted on U.S. soil.

Record-breaking hurdler, thrower named AAC Athletes of the Week
Following their record-setting weekends, sophomore hurdler Amere Lattin and senior thrower Cameron Cornelius were the Co-Athletes of the Week in the American Athletic Conference. Both earned the distinction by setting season bests and placing in the top 3 for their respective events.
Lattin ran in his toughest meet all season at the Tyson Invitational in Fayettville, Arkansas. At the meet, Grant Holloway of Florida set the fastest time this season, 7.58s, to win the 60m hurdles. This competition resulted in Lattin setting both a new personal best and the No. 3 time in school history.
“It shows that I can compete with the best,” Lattin said. “That I can run with the top in the nation. That guy is predicted to win nationals, but if I keep training the way I’m training, I know I can win it myself.”
Lattin’s time moved him from No. 14 to No. 7 in the NCAA, solidifying his place as the top hurdler in the American Conference as the Cougars prepare for the indoor conference. Wondering why this is capitalized
Cornelius has thrown in four events this season and claimed victory each time. His 18.16m throw at the Howie Ryan Invitational was his top mark this season. The throw is currently No. 38 in the NCAA, leaving Cornelius with work to do if he hopes to qualify for nationals.
With the addition of Lattin and Cornelius, the Cougars now have six athletes who have been honored as athletes of the week.
With indoor conference coming up, Cornelius could claim his third indoor title in four years. He has already bested his championship throw from a year ago, 18.11m. He could end up being left behind, however, when others on his team travel to College Station for the Indoor National Championships.

rewrite:
Following their record-setting performances, University of Houston sophomore hurdler Amere Lattin and senior thrower Cameron Cornelius were named Co-Athletes of the Week by the American Athletic Conference. This distinction was awarded in recognition of each athlete achieving season-best marks and securing top-three finishes in their respective events during the previous weekend's competitions.

Lattin delivered his performance at the highly competitive Tyson Invitational in Fayetteville, Arkansas, which represented his most challenging meet of the season. The event was notably won by Florida's Grant Holloway, who set the current national collegiate leading time of 7.58 seconds in the 60-meter hurdles. In this elite field, Lattin established a new personal best, which also ranks as the third-fastest time in University of Houston history. Reflecting on his achievement, Lattin stated, "It demonstrates my capacity to compete with the nation's top performers. That athlete is projected to win the national championship, but with continued dedicated training, I am confident in my own potential to secure the title." This result elevated Lattin from fourteenth to seventh in the national rankings, solidifying his status as the premier hurdler in the American Athletic Conference as the team approaches the indoor conference championships.

Cornelius has maintained an undefeated record across four throwing events this season. His top mark of 18.16 meters, achieved at the Howie Ryan Invitational, currently ranks thirty-eighth nationally, indicating that further improvement is necessary to qualify for the national championships. Nevertheless, Cornelius is positioned to contend for his third indoor conference title in four years at the upcoming meet, having already surpassed his championship-winning throw of 18.11 meters from the previous year. The inclusion of Lattin and Cornelius brings the total number of weekly conference honorees from the University of Houston to six this season. While Cornelius pursues a conference title, he may not accompany teammates who qualify for the Indoor National Championships in College Station, Texas.

A Bourbon County, KS roofer is banned from operating as a roofing contractor in the State of Kansas.
District Judge Mark A. Ward approved the default judgment after Shane Bailey, of Fort Scott, doing business as Bailey Construction, failed to respond to a lawsuit filed against him. Bailey was also ordered to pay the attorney general's investigation costs and a civil penalty.
Kansas Attorney General Derek Schmidt accused Bailey of operating as a roofing contractor without properly registering as required by the Kansas Roofing Registration Act (KRRA). Schmidt also alleged that Bailey violated the Kansas Consumer Protection Act by engaging in a door-to-door sale without giving the required notice of the consumer's three-day right to cancel and cashing the consumer's check before the required five-day waiting period.
Schmidt also announced he has entered into consent judgments with seven other roofing contractors for violations of the KRRA. The settlements require the companies to pay civil penalties for KRRA violations. They also require the companies to comply with the KRRA when providing roofing services in the future. The seven roofing contractors fined are:
• A-1 Roofing, Renovation & Construction, LLC, Shawnee County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-143
• Above it All Roofing & Contracting, LLC, Johnson County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-1310
• Jason Bowman, dba Bowman Property Solutions, formerly Grounds Care, LLC, Johnson County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-735
• George Cook, Crawford County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-14-P
• Bill Haley, dba Haley & Sons Construction, dba Haley & Sons Quality Restoration, Bourbon County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-26
• Rafael Menjivar, Harvey County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-32
• Paulo Soares dba Roof Restoration, Johnson County, Case No. 2018-CV-1315
In each case, Schmidt alleged the defendants engaged in advertising, soliciting or performing roofing contractor services in Kansas without registering with the attorney general's office as required by the KRRA.
Copies of the judgments are available at www.ag.ks.gov/roofer-enforcement.
rewrite:
A roofing contractor operating in Bourbon County, Kansas, has been permanently enjoined from conducting business as a roofing contractor within the state. This default judgment was issued by District Judge Mark A. Ward following the failure of Shane Bailey, proprietor of Bailey Construction in Fort Scott, to respond to a lawsuit filed against him. The court order additionally mandates that Mr. Bailey reimburse the investigative costs incurred by the Attorney General’s office and pay a civil penalty.

The legal action was initiated by Kansas Attorney General Derek Schmidt, who alleged that Mr. Bailey operated as a roofing contractor without being properly registered under the Kansas Roofing Registration Act (KRRA). The complaint further asserted violations of the Kansas Consumer Protection Act, specifically that Mr. Bailey conducted a door-to-door sale without providing the mandated notice of a consumer’s three-day right to cancel and deposited a consumer’s check prior to the expiration of the required five-day waiting period.

Concurrently, Attorney General Schmidt announced the execution of consent judgments with seven additional roofing contractors for violations of the KRRA. These settlements obligate the companies to pay civil penalties and to adhere strictly to the KRRA’s registration and operational requirements for all future roofing services within Kansas. The cited contractors are: A-1 Roofing, Renovation & Construction, LLC (Shawnee County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-143); Above it All Roofing & Contracting, LLC (Johnson County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-1310); Jason Bowman, doing business as Bowman Property Solutions, formerly Grounds Care, LLC (Johnson County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-735); George Cook (Crawford County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-14-P); Bill Haley, doing business as Haley & Sons Construction and Haley & Sons Quality Restoration (Bourbon County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-26); Rafael Menjivar (Harvey County District Court, Case No. 2018-CV-32); and Paulo Soares, doing business as Roof Restoration (Johnson County, Case No. 2018-CV-1315). In each instance, the Attorney General alleged the defendants advertised, solicited, or performed roofing contractor services in Kansas without the registration required by statute.

Copies of all judgments referenced are available for public review on the Attorney General’s official website.

* TSX down 65.99 points, or 0.42 percent, to 15,481.76
* Nine of the TSX's 10 main groups were down
TORONTO, April 3 Canada's main stock index was broadly lower late morning on Monday, reversing earlier gains as a retreat led by financial stocks offset advances by mining stocks.
The financials group slipped 0.8 percent, as six of the 10 most influential decliners were banks and insurers. Royal Bank of Canada was down 0.9 percent at C$96.02, while Sun Life Financial fell 1.8 percent to C$47.68.
Enbridge Inc, another influential decliner, fell 1.3 percent to C$54.99. The energy group, which retreated 0.7 percent, tracked oil prices which were pressured by a rebound in Libyan oil output. U.S. crude prices were down 0.7 percent to $50.25 a barrel, while Brent crude lost 0.6 percent to $53.19.
Magna International Inc also dragged on the index, sliding 2.8 percent to C$55.81, helping push the consumer discretionary group down 0.5 percent.
At 10:59 a.m. ET (1459 GMT), the Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX composite index fell 65.99 points, or 0.42 percent, to 15,481.76. All but one of the index's 10 main groups were in the red. The index mirrored moves lower on Wall Street.
Teck Resources Ltd was up 4 percent to C$30.25, as thermal coal prices and European coal futures climbed. Prices rose due to a disruption of coal exports caused by rail line damage in northeast Australia from Cyclone Debbie, which struck last week.
Gold miners including Barrick Gold Corp, which advanced 1.6 percent to C$25.67, and Franco Nevada Corp , which climbed 1.6 percent to C$88.52, helped give the overall materials group a 1.1 percent boost.
In economic data, Canadian business were more optimistic about future sales and exports, and plan to boost hiring and investment to meet demand despite uncertainty about U.S. protectionism, according to the Bank of Canada's quarterly business outlook survey.
Declining issues outnumbered advancing ones on the TSX by 143 to 98, for a 1.46-to-1 ratio on the downside.
The index was posting 5 new 52-week highs and no new lows. (Reporting by Solarina Ho; Editing by David Gregorio)
rewrite:
On Monday, April 3rd, Canada’s primary equity benchmark, the S&P/TSX Composite Index, traded broadly lower by late morning, relinquishing earlier gains. The retreat was driven principally by the financial sector, which offset modest advances within the materials group. At 10:59 a.m. Eastern Time (1459 GMT), the index declined by 65.99 points, or 0.42 percent, to settle at 15,481.76. Market breadth was notably negative, with nine of the ten major sector groups declining and a preponderance of declining issues over advancing ones by a ratio of 1.46-to-1.

The financials sector, a substantial component of the index, decreased by 0.8 percent. This movement was largely attributable to weakness among major banks and insurers, which constituted six of the ten most influential decliners. Specifically, Royal Bank of Canada declined 0.9 percent to C$96.02, while Sun Life Financial fell 1.8 percent to C$47.68. Concurrently, the energy group retreated 0.7 percent, tracking lower crude oil prices pressured by a rebound in Libyan production. U.S. crude futures declined 0.7 percent to $50.25 per barrel, and Brent crude fell 0.6 percent to $53.19. Enbridge Inc., a significant constituent, contributed to the downturn, falling 1.3 percent to C$54.99. Further pressure emerged from the consumer discretionary sector, which declined 0.5 percent, influenced by a 2.8 percent drop in Magna International Inc. to C$55.81.

In contrast, the materials sector provided a countervailing influence, advancing 1.1 percent. This strength was supported by rising thermal coal prices and European coal futures, which benefited Teck Resources Ltd., whose shares increased 4.0 percent to C$30.25. The price appreciation followed supply disruptions from cyclone damage to rail infrastructure in northeastern Australia. Precious metals miners also contributed; Barrick Gold Corp. rose 1.6 percent to C$25.67, and Franco-Nevada Corp. gained 1.6 percent to C$88.52.

The overall market sentiment reflected concurrent declines on Wall Street. In separate economic developments, the Bank of Canada’s quarterly business outlook survey indicated heightened optimism among Canadian firms regarding future sales and exports, with plans to increase hiring and investment despite concerns over U.S. protectionist policies. During the session, the index recorded five new 52-week highs and no new lows.

Vice President of Sierra Leone Victor Foh said on Monday that 200 people have likely been killed in a mudslide in the outskirts of Freetown.
“It is likely that hundreds are lying dead underneath the rubble,” Foh told Reuters at the scene of the mudslide in the mountain town of Regent, adding that a number of illegal buildings had been erected in the area.
“The disaster is so serious that I myself feel broken,” he added.
“We’re trying to cordon (off) the area (and) evacuate the people.”
The mudslide happened in the early morning in the mountain town of Regent, where dozens of houses were submerged after a night of heavy rain.
A major rescue operation is now underway although emergency workers are struggling to reach the worst-affected areas.
Mudslides and floods are fairly common during the rainy season in West Africa, where deforestation and poor town planning put residents at risk
rewrite: On Monday, Sierra Leone’s Vice President Victor Foh stated that approximately two hundred individuals are presumed to have perished in a mudslide on the outskirts of Freetown. Visiting the affected mountain town of Regent, Foh informed Reuters that “it is likely that hundreds are lying dead underneath the rubble.” He attributed part of the devastation to the proliferation of unauthorized constructions in the area. Expressing profound distress, Foh remarked, “The disaster is so serious that I myself feel broken,” and noted ongoing efforts to cordon off the site and evacuate residents. The mudslide occurred in the early morning following intense overnight rainfall, submerging numerous homes. While a major rescue operation is currently underway, emergency personnel face challenges accessing the most severely impacted zones. Such disasters, including mudslides and floods, occur with relative frequency during West Africa’s rainy season, exacerbated by deforestation and inadequate urban planning, which heighten risks to local populations.

KOKO — A socio-political pressure group in in Delta State, Developmental Advocates of Warri North, DAWN, has challenged immediate past governor of the state, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, to declare for Delta South senatorial seat ahead of the 2019 polls.
In a communiqué after an emergency meeting of the group at Koko, headquarters of Warri North Local Government Area of the state, DAWN said the call on Uduaghan to contest the senatorial seat became necessary after a committee it set up to study potential aspirants for the position recommended him based on his antecedents in peace building and achievements in the public offices.
The communiqué by Inojulagho Amaju, Coordinator, and Ayonuwe Clifford, Lead, Grassroots Education, said: “We reserve the right to be represented by intellectuals, who will return the respect we are almost losing at the national stage.
“The 7.6-kilomete Umeh Road in Isoko, which ended 30 years of abandonment of the agrarian community, the Abigborodo Bridge project in Warri North, Ugbenu Koko Road, the zero to five years free health care delivery programme across the state and the revolutionary Uduaghan Park, which brought transportation across Delta State to an easy and comfortable ride with lowest fares are Uduaghan’s achievements that make him eminently qualified to vie for the legislative position in 2019.
“Also, the 10 model schools in the three senatorial districts of Delta State, the construction/renovation of hundreds of schools, the introduction of EDUMARSHAL to ensure downtrodden children go to school free of charge and payment of enrolment fees for SSCE candidates are some other reasons that informed our decision to back Uduaghan to go to the Senate.”

A Somali police officer says a suicide car bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle at a security checkpoint near Mogadishu’s international airport, killing at least three people.
Capt. Mohamed Hussein says the car bomber detonated the bomb Monday as security forces were searching cars at the checkpoint, few hundred meters (yards) from the main base of the African Union mission.
The checkpoint is close to United Nations offices and the Peace Hotel, which is often frequented by foreigners and officials. The powerful blast blew roofs off nearby buildings.
A second blast and heavy gunfire could also be heard at the checkpoint after the attack, but there were no immediate details.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack. However, the al-Qaida linked Islamic extremist group al-Shabab often carries out such attacks.
Despite being ousted from most of its key strongholds across large parts of south and central Somalia, the group continues to wage deadly attack across the country.
Somalia’s capital has seen frequent bomb attacks at hotels and military checkpoints. The assaults have threatened this Horn of Africa nation’s attempts to rebuild from decades of chaos. The country’s presidential election, a key step toward recovery, already has been delayed multiple times because of security and other concerns.

Image caption This shop in a small Northamptonshire town was the first British retailer to sell Lego
The owner of a family-run shop which was covered in Lego for the toy's 60th birthday has said people came from as far as France to see it.
Osborne's in Rusden, Northamptonshire, was the first British retailer to sell the bricks.
Lego offered to give the shop front a makeover with 277,500 bricks to mark the anniversary last weekend.
Will Osborne said: "It was like a carnival, with people outside from dawn to dusk taking pictures and pointing.
"I was talking to one chap who came from Norwich and one guy apparently came from France - obviously a Lego fan who thought he would never see this again.
"It was a feel-good event for the town and was good, not just for us, but businesses up and down the high street."
Image copyright AFP Image caption It took 277,500 individual bricks to cover the shop front in Lego
The shop's door, signage and part of the outer walls were covered in the toy bricks.
It took 41 people to create, but was only there for three days before being dismantled earlier this week.
Virginia Pope, who lives in the town, said: "It was absolutely fantastic for Rushden, it is just a shame it was not there for longer."
Image copyright Twitter/@NorthantsTST Image caption Lego fan, Sgt Tony Payne from Northamptonshire Police, posted his souvenir photo on Twitter
Pam Osborne and her late husband Jim opened the shop in 1955 and placed an order for Lego after seeing it at a trade fair while on honeymoon in Brighton in 1960.
Their son, Will Osborne, said events like this help to highlight what businesses like his have to offer.
"It's no secret the retail landscape is changing and you do your best to keep up, but it's difficult sometimes.
"Small, independent businesses have their own peculiarities and personalities which shine through and offer what the big chains can't.
"Running a toy shop is a joyful profession and I have no plans to retire yet."
rewrite:
Osborne’s, a family-run retail establishment in the Northamptonshire town of Rushden, recently received a distinctive façade comprising 277,500 Lego bricks to commemorate the toy’s sixtieth anniversary. This temporary installation, which covered the shop’s door, signage, and sections of its exterior walls, held particular historical significance: Osborne’s was the first retailer in the United Kingdom to stock Lego bricks. The celebratory transformation, offered and executed by the Lego Group, remained in place for a three-day period last weekend before being dismantled.

The event attracted considerable public attention. Will Osborne, the current proprietor, described the atmosphere as “carnival-like,” with visitors gathering outside from dawn until dusk to photograph the structure. He reported that attendees included individuals from distant locations such as Norwich and even France, suggesting the appeal of this unique, ephemeral display to dedicated enthusiasts. Local resident Virginia Pope echoed this positive sentiment, describing the installation as “absolutely fantastic for Rushden,” while expressing regret that its duration was so brief. Mr. Osborne noted the broader communal benefit, characterizing the event as a “feel-good” occasion that generated footfall for numerous businesses along the high street.

The shop’s association with Lego dates to 1960, when founders Pam Osborne and her late husband Jim, having opened the store in 1955, first encountered the product at a trade fair in Brighton during their honeymoon and subsequently placed an initial order. Reflecting on the contemporary retail environment, Will Osborne acknowledged the challenges posed by a rapidly changing landscape, wherein small independent businesses must strive to remain relevant. He argued, however, that such establishments possess distinct personalities and peculiarities that enable them to offer experiences beyond the capacity of larger chains. For Mr. Osborne, operating a toy shop remains a profoundly joyful vocation, and he expressly stated he has no present plans for retirement, viewing events like the Lego installation as valuable opportunities to highlight the enduring role of specialized independent retailers.

ZURICH, April 5 The Swiss attorney general's office (OAG) has now confiscated $1 billion worth of assets linked to Brazil's scandal-plagued oil firm Petrobras, up from $800 million seized through 2015, it said on Wednesday.
The rising figure was disclosed in Attorney General Michael Lauber's 2016 annual report, in which his agency outlined efforts to tackle not only global corruption, but also domestic financial crime and Islamist extremism.
Lauber's three-year investigation into state-owned Petrobas and construction group Odebrecht has targeted Brazilian officials who used Swiss bank accounts to stash bribes paid in exchange for public projects.
So far, more than 1,000 Swiss accounts have been examined, Lauber said, including from Brazil's former speaker of the lower house, Eduardo Cunha, who last month was sentenced to more than 15 years in prison.
In his report, Lauber once again acknowledged his probe of Malaysia's scandal-hit state fund 1MDB has been hampered by Malaysian authorities' refusal to cooperate.
But Switzerland's top enforcement officer reiterated that other countries are helping to resolve billions of dollars in suspected misappropriations involving fund employees, banks and officials from Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates.
Lauber's office is also pursuing a corruption investigation against Sepp Blatter, ex-president of the world soccer body FIFA, and German soccer great Franz Beckenbauer for his role in his country's tarnished bid for the 2006 World Cup.
The 2016 report separately outlined the AG's probes against Islamists and so-called "jihad tourism," including prosecutions of three Iraqi nationals for supporting illegal organisations as well as a 25-year-old Swiss who sought to travel to Syria to join Islamic State.
Switzerland is getting more queries for help from abroad, with Lauber's office fielding 193 new requests for international legal assistance last year, up from 145 in 2015, according to the report.
In just four cases did the AG's office refuse assistance. "With the increasing complexity of the cases, the good interconnection among law-enforcement authorities is becoming more relevant," Lauber's office said. (Reporting by John Miller; Editing by Tom Heneghan)

The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland (OAG) announced on Wednesday, April 5, that it has confiscated assets valued at approximately one billion U.S. dollars in connection with Brazil’s state-owned oil company, Petrobras, which is embroiled in extensive corruption scandals. This represents an increase from the eight hundred million dollars seized as of 2015. The updated figure was published in the 2016 annual report issued by Attorney General Michael Lauber, which delineates the OAG’s ongoing efforts to combat not only international corruption but also domestic financial crime and Islamist extremism.

A central focus of the OAG’s work, as detailed in the report, is a three-year investigation into Petrobras and the construction conglomerate Odebrecht. This probe targets Brazilian officials alleged to have utilized Swiss bank accounts to conceal bribe payments received in exchange for awarding public contracts. To date, the investigation has examined more than one thousand Swiss accounts, including those linked to Eduardo Cunha, the former speaker of Brazil’s lower house, who was sentenced to over fifteen years’ imprisonment last month.

The report further notes that the OAG’s parallel investigation into Malaysia’s troubled state fund, 1MDB, continues to be impeded by a lack of cooperation from Malaysian authorities. Nevertheless, Attorney General Lauber affirmed that assistance from other jurisdictions is aiding the effort to resolve suspicions of multibillion-dollar misappropriation involving 1MDB employees, financial institutions, and officials from Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates.

Additional significant investigations highlighted in the document include a corruption case against former FIFA president Sepp Blatter and German football figure Franz Beckenbauer, related to Germany’s bid for the 2006 FIFA World Cup. The report also outlines prosecutorial activities concerning Islamist extremism and “jihad tourism,” citing proceedings against three Iraqi nationals for supporting illegal organizations and a 25-year-old Swiss citizen who attempted to travel to Syria to join the Islamic State.

The OAG reported a rise in international legal assistance requests, from 145 in 2015 to 193 in 2016, reflecting growing global judicial cooperation. Assistance was denied in only four instances. The office emphasized that “with the increasing complexity of the cases, the good interconnection among law-enforcement authorities is becoming more relevant.”

Penny Hardaway does not think Kawhi Leonard is a superstar
Everybody has their own definition of what constitutes a superstar, and apparently Kawhi Leonard does not fit Penny Hardaway’s.
In an appearance Monday on SiriusXM’s “Bottomline,” the retired NBA great said he doesn’t consider Leonard a superstar, citing his reserved demeanor but crediting the San Antonio Spurs forward for being “a good player.”
I respect the viewpoint… even if you don't agree…respectful thoughts? #Spurs pic.twitter.com/1dBOkJlbQ9 — Jabari Young (@JabariJYoung) August 14, 2017
At the age of 26, Leonard has already racked up two All-Star appearances, two All-NBA First Team nods, two Defensive Player of the Year Awards, and a Finals MVP (not to mention that his offense may have already caught up with his otherworldy defense). But Hardaway, who, on top of his accolades, starred in a number of TV ads (most notably, Nike’s “Lil Penny” campaign) and largely kept in the limelight during his own career, fails to draw a distinction between a superstar talent and a superstar persona, which is interesting.
For what it’s worth, Hardaway’s comments come just a matter of days after this fellow ’90s star you may have heard of showered Leonard with praise, so he definitely appears to be in the minority with his appraisal of The Claw.
rewrite: The classification of an athlete as a "superstar" remains a subjective matter, contingent upon individual criteria. Recently, retired NBA luminary Penny Hardaway articulated a perspective wherein San Antonio Spurs forward Kawhi Leonard does not meet his personal definition of such a status. During a Monday appearance on SiriusXM’s “Bottomline,” Hardaway acknowledged Leonard as "a good player" while suggesting his reserved public demeanor precludes superstar designation. This assessment is notable given Leonard’s considerable achievements at age 26, including two All-Star selections, two All-NBA First Team honors, two Defensive Player of the Year awards, and a Finals MVP accolade—a portfolio indicating his offensive capabilities have evolved to match his renowned defensive prowess. Hardaway’s commentary appears to conflate superstar-level talent with a requisite superstar persona, a distinction underscored by his own highly visible career, which featured prominent television advertising campaigns. His viewpoint stands in contrast to other contemporary evaluations, including recent effusive praise from a fellow 1990s star, positioning Hardaway’s appraisal as a minority opinion within the broader discourse on Leonard’s standing in the league.

More than one in 10 New Jersey Transit train engineers who were screened for sleep apnea tested positive for the condition, which can make them spontaneously fall asleep while on the job, according to agency officials.
Out of the 373 train engineers tested, 57 were taken off duty because an initial screening showed that they had symptoms of sleep apnea, NJ Transit spokeswoman Nancy Snyder said Wednesday.
Of those, 44 tested positive for the disorder and were kept off trains until they started treatment. A pair of engineers are still not back on the job, said Snyder.
NJ Transit started testing its train operators late last year after they learned that the engineer who was operating the train that crashed at the Hoboken Terminal in September 2016 suffered from the deadly condition.
The train, which was supposed to be traveling at 10 mph into the station, accelerated to more than twice the limit before slamming into a barrier. The crash injured several and killed a woman waiting on the platform.
The MTA also instituted rules this year that require all train and bus operators to be tested for the condition. The agency admitted last month that it has so far only tested about half of the 20,000 who fall under the mandate.

Agency officials reported that more than ten percent of engineers screened were diagnosed with the condition. Subsequent diagnostic testing confirmed sleep apnea in 44 of those cases. These personnel remained out of service until initiating treatment, with two engineers yet to be medically cleared for return.

This testing program was implemented following the September 2016 Hoboken Terminal derailment, an incident attributed to an engineer afflicted with severe sleep apnea. The train, which should have entered the station at 10 mph, accelerated beyond twice the speed limit before colliding with a barrier, resulting in multiple injuries and one fatality on the platform.

Concurrently, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority has enacted a policy mandating sleep apnea screening for all train and bus operators. The agency acknowledged, however, that compliance is ongoing, having tested approximately half of the mandated 20,000 personnel to date.

FOXBOROUGH, Mass. — Teal Bunbury scored on a penalty kick in the 88th minute as the New England Revolution tied Atlanta United 1-1 on Wednesday night.
New England (5-4-4) has one win in its last five games — with two straight draws. Atlanta (8-3-2) had won four straight on the road.
Krisztian Nemeth drew the late foul in the corner of the penalty box after capitalizing on a defensive turnover. Atlanta goalkeeper Brad Guzan chose the right direction but Bunbury found the upper-right corner. Guzan was given a yellow card for kicking the ball into the stands after the goal.
Josef Martinez opened the scoring for Atlanta in the 23rd minute by redirecting Julian Gressel’s cross. It was Martinez’s league-leading ninth goal of the season.
New England goalkeeper Matt Turner kept the Revs within reach by denying Ezequiel Barco’s point-blank attempt in the 82nd.

Bayern Munich boss Jupp Heynckes returned the pressure to Real Madrid by warning Robert Lewandowski is just as dangerous as Cristiano Ronaldo.
The prolific pair could line up as team-mates next season if Los Blancos' reported interest in the Poland international leads to a move.
But they will first meet as opponents at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday as Bayern host the European champions in the opening leg of a highly-anticipated Champions League semi-final.
While Heynckes acknowledged it will be difficult to stop Ronaldo - who has netted 15 goals in the competition this term - he issued a reminder of the danger facing Zinedine Zidane's men.
"I respect Cristiano Ronaldo. He has had a superb career. But you need to play well as a team to win the Champions League," Heynckes said.
"We analyse our opponents and prepare to beat them.
"In Robert Lewandowski, we also have a striker who has already scored 39 goals this season. So you might ask: how do you stop Lewandowski?"
Asked whether he would swap the two, Heynckes would not be drawn into the debate, responding: "This is a question for journalists, not for us."
Heynckes, who is set to re-enter retirement at the end of the season, is attempting to sign off by winning the Champions League for a third time, having led Madrid to glory in 1998 before overseeing Bayern's win at Wembley at the end of his last spell with the club five years ago.
Zidane is in the hunt for the same distinction after prevailing in the past two finals and his measured approach to management has won Heynckes' respect.
"I was always a great admirer of Zizou the player, but now I also admire him as a coach. I like how calm he is," the German said.
"This shows me that he's not showcasing for the public or the camera. He's a top trainer."

One might therefore pose the question: how does one stop Lewandowski?" When queried on a potential exchange of the two players, Heynckes declined to engage, remarking, "That is a question for journalists, not for us."

Heynckes, who is poised to retire from management at the season’s conclusion, aims to conclude his career by securing a third Champions League title. He previously guided Real Madrid to victory in 1998 and oversaw Bayern Munich’s triumph at Wembley Stadium five years ago, at the end of his prior tenure with the club. Zidane, meanwhile, seeks to match this accomplishment after prevailing in the previous two finals. Heynckes expressed admiration for Zidane’s composed managerial style, noting, "I was always a great admirer of Zizou the player, but now I also admire him as a coach. I appreciate his calm demeanor. This indicates to me that he is not performing for the public or the camera. He is a top trainer."

OTTAWA – Foreign Affairs Minister Chrystia Freeland is laying out Canada’s core objectives for the upcoming renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement.
In a speech Friday, Freeland shared a half-dozen NAFTA goals – including opening up access to government procurement rights, more professional movement, defending Canadian rights to supply management and reform of the investor-state dispute settlement process.
“In all these discussions, we will come to the table with goodwill, and Canada’s characteristic ability and willingness to seek compromise and find win-win solutions,” she said.
“But we are committed to a good deal, not just any deal.”
She is also calling for new “progressive” elements in NAFTA 2.0: stronger labour standards, tougher environmental protection provisions as well as chapters on gender and Indigenous rights.
On that front, Canadian negotiators plan to use Canada’s recently negotiated trade agreement with the European Union as a reference, Freeland said.
“Progressive elements are also important if you want a free-trade deal that’s also a fair-trade deal,” Freeland said in a question-and-answer session following the speech at University of Ottawa.
Ottawa also aims to cut down on bureaucracy, harmonize regulations to ease the flow of cross-border business, push for more mobility for professionals and free up the market for government procurement, she told her audience.
Canada’s positions will also include work to maintain key elements of the 23-year-old deal, including the process to ensure anti-dumping and countervailing duties are only applied when truly warranted.
Ottawa’s negotiating team will sit down with their American and Mexican counterparts Wednesday in Washington for the first round of talks.
Last month, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer released the Trump administration’s set of priorities for the NAFTA talks.
During the question and answer session, Freeland said she believes Canada and its NAFTA partners can find common ground on new chapters for labour, the environment, gender and Indigenous rights.
But she also warned that Canadians should brace for some tense exchanges during the NAFTA talks, in general.
“I think we all do need to be prepared for some moments of drama,” she said. “We should just see that as an expected part of any trade negotiations.”
MORE ABOUT NAFTA:
rewrite:
In a public address delivered at the University of Ottawa, Foreign Affairs Minister Chrystia Freeland articulated the principal objectives that will guide Canada’s approach to the forthcoming renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA). Minister Freeland outlined a series of six core goals for the modernization of the agreement. These include enhancing access to government procurement markets, facilitating greater mobility for professionals, safeguarding Canada’s system of supply management in key agricultural sectors, and pursuing reform of the investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) mechanism.

Minister Freeland emphasized that Canadian negotiators will engage in discussions with a constructive attitude and a demonstrated propensity for seeking compromise. “In all these discussions, we will come to the table with goodwill, and Canada’s characteristic ability and willingness to seek compromise and find win-win solutions,” she stated. However, she underscored that this cooperative spirit is tempered by a firm commitment to securing a substantively beneficial outcome, noting, “we are committed to a good deal, not just any deal.”

The Canadian position advocates for the incorporation of new progressive elements into a modernized agreement. These proposed additions encompass strengthened labour and environmental standards, as well as dedicated chapters addressing gender equality and Indigenous rights. According to Minister Freeland, such provisions are integral to ensuring that a revised NAFTA functions as a fair-trade arrangement, not merely a free-trade one. Canadian officials intend to reference the recently concluded Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the European Union as a model for these progressive components.

Further objectives involve reducing bureaucratic impediments, harmonizing regulatory frameworks to simplify cross-border commerce, and liberalizing government procurement. Concurrently, Canada will seek to preserve fundamental aspects of the existing 23-year-old pact, including its disciplined processes for applying anti-dumping and countervailing duties.

The inaugural round of trilateral negotiations with American and Mexican counterparts is scheduled to commence in Washington. While expressing confidence that common ground can be found on new progressive chapters, Minister Freeland cautioned the public to anticipate periods of tension during the process. She characterized such “moments of drama” as an anticipated feature of complex trade negotiations, advising that they be viewed as a standard component of the diplomatic process.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Supreme Court Justice Neil Gorsuch wasn’t shy Monday about making his voice heard as he took his seat on the bench for the first time to hear arguments.
The new justice took less than 15 minutes before asking questions during an employment discrimination case. Gorsuch and his colleagues were hearing cases for the first time since President Donald Trump’s pick was sworn in April 10.
The case before the justices involved a technical issue about the process for a federal worker to appeal his discrimination claim. Gorsuch asked the worker’s lawyer Christopher Landau four questions in a row about the wording of a statute, saying he was “sorry for taking up so much time.”
Gorsuch later sparred with Justice Department lawyer Brian Fletcher over the meaning of the Civil Service Reform Act, sticking to his reputation for focusing on the text of the law.
“Wouldn’t it be a lot easier if we just followed the plain text of the statute,” Gorsuch asked.
It was the first of three hour-long arguments the high court was set to hear on Monday. The court is back to its full contingent of nine members after being short-handed since Justice Antonin Scalia’s death more than 14 months ago.
The session started with Chief Justice John Roberts welcoming Gorsuch and wishing him “a long and happy career in our common calling.”
Gorsuch responded briefly to thank Roberts for the “warm welcome.”
Gorsuch took his seat at the end of the bench next to Justice Sonia Sotomayor, with the two sharing a laugh together before arguments began.

rewrite:
On Monday, April 17, 2017, Associate Justice Neil Gorsuch participated in oral arguments before the Supreme Court of the United States for the first time since his confirmation. Demonstrating immediate engagement, Justice Gorsuch initiated questioning within fifteen minutes of the commencement of the first case, which concerned a procedural technicality in a federal employment discrimination appeal. His inquiries were directed to the petitioner’s attorney, Christopher Landau, and focused intently on the precise statutory language governing the case. Justice Gorsuch subsequently engaged in a substantive exchange with Justice Department lawyer Brian Fletcher regarding the interpretation of the Civil Service Reform Act, emphasizing a textualist approach by inquiring whether adherence to the statute’s plain text would provide the most straightforward resolution.

This session marked the restoration of the Court to its full complement of nine justices, following a fourteen-month vacancy subsequent to the passing of Justice Antonin Scalia. Chief Justice John Roberts formally welcomed Justice Gorsuch at the opening of proceedings, expressing a wish for his “long and happy career in our common calling.” Justice Gorsuch acknowledged this welcome with a brief expression of gratitude. Seated at the bench’s end adjacent to Justice Sonia Sotomayor, the two justices shared a moment of levity prior to the formal commencement of arguments. The day’s schedule comprised three hours of oral arguments, with Justice Gorsuch’s active participation signaling his prompt integration into the Court’s deliberative processes.

Yellowstone is one of the most remarkable places on the planet.
It’s home to North America’s most famous wildlife and every year these animals must survive The Thaw – one of the harshest seasonal changes on Earth.
Temperatures swing from minus 40 Celsius in the winter to approaching 40 plus in the summer months. To understand how the animals cope and to witness the effects of our changing climate, presenters Kate Humble and Patrick Aryee are joined by a team of scientists and wildlife cameramen. They capture the wildlife dramas as they unfold and analyse the impact on individual animal families of wolves, grizzly bears, beavers and the great grey owls.
In the first episode Aryee follows the grizzly bears, who are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early, while Humble gets to grips with the science behind this remarkable season and discovers how Yellowstone’s unique geology is posing problems for some grazers’ teeth.
Yellowstone: The Wildest Winter, BBC2, Tuesday, January 3, 9pm
rewrite: Yellowstone National Park stands as one of the planet's most extraordinary ecosystems. It serves as the primary habitat for an iconic assemblage of North American wildlife, species which must annually endure The Thaw—an exceptionally severe seasonal transition. Temperature extremes range from -40°C in winter to nearly 40°C in summer. To document the adaptive strategies of these animals and to observe the consequences of a changing climate, presenters Kate Humble and Patrick Aryee collaborate with a scientific team and specialist cinematographers. Their mission is to record unfolding behavioral dramas and to assess the climatic impact on specific familial groups of wolves, grizzly bears, beavers, and great grey owls. In the inaugural episode, Aryee monitors grizzly bears risking early emergence from hibernation, while Humble examines the underlying environmental science, discovering how the region's unique geothermal geology adversely affects the dentition of certain grazing herbivores.

Hamilton Mountain Coun. Terry Whitehead is once again considering a run for mayor.
Whitehead, who was first elected in 2003 as Ward 8 councillor, said he started thinking about running after a number of people told him he should over the last few months.
“It’s clear to me that a lot of friends and allies say I should seriously consider it. So I am,” said Whitehead.
This isn’t the first time the veteran politician has thought about campaigning for the mayor’s chair. In 2014 he was leaning towards running, but finally decided not to take the plunge. The 2014 mayoral election had a crowded field with 12 contenders including Eisenberger, and former councillors Brad Clark and Brian McHattie all jostling for the top spot.
"It's clear to me that a lot of friends and allies say I should seriously consider (running for mayor)." — Terry Whitehead
“I’ve got to look to see if I can contrast myself with the other candidates to really bring the deliverables and style in which Hamilton would be proud and inspired,” said Whitehead.
Over the course of this term Whitehead has become a polarizing figure, especially among social media activists for his views on transit, bike lanes and roads.
However, Whitehead says he has received more encouragement from people living in the downtown area than negative messages.
A decision about his political future will be made in about a month, he said.
So far Mayor Fred Eisenberger has already said he will seek re-election, while Flamborough resident Roman Sarachman has said he will run for mayor as well.
There is a shorter time frame for municipal candidates to decide whether to run in this election after changes to the Municipal Elections Act were passed last year. Nominations open up on May 1 and close July 27.

Councillor Terry Whitehead of Hamilton Mountain is once again contemplating a candidacy for the office of Mayor. First elected as the Ward 8 representative in 2003, Councillor Whitehead indicates that his consideration follows sustained encouragement from numerous associates over recent months. “It is clear to me that a significant number of friends and allies have advised that I should seriously consider this prospect. Consequently, I am doing so,” stated Whitehead. This does not represent the inaugural instance of such deliberations for the veteran politician; in 2014, he strongly inclined toward a mayoral campaign but ultimately declined to formally enter the race. That election featured a crowded field of twelve contenders, including the incumbent Fred Eisenberger and former councillors Brad Clark and Brian McHattie, all vying for the position.

In outlining his potential candidacy, Whitehead remarked, “I must assess whether I can effectively distinguish myself from other candidates to deliver tangible results and a leadership style that would instill pride and inspiration in the City of Hamilton.” Throughout his current term, Councillor Whitehead has emerged as a polarizing figure, particularly among social media activists, due to his pronounced stances on public transit, bicycle infrastructure, and roadway policy. He contends, however, that he has received greater encouragement from residents within the downtown core than negative feedback regarding these positions. A definitive decision regarding his political future is anticipated within approximately one month.

To date, Mayor Fred Eisenberger has declared his intention to seek re-election, while Flamborough resident Roman Sarachman has also announced a mayoral campaign. Following recent amendments to the *Municipal Elections Act*, the period for municipal candidates to formalize their intentions is now more condensed. The nomination period will commence on May 1 and conclude on July 27 of this year.

* Top lender Bangkok Bank Q1 profit down 0.15 pct yr/yr
* Most banks report weaker-than-expected profits
* NPLs higher at most banks as economic recovery slow
By Orathai Sriring
BANGKOK, April 20 Most major Thai banks reported weaker-than-expected quarterly earnings on Thursday as they booked higher provisions for bad debt, with loans weak amid a tepid recovery in the country's economy.
Growth in Southeast Asia's second-largest economy has lagged its regional peers despite the military government's efforts to ramp up spending and investment.
Bangkok Bank Pcl, Thailand's top lender by assets, reported a first-quarter net profit of 8.3 billion baht ($241.42 million), down 0.15 percent from a year earlier.
That was below the average forecast of 8.6 billion baht by four analysts polled by Reuters.
The bank's set aside 5.8 billion baht in the March quarter, a 59 percent jump in provisions, as non-performing loans (NPLs) rose to 3.5 percent of lending from 3.2 percent at the end of 2016.
The bank's lending contracted 0.9 percent in the first quarter from the previous three months, it said. It blamed weak domestic activity and highlighted risks, saying "the economy, despite having a better outlook, still faces a considerable degree of uncertainty."
Third-ranked Siam Commercial Bank's net profit rose 1 percent rise in the first quarter to 11.9 billion, but that missed market expectations. It set aside 5 billion baht in the March quarter, when NPLs rose to 2.7 percent of lending.
The fourth-biggest lender, Kasikornbank Pcl, reported a smaller-than-expected 5.4 percent rise in first-quarter net profit.
Krung Thai Bank Pcl, Thailand's second-largest lender, reported a 13 percent rise in first-quarter net profit as provisioning expenses fell 13.5 percent.
But its non-performing loans rose to 4.36 percent of lending from 3.97 percent at end-2016, raising concern its provisioning will rise later this year.
Fitch Ratings said in January Thai banks' profits were likely to remain under pressure from asset-quality issues and slow fee-income growth .
($1 = 34.3800 baht) (Editing by Larry King)
rewrite:
A majority of Thailand's major commercial banks disclosed weaker-than-anticipated quarterly financial results on Thursday, April 20. This performance was primarily attributed to increased provisions for credit losses, subdued loan growth, and a gradual economic recovery. Despite fiscal stimulus and investment initiatives undertaken by the military government, economic expansion in Southeast Asia's second-largest economy continues to trail regional counterparts.

Bangkok Bank Public Company Limited, the nation's largest lender by assets, reported a first-quarter net profit of 8.3 billion baht (approximately $241.42 million). This figure represents a marginal year-on-year decline of 0.15 percent and fell below the Reuters poll consensus forecast of 8.6 billion baht. The bank significantly increased its impairment provisions by 59 percent to 5.8 billion baht for the quarter, reflecting a rise in non-performing loans (NPLs) to 3.5 percent of total lending, up from 3.2 percent at the close of 2016. Concurrently, its loan portfolio contracted by 0.9 percent quarter-on-quarter. The bank cited weak domestic activity, noting that while the economic outlook has improved, a considerable degree of uncertainty persists.

Among other major institutions, Siam Commercial Bank (SCB), the third-largest, recorded a modest 1 percent year-on-year increase in first-quarter net profit to 11.9 billion baht, which also missed market expectations. Its provisions amounted to 5 billion baht as NPLs climbed to 2.7 percent. Kasikornbank Pcl, ranked fourth, posted a smaller-than-forecast net profit increase of 5.4 percent. In contrast, Krung Thai Bank Pcl, the second-largest lender, reported a 13 percent rise in net profit, aided by a 13.5 percent reduction in provisioning expenses. However, its NPL ratio increased to 4.36 percent from 3.97 percent at end-2016, raising concerns that provisioning may need to increase later in the year. These results align with a January assessment from Fitch Ratings, which indicated that Thai banks' profitability would likely remain constrained by asset-quality pressures and slow growth in fee-based income.

Chinese factory activity grew at its fastest rate in eight months on stronger demand, a survey showed Thursday, in a positive sign for the world's No. 2 economy despite trade tensions with the U.S.
The official purchasing managers' index rose to 51.9 in May from 51.4 the previous month. Readings above 50 indicate expansion, while lower numbers indicate contraction on the index's 100-point scale.
Production, new export orders and overall new orders all increased from the previous month, indicating an uptick in demand, the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing's survey found.
"The pace of manufacturing expansion has accelerated and development momentum has been further strengthened," said Zhao Qinghe, senior statistician at the National Bureau of Statistics, which released the data on its website .
The latest figures show China's outsized export-manufacturing sector remains resilient despite continued tensions with the U.S. over the trading relationship between the world's two biggest economies.
The tensions had been ebbing until earlier this week, when President Donald Trump's administration renewed its threat to slap $50 billion worth of tariffs on Chinese goods and said it would also limit U.S. exports of high-tech goods to China. It's part of U.S. efforts to contain China's state-directed efforts to transform itself into a tech superpower.
But despite Washington's efforts, activity expanded in May, according to the survey's high-tech manufacturing sub-index, which rose in May to 54.8, up 1 point from the previous month.
The tariff threat came ahead of U.S. Commerce Department Secretary Wilbur Ross's visit to Beijing on Saturday for further negotiations on economic and trade issues.
Activity in China's increasingly important services sector also expanded. The group's non-manufacturing PMI rose to 54.9 for the month from 54.8 previously.
China's services industry is playing a bigger role as communist leaders upgrade economic growth, shifting it from a worn-out model based on wasteful trade and investment to one focused on domestic spending.
rewrite:
A survey released on Thursday indicated that Chinese manufacturing activity expanded at its most rapid pace in eight months, propelled by heightened demand. This development represents a positive signal for the world's second-largest economy, even amidst ongoing trade frictions with the United States. According to the data, the official purchasing managers' index (PMI) increased to 51.9 in May, rising from 51.4 in April. Within this index's 100-point scale, readings above the threshold of 50 denote expansion, while figures below signify contraction.

The survey, conducted by the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing, revealed month-on-month growth in production, new export orders, and overall new orders, collectively pointing to a resurgence in demand. Zhao Qinghe, a senior statistician at the National Bureau of Statistics—the agency that published the data—remarked that "the pace of manufacturing expansion has accelerated and development momentum has been further strengthened." These latest metrics demonstrate the continued resilience of China's substantial export-oriented manufacturing sector, notwithstanding persistent tensions in the trade relationship between the two global economic leaders.

Those tensions had shown signs of abating until earlier in the week, when the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump revived threats to impose tariffs on approximately $50 billion of Chinese imports and announced intentions to restrict exports of high-technology goods to China. These measures form part of broader U.S. initiatives to counter Chinese state-directed policies aimed at achieving technological supremacy. Despite these pressures, the survey's sub-index for high-tech manufacturing indicated expansion, climbing to 54.8 in May, a one-point increase from the preceding month. The tariff warnings preceded a scheduled visit to Beijing by U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross on Saturday for further negotiations on bilateral economic and trade issues.

Concurrently, activity in China's services sector, which is of growing importance to the economy, also expanded. The non-manufacturing PMI rose to 54.9 for May, up from 54.8 in April. This growth reflects a deliberate strategic shift by policymakers, who are transitioning the economy from a legacy model reliant on extensive trade and investment toward one increasingly driven by domestic consumption, thereby elevating the role of the services industry.

Mikhail Bora, a prosecution witness in the Sheena Bora murder case, has written to the CBI alleging that there is a threat to his life from his mother Indrani Mukerjea, the prime accused.
The central agency approached the trial court here, seeking a direction to authorities in Assam — as Mikhail lives in Guwahati — to look into his safety concerns.
CBI officer K K Singh, who filed the application before the court, said he received an email on Monday morning from Mikhail, saying he feared for his life and that his mother, accused of killing his sister Sheen Bora, would try and harm him too.
“The authority concerned in Assam is required to be informed about the threat to the life of the witness,” the CBI application said.
The email alleged that Indrani, who is lodged in prison here, did not want her mother Durga Ranee Bora’s will to be probated (to be certified as valid by the court), and hence she was using various means to harass Mikhail.
The will reportedly bequeaths all the property to Mikhail, cutting out Indrani.
“I stay all alone in the house with no help….I really fear for my life due to threat from Indrani Mukerjea,” the email said.
The court passed no order on the CBI plea, while continuing to record the testimony by Indrani’s former secretary Kajal Sharma.
Indrani, her ex-husband Sanjeev Khanna and her current husband and former media baron Peter Mukerjea are facing trial for the murder of Sheena Bora in April 2012.
Sheena was Indrani’s daughter from an earlier relationship. Mikhail is her second child.
According to the CBI, Indrani, after murdering Sheena, tried to kill Mikhail too by spiking his drink, but he escaped.
The agency alleged that financial disputes led to Sheena’s murder.
