TOKYO (Sputnik) - Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) on Saturday carried out a successful launch of the world's smallest carrier rocket SS-520-5, according to live broadcast by JAXA.
The liftoff took place from the Uchinoura Space Center at 02:03 p.m. local time (05:03 GMT).
The rocket is set to place into orbit a TRICOM-1R satellite for geological surveillance and communications with a mass of just three kilograms (6.6 pounds) developed at the University of Tokyo. The satellite would be used, in particular, for photographing the Earth's surface.
​The SS-520-5 is a three-stage rocket that is a modification of the SS-520 two-stage sounding rocket. The rocket is over 9.5 meters (29.5 feet long), with a diameter of 52 centimeters (1.71 feet) and a total mass of about 2,6 tonnes.
​The predecessor of this rocket, SS-520-4 was unsuccessfully launched on January 15, 2017. The transmission of the telemetry data stopped 20 seconds after liftoff and the decision was taken not to send a signal to the second stage of the rocket to turn on the engine. After disabling the first-stage engine, the rocket fell into the ocean.
rewrite:
On Saturday, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) successfully launched the SS-520-5, currently recognized as the world's smallest orbital launch vehicle. The launch was conducted from the Uchinoura Space Center at 14:03 local time (05:03 GMT) and was broadcast live by the agency. The rocket’s payload is the TRICOM-1R satellite, a three-kilogram device developed by the University of Tokyo for geological observation and communications, with a primary function of capturing imagery of the Earth's surface.

The SS-520-5 is a three-stage modified version of the two-stage SS-520 sounding rocket. It measures over 9.5 meters in length, has a diameter of 52 centimeters, and a total mass of approximately 2.6 tonnes. This launch follows a previous unsuccessful attempt with the SS-520-4 on January 15, 2017. During that mission, telemetry transmission ceased 20 seconds after liftoff, prompting controllers to withhold the ignition command for the second-stage engine. Subsequently, the first-stage engine was deactivated, and the vehicle descended into the ocean.

KEARNS, Utah — Canada’s Ted-Jan Bloemen set a world record Sunday on the final day of the World Cup speedskating event at the Utah Olympic Oval.
The Calgary native finished in six minutes 1.86 seconds in the men’s 5,000. Dutch skater Sven Kramer held the previous record of 6:03.32.
Germany’s Patrick Beckert was second in 6.10.80, and countryman Moritz Geisreiter followed in 6:11.47.
“That was amazing,” said Bloemen, who also holds the world record in the 10,000-metre distance. “I saw the other skaters do times of 6:07 before me, so I knew the ice was quite a bit faster than last weekend, and that maybe it was possible to beat the world record. But this fast? I didn’t expect it.”
Japan’s Nao Kodaira also set a record by finishing in 1:12.09 seconds in the women’s 1000 metres, her third race victory in three days. American Brittany Bowe held the previous record of 1:12.18. Japan’s Miho Takagi was second in 1:12.63, and Russia’s Yekaterina Shikhova followed in 1:13.23.
Bowe improved on a pair of 13th-place finishes in the 500s. She finished in 1:13.55 to place sixth in the 1,000.
Russia’s Denis Yuskov won the men’s 1,000 in 1:06.92. Yuskov edged Dutchman skater Koen Verweij, who finished in 106.94. Russia’s Pavel Kulizhnikov followed in 1:06.96.
Jonathan Garcia was the top American. Garcia was seventh with a personal best of 1:07.40. Joey Mantia was 10th, and Shani Davis 12th.
Russia’s Natalia Voronina took the women’s 3,000 in 3:57.70. The Czech Republic’s Martina Sablikova was second in 3:57.84, and Germany’s Claudia Pechstein finished third in 3:58.69.
Ottawa’s Ivanie Blondin finished fourth to end up fourth in overall standings following the four fall World Cups. She qualified for the 3,000 for the upcoming Winter Olympics with a top-five finish and a bronze collected earlier this year.
rewrite:
On the concluding day of the World Cup speedskating event at the Utah Olympic Oval in Kearns, Utah, Canadian athlete Ted-Jan Bloemen established a new world record. Bloemen, a native of Calgary, completed the men’s 5,000-meter race in six minutes and 1.86 seconds, surpassing the previous record of 6:03.32 held by Dutch skater Sven Kramer. The podium was completed by Germany’s Patrick Beckert, who secured second place with a time of 6:10.80, followed by his compatriot Moritz Geisreiter in third with 6:11.47. In post-race remarks, Bloemen expressed astonishment at his performance, noting that while favorable ice conditions suggested a record might be possible, the margin of improvement exceeded his expectations. Bloemen also holds the world record for the 10,000-meter distance.

In the women’s 1,000-meter event, Japan’s Nao Kodaira set a new world record with a time of 1:12.09, marking her third victory in as many days and eclipsing the previous record of 1:12.18 held by American skater Brittany Bowe. Kodaira was followed by Japan’s Miho Takagi in second place (1:12.63) and Russia’s Yekaterina Shikhova in third (1:13.23). Bowe improved upon her prior performances to place sixth in the 1,000-meter with a time of 1:13.55.

Other notable results included Russia’s Denis Yuskov winning the men’s 1,000-meter in 1:06.92, narrowly defeating Dutch skater Koen Verweij (1:06.94). Russia’s Pavel Kulizhnikov placed third with 1:06.96. The top American finisher in that event was Jonathan Garcia, who achieved a personal best of 1:07.40 for seventh place. In the women’s 3,000-meter, Russia’s Natalia Voronina claimed victory in 3:57.70, ahead of the Czech Republic’s Martina Sablikova (3:57.84) and Germany’s Claudia Pechstein (3:58.69). Canadian skater Ivanie Blondin placed fourth in the 3,000-meter, securing a top-five finish that qualified her for the event in the upcoming Winter Olympics and contributed to a fourth-place overall standing in the fall World Cup series.

Lakeshore Community Chorus invites singers to audition for its fall season.
The eighth-year ensemble, directed by W. Gene Coburn and Nancy Plantinga, will begin its season with a “Sunday Sing Through” Sept. 10 at First Congregational Church of Saugatuck, 296 Hoffman St., from 2 to 5 p.m. The event will give members an opportunity to get acquainted with the music and their peers.
Weekly Thursday rehearsals from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. start at the church Sept. 14.
The chorus will perform a collaborative concert with the New Century Chorale in Grand Blanc Nov. 5.
Its fall season will conclude with local Holiday Reflection concerts Saturday, Dec. 2, at 7:30 p.m. and Sunday, Dec. 3 at p.m. Members will also perform for Resthaven Maplewood residents in Holland this December.
Singers interested in auditioning should contact Nancy (616) 405 3399 or lakeshorecommunitychorus@gmail.com. For more information, visit lakeshorecommunitychorus.org.

SOME sellers are prepared to go to great lengths to get a quick sale on their property.
Richard Kruschel is one of them, offering a $3000 travel voucher to whomever buys his 29b Gardiner Ave, Warradale home before the end of July.
MORE NEWS: PASSING ON THE BATON IN ROSE PARK
MORE NEWS: COOL DESIGN IN HOT LOCATION
Mr Kruschel, who developed the property, said he came up with the idea with his selling agent, James Packham of Harcourts Packham, as a way of attracting a buyer quickly.
“As a developer you need to come up with new and inventive ideas to make your property stand out from the other homes on the market and this is a unique way of recognising what people need,” Mr Kruschel said.
“Often people are saving for a house or a holiday and most times they can’t have both, so this is a win-win in that it gives any potential purchaser what they need – who doesn’t need a holiday?”
Mr Kruschel said the home had been on the market for about a month before he added the incentive and that inquiry in the home had increased significantly since. “There’s certainly been a lot more interest and it’s really captured people’s attention,” Mr Kruschel said.
The three-bedroom, two-storey townhouse is on the market for $569,000 to $589,000 and, in order to qualify for the $3000 travel voucher, the home must be under contract by July 31, with settlement no later than September 30.
Mr Kruschel said the voucher was paid for in a deal between Mr Packham and himself, and that the travel agent, Hello World Travel, was selected because they both wanted to support a local business.
rewrite:

Richard Kruschel exemplifies this approach by offering a $3,000 travel voucher to the purchaser of his townhouse at 29b Gardiner Avenue, Warradale, provided a sale contract is finalized by July 31st. Kruschel, who developed the property, conceived this strategy in collaboration with his sales agent, James Packham of Harcourts Packham, as a mechanism to accelerate buyer interest. He posits that developers must utilize innovative methods to differentiate their listings, and this incentive uniquely addresses prospective buyers' concurrent needs. "Prospective purchasers are often compelled to choose between saving for a property and saving for leisure travel," Kruschel stated. "This initiative represents a mutually beneficial arrangement by providing a tangible reward that addresses a common aspiration."

Kruschel reports that the three-bedroom, two-storey townhouse, priced between $569,000 and $589,000, had been listed for approximately one month prior to the introduction of the voucher. Since its implementation, he has observed a marked increase in inquiries, noting that the offer has successfully captured market attention. To qualify for the incentive, the transaction must reach settlement no later than September 30th. The voucher's cost is shared between Kruschel and Packham, and the designated provider, Hello World Travel, was selected specifically to patronize a local business. This case study illustrates a tactical marketing deviation from standard practice, designed to create urgency and added perceived value within a specific transactional timeframe.

Galatasaray have dismissed reports their Portugal under-21 international Bruma has agreed a move to Tottenham.
Turkish newspaper Sabah claimed on Monday a deal worth in the region of £12.5million had been struck with the Premier League club.
But Galatasaray posted a withering statement on their official website to deny this was the case, while also rejecting suggestions Bruma had sought "a 100 per cent raise as a condition to sign a new contract with our club".
The statement read: "In this news that is not really interesting, there is no official offer to reach us, just as there is no secret agreement for the price [with] the club that has been named [Tottenham]."
Bruma joined Galatasaray from Sporting CP in September 2013 and has spent time on loan at Gaziantepspor and Real Sociedad.
The 22-year-old has starred with eight goals and six assists for Igor Tudor's side in the Super Lig this season and his current deal expires in June 2018.
rewrite: Galatasaray has formally refuted media reports alleging that their Portuguese under-21 international player, Bruma, has agreed to transfer to Tottenham Hotspur. The denial was issued via an official club statement in response to claims published by the Turkish newspaper Sabah, which suggested a fee of approximately £12.5 million had been settled with the Premier League side. The club explicitly dismissed the existence of any such agreement, while also countering assertions that Bruma had demanded a one hundred percent salary increase as a precondition for renewing his contract. The statement clarified that no official offer from the named club has been received, nor has any clandestine arrangement been made. Bruma, who joined Galatasaray from Sporting CP in September 2013 and has had loan spells at Gaziantepspor and Real Sociedad, is under contract until June 2018. The 22-year-old has contributed eight goals and six assists in the Super Lig this season.

Max Verstappen says he had no warning of the brake failure that saw the Red Bull driver end his Bahrain GP in the tire wall.
Verstappen had just copied Sebastian Vettel by making an early first stop, but soon after resuming he suffered a loss of rear brake pressure that left him with stopping power only in the front. He skated across the run off and just clipped the tire wall.
“It’s not a very nice feeling if you hit the pedal and the pedal just goes very long and you can’t stop the car properly,” he said. “As soon as I hit the brakes, it just went long. This track is always a little bit harder on the brakes, and then with the pit stop they heat up even more. Something just overheated too quickly.
“The brakes in general are always a little bit on the limit here, but I didn’t see it coming. I hit the brake pedal and suddenly it failed.”
The frustration for Verstappen and his team was that he had enjoyed a good first lap and was pushing Lewis Hamilton before the stop.
“It was a good start, I chose the outside at Turn One, and that seemed to work pretty well. I already got two positions on lap one, and from then on I was keeping up with the guys in front of me.
“I was trying to push up to Lewis, and Lewis was pushing to the guys in front, and it seemed to work pretty well for us.
“The car was performing really well, especially in the race, we were just up there with the guys. I think the car is really good on the tires, and that was a good advantage for us on this track. It was a positive race up until that point for me. It should have been a lot of points.
“The pit stop was the right call, we would have ended up second after that lap. That was very good, but it was not meant to be.”
What’s racing this weekend?
rewrite:
Max Verstappen reported experiencing no prior indication of the brake system failure that culminated in his retirement from the Bahrain Grand Prix following an impact with the tire barrier. The Red Bull driver had emulated the strategy of Sebastian Vettel by executing an early first pit stop. Shortly after rejoining the circuit, however, he encountered a critical loss of hydraulic pressure in the rear braking circuit, resulting in deceleration capability being confined solely to the front brakes. This imbalance caused the car to traverse the runoff area and make contact with the tire wall.

Verstappen described the incident, stating, “It is a particularly disconcerting sensation when the brake pedal travel becomes excessively long and the car cannot be decelerated adequately. Immediately upon braking, the pedal travel was abnormal. This circuit consistently presents elevated brake demands, and the thermal cycle associated with a pit stop exacerbates their temperature. In this instance, a component overheated precipitously. While the braking systems operate near their thermal limits here, the failure was entirely unforeseen. I applied the brakes and the system abruptly failed.”

The episode proved particularly frustrating for Verstappen and his team, as his competitive performance prior to the failure had been strong. He executed an effective opening lap, gaining two positions, and subsequently maintained pace with the leading group. “The initial phase was positive,” Verstappen noted. “I selected the outside line at Turn One, which proved advantageous. Having gained those positions, I was able to match the pace of the cars ahead. I was applying pressure to Lewis Hamilton, who was in turn challenging the leaders, and our performance was competitive.”

He further emphasized the car’s race performance, adding, “The car was performing at a high level, particularly in race trim, allowing us to compete with the front-runners. Its tire management appeared to be a distinct advantage on this layout. The race was progressing very positively for me until that moment. A significant points haul was anticipated.” Reflecting on the strategic decision, he concluded, “The pit stop itself was the correct call; we would have emerged in second position following that sequence. The potential outcome was favorable, but it ultimately was not realized.”

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has of late taken unprecedented moves to modernize the country, with the most recent move including lifting the ban on movie theaters.
After more than 35 years Saudi Arabia will allow movie theaters to open all around the kingdom. The latest move is in tune with the reformist mission that the young Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman has embarked on.
The resolution was passed on Monday heralding licenses to be given to commercial movie theaters, decades after all cinemas were shuttered in the 1980's during a wave of ultraconservatism in the country.
"Commercial cinemas will be allowed to operate in the Kingdom as of early 2018, for the first time in more than 35 years," the culture and information ministry said in a statement.
© REUTERS/ Faisal Al Nasser Driving Licenses for Women in Saudi Arabia to 'Boost Economy'
The country is expected to have more than 300 cinemas with over 2,000 screens by 2030, the ministry said.
Earlier Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud had spoken out in favor of returning to "moderate Islam."
He has been pushing for socio-cultural reforms which include lifting the ban on women driving in the country and allowing women to attend sports events at stadiums.
"We will return to the former state or affairs, to moderate Islam, which is open to the world, and all other religions. We will not wait for 30 years, we will swiftly deal a blow to extremist ideologies," the crown prince said during the Future Investment Initiative forum held in Riyadh in October.
In September, Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud signed a royal decree permitting Saudi women to drive cars, for the first time in history of the country. The decree is set to come into effect in June, 2018.
The Saudi authorities will also start renovating the main stadiums in the cities’ of Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah to be ready to receive families starting in 2018.
According to the Arab News newspaper earlier in October, President of the Saudi Olympic Committee, Turki Al-Asheikh, appointed Princess Reema bint Bandar president of the Saudi Federation for Community Sports.
rewrite:
In a significant shift toward societal modernization, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has recently enacted a series of unprecedented reforms, most notably the decision to end a decades-long prohibition on public cinemas. This move marks the imminent return of commercial movie theaters to the nation, a development not witnessed in over thirty-five years. The policy aligns with the broader reform agenda, known as Vision 2030, championed by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The official resolution, announced on Monday by the Ministry of Culture and Information, will permit the licensing and operation of cinemas beginning in early 2018. This reverses a policy instituted in the 1980s, when cinemas were closed amid a period of heightened religious conservatism. The ministry further projected that, by the year 2030, the kingdom will host more than 300 cinemas containing over 2,000 screens.

This cultural liberalization forms part of a wider initiative endorsed by the Crown Prince, who has publicly advocated for a return to a "moderate Islam" that is open to global engagement. His reform program includes several landmark social changes. Among these is the historic royal decree, signed by King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud in September, which grants women the right to drive, effective June 2018. Additionally, women will be permitted to attend sporting events in stadiums, with major venues in Riyadh, Dammam, and Jeddah undergoing renovation to accommodate families starting in 2018. The commitment to integrating women into public life is further evidenced by the October appointment of Princess Reema bint Bandar as President of the Saudi Federation for Community Sports, as reported by *Arab News*.

During the Future Investment Initiative forum in Riyadh in October, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman explicitly framed these measures as a decisive break with extremist ideologies, stating an intent to swiftly foster a more open and moderate society. Collectively, these policies represent a concerted effort to transform Saudi Arabia's socio-cultural landscape and diversify its economy, signaling a notable departure from long-standing social restrictions.

WOOLWICH TOWNSHIP, N.J. (AP) - Police in New Jersey were put to the test over the weekend when they were called to catch a loose pig.
Three Woolwich Township police officers responded to a call about a mischievous pig roaming a neighborhood Saturday morning. Police said three officers used a makeshift lasso and dog treats to lure the pet pig back into its owner's yard.
In a self-deprecating Facebook post , the Woolwich Township Police Department quipped, "No pig(s) were hurt in the process." The department also invited commenters to make their best "pig/bacon/cop" jokes.
The department's piggy post has received more than 700 likes and 70 comments.
One commenter asked if the pig could become the station's new mascot. Several said the post made them want to move to the township.
Another commenter wrote, "Way to bring home the bacon, fellas."

rewrite: On Saturday morning, officers from the Woolwich Township Police Department in New Jersey responded to a call concerning a domestic pig at large within a residential area. The department subsequently documented the incident in a lighthearted Facebook post, noting that no pigs were harmed during the procedure and inviting public engagement through humorous commentary related to pigs and law enforcement. The post garnered significant public attention, accumulating over 700 reactions and 70 comments. Community responses ranged from suggestions to adopt the pig as a departmental mascot to expressions of increased residential interest in the township. One notable comment praised the officers' efforts with the phrase, "Way to bring home the bacon, fellas."

The Arizona Cardinals have not yet signed any cornerback since the start of free agency, but a couple have been on their radar. They wish to re-sign veteran Tramon Williams and also brought in E.J. Gaines.
They reportedly have interest in another free agent, one who has some familiarity with new Cardinals coach Steve Wilks.
According to Aaron Wilson, they, along with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, are interested in CB Robert McClain.
Cardinals and Buccaneers among NFL teams interested in free agent cornerback Robert McClain, according to league sources — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) March 19, 2018
McClain is a small cornerback at 5-9, 180 pounds. He has been in the league since 2010, drafted originally by the Carolina Panthers in the seventh round. He has bounced around a bit, going from Carolina to the Atlanta Falcons, back to Carolina in 2015 and 2016, then to the San Diego Chargers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
He has some position flexibility, playing both cornerback and safety. Last season in Tampa, he played in 14 games, starting nine. He had 44 tackles, five broken up passes and three interceptions, one of which he returned for a touchdown. It was a career high in picks.
While in Carolina for his second stint, his position coach was Wilks.
Perhaps McClain is a backup plan for the Cardinals in case they cannot re-sign Tramon Williams or sign Gaines, or perhaps he would be added to simply add depth to Arizona’s defensive backs.
Listen to the latest from Cards Wire’s Jess Root on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Apple podcasts or Stitcher Radio.

McClain potentially serves as a contingency option should the Cardinals fail to secure Williams or Gaines, or he may be targeted to augment depth within the defensive secondary.

PSM’s Latching Water Level Indicator: Alerting Operators to Sub-Station Flooding Hazards
PSM’s Latching Water Level Indicator was initially designed and manufactured over 10 years ago, and to date PSM have sold nearly 10,000 units to energy companies throughout the world for use in subterranean distribution and control stations and other areas liable to flooding.
Mainly intended for use in areas which are normally unmanned and visited infrequently, the indicator provides an immediate visual warning of possible hazards due to flooding that may have occurred and subsequently receded, leaving no indication otherwise. One risk scenario is that oil insulation on high voltage switching may have been displaced by water with potential life-threatening consequences should the equipment be operated.
Designed to be highly visible from a safe distance, the float will automatically rise with any incoming floodwater and latch at the highest recorded level to provide an immediate visual alert to the risk, without the need to enter the immediate area.
One or more switch modules may be fitted on the Indicator, and in a flood condition, a magnet embedded in the float will activate these to trigger local or remote alarms. In unmanned locations, the signal can be sent via telemetry to a central office.
Once the installation has been examined and made safe the indicator may be mechanically reset by the operator ready to alert of further dangers.
There are very good reasons why so many energy companies have turned to PSM’s Latching Water Level Indicator to ensure the safety of their sub stations from flood hazards, so for additional information about the product, please visit www.psmmarine.com or contact Mark Jones, Sales & Marketing Manager at PSM Instrumentation, by e-mail: [email protected] or telephone: +44 (0)144 410 040.
For press information email Charmaine Kimpton at [email protected] or telephone 01483 203010/07414 749973.
This is a promoted article.
rewrite:
The PSM Latching Water Level Indicator, originally engineered and introduced to the market over a decade ago, serves as a critical safety device for monitoring water ingress in subterranean electrical distribution and control stations. To date, approximately 10,000 units have been deployed by energy utilities globally in environments susceptible to flooding. The apparatus is principally intended for deployment in normally unoccupied locations that are subject only to periodic inspection. It provides a persistent visual warning of flood events that may have occurred and subsequently receded, leaving no other immediate evidence. This function is vital, as one significant risk involves the displacement of oil insulation in high-voltage switching equipment by water, creating a potentially lethal hazard upon subsequent operation.

Engineered for high visibility from a safe distance, the device incorporates a float mechanism that ascends with rising water and mechanically latches at the peak level attained. This latching feature provides an unambiguous, immediate visual alert to the flooding risk without necessitating entry into the potentially hazardous area. Furthermore, the indicator can be equipped with one or more switch modules. During a flood condition, a magnet integrated within the float activates these switches, which can then trigger local or remote alarm systems. In unattended installations, this signal can be transmitted via telemetry to a central monitoring facility. Following a site inspection and the restoration of safe conditions, an operator can mechanically reset the device, preparing it to detect subsequent events.

The widespread adoption of this indicator by energy companies underscores its demonstrated utility in mitigating flood-related risks to critical infrastructure. For further technical specifications or commercial inquiries, please consult the manufacturer's website at www.psmmarine.com or contact the Sales and Marketing Manager, Mark Jones, at PSM Instrumentation via email at [email protected] or by telephone at +44 (0)144 410 040.

STERLING, Va. (AP) — President Donald Trump wished America a happy Fourth of July holiday Wednesday and reserved special praise for the "American heroes" whose sacrifice he said helped the nation win her independence 242 years ago.
Trump tweeted a short video that included well wishes from him and first lady Melania Trump. The Trumps were hosting a White House picnic for military families later Wednesday, followed by a concert and viewing of the fireworks on the National Mall.
"Our freedom has been earned through the blood and sweat and sacrifice of American heroes," Trump said.
Trump left the White House on Wednesday morning clad in a white short-sleeved shirt, dark slacks and a cap and was driven west across the Potomac River in the direction of the private golf club he owns in Northern Virginia.

The White House did not immediately confirm that Trump is at the club. Reporters were not allowed to accompany him to his destination, as is the case with virtually all presidential travel.
Trump got into the Independence Day spirit a day earlier by celebrating active-duty service members during a military tribute Tuesday night in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia. At the "Salute to Service" charity dinner, Trump praised "Americans of every generation" who have served in the armed forces.

rewrite:
On Wednesday, July 4th, President Donald Trump extended holiday greetings to the nation in observance of Independence Day. The First Family was scheduled to host a picnic for military families at the White House later that day, culminating in an evening concert and fireworks display on the National Mall.

Ile-Ife (Osun) – The Governing Council of Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, has appointed Mrs Margaret Omosule as the 12th Registrar and Secretary to the Governing Council of the university.
A press release issued on Wednesday in Ile-Ife by the Public Relations Officer of the institution, Mr Abiodun Olarewaju, said Omosule was the Deputy-Registrar and Acting Director, Vice-Chancellor’ s Office, prior to her appointment.
The release said that Omosule, a native of Ughelli South Local Government of Delta, holds a Bachelor of Arts (B.A) (Ed.) Degree in History (1984) and Masters Degree in Guidance and Counselling (1990), both from OAU.
“She is currently on her Ph.D Programme in the Department of Educational Foundation and Counselling, Faculty of Education, OAU, Ile-Ife.
“The new appointee began to garner work experience as an Education Officer at the Ministry of Education, Akure, during her NYSC schedule between 1984 and 1985,’’ the release added.
It also said that Omosule worked at Moremi High School, OAU, between 1991 and 1995.
Omosule, it added, joined the service of OAU as an Administrative Officer 1 on Jan 23, 1995 and rose through the ranks to the post of Deputy Registrar in 2011.
It said that since Omosule joined the university, she had served in different capacities and in various arms of the university.
Omosule, according to the release, acquired knowledge and experience in the university’s administration processes and procedures at junior, intermediate and higher levels. (NAN)
rewrite:

According to a press release issued in Ile-Ife on Wednesday by the University's Public Relations Officer, Mr. Abiodun Olarewaju, Mrs. Omosule previously held the positions of Deputy Registrar and Acting Director of the Vice-Chancellor’s Office.

She subsequently advanced through the ranks, attaining the position of Deputy Registrar in 2011. Throughout her tenure, Mrs. Omosule has served in diverse capacities across multiple university divisions, thereby acquiring comprehensive knowledge and experience in administrative processes and procedures at junior, intermediate, and senior levels.

"They showed a lot of character and will and desire, and we bounced back after a disappointing result."
The Whitecaps (15-10-6) have the third-best road record in all of MLS at 6-7-2, and also picked up a 1-1 draw against the Red Bulls (12-12-7) in Harrison, N.J., in the first leg of their CONCACAF Champions league quarter-finals back in February before the regular season.

Newsflash: Uranus stinks!
The seventh planet from the sun — and the butt of all cosmic fart jokes — actually does smell like flatulence, according to a new study from the University of Oxford.
The space rock’s upper atmosphere is made up of hydrogen sulfide, the compound that creates the smell of rotten eggs — and human farts — according to the research published in the journal Nature Astronomy.
“If an unfortunate human were ever to descend through Uranus’s clouds, they would be met with very unpleasant and odiferous conditions,” Patrick Irwin, an Oxford physicist who led the study, said in a statement.
But thankfully humans will likely never catch a whiff of the gassy planet.
“Suffocation and exposure in the -200 degrees Celsius atmosphere made of mostly hydrogen, helium, and methane would take its toll long before the smell,” Irwin pointed out.
To sniff out the discovery, scientists used a high-tech 8-meter telescope to take a peek at light bouncing off Uranus.
Researchers determined a layer of clouds above the planet were hydrogen-sulfide molecules based on wavelengths of light — much to the delight of Twitter users, who called the fart-centric discovery a gas.
“Oh my god… WHAT!!! Every joke about this planet was true. Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha! LOL!!!” tweeted one twitter user @romelojames.
Deborah Netburn, an L.A. based science writer added, “Thank you, universe, for this cosmic fart joke.”

Recent research from the University of Oxford, published in *Nature Astronomy*, has confirmed the presence of hydrogen sulfide in the upper atmosphere of Uranus. This compound, known for producing the odor of rotten eggs and being a component of flatulence, substantiates the long-standing humorous association regarding the planet's olfactory characteristics. According to the study's lead, physicist Patrick Irwin, any hypothetical human descent through the atmospheric clouds of Uranus would encounter profoundly unpleasant and malodorous conditions. However, such sensory exposure remains improbable, as the extreme environment—with temperatures near -200 degrees Celsius and an atmosphere composed primarily of hydrogen, helium, and methane—would prove fatal well before the odor could be perceived.

The detection was achieved through spectroscopic analysis of light reflected from Uranus, utilizing an 8-meter telescope. By examining specific absorption wavelengths, researchers identified the spectral signature of hydrogen sulfide within a distinct cloud layer. This finding has elicited considerable public amusement on social media platforms, with users noting the ironic validation of prior comedic assertions about the planet. One representative reaction expressed astonishment and humor at the confirmation, while science commentator Deborah Netburn remarked on the universe's provision of a "cosmic fart joke." The study thus provides a concrete chemical basis for a pervasive cultural trope while advancing the detailed atmospheric characterization of an outer planet.

Author Philip Pullman has announced he will be doing a follow-up trilogy to the hugely successful His Dark Materials.
The first novel will be called The Book of Dust and is set to hit shelves in October - it comes 17 years after the last instalment.
Pullman has revealed the series will return to the story of Lyra Belacqua - a young girl who wanders through a parallel universe.
The trilogy will begin when the heroine is a baby and move on to when she is 20-years-old - it will be set between London and Oxford.
It is believed at least one of the instalments will be set ten years after His Dark Materials ended.
The 70-year-old author says the new trilogy is an "equel" meaning it is neither a sequel or a prequel.
Speaking on BBC 4's Today Programme he said: "People say, 'Is it prequel? Is it a sequel?' Well, it is neither.
"It's an 'equel'. It's a different story which begins roughly 10 years before His Dark Materials and ends roughly 10 years after."
Dust is a mysterious and troubling substance at the centre of the original books and Pullman said he has always wanted to return to it and discover it more.
On Pullman's website, Dust is described as: "A source of great anxiety to the Authority, that is the church.
"Dust, it believes, is the physical evidence of original sin. Dust comes to us when we grow up and become corrupted by the wickedness of the world, of knowledge."
The His Dark Materials trilogy consists of Northern Lights (1995), The Subtle Knife (1997) and The Amber Spyglass (2000).
In addition there are also two short novels Lyra's Oxford and Once Upon a Time in the North.

In light of the inter-community nature of the case, police have intensified patrols in the vicinity as a precautionary measure to prevent further unrest.

SYDNEY, Australia — Cardinal George Pell, the most senior Catholic official to face sex offence charges, was jeered by protesters as he made a court appearance in his native Australia in a case that has rocked the Vatican and placed scrutiny on the pope's stance against abusive clergy.
Australia's highest-ranking Roman Catholic and Pope Francis' top financial adviser, Pell entered the Melbourne Magistrates Court Friday flanked by police and media as a small group of placard-waving protesters yelled from the sidewalk. He did not react to the hecklers.
The 20-minute hearing focused on planning for the committal hearing starting March 5 that will determine whether he goes to trial. As many as 50 witnesses could be called for that proceeding, expected to last a month.
Pell, who remained silent throughout, has been charged with multiple offences involving multiple complainants. The exact detail and nature of the charges have not been disclosed to the public, though police have described them as "historical" sexual assault offences, meaning they are alleged to have occurred years ago.
Pell through his lawyer has vowed to fight the charges. The 76-year-old cardinal has taken leave from his position as Vatican treasurer to return to Australia and defend himself. He has not been required to enter a plea in court, though his attorney said at his first court appearance in July that Pell intended to plead not guilty.
Pell's lawyer, Robert Richter, told Friday's hearing at least one of the allegations could not have happened.
"We propose to demonstrate to Your Honour that what was alleged was impossible," Richter told magistrate Belinda Wallington.
Today's brief hearing centred on which witnesses would be cross-examined at the committal hearing, and touched on a factor likely to feature prominently in the case — the memories of witnesses speaking about incidents alleged to have occurred up to several decades ago.
After years of alleged coverups and silence from the church over its pedophilia scandal, abuse survivors and their advocates have hailed the prosecution of Pell as a monumental shift in the way society is responding to the crisis.

A group of demonstrators, bearing placards, shouted from the sidewalk, though the Cardinal exhibited no visible reaction.

The procedural hearing, lasting approximately twenty minutes, primarily addressed logistical preparations for the forthcoming committal proceeding scheduled to commence on March 5. This committal hearing, which may extend for one month and involve testimony from as many as fifty witnesses, will determine whether sufficient evidence exists for the case to proceed to trial. Cardinal Pell, who remained silent throughout the session, faces multiple charges from several complainants. While the precise details and nature of these charges have not been publicly disclosed, authorities have characterized them as “historical” sexual assault offences, indicating the alleged incidents occurred years in the past.

Cardinal Pell, aged 76, has taken leave from his position as Vatican treasurer to contest the charges in Australia. Through his legal counsel, he has vigorously declared his intention to defend himself. Although no formal plea was entered during this hearing, his attorney, Robert Richter, indicated in a prior court appearance in July that Cardinal Pell would plead not guilty. During Friday’s proceedings, Mr. Richter asserted that at least one of the allegations was factually impossible, stating to Magistrate Belinda Wallington, “We propose to demonstrate to Your Honour that what was alleged was impossible.”

The hearing focused on establishing which witnesses will be subject to cross-examination during the committal process. A central and anticipated challenge discussed was the reliability of witness testimony concerning events alleged to have transpired several decades prior. This prosecution is viewed by many abuse survivors and their advocates as a pivotal development, representing a significant societal shift in addressing the clerical abuse crisis following years of alleged institutional cover-ups and silence within the Church.

Updated at 2:10 p.m. ET
A judge declined to set bond for an Ohio man during his first court appearance after allegedly ramming a vehicle into a crowd of people demonstrating against a white supremacist rally Saturday in Charlottesville, Va.
Charlottesville resident Heather Heyer was killed, and at least 19 other people were in injured in the attack.
The Charlottesville Police Department said Saturday that James Alex Fields Jr., 20, of Maumee, Ohio, was charged with one count of second-degree murder, three counts of malicious wounding and one count of hit-and run.
During today's Charlottesville court hearing, as NPR's Debbie Elliott reports, Fields "appeared by video from jail, dressed in a gray and white-striped prison jumpsuit."
He answered the judge's questions with a simple "Yes, sir" and "No, sir," according to The Associated Press.
Fields told Judge Robert Downer that he could not afford a lawyer. "Downer assigned a court-appointed attorney to represent Fields, and set another hearing for Aug. 25," Debbie adds. "Until then, the judge said, Fields would remain in jail with no bond in part because he has no ties to the area."
The AP adds that the judge told the court that the "public defenders' office informed him it could not represent Fields because a relative of someone in the office was injured in Saturday's protest." Fields was taken into custody on Saturday after the incident.
Details are emerging about Fields' background and his interest in Nazi Germany. One of the suspect's high school teachers in Ohio told member station WVXU that Fields "was intelligent and didn't cause trouble," but was "also deeply into Adolf Hitler and white supremacy."
Derek Weimer, who had Fields in three classes at Randall K. Cooper High School in Union, Ky., told WVXU, "He went to a good school. Lived in a good neighborhood. There were plenty of people around to try to guide him in the right direction. My first feeling is we failed. I failed."
Fields' mother, Samantha Bloom, told The Toledo Blade that she was aware her son was going to what he called an "alt-right" rally. "I told him to be careful," Bloom said, according to the newspaper. "[And] if they're going to rally to make sure he's doing it peacefully."

The attack resulted in the death of Charlottesville resident Heather Heyer and injuries to at least nineteen other individuals.

According to the Charlottesville Police Department, James Alex Fields Jr., a twenty-year-old from Maumee, Ohio, has been charged with one count of second-degree murder, three counts of malicious wounding, and one count of hit-and-run. As reported by NPR’s Debbie Elliott, during the Charlottesville court hearing, Fields appeared via video link from jail, attired in a gray and white-striped prison uniform. The Associated Press notes that he responded to the judge’s inquiries with simple affirmations and denials, stating only “Yes, sir” and “No, sir.”

Fields informed Judge Robert Downer that he could not afford legal counsel. Consequently, Judge Downer assigned a court-appointed attorney to represent him and scheduled a subsequent hearing for August 25. The judge ordered Fields to be detained without bond until that date, citing in part the defendant’s lack of ties to the local area. The Associated Press further reports that the judge informed the court the public defenders’ office had declared a conflict of interest, as a relative of an employee in that office was injured during Saturday’s protest. Fields was taken into custody on the day of the incident.

Information regarding Fields’ background and ideological leanings is emerging. A former high school teacher from Ohio informed member station WVXU that, while Fields was academically capable and not disruptive, he exhibited a profound fascination with Adolf Hitler and white supremacist ideology. Derek Weimer, who instructed Fields in three classes at Randall K. Cooper High School in Union, Kentucky, stated to WVXU, “He went to a good school. Lived in a good neighborhood. There were plenty of people around to try to guide him in the right direction. My first feeling is we failed. I failed.” In an interview with The Toledo Blade, Fields’ mother, Samantha Bloom, indicated she was aware her son intended to attend what he described as an “alt-right” rally. She advised him to exercise caution and, if he chose to participate, to ensure his actions remained peaceful.

AUGUSTA, Georgia, April 9 Fan favourite Fred Couples vowed to return next year to the tournament he loves after completing his 32nd U.S. Masters on Sunday.
The 57-year-old American admitted to feeling fatigued after finishing equal 18th at one-over 289, but said the applause that greeted him as he walked up the back nine gave him a lift.
"It's a fun, great tournament," he told reporters. "I enjoy it and I'll be back next year."
Couples, who missed most of the last season with back issues, credits a specialist he brought with him to Augusta for helping him endure the taxing four rounds.
"It was very good to bring him here, and he was a big help."
Couples, who one his only Green Jacket 25 years ago, last won a PGA Tour event in 2003 at the Houston Open.
But he has also had 12 wins on the Champions Tour, including one this year.

Barcelona have agreed a deal with Guangzhou Evergrande to sign Brazilian midfielder Paulinho for €40million, the Spanish club confirmed.
The new Barcelona player will sign for the next four seasons (and) the players buyout clause is set at €120million , Barcelona said in a statement.
Paulinho will undergo a club medical on Thursday when the signing of the contract and his official presentation will also take place.
The 29-year-old is Barcelona's first signing since the Spanish giants sold Neymar to Paris St Germain earlier this month for a world record €222million , with the Catalans still looking to make further reinforcements.
Liverpool's Philippe Coutinho and Borussia Dortmund's Ousmane Dembele have both been targeted by Barcelona as they search for a player capable of replacing Neymar's spark on the left of the attack.
Coutinho has handed in a transfer request at Anfield. Barcelona have had two bids rejected for Coutinho and are poised to return with a third offer, according to reports in Spain.
The arrival of Coutinho's Brazil team mate Paulinho will allow Barcelona to add more muscle and energy to a midfield which struggled to keep control of games last season.
"Paulinho is a player who stands out for being a powerful midfielder at 1.82m tall who can get into the box and play anywhere in the middle of the park. He has plenty of experience in the game on various continents, Barcelona added.
Paulinho failed to make an impact in the Premier League with Tottenham Hotspur after joining from Corinthians and departed to Guangzhou Evergrande in 2015 for €14million.
While in the Chinese top flight Paulinho found his best form, scoring 25 goals in 95 games for Guangzhou, and earned a recall to the Brazilian national side.

The club's statement highlighted his profile as a powerful, box-to-box midfielder standing 1.82 meters tall, capable of operating in various central roles and bringing considerable multinational experience.

× Woman, 92, Allegedly Killed Son Who Wanted to Put Her in a Nursing Home
FOUNTAIN HILLS, Az. — A 92-year-old woman allegedly killed her son in Arizona because she did not want to be sent to an assisted living facility, authorities said.
Anna Mae Blessing was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after authorities found her 72-year-old son dead Monday at their home in Fountain Hills, Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office said.
Blessing hid two pistols in the pockets of her robe and shot her son several times in his bedroom, the sheriff’s office said in a statement.
Her son’s girlfriend was also in the room and said she heard Blessing telling her son she was tired of the way he treated her, court documents said.
“From my understanding, she had thought about it for a few days because there was a dispute regarding her son wanting to put her in an assisted living home,” Maricopa County Sgt. Bryant Vanejas told CNN affiliate KPHO.
Blessing then pointed the gun at her son’s girlfriend, who struggled with her until she lost her grip of the gun. When Blessing pulled out the second pistol from her robe, her son’s girlfriend also knocked it out of her hand, the statement said.
Once she was disarmed, Blessing sat on a reclining chair until deputies arrived and arrested her, officials said.
“As the suspect was being escorted from the residence, she made a spontaneous statement to the effect of ‘You took my life, so I’m taking yours,'” court documents said.
Blessing moved in with her son and his girlfriend about six months ago, the affiliate reported.
She told deputies she had purchased one of the guns in the late 1970s and that her husband gave her the other pistol, court documents say.
Information on her attorney was not immediately available.
rewrite:
A nonagenarian woman in Arizona has been charged with the homicide of her son, reportedly motivated by her opposition to potential institutionalization in an assisted living facility. According to the Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office, Anna Mae Blessing, 92, faces charges of first-degree murder, aggravated assault, and kidnapping following the discovery of her 72-year-old son’s body at their shared residence in Fountain Hills. Authorities allege that Blessing concealed two firearms within her robe and fired multiple rounds at her son within his bedroom.

Per court documents, the son’s girlfriend, who was present during the incident, reported hearing Blessing express frustration with her son’s treatment of her. Investigative statements indicate the conflict stemmed from a protracted dispute regarding the son’s intent to relocate his mother to a care facility. “From my understanding, she had thought about it for a few days because there was a dispute regarding her son wanting to put her in an assisted living home,” stated Maricopa County Sergeant Bryant Vanejas.

Following the initial shooting, Blessing reportedly aimed a weapon at the girlfriend, who subsequently disarmed her after a physical struggle. When Blessing produced a second pistol, it was also wrested from her grasp. Upon being disarmed, Blessing awaited law enforcement’s arrival seated in a recliner. During her arrest, she allegedly made a spontaneous utterance to the effect of, “You took my life, so I’m taking yours.” Blessing had reportedly resided with her son and his girlfriend for approximately six months prior to the incident. She informed deputies that one firearm was purchased in the late 1970s and the other was a gift from her deceased husband. Information regarding legal representation was not immediately available.

GRAND HAVEN, Mich. - A young Michigan girl is helping her classmates this holiday season, making sure they get a hot lunch at school by selling handmade "stretchy straw fidgeters," according to WXMI.
"Big ones are a dollar and little ones are 50 cents," said Lexi Bergeron, whose mother said she was inspired after hearing about students who couldn't afford lunches on the nightly news. She found out that some of her classmates would only get cheese sandwiches if they have a debt on their lunch account.
Lexi is in 4th grade at Ferry Elementary. She is "Paying It Forward" not just for her school, but the whole district. Lexi started making fidget strings for $1 each, and made $11 the first week.
Lexi's mother, Sara, put together a GoFundMe page, hoping to raise $188 to pay off the entire Ferry Elementary school lunch debt. That effort exceeded expectations and now they are hoping to raise thousands to wipe away all lunch debts in the district.
Their goal is $2,200 by the end of December. If you'd like to help, visit the GoFundMe page here.
rewrite:
In Grand Haven, Michigan, a fourth-grade student at Ferry Elementary School is undertaking an initiative to address school lunch debt among her peers. Motivated by a news report concerning students unable to afford full meals, Lexi Bergeron learned that some classmates receive only cheese sandwiches when their accounts are in arrears. In response, she began crafting and selling handmade "stretchy straw fidgeters," pricing larger versions at one dollar and smaller ones at fifty cents. Her initial week of sales yielded eleven dollars.

Lexi’s efforts, described as "Paying It Forward," aim to benefit not only her school but the entire district. Her mother, Sara Bergeron, established a GoFundMe campaign with an initial objective of erasing the $188 lunch debt at Ferry Elementary. This fundraising initiative has surpassed its original target, and the goal has been expanded to eliminate all district lunch debts, with a new aim of raising $2,200 by the end of December. The campaign continues to solicit community support to achieve this outcome.

AUGUSTA,Ga (WJBF) Augusta Commissioners say reassigning the city’s Chief Probation Officer was necessary to keep the city from getting sued.
Commissioners voted at last week’s meeting to make Chief Probation Officer Marie Boulton the deputy warden at R-C-C-I.
THAT position was eliminated more than 5 years ago.
Commissioner Wayne Guilfoyle voted against it, and blasted the move, calling it just plain wrong.
But at least one other commissioner says Guilfoyle is wrong.
“”We came out a whole lot cheaper taking one of the jobs that was vacant and put her in it versus being sued the city now I guess commissioner Guilfoyle has plenty of money so he can pay that lawsuit I totality disagree with that I think he’s wrong that we were out of place to do that,” says Commissioner Marion Williams
Boulton had hired an attorney after she was placed on administrative leave from her job at the probation office by Judge David Watkins.
Her salary at R-C-C-I will be 79-thousand dollars per year.
rewrite: In Augusta, Georgia, the City Commission has reassigned Chief Probation Officer Marie Boulton to the position of deputy warden at the Richmond County Correctional Institution, a role that had been eliminated over five years prior. Commissioners assert this action was necessary to avoid potential litigation against the city. The decision, ratified during a recent meeting, was opposed by Commissioner Wayne Guilfoyle, who criticized the move as fundamentally improper. However, Commissioner Marion Williams defended the reassignment, arguing it represents a more fiscally prudent alternative to a lawsuit, and contested Guilfoyle's characterization of the action as inappropriate. This administrative transfer follows Boulton being placed on leave by Judge David Watkins, after which she retained legal counsel. Her annual salary in the new position will be $79,000.

(Reuters) - Everton manager Sam Allardyce believes Arsenal are defensively weak and their tendency to commit players going forward will leave counter-attacking opportunities for his team when they visit the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.
Arsene Wenger’s Arsenal have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last seven Premier League matches and were punished for some glaring defensive errors in a 3-1 defeat by Swansea City on Tuesday.
“I always felt defensively they are weak,” Allardyce told a news conference on Friday.
”If we break out with some quality forward passes, then create some good counter-attacking opportunities.
”Swansea managed to get a result against them but the Emirates is a different kettle of fish. It’s about nullifying the strengths of Arsenal.
“Arsenal’s attacking force is something you have to manage. Even though they haven’t scored as many goals this year as they have in recent years at this stage of the season.”
Theo Walcott is one of the Everton players Allardyce could use on the break, with the forward set to play against Arsenal for the first time since leaving the club last month.
The 28-year-old England international has made a good start at his new club, contributing an assist in Everton’s 1-1 draw against West Bromwich Albion before scoring twice in a 2-1 victory over Leicester City on Wednesday.
Allardyce expects Walcott to improve further and build a partnership with fullback Seamus Coleman, who made a return to the starting lineup against Leicester following 10 months out of action following a double leg break.
“Theo has seen a lot of Seamus and Seamus has seen a lot of Theo over the years. From a distance they know each other’s games very well,” the manager said.
“He’s (Theo) got an opportunity to be a key player at Everton now. He played 30-plus games last season and scored 19 goals. Hopefully, he can have as good a performance at the Emirates as he did Wednesday night.”

This frailty was notably evident in a recent 3-1 defeat to Swansea City, a result precipitated by significant defensive errors.

In a pre-match press conference, Allardyce elaborated on this tactical perspective, stating, "I have consistently perceived defensive weakness in their structure." He emphasized that disciplined defensive organization, coupled with incisive forward passing upon regaining possession, could generate high-quality counter-attacking situations. While acknowledging Swansea's success, Allardyce noted the distinct challenge of facing Arsenal at home, framing the contest as one requiring the nullification of the host's attacking strengths. "Managing Arsenal's offensive capacity is imperative," he observed, "even considering their current comparative reduction in goal output at this stage of the season."

A potential instrument in executing this counter-attacking strategy is forward Theo Walcott, who is poised to face his former club for the first time since his January transfer. The 28-year-old England international has commenced his Everton tenure positively, providing an assist in a draw against West Bromwich Albion and scoring twice in a midweek victory over Leicester City. The manager noted their pre-existing familiarity, suggesting it would facilitate effective collaboration.

Allardyce expressed confidence in Walcott's capacity to assume a pivotal role, citing his previous season's tally of 19 goals. "He now has the opportunity to be a key player for Everton," Allardyce concluded, expressing hope that Walcott's performance at the Emirates would mirror his impactful display against Leicester.

Poland’s chief judge has turned up for work on Wednesday refusing to comply with an order to retire as part of controversial reforms that critics say undermine the judiciary’s independence.
Malgorzata Gersdorf, the head of the Supreme Court, had vowed to go to work as usual, despite being told she had to step down on Tuesday under new rules that came into effect at midnight.
She was seen entering the court building in Warsaw. “My presence here is not about politics, I am here to protect the rule of law,” she said at the court’s entrance, surrounded by supporters and opposition politicians.
The chief justice has described as a “purge” the reforms requiring judges to retire at 65 instead of 70 years old. Up to 40% of Supreme Court judges are expected to be forced out.
Under the changes, Gersdorf could have asked President Duda for an extension of her mandate. However, she refused to do so, saying “that would mean subordination”.
The changes brought in by the ruling nationalist party have escalated tensions between Poland and the European Union over democratic values. On Monday the EU launched legal action against the Polish government, which faces the threat of losing its voting rights.
The conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party has been accused of trying to take effective control of the judicial system by seeking to stuff the courts with sympathetic judges. The ruling party argues the changes are needed to overhaul a system that has changed too little since the communist era, and will help fight corruption.
“The court system… is an entirely internal matter,” the PAP news agency quoted PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski as telling the Gazeta Polska newspaper.
The ruling party has maintained support of around 40% during the row with the EU, according to opinion polls, well above that of any single rival party.
rewrite:
On Wednesday, Poland’s First President of the Supreme Court, Małgorzata Gersdorf, reported for duty in defiance of a mandatory retirement order enacted under contentious judicial reforms. These reforms, which critics argue erode judicial independence, compelled her to step down upon turning 65, rather than the previous retirement age of 70. Despite the new regulations taking effect at midnight on Tuesday, Justice Gersdorf affirmed her intention to continue her professional obligations and was observed entering the Supreme Court building in Warsaw. Addressing supporters and opposition politicians at the entrance, she stated, “My presence here is not about politics; I am here to protect the rule of law.”

Justice Gersdorf has characterized the reforms, which could affect up to forty percent of Supreme Court justices, as a “purge.” Although the revised law permitted her to petition President Andrzej Duda for an extension of her mandate, she declined to do so, asserting that such a request “would mean subordination.” The reforms, advanced by the ruling nationalist Law and Justice (PiS) party, have intensified diplomatic strains with the European Union concerning democratic standards. In response, the EU initiated infringement proceedings against Poland on Monday, a move that could ultimately lead to the suspension of the nation’s voting rights within the bloc.

Opponents accuse the PiS of seeking to consolidate control over the judiciary by appointing politically aligned judges. The government, however, contends that the overhaul is necessary to modernize a system largely unchanged since the communist era and to enhance anti-corruption efforts. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński emphasized to the Gazeta Polska newspaper, as reported by the PAP news agency, that “the court system… is an entirely internal matter.” Despite the ongoing dispute with the EU, opinion polls indicate that public support for the ruling party remains stable at approximately forty percent, significantly exceeding that of any individual opposition party.

Montecito celebrated Independence Day with the 18th Annual Village Fourth Parade, complete with fire trucks, scout troops and residents decked out in red, white and blue.
The parade meandered down San Ysidro Road from Upper Manning Park to Lower Manning Park, where the Montecito Association set up live music, barbecues and bounce houses for festivities all afternoon.
Earlier in the day, the Montecito Firemen’s Association hosted its annual Fourth of July Pancake Breakfast at the San Ysidro Road firehouse, with all proceeds benefiting the Montecito Firefighter’s Charitable Foundation.
It’s been a Fourth of July staple for about 20 years, and had huge lines all morning, Battalion Chief Stu Pfister said.
It would only draw about 100 people when it first started, but the number of fans quickly multiplied.
“If we ever stopped doing this, there would be a riot,” he said.
The Los Padres National Forest Hot Shots showed up with reinforcements – more huge bags of pancake mix – near the end of the breakfast.

A bird flies by the Vedanta office building in Mumbai August 16, 2010. REUTERS/Danish Siddiqui
Indian mining company Vedanta Resources Plc (VED.L) said on Thursday it has extended Chief Executive Tom Albanese's contract by five months until the end of August.
The three-year contract was due to expire on Friday.
Vedanta's executive chairman Anil Agarwal is leading the succession process to identify candidates to replace Albanese, the company said.
Vedanta was hit by the slump in commodities prices. Its revenue fell 16.6 percent last year to 10.7 billion pounds, its lowest in six years, while profit before tax, excluding special items, plunged 79.5 percent.
Vedanta's shares have fallen 12.4 percent since Albanese, the former head of Rio Tinto Plc (RIO.L) (RIO.AX), took the helm in April 2014.
(Reporting by Arathy S Nair in Bengaluru; Editing by Susan Fenton)

BEIRUT More than 7,000 people have escaped Islamic State control in the Tabqa area west of the Syrian city of Raqqa since last week, U.S.-backed local forces fighting the jihadists said on Friday.
The Syrian Democratic Forces, an alliance of Kurdish and Arab milita fighters, has been battling Islamic State around Tabqa, nearly 40 km (25 miles) west of Raqqa city.
Last week, they captured the northern entrance to the Tabqa Dam, a major target in their military campaign to isolate and capture Islamic State’s biggest urban stronghold.
With air strikes and special ground forces from the U.S.-led coalition, the SDF has been advancing on Raqqa city from the north, east and west.
Thousands of families have arrived at SDF-held positions since last week after managing to flee Tabqa and nearby villages, the SDF said.
The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, a UK-based organisation that monitors the war, said clashes and air strikes had pushed nearly 3,000 people to escape those areas over the past week.
The offensive to capture Raqqa will last a number of months, the operation's commander told Reuters earlier on Friday.
(This version of the story corrects date in paragraph five)
(Reporting by Ellen Francis; editing by Ralph Boulton)
rewrite:
BEIRUT – According to statements issued on Friday by U.S.-backed local forces combating jihadist groups, over 7,000 individuals have fled territories under Islamic State control in the vicinity of Tabqa, located west of the Syrian city of Raqqa, since the preceding week. The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), a coalition comprising Kurdish and Arab militia units, have been engaged in military operations against Islamic State in the Tabqa region, approximately 40 kilometers west of Raqqa. Last week, these forces secured the northern approach to the Tabqa Dam, a strategically significant objective within their broader campaign to isolate and ultimately seize Islamic State’s primary urban stronghold. Supported by coalition airstrikes and specialized ground personnel from the U.S.-led alliance, the SDF has continued its multi-front advance on Raqqa from northern, eastern, and western axes.

The SDF reported that thousands of families have reached positions under its control after escaping from Tabqa and adjacent villages. This assessment is corroborated by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, a United Kingdom-based monitoring organization, which noted that intensified clashes and airstrikes have compelled nearly 3,000 people to evacuate the area within the past week. The commander of the operation informed Reuters earlier on Friday that the offensive to capture Raqqa is anticipated to extend over several months.

She said "plants, trees and flowers have been a source of pleasure throughout my life".
The Queen has admitted that she is “not any sort of expert on gardening” as she shared a special message to mark the 70th anniversary of BBC Radio 4 show Gardeners’ Question Time.
The special-edition programme on Friday featured an item on traditional royal residence Frogmore House and Garden, in Windsor.
In a pre-recorded speech, she told listeners: “I very much hope you have enjoyed visiting Frogmore House and Garden, which holds a special place in my family’s affection.
In case you missed it on @BBCGQT, here's the message The Queen recorded about Frogmore House and Gardens. pic.twitter.com/Hf55GVEJmn — The Royal Family (@RoyalFamily) October 6, 2017
“Indeed, I would echo the sentiments of Queen Victoria who, 150 years ago, rode to this dear lovely garden, where all is peace and quiet and you only hear the hum of the bees, the singing of the birds.
“These days, there is more noise from the air than in 1867, but Frogmore remains a wonderfully relaxing environment.”
She continued: “I’m not any sort of expert on gardening, but plants, trees and flowers have been a source of pleasure throughout my life.
“I have an early memory of my mother, Queen Elizabeth, being a hands-on gardener – a tradition that has been followed by other members of my family, and I know this passion is shared by your listeners, and many other people besides.
A landmark moment in the history of this programme – thanks to @RoyalFamily The Queen for hosting us at Frogmore House and gardens. pic.twitter.com/78sgGUBxyM — BBC Radio 4's GQT (@BBCGQT) October 6, 2017
“As you mark the programme’s 70th anniversary, I send my congratulations, and wish you continued success.”
The programme also included interviews with the keeper of the garden and the deputy surveyor of the Queen’s art by presenter Peter Gibbs.
While the house is now mostly used for entertaining, it was made popular by Queen Charlotte, consort of George III, in the 1700s.
The house contains a whole room dedicated to works of art by 18th-century flower painter Mary Moser, and the garden features a tea house later installed by Queen Victoria.
© Press Association 2017
rewrite:
In a pre-recorded address commemorating the seventieth anniversary of the BBC Radio 4 programme *Gardeners’ Question Time*, Her Majesty The Queen reflected upon her personal appreciation for horticulture while expressly disclaiming any professional expertise in the field. The special edition of the programme, broadcast on Friday, featured a segment focusing on the traditional royal residence of Frogmore House and its gardens in Windsor. Addressing the audience, The Queen expressed her sincere hope that listeners had enjoyed the virtual visit to Frogmore, a location she described as holding “a special place in my family’s affection.”

Her Majesty proceeded to align her sentiments with those of her predecessor, Queen Victoria, who, one hundred and fifty years prior, had famously remarked upon riding to this “dear lovely garden, where all is peace and quiet and you only hear the hum of the bees, the singing of the birds.” The Queen observed that, while contemporary auditory intrusions from air traffic are absent from Victoria’s nineteenth-century account, Frogmore endures as “a wonderfully relaxing environment.”

“I am not any sort of expert on gardening,” The Queen stated, “but plants, trees and flowers have been a source of pleasure throughout my life.” She recalled an early memory of her mother, Queen Elizabeth, engaging directly in gardening—a practice subsequently adopted by other members of the Royal Family. The Queen acknowledged that this horticultural passion is widely shared by the programme’s listeners and the broader public. In conclusion, she extended her congratulations on the programme’s milestone anniversary and wished it continued success.

The anniversary broadcast also included interviews conducted by presenter Peter Gibbs with the keeper of the garden and the deputy surveyor of The Queen’s works of art. While Frogmore House is now primarily utilised for official entertaining, its historical significance was established in the eighteenth century by Queen Charlotte, consort of George III. The house contains an entire room devoted to the works of the eighteenth-century floral artist Mary Moser, and the garden features a tea house that was later added during the reign of Queen Victoria.

Smartphones are the Swiss Army knives of the digital age, serving as cell phone, camera, map, social networking hub, game console and more. Now one more amazing utility can be added to the list: eyesight.
Aipoly is one such smartphone app. It can nearly instantaneously identify over 4,000 objects around the home, such as tools, cutlery and bathroom items. It displays a text identification on screen and speaks the object’s name aloud to the user.
Aipoly’s vocabulary is now about as complex as that of a five-year-old child. The app offers paid upgrades that expand its available vocabulary, and new words and subjects are constantly being added.
Comprehensive image recognition training is key to accurate identification, and it is this quality that is essential to assisting those with visual impairment.
“With a blind person, you can’t have 70 percent accuracy and call it a day,” said Alberto Rizzoli, co-founder of San Francisco-based Aipoly.
Read the entire article here, How GPU Technology Aids the Vision-Impaired
via the fine folks at NVIDIA.
rewrite: Smartphones function as multifunctional tools within the digital era, integrating capabilities such as telecommunication, photography, navigation, social connectivity, and gaming. A significant emerging utility is their potential to augment human vision. The application Aipoly exemplifies this development, enabling near-instantaneous auditory and textual identification of over 4,000 domestic objects, including tools, cutlery, and bathroom items. Presently, the application's lexical database approximates the complexity of a five-year-old's vocabulary, with expansions available through premium upgrades and ongoing updates. The efficacy of such assistive technology hinges on comprehensive image recognition training to achieve the high accuracy essential for users with visual impairments. As emphasized by Alberto Rizzoli, co-founder of the San Francisco-based Aipoly, marginal accuracy is insufficient for this demographic; reliable precision is paramount. This innovation is further detailed in the article "How GPU Technology Aids the Vision-Impaired," courtesy of NVIDIA.

THE long arm of the law appears to have been eclipsed by the longest snake in Australia.
Two police officers stumbled upon this monster-sized scrub python on a road during a recent night patrol in the bush area surrounding Wujul Wujul, about 120km north of Cairns.
The elongated serpent is estimated to be about 5m long.
Police said there was no passing in the police vehicle until the python was “good and ready to move.”
Camera Icon Queensland Police came across this very long python on a recent night patrol near Wujul Wujul 120km north of Cairns. Picture: Twitter Picture: Supplied
“Seizing the opportunity for a quick photo, Sergeant Ben Tome sent his colleague Acting Senior Constable Chris Kenny out of the car to stand next to the giant,” they said.
“Not fond of the police attention, the scrub python made his way quickly off the road so the officers could continue on their way.”
Scrub pythons, also known as amethystine pythons, are Australia’s largest snakes, growing up to 8m long.
The non-venomous reptiles, which live in rainforest, coastal scrub and open forest from Townsville to Cape York, kill their prey by using constriction.
They feed mainly on mammals and birds but are capable of taking animals as large as wallabies.
The animals have also been known to consume domestic pets, particularly in rainforest areas.
rewrite:
During a routine nocturnal patrol in the vicinity of Wujul Wujul, approximately 120 kilometers north of Cairns, two police officers encountered a substantial scrub python (Morelia amethistina) obstructing the roadway. The serpent, estimated to measure five meters in length, necessitated a temporary halt of the police vehicle until it voluntarily vacated the thoroughfare. The officers utilized the interval to document the encounter photographically, with Acting Senior Constable Chris Kenny positioned adjacent to the specimen for scale prior to its departure into the surrounding bushland.

Scrub pythons, alternatively designated amethystine pythons, constitute the largest extant snake species in Australia, with recorded lengths approaching eight meters. As non-venomous constrictors, their habitat encompasses rainforests, coastal scrub, and open forests from the Townsville region to Cape York. Their diet primarily consists of mammals and birds, though they possess the capacity to subdue prey as substantial as wallabies. Incidents of these reptiles consuming domestic pets have also been documented, particularly within rainforest environs. This encounter underscores the intersection of human activity with indigenous wildlife in remote Australian locales.

MILWAUKEE — Kyron Cartwright totalled 15 points and eight rebounds and his steal with three seconds left in the game helped Providence outlast Marquette 77-75 on Saturday.
Maliek White made 1 of 2 free throws with 27 seconds left to give the Friars (15-8, 6-4 Big East Conference) a 75-71 lead. But Jalen Lindsey fouled Markus Howard, who leads all Division I players with a 94.3 shooting percentage at the free-throw line. Howard sank a pair to pull the Golden Eagles (13-10, 4-7) within 75-73 with 21 seconds remaining.
Alpha Diallo was fouled and hit both of his free throws to stretch Providence’s advantage to four, but Howard buried a jumper with six seconds left to cut the deficit back to two. Greg Elliott fouled White, who missed both of his foul shots, Elliott grabbed the rebound and passed to Howard near midcourt. Howard turned to head up court, but Cartwright poked the ball away and the Friars claimed the victory.
Howard, who finished with 16 points and nine rebounds to pace Marquette, scored a school- and Big East-record 52 points in the Golden Eagles’ 95-90 overtime win at Providence on Jan. 3.
Diallo topped the Friars with 16 points, while Isaiah Jackson added 13 points and seven rebounds.

His decisive steal with three seconds remaining in regulation ultimately preserved the win for the Friars (15-8, 6-4 Big East). The closing moments featured a sequence of strategic fouls and free throws. With 27 seconds left, Providence's Maliek White converted one of two free throws to establish a 75-71 lead. Marquette's Markus Howard, the national Division I leader in free-throw percentage at 94.3, then made two shots after being fouled, narrowing the gap to 75-73. Following two free throws from Providence's Alpha Diallo, Howard sank a jumper with six seconds left to again reduce the deficit to two points. After Greg Elliott fouled White, who missed both ensuing free throws, Elliott secured the rebound and passed to Howard near midcourt. As Howard advanced, Cartwright executed the critical steal to seal the game. Howard led Marquette (13-10, 4-7) with 16 points and nine rebounds. Diallo paced Providence with 16 points, supported by Isaiah Jackson's 13 points and seven rebounds.

Sarthak Kanjilal
Port Blair, Feb 26: Expressing his anger over demolishing of shops and a few private houses in city, the Member of Parliament, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Mr Bishnu Pada Ray today said that the administration has no right to demolish private buildings in Port Blair city and the rights are solely rest on the shoulders of Chairperson of PBMC and the Port Blair Municipal Council.

Regarding new Property Tax rules of PBMC the MP said that, he has received a lot of complaints on this issue.
