rewrite:
In a press conference held at the Member of Parliament’s office at 11:00 a.m. today, Mr. Bishnu Pada Ray, the Member of Parliament for the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, expressed strong disapproval regarding the recent demolition of several shops and private residences within Port Blair. Mr. Ray asserted that the local administration lacks the authority to undertake such demolitions of private structures within the city, clarifying that this jurisdiction rests solely with the Chairperson and the Port Blair Municipal Council (PBMC). He emphasized an urgent need for amendments to the existing Building Bye-Laws.

During his address to the media, the MP also provided updates on several infrastructure projects. He reported that the National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation (NHIDCL) has awarded the contract for the construction of a bridge over Humphrey Strait to RDS Projects, A & N Islands. This project, with an estimated cost of ₹223 crores, is scheduled to commence imminently. Furthermore, Mr. Ray stated that a tender has been floated for road development from Austin to Karala Junction (covering kilometers 242-298), a project valued at ₹317 crores. He added that a recent meeting concluded with the decision that NHIDCL will temporarily assume responsibility for repair work on the Andaman Trunk Road.

Regarding municipal affairs, Mr. Ray noted he has received numerous complaints concerning the PBMC’s new Property Tax rules. He informed attendees that a special meeting was recently convened, resulting in the formation of a committee to examine the issue. A satisfactory resolution is anticipated to be announced shortly, with the MP assuring that no tax will be imposed on vacant land.

Concluding the conference, Mr. Bishnu Pada Ray shared positive news, announcing that Medica Speciality Hospital will now extend its campus selection for nursing positions to include candidates from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

French President Francois Hollande talks to reporters beside Indonesian counterpart Joko Widodo during joint news conference at the presidential palace in Jakarta, Indonesia March 29, 2017. REUTERS/Beawiharta
PARIS French President Francois Hollande told British Prime Minister Theresa May on Thursday that Brexit negotiations must first deal with how Britain will leave the bloc before talks could be held on Britain's future relations with the EU, his office said.
The outgoing French president told May in a telephone call that the negotiations must be held in a "clear and constructive manner, so as to lift uncertainties and to fully respect the rules and interests of the 27-member European Union."
"The President indicated that the talks must at first be about the terms of withdrawal, dealing especially with citizens' rights and obligations resulting from the commitments made by the United Kingdom," a statement from Hollande's Elysee office said.
"On the basis of the progress made, we could open discussions on the framework of future relations between the United Kingdom and the European Union," it said.
(Reporting by Adrian Croft and Sudip Kar-Gupta; Editing by Richard Balmforth)
rewrite: On March 29, 2017, French President Francois Hollande and Indonesian President Joko Widodo held a joint press conference at the presidential palace in Jakarta. Subsequently, on Thursday, March 30, President Hollande communicated by telephone with British Prime Minister Theresa May regarding the impending Brexit negotiations. According to a statement issued by the French presidential office (the Élysée), President Hollande emphasized that the discussions must initially address the specific terms of the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union. This preliminary phase would prioritize resolving matters pertaining to the rights and obligations of citizens, stemming from the UK's prior commitments as a member state. President Hollande asserted that these negotiations should be conducted with clarity and constructiveness to mitigate uncertainties and to uphold the regulations and collective interests of the remaining twenty-seven EU member states. Only upon achieving sufficient progress on these withdrawal terms, the statement clarified, could dialogue commence concerning the framework for the future relationship between the United Kingdom and the European Union.

A quirky Indian street food company is opening in Walsall .
Wrapchic specialises in “exciting and vibrant flavours of Indian street food” and transforms them into an easy-to-eat Mexican format in the style of burritos, wraps and nachos.
The idea is quite simple: you choose your style and then your filling, from the classic chicken tikka to mutton madrasi – a south Indian-spiced meat served with chettinad sauce.
(Image: TripAdvisor)
Also on the menu is lamb kheema – spiced minced lamb with red onion, mint chutney and fresh mint – and paneer masala, an Indian soft cheese coated in tava spice served with tikka sauce.
Breakfast is served too in the form of egg and cheese-filled flour tortilla wraps complete with a choice of filling. Toasted samosas, spicy chicken wings and yogurt-based Indian drinks are also on the menu.
Wrapchic currently has 14 franchises in the UK – including Solihull and Birmingham – with another two operating from Dubai.
In Walsall, according to its website, Wrapchic will open in 19 Park Street in the town centre and will replace the EE mobile phone shop near the Saddlers Shopping Centre.

Options range from classic chicken tikka to mutton madrasi, a south Indian-spiced meat accompanied by chettinad sauce.

Additional menu items include lamb kheema, consisting of spiced minced lamb with red onion, mint chutney, and fresh mint, as well as paneer masala, an Indian soft cheese coated in tava spice and served with tikka sauce. LAGOS Unilever Nigeria (UNILEVE.LG) said on Wednesday it will seek shareholder approval next month to raise 63 billion naira (160 million pounds) through a rights issue.
The household products maker also said it would seek approval to increase its authorised share capital to 5 billion naira by creating an additional 3.95 billion new ordinary shares of 0.50 naira each.
The local unit of Unilever (UNc.AS) (ULVR.L) plans to seek a vote at a shareholder meeting on May 11, it said in a notice, adding that it would also ask for approval to convert shareholder loans to stock as part of the share sale.
(Reporting by Oludare Mayowa; editing by Chijioke Ohuocha and Jason Neely)
rewrite: Unilever Nigeria Plc (UNILEVE.LG) announced on Wednesday that it will seek shareholder authorization at a forthcoming meeting to raise 63 billion naira (equivalent to approximately 160 million pounds) via a rights issue. The consumer goods manufacturer further stated it will propose an increase to its authorized share capital, elevating it to 5 billion naira through the creation of an additional 3.95 billion ordinary shares, each with a nominal value of 0.50 naira. According to a corporate notice, these resolutions will be presented for a vote at a general meeting scheduled for May 11. The agenda will also include a proposal to convert existing shareholder loans into equity, as an integral component of the broader capital restructuring initiative.

Source: GHANAsoccernet.com
2017-10-07
Christopher Bonney
Ebusua Dwarfs defender Christopher Bonney has rubbished bribery allegations against him which forced the club to omit him from the squad that beat Inter Allies 3-1 in Cape Coast on Wednesday.
Section of the club’s supporters accused him of negotiating a match of convenience after being spotted at the Elmina Beach Resort with alleged officials of Eleven Is To One.
The former Kotoko defender was subsequently left out of the mid-week clash at the Cape Coast stadium.
But he has vehemently denied the claims as a complete falsehood.
“ I have never met any official of Inter Allies let alone to collect money from him, I only met my former coach Didi Dramani who rather took me to the Elmina Beach Resort to have a meal and nothing like football related issues were even discussed so I don’t understand why some of the supporters are surprisingly accusing me of taking bribe from Inter Allies officials,” he told Cape Coast-based ATL FM
’’ It is never true and I can never do that because I love Dwarfs that is why after my stint with Kotoko, I returned to the club.”
rewrite:
In a statement issued on Saturday, 7 October 2017, Christopher Bonney, a defender for the Ghanaian football club Ebusua Dwarfs, has formally refuted allegations of bribery that led to his exclusion from the squad for a mid-week match. The allegations, circulated by a segment of the club's supporters, asserted that Bonney had engaged in negotiations for a pre-arranged match outcome. This followed his reported presence at the Elmina Beach Resort with individuals alleged to be officials of the opposing team, Inter Allies, prior to Dwarfs' 3-1 victory on Wednesday.

Bonney has categorically denied these accusations, describing them as entirely false. In an interview with Cape Coast-based ATL FM, he clarified the circumstances of his visit to the resort, stating he had met only his former coach, Didi Dramani, for a social meal. He emphasized that no football-related matters were discussed and expressed bewilderment at the allegations, noting he has never even met officials from Inter Allies. Bonney further affirmed his commitment to Ebusua Dwarfs, citing his deliberate return to the club after his tenure with Asante Kotoko as evidence of his loyalty and integrity.

In “Journeys: An American Story” (RosettaBooks), Andrew Tisch and Mary Skafidas have compiled 72 essays by immigrants or their descendants, some of whom are famous, like Michael R. Bloomberg, while others are everyday — albeit exceptional — Americans. The diverse tales, presented together, show how immigrants have built and strengthened the culture of New York and the country at-large.
Mr. Tisch, the co-chairman of the board of the Loews Corporation, decided to ask celebrities and acquaintances to recount immigration stories after researching his own family history in preparation for a speech at a swearing-in ceremony of new citizens. (He contributed an essay to the book, as did Ms. Skafidas).
Ms. Skafidas, Loews’ vice president of investor relations and corporate communications, was born in the United States and had Greek immigrant parents but didn’t speak English until she was 6; her aunt was undocumented.
Among the book’s featured raconteurs are Pete Gogolak, the former Giants place kicker who was 14 when he fled Hungary; Linda Hills, a great-granddaughter of Andrew Carnegie; Arlene and Alan Alda; and the executive Morris Sarnoff, who emigrated from Belarus with his brothers David and Lew and their mother after their father had worked for five years as a house painter in New York to earn enough for their passage.
rewrite:
In the volume “Journeys: An American Story” (RosettaBooks), editors Andrew Tisch and Mary Skafidas present a collection of seventy-two essays authored by immigrants or their descendants. The contributors range from prominent public figures, such as Michael R. Bloomberg, to lesser-known yet exemplary individuals. Collectively, these diverse narratives illustrate the integral role immigrants have played in constructing and reinforcing the cultural fabric of both New York City and the nation.

Mr. Tisch, who serves as co-chairman of the board of the Loews Corporation, conceived the project after investigating his own familial history for a speech at a naturalization ceremony. This prompted him to solicit immigration accounts from both notable figures and personal acquaintances. Both he and Ms. Skafidas contributed essays to the compilation.

Ms. Skafidas, Loews’ vice president of investor relations and corporate communications, is a first-generation American born to Greek immigrants. She did not learn English until the age of six, and her aunt resided in the country without documentation.

Notable essayists featured include Pete Gogolak, the former Giants placekicker who escaped Hungary at fourteen; Linda Hills, a great-granddaughter of industrialist Andrew Carnegie; actors Arlene and Alan Alda; and executive Morris Sarnoff. Sarnoff emigrated from Belarus with his brothers and mother after their father labored for five years as a house painter in New York to secure their passage.

BROOKFIELD TWP., Ohio (WYTV) – Brookfield Township police are warning residents of a new scam involving fake “representatives” of a power company going to people’s houses saying their power may be affected by recent electrical work.
Friday evening, an elderly woman from Steward Sharon Road reported her house had been robbed while she was in the basement.
The woman told police two men were at her house earlier saying they were employees of her power company. They told her they were working on an adjacent street, so her power might be affected.
The woman then reported that the men asked to see her breaker box, located in the basement. They then told her to stay downstairs while they checked something outside but would signal her from a basement window when they needed her to turn the breaker off.
After a lengthy amount of time, the woman saw the men’s silver or grey Chevy Silverado pickup driving away, so she went upstairs and called police after noticing the men stole items from her home.
The Brookfield Township Police Department posted the incident on its Facebook page warning residents to call them if they have any information about the incident, or if they have also been victim to this scam.
The department can be reached at 330-448-6960, dispatch at 330-675-2730 or you can leave a message on their tip line at 330-969-1110.
rewrite:
Authorities in Brookfield Township, Ohio, have issued a public warning regarding an emerging fraudulent scheme involving individuals falsely presenting themselves as utility company employees. According to a report filed on Friday evening, an elderly resident of Steward Sharon Road was victimized after two men arrived at her residence claiming to be power company representatives. They informed her that ongoing electrical work on a neighboring street might disrupt her service. The individuals requested to inspect the residential circuit breaker panel, which was located in the basement. They instructed the homeowner to remain downstairs, stating they would signal via a basement window when she should switch the breaker off. After a prolonged period, the resident observed a silver or grey Chevrolet Silverado pickup truck departing the premises. Upon ascending to the main living area, she discovered that property had been stolen and subsequently contacted law enforcement.

The Brookfield Township Police Department has disseminated details of this incident through its official Facebook page, urging community members to exercise caution. Residents are advised to verify the credentials of any unexpected utility workers and to contact authorities immediately with any relevant information or if they experience similar suspicious encounters. The department can be reached at 330-448-6960, via dispatch at 330-675-2730, or through the anonymous tip line at 330-969-1110.

input: The decomposed body of a 75-year-old man was found in a flat here, more than a month after he is suspected to have died when he stepped on a lizard and fell, suffering fatal head injuries, police said on Friday.The death of Lakshminarayana Murthy came to light only after his wife and two daughters returned from the US two days ago. The shocking incident took place at Sai Maruti Residency in Rocktown area.The man, who lived alone in a top floor flat, is suspected to have died on August 18 after the fall. Since all the doors and windows were closed, other residents in the building did not get any foul smell.A police officer said Murthy seemed to have stepped on a lizard and fallen down while coming out of the bath. He sustained head injuries and died on the spot.A dead lizard was found near his feet, indicating he skidded after stepping on it.Murthy was not answering phone calls from his wife and two daughters in the US. As he had kept the mobile phone on charging, they simply assumed he was unhappy with them.But when there was no response even after a month, they decided to return to Hyderabad and check on him.The flat, owned by one of Murthy's daughters, had a central locking system that does not give scope to guess if someone is inside.As there was no response from inside, the wife and daughter broke open the door to find his body in a highly decomposed state.Originally hailing from Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh, Murthy, a retired government employee, was not known to people in the apartment. Residents thought the flat was locked from outside and that the owner lives in the US.Murthy had turned down repeated requests by his daughters to move to the US to live with them. In July, he had sent his wife to the US but preferred to live alone here.
rewrite:
The decomposed remains of a seventy-five-year-old man were discovered within a residential apartment, following a suspected fatal accident occurring over one month prior, as confirmed by police authorities on Friday. The deceased, identified as Lakshminarayana Murthy, is believed to have succumbed to head injuries on August 18 after slipping on a lizard and falling upon exiting his bathroom. The incident occurred at Sai Maruti Residency in the Rocktown locality, where Murthy resided alone in a top-floor unit. The situation came to light only upon the return of his wife and two daughters from the United States two days prior to the discovery.

Investigating officers reported that a deceased lizard was located near the victim’s feet, supporting the hypothesis that he lost his footing after stepping on the reptile. Due to the sealed nature of the apartment’s doors and windows, the decomposition process did not generate detectable odors, thereby preventing awareness among other building residents. Murthy, a retired government employee originally from Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh, was largely unknown to his neighbors, who assumed the property was unoccupied and that the owner resided abroad.

Communication attempts by his family members from the United States went unanswered. As Murthy’s mobile phone remained on its charger, they initially interpreted the silence as displeasure. However, after a prolonged period without contact, they elected to return to Hyderabad to investigate. The apartment, owned by one of Murthy’s daughters, featured a central locking system that offered no external indication of occupancy. Receiving no response upon their arrival, the wife and daughter forcibly entered the premises to encounter the severely decomposed body.

It is noted that Murthy had previously declined repeated invitations from his daughters to relocate to the United States. In July, he had facilitated his wife’s travel abroad but chose to maintain his solitary residence in Hyderabad.

Cycling - UCI Track World Championships - Men's Scratch Race, Final - Hong Kong, China – 13/4/17 - Germany's Lucas Liss, Poland's Adrian Teklinski and Britain's Christopher Latham celebrate with their medals on the podium. REUTERS/Bobby Yip
HONG KONG Australia successfully defended their men's team pursuit title at the world track championships on Thursday, storming to victory over New Zealand in a seesaw battle at the Hong Kong Velodrome.
Australia, who were favourites after coming within a whisker of breaking the world record in qualifying on Wednesday, fell behind midway through the race but recovered impressively to surge to victory with a 2.476 second gap over their rivals.
The win for Sam Welsford, Alexander Porter, Cameron Meyer and Nicholas Yallouris is Australia's seventh world title in the past 11 editions of the event, while Italy took bronze over a new-look Britain side.
Poland's Adrian Teklinski won the men's scratch race for his first world title after risking everything with a surprise attack in the final kilometre that saw him open up a half-lap lead over the pack.
Germany's Lucas Liss, the 2015 champion, chased hard as Teklinski tired but could only manage silver, while Britain's Chris Latham held on in third for his first championship podium finish.
Azizulhasni Awang won Malaysia's first world title with a comprehensive victory in the men's keirin, finishing three lengths clear of silver medallist Fabian Hernando Puerta Zapata of Columbia, with Czech cyclist Thomas Babek in third.
Awang, known affectionately as "Pocket Rocket Man", won bronze in each of the last two editions of the world championships.
The day ended on a high note, with the U.S. women's pursuit team defending their title in a thriller against Australia that had the crowd on its feet.
The U.S. team of Kelly Catlin, Chloe Dygert, Jennifer Valente and the veteran Sarah Hammer charged into an early lead, but Australia recovered by the 2,500 metre mark and the teams raced to the finish with neither able to stay in front.
Australia were ahead by 0.412 seconds going into the final lap, but an inspired effort from Dygert pulled the Americans over the line with a 0.417 second margin of victory, while New Zealand took bronze over Italy.
(Writing by Hardik Vyas in Bengaluru; Editing by Alison Williams)
rewrite:
The 2017 UCI Track World Championships in Hong Kong concluded its Thursday programme with several finals, including the successful title defence by Australia in the men’s team pursuit. Entering as favourites following a near world-record performance in qualifying, the Australian quartet of Sam Welsford, Alexander Porter, Cameron Meyer, and Nicholas Yallouris faced a determined New Zealand team. The final proved a seesaw affair, with Australia falling behind midway before mounting a strong recovery to ultimately secure victory by a margin of 2.476 seconds. This triumph marks Australia’s seventh world title in this discipline over the past eleven championships. Italy claimed the bronze medal, defeating a reconfigured British squad.

In the men’s scratch race, Poland’s Adrian Teklinski secured his maiden world championship title through a daring tactical move. Launching a surprise attack within the final kilometre, Teklinski established a half-lap advantage over the peloton. Although the 2015 champion, Germany’s Lucas Liss, pursued vigorously as the leader fatigued, he could only close the gap sufficiently for the silver medal. Britain’s Christopher Latham completed the podium, earning his first medal at this level with a bronze.

Malaysia celebrated its first ever UCI world champion as Azizulhasni Awang dominated the men’s keirin final. Awang finished a decisive three lengths clear of the silver medallist, Colombia’s Fabian Hernando Puerta Zapata, with the Czech Republic’s Thomas Babek taking bronze. This victory represents a significant upgrade for Awang, who had secured bronze medals in the two preceding world championships.

The evening session concluded with a thrilling defence of the women’s team pursuit title by the United States. The American team, comprising Kelly Catlin, Chloe Dygert, Jennifer Valente, and veteran Sarah Hammer, established an early lead against Australia. The lead changed hands multiple times in the latter stages, with Australia holding a slender 0.412-second advantage entering the final lap. A powerful final effort from Dygert, however, propelled the United States to a narrow victory by a margin of 0.417 seconds. New Zealand defeated Italy to secure the bronze medal.

It’s finally draft week. There is time for one final writer mock draft.
So here we go:
Round 1
It’s difficult to imagine a world where five quarterbacks don’t come off the board before the Arizona Cardinals make their first-round selection.
All the talk this week leads me to believe that Lamar Jackson is valued by the NFL, and that he very well could be off the board. This, coupled with Steve Keim’s recent comments about not feeling pressure to get a quarterback make it appear that, unfortunately, Arizona will likely not be drafting a quarterback in the first round.
Sure, it’s possible they trade up to get one, especially if the rumors are correct they really like Josh Allen and Baker Mayfield. It does seem more likely they would trade down, but it would appear difficult to find someone willing to trade up. That would likely be for a quarterback the Cardinals would want or for a high-caliber player that Arizona might also covet.
On that note, the good news is that if five quarterbacks do indeed go before Arizona selects, it increases their odds of getting a possible star player to fall to them — someone like Minkah Fitzpatrick, Denzel Ward, Tremaine Edmunds, or Roquan Smith.
Assuming that it doesn’t work out quite that way either, Arizona has a wealth of options. They could go with Calvin Ridley or DJ.. Moore at receiver, Isaiah Wynn or Will Hernandez or even James Daniels along the offensive line interior; Josh Jackson or Jaire Alexander at cornerback. These are all great possibilities.
The solution seems to keep coming back to fortifying the trenches: it’s what appears to bring Wilks and Keim together. And there’s one man to do the job
The pick: Mike McGlinchey, OT, Notre Dame
rewrite:
As the final week preceding the draft commences, one concluding speculative exercise remains feasible. The following represents a final mock draft projection.

**First Round Analysis**
Current indications strongly suggest that as many as five quarterbacks will be selected prior to the Arizona Cardinals’ initial first-round selection. Widespread reporting this week underscores Lamar Jackson’s perceived value across the league, rendering his availability at Arizona’s pick improbable. This assessment, combined with General Manager Steve Keim’s recent remarks indicating no pressing urgency to select a quarterback, leads to the conclusion that Arizona is unlikely to draft a quarterback in the first round.

While a trade-up scenario remains possible—particularly if rumors regarding the organization’s affinity for Josh Allen and Baker Mayfield hold merit—a trade-down maneuver appears more plausible. However, identifying a trade partner may prove challenging unless a quarterback coveted by Arizona, or another elite prospect, remains available to motivate another team to move up.

Should five quarterbacks indeed be chosen early, the Cardinals would benefit from an increased probability of a highly-rated non-quarterback prospect falling to their selection. Players such as Minkah Fitzpatrick, Denzel Ward, Tremaine Edmunds, or Roquan Smith represent potential outcomes in such a scenario.

If the draft order unfolds differently, Arizona possesses considerable flexibility. Viable alternatives include wide receivers Calvin Ridley or D.J. Moore, interior offensive linemen Isaiah Wynn, Will Hernandez, or James Daniels, and cornerbacks Josh Jackson or Jaire Alexander.

A recurring strategic theme, however, centers on reinforcing the line of scrimmage—an apparent point of alignment between Head Coach Steve Wilks and General Manager Keim. One prospect distinctly fits this objective.

**The Selection: Mike McGlinchey, Offensive Tackle, Notre Dame**

A 43-year-old Warren Park woman is appealing for help after she was allegedly injured in an accident caused by a ZRP traffic cop spike.
Nyarai Chituu was injured on January 25 at around 8pm on her way from work at corner Mbuya Nehanda Street and Nelson Mandela Avenue when a police officer threw a spike and missed the target, hitting her in the process.
As a result, Chituu sustained a deep cut on her right leg and she is still nursing the wounds. Chituu told H-Metro that she was shocked and surprised by the conduct of the police officer.
“After hitting me with a spike, the police officer ran away instead of helping me leaving me injured at the scene.
“I used to think that the duty of the police is to serve and safeguard the nation and its people but that is not what I see considering what happened to me.
“No action has been taken against the police officer. I went and lodged a complaint at Harare Central Police Station and up to now no action has been taken,” said Chituu.
She added: “The use of spikes by the police should be banned permanently because the incident occurred at around 8:05 pm and the police were still using spikes at that hour and injured me yet nothing has been done.
“My children need food, clothes and school fees, I also need clutches so I am seeking for assistance in any kind so that my condition will improve.”
Those wishing to assist Chituu can be contacted on 0773906609. H-Metro
rewrite:
A 43-year-old female resident of Warren Park is publicly seeking assistance following an incident in which she sustained injuries allegedly caused by a Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) traffic officer deploying a spike strip. The individual, Nyarai Chituu, was injured on January 25 at approximately 8:00 PM while returning from work. The incident occurred at the intersection of Mbuya Nehanda Street and Nelson Mandela Avenue, where an officer reportedly attempted to deploy a spike strip but missed the intended target, striking Ms. Chituu instead.

Consequently, Ms. Chituu suffered a deep laceration to her right leg and continues to require medical care for the injury. In a statement to H-Metro, she expressed profound shock and dismay at the officer's conduct, noting that he fled the scene rather than rendering aid. She further articulated a loss of confidence, stating that the incident contradicts the expected duty of police to serve and protect citizens. Ms. Chituu reports having filed a formal complaint at Harare Central Police Station, but alleges that no disciplinary action has been initiated against the officer involved.

Additionally, she has called for a permanent ban on the use of spike strips by police, particularly highlighting that the deployment occurred during evening hours. Ms. Chituu emphasizes the practical repercussions of her injury, which includes an inability to work, thereby affecting her capacity to provide food, clothing, and school fees for her children. She also requires crutches for mobility and is appealing for any form of assistance to improve her situation. Parties willing to offer support may contact her at 0773906609.

New York commuter who led cleanup of anti-Semitic graffiti on subway being honored by the Anti-Defamation League.
The New York commuter who led several others on a Manhattan subway to clean away anti-Semitic graffiti with hand sanitizer is being honored by the Anti-Defamation League.
Jared Nied, 37, will receive ADL’s Stand Up New Yorker Award, which recognizes city residents for taking immediate action to help those being singled out for bigotry, or initiating efforts to denounce hate. Evan Bernstein, director of the ADL New York region, will present Nied with the award on Wednesday.
Nied's actions went viral after one of the commuters described the scene from the night of Feb. 4 on Facebook.
“The train was silent as everyone stared at each other, uncomfortable and unsure what to do,” Gregory Locke wrote in his post. “One guy got up and said, ‘Hand sanitizer gets rid of Sharpie. We need alcohol.’ He found some tissues and got to work.”
Nied, who works as a sous chef in New York, also posted about the incident on Facebook that night.
"Sitting across from this ... stay classy, New York," read the post, which included a photo of some of the graffiti. It read "Destroy Israel Heil Hitler" and included a swastika.
The post continued: "VERY IMPORTANT EDIT - hand sanitizer and tissues will totally erase sharpie graffiti. Share and spread the word!"
The following day Nied posted: "Bewildered, confused and pleasantly shocked doesn't even begin to describe this ... never in a million years did I think anybody would record my moment, let alone that it would explode like this. I'm honestly not sure what to say other than that I was just doing the right thing, the thing that needed to be done."
rewrite:
A New York commuter who organized the removal of anti-Semitic graffiti from a subway car is to be formally recognized by the Anti-Defamation League. Jared Nied, aged 37, will be presented with the ADL’s Stand Up New Yorker Award, an honor conferred upon city residents for taking direct action to assist individuals targeted by bigotry or for initiating efforts to publicly condemn hatred. The award will be presented by Evan Bernstein, director of the ADL’s New York region, in a ceremony scheduled for Wednesday.

The incident, which occurred on the evening of February 4th, gained widespread attention after a fellow commuter, Gregory Locke, detailed the event in a Facebook post. Locke described a silent and uncomfortable train car where passengers were uncertain how to respond to the graffiti. Nied reportedly stood and announced, “Hand sanitizer gets rid of Sharpie. We need alcohol.” He then procured tissues and commenced cleaning. Nied, who works professionally as a sous chef, also documented the incident online that same night, posting a photograph of the graffiti—which included the phrases “Destroy Israel Heil Hitler” and a swastika—with the caption, “Sitting across from this ... stay classy, New York.” In a subsequent edit to his post, he added a practical observation: “VERY IMPORTANT EDIT - hand sanitizer and tissues will totally erase sharpie graffiti. Share and spread the word!”

Reflecting on the unexpected public response in a follow-up post, Nied expressed his astonishment. He stated that he was “bewildered, confused and pleasantly shocked,” noting he never anticipated his actions would be recorded or achieve such widespread recognition. He concluded by emphasizing that his intervention was merely an attempt to perform a necessary and correct action in the moment.

RIO DE JANEIRO Brazilian federal police arrested the former head of the country's water sports association and two others on Thursday for alleged embezzlement of up to 40 million reais (10.21 million pounds) in public funds.
The arrests came after complaints from athletes, ex-athletes and business people tied to the sport that officials at the Brazilian Confederation of Aquatic Sports (CBDA) pocketed funds meant for training and equipment, police said at a press conference.
The case follows corruption scandals in other Brazilian sports such as soccer and volleyball.
Former CBDA president Coaracy Nunes was detained along with the group's one-time financial director and the technical coordinator of the water polo team, a police spokesman said.
"I cried with relief," former Olympic swimmer Joana Maranhao, a long-time critic of the CBDA leadership, said on Twitter. "You have no idea how I hoped for this."
A fourth person with a warrant out for his arrest was declared a fugitive.
Police also detained four people for questioning and carried out 16 search warrants as part of the operation, according to an official statement. An earlier police statement said that five had been arrested.
The CBDA, which represents sports such as diving, swimming and water polo, said Nunes, who was first elected to lead the organisation in 1988, left the organisation as president in March and elections for his successor were yet to be called.
The CBDA is a private entity which is partly funded by the public sector.
(Reporting by Pedro Fonseca; Additional reporting by Andrew Downie; Writing by Bruno Federowski; Editing by W Simon and Andrew Hay)
rewrite:
On Thursday, Brazilian federal police in Rio de Janeiro arrested the former president of the Brazilian Confederation of Aquatic Sports (CBDA) and two other individuals on allegations of embezzling up to 40 million reais (approximately 10.21 million pounds) in public funds. According to authorities, the arrests followed formal complaints from current and former athletes, as well as associated business figures, who alleged that CBDA officials had misappropriated resources designated for athlete training and equipment procurement. This investigation emerges amidst a broader context of corruption scandals affecting other Brazilian sporting bodies, including those governing soccer and volleyball.

A police spokesperson confirmed that former CBDA president Coaracy Nunes was detained alongside the organization's former financial director and the technical coordinator of the national water polo team. A fourth individual subject to an arrest warrant has been declared a fugitive. As part of the operation, police executed 16 search warrants and detained four additional persons for questioning; an initial police communiqué had indicated five arrests. The CBDA, which oversees disciplines including swimming, diving, and water polo, is a private entity that receives partial public funding. The organization stated that Nunes, first elected to lead it in 1988, concluded his tenure as president in March, and a succession election has not yet been scheduled.

The development was met with approval from certain athletic quarters. Former Olympic swimmer Joana Maranhão, a longstanding critic of the CBDA administration, expressed profound relief via social media, stating, "I cried with relief... You have no idea how I hoped for this."

Spanish publication Don Balon indicates that the 25-year-old Egyptian international, who has scored over forty goals this season and won the PFA Player of the Year award, has requested additional time from Liverpool’s management to consider his future. The same source previously suggested a comprehensive agreement with the player is already in place.

Real Madrid’s purported motivation for the acquisition extends beyond sporting merit, interpreted by some outlets as a strategic maneuver intended to challenge rival club Barcelona. Club president Florentino Pérez is reportedly prepared to offer approximately €200 million to secure Salah’s transfer. Concurrently, reports suggest Liverpool’s awareness of Salah’s potential desire to depart, with the club having allegedly requested the player’s discretion regarding any potential move. Discussions may involve players such as Marco Asensio or Lucas Vázquez moving to Liverpool as part of any agreement.

In related transfer speculation, Diario Gol reports that Real Madrid is also seeking to facilitate the departure of Gareth Bale, with a valuation of at least €90 million for the Welsh international. The same report contends that while Real Madrid values Salah at approximately €180 million and Bale at €90 million, Liverpool’s internal valuation is notably higher for Salah, at €200 million, and significantly lower for Bale, at an estimated €60 million. These divergent valuations could present a substantial obstacle to any potential transaction.

MILWAUKEE — Enes Kanter seems to play better with a stitched-up mouth.
He had another monstrous double-double outing Friday night, with 17 points and 18 rebounds, keeping the Knicks in the game throughout before Giannis Antetokounmpo’s game-winner in the Bucks’ 92-90 victory.
Kanter has had 18 stitches sewn into his mouth since Monday, making it tough to talk, but not too tough to be underneath the rim snatching offensive boards. He hauled in another eight on Friday, and is one of the league’s leaders.
“I’m giving the team so much confidence — I’m telling them whenever you shoot the ball, shoot it with confidence because I’m down there and I’ll go get the rebound,’’ Kanter said.
Coach Jeff Hornacek said Kanter has played like “a warrior’’ these past three games — hitting for 20 points and 20 rebound Tuesday against the Nets, and nearly matching those numbers in Boston and Milwaukee.
“You know at some point in the game he’s getting hit in the mouth,’’ Hornacek said. “You look at his lips, he’s a warrior out there, plays as hard as he can. He cleans up the misses. You can’t say enough good things about his effort because you know he’s not feeling great with stitches in his mouth. He wants to get out there.”
Asked if he enjoyed playing for recently fired Bucks coach Jason Kidd last season, Michael Beasley said, “I’m here now, so.”
Beasley was out of the rotation late last season in Milwaukee.
rewrite:
MILWAUKEE — Enes Kanter appears to perform at a heightened level while managing a stitched mouth injury. On Friday evening, he delivered another formidable double-double performance, recording 17 points and 18 rebounds, thereby sustaining the Knicks' competitiveness until Giannis Antetokounmpo’s decisive shot secured a 92-90 victory for the Bucks. Since Monday, Kanter has required 18 stitches in his mouth, an injury that impedes his speech but does not hinder his effectiveness in securing offensive rebounds near the basket. He captured an additional eight offensive rebounds in Friday’s contest, maintaining his position among the league leaders in this category.

Kanter remarked, “I am instilling considerable confidence in the team—I instruct them to shoot with assurance, as I am positioned to retrieve any missed attempts.” Head coach Jeff Hornacek characterized Kanter’s recent three-game performance as that of “a warrior,” noting his 20-point, 20-rebound achievement against the Nets on Tuesday, followed by nearly equivalent performances in subsequent games against Boston and Milwaukee. Hornacek observed, “He consistently endures physical contact, evident in his condition. He competes with maximum intensity, capitalizing on missed shots. His effort is commendable, particularly given the discomfort of his injury, yet he remains determined to contribute.”

When questioned regarding his experience playing under recently dismissed Bucks coach Jason Kidd last season, Michael Beasley offered a succinct response: “I am here now.” Beasley had been excluded from the regular rotation during the latter part of the previous season in Milwaukee.

National Reconstruction Authority (NRA) Chief Executive Officer Yubaraj Bhusal said that he has not received any direction or information from the government regarding the recently reported increase of earthquake housing grant of Rs.100, 000.00 to earthquake victims. “Since there is no budget for new increase, NRA is going to precede its program providing Rs.300.000.00 as per schedule.
Two weeks ago cabinet decided to increase the housing grant increasing Rs.100.000.000 to the victims.
Addressing media, he said that as many as 100,000 houses damaged by 2015 earthquake would be reconstructed by this mid-February. NRA Chief Executive Officer Bhusal informed that by that time number of houses being reconstructed would reach 450,000. Efforts are underway to ensure permanent shelter to 60 percent of the earthquake affected ones by coming monsoon.
During an interaction in the capital, NRA CEO Bhusal further said, “So far, 95,000 houses have been reconstructed, while 284,000 are under construction. The engineers have been mobilized in five different groups in the 14 districts which suffered most in the earthquake. After they are provided the allowance, they are encouraged for working.”
According to him, those mobilized in the hard hit district are provided Rs 58,000 and those inconvenient districts Rs 42,000 every month.
The engineers have been working in 1,186 wards of 131 local levels in 14 districts. Similarly, 21,000 have been given training in these districts to prepare necessary human resources for the reconstruction of the houses.
In 18 districts which witnessed partial damages, 5,000 people have been trained.
The reconstruction priority is given to the houses for senior citizen above 70 years of age, single women above 65 years of age, and under-16.
rewrite:
The Chief Executive Officer of the National Reconstruction Authority (NRA), Yubaraj Bhusal, has stated that the Authority has not received any official directive or notification from the government concerning the recently reported cabinet decision to augment the earthquake housing grant by an additional Rs. 100,000 for affected individuals. He clarified that, in the absence of a corresponding budgetary allocation for this new increment, the NRA will proceed with its existing schedule of disbursing Rs. 300,000 per household.

Addressing members of the media, CEO Bhusal provided an update on reconstruction progress, indicating that approximately 100,000 houses damaged in the 2015 earthquake are projected to be fully reconstructed by mid-February. This achievement is expected to bring the cumulative total of reconstructed residences to 450,000. He further noted that concerted efforts are being made to ensure permanent shelter is secured for 60 percent of the affected population before the onset of the forthcoming monsoon season.

Elaborating on current operations, Bhusal detailed that 95,000 houses have been completed to date, with an additional 284,000 currently under construction. To facilitate this work, engineering personnel have been organized into five distinct groups and deployed across the fourteen most severely impacted districts. These professionals receive a monthly incentive allowance—Rs. 58,000 in the hardest-hit districts and Rs. 42,000 in other affected districts—to encourage their continued participation. Their efforts are concentrated across 1,186 wards within 131 local levels. Furthermore, to build local capacity, training has been provided to 21,000 individuals in these fourteen districts, with an additional 5,000 trained in eighteen districts that sustained partial damage.

The NRA has also established a prioritized reconstruction sequence, focusing first on households headed by senior citizens above 70 years of age, single women over 65, and those with dependents under the age of 16.

Hot and Humid, with Daily Storms
by Ryan Stinnett
To our west, an upper-level feature is going to eject out of the Plains and move along the boundary across the state. Our Monday looks to be a bit wetter than our Sunday, with widespread and numerous showers and storms across the state especially this afternoon and evening. Of course, we will be watching for localized areas of flash flooding as that will certainly be a possibility with some of the heavier rainfall this afternoon and evening.
REST OF WEEK: Little change in the air mass over the state, and with upper-level feature traversing the state regularly, we are going to maintain the threat for scattered to numerous showers and storms on a daily basis. When it is not raining, expect a mix of sun and clouds with highs mostly in the 80s to lower 90s. Of course each day, any storm will have intense tropical downpours, which could cause flash flooding.
WEEKEND SNEAK PEEK: More of the same is expected into next weekend. We are still not seeing any big pattern shift across the U.S. which of course is not unusual for August. Both Saturday and Sunday are expected to have a partly sunny sky with randomly placed showers and storms mainly during the afternoon and evening hours.
ONE WEEK UNTIL ECLIPSE: Monday August 21st is rapidly approaching when much of the U.S. will experience the total solar eclipse. Most of Alabama will have on average 90% of the sun blocked by the moon. The 70 mile totality area of darkness will be just to the north and east of Alabama. The eclipse will occur between 12PM and 3PM that day, and just over a week away, there is no way of knowing a forecast. However, we do look at trends in the models, and as of now the forecast for that day looks to feature sun, clouds, and the threat of rain. Hopefully the viewing time will yield mainly clear conditions, but rain or shine, and eerie darkness will befall the state for a short while.
Have a great day!
Ryan

Meteorological Synopsis: Persistent Humid Conditions with Diurnal Convective Activity
By Ryan Stinnett

An upper-level atmospheric feature is projected to propagate eastward from the Plains region, subsequently tracking along a frontal boundary situated across the state. Consequently, Monday is anticipated to experience increased precipitation compared to Sunday, characterized by widespread and numerous showers and thunderstorms, particularly during the afternoon and evening hours. Due to the potential for high rainfall rates, localized instances of flash flooding will be monitored closely.

For the remainder of the week, a stagnant air mass will persist over the region. The regular traversal of upper-level disturbances will maintain a daily probability of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Intermittent periods of precipitation will feature a mixture of sun and clouds, with high temperatures generally ranging from the mid-80s to lower 90s Fahrenheit. Any convective development will be capable of producing intense, tropical downpours, reiterating the ongoing risk of flash flooding.

Current model guidance suggests a continuation of this pattern into the upcoming weekend, with no significant synoptic-scale pattern change anticipated across the United States—a typical climatological feature for August. Both Saturday and Sunday are expected to be partly sunny, with diurnally driven, randomly distributed showers and thunderstorms, primarily during the afternoon and evening.

In other developments, the total solar eclipse of Monday, August 21st, is approaching. While the path of totality will be located approximately 70 miles to the north and east of Alabama, the state will experience an average obscuration of 90% of the solar disk during the event, which is scheduled between 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM local time. Precise cloud cover and precipitation forecasts for an event over a week in advance remain highly uncertain. However, based on current model trends, conditions are projected to feature a combination of sun, clouds, and a potential for rain. Optimal viewing conditions would require predominantly clear skies; nevertheless, irrespective of weather, a period of notable darkness will occur across the state during the eclipse.

A former Stoke City youngster has signed for the Lambs after being on the radar for the last 18 months.
Defender Curtis Strong has put pen to paper on a short-term deal to join Tamworth FC from Telford.
Strong, who impressed Lambs manager Andy Morrel during his stint at the club the season before last, has been hotly chased by the boss as he looks to strengthen his squad for the remainder of the season.
Speaking to the Herald about the signing, Andy Morrell said: “We are really pleased that Curt has agreed to join us.
“We have been watching him for nearly 18 months and have been trying to get him with us for some time.
“He has got a lot of pace and can get goals even though he is more of a defensive player.
“We have got him on a short term deal and we hope he can hit the ground running and show us exactly what he can do.”
The 22-year-old started his career at the Potters, playing in the under 18s and under 21s, before making the move to the Lambs back in August 2015.
He picked up a serious injury which put him out of action for the whole of last season.
He moved to Telford but has now signed a short-term deal to return to the Lamb to the delight of his teammates.
George Delves, general manager of Tamworth FC, said: “We are really looking forward to getting Curtis back.
“He has got so much pace and goals in him as well. He was really popular when he was last here and I know that a lot of the older players are excited to see him back at the Lamb.
“Hopefully he will bring a bit of competition and keep the lads on their toes. He has got a chance to show us what he can do.”
rewrite:

The acquisition concludes a pursuit lasting approximately eighteen months by Tamworth manager Andy Morrell, who had been keen to reinforce his squad for the ongoing campaign. Morrell initially noted Strong’s potential during the player’s previous stint with the club two seasons ago.

In a statement provided to the Herald, Morrell expressed his satisfaction with the signing: “We are very pleased that Curtis has agreed to join us. Our observation of him has been sustained over nearly eighteen months, and we have endeavoured to secure his services for some time. He possesses considerable pace and a capacity to contribute goals, despite his primary defensive orientation. This is a short-term arrangement, and we anticipate he will make an immediate impact, demonstrating his full capabilities.”

Strong commenced his career within Stoke City’s youth system, featuring for both the under-18 and under-21 sides, before initially joining Tamworth in August 2015. It is hoped his presence will stimulate healthy competition within the team and motivate the squad. This represents an opportunity for him to exhibit his talents.”

A prominent Manhattan surgeon – best known for treating Bono – had been stripped of his privileges to practice at New York-Presbyterian Hospital just days before his apparent suicide, a law enforcement source told The Post.
Dr. Dean Lorich was told Friday he would be persona non grata at the landmark Upper East Hospital – and he was found dead inside his Manhattan apartment on Sunday with a self-inflicted stab wound, according to a source.
“It was a big deal” to lose his spot at New York-Presbyterian, a law enforcement source said.
As of late Monday night, Lorich was still listed on staff on the hospital’s website.
It’s believed Lorich backed the wrong horse in a political battle within the hospital, leading to his ouster, the source said.
A hospital spokeswoman declined comment Monday night on the doctor’s status at New York-Presbyterian.
She would only refer to a hospital statement made Sunday night, confirming Lorich’s death: “We mourn this tragic development and extend our deepest sympathies to Dr. Lorich’s family, friends and patients.”
Lorich is best known for performing surgery on Bono after the U2 frontman lost control of his bike in Central Park, suffering multiple fractures in 2014.
Additional reporting by David K. Li
rewrite: A prominent Manhattan surgeon, notably recognized for treating the musician Bono, had his clinical privileges revoked at New York-Presbyterian Hospital shortly before his apparent suicide, according to a law enforcement source. Dr. Dean Lorich was informed on Friday that he was no longer permitted to practice at the Upper East Side institution. He was subsequently discovered deceased in his Manhattan residence on Sunday, having sustained a self-inflicted stab wound. A source indicated that the loss of his position at the hospital constituted a significant professional setback. As of late Monday evening, Dr. Lorich remained listed on the hospital's official staff directory. The same source suggested that his dismissal may have resulted from aligning with the unsuccessful faction in an internal institutional dispute. A hospital spokeswoman declined to comment on the specifics of the physician's status, referencing only a prior statement issued Sunday night which confirmed his passing and expressed condolences: "We mourn this tragic development and extend our deepest sympathies to Dr. Lorich’s family, friends and patients." Dr. Lorich gained particular renown for performing orthopedic surgery on Bono following the artist's 2014 bicycle accident in Central Park, which resulted in multiple fractures.

Israel's transformation into a world power with the supply and consumption of desalinated water has a health price, Hadashot 2 reported tonight, Wednesday.
According to the report, a new large-scale study of some 180,000 Israelis found that in areas where desalinated water is consumed, there is a significant increase in heart disease. Today, most of the public in Israel is drinking desalinated water.
The researchers examined 178,000 members of Clalit Health Services in two groups. One group included two areas in the country that have received desalinated water for 6 years. The second group included an area that receives only natural water. The study found that in the areas with desalinated water there was a 6 to 10 percent increase in heart disease compared to the area that received natural water.
As early as 2011, the World Health Organization (WHO) issued a warning that the desalination process removes essential minerals, such as magnesium. The organization recommended adding magnesium artificially.
Two years ago, the prime minister ordered the minister of health to expedite a pilot program to introduce magnesium into one of the desalination plants, but nothing has been done since then.
rewrite:
A recent report from Hadashot 2 indicates that Israel's emergence as a global leader in the supply and consumption of desalinated water carries significant public health implications. A large-scale epidemiological study, encompassing approximately 178,000 members of Clalit Health Services, reveals a correlation between desalinated water consumption and increased incidence of heart disease. The research compared populations in two regions receiving desalinated water for six years against a control region utilizing only natural water sources. Findings demonstrated a 6 to 10 percent higher rate of heart disease in the areas supplied with desalinated water.

This health outcome aligns with a 2011 World Health Organization warning that desalination removes essential minerals, notably magnesium, from water. The WHO subsequently recommended artificial remineralization. Despite a prime ministerial directive two years ago instructing the health minister to accelerate a pilot program for magnesium reintroduction at a desalination facility, no substantive action has been taken to date, while most of Israel's population now consumes desalinated water.

In a rather shocking development, the Supreme Court recently pulled up Tamil star Rajinikanth's wife Latha for failing to pay the Rs 6.20 Crore she owes a noted advertising company. While rebuking the former playback singer, the Supreme Court also asked her to either clear her dues or face trial. The SC has given her nearly a week to make it clear whether she plans to clear the dues. The advertising firm was associated with the highly ambitious 2014 release Kochadaiiyaan and had given nearly Rs 10 Crore to Latha's company.
The lady's company was supposed to refund the amount and pay an additional Rs 1.2 Crore as 'guaranteed profit'.
Latha's troubles started when a trial court asked the Police to look into the matter. In 2016, the Karnataka High Court quashed the order. Following this, the advertising company approached the Supreme Court. Earlier this year, the 'apex court' made it clear that she would have to clear the dues.
In case you did not know, Kochadaiiyaan was directed by Soundarya Rajinikanth and marked her directorial debut. Shot using motion capture technology, it featured Rajinikanth and Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone in the lead. The supporting cast featured names such as Jackie Shroff, Nassar and R Sarathkumar. Released on May 23, 2014, it opened to a good response at the box office but ultimately failed to live up to the expectations. Its distributors suffered losses and this proved to be an embarrassment for 'Thalaiva'.
Interestingly, this controversy involving Latha comes at a time when the Superstar is busy with his political commitments. On the film front, he currently has 2.0 and a film with Karthik Subbaraj in his kitty. 2.0 is a Shankar directorial and will see Rajini reprise his Chitti character from the 2010 hit Enthiran. Recently, it was reported that the makers of 2.0 are in a fix because of the unsatisfactory performance of Kaala. As such, it is not very clear when the sci-fi thriller will ultimately hit the screens.
rewrite:
In a significant legal development, the Supreme Court of India has issued a reprimand to Latha Rajinikanth, spouse of prominent Tamil film actor Rajinikanth, for her failure to settle a debt of ₹6.20 crore owed to a prominent advertising firm. The Court directed her to either discharge the outstanding amount or face criminal proceedings, granting a period of approximately one week to declare her intention regarding the settlement. The financial obligation originates from an agreement associated with the 2014 film *Kochadaiiyaan*, for which the advertising entity had provided an advance of approximately ₹10 crore to Mrs. Rajinikanth’s company. The terms stipulated that the company was to refund this advance along with an additional ₹1.2 crore designated as a ‘guaranteed profit’.

The litigation commenced following a trial court order directing police investigation into the matter, which was subsequently quashed by the Karnataka High Court in 2016. The advertiser then petitioned the Supreme Court, which earlier this year affirmed the liability, mandating the repayment of the dues.

For context, *Kochadaiiyaan* was the directorial debut of Soundarya Rajinikanth. Utilizing motion capture technology, the film starred Rajinikanth and Bollywood actress Deepika Padukone in lead roles, with a supporting cast including Jackie Shroff, Nassar, and R. Sarathkumar. Released on 23 May 2014, it initially garnered a positive box office response but ultimately underperformed relative to expectations, resulting in financial losses for its distributors—a circumstance that proved professionally embarrassing for Rajinikanth.

This legal controversy emerges concurrently with Rajinikanth’s active engagement in political commitments. Regarding his cinematic projects, he is currently associated with two films: *2.0*, a science-fiction sequel directed by Shankar in which he reprises his role from *Enthiran* (2010), and an untitled project with director Karthik Subbaraj. The release schedule for *2.0* has reportedly become uncertain due to the underwhelming commercial performance of his recent film *Kaala*, leaving the precise theatrical date for the anticipated sci-fi thriller unclear.

rewrite:
The release of iOS 11.4 and HomePod 11.4 by Apple has enabled the AirPlay 2 feature, permitting owners of multiple HomePod speakers to configure a stereo pair. As the process is managed through the Home application rather than a dedicated HomePod app, users may require guidance. The following procedure details the necessary steps.

When it comes to comedy shows, hecklers come with the territory.
"He was just basically a disruptive customer that wanted to be center of attention during the show," said Brien Spina, who owns Off the Hook Comedy Club in North Naples.
Spina said what happened Saturday night went too far.
"It's highly inappropriate. We have no place for it," Spina said, "And I think that some of the things probably he had coming to him."
He was talking about Joseph Lanham, a Fort Myers man who went to see comedian Gary Owen's show.
"At one point I was doing a Trump joke, and he said 'Yeah, there's more of us than there is of them.' And he kept talking, so I kicked him out," Owen said in part of a Facebook video he posted about the incident.
Owen went on to say in that video what happened after the show. He said Lanham sent him a racially charged Facebook messaged using the n-word multiple times. Owen showed the message to his followers in the Facebook video.
"Now everybody knows who you are. Hope your boss sees it if you got a job," Owen said in the video.
Lanham ended up being fired from his job as Vice President of Sales for National Roofing of Collier.
"It angers you. I mean, there's no call for it," said Lanham's former boss Ralph Goddard.
Goddard said his company had received threats of violence from Lanham's choice of words.
"I was fearful for my employees to even come in this morning because I didn't know what to expect," Goddard said.
He also fired Lanham's wife.
NBC 2 tracked down Lanham, who refused an on-camera interview. He told reporter Bryan Anderson he's not a racist, blaming his behavior on alcohol.
"He sent me an apology, said he was drunk," Owen said in a second Facebook video, "but I don't know if I accept it yet because a drunken tongue speaks a sober mind."
rewrite:
The phenomenon of audience members vocally disrupting performances, commonly known as "heckling," is an occupational hazard within the context of live comedy. Brien Spina, proprietor of the Off the Hook Comedy Club in North Naples, characterized such an individual as "essentially a disruptive patron seeking to command attention during the performance." Spina asserted that an incident occurring on a recent Saturday evening constituted a significant transgression, describing the behavior as "highly inappropriate" and affirming that the establishment has "no place for it." He further suggested that the individual in question, Joseph Lanham of Fort Myers, who attended a show by comedian Gary Owen, faced foreseeable consequences.

The confrontation originated during Owen's set. The comedian recounted in a Facebook video that, while delivering a joke about Donald Trump, Lanham interjected, stating, "Yeah, there's more of us than there is of them," and persisted in speaking, prompting his ejection from the venue. Owen subsequently detailed in the same video that following the performance, Lanham sent him a private Facebook message laden with racial epithets, including multiple uses of the n-word. Owen publicly shared this correspondence with his followers, stating, "Now everybody knows who you are. Hope your boss sees it if you got a job."

The repercussions were swift. Lanham was terminated from his position as Vice President of Sales for National Roofing of Collier. Ralph Goddard, Lanham's former employer, expressed dismay, noting, "It angers you. I mean, there's no call for it." Goddard revealed that the company had received threats of violence precipitated by Lanham's statements, causing him apprehension for employee safety. Consequently, Lanham's wife was also dismissed from the company. When contacted by NBC 2, Lanham declined an on-camera interview but informed reporter Bryan Anderson that he did not consider himself racist, attributing his conduct to alcohol consumption. In a follow-up video, Owen acknowledged receiving an apology from Lanham citing intoxication, but expressed skepticism, remarking, "I don't know if I accept it yet because a drunken tongue speaks a sober mind."

LOS ANGELES —
The winners of the International Design Awards (IDA) have been announced. The Awards recognize, celebrate and promote legendary design visionaries, while seeking to uncover emerging talent in architecture, interior, product, graphic, and fashion design.
The jury for the 10th Edition of IDA was comprised of 25 design experts and professionals, who reviewed thousands of entries from over 60 countries, based on originality, function, innovation and statistics. The Top Five Designers include:
Architectural Design of The Year – Stinessen Arkitektur – Manshausen Island Resort
Interior Design of The Year – Alisa Sibgatova, Witch Craft – New Classics
Graphic Design of the Year – Phoenix The Creative Studio – Cannes Lions Survival Kit
Fashion Design of the Year – Panorama International Ltd. – Wateryard House
Product Design of the Year – Elica S.p.A. – Nikola Tesla
“As we reflect on a decade of design excellence at IDA, it is clear that the quality of new ideas and designs only improves as we move forward,” said Hossein Farmani, Director of IDA.
The five disciplines honoured in IDA (architectural, interior, fashion, graphic, and product design) are further divided into 300 categories that span the world of design. Whether it be emerging talent or names that set industry standard, IDA recognizes the people behind cutting-edge design from all over the world.
A selection of winners of categories for the 10th Edition include:
GOLD – Fashion Design I MOMOKAMEI, Alphabet Block Chatter (aka A, B, C)
GOLD – Architectural Design I Torres & Bello Arquietos, Residencial Kalil
SILVER – Product Design I Valsfer, Grasslamp
SILVER – Graphic Design I Janusz Janek, Papilarnie
BRONZE – Interior Design I Aesthetic Movement, Regular Visitors Retail
BRONZE – Product Design I Fraction Design Studio, Hide and Seek
To view all of the winners of the Awards, please click here.

The International Design Awards (IDA) have formally announced the recipients of its tenth annual honors. The IDA program is dedicated to the recognition, celebration, and promotion of distinguished design visionaries, concurrently aiming to identify emergent talent across the principal disciplines of architecture, interior, product, graphic, and fashion design.

A jury panel consisting of twenty-five design experts and professionals adjudicated the competition, evaluating thousands of submissions from more than sixty nations. Assessments were conducted according to criteria of originality, functional utility, innovation, and statistical performance. The premier accolades, designated as "Designer of the Year" across five categories, were conferred as follows: Architectural Design to Stinessen Arkitektur for the Manshausen Island Resort; Interior Design to Alisa Sibgatova of Witch Craft for New Classics; Graphic Design to Phoenix The Creative Studio for the Cannes Lions Survival Kit; Fashion Design to Panorama International Ltd. for Wateryard House; and Product Design to Elica S.p.A. for Nikola Tesla.

Reflecting on the decade-long initiative, IDA Director Hossein Farmani observed, "As we consider a decade of design excellence at IDA, it is evident that the caliber of novel concepts and designs continues to advance." Beyond these top honors, the five core disciplines are subdivided into approximately three hundred specific categories, encompassing the breadth of contemporary design practice. The awards scheme acknowledges both pioneering newcomers and established figures who define industry standards, thereby highlighting the global contributors to avant-garde design.

A representative selection of category winners from the tenth edition includes gold awards for Fashion Design (MOMOKAMEI, Alphabet Block Chatter) and Architectural Design (Torres & Bello Arquitectos, Residencial Kalil); silver awards for Product Design (Valsfer, Grasslamp) and Graphic Design (Janusz Janek, Papilarnie); and bronze awards for Interior Design (Aesthetic Movement, Regular Visitors Retail) and Product Design (Fraction Design Studio, Hide and Seek). A comprehensive listing of all award recipients is available for review through the official channels.

CAPE TOWN, South Africa — South Africa fast bowler Kagiso Rabada has had his two-test ban overturned on appeal and will be available for the remainder of the series against Australia.
Test cricket’s No. 1-ranked bowler was initially banned for the third and fourth tests after being found guilty of two charges of misconduct for aggressive wicket celebrations in the second test in Port Elizabeth.
Rabada’s first offence, of intentionally bumping into Australia captain Steve Smith after dismissing him in the first innings, earned him three demerit points and took him over a disciplinary threshold. That led to an automatic two-test ban.
Michael Heron, who heard the appeal, said he couldn’t be “comfortably satisfied” that Rabada intended to make contact with Smith and found him not guilty of the charge under the International Cricket Council’s code of conduct.
Heron instead found the 22-year-old Rabada guilty of a lower-level offence and issued him with a one demerit point penalty and 25 per cent of his match fee.
“I consider the conduct was inappropriate, lacked respect for his fellow player and involved non-deliberate and minor contact,” Heron said in a statement Tuesday. “The actions contravened the principle that a dismissed batsman should be left alone.”
Rabada was voted player of the match after taking 11 wickets series-levelling win in South Africa at Port Elizabeth and his availability for the third test in Cape Town starting Thursday is a boost for the hosts.
rewrite:
In a significant development for the ongoing Test series, South African fast bowler Kagiso Rabada has successfully appealed a two-match suspension and will consequently be available for selection in the remaining fixtures against Australia. The premier-ranked Test bowler had initially received the ban following two separate charges of misconduct arising from aggressive post-wicket celebrations during the second Test in Port Elizabeth. The primary charge, which carried three demerit points, stemmed from an incident where Rabada made contact with Australian captain Steve Smith after dismissing him. This infraction elevated his cumulative demerit points beyond the disciplinary threshold, triggering an automatic two-Test suspension.

Upon review, judicial commissioner Michael Heron ruled that he could not be “comfortably satisfied” Rabada had intended to make contact with Smith, thereby finding him not guilty of the original level two charge under the International Cricket Council’s code of conduct. Heron instead adjudged the 22-year-old guilty of a lesser offence, imposing a penalty of one demerit point and a fine equivalent to 25 percent of his match fee. In a statement, Heron clarified the rationale, noting, “I consider the conduct was inappropriate, lacked respect for his fellow player and involved non-deliberate and minor contact. The actions contravened the principle that a dismissed batsman should be left alone.”

Rabada’s reinstatement is a considerable advantage for the South African team, particularly following his performance of eleven wickets in the series-levelling victory in Port Elizabeth, for which he was named player of the match. His availability for the third Test, commencing in Cape Town, thus provides a substantial boost to the host side.

iStock/Thinkstock(NEW YORK) — Jenny Cavnar has had a long-running career in Major League Baseball, but she slid into a historic new role in the broadcast booth Monday night, becoming the first woman since 1996 to call the televised play-by-play for a major league team.
Cavnar called the Colorado Rockies and San Diego Padres matchup in Denver alongside analyst Jeff Huson and former Rockies outfielder-turned analyst Ryan Spilborghs. It was a fitting assignment for Cavnar, who previously reported for the Padres before joining the Rockies as a pre- and post-game host in 2012.
With more than a decade of baseball reporting in various capacities under her belt, Cavnar called her first televised homerun Monday night when Rockies’ third baseman Nolan Arenado stepped up to the plate.
“That ball is shot into left field, fire up the fountains she’s gone,” Cavnar announced, describing the two-run shot in the bottom of the first inning. Her run call coincided with the eruption of the classic Coors Field fountains whenever the home team hits a home run.
Cavnar joins a shortlist of women who have called America’s pastime.
Mary Shane was the first female in a booth, doing radio for the Chicago White Sox in 1976 before moving on to television; and Suzyn Waldman was the first woman to do baseball game commentary, for a few New York Mets games on radio in June 1993, according to ESPN. Waldman called her first TV broadcast in July 1995 for a New York Yankees versus Texas Rangers game on ABC’s “Baseball Night in America” and her first play-by-play in 1996.
Other notable women who have spent time in the booth include Gayle Gardner, who replaced Charlie Jones on the Rockies TV broadcast for the Aug. 3, 1993 Rockies and Cincinnati Reds game. Pam Boucher announced 36 games on Yankees TV, WPIX in 1977.
Cavnar, a Colorado native, previously made history in 2015 as the first female analyst for a series of National League games in the radio booth.
She felt the love with messages of support from around the league and other women in the industry, including ESPN “Sunday Night Baseball” analyst Jessica Mendoza.
Although the Rockies fell to the Padres 13-5, the night will go down as a win for Cavnar.

rewrite:
On Monday evening, Jenny Cavnar achieved a historic milestone in Major League Baseball broadcasting, becoming the first woman since 1996 to serve as the primary play-by-play announcer for a televised major league game. Cavnar called the contest between the Colorado Rockies and the San Diego Padres from Denver, working alongside analyst Jeff Huson and former Rockies outfielder Ryan Spilborghs, who now serves as a broadcaster. This assignment held particular significance for Cavnar, whose professional background includes prior reporting for the Padres before joining the Rockies’ broadcast team in 2012 as a pre- and post-game host.

Leveraging over a decade of experience in baseball media across various roles, Cavnar described her first televised home run call during the matchup. When Rockies third baseman Nolan Arenado connected in the bottom of the first inning, Cavnar announced, “That ball is shot into left field, fire up the fountains she’s gone,” narrating the two-run homer. Her call synchronized with the activation of the iconic Coors Field fountains, a tradition marking home runs by the home team.

Cavnar’s achievement places her within a select group of women who have broadcast professional baseball. According to ESPN records, Mary Shane pioneered the role as the first woman in a broadcast booth, providing radio commentary for the Chicago White Sox in 1976 before transitioning to television. Suzyn Waldman followed as the first woman to provide commentary for baseball games, calling several New York Mets radio broadcasts in June 1993. Waldman later called her first television game in July 1995 for ABC’s “Baseball Night in America,” featuring the New York Yankees and Texas Rangers, and delivered her first play-by-play in 1996. Other notable figures include Gayle Gardner, who substituted for Charlie Jones on a Rockies television broadcast in August 1993, and Pam Boucher, who announced 36 games for the Yankees on WPIX television in 1977.

A Colorado native, Cavnar had previously made broadcasting history in 2015 as the first female analyst for a series of National League games on radio. She received widespread support following her Monday night debut, including messages from peers such as ESPN “Sunday Night Baseball” analyst Jessica Mendoza. Although the Rockies lost to the Padres with a final score of 13-5, the evening represented a landmark professional victory for Cavnar and a significant moment in the evolution of baseball broadcasting.
