Ever since I was 16 years old, I have identified as a Republican. For years, I have worked for Republican elected officials across the ideological and leadership spectrum. When Republicans talked about the need for a more transparent government that was accountable to the American people — I believed it. When Republicans talked about balancing budgets and living within our means — I supported it. When Republicans talked about adhering to a governing vision outlined in the Constitution and Bill of Rights — I championed it.
I still believe in those things, but the Republican Party does not.
For decades, the Republican Party has marketed itself as the “rule of law” party. From immigration to police brutality, the GOP falls on the side of “law and order.” It is a theme that lies at the very heart of the Republican Party’s moral foundation and rhetoric.
And yet, in the case of Roy Moore and this week’s Alabama Senate race, morality has been abandoned for political expediency.
How else can you explain the president of the United States calling former U.S. Attorney Doug Jones — a man who successfully prosecuted the Birmingham bombings — “soft on crime?”
What is happening right now in Alabama illustrates everything wrong with the Republican Party and it’s a big reason why I’ve made the personal decision to leave the GOP and join the Democratic Party. The reality is there is no moral compass guiding the Republican Party. There is no leadership or courage.
rewrite:
My political affiliation has been with the Republican Party since the age of sixteen. Throughout my career, I have served under Republican officials representing a diverse range of ideological positions and leadership styles. I consistently endorsed the party’s stated principles: the imperative for a more transparent and publicly accountable government, the necessity of fiscal discipline through balanced budgets, and a steadfast commitment to a constitutional framework of governance as delineated in the Constitution and the Bill of Rights. While my belief in these foundational tenets remains unwavering, I contend that the contemporary Republican Party has fundamentally diverged from them.

For decades, the party has strategically positioned itself as the champion of the "rule of law," invoking "law and order" as a central tenet of its moral and rhetorical platform across issues from immigration to criminal justice. However, the party’s conduct in the recent Alabama Senate race, particularly its support for candidate Roy Moore despite serious allegations, demonstrates a wholesale abandonment of morality for political expediency. This contradiction is starkly illustrated by the President of the United States disparaging former U.S. Attorney Doug Jones—who successfully prosecuted the perpetrators of the Birmingham church bombings—as "soft on crime."

The present circumstance in Alabama epitomizes the profound deficiencies within the Republican Party. It reveals an organization devoid of a coherent moral compass, lacking in principled leadership and political courage. This disillusionment is the primary reason for my personal decision to renounce my Republican affiliation and align with the Democratic Party.

(CNN) -- Rumor Has It V Kenlyn, a female German shepherd known as "Rumor" won the Best in Show award at the 141st Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show at Madison Square Garden in New York City Tuesday night.
"Unbelievable," said handler and co-owner Kent Boyles.
Rumor was the nation's No. 1 dog last year but fell short to California Journey.
But this year, Best in Show Judge Thomas H. Bradley from Watertown, New York, saw something special in her.
"The German shepherd standard talks about quality and nobility. Sometimes unrecognizable. When you recognize it, it hits you home, and that's what it really is. She is just magnificent."
Earlier Tuesday, Boyles said this would be Rumor's last major show. "She's going to be relaxing for a while, and we'll find an appropriate husband for her. There will be some puppies in the future," Boyles said after the win.
Rumor is named for Adele's hit song "Rumor Has It."
The German shepherd was one of seven dogs to advance to the Best in Show competition.
The 5-year-old won the herding group category -- becoming the second dog from that group to ever win. It was the 39th time that a female has won the top prize.
Sea Breeze, a male Irish setter known as "Adrian," won Reserve Best in Show, second place.
The seven Group winners from Westminster
Best Hound: Daggarwood Delight, a female Norwegian elkhound known as "Duffy"
Best Toy: Pequest Pickwick, a male pekingese known as "Chuckie"
Best Non-sporting: Danfour Avalon As If, a female miniature poodle known as "Aftin"
Best Herding: Rumor Has It V Kenlyn, a female German shepherd known as "Rumor"
Best Sporting: Sea Breeze, a male Irish setter known as "Adrian"
Best Working: Speak Of The Devil, a female boxer known as "Devlin"
Best Terrier: Twice As Nice, a male Norwich terrier known as "Tanner"

rewrite:
On the evening of Tuesday, February 14, 2017, the female German shepherd Rumor Has It V Kenlyn, commonly known as “Rumor,” was awarded Best in Show at the 141st Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show, held at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Handler and co-owner Kent Boyles characterized the victory as “unbelievable.” Although Rumor was the nation’s top-ranked dog in the previous year, she was ultimately defeated by California Journey. This year, however, Best in Show Judge Thomas H. Bradley of Watertown, New York, identified exceptional qualities in the animal. In his assessment, Bradley referenced the breed standard, noting, “The German shepherd standard talks about quality and nobility. Sometimes unrecognizable. When you recognize it, it hits you home, and that’s what it really is. She is just magnificent.”

Prior to the final competition, Boyles indicated that this event would represent Rumor’s final major appearance. Following her win, he stated, “She’s going to be relaxing for a while, and we’ll find an appropriate husband for her. There will be some puppies in the future.” The dog’s name derives from the popular Adele song “Rumor Has It.” Rumor, aged five, first secured the Herding Group title, thereby advancing as one of seven finalists to the Best in Show competition. Her victory marks only the second occasion a dog from the Herding Group has won the overall championship, and the thirty-ninth time a female has received the top honor. Reserve Best in Show (second place) was awarded to Sea Breeze, a male Irish setter known as “Adrian.”

The seven group winners that proceeded to the final round were as follows: Best Hound—Daggarwood Delight, a female Norwegian elkhound (“Duffy”); Best Toy—Pequest Pickwick, a male Pekingese (“Chuckie”); Best Non-Sporting—Danfour Avalon As If, a female miniature poodle (“Aftin”); Best Herding—Rumor Has It V Kenlyn (“Rumor”); Best Sporting—Sea Breeze (“Adrian”); Best Working—Speak Of The Devil, a female boxer (“Devlin”); and Best Terrier—Twice As Nice, a male Norwich terrier (“Tanner”).

SYDNEY, March 29 Australian retail group Premier Investments Ltd on Wednesday said it had purchased a 10.8 percent stake in department store owner Myer Holdings Ltd , but added it had no plans to make a takeover offer at this time.
Shares in Myer, Australia's biggest department store operator by sales with a market value of A$980 million ($748.23 million), surged 18 percent on Monday after about 10 percent of the stock changed hands in a single trade. That sparked speculation of corporate activity.
At Monday's price, Premier bought the stake for around A$100 million, according to Reuters calculations.
Premier's largest shareholder is Century Plaza Investments, whose director and major shareholder is Australian retail magnate Solomon Lew, a former chairman of Myer's predecessor Coles Myer.
Lew has previously used shareholdings to gain leverage in takeover situations, including David Jones and Country Road.
Lew bought a 9.9 percent stake in rival department store owner David Jones before it was taken over by South Africa's Woolworths Holdings Ltd in 2014.
Myer shares closed down 0.4 percent on Wednesday before the announcement from Premier. A Myer spokesman could not be immediately reached for comment.
($1 = 1.3098 Australian dollars) (Reporting by Jamie Freed; Editing by Randy Fabi)
rewrite:
On March 29, Premier Investments Ltd, an Australian retail group, disclosed the acquisition of a 10.8 percent equity interest in Myer Holdings Ltd, a department store operator. The announcement clarified that no takeover bid is presently intended. This disclosure follows significant market activity earlier in the week. On Monday, shares in Myer, the nation's largest department store chain by sales with a market capitalization of A$980 million (US$748.23 million), appreciated by 18 percent. This surge coincided with a single block trade involving approximately 10 percent of the company’s equity, which had prompted speculation regarding potential corporate actions. Based on prevailing prices, Reuters calculations estimate the value of Premier’s acquired stake at approximately A$100 million.

Premier Investments’ majority shareholder is Century Plaza Investments. The director and principal beneficiary of Century Plaza is Solomon Lew, a prominent Australian retail figure and former chairman of Coles Myer, a corporate predecessor to Myer. Mr. Lew has historically utilized strategic equity positions to influence takeover proceedings, as evidenced in prior engagements with entities such as David Jones and Country Road. Notably, he accumulated a 9.9 percent stake in David Jones prior to its 2014 acquisition by South Africa’s Woolworths Holdings Ltd. Myer’s share price concluded Wednesday’s trading session 0.4 percent lower, preceding Premier’s formal statement. Company representatives were unavailable for immediate commentary.

ABUJA – THE Senate has assured that with the level of work carried out so far on the amendment of Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas, NLNG Act, the report would be presented at plenary when the lawmakers resume in September from the annual recess.
Disclosing this to Vanguard Monday, Chairman, Senate Committee on Gas, Senator Bassey Albert Akpan, PDP, Akwa Ibom North East said that at a meeting of the committee Monday, major areas in the concurrent of the Amendment Act recently being passed by the House of Representatives.

The committee at its meeting today looked at it and has done a serious work on it to report back to when the Senate resumes September.”
THE House of Representatives had in May passed the NLNG Amendment bill which seeks to make the payment of three percent of annual budget of Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Limited into the coffers of Niger Delta Development Commission, NDDC, through third reading.
Following the passage of the bill promoted by Leo Ogor, Minority Leader, sought to amend the Nigeria LNG (Fiscal Incentives, Guarantees and Assurances) Act, the House is expected to transmit the bill to the Senate for concurrence.
In the new provision, the Act was amended by adding section 7b to the Principal Act, which provides that “Notwithstanding section 7 or any other provision of this Act, the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Limited shall pay 3% of its total annual budget to the Niger Delta Development Commission Fund as required by section 14 subsection 1 and 2b of the NDDC Act establishment Act, 2000.
Also recall that the Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company, NLNG, Limited, had taken its battle against amendment of NLNG Act by the House of Representatives to the Senate.
The essence of the interface with the Senate is to get the House of Representatives to reverse the amendment.
The move, which was supported by the shareholders of the company, such as the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, NNPC; Shell Petroleum Development Company Limited, Total Exploration and Producing Company and Agip, was however based on the need to remove huddles capable of hindering the implementation of the nation’s $25 billion trains seven and eight project.
rewrite:
Senator Bassey Albert Akpan, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Gas, has indicated that the committee’s report on the proposed amendment to the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) Act will be presented upon the Senate’s resumption in September. In a statement provided to Vanguard on Monday, Senator Akpan (PDP, Akwa Ibom North East) confirmed that the committee convened to examine the concurrent version of the amendment legislation recently passed by the House of Representatives. He stated that the committee has undertaken substantial work on the matter and will report its findings when the Senate reconvenes.

The House of Representatives passed the NLNG Amendment Bill in May, following a third reading. Sponsored by Minority Leader Leo Ogor, the bill seeks to amend the Nigeria LNG (Fiscal Incentives, Guarantees and Assurances) Act. Its central provision is to mandate the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Limited to allocate three percent of its total annual budget to the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) Fund. This requirement is intended to align with Section 14, Subsections 1 and 2(b) of the NDDC (Establishment) Act of 2000. The proposed amendment inserts a new section, 7(b), into the principal legislation to enforce this contribution. Following passage, the bill is expected to be transmitted to the Senate for concurrence.

Concurrently, the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas Company Limited has engaged the Senate in an effort to contest the amendment passed by the House. The company, supported by its shareholders—including the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC), Shell Petroleum Development Company Limited, Total Exploration and Production Company, and Agip—argues that the amendment poses significant obstacles. Specifically, they contend that the proposed financial obligation would impede the implementation of the nation’s $25 billion Trains Seven and Eight expansion project. The company’s engagement with the Senate thus aims to persuade the House of Representatives to reconsider and reverse the amendment.

Lancaster City Council has won a prestigious award for its successful redevelopment of Salt Ayre Leisure Centre.
The council picked up the Connected Procurement and Commissioning gong at the iNetwork Innovation Awards.
The award celebrates the innovative approach taken by the council to the commissioning and procurement of a partner to revitalise the ageing centre.
A team of experts was formed from across the council to lead the project, ensuring that the knowledge, skills, capacity and experience needed were involved from the first concept meeting.
This team was instrumental in commissioning a specialist leisure development partner, Alliance Leisure, to transform the facility.
The renovation of the centre has seen a significant increase in the number of local residents using the facilities and new clubs are extending and broadening the offer.
Further evidence shows that visitors are now travelling from out of the district.
Coun Darren Clifford, cabinet member with responsibility for sport and leisure, said: “From the outset it was evident that Salt Ayre had to change its offer to increase the number of customers and income and reduce the operating cost to the council and secure its future.
“This was a large and complex project and the team have delivered a redevelopment that has exceeded all expectations.
“This award celebrates that work and everyone involved should be proud of what they have helped the council to deliver – a hub for fitness and leisure.”

ABUJA May 3 Nigeria's central bank has suspended several lenders from its weekly spot and forward interventions because they had made it difficult for small firms to access foreign exchange, it said.
Last month the central bank cut the amount of paperwork small firms require to buy dollars, to improve the ease of doing business and help narrow the gap between official and black market exchange rates.
It said it will offer them up to $20,000 per quarter.
The lenders were meant to sell dollars bought from the central bank to small firms to enable them import eligible finished and semi-finished goods but they declined, spokesman Isaac Okorafor said in a statement.
Okorafor said the regulator took action based on field reports which showed that only eight lenders sold foreign exchange to small firms since the start of the window in April. Nigeria has 22 commercial lenders.
Nigeria runs a system of multiple exchange rates and has created different exchange rates for various customer categories. Okorafor said the bank has used the convoluted system to eliminate "frivolous demand" for foreign currency.
"The action will be lifted immediately any of the affected banks show evidence of significant utilization of the fund allocated to them under the SME window," he said.
The naira was quoted weaker on Wednesday at an investor trading window, at 382.33 per dollar, data from market regulator FMDQ OTC Securities Exchange showed. The official market rate was 305.80 and the black market rate 391.
Okorafor said the bank sold a total of $196.2 million into the currency markets on Tuesday, including $52 million to small firms and $44.2 million to individuals with certain foreign expenses such as school fees and medical bills. (Reporting by Camillus Eboh; Writing by Chijioke Ohuocha)
rewrite:
On May 3, in Abuja, the Central Bank of Nigeria announced the suspension of several commercial banks from its weekly spot and forward foreign exchange interventions. This disciplinary measure was enacted due to findings that these institutions had impeded small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) from accessing foreign currency. The action follows a recent regulatory amendment intended to streamline documentation requirements for SMEs purchasing dollars, a policy designed to enhance business facilitation and reduce the disparity between official and parallel market exchange rates. Under this framework, SMEs are eligible to access up to $20,000 per quarter.

According to a statement issued by spokesman Isaac Okorafor, the suspended banks had failed to fulfill their obligation to sell dollars, procured from the central bank, to small businesses for the importation of approved finished and semi-finished goods. The regulator’s decision was informed by field reports indicating that, since the dedicated SME foreign exchange window commenced in April, only eight of Nigeria’s twenty-two commercial lenders had effectively sold foreign exchange to this sector. Nigeria maintains a system of multiple exchange rates, establishing different rates for distinct customer segments. Okorafor noted that this complex structure is utilized to curtail non-essential foreign currency demand.

He further stated that the suspension would be rescinded for any affected bank upon demonstration of significant utilization of the funds allocated to it through the SME window. Concurrently, foreign exchange data revealed a depreciation of the naira within the investor trading window, quoted at 382.33 per dollar on Wednesday, as reported by the FMDQ OTC Securities Exchange. This contrasted with the official rate of 305.80 and a parallel market rate of 391. In previous market interventions, the central bank sold a total of $196.2 million on Tuesday, comprising $52 million to small firms and $44.2 million to individuals for eligible external obligations, including educational and medical expenses.

OTTAWA — A group representing survivors of the so-called '60s Scoop says the federal government's proposed $800-million settlement does not go far enough.
The government failed to adequately consult those who experienced forced adoptions before it announced the compensation package in October, said Duane Morrisseau-Beck of the National Indigenous Survivors of Child Welfare Network.
Thousands of Indigenous children were taken from their homes by child-welfare agents and placed with non-Indigenous families starting in the 1960s, a practice that stripped them of their culture, language and traditions.
Morrisseau, who is a survivor, said the network will campaign against the proposed settlement and plans to hold rallies in cities across the country on March 16 to demand fair and inclusive compensation.
"We deserve to be heard," he said Friday. "We feel that this agreement is unfair, unreasonable and not in the best interest of '60s Scoop survivors."
The network also took issue with the settlement's exclusion of Métis survivors and those without legal Indian status or who are unable to prove it.
Sabrina Williams, a spokesperson for Carolyn Bennett, minister of Crown-Indigenous relations, described the settlement as a first step and said the government is committed to addressing the harm suffered by others involved in the '60s Scoop, including Métis and non-status people.
"The Sixties Scoop is a dark and painful chapter in Canada's history," she said in an email.
"The government is interested in working with all parties — provinces, territories, Métis leadership, plaintiffs and their counsel — to work towards resolving the litigation outside of the courts."
Survivor Lesley Parlane said it is irresponsible and dismissive of the government not to take an accurate survey of how many people were affected by the '60s Scoop.
rewrite:
In Ottawa, an organization representing survivors of the '60s Scoop has declared the federal government’s proposed $800-million compensation settlement insufficient. According to Duane Morrisseau-Beck of the National Indigenous Survivors of Child Welfare Network, the government did not conduct adequate consultations with those subjected to forced adoptions prior to announcing the compensation package in October. The '60s Scoop refers to the widespread removal of thousands of Indigenous children from their families by child-welfare authorities beginning in the 1960s, leading to their placement predominantly in non-Indigenous households. This practice systematically severed these children from their cultural heritage, languages, and traditional communities.

Morrisseau-Beck, a survivor himself, stated that the network intends to oppose the proposed settlement and is organizing nationwide rallies scheduled for March 16 to advocate for a more equitable and inclusive compensation framework. He emphasized on Friday, “We deserve to be heard,” adding that the current agreement is perceived as “unfair, unreasonable and not in the best interest of '60s Scoop survivors.” Further criticism concerns the settlement’s exclusion of Métis survivors and those lacking legal Indian status or unable to document it.

Responding to these concerns, Sabrina Williams, a spokesperson for Crown-Indigenous Relations Minister Carolyn Bennett, characterized the settlement as an initial step. She affirmed the government’s commitment to addressing harms experienced by all affected by the '60s Scoop, including Métis and non-status individuals. In an emailed statement, Williams described the Sixties Scoop as “a dark and painful chapter in Canada’s history” and expressed the government’s interest in collaborating with all relevant parties—provinces, territories, Métis leadership, plaintiffs, and legal counsel—to seek resolutions outside judicial proceedings.

Survivor Lesley Parlane additionally criticized the government for what she termed an irresponsible and dismissive approach, noting the absence of a comprehensive survey to accurately determine the number of individuals impacted by the '60s Scoop.

Ponoka RCMP are looking for this man alleged to have taken some items from Main Street Hardware in Ponoka without paying. When asked, the man told the clerk he was ‘borrowing’ the items. RCMP photo
Ponoka RCMP are looking for a man claiming he was ‘borrowing’ items from Main Street Hardware.
Police were called to the hardware store March 17 after the man allegedly left the store with several items without paying. It appears that the suspect left the store with a hammer and scraper. When asked by the clerk to pay for them he said he was borrowing the items.
“The store manager explained that the items had to be paid for before leaving but the male left with the merchandise,” say police.
Investigators say they are looking for a Caucasian man in his 30s. At the time he was wearing a black hoodie.
Ponoka man arrested for impaired driving
Police charged a 56-year-old Ponoka man with impaired driving last week.
At about 10 a.m. on March 16 witnesses called the police of an erratic driver heading westbound into Ponoka on Highway 53.
Police say two witnesses reported a white Dodge Ram driving erratically into oncoming traffic. Police say he travelled at a high rate of speed through the Mecca Glen school zone and almost hit the ditch.
“RCMP located the vehicle at the intersection of Highway 2A and Highway 53 and proceeded to observe the occupant’s driving pattern,” states a Ponoka RCMP release.
He was arrested and charged with impaired driving. A court date is yet to be set.
-Heyden-Kaye
If you have information, please call the Ponoka RCMP at 403-783-4472. If you want to remain anonymous, you can contact Crime Stoppers by phone at 1-800-222-8477 (TIPS), or by internet at www.tipsubmit.com. rewrite:

When confronted by a store clerk, the individual asserted that he was merely "borrowing" the items. Investigators describe the individual as a Caucasian male, approximately in his thirties, who was attired in a black hooded sweatshirt at the time of the incident.

HALIFAX — A Nova Scotia swim team is taking a creative approach to its training.
The Dartmouth Crusaders lost their home pool for more than an entire season while it undergoes renovations, so the head coach looked into a site suggested by some parents.
That lead the team to the Marine Aviation Survival Training Facility — a state-of-the-art multimillion-dollar facility that specializes in simulated at sea and underwater training scenarios.
Dan Latremouille, training and operations Manager for the facility, told Global News that it normally provides safety and survival training for offshore, marine, industrial and military aviation segments.
It had never before been used by a swim club for practice, solely operating as a training ground for rescue and survival.
But it has its challenges, as a current pulls swimmers to one side, a lack of painted lines on the floor makes staying in their "lanes" tricky and water temperatures are 10 to 15 degrees cooler than a normal pool. (Global News)
The Canadian Press
rewrite: In Halifax, a Nova Scotian swim team has adopted an innovative training solution due to the extended closure of its home pool for renovations. The Dartmouth Crusaders, upon parental suggestion, relocated to the Marine Aviation Survival Training Facility—a multimillion-dollar center designed for simulated maritime and underwater survival exercises. According to Dan Latremouille, the facility’s training and operations manager, it typically serves offshore, marine, industrial, and military aviation personnel with safety and survival training. Historically, it had not accommodated swim clubs, being dedicated solely to rescue and survival preparation. However, the facility presents distinct challenges for swimming practice: a persistent current displaces swimmers, the absence of lane markings complicates navigation, and water temperatures remain 10 to 15 degrees cooler than those of a conventional pool. (Source: Global News, The Canadian Press)

“Oi! Get your beak out of my lunch!”
“Well, give us a go of your fork then. Although, between you and me, I’d prefer a bite of a Big Mac any day.”
The expression “bird brain” doesn’t look so clever any more, now that we know exactly how smart our feathered friends – especially those of the crow family – can be.
This rook certainly knew which side its bread was buttered when it helped itself to a generous mouthful of the picnic lunch belonging to the baby, who is named in the caption as 21-month-old Karl Daly from Enniskerry, Co Wicklow.
The photo was taken at Dublin Zoo – where, if feathers are to be ruffled, they might reasonably be expected to come in a more exotic set of colours. There’s no denying that, with those baggy-trousered leg feathers and that honking great bill, rooks aren’t exactly the cutest corvids on the block.
They are, however, famously gabby birds. Anyone who has spent any time near a rookery will have experienced their lengthy busybody conversations as they caw and call back and forth from the tops of tall trees in an apparently endless avian soap opera.
This image turns the tables by having the bolshie baby talk back. Young Karl is fearlessly making eye contact with a wild creature that is almost as big as he is. Beak extended, he may be giving the rook a stern telling off. Or is he waiting – baby bird-style – for his new chum to share?
For the sake of retrospective health and safety, we can only hope not.
But the best thing about our picture is that it celebrates the joy of the unexpected encounter. We go to the zoo to see an Abyssinian hornbill, only to find ourselves up close and personal with an ordinary, everyday rook. It just goes to show that, as the celebrated biologist EO Wilson wrote, when you’ve seen one ant, one bird, one tree, you have not seen them all.
You can buy this and other Irish Times images from irishtimes.com/photosales. A book, The Times We Lived In, with more than 100 photographs and commentary by Arminta Wallace, published by Irish Times Books (€19.99), is available from irishtimes.com/irishtimesbooks and from bookshops
rewrite:
The exclamation, "Remove your beak from my meal!" is met with a retort suggesting the provision of cutlery would suffice, though a preference for fast food is humorously implied. This exchange underscores a shifting perception of avian intelligence, particularly among corvids, challenging the derogatory term "bird brain." The depicted rook demonstrates discernment in selecting a portion of a picnic lunch belonging to a child identified as 21-month-old Karl Daly from Enniskerry, County Wicklow.

Photographed at Dublin Zoo, a setting typically associated with more vividly colored species, the rook’s somewhat disheveled plumage and prominent beak may not align with conventional aesthetics. Nevertheless, these birds are recognized for their vocal communicative complexity. Observations near rookeries reveal protracted auditory exchanges among individuals, resembling a continuous narrative broadcast from the treetops.

This image subverts expectation by presenting the infant as an active participant. Karl engages in direct visual contact with a wild bird of comparable size. With his mouth agape, he may be issuing a reprimand or, perhaps, anticipating a reciprocal offering in the manner of a nestling. From a contemporary health and safety perspective, the latter scenario is not advisable.

The photograph’s principal merit lies in its commemoration of a spontaneous interspecies interaction. A visit intended for observing exotic specimens culminates in an intimate encounter with a common native bird. This serves as an apt illustration of the principle articulated by biologist E.O. Wilson: observing a single organism within a taxonomic group does not convey an understanding of the collective. Each instance holds unique value.

This photograph is available for purchase, along with other images, via irishtimes.com/photosales. Additionally, the publication *The Times We Lived In*, featuring over one hundred photographs with commentary by Arminta Wallace and published by Irish Times Books (€19.99), can be acquired through irishtimes.com/irishtimesbooks and various bookshops.

TOKYO, March 30 Japanese government bond prices were weaker on Thursday as the longer-dated maturities came under profit taking following large gains, but the market came off lows after an auction of two-year debt attracted sufficient investor demand.
June 10-year JGB futures were down 0.05 point at 150.40 after stooping to 150.33 earlier in the session.
The two-year yield was 2 basis points higher at minus 0.235 percent after rising to as high as minus 0.230 percent.
The bid-to-cover ratio, a gauge of demand, at Thursday's 2.2 trillion yen ($19.78 billion) two-year auction remained at a relatively high 3.82, compared with the previous sale's ratio of 3.92.
Concerns about the Bank of Japan trimming the amount of shorter-dated JGBs it buys at its regular market operations were offset by the lower auction amount, traders said.
Starting this month, the finance ministry has opted to reduce two-year auction amounts by 100 billion yen.
The 30-year yield rose 1.5 basis points to 0.835 percent as investors sold into the previous day's bullish move, when super long yields fell on month-end demand stemming from index-following participants. ($1 = 111.2500 yen) (Reporting by the Tokyo markets team; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)
rewrite: Japanese government bond (JGB) prices experienced a decline on Thursday, March 30, primarily driven by profit-taking activity in longer-dated maturities subsequent to significant prior appreciation. The market, however, recovered partially from its intraday lows following a two-year debt auction which demonstrated adequate investor demand. June 10-year JGB futures concluded the session down 0.05 point at 150.40, having earlier declined to 150.33. The two-year yield increased by 2 basis points to -0.235 percent. Demand metrics from the auction of 2.2 trillion yen in two-year notes remained robust, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.82, slightly below the preceding ratio of 3.92. Market participants noted that concerns regarding potential reductions in the Bank of Japan's purchases of shorter-dated bonds were mitigated by the diminished auction size, a deliberate reduction of 100 billion yen instituted this month by the finance ministry. Concurrently, the 30-year yield rose 1.5 basis points to 0.835 percent as investors sold following a bullish movement the previous day, which had been fueled by month-end demand from index-following participants.

The Jonathan Hunt Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution held a tea at Parkwood Assisted Living in Elkin recently to honor the good citizens selected from seniors in eight high schools located in the chapter district.
The purpose of the Good Citizens scholarship program is to encourage and reward qualities of good citizenship, including dependability, service, scholarship and patriotism.
The students submitted an application plus an essay on the topic of “Our American Heritage and Our Responsibility for Preserving it.” The focus question posed to each student was “How has America advanced the cause of freedom in the rest of the world?”
Five of the eight Good Citizens attended the tea with family members. After they read their essay, each received a wallet card and lapel pin in recognition of the program purpose. The overall winner received a monetary award and all will receive a certificate of achievement at their Spring Awards Day.
rewrite: The Jonathan Hunt Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution recently convened a formal tea at Parkwood Assisted Living in Elkin. This event honored senior students from eight high schools within the chapter’s district who were selected as Good Citizens. The scholarship program aims to recognize and promote the essential civic qualities of dependability, service, leadership, and patriotism. Each honoree submitted a formal application and an essay addressing the theme, “Our American Heritage and Our Responsibility for Preserving It,” specifically responding to the prompt: “How has America advanced the cause of freedom in the rest of the world?” Five of the eight awardees attended the ceremony with family. Following a reading of their essays, each student was presented with a commemorative wallet card and lapel pin. The overall scholarship recipient was granted a monetary award, and all honorees will receive formal certificates of achievement during their respective schools’ Spring Awards Day.

Lifestyle differences are to blame for regional variation in obesity rates in Scotland, research has found.
Genetic factors cannot completely explain why obesity is more common in some areas and not others, scientists say.
Public health initiatives that focus on postcodes in deprived areas could help to close this gap and tackle health inequalities between regions, researchers say.
Rates of obesity vary between different regions of countries. Until now, the relative impact of genetics and lifestyle on this variability was unclear.
Scientists led by the University of Edinburgh examined health information from 11,000 people from across Scotland, to determine whether genetic factors or lifestyle differences were the cause of regional differences in obesity rates.
They looked at health traits related to obesity, including weight and body mass index (BMI), from people living in different regions.
These figures were analysed together with genetic information from DNA tests and records of lifestyle and socio-economic factors.
When the team compared data between geographical regions, they found that lifestyle factors such as smoking, alcohol, diet and other measures of deprivation, had the biggest impact on differences in obesity rates.
There are major health inequalities between regions in Scotland. People living in the most deprived areas can expect to live up to seven years less than those living in the most affluent regions.
Researchers say helping people to change their diet, activity levels and behaviour could reduce differences in obesity rates, and so help narrow the health divide between regions.
The research published in the journal Nature Communications, was funded by the Medical Research Council. Participants for the study were drawn from Generation Scotland, a research resource with health data available from more than 20,000 volunteers.
Lead researcher Professor Chris Haley, of the MRC Human Genetics Unit at the University of Edinburgh, said: "Our findings reveal that the factors that have the greatest impact on regional obesity rates can be modified. This is good news because it means we can do something about the problem and potentially narrow the health gap between areas that are least and worst affected.
"Our research supports the conclusion that if we are to understand and then reduce the causes of health inequalities, we need to take into account both genetic and lifestyle differences between individuals."
###
rewrite:
Regional disparities in obesity prevalence across Scotland are primarily attributable to variations in lifestyle, according to recent research. Scientific analysis indicates that genetic factors alone cannot fully account for the geographical heterogeneity observed in obesity rates. The study suggests that public health interventions specifically targeting deprived postcode areas could mitigate this disparity and address broader health inequalities between regions.

Obesity rates exhibit considerable variation across different geographical areas within nations. The relative contributions of genetic predisposition and lifestyle to this spatial variability had previously been ambiguous. To investigate this, researchers from the University of Edinburgh analysed health data from approximately 11,000 individuals across Scotland. The aim was to ascertain whether regional differences in obesity were driven more by genetic or lifestyle factors. The team examined obesity-related health metrics, including body weight and body mass index (BMI), from participants residing in diverse regions. These data were integrated with genetic information derived from DNA analyses, alongside records detailing lifestyle choices and socio-economic indicators.

Upon comparing data across geographical regions, the researchers determined that lifestyle factors—including smoking, alcohol consumption, dietary patterns, and other indices of socio-economic deprivation—exerted the most substantial influence on the observed differences in obesity prevalence. Significant health inequalities persist between Scottish regions; for instance, individuals in the most deprived areas have a life expectancy up to seven years shorter than those in the most affluent areas. The researchers posit that initiatives designed to modify diet, physical activity, and related behaviours could reduce disparities in obesity rates, thereby helping to narrow the health divide between regions.

This research, funded by the Medical Research Council and published in the journal *Nature Communications*, utilised participants from Generation Scotland, a research resource containing health data from over 20,000 volunteers. Professor Chris Haley, lead researcher from the MRC Human Genetics Unit at the University of Edinburgh, stated: "Our findings demonstrate that the factors most strongly influencing regional obesity rates are modifiable. This is encouraging, as it implies actionable avenues to address the issue and potentially reduce the health gap between the least and most affected areas. The study substantiates the conclusion that a comprehensive understanding and reduction of health inequalities necessitate the consideration of both genetic and lifestyle differences among individuals."

Honda’s exciting mini-bike, the Navi is now available in two more avatars: Chrome and Adventure
Less than a year after the Navi was launched, it still delivers on excitement and quirkiness for those bold enough to buy it. This new year, Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India (HMSI) have decided that the Navi is due for a couple of aesthetic upgrades.
The Navi is now available in two major variants, the Chrome and the Adventure. While the style of the scooter remains intact, you can see that it has a distinct personality in both the avatars. The Adventure edition is for those of you who are willing to rough it out. It comes laden with a knuckle-guard set, bash-plate, headlight protector, adventure visor, custom dual-tone seat cover, luggage box and adventure stripes.
The Chrome variant is slightly short of goodies but makes up for it with liberal splashes of chrome on the black paint that is standard for both variants. It has a headlight protector, side lower cover, rear grip, bash-plate and luggage box. Although some of the features mentioned here are not visible in the picture, Honda have claimed that it comes as standard on the vehicle.
Both the variants are out in the market. You can book the Adventure edition or the Chrome edition on the Navi app (available on Google Play); they are priced at Rs 49,720 and Rs 46,260 (ex-showroom, Pune) respectively.
Related Posts via Categories
rewrite:
Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India (HMSI) has introduced two new aesthetic variants of the Navi model: the Chrome and the Adventure editions. These releases occur less than a year following the Navi's initial launch, with the vehicle continuing to offer its distinctive blend of excitement and unconventional design. The core styling of the scooter remains consistent, yet each variant projects a unique character.

The Adventure edition is tailored for enthusiasts seeking a rugged aesthetic. It is equipped with several functional and stylistic accessories, including a knuckle-guard set, a bash-plate, a headlight protector, an adventure visor, a custom dual-tone seat cover, a luggage box, and distinctive adventure stripes. In contrast, the Chrome variant features extensive chrome accents applied to the standard black paint scheme, which is common to both editions. Its accessories comprise a headlight protector, side lower cover, rear grip, bash-plate, and luggage box. Honda confirms that the listed features are standard for each variant, although some may not be immediately visible in promotional imagery.

Both variants are currently available for purchase. Prospective buyers can place orders via the official Navi application, accessible on Google Play. The ex-showroom price in Pune is set at ₹49,720 for the Adventure edition and ₹46,260 for the Chrome edition.

Club record signing Jota scored the first two goals of his Birmingham City career to lift Blues further away from trouble.
The £6m man grabbed a lucky long ranger in the 21st minute, then tapped in for another just before half time.
By then Blues had taken control through an early David Davis poacher’s effort.
Manager Steve Cotterill was forced into making one change, with Jota coming in for the injured Jacques Maghoma.
And however unsettled Blues felt by that, it didn’t show as the hosts gave them a huge helping hand.
There seemed no danger when Maxime Colin’s eighth minute cross looked to be rolling through to Joe Wildsmith until Frederico Venancio chested the ball back to his own goal.
That allowed Davis to nip in on the blindside and poke into the unguarded net for his second in as many games.
Wildsmith was at fault for the second after Sam Gallagher won the ball back high up the pitch and fed Jota.
The former Brentford man fired a weak shot from 27-28 yards which was straight at Wildsmith.
But it confounded the goalkeeper who let it slip through his grasp and into the net.
Worryingly Blues had Jonathan Grounds carried off soon after, but Wednesday were reduced to ten men after that when Marco Matias appeared to dip his head at Cohen Bramall.
Blues hammered home their dominance in the fifth minute of first half added time when Wildsmith palmed Davis’ cross-shot into Jota’s path.
But the Owls ensured it wasn’t too comfortable a second half as Lucas Joao hammered in after 54 minutes.
However, any hopes of mounting a sensational comeback were ended in the 72nd minute when the home team was reduced to nine after Daniel Pudil was booked for a second time for taking out Colin.
rewrite:
Birmingham City's record signing, Jota, marked a significant contribution to the club's efforts to distance itself from relegation concerns by scoring his first two goals for the team. The £6 million acquisition fortuitously struck from long range in the 21st minute before adding a close-range finish just prior to halftime. By that juncture, Birmingham had already established control through an early opportunistic goal from David Davis. Manager Steve Cotterill was compelled to make one alteration to the starting lineup, with Jota replacing the injured Jacques Maghoma. Any potential disruption from this change was not evident, as the home side, Sheffield Wednesday, provided considerable assistance.

There appeared minimal threat in the eighth minute when Maxime Colin’s cross seemed destined to reach goalkeeper Joe Wildsmith, until defender Frederico Venancio inadvertently chested the ball back toward his own goal. This error allowed Davis to exploit the defensive lapse, stealing in to prod the ball into the unguarded net for his second goal in consecutive matches. Wildsmith was culpable for the second goal, which originated from Sam Gallagher regaining possession high on the pitch and supplying Jota. The former Brentford player delivered a tame shot from approximately 27 yards directly at Wildsmith, yet the goalkeeper misjudged it, allowing the ball to slip through his grasp and into the net.

A concerning incident for Birmingham saw Jonathan Grounds stretchered off shortly thereafter, but Wednesday were subsequently reduced to ten men when Marco Matias appeared to lower his head toward Cohen Bramall. Birmingham emphatically reinforced their dominance in the fifth minute of first-half stoppage time when Wildsmith could only parry Davis’s cross-shot directly into the path of Jota for a simple finish. The Owls ensured the second period was not entirely comfortable, with Lucas João firing in a powerful strike after 54 minutes. However, any prospects of a dramatic comeback were effectively extinguished in the 72nd minute when the home team was further reduced to nine men following Daniel Pudil’s second bookable offense for fouling Colin.

CAMDEN, Ark. (KARK/NBC News) – A young Arkansas mother’s final moments were streamed on Facebook Live as friends watch helplessly from afar.
25-year-old Keiana Herndon went live Wednesday from a friend’s home, where she was staying with her young son.
The video starts out with Keiana singing. You see and hear her respond to viewers and even put the spotlight on her son.
A few minutes later, Keiana falls and the phone drops out of her hands.
Her uncle, Jeffrey Herndon, said he could hear his niece struggle to breath and her son scream in the background.
“It was real hard,” he said.
All the while, the number of eyes on her grew.
A friend showed up nearly 30 minutes after Keiana hit the floor.
Keiana’s father wishes someone watching would have acted sooner.
“It’s amazing for someone to sit there and see somebody or hear them take their last breath and nobody did anything,” said Richard. “So, I want to take my hat off to everybody that actual did something.”
rewrite: On Wednesday, 25-year-old Keiana Herndon of Arkansas initiated a Facebook Live broadcast from a friend's residence, where she was temporarily staying with her young son. The stream initially depicted Ms. Herndon singing and interacting with viewers, including moments featuring her child. Shortly thereafter, the transmission captured her collapsing, with the device falling from her grasp. According to her uncle, Jeffrey Herndon, audible signs of respiratory distress from Ms. Herndon and her son's screams were discernible in the background. Concurrently, the viewership count escalated. A friend arrived at the scene approximately thirty minutes after the fall. Ms. Herndon's father, Richard, expressed profound dismay that no observer intervened more promptly, stating it was "amazing" that individuals witnessed or heard her final moments without acting. He extended gratitude to those who ultimately responded.

input: Ten minutes, 74 hotdogs and an estimated 22,200 calories later, Joey "Jaws" Chestnut is once again the undisputed chow champion. Today marked Chestnut's 11th win at the annual Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest in Coney Island."Seventy-four hot dogs -- I've earned it," he said after the event in an interview with ESPN. Chestnut marked a new world record set using his signature style of stuffing two frankfurters down his throat at a time. "This was a beautiful day. I love to eat and I tried to enjoy the food."For yet another year, the favorites in both the men's and women's categories -- Chestnut, 34, and Miki Sudo, 33, -- strutted off the stage after braving the broiling heat to brandish mustard title belts and oversized checks, proving they reign supreme when it comes to speed-eating encased meat.Chestnut, the current hotdog-eating world record holder from Vallejo, California , downed a whopping 74 weiners, dipping the buns in super-sized plastic cups of water during the 10-minute-long contest. Judges peered below and Nathan's helpers stood by with paper plates loaded with more hotdogs.Chestnut said he had "a vision" for this year's win, and seemed to be unfatigued after "10 minutes of work.""I'm going to keep riding the wave," he said of his carer on the competitive eating circuit.New Jersey native Carmen Cincotti finished second by eating 64 hot dogs. Third place finisher Darron Breedon got 43 frankfurters down.The Fourth of July event, considered by some to be the Super Bowl of competitive eating, also featured 74-year-old Rich "The Locust" LeFevre -- the oldest competitor in the contest's 101-year history.In the women's competition, Sudo, a native New Yorker by way of Japan and Hawaii, accomplished her goal to "5-pete" the competition by gobbling 37 hot dogs and water-dipped buns in 10 minutes."I had a comfortable lead, and I left room to eat more for next year," Sudo told ESPN while hoisting her pink title belt.Sudo's dad was in the crowd to watch her win. While her grand total was four fewer than her tally last year, it was nine more than the closest challenger, Michelle Lesco.Third place finisher Juliet Lee came in with just 25.
rewrite:
In a display of remarkable gastronomic endurance, Joey “Jaws” Chestnut secured his eleventh title at the annual Nathan’s Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest on Coney Island. Over the course of ten minutes, Chestnut consumed seventy-four hot dogs, thereby establishing a new world record and ingesting an estimated 22,200 calories. “Seventy-four hot dogs—I have earned it,” Chestnut stated in a post-event interview with ESPN, attributing his success in part to his signature method of consuming two frankfurters simultaneously. He further reflected, “This was a beautiful day. I love to eat and I tried to enjoy the food.”

The event, often characterized as the premier spectacle in competitive eating, once again concluded with victories for the favored contestants in both the men’s and women’s divisions. Chestnut, a thirty-four-year-old from Vallejo, California and the current world record holder, and Miki Sudo, thirty-three, each departed the stage bearing mustard-colored championship belts and oversized ceremonial checks, having prevailed despite the intense summer heat. Chestnut’s technique involved dipping the buns in water to facilitate consumption, while official judges observed closely and event staff ensured a continuous supply of prepared hot dogs. Remarking on his performance, Chestnut noted he had possessed “a vision” for this victory and expressed no fatigue following what he termed “ten minutes of work,” adding his intention to “keep riding the wave” of his professional eating career.

In the men’s competition, Carmen Cincotti of New Jersey finished second with sixty-four hot dogs, followed by Darron Breedon in third place with forty-three. The historic Fourth of July contest, now in its 101st year, also featured seventy-four-year-old Rich “The Locust” LeFevre, the oldest participant in the event’s history.

The women’s division was decisively won by Miki Sudo, a native New Yorker with familial roots in Japan and Hawaii. By consuming thirty-seven hot dogs and buns within the allotted time, Sudo achieved her stated goal of a fifth consecutive victory, or “five-peat.” Although her total was four fewer than the previous year, it exceeded that of her nearest rival, Michelle Lesco, by nine hot dogs. “I had a comfortable lead, and I left room to eat more for next year,” Sudo commented to ESPN while displaying her pink championship belt, an achievement witnessed by her father in the audience. Third place was claimed by Juliet Lee with a total of twenty-five hot dogs.

Dubai: Initial data on Abu Dhabi hotels released by STR on Monday highlighted that increases in supply had outstripped demand by 1.5 per cent, whilst room occupancy was down -1.4 per cent to 74.2 per cent.
The findings from STR, a data analytics service headquartered in London, England, are based on daily data from January, presenting year over year comparisons on rates and occupancy.
The preliminary data indicates sharp rate declines, including a drop of -10 per cent in the city’s average daily rate (ADR) to Dh 465.80.
In addition to the fall in ADR, the revenue per available room (RevPAR) slipped by -11.2 per cent to Dh 345.68.
STR analysts note in the statement that Abu Dhabi’s ADR levels were once again pressured by supply growth in the market. However, the market’s hotels did record a significant uptick in RevPAR (+23.6%) on the last day of the month, mainly due to the Global Space Congress (January 31-February 1).
The situation is largely the same in Dubai, with a number of new hotels in 2016 coupled with slower demand pushing hotels’ profits down 6.8 per cent year-on-year.
In the first half of last year, the profit per room of hotels in Dubai suffered under the pressure of this additional supply, falling by 13.2 per cent. This was primarily due to a declining RevPAR, which dropped by 11.3 per cent.
rewrite:
Preliminary data for Abu Dhabi's hotel sector, released on Monday by STR, indicates that supply growth has exceeded demand by 1.5 percent. Concurrently, room occupancy declined by 1.4 percent to 74.2 percent. These findings, derived from the London-based analytics firm's daily January data, provide year-over-year comparisons for occupancy and rate performance. The initial figures reveal pronounced declines in key metrics. The Average Daily Rate (ADR) fell by 10 percent to 465.80 UAE Dirhams. Furthermore, Revenue Per Available Room (RevPAR) experienced a more substantial decrease of 11.2 percent, settling at 345.68 Dirhams.

Analysts at STR attribute the continued pressure on Abu Dhabi's ADR to ongoing supply expansion within the market. Nevertheless, a notable exception was recorded on the final day of January, when RevPAR surged by 23.6 percent, largely attributable to the Global Space Congress held from January 31 to February 1. A similar dynamic is evident in Dubai, where the introduction of numerous new hotel properties during 2016, combined with moderated demand growth, contributed to a 6.8 percent year-on-year decline in overall hotel profits. This trend was particularly acute in the first half of the year, during which profit per room decreased by 13.2 percent, driven principally by an 11.3 percent contraction in RevPAR.

As speculation mounts over the Prime Minister's future, here is a look at how Theresa May could be replaced.
According to Conservative Party rules, a leadership contest can be triggered in two ways, with the most obvious being if Mrs May resigns.
If the PM is determined to stay, a leadership election can be triggered if 15% of Tory MPs write to Graham Brady, the chairman of the 1922 Committee - made up of backbench Conservative MPs - saying they no longer have confidence in the leader.
Some 48 MPs would be needed to oust Mrs May with the party's current crop of 318 MPs, including the speaker and deputy speaker.
Once that threshold is crossed, Mr Brady would announce the start of the leadership contest and invite nominations, with candidates needing the support of at least two MPs to get on to the ballot paper.
If there is only one candidate, they will be automatically declared leader.
But if multiple MPs are successfully nominated, Tory MPs then vote, with the candidate achieving the lowest number of votes forced out of the race, until only two candidates remain.
Conservative Party members then vote for their preferred candidate on a "one member, one vote" basis, with the winner becoming the new leader.
When David Cameron resigned following the EU referendum, five Tory MPs stood for the leadership.
Mrs May and Andrea Leadsom were due to go to the ballot of the Conservative Party membership.
But Mrs May was formally confirmed as the new leader after Mrs Leadsom pulled out of the race.
In 2005, Conservative Party members chose Mr Cameron over David Davis, while in 2003 Iain Duncan Smith was ousted as leader after the chairman of the 1922 Committee received 25 letters from Tory MPs.
Michael Howard was then elected leader as the only nominated MP to replace him.
rewrite:
Amidst increasing speculation regarding the tenure of the Prime Minister, the mechanisms by which Theresa May could be replaced warrant examination. Under the regulations of the Conservative Party, a leadership contest may be initiated through two principal avenues. The most direct method would be the resignation of the incumbent Prime Minister. Should the Prime Minister opt to remain in office, however, a contest can be instigated if fifteen percent of Conservative Members of Parliament submit letters to Sir Graham Brady, the Chairman of the 1922 Committee—a body comprising backbench Conservative MPs—expressing a loss of confidence in the leader.

Given the current parliamentary party composition of 318 MPs, inclusive of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, this threshold equates to letters from 48 parliamentarians. Upon receipt of the requisite number of letters, Sir Graham Brady would publicly announce the commencement of a leadership contest and invite nominations. Prospective candidates must secure the support of a minimum of two fellow MPs to be placed on the ballot. Should only one candidate be nominated, that individual would be declared leader without further process.

If multiple candidates are successfully nominated, Conservative MPs participate in a series of eliminative ballots. In each round, the candidate receiving the fewest votes is removed from contention until only two candidates remain. The final selection is then determined by a ballot of the broader Conservative Party membership, conducted on a one member, one vote basis, with the victor assuming the leadership.

Historical precedents illustrate this process. Following the resignation of David Cameron after the European Union referendum, five Conservative MPs stood for the leadership. Theresa May and Andrea Leadsom emerged as the final two candidates slated for a membership vote; however, Mrs. May was confirmed as leader after Mrs. Leadsom withdrew from the contest. In 2005, the membership selected David Cameron over David Davis. In 2003, Iain Duncan Smith was removed as leader after the Chairman of the 1922 Committee received twenty-five letters from MPs, leading to the uncontested election of Michael Howard as the sole nominated successor.

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. - Terry Kimball, an Uber passenger in St. Petersburg punched by his driver, has died as a result of his injuries, officials said Saturday, Aug. 12.
St. Petersburg police said no charges have been filed yet and the investigation continues.
Police said at 7:30 p.m. Thursday, Uber driver Kabir O' Farril Diaz, 38, picked up 56-year-old passenger Terry L. Kimball.
They had a dispute over the route the driver was taking. Diaz pulled over at a Quick Pick Foods store in St. Petersburg, where they had a physical altercation.
Authorities said the driver punched Kimball, and he did not regain consciousness.
"I saw this guy laying on the ground. This woman was pressing on his chest trying to bring him back," Carlton Reid said. "He wasn't responsive. It was pretty tough, really I was really scared, I didn't know what was going on with him and I was pretty worried."
Reid said he witnessed the aftermath of the fight.
Kimball went to the hospital with serious brain trauma and life-threatening injuries.
Police said a witness told them Kimball appeared to be the aggressor. A friend of Diaz told Tampa-based WFTS reporter Michael Paluska he has a baby on the way and is not a violent person.
According to Pinellas County court records Kimball's been arrested multiple times for crimes that include DUI, simple battery, resisting arrest, and disorderly intoxication.
"That's very sad," Reid said. "It really is I would like to know what happened now, truly."
Investigators are speaking with witnesses and they say Diaz, who has not been charged at this time, is cooperating.
rewrite:
On Saturday, August 12, officials confirmed the death of Terry L. Kimball, a 56-year-old resident of St. Petersburg, Florida, who succumbed to injuries sustained during a physical altercation with his Uber driver. The St. Petersburg Police Department reported that the incident occurred on the evening of Thursday, August 10. According to authorities, the driver, 38-year-old Kabir O’Farril Diaz, picked up Kimball as a passenger. A dispute subsequently arose concerning the selected route, prompting Diaz to pull the vehicle over at a Quick Pick Foods store. The verbal disagreement escalated into a physical confrontation, during which Diaz allegedly struck Kimball. The passenger lost consciousness and did not regain it.

Kimball was transported to a hospital with severe brain trauma and life-threatening injuries, where he later died. A witness at the scene, Carlton Reid, described observing an unresponsive Kimball on the ground while a woman attempted CPR. Reid expressed distress over the event and a desire for clarity regarding the circumstances. Police indicate that the investigation remains ongoing, with detectives interviewing witnesses. While one witness reportedly stated that Kimball appeared to be the aggressor, no charges have been filed against Diaz at this time, and he is said to be cooperating with the investigation. Public records from Pinellas County indicate a prior criminal history for Kimball, including arrests for offenses such as driving under the influence, simple battery, resisting arrest, and disorderly intoxication. A friend of Diaz, speaking to a local reporter, characterized him as non-violent and noted he is expecting a child.

Mayor Bill de Blasio’s recent assertion that motorists should be exempt from penalties for double-parking in bicycle lanes during passenger drop-offs and pickups raises significant questions regarding its alignment with the Vision Zero initiative, which aims to eliminate traffic fatalities. These disparate events collectively illustrate the complex and often contentious interplay between urban transportation policy, infrastructure design, legal accountability, and public safety.

Tina Turner's firstborn son, Craig Turner, died of apparent suicide Tuesday, the Los Angeles coroner's office confirms to USA TODAY. He was 59.
Police found him dead at 12:38 p.m. of an apparent gunshot wound inside his Studio City, Calif. home, according to Ed Winter, assistant chief of investigations for the Los Angeles.coroner's department.
An autopsy is pending.
Craig worked in real estate and was Tina Turner's firstborn son, whom she had at age 18 with saxophonist Raymond Hill. Craig was adopted by Ike Turner after they wed in 1962.
Turner told Oprah Winfrey in a 2005 interview that Craig was "a very emotional kid" who offered support when she was physically abused by Ike Turner.
Craig was in high school when Turner finally left the abusive relationship with Ike.
"Before you can really help them, you have to strengthen yourself," Turner said.
Tina Turner divorced Ike in 1978. She married German music producer Erwin Bach, her partner of nearly 30 years, in 2013.
Turner and Bach were in Paris Tuesday night attending a party for Giorgio Armani Prive Haute Couture.
USA TODAY has reached out to representatives for Turner.
© 2018 USATODAY.COM

Craig Turner, who worked in real estate, was born when Tina Turner was 18, to saxophonist Raymond Hill. He was later adopted by Ike Turner following his marriage to Tina in 1962. In a 2005 interview with Oprah Winfrey, Tina Turner described Craig as "a very emotional kid" who provided her support during periods of physical abuse by Ike Turner. She stated, "Before you can really help them, you have to strengthen yourself," noting that Craig was in high school when she ultimately left the abusive marriage. Tina Turner divorced Ike in 1978 and married her long-term partner, German music producer Erwin Bach, in 2013. The couple was in Paris attending a fashion event on the evening of Craig’s death. USA TODAY has contacted representatives for Turner for further comment.

Johannesburg - Deputy President David Mabuza arrives in the Kenyan capital Nairobi on Thursday on a working visit and to attend the Madaraka Day (Freedom Day) celebrations, marking the day when Kenya gained independence from Britain in 1963.
South Africa and Kenya enjoy strong bilateral relations, with the two countries’ heads of state meeting on the margins of various international and multilateral engagements to discuss matters of mutual interest. South Africa also undertook a state visit to Kenya in 2016.
Following his re-election in November 2017, President Uhuru Kenyatta undertook a working visit to South Africa at the beginning of this year to attend the ruling African National Congress's annual anniversary celebrations in East London.
The latest engagement forms the basis for the invitation to the deputy president from Kenya's governing Jubilee Party to strengthen party-to-party relations as well as trade and economic relations on the occasion of the Madaraka Day celebrations.
During the working visit, it is envisaged that Kenyatta and Mabuza will discuss issues of mutual concern, including the proposed reform initiatives of the African Union, the ongoing security challenges in South Sudan and Somalia, as well as mutually beneficial economic opportunities between the two countries.
African News Agency/ANA
rewrite:
Deputy President David Mabuza of South Africa commenced a working visit to Nairobi, Kenya, on Thursday. The visit coincides with his attendance at the Madaraka Day celebrations, which commemorate Kenya’s attainment of independence from British rule in 1963. Bilateral relations between South Africa and Kenya are robust, characterized by periodic consultations between their respective heads of state on the sidelines of international and multilateral forums. This diplomatic engagement was further solidified by a South African state visit to Kenya in 2016. Subsequently, following his re-election in November 2017, President Uhuru Kenyatta of Kenya undertook a working visit to South Africa at the start of this year to participate in the African National Congress’s annual anniversary events in East London.

The current invitation, extended by Kenya’s governing Jubilee Party, aims to reinforce party-to-party ties and enhance trade and economic cooperation within the context of the Madaraka Day observances. During the working visit, discussions between Deputy President Mabuza and President Kenyatta are expected to address matters of shared concern. These will likely include proposed reform initiatives within the African Union, ongoing security challenges in South Sudan and Somalia, and the exploration of mutually advantageous economic opportunities for both nations.

Fabrizio Ravanelli Says He Is Interested In Dundee Managerial Job
Fabrizio Ravanelli says he is interested in taking over at Dundee after Paul Hartley’s sacking on Monday.
He told The Sun: “I believe I can keep Dundee in the Premiership and I am very interested in this job. I can save the club from relegation. I could definitely get results and get the best out of the Dundee players.
“I am ready to get a flight to Scotland very quickly. It is an exciting opportunity and I would love to go back. I am looking for a new project in management and this would be the perfect fresh start for me. I would bring energy, enthusiasm and motivation to the club.”
“Dundee are in danger but there are five games to play and I am 100 per cent confident that the team can survive.
“I was only at Dundee for a short period of time but it’s a special club and I love the passion of Scottish football. It is a fantastic country. I have played football in Britain and it would be an honour to manage there too.”
Paul Hartley was dismissed following Dundee’s 2-0 defeat to Hamilton on Saturday, their seventh successive loss, which leaves them 11th in the Scottish Premiership table

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) is set to unveil a plan that would give American workers who want or need jobs guaranteed government jobs that pay at least $15 per hour and have health benefits.
The progressive Vermont senator’s guaranteed jobs plan would entitle any American a job or job training in U.S.-funded projects in infrastructure, the environment, caregiving, and education, but he did not provide a cost-estimate or plan to fund the proposal, the Washington Post reported.
A representative from Sanders’ office said no funding estimate was available for the project because staffers were still crafting the proposal.
Two other potential 2020 presidential candidates—Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Sen. Kristen Gillibrand (D-NY)—have expressed interest in crafting similar proposals.
“The goal is to eliminate working poverty and involuntary unemployment altogether,” said Darrick Hamilton, an economist at The New School who expressed support for a guaranteed jobs program. “This is an opportunity for something transformative, beyond the tinkering we’ve been doing for the last 40 years, where all the productivity gains have gone to the elite of society.”
Critics of the plan have said guaranteed jobs proposals would not be sustainable or affordable, and would cause massive job losses in the private sector.
Studies have shown that states and cities which choose to enact a $15 per hour minimum wage trigger job losses. A December 2017 study found that once California’s minimum wage hike takes effect in 2022, the state would lose 400,000 jobs.
“It completely undercuts a lot of industries and companies,” Brian Riedl, a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute who opposes the program, told the Post. “There will be pressure to introduce a higher wage or certain benefits that the private sector doesn’t offer.”
The proposal is unlikely to gain favor with Republicans in control of Congress, and even most Democrats have slammed similar plans as unrealistic.
“It would be extremely expensive, and I wonder if this is the best, most targeted use of the amount of money it would cost,” said Ernie Tedeschi, an economist who worked for the Treasury during the Obama administration.
The Vermont senator’s proposal comes days after he declared President Trump’s agenda “dead” if the Democratic Party wins the majority in the House or Senate.
rewrite:

This initiative would provide positions paying a minimum of fifteen dollars per hour and include healthcare benefits. According to a report by the Washington Post, the plan, advanced by the progressive senator from Vermont, would entitle any American citizen to either a job or job training through federally funded projects in sectors such as infrastructure, environmental conservation, caregiving, and education. However, the senator has not yet released a cost estimate or detailed a method for financing the proposal. A representative from Senator Sanders’ office indicated that a funding estimate remains unavailable as staff members are still developing the specifics of the plan.

The concept has attracted preliminary interest from other potential presidential candidates for the 2020 election, including Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), who have signaled openness to formulating similar policies. Proponents argue that such a program addresses fundamental economic issues. Darrick Hamilton, an economist at The New School who endorses the guaranteed jobs approach, stated, “The goal is to eliminate working poverty and involuntary unemployment altogether.” He characterized the proposal as “an opportunity for something transformative, beyond the tinkering we’ve been doing for the last 40 years, where all the productivity gains have gone to the elite of society.”

Conversely, critics contend that guaranteed employment programs are neither fiscally sustainable nor economically feasible, warning of potential large-scale job displacement within the private sector. They cite research linking minimum wage increases to employment reductions; for instance, a December 2017 study projected that California could lose approximately 400,000 jobs following the full implementation of a scheduled minimum wage increase in 2022. Brian Riedl, a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute and an opponent of the plan, argued to the Washington Post that such a policy “completely undercuts a lot of industries and companies,” creating pressure to raise wages or offer benefits beyond what the private sector can provide.

The proposal faces significant political hurdles, including likely opposition from the Republican-controlled Congress. Even among Democrats, similar plans have frequently been criticized as impractical. Ernie Tedeschi, an economist who served in the Treasury Department during the Obama administration, questioned the efficiency of the approach, noting, “It would be extremely expensive, and I wonder if this is the best, most targeted use of the amount of money it would cost.” Senator Sanders’ announcement follows closely on his recent declaration that President Trump’s agenda would be “dead” should the Democratic Party regain a majority in either chamber of Congress.

PINK HILL, N.C. (WNCT) — A revival is underway in the small Lenoir County town of Pink Hill.
From home renovations to a complete overhaul of the internet system in town, the community is hard at work.
County leaders are hoping the changes in Pink Hill serve as an inspiration to other small towns in the region.
“Our town died,” said Susan Myers. “Everybody moved out, and I didn’t want that to happen here.”
Susan Myers moved to Pink Hill eight years ago, quickly becoming an active part of the small town. She says she knew something needed to be done to keep her new home from dying, too.
“We started buying up properties in downtown,” said Susan Myers.
Susan and her husband Al Myers now own 35 commercial or residential buildings, and whatever they could work to revive, they did.
“If you go around Pink Hill and see something that doesn’t look good, that’s because I haven’t been able to buy it,” Susan Myers said.
Community leaders like Lenoir County Commissioner J. Mac Daughety took notice of the changes in Pink Hill, and those leaders are using the revival in the town as a template for other small communities in eastern North Carolina.
“The things where citizens come together, groups come together, and they say, ‘Let’s make this a better community,’ that’s where you see a community like Pink Hill start to blossom,” Daughety said.
With the addition of nearly 2,400 pink roses around town, another initiative working to rejuvenate the spirit of the community, Commissioner Daughety hopes others are inspired to take action.
“I’m going to do what I can do,” Daughety said. “I’m going to try to motivate others to help do better things for our community. If I start the engine, then surely other people will get on board.”
Myers says no matter how you are able to get involved, you should do something.
“Some of us have money to invest, others have time to volunteer,” said Myers. “We can help in different ways, but we have to take the leadership, and we can’t depend on government to come help and save us.”
rewrite:
