Local governance figures posit that the transformations occurring in Pink Hill may serve as a replicable model for other small towns within the region confronting similar challenges of stagnation and decline.

The impetus for this revival is significantly attributed to the concerted efforts of private citizens, notably Susan Myers and her husband, Al. Upon relocating to Pink Hill eight years ago, Susan Myers became acutely aware of the necessity for intervention to prevent further deterioration. “Our town had effectively expired,” Myers stated. “Residents were departing, and I was determined to avert that outcome here.” In response, the couple embarked on a strategic acquisition of properties within the downtown district. They now hold ownership of thirty-five commercial and residential buildings, undertaking restoration projects wherever feasible. Myers remarked, “Any structure in Pink Hill that appears dilapidated remains so only because it has not yet been possible to purchase it.”

These observable changes have garnered the attention of county leadership. Lenoir County Commissioner J. Mac Daughety has identified the Pink Hill revival as a potential template, emphasizing the foundational role of civic engagement. “When citizens and community groups coalesce around a shared goal of improvement, that is the precise moment a community like Pink Hill begins to flourish,” Daughety observed. Symbolic and aesthetic enhancements, such as the installation of approximately 2,400 pink rose bushes throughout the town, further contribute to rejuvenating communal spirit.

Commissioner Daughety views his role as catalytic, stating, “My objective is to undertake actionable measures and to motivate others to contribute positively to our community. Initiating momentum encourages broader participation.” This sentiment is echoed by Susan Myers, who underscores the necessity of local agency, irrespective of an individual’s capacity for contribution. “Diverse resources are available; some possess capital to invest, while others can volunteer time,” Myers noted. “Assistance can manifest in various forms, but it is imperative that local leadership is assumed. Reliance on external governmental intervention is not a sustainable strategy for preservation.”

Raekwon Harney scored at the basket in the final minute of the first half to give NC Central a 40-34 lead, but Artem Tavakalyan hit a 3 with :38 left to send Delaware State into intermission trailing by just three, 40-37.

Reginald Gardner Jr. and Pablo Rivas scored 13 and 12 points, respectively, for NC Central (11-10, 5-2) and Jordan Perkins added 10 points, seven boards and six assists.
Jonathan Walker scored 19 points for Delaware State (2-21, 0-8). Tavakalyan added 17 points and Marquis Collins contributed 15.

There are three reasons to watch the Outback Bowl between the Florida Gators and Iowa Hawkeyes at 1 p.m. this afternoon:
You attended one of the schools and university pride is important to you
You hate yourself
You crave a free appetizer from Outback Steakhouse and you’re pulling for it to be coconut shrimp or a bloomin’ onion
In the interest of marketing, branding and bowl season, Outback is again giving away a bloomin’ onion if the SEC team (Florida) wins and an order of coconut shrimp if the B1G team (Iowa) wins. This much like when Ross was offered a free crab cake appetizer when he was “stood up” on a blind date on an episode of Friends.

Hitting the heights: Bank stocks reached milestones Tuesday as their share prices continued to rise. Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase both hit all-time highs, with Goldman recouping all it had lost since the 2007 financial crisis. Bank of America traded in line with its book value for the first time since late 2008; it had traded as low as 15% of book value back in March 2009.
Ambitious move: Japan's SoftBank, which despite its name isn't a bank but a technology and communications conglomerate, made a big step into becoming a serious player in the financial services business Tuesday when it agreed to buy asset manager Fortress Investment Group for $3.3 billion. The acquisition of Fortress, which manages about $70 billion in assets in real estate, credit and private equity, fits Softbank chief Masayoshi Son's "ambitious long-term plans to become one of the world's biggest asset managers, focusing on technology but with a broader platform to raise money and shepherd companies across different sectors," the Wall Street Journal said.

March 19 (UPI) -- Actor Cynthia Nixon on Monday announced her bid to run for governor of New York, challenging incumbent Gov. Andrew M. Cuomo in the state's Democratic primary.
Nixon, known best for her role as Miranda Hobbes in HBO's Sex and the City, shared a video to Twitter declaring her candidacy and calling out leaders in government for "letting us down."
"Something has to change," she said. "We want our government to work again, on healthcare, ending mass incarceration, fixing our broken subway. We are sick of politicians who care more about headlines and power than they do about us. It can't just be business as usual anymore."
The 51-year-old Nixon is described as "a lifelong New Yorker and progressive activist" on her campaign donations page and if elected would be the first female and the first openly gay mayor of New York.
A Sienna College poll released Monday showed 66 percent of state Democrats prefer the incumbent Cuomo over 19 percent who prefer Nixon.
"With an overall 20-19 percent favorability rating -- 26-16 percent among Democrats -- Cynthia Nixon is far from a household name in New York," Siena College pollster Steven Greenberg said.
Cuomo, who has served two terms as governor, said last week he's "not nervous about whoever runs."
"There'll be people who run. That's called elections, and that's fine," he said.
Two former advisors for New York Mayor Bill de Blasio -- Bill Hyers and Rebecca Katz -- joined Nixon's campaign as advisors and her wife, Christine Marinoni, also recently stepped down from her role in his administration.

Nixon, widely recognized for her portrayal of Miranda Hobbes on the television series *Sex and the City*, publicly declared her campaign via a video posted to Twitter. In her announcement, she criticized current government leadership for failing constituents, stating, “Something has to change.” She further articulated a platform focused on healthcare reform, ending mass incarceration, and repairing the New York City subway system, while condemning a political culture she described as prioritizing “headlines and power” over public service.

Nixon’s campaign identifies her as a lifelong New Yorker and progressive activist. If successful, she would become both the first female and first openly gay governor of the state. However, initial electoral prospects appear challenging. A Siena College poll released concurrently with her announcement indicated that 66 percent of registered state Democrats prefer Cuomo, compared to 19 percent for Nixon. Pollster Steven Greenberg noted Nixon’s relative lack of broad political recognition, citing a favorability rating of 20-19 percent statewide.

In response to the challenge, Governor Cuomo, now serving his second term, expressed no apprehension, remarking that electoral competition is expected. Nixon has secured notable campaign advisors, including Bill Hyers and Rebecca Katz, both former aides to New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio. Additionally, her wife, Christine Marinoni, recently resigned from a position within the de Blasio administration.

Why it matters to you Fans of HBO's Insecure will get even more of the Issa Rae series in season 2, which will consist of 10 episodes instead of eight.
If you are still searching for closure after the ending of season 1 of the HBO series Insecure, you will not get it here. But you can get a glimpse into the new season. Insecure co-creator and lead actress Issa Rae released a teaser trailer for season 2 on Twitter on Wednesday.
The teaser trailer will surely agonize die-hard fans still reeling after season one’s emotional finale. At the end of last season, the relationship between Rae’s character, Issa, and her boyfriend, Lawrence, played by Jay Ellis, seemed to be over. In the teaser trailer, the two can be seen on a couch with a pillow in between them that reads “hella confused.”
Initially, season 2 was reported to consist of eight episodes, just like season one. But IMDB has listed acting credits for 10 episodes. Interestingly, Issa’s former love interest, Lawrence, is only credited with appearing in one episode in the new season — and not until episode 4. The first two episodes of the new season are entitled Hella Great and Hella Questions, respectively. With names like that, it may be safe to say we are in for an emotional roller coaster to start the new season.
When you watch the new season, it may not look the same as last season, thanks to all the new faces. Bosch‘s Spencer Garret appears as John Merril in six episodes this season, including the season premiere. Sarunas J. Jackson is another newcomer to the show. He’ll play the role of Alejandro ‘Dro’ Peña in six episodes. Jackson may be best known for his voice-over work on NBA 2K as Frequency Vibrations, the player character in NBA 2K16’s MyCAREER mode.
Insecure may have inspired a lot of relationship tweets last fall, but it was not a ratings hit. Season 1 averaged roughly 413,000 viewers per episode — and only one episode from its first season topped 500,000 viewers. Even without a Silicon Valley audience size, Rae still garnered a Golden Globe nomination for best actress in a comedy series.
Insecure returns to HBO at 10:30 p.m. ET on July 23.

SHANGHAI China's economic planner on Thursday approved China Eastern Airlines' (600115.SS)(0670.HK) 13.2-billion-yuan (1.54 billion pounds) plan for a base at an expansive new airport in Beijing that could eventually be the world's largest, when completed.
The National Development and Reform Commission said in a statement on its website that the base will cover 1.17 million square meters, and 30 percent of the investment, or 3.96 billion yuan, will be funded by China Eastern.
The remaining 92.4 billion yuan will be financed using domestic bank loans, the statement added.
China plans to complete the first phase by 2019, and will be able to serve 45 million passengers a year with four runways on the first opening. Two more phases would push the capacity to an annual count of 100 million passengers.
That would put the airport as the world's largest in surface area, roughly in line with Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, the world's busiest by number of annual passengers.
Upon completion, rival state carrier, China Southern Airlines Co Ltd (600029.SS), will also relocate to the new airport from the existing Beijing Capital International Airport, the airport project managers told reporters last year.
They said China Eastern and China Southern will handle 40 percent of the new airport's footfalls.
(Reporting by Brenda Goh; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips)
rewrite:
On Thursday, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), China's principal economic planning agency, granted approval to China Eastern Airlines (600115.SS, 0670.HK) for a 13.2-billion-yuan (approximately £1.54 billion) operational base at Beijing's expansive new airport. According to a statement published on the NDRC's official website, the base will occupy 1.17 million square meters. China Eastern will provide 3.96 billion yuan, representing thirty percent of the total investment, with the remaining 9.24 billion yuan to be financed through domestic bank loans.

The airport's construction is planned in phases, with the initial stage scheduled for completion by 2019. This first phase, featuring four runways, is projected to accommodate 45 million passengers annually. Subsequent development phases are intended to increase total capacity to 100 million passengers per year. Upon full completion, the airport's surface area will position it as the world's largest, with a passenger volume comparable to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, currently the globe's busiest aviation hub.

As confirmed by airport project managers last year, the state-owned carrier China Southern Airlines (600029.SS) will also relocate its operations from Beijing Capital International Airport to the new facility. Together, China Eastern and China Southern are anticipated to manage forty percent of the new airport's passenger traffic.

rewrite:
On February 2, Sprint Corporation released its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2017. The telecommunications firm reported its highest retail net subscriber additions in nearly three years and concurrently revised its annual financial guidance upward. Specifically, the company raised its fiscal 2017 adjusted free cash flow projection from an approximate break-even point to a range of $500 million to $700 million. Furthermore, Sprint increased its 2017 operating income expectation to between $2.5 billion and $2.7 billion. The company anticipates its 2017 adjusted EBITDA will be near the midpoint of its prior forecast of $10.8 billion to $11.2 billion, while cash capital expenditures, excluding devices leased through indirect channels, are expected to be at the lower end of the $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion range.

For the quarter, Sprint posted total net operating revenues of $8.239 billion, a decrease from $8.549 billion in the prior-year period. Quarterly net income included a favorable non-recurring impact of approximately $7.1 billion related to recent tax reform legislation. Basic earnings per share for the quarter were $1.79, with diluted earnings per share at $1.76. Key operational metrics showed mixed performance: total wireless postpaid churn increased to 1.80 percent from 1.67 percent, while prepaid churn improved significantly to 4.63 percent from 5.74 percent. The company added 256,000 net postpaid wireless subscribers, a decline from 405,000 additions in the same quarter last year. Conversely, it achieved 63,000 net prepaid additions, a notable recovery from a net loss of 460,000 subscribers in the prior-year period. Total wireless connections reached 54.6 million at quarter-end, up from 54.0 million at the end of the previous quarter.

Average revenue per user (ARPU) trends were divergent. Postpaid ARPU declined to $45.13 from $49.70, and postpaid phone ARPU fell to $51.26 from $57.12. In contrast, prepaid ARPU rose to $37.46 from $33.97. The company reported approximately $260 million in year-over-year reductions in combined cost of services and selling, general, and administrative expenses, bringing the cumulative year-to-date reduction to over $1 billion. The quarter also included approximately $100 million in charges related to hurricane impacts and other non-recurring items.

input: With having out a Core i7 "Broadwell" ThinkPad X1 Carbon laptop for the MoCA 2.0 network tests , I decided to run some end-of-year graphics tests on this Core i7 5600U system with OpenGL and Vulkan.The last time I had out this particular system with i7-5600 CPU sporting HD Graphics 5500, the Vulkan experience wasn't really working out at that time. But a half-year has passed and now it's in better shape for this low-power ultrabook.I ran tests with the Linux 4.10 and Mesa 13.1-devel Git stacks atop Ubuntu 16.10 x86_64.The HD Graphics 5500 on this i7-5600U ultrabook aren't the fastest, but at 800 x 600 for Dota 2 we see the performance is about the same between the Vulkan and OpenGL drivers.Still close at 1280 x 1024.The performance is rather low, but those are the numbers for those always craving fresh Intel graphics results.Unfortunately no Talos Principle results for Vulkan as the game was hanging in this configuration.Still working on some other fresh tests with Iris Pro Graphics as well as the Skylake HD Graphics that provide for more playable Linux OpenGL/Vulkan gaming experience. Great to see overall though how the Intel "ANV" Vulkan driver has matured this year and is quite a competent driver while the i965 Mesa driver has also advanced in 2016 to supporting OpenGL 4.5, performance optimizations, and other improved functionality.
rewrite:
For the purpose of conducting MoCA 2.0 network evaluations, a Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon laptop equipped with a Core i7-5600U "Broadwell" processor was utilized. Subsequently, this system, featuring Intel HD Graphics 5500, was employed for a series of year-end graphical assessments using the OpenGL and Vulkan application programming interfaces. Previous testing conducted approximately six months prior indicated that the Vulkan implementation was not fully functional on this specific low-power ultrabook configuration. However, subsequent driver developments have improved its operational state.

Benchmarks were executed using the Linux 4.10 kernel and the Mesa 13.1-devel Git software stack, installed on an Ubuntu 16.10 x86_64 operating system. While the integrated HD Graphics 5500 solution does not deliver high performance, comparative testing for *Dota 2* at resolutions of 800 x 600 and 1280 x 1024 revealed nearly identical frame rates between the Vulkan and OpenGL drivers, albeit at generally low absolute levels. These results are presented for those interested in contemporary Intel graphics performance. Regrettably, *The Talos Principle* could not be evaluated under Vulkan due to system hangs in this configuration.

Additional testing is ongoing with more capable Intel Iris Pro and Skylake-era HD Graphics hardware, which enable a more viable gaming experience under Linux. Overall, the maturation of the Intel "ANV" open-source Vulkan driver over the past year is noteworthy, as it has evolved into a competent implementation. Concurrently, the i965 Mesa driver for OpenGL achieved support for OpenGL 4.5, along with various performance optimizations and functional enhancements throughout 2016.

Former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg has vowed to write a $4.5 million check to the United Nations body that oversees climate change negotiations to make up the shortfall in the agency's budget caused by U.S. funding cuts.
President Donald Trump last year formally announced the U.S. would pull out of the Paris climate accord deal, stating that it was not fair. Congress also cut funding for the Bonn, Germany-based UNFCCC from $7.5 million in previous years to $3 million this year.
"America made a commitment and as an American if the government's not going to do it we all have responsibility. I'm able to do it,” Bloomberg told CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. “So, yes, I'm going to send them a check for the monies that America had promised to the organization as though they got it from the federal government."
Bloomberg has long championed the fight against global warming.
“America is part of the problem. America is a big part of the solution and we should go in and help the world stop a potential disaster," Bloomberg added.
Bloomberg's charitable foundation linked the donation to the billionaire philanthropist's effort, with California Gov. Jerry Brown, to show that the United States remains committed to the Paris climate accord despite Trump's plan to withdraw from the agreement.
In a statement late Sunday, Bloomberg Philanthropies said further donations would be made if the U.S. fails to pay its share of the budget in 2019.
rewrite:
Former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg has pledged to personally contribute $4.5 million to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). This donation is intended to offset a budgetary shortfall resulting from reduced funding by the United States government. The reduction follows President Donald Trump’s formal announcement last year of the U.S. intention to withdraw from the Paris Climate Accord, a decision he justified on grounds of inequity. Consequently, congressional appropriations for the Bonn-based UNFCCC were decreased from $7.5 million in prior years to $3 million for the current fiscal period.

In a televised interview, Bloomberg stated, “America made a commitment, and as an American, if the government is not going to do it, we all have responsibility. I am able to do it.” He characterized his contribution as fulfilling the financial pledge originally made by the U.S. federal government to the organization. A long-standing advocate for climate action, Bloomberg further emphasized, “America is part of the problem. America is a big part of the solution, and we should go in and help the world stop a potential disaster.”

His philanthropic foundation explicitly connected this donation to a broader initiative, undertaken in partnership with California Governor Jerry Brown, to demonstrate continued U.S. subnational support for the Paris Agreement. Bloomberg Philanthropies additionally indicated that further private donations may be forthcoming should the U.S. government fail to meet its budgetary obligations to the UNFCCC in 2019.

NEW YORK — Fox News said Friday that the network’s legal counsel, who is named in lawsuits relating to the late former CEO Roger Ailes’ regime, is taking a “voluntary leave.”
Fox offered no additional details Friday on the departure of Dianne Brandi, including whether she is being paid or if she will return. She was a powerful leader at Fox under Ailes, who was forced out last year because of harassment charges.
Brandi has been named in pending lawsuits by former and current employees who alleged she did not act on complaints of harassment or discrimination against them by executives, and even retaliated against people who made charges. Brandi has denied the accusations.
She was named in cases filed by former on-air contributors Julie Roginsky and Andrea Tantaros, who both had complained about harassment by Ailes. She was also a part of a racial discrimination case involving several employees and a since-fired financial executive at Fox.
Douglas Wigdor, a lawyer for several of the people with cases against Fox, called the announcement of Brandi’s leave “long overdue.” He said the real question is whether Fox will apologize to the people he represents.
Former Fox co-president, Bill Shine, left the network in May after also being named in lawsuits for failing to correct behaviour at the network. Popular personality Bill O’Reilly was ousted this spring when it was revealed Fox had paid five women a total of $13 million to keep quiet about harassment allegations.
rewrite:

Ms. Brandi is named in multiple pending lawsuits connected to the tenure of former CEO Roger Ailes, who was compelled to resign last year following allegations of harassment. The network provided no further details regarding the terms of her departure, including her compensation status or potential return.

The lawsuits, brought by both former and current employees, allege that Ms. Brandi failed to address complaints of harassment and discrimination by network executives and, in some instances, retaliated against those who came forward. Ms. Brandi has denied these accusations. Her name appears in cases filed by former contributors Julie Roginsky and Andrea Tantaros, who reported harassment by Mr. Ailes, as well as in a racial discrimination case involving several employees and a since-dismissed financial executive.

This development follows other high-profile departures linked to the network’s workplace culture. Former co-president Bill Shine left in May after being similarly implicated in lawsuits for inaction, while prominent host Bill O’Reilly was ousted this spring following revelations that Fox paid substantial settlements to silence harassment allegations.

To apply for this assistance, individuals must complete the designated Hardship Assistance Application and submit all required supporting documentation to the County Administrator’s office. This submission must be received by May 1st of the applicable year. Upon verification of eligibility, the Administration will forward a copy of the approved application and an official approval letter to the Tax Collector’s office for processing.

The assessment rates for the 2016-17 fiscal year are structured as follows: residential dwelling units are assessed a flat fee of $75.00. Non-residential properties are assessed per square foot, with commercial and institutional uses at $0.12, and industrial/warehouse uses at $0.01. Agricultural and vacant land is assessed at a rate of $0.07 per acre.

Boston Tea Party is believed to be the first coffee chain in the UK to implement a complete ban on single-use plastic cups.
The independently-owned company, which has 21 branches across the Midlands and the South West, said the ban will come into effect on 1st June 2018.
Customers will be able to bring their own reusable cups, buy cups at the cafes at a subsidised rate or grab a loan cup, for which a deposit would have to be paid which would be refunded upon return to any of its outlets.
The coffee chain currently gives away around 340,000 takeaway hot drinks a year. Customers were previously offered a 25p discount on drinks if they used their own cup but only 2.8% of people took up the offer.
In the UK, only one in 400 of the estimated 2.5 billion plastic coated coffee cups are said to be recycled.
Sam Roberts, Owner and MD of Boston Tea Party said: “Lots of coffee chains are making pledges about how they plan to tackle cup waste in the future. But theirs is a future which is too far away. We need to stop right now.”

Annually, the chain distributes approximately 340,000 hot beverages for takeaway. Previously, a 25-pence discount was extended to customers supplying their own cups; however, only 2.8% accepted this incentive. Within the UK, it is estimated that merely one in 400 of the 2.5 billion plastic-coated coffee cups consumed is recycled. Sam Roberts, Owner and Managing Director of Boston Tea Party, remarked: "Numerous coffee chains are declaring intentions to address cup waste prospectively. Yet their timelines remain distant. Immediate cessation is imperative."

WASHINGTON, United States – The United States on Sunday sharply condemned a North Korean plan to test-fire an intercontinental ballistic missile and warned Pyongyang against “provocative actions.”
The toughly worded US statement called on “all states” to show the North that any unlawful actions would have “consequences.”
It was issued by the Pentagon at a sensitive time – just weeks before President Barack Obama is due to hand power over to his successor, Donald Trump.
ADVERTISEMENT
The statement came hours after Kim Jong-un, the North Korean leader, said his country was close to testing such a missile, which would be capable of reaching American shores.
“We are in the final stages of test-launching the intercontinental ballistic missile,” Kim said in a televised New Year’s speech, pointing to a string of nuclear and missile tests last year.
He said Pyongyang was now a “military power of the East that cannot be touched by even the strongest enemy.”
The Pentagon statement noted that “multiple UN Security Council resolutions explicitly prohibit North Korea’s launches using ballistic missile technology.”
It urged Pyongyang to “refrain from provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric that threaten international peace and stability.”
The statement reaffirmed Washington’s “ironclad commitment” to defend its allies, using “the full spectrum of US extended deterrence capabilities.”
Pyongyang has never successfully test-fired an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), and analysts are divided over how close it is to doing so.
But all agree it has made enormous strides in that direction since Kim took over as leader from his father Kim Jong-Il, who died in December 2011.
rewrite:
On Sunday, the United States issued a stern condemnation of North Korea's declared intention to conduct a test launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), cautioning Pyongyang against further provocations. The formal statement, articulated in robust terms, implored all nations to demonstrate that such unlawful endeavors would incur significant consequences. This diplomatic communication was released by the Pentagon during a politically sensitive period, occurring mere weeks before the scheduled transition of presidential authority from Barack Obama to Donald Trump.

The American response followed a New Year's address by North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, in which he asserted the nation was in the final phase of preparing an ICBM test, a weapon system theoretically capable of striking the United States mainland. Kim referenced a series of prior nuclear and missile tests, proclaiming North Korea had become an inviolable "military power of the East." The Pentagon's statement emphasized that these planned activities directly contravene multiple United Nations Security Council resolutions, which explicitly prohibit ballistic missile technology launches by North Korea. It further urged Pyongyang to desist from actions and rhetoric that jeopardize international peace and stability, while reaffirming the unwavering U.S. commitment to the defense of its allies through the full spectrum of extended deterrence capabilities.

Although Pyongyang has not yet successfully tested an ICBM, analysts concur that substantial advancements have been made in its missile program under Kim Jong-un's leadership since 2011. There remains, however, expert disagreement regarding the imminence of a fully operational capability.

Kangana's On Her Long List Of Affairs
Speaking about the same, Kangana said, ""I've had so many affairs. After every breakup I feel like this is the end of my love life potential. At every point you feel that you will be let down and you will never love again.
I have been feeling like that since I was 16. I've always felt that life has taken everything away from me and that I cannot fall in love again."
Kangana On Her Spat With Hrithik
"Even after this thing (the Hrithik affair) fell apart, another man came into my life and I felt I couldn't handle it anymore. But everything changed in two to three months and I felt that I was ready, and how!"
She Further Added..
"But just when you feel you are so high in love, that person says, ‘Oh, you are psycho!' and that person also left. You burst into tears every time you kiss and you are called a psycho."
Kangana Says She Never Dumped Anyone
"Even if my sister asks me where do you find these characters? Even then I have to admit that every time I have been dumped, I never got the privilege of dumping someone. There has not been a single relationship from the age of 16 to 31 where I could dump someone."
'Everyone Leaves Me'
She further added, "And if I tell you the names, you would be like ‘even this person left you'! Everyone leaves me and they come back also and I never take them back because I have been moved on to another loser."
Kangana On Changing Karan's POV On Nepotism
Speaking about the same, she told, "I am no one to do that, my intention was not that. He believes in bloodlines, dynasty and such talents worked for him, isn't it?
I cannot make him believe in talents that he does not believe in. but I can say what I want to say."
Kangana Says Her Comment Worked As A Catalyst
"I said it (about nepotism) out of observation. I am not an activist here, though I would love to serve the society; nepotism exists everywhere, we have grown up seeing it.
When I talked about it, perhaps people were subconsciously observing it, they wanted to talk about it. My comment worked as a catalyst."
rewrite:
In a discussion regarding her personal history of romantic engagements, Kangana Ranaut reflected upon the frequency of her past relationships. She stated, “I have experienced numerous romantic affairs. Following the conclusion of each relationship, I am invariably confronted with the sentiment that my capacity for a fulfilling love life has been permanently extinguished. One consistently anticipates disappointment and harbors the belief that the ability to love anew is lost. This particular feeling has persisted since I was sixteen years of age. I have perpetually felt as though life has deprived me of all romantic possibility, leaving me incapable of experiencing love again.”

Addressing the period subsequent to her widely publicized dispute with Hrithik Roshan, she elaborated, “Even after that situation dissolved, another romantic partner entered my life, and I initially believed I could no longer manage such emotional investment. However, my perspective transformed entirely within a span of two to three months, and I felt prepared to engage once more, and with considerable intensity.” She further added, “Yet, precisely at the moment one feels most elevated by love, that individual may levy a charge such as, ‘You are psycho,’ and subsequently depart. One is then reduced to tears during moments of intimacy, all while being labeled with that term.”

On the subject of relationship conclusions, Ranaut clarified that she has never been the instigator of a breakup. “Even when questioned by my sister regarding where I encounter such individuals, I must concede that in every instance, I have been the one who was ended a relationship with; I have never possessed the privilege of terminating one myself. From the age of sixteen until thirty-one, there has not been a single romantic association wherein I was afforded the agency to end it.” She expanded upon this theme, noting, “And should I divulge the names of these individuals, the common reaction would be astonishment that even that person left me. Everyone departs. They occasionally attempt to return, but I do not reconcile, as I have invariably progressed to another unsuitable partner.”

Shifting to a professional critique, Ranaut discussed her public comments on nepotism within the film industry and their impact on Karan Johar’s perspective. “It is not my place to alter his viewpoint; that was never my intention,” she said. “He subscribes to beliefs in bloodlines and dynastic success, and such talents have proven effective for his purposes. I cannot compel him to recognize talents in which he does not believe. However, I retain the right to express my own observations.”

She characterized her commentary as having served a catalytic function. “I spoke regarding nepotism from a place of observation. I do not position myself as an activist, though I possess a desire to contribute to society; nepotism is a ubiquitous phenomenon, and we have been conditioned to witness it from a young age. When I addressed the topic, it is possible the public had been subconsciously noting its prevalence and desired its discussion. My remark acted as a catalyst for that conversation.”

So-called ‘good families with multiple children should leave big cities because such places are full of sin and relocate to agricultural settlements allocated to them by the government’, he demanded.
In one of his more incendiary statements, he said:

Archpriest Vsevolod Chaplin, a prominent and doctrinally conservative Russian Orthodox cleric based in Moscow, has publicly advocated for the restoration of the monarchy in Russia, proposing that Vladimir Putin be named emperor. As an alternative, he suggested reinstating the Romanov dynasty, which was deposed a century ago in 1917. He articulated these views during the launch of his recent publication.

Chaplin asserted, "We are a nation with a monarchical mentality. The absence of a formal monarchy is inconsequential; I believe we can reestablish it with Putin at its apex. Alternatively, it could involve a descendant of the Romanov house or an elected individual as sovereign." He further contended, "Although a formal monarchy does not exist, we possess a monarchical understanding that Russia cannot exist without a tsar. He opposes the inclusion of contraception information in sexual education curricula and previously advocated permitting marriage at age fourteen for girls and sixteen for boys without parental consent. He stated, "It would be preferable if women bore several children by age twenty and pursued professional careers only after thirty or forty, once their children are grown."

He demanded that what he termed "good families with multiple children" vacate major urban centers, which he described as environments rife with sin, and relocate to government-allocated agricultural settlements.

DOHA, April 5 Qatar Petroleum (QP) and ExxonMobil will start drilling for oil and gas off the southern coast of Cyprus in 2018, the Qatari firm said after signing an exploration and production sharing contract with the Mediterranean island.
Exploring the Mediterranean's Levant Basin has become more attractive since Eni discovered Egypt's offshore Zohr field in 2015, the biggest gas field in the Mediterranean and estimated to contain 850 billion cubic metres of gas.
State-owned Qatar Petroleum and ExxonMobil were among bidders last year for a contract for Cyprus's offshore Block 10.
"A 3D seismic survey is already underway, as the consortium partners prepare to begin exploration drilling in 2018," QP said in a statement.
To maintain its dominance over competitors in the United States and Australia, QP is cutting costs at its domestic operations and seeking to expand overseas through joint ventures with international oil firms, QP said in February.
(Reporting by Tom Finn; Editing by Edmund Blair)
rewrite: On April 5 in Doha, Qatar Petroleum (QP) announced that, following the signing of an exploration and production sharing contract with Cyprus, it will commence joint offshore oil and gas drilling with ExxonMobil off the island’s southern coast in 2018. This activity targets Block 10, for which both companies submitted bids last year. The decision to explore the Levant Basin in the Mediterranean has been incentivized by the 2015 discovery of Egypt’s Zohr field by Eni, the largest known gas field in the region with estimated reserves of 850 billion cubic metres. According to a QP statement, a three-dimensional seismic survey is currently in progress in preparation for the planned exploration drilling. This international venture aligns with QP’s broader strategic objective, noted in February, of sustaining its competitive position against rivals in the United States and Australia by reducing domestic operational costs and pursuing overseas expansion through partnerships with major international firms.

China will further tighten controls on individuals’ foreign currency purchases to try to curb massive capital flight from the country as the yuan falls sharply against the dollar.
Individuals wishing to convert yuan to foreign currencies will now have to provide more detailed information to their bank, including an explanation of the funds concerned in addition to their identity papers, said the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), according to AFP.
Each year individuals can convert up to the equivalent of $50,000, a maximum sum that will not change, it said on its website.
The tighter controls are aimed at preventing attempts to circumvent this quota.
The idea is to “combat illegal transactions, money-laundering and clandestine banks,” the agency said, vowing to multiply random checks and toughen its sanctions.
Banks must verify the authenticity of the information provided. In addition, from July, financial institutions will have to report to the central bank any international transfer exceeding 200,000 yuan ($28,800), in order to fight laundering, the central bank announced.
The tighter controls are part of an array of measures taken by the government to curb huge capital outflows.
The equivalent of about $1 trillion was transferred out of China in 2015 and another $690 billion in the first 10 months of 2016, according to Bloomberg Intelligence estimates.
Slower growth in China, the weakness of the yuan and the recent rise in US interest rates are encouraging savers to invest their money in other currencies.
The yuan is at its lowest in eight years against the dollar and the outflows are putting further pressure on the currency.
Authorities are trying to support it by buying yuan, drawing on China’s foreign exchange reserves, which fell by nearly $70 billion in November.
rewrite:
In response to significant depreciation of the yuan against the US dollar, Chinese authorities are implementing stricter regulatory measures on individual foreign currency purchases to mitigate substantial capital outflows. According to an announcement by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), individuals seeking to convert yuan into foreign currencies must now furnish their banks with more comprehensive documentation. This includes not only standard identification but also a detailed justification for the intended use of the funds. The annual conversion limit for individuals remains unchanged at the equivalent of $50,000. The enhanced scrutiny is explicitly designed to prevent circumvention of this established quota.

SAFE stated that the objective of these measures is to "combat illegal transactions, money-laundering and clandestine banks," accompanied by a commitment to increase randomized inspections and impose more severe penalties for non-compliance. Financial institutions are mandated to verify the authenticity of the information submitted by clients. Furthermore, as separately announced by the central bank, commencing in July, all international transfers exceeding 200,000 yuan (approximately $28,800) must be reported to facilitate anti-money laundering efforts.

These tightened controls constitute one component of a broader governmental strategy to curtail extensive capital flight. Estimates from Bloomberg Intelligence indicate that outflows amounted to roughly $1 trillion in 2015, followed by an additional $690 billion within the first ten months of 2016. This trend is driven by several factors, including moderated economic growth within China, the relative weakness of the yuan, and recent increases in US interest rates, which collectively incentivize savers to seek investments denominated in other currencies. The yuan currently trades at an eight-year low against the dollar, and persistent outflows exert further downward pressure on its value. In an effort to provide support, monetary authorities have intervened in currency markets by purchasing yuan, drawing upon the nation's foreign exchange reserves, which diminished by nearly $70 billion in November alone.

COLUMBUS, Ohio — The San Jose Sharks took advantage of its power plays and a Columbus scoring slump to get a needed win.
Kevin Labanc and Logan Couture each had a goal and an assist, and Martin Jones stopped 28 shots to lift the Sharks to a 3-1 win over the Blue Jackets on Friday night, snapping a four-game skid.
The Sharks' first two goals came on power plays, with Labanc getting a wide-open look at the net with a 5-on-3 advantage in the second period. Marc-Edouard Vlasic also scored for San Jose.
"The power play has been the key for us for the last 2 1/2 months," San Jose coach Peter DeBoer said. "The one thing we have is a lot of options there. We have a lot of guys who are comfortable on the power play, and they're playing with a lot of confidence right now."
Sergei Bobrovsky had 25 saves for the Blue Jackets, who have lost two in a row and five of their last seven. Boone Jenner had the lone goal as Columbus continues to have trouble finding the back of the net. The team has scored two or fewer goals in regulation in 11 of the last 12 games.
"We just have no rhythm offensively," Blue Jackets coach John Tortorella said.
Couture tallied 5:07 into the game with the Blue Jackets' Matt Calvert in the penalty box for tripping. Couture got his 22nd goal of the season when he snapped a shot from the high slot over the glove of Bobrovsky, who was shielded by 6-foot-5 defenceman Brent Burns.
Jenner tied the score 4:30 into the second period with his fifth goal of the season and first in 13 games when he rifled a shot off the bar from the top of the left circle.
Columbus was victimized on another power play at 10:20 in the second when Labanc scored from 15 feet out while Seth Jones and Nick Foligno served penalties. Tororella was so angry that he benched Foligno, the Blue Jackets' captain, for the rest of the period and much of the third.
Tortorella said the punishment didn't result from just the untimely penalty. "It was a few other things," he said, but declined to discuss it any further.
rewrite:
On Friday evening in Columbus, Ohio, the San Jose Sharks secured a 3-1 victory over the Columbus Blue Jackets, thereby ending a four-game losing streak. The outcome was significantly influenced by the Sharks’ effective utilization of power-play opportunities, coupled with the Blue Jackets’ ongoing offensive difficulties.

San Jose’s scoring commenced early in the first period. At the 5:07 mark, Logan Couture capitalized on a power play resulting from a tripping penalty assessed to Columbus forward Matt Calvert. Couture registered his 22nd goal of the season with a shot from the high slot that eluded goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky, who was partially screened by defenseman Brent Burns. Columbus equalized early in the second period when Boone Jenner recorded his fifth goal of the season, ending a personal 13-game scoring drought with a shot from the top of the left circle that struck the crossbar before entering the net.

The Sharks reclaimed the lead later in the second period during a two-man advantage. With a 5-on-3 power play, Kevin Labanc converted from approximately 15 feet, giving San Jose a lead they would not relinquish. Marc-Edouard Vlasic added a further goal to solidify the victory. Goaltender Martin Jones contributed 28 saves for San Jose. Sharks coach Peter DeBoer emphasized the critical role of the power play, stating, "The power play has been the key for us for the last two and a half months. We have a lot of options there and a lot of guys who are comfortable on it, playing with a lot of confidence."

Conversely, the Blue Jackets, who have now lost two consecutive games and five of their last seven, continued to struggle offensively. The team has been limited to two or fewer goals in regulation time in eleven of its last twelve contests. Coach John Tortorella summarized the issue succinctly: "We just have no rhythm offensively." His frustration was further evidenced by his decision to bench captain Nick Foligno for the remainder of the second period and much of the third following the penalty that led to Labanc’s decisive goal. Tortorella indicated the disciplinary action stemmed from "a few other things" beyond the untimely infraction but declined to elaborate further. Bobrovsky finished the contest with 25 saves for Columbus.

TRIPOLI May 3 Rival Libyan camps issued separate statements on Wednesday promising to calm tensions in southern Libya and fight terrorism, but offering no shared way forward for a political deal to unify the North African country.
The statements came a day after intense diplomatic pressure resulted in a meeting in Abu Dhabi between eastern-based commander Khalifa Haftar and the head of the U.N.-backed government in Tripoli, Fayez Seraj.
Haftar is the key figure for eastern factions that, frustrating international efforts to end Libya's conflict, spurned Seraj's Government of National Accord (GNA) after it was established in the capital last year.
There was no mention in the statement from Seraj of plans reported by pro-Haftar media on Tuesday to restructure the unity government's leadership and hold fresh elections next year.
A source close to the GNA leadership said the two sides had initially tried to agree on a joint statement before deciding to issue separate declarations.
Conflicting accounts of initial agreements and leaks of documents neither side signed have in the past confused international mediation and negotiations to end the conflict in Libya, which fell into factional fighting in the years after a 2011 civil war ousted Muammar Gaddafi. (Reporting by Aidan Lewis in Tunis, Ahmed Elumami in Tripoli and Ayman al-Warfalli in Benghazi; editing by Patrick Markey and John Stonestreet)
rewrite:
On Wednesday, May 3rd, rival Libyan factions issued separate declarations pledging to de-escalate tensions in southern Libya and to combat terrorism. However, these statements provided no mutually agreed framework for a political settlement to unify the North African nation. This development followed a meeting in Abu Dhabi the previous day between Khalifa Haftar, the commander of eastern-based forces, and Fayez Serraj, the head of the United Nations-backed Government of National Accord (GNA) in Tripoli, a meeting convened under considerable diplomatic pressure.

Commander Haftar, a pivotal figure for eastern factions, has previously rejected the GNA since its establishment in Tripoli last year, thereby obstructing international efforts to resolve Libya's conflict. Notably, the statement from Serraj’s government did not address reports from pro-Haftar media outlining alleged plans to restructure the unity government's leadership and to conduct new elections next year. According to a source proximate to the GNA leadership, the two sides initially attempted to formulate a joint communiqué before opting for independent declarations.

Historically, such parallel statements, alongside contradictory reports of preliminary agreements and the leakage of unsigned documents, have complicated international mediation aimed at ending Libya's conflict. The nation has been mired in factional strife since the 2011 civil war that ousted Muammar Gaddafi.

DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) – Police in Dayton were called to the 2700 block of Wayne Avenue Sunday after a man said he was robbed.
The incident happened around 6:30 pm Sunday when a man was trying to sell a sweatshirt using a popular phone app.
When officers arrived they met with a man who said he was there to meet with a man to sell his “Peace Skateboard” sweatshirt using the app “Let Go”. The victim told police the person he was there to meet identified himself as Glen Smith, who claimed to be 15-years-old and could not drive.
According to a police report on the incident, when the victim arrived at the agreed meeting place, Smith was not there. Through several text messages, the victim agreed to meet Smith in another location.
When the victim arrived at the intersection of Maplewood Avenue and Kathleen Avenue, he met with Glen and a third person. The men talked for about an hour when Smith claimed he had lost his money. The victim then told Glen he had other things to do and had to leave.
According to the report, the man who identified himself as Glen Smith gave the sweatshirt to his masked friend who then ran off. When the victim confronted “Glen” about it Gen pulled a silver, semi-automatic handgun from his waistband and fired one shot into the air.
The victim then ran away and told police he heard a second shot fired.
No arrests have been made in this case.
rewrite:
On Sunday, February 25th, at approximately 6:30 p.m., law enforcement officers in Dayton, Ohio, responded to a reported robbery in the 2700 block of Wayne Avenue. The victim, who had arranged to sell a "Peace Skateboard" sweatshirt via the digital marketplace application "LetGo," informed authorities that he had agreed to meet an individual identifying himself as Glen Smith. This individual claimed to be fifteen years of age and stated he was unable to drive.

Per the official police report, the initial agreed-upon location was altered through a series of text messages, culminating in a meeting at the intersection of Maplewood Avenue and Kathleen Avenue. Upon arrival, the victim encountered Smith and an additional, unidentified individual. Following an hour of conversation, during which Smith alleged he had misplaced his funds, the victim expressed a need to depart. At that juncture, Smith transferred the sweatshirt to his companion, who was wearing a mask and subsequently fled the scene. When the victim confronted Smith regarding this action, Smith produced a silver semi-automatic handgun from his waistband and discharged one round into the air. The victim immediately fled and reported hearing a second gunshot as he retreated.

The investigation remains ongoing, and no arrests have been made at this time.

The selection concludes with cultural events, including a Thai New Year celebration involving elephants, and novel social interactions, exemplified by a detailed dating application created by a college student.

A woman walks past a branch of The Co-operative Bank in London, Britain.
London: Britain’s Cooperative Bank, rescued from the brink of collapse by a group of hedge funds in 2013, has put itself up for sale as it seeks to build up its capital to meet regulatory requirements.
The bank said on Monday that it had made considerable progress implementing its turnaround plan, cutting its cost base by a fifth since 2014.
But it still expects to make a “significant loss” for last year and said that building up capital has proved difficult given low interest rates.
“As a result, and having concluded its annual planning review, the board is today commencing a sale process, inviting offers for all of the issued ordinary share capital in the bank,” the bank said.
The Bank of England’s Prudential Regulation Authority, which regulates Cooperative Bank, said it welcomed the measures announced on Monday.
“We will continue to assess the bank’s progress in building greater financial resilience over the coming months,” the PRA said in a statement.
The Cooperative Bank, which has four million customers, said it was also considering ways to raise equity capital from existing and new capital providers, and a potential “liability management exercise” of its outstanding public debt.
Last month, the bank said it expected its core capital ratio to fall below 10 per cent, falling short of regulatory requirements.
The bank’s immediate issue is the repayment of £400 million (Dh1.8 billion) worth of bonds that mature in September.
Co-op Bank nearly folded in 2013 with a £1.5 billion hole in its capital after losses from problem real estate loans.
The bank was rescued by bondholders, including hedge funds, mainly from the United States, who bet that rising interest rates and a cost-cutting turnaround plan would improve the bank’s fortunes and make them a return on their investment.

The Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) of the Bank of England, the bank’s regulator, has expressed support for the measures disclosed on Monday. With a customer base of four million, The Cooperative Bank is also exploring avenues to raise equity capital from both existing and new investors, alongside a potential "liability management exercise" concerning its outstanding public debt. There’s all kinds of threats flying around these days — North Korea threatening Guam, China threatening to cut off trade to North Korea, and Donald Trump threatening pretty much everyone. Now you can add a new ultimatum to the list, this one from Nicolás Maduro Guerra, the son of the Venezuelan president. He didn’t take kindly to Trump’s pronouncement that he would use military force in Venezuela if necessary, and now Guerra says not only would he retaliate if that came to pass, that retaliation would come in the form of actually taking the White House by force.
“If the unlikely event of defiling the homeland came to pass, the rifles would arrive in New York, ” Guerra announced to Venezuelan state media. “Mr. Trump, we would arrive and take the White House.”
Ignoring for a moment that the White House is not in New York, this is Guerra’s comeback to Trump’s recent comment that “Venezuela is not very far away and the people are suffering, and they are dying. We have many options for Venezuela, including a possible military option if necessary.”
That was a response after Maduro’s recent dismissal of Venezuelan parliament and replacement with his own Constituent Assembly. At least for now, Venezuela’s military is busy keeping the peace in Caracas, where protests have broken out amongst Venezuelans tired of food shortages, worthless currency, the not-so-mysterious disappearance of their fellow citizens, and general chaos.
Guerra isn’t the only Venezuelan to respond to Trump’s threat, though. Venezuelan Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino said it would be a “crazy act” if Trump actually tried it. Not that it would it be the first time the U.S. involved itself in Venezuela’s political woes or the governments of Latin American nations. None of those contras have yet resulted in Venezuelans storming the White House, but as always, these are complicated situations with one very uncomplicated U.S. president in charge.
(Via CNN)
rewrite:
In the contemporary geopolitical landscape, a multitude of threats are being exchanged. These range from North Korea’s menacing statements toward Guam and China’s warnings to curtail trade with North Korea, to the frequent adversarial pronouncements from U.S. President Donald Trump directed at various nations. To this list must now be added a new ultimatum issued by Nicolás Maduro Guerra, the son of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. This statement constitutes a direct response to President Trump’s recent assertion that he would consider employing military force in Venezuela if deemed necessary. Guerra has declared that any such intervention would be met with retaliation, audaciously specifying that this countermeasure would involve an armed assault to seize the White House.

Addressing Venezuelan state media, Guerra proclaimed, “If the unlikely event of defiling the homeland came to pass, the rifles would arrive in New York. Mr. Trump, we would arrive and take the White House.” This rhetoric, notwithstanding the geographical inaccuracy regarding the location of the White House, serves as a rejoinder to Trump’s comments concerning the Venezuelan crisis. Trump had previously stated, “Venezuela is not very far away and the people are suffering, and they are dying. We have many options for Venezuela, including a possible military option if necessary.” The U.S. president’s remarks themselves were a reaction to President Maduro’s recent dissolution of the Venezuelan National Assembly and its replacement with a government-loyal Constituent Assembly. Presently, the Venezuelan military remains occupied with maintaining order in Caracas, where protracted protests continue against severe food shortages, hyperinflation, unexplained disappearances, and widespread social disorder.

Guerra is not the sole Venezuelan official to rebuke Trump’s threat. Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino López similarly denounced the prospect of U.S. military action as a “crazy act.” Historical context underscores that U.S. involvement in Venezuelan and broader Latin American political affairs is not unprecedented. While past interventions have not precipitated an assault on the White House, the current situation remains complex, further complicated by the characteristically unambiguous posture of the U.S. administration.

Shaner Elementary in Topeka is one of three elementary schools ceasing elementary operations after this year, and the students there are planning to give it a proper sendoff.
“At Shaner, we’re going to be holding a very special community publishing party,” said Communities in School coordinator Susan Ortega. “This is an opportunity for our students to sort of write a good-bye letter to Shaner, letting us know what their best memories and good times were, as well as if they have something they want to say to the building one last time before they head on to Jardine Academy.
The publishing party event is this coming Sunday, April 23rd from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. at the school.
“We want our community members, either former students or former staff members to come back in and really have a chance to share their memories, as well,” said Ortega. “At 2:30 on the day of our celebration, we’re going to be recognizing all the former teachers and staff members.”
The Shaner group has been close knit from the beginning.
“We’re talking about a student population that’s been less than 190 students,” said Ortega. “When you consider some of the sizes of the other elementary schools in Topeka, that’s actually a pretty small school. We only have 11 total classes in our entire building. Getting to have that sort of intimate contact with students where you get to see them on a daily basis and you learn every person’s name, it’s been amazing.”
Shaner, Bishop and Avondale West elementary students will combine to form Jardine Academy beginning this fall.
rewrite:
Shaner Elementary School in Topeka, one of three district elementary schools concluding operations at the end of this academic year, is preparing for a formal closure. The school community has organized a commemorative event to mark this transition. According to Susan Ortega, coordinator for the Communities in Schools program, a distinctive community publishing party will be held. This event is designed to provide students with an opportunity to compose farewell letters to the school, documenting their most valued memories and experiences. Additionally, it offers a final occasion for students to express any parting sentiments to the physical building before they transition to Jardine Academy this fall.

The publishing party is scheduled for Sunday, April 23rd, from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. at the school. Ortega emphasized that the event is also intended to welcome former students and staff members, inviting them to return and share their recollections. A specific recognition ceremony for all former teachers and staff is planned for 2:30 p.m. during the celebration. Ortega further noted the notably close-knit nature of the Shaner community, attributing this in part to its small size. With a student population consistently below 190 and only eleven classes in the entire building, the school fostered an environment of considerable intimacy. This scale allowed for daily, personalized interaction between staff and students, facilitating the ability to know each individual by name—a characteristic described as a remarkable aspect of the school’s culture. Following the closures, students from Shaner, Bishop, and Avondale West Elementary Schools will consolidate to form the new Jardine Academy beginning in the upcoming autumn semester.

World production of major foods set records last year, according to this week’s outlook analysis from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Cereal stock levels have climbed to all-time highs.
A joint outlook prepared by the OECD and the United Nation’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) predicts weakening growth in global demand for agricultural commodities and food, while anticipating continuing productivity improvements in the sector.
As a result, prices of main agricultural commodities are expected to remain low for the next 10 years.
The report attributes the demand slowdown to a deceleration of demand growth in major emerging economies, stagnating per capita consumption of staple foods and a further gradual decline in global population growth rates.
The global agricultural and fish production is projected to grow by around 20 per cent over the coming decade, but with considerable variation across regions.
Strong growth is expected in developing regions with more rapid population growth, including Sub-Saharan Africa, South and East Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa. By contrast, production growth is expected to be much lower in developed countries, especially in Western Europe.
Declining demand growth for meat products will put a brake on the demand for cereals and protein meal used in animal feed.
With slower consumption and production growth, agricultural and fish trade are projected to grow at about half the rate of the previous decade.
Net exports are expected to increase from land-abundant countries, such as Canada and the Americas.
Countries with high population growth, in particular in the Middle East and North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa and in Asia, will see rising net imports.
Demand for cereals and vegetable oil for the production of biofuels is expected to be largely unchanged over the forecast period, in contrast with the past decade, when biofuels expansion led to more than 120 million tonnes of additional cereals demand, predominantly corn.
With existing policies in developed countries unlikely to support biofuels expansion, most demand growth will come from developing countries that have introduced policies favouring biofuel use.
In particular, the use of sugarcane for biofuel production is expected to increase.
rewrite:
According to a recent outlook analysis published by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), global production of principal food commodities achieved unprecedented levels in the preceding year. Concurrently, global cereal stocks have ascended to historical peaks. A collaborative forecast issued by the OECD and the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) projects a moderation in the growth of worldwide demand for agricultural commodities and foodstuffs over the coming decade, while also anticipating sustained enhancements in agricultural productivity. Consequently, the prices of key agricultural commodities are forecast to persist at subdued levels for the foreseeable ten-year period.

This projected deceleration in demand is ascribed to several interrelated factors: a slowdown in demand growth within major emerging economies, stagnant per capita consumption of basic staple foods, and a continued gradual decline in global population growth rates. Aggregate global agricultural and fisheries output is projected to expand by approximately twenty percent over the next decade, albeit with significant regional disparities. Robust production growth is anticipated in developing regions characterized by more rapid demographic expansion, notably Sub-Saharan Africa, South and East Asia, and the Middle East and North Africa. In contrast, production growth in developed nations, particularly within Western Europe, is expected to be markedly more subdued.

A declining growth rate in demand for meat products is further predicted to constrain demand for cereals and protein meals utilized in animal feed. Given these moderated trajectories for both consumption and production, the growth of agricultural and fisheries trade is projected to proceed at roughly half the pace observed in the previous decade. Net exports are anticipated to rise from land-abundant regions, including the Americas and Canada. Conversely, nations with high population growth, especially in the Middle East and North Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa, and parts of Asia, are expected to experience increasing net imports.

Demand for cereals and vegetable oils destined for biofuel production is forecast to remain largely static over the outlook period. This represents a distinct departure from the previous decade, during which biofuel expansion precipitated an additional demand exceeding 120 million tonnes of cereals, predominantly maize. As existing policy frameworks in developed countries are unlikely to incentivize further biofuel expansion, the majority of future demand growth in this sector is expected to originate from developing nations that have implemented policies favoring biofuel utilization. Specifically, the utilization of sugarcane for biofuel production is projected to increase.

General News of Friday, 6 October 2017
Source: Starrfmonline.com
2017-10-06
Sophia Akuffo, Chief Justice
The Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo has bemoaned the growing indiscipline at the BAR of Ghana as she charges newly enrolled lawyers to be of good behaviour.
According to Justice Akuffo, the high level of indiscipline amongst lawyers in Ghana is alarming and disappointing.
Addressing 208 newly enrolled lawyers to the Ghana BAR at the enrollment ceremony held at the Banquet Hall of the State House Friday, the Chief Justice said the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council (GLC) is overwhelmed by the several misconduct complaints against lawyers.
She charged the newly enrolled lawyers to uphold all the rules governing the Profession they have chosen.
“We are witnessing these days a distressing increase in a number of disciplinary complaints that come before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council against lawyers especially the younger ones at the BAR.
“The root cause of most of these is lack of self-discipline and the desire to get rich quick on the part of new lawyers,” the Chief Justice said on Friday.
Justice Akuffo called on the lawyers to at all times observe the rules and ensure that none of them ever appears before the disciplinary committee of the General Legal Council.
rewrite:
On October 6, 2017, Chief Justice Sophia Akuffo addressed a cohort of 208 newly enrolled legal practitioners at a ceremony held in the Banquet Hall of the State House. In her remarks, Justice Akuffo expressed profound concern regarding escalating levels of professional misconduct within the Ghanaian legal community, describing the trend as both alarming and disappointing. She reported that the Disciplinary Committee of the General Legal Council (GLC) is currently inundated with complaints of misconduct against lawyers, particularly those newly admitted to the Bar.

The Chief Justice attributed this distressing increase primarily to a deficit in self-discipline and an imprudent pursuit of rapid financial gain among recent entrants to the profession. She explicitly charged the newly enrolled lawyers to steadfastly uphold the ethical codes and regulations governing their chosen vocation. Emphasizing the imperative of professional integrity, Justice Akuffo urged the practitioners to consistently observe all prescribed rules, thereby avoiding any future appearances before the GLC's Disciplinary Committee. Her address served as a direct admonition to prioritize ethical conduct and to counteract the patterns of indiscipline currently challenging the legal profession in Ghana.
